author: Raymond Yee

review_text: Went for sunday brunch. The restaurant was a little smaller than I thought. Food was good, such as the 6 different types of oysters, grilled seafood, salad bar, cheese station. There was a second restaurant for desserts, but the desserts were rather ordinary since there’s no tiramisu or durian. Overpriced considering other buffets I went to. About $150 per person inclusive of 9% GST.
author: Charsy Cat

review_text: the kitchen table offers a wonderfully relaxing ambiance with its modern decor. The friendly staff provided attentive service throughout our meal. They have a good food variety focusing on international cuisine, and while the regular food is decent, their Christmas menu was absolutely shiok! We also loved the fireworks birthday dessert – a really nice touch. It’s a great spot for a special occasion.
author: Lawrence Tan

review_text: I was very impressed by every dish we ordered! The charcoal grilled fish was fresh and had crispy skin plus the charcoal flavour. The pork chop had very tasty sauce and comes with one of the best fries I've eaten in awhile. The lobster bisque was enhanced with local flavours, resulting in a very unique and delicious dish. Service was impeccable as well! Special mention to Bhavani who patiently served us with a smile and helped us with selecting a fish for the grill!
author: Hungry Yeen

review_text:
We reserved a table for dinner on the 30th and got a very nice experience. The staff were friendly and nice to us. They explained clearly about different kinds of cuts for steak and recommended a good one based on our preferences. We also asked them for recommendation for wine, which turned out really good with the dishes.
I ordered medium rare. 50% of the steak was medium rare, however, it still tasted very nice.
The duck was tender and rich. The steak was so good that my husband said it was even better than Ruth’s Chris’.
author: Trang Pham

review_text:
Second time here.
Celebrate my wedding anniversary and birthday precious.  And the food melt my mouth, so I bring my friends today for another unforgettable yummy food. Of cos, they enjoy it. Everything was damn good.
From vibes, to services to food. Everything was just first class.
Thank you skirt for your wonderful service.
author: Daphane Yeo

review_text:
This is the 3rd time returning to Skirt and their steaks are excellent and great variety and selection of cuts and high quality suppliers. This time we especially loved the cabbage which was the pleasant surprise in taste and quality which surpassed expectations. We had the David Blackmore Rohnes Skirt steak 200g Australia and the Tournedos Rossini and Black Winter Truffle
Beef Tenderloin, Foic Gras, Périgueux. The Skirt steak I felt was more flavourful but on the tough side compared to the tenderloin cut which was more tender less intense flavours but with the foi gras was a great balance. The waiters were welcoming and engaging and the Sylvester Kua who was serving us gave great recommendations on the wine pairing and dishes. The only down side was it was a bit too dark for us to see our meals despite the table lamps. But overall the good food and service more than made up for it.
author: Jeremy Ong

review_text: Hospitality was warm and attentive from the moment we were greeted, to being seated, to the food recommendations and dessert service. The meat selection was limited as several items were sold out — understandable, as all their meats are aged. The bone in rib eye, fish, and duck were excellent, and the octopus was perfectly tender. The cakes were great as well. Especially loved the pistachios Kunafa.
author: Belle Ng

review_text:
We had the set lunch and there was the unlimited appetizer which has beef tartare, dry-aged hamachi and beetroot. We loved it so much that we went for second servings. For the mains, we tried the dry-aged duck and the Sanchoku picanha. The duck had a crispy skin with tender and juicy meat. The steak was tender and cooked to perfection.
For dessert, the smoked cheesecake was rich, creamy and full of cheesy goodness, while the corn nutty tart delivered a punch of strong corn flavour paired with a textured nutty crust. Every dish was beautifully plated. On top of the delicious food, the staff were attentive and friendly.
author: Madeleine Tan

review_text:
I can say you will feel like not in Singapore when u dine with the wonderful rows of yatch beside you.

The food spread is not alot, but definitely quality with good vibes and live singer to chill the evening .

The korean mid wings is amazing..

Mushroom skewers is a must..

Service is excellent,  no rush let you relax more when u dine.

Best time is 630 onwards to see how the bay changes it form when sun sets
author: joe fong

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
We celebrated Halloween at Boater Bar and had an amazing time! The decorations were fantastic and the live DJ kept the vibe lively all night. My kids loved the candies and sweet treats from the staff. The pizza was super delicious, and even though it was a full house, the team was efficient and very attentive. Great atmosphere — we’ll definitely be back! 🎃🍕🎶
author: Just Me Chili

review_text: I had a great evening at Boatus Bar, thanks to the fantastic service provided by Kate, Winston, and Paul. They were attentive, friendly, and efficient, making our night even more enjoyable. The service was impressively fast, We tried a Beef burger Charcoal Bread comes with generous amount of tasty fries and we also got to enjoy a great promo just $10++ per beer, which was a nice bonus. F I ordered a gin atonic, and it was perfectly made. Overall, a wonderful experience. I’ll definitely be back!
author: Jess SP

review_text: Been here a few times. Always a nice place to have drinks and food. Choices of pizza or burgers or grilled steaks. Service is great!
author: Renut

review_text: Great place to chill outdoors. The food and drinks were really good and the vibes were relaxed. Staff were friendly and attentive.
author: nan tinzarchiwin (Chili)

review_text: Food looks fancy, but taste was just moderate. However, draft beer was good, service was excellent. Atmosphere was great to chill.
author: Jasie

review_text:
June 2024
- Managed to get a seat without trouble.
- Tried the good old Italian classic, the Margherita Pizza. If a shop cannot do a simple classic, then no point to try any others. Glad to say it was decent.
- There's a decent collection of wine on the shelves, and took some time to look through them.
- Overall, the main selling point about the place is the location. It's the first restaurant leading to the marina waterfront, and has appropriate decoration, and vibes.
author: Wei Yuet Wong

review_text: Ordered frutti di mare the seafood pizza and it was great! Liked that the clams were silky soft n the taste of pasta was very unique like yall gotta come down n try yourselves. Cld taste a little bit of lemon which made it refreshing too ! However pasta was slightly hard but its ok
author: soot candies

review_text:
Nice pizza place besides W Singapore. Definitely expensive place but they have a big nice oven which customers can see the chef putting the pizza and cooking them.

Ambient is nice and relaxing without the buzz and huzz of RWS areas at the same price.
Overlooks Marina and on weekday evening a nice place to enjoy a quiet dinner.
Staff was prompt to take our orders but didn’t offer to top up our glasses of iced water at all 😝
Walked the whole stretch of restaurants in the quayside before deciding on this one.
author: mark Lim

review_text: It’s a pity that in such a pristine spot, an Italian food restaurant is not ran properly. Hope to see a step up in quality of service and Pizzas.
author: Salvatore Sabbatino

review_text:
I ordered BBQ Chicken Pizza and Pepperoni Pizza for takeaway at Two Chefs Bar, and both were really delicious. The pizza crust was thin but full of flavor, with generous toppings and well-balanced seasoning. There was a nice crunchy texture, combined with a savory, satisfying taste in every bite.

The location is very convenient, especially if you’re staying around the W Hotel area. The place has a pleasant vibe, and the staff were friendly and helpful, even for takeaway orders.

Definitely a great spot if you’re craving good pizza nearby. Highly recommended!
author: Lusy Kusumawati

review_text:
We went to Two Chefs Bar in Sentosa Cove on 9/12/2025 (Tuesday) to have a simply celebration for our 35th Wedding Celebration.

(This was our 3rd time visiting the bar😊)

The crews' service were excellent! 👍

All service staffs, including the Manager, Vkey were incredibly attentive🤩  , smiley😊 , and made us feel truly welcome💕 . They introduced to us with right choice for our prefer menu with the right portion of foods, so we don't wasted the foods.👌

We ready enjoyed our happy dinner there for our 35th Wedding Anniversary😍!

Good job for all the service crews in Two Chefs Bar (Sentosa Cove) and like to say Thank You to all for your good service✌️!

Highlight recommended to have your meal here, with the perfect ambience. There are huge industrial fans above the outdoor tables that keep you 🆒
author: Ah Heng Koo

review_text: My family had a wonderful Christmas lunch here. We enjoyed the food and ambience. It’s wheelchair and pet friendly. Enjoyed the steak and pizza 👍We are impressed by the warm and excellent service of staff Vicky. Would recommend friends here!👍 thank you !
author: Oi Lin Poon

review_text: Service was attentive, excellent, staff were jovial and seemed to bond and work together well; thank you for the extra birthday number and me and my partner enjoyed the lamb shank (soft, falls off the bone) and the Angus Beef Lasagna~ incredible
author: Terence Yong

review_text:
This spot is a real gem! We absolutely love the marina waterside seating – the perfect ambience. Plus, there are huge industrial fans above the outdoor tables that kept us cool especially with the recent heat and humidity.

The menu offers a fantastic large choice of Mexican and Italian dishes, and whatever we ordered was delicious! The Steak Fajitas were a highlight – the steak was cooked to perfect doneness and was so juicy, complemented by slightly charred flavorful onions and bell peppers. We also thoroughly enjoyed the BBQ chicken wings (which u can request for sauce on the side instead of on top of it) and the creamy truffle mushroom soup.

The service was excellent!  They even chilled my beer glass in a tub of ice water, which was such a thoughtful touch! Both service staff, including the Manager, Vicky, were incredibly attentive, smiley, and made us feel truly welcome. We enjoyed our weekday lunch there very much!

Plus, it's dog-friendly! We'll definitely be back
author: jot

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Sentosa
review_text:
This was my first time visiting the Sentosa outlet, and we went on a Sunday evening with a reservation, it was super crowded, which speaks to its popularity. The menu here is slightly different from the other outlet. We ordered the Spanish grilled octopus, black cod, sashimi platter, and spaghetti vongole. As usual, the restaurant delivers on top-quality seafood with a huge variety, and most of the dishes were as good as always.

We were informed that they had run out of clams and would replace the spaghetti vongole with more crabmeat. While it was still alright, it didn’t quite feel like a vongole without the clams. The sashimi platter was a bit of a miss for me……at this price point, I felt I could have gotten better quality elsewhere. That said, the octopus and black cod were excellent and lived up to expectations.

A big shout out to manager Madhu, who was incredibly sweet and attentive. When he found out we were celebrating a birthday, he kindly offered us a cake, which was such a thoughtful gesture. Overall, despite a few minor misses with the food, the service truly elevated the experience, and I would definitely return again.
author: Nicole Ng

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Sentosa
review_text: Happened to be there on a weekday when they had their lobster promotion hence it was more affordable and tasty. We also order the seafood platter and server was kind to inform that our orders were sufficient for 2 persons.  The batter was thin, light & fluffy and the seafood fresh. The view of the marina was also nice. The only setback was the rancid olive oil that was served at the start. When we informed the staff, they took quite a while amongst themselves to sniff it and concur. Why would we say something untrue. By then the bread was not warm anymore.
author: Jeannie Cheang

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Sentosa
review_text: Visited on a crowded Friday night but managed to find a table. Service was quick, friendly and efficient. We didn’t have to wait long for the mussels with cream sauce and the fish and chip. Only the man tou was a little delayed but it came after some prompting. Luckily they gave a lot of saffron cream sauce for dipping. Food was delicious. Mussels were fresh.
author: HC L

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Sentosa
review_text:
It was a nice experience. It was difficult for us to choose what to try first. For this dinner we got a couple oyster, lobster Monday, grilled red snapper, watermelon juice, ice tea and ice cream for dessert. We got discount as we stayed at the nearby hotel.
A really nice place for seafood, for sure.
Highly recommended. Along that path, you can find different cuisines, such as Indian, Italian, Greek, Chinese, French, etc.
author: Trang Pham

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Sentosa
review_text: Great location, delicious food, and nice atmosphere. I really enjoyed cold seafood platter which came out with shrimps, salmon, oysters and others. Can be a bit pricey depending on what you eat, but considering the quality of the food and other factors, it was totally worth it. The place can be good for both business and personal settings. Thumbs up 👍
author: Peter Woosouk Choi

review_text:
Row of restaurants interspersed with 2 supermarkets and a convenience store.
Mostly western food with 1 Chinese, 2 pizza, 1 Mexican.
Facing the marina with its numerous yachts.
Place frequented by residents of Sentosa Cove area which is probably the most expensive place to stay in SG and nearby hotels.
Boardwalk offers a nice stroll around the marina.
Food is expensive for sure
author: mark Lim

review_text: Dinner at Sabio. Spanish restaurant. Good ambience. Good food. Good service by this lady(Margaret, I think). She brought out aged pork to let us try. Very good.
author: Peteryeo Lock Peow

review_text:
A great place to take in the local vibes of the area. There are several places to enjoy a drink or connect with friends over food.

There’s a nice walkway along the harbour. A nice change of scenery from the city.
author: Melanie E

review_text: Quayside Isle was a delightful experience. The waterfront views were beautiful, and there were plenty of restaurants and cafes to enjoy. It was a relaxing and enjoyable place to spend time, and I would definitely visit again.
author: Bhutan Travel Center

review_text:
After our meal, we strolled around Quayside Isle a little (an opportunity for us to hang out where the rich hangout 😋)

Love the atmosphere, walks by the waters, checking out the yachts and the dining scene here. Do check it out!
author: 2bearbear Tom Lim

review_text: Woobar at Hotel W Sentosa is a hidden gem! Karan, the supervisor, was absolutely fantastic - super attentive and made our evening truly special. We loved the Cheeseboard Charcuterie and Cheese platter - a must-try! The setting is gorgeous, overlooking the poolside with stunning views. We timed it just right, arriving early evening to soak in the beautiful dawn colours. Highly recommend this spot for a relaxing and indulgent experience!"
author: Barry See

review_text: We had a great evening at the Woobar on Saturday night.  The themed event, After Dark, was well planned, and the music was great, creating an atmosphere for everyone to chill out on a Saturday night.  Special thanks to Susan and the team for professionally looking after each guest's interests!  A team full of energy and pulse to deliver the best outcome possible.  Don't miss it if you haven't tried WOOBAR yet!
author: Bonnie Tan

review_text: Enjoyed a relaxing weekend tea - pink edition. Good selection of teas and coffees to go with the excellent and friendly service
author: John Turban

review_text:
Woo Bar at W Singapore is the perfect spot for a relaxing night out. The bar offers excellent night views that set the tone for a chic and sophisticated evening. The atmosphere is stylish yet cozy, making it an ideal place to chill and chat with friends.

The food and drinks are simply delightful. Their menu features a great selection of delicious bites that pair perfectly with their impressive list of alcoholic beverages. Whether you’re a fan of classic cocktails or enjoy exploring creative concoctions, Woo Bar has something for everyone.

The service is top-notch, with attentive staff ensuring you have everything you need for a memorable experience. If you’re looking for a trendy yet laid-back venue to unwind, Woo Bar is definitely worth a visit.
author: Doreen LSW

review_text:
Cool and chic ambiance within W Hotel lobby. Great place to chill and enjoy a cup of cappuccino by Tanamera Coffee. (even if you are not a hotel guest)
Great choice of music playing in the surroundings.
Attentive staff too.
author: Cindy Ong

restaurant_name: Latitude Restaurant & Terrace (ONE°15 Marina Members only)
review_text: Fantastic revamp of restaurant! New menu too. Great customer service from staff. Food is tasty.
author: Calbee Cracker

restaurant_name: Latitude Restaurant & Terrace (ONE°15 Marina Members only)
review_text: Aggressively average food. Price point is decent but all things considered it’s worth a miss.
author: Jeremy Lim

restaurant_name: Latitude Restaurant & Terrace (ONE°15 Marina Members only)
review_text: Exclusively catering to club members, this restaurant nestled within the clubhouse seamlessly blends Asian and Western culinary delights. Whether indulging in the perfectly crafted spaghetti or savoring the flavorful Singapore fried Hokkien noodle, the culinary experience is nothing short of extraordinary. The taste transcends expectations, transforming each dish into a symphony of flavors that caters to the discerning palates of the privileged members. In this exclusive dining haven, the fusion of Asian and Western cuisine becomes a culinary journey that leaves an indelible mark of excellence on every plate.
author: Wesley Wong

restaurant_name: Latitude Restaurant & Terrace (ONE°15 Marina Members only)
review_text: I love the place for being quiet and having excellent staff service. They are polite and accomodating. The food is superb. We ordered Chicken Satay and Clay Pot Chicken, and its serving is good enough to last as a meal alone. It has strong, savory flavors which is expected for their culture, which I enjoyed.
author: Eunice Raquinel

restaurant_name: Latitude Restaurant & Terrace (ONE°15 Marina Members only)
review_text: Had chance to dine at this place. We ordered Angus beef har fun and laksa and both are very good. The taste is savoury and strong enough. The portion is more than sufficient for a full meal. The location is a bit far and secluded though. Do give a trial if there is a chance.
author: S WK

review_text:
Went to try the chili crab, but they only had a 900g crab at $12.40 per 100g , definitely not worth it. If you’re going solo, I’d recommend going for the lobster or prawns instead; better prices and portions.
The bao buns are a must-order , absolute perfection!
Finished off with the lime kefir, jelly, and sorbet , surprisingly refreshing after that chili pomelo sauce!
Chef David Muñoz calls it the best in town, and I think he’s right. My tongue literally went numb and came back to life.
Highly recommended , great food and top-notch service!
author: Jose Maria Moyano Suarez

review_text:
Great Food and Atmosphere

Having been here for dinner several times, I must say it has never disappointed me. The welcoming staff, the colourful lanterns and the great food have always been a great experience.

Staff are always on hand and available. They will do what it takes to make it good for you. Service is fast, prompt and sincere.

The food is made from fresh ingredients. It is not made from pre-mixes like some chain stores so stuff like the chili crab is extra fresh with vibrant flavours not found at the chain stores. Quality of most of the dishes is excellent, befitting of most top Chinese restaurants.

The colourful lanterns and decor give you a celebratory vibe. They have al fresco seating outside, partial aircon seats downstairs and full aircon upstairs and you can choose what you mood tells you.

This place has been around for quite some time now and appears they will be around for a lot longer.
author: Beary Beary

review_text:
Headline: Overhyped "Pomelo Chili Crab" Fails to Deliver
I specifically visited Sentosa (made a reservation) for the critically acclaimed "Pomelo Chili Crab," a decision that proved to be a major disappointment. The dish lacked any nuance, tasting overwhelmingly of pure chili without the expected crab infusion or the signature sweet/sour mix from the pomelo. The sauce was so one-dimensional that even the customary practice of dipping the accompanying bun became unappealing.
Worse, the crab meat itself was mushy and tasted distinctly unfresh. Even judged by regular "Chili Crab" standards, this signature dish was a complete failure.
While the service was good and the side dishes like the tender pork ribs were fine, the main selling point was so disastrous that it made the entire dining experience underwhelming and not worth the trip to Sentosa. Skip it unless you're already on the island and just want the basic side dishes.
author: Ryan G.

review_text:
A very nice place located at quayside isle within Sentosa. Very good service provided, yummy food and great presentation. The pork ribs is one of the best we ever had, and the chili crab is really unique with pomelo. Every dish is excellent, with good portion.
Just a bummer that the prawn paste chicken had been taken out of the menu now. really miss that too.
author: Jiang Hao Lau

review_text:
Blue Lotus consistently delivers a high quality menu. The chilli pomelo crab is a must have. Do make your reservation and let them know your intention. The crabs come in fresh every late afternoon.
The outdoor seating is a must book as well, the ambience is very enjoyable.
author: Alvin L.

review_text:
We enjoyed the food and appreciated the service.

Every dish was delicious and well above the standard you’d expect from an average Thai restaurant. The Signature Steamed Spicy Pork Ribs stood out with tender meat and an intriguing soup—reminiscent of peppery bak kut teh, yet balanced with a distinct Thai sourness. Both the Phat Thai Talay and pineapple fried rice were loaded with ingredients, each plate featuring several large prawns.

The Thai tofu (Tao Hu Tod) on its own was ordinary, but paired with the accompanying Thai sauce, it became surprisingly appetising. A pleasant surprise was the simple stir-fried kangkong, which turned out to be one of the star dishes—fresh, flavourful, and perfectly cooked. The mango salad (Yum Mamuang) was smooth and refreshing, offering a nice contrast to the richer dishes.

Drinks were equally tasty; the Thai milk tea and lemongrass tea had a well-balanced sweetness that wasn’t overpowering.

Service was polite, friendly, and efficient. The staff were attentive without being intrusive, and the outdoor seating provided a relaxed and comfortable ambience. While the prices are slightly higher than typical heartland Thai eateries, the quality of food and service makes it well worth the price.
author: Agus Wiwanto

review_text:
Visited on xmas eve and it was such a pleasant experience. Despite being busy the staff took time to check on us and cleared the plates as and when. Food was great and it’s not pricey too! Definitely recommended.

Oh yes theres outdoor pet friendly seating!
author: tickledhungry

review_text:
Service was excellent, where the waitstaff were cheerful, accommodating, and had our table for 5 prepared well before our reservation time. The space felt airy and comfortable, helped by the huge ceiling fan overhead. Orders were taken promptly and food arrived soon after.

The food itself was decent, though flavors were on the lighter side. Fried items leaned a bit soggy, while stir-fried dishes lost some taste as they cooled. Prawns were a hit-and-miss, some fresh, others less so, but seafood portions overall were generous.

Prices, however, were the highlight. We ordered nearly 20 items including drinks, and the bill came to just $260, which is incredible value.

Will definitely return for drinks and finger food in a relaxed setting!
author: MH Tham

review_text:
Pet friendly! Great food and friendly staff! 🍽️ Service was warm and approachable.

The watermelon rice dish was huge - more than enough for 3 to share. Portions are generous, prices reasonable. Nice spot for a relaxed meal by the water!
author: Mint

review_text: Had a wonderful dining experience at Gin Khao. The food was really nice and flavorful, and the staff were very friendly and attentive throughout our meal. The service made us feel welcome and well taken care of.
author: J Huang

review_text:
Little Farms Sentosa is my go to for breakfast and dinner - and it never disappoints 🤩

My favourites are chicken breast barley risotto, tiger prawn fettuccine, ox cheek pappardelle and smash burger! The matcha latte is a must, and the coffee is great too.

Everything feels fresh and thoughtfully prepared, and you can tell the quality of ingredients is good. It’s the kind of place where you actually feel good about what you’re eating.

Service is warm and friendly. Good vibes. Special shoutout to Chaki, the manager, who is always personable and makes the whole experience even better :)

I just love it here, it’s also pet friendly ❤️
author: Chelsea Tan

review_text:
We had such a lovely brunch at Little Farms Sentosa today. I ordered the shakshuka, which was rich, flavorful, and perfectly comforting, while my husband enjoyed the smoked salmon bagel—fresh, light, and beautifully presented. Both dishes were delicious and thoughtfully prepared.

What made the experience even better was the setting: a relaxed atmosphere with a wonderful view that added to the charm of the meal. It’s the kind of place where you can linger, enjoy good food, and soak in the surroundings.

Definitely a spot worth revisiting for both the food and the ambience!
author: Syy

review_text: Visiting every weekend has become our little tradition. The salmon bagel and açaí bowl are consistently amazing, and the manager, Chaki, greets us with such genuine warmth each time:) Highly recommended!!
author: 이윤아

review_text: Our go-to place for a relaxing brunch. Food is  high quality and delicious. Atmosphere is family and pets friendly. Surprisingly it’s quite windy, not hot at all. Service staff are friendly and very prompt! Recommended to come here for a nice meal!
author: Christina C

review_text:
I just want to share a note of appreciation for the amazing staff at Little Farms in my neighbourhood. I come here almost every day (even if just for a quick coffee) and I’ve consistently had a great experience.

The team here is genuinely warm, welcoming, and kind. They greet you with smiles, remember your preferences, and take real pride in making sure customers feel good and taken care of. The food has always been fresh and delicious, and I’ve never had any issues with quality.

Of course, like any place training new staff, there have been the occasional small order mix-ups, and every single time they were corrected immediately and I was never charged. That’s part of any business that invests in people and gives new team members a chance to learn. We’ve all been there in our own careers, and I truly admire how gracefully the team handles it.

I’ve heard how challenging it can be to hire on Sentosa, yet the staff here show up every day full of warmth, energy, and hard work. For a neighbourhood spot, that means everything - it’s a place that makes you feel relaxed, welcomed, and at home.

Thank you, Little Farms Sentosa team — we see you, we appreciate you, and we’re grateful for all you do.
author: Kristina Anguelova

review_text: Absolutely loved this place! The food is incredibly delicious, the service is warm and attentive, and the manager is exceptionally friendly. Everything from start to finish was perfect. Truly deserving of a full 5 stars! Highly recommended!
author: Mary San

review_text:
We went on New Year’s Eve, it wasn’t packed, so we are able to get a table 😊
Pita Gyros recommended by the service manager was nice, the pork is tender and tasted great, goes well with beer 🍺
author: Eileen Tay

review_text: Love the greek food! Feels like the one i had in greece💙 Great service and even had complementary dessert 😍
author: kaixin teo

review_text: First time trying Greek food and was not bad. Cheese very fresh and tasty, meats fresh and veggies taste so good. Seafood also fresh!  Dessert Okie too but their cocktails really cannot make it. We tried 2-3 different cocktails each person but just confirmed that the drinks really can’t make it.  Order normal soft drinks will do.
author: Beary Lun

review_text: I LOVE the food ~ every dish was very satisfying and well presented like a piece of art. Hummus is so smooth & creamy. It goes so well with the pita bread that was served warm. Seafood were fresh. Service was great too; the staff were friendly, patient and attentive (they changed my plates twice as they noticed it was piling up with mussels shell etc lol). Looking over the yachts during the evening is an added bonus. I would love to come back again!
author: Julie Sin

restaurant_name: Common Man Coffee Roasters - Quayside Isle
review_text:
Great vibes at Sentosa Cove!

Loved everything — the food was hearty and delicious (the full breakfast is a winner 🥓🍳), and the coffee? Pure perfection ☕. You can tell the baristas really know their craft. The service was friendly and fast, and the marina view made it all even better. A perfect spot to chill!
author: Vlad Tapia

restaurant_name: Common Man Coffee Roasters - Quayside Isle
review_text: Loved the jchill seaside vibes here! The crab salad was fresh and flavourful – loved the pomegranate pops and mango mint dressing. Coffee was excellent too (Muje Mesina had beautiful black tea and berry notes) brewed by the Barista , Leo. Super warm service and made an amazing cup of coffee  Staff  were friendly and attentive, and the location is perfect for a relaxing afternoon. Will definitely be back!
author: Karen Chai

restaurant_name: Common Man Coffee Roasters - Quayside Isle
review_text:
Love Common Man,  definetly the best Coffee in Singapore. Dinner is also completely underrated, it is actually very nice. The duck confit curry is a hit.
Just a little sad that you are beeing kicked out at 20:00 and no coffee machine is closed at 19:30. So don't trust the 22:00 that they state .
author: Heiko Sundermann

restaurant_name: Common Man Coffee Roasters - Quayside Isle
review_text: I went here for the second time, both times just for drinks. Unfortunately, on both occasions the staff were unfriendly, a bit arrogant, and even eating food while taking orders. It’s sad that the good taste of the drinks is affected by the poor service quality.
author: Han

restaurant_name: Common Man Coffee Roasters - Quayside Isle
review_text:
food is good, vibes are great, service could be better.

staff are inattentive, distracted. takes multiple hand waves just to catch a waiter’s attention.
author: Ryan Ho

review_text: The food was amazing and the vibes were great! I forgot to mention that it was my wife’s birthday, but the staff went out of their way at the last minute to bring a candle and sing a birthday song. Such a thoughtful gesture — kudos to the entire team for making our evening special!
author: KULVERSINGH

review_text:
Taste of food is acceptable, not great compared to other Indian restaurants. We came here hungry, but didn’t like the taste unfortunately. For us, not to try again.

The dishes were in small size, don’t exactly match the pictures in the menu.

Juice is not juice I think, it’s more like flavor nonetheless.

At least the view was amazing 👍🏻
Prices kind of expensive based on the quality of food. I think they need a new chef to fix the food and make a transformation. It could be better ✅
author: Abdulrahman

review_text: A spacious, modern Quayside Isle restaurant with indoor and outdoor seating, with views of the exclusive Sentosa Cove. Relaxed and cheerful atmosphere. Interesting, easy to read menu. Their fabulous food is combined with a well choreographed service.
author: Toni MacLaughlin

review_text: Our family had a lovely meal here! The service was warm and attentive throughout, and shoutout to the staff for accommodating with a non-spicy noodle dish for my noodle-loving child.
author: Sheryl Koh

review_text:
First time my partner and I are patronising the restaurant. For pet lovers, the restaurant is pet friendly at the al fresco area. Staff brought ice water for my doggie which was very nice. Twice, once after the ice melted.

The food was really good. Always been a fan of north indian cuisine. We had chicken curry and a chicken vindaloo with garlic naan, samosas and a cream of chicken soup. Everything was so tasty.

Jas was very attentive and polite even though he was busy at times. Also made time to chat with us when he could. Its clear the regulars appreciate him judging from the number of fistbumps, handshakes and hugs he gets from customers.

I notice lots of take out customers as well, which caused food service to be slightly on the slower side but everything is warm and freshly made so that makes up for the wait.

We will definitely be back. Thanks Jas!
author: Adrian Lee

review_text: We went for a family dinner at the Rock Bar Burger & Steakhouse, and I would say that it lived up to our expectations. The location is inside the Quayside Aisle, just at the entrance on the left side, and it's very easy to find. The menu features a mix of American, Mexican, and Italian cuisine, offering a good variety, especially if you are coming intending to enjoy some good drinks. There is a good variety of tidbits, appetizers, and main courses. We tried their chicken satay and chicken quesadillas. We wanted to try the nachos, but they did not have the vegetarian option that my wife wanted to try. We ended up sharing an Australian rib-eye for our main course, as we were a bit full from our drinks and starters. It tasted good, but I thought it was done well against our request for medium-well. The service was excellent, with two smiling gentlemen serving with enthusiasm. The place itself has a good vibe because it's right beside the yacht club, and all the fancy, expensive yachts are docked here. We took a good walk after dinner and said goodbye to this place. We would definitely go here again to enjoy a drink or two with good food together with our friends
author: Vishal Shirsat

review_text:
Over the years I have been to Rock Bar whenever I visit Sentosa Cove. This is my go to restaurant as somehow it gives me a very welcoming vibes with the relax atmosphere and the ambience. The food is also up to my expectations, service staff are friendly and helpful and the price is reasonable.

I am glad that after so many years, the standard has been maintained and I will surely be back again when I am at Sentosa Cove.
author: Richard Tan

review_text: always a joy getting food from rockbar , i find myself coming to this specific place to eat a lot. their food is always consistently delicious and worth every cent. customer service is also nice!
author: minjia leu

review_text:
We expected a nice steak since the name of the resto includes "steakhouse" but sadly for us it didn't meet our standard of a nice steak considering the price. The grilled chicken with shrimp tastes good but it didn't execute well the grilled part, can't hardly taste the grill sense on it. The food we had...not really something we would crave to come back.
But we will surely come back for the fast service and lava cake.

We appreciate the free dessert and birthday singing, especially the excellent service of Lea, Radzy and Hikal.
author: CATH GT

review_text:
Came here for early dinner while doing a short staycay in Sentosa. We tried their wagyu burger as well as the beef lasagna. Not really up to my standards, given the price point I'd expect a bit better. Lasagna was a bit on the drier side, could've had more cheese, where's the burger patty could've been more juicier...

Food was still decent and satisfying, but nothing remarkable. Plenty of seating (came here late afternoon on a Sunday) and nice sea views! ⛵
author: Alex A.

review_text: Very good Food 😋
author: Namira Khan

review_text:
👍 What works well

Good variety & familiar flavours: Al-Rich offers Indian Muslim cuisine which tends to appeal to many residents in Tuas dorms. Curry, biryani, etc., are comforting and satisfying, especially after long work hours.

Convenience / location: Being in or near Tuas South Dormitory makes it very handy for residents. No need to travel far; quick access to a decent meal is a big plus.

Casual / friendly atmosphere: For many, these eating places are informal, relaxed, and feel familiar — kind of like home-style food rather than fancy restaurant meals.

Affordable pricing: Indian Muslim stalls generally try to keep prices within reach of workers; portion sizes are often reasonable.

---

⚠ Potential limitations (minor)

Mixed reviews on rating: On BipperMedia, Al-Rich has a rating around 2.3 out of 5 from a few reviews.  That suggests some people have had less good experiences, perhaps with food quality, service, or consistency.

Possible variation in service or food quality: Since many dorm-area food places serve many people, sometimes hygiene, food temperature, or serving speed can vary.

Limited upscale features: Probably not much in terms of fancy ambience, décor, or premium ingredients — it's more about basic, filling, home-style meals.

---

✅ Overall impression

Al-Rich Indian Muslim Foods seems like a reliable go-to option for many staying in the Tuas South dormitory area when they want hearty, familiar Indian Muslim food. It may not always be perfect (based on low average rating), but its convenience, flavour, and value make it worth trying, especially when you want something satisfying and accessible
author: S KV

review_text:
As authentic as you can get. Prices are about 20% cheaper than those in the heartland.

Fuss free, fill your stomach food with an industrial environment. Taste wise no complaints, had worse.

So if your in the area for work or any reasons can consider.

review_text:
If you like DRY CHUNKY Carrot Cake, that is not too sweet and slimy, you will be very very please to dry this. If you like the wet slimy smashed up carrot cake, go somewhere else; you will be disappointed. So you can stop reading now.
Believe it or not, it is so difficult to find carrot cake that are DRY AND CHUNKY, so that you actually taste the "Carrot Cake" itself. They actually do have a smell and taste by itself, without the egg, without the sauce. However when it is smashed up ant meshed with the egg, sauce, and whatever not, you have a pancake of some sort.
Back in the day when we eat carrot cake, they are big chunks, fried in a huge flat round pan. And the carrot cake are seared to perfection, then the sweet sauce and chili are put on top of it. And then the last is the egg (pay 10 cents more). This is served in large green leave, clipped together with toothpick. Man, I wish I could have that today.... So this stall come close to it (not exactly at all), and it's satisfying!
You have the option to have "Ebony and Ivory", amazingly some people like it white :P (incomprehensible). But to each his/her own.
Their biggest strength they have a good amount of Chye Poh and Garlic, and the egg is NOT too overwhelming. And most of all the sweetness is very tamed and with a good touch of saltiness.
Go before 10am, or else be prepared to queue. I'm dead serious.
I'm going next week, hopefully every week!!

review_text:
Visited on Monday lunch, arrived at 12.35pm and there was only 2 persons before me. How lucky, cos after that, a long queue started to form.

Prices were $3.50, $4, or $5. And you choose whether you want it black, white or yuan yang (mixed black and white). I had the $4 yuan yang so I may try both out. The mixed option is not stated on their signages.

Auntie chef sure is a multi-tasker. She takes orders, chit chat with customers while frying, and still has time to thank you for ordering from her. I love friendly and polite hawkers and even more so, those who can still remain nice despite being busy!

The taste test. My friend who ate it on another occasion said the white carrot cake was very crispy. Mine wasn’t really crispy (or perhaps it was sitting for too long as I ordered a drink and to photos). But the wok hei was unmistakable.

The black carrot cake seemed sufficiently black and I thought it would pack a sweet punch. But it wasn’t, which is a good thing, but I might still have preferred my back carrot cake slightly sweeter.

Overall, a decent carrot cake and the portion was quite huge.

review_text:
Seeking to treat my companion, Kitty, to a memorable Valentine's Day dinner, I chose Himawari, a Japanese restaurant previously recommended to me by my motorcycling associates. To make the evening even more special, as Kitty and I first connected through cycling, we undertook a rather ambitious cycle from Punggol to reach the Alexandra Road location. Initially drawn in by the appeal of the weekend dinner buffet, a careful perusal of the menu with Kitty revealed that the buffet options did not entirely align with her preferences.

While the S$60 buffet is reasonably priced in principle, it became apparent that an a la carte selection, focusing on higher quality ingredients such as salmon belly and snow crab, would have been more judicious for our appetites. The buffet predominantly featured rice based dishes, assorted sushi rolls, and, unfortunately, many flour based items, which can be quite filling. A highball was also ordered, though the absence of a plum infused variant, a lemon highball being the sole option, was a minor disappointment.

On a more positive note, the restaurant boasted a welcoming and intimate atmosphere, complemented by attentive and helpful service from the staff. Conversely, the grilled fish head we sampled was regrettably overcooked, imparting an unpleasant burnt aroma. However, the sashimi and sushi were commendable for their generous, thick slices. Potential diners should also be aware that beverages are not encompassed within the buffet price, constituting a supplementary expense. After our meal, Kitty and I agreed that in the future, we'd opt for the a la carte menu to better enjoy their more premium offerings.
author: Doraemon

review_text:
If you're looking for a generous and fresh Japanese buffet in the Alexandra area, Himawari Japanese Restaurant is definitely worth considering. We opted for the Buffet Dinner at $$53++ as the à la carte pricing, especially for sashimi, seemed less economical—and we were certainly not disappointed with our choice!

🌟 Highlights of the Buffet
The star of the show is undoubtedly the sashimi. It was served thick-cut and fresh, offering excellent value for money within the buffet price. The variety is impressive, including popular choices like:
* Salmon
* Tuna
* Hamachi (Yellowtail)
* Octopus
* ...and several others!
Beyond the sashimi, the buffet menu boasts a vast selection of Japanese favourites. There are so many options that everyone in your group is likely to find something they love! Key offerings include:
* Unagi (Grilled Eel)
* Chicken Katsu Donburi
* Tempura
* A Wide Range of Sushi, Rolls, and Maki
* Shabu Shabu

💨 Service & Ambiance
The service was friendly and prompt. Dishes were served with impressive speed upon ordering, which is fantastic for a buffet setting.

We arrived around 6:30 PM and found the restaurant relatively quiet with only one other table occupied. However, the space filled up quickly shortly after. Given how fast the restaurant became busy, it would be wise to make a reservation, especially for special occasions or weekend dinners.

For the price of the buffet, Himawari offers an excellent spread, characterized by high-quality, thick-cut sashimi and a wide variety of other well-executed Japanese dishes. The prompt and friendly service is the cherry on top. It’s a great spot for a satisfying Japanese feast!

The porridge was a generous portion for 2 pax. Porridge is very smooth, pork pieces soft and well marinated. Overall, a well executed and flavorful comfort food.

Crispy char siew bun has a crispy texture and bouncy bread interior coupled with savoury sweet char siew filling. No wonder it is one of their signature dishes. We were so full though that we had to take away the third bun.

Braised chicken feet - well balanced of sweet and savoury with a hinge of black bean. The ingredients were complementing each other. They have also cut the chicken feet into easy to handle segments and there was a piece of bean curd skin to possibly retain the moisture from the gravy during the cooking process.

Overall, the food are well executed. We will be back.

review_text: I ordered the Mee Goreng with chicken meat for $7. It was a big plate, and the amount of chicken meat was probably the most I've ever encountered in a plate of Mee Goreng. Overall, the taste was good, and the price was fair.
author: LP Pua

review_text:
First time experience here, came during dinner hours. Food was amazing & the atmosphere was chill.

Would recommend trying the Crispy Fried Octopus as well as the Truffle Shrooms Pizza. You can consider getting the “For Sharing” platter as well if you have about 4-5 people.

Server name Judy Choo was helpful & friendly. Was given a complimentary dessert as it was my birthday. Overall, it was a great experience for me, recommended.
author: Yee Hian Tay

review_text: Delicious platter in a nice relax environment. The truffleshroom pizza was simply tasty. That of course if you like truffle. Also ordered the crispy fried octopus. Crunchy and tasty.
author: John Tay

review_text: Had lunch with colleagues here. They had a 1 for 1 special for lunch sets, which comes with salad and a main. Food was decent but not fantastic. Portions were a bit on the small size, so we ordered 2 more 1 for 1 specials (4 sets total) to share, and the total still only came up to just over $135, which is cheap! Service was pretty good. There's self service iced water.
author: Sihan Goi

review_text: Had my 1st company Christmas lunch here and was absolutely delighted with the delicious food! The service was truly wonderful, especially from Judy Choo, who was incredibly friendly and warm throughout our meal. It made our holiday celebration extra special. I am already looking forward to visiting again soon! Highly recommend for a fantastic dining experience. 🎄🍽️✨
author: Karen New

review_text:
Harry’s at Mapletree has quickly become one of my favourite spots, and a big part of that is thanks to Judy, the incredible manager who runs the place with genuine warmth and professionalism. Every visit feels welcoming Judy always goes out of her way to check in, make thoughtful recommendations, and ensure everyone is comfortable and well taken care of.

The food and drinks are consistently great, the atmosphere is relaxed, and the service is spot on. But it’s Judy’s attentive, friendly approach that truly elevates the entire experience. You can tell she cares deeply about her guests and her team.

If you’re looking for a place that delivers not just good food and drinks but outstanding hospitality, Harry’s Mapletree is an absolute must. Huge thanks to Judy and the team you make every visit memorable!
author: Dennis Aloysius Tan

review_text:
Everything was Perfect in the breakfast from taste, Service, Ambience and spread of breakfast.
Mr. Willson and his team made sure since we are Vegetarians we get variety in our breakfast to eat. Their Hospitality is remarkable.
Thanks for making our 3 day Stay at Hotel Equarius Comfortable and Amazing.
author: mmkabra

review_text: It’s a buffet and they have everyday change menus you can order something different for you.The food is delicious and the staff Willson and Jasmine are very nice , both of them are good looking and they gave me the best service.
author: ZIX DENG

review_text:
I had breakfast at Tangerine and wanted to commend the exceptional service provided by the server, Fish. He was very friendly and polite, recommending several different breakfast options, including Western, local specialties, and healthy meals. His suggestions were thoughtful and perfectly suited my taste.

Although the restaurant is relatively small and quiet, and doesn’t offer a full buffet breakfast, this makes the dining environment more comfortable and private. If you’re looking for a more extensive buffet, you can visit the nearby Ora Hotel. Breakfast at Tangerine is served from 7 AM to 11 AM (last order at 10:30 AM), which is great for those who want to sleep in.

Overall, this is a great place to enjoy a delicious breakfast, and Fish’s service added a lot to my dining experience. Highly recommended!
author: Audrey lsw

review_text:
Very very disappointed with the breakfast! Being a Ocean Suites guest, I was expecting a better breakfast, rather than a below average breakfast.

It is a semi buffet breakfast, they made us decide our choices of breakfast, before we can get seated. Maybe they lacked of staff to enhance their table service.

We tried  both Asian & the western set. Both taste worst than normal cafe breakfast.

To make it worst, the coffee taste like plain water, so diluted (see my picture), and they don’t serve latte or cappuccino, just “freshly brewed” from dispenser. To me, this is not acceptable for a guests who are from Suite Room.

The only comforting factor is the surrounding greenery ambience .
author: Chris

review_text:
Had the 3-course ($38++) lunch while my friend ate 4-course ($62++). Portions are quite substantial contrary to my original assumption. Food is of very good quality and very fresh, especially the fish. Short rib beef is superb, breaks apart in your mouth easily.

Area is serene and quiet, located inside Espa, so it's good for a nice, relaxing lunch.
author: Crystal Koh

review_text:
The place is seriously one of the best Thai places I’ve been to in Singapore!
For one, the tom yum is friggin amazing! Thick, flavourful and not salty at all. The generous amount of seafood and mushrooms inside are yet another good point for this dish.
The basil pork was also really great, bearing a satisfyingly flavourful punch of basil.
The instant noodle salad was also somehow absolutely delicious. Marinated without being overly soggy or salty, they went well with the seafood served with it.
The vegetables were nicely cooked and sauced, crisp and savoury.
The shrimp cakes were, surprisingly, made out of actual shrimp, which was a nice surprise. Anyway, they also tasted great.
The milk tea and the rice was nice, but nothing really outstanding.

All in all, one of the best Thai places on this island. I would definitely recommend going here to eat, but as seating is limited, I would advise to get a booking beforehand.
author: Yip Lim Bing

review_text:
Popped by for a quick meal for two pax. We were welcomed at the door by one of the young men working there. First impression was pleasant! At least it felt like a genuine warm welcome.

Food was served pretty quick. We had a Tomyam soup and basil chicken, even though we would’ve loved basil Pork instead. On top of that, we also had 2 glasses of Thai milk tea!

Loved the milk tea, it was fragrant, not too sweet and just $2 a glass. Also really appreciate the fact that it came without straws. Server made an effort to highlight that they are trying to go green by excluding straws. Of which , we greatly welcome!

Overall it cost us $22 for this dinner pictured below (without the teas though!)
author: Any

review_text:
16/11/20
Garlic chicken set is good. Like the fried garlic bits. Taste kind of sweet. The Tom Yam soup taste authentic and delicious. But not much ingredients. Small bowl. The set meal comes with one fried egg as well. Will return to try other dishes. Overall not bad.
author: Luke Skywalker

review_text: Simple and casual thai food at affordable prices. Though presentation isnt fancy, fried rice was fragrant and had wok-hei. Pad thai was on the sweet side and tasted like kuey tiao stir fried with just black sauce.
author: Ernest Ezra

review_text: Spicy. Mango salad was sold out. $6
author: Ember Shen

review_text:
We visited during the Lunar New Year period for a family dinner and had a wonderful experience. The food was excellent — the seafood was fresh, and the portions for the 6-course menu were just right. The view of the aquarium was fantastic, and the restaurant had a calm, quiet atmosphere that made it easy to enjoy good conversation.

What impressed us most was the outstanding service. The team was attentive and responsive throughout the evening. Special mention to Huck Sen — despite our table of 6 having quite a few requests (2 vegetarians, 3 no beef, and 1 request for seafood and pork to be fully cooked instead of the usual medium), he remembered every detail. He was attentive, pleasant, and always positive. When he overheard us talking about the sharks in the aquarium, he even took the time to share interesting facts about the different species and their unique characteristics.

Overall, the ambience, food, and service came together perfectly for a truly memorable dining experience. Highly recommended!
author: Wee Yong O

review_text:
I had a wonderful birthday dinner at Ocean Restaurant 🐠✨
A huge thank you to the staff for their sincere service. We initially planned for the 8-course menu, but they thoughtfully recommended the 6-course instead to ensure we weren't overwhelmed. It’s rare to find a team that prioritises the guest’s experience over upselling!
For the main course, the A4 Wagyu beef was incredibly tender and paired beautifully with caviar rich, flavorful, and indulgent.
To end the night, they surprised me with a complimentary birthday cake, which was such a sweet and thoughtful touch.
Highly recommend this restaurant for birthdays or special occasions. Delicious food, beautiful presentation, great service, and an amazing underwater view where you can dine while watching fish swim by truly a unique experience.
author: Sue Nguyen

review_text:
Dining at Ocean Restaurant is truly a one-of-a-kind experience in Singapore. Located at B1M of the Equarius Hotel, the highlight is undoubtedly the massive floor-to-ceiling windows looking directly into the S.E.A. Aquarium. Watching manta rays and sharks glide past while you eat creates a serene and magical atmosphere that is perfect for special occasions.
​
-​The View: Absolutely world-class. If you want a table right against the glass, be sure to book well in advance!
-​The Food: The Mediterranean-Californian menu is sophisticated and focuses on sustainable seafood. The lobster and scallops were standout dishes—perfectly cooked and beautifully presented.
-​Service: Professional, attentive, and very knowledgeable about the menu and wine pairings.
-​Ambience: Calm and upscale. It’s tucked away from the busier parts of Sentosa, making it feel very exclusive.

​It is a premium price point, but for a landmark celebration or a breathtaking date night. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a "wow" factor!
author: Gregory Athanasius

review_text: My husband and I had the most unforgettable evening at Ocean Restaurant, and it was truly one of the most romantic dining experiences we’ve ever shared. Sitting side by side beside the stunning glass panels overlooking the S.E.A. Aquarium, watching manta rays and tropical fish glide gracefully past our table, created the most magical and intimate atmosphere for us. The fine dining menu was exceptional — every dish beautifully presented, perfectly balanced, and full of refined flavors that showed incredible attention to detail. The wine pairing complemented each course flawlessly and elevated the entire experience. Chef Frederick’s culinary artistry shone in every bite, and Manager Winnie made my husband and me feel so warmly welcomed and genuinely cared for; both are consummate professionals who went above and beyond to make our evening special. From the impeccable food and wine to the breathtaking underwater view and romantic ambiance, it was a perfect 5-star experience that we will always cherish and highly recommend to anyone looking for an extraordinary night in Singapore.
author: Rocky

review_text: Went on a weekday lunch. And still has lots of people. Recommend to reserve your seats. 3 course menu and all was good, but the atmosphere was the best. Romantic or what not, we bought our baby and it was a superb experience. However, dont think there is any private corner as the seating is quite open and in front of everyone else.
author: Ronald Ho

review_text:
Naked Fin offers a pleasant and convenient dining experience. The space has an open, airy feel but is fully air-conditioned and neatly arranged. A major plus is the convenient parking available outside, which makes the visit hassle-free.

I went for lunch, and while the menu options were somewhat limited, the seafood dishes truly shined. I would highly recommend focusing on the fish and prawn items. The seafood pankcake was a standout – the base was incredibly flavorful and well-seasoned, a clear highlight. We paired it with the thin noodles, which did an excellent job of holding the delicious sauce.

A couple of notes: the vegetable sides and the salad were rather underwhelming and I wouldn't recommend them. Overall, the meal felt refined and detail-oriented (especially in the sauce and seasoning), but the pricing leans toward the higher end. You're paying more for the craftsmanship than for abundance.

It's a great restaurant to consider if you want to experience authentic Singaporean/Nanyang flavors in a comfortable setting, particularly for the seafood. It's perfect for someone appreciating culinary details. However, if you're primarily looking for high-value, large-portion meals, you might want to manage your expectations or explore other options.
author: Yoyo

review_text:
Finally made it to Naked Finn, a seafood spot I first noticed more than a decade ago when it was just a humble roadside shack in Gillman Barracks. Since then, it has evolved into a sleeker, more polished space just a stone’s throw away, without losing its soul. The trek down was well worth it – the seafood here is all about pristine freshness and precise, respectful cooking - a nod to the "Naked" in its name.

A zesty chilled beehoon crowned with crisp sakura ebi set the tone: bright, refreshing, and perked up by a punchy sambal that made for a super additive starter; we had to have seconds. The sugarloaf cabbage arrived beautifully charred and naturally sweet, lavishly cloaked in rich anchovy butter.

The undisputed star of the evening was the Soon Hock – a whole marble goby, deep-fried with its scales on so the skin turned shatteringly crisp, the flesh beneath moist and delicately sweet, lounging in a pool of light soy sauce. It’s a dish that perfectly encapsulates the kitchen’s quiet mastery of seafood.

For something more substantial, the Donabe is a no-brainer: this evening’s version featured a fillet of Madara, a flaky Pacific cod, nestled atop fluffy Koshihikari rice that soaked up all the savoury juices. Desserts kept to the same thoughtful, unfussy spirit: a house-made chendol and Thai red ruby with coconut sorbet provided a cool, nostalgic finish.

All of this was wrapped in top-shelf service – warm, genuinely friendly, and backed by authoritative knowledge of where every ingredient comes from – making for a casual yet refined seafood dinner that feels special without ever trying too hard.
author: Roger Yuen

review_text: It was the best food we had in singapore! I wish we went with more people to try everything. Fresh and delicious! Staffs are nice too. Go early for dinner since some menus were already sold out.
author: HeeJin Park

review_text: Had a delightful birthday meal at The Naked Finn. The Iberico Pork Grill was tender, juicy, and perfectly charred — rich in flavor without being heavy. The Sugarloaf Cabbage surprised me with its sweetness and light smokiness, a simple dish done exceptionally well. The Fish Soup was clean, comforting, and full of umami depth. To top it off, the Lobster Roll was indulgent — buttery, fresh, and generously filled. A minimalist setting that lets the seafood and produce shine. Definitely a place for those who appreciate honest, ingredient-focused cooking.
author: Andrew Ong

review_text: Dinner with family. Place was fairly empty in a weekday night. Service was fantastic and the food was great. My favourites were the kangkong, donabe clay pot which had great cod and the Taiwan cabbage.
author: R T

review_text:
Came here on a Sunday evening! We sat outdoors as the weather was cooling by then. The tables were spread out pretty well such that it doesn’t feel too claustrophobic.

Food was amazing - we ordered 1 Pizza Prosciutto and 1 squid ink spaghetti with vongole.

I personally prefer thin crust which was perfect and the generosity was the Parma ham made it satisfying.

But the pasta beats the pizza. The spaghetti’s texture was unique and felt homemade. The sauce was reduced well and the overall dish was so delightful. My only wish was that they have made the portion slightly bigger!

Service was okay but not amazing. Slightly strange that the cups used for water ($3 by the way) are beer cups.

Overall, I enjoyed the food and I’m really fond of the pasta. I’d recommend for others to come try the food.
author: Annabelle Ho

review_text: A special shoutout to the Trapizza team for making a birthday celebration for for a large group so smooth! Big thank you to Jason and Lalit for being so accomodating and efficient and making the night so memorable. They really went out of their way amidst the busy night to see to our needs. Amazing!
author: Shan Mano

review_text:
Come for the Food – Stay for the View
Visit Date: 25 January 2026

The servers wear T-shirts printed with “Come for the food – Stay for the view.” I’d make a small adjustment: come for the food, stay for the ambience.
Unless you’re seated right by the beach fence, the sea view is partially obstructed by other tables and sun umbrellas. But in truth, it hardly matters. A gentle sea breeze, a near-festive buzz of happy diners out for the evening, and attentive servers weaving efficiently between tables create a warm, relaxed atmosphere. You start unwinding almost the moment you sit down.

Food
We ordered a pizza and a burger to share. As I’m not particularly fond of red sauce, we opted for the Pinsa Milano with a rich saffron sauce, and it paid off. The thin, slightly crispy crust pizza with a hint of sweetness in the sauce paired beautifully with the mozzarella and parmesan, complementing the braised, savoury, juicy shredded beef. Paper-thin garlic flakes added an extra layer of flavour that made every bite interesting.
The Manzo Wagyu Burger came with a thick, juicy grilled patty, bacon slices, onion, tomato, lettuce, and cheese, alongside generous potato wedges and tomato ketchup. Personally, I felt a touch of sweetness, perhaps caramelised onions, might have worked better than raw onion. Still, a quick baste of mayo and sweet chilli sauce on the bun did the trick nicely.
Both the pizza and burger paired well with a medium-bodied Tempus Two Cabernet Sauvignon by the glass. I was also on the lookout for a lower-sugar soft drink, and the Ginger Ale (a Nutri-Grade B option) turned out to be a good choice.

Service
We booked a table earlier in the day via Chope and were promptly ushered past the queue waiting for walk-in seats. Ordering through the QR code was seamless, and the food arrived quickly. We were served by Guo Wei, who was attentive and efficient. When I asked for mayo or chilli sauce for the wedges, he returned almost immediately with both and later kindly helped pack our leftovers.

It was a very pleasant evening. This was our second visit. The first one, several years ago, remains a blur, except for a large jug of Singapore Sling. Safe to say, this place deserves a spot on our regular rotation.
author: Barnali Roy

review_text: Disappointing experience here. Tried to book for on the day online but appeared full as we cld only book a day ahead. Funny given how quickly tables turn over, we certainly saw opportunity for extra bookings on the day. Not sure if you cld walk in. We were sat at a table, told how to order using the QR, no offer of water for the table at all and were left to ourselves, so we assumed you needed to order it. No free water on the menu, so we ordered bottled water instead. The service was poor, staff standing round taking photos of the sunset not really paying attention to tables, I had to go find someone to wipe down our table. When someone did start to clear, they took 2 things and never returned! So many staff on as well! The food was ok, pizza was really nice the steak was overcooked to order and the vegetables was a lump of sliced eggplant, that's all which is great if you like it. Overall for a Shangri-La venue with Shangri-La prices we expected more from the service and attention to customers. Wouldn't really recommend it.
author: Denise Brown

review_text:
Good place for light lunch by Siloso Beach, food portion is quite generous.
There’s a small fountain for kids to play, it’s also close to the playground near Mega.
author: Cindy S

review_text: Bay Restaurant offers a truly enjoyable dining experience with its relaxed ambiance and beautiful setting. The atmosphere is calm and welcoming, making it a great spot for both casual meals and special occasions. The food is well prepared and flavorful, with a good variety on the menu to suit different tastes. Portions are generous and presentation is appealing. The service deserves special mention. The staff are friendly, attentive, and efficient without being intrusive. Overall, Bay Restaurant strikes a nice balance between quality food, pleasant surroundings, and good service. A great place to unwind and enjoy a satisfying meal.
author: Vachintha Piyadasa

review_text:
Only one, the rest is snack.

author: Haryenny Lim

review_text: Minimal gluten free options so Vincent and his team organised an off the menu chicken salad for lunch. So grateful for the above and beyond service by Vincent! And the salad was yum! Would definitely recommend!!
author: Laura

review_text: Even though it is pretty pricey, the food is pretty decent. Go for the biryani as it has more for the same price, and comes with vegetables. Place is very clean and fast-working staff so that is appreciated. Avoid paying $5 for water or other drinks. Also pay attention that the red packets at the cashier are chili sauce and not ketchup!
author: Johnson K

review_text: Food looks great and tastes fresh! 🐟🍽️ Staff are super friendly, and the prices are reasonable. Perfect place to relax after some fun in the water. 🌊☀️🩴
author: songpon tito

review_text:
ASHMI still serves very good thosai after all these years. Came to check out their refreshed shop and it looked clean and inviting. There're more than 50 types of thosai on the menu! The real test of the cooking skill and ingredients used can be examined by the Plain Thosai, and it doesn't disappoint.
This is the go-to place for a quick and tasty thosai fix!
author: KC Cheang

review_text: Chanced upon this traditional south Indian eatery. Had a Mint Basil Lemon tea to sooth my tummy. Indeed the concoction was refreshing and light. Egg onion thosai was crisp and tasty together with fresh chuckney and sambas. A not too heavy meal worth another visit. Will check out the briyani next round.
author: Josh M

review_text: Newly renovated, the place looks refreshed and inviting, and the food is outstanding. Authentic Indian flavors, well-balanced spices, and generous portions made the meal truly enjoyable. Definitely a must-visit for anyone looking for real Indian taste. Highly recommend.
author: Kumar

review_text: Yesterday brought some parupu vadais and a packet of mutton perratal. The worst food have eaten.  The vadai was super salty! Can't even eat properly eith so much salt in it. No taste from the mutton. After leaving it the fridge, we took out to warm them and ate some. When we wash away the orange looking oil, was shock to see that the oil patch feel like rubber and will not disolve in water, stays like a plastic! See the attached picture.  Do not know what oil they using to cook. Beware of such restaurants food! Do not poison yourself. Never ever I will buy anything from here. Horrible!
author: Viswa Nathan

review_text:
This restaurant has been recently renovated and has a nice and clean ambiance.

I tried the thali meals several times and it has a nice home cooked feel and taste.

They also have good briyani.
author: Yogeswaran Gopala Krishnan

review_text: Have a good dinner buffet. Good varieties and the items taste good. Special mention to the cakes - the cheese cake, strawberry cake, onde onde cake all exceed my expectation. Another item I like is the bak kut teh soup which is located at a corner which you may easily miss. The kids friendly corner also offer many items like the cheese sticks, tomato salmon, pasta, chocolate fondue, candy floss and ice creams. The staff are attentive and plates are always clear fast. The restaurant also replenish the food fast. Will certainly return again.
author: H P Lim

review_text:
Visited with relatives from overseas. Had a spend target and set on mission to try as many dishes as possible.

Tenderloin steak - hands down the best tasting dish among all.

Avocado salad - the greens were fresh.  Peeled prawns looked and tasted a little suspect, cant help but wonder if these were additionally treated.

Wanton noodles with fried dumplings - worst dish.  Not sure if this is HK or local SG style.  Sauce was way too salty.  Even after replacing the dish, it still tasted salty but edible.  Fried wantons were OK.  Char siu below average .. cannot make out whether these were boiled or BBQ'd

Laksa - gravy was fragrant n tasty without being too salty.  Again, a little suspect with the whole prawns

Hainanese Chicken rice - the rice itself was nice.  The poached chicken meat was average.

Char Kway Tiao - tasty, but different to local style CKT.

Sweet Sour Pork was average.  It came with a serving of steamed rice which was not indicated in the description or menu pic.

Crab meat fried rice - average.

Fruit platter - mango was a little unripe, sour.   For cutlery, we were given teaspoons and cup saucers to share the fruits .. strange, no dessert fork or small plates ?

Creme Brule with vanilla ice cream - good

Cheese cake with vanilla ice cream - good

On the whole, the Western dishes were more well received.  For the local dishes, I guess it's not fair to compare with specialist hawkers who are at it 24/7 ?? ...

Coffee was from the automatic coffee machine.  For the price, can get much better coffee elsewhere.
The noise when making Latte was rather loud.  No complimentary refills for a la carte orders.

Service staff were attentive and friendly.

Making a reservation was confusing.  Firstly, the reservation line did not connect.  I had to reserve via Quandoo the night before.

On day itself, I also called the main hotel line to make a reservation just to be sure I'd be eligible for the MasterCard 15% discount promotion.

I feedback that the Reservation Line was not working, but was told perhaps they are busy or already closed.  Somehow, I felt my feedback was not taken seriously.

I also sent an email and got a reply that indeed, the reservation line was not connected.

It would be useful to clarify in the marketing material whether the 15% MasterCard promotion applies to Buffet only or for a lar carte menu as well.

Too bad, we did not meet Magician Ben or Max.
author: BC Woo

review_text:
A buffet with such a great variety of dishes!
There were cuisines from many different countries, and it was so much fun to try everything
The range of flavors was impressive, so I never got bored
There was a time limit, so I couldn’t stay too long, but the atmosphere was great!
I’d definitely love to come back!
author: moon Luan

review_text:
Always a pleasure and delight to dine at silver shell cafe. Was very well taken care by the staff, Amirah, Mark Aung, Sakun and Daisy. They were friendly and attentive.  We have been dining at silver shell cafe whenever we're at Rasa Sentosa since 2017 so we were very happy to see familiar faces. We missed Rinah.

Food was great as usual. Enjoyed the lobster roll and cheese naan. Very delicious lunch.

Highly recommended. And will definitely return.
author: Yv Onne

review_text: Nice ambient,  excellent service, very friendly staffs & Magicians really do have a way of making fun feel larger than life.
author: Venus LY Yun

review_text: Definitely suggest ordering their kway tiaw. It's really chewy and flavorful. The prawns are substantial and crunchy, while the sausages are rich. The Hakka noodles were also great.
author: Evan Sidarto

review_text:
So this is a seperate restaurant within a restaurant at the Rasa Sentosa resort (in case you can't find it and the staff have no idea what you are talking about). It's near the bubble bar, which is also a bar within the main restaurant at the end.

Is the food any good? Nope. Properly the worst Laksa, wonton noodle soup we've ever had in Singapore. Didn't expect much from a hotel restaurant but this was exceptionally bad. The laksa was watery and the char Siew in the wonton noodles was coloured pork fat. Disappointing to say the least.

We also had the pleasure of the staff leading us to 2 outdoor tables which were wet and dripping with water from the rain which had just happened. So a bit fail on the service part.
author: Bru L

review_text: Need to ask a few people before locating this restaurant. Cosy ambience. Ordered Fish Udon Herbal, Char Kway Teow and Roasted duck, all sumptuous!
author: KK Lim

review_text: Great salad, one of the best fish curries and delicious steak. Thanks for having us!
author: Bogdan Ripa

review_text:
Good staff but super slow service.
Ordered kids meal and 2 noodles - shredded chicken and sliced fish, came after 25 mins during a lunch time when there’s literally another 1 table in the entire restaurant.
Kids meal came fast in 10 mins but apple juice along with it not until my kid finished the meal. Can’t understand it.
The 2 noodles are mediocre at best, plain. Fried rice for kid too greasy.
Not a restaurant flavor standard for the price.
Order something else if you have to eat here.
author: Richard Yu

review_text: This restaurant is an old school institution, doing a good job in preserving the nostalgic elements. Unfortunately, the food standard is shockingly poor now. Their claypot dishes, ironically their signature, are watery and tasteless. Only the paper chicken is worth returning for.
author: CK C

review_text:
We ordered the famous paper chicken, claypot with mixed ingredients, and fried rice

The paper chicken had a nice ginger flavor and was tasty but personally, I felt satisfied after just one piece
The claypot was served piping hot and had plenty of vegetables, which was great
However it contained battered fish inside and it was far too salty for me to eat
The fried rice was also quite salty
I think it would have been much more enjoyable if the seasoning had been a bit lighter
Overall, the dishes had good potential but the saltiness was a bit overwhelming for my taste
author: moon Luan

review_text: The pork ribs, noodles, and Malay Kangkong are must-tries. It's one of the better ones I tried amongThe the old school restaurant.  fried rice was a bit too salty, and I tasted some "salt" on my first bite, like it wasn't fried thoroughly. The 红烧豆腐 was underwhelming, and the roast pork was soggy; for $20 (S) it could be served in a more appealing setting. I believe corkage is free, which is a plus. Their alcohol selection isn't very tempting—$7 for a can and $14 for a bottle of Tiger, and they only offer Tiger. The service was prompt and friendly. The restaurant has a very "traditional” vibe and isn't crowded due to its location. It would be helpful if they offered promotions or set meals to attract customers back or introduced other deals to increase repeat visits.
author: Empress Ker

review_text: Had a nice office lunch there for a small celebration. Ordered the signature dishes all to the delight of the colleagues. There was a big miss with the fish though (something that I have neverl ordered from them before. That was a bit disappointing. Else all other foods were on point!
author: Desmond Lee

review_text:
Good place for good Cantonese cuisines- I love the salt fish fried rice . Fried sauté black sauce big prawns. Paper wrapped chicken ,fried garlic kailan veggies.

31st October 2025- went back again for DINNER n enjoyed the fried bean sprouts with salt fish ;paper wrapped chicken;claypot pigs liver n fried big prawnd with black sauce- all yummy as ever.😜😝👍👍

Bit of history:  Original Hillman restaurant  opened in 1963 in an open air corner coffee shop in cantonment road( now site occupied by The Pinnacle @ Duxton)i started eating at that place in 1967 which later relocated to Hillman at Kitchener rd( to make way for Pinnacle construction)- classical cantonese food. They opened a branch in Pasir Panjang rd called Manhill in 1973 which later renamed Hillman 99 at same place- where i m eating here now). The late Queen Elizabeth 11 ate once in the old original Hillman at cantonment road when she visitedSpore back then.
The current Hillman at Kitchener Rd n Hillman99 at Pasir Panjang Rd are run by members of d original family.
author: TPH

review_text: (we visited weeks ago), worse place to be ... poor ambience, asked to clear your own table, and worse ... we found the coconut drink not fresh but the myanmar woman refused to change it and show hostile face, so we left the undrank cups and walked off. My other child who drank it has stomach upset the next morning. Is hygiene a concern?
