This place has been around for years, it’s nice to see nothing has changed ! Came back for the nostalgia and of course the flavourful chicken broth. The taste has not changed at all, which shows the consistency and quality this chain upholds itself to. ☺️

I got the special(around 22.90) and it came with a whole chicken leg, two meatballs, two thick pork slices, seaweed, and a egg, and I added menma(bamboo shoots) which were very juicy and crunchy.

Honestly wished that they had a meatball ramen or ramen that didn’t have the chicken leg, because I enjoyed the meatballs and the pork slices more than the chicken leg (I think it’s by customers preference because they all taste great.)

I ordered the normal soup and it was already rich enough, if you want it richer go ahead they have an option for it too. You can grind sesame seeds to put into the broth too!

Tbh ordering the ramen with all the toppings is great if two people were to share one, or if you have a big appetite this would be great for you. You’ll feel really full after.

Really enjoyed the free flow hard boiled eggs and marinated bean sprouts too. The marinated bean sprouts are a little spicy and have a refreshing taste to them, cleansing the palate before you take another bite / sip of the rich ramen and helps to cut the gelatness.

10/10 looking forward to come again 💕
author: Tiffany Boogaloo

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant |100AM Tanjong Pagar | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text:
Went to YAYOI @ 100AM for a weekday lunch during the CNY period. The restaurant was relatively quiet around noon, which made it a comfortable spot for a group lunch (we had 6 pax).

We ordered several teishoku sets - Amazu Chicken Steak, Hakata Mizutaki, Namban & Ebi Fry, Tori Katsu Toji, and Sukiyaki, along with their Salmon Yu Sheng for the festive season (it was repeatedly recommended by their staff).

The portions of their mains were generous, but my Amazu Chicken Steak had too much sauce, which overpowered the entire dish. A few of my colleagues felt the same about their dishes - meat was nicely cooked, but way too saucy overall.

That said, the value of their lunch meals is pretty good. Each teishoku set comes with rice, miso soup, and access to the free refill counter. The salad bar was a nice touch as it had cherry tomatoes, corn, pickled ginger and other small sides that you can help yourself to. The unlimited rice and miso soup definitely made it more satisfying, especially for bigger eaters. The hojicha (both hot and iced) was also included in the lunch set :)

The highlight for us was actually the Salmon Yu Sheng. The ingredients were fresh, the salmon sashimi slices were thick, and the overall mix was well-balanced. Really yummy!

Overall, mains were slightly underwhelming due to the saltiness, but the free refills and seasonal offerings helped balance out the experience. A decent option for a casual weekday lunch, especially if you value set meals with unlimited sides :)
author: Joy Ong

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant |100AM Tanjong Pagar | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text:
I went on a weekday evening, the place was quiet with a few customers. I ordered the Amazu Chicken Steak and Chicken Namban sets at YAYOI. The mains were alright, but the unlimited salad, rice, and miso soup are the true selling points that make the price worth it.

The ordering process is now entirely through your own phone as they've removed the tablets. The staff did try to upsell us to more expensive sets, but it didn't take away from an otherwise very enjoyable meal.
author: Anson Chew

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant |100AM Tanjong Pagar | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Visited on a Saturday afternoon and it was nice to be able to have a quiet and unrushed lunch in the middle of town. There was no wait time and I was given a rather generous space for a solo diner. Their namban chicken was delicious. The chunky chicken pieces were battered well and crispy, while the meat remained moist and tender. Together with the egg tartar and namban sauce, it was a really satisfying combo. The only negative was that the ebi fry could have been better as it was not as crispy and the meat didn't taste fresh. Will definitely visit again for the namban chicken!
author: Jk l

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant |100AM Tanjong Pagar | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Our family of 5 (2 adults and 3 teenagers) had a scrumptious lunch/dinner at this restaurant on 05 Dec 2025,Friday … we were searching for food options as most restaurants are closed at 3pm ish before the dinner service. We were lucky to chance upon this restaurant which is still open . Our first time here and i find the price is reasonable and portion is really big. The rice is really good. I was worried that the tonkatsu might be dry but omg, it turn out to be crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside and it’s done perfectly!!! Authentic taste that we had in Japan. すごい😍。 the portion was really generous. My children ordered udon and ramen which were also very delicious. We didn’t take many photos of the food as we were too busy enjoying our food…seats are comfortable, ordering is by QR code…they serve the food really fast. We also ordered 5 pieces of gyoza and the fried squid to share. Delicious! Their chawamushi is also very good. If u order together with your set, the chawamushi is slightly cheaper than the ala carte price. Good deal. My daughter also ordered their dessert which is also satisfying… overall we love the food here!! Will visit again.
author: Joanne Peng

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant |100AM Tanjong Pagar | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Had their value set lunch and the food was spectular. Even more spectacular dining experience with the great service and cleanliness of the place. Shoutout to Simon with his exceptional service in ensuring we are well taken care of and served.
author: Brendan “SalmonIsNice”

review_text: Joey (Management staff), on 4th May 2025 about 12.50pm me, my wife & her sister had visited Saboten Restaurant at Vivo City. Joey walk us to our table, and she use a very rude vocal & hand gesture like “ hello sir, not outside foods are allowed in the restaurant with her finger point right in front our faces” to warn us not to consume any outside foods in the restaurant. I think is very inappropriate way of approach, without a proper polite sentences. Firstly, we only buy Jollibee to bring home eat & don’t even have an intention to eat in the restaurant. Secondly, we are not first time visiting restaurants in Singapore. Thirdly, who is she to point her rude finger in front of our faces & give a warning. Fourth, we just walked in & haven’t even seated down yet. Joey, her rudeness had totally ruined our days ! We had even been into this kind of bad experience & services provided. There are CCTV around, review the CCTV I think can see the whole bad experience that we had .
author: Jiak Bao

review_text:
Tried the signs cold soba with less noodle and the Kokoro Iekei ramen.
The portioning is a little small for the cold soba.
Only a few slices of beef on top. It mixed very well with the half boiled egg. It doesn’t have any weird taste at all.
Good to mix with the vinegar to reduce the heaviness. The vinegar is not that sour.
The ramen is great, char siew is nice and the ramen is chewy.
author: Skye Cai

review_text:
The classic tonkatsu at Saboten was ok, served steaming hot, but it may get quite unbearable to consume the final pieces as oil is sucked deep into the bread crumb batter. the meat is fresh, firm and juicy. The steamed egg turned out to be the star of the meal with its amazing umami flavor and diversed texture of silky steamed egg, corn, chicken and mysterious sauce on top. Big portion of shredded cabbage and nice matcha icecream.
The salt-grilled markerel meal set at Yayoi was ok, fresh fillet but nothing so special. The side dish of 3 pieces of fried gyoza surpriced me with its veggie stuffing, quite small but good to be a tastebud kicker.
author: Thanh Loan Tran

review_text: Had dinner at one of its brand - Nadai Fujisoba NI HACHI. Every piece of their seafood was very fresh, rice is soft and the place wasn’t too crowded (which is good especially for this Covid period). It may seem that the bowl is small, but once you finish it up, you can have a very satisfying and filling tummy. The service crews were attentive as well, refilling the hot green tea from time to time.
author: shzhong

review_text:
Tried Kagoshima kitchen after seeing a youtuber’s recommendation.  Either the YouTuber is not honest (only see money) or don’t know how to differentiate good food (not his fault).
The tonkatsu was very so so.   The salad was drenched in dressing.  The rich is half a bowl and too wet and an insult to the farmer.  I love rice but this is a 3/10 quality. The soup is also half bowl and taste average. The chawanmushi is overly steamed and half a cup?!   Look at the bubble on to the steam egg!  My friend ordered an unagi don.  Omg!   I was luckily that day to have not ordered that.  Else, I would have cursed someone.  Stole a piece from my friend and you can see how pathetic the slice of unagi is.  Dry, thin and filled with bones.  One stuck in between my teeth (May be not so lucky anyway). The best comes with the dessert.  Dragon fruit tasteless and even sour.   Better don’t give the dessert than give.
As for the service, so so and staff definitely need trainings on table layout and more attending to the customers
Food : 4/10
Money worth : 4/10
Service :5/10
Overall : 4/10
author: Lim TY

review_text: Couldn't wait to try Kaya Toast in Singapore, and it was as good as I'd hoped. Prices reasonable for the combo meals. Coffee was good too. I look forward to returning soon.
author: Dan Pieloch

review_text: Ordered two teh gao. Drank the first cup and realised it was teh not-so-gao. Asked them to add more tea. They poured half away, topped it up… and somehow made it taste even more like water. At this point I’m convinced the entire pot was brewed by someone who merely thought about tea while boiling plain water. Utterly disappointed, especially after paying $6 for two cups of… weak English tea with a spot of milk.
author: James Lim

review_text: That was my first time in Ya Kun Kaya Toast and I was so delighted. My breakfast was amazing delicious and the staff were so friendly and welcoming. Can’t wait to visit again. Thank you so much.
author: Marie.L Am

review_text: The kaya toast is stale and cold. The boy doing the toast is daydreaming and dont think he knows how to cook. Why is Yakun’s standard dropping and cant even deliver good toast? Despite me telling the cashier, manager and the toast boy twice and saying that this cold toast is unacceptable, the food still cannot make it. For those wanting toast in Singapore, don’t bother coming here. This outlet is giving kaya toast a bad name.
author: C Gan

review_text: Worse services rendered by male staff ( kelvin) when approach him about the drink can it be less sweet because the original taste is too sweet for individual tastes. He refuses as he FIERCELY answers is COMPANY SOP. Not willing to even compromise!!! Dun tell me, YaKUN encourage us to have diabetes!!!???
author: Emmuanel

review_text: We just want to say how amazing Emerald was! She was kind, helpful, and went above and beyond to make sure everything was taken care of. Customer service like hers makes a real difference. Emerald’s customer service was exceptional. She listened carefully, responded quickly, and handled everything with such warmth and professionalism. She’s a real asset to the team and your company!
author: Vicky Wong

review_text:
The service here is amazing. Shoutout to the Malaysian auntie manning the oden section especially - she is super sweet and warm.

We sat at the oden bar which gave a panoramic view of the cooking and prep of the oden, accompanied by the warm lights and the rustic wooden Japanese decor.

The food was also tastefully made with heart as you can see that every bite was perfection. The yakitori was grilled with a hint of the smoky charcoal char while not being dried out and burnt at the same time. The meat was still juicy and adequately seasoned/marinated. The oden was comfort food. The chicken katsu ball is a BEHEMOTH. Take note you cannot takeaway anything (except the chicken katsu ball), so make sure you don’t order in excess.

Overall lovely experience. Will visit again.
author: Christopher Gerald

review_text:
Decided to share a bottle of sake here and ordered some snacks (ika shiokara and karaage) to go along with it.

The ika shiokara was sufficiently salty and went rather well with the sake. The size and appearance of the karaage was not what I expected and I preferred if it was bite size to make it easier to eat.

The environment was also quite comfortable so we were able to chat for a few hours here.
author: Alvin Choo

review_text: Super awesome izakaya! The food’s absolutely great – the skewers and sashimi are so tasty! Plus the place has such a cool vibe and atmosphere!
author: Butler畢拿

review_text: Service is pretty good here. Got our lunch pretty fast. Would say it’s generally decent Japanese food, portions are generous. The amazing thing is that the lunch set includes some free dishes (like buffet style, great for growing boys 👦)
author: Daniel Bok

review_text: Enjoyed a relaxing pre Chinese New Year buffet here with friends. Relaxing ambience in a spacious and modern environment. Good selection of Asian and Western dishes, with a popular selection of Seafood on Ice. Love the dedicated sushi bar where you could pick Sashimi or Rolled Sushi.
author: Scribbling Geek

review_text:
The restaurant was not overly crowded, hence making it easy for conversations.

The food variety was quite lacking, with only 1 aisle of cooked food (Chinese style, 6 dishes), and 1 aisle of cooked food (Indian curry chicken with blue pea rice only, with some condiments like chilli). Noodle station was okay.

The other varieties were mainly cold dishes and sashimi.
The taste of all the cooked dishes were mediocre and not the freshest. Only seafood was fresh.

Lack of attentiveness from the service staff as well, as the plates were not being cleared, and water wasn't being topped. Even observed a service staff cleaning the tables and shaking the food crumbs onto the floor. From the image, you can see the amounts of plates being pushed aside without anyone clearing.

Overall, will not come again. Not value for money too. Wasn't a very "festive" dinner as the menu suggested.
author: Caroline B

review_text: The variety is good enough with cold seafood station, sushi, salad bar, sausages, turkey ham, soups, noodle station only have laksa, cooked food such as fried rice, sweet and sour pork, penne, stew beef. For dessert, there’s fruits, cakes, kueh and ice cream. And a freshly made pancake on the spot machine. The server is fast enough to clear the plates and replenish the seafood. The ambiance was nige and cozy, aircon was cool too.
author: BMWGal

review_text:
I had a weekday dinner at Element Restaurant and we had a wonderful time. The buffet spread was fresh and tasty, highlights were the salmon sashimi, wagyu burger and smoky aburi salmon. Though desserts were limited, the overall selection was enjoyable.

Service was excellent. Staff were attentive, quick to clear plates and refill drinks, and the Manager made us feel especially welcome by introducing the buffet and engaging with our table. His warmth and hospitality made the evening memorable.

The ambience was relaxed and perfect for conversation. We truly enjoyed the food and service, and I’d happily recommend Element to friends and return again.
author: Yordan

review_text:
Celebrating my girlfriend birthday on 12th Aug in Element Restaurant. Nice layout buffet stations with flavourful food. We enjoyed the dishes, ambience and felt relaxed as it was not too busy time in the restaurant, good for conversation.
Staffs were friendly, very attentive and fast in clearing empty plates and refill drinks. The manager Shahri was so welcoming, he even present the buffet spread to me. While we were eating he comes by and talk to us, very accomodating, my friends enjoyed his conversation and even asked him to have a photo together with us before we left the restaurant. His service is excellent 👍👍👍 and makes our dining so delightful.
Would recommend my friends and we will come back again.
author: Nora Wee

review_text: Cold baingan bharta served
author: Dileep Marar

review_text: A very cool and chic cafe at Amara hotel lobby. Had Nasi lemak. Taste was so so but the crispy chicken was very tasty. Server forgot about my coffee order thou. Other that that service was great and I’d come back again.
author: Pauline Yoong

review_text:
Had a lovely lunch at Café Oriental in Amara Hotel, near Tanjong Pagar. The location is super convenient and easy to find, especially if you’re working around the area. What really stood out was how calm and quiet it was during weekday lunch hours—not too crowded at all, which made it a great spot for a relaxed meal or even a quick discussion or catch-up with colleagues.

The staff were attentive and genuinely helpful, which made the experience even better. The food was tasty and came out pretty fast too. All in all, a great place for a peaceful lunch and some good conversation. Would definitely return!
author: Rajendra Giri

review_text:
It was Xmas Eve night and we were around the vicinity of Amara Hotel. We decided to have our dinner there and we walked in with our 2 kids. it was 7pm and indeed a busy time for the chefs and servers. We were directed to an outdoor dining area by an Indian manager, I didnt get his name. He went through the dishes with us and we were given 2 glasses of wine per adult with the price. The selection of food was good. The cakes were amazing. Laksa was good, my boy had 2 bowls. Sashimi was fresh. Roasted beef was good.
The Indian manager informed us there was a promo by DBS bank! Thank you!
There were 2 waitress who were coming out to clear our plates and give us new cutlery sets.
It was a good family time at Cafe Oriental on Xmas Eve! Thank you!
author: Kalaivani Paneer Selvam

review_text:
Spent a wonderful evening in good company trying out Chef Damian D’Silva’s collaboration with Cafe Oriental. Featuring specially curated Peranakan favourites reminiscent of Rempapa’s, diners can choose from 3 dishes or 5 dishes sharing plates. We went with the 5 dishes sharing plates, omitting only the kedondong salad (sorry it’s me, i love my proteins). Since the sharing plates are good for two and we had 5 pax, we also ordered an extra main of Hainanese pork chop.
We were not disappointed , and my favourite dish had to be the Ayam Buah Keluak. The chicken was tender and the sauce tasted amazing with the jasmine white rice. The Eurasian grilled snapper was a pleasant surprise , with the spice paste tasting light and fresh. The chi pow kai was a tad small for sharing, and too salty for my taste even though the manager did explain to us that we had to try it with the accompanying chilli sauce to balance the taste. Do try that! Also loved the small desserts that came after our meal - bingka ubi, kueh salat and kueh kosui. The collaboration runs for two weeks, so try it out if you can !
author: Lynn Tan

review_text:
Amara Singapore’s Local Legends series returns, spotlighting the rich traditions that define our food culture.

Starting from today till 17 April, Chef Damian D’Silva — the Grandfather of Heritage Cuisine — will oﬀer a special menu at Amara Singapore’s Cafe Oriental, a restaurant which reimagines Singapore’s beloved local favourites.

Expect soulful, time-honored dishes like Ayam Buah Keluak, Eurasian Lamb Dhalcha, Brinjal Pacheree, Eurasian Grilled Snapper and Chi Pow Kai (paper-wrapped chicken) — each one a story on a plate. And don’t skip the Kedondong Salad, a favourite from Rempapa’s menu, and assorted Kuehs for that perfect sweet-sour-spice balance. Whether you opt for the three- or five-course sharing menu (S$60++/S$70++ per person) or go à la carte, you’re in for a treat!

Singapore turns 60 this year, and there’s no better way to celebrate than by indulging in the deep, multicultural flavors that make our food scene legendary.
author: fatspoting

review_text: Great food to come back for! Beef Wellington is a must. Oh the appetiser too, thin crisp flat flambee is a winner. Jack has a rustic charm & his subtle attentive style made the bday celebration lovely, the entire crew is warm; chatting with regulars. Suggestion for improvement: touch up the indoor dining area, lacks a bit of oomph factor
author: Ix Chow

review_text: Had our wedding anniversary dinner at Bar-Roque Grill. Ordered their signature Beef Wellington and Lamb Couscous 4 Ways, and they were absolutely delicious. The food quality and service were amazing. Special shoutout to amazing Satia for his awesome service, 10/10, and for making our anniversary dinner a memorable one! We will definitely visit again!
author: Yu-Chen WU

review_text: Highly recommend this place for delicious food and amazing presentation. Service is very good, thanks to Rose and Emily for that. We had roasted chicken with mushroom sauce, cote de bouf and hanging wagyu beef. For the dessert, madeleine and burnt cheesecake are all so good! Really must try.
author: Rose Asis

review_text:
The oysters served were surprisingly fresh and beef wellington was delicious. Jack did a good job in engaging customers with their food and gave a very detailed explanation on the origin of the super fresh oyster. That's how a restaurant should be like when the environment is full of humours, good food and wines. In house red wine is not bad to pair with the beef. Proscesso was smooth to go with the oyster.

Will highly recommend this steak place.
author: Chloe Chin

review_text:
Came here many times, my favourite steak house. love the steak selection and the always excellent and efficient services.

Beef tartare is my favourite. And we ordered the beef platter for 4 of us.

Btw, the waitress was attentive and friendly, gave my daughter a free birthday dessert. Thanks!
author: Ken Poh

review_text:
OSO is a place where you can bring your client, best friend, boss or your date. The atmosphere is chic but you will still feel comfortable in your weekend chillax outfit. The staff are attentive, obliging and they think ahead to ensure your experience is enjoyable. We ordered a truffle pasta to share, they divided it up into individual servings so we get the right amount of truffle eat without messing the angel hair pasta.
The food choices were wide (antipasti, meats, seafood, pasta.. pasta, dessert..) and there was someone for everyone, and if you are curious what they cooked for Pope Francis when he was in Singapore, you can order it for yourself to try.
And the dessert was the one item which draw the lunch to an amazing close.. did we also mentioned we had. a lovely bottle of Chianti and we are still surprised at the the bill (in a positive manner).
author: Joyce Law

review_text:
The restaurant is absolutely stunning—like walking into a classy art piece. My girlfriend took me there for a birthday lunch, and the ambiance alone made it feel special. To top it off, they surprised me with a beautifully presented complimentary birthday cake, which was a lovely touch.

I started with the crab appetizer, which was perfectly done—fresh, delicate, and full of flavor. For mains, I had the angel hair pasta, while my girlfriend went with the pork. Hers was definitely the winner: rich, tender, and well-balanced. Mine, on the other hand, was just okay—nothing bad, just not memorable.

What really stood out for me was their complimentary freshly baked focaccia served with vinaigrette and olive oil. It was damn good—warm, soft, and full of flavor. Honestly, I could’ve eaten a basket of that alone.

For dessert, I had the chocolate option, which was very thick and rich—almost too intense, but still enjoyable if you’re a chocolate lover.

Overall, a beautiful setting with thoughtful service and a few standout dishes. Would return, especially for that focaccia and the pork.
author: Bon Ang

review_text: Love it, love it, love it! We had their 6-course dinner and I thought it was gonna be too much -- but the portions were just right. Complete the feast without any undue discomfort. Enjoyed the Cod serving and the lamb especially (nice and tender). Good and wide selection for each course so everyone in our party of 9. The service -- now that's something others can only try to  emulate. Will be coming back for sure. Thanks to the crew for taking care of us so well!
author: Eileen Chan

review_text:
One of the best italian restaurants I’ve ever been to (incl. my trips to Italy). The atmosphere, the staff, the food it all works together perfectly. You can feel the passion of the people working there - they put their heart into every dish and service☺️

We went there 3 times and tried something different every evening with the Tomahawk as the big bang on the last evening. I look forward to my next visit if I’m ever in Singapur again.

Thank you all for making our dinner so lovely and enjoyable.
author: JH

review_text:
Had an amazing dinner at OSO Italian restaurant recently. The ambience is cosy and intimate, perfect for a romantic dinner or a catch-up with friends.

The food is authentic Italian cuisine at its finest. We ordered the set dinner and I chose Crab meat & avocado for my Antipasti, Burrata cow milk cheese for my Primi, Ravioli filled with Seabass for my Pasta and Tuna Loin roasted with turnip for my Main. As for dessert; I had Dark chocolate 85% Venezuelan Budino"Flan".

È stato delizioso!
author: Burt Lin

restaurant_name: The Marmalade Pantry - Cafe Bistro @ Tanjong Pagar
review_text:
Food was okay. Highlight was the duck skewers. The sweets pastries were mostly average.

Service, they were not rude but not what you would expect from hotel standard service...

Went on the day after valentines and it wasn't crowded at all. So it was a great place to chill and enjoy the afternoon tea. View was good and decorations were nice.
author: Cheralyn

restaurant_name: The Marmalade Pantry - Cafe Bistro @ Tanjong Pagar
review_text:
I had an extremely poor dining experience at The Marmalade Pantry (Tanjong Pagar) tonight. Both my partner and I are currently suffering from severe food poisoning, including diarrhea, after dining here.
We ordered the $40 ribeye steak, their recommended pan-seared barramundi, sticky date pudding, and a zesty pear fresh juice, spending a total of $118.70. I strongly believe the issue was the ribeye steak, which was a poor-quality cut with excessive sinew and heavy seasoning that appeared to mask its lack of freshness. I had specifically requested the steak to be cooked medium (see below photos), but it was not prepared as ordered.
Regardless of it being the Christmas holiday period, we are paying customers and should be treated fairly. Unfortunately, service was also disappointing, especially considering there were only four tables occupied at the time we were dining.
Overall, this experience was unacceptable given the price point and reputation of the restaurant. Management should seriously review both food quality and service standards, as food safety should never be compromised.
author: Karen L

restaurant_name: The Marmalade Pantry - Cafe Bistro @ Tanjong Pagar
review_text: Every touchpoint was taken care very well. Very hospitable and making our friend surprise birthday successful. Thank you Noel, Sky, Shu Hui, Ci Yu and Joon for making it possible. Wonderful service!
author: wong wanqi

restaurant_name: The Marmalade Pantry - Cafe Bistro @ Tanjong Pagar
review_text:
June is a great host, friendly and attentive from start to finish. Our coffee cups were warmed up which made our evenings.

The chicken tabbouleh was fantastic.

We took a lovely photo with the floral arrangement outside the restaurant.
author: Johnie Goh

restaurant_name: The Marmalade Pantry - Cafe Bistro @ Tanjong Pagar
review_text:
It was a great experience dining here. Shu Hui is very professional and the team served the food very fast.

Highly recommended
author: E C

review_text: The chirashi was outrageously priced for what it was. At 42 SGD I expected way more than a few cubes of fish over soaked in wasabi sauce with no hint of the truffle butter it was named after. The teppan wagyu was ok at 36 but was a small portion with some greens that looked a few days too old and which were wilted. We ended up spending a hundred dollars for two small dishes which weren't any good. Went elsewhere for a second dinner instead. Honestly, I'm not even sure why this place exists
author: Eddie Wang

review_text: I'm afraid this was the worst Japanese restaurant I've ever been to. Everything on the menu is overpriced. I figured I would just be conservative and get the truffle butter chirashi, which was 45 dollars. The sashimi cubes were quite small, and covered in some wasabi taste sauce. I totally forgot it was supposed to be "truffle butter". The wasabi taste covered all other flavors and there was way too much sauce that I couldn't really eat because the wasabi was so spicy. And the rice was messed up too. Very dry and no taste. I can't believe I paid 45 dollars for a dish like this. Never again please.
author: K Liu

review_text:
Quite a disappointment really. I was looking at DBS' app and found this place.

I was glad I didn't spend even more on Omakase (the type of set meal that you pay a fixed amount and the chef selects your dishes) and tried on a la carte first (plus used the 1 for 1 main course so the damage was a little less)

The restaurant was not fully connected and the dishes were passed from one place, through the street for 10-15 metres, then to the next seated area. If it's local hawker food, fine. If it's sit-down dining Japanese? Please no.

They said on their website the concept is Japanese mixed with Western, maybe that's why I have my wagyu sitting on salad greens, and same with my Kurobuta. I don't mind a mixed fusion but just putting fine meat on salad greens is far from justifying the concept. The Kurobuta was not so bad in terms of presentation, but the wagyu (Teppan Wagyu with Wild Rocket and Ponzu Sauce) as they indicated being one of the mains - the presentation was quite overly plain if not disappointing. Feel free to judge the pictures I posted on Google / TripAdvisor.

The spicy avocado roll was not bad in taste but suffered from the same presentation issues. As for the scallops + foie gras skewer - scallops were overcooked. The torched salmon roll was the only dish that was up to standard though. Wagyu - portion was small but the taste was not bad. Kurobuta - cooking method was right, sauce was right, the raw material though was far from decent, it wasn't fat enough as a good piece of Kurobuta.

I did not want to order desserts after all that so I cannot comment. But I will not come again nor try the Omakase, and they have made it very hard for me to review it any better.
author: Eddie Sit

review_text: Great food. Maybe a bit pricey :/
author: Daniel Rouquette

review_text: Good sushi but really overpriced.
author: Janeki-neko

review_text: Visited in the evening, it's a nice bistro setting with a good choice of craft beers, wines and food. Indoor seating is not big, comfy for smaller groups. Pet friendly for their alfresco area. Friendly svc too.
author: Berlinda Goh

review_text: A great place to chill with friends after work. We enjoyed our Halloween Nights here. Must try their garlic butter mussels and thin pizza especially fungi bianco!! Definitely will come back again 🥰
author: Gt Kee

review_text: Came here on a Sunday for early lunch. The café has cozy indoor seating and nice outdoor seating with a street view. The food portion servings are generous and it has nice music vibes that doesn't overpower conversations.
author: Ong Lynn

review_text:
Came here cause it was recommended online but the food was really really disappointing.

Drinks:
The hot latte was lukewarm at best. The hot chocolate had a powdery/sandy texture when drinking.

Appetiser:
The buffalo wings were okay.

Mains:
The brunch skillet was extremely greasy. The egg was really undercooked (The whites were still transparent). The meat was too salty but the potatoes were not salty enough.
The scallop mentaiko spaghetti had no seasoning and overly creamy (made me feel nauseous). The scallops were overcooked and were rubbery/chewy.

Overall, although the cafe looked nice and had a nice atmosphere, the food felt like a waste of money.
author: Abby Char

review_text:
First time here and the food was good! Even the craft beers were interesting and unique.

What stood out was the mussels and nachos. Best of all... Everything is nett price.
author: Jason Tung

review_text:
Kueh Dadar ($2.50 for 2) was bursting with coconut but the skin could be more flexible and more chewy. Still a pretty decent kueh dadar.
Ang Ku Kueh ($3.20 for 2) skin was very QQ and the peanut filling was sweet and super crunchy. The peanut texture tasted very homemade. It is a worthy competitor to Everton Ji Xiang but it is pricier.
author: Puay Khoon Yeo

review_text:
Excellent ang ku kueh. It stands out for the taste and portion. Not too oily or dry. They are sold in two sizes - normal and mini. Ideal for those with small appetite or prefer a snack portion.

They are sold in boxes. A set of kueh starts at SGD2.50. It offers mung bean, peanut, and other flavours which are not specified. Ask the hawker operator and she will be happy to explain.

The store also sell economy rice, although I did not managed to try.

Highly recommended. I would visit again.
author: Cal L

review_text:
I couldn't resist the attractive display of kuehs and bought two items to try. The ondeh ondeh cost $3.20 for 6 pieces, and the banana cake was $2.50 for 2 thick slices. The price was fair for the quality. The banana cake was aromatic and perfectly sweetened, though I do wish they had left some chunky bits for a better texture. The ondeh ondeh, though not the best, but was one of the better ones I have had, as the centre truly burst 爆浆 as it should. This was especially good considering I had an exceptional one only last week.

Update: came back for Tapioca Kueh ($2.50 for 2) and I love their lighter texture version as compared to those typical dense texture elsewhere.
author: Touristmouse

review_text:
My friend and I recently attended a Kueh workshop which we really enjoyed. The booking process was easy through WhatsApp, very responsive and flexible with days and times.
The workshop was well organised, we learnt about the history of Kueh, steps this family is taking to keep the tradition alive and make it attractive to the younger generation. We had fun getting our hands messy making dough and fillings. It is a bit like crafting, using different colours and molds. The best bit is that you get something yummy to eat at the end.
I'm hooked on  making Kueh and have even purchased my own molds. Many thanks to the team for a wonderful afternoon. I would highly recommend this workshop 😊
author: Tracey Ramsay

review_text:
Her food are healthy cooking. I love her fried bee hoon & kuehs. I feel safe to enjoy her cooking. This is a rare gem hawker. She has the love of our health!

Thumb up!
author: Genesis

review_text:
Strategically located on the ground floor of International Plaza and open 24 hours, this coffee joint is an excellent spot for both business meetings and casual catch-ups with friends.

While it boasts a reasonably large space, it's frequently quite crowded. As a result, it's not uncommon to find the overall cleanliness of the area falling short of the highest standards during certain times of the day.
author: Flo Yeow

review_text:
I recently visited The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf at International Plaza, located at 10 Anson Road, #01-32, Singapore. The café offers a cozy and inviting atmosphere, making it a pleasant spot for a quick coffee break or a casual meeting. ￼

I ordered their signature Ice Blended Mocha, which had a delightful balance of sweetness and creaminess without being overly rich. It paired well with their selection of teas, providing a satisfying experience. The staff were courteous and efficient, ensuring a smooth ordering process. ￼

While the seating area is somewhat limited, especially during peak hours, the overall ambiance remains comfortable. The café’s location within the bustling Central Business District makes it a convenient stop for professionals seeking a caffeine fix.

Overall, The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf at International Plaza delivers consistent quality in both its beverages and service. It’s a reliable choice for those in the area looking for a familiar and satisfying coffee experience.
author: preba moodley

review_text: I love the service here, The drinks and croissants are also delicious. Plus, it’s always busy here, but there’s always a suitable table available if you want to sit down and use laptop.
author: Bie Ng

review_text:
Good customer service experience.
Staffs were helpful and patient to explain about the points system.

One of the few places to be open on  Sunday in the Central Business District.
There was a decent crowd despite it was a Sunday.

Had Seafood Spaghetti. It was good!
author: DR DAVY GOH

review_text:
It's open 24/7! This is amazing for those looking to pull in some late night meetings or last minute work or studying before the next morning.

It is spacious with a variety of seats - single sofa seats, standard chairs, cushioned seats without back rest, etc.

PRO TIP: For those who wish to be alone and undisturbed, seats near the pillars are a good hideout.
author: Reviewers

review_text:
Finally we decided to give this eating place a try. We always noticed a long queue outside and skipped it. This time round since it's rather late on a Sunday evening there is no queue outside. There were about 4 empty spots and we occupied 2 of them. All counter seating and it's quite narrow. Just enough to seat and someone to squeeze by. More of a eat-and-go place.

We went for the set meals: I picked the pork gyoza with sides of Scramble Egg with Chives and Eggplant with miso. My fiancée had the prawn gyoza and Spinach with Soya Sauce & Bonito Flakes and Chicken Nanban with Tartar Sauce. A bowl of miso soup comes with the meal. I mistakenly ordered the Green Tea Soda, thinking that it's hot green tea. Turns out that it's pretty good.. phew... for rice we opt for small portion.

The everything is good. Well prepared and delicious. Loved the free-flow bean sprout and pickled vegetables as well. The Yuzu dipping sauce is refreshing and tasty, not too salty.

We enjoyed our meals and it's quite feeling at the end. Good thing we did not go for the full bowl of rice. Upon request they offer pasteurized eggs on rice which we will try next time. Apparently their rice is free flow as well. Good deal. We will definitely come again for quick meals.
author: Melvin Lim

review_text: So happy to revisit this gyoza eatery — it really feels like being in Japan. The place is small, so expect a queue during lunch hours, but the gyoza tasted superb, maybe even better than what I’ve had in Japan. Side dishes were great, and the free egg and rice top-ups were a bonus. Will definitely be back again
author: YL

review_text:
*TLDR - Pork gyoza not properly cooked, standards have dropped as much as prices have increased*

Live in the area, this place used to be a fav and have been coming here for over 10 years.

Some things I can put up with - price increases over the years, charging 50cents for water, recent shrinking of portion size of the sides. But today was the final straw.

Lunch 3 Dec 25, pork gyoza set. 2 staff members at the tail end of lunchtime - both looked unhappy and almost irritated with customers arriving.

Not the same cook I am used to, but last time here was a few months ago. Pork gyoza was not hot on the inside and on some pieces, it was not thoroughly cooked. Pork was pink, and temperature was lukewarm at best.

Told the staff, and they said "it's always like this" and when I told them I have been here many times, "we cannot change the timer of the fryer".

Wow...surely not-well cooked pork is a health risk.

Could be the gyoza was not thawed properly, oil wasn't the right temp, etc. Instead, I just got retorts that it's the way it is, and they will feedback to mgmt.

If you want to understand how to lose loyal customers over time, this place has got it down.
author: Kelvin

review_text: A no-frills spot with limited seating. I tried the pork gyoza—it was tasty and satisfying, though not the best I’ve had. I wouldn’t queue for more than 20 minutes for it if I came by during a busier time. That said, I really appreciated the free-flow beansprouts, cabbage, and sauces
author: Sandra Tam

review_text:
Tried their chicken as well as prawns gyoza. Didn't like the prawns one; the chicken was good in flavour but extremely oily. With the rice paired it with the vegetable broth of which wasn't a big fan. On the sides, their deep fried prawns were very good; the others were above average.

The concept overall is interesting though and how you're seated around the kitchen itself.
author: Vaibhav Aggarwal

review_text:
My go-to place for a good Kaisen Don.
Always had the Unagi Don and Ebi which is fantastic. The rest of it is authentic and flavourful.

Location is great but service here is another level.
Even though I come here often 1-2 a week, the staff here are always friendly and welcoming, treating me like it’s my first time. Shout out to the aunty at the cashier and sometimes the grandma who does the cleaning. Extremely friendly to my nieces!

Thank you for making my experience here a great one each time!
author: Adil Yusof

review_text: One of the best omakases in Singapore, and at very reasonable price too. Every dish is unique, flavorful and highly presentable. Some of the main dishes in the end are a bit salty for me, but it might be more of a personal palette thing. I will definitely be back
author: Yen Trinh

review_text:
Happy to be back at my fav fuss-free chirashi don spot! Here for their affordable lunch menu for the umpteenth time, and it never disappoints 🤤

I had the Aburi Salmon Kaisendon while my partner had the Crab Kaisendon - both were amazing!! I’d rate my aburi salmon kaisendon a 10/10 - the fish was super fresh, sashimi portions were generous, and the aburi salmon had that perfect smoky, melt in your mouth texture ❤️

All seating is at the bar counter, so you get a front row view of the chefs in action, which makes the whole experience even more enjoyable! Love that they serve free iced green tea, miso soup, braised daikon, and chicken wings - such a warm & thoughtful touch 🥰

The ambience is chill and nice, and the location is super convenient if you work in the CBD. Portions aren’t huge, which makes it the perfect lunch spot that won’t leave you in a food coma. Always a pleasure to dine here!
author: Joy Ong

review_text: We celebrated our anniversary at Teppei and thoroughly enjoyed both the food and the experience. While the restaurant’s décor is a little old, it actually adds a cozy, homely charm to the place. The food was excellent, with great variety and top-quality ingredients. The wagyu beef and the fish of the day were absolutely scrumptious, and every dish felt thoughtfully prepared. It was a truly delightful evening, and we left with happy hearts and full stomachs.
author: Weiwei Xu

review_text:
A generous-portion, traditional-leaning spot with well-blended flavors and friendly service, though the ambience could use some refinement.

Food Quality: Above average with well-balanced flavors.
Food Portion: Very generous—come hungry.
Food Creativity: Standard and traditional menu, not much innovation.
Staff: Generally friendly, though the cooks seemed a bit stressed at times.
Ambience: Average; music selection could be improved, and conversations between cooks over the counter are easily heard.
Price: Acceptable for the quality and portion size.
Best For: Groups of 2–4 looking for hearty, classic dishes.
author: Soo A

review_text:
I ordered the penne pesto and were pleasantly surprised. My husband usually avoids pesto, but he said this was the best pesto pasta he’s ever had. The butter garlic bread served alongside was rich, crispy, and absolutely delicious.

The bolognese was okay. Flavorful, but it could be improved with a bit more depth.

As for the pizza, it came out fresh and hot. It’s best enjoyed as a starter—great for sharing and sets the tone for the meal.
author: Angel Zaw

review_text:
Came on Valentines and service was exceptional. Waiter was welcoming and friendly, felt right at home.

Food: 10/10
We ordered a Caprese Risotto and a Tortellini e Pancetta. Food was served quickly and piping hot to our liking. Food was worth every dollar.

Atmosphere: 9/10
Don't be fooled, as interesting the location where this restaurant is situated, the place had a very homey vibe. Especially getting a very welcoming greeting by the waiter.

Will definitely be back!
author: Miguel Escanan

review_text: Service was exceptional, very friendly and gave good recommendations. Food was definitely good, nice variety with unique dishes like tandoori chicken gnocchi and food also came out fast
author: Ishshal Manocha

review_text: Fusion/cafe type pasta which was pretty good. The best of the 3 pastas we tried was the curry prawns pasta was rich and flavourful without being too salty. They had a promo where you get your third pasta at $1
author: racx iu

review_text: food was immaculate and service was top-tier! staff was super friendly with us, received a complimentary dessert on our date night for valentines and definitely did not disappoint! Will definitely be coming back here again :)
author: jernise toon zhiyi

review_text: Seeing many mixed reviews here, so was my experience, with the food far netter than the service. Just two of the mire senior female staff seemed to understand  Service, with the rest needing serious basic training. One cleared away the teapot when he asked if he could clear some wine glasses away. For the pricey seafood ordered, it was also very odd no vinegar or chilli sauce was available. At least the fish and crabs were fresh but at that price, no less is to be expected.  加油， 你们可以做到更好的。
author: Bike Wise

review_text: One of my friends just went there a few months ago and highly recommended me to try this restaurant out. The waitress who served us was very friendly. Those signature dishes were very tasty too. That’s why they are so famous. After dinner, my friends and I walked around Tanjong Pagar. It’s a very beautiful area to visit.
author: Jessie CHEUNG

review_text: I tried their signature crab dish along with other local favorites. It has a different taste from chili crab, with a rich and flavorful sauce that goes perfectly with the crab. Your hands do get messy, but the food is delicious and definitely worth it.
author: Catherine

review_text:
Food was good, but I feel the price is a bit too high. I can get the same quality elsewhere for a lower price. If the portion or quality was significantly better or different, then the price would make sense. But overall, it was still a good experience.

We had butter cream crabs, drunken prawn and claypot tofu- $198
author: EileenBb Lim

review_text: The prices here are quite high, but unfortunately the food quality didn’t match. The broccoli with scallops was disappointing — the scallops were not fresh, and the dish had a lot of excess water. When it came time to pay, I noticed that UnionPay was listed as an accepted payment method, but the staff refused to take it. Overall, not a satisfying experience, especially considering the cost.
author: I ZZ

review_text:
Updated: Second visit on a Tuesday night and I had a fantastic meal once again. We ordered chicken floss seaweed tater tots, umami butter squid, vongole pasta and beef stroganoff pasta. As fans of chicken floss, we enjoyed the tater tots very much and emptied the whole plate. We also loved both pastas which had al dente texture and were flavourful! Fresh vongole too! I also tried the snow pear drink which was light and refreshing. The lady boss was kind to offer us some nougats - we liked biscoff the most! :)

Wonderful dining experience on a Friday night ft. quality pasta and beef cubes! We had the tomyum prawn pasta and creamy crab broth pasta which were appetizing and delicious. Pasta was cooked al dente perfectly (so rare to find this honestly!) by the chef Sebastian and perfectly infused with umami and sweet seafood flavours. The seafood was very fresh too ~ can't wait to be back to try other pastas and rice bowls! Not forgetting the lovely, warm and great hospitality by the lady boss, who remained calm and cheerful in spite of the crowd. Thanks for the awesome food and service!
author: Gay Hui Hui

review_text:
Came here with colleague for lunch. The restaurant is a bit small so, we reach around 12.20pm and it was almost full.

We ordered a few pasta and sides to share, I recommend the prawn paste chicken, very generous with the portion, fried to perfection. We also had the umami butter squid but so-so in our opinion. I had pink salmon pasta which were not bad, my colleague say the tom yum pasta were abit creamy and soupy kind.

The staff were friendly and nice but the food took awhile to come I think only 1 chef perhaps.

10% discount to hospital staff across.
author: Vieon Wu

review_text: A cosy hole-in-the-wall gem that my family really enjoys dining at from time to time. The food is tasty, the service impeccable and the ambience comforting. A standout is the prawn paste chicken, and virtually every pasta dish is delightful. Meals are typically capped by a complimentary sampler of chewy nougat which are deserving of a visit on their own.
author: Ivan Yap

review_text:
Found this casual restaurant by chance and thankfully we managed to snag a table as the space is small with few tables.

We were warmly greeted by a lady staff although she was busy serving and clearing tables. Later on I found out that the place is ran by a duo with each dish freshly cooked upon order. No service charge in exchange for a smile and a little patience.

We were given some housemade nougats while we waited for our food and they had a nice soft chew and subtle sweetness. Pretty good! I had the cheese chicken cutlet with curry and it was delicious. The chicken was fried to golden crisp and the meat was tender and juicy with cheesy goodness. And the curry was different that expected in a good way with a little heat. Everything on the plate was definitely freshly made, even my friend's cauliflower rice was tasty.
author: Jessica Chew

review_text: Surprisingly good meal! Looking at menu, had assumed this was just going to be just another cheap and bland pasta joint. But food was packed with flavor and executed very well. Would have loved to see more diverse sides though - would have ordered more stuff to eat. No GST and service charge too. Will certainly be back!
author: Yoon ZY

review_text: A pleasant spot for a relaxed meal or casual drinks. The beer selection is good and reasonably priced, making it easy to linger, while the food selection offered different stalls offers a variety to suit different tastes. Overall, a comfortable and enjoyable venue with solid offerings on both food and drinks.
author: Isaac Sam

review_text:
I recently visited Essen @ The Pinnacle, and it was such a pleasant surprise! At first glance it looks like a modern, upgraded food court, but the quality here feels a lot more elevated than your usual kopitiam. The atmosphere strikes a nice balance between laid-back and stylish — with both indoor and al-fresco seating that’s great for casual lunches, dinner with friends, or even just drinks after work.  ￼

What really stood out to me was the variety of food on offer. Instead of being tied to just one cuisine, Essen brings together several stalls under one roof — from Western burgers and pizzas to hearty Asian and fusion dishes — so everyone in the group can find something they’ll enjoy. Each stall feels like its own little kitchen, and many of the dishes we tried were genuinely tasty and well-executed.  ￼

Despite being a collective space, the ambience didn’t feel chaotic or noisy; in fact, it felt thoughtfully put together, kind of like a convivial neighbourhood hangout rather than your typical food court. The staff were friendly too, and the price point (about $$ per person) makes it easy to come back often without feeling like you’re overspending.  ￼

Overall, Essen is a great place to gather with friends, enjoy a surprisingly good range of food, and soak in a warm, welcoming vibe — definitely worth a visit if you’re around Tanjong Pagar or Outram Park.  ￼
author: Mcw Chow

review_text:
There's inside and you can drink here so it's really comfortable
We ordered from the Italian, Indian, Chinese and Thai stalls
This is my fav pizza which has a thin and crispy crust and it is topped with lots of mushrooms!
The deep fried sweet potato is also crispy and crunchy
Kashmiri Pulao is a liiitle bit spicy but really good taste
This Pad Thai has a texture similar to konjac noodles
It felt like healthy
author: moon Luan

review_text:
Had Papadum, The lamb masala is soft, cooked on site so it is hot, but a bit salty, should had added basmati rice.
Butter Naan I cannot taste the butter, I think garlic naan is better.
author: mag leong

review_text:
I love having dinner here! This place is like a premier hawker center.
Personally, I prefer to eat indoors always.
In that sense, this place is good for me while providing multiple food options.
I've tried the Thai, Vietnamese, and Burger shops. All of them were excellent. The prices are reasonable, and the environment is clean and cool.
author: Harry HM

review_text:
This was my second visit to Hakata Ikkousha, and I’m so glad I decided to try the God Fire Special. While the broth looks intimidatingly fiery, the heat is remarkably well-balanced; it delivers a rich, spicy kick without overwhelming the palate.
The noodles were the highlight for me—cooked to a perfect al dente texture that provided a satisfying chew in every bite. Beyond the food, the service remained consistently friendly and efficient throughout the meal.
This spot has officially earned a permanent place in my top three favorite ramen shops. If you’re looking for depth of flavor and quality craft, I highly recommend giving them a visit.
author: Winson Tay

review_text:
Comfortable dining environmemt, had the God Fire special upgraded set. Ramen came in flavourful soup and ramen cooked in right softness. Although i would prefer the soup to be spicier, it will still pack a challenge for some.

The servings are pretty big so check with their staff before deciding on adding noodle or ingredients. The staff are really super friendly

Overall, a good spicy ramen shop to try for my chilli loving friends!
author: A T

review_text: Reach there almost noon time with a group of 6 having lunch. Ordering food is via piece of paper by selecting which raven you like. Service is good as they serve food and drinks quite fast as I suppose for the quick turnaround. Only issue is the small shop have limited seatings therefore have to quickly eat and leave the place for other patrons. Their signature ramen is quite good except I not a fan of thick broth therefore it is okay for me. Maybe if you are a fan of thick broth, the signature ramen is good. Overall, worth coming but if you come late might need to wait for awhile to get a seat.
author: Kenneth Khoo

review_text:
Singapore is not shortage of Japanese Ramen, yet this one stands out.

Under a HDB, blended into local.. but amazing Ramen better than those in the malls.

This makes u feel Japanese because in japan many great Ramen are in neighborhoods.

Ordered the God fire special L1 spicy,  good generous slices of meat and full egg.  Portion is good for me.. broth is rich but not over powering.  Noodles is the thin type goes well with the broth spice...

This definitely will be my choice of Ramen in Singapore now

Service is fast and quality not compromised.
author: joe fong

review_text:
broths here were rich but on the thinner side of  things, less fatty too. black garlic tonkotsu broth was fragrant, volcano broth was proper spicy.

noodles were hard as requested, stayed hard through the meal too. cha sue was quite thin though.

portions here were also smaller in general compared to the competition, but overall a good meal
author: Marcus Ang

review_text:
I’ve been to Ryo more than 30 times now and every single visit still moves me. Each meal feels new, sincere, and crafted with heart. Chef Roy is not only incredibly skilled but also one of the kindest and most humble people I’ve met. His passion and respect for Japanese cuisine truly shine through every course. Also there is THE BEST ICE BEER 🍺

What amazes me is how consistently perfect everything is from the freshness and quality of the ingredients to the balance, creativity, and warmth behind every dish. The portions are just right, the flavors are refined yet comforting, and the experience always feels personal.

Singapore may not be known for authentic Japanese cuisine, but every time I travel abroad, I find myself missing Ryo. The staff are wonderful too-attentive, genuine, and always welcoming. You can feel the care and pride in everything they do.

This place is not only my favorite but truly one of the best Singapore’s hidden gems and a place made with love and care.
author: Ki Won Sung

review_text: I've revisited Ryo 4 times as this is my absolute favourite sushi omakase in Singapore. If you are interested in having a simple yet delicious sushi omakase, look no further. I've been to about 10 sushi omakase across Singapore and Japan, and this restaurant is easily the most value-for-money one out of all of them. 10/10 will recommend!
author: Eugene

review_text: Affordable Japanese Omakase at $98/pax incl taxes. The chef handmade each sushi right infront of you. Very fresh and delish! Will go again
author: Jacqueline Lee

review_text:
Hands down, the best Omakase experience I’ve ever had.
Every single course was a masterpiece — from the piping hot dishes that warmed the soul to the sushi that was so fresh, you could practically taste the ocean in every bite. The chef’s generosity with premium ingredients truly elevated the entire meal, turning it into an indulgence worth every single penny. A perfect harmony of flavors, textures, and presentation — this is Omakase done right.
author: Apple L.

review_text: Very bad. Avoid at all cost. If you frequent omakase places enough, you can tell this place is not fresh at all. Had food poisoning after. All the sushi had similar texture & the sashimi was already pre cut. Chef had 0 interaction & just put the rice & sashimi together. The crab roll just put me to shock, it was grey?? How long has it been left in the fridge? Had shells in it also. Gagged while eating.
author: Poh Wei

review_text: Horfun sauce didn't had any garlic so tasted quite plain. Burger was made with all the premade items that you can buy at ntuc. Fries tasted good but was cold. Waited for a while even thou the restaurant was pretty empty. Price was on the higher side and doesn't really justify the quality.
author: Z Ong

review_text:
To a meal I can only describe as to solely satiate my hunger, I felt compelled to leave this review because of the ‘Mini Lo Hei’ which costed $16.80. Starting of with what I liked about the dish: portion was acceptable (not to be confused with large, just acceptable).

The 4-5 mini pieces of smoked salmon on it is sized as photographed. The ingredients were totally out of proportion and the dish is very spice-forward. For a dish that costed $16.80, I’d say I’ll gladly pay $5 at max for it.

Burger I had was dry and tough, but that’s what I get for paying $7.80 for a burger. Can’t complain there.
author: Marcus Lee

review_text: The hor fun tasted especially salty, like 200% salt. Inedible! Very strange taste compared to the usual. What happened? The food used to be better here. Change of chef? Please improve!
author: ETH

review_text: i don’t usually hate on restaurants and I’m a fan of Han’s but this is just really disappointing. I eat SAF ration everyday and this is genuinely worse. tastes like it was left over from 5days ago and they microwaved it😭
author: Crazy Kimchi

review_text: Food was edible, not the best but not the worst. Service is pretty fast, guess they are just here to feed empty stomachs. They’ve got promos where if you come in pairs, you can save 20% off the second item. Place is generally clean.
author: Daniel Bok

review_text: My colleagues invited me to try the food from this establishment for lunch since there was a whole bunch of them wanting to eat clean. Now I typically would steer clear of these "bowl" type cuisines but egged on by my counterparts i thought sure lets give it a shot. Available only via Deliveroo, the food arrived warm still - thank goodness it was an almost 30 minute travel time. Now I ordered a Base of Romaine Lettuce, Pasta, Sautéed Mushrooms, Rosemary Chicken, Long Beans and Pesto Sauce. Now I wasn't expecting much hence I opted for a Petite Bowl but it was huge! For 10 bucks there's a fair bit of quantity and the ingredients were pretty good too. The mushrooms were expertly fried till they had a smokey taste akin to wok hei, the long beans provided good crunch without that raw taste. The chicken thigh provided the protein and tasted actually not bad, tender and juicy. The pasta gave the carbs and finally the pesto sauce blended the various flavours into a appetitising sweet, sour and savoury medley. Impressed? Yes, I finished the entire bowl with glee. Satisfied? Yup, I am full, who knew eating healthy could taste this good.
author: Jechtto

review_text:
I’ve been a long-time customer of The Daily Cut for years, and have been patronising them even more often in recent times after deciding to be wiser with my diet.

I had patronised all three of their outlets but my most recent unpleasant experience at the Guoco Tower outlet and with their nonchalant management left a bitter aftertaste and an affirmation of my complete abstinence from this brand and their umbrella group of brands (e.g., Muchachos) in the future.

On this occasion, I had ordered the usual large size bowl which comes with two protein portions. When I was served my bowl, the whole portion, especially the two proteins, looked appallingly and unusually small and miserly. For context, I also ordered a large bowl just the evening before so I was clear about their usual portioning size.

I approached the store manager, Necie, to complain that the portion given this time was extraordinarily little compared to the usual portions that I had received on all previous visits. After casually eyeballing my bowl, she was dismissive and insisted that the portion given was correct. I tried to tell her again that I had order the same bowl the night before but clearly the portion on this day was much smaller, but she still replied adamantly that it was correct and there was nothing she was willing to do about. I attempted to get her to weigh my bowl, but she fervently denied. Seeing that further conversation with her was going to be futile, I requested for her name and the management’s email address to file a complaint. Interestingly enough, she told me that her name was “Cindy” and even wrote that name on a piece of paper together with the email address. It was in the management’s email reply later that I found out her name was actually Necie…

Anyhow, the management replied with a response siding with their staff’s actions, and included canned responses that all feedback would be taken seriously. No attempt at service recovery was made, and the email sounded as if their staff’s actions were condoned.

I will never dine with such businesses with unethical and unfair business practices where their management only cares about maximising their profits at the expense of customer service and satisfaction.

It is definitely not the case that I am overly anal about being shortchanged with a smaller portion, but it is imperative for people like me, who are counting their macros to hit their daily protein targets, that we actually get the protein count which The Daily Cut’s nutritional calculator claims that each bowl would provide.

I will NEVER dine with this fraudulent establishment in the future, and do not recommend this brand with severely deteriorating standards to anyone who cares about their meal and nutritional intake. They absolutely have no standards nor customer service and recovery.
author: Bradford Loh

review_text:
Ordered the large bowl and portions were pretty generous, which is always a good thing. However, the tofu skin was quite hard as it was probably left out after cooking for quite a long time. Would not order the tofu again in future.

Staff was not the friendliest but also not the coldest, seems like they did not really enjoy their jobs and were just trying to do the bare minimum 😅

Don’t forget to sign up for their membership as you can earn and claim cash back for future orders!
author: Arnold Teo

review_text:
5/5 for roasted chicken leg.... cuz it was juicy as chicken should be... but condolences to whoever got chicken breast cuz i saw those cubes n it looked so dry...
Thai tofu just tasted like plain tofu.... my friend said the other outlets are better at doing it so i guess I got unlucky with it. Nice meal but i mean they r just tossing stuff together so!!!!!! But I enjoyed the Harissa aioli.... tangy, spicy, soury... !!!!!!
author: elizabeth wee

review_text:
I am a frequent patron of TDC at TP branch hence I am quite familiar of their portioning. I am however very very surprised and shocked when my daughter brought the order to me in my office. I had to pay extra $1.20 for the falafel as protein and I only was given 1 piece? I would have chosen the chix then. And the pumpkin, only 1.5 slices?

This is really very disappointing and I wonder if all staff are trained to portion equally.
author: Alice She (His beloved)

review_text: Very authentic Japanese restaurant. The chef has over 40 years of experience. Love their wide variety of choices to choose from. Not your typical Omakase style. You can freely ask what is their seasonal or special dish, not found in the menu! I love how cozy and comfortable the place feels. You can enjoy the food slowly and chat with the friendly chef. They serve high quality and fresh food. I am truly amazed and this restaurant is totally underrated! I will come back again.
author: Wei Ling Tay

review_text:
We really wanted to love this - but it just didn't meet our expectations. Sashimi was fine and sushi was okay. But the aburi sushi was very mid and the prawn was supermarket bad. Also disappointed by the bubbly chawanmushi.

Chef and the service team were very nice but the food didn't match up to them and the price.
author: Phoebe Ting

review_text:
A small restaurant with warm service.
Really enjoyed all the recommendations by Chef Paul.
* Aburi Engawa Sushi 🍣  is highly recommended as it literally melts into your mouth.
* Canadian Oyster is fresh, big, fleshy and creamy.
* Akagai Sashimi is fresh. My personal favourite Sashimi. Love the texture.
* Shima Aji Sashimi is beautifully sliced and thick.
* Appertizer (not too sure if is squid) is very tasty too.
I would definitely go back again!
Thank you, Chef Paul for his recommendations and friendly service.
author: Yvonne T

review_text:
Nothing fancy here, just a super good sushi chef handling and preparing very authentic sushi and sashimi.

Right infront of you, the delicious creation are made.

The best Uni I have ever tried. Perfection!
author: Tze Kiat Lee

review_text: Always a yes to this hole-in-the-wall sushi place that just celebrated its fourth anniversary, and I hope they do celebrate many, many more. The food is fresh, and the chefs are friendly.  Get a seat at the bar and watch the chefs at work. The place also has a fine selection of sake - go with the chef’s recommendations; they know what works best with their food
author: Jo T

review_text:
This place has been on our radar for its exceptional fish and chips. It seems They’ve truly mastered the art of battering and frying the fish and chips, as well as the scampi. The batter is perfectly thin and not overly oily, while the scampi is fresh and cooked to perfection. The fish is also well-cooked and easy to eat.

However, the tartar sauce could use some improvement. It lacks the kick that gives it a good flavor, but the lemon seems to enhance its taste. The curry sauce is also not as good as expected, opt for other sauce instead.

The thick-cut fries are very nice and pair well with the fish and chips. Enjoy them all with some malt vinegar, the British way.

The beer selection is okay, and they also have some gin and other alcoholic drinks. However, the gin is too much tonic and not enough gin, which is not ideal.

Overall, this place is worth trying for its excellent fish and chips.
author: M *

review_text: One of the best fish and chips in Singapore! Love their scotch eggs too! Sat outdoor with high chair thinking it might be warm but it was actually quite windy. Service was good! Friendly staff with all smiles. Didnt wait till long for food. Fish and prawn were fresh. Their batter is one of the best!
author: Joanne Tan

review_text: Got the large fish and chips, bangers and mash, and scotch egg to share. Filling meal! Enjoyed the batter being crispy, fish fresh with nice sauces to go with too! Bangers and mash was.. bangers and mash. scotch egg was pretty interesting and a nice mix in between bites of the fish. They didn't have the beef stew when we were there though, hopefully can try it again some day.
author: Daniel Lee

review_text: One of the best fish and chips I had! Fish was crispy on the outside and super tender on the inside. We got the curry, tartar, and salted egg sauce (CNY Special) and they were all amazing. There were several condiments on the table which includes the quintessential malt vinegar, a must have for British fish and chips. Scottish Egg was done well with the evidently runny eggs. Overall, a a delightful meal and worth giving it a try if you’re in the area or craving some good British fish and chips. Would be back to try the other mains!
author: Jay Lim

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Absolutely outstanding fish and chips! The fish was perfectly cooked with an ultra-crispy, golden batter that stayed light and crunchy with every bite. Inside, the fish was fresh, flaky, and beautifully moist — the ideal contrast to that irresistible crunch. Portions were generous, the seasoning spot on, and it was clear real care went into the preparation. Easily some of the best fish and chips I’ve had — a must-order and well worth coming back for!
author: Rodney Loh

review_text:
Ordered the Taiwan original karaage & chashu mazesoba. Karaage is juicy and well marinated, have to mix the noodles well before eating. Noodles is springy and quite big portion. Like the chashu too as it’s not too fatty kind and the taste is nice! Recommend the gyoza as well!
However, the indoor seating & space is limited.
author: Chloe

review_text:
Limited seating, and the food can sometimes be a slight miss, but 90% of the time you’re getting just a nice bowl of mazesoba that hits the spot.

Gets crowded, but outdoor seating make for some nice people watching opportunity, staff are really nice too, and you can tell that they’re working hard to make sure everything’s in place.

Were I an unhealthier person, I’d be here way more often. But this is your perfect Friday night meal before a night out, or a cozy night in.
author: William Lim

review_text:
The Ultimate Mazesoba Experience: A Love Letter to Kaijiken

Since the day Kaijiken first opened its doors in Tanjong Pagar, it has been my undisputed go-to. If there is a "King of Mazesoba," I’ve certainly eaten enough bowls to claim the title. This isn't just a meal for me; it’s a weekly ritual that never fails to hit the spot.

Why It’s the Best in Town:
* The Signature Taiwan Mazesoba: This is the undisputed star of the show. Every bowl is a masterclass in texture and flavor—the chewy, perfectly al dente noodles acting as the perfect canvas for that rich, savory minced meat and the creamy richness of the egg yolk.

* Consistent Excellence: Being a "regular" is an understatement. Even after countless visits, the quality remains top-tier. Every single time I visit, I leave as a "happy camper," satisfied by the soul-warming depth of their secret sauce.

* The King’s Privilege: There is a certain magic in returning to a place where the flavors feel like home. Having worked my way through a mountain of bowls here, I can confidently say that Kaijiken offers the most addictive dry ramen experience in Singapore.

If you’re in Tanjong Pagar and haven't tried their Taiwan Mazesoba, you are truly missing out on a weekly delicacy that defines comfort food.
author: Hoey Siang Ong

review_text:
My go-to place for dry noodles in Singapore, I’ve been a loyal customer for more than 8 years. The taste is consistently amazing and the quality is always great.

The staff are friendly, and I’ve heard they’re expanding to the Philippines. Really happy for them and wishing them continued success!
author: Skylar Wang

review_text:
The price is considered similar to others nearby.

The soup is a small cup, limited one time refill.

Noodles average.
The flavor mainly from onion, eggs and the chili oil I added myself.

Soup not much taste.
author: Alex Lim

review_text:
Yesterday was the third time my family and I came this restaurant (6th Feb, 11th Feb & 25th Feb). All for different occasions.

What we love about this restaurant is that the ambience and service of the restaurant.

I wish to compliment these wonderful people who made our visits good and memorable ones.

Ms Amylyn, Ms Jasmine, the part-time staff - Nursyamin, the two servers a slender and tall Malay guy and also the lady from East Malaysia.

Kudos and keep up your good work!
author: Hart Tzar

review_text:
Excellent service from Jo, Amelyn, yoyo, Zaine and Jas.
Loved the old fashioned gilded tea set !
Blue pea lemonade with an ice rose was a nice touch.
Laksa, blue pea nasi lemak, achar, pegedel and otak were delicious.
Other fusion items : buah keluak tart was cold and dry but tasty; beef rendang puff was a tad dry but the beefy flavour was nice; haebee hiam toast was spicy and adequate.
Rojak dough fritter was great disappointment- stale, dry and chewy.  So was the tofu puffs.  Most unpleasant although the sauce and fruit were ok
Chicken char siu soh was very strange tasting - not like char siu at all.  Chicken siu mai was better than the char siu soh.
Beetroot chicken looked inviting but was bland
Ondeh ondeh and ondeh cake were good.  The durian cake didn’t need the gula melaka.  The pulot kaya was a non-event.  But the rainbow kueh was fragrant.
Directions given to the restaurant were totally wrong.  From the carpark lift one had to change lifts to access the restaurant, unlike what I was told.  I had elderly guests - they had to walk quite a bit.  Thank goodness they could handle stairs - there are 3 steps to access the restaurant ! So wheelchairs would find it a problem.
For the price of $28.80++ i might not come again unless the food really improves.
author: Li Huan Quek

review_text:
The restaurant is located on the 2nd floor of the hotel. Timing of the buffet is 12pm till 2.30pm.
The theme is "Peranakan". So you will find all sorts of different peranakan cusine like chicken cook in redang, otak otak, blue pea flavour rice, sambal, asam laksa and more.
Free flow of hot and cold drink and also cold dessert like cendol and hot dessert like pulut itam.
There is Christmas promotion now for a price of $36++.
author: peter liew

review_text: I come here often when I need to host large groups for halal dining. Not a lot of places serve halal hotpot, and this restaurant does it very well. You'll be spoiled for choice for both cooked and hotpot items. Leave room for their famous dessert birdcage. Staff here are friendly and make you feel at home. The execitive chef makes and appearance to thank your group for coming personally.  reservations are highly recommended. Must come.
author: Moiz Malik

review_text: The steamboat buffet at M Hotel was outstanding from start to finish. The spread was generous, fresh, and beautifully presented, with flavors that impressed at every station. What truly elevated the experience was the service. Jasmine and Amelyn were exceptional—warm, attentive, and genuinely caring. They anticipated needs, explained dishes thoughtfully, and made every guest feel welcome. Their professionalism and kindness turned a great buffet into a memorable dining experience I would happily return for without hesitation anytime soon at M Hotel.
author: Stephanie Ow

review_text:
The team here deserves a shout-out for their fantastic service! I accidentally sent my order to another location via the GYG app. Despite the busy lunch hour, the staff at both outlets handled it so smoothly.

This is my second time interacting with the same lady at the counter (I’ll get her name next time), and she’s always been very helpful. She and her colleague resolved the issue immediately—no questions asked—and didn't make me feel bad about the mistake, which I really appreciated.

And the food was amazing! The butter chicken was so good I came back within the same week. Great food and excellent service make this outlet a standout. Thank you, Guoco team!
author: Sarah L

review_text:
Food taste is consistent with other outlets, which were so so but a good place to fix hunger quick.
dine in at 8pm+, and it's still crowded and packed. Food is ready within 10mins after your order.
author: Lyla (ZL)

review_text: My favorite pit stop after a workout — it’s like fast food, but the kind your trainer wouldn’t judge you for. Fresh, quick, and super tasty. Feels good to actually enjoy a meal that’s healthy without trying too hard.
author: Timothy Leong

review_text:
Standard and quality had been dropping
- hard shell taco meat filling quantity reducing, the taco shell also tastes a bit stale/soft and no longer crispy
- seasoning for fries and others is also saltier than normal
- top up 1.80 additional for coffee but it is a can drink that tastes so bad….
Not going to come back as frequently anymore
author: gee M

review_text:
Tried the butter chicken burrito bowl
- tasted v mild
- nothing much stands out
- chicken not v flavourful and not highly seasoned

I still love the free flow cilantro and onion.
author: Jane

restaurant_name: Outram Park Ya Hua Rou Gu Cha
review_text:
Came on a Sunday around 1300-1400. Plenty of free tables. Ordered the most basic dish: pork ribs soup with rice — and it hit just right. The peppery broth gave a bold (but refreshing?!) warming flavour that was a nice contrast to the usual (Malaysian) herbal bak kut teh I preferred and usually go for.
It was clean, savoury, and comforting without being too heavy.
