I didn’t order the fried dou stick (you tiao), and only found out after that they refill the soup(!) — next time I’m definitely pairing it with the sticks for extra dunk-and-soak joy, since I know there will be enough soup for all the carbs I want. 🤤

Simple, honest, and satisfying meal. If I'm around this area again, if come back. You should come too for a peppery twist on a classic.

@jonatology
author: Jonathan Ha

restaurant_name: Outram Park Ya Hua Rou Gu Cha
review_text:
Ordered:
Premium spare ribs (fat) - highly recommend
Spare ribs (lean) - should order fat instead of lean
Pig tail soup - pig tail is nice but somehow the soup is a little too salty but overall a good dish
Fresh sliced fish soup - soup is peppery and it came with watercress
Sliced pork loin soup - pork slice is generous, not small and not very 柴 would recommend to people who’s not a fan of spare ribs
Chye sim oyster sauce - not oily, pretty good
Braised tau pok - good but will go well with rice Cux a little salty
Braised peanuts - good
You tiao (fried dough stick) - it’s not served hot but surprisingly still very crispy and we even had 2nd serving.  Highly recommend if you are a fan of you tiao.

All soup are peppery base and tastes great.  Soup is refillable.
author: Yami lim

restaurant_name: Outram Park Ya Hua Rou Gu Cha
review_text:
The soup and pork ribs were great.
Vegetables menu OK, lot of fried onions on top. If you not a bog fan of it need to tell the staff who takes orders not to put it on.

(Fresh lemonade is just a name, it’s not fresh lols)
author: Chan T

restaurant_name: Outram Park Ya Hua Rou Gu Cha
review_text: Had lunch here recently. The soup for the bak kut teh is nearly tasteless. There is a distinct aroma of white pepper–yes, but the soup itself does not carry any pork bone or white pepper flavour. It's also oddly clear, which makes me think that perhaps it wasn't boiled for long enough. The taste of the bkt soup is less savoury and less flavourful than the plain bee-zeng-spring-onion soup you get at the side when you order chicken rice.. As for the spare ribs itself, it was moderately tender and still had a chew to it; good for those who like lean meat. I was given 4 half-ribs which is not a lot for the price of $11.50. I think The pig trotter fared better, and had just the right proportion of fatty skin:lean meat. Rice portion is rather miserable. Please give more rice. It looks like someone stole half my rice. Youtiao ($3) nicely fried and crisp (a little oily though). Kiam chye just tastes like any other kiam chye. Price here is quite high and the quality does not make up for it. Something has to be done about the soup. Youtiao is also too expensive given that it is probably just 1 dough fritter cut into many small chunks. My glass of chinese tea was $1.70. Judging from the space and the number of employees the shop has, a larger proportion of the cost goes back to labour. I just wish some of it could go back to providing a larger portion of rice.
author: Sg Hungry Ghost

restaurant_name: Outram Park Ya Hua Rou Gu Cha
review_text: A long-standing bak kut teh spot known for its peppery soup. The broth is robust and comforting, and there are many watercress vegetable options to go with the soup. A satisfying, no-frills meal.
author: RACHEL NG

review_text:
Went on 22nd Nov 2025 for anniversary dinner. My partner knew of this place from some videos online and wanted to try the grilled maguro rib and the grilled maguro collar. We had a reservation prior to coming.
While ordering, the staff patiently responded to all our queries and explained some of dishes.
We had the maguro 5-cut sashimi. The staff explained to us the order we should eat the pieces and the corresponding parts. Despite being on the pricier side, we could tell the quality of the fish was really good. The akami, the cut which is supposed to be the least fatty, left the surface of the soy sauce with a layer of fat. The wasabi provided is also from the actual wasabi plant, not from some packaged wasabi which tend to be too spicy.
We also tried the fish heart/ventricle, which is on their seasonal menu, it tastes exactly like what you would expect innards to taste like if you had tried innards from other animals such as chicken.
The maguro rib was a surprising one for me, the charred part didn't feel like fish but you could still tell it's still fish from the meat closer to the bones.
Their hot tea has free refills btw :)
This place can accommodate large groups, there was a large family dining here as well while we were here, counter seats are also available.
author: Qing

review_text:
Amazing experience at Kuro Maguro. Perfect for tuna lovers who want to try more than just sashimi.
From smoked tuna heart and stomach to tender tuna cheek and spicy tuna stomach, everything was well done. The assorted tuna cuts (otoro, chutoro, akami, kamatoro) were fresh and melt-in-your-mouth.
The Megumi Gunkan was overflowing, the aburi toro roll with truffle sauce was delicious, and the grilled Kuro Maguro ribs were incredibly tender.
Great quality, thoughtful dishes, and definitely a must-visit. Will be back!
author: Sheen Cher

review_text: The food is great. Very fresh and grill just right. Highball can be more alcoholic. Service crew really professional, table is double wipe, hand written menu is really cute. But the place is really a bit cramp. I sat outside hence a little warm...
author: Wu Chunhui

review_text: Kuro Maguro Sushi & Dining was absolutely amazing – so good that we came back several times during our stay! The sushi is incredibly fresh, beautifully presented, and full of flavor. The quality of the fish and the skill in preparation really stand out. Service is friendly and attentive, and the overall dining experience is top-notch. A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic, high-quality sushi!
author: Didier Demange

review_text: I’m not a Tuna lover but had amazing tuna at a DIFFERENT restaurant in Ngee Ann City and decided I wanted to try this place which specialises in Tuna and was featured by a prominent Japanese influencer who reviews Singapore food, thinking that a place that specialises in Tuna would be way better than a sushi restaurant that serves a much wider menu. The texture, flavour and freshness for their cooked tuna collar and tuna sashimi was disappointing. The photo of the $52 tuna sashimi platter showed and indicated in text that it was 3-cut x 5 variations of tuna but when it was served it was only 2-cut x 5 variations. We asked why it was not 3-cut and the staff said it’s “just like that”. The otoro was extremely sinewy and did not have the melt in the mouth quality, and was chewy and lacked flavour. They included tuna brain (at least this is what I heard) which was not defrosted upon serving and when it finally defrosted, it tasted like the inside of a freezer and the texture was rough and chewy. I might have not left this review if not for the fact that the meal was expensive and the name of this restaurant gives the expectation that tuna is their specialty. The only things that were good were the sushi rice and green tea. I will be recommending my friends to stay away from this place.
author: X L

review_text: If this restaurant was ‘a one night stand’ you’re guaranteed a fun night with no regrets. We chanced upon this place for a quick dinner and weren’t disappointed. The vibe is very casual and unpretentious and we were greeted with a warm welcome. The atmosphere makes you want to have a cold beer and enjoy some tasty snacks so we got stuck in. We tried the deep fried wagyu beef steak, which wasn’t the most amazing we have experienced but it was pretty good, soft tender meat with a crispy coating of breadcrumbs. We also had a medium sashimi platter which was surprisingly fresh and pretty good quality comprising of tuna, white bait, salmon, fish roe and another assorted fish. The croquettes we tried were a little different from others I’ve tried as they were ball shaped rather than flat, but the filling was creamier and filled with tasty potato pieces. We also had a plate of karage fried chicken, which for 6 dollars was a generous and tasty portion. We helped our meal along with a bottle of sake which we had hot. The service throughout was attentive and efficient, despite us changing our sake order around 5 times. The atmosphere was fun and relaxed (a lot of Japanese patrons having highballs, always a good sign of authenticity), and the food good. The price was a little above average, but in our opinion, well worth it for the experience and a good night out.
author: Jit Sandhu

review_text: We came by for dinner, and I enjoyed the food and drinks very much! Ordered the octopus sashimi as starter, which was very nicely accompanied, and their soba was good as well. The chicken karage came in a really big potion, and it was well battered. Enjoyed the whiskey mix as well!
author: Nicholas Loo

review_text: Great lunch deals are found here. Charcoal grilled pork belly set is delicious, as is their sashimi bowls. Miso soup is special as well, rather different from the usual. Quick and decent service from the staff. Always polite and fuss free.
author: Y Wong

review_text:
Second visit to this Izakaya. First one was in April 2016. This place has a good feel of what an Izakaya should be. Staffed by both native Japanese & other Asians, you'll be warmly welcomed you enter and that attention does not abade until you leave.
This bar hole has a seasonal menu that changes according the the seafood availability of the month.  Customers are mainly Japanese as expected with a mingling of Singaporeans & other nationalities. Menus are both handwritten & printed in Japanese & English. Besides munchies, the selection of beer,  mixes,  sake & other liquor is impressive.
As for how the food tasted,  I've only one advise - go see for yourself!
author: Joseph Ong

review_text:
Food is not bad. Service is good. Soba was good but portion may be a little big. The sliced wagyu for the soba was very bland but the tempura was great.

Also ordered the hokkaido fish and chips. It was interesting and tasted great, however the portion is really small so i wouldn't consider it a main.
author: T

review_text:
We came from 100AM mall and was ravenous. I was craving for some Prata and just looked up any Prata places near me and this was one that was relatively near. We decided to give it a shot and I have to say just a couple of words. AFFORDABLE, DELICIOUS, OVERALL PLEASANT!

The staff were polite and friendly, the service was great and most importantly, the food was absolutely tasty! We got Pratas and a Mutton Murtabak to share along with a cup of tea and coffee. Everything was so good. The Pratas were crispy, with the right amount of softness. The fish curry was flavourful. The mutton in the Murtabak was very generously given and even our drinks were delightful.

If you’re ever near Tanjong Pagar and are looking for some scrumptious Prata/Murtabak etc and don’t want to break your bank, come to Curry Village!

P.S: We were hungry so we didn’t manage to get pictures of the food but we took an after pic (we cleaned our plates) and you can see how much we loved it!
author: Farhana Mazlan

review_text: I woke up super early jet lagged around 4:30 am and was quite hungry. I came to this place early around 5am and the owner informed me they don’t serve until 5:30, but still decided to make me some garlic Prata and daal since I was here so early. Delicious and filling and the staff was so kind serving me before their opening hours. Highly recommend!
author: Yung Turkish Man

review_text: Had a late night prata with chicken curry on a Friday and ‘white’ stir fried Bee Hoon. Bee Hoon was tasteless prata was ok but the chicken curry was tasteless too, a bit strange but could not find anything wrong with it. That night onwards stomach was feeling hot and the food does not seem to go down the gut. Could not sleep too. Saturday onwards was feverish and having diarrhoea whole day. Thought it would go away after taking charcoal pills but until Sunday, it was getting worse & decided to visit doctor. Highly suspect the bland chicken curry that went with the prata could be the cause. As it is operating 24hrs, its SOP for replenishing cooked food is highly questionable. For your health pls avoid this shop.
author: Kam Heng Ng

review_text:
The murtabak is smaller and less crispy than next door, tastes lighter on the stomach. It has less onions and egg too. But still tasty.
Nasi briyani is pretty good - full of aroma, not too moist, fresh and warm from 8am!
author: Colin Tan

review_text: Actually you dont even deserve single star. I ordered 5 veg fried rice and you delivered 5 egg rice i claimed refund or delivery of 5 veg fried rice but no support received from hotel and geab
author: nilesh thange

review_text:
SBCD Korea Tofu House is a chain at the basement of guoco that serves Korean set meals that are a definite notch above average and is very well seasoned, making for a satisfying meal. We tried the chicken and spicy pork bulgogi combo, which comes with a seafood stew. The stew included a special touch with a minicrab, though it was quite tiny. The variety of flavors was enjoyable.

However, the pricing feels too high for what you get. A rib set costs around 50 dollars after service charge and GST, which is steep considering the ingredients are not exceptional and are relatively inexpensive cuts. While the meal was tasty, the value isn't really there.
author: Ribeye

review_text:
This is rapidly becoming my favorite Korean place!

Enjoyed our dinner here, the Spicy Grilled Chicken Combo was done well, the grilled bits were fragrant and crispy, exactly what you want from grilled meat.

The Sesame Soontofu was hot and filling, a little bland which allowed the sesame taste to come to the fore (which is what I think they were going for), would have again.

One thing I like about SBCD is how you can customize how much and how crispy you want your rice to be, merely by controlling how long you open the rice pot. When you open it and allow moisture to escape, then the bottom of the rice will become drier and more crispy.

So it allows you to control it according to how long you leave the lid on. Is this a feature or a bug? Feature, I'd say, completely non-sarcastically.

While my partner didn't like the complimentary deep fried fish, I'm quite taken with it and how it's properly deboned. As for banchan, the ddeokbokki was alright, cucumber good, seasoned korean seawood good, squid and kimchi alright.

Both of us really like the complimentary yakult as you're going to pay though. Always somehow hits the spot after an SBCD meal. Or rather, Korean yakult.

Must say that this shop is a little hot though. Would have appreciated a cooler environment. The management did put fans to compensate, but still.
author: JR FF

review_text:
Very Singaporean Korean. I understand now why they're packed during lunch

Banchan was fine, kimchi esp had some funk, some body, and clearly had effort. The fried fish was great, tender, flavourful, and well brined

Rice portion and combo portion is quite big, is seems too much for 1 pax
Rice is v soft, abit too much water honestly, it's not particularly good for something cooked in an individual claypot

Their tofu soup is special. Most are bland, but theirs is cooked down so much that there's hardly much liquid, is all umami. Unlike most sundubu, this one actually works and is a joy to eat. Better than most for sure, I don't understand anyone who complains it's bland, because it's alr a lot more flavourful than most

The bulgogi used good beef, V thin and quite tender, and the Singaporean spin is using very strongly sweet sauce so it doesn't taste bland, although it's highly untraditional. Technical mistake of not brining the beef before, so it tastes a little lacking in body, but most people would not notice due to the strong sauce

Overall it's quite good and despite the price, this is the only place I'll come back to if I want to have sundubu
author: Yizhou Wu

review_text: The food was okay, but not the best Korean I've ever had. I think it's a bit pricey too. I had lunch for two and ordered a combo meal (Original Pork Soontofu + Bulgogi) and a Seafood Pancake. I wasn't a fan of the Soontofu (it was a bit bland), but the Bulgogi was delicious. I was a bit taken aback when I saw the combo meal portion was smaller than the ala carte—I thought I had scored a good deal! There weren't many freeflow side dishes, and not everything was my cup of tea. It was a weekend so the place was pretty full, but it wasn't too noisy.
author: Darwin K

review_text:
I wasn’t very impressed with the food here.
The LA rib was quite oily and fatty, and it was also overcooked and burnt. As for the side dishes, you’re required to finish all of them before getting a new set, which means there’s no option to choose the ones you prefer. I only liked the cucumber; the rest were too salty for my taste. The squid was the most surprising — I received just two tiny pieces, and the second time around, I was only given the sauce! 😅

The portion is quite small considering the price.

The tables are placed too close to each other, making it hard to have a comfortable dining experience. I couldn’t help but overhear conversations from the table next to mine

Won’t come again.
author: Sarah Lim

author: 김태민

review_text: The quality of the breakfast and dinner was superb, and it was pretty friendly but quite expensive.

review_text: Very² bad food  totally not tasty and  the food court not clean

author: Local Guide

review_text:
A fantastic McDonald’s outlet that blends fast food with nature. Located right inside West Coast Park, this branch of McDonald’s is a great rest stop after spending time walking, cycling, or enjoying the playgrounds in the park

What makes this outlet special is the mix of indoor air-conditioned seating and spacious outdoor dining areas surrounded by greenery. Sitting outside feels almost like dining in a garden — it’s common to spot birds and even squirrels wandering nearby, which adds to the relaxed park atmosphere

The restaurant itself is modern and well maintained, with plenty of seating and self-ordering kiosks. The outdoor pavilion seating is especially nice if you want to enjoy the breeze and shade from the surrounding trees

Do note that weekends can get quite crowded, as many park visitors stop by here for a drink, ice cream, or meal after their activities. Despite the crowds, the atmosphere remains lively and family-friendly
author: Loki

review_text: The place is really nice and quiet.  Located in West Coast Park!  Good place for couple to come for a quick bite
author: 一言天成

review_text:
Used to be a regular here for breakfast on my way to work, and often grabbed lunch via drive-thru to save time deciding what to eat.

Haven't been back in ages – almost half a year! But since I was nearby today, I dropped by for some takeaway bites and to use the toilet – perfect for a chilly day like today!
author: Low Bao Heng

review_text:
This place is a part of my daily life! Usually take lunch or dinner here, nearly everyday.
I am happy with Food & atmosphere.
One thing is, very often get the tables are not clean, and washroom have cleanliness issues also. But as this is a very busy outlet with lot of customers, so I think this can be ignored. Boosting the cleanliness can make this outlet one of the bests 👌
author: AbuObaida Khan (Dr. Khan)

review_text: Feedback to the Indian guy at front counter that my order number is still under “preparing” status for more than 30mins. He didn’t bother to check and just reply “too much order at the moment”. There’s only a few people waiting at the counter. After I reached home, corn and chilli source are missing. Mcspicy w cheese is without cheese. One of the worst services u get for food
author: Mark Low

review_text:
Went to dine on a Sunday morning
Very quiet place, almost empty.
Service was horrendous.
There is only one service staff to take your order, thereafter, you won’t be able to see any staffs around. The morning breakfast set stated comes with free flow of coffee. When we requested for coffee, the staff said is not eligible, as free flow is only within the breakfast period till 11am. Pls inform customer earlier if there is such a terms.
During check out, we try to give some feedback to the supervisor, however, he seem not to be bother. Then we was told weekend is actually not open for public, nobody told us when we enter. Overall, this place is not welcoming to public. And do note there will be additional 5% sur charge for non member, plus the standard 10% svc charge and 9% gst.
author: Cat Ong

review_text:
Tuesday, 29 July 2025

We were disappointed and shocked to receive our bowl of $11 Prawn Noodle Soup, containing a visibly meagre portion of noodles, 2 small pieces of prawn and 1 small piece of Pork Rib (see photo).

As long-term RSYC members, we felt rather short-changed by the meagre portions and high prices. Totally unacceptable!

Thankfully to F&B Staff Mr Kumar (Supervisor Designate). The prawn noodles were sent back to the kitchen and replaced with Beef Hor Fun.

RSYC Wharf, you could do better right? Food quality has deteriorated over the years!
author: Komson WHO

review_text:
Nice atmosphere, fine views, nice wind.

Food quality is ok. But service was very bad.
We have ordered food and it was served very late. Then the ordered sunny dip egg was missing. When asked, she said she forgot and after half of my meal is finished I got my egg.

When reminded about egg, I also requested for some chillies. She asked me what exactly I want, but it was never delivered. Very bad service.

Definitely think twice before going there. Very late delivery and missing items for such  a restaurant is not good.
author: Dr Ganesh Neelakanta Iyer

review_text:
Tried a new dish on the menu
- The Mutton Rogan Josh… sadly the Nan was not available, then they replaced with chapati.

Mutton was good and tasty …. Sadly there was  only 3 & a half small pieces of mutton (1/2 being the fat chunk)

Disappointment for $19.00 meal.  Won’t eat that no more …
author: Robert Tan MRT-atis (atis)

review_text:
The restaurant is located inside a private club but is open to the public. There is free parking from 12 pm to 2 pm (not sure if it's every day or weekdays only). The food was above average, the prices were reasonable, and the atmosphere was good, except that it is an open-air restaurant and not air-conditioned. The service was excellent.

[Edit 8 months later] The food was disappointing. The beef in the Beef Bee Hoon Wokhey was too tough to eat, and the Chengdol was not good.
author: LP Pua

review_text: One of the few ‘cooked food’ places which opens late in the west. However - so so taste. Ordered steam fish and various noodles. Standards have dropped as we recalled. Good atmosphere, decent service by the staff. But much to be desired from the quality of food.
author: Julian W

review_text: Can say no need to visit if best. Food not good. Poor service. Got fly in the food. The waiter very rude. Offer to change the veg with the fly. Complained say the fan blow the fly there.
author: Cecilia Tan

review_text: The Thai food is very tasty and flavorful, prepared by Thais. I particularly love the Pandan chicken; it’s crispy and delicious. The Pad Thai and other dishes are all cooked to an excellent standard. However, the prices are on the higher side—our total for five dishes and three drinks was
author: Empress Ker

review_text:
Ordered delivery for dinner. The Sunny Scramble Platter was very generous in portion. The Thai tofu soup had a slightly sweet note.

Disappointingly, the Thai Green Tea was half spilled on arrival.

Food portions are solid & flavours ok, but packaging & delivery handling could use improvement to ensure a better customer experience.
author: L Chan

review_text: i order from here at least once a week everything is so delicious. the green thai tea is perfectly creamy but just slightly too sweet. if you like a milky, decadent drink you would love the green thai tea. the pad thai and pad see ew are both amazing. the portions are huge too!
author: Hanyu

review_text:
Food - Wide selection to choose, spoilt for choices. Generally the food order is average, though I do find some of the portions can be improved.
Drink - Teh pandan hahaha(upside) is a good selection but ask for less sweet as it is of a cut-leg sweetness category!
Service - Online order via qrcode, pretty convenient and it takes about 20mins for food to arrive.
Payment - Cash n paynow option available
Damage - $41.90 for 5meals n 3 drinks. Receipt as attached. A bit on the pricey side.
author: Mohd Amin

review_text: The standard cheese prata was good (as expected), but the plain prata was underwhelming. We were a bit disappointed though, to be fair, it wasn’t entirely surprising since this shop specialises in cheese prata. The teh tarik was good, too. If you’re coming here, stick to the cheese prata.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text: My favourite prata shop. Clean. Friendly staff and competitive prices for the prata and teh tarik. The NUS students help create a positive atmosphere there with their giggles and laughter :)
author: Firhin Yusoff

review_text: No service recovery even after explaining and end up doing this [individually seperating TAUGEH out of the dish and not a few but a hand full] just to enjoy the food. Its lethal for my husband to consume yet they said, we cannot change. Poor empathy in customer service.
author: Nur Darme Daud

review_text: The roti prata (tried cheese and egg onion) have been quite delicious. The curry was thick and flavourful. The nasi goreng, however, was mushy and barely fried, and grossly overpriced. Teh halia was also not bad but the ginger taste could be stronger. Teh and kopi terik were OK. Staff were polite and friendly. The prices are much more expensive than the usual prata shops.
author: CK C

review_text: Service 10/10. Staff Arif was very polite and friendly and offered to take care of my school project while my friends and I ate. Food was fabulous and came very fast to our table. Pricing is very worth it with huge portions and a wide variety of cuisines too! Always a blast coming here with friends. Thanks Al Amaan!!! ❤️❤️
author: Fatimah Mazlan

review_text: A great spot for supper! Can get really crowded and packed during the 8pm-9pm timing. Their fried rice and garlic naan are really yummy! Service is quick as well
author: Charm C

review_text: Al Amaan Restaurant in Singapore offers a great variety of food, from delicious biryani burgers to many other tasty options. It’s a good spot not just for Indian cuisine, but for a mix of other dishes as well. Conveniently located near NUS and the terminal. The area also has plenty of other dining choices nearby, making it a great place to stop by.
author: Moch Faisal Karim, PhD

review_text: Was recommended this place by a friend, but it fell a bit short of expectations. The food wasn't bad, but not exceptional. I still enjoyed the meal, but a friend I went with would rate it lower compared to the ones he's been to.
author: Dylan Li

review_text:
-Chocolate prata was crispy with lots of chocolate sauce.
-Banana split was decent.
-Chicken satay was delicious, soft, tender and full of flavour.
-Beef satay was a little tough but still delicious.
-Nasi goreng was a little bland, not much fragrance.
Overall, it's affordable and food is not too bad.
author: Emily Ho

review_text: Have bn here for few times everytime after my Bt Timah hike. My favourite dish is their 'sup buntut' (ox tail soup) which is their speciality I think
author: Ray Asyara

review_text: First of all, the staff at the front desk is very welcoming even though after you are seated, he still welcomes other guests where revenue comes from, he’s technically not wrong but if he had someone else to help, he would have given a better service. On a side note, besides have one of the most on point nice Bandung, their buttermilk chicken is superb. Their Thai style Mee Goreng is super tasty except that the chicken they added is a straight up 1/10. Their Garlic naan is tasty but belong to the thinner end. If can be thick and still crispy thus I find this a miss. All in all, pretty good place to eat supper at.
author: Kong Wen Sheng

review_text: Food was nice except that the patty was grilled a bit too long. Portion is also generous. Love how the Rose Syrup Limau does not taste too sweet. It’s perfect for me. The place is clean and pleasant. For curry puffs, will recommend the potato rather than the sardines. Waiters were friendly. Overall, a pleasant dining experience here.
author: Evangeline Tan

review_text:
Lots of comfort food at its best here. They've range from Western food to indian dishes.

The dishes we ordered are served warm and taste acceptable.

With all the price rising, we are surprised that their price is still reasonable.
You'll find fried rice with a side dish from $5+ only.
Portion is generous too

It was a weekday when we visited the restaurant, and it was busy with customers, but their staff were incredibly fast.

Reasonable rate + Great service.
It's definitely a great supper place to lepakz with friends

And the cheese naan & butter chicken is a must try! Highly recommend!
author: Fadhilah Muhamad

review_text: Food portion and taste are decent. The waiter is attentive enough to explain the food selection to me as I have no idea about Indian food. The lassi is too sweet to finish more than half a cup and the waiter offer to make a less sweet version to me.
author: Jackie (CJ)

review_text:
Had a really lovely meal at this yacht club restaurant — the kind of place that makes you want to linger a little longer just to soak everything in.

The food was genuinely impressive. We started with fresh oysters that were clean, briny, and beautifully chilled — super fresh and done right. The crispy squid tentacles were a highlight: perfectly crunchy on the outside, tender inside, and dangerously addictive. For mains, the spinach ravioli with ricotta and mushroom truffle was rich, comforting, and well-balanced — earthy truffle without being overpowering, and the pasta was cooked just right.

Add to that a gorgeous waterfront view, boats gently bobbing in the background, and you’ve got a great setting for a relaxed yet special meal.

What really elevated the whole experience, though, was the service. Alan and Satesh were absolute stars — warm, attentive, genuinely friendly, and clearly proud of what they do. They struck that perfect balance of being present without hovering, and made us feel welcome from start to finish. Honestly, they deserve a raise — service like that is rare and makes a huge difference.

Great food, beautiful views, and outstanding service. Definitely a place worth coming back to. 🌊🦪✨
author: Amir Shearer

review_text:
We came here for my birthday dinner, and the view was impressive. It really looks like a getaway from the city with the yachts docked by the bay and children swimming by the pool against the sunsetting in the background.

I ordered the lamb shank and oxtail stew, both were very tender and well cooked.

Our servers Sateesh and John left a great impression on my little nephews and family members who were present. They really livened the atmosphere with their multilingualism and jokes.

The wine they recommended paired well with the lamb and oysters we ordered too. I would definitely come back here when I get the chance!
author: Valent Ong

review_text:
13 June 25
great wine pairing session.
great wine and food

26 Sept 25
Celebrated my 50th birthday in the restaurant.
- right ambience
- great food and vibe
All my guests (30) loved the place, food and wine.
Thanks Saran and the team!
author: Yvonne Tay

review_text: Had dinner at this restaurant located in the yacht club and caught a stunning sunset, such a beautiful setting to enjoy a meal. The food was satisfying and the service was decent too. A nice spot for a relaxing meal and take in the peaceful views.
author: iamjess

review_text:
The worst dining experience ever! 🤬

If I could give 0.5 stars instead of 1, I would! On Valentine’s Day of all days, they completely ruined the experience by taking 30-minute intervals to serve each dish—leaving everyone waiting endlessly. And the best part? They took a glass of water from another table, REFILLED it, and gave it to me—while giving MY glass to someone else! 🤢 How unhygienic and ridiculous is that?!

Despite having so many staff, they couldn’t serve proper food, nor could they provide even the most basic service.

Absolute worst place! 🚨 I DO NOT recommend coming here at all! Save your time, money, and sanity! 🤬
author: Winnie Ng

review_text:
THIS IS NOT A PAID REVIEW

My husband and I are VERY cerewet with our food (picky eaters), thus we have very high expectations, especially when it comes to nasi lemak. Usually, we find the rice too dry/oily or the sambal too sweet/spicy, but this.....THIS....... Perfection on a plate.

Everything from the fragrance of the rice (oooof), to the chicken (wow), to the SAMBAL (literal perfection), everything was spot on! My husband is rarely impressed, but he was already planning our next order before we even finished. Highly recommended for those who are picky about their nasi lemak!!!!
author: Natasha Iriawan

review_text: Enjoyed the traditional Nasi Lemak. The sambal is on point and the basmati rice is perfectly fragrant
author: Hong khanh Pham

review_text: The food here is INCREDIBLE (try any of the nasi lemak and the nasi pattaya - all are amazing), the nasi lemak esp just hits different from any other nasi lemak u might have had, and the owners are incredibly sweet and grounded and easy to talk to. Do come and try their food, u won't regret it!!
author: Behlul Rangwala

review_text: This have been my go to Nasi Lemak shop after class. I normally go for their Nasi Lemak chicken wings set. Love that their rice have that authentic kampung taste. Their sambal is so good. I tend to ask abit more
author: Hannah KSH

review_text: Tasty rice and one of the best nasi lemak I've eaten
author: Muhammad

restaurant_name: Pham Quyen Halal Vietnamese Cuisine @ Pasir Panjang
review_text:
Pham Quyen offers a satisfying mix of Vietnamese and local flavours, making it a great spot for a quick yet fulfilling meal. The banh mi stands out with its crusty baguette, generous fillings, and well-balanced flavours—fresh herbs, savoury protein, and just the right amount of sauce without being overwhelming. Each bite feels authentic and thoughtfully prepared.

The nasi lemak is equally enjoyable, with fragrant coconut rice that’s light and fluffy. The sambal has a pleasant kick without being overpowering, complementing the dish nicely. Portions are decent, and the overall presentation is clean and appetising.

Service is generally efficient and friendly, making it suitable for both takeaway and a casual dine-in. Pricing is reasonable for the quality and taste delivered.

A near-excellent experience overall—just a little more consistency during peak hours would make it perfect. Highly recommended for anyone craving a good banh mi or comforting nasi lemak in one place.
author: Zainal Mubarak

restaurant_name: Pham Quyen Halal Vietnamese Cuisine @ Pasir Panjang
review_text: Absolutely love this place! The owner and staff really made this food experience worthwhile. The food is super good too and flavour packed, can’t believe we almost missed this place while walking to SS… Defo recommend anyone!
author: Malvika Jamwal

restaurant_name: Pham Quyen Halal Vietnamese Cuisine @ Pasir Panjang
review_text:
Went with a group of friends and ordered before the place got crowded, but our last dish still took about 30 minutes to come out.
Other tables that ordered later got theirs first.

The food was overall alright — we had the beef pho and Thai basil chicken — but the basil chicken didn’t have much meat, which was disappointing, especially for the price.
author: Elizabeth Low

restaurant_name: Pham Quyen Halal Vietnamese Cuisine @ Pasir Panjang
review_text:
Have been a fan of their food since when I was in uni (grad a few years ago).

Their fried spring rolls are so good - especially when they’re fresh out the pan. Crispy on the outside, and piping hot on the inside. Their banh mi is quite tasty but the bread is toasted quite a bit so it’s crispy - but borders on dry. Emperor bun cha was so good! If you’d like to get a taste of the spring roll and the meats, I recommend this.

Waiting time was a bit long though… the waiter who took our order got a little confused and ended up not keying in our mains so we waited really long… Thankfully we checked - but the food still took a while to come out. Apart from that, was pretty alright.
author: skrrt skrrt

restaurant_name: Pham Quyen Halal Vietnamese Cuisine @ Pasir Panjang
review_text: Had supper here and did not regret it! The service was excellent. The fried rice was good and the nasi lemak was delicious! One of the best nasi lemak in Singapore definitely. Everything was cooked to perfection. The rice was flavorful, the chicken was crispy and full of spice, the eggs runny, and the sambal was a perfect balanced of sweet and spicy. Prices were affordable too. Would definitely come back here again to try their other dishes!
author: Shadiqin Kenway

review_text:
So food is quite decent, though not for the price.

What is amazing is that the place calls itself the ‘Italian neighbour’ but won’t allow a family to get food from their neighbours. We, a family of 6 - five of us ordered main course from Dario and a child wanted Açai from next door. Dario asked the child to sit at seperate table and eat - away from family. Talk about eating being a family time! The server was extremely nice but that can’t be said about her bosses.

And pls, stop being petty over wifi - a pizza at your place costs 30$.
author: Rajat Agarwal

review_text:
Went to Dario for some fine Romana style pizza. As differentiated from Napolitana, Romana pizza has a thinner crust.  Though still airy, it has a crispier texture. Napolitana or Neapolitan pizza is airier, a bit thicker and is more chewy.

We tried their S$19 lunch special that is on from Tuesday to Friday. It consists of Pizza or Pasta plus a drink of your choice.

Food - 5*, we had orders of 1 Aglio Olio Pasta and Lime Juice, 1 Diavola (Spicy Salami) Pizza and Apple Juice and 1 Zola (Gorgonzola) Pizza and Lemon Tea. These  were all S$19 combo. We then ordered a Home made Tiramisu  (S$3 taken with combo vs S$5 ala carte).

The pizza made by their pizzaiolo, Marco was of good quality. It had the delectable aroma and delicious taste of Italian ingredients. I've always believed in "less is more" when it comes to pizza. I want the star of the dish to really shine that's why I tremendously enjoyed both pizzas.

The Aglio Olio was also a great pasta. I appreciated the delicate nature combined with the spicy kick and freshness of the shrimps.

The Tiramisu was creamy but not at the same level as the main dishes.

Service - 5*, was attended to by Dario himself. He was a fantastic host. Marco was friendly, accommodating and explained his pizza style. Sandhya, our server was gracious and efficient.

Atmosphere - 4*, fine artisanal spot
author: Chito Mauleon

review_text:
Located at the end of "NUS supper row". It's a proper Italian joint. However, very small space and most tables were located outside shop space (al fresco style).

Ordered a variety of dishes. Very nice. Love the thin crust pizza dough. Ravioli is nice. So is their chef special pasta.

Minus 1 star for noisy street traffic if sat outside.
author: Jimmy Liaw

review_text:
Landed here out of accident..
Service was good - the waiters were very cheerful and friendly, and the place had decent veg options. Tastewise a 4. Some items were really good and some could have been better.
We ordered Bruscettine which was basically Bruschetta with tomato. Pretty decent.
We chose Pasta - so went with a Gnocchi and a Red Sauce Sphagetti. Gnocchi was out of the world. I can't praise it enough. My wife felt bad about ordering the Sphagetti.. Gnocchi was that good.
The other pasta they got Penne by mistake. We didn't want to make a fuss so we just went with it. Penne was very average. Pasta quantity looked less but it was very filling..
I added a Foccacina to go with the pasta and that was a bit underwhelming. Felt like a crispy pizza while I'd expected Foccacia bread..
Dessert - we ordered Pistachio gelato and I have to tell you it was sinful. Easily puts some of the very good dessert places to shame !! I'd come here again just for the Gelato.
author: Sairam Subramanian

review_text:
Had a prosciutto and funghi pizza and it was quickly served and delicious. It's a rather thin and crispy dough, which I like. Price was reasonable (25 SGD incl tax/service).

The service of the two ladies was functional, but there seems to have been a misunderstanding - one of them kindly asked if I wanted a water while I was waiting for my takeaway pizza. I said "oh, yes, thanks", but in the end it seems she took it for a "no, thanks".

Outside there's a big road which is frequented by trucks, so this is not necessarily the place for a quiet meal with your date.
The Italian music was nice and not too loud
author: Jan H.

review_text: Had a fantastic meal here! The service was excellent—very attentive and friendly. The crispy pork (or duck) was delicious, perfectly cooked and full of flavor. Plus, the restaurant was spotlessly clean. Highly recommend!
author: 许绣荧

review_text: Place was very clean, spacious and well ventilated. Good place to chill with family and friends. Food was amazing!! Taste hits the spot everytime. From western to indian food, from seafood to malay dishes- all cooked right. Does justice to every dish. Highky recommend. Keep coming back, even though we stay far away. Staff Md Sahed (service staff) is polite and super helpful. Makes good recommendations. Very hardworking. We saw him during our dinner the day before and he was working again in the morning at 8am. Salute!!!
author: Aishah Binte Mohammed Sim

review_text:
Stayed around NUS for more than a month, I like Nur Fayidha the most and almost have lunch or dinner here everyday.
The environment is bright and clean.
Staffs are all nice and friendly.
They serve a wide variety of food, and everything tastes good. Too many to recommend, so I just show the pictures.
Prices are very reasonable.
I would be happy to come back and eat here again if I visit Singapore.
author: Ming Wei

review_text:
The egg and plain pratas are buttery. The milk tea is thick and milky and frothy. The chicken in the biryani is tender and flavorful. The nasi goreng tastes good.

The chicken curry ($5) is nice 👍

They use good spices and good recipes.

Good quality food.
author: T

review_text: Ordered the chicken biryani based on the many positive reviews, but it was a big disappointment. The chicken was extremely dry and bland, with hardly any flavour. What made it worse was realizing that the rice seemed to be taken from the mutton biryani — the mutton smell from the gravy was very obvious. This is a major turn-off, especially for someone who does not eat or like mutton. Overall, the experience did not match the reviews at all
author: Prash Akash

review_text: I ordered tuna mayo sandwich on November 2024. It was nice and tasty! I got a cup of coffee as a complementary drink as well. You need to try this, especially if you stay at Ibis hotel or other places nearby.
author: Jony Eko Yulianto

review_text: Prices are pretty good for their drinks. The pita is made on the spot so the wait can be a little longer. Perfect for today's cloudy day. Can't wait to try the other flavours. No gst! Pita is whole grain
author: rebekah lee

review_text:
A pretty decent place for Chinese cuisine as it offers both Taiwanese and Chinese cuisine.
Most of the items on the menu are more towards spicy so do take note for people who can't take spicy.
Price are pretty reasonable and it do have have happy hour beer promotion as well.
author: Koh Jia Wei

review_text:
I had a really enjoyable meal at Formosa Delights. The food was comforting and flavorful. The handmade noodles had a great chewy texture. Portions were generous. A good place to gather with friends.
Overall, a solid spot for Taiwanese/China comfort food.
author: Grace Ng

review_text: This is my go-to place when I couldn’t think of any place to go for food. Love the small bites and cold dishes. The staffs are very efficient and friendly and the restaurant has a cosy atmosphere that always makes me feel comfortable and at ease while I enjoy my  glass of beer with my hubby.
author: Jeslyn Teo

review_text: Returning to this restaurant after ten years, I was initially impressed by the sleek renovations and enticing new beers on tap. Unfortunately, my excitement quickly faded as the food quality had noticeably declined, despite the prices nearly doubling. The braised pork rice, once a signature dish, was disappointingly soggy and lacked its signature umami depth. The mapo tofu, while passable, failed to leave an impression. Considering the current quality, the food feels significantly overpriced, and I wouldn't recommend it. To compound the issue, the service staff appeared indifferent and created an unwelcoming atmosphere.
author: Terry Ding

review_text:
Went there for the first time last night to have dinner. It was a wonderful experience of culinary delight, even though my wife felt the dishes were a little too oily.

Service was good. We didn't have to wait too long.

Alhough the restaurant has a cosy feel with nice mood lightings, it was very noisy. Quite typical of Chinese restaurants in Singapore. People tend to speak loudly.

Located quite near the National University of Singapore. Public carpark is across the road.
author: Richard Tan

review_text:
I get why this place is famous as a meeting place for NUS students, particularly for suppers. Airy semi-outdoor place, relatively affordable and filling meals (some set menus are priced at around $4) and opens well into the early hours.

Went there before the dinner crowd came over and ordered the boneless teriyaki nasi lemak set, with veggie achar as side. The sambal was absolutely spot on for a nasi lemak - not too sweet, with enough hot spicy punchiness. The teriyaki chicken was soft and well-marinated. Will come back for dinner to try their other sets if I'm in the area.
author: lontongstroong

review_text: The food is really good! the sambal was sweet and spicy. the fried chicken, fish fillet, fried prawn was so crispy. the egg yolk was also oozing on the rice. the only downside is the service is really slow. i went in the morning, only one aunty working, the aunty works a little bit slower, taking orders one by one slowly. the place was a little too hot. luckily i went in the morning before the sun rise and got to sit outside with some cool wind.
author: Chloe Lim

review_text: Came for a late weekend supper and was quite surprise with the variety of sides and add ons that they have. The sambal had a very nice kick, but fried chicken was a tad too salty that night. Portions are good, can even share a plate for 2 people. Will come again to try new combinations next time.
author: khrhms

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $9) @ Fong Seng Nasi Lemak.
.
Established in June 1983, this stall caters primarily to hungry university students and port workers, the result of which means large and generous portions at affordable wallet-friendly prices, coupled with long operating hours through most of the day and night. The place isn't a culinary bastion, but it is a place for fast, cheap, and good eats.
.
The sticky and moist white rice carries a mild fragrance of coconut cream, a touch of grainy earthy floral sweet flavour. The achar / Peranakan pickled salad is crunchy and juicy with bright vegetal sour sweet spice flavour, the deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies is crisp and crunchy with fishy savoury salty flavour, and the fried chicken egg with runny yolk is wobbly and soft with eggy sweet savoury flavour.
.
The sotong / squid balls are springy bouncy with savoury sweet flavour, the battered crab stick surimi is tender and crisp with mild sweet savoury briny salty flavour, and the battered chicken wing is tender though not as crisp as I'd hoped yet carrying meaty sweet savoury flavour. Their grainy sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste is mild with sweet savoury salty spice flavour.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text: Lured by reviews and hearsay, I'm usually pretty skeptical about these so called famous brands that have multiple outlets everywhere. So imagine when we rolled up to this rather out of the way locale and discover a snaking queues. Mind you these won't even students from NUS, these were corporate types perspiring in their long sleeves - thank goodness we were in causal wear due to an outside appointment. 30min queue aside, it just only raised expectations even higher since whatever is making these office types brave scorching weather must be worth it right? Well, to be fair the Nasi Lemak ain't too shabby. My requirements for awesomeness has to be the divine trinity of fragrant coconut rice, fiery sambal and lip smacking hot, crisp and juicy chicken wings. Get all these right and your will immediately get a 4 stars. For Fong Seng its nothing mind blowing, everything was done to above average levels. The sambal had heat and wasn't overtly sweet, the chicken wings were hot and crisp, though you can its frozen, the meat on the bone usually retains a purple hue and the rice was somewhat fragrant. I also ordered otah which was forgettable, sotong ball also passable and a side of long beans that were not bad. I have had better but if I dont want to compare with the best, the dish here with its condiments is decent, however to stand in the scorching sun just to eat this i probably will only come here pass lunch hour or if I ever find myself at West Coast with an insane Nasi Lemak craving.
author: Jechtto

review_text:
Would say that this is a place to head to if you have a big family looking for affordable options that can feed big appetites!

The portions were generous, even the rice bowls would come overflowing with rice! The dishes were all well priced given that the quantity of meat in every dish is really big, just look at the photos of the dishes! Compared to most tze char places out there, they definitely do not skim on the servings here!

Also, each dish was flavourful with a lot of wok hey taste. However, just note that delicious food tend to be more on the unhealthy side so I would say the flavours also come from the generous amount of oil. Regardless, if you’re rating high on the taste side, this place definitely does a great job 👏

Our recommended dishes here include the beef (beef slices are always soooo tender), chicken in kungpao sauce, tomato egg and the tofu (generous servings of spinach under the tofu not pictured).

Service is generally ok, more of a casual dining style. The servers are rather attentive so not to worry about wanting to add on more orders. Drinks are self service which was quite interesting and fuss free.

All in all, love this place!

Note: dine in earlier before the peak dinner period. Tend to be filled with many students and parking may be further out from the restaurant
author: Shermaine Tan

review_text: Good food, decent price. Yes, there isn’t much of a service but is that good enough reason to rate them 1 star? I used to patronise them often when I stayed in the west but stopped after moving away. I had the opportunity to drop by today as I was in the vicinity and am glad they maintained their food standards. I’m appalled by the recent 1 star reviews thus it nudged me to drop this review.
author: Yan C

review_text:
Worst place to eat ever. Been there multiple times to give them chance but no. Everytime they will mess up the order, and then gaslight you to tell you that’s correct. Once I ordered eefu noodles, and they gave me ee-mian (which is entirely different) and insisted.

Another time they added 2 drinks to my order and forced me to pay for it.

Other times they will add random skewers and insist on us paying as well. Won’t let you leave if you don’t pay.

Scammers. The food isn’t even that great.

In my history of ratings, I hardly ever give out less than 4 stars, let alone 1. But this place deserves 1 star. Would give zero if I can.
author: Ernest Yee

review_text: Located along Clementi Road towards west coast highway, this restaurant was highly visible and a public car park was nearby for those who drive. The food were priced competitively and a reasonably big place with round tables. Ordered some cooked food, skewers and noodles. The beef kway teow was nice with wok taste. Overall nice home cooked food and will be back again.
author: Blue Angel

review_text:
Decent Chinese food. Savoury skewers, tasty tomato egg soup, and eefu noodles drenched in sauce.

Rather crowded at night. Service isn’t the main concern here - but the value for money is pretty good.
author: Pun Punyasavatsut

review_text:
So I recently checked out The Lazy Lizard in Pasir Panjang and honestly? Straight bussin. I'm surprised more people aren't talking about this place. The prices won't break the bank and the service was really good throughout.
I went a bit overboard and ordered the pork rack, messy burger, and lazy burger. No regrets though.
Can we talk about the fries for a second? Both the straight-cut and curly fries were on point – crispy, well-seasoned, just perfect. And the mashed potatoes? Buttery goodness with just the right amount of truffle oil. Not too much that it overwhelms everything, you know?
But okay, the pork ribs. THE PORK RIBS. I need to emphasize this because they were absolutely insane. So tender they literally fell off the bone, super juicy – I'm pretty sure they sous vide these for like 32 hours or something because the texture was unreal. Honestly, they need to advertise these more because this dish alone is worth the trip.
The burgers were also really solid. I mean, they could've asked how I wanted my beef patty cooked, but even without that, both burgers exceeded what I expected. Good quality ingredients, and that melted cheese with bacon? Chef's kiss. Absolutely bomb.
If you're around Pasir Panjang, seriously give this place a shot. It's one of those low-key spots that really delivers. Just make sure you order the pork ribs fr fr no cap fax.
author: Jonathan is a good boy

review_text:
Lovely place! Staff are very friendly and food is delicious.
The ambiance is suitable for chill drinks as well!
author: Qian Wen

review_text: If you’re looking for a cozy and atmospheric place to enjoy a hearty meal, this is it! I couldn’t find a good restaurant near NUS before, but now I’ve found one. The chicken in the chicken curry is perfectly crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, delicious! I left feeling full and satisfied. The ice cream was beautifully presented and tasted great too. I’ll definitely be coming back!
author: 이은미

review_text: First time here, place was cosy and service was good. Food was good and nice portions. Haven't try the bar yet. Definitely will be back.
author: MrIcegiant

review_text: I like the Japanese rice bowl and fresh oysters. Pineapple juice good.
author: Desmond Tay

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Highly Recommended Mookata Experience!
I had an amazing dining experience at Le West Den Mookata. The food quality was excellent, and everything tasted fresh and flavourful. The marinated meats were well-seasoned, tender, and grilled perfectly, while the soup was rich and comforting.
There’s a wide variety of choices, from juicy pork and chicken to fresh seafood and vegetables, so it’s great for sharing with friends or family. Portions are generous and definitely worth the price.
The environment was clean and comfortable, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole experience even better. Overall, it’s a great place for a satisfying mookata meal. I will definitely come back again! 👍
author: Olivia Tong

review_text:
I had a wonderful experience at Ah Bear Mookata & Le West Den Prawning. The environment was clean, spacious, and very comfortable, creating a relaxing atmosphere whether you are dining with friends, family, or enjoying a casual night out. The prawning area was well-maintained and organized, making the whole experience smooth and enjoyable.

The food quality was outstanding, with fresh ingredients and high preparation standards. The marinated meats were flavourful, tender, and grilled perfectly, while the soup base was rich and satisfying. There was a great variety of selections, including fresh seafood, meats, and vegetables, ensuring there is something for everyone. Portions were generous and definitely worth the price.

What impressed me most was the excellent service. The staff were friendly, attentive, and always ready to assist, making the entire visit even more pleasant. Their professionalism and warm hospitality truly enhanced the experience.

Overall, Ah Bear Mookata & Le West Den Prawning is a fantastic place for good food, fun activities, and great service. Highly recommended, and I will definitely visit again! 👍
author: Winnie Ng

review_text:
I recently visited Le West Den and had an absolutely fantastic time! This hidden gem in Singapore offers a unique combo of Mookata and prawning, making it perfect for a fun outing with friends or family.
The Mookata was spot on – fresh ingredients, flavorful marinades, and that perfect char from the grill. We grilled up a storm with juicy meats, seafood, and veggies, all washed down with their tasty dipping sauces. The food quality was top-notch, and portions were generous without breaking the bank.
But the real highlight was the prawning experience! It's such a relaxing and exciting activity – we spent hours hooking fresh prawns from the ponds. Catching our own prawns and grilling them fresh added that extra thrill to the meal.
Service was impeccable too; the team was friendly, attentive, and quick to help, even during a busy evening. The vibe is casual and welcoming, with clean facilities and a great atmosphere.
Highly recommend Le West Den for anyone looking for delicious food and a memorable adventure. I'll definitely be back soon! 5 stars!
author: Samson Chew

review_text:
Had a great time here! Went for their prawning and ah bear mookata. We managed to catch prawns even though we are not a pro. The boss was very welcoming and hosted us really well. The vibes were amazing and the whole experience was enjoyable from start to finish.
My friends and I never once disappointed when we are there .
Will definitely come back again!
Thank you for the good hosting 🙏
author: Amanda Lim

review_text:
Le West Den is a great all-in-one hangout spot that works especially well for families and groups.

The prawning experience is enjoyable and well set up. The place is clearly kids-friendly, with many families around, and the overall atmosphere feels relaxed and welcoming. The prawns are decent-sized, which makes the experience satisfying and worth the time, especially when you finally land a good catch.

One thing that really stands out is how integrated everything is. While prawning, you can easily take a break and head over to the mookata area for dinner if hunger kicks in, or chill at the KTV bar. It makes the whole experience feel flexible and social, perfect for groups where people want to do different things without splitting up.

The space is well cooled, which is a big plus in Singapore’s heat. You can hang out comfortably without feeling stuffy or drained, even on a hot day. The environment is spacious, decently maintained, and pleasant to spend a long time in.

The owner is friendly and approachable, adding to the overall good vibes of the place. It feels like somewhere people genuinely enjoy running, not just another business trying to rush customers through.

Overall, Le West Den is a solid choice if you’re looking for a place to prawn, eat, sing, and relax all in one location. Great for family outings, casual gatherings, and group hangouts where everyone can find something to enjoy.

Highly recommended for a chill, no-pressure experience.
author: Weng Sum “Wayne” Wong

review_text:
The worst ever, low quality and un-fresh food

The meat is hard. The vege is not fresh and turned to other colour only after a few days even I stored in my cold fridge

Delivered on Monday, I put in fridge and this is what it looks like on Thursday
author: Vu Tran

review_text: I’ve been pleasantly surprised with the quality, variety & taste of the food! Starting on with Eat Fit freshly prepared food packed with healthy & nutritious ingredients have made my life much easier. I no longer have to think about what O am going to eat!
author: happy lim

review_text:
Not sure why they rejected my weekly order request. I find that the reason that they do not know whether the Government may issue new regulations / lockdown is not justifiable.

In summary, rude and insincere customEr service.
author: Lucas Tan

review_text: Didn't aspect healthy meal can be such tasty & yummy 😋. Portion just right and custom made to my order. Will definitely help me lost weight if I committed as regular customer 😊
author: Jennifer Wong

review_text: Nice dinner, taste just right, balanced & yummy meal. Will recommend to my friends for the pre order and custom make my favourite flavour too.
author: maurene tan

review_text: New F&B enclave in the quiet science park area. Have a few interesting new F&B concepts that serves affordable and value for money meals.
author: Foo Sze Ming

review_text: Nothing spectacular. There are a cafeteria Chilli Api, Starbucks and a vegetarian. The place is mostly filled with office workers around the area.
author: Thomas Lew

review_text: Ate at Chili API. Food is decent but price is a little on the high side ..
author: JL

review_text: Closed on weekends, wasted trip. And on another occasion the only open restaurant was having a private function.
author: Duane Bong

review_text: A place that make heart warming at night
author: Catherine Lam

review_text:
Build your own pasta/rice/salad; it has nothing really special.

The ingredients are limited - not all the main proteins listed are available, then choose 4 out of 9 toppings. The options can get quite odd to go with pasta like peanuts, cucumber, corn, and boiled eggs. The serving size can be rather small.

The place is clean, spacious, and comfortable.

Vegetarian option available.
author: Andy Andy

review_text: Impatient elderly service staff. Overpriced and horror tasting pre-packed bento. Lunch can only be served strictly from 11am (not even a second earlier!) with the staff standing around watching the clock on their handphone to strike 11am before they can proceed to take order. A really strange practice.
author: M C

review_text:
Every single staff was rude and impatient even when there are not much customers they were screaming at their customers just because they don’t understand english.

If you are unhappy with your job and unwilling to serve customers then quit? Very insincere staffs. Also the food sucks, it made me sick i guess they do not practice food hygiene properly.

Please don’t waste your time and money here only to be served with disrespect and food that only makes you get food poisoning lol.
author: Mel Elissa

review_text:
Bad service, food tasted disgusting and drinks are below subpar. We hope u will close down and open kopitiam.

Future customers, we hope you are okay with soggy waffles which takes 10-12mins, tasteless pasta, inconsistent coffee (could be lukewarm/taste/look weird). If you’re not then please don’t waste a minute or a single penny here.
author: K Emika

review_text: Food is good while the options are limited but worst part is the service there is so bad . I understand if they are impatient in peak hours like lunch time . I also understand that they are mad at some discipline people there (esp who slam the door really loud or smth) . But that time they are still impatient and very rude even in there’s no people or few people there . They made unnecessary comments about me in ordering process . Some staffs are okay but more experienced staffs are really impatient and rude .Only been few times but will try to avoid going there as much as possible .
author: Jsgood ami

review_text: The food here is good, in a very nice and cool ambience in a serene environment. Sat outdoors and there’s a live band singing great songs from the 80s. Ordered the beef sirloin steak and seafood pasta, both tastes good and serving size is decent. Paired with great beer on tap.
author: WS Tan

review_text:
Came because I had Grabfood-ed their chicken wings and was really impressed. Both the salted egg chicken wings and chili crab chicken wings were super impressive tender and fall off the bone!

At the restaurant, tried their dry aged ribeye which was slightly on the dry side but paired with a really good beef jus and blue pea seasoning salt. Their baby pork ribs were juicy and also fall off the bone. This time we also tried their sesame yuzu chicken wings which were my parents favourite! My mum said that based on the aglio olio, can tell that the rest of the food will be great, and she was not wrong!!

Really impressed and look forward to going again :) will bring some friends over for drinks soon
author: Reuven Cheng

review_text:
Got to know this place through Level Ground.
Nice ambience with outdoor live band. Wasn’t too crowded on a Friday night. Food was good and reasonably priced. Prompt and attentive service.

Wagyu rib on hot stone. Oil fats will splatter so grill with caution. But meat was good. Good for 4 pax.
Duck and mango pizza. Taste good together. Not a bad combination.
Salted egg chicken wing was well coated yet not too salty.
Truffle fries was crispy and not greasy unlike other places drenching it in truffle oil.
author: Tan Jun Yang

review_text:
Food was good! Ribs were great and perfectly cooked. Fish & chips was good and also generous.
Small improvements can be made. I ordered a full rack but received a half. I could hear most of the convo between the wait staff and the kitchen about it. They served the next half rack in the end, and I felt they were generous about it because it came with all the sides as well - I was just expecting a plain plate of an extra half rack. We got the cheese fries. The blanket of cheese was unexpected, appearance wise but it was yummy nonetheless. Drinks were good. Maybe something to note is mosquitoes? I got 3 mosquito bites on my legs while there, indoors. Overall a good experience.
author: S. K.

review_text: Excellent food! The baby back ribs were very tender and tasty, salted egg chicken wings were perfect and the seafood platter was good for 2! The charcoal batter was very unique and with the right amount of crisp! We will be back :)
author: Rachel Lim

review_text:
Had lunch on a quiet Sunday at Chilli Padi Tok Panjang — the space is large, peaceful, and almost empty at midday, making it an easy, comfortable choice for families and groups. The buffet is good value for money, with a decent spread and well-prepared dishes.

Chilli Padi Tok Panjang celebrates Peranakan heritage through the traditional tok panjang feast — the iconic long-table communal dining experience. The buffet highlights classics like Ayam Buah Keluak, Babi Pongteh, Chap Chye, and Sambal Udang, all prepared with time-honoured rempahs and traditional methods that bring out the depth and richness of true Nyonya flavours.

A calm, family-friendly spot with hearty Peranakan staples and plenty of room to dine unhurried — a lovely choice for a relaxed weekend meal.
author: C

review_text:
was too hungry to take pictures of the buffet spread, but trust me this is gooood

at $40 per adult, this is such a steal! i like that u won't feel compelled to overeat since the price tag is not exorbitant

cheap price notwithstanding the food is actually really good. we enjoyed the mee siam, kueh pie tie, prawns (super fresh). there is also a decent range of other food - laksa, ayam buah keluak, babi ponteh, chap chye, fried chicken wings. even the dessert assortment was sufficient - nyonya kueh (kueh dardar was v moist), jelly, daohuey, pulat hitam and cut fruit

the presentation / decor / crockery is all very no frills. but who cares amirite as long as the food is yummy
author: Nic

review_text: The spread isn’t huge, but the flavours are authentic, especially the ayam buah keluak and chap chye. kueh kueh are delicious. Cozy vibe and friendly service. Worth a visit if you’re craving Peranakan comfort food.
author: Chomeh Alex

review_text: Probably won’t come back again. Pricey buffet of 28+++ don’t have a strong nyongya flavor. Laksa and mee siam is watery. Only beef redang is ok. The pastries can be improved, so far the coconut green long one is nice. Because there isn’t much crowd, food turnover is a problem. Some fried chicken left on the table become rough and cold, hard to eat so u must wait for the next batch when they top up for a better chicken option. Coffee is fine, tea is ok too. Oh ya if u are not having buffet with your friends, you have to sit on another table. No trust haha. They only give you one complementary bowl of big prawn and fried fish cubes. Probably to cut cost. Overall experience feels like eating in a nygonya cafe with a lot of decorations and music but after awhile, the variety of food feels about there. Btw they start chasing people away at 2.30pm!
author: FROSTY

review_text:
Ordered set lunch and expected separate serving of items but came on a plate like economy rice.. Soup was yummy and pulut dessert was great. Service was awesome. Good food with fair portion
but presentation can be better or show the same in the menu..
author: Shanti Arasan

review_text: We came here for our reunion meal and loved that it was very quiet and not overcrowded. Most of the food we ordered was average, and what you would expect from a tze char place. We made the mistake of ordering the shark's fin soup - the texture of the shark's fin was more like vermicelli (tang hoon), and most definitely fake. It was a disappointing experience. Service was ok until the server tried to clear my plate when I hadn't finished eating. Will not be making a return visit.
author: G Z

review_text:
Diamond Kitchen isn’t new in the SG F&B scene. Having patronized their Marine Parade branch, I know the standard of their food wouldn’t go too wrong. We came to the Science Park branch as it’s nearer to home to celebrate my dad’s birthday and am glad he loved the food.

We ordered everything in medium size and while portion was decent, strong suggestion if you have more than 10 pax to go with the large instead.

Let’s see what I ordered:
1. Champagne Pork Ribs 4.5 / 5
2. Three Eggs Chinese Spinach 4 / 5
3. Pumpkin Bean Curd 4.5 / 5
4. Superior Chicken Soup 3.5 / 5 (nice but the mushroom used causes the soup to have a strong after taste)
5. Salted Egg Sotong 4 / 5
6. Spicy Garlic La La 3.5 / 5 (Not as spicy as I expected)
7. Ginger Spring Onion Pork 4 / 5
8. Braised Pork with Bun 4.5 / 5

Added a 寿桃包 as last item.

Overall, taste is good and price average ard $32 per pax.

Only thing is the sitting arrangement. Their table are sized based on 10 pax; anything more than that and you are likely to be very cramp. This is even when I have two primary schooler amongst my table. Imagine 12 full size adults and you would be in a “tight spot”.
author: Calvin Lee

review_text:
Had reunion dinner here. The place is very comfortable and spacious, floor to ceiling glass house, so lots of natural daylight.

The staff were very attentive, food was good. Making reservation was easy and straightforward. Highly recommended especially if you have a large group to cater.

We also won a lucky draw from the cny dinner promotion. Thanks!
author: Christina Teng

review_text: The restaurant was not crowded on a weekday night. Went there with some friends due to a crab promotion. The black pepper crab tasted decent but the crabs were a tad small making the eating a little tedious. The other dishes such as deep fried baby squid, herbal chicken and claypot chicken with salted fish were satisfactory. Good and attentive service
author: CK Cheong

review_text:
The restaurant has high ceilings and full-length windows, creating a spacious and airy ambiance filled with natural light that enhances the dining experience and stimulates the appetite.

The food is well-prepared and delicious, complemented by attentive service. I particularly enjoyed the steamed fish — fresh and tender. The fried chicken mid-wings were another tasty dish, with crispy skin and juicy meat.

Overall, it was an enjoyable meal in a pleasant setting.
author: J Seng

restaurant_name: Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe - NUH Medical Centre
review_text:
Went here for dinner and shared a few dishes.
Vermicelli claypot with pork ribs was very nice. Quite a big amount (tbf not cheap either) of both noodles and meat. It was well seasoned and the meat was juicy and tender.
Also had a few dim sum. Char siew bun was nice but tasted a bit.. normal iyk. Roasted duck bun was nice and the glutinous rice was p good too. Overall good spot for dinner.
author: L

restaurant_name: Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe - NUH Medical Centre
review_text:
We order vegi and soya chicken everything was good before the vegi. It is old and difficult to bite.
Upon sharing this Info to the Philippine staff, she just ask what you wan? To cancel or to redo? I ask her to check for those who pick the vegi. And she say it's supplied to them (waaa what a quick and fluent reply.)!!!! Was it a common answer to the common feedback by many customer ?,  also mean they have no control over it and a redo dish will end up to be the same !After deciding, We cancel this dish and quickly finish our lunch with great disappointment.  How can you run a restaurant allowing supplier just to send in the ingredient without checking and inspection. Wish you guys have a long business
author: Mike Ang

restaurant_name: Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe - NUH Medical Centre
review_text:
I visited Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe at NUH and ordered the Western Breakfast Set, which came with butter toast, macaroni soup with luncheon meat and fried egg, along with a cup of Teh C. It was a comforting and hearty option, especially for a casual cafe inside a hospital setting.

The butter toast was simple yet satisfying, crispy on the outside and soft inside, with just enough butter to give that nostalgic Hong Kong cha chaan teng flavour. The macaroni soup was light and homely, not overly salty, with slices of luncheon meat and a fried egg that made it feel like a classic Hong Kong breakfast staple. It’s the kind of dish that warms you up without being too heavy.

The Teh C was smooth and well-balanced, neither too sweet nor too bitter, and paired nicely with the meal. Service was quick and efficient, which I appreciated given the hospital crowd and busy lunchtime atmosphere.

Overall, while it may not be gourmet dining, Xin Wang delivers exactly what you expect: affordable, nostalgic comfort food with a Hong Kong café vibe. It’s a convenient spot to grab a satisfying meal if you’re around NUH.

——

Came again & ordered my favourite stir fried dou Miao and nissin noodle with luncheon meat 😍
author: Yvonne Chou

restaurant_name: Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe - NUH Medical Centre
review_text: The food here is really good and on a weekend, its not really crowded. I suppose thats because its in a hospital. But that said, only issue I felt was that because it was not too crowded, the number of staff to guests werent great. But still, I enjoyed the food especially the rice with curry chicken and coffee was pretty good too.
author: Calvin Work

restaurant_name: Xin Wang Hong Kong Cafe - NUH Medical Centre
review_text: The only Chinese restaurant in NUH. Only some dishes were tasty eg curry rice, beef stew, stir fried veg. The rest were below par. Sometimes the staff were friendly but other times they could be quite impatient.
author: Flying Molen

review_text: Nice Thai food.  Slightly pricy in my opinion.
author: Michelle Sim

review_text: Well, it is ok-ish, but quality of the food is really so so, for the price...
author: Jon Tan

review_text: Food is just so-so.
author: Marco Carlos

review_text: Very very bad experience. Nvr before went to a western food place and had to wait 45 mins just for 1 packet of french fries. review_text:
Le White Bar has easily become my go-to spot since January, and honestly, it deserves the love.

First off, the space. This place gets it. Spacious seating, proper table layout, and you don’t have to contort your body or apologize to strangers just to walk past. After long workdays, that alone already feels like a luxury.

The karaoke system deserves a special mention. The audio quality is genuinely top-notch, not the usual distorted, echo-heavy setup you endure for the sake of fun. They also have private rooms for karaoke and events, which makes it perfect whether you’re there with friends, family, or hosting a small gathering. Bonus points for being kids-friendly, which is surprisingly hard to find in places that also cater well to adults.

Now, the food. Extensive menu, solid execution. My personal favorite so far is the German sausages with fries. The fries are crispy on the outside, fluffy inside, and the sausages are properly juicy and satisfying. This is the kind of comfort food you actually look forward to when winding down after work, not just something to snack on while drinking.

The atmosphere is what really seals it. Super chill, relaxed, and welcoming. The owner and staff are friendly without being intrusive, and even the other guests are genuinely pleasant. It feels like one of those rare places where everyone just… behaves like decent humans.

For entertainment, they’ve got a pool table and darts, which adds to the laid-back, hangout-friendly vibe. And if that wasn’t enough, there’s a waffle, ice cream, and coffee shop next door, and they’re cool with you bringing those treats into the bar. That level of flexibility is underrated and appreciated.

Overall, Le White Bar strikes a rare balance: good food, great sound system, comfortable space, friendly people, and zero pressure. It’s become my new favorite place to unwind, and I’ll definitely keep coming back.

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a genuinely chill spot in the Pasir Panjang area.

review_text:

After prawning, we tried the mookata. The grill and soup combo is great for sharing, and the food portions are decent. Meats were fresh, and the soup base added a nice flavour when grilling. It’s more about the experience than fine dining, but it hits the spot after a long prawning session.

Overall, nice chill-out place for groups, with food, drinks, and an activity all in one location. Good for casual gatherings, birthdays, or just unwinding after work. Would come back again.
