review_text:
Now nestled along Pasir Panjang Road since late 2025, Bacino Trattoria continues to embody heartfelt Piedmontese hospitality under the stewardship of Francesco Sottile and his partner Evelyn. Hailing from Turin, Francesco brings with him the soul of northern Italy — a passionate chef-entrepreneur whose menu celebrates rustic traditions through handmade pastas, wood-fired pizzas, and slow-simmered ragù crafted from premium ingredients that echo the flavours of his homeland.

The garlic focaccia deserves special mention — beautifully blistered from the oven, its crust delicately crisp while the crumb remains airy and perfumed with sweet, roasted garlic. It is dangerously addictive. The penne arrabbiata arrives perfectly al dente, coated in a vibrant, punchy tomato sauce with just the right chilli heat — simple, honest, and deeply satisfying. Equally memorable is the grilled Iberico pork, succulent and richly marbled, kissed by flame to achieve a smoky caramelised edge while remaining tender within.

Evelyn’s warm, attentive service completes the experience, making diners feel instantly at home. With an approachable wine list thoughtfully curated by Francesco, Bacino feels both intimate and authentic. I must return soon for their Italy-certified, legit Carbonara — if the rest of the meal is any indication, it will be the real deal.
author: Roger Yuen

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Another Wonderful Evening at Bacino Italian

This was our second visit to Bacino Italian, this time bringing a friend who was visiting from Hong Kong — and once again, the experience was exceptional.

We were warmly welcomed by Francesco the moment we arrived. The restaurant was full, but they made us comfortable outside while preparing a table indoors. Both servers, Rehingie (hope I got her name & spelling right) and Angeline, were incredibly attentive and made us feel well taken care of throughout the evening.

We ordered the Polpette Sugo (meatballs), Parmigiana di Melanzane (Eggplants with cheese & tomato sauce), Linguine Vongole, and Seafood Spaghetti — every dish was delicious and full of flavour. Our friend had the Diavola pizza and absolutely loved it, commenting on how crispy and tasty it was.

To end the night, the owners surprised us by placing two bottles of Grappa and a huge bottle of Limoncello at our table for us to help ourselves — such a generous and thoughtful touch. Truly above and beyond hospitality.

We’re so glad to have Bacino as our new neighbourhood favourite. We will definitely be back to try the rest of the menu😋😍

review_text: The food was divine. Me and my brother ordered the homemade bread, seafood linguine vongole, carbonara, half a buratta pizza and tiramisu for dessert. For a starter, homemade bread was crispy and fresh and more than enough for 2 pax. Whether paired with vinaigrette and olive oil, butter or plain, tastes delicious. Definitely ask for the butter. Top notch quality and tastes incredible with the bread. Next, for mains, we tried the pastas. Carbonara is more on the saltier side because of the pork cheek and the type of cheese used. Tbh, it was a bit too salty for me but very rich and flavoursome so I still enjoyed it haha. As for my brother’s main, the vongole was above average. However, it was not flavoursome enough, suggesting that more white wine and garlic could have been added to improve it. Pizza-wise, YOU ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO ORDER THE BURATTA PIZZA. It was. Splendid. My brother and I agreed that it was one of the best pizza we have ever had in our lives 😂 (considering we have tried many italian restaurants in singapore) The crust had the perfect texture combination. It was so freaking airy, fluffy, soft and moist on the inside, yet crispy on the outside. Burrata tasted milky and smooth, blending well with their use of fresh pizza toppings. Overall, really authentic pizza u can’t find anywhere else. Would 100% come back just for the pizza honestly. Lastly, for dessert, tiramisu is a must. So creamy and coffee-rich. Not too sweet, perfect for coffee lovers. All in all, the pizzas and desserts really stole the show. Really enjoyed the meal and very worth the money. It was $96 for the two of us.
author: alyssa kwok

review_text:
Been vegan for nearly 10 years and this was one of the most creative and unique vegan meals I’ve ever had. I do not typically seek out or opt for fine dining given the price and smaller portions but this was definitely worth the gastronomic experience. The variety of textures and flavours was insane and Chef Joyce makes even the basic seasonings (dashi, sauces, wasabi) entirely from scratch. No added sugar, salt, garlic or onion yet everything was soooo good and flavours were incredibly complex. She also changes her menu every 2-3 months!

Every part of their menu felt intentional and curated. Their sake is sourced from a small family-owned sake business from Japan, who apparently only supplies to them because of a personal connection with Joyce / wakamama. It’s clear Joyce (and her co-chef Charles) care deeply about not just flavour but presentation, even adding in embellishments like edible glitter and smoke to make the experience more memorable.

The setting was intimate and it felt personal and relaxed even with other guests. Her sweet dog was also a joy to play with!

We dined with two other sets of guests who were return customers from abroad (who’d deliberately stop by wakamama on their transit through Singapore). Truly an underrated gem and hope more SGeans find their way here. Thanks Joyce and will be back in the future!
author: Vic

review_text: What a beautiful experience! Joyce was such a wonderful host, not only was she very responsive via WhatsApp in confirming my private dining experience, but when I arrived and took off my shoes, I had the choice of a range of gorgeous slippers to wear, to then be welcomed into a fun, cosy, quirky, sustainable, and colourful dining area. While Joyce prepares, you are lost amongst all the items in the shelves and in the kitchen, all collected by Joyce amongst her travels. All items are carefully crafted and tick all the dietary needs, no gluten, no garlic or onion and all vegan! It’s her twist on Japanese reimagined into a 16 or 22 course of mind blowing food! I have never tasted and experienced food in such a way before. Joyce is the master of creating moments of sweet and savoury heaven! I cannot rave more about this, please do yourself a favour and visit Joyce when you’re in Singapore. Thank you again, I loved everything!
author: Ash

review_text: It's a really really great vegan fine dining! Each dish was particularly flavourful and muli-layered favours! It was a tailored dining experience for only a few customer in the restaurant , so my wife and I were able to fully enjoy our meal! There are so many dishes that I love! I particularly love the sushi and the cheese cake... My goodness it's so good!
author: Jimmy Chan

review_text: Five stars for food, service and atmosphere. For a weekend lunch it was just us two pax so it was very much like a private dining session. First ever omakase for us and it was a vegan one. We knew about the price up front, just overlooked that drinks were separately priced. The food was fun and unique and Chef Joyce took her time in explaining each dish and made small talk with us. It was a very different experience with food as no sugar or salt was used, whilst sweet and savoury were made with different natural ingredients. It’s like a science experiment we could eat. In total with some chocolates and a condiment jar to take home, after our two person premium omakase, I think we spent nearly S$500 for 2. Very pricy but not too far off from a good Japanese omakase. Those who have dog allergy or mind pets in an eating place, note that she had her dog in when we were there. No problem for us but just something for others to note.
author: E

review_text:
This is probably the best meal I’ve ever had. I find it surprising that this place has such a low profile. I’ve tried quite a few high quality plant-based restaurants across the world, some of them with Michelin stars - but I don’t think any of them can match the experience I had with Wakamama.

The food and drinks were incredible. I am usually skeptical when people try to imitate non-vegan dishes with plant-based ingredients, but Wakamama manages to do it in such a thoughtful, innovative and fun way that you can’t deny its artistry - it’s truly remarkable what they do and it made my skepticism fade away very quickly.

Chef Joyce was an excellent hostess and created a welcoming and engaging experience for me and my partner. The atmosphere is very cozy and intimate - at times you could almost feel like you’re just sitting in your friend’s kitchen, but your friend happens to be a culinary genius.

We had only one free evening during our visit to Singapore and are very happy that we chose to dine at Wakamama - frankly, this place alone is worth traveling to Singapore regardless of where you live. Hopefully we’ll manage to visit again soon!
author: Makar Tsurkan

review_text: One of my favourite Korean restaurants. Reasonable prices for delightful dishes, and the kimbap is freshly made. All the dishes are homemade and the food is absolutely amazing. The kimchi fried rice is also very tasty. Definitely recommend this restaurant!
author: Calreen Chan

review_text: Authentic Korean food with delicious kimbap! They offer set meals for lunch and dinner, perfect for dine-in or takeout. All dishes are tasty, and the freshly made kimchi is a standout. Will always support this place!
author: Pearly N.

review_text: Cozy little authentic korean eatery! Concise menu but everything is a knockout! The ramyun was cooked with love and so satisfying to eat, and the gimbap was so fresh and generous! Will definitely come back.
author: Brandon

review_text:
Saw this cute Korean cafe when I went for my monthly manicure at Icon.
The food tasted yummy & the pretty eonni who prepared the food was very friendly. Would definitely go back again.
author: I Kee

review_text: Surprisingly tasty kimchi fried rice at a cozy little Korean eatery! I was double surprised by the fish-shaped waffle filled with sweet potato—absolutely loved it!
author: PeiJy

review_text:
Pretty popular zi char near its namesake, which is the infamous 99 hairpin bends of Buona Vista.

Had a dinner with some of my friends here - by the time of our arrival there are several groups having their meals already. The eatery was an old school zi char place which is almost entirely semi-outdoor with strong fans everywhere. We had the flavorful free range chicken dish with ginseng, hor fun with more chicken, stir fried spicy beef, kailan with oyster sauce, and their signature dish hotplate tofu and veggies. All of them were very solid and the price was quite fair for the portions and quality. The dishes came rather quickly upon the order. All in all, it's a satisfying meal.

Just an interesting random fact I found, it seems the place is also frequented by Japanese expats who crave local foods and often live around the West Coast and the stretch up to Haw Par Villa. So much so that they added the dishes name in not only Mandarin and English, but also Japanese.
author: lontongstroong

review_text:
Today, Thursday 8 Jan 2026, I visited 99 Buona Vista Kitchen.

Great prices overall. I tried the fish slice soup with milk — very tasty, generous portion, and only $8.80 per bowl, which is really reasonable 😋

There are plenty of food choices here. The fried noodles were a bit too salty for my liking, but the sweet and sour pork and frog legs were just nice.

Do come here for the food. Just note that the ambiance is like a typical coffee shop (no air-conditioning). If you’re looking for good food at affordable prices, this place is worth a visit.
author: Yiling Lai

review_text:
Delicious Food at Great Prices
Tried the fish slice soup with milk and it was very tasty, generous portion and only $5.50 per bowl, which is really reasonable! 😋
There are lots of food choices here, and the Hor fan sambal was a standout, so yummy with a unique flavor I’ve never had before. Really special!
Highly recommend this place for the food. Just note that the ambiance is like a typical coffee shop (no aircon) but if you're here for good food at affordable prices, it’s definitely worth it!
author: Angelia Chen

review_text: Had the salted eggs pork ribs, hot plate tofu and the prawn paste chicken which were really quite decent! Seats were decently space apart. The indoor area can be quite stuffy and hot even in the evenings but the area closer to the outdoor area is still pretty chill. The staff were quite attentive and friendly! Overall had a pleasant surprise, will definitely recommend this place.
author: Frederick Tan

review_text:
Pretty good Tze Char dish in South Buona Vista area. A lot of varieties on the menu that you can choose. What we have ordered were Salted Egg Pork Ribs, Hotplate Tofu with Seafood, Stir Fried Chicken with Black Bean Sauce, Fried Chicken Sliced with Salt and Pepper, Steamed Egg with Minced Meat, Sambal Sweet Potato Leaves.
Service was efficient, food came quickly not long after we ordered. Price were reasonable, decent portion, presentation quite good, and the taste was nice too. Recommended.
author: DP

review_text: Good solid Indian fare. My favourite here is the keema kuchar. Didn’t like the raita, but other than that good place for beers and Indian food.
author: Chi Ling

review_text: Always have the best time here. Delicious Indian food, lively and cozy vibe, super friendly staff. They do screen football league, pet-friendly place.
author: Milly

review_text:
tl;dr decent taste, small quality and on the expensive side.

Pretty easy place to find beside paddy hills. This place have a bar and it is also an Indian restaurant, haven't seen this combo before. Taste is decent.

Lamb korma is very good, but has about 90g of meat for $19 (see pics)
Butter chicken is a bit too sweet for my liking and has about 100g of meat for $19
Chicken Biryani @$13.

The price to value for here not great, I think it is quite expensive for the amount of food you get.

Overall I would rate this place with the following:

Location: 6/10
Ambient: 8/10
Taste: 7/10
Service: 7/10
Price: 3/10
author: Mike

review_text: Extremely tasty Indian cuisine. Definitely one of the best in town along with an British pub atmosphere. Seems to be a local favourite on a Friday & Saturday night.
author: Mark Azzopardi

review_text: Surprisingly the Indian food here wasn't bad. I didn't expect it considering it looks more like a bar. The rice was well cooked and the fish was delicious. Portions are on the small size though in ratio to the prices.

author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: One of the few places where I noticed with every bite that they used freshest ingredients and still kept the prices affordable. Vegetarian Minestrone Soup is my personal favourite as of now. Soup’s not in the menu near the entrance but it’s on the screen. The assorted hummus are delicious but this branch didn’t have all the flavours. I recommend going to their flagship store Asian Twist by 365 Food. My friends found the veggie bowl (fun guy) really really good. 10/10
author: Harsh Patel

review_text:
The food is yummy and tastes clean. You can choose the main food item (e.g. salmon and chicken breast), base (e.g. rice), and topping at additional costs (e.g. mushrooms). They also serve good traditional coffee as well as decent selections of home made cakes and cold brewed teas.

The place itself is spacious and comfortable. Surprisingly not much office crowd even during lunch hour. Expect to spend at least $10 for food and drink.
author: Andy Andy

review_text: One of the most disappointing place, hidden inside science park. Service rude. Food is premade and microwaved, but taste is good and tender.
author: Edward Zhang

review_text:
I was trying my luck to get turkey for coco last min.

Then I saw this 365 food advertising their turkey breast to be super juicy! Chef Kenneth also very specific about how to eat it, to ensure the taste and texture at its best! A bit expensive ah $91 but it was actually quite good! Coco and loki love it too! We finished everything on one sitting!
author: Glam Maven

restaurant_name: Plank Sourdough Pizza - South Buona Vista
review_text: Pizza is great, pasta i feel it was normal. Unfortunately, if you use grab dine out for takeaway, they charge service charge too. So resulting in a higher price.
author: zxzx

restaurant_name: Plank Sourdough Pizza - South Buona Vista
review_text: Pleasant tasting sourdough pizza. Generous topping. Would prefer if the crust is crispier. Tomato base on pizza is sweet instead of sour. Can see the real cherry tomatos in the sauce, so not those puréed type. Order at the cashier of Baker and Cook.
author: Calbee Cracker

restaurant_name: Plank Sourdough Pizza - South Buona Vista
review_text: Sourdough chicken BBQ pulled pizza was not up-to my expectations. Chicken smells funny, maybe it’s a frozen chicken, pizza base is ok I guess. The Bolognese pasta too sour for my liking lacking of umami taste. The only good thing was fries, chicken tender and beer.  Need improvement.
author: Lis R.V

restaurant_name: Plank Sourdough Pizza - South Buona Vista
review_text: Well made pizza with chewy sourdough base. A tiny but burnt on the bottom part but overall pretty good. On the more expensive price range for a pizza.
author: Dian Elvira Rosa

restaurant_name: Plank Sourdough Pizza - South Buona Vista
review_text: Plank has many branches across the island, and I've yet to find a branch that wasn't satisfactory. Get the pizzas, the pastas are good but not mind-blowing.
