review_text: I am a foreigner who works near by in the science park. This is a simple salad bar. But it is fresh and tastes really good! They are serious about delivering a high quality meal.  In some ways this is my favorite place in all of a Singapore to eat. I might cry like a baby if they ever close. Hope more food centers in Singapore can open this type of natural, healthy food and sell it at a good value!!!
author: Adam Sobieski

review_text: Not sure why this place doesnt have reviews, its quite good! For $5.80 you get chicken thigh, brown rice, corn, broccoli, lettuce and some thai chili sauce. Probably the longest line in the food court at lunch time. Well done!
author: Bryan Hu

review_text: Very delicious and healthy food , price reasonable,
author: James Lim

review_text: Tasty and delicious, plenty of options for all types of diet at a very affordable price. Friendly auntie too
author: Chan Xi Jin

review_text:
This is the 2nd time we have reunion dinner here. What is nice about this place is the food is served slowly no rush / no GST / no service charge.
Free flow of ice cream.

This year we ordered the $1288 set with a sucking pig.  I particularly like the fried rice. Delighted to see Japanese eel, scallop & large prawn - not your typical fried rice.
author: Pauline Ng

review_text:
Company event, if not i wont know there a makan place here.
The food is really nice and fresh. Fish head curry, crab bee hoon, super sweet. They are quite under staff so you have to be more independent and get your own change of bowls and plates. The drinks also came rather late. Place is also a bit isolated.
author: Wu Chunhui

review_text: Fried porridge is top notch with wok hei and yam and prawn taste. Har cheong Kai, coffee pork ribs all good. Parking is easy under the Aries building! Quiet and peaceful on Saturday lunchtime. Best kid friendly zi char with small toys play area (although the little tikes car wheels need some maintenance). Kopi is a little diluted.
author: Colin Tan

review_text:
Came during weekday lunch online ordered payment kept showing error. Waitress said to order at counter. Signature fried pork which is $16 on their online ordering became $18 on their menu. Highlighted to male cashier and he said the online is not updated. Can only pay via Paynow at counter. Card payments only if bill above $50.
Later he came and informed that my Apple Pay payment did went through as they had the same order in the kitchen. At least they are honest about this and did not charge me twice. After a while he refunded me $36.80 cash (online amount apply pay amount) and not the $38.80 I Paynow at cashier counter. though is only $2 it doesn’t feel good I paid more for the same item. As you can see from the receipts attached the item no. for the same item is different K01 vs Z04
, so clearly the cashier don’t know his own menu well enough. suggest for them to update their webpage and improve on their online payment error msg.
author: Christie Kua

review_text: Went there for dinner (11 pax) on 24 May 6.30pm, total costs $568. Reservation made with a breeze. It’s a bit cramped for 11 pax. Crab bee boon is a must try dish. Stir fried Qing Long Veg and hot plate tofu is nice. Har Cheong mid wings are crispy. Steam red grouper cost $95 but I won’t recommend because it’s not fantastic, the freshness is a bit disappointing. However, the live band made the dinner place quite pleasant and relax. Also, free flow of ice cream for diners. Service was great and staff were very attentive. Drinks were served within 5 mins. Overall, it is great place for gathering.
author: Charlotte Teo

review_text:
Hidden gem in the middle of science park and worth the trip here. We came on the weekend and it wasn’t crowded at all. Staff was friendly and helpful. The restaurant has an indoor and outdoor seating, plenty of seats for all group sizes and well decorated to a dessert oasis theme, with music and birds chirping in the background.

Their signature beef cheese fries is pretty saucy. Their fruit juice is very refreshing and unique, a must try. We also ordered the lamb shank.

Overall, enjoyed the experience.
author: Masaki Wong

review_text:
Had a really satisfying meal here!
The grilled chicken was juicy and tender, paired perfectly with the fries and fresh salad. The baked cheesy pasta was rich and comforting — definitely a must-try if you love cheese.

The tomato pasta with roasted chicken was light yet flavourful, and the fried rice had a nice spicy kick. Portions were generous and great for sharing.

Overall, good food, nice presentation, and a cozy place to enjoy a hearty meal.
author: Hanhan

review_text:
This restaurant delivers an outstanding experience from start to finish!
Before we even arrived, Mindy went above and beyond by warmly welcoming us over the phone and guiding us with directions to find the place easily. When we got close, a staff member came out to greet us and show us the way to the restaurant – such thoughtful service!
The ambience is lovely – nice and calm, creating a really pleasant dining atmosphere. All the food was not only delicious but also beautifully presented, and we were impressed by how quickly it was served. Every single staff member we encountered was friendly and welcoming. Special mention goes to Mindy, who checked on us regularly to make sure everything was okay. Even though she was supposed to finish her shift, she stayed back just to sing a birthday song for our group – that personal touch made our day extra special. The male waiters were also great – polite, and he cleared our table carefully without disturbing us, esp the one with a cap.
Overall, we had a fantastic time and would absolutely recommend this place to others! Thank you guys! ❤️❤️❤️
author: ctj sam

review_text: All their branches, I truly love the quality and wonderful service from the staff! This is the reason why I keep coming back plus they close late at night! Check out the timings per restaurant but anyways what's also nice here is that it's halal and also a lot of parking available plus near the bus stop and short walk to Kent Ridge MRT or u can take the bus one stop Bus 200 from Exit B of Kent Ridge MRT super convenient!!! Must try their steak, salmon, seafood aglio olio, oh they also have thai and western food in this branch, and the desserts not to miss out!! and also the pad thai and thai sweet and sour fish was the best too!!! I love it here!! Special thanks to all the staff Chef : Bryan, Nik, Bar : Bel, Host / Server : Mindy, Din and also to Ms Sherlyn! By the way, every corner here is insta worthy spot!and u can watch the sunset here!!! Oh they even surprised me with Happy Birthday song! super sweet indeed!☺️💛thank u so much! Love the ambience and overall experience 10/10✨
author: Rochelle (OchieBon)

review_text:
Had a wonderful dining experience at Citrus Kitchen. The food was consistently good and the service was warm and attentive throughout the meal.

We started with the 【salmon salad】which was fresh and well-balanced, followed by the 【signature cheesy fries】—crispy, cheesy, and perfect for sharing. The 【seafood aglio olio】 was flavorful and generously loaded with premium scalop. The 【pineapple fried rice】 was fragrant and comforting, a great option to balance out the heavier mains.

The highlights for us were definitely the steak and the slow-braised lamb rack. The Christmas limited 【beef-ed up toasties】was nicely cooked and satisfying - juicy, tender, and well-balanced garlic parmesan cream sauce.
The slow-braised 【lamb rack】 was equally impressive. The meat was incredibly tender, almost falling off the bone, and full of deep, comforting flavor from the slow cooking.

For dessert, both the vanilla ice cream waffle and the tiramisu were excellent—light, not overly sweet, and a great way to end the meal.

Drinks were equally enjoyable: the strawberry chrysanthemum tea, passionfruit mango tea, and lychee citrus tea were refreshing.

Overall, delicious food, a wide variety of options, genuinely friendly service, and affordable price. Would definitely return and recommend to others.
author: GLORIA GUO

review_text: Lovely cozy place with little crowd on weekday night. Service staff very polite and helpful. Had Army Stew and it’s very good! Had Korean fried chicken and they are sooo yummy! 5 different flavors and I personally like the soy sauce and honey butter flavor
author: Daisy Snowdrop

review_text: The place was quite a hidden restaurant if you don’t work around that area. Love the stew but the chicken was a  disappointment. Can tell it wasn’t fresh chicken and has a stench, the chili chicken wing theme didn’t go well in my palete.. wish it was better . Will recommend to go and try their lunch set, service was prompt and welcoming.
author: Empress Ker

review_text: What a gem nestled in this hidden corner in the south. Not many people know about it and we happen to walk past on our way to another nearby restaurant and decided to do a detour. Best decision of the evening. Amazing korean pancakes and fried chicken. Love that it's very quiet but I hope it gets more business here so it stays open. The food is just top quality stuff. Parking is easy at the Crimson building just right next door. Perfect place to do dinner with friends and family on a weekend!
author: Charles J

review_text:
There isnt an option for 4.5 stars but thats what i would rate it. My experience at this Korean food place was generally positive. The prices were reasonable, and the food tasted good overall. Their lunch deals are also worth noting.

One dish that didn't quite hit the mark for me was the kimchi pork soup - the pork had a strange taste. Not sure what it was. The kimchi soup however was good and full of flavour
author: suckms

review_text:
Un-gatekeeping this hidden gem so that more people can support this awesome Korean restaurant!

Location wise it’s a little out of the way but if you drive there’s a carpark next to it

Onto the food:

Sundubu jiggae- first time seeing (half) crab in this dish, good amount of clams and tofu as well. Delicious and worth it for $15

Korean fried chicken- got the platter of 10 with 5 different flavors. Good way to try the different variations! Found it comparable to the ones we had in Korea, personally liked the original and yangnyeom, while wife likes the soy and chilli. For $30++, this works out to be ~$3 per piece (that’s even cheaper than KFC)
author: Wei Ian

review_text:
Hot Hideout is THE place I go to for my mala fix! It also so happens that I study here so the outlet at NUS makes it really easy to satisfy my cravings.

The one mala variant I always get here is the mala collagen soup. If you want dry mala, the one at Chinatown complex (iykyk), is way better. However, where this place beats every other mala place is the fact that they offer to deep fry certain ingredients like the luncheon meat, potato, lotus root etc.

Is it cheap? Most definitely not. As a big eater, and as a guy, I often spend $20 for my portion. A tip from me: if you’re dining by yourself or you and your friends are not sharing, don’t order the potato. It’s a good 300g+ and you’ll end up paying easily over $8 for a single potato - which is ridiculous imo.

Maximise your budget by getting meat, and if you want something deep fried, try the mantou buns. They pair beautifully with the peanut sauce 🤤

Another tip: come here on the weekends as there are barely any students around and you won’t need to queue.
author: Joel Mathews

review_text: Had it twice within a week. Tomato collagen ($43 for 4 pax) and original collagen soup ($31 for 2 pax, Takeaway). Soups were tasty but not overly salty. Ingredients were fresh and priced at $2.68 / 100g. So be mindful of over loading your bowl unknowingly 😂.
author: Ann G

review_text:
You might get lost a little if you are first time here parking and looking for the place. Basically the food area are sort of together.

This place is definitely a heaven and comfort food for the university students.

I really enjoyed the mala collagen soup. It isn't crazy oily or crazy spicy, it was comforting for me to drink!

Lotsa people like to pick lotus root, potato and mantao to be fried paired with the secret powder;)
author: Pui Cheng Lum

review_text:
Good food, good concept.
Easy to order. Food is delicious.
author: Chin Kang Teh

review_text: A decent place to try Mala, but just be careful in choosing your spicy level. I tried medium and my stomach turned into a volcano. Dinner time can be quite crowded. And portions are quite generous. So if two people can actually order one and choose a few sides. I would go after 6 months maybe, after the volcano eruption cools down.
author: chiranjeet narayan dev

review_text:
19/4/2022 tuesday lunch 12.30pm

yummy unhealthy food near PGP and KE7: freshly fried nuggets 🍗, cheese fries 🍟, waffles 🧇, tasty soy ice cream 🍦! Opened till 1am for your food cravings! Prices are standard, $3 for 6 nuggets. Better options available but this is most convenient late at night.

Convenient self-serve kiosks. Payment is via most cashless apps like paylah or cash at counter 💵. Cutlery 🍴 are all plastic and readily available with tissues and sauces 🍅🌶 at their counter too!

lunch menu 🍱 is decent and comes with a drink 🥤. Their fried chicken is nubbad and filling meal for $5. Their hard boiled egg 🥚 comes with a thick dab of mayo lol. Rice 🍚 and salad 🥗 are standard stuff.

Their cheese waffle 🧀🧇 is nacho cheese which doesnt really taste well. but their chocolate 🍫🧇 waffle and stuff tastes amazing!! The cheese quesadilla 🌮 is also nacho which isnt that nice lol. Sometimes their waffles are not that crispy and a little doughy inside, so can ask for crispier!

Wait times can be long, especially during peak lunch hours and at 12am.

Overall, worth frequenting if you stay nearby for sinfully good and convenient food! 😁
author: chu xuan

review_text: Mediocre food, more costly than canteens, aircons usually do not run during the day, the staff just simply do not write down orders and tend to make mistakes now and then. The place is relatively quiet and good for hang out. Beware when you order the chocolate waffle. Ask for more crispy and when the chocolate goodness oozes out, don't spill it on your clothes!! 🍫🥞🤤
author: Andy Andy

review_text: Kiat made the best waffles ive ever tasted, and im a regilar at pgp. he is very well mannered, i hope he gets promoted or a bonus
author: Isaac Tay

review_text: I love super snack! The best place for onion rings and fries. Very hot and crispy. Opens at night as well. The price is really worth it! Highly recommend all nus students to at least try it once.
author: Yingying

review_text: The quesadillas are truly mid. For $6 u get to eat cardboard with a dash of bbq sauce. I wouldn’t wish this on my worst enemy.
author: Isaac Lim

restaurant_name: Zhen Mei Shi Mixed Veg Rice
review_text: The braised pork was melt-in-the-mouth tender, and the cabbage was cooked just right. Paired with a fish cake and a bowl of porridge, the total came to $5.50. Overall, an enjoyable meal—though a little pricey for what it was.
author: LP Pua

restaurant_name: Zhen Mei Shi Mixed Veg Rice
review_text: When I first saw this stall, I was not interested to eat anything there. On my second visit, I saw some people in the queue, then I realized that the dishes looked depleted not because the stall is not ready! On the contrary, they must have sold quite a lot! I ordered what was left over at 7.40am in the morning. The braised pork was heavenly! I am already dreaming of my next session with it! All the items here with the porridge cost me $6, it’s considered pretty cheap for Teochew Porridge! Only old hawkers like them could have pulled this off! Heart warming and tummy filling breakfast! Good stuff!
author: Wang Teck Heng

restaurant_name: Zhen Mei Shi Mixed Veg Rice
review_text: A decent store run by an elderly friendly couple. The food looks decent and is not expensive for this area at all.
author: Quittance

restaurant_name: Zhen Mei Shi Mixed Veg Rice
author: Joel Tan

review_text:
Heng Huat is known for serving a “healthier” version of fried kway tiao.

A standard plate costs S$8, fried with egg, bean sprouts, cai poh & blood cockles, then topped with a huge pile of boiled cai xin (Chinese mustard greens).

Personally felt the portion wasn’t very generous. Without pork lard, Chinese sausage, or fish cake, the dish also ends up being less fragrant than the usual version. The large amount of greens tasted a bit too raw or slightly odd when paired with the noodles.

Still an interesting option if you’re looking for a lighter plate of fried kway tiao 🍜
author: Ben MA

review_text: Taste is average, best thing is the boiled veggies to balance the greasiness of the CKT. Worth coming back? In my option, no. Why? Taste isn’t good enough, forget about the $4 portion, even the $6 portion is small. Worst thing is dealing with the grumpy owner.
author: Eric Lee

review_text: This is probably the healthiest char Kway teow in Singapore 😆 with a generous heap of cai xin and fresh cockles. This is the smallest $4 portion. The taste might not be to everyone’s liking as the flavor is lighter, less sweet, less oily than typical CKT. Good for days when you crave for a guilt-free CKT 😜
author: MK L

review_text:
The fried kway tiao wasn't quite what I had hoped for. The dish leaned more towards yellow noodles rather than the traditional kway tiao, which is not my preferred type. Additionally, I found the dish a bit too spicy for my taste and felt it lacked the distinctive "wok hei" that I look for in a good fried kway tiao.

I was also quite puzzled by the abundance of raw vegetables in the dish, which didn't quite fit the overall flavor profile. On the bright side, they were quite generous with the cockles, which was a pleasant surprise.

Overall, while there were some positive aspects, the dish didn't quite meet my expectations.
author: Henry Cheng

review_text:
Ordered a $5 portion. It's interesting if you add an egg or have oyster options.

Taste very normal char kway teow. Wok hey is not strong. Just sweet, don't even feel the spicy taste.

Only upside is the veggies that's seems to be boiled. Would skip this, portion is not sufficient for me but ok for most people.
author: Thaddeus Zheng

review_text: This place is very affordable and they provide good food and excellent customer service
author: Yumi

review_text: Got food poisoning twice , only ate there twice
author: Crystal

review_text: The most awesome place to hv lunch in SP12!!!!
author: Dr Lcs

review_text: Good food and good customer service, 😁
author: May May

review_text:
if lucy's has million fans, then i'm one of them.
if lucy's has one fan, then i'm THAT ONE.
if lucy's has no fans, that means i'm not alive.
author: rachel

review_text:
This plate of fried white carrot cake was truly impressive. The aroma of the egg and preserved radish blended beautifully, and there was still moisture within the carrot cake pieces, giving it a wonderfully soft and pleasant texture.

It wasn’t dry at all, and the balance was just right. The portion was also generous, making it very satisfying.

The lady boss was friendly and welcoming, which added to the overall dining experience.

A delicious plate of white carrot cake that I’d definitely return for!
author: chan jasmoon

review_text:
A very good plate of white carrot cake,  with lots of umami and chye poh bits. Have eaten the black version before, and the sweetness is balanced.

Can't tell if the carrot cake bits are factory made, but they're the softer kind. Overall, would come back to eat!
author: Jermyn Eng

review_text: The black carrot cake was delicious with a good amount of black sauce and wok hei, the white carrot cake was good too! Hokkien Mee was standard and prawns were fresh! Waiting time is slightly on the longer side but that’s because there’s only person cooking and she prepares each batch one by one. Will definitely return!
author: Jona Yip

review_text:
Rude Aunty very slow in cooking.
Customers' waiting time = 30 mins.

THERE IS A HOUSEFLY IN MY $4 BLACK CARROT CAKE!!!
author: Meow The Cat

review_text:
Order the white carrot cake.
Very good. One the the best.
Crispy outside, soft and moist inside.
author: Ronnie Seah

review_text: Fauziah's is a delightful find when I visited this popular food center recently. I was recommended by a fellow hawker as I was seeking halal offerings. The lady owner is so polite and helpful. I could see fellow customers chatting with her too. They were so enthusiastic to recommend me the mee rebus, mee siam etc.  I like that her dishes looks so well made with patience and love. Looks like what my grandma used to make, patiently and with care for the family. I also like it that the stall overall looks very clean and organised. I will certainly be visiting the stall again when I here. Sorry I didn't check out the opening hours with owner. Most likely it's opened for breakfast and lunch. Do support our local hawkers! All the dishes are yummy!
author: Winnie S

review_text: I know the cook when she was having the PSA cafeteria. She really cooks excellent nasi padang and other stuff as lotong, tawhu goreng and mee rebus. Her tawhu goreng are excellent with her strong gravy. Presently she with her husband are selling nasi padang, bee oon, mee rebus and lotong too. The lotong are still the excellent taste as before. The lodeh gravy and vegetables are the best taste and fresh. I never miss the stall whenever I pass the place near to Pasir Panjang mrt stn.
author: syed Ibrahim Yusoff

review_text:
I've been having food from this shop in its various iterations and locations for almost 40 years. I am invariably greeted with the warmest of smiles and the food reminds me of my childhood. The food is cooked and served with so much love you will not be able to resist coming back.

My highlights will always be the Mee Siam and the Mee Rebus, but don't sleep on their other offerings as well.
author: Fazil Musa

review_text: Restaurant operated within previous Keppel Club location. Food now taste just as good as before. Stall owners are very friendly.
author: Violin Ling

review_text: Nice food...love thier Nescafe ...keep it up..this morning just try ...tq for the free breakfast
author: Lolli Jane

review_text:
1st time here. Was recommended by my brother Habib. Place is at Pasir Panjang Food Centre. A few minutes walk from the Pasir Panjang MRT(Exit A). Only an aunty was at the stall. Very friendly and humble. Stall was quite clean. They do have some combo pricing as well. Bought one Mutton biriyani to dine in. The taste was good.
Dalcha was nice but could be a bit thicker. Portion was decent. Mutton piece was good. Mutton was cooked well and was soft. The mutton gravy(masala) was not a lot but decent.
Rice was good. Comes with achar also. Achar taste is good.👍
They even sell achar in bottles each at $4.50.
I didn't get one but maybe will, in the near future😇. They do take orders for small functions. Do check them out.
author: Mohamed Haniffa

review_text:
Very unassuming and yummy Dum Briyani. Why Dum? Cos the meat is cooked together with the rice hence the rice is more flavourful after absorbing the jus from the meats. This amazing Mutton Briyani is served with homemade Indian achar.

Support this young lady, trying to make a living in F&B sharing with everyone her family recipe.

Follow me on all social media @eatwithroy for more hotel, food and product reviews!
author: Big Roy [eatwithroy]

review_text:
The basmati rice is cooked to perfection and the chicken is nice. The accompanying curry is too salty and the vegetables are hard. The papadam are sold for $1 each packet. It is nice and crispy. The portion is big and enough for 2 persons.
The lady serving the food is friendly.
author: Jacob TAN

review_text: Mutton briyani  is super tender and flavourful. no papadum given...unfortunately  ;)
author: Shop S

review_text: Delicious and generous serving for $8 mutton biryani.
author: Daniel Ang

review_text:
Very nice chicken rice with succulent chicken and fragrant rice. The chicken is always tender and never disappoints no matter what cut of meat you take. They only have the $4 option which comes with vegetables but you get to pick bean sprouts or another vegetable.

It's a very well balanced meal, couple with the spicy chili that gives a kick when you wolf it down. They also have the ultra rare Fried ginger and spring onion condiment which is hardly found in hawker center based chicken rice stalls, which would elevate the chicken texture.

Very good quality too, especially if you compare to Sin Kee
author: Jermyn Eng

review_text:
Pasir panjang resident and staffs are so lucky to have this heartland stall!

Remember they sell out fast after lunch hour! Go and eat now!
author: V

review_text: Firstly I was attracted by the rice! So fluffy and loose with a nice aroma. It was so delicious and I can finish it without any chilli or dark sauce. Haha. And for the roast chicken, I requested for breast meat because it’s my favourite part! The plate of tender and juicy meat was drizzled with light soy sauce and sesame oil, enhancing the flavours! Everything including the braised egg was only $4! Will definitely return for more!! Yum!
author: Benito Linus

review_text: Fantastic plate of chicken rice. Fragrant rice and tender chicken. +points for the affordable pricing as well.
author: rn_1604

review_text:
A very good and reasonable stall at Pasir Panjang Hawker center.

A queue started as soon as they opened at around 9am.

Took away drum stick with gizzard rice at only $4.50.

Will be back …
author: Flo G

review_text:
Good hawker centre right next to MRT station with plenty of good choices at reasonable prices.

There’s a segregation of Malay Indian stalls and a non-halal local side.

Favourites are Jubilant chicken rice!
Many other stalls like roasts, BCM fishball noodles are highly rated.

Also a Japanese ramen with high ratings!

Good coffee too!

I found prices are generally lower here than other hawkers in the city.

Only gripe is the amount of smokers who stood or sit around the hawker centre to smoke. Sometimes the smoke comes right to the seated eating areas.
author: Flo G

review_text: A spacious spot with plenty of seating, though it can get a little hot during midday. The curry rice is tasty and satisfying — definitely worth trying! The friendly aunty at the stall makes the experience even better, and she accepts all sorts of payment methods, making it super convenient.
author: Geraldine Koh

review_text: While this place at first look may not seem to have much to offer, it does have a few GEMs. I like the teochew porridge, curry rice, mutton soup, bbq and western here. You just need to try the stalls out and I am sure you will find something to like.
author: Wang Teck Heng

review_text: Excellent teahouse, I recommend it to my friends who like drinking tea 😄
author: YANG, FANG

review_text: Had dinner here, food and service were good, but it was a bit too crowded for a Friday night.
author: iamjess

review_text:
This food market offers a good variety of dishes, and several stalls are worth trying. The steam fish was especially fresh and flavorful. The BBQ pork rice came with tender, well-cooked meat that made the dish satisfying. The wan ton mee was not bad overall, though the wan ton itself can be skipped—especially since the dumplings were sold out during my visit.

There’s also a freshly baked bread stall that serves a lovely muffin, definitely a nice treat to end the meal.

Overall, a pleasant stop with a few standout items worth returning for.
author: Geraldine Koh

review_text: First visited to this market. Tried the traditional Rojak which was prepared by two seniors lady and taste was really good and realised that with 4 SGD, few slides of apples were found whereas it is hardly found from others similar store. Love it👍
author: Ls Lin

review_text: ABC BRICKWORKS Have many good hawker stalls with different varities of Chinese, Indian & Muslim stalls providing choice of food
author: Lui Matthew

review_text: Just discovered this Generous portion desserts shop with variable hot dessert! Located right next to Wow Wow West. Hot 绿豆汤 is full of green beans, cold 清汤 also have alot of filling with just $2.20 each. Aunty and uncle were talking softly. Good to have these on rainy days. I also tried the other dessert stall at row 1, it was much lesser and always wait very long.
author: ssin

review_text: A very good place to havr a variety of great food. The Price is very reasonable in most shops and the variety is really great. My favourite must eat dishes are  are Wow Wow West Pork Chop, Cheese Sausages and Fish& Chips, Hokkean Mee and Carrot cake. The ambiance is not great. Bit, the food will compensate for it.
author: Karthick Sonaimuthu

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
review_text:
First time trying as previous visits were sold out.  Tried all 3 flavours - turnip, red bean and yam.  Perfect the sweet flavours.  Skin is chewy quite interesting though some parts may be a bit tough/thick.
Good taste in general for a snack though the size is quite small @ $1.2-1.3 each
author: Ken Tan

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
review_text:
I must say the quality of the Shui Jing Pau had dropped.
The chopped turnips were “rough”, it used to be quite small chips.
Flavor had totally changed - perhaps lacking of meat, mushrooms and dried shrimps.
My box of 10 pieces cost $12; which is rather expensive.
Rather disappointed with their standard - they used to be famous with customers queueing to buy.
author: Alan Tang

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
review_text: Ordered the jicama fillings. Skin is nice and chewy, while fillings has a unique lard aroma.
author: Stanley Pang

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
review_text: Absolutely outstanding. The skin was impossibly thin yet perfectly structured, and the filling was unmistakably hand cut with bold, incredible flavour. The chilli on the side was spot on, just the right kick to elevate every bite. You can feel the craftsmanship and heart behind this. Pure artisanal excellence. Support this gem before it disappears.
author: Veronica Ong

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Lien Fa Shui Jing Pau
review_text:
A nostalgic childhood taste that brings lots of good memories. This diminishing trade which seems that no where else has.
So for all the poor reviews, we cut them some slack.

Only manage to get the last of the savoury ones close to 1pm, sold out after.

Skin is thin and QQ, Taste is still as good as I remember. So good the chill..

Love the sweet versions, do call to reserve before heading down to save disappointment.

Don’t expect service or warm hospitality, won’t be disappointed.

$1.10 each min. 4 pcs at Feb24

Definitely coming back to satisfy my sweet cravings for their redbean & yam paste.
author: Flo G

restaurant_name: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
review_text:
Keng Eng Kee Seafood is one of the most famous zi char restaurant in Singapore.
Very local atmosphere but food quality is amazing.
I tried several dishes and everything had strong flavor and good wok technique.
Especially the Moonlight Hor Fun was incredible. The raw egg mixed with noodles makes very rich taste.
Chilli crab style dishes also very good.
It is not fancy restaurant but very authentic Singapore food experience.
ローカル感が最高。
Highly recommended if you want to try real Singapore seafood cooking.
author: GYOUZA DAISUKI

restaurant_name: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
review_text:
Sometimes I still think of this place... A friend recommended this to us and this may be one of our fav meals in Singapore! Service was so efficient and super nice, we ate very comfortably.

We ordered the ho fun with egg, veggies with eggs 3 way, and chili crab.
- ho fun with egg: It was our first time trying ho fun with an egg and that egg adds so much more creamy silky texture to the perfectly cooked noodles. It also has lots of "wok" flavour. We inhaled this.

- veggie eggs 3 way: the veggies were our second fav dish. The veggies were cooked perfectly and fresh. The eggs 3 way elevates the dish by giving it texture (egg drop and century egg), a kick (salted egg yolk). We inhaled this as well.

- chili crab: a popular dish in Singapore, it was flavourful (sweet and spicy but we found it more sweet) and saucy. You can get a side of bread to dip the sauce.
author: C

restaurant_name: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
review_text: Crazy crowded on a weekday night. Could only get the 8pm seating. It’s mostly alfresco seatings though they also have an ac area on the other side. Ordered many dishes and of course the chili crab($108). Crab was not bad, gravy has enough heat. Some notable dishes i like will be the salted egg squid ($21.80), butter cereal prawns ($42.80) and the moonlight horfun($18.80). The salted egg squid is nicely fried and crispy. Salted egg flavor also not too overpowering. The prawns were huge. I’m guessing XL size tiger prawns. Texture also fresh and bouncy. The moonlight horfun is v flavorful. Even without the raw yolk, i think it’s nice. Total dmg $270 for 6 pax. Overall it’s not a bad meal. i can see why it’s so crowded. Nice qc maintenance. Reservations highly recc.
author: Ray Tan

restaurant_name: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
review_text:
Honestly, I have never tried Singapore chili crab despite visiting Singapore many times. I finally had the chance, but we opted for the crab meat version instead of the whole crab because we were too lazy to pick the meat from the shell. Perhaps that was the wrong choice because the chili crab sauce tasted average to me. I would go for the whole crab next time if I revisit.

The curry fish head was good, although the consistency reminded me more of soup curry noodles rather than the richer, thicker curry I would expect from a claypot version.

The fried kuey tiao with raw egg yolk was surprisingly full of wok hei and very delicious, but it was not as nice once it cooled down.

The fried chicken wing was a bit hard and crunchy instead of light and crispy, though the flavour was good.

The fried squid was absolutely delicious.

Service was friendly and attentive.
author: Leh

restaurant_name: Keng Eng Kee Seafood @ Alexandra Village
review_text:
My siblings and I revisited Keng Eng Kee Seafood at Bukit Merah last month, and it’s still as good as we remembered. We couldn’t resist packing home a few of our favourites.

The Seafood Hor Fun was wonderfully smoky with that unmistakable wok hei, and the Coffee Pork Ribs remained as finger-licking good and fragrant as ever. Portions were generous, flavours were spot-on, and everything tasted freshly cooked.

Always a reliable spot for comforting, delicious zi char! Highly recommend dropping by if you’re in the area. 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
author: Xiao Ting

review_text: Amazing food and vibe! Loved both the indoor and outdoor seating. The food was absolutely top-notch — highly recommend this place. They have a great variety of vegetarian options. The vegan burger was delicious, the orecchiette pesto pasta was superb, and the grilled chicken was cooked to perfection 👌
author: Aditi Gandhi

review_text:
Very nice ambience.
Food is excellent except limited choice of vegan menu.
Service is excellent.
We were served by staff Darmen , he was attentive and professional.
Knowing that was my birthday, surprised me with a beautiful birthday cake 🎂
Thanks for giving us a memorable day .
author: Carina Lai Lan Eng

review_text:
Heard this charming B&W Bungalow was once the residence of an iconic tycoon.. Nested within the grounds of Telok Blangah Hills (linked to Mt Faber via Henderson Wave Bridge).  Once u arrived, the smell of forest greets u.  It doesn’t feel like u are in Urban Concrete Spore.
It has a nice courtyards, and manicured gardens, water fountain… the building now houses a few eateries offering different concepts  eg cafe,  a restaurant on the 2nd Flr…
And take your time sipping your coffee and having your food here in a relaxed environment.
Perfect for dates… or catching up with frens with undistracted attention.  Some days they do wedding ROM events at the courtyards too.

The only cons is, long walk fm bus stops.  Best to drive or grab.
author: YL Wong

review_text: A really nice place with lovely vibes, attended a wedding here! Food was good, I had the vegetarian menu btw which I would recommend (even if you’re not a vegetarian like me). Transport-wise, no covered parking, and might be difficult to get a cab out of the park.
author: Rennie Lee

review_text:
I had such a lovely time attending my friend’s wedding over the weekend. The food was not only top quality but also served in generous portions—we were all completely stuffed by the end of the meal! The staff, especially Moe, were incredibly friendly and accommodating. We had a child with us, which can sometimes mean a bit of mess and extra requests, like switching to kid-friendly plates or asking for a cup with a straw—but nothing was too much trouble for them.

The venue was also very kid-friendly, with a dedicated play area where children could draw, ride, and slide. My little one absolutely loved it! I’ll definitely be coming back with my family for a meal.
author: C long

review_text:
IMPORTANT NOTE!!! I was informed that they would be closing in May 2025, if you are considering visiting , please call and confirm they are open

Visited joe(which is owner and cook) kitchen on a random weekday night for dinner

Which such great reviews on Google, one would expect a queue during dinner time. Instead there was only 1 other diner when I visited the place. My partner says it’s looks deserted and we should go somewhere else. I persisted

Service was absolutely stunning. Waitress was kind and polite, much more so then 5 star Michelin restaurants

Atmosphere was cosy

Let’s talk about food , Tom yam soup was absolutely stunning. Blend of spicies dancing in your mouth. It was neither overly spicy nor overly sour, it was a perfect blend. 5/5

Red curry chicken looks nice on picture but was rather disappointing. Curry was really sweet 1/5

Kang Kong tasted fresh and crunchy but nothing much to shout. But this is to be expected. I won’t recommend this dish as it was too over priced for what you are getting. 2/5

For all of above and 2 tea costed $40+
author: J

review_text: We’re back after few years. Overall the foods still as nice as before. Mango salad and steam fish are nicest, sweet and sour enough. The fried tang hoon will be nicer if dry more. I walked pass by the kitchen area while went toilet and noticed the washing place is not hygiene, and the restaurant looks old. Price consider a bit high compared to others (not food courts / hawker)
author: khanh linh

review_text: Mango salad is probably the best that I have ever tried - thinly sliced with the right texture (between ripe and unripe mangoes) and balanced taste (not too spicy). Tofu soup was not bad. Claypot prawn vermicelli was generous in portion with six large prawns but the taste was rather one-dimensional. Service was OK. The restaurant was quite messy inside so the ambience was almost non existent.
author: CK C

review_text:
Very prompt and friendly service. Small place with few tables only. Advisable to make reservations. We were lucky to try crab vermicelli which required pre-ordering. Save stomach space for the mango sticky rice.
Lady boss is very friendly and will make appropriate food recommendations.
author: Grace Chia

review_text: food was decent however there are better options out there. ordered the pineapple rice, honey chicken, garlic pork, prawn cakes,baby kai lan and tom yum soup. the garlic pork and pineapple rice were mediocre only. was given 2 complimentary red ruby for father’s day, kind gesture from the staff, thank you! 😊
author: Cheyenne Chong

review_text: Nice relaxing place. Plenty of outdoor seating.  Very cooling as they hv a big fan blowing. Don't worry, there's no mozzy. Food was good. Drinks Good too. Nothing really to complain except that it is located a bit out of the way.
author: roy lai

review_text:
Wah this is really the BEST restaurant/bar in Singapore!

Great for dates, great for family, great for groups and great for everything.

Kid friendly, pet friendly, LGHDTV friendly everything also friendly.

Very nice and good food and drinks and service/staff and ambience.

5 stars not enough. Fantastic place. Must go. Highly recommend!
author: Bram

review_text:
First time went to Handlebar with my car group and really enjoyed food there. The atmosphere is like those countryside feel where you can dine under the sun or moon. The middle well done lamb is soft and nice even without any sauce. Also the pork rib is big in serving and soft and easy to remove from the bones. We had dessert platter where we tried 5 different desserts. My favourite was the Creme Brulé. Also not to forget the mushroom soup, solid with the bread. Overall great place to chill and makan.

Also the place is pet friendly and kids friendly cos a lot of spaces to roam around. Will go back soon for other dishes.
author: Edmund Tan

review_text:
It's been some time me and my wife patronise here...
The food is still so awesome,the staffs are still so friendly and efficient. Good job!
author: Jason Gan

review_text: On 19 Sept 2025, We had a wonderful experience dinning here. The stuff were very friendly, attentive and made us feel very welcomed. The food was delicious and well prepared. Esp the special once a year beef noodles. The cosy environment is a surprise. Prices are reasonable too. Overall, it was an excellent experience, and i will be coming back for sure.
author: HB

restaurant_name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
review_text:
My siblings and I stumbled upon this stall and decided to give their roasted duck and pork rice a try — and we were pleasantly surprised! The roasted pork was tender and practically melted in our mouths, and the roasted duck was flavourful and juicy.

We especially loved the rich, dark sauce that tied everything together. The whole plate tasted like the kind of old-school roasted meat rice we used to enjoy after school for lunch. So nostalgic and comforting!

A lovely find, and definitely worth a visit if you’re craving traditional roasted delights.
author: Xiao Ting

restaurant_name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
review_text:
Old school roast meat shop.

If you like heavy garlic sauce on your char siew this is the place.

Other reviews may have overstated the rudeness of the staff. I found that it was absolutely fine. Some people just speak in a more direct and less customer service oriented way, they don't mean anything by it.
author: JR FF

restaurant_name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
review_text: Quite unique serving and presentation of the common char siew, roast pork (烧肉) and roast duck rice - generous drizzle of thick black gravy and a spoon of chilli paste. There is some cucumber too. Everything is over run by the dark gravy.
author: Mark Yeo

restaurant_name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
review_text:
Paid $16 for a serving of boneless duck and char siew. The char siew still delivers on flavor—tender, slightly charred, and satisfyingly sweet.

The sauce that came with the dish looked heavy, but surprisingly wasn’t overly salty—balanced and pleasant. Everything was paired with plain white rice, which helped soak up the flavors well.

The accompanying soup was average—nothing much to shout about.
author: Orange

restaurant_name: Lau Phua Chay Authentic Roasted Delicacies
review_text: In Alexandra Village Hawker. Next to the famous avocado drink stall. Decent plate of charsiew rice. The sauce is very different from most stores. Savory rather than sweet
author: Justin Chu

restaurant_name: Sunnychoice Vegan Cafe and Healthy Option Store
review_text:
Dropped by this Sunnychoice cafe for a quick lunch on Monday noon, and it was a pleasant visit. Seats were available, which made it very convenient.

The aunty staff at the counter was welcoming and friendly while taking our order. We had the Vegetarian Pad Thai Noodles and Vegetarian Pho Noodles Soup. The Pad Thai was very tasty, and the pho soup was refreshing and ingredients are simple yet delicious. The price are reasonable too. We will definitely return here to try other food!
author: Angel Harbulot

restaurant_name: Sunnychoice Vegan Cafe and Healthy Option Store
review_text:
Visit dated on 2nd week of December 2025
We ordered achar, curry vegetables, vegetable sushi roll and Taohu goreng.

First time try Taohu goreng that have 2 kinds of sauces for you to choose, either satay sauce or pumpkin sauce. For healthier choice, we chosen pumpkin sauce.
Given 2 limes when served. Lime juices match with pumpkin sweetness and totally tasted differently from traditional peanut sauce.

Achar tasted normal.

Vegetables sushi comes with special sauce wasabi tasted like diluted with water, smell not so pungent.

Curry vegetables comes with potatoes, tofu and turnip, good match in curry but personally felt the curry sauce not thick enough but tasted ok.

Attached the photos when noticed forgotten to take proper pictures before we eat as we are first time here and too curious to try all the dishes...
We will be back to try other dishes for sure!
author: IVY MU

restaurant_name: Sunnychoice Vegan Cafe and Healthy Option Store
review_text:
It’s vegan day so trying out this outlet.
Staff were friendly and courteous.
Nice and clean atmosphere.
Ordered the Bak Kut Teh set and satay yummylicious. The rice is tasty and fragrant like the barley texture.
Highly recommended 👍🏻
author: Christina Lim

restaurant_name: Sunnychoice Vegan Cafe and Healthy Option Store
review_text: I had a take away rendang curry. It had potato, white radish, carrot and tofu. Vegetables were okay but the curry had a sour smell to it. Maybe I should have ate immediately instead of keeping in fridge and reheat. Look forward to try the laksa next visit.
author: TravelWithMo

restaurant_name: Sunnychoice Vegan Cafe and Healthy Option Store
review_text: A good range of food choices. We had thunder tea rice, olive fried rice and pineapple fried rice respectively. The rice tastes chewy. Good taste profile. And generous portion.
author: Han

restaurant_name: Hei Lun Shi Tang 黑轮食堂
review_text:
Hidden gem in one corner of Queensway shopping centre level 2 away from the laksa stores. I got the gong wan soup with lu rou fan and I was damn full after. The lu rou fan was flavourful yet not too oily and the meat wasn’t too dry nor fatty.

Soup was so good with radish and I think there’s not much MSG as I didn’t feel thirsty after. It came with 5 big gong wan which was so good as well.

The service was very fast despite being a crowd and queue but can get a little warm (maybe cause I was drinking the soup). Price wise, I think it’s affordable for the portions and the quality.
author: Kah Wang Tan

restaurant_name: Hei Lun Shi Tang 黑轮食堂
review_text: Nice spot at Queensway for Taiwanese food. The mains are served in retro metal tins, which is a nice touch. Tried the curry braised pork rice, flavourful and satisfying. The stewed pork belly bento not bad too. Gongwan soup was comforting with handmade meatballs.
author: NomNomFables

restaurant_name: Hei Lun Shi Tang 黑轮食堂
review_text:
Ordered a small Signature Braised Pork Bento ($5) and this was an amazing find. Really lovely home cooked taste. Apparently the large (+$1) will have more rice and more meat, but even the small was hearty enough. I want to try the soup and other dishes next! Will definitely be back again :)

Update: I’ve been back multiple times since my first review and each time it’s SO GOOD. Seems like they change up the soup every so often. It’s definitely of my favorite places to eat in this area.
author: Keika Sugiyama

restaurant_name: Hei Lun Shi Tang 黑轮食堂
review_text:
Tried the meatball soup and braised pork rice combo. Rice was decent, though not spectacular. Soup, on the other hand, was memorable. Very tasty, which also meant the radish was infused with flavour. Meatballs were substantial, had a good bite and incorporated mushrooms for additional flavour and texture.

Menu is rather extensive - would return to try their other dishes
author: Wong Wei Jian

restaurant_name: Hei Lun Shi Tang 黑轮食堂
review_text:
Never try never know.
Lovely quaint neighbourhood corner stall serving up home cooked style rice and noodles.
Tried the curry with braised pork rice 👍🏻 and a scallion braised pork noodles.
author: Sebastian Oh

review_text: These tutus are hard to find today and of cos the vendors are aware of it that they keep jacking up the price so much that it now costs $1 each. I am okay if it’s delicious but the current quality doesn’t warrant it. It’s so much flour and so little filling. It’s dry and need to wash it down with water. Tbh, I’d rather buy tau sar pieh.
author: Harlee Q

review_text: The tutu quality is getting worse. When I opened the box, the white top was stick to the box and left the fillings separately. Taste also not fragrant as before. They taking own sweet time to make kueh during weekdays.
author: Melody

review_text:
Extremely unsanitary, repeated rude and poor service by all the different aunties working here across multiple visits. Will not support them moving forward and I do not recommend people to do so either, they arent selling “necessary” food after all so really just buy ur teatime snacks elsewhere.

1. Found the biggest fattest fly in my drink AFTER I had already finished it. Vomitted immediately and also got food poisoning from it the day after. I went back to the store to inform them, asked for a refund + a bottled of mineral water (which is what, probably less than $0.50 worth in term of costs to them) because i vomitted so badly that i was very dehydrated. Well they were so petty and did not even apologise about it, just outright dimissive. And yup, refused to give me a bottle of water for free but ok trying my luck because if i didnt vomit, i wouldnt have been thristy LOL.

2. Purchased a waffle, it was offpeak timing so there was no queue. After ordering i immediately walked towards the waffle making section (3 seconds walk probably) and saw that they had premade ones, and the moment i reached they gave it to me and it was COMPLETELY COLD. Immediately i told them, that i want a freshly made one, like excuse me at this price i expect that it is at least warm, its so cold that it was probably made 1hour ago. Well they just replied “ no we already make already”. Absolutely no thought or care for customer’s needs at all.

3. Peak period, purchased 3 pieces of coconut tutu (horrible taste and quality btw). I literally waited for 30minutes for this 3pcs, and during the wait they were calling by queue number ON the receipt. Suddenly out of no where instead of saying queue number, they called out “3pcs coconut tutu” instead.

Since i alr know that i was waiting for a long time, i started to walk towards the counter, but there was another lady whose queue was definitely way behind me (i was waiting around 15mins when she came). The lady reached the counter few seconds before me and the aunty handed her the tutu and she left immediately. I asked the aunty whether that was mine and after checking my reciept number she said yes, then obvsly im like ??? Why would they suddenly NOT call for the queue number to cause this inconvience. At this point I dont even want the tutu anymore like all i ordered was 3pcs, 30minutes is so not worth the wait. Now i asked them to cancel my order due to their mistake, surprise surprise they REFUSED. You would think that they will prioritise my measly 3 pcs after that, but no. I waited for another 15minutes and they were fulfilling other orders before getting to “mine” which i guess that they swapped my queue and that lady who took mine. Overall they made me wait 45minutes just for 3pcs of tutu and it was a huge waste of time and reallt disappointed that they couldnt even refund and cancel my order and forced me to wait even longer. My order is just under $3 like really.

Seriously the worse people running this business and I also know for a fact from other people that work in the mall that often the aunties don’t even wash their hands after they visit the toilet lol.

Please don’t support them.
author: ethan tan

review_text:
Bought waffles and the tutu kueh. Waffles sat there for about 10 mins getting soggy while waiting for tutu kueh that was not made in the correct order that we bought it, we bought first yet many orders got theirs first while our waffles got soggy.

Taste wise, disregarding the sogginess, waffles tasted bad, for a price of $3+ for waffles at a premium still tasted worse than the neighbourhood $1 ones, filling is stingy.

The tutu kueh also came at $3, and is very dry as well and tasted interesting. Do not buy.
Bought the corn with milk for $3, also quite ex but can’t go wrong with corn.
author: Nasrudin Salim

review_text: I wanted to buy peanut and chocolate tutu kueh but I understand from the staff cannot mixed ($3 for 3), so I ordered 3 peanut and 3 choc as recommended by the staff. I waited for few minutes and the other staff prepared and passed me my kuehs in a small plastic box container. It was not crowded at that time and I didn't really check. But when I gotten back home,  I found out it was chocolate and coconut tutu kuehs instead!! There was no peanut at all and I think the staff preparing mixed up my order! Very terrible and how can they mix up customer's order?! It was not even busy at that time! Will not patronize this stall anymore in future! Please reflect on your service quality.
author: Shawn Chang

review_text: Outstanding ramen that’s worth traveling for. In the running for the best in Singapore — it’s certainly among my personal favorite. Rich and beautifully balanced broth, toppings are also well done. I loved their pickled cucumbers. Service is fast and efficient.
author: incorgnetius

review_text:
Enjoyed a solid bowl of ramen here.  The broth was just right - one issue I face a lot with ramen broth is that towards the end the remaining broth gets too intense and sometimes overpowering and too salty.

However the broth from here was just right and I finished the whole bowl all soup remaining without the heavy feeling.

Also the hiyashi tofu is great. Didn't manage to grab a pic for it as we ate it too fast
author: Melloh Sg

review_text: Have been ordering their limited / seasonal ramen and IT IS GOATED 💯 I love their ramen idk what they do with it but sooo good. (This was their seasonal Otokogi ramen) Tried the seasonal Dan Dan mian back in Dec and enjoyed it a lot too. Pls keep these seasonal rotating / let some of them come back!!! 🥹❤️‍🔥
author: Yilin

review_text: Been on my to go list for a while, since nearby might as well go try. I wanted shoyu ramen, but doesn't seem to have. Seem quite popular with Japanese people. Ordered the new tantanmen chicken broth and it was very thick until a bit cloyed. The free boiled egg can skip, cannot make it. Noodles like our sg thicker meepok. Its an eat and rush go environment.
author: xinwei

review_text:
I ate the original tonkotsu ramen and aji fry. Tonkotsu ramen was not beyond I anticipated. But what I liked was very hot soup. I have almost never eaten ramen with hot soup in Singapore.
After I ordered, staff took frozen aji fry from a fridge facing diners' tables. I thought aji fry should be frozen, it's common. But after I saw the staff's action, I felt a bit disappointed. They should put the fridge inside kitchen.
author: RYKAYOYU

review_text:
We have visited Ma Maison at Anchorpoint quite a few times, but I finally decided to write a review. The biggest draw for us is consistency; you might not get the absolute "best" food in Singapore here, but you are assured a certain quality and you can tell they try their best.

​Our party of 5 decided to order one of each item from their Lunch Set Menu. It was a great way to sample everything.

​The Sets: Great value. Most come with a comforting soup of the day ( today is corn soup), salad, and drink. The Tonkatsu set swaps these for Miso soup and cabbage salad.

​The Star: Surprisingly, the Sirloin Steak Lunch ($27.80) was the winner. My wife is very particular about her steaks, yet she sang praises about this one. It was done very well.

​The "Competent": I had the Tonkatsu Set ($22.30). It was decent—the batter was crispy, but the meat was a bit too lean and not tender enough for my liking. The rice was also slightly overcooked. It’s a passable Tonkatsu, but not a memorable one.

​Other Dishes: The Omu-Rice, Hamburger Steak and Plate Lunch (Hamburger Steak & Omu-Rice combo) were visually appetizing and satisfied the rest of the table.

​Value:
We were thankful for a 20% Postcard Member discount for the festive period, bringing our total for 5 pax to just $105.99. For this quality and portion size, it is very reasonable. We will continue to visit for the reliable quality.
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text: Was seated at an area where the waitress gave me a heads up it would be slightly cold. Appreciated the heads up as it really turned out to be a bit cold. Service was attentive throughout. Had the Ho Ba wagyu steak and the famous hamburger steak. Both were really good though the Ho Ba serving was smaller than I expected. Probably should've clarified the serving size before. Desserts didn't seemed impressive on the menu so we passed on that. Overall tasty food but just slightly expensive next to serving size.
author: Danny

review_text: I was here today to take away my all time favourite from Ma Maison - its Choux Cream. At $2.80++ each, the biggish size of the Choux Cream and with the super generous amount of custard cream inside the pastry, make each one of it more than well worth its price. By the way, the Japanese Western food here is also very very good - something which I enjoy from time to time, but admittedly, I am more often here for my Choux Cream fix. Service here is very very good - very very polite and helpful. The dining ambience (which I find myself in when I dine here) is comfortable enough - although I (and this is just my personal opinion) a tad dark for me. That said, it doesn't deter me from dining here.
author: edtayjb

review_text: Been a long while since I visited this outlet. Food is still as good. Our fav remains for squid ink pasta and beef stroganoff. Very friendly and proactive service here.
author: Berlinda Goh

review_text: Quite worth to visit. Had the daily set lunch which was chicken nanban on that day. The set also comes with small salad, soup of the day and choice of drink. Service was great. Personally it would have been better to have more tartar sauce on the chicken, but overall the meal tasted honest and comforting.
author: Huang

review_text: You need to wait a very long time to eat the food. and they are not delicious at all!!! It has no local characteristics, l guess KFC is much more better than this!
author: Zoe Zhu

review_text: Essentially, Bountiful  Restaurant's customer sectors are tourist groups. It is located at level 3, it is unlikely to draw walk in customers. I believe they are willing to entertain if any.
author: TAN TEE YONG

review_text: Came here for elderly birthday celebration, food was mediocre at best, service of staff was bad; they were rushing to clear your dishes so that they can pack up and leave early.
author: Cliff Ang

review_text: Serving mostly tour groups.
author: Daisy Tan

review_text: Very good
author: Đinh Văn Hùng

review_text: Had a fantastic meal at Fish Mart Sakuraya. The mackerel was incredibly delicious and impressively large, perfectly grilled with rich flavour. The don was tasty and comforting, while the soba was smooth, refreshing, and well prepared. We finished with their crepe cake, which was light, creamy, and surprisingly good. Overall, a consistently solid spot for fresh, quality Japanese food that never disappoints.
author: Sean T

review_text: We came at around 1PM. Plenty of seatings. You can choose the fresh sashimi from the front counter. My friend ordered a sashimi platter, a ramen, a don & a dry noodles. Simple lunch but delicious. Ingredients are fresh. Good place for lunch which can talk comfortably within yelling to each other if you get what I mean especially an eatery in the mall 😆. We enjoy this catch up lunch meeting with fantastic meal. 👍
author: Why Why

review_text:
Been eating here with my family for many many years.
Today’s service raised a few hygiene concerns I wish to raise to the management.

First, they use a pen to write and tick off orders. When the server serve my dish, the pen tip touched my food.

Second, we were served sashimi and i let the staff know the swordfish tasted off. The staff came and took 1 slice of it to let the chef taste. Came back and say its not spoiled, its just ‘soft’. They offered to give us a new portion that was fresh but didnt clear the old one. I’ll just leave the pictures here to show the difference.

I really have nothing against you guys and have been supporting for a long time, but the amount of nonchalance during service reflects a level of attention that is concernjng for a establishment thats serving raw food.
author: seah szehao

review_text:
sashimi bowl is a fresh, vibrant delight. The salmon and tuna are buttery and rich, paired with bursts of sweet ikura and luxuriously creamy uni. Daily-sourced seafood shines atop perfectly seasoned rice. Generous portions, Instagram-worthy presentation, and friendly service (arrive early for lunch!). A must-try for sashimi lovers—worth every penny.

Pro tip: Ask for less rice to let the fish take center.
author: Christopher Ho

review_text:
October 2025: food was so so. Portion size was small for the price paid. However the dishes were fresh. I liked the octopus cubes side dish! Really fresh and tasty.

Nov 2025: re visit to give it another chance. This will be the last. The tempura batter was flat as though the wrong flour was used. Not flaky at all. More like normal flour. V disappointing
author: S Wun

restaurant_name: Jin Jin Dessert 津津甜品
review_text:
Power chendol uses thick gula melaka. Need to make sure it is well mixed.
Loved how the the jelly are placed, almost like we were mining for green gem
author: Alvin Heng

restaurant_name: Jin Jin Dessert 津津甜品
review_text: Super affordable chendol at just $2.50! The brown sugar syrup is super fragrant and really elevates the whole dessert.
author: Jackie

restaurant_name: Jin Jin Dessert 津津甜品
review_text: I think they call it the “power cendol” cause you have to power your way through the mound of ice and gooey gula melaka. Some might think it’s too sweet, but why eat desserts if not to satisfy a sweet tooth? Their gula melaka is powerfully sweet and has a hint of a burnt flavor, kind of like burnt caramel. After digging my way through the ice sweet coconut mound, I discovered all the red beans and pandan jelly underneath. My only question is how natural the pandan jelly is, cause its bright green color makes me think otherwise. Other than that, this cendol definitely packs a powerful sweet punch that I’d recommend anyone with a sweet tooth.
author: Jennifer L

restaurant_name: Jin Jin Dessert 津津甜品
review_text:
It has been many years that I have not been back for this very popular dessert stall in ABC market.
As usual, there was a queue even before the peak lunch hour as there were many orders for take away.
The stall holder was however kept bickering with an elderly female customer who was impatient for not being able to serve despite queuing for a while.
The power chendol was still as good, chewy gula melaka coated over the shaved ice, there were generous amount of other ingredients that added up for a wholesome bowl of delicious power chendol.
author: Sam Liew

restaurant_name: Jin Jin Dessert 津津甜品
review_text: I ate the tau suan and the bubur hitam today. They taste exactly like the ones I ate in my childhood! So good! They are still hot until the last drop, not like other stores where after 3 -4 spoons, become cold already. The youtiao is still crispy also, i ate in the afternoon. SO GOOD!
author: David Huang

review_text:
A simple steamboat with your usual steamboat ingredients like prawn, meat, fishballs etc. what makes this steamboat tick is the broth that accompanies these ingredients. As the broth simmers and takes in the essence of the ingredients that you dish inside, it becomes rich, sweet and very tasty. It helps that it doesn’t make you thirsty even after taking in copious amount of  the broth.

For the finale, cook the accompanying eggs and wash all remaining broth down!

This hawker gets very quiet when dinner time dawns upon as majority of the other stalls have closed for the day.

It helps that this hawker is wide and airy so it makes eating this steamboat more comfortable and you won’t end up drenching in sweat as you savour the sweetness of the broth.

Would recommend this store!
author: Damien Wong

review_text: It’s like going back to grandma’s home for steamboat on cny. The broth is tasty yet it doesn’t make u thirsty after meal. The ingredients are simple and fresh. The beef is surprisingly very tender and subtly marinated. Prawn paste is full of prawn bits. Ample seatings in the bright and airy hawker centre. Price is very affordable. Lady refills our pot readily and free tissue on table. Checks all my boxes for a hearty and comforting meal.
author: Calbee Cracker

review_text:
Tried this old-school steamboat stall for the first time and was thoroughly impressed. Since my family usually goes for heavy Zi Char or fast food, this was a much-needed wholesome and healthy alternative.

The highlights were definitely the soup and the ingredients. The boss shared that the broth is slow-simmered for hours without any MSG, and true enough, we didn't feel thirsty at all after the meal. The ingredients were incredibly fresh and affordable (Unlike HaiDiLao, expensive yet so so)—especially the cockles, which were a rare and delightful find! Homemade chilli 🌶 is fantastic.

To top it off, the service was heartwarming. Even though we stayed late and the drink stalls had closed, the boss kindly gave us two bottles of mineral water on the house. I highly recommend this spot for a nutritious and satisfying family dinner.
author: Mister Fong

review_text: My family always come to Ah Pang Steamboat. It offers an exceptional dining experience with its flavorful and wholesome soup. The absence of MSG ensures a clean, natural taste that enhances the quality of the ingredients. The food is fresh and well-prepared, making each bite delightful. If you're looking for a satisfying and healthy steamboat meal. I super like 🌶️ freshly made by them Ah Pang seafood definitely my first choice for steamboat . Highly recommended 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
author: Evelyn Lee

review_text:
The distilled steamboat experience, without all the frills of other hotpot restaurants, but doing all the basics right. The food served is fresh, the meat is tender, and the soup is comforting. All of this for a fraction of the price of other steamboats.

The preselected set meals are well portioned and i recommend getting them as they give you a good selection of meats and seafood.
author: Reynard Seow

review_text:
Seldom write a 5 star review
This place is basically 3 decades old

Chef - same person that founded the place

Chicken rice
1. Old school taste , note if u are 重口味 not exactly will be to your liking
2. I ordered white chicken breast rice with 2 eggs ( sunny side up )
The chicken was so tender and fresh, black sauce was standard infused with some chilli paste which they had prepared.
It was excellent

Have a taste of it and you will return.

Greatful for good food at best affordable price
author: Josh k

review_text:
Overall TakeAWAY experience is good.

Took the 100+ steps stairs from Leng Kee Road to the restaurant that cut-thru a scenic park that oversee the washing bay of Borneo Motors.

Senior uncle is very friendly and shared the restaurant is closed on FRIDAY.

Ordered a pack of $2 and a pack of $3.80 chicken rice to differentiate the quantity.

$2 pack came with 5-pieces of chicken breast meat and a small portion of rice as seen. Good proportion if you are NOT too hungry. Happy with the Chicken Rice !

The black enamel sauce, and red chilli sauce are very old school style (LUV it). 古早味。

Will come back and dine at this ULU OLD school Chicken Rice stall soon !!!
author: Alan Goh

review_text:
A decent chicken rice hidden away.
Opening hrs bit hard for me to catch but finally got to try.
The cuttlefish is really something special that most other chicken rice stall will not have.
Worth revisiting for me.
author: Samuel Ang (Zeonified)

review_text:
Old school chicken rice at old school pricing. Not frills but taste what an old school chicken rice should. You just need to set your expectations right.
Cozy and clean restaurant that is well managed. Lots of respect for the owner to keep it going.
author: Ryan T

review_text: Under the radar old school chicken rice which turned out to be a real treat. Fluffy fragrant rice paired with tender tasty chicken and good soup.
author: John Turban

review_text:
