author: Alvin Ho

review_text:
Fried fritters (you tiao) was consistently good but the other items were bad. The ham chim peng (salted bun) was tough with little fillings while the tau suan contained too much corn starch. Also, everything served in disposables.

Staff were polite and E-payment was available.
author: CK C

review_text:
I have very rarely given a 1 star review as there are usually some good points to speak of for even the worst foods I've encountered. For this franchise stall, I'm making an exception as I can't find anything that can remotely allow me to redeem its reputation for one of the  the worst butterfly and yellow bean filled doughball I've ever eaten.

The doughball was like it's name, unpleasantly doughy in texture and I didn't know it was possible to render the yellow bean filling into almost dry powdery form.

Butterfly was just not edible.. that's my take as I don't want to waste time with this stall as it's likely not redeemable or going to change.
author: LexTeo8888

restaurant_name: Ristorante Takada : Japanese Italian restaurant : Pasta Pizza Wine (Alexandra)
review_text:
Came here to celebrate a dear friend’s birthday and ended up enjoying a surprisingly memorable meal. We ordered a mix of pastas, fish, and steak — all well-executed and dressed to impress, matching the restaurant’s luxe Italian ambience.

But the true stars of the night were the desserts. Both the tiramisu and the Mont Blanc were exceptional, the kind that make you quietly pause mid-conversation just to take another bite.

A lovely spot for a special occasion, where the meal builds nicely — and ends on a high (pun intended).
author: Levi Aw

restaurant_name: Ristorante Takada : Japanese Italian restaurant : Pasta Pizza Wine (Alexandra)
review_text: We had a private party with a group, and they were very accommodating with advance orders and arrangements. The food looked and tasted delicious, and we were able to meet all of our requests. I personally highly recommend the beef cheek braised in wine.
author: eiko tamura

restaurant_name: Ristorante Takada : Japanese Italian restaurant : Pasta Pizza Wine (Alexandra)
review_text:
Nice little upscale Italian - Japanese restaurant in the neighbourhood. Been here multiple times for celebration dinner and also lunch and so far it never disappoint. Price vs quality ratio is good.
Love the Tiramisu!
author: Albert Kwan

restaurant_name: Ristorante Takada : Japanese Italian restaurant : Pasta Pizza Wine (Alexandra)
review_text:
Ambience: Cozy and small setting but yet still provides a sense of premium dining with its interior decor lighting and art choices. Located right next to a bus stop so very easy to get to.

Food: The food is great overall but at this price point ($189++ per pax) I was hoping to see more culinary experimentation  I enjoyed the appetisers especially with the corn mousse paired with uni. Would also recommend the Mont Blanc. Rest of the dishes were well prepared but wouldn’t say truly knocked it out of the park. Ingredients were fresh but I would point out 2 low lights - a small fish bone in the kanpachi sashimi and some grains of sand in the clam.

Service: Had a great experience with a Japanese lady who explained the dishes before setting it down and would help to fold the towel if you go to the bathroom. The other waitress who sometimes helped (?) however mainly just set the plate and left. Not sure what's the arrangement here but it would've better if the initial waitress served the dishes throughout the meal. Chef was friendly as well and would indulge in small conversations around the food. They also offered to change our set menu dessert to another so that we can try both their desserts.

Overall a decent place if looking for a sub-$200 safe Italian Japanese fusion experience. Would've been 5 stars if not of fish bone and sand in clam.
author: Danny

restaurant_name: Ristorante Takada : Japanese Italian restaurant : Pasta Pizza Wine (Alexandra)
review_text: Restaurant has been around for many years and the quality has always been very consistent. Menu changes often so there’s anyways something new to try. Service is also very good and the Japanese chef always makes sure that everything is done to the highest standards. Great place to visit both for lunch and dinner.
author: Teck Boon

review_text:
Seatings are extremely limited. We visited on a Saturday and it was crowded, with a queue formed outside the store. We were waiting in line with two groups behind us.

I was quite surprised when a lady who arrived after us walked straight in. We initially thought she was ordering takeaway. However, after she placed her order, a group inside left and 2 tables for 2 became available. She immediately took one of the tables.

While there were still seats left for us, I felt this was unfair to the other groups waiting patiently outside, especially a group of 2 behind us. What was more disappointing was that the staff did not intervene or manage the situation at all.

I understand that its free seating, but when theres an obvious queue, it would be good for the staffs to be more alert and considerate toward customers who are waiting in line.

While the food is good, the standard of customer service, particularly the tone that staff who is taking order could be improved. The tone may come across as offensive to some people and does not reflect well...
author: Joanne Chan

review_text:
interesting bao place! extremely limited seating, just one table for 4 and table for 2. the vegetable chips were yummy and very crunchy! for the baos, i’d highly recommend the chilli crab (AMAZING bun, but also very oily) and the blackened chicken (the garlic mayo was 💯, super crispy chicken 🤤). however, other than the chilli crab, the other buns were all steamed sesame bun, which did not really have any taste.

i would suggest avoiding the noodles, and just stick with the baos. they were quite underwhelming.
author: penny

review_text:
The following items were sampled:
1. Chilli crab bao - the fried bun was satisfactory
2. Truffle mushroom bao
3. Belly of pork bao - the meat was palatable and not fat, and the steamed bun was enjoyable
4. kakiage bao - the flavour profile was unclear; i believe the addition of a condiment such as mentaiko or teriyaki sauce may enhance the taste
5. Taro chips

The buns are smaller than a fist; ordering two different flavours is recommended for satiety.  The shop offers the option of having buns halved. Service speed was a noted area for improvement.
author: Wong Teck Jung

review_text: The restaurant serves unique and fantastic fusion food that I’ve never anywhere else. I love the idea of each dish was designed. Chili crab bao is a must dish to try. I had a great dinner here. Price is around $40 per person.
author: Nichy Han

review_text:
Walked in on a Sunday afternoon and got outdoor seats.
Food was great - the beef sando and beef pasta were my top choices. They didn’t get the doneness of the beef quite right as I had requested for medium but it came more like medium well but still tasted good.
Coffee was also very good.
I will come back again to try other dishes.
Overall a pleasant experience and delicious food.
By the way, they don’t serve drinking water but you can purchase still or sparkling water for five dollars.
author: Sel L

review_text:
Its always crowded even though its 1.30, but it is indeed the best fried rice in singapore, $7 but taste like any restaurant quality one

$7.50 red wine chicken rice, i thought it is the soup kind but its not. My motivation for f45 class nearby

$2.50 葱油饼

$2.50 cola wings is nice

$5.80 minced meat noodles is not what i expected, its not like zhajiangmian. I think their rice is better.

$1.80 韭菜盒子，猪肉饼

$6.50 bak kut teh

$6.20 12 dumplings

$6 herbal chicken

$6.70 fried dumplings

$3.20 chicken wrap
author: Ember Shen

review_text: Have been trying their food - fried rice, beef noodles and latest dish - chicken soup. Taste like home made food.
author: Joanne Lee

review_text:
Tucked in a corner with a simple set up.

An order of steamed dumpling consisted of 12 pieces.

Each dumpling was plump with finely minced pork with fragrant chive. They were tasty.

Condiments of minced garlic, Chinese chili oil, cut chili and soy sauce or vinegar options.

The elderly uncle was amicable and the shop enjoy quite a loyal following.

They also offer various frozen dumplings for takeaway.
author: MNG

review_text:
It's OK. Fried rice normal - not sure what the earlier comments talking about.
Dumpling pic I ate halfway already, it comes in 12 pcs.

Honestly mid. But the ambience is kind of unique (not necessarily good, just different) for a restaurant, so it's worth a try.

I genuinely think one could cook better food by themselves, but I guess if you're hungry, there's no really any option in walking vicinity.
author: Mr A

review_text:
I always pop into this stall to have a quick bite for supper before heading home. There are a lot of dishes on offer but I like to order the dumplings to eat.

They are all bite sized and a good ratio of meat and vegetables in each of them. The cook will pour a bit of sesame oil on it so they don’t clump together quickly. For $6, I think it’s a steal.

I also ordered their signature fried rice on a separate occasion. Pretty good I would say and it has cucumber bits in it, so quite unique!
author: Leon T

review_text:
Visited Janggut Laksa at Queensway Shopping Centre on a Saturday morning and it was a solid 8/10 experience.

The laksa here is wonderfully creamy, and in true traditional style, the noodles are cut up so you only need a spoon to eat—it feels very nostalgic. The bowl comes loaded with fresh prawns, fish cakes, and cockles. The only minor miss for me was the lack of an egg, which is just a personal preference.

Service was excellent; the lady boss is very friendly and my food arrived in less than 5 minutes! While the seating is a bit limited, the environment is comfortable enough. Plus, parking at Queensway was a breeze on a Saturday morning. Definitely worth a visit for an authentic bowl!

Wait Time:
author: E L

review_text:
Love this laksa & otah!
Laksa is amazingly addictive, the otah is well grilled!
Aunties shouting out the orders adds to the atmosphere!

All tourists should make a trip here!
author: Elaine K

review_text: A pretty solid bowl of laksa! The flavour of the soup was nice, though I personally would have preferred it to be a bit thicker. The portion was also a little smaller than I expected for the price. The real bonus here was the staff – they were incredibly friendly and welcoming, which really made the experience pleasant. A good spot for a quick laksa fix.
author: edwin

review_text:
The best laksa in Singapore! We live nearby and we highly recommend this Janggut Laksa from Katong!

We always order - laksa, curry chicken rice, chicken cutlet and iced lemon tea, milo dinosaur for the kids.

You can tell aunty not to put spicy chilli on your laksa.

Fast service. Food is yummy!
author: Mommy Chriszy Karunungan

review_text: I've always loved eating curry chicken rice and laksa here while listening to the aunty shout across the shop. It's been 17 years since I first came here and her voice is still full of power and vitality.
author: Jonathan Ong Wei Jie

review_text: We had our dinner on the 2nd day of CNY. We requested in advance for a round table. The otah and ngoh hiang were great appetizers. The chicken buah keluak were nicer than some peranakan restaurant. We had rendang and chap chai and prawns too. Finished off with apom bok kwa and sago Melaka. I love the decor of the place and the plates and dishes ie the way they cook reminds me of my grandma who is peranakan. The glass Bohemia look. Service was excellent. This is my second time here. All eight of us enjoyed ourselves including 4 who are between 23-26 years old. The other four were the parents. The Gen Z kept taking Instagram of the deco, Apparently the waitress told us they just opened a new branch at orchard towers which can sit 180 pax.
author: Estelle

review_text:
One of the best and most authentic traditional peranakan restaurants in Singapore. All the dishes are on point and well presented!

I missed taking a photo of the soup bakwan kepiting, which was amazing. Don't judge its size, it's small but so packed with crab meat and flavours!
author: Giang Nguyen

review_text: Found this place through google and decided to give it a try. Very nicely decorated Peranakan restaurant, whole restaurant is not big, feels very cosy and homely. Most of the signature dishes were great, probably give the nonya chap chye a miss. Celebrated my mum’s birthday too and thank you to the restaurant for the song and borrowed crown. Took us all by surprise and made my mum very happy. We will visit again sometime soon!
author: Angeline Ang

review_text: The cuisine is exquisite, and the ambiance perfectly complements the theme. Prices are reasonable, and both the staff and manager, Andrew, are friendly and courteous. However, the limited seating capacity is a notable constraint, necessitating reservations to avoid potential disappointment and wait times.
author: Bryan Tang

review_text: Dining at this restaurant gave me a fully immersed experience of the Peranakan culture that included non-stop Kerongchong playing in the background. The sound, visual display and TVs meant a constant stream of stimulation on top of the amazingly good food!
author: EL (Couch Blogger)

review_text: Went straight to the shop to order. Very fast and efficient. Apparently their systems freeze after 11pm so best to order in shop before then. After that gotta order via app. Didn’t know they have like an ultra small pizza so we ordered that. Staff also very nice to tell us all the good deals currently. Wouldn’t have known otherwise.
author: Daniel Bok

review_text:
Placed order on Foodpanda at 7:48pm. Received my order at 10:30pm. Estimated delivery time said 25-35 minutes. I called the store 4 times and no one answered. You guys should probably look for another profession. Clearly you kinda suck at what you do.

I live 850 meters from this place. Takes 7 minutes by car or 18 minutes to walk. I guess it takes 2+ hours to make a tiny pepperoni pizza (photo for reference). The pizza was so cold and hard that i could probably hurt someone with it. I can’t believe i paid $29 for this miserable piece of sheet.
author: J C

review_text: Would give them 0 stars if I could. Please do not buy unless you want unfresh pizza. Pizza hut or any other pizza shops are still better. We were appalled when we ordered delivery, and they had the cheek to give us individual slices of pizza made into a "whole pizza". Who knows how many days old are these slices.
author: Vanessa Allison

review_text:
Ordered immediately when the system is opened for the day to take in orders at 11am. There was an estimated delivery time given for 1140am to 12pm, and a bold statement for 30mins guaranteed delivery. But actual delivery took 2.5 hours and item arrived only at 1.30pm. Food was cold on delivery. Multiple calls to the branches went unanswered until at 1pm when someone finally picked up the line. The saving grace were that at least the guy over the phone apologised for the late delivery, and the delivery rider was also courteous and apologised for the late delivery.

Updated : 3 stars. Management reached out to apologise and provided compensation voucher. Considering that the phone guy and delivery driver were also sincere, apologetic and polite, these greatly cushioned the impact, hence will be adjusting the rating to 3 stars. Apart from the lateness, everything else is acceptable. Will give benefit of doubt that this might be due to a sudden surge in orders or staff shortages due to absenteeism.
author: Fatfatpanda

review_text:
Good Day,

The staff was very rude when I ask for the duration of the order preparation. There was 2 lady inside preparing the pizza, both use bare hands without gloves on and one old lady without mask on. Keeping talking with another lady while preparing the pizza. It was an unpleasant sight to see through the glass door from outside.
author: Alvin Lim

review_text: Had a dim sum craving in Redhill area and decided to pop by. This place serves above average dim sum, which is very much comparable in quality to big dim sum chains, without breaking the bank. The service was prompt and it feels like dining at your own home. Will be back!
author: S W Oon

review_text: I simply can’t get enough of these delectable and affordable dim sum from Zi Yean. My favourites include — ✔️ Golden brown, crispy fried prawn dumpling and fried beancurd skin roll with a whole firm and crunchy prawn within, that goes perfectly well with their homemade sriracha mayonnaise dipping. ✔️Pan fried pumpkin cake that is crisp and moist with added flavour and fragrance from the Chinese sausage. ✔️The highly sought-after mini egg tart (I managed to get my hands on it, on my third visit) with delicate, flaky crust and a good hint of buttery fragrance that melts-in-my-mouth when I popped it in.
author: AC Chan

review_text:
Shifting day for us , came here for a quick late lunch. Value for money dim sum . 40 plus for the 2 of us ! 🥰😍😘 Full & satisfying  ! 价廉物美！经济实惠！物超所值!
Cannot complain lah !!! A dim sum place & restaurant in a hdb estate! Very cool ! Good food at reasonable pricing  !  Come ! Come and support them ! Worth the trip ! Their Seafood and zichar restaurant is just next door ! Actually the whole stretch along the corridor is theirs !
In future we will probably be coming here very often ! 😛😋😝 大家都要来捧场啊 !
author: Shaolin Leong

review_text: Reasonable price, fresh, good taste. Especially the porridge and fried rice. Aircon is hardly there.. means not cold.
author: Samantha D.

review_text: Best dish is the yam ring. Crispy and interesting filling used - got even some white fungus. Good dishes include the prawn, the emperor chicken as well as the liver. The tofu cubes didn't look like the menu picture at all but was ok. Easy parking around the area.
author: Julian Lim

review_text:
Mei Ling Market & Food Centre may not be well known among foodie circles, but it’s truly a hidden gem. The place is quiet, well-ventilated, and comfortable even during peak hours. Best of all, you can still find cheap, delicious, and affordable local fare here.
If you’re around Queenstown, it’s just a short walk from the MRT — perfect for a no-frills, satisfying hawker meal away from the crowds and plenty of seats.
author: K Tan

review_text: The rating for Mei Ling Market is rather spot on. I would rate this a 3.85. The food centre is rather quaint and gives off an old school vibe similar to that of tiong bahru. There are murals to be found in the hawker centre, and there are some pretty interesting options to choose from. For example, the gula melaka soya beancurd, the beef brisket noodles and the chinese/western/japanese fusion curry rice. There is even a stall selling fishball noodles that drew a chord with me, as their signboard shows a wolf herring(西刀鱼) also known as saito to the locals. It is said that fishballs made from this fish are of good quality and fishballs used to be made from this fish in the past. Unfortunately, I have yet to taste their noodles. To date, I have not eaten anything bad in this hawker centre. The hawker centre is also very airy and spacious, and could be the best ventilated hawker centre in Singapore. I might have well stumbled on my favourite hawker centre in the Queenstown/Alexandra area.
author: Hatsune Miku

review_text: This hawker centre is clean, brightly lit, airy, cool and there’s plenty of delicious food sold here. It’s easy to get a table here. The stall holders are friendly and I’ve yet to try out all the foods.
author: Kriz A

review_text: This hawker centre is spacious and airy, we tried the fishball noodles with the long Q, the kopi O besides, the soya beancurd and the breakfast bee hoon… all good. Too bad I stay quite far, if not I will frequent this hawker.
author: Leow Een Tiong

review_text:
This is popular hawker centre at Queenstown area. It has a few very popular stalls.

This hawker centre is quite clean and convenient, next to the multi storey carpark.
author: Steven Teo

review_text: The shift manager Mr David seeing us had difficulty with ordering via the mobile phone, personally came over to our table to assist. I am very thankful for the excellent service. The pizza was delicious! I rate 5 stars for the service.
author: ongseebu

review_text:
Thank you Pizza Hut Bukit Merah! 🍕

The manager there, Wani, was so friendly and helpful. I was quite curious about what to order, but she suggested the new promo pizza and even recommended sides and add-ons for us. Because of her great suggestion, we didn’t have to think too long or wait.

Really appreciate the excellent service. Thank you, Wani! 😊
author: Nur Ailmiah

review_text: The staff here genuinely cares about their customers, they were courteous and pleasant. Ordered a regular pan BBQ chicken pizza and it was truly outstanding. Every bite I had was full of flavour and cooked to perfection! Highly recommended! Thumbs Up!
author: AL VIRTUOSO

review_text: Service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive. Food preparation time was reasonable even during busier hours. Pricing is slightly on the higher side compared to some other pizza chains, but the portion sizes and quality make it worth it.
author: Charisma Fauzi

review_text: Pizza is very good served piping hot. Mushroom soup is very thick and yummy.
author: Cherrlyn Lim

review_text: We enjoyed the time spent here. The service was excellent. We celebrated our friends’ birthday and xmas gift exchange! I would like to thank the service staff whom had served our table on 19 dec dinner. (12 of us) He was really patience and served us well. Keep up the good job!
author: Kris Ng

review_text:
It was our first time visiting Vineyard, even though we’ve been staying nearby for years. We went on a Friday evening, and while the restaurant was quite quiet at first with only a handful of diners, it gradually filled up as the night went on.

The staff were attentive and friendly, checking in to make sure everything was alright. We ordered two appetisers and two main courses to share — the food was decent, and the portions were generous enough to be satisfying.

Overall it was a pleasant experience to have our dinner here.
author: Sam Liew

review_text:
Service could be improved with better training. The seafood bisque was spilled to the edge of the bowl and the potato pave had shifted as well, affecting presentation. It would also be nice if staff could ask whether patrons want to take a video before preparing the Baba Au Rhum tableside.

Food was generally good. The seafood bisque was rich and flavourful. Potato pave was crispy outside and soft inside. Vongole was a bit spicy but the spice enhanced the dish. Oven-roasted poulet was tender and paired well with the sauce (also comes with a potato pave). Dessert alcohol was a little strong for me, and drinks were average.
author: Angelynn Seet

review_text:
It’s a great place for lunch, surrounded by lovely greenery. You feel like you are in a glass house.

The food is very good. The service is average. I had to ask for my cappuccino twice over a 45 minute period and still never got it!

The atmosphere is lovely, but the place has nothing to absorb noise and feels really really loud when it’s full
author: Anju Patwardhan

review_text:
Had a great Valentine's day dinner with my loved one. Service was great. Staff members were super friendly and welcoming.
Only downside was the booking disappeared on the day of the event but managed to secure one last minute.
author: Felix Lim

review_text:
been this kfc for so many times as i stay nearby and today i finally im writing this review because of my favorite Butterbear!! HAHAHAHA i am so happy when i saw
KFC x Butterbear!! as a big fan of butterbear, been to bangkok to visit the store and buy so many items from it!! i cant contain my excitement when i saw it!!

i bought Thai-Thai sauce bites box and Thao fritters!! honestly its better when it’s hot for the thai fritters and dip with condensed milk.
as for the Thai-Thai saucy bites chicken, for me is a little bit of spicy as im not a spicy eater hahaha but i still can finish it!!

been to this kfc to dine in, to take away and to even collect orders for foodpanda delivery, everything is okay, no any drama or any thing that needs to be a bad reviews hahaha. all is okay only can get crowded when its lunch time or dinner time which is normal.

i just wanna say thank u for collaborating with butterbear, and i wanna get the other butterbear blindbox but i got the drumstick butterbear hahaha but it’s still adorable!!

tbh i also miss the bbq cheesy meltz! idk if it will comeback or not coz that’s my all time favorite thing to order on the menu haha besides the original chicken and cheesefries!!

also just to add if u come here in the morning for breakfast, it’s actually peaceful!! came here a few times to dine in for breakfast and i realised how peaceful it is with the chicken porridge… perfect!!
author: ri fieschi

review_text:
Typical kfc joint. The self service machine was faulty when I used it. It co-share a place with pizza hut. No printing paper so you need to take a photo.

The man tou chilli crab is better tasting than macdonald's.
author: William Ow

review_text:
Had a great visit at KFC Bukit Merah! 🍗
Food was fresh and served hot, the place was clean, and the staff were friendly and efficient. A quick, satisfying stop that hit the spot—will definitely be back.
author: Maricon Rizelle Bago

review_text:
The food is good, but some of the workers, specifically the younger ones, are kind of awkward and rude tbh. Like, I accidentally pressed the ‘dine-in’ option and when she called my number, I just noticed that I ordered ‘Dine-in’ instead of ‘Take-away’.

Then, when I told her that I actually wanted takeaway, she decided to give me a reluctant look for like…a few seconds before repackaging it.

Yes, it is in fact my fault, and I know that it’s Ramadhan, but I’m also fasting myself. I just don’t see why she had to remain eye contact with me. It wasn’t even the rush hour bsffr rn🫩.
author: Syanna Widjaya

review_text: I loved how welcoming this place felt. The menu had plenty of options, and everything we ordered tasted great. It's the kind of place you stumble upon and then keep returning to.
author: Francis Bago

review_text:
If you love authentic Punjabi and North Indian cuisine, this place is a must-try gem tucked in Alexandra Central Mall! The moment you walk in, you’re greeted with warm Indian hospitality and an inviting aroma of spices.

🍛 Food & Flavors
The menu is a delightful journey of classic Punjabi dishes — think rich butter chicken, hearty dal makhani, tender tandoori platters, flavorful biryani, and soft, fresh naan and paratha. Many regulars rave about how well-cooked and flavorful the mains are, with plenty of options for both vegetarians and meat lovers.

🥘 Highlights
Butter Chicken & Chicken Biryani – tender, juicy, and satisfying.

Parathas & Naan – perfect accompaniments to the rich curries.

Lamb Shank Biryani – succulent and packed with flavor

Vegetarian options like palak paneer, dal, and paneer dishes also get high marks.

👨‍🍳 Ambience & Service
The restaurant has a casual yet cozy vibe, great for lunches with friends or family dinners. The staff receive praise for being friendly and attentive, making the dining experience even better.

They often serve an all-you-can-eat weekday buffet lunch at a good value if you want to try lots of dishes in one go.

Good for small gatherings and casual meals.

A lovely spot for Punjabi and North Indian food in Alexandra — flavorful, generous portions and lots of classic dishes to enjoy. A fantastic choice if you’re craving that rich, comforting Indian taste in Singapore! 🍽️😋
author: Sachin Kamble

review_text:
The starters chicken Tikka and paneer tikka was very good. However mutton biryani was way below standard.

First of all the quantity of biryani was very less and the taste of biryani was poor not expected of a biryani.

The chicken chilly garlic noodles was okay. Not very good however not bad as well. Overall an average taste.

The lemon soda and ice milo was not up to the standard.

Definitely have room for improvement.
author: Prasanth S Joseph

review_text:
I recently tried the meal plan offered by Yummy Punjaby, and it was really good. The food is fresh, flavorful, and of great quality. Every dish tastes like authentic Indian food, which is a real treat.

Visiting the restaurant was also a great experience. The ambience is nice and welcoming, and the staff are friendly. It’s a comfortable place to enjoy a meal.

It’s nice to find real Indian food in Singapore. Whether you try the meal plan or eat at the restaurant, Yummy Punjaby doesn’t disappoint. Highly recommended!
author: Tejas

review_text: Yummy Punjaby is a delightful spot for authentic Punjabi cuisine. The butter chicken was rich and flavourful, perfectly complemented by the fragrant garlic naan. The mutton briyani was well-prepared, with long grains of basmati rice and tender, spiced meat. Service was attentive and friendly, making the overall dining experience very pleasant. A great choice if you are craving hearty, traditional Punjabi food.
author: Isaac Sam

review_text: Yummy Punjabi Restaurant is a really nice place for authentic Punjabi food in Singapore. The food tastes fresh and homemade, with good flavors and generous portions. The naan and rotis are soft, and the curries are comforting and not too heavy. The staff is polite and service is quick, which makes the experience pleasant. It’s a good spot for both dine-in and takeaway. Love their affordable Punjabi thali.
author: Anupreet kaur

review_text:
Ordered a mac n cheese and was shocked upon receiving it. The outlook of it was disgusting. It was mashy and no sign of macaroni. Ordered this many times before and never once received something like that. Feedback to the staff and all she did was to insist this is normal and is like that. My child ate and she said it tasted weird and not the usual she ate but still the staff insisted it was like that.

Also, i ordered two toasties, as the toasties were quite dry- i asked to have some mayonnaise on it and was rejected again by the staff. She firmly said toasties do not have any sauce. While i understand that, but cant customers request to add? what is the issue with adding sauce.

This is the worst branch i ever visited. The others were more accommodative. We are definitely not visiting this again!
author: Sunny Side Up

review_text: I had an enjoyable dinner at Subway Mount Faber on Tuesday. It was easy to find a table. There are two staff mending this outlet and they are very helpful. I like the buffalo chicken with chipotle southwest sauce. Keep up the good work!
author: MrA

review_text: Bread looks sad. No more oatmeal raisin cookie. Safra members has 10% discount for ala carte sandwich but this outlet is more expensive than others.
author: William Ow

review_text: Enjoyed a freshly made sandwich, raspberry cheesecake cookie with Fanta Zero orange on a Sunday afternoon. This Subway is a small outlet at a corner of SAFRA Mount Faber. Sitting area is limited yet cosy, ingredients were fresh and staff, Raihan, was polite & diligent. Pleasant experience! 😋👍🏼
author: Serguin Tan

review_text: Visited on a Sunday night and would like to compliment a staff, Raymond. Even though he was the only one taking orders and serving the food, he remained very friendly and helpful throughout. The food was great, and the excellent service made the experience even better.
author: Jaslin Yeo

review_text:
Very happy with the courts upgrading though Court 1 has some issues but it's minor enough to ignore for casual players lile myself.

Played for 6 months here and always see the same faces all the time for other courts (which is good!)

Super hard to book but still bookable with some effort (not botting), very happy to know that the SAFRA staffs does court booking checks from time to time to allow genuine users/members to enjoy the facilities and yes! The booking App has improved to deter bots as well.

One of the better maintained badminton courts for SAFRA.
author: Donald “Ludification” Yeo

review_text:
Everything you need is definitely in here.

From bowling, gym, darts, soccer and more! There is at least something for someone here.

Lets dive in!

Carpark:
There are lots of Carpark spaces here under the main building. Charges apply as well ya. But do note that you may need to walk abit, to come over if in Safra, the lots are all taken up.

Amenities:
There are plenty to do here. From swimming to soccer, cycling..etc. Food can be found easily. We recommend coming here to see what you wana do🥳🥳😁😁

Location:
Nestled among residential areas, this is a great place to chill and unwind.

We particularly enjoy this place since it has all the amenities that one can use. And it also felt homely and true to its tagline, 'Building Bonds, Creating Memories'.

Recommended to all to pop over if you have yet to see what they have here.

Cheers!
author: Sten (Piqued Wanderer)

review_text:
I had the utmost worst experience here at Mount Faber Safra's Subway outlet. I came in for lunch, and there was no one watching the front of house. This malay lady was in the back of the outlet. Said, "Hello" to get her attention and all i got back was "wait". She came out and from the time i said my order till the very end of my payment, her service and her actions felt like she was so done with her job and life. I'm not expecting a standard service but atleast a decent one? I sat in dined in near the sandwich prep area, and as customers kept coming in, her service was the same throughout everyone. I was shocked to even hear her telling a father who brought his kid in, saying "What you want".

I don't usually review services in FNB as i am an Operations Manager myself in the same industry. But i honestly feel someone should make her reflect on her own actions. I wanted to review on Subway, but i don't see any replies to any reviews made. But i do observe Mt Faber Management actually do reply to reviews. So i want to make sure my feedback is reached and proper action is going to be taken.

For more info, The incident happened today on 17th Aug 2025 @ approx 4:10pm. I am in the store still as i am typing.
author: Joe Pereira

review_text:
I like to express my deep concern and disappointment regarding the persistent poor condition of the swimming pool water at SAFRA Mount Faber.

Having abstained from using the pool for the past few months due to the visibly dirty water, I recently returned on Sunday and Tuesday with the hope that the situation had improved. Unfortunately, it was immediately apparent that there has been no meaningful progress in addressing the issue.

The water remains cloudy and murky (See video), raising serious hygiene and safety concerns. As a regular pool user both in Singapore and overseas, I must say that this is one of the worst-maintained pools I have encountered. It is unacceptable for a facility of this nature to be in such a state, and frankly, it is embarrassing that this is in Singapore.

During my recent visit, I attempted a few laps but found it difficult and unsafe, as visibility in the water was reduced to barely two meters ahead. This not only poses a risk to swimmers but also reflects poorly on the standards expected of a SAFRA club.

I urge SAFRA Mount Faber to take immediate and decisive action to improve the maintenance of the pool. Regular and proper cleaning must be enforced without delay to ensure the facility meets basic hygiene and safety standards.
author: Anthony W

review_text:
Newly renovated gym open from 630am-1030pm with plenty of new equipments. Jerome, the staff here was really nice despite not on duty. He corrected my form and even volunteered to keep the weights as I was struggling with it. He was helping those with their post-gym recovery also.
Disclaimer: photo posted under his acknowledgement
author: My

restaurant_name: Rong Kee HK Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 - Redhill
review_text: I love unpretentious grub, and charsiew noodles is one of those dishes that might be readily available just about everywhere but finding one that satisfies is another story altogether. Asking a colleague to pack lunch for me from this stall i was honestly not expecting much, just something to fill my stomach would suffice. I added extra noodles and charsiew for a grand total of $6. Opened the lid and immediately the sweet aroma of smoked and caramelised pork filled my pantry. Suddenly my senses were all fired up. I stabbed a slice of the BBQ protein with my chopsticks, some edges were burnt, a good sign, it was a little harder than I would have liked but the taste and bite was actually above average, heck its not bad, pair it with the well sauced noodles that were perfectly al dente and I was hooked, before I knew it I had slurped down the entire bowl. I would have preferred if the meat was a little tender but otherwise this is a damn good bowl of noodles.
author: Jechtto

restaurant_name: Rong Kee HK Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 - Redhill
review_text: Convenient place to get simple chicken rice and char siew wanton noodles. Basic food, nothing outstanding.
author: Mark Yeo

restaurant_name: Rong Kee HK Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 - Redhill
review_text:
Fellow foodies, I had a mouthwatering meal at Rong Kee Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 in 75D Redhill Road!

If you're on the hunt for some epic roasted delights, this place is quite good too. I went for their roasted duck and chicken rice, and oh boy, it was so shiok!

The roasted duck was crispylicious on the outside, very tender on the inside, and that chicken was super tender as well. The flavor from the sauce were on point making the meal delightful with every bite.
author: Mr Food Uncle

restaurant_name: Rong Kee HK Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 - Redhill
review_text:
Overrated
Char siew and chicken was really dry and overcooked. Not even tender or juicy. Service is ok but guy a bit forgetful. I was the only customer but forget my egg :(
this is a stall I will only come to eat if I have no choice or no queue. Won’t say it’s totally cui but really not worth the price or calories
author: June Blog

restaurant_name: Rong Kee HK Roasted Delights 榮記烧腊 - Redhill
review_text:
Never given a one star review before but I guess there's a first time for everything?

Ordered 2 packets of roast pork rice with added meat and 1 packet of roast pork and duck rice. Requested no sauce and achar. Ordered from them previously and was given white rice.

Today the dude selling was pretty rude and hostile but nevermind, people have bad days. Came home and found sauce and achar in the rice. Nevermind. But dude why did we get chicken rice instead of normal white rice?

Not sure if this was intentional, but I'm disappointed. The last time I went the food was ok, but this time, the exeprience was a major no go. Probably won't be back.
author: Nicholas Goh

review_text: These are just some of the dishes we’ve enjoyed here over the years. The food has always been consistently good, and it’s a wonderful place to unwind over a meal. The calm, comfortable atmosphere makes it ideal for quiet conversations with friends or colleagues, allowing you to enjoy both the food and the company without feeling rushed or overwhelmed.
author: P Lim

review_text:
I had a great experience at Café Melba at Mediapolis. The highlight for me was the Chicken Sandwich – perfectly cooked, juicy chicken served on delicious, fresh sourdough bread with just the right crunch. The accompanying salad was crisp and well-balanced, making the whole dish feel light yet satisfying.

The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, and it’s a lovely spot whether for a casual lunch or a coffee break.
author: Bernhard R.

review_text: Perfect for families! There’s an outdoor bouncy house, a kids’ area, and a large grassy space for families to enjoy, plus a terrace seating area. All the food we ordered was amazing, the vongole pasta was especially good, perfectly balanced with garlic and chili. Service was excellent, and the staff handled our large group very well. Thanks!☺️
author: Kristee Chua

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐
Dining outdoors with a view of JTC park is a great way to convince yourself you’re eating “healthy.” The French fries are crispy, addictive, and disappear faster than expected. The broccoli side dish is nicely done and nutritious — though slightly less salt would help it stay on the health team. The burger is huge, filling, and clearly not shy about showing off its portion size. Overall, a very enjoyable dinner experience. Just a heads-up: coming from One-North MRT means a 15–30 minute walk, so driving is recommended unless you want to earn your fries with cardio first. 🚶‍♂️🍔🍟
author: Awesome Ness

review_text:
Visited for the first time today with my child. The restaurant is known for being kid-friendly, and that was certainly our experience. The interior is cosy, and I particularly liked the lighting, which adds a nice touch to the atmosphere.
The premises were clean and well-maintained. As for the meal, the food quality met the price point well. Overall, it’s a solid, comfortable spot for a family lunch or dinner. We would consider returning.
author: Jehyun Lee

review_text: Located next to the ATMs between the NTUC main entrance & the bakery, this outlet is a convenient stop for snacks or breakfast. It’s especially popular in the mornings, with many commuters picking up food after alighting from the nearby bus interchange on their way to work.
author: L Chan

review_text:
Potatoes curry puff fillings were very salty.

Staff didn't understand what is kopi kosong, she insisted that it is kopi black kosong despite my efforts to explain. She refused to acknowledge her wrong understanding.

Very hot inside the shop.
author: Lis Huang

review_text: I wanted to try their chicken pop corn with cheesy sauce but it is not available so I tried their Curry puff and it tasted super nice with a good combination of potato curry and egg.
author: Venkata Ratnam Rayala

review_text: Bought two “Real Chili Crab” Curry Puff.   The “Real” was what hooked me.  It tasted really bad,  there is no trace of crab meat.  One for $3.50 each,  two for $6.
author: Kaye Ng

review_text: Curry o puff has shrunk with the increase in price. Definitely not value for money.
author: Violin Ling

review_text: Loved the alfresco dining ambiance. The classic Hainanese pork chop is just as good as ever, and the beef liver was expertly cooked. Glad to see that they kept the craft beer selection.
author: Pamela S.

review_text:
blue and white bistro with #69Years
of history.

Happiest chatting with owner nostalgia lady as she loves talking and sharing with me her stories of her past traditions heritage, The food was very delicious and it was very worthwhile. Last visit it was 2022.

We will definitely come back again.

#HappyValentineDay2026
author: Yu Wei King

review_text: Love the rustic decor and atmosphere. Even the food tastes so traditional and has good wok hey. Highly recommend the dry fried bee hoon, hor fun and hainanese pork chop. Though can be quite pricey, come for the nostalgic vibes
author: nicole chan

review_text: I feel the main attraction is the nostalgia factor. It’s a place thrown back in time, from the floor to the furniture. Something that’s quite hard to find nowadays. The food for me was alright, nothing much to rave about. Price point was quite high and it’s not very accessible if you don’t have a car. Cash only.
author: Jennifer

review_text: They serve the best bee hoon and hor fun in Singapore.  Been coming here since I was much younger, which is more than 40 years ago. I absolutely love this place with all the lush greenery.
author: Stephanie Ong-Thomas

review_text: At Anchorpoint and decide to try out the lunch at jacks place here. New England’s fish and chips were delicious with the fish chunky and juicy under its thin fried batter skin.  Also ordered the baked cilantro lime chicken set with iced mocha, tomato  soup and pudding dessert.  Chicken is also reasonably well flavored and comes with mushrooms long beans and baked potatoes. Overall delicious meal.  Popularity can be seen with the crowd at weekend noon.
author: Ken Tan

review_text:
lovely place food and staff

in the past i had bad experiences with jacks place (other stores) which deterred me from eating at jacks place. this time i visited as i had a voucher and i completely changed my mind 180°. ill actually visit jacks place anchorage again.

the staff was so nice and welcoming. they brought us to our table very quickly, and also helped us when we had issue with our voucher.
they are very attentive as well, noticing the smallest details, like when we finished our food, they served the ice cream without us waiting for it.

the food is also really good. the whole place is nice and clean, cutlery is clean, the food is cooked really nicely. i would say this is worth the trip and i would actually consider visiting again. thank you for the amazing experience.
author: e t

review_text: We used to frequent Jack’s Place for their value set lunches years ago, and today we chanced upon their pre‑Christmas set lunch and decided to give it a try to relive old memories. I chose the NZ Striploin Steak set lunch ($18.50++), which came with the usual soup, garlic bread, coffee or tea, and dessert. While the steak wasn’t outstanding, it was well worth the price paid. Service was standard, and the environment was conducive for dining.
author: LP Pua

review_text:
Came here to have dinner…
Jack’s place is an iconic old dame.. has been around for a few decades…way before Aston’s or Collin came into the picture.  And many places now is all about aesthetics then food.
Jacks place is food first, aesthetics takes a back seat.

The grilled salmon with baked potato was good. The fish was nicely grilled / baked to perfection. And the fish portion was thick for this price. A lot of places elsewhere the salmon portion are pathetic.
Came here once a while to support all these eateries…
author: YL Wong

review_text:
Love the food, especially the baked potato topped with sour cream and spring onions. Staff were friendly too.

The waitress noticed that the chef gave the wrong sauce and went back to the kitchen to get the correct one for us without hesitation. It’s really a nice change of pace as at other restaurants, you have to notify the waitress staff instead. Kudos to this staff who spotted the mistake first.

It’s pricy but a good spot to have a nice meal once in a while. Would recommend this place to have a good meal.
author: Kurohime242

review_text:
It was okok only. Chicken cutlet rice (large) was actually quite small or at max normal-portion only and it was ~$8. The curry was soso, nothing special.

Service staff was a the shout-at-kitchen type and they kept asking customers if they had already ordered because there is no proper delineation of roles. Not many seats available so do eat fast if possible
author: Lee JI

review_text:
7/12/2025
Nice laksa.
Can be quite crowded at times.
Not bad eat, can try.
author: Jinghorjiak

review_text: Went there for my curry/laksa fix after 3 months away from Singapore. Curry chicken was disappointing and salty with 3 pieces of untoasted square gardenia kind of bread. Laksa was watery. And both selling for $6. Otar @ $1.80/piece is probably the best tasting item. Place is small, uncomfortable and even a little filthy. Have to remind myself not to frequent the place again.
author: Eng Siong Lee

review_text: My go to stall when I am at Queensway. Love the way the curry tastes. Tried their curry chicken cutlet which is just as good as curry chicken.
author: Vincent F

review_text: Always love a good bowl of laksa. As others have pointed out, the gravy seems to be more watery these days, but nonetheless still tasty. The large bowl at $8, while appearing to be slightly on the steeper pricing, is chock full of prawns and cockles. Otah ($1.80) is also pretty good. The stall remains popular, that even at 4pm on a Saturday, people are waiting for a table.
author: Samuel Swee

review_text: Warm and old school vibe. Mainly chinese food. Cheap and good. Stalls that have been around for decades. This is a tourist spot and part of the Tiong Bahru heritage trail. I highly recommend the mixed pork porridge from Hua Yuen Porridge at the level 2 hawker centre of the market. It's cooked in cantonese style, in rich broth, makes a very tasty and satisfying meal.
author: Ying Yih Low

review_text: One of the best food centre here. Not only because of the sheer number of popular food stalls but also its comparatively comfortable environment with its high ceiling and the well spread-out space where all the long queues hardly causing obstruction to the tables, unlike the scenarios you would often witness at places like Golden Mile Food Centre.
author: Mr Yang

review_text:
This hawker center has the best layout for stalls that we've seen. They are all in a row, so you can see them all at once, instead of there being rows after rows of stalls. There's also plenty of seating, seemingly even when it's busy.

We got two iced coffees at 33 Cafe, and two iced sugar cane drinks at Wang Wang Sugar Cane. All the drinks were made right in front of us, and were solid. This place is underrated and worth a visit.
author: Dan Pieloch

review_text:
I have been to this hawker centre more than a few times.

There are many good food stalls at this eating place. Hokkien Mee lovers should try the noodle at Hong Heng Fried Sotong Prawn Mee stall #02-01.
author: Raymond Tan

review_text:
178 Lor Mee (*) $4.50
- first photo before mixing
* 1 pieces fish fritters
* Bits & pieces of batter
* 2 pieces of miserably extremely thin fishcake slices
* 1 pieces of meat

- 2nd photo after mixing and eating
* 1 pieces fish fritters (very little fish meat, all flour batter)
* Bits & pieces of batter (flour only)
* 2 pieces of miserably extremely thin fishcake slices (taste not fresh)

* Beehoon Mee (Normal)

Service - stall owner or helpers' attitude really bad

Summary - not worth coming back again when there are much better alternatives that are value for money.

7 Tiong Bahru Fishball (*) 8 for $2
- fishball got no fish taste, just salty
- fishball is springy

Wang Wang Sugar Cane (*)
- Coffee $1.40 does not taste nice at all
author: DAFFODILUK

review_text:
Lovely little place, very tasty. Lots on offer as well.

I arrived about 8:30 and a few of the tables had gone. Its now 9 am and most of them have gone now.

There are some small tables and chairs outside but the majority are inside where it is air conditioned.

All the baked goods are freshly made and you can have them hot or cold. The almond croissant is the best I've had outside of Paris.

24 SGD For 2 baked goods and a chai tea.

I would definitely come back here.
author: chris cook

review_text:
I visited Tiong Bahru Bakery around 9 a.m., and it was relatively quiet, making it easy to browse and order. There are plenty of seats, including additional seating further inside the shop, so finding a place to sit wasn’t a problem.

I ordered the following items:
・Croissant
・Pain au Chocolat
・Raspberry & Vanilla Cream Ribbon
・Banoffee Pain Suisse
・Canele

The Raspberry & Vanilla Cream Ribbon looked very cute, and the raspberry sauce inside added a nice sweet-and-tangy flavor that made it especially delicious. The Banoffee Pain Suisse was rich and indulgent, with a generous filling of chocolate and banana sauce that was very satisfying.

Both the croissant and pain au chocolat had a great buttery aroma and tasted consistently good. The canele had a nicely firm exterior with a moist interior.
Overall, everything was high quality, and it’s a great bakery for breakfast or a light brunch.
author: TooGood

review_text:
Always a must-visit whenever I’m in Singapore. This is the flagship store of Tiong Bahru Bakery, and you’ll also find their branches all around the city.

We stopped by for breakfast and ordered a mix of savory and sweet pastries. The space is beautiful and welcoming, filled with that irresistible smell of freshly baked bread. There are plenty of seating options, both indoor and outdoor, which makes it perfect for a relaxed morning.

Highlights for me were the Kouign-Amann, the sandwiches, and the hot chai latte—everything was beautifully made and absolutely delicious. I even took a Kouign-Amann to go, and it stayed fresh throughout a two-hour flight.

Highly recommended and definitely not to be missed when visiting Singapore.
author: Rinny Hafid

review_text:
I stopped by after their renovation and new concept, and I love the wider assortment of choices 😉. I tried the lychee, strawberry & rose croissant — very sweet, but the fragrance of the combo was lovely. I asked for it to be warmed slightly, and the cream oozed out even more 😋.

I just wish their baking was more consistent; sometimes it’s overbaked, sometimes it’s just right. Still, it’s a nice spot for a break. They just need to add some acoustic panels — it’s quite noisy for a café.
author: Monda S.

review_text:
I visited Tiong Bahru Bakery three days ago and ordered two breads for takeaway, including a croissant sandwich with mushrooms. I am extremely disappointed and honestly quite disturbed by what I experienced.

To begin with, the croissant sandwich was overly salty and unpleasant. However, the real issue was the hygiene. I found a strand of hair outside the packaging, which I initially tried to ignore. Unfortunately, when I started eating the sandwich, I discovered another piece of hair inside the sandwich itself, mixed in with the mushrooms. It was not immediately noticeable and could easily have been consumed if I hadn’t been paying close attention.

Finding hair inside food is completely unacceptable and deeply unhygienic. This is not a small oversight, it reflects very poorly on your food preparation standards and overall cleanliness.

I contacted the management team directly to address this issue before leaving a public review. I was told that they would investigate the matter and that they would contact me the next day after looking into it. However, despite this assurance, I have not received any follow-up or communication from them at all.

What made the situation even more frustrating was the way the matter was handled during our conversation. Rather than addressing the issue with concern and accountability, the response suggested there were doubts about my complaint and that it would need to be investigated carefully. I was even asked whether I had visited other places, despite the fact that I had just opened the packaging for my dinner.

This entire experience has been incredibly disappointing. Not only was the food unhygienic, but the handling of the complaint has shown a lack of professionalism and customer care. Being told that I would be contacted and then receiving no response only adds to the frustration and leaves me feeling completely disregarded as a customer.

I will not be visiting again. I sincerely hope management takes this feedback seriously, improves hygiene standards, and learns how to handle customer complaints with transparency, respect, and responsibility. This experience has significantly damaged my trust in your brand.
author: 이정현

review_text:
Overall a good experience and considering it’s CNY eve, the standards Ting Heng delivered is above average. Went for the 888++ set and CNY eve was packed with people.

We settled in quite fast as we made reservation way before hand and we spent about $1096 for 9 pax. Seafood is really fresh and I’m particularly impressed with their lobster noodles and the steamed fish. As they have a full house to serve, the standards are not compromised and our family was glad  with overall food standards. Their seafood lived up to their name and I will return in future for their live seafood for sure.

We ended off the dinner with red bean paste soup and we love the dessert too as it was not too sweet. Some of us even had two bowls of the dessert :)
author: Lee Wayne

review_text:
Food is very good. But the prices are on the higher side.

Each plate of prawns costs 25.5++, for only around 5 prawns. That adds up to ard 6 dollars per medium-sized prawn after taxes. Taste-wise, its very good. Loved the signature prawns... Just a tad too expensive for my wallet.

Crab bee hoon was also fantastic. But it cost ard 84++ per portion. And the crab is only 500-600g at the max... Maybe even smaller?

Of course, there is still no lack of loyal (and probably wealthy as well) customers for this place. Just that prices have went up quite a abit...(probably because of rising rents and manpower costs in the fnb industry)...and the value for money is now harder to justify.

Would have given it 4.5 stars though if google allows for it.
author: Hong GZ

review_text: Every time I pass by this Ting Heng Seafood Restaurant it is always packed. Being in & out of S’pore for so many times and staying around this chinese seafood restaurant but haven’t had the chance to try their food. Finally got the chance to taste their seafood and have done it straight in 2 days for dinner🤭. 1st night simple dinner with steam red grouper and garlic stir fried sweet potato leaf c/w 2 Heineken. It was delicious. The steam fish was SUPER fresh and vege was excellent. 2nd night we tried their signature dish in the menu - red grouper steam pot with add on extra vegetables and deep fried FOO CHUK & black pork meat slices. I still remember the last time the best same fish head steam pot I had was almost 10 years ago in Pontian, Johor. After that none of the same steam pot I had even come close to the taste of it. This kind of 魚頭爐 is 潮州style and must have good technics to cook the base soup, all factors count including the freshness of the ingredients. And most importantly, NO MSG. Well we really enjoy the dinner and service was good. Inside seatings are limited and outdoor seatings are plenty. I saw a lot of customers brought their own whiskey & liquors and came to know that there is no corkage charges. Will bring my family here in future during their visit. 👍👍👍
author: Why Why

review_text: Yummy, yummy, YUMMY!  We ate outdoor on a very hot evening. But the wonderful food made up for the discomfort. Wish they have multiple fans for each big table!!
author: Lois Amaral

review_text: Busy restaurant which serves Fish Steamboat as signature. We ordered some standard dinner dishes as we do not prefer steamboat. Food was excellent (all 4 dishes we ordered). Price was very reasonable. Will patronize this restaurant again.
author: J S

restaurant_name: De Golden Spoon Seafood 金匙小厨
review_text:
These 3 dishes are my absolute favourites here! 😍
Came back again mainly for the coffee pork ribs — the flavour is so unique and addictive. I honestly haven’t found another place that serves it with the same taste so far.
The prawns were very fresh, perfectly cooked and some sauce which the boss recommended. It was sinple but delicious. We ended our gathering with the crab bee hoon, which was rich, comforting and great for sharing. 🦀
Such a satisfying meal with great company. Definitely a place I would come back to again!
author: Onycass Lim

restaurant_name: De Golden Spoon Seafood 金匙小厨
review_text:
Celebrated CNY here and was impressed by the quality of the festive menu. The yu sheng had a great balance of sweetness and crunch, the fish was tender, and the prawns were fresh and juicy. Each course was served promptly and piping hot.

What stood out was how well the kitchen managed the timing, even though the restaurant was full. Service staff were attentive and quick to refill tea and clear plates. Overall, a satisfying reunion dinner experience. Worth booking early!
author: Lim Joline

restaurant_name: De Golden Spoon Seafood 金匙小厨
review_text: The place is clean and always bussy. The food is ok. My favorite food was coffee rib, its something new for me. The vegetable also nice, forgot the name. The crab bihun was ok. The parking space is huge. Easy to access.
author: bimo ariobuwono

restaurant_name: De Golden Spoon Seafood 金匙小厨
review_text: Had a wonderful dinner and all dishes were delicious, service was prompt and excellent. We had change of plates and top of tea frequently.
author: A T

restaurant_name: De Golden Spoon Seafood 金匙小厨
review_text:
Very yummy food, especially the noodle with crab. Service was a little bit slow. Recommended to make a reservation in advance.

There are air cons inside the restaurant, but when it is crowded, it becomes very noisy. Outside does not have air cons, but it is better for us as it is less noisy.
author: Gvavalin Mahakunkitchareon

review_text:
Came here with a group of 12 and overall, I agree with the general reputation — solid, old-school zi char with reliable flavours.
Food was consistently good across the board. Highlights include the coffee pork ribs, which were rich, aromatic and well-executed, and the steamed fish, which was fresh and nicely done. The yusheng was generous with ingredients and great for sharing.

One pleasant surprise was the fish maw soup — quite premium for a zi char place. It wasn’t just fish maw; it also included sea cucumber, abalone and mushrooms, giving it a rich, hearty and almost banquet-style feel.

👍 Service was warm and thoughtful. Staff helped us take a group photo and even checked if the photo turned out well — a nice personal touch.

🚗 Parking is very convenient, with a car park right in front of the restaurant.

⚠️ Areas for improvement:

Lunch can be quite warm. Even with fans, the space under the canopy felt stuffy. Adjusting fan direction/placement could help.

Table arrangement for large groups needs improvement. For 12 pax, the table felt cramped and no bigger table was arranged, which affected the dining comfort.

💬 Overall
A reliable and enjoyable zi char spot with good food and friendly service, though comfort and seating arrangements can be improved.

Would still return — but probably for dinner instead of lunch 👍
author: YM Tan

review_text: Had a cny dinner here with friends. Reasonably priced. Food was still on point but serving size seemed smaller than the last time. 2 dishes that stood out for me is the sweet n sour pork and the de shell salted egg prawns. Their signature is also the champagne pork ribs.
author: Kelvin Chua

review_text: Had dinner on a Sunday so super busy time but manage get a table. Sweet sour pork is succulent and crunch not so sweet like most other restaurant. Cereals Prawns was big and fresh juicy. Salted egg Fried Sotong not recommended as too wet with a lot or bater. Overall highly recommended 👌 and food was served fast eventhough packed.
author: Paul Lui

review_text:
Traditional zhecar with quite a quality food.

We had a great meal at Por Keng Eating House 1996. The standout dish for us was the Champagne Short Pork Ribs. The pork was tender, nicely glazed, and had a good balance of sweetness and aroma that made every bite enjoyable. We also tried several other dishes, and everything came out flavorful and served hot. Portions were reasonable for sharing, and the prices felt fair for the quality.

Service was prompt and straightforward. The staff checked in on us and made sure dishes came out in a smooth flow. The place has that classic local zi char vibe, perfect for a casual meal with family or friends.

Overall it was a satisfying dining experience and worth returning for those delicious pork ribs alone. If you are around the area and craving a hearty meal, Por Keng Eating House 1996 is definitely a good choice.
author: Hary Luo

review_text:
One of the best zhi char places I’ve been to in singapore. Literally a hidden gem.
Waitress were attentive and fast. I would rate the SASP being one of the best I’ve had internationally. The tofu was so silky and smooth, I could have devoured the entire dish myself.
I would definitely be back to try more dishes. Highly recommend!!
author: Who’s Khoo

review_text: One of the best local Bak Kut Teh, within walking distance from Havelock MRT Exit 5. Peppery Soup Base with tender meat, good to go with their homemade warm and crispy you tiao and Braised Intestine (no smelly taste at all!). You can opt for refreshing Seaweed and Mushroom Soup as well. Though we only ordered 1 premium ribs, the staffs were kind enough to give another bowl of soup which also topped up when the mains is refilled.
author: Alexander Reinaldo

review_text: Had lunch here and was surprised by the meat on the pork ribs that were fall-off-the-bone tender. One of the nicest pork ribs I've ever had with no  porky smell at all. Flavour however was a tad on the peppery side and  felt the soup was a bit lacking in depth. The fried prawn roll was not so good as there was barely any shrimp in it and did not have a springy texture. A decent find if you're in the Havelock area and crave bak kut teh! However, the place is a bit chaotic and old school so some may not find it so comfortable, even though they do have air conditioned seating.
author: Elizabeth Cheong

review_text:
Very wonderful meals we (my husband & I) had today. We took the MRT and from Havelock MRT (Exit 3), we walked to Ya Hua Bkt Eating House at Isetan Building.
The soup is free flow and serve hot as other reviews mentioned, without asking. Service is Top Notch. Best BKT in Singapore.  Also, they accept Alipay which is so convenient. Feeling blessed with such operators and staff. They truly give their BEST! Thank you for your service, taking gd care of your customers. My daughter brought us here long ago. Now that we are here, we tried coming on our own.
author: Lillianne Soon

review_text: It’s been awhile since I’ve been back here. This used to be my fav  outlet as it’s the main branch IMO. But I was sorely disappointed. Standards have dropped drastically. The soup was lackluster, mee sua has the unpleasant flour taste.  No longer the traditional taste. Meat slices covered with too much flour. The only highlight, was the Yutiao! 🤣 With  the price increase, I definitely won’t be back anymore.
author: D. Lim

review_text: Restaurant is clean and quiet but I went there after lunch peak hour at 14.30pm. Order a pork kidney soup, steam egg, braised small intestines, tau pok, salted vegetable, rice and Coke lite. Total cost is $47.60. Price is abit expensive (was expecting around $40 max) but food is delicious. Was too hungry so I took a bite before taking photos.
author: Lawrence Ho

review_text:
Chicken rice : 6/10 rating
Chicken meat : 5/10 rating
Chee Cheong Fun : 7/10 rating
Chicken liver : 2/10 rating

This Boon Tong Kee Is at River Valley branch.  This is a popular chicken rice chain in Singapore.  I find this stall the chicken rice okay, unfortunately chicken meat not as juicy and fresh comparing to the main Balestier stall.  Also the chicken liver is very hard and tasteless.  But I like the Chee Cheong Fun.  If want to eat Boon Tong Kee chicken rice, I will suggest you guys to go the main Balestier stall.
author: Louis

review_text: Visited the well-known Boon Tong Kee in Singapore. Their signature chicken rice was delicious, and the seafood dishes and kang kong were all great. The restaurant is spacious, and the food came out quickly, which made the experience even better. A solid place to enjoy local Singaporean dishes.
author: Catherine

review_text: Their chicken is good. Like toufu and the three eggs vegetable. I am surprised what the Zichar they offer and quality even though some say it drops but I like this stall though . Just a bit narrow space
author: J A

review_text:
We arrived at 11:45am on a Wednesday and were seated promptly. We wanted to sample Chicken Rice again but not in a Hawker stall. We were going to Great World Mall anyway so we stepped out to dine at Boon Tong Kee at River Valley Road.

Food - 5*, the Chicken Rice combo meals provided great value at S$10 each. We got one with Crispy Tofu and another with Shrimp Fritters. Service was fast indicating that the Chicken Rice Meals were ready beforehand. They provided twin sauces of Dark Thick Sweet Soy and Chili. Pickled vegetables were also given together with the Chicken Rice. Reduced Chicken drippings/broth was poured over the steamed chicken. The chicken was tender, succulent and flavorful specially when the sauces were mixed in. The rice was fragrant with the mild taste of chicken broth.

The sides we chose were a good foil to the steamed chicken. Since both Tofu and Shrimp Fritters were fried, they provided another level of texture with their crispiness. The tofu had a mayonnaise based sauce while the shrimp  had honey based.

Service - 5*, service was prompt, attentive and cordial

Atmosphere - 3*, clean and functional
author: Chito Mauleon

review_text:
More upscale chicken rice place with a slightly premium price tag. At least there’s aircon to escape the heat.. Chicken was good and succulent. But came here mainly for the fried tofu.
Paid about $40 for 2 set of chk rice and 10pc fried tofu.
They also sell other “zhi char” dishes.
author: Lim

review_text:
Convenient, reliable spot for local Western and Hainanese/Asian comfort food, offering a nostalgic atmosphere similar to other branches but somewhat  overpriced for the portion and quality.

The menu has seen updates over time, with some older favorites being replaced.

Spaghetti in Tomato Sauce w Chicken ($13.80)
Aglio Olio w Chicken ($13.80)
Aglio Olio w Chicken & Fungi ($13.80)

= Chicken Curry w Rice ($14.80)
= Hainanese Pork Chop w Rice ($15.80)

= Horfun ($10.50)
= Beef Horfun ($11.50)

Ice Lemon Tea ($3.20)
- Plain water (50 cents) !!

+ There are holiday menu items (e.g. Xmas roasts, Prawn Pasta) but they're not cheap.

+ Prices are nett. NO Service charge.

+ CDC Vouchers can be used here @@

- Cashier lady can be less hurried in chasing customers to order as the menu is quite extensive.

- SLOW cooking time. 20 min wait is possible.

+ One of few places nearby with long tables suitable for 6-8 pax, great for colleagues having a lunch gathering. The spaciousness and quiet environment helps.

+ There is aircon, but it can get warm  and smokey if sitting near the open cooking area behind the counter.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: For those working in the Bukit Merah area, this Han's outlet offers a great "no-frills" environment. It functions very much like a large community canteen, providing plenty of seating which makes it ideal for casual business meetings or a quick lunch break. The offerings are classic and consistent, focusing on simple comfort foods that get the job done when you need a reliable energy boost.
author: Flo Yeow

review_text:
Haven't been to Han's for some time.

Decent food, decent service, decent place.  Good for a group lunch coz the space is huge. Not the cheapest though.

Add-on soup and drinks costs additional $5.  The cake costs $4.80 (on discount).
author: Yew Fai Tong

review_text:
I recently ordered the Christmas platter from Han’s and had an excellent experience, thanks especially to Sin Tat’s outstanding service.

I first called the outlet to enquire about the platter, and the phone conversation with Sin Tat was clear, pleasant, and helpful. He answered all my questions and made the ordering process smooth.

When I visited the outlet to confirm the order and make payment, Sin Tat continued to provide exceptional service (25 Dec pick up between 11am-1pm). He was attentive, professional, and clearly very hardworking. His genuine care and efficiency left a strong positive impression.

Thank you, Han’s, for the great experience and special thanks to Sin Tat for a good job!
author: Krista E.

review_text: Nice and cosy family restaurant! Has a wide variety of dishes from western to asian favorites. The Hong Kong noodles were especially nice with wok hei! Would recommend for a easy and quiet spot for a quick meal!
author: Wei Liang Ng

review_text:
I think it's time I will say goodbye to LJS, I been eating at LJS since I was 14yrs old. More than 30 yrs now , how I long to have the 1980 LJC ,like Pirates combo, chicken pedlegs combo ,corn on the cob, pecan pie, apple pie,

I ate at Far east in 1980 ,the batter was golden brown , beautiful golden brown, the shrimps was like butterflies when they cook, they even have 3 pieces of big fried fish balls

Now the food appearance and taste hmmmmm sad really sad ,I eat for the sake of eating as it cost me $9.50 ,you just look at my video,they just dump the products into the batter like a lump of batter on my fish, chicken n shrimps ,dark color like they don't care anymore the quality.

Fish just so dried Sigh, it just so sad,
Sad really really sad .

Good bye Long John Silver.
author: Feliz

review_text: Visited Tiong Bahru outlet on 23rd Nov around 4pm. Food was past holding time, dried and oily. Crumps dark and hard. Entire restaurant was empty but didn't cook to order. Tartar sauce was left standby openly on the table but doesn't serve to customers ordering fish? Why can't squeeze on dish tray when request. I urge those in charge to look into this matter urgently or else you're losing more customers.
author: JOHNNY KOH

review_text:
Improved menu and touchscreen ordering.

Alaska pollock was nice and soft. Spicy chicken was mild spicy.  Crumbs were same delicious standard. Clam chowder was diluted and watery, disappointing compared to other fastfood brand. Black coffee was strong and aromatic.

Self-collect food by queue numbers flashed on display screen.

Tables were dirty. No staff available to clean.  We had to get some servettes and clean the tables and seats ourselves. Had a basin for washing hands.
author: Lenon Tan

review_text: Disappointed again with this branch in Tiong Bahru  as I’ve ordered Crazy Potato and ask for extra crumbs at the counter. Seems like they are more interested to chat among themselves than to take note and served it right.
author: Ivan Chong

review_text:
Slow service. See pic for small chicken. Questioned me when I said an item was missing. Made me bring the whole tray back. Overall just poor.

The self order kiosk doesn’t even print the receipt. The chilli sauce not topped up.
author: Taufiq Nazri

review_text:
This has been one of my go-to lunch spot for years. Among all the outlets that I frequent, I would say the one at Tiong Bahru definitely has the best service staff.

Customers are always warmly welcomed by the friendly and approachable Hanily, no matter how busy she is at the front counter. Thanks to the efficient staff, I also never have to wait long for my meal, even with the crazy lunch crowd. Food is always served fresh, hot and well presented.

I do notice some unhappy and unreasonable customers due to the occasional system failure (order kiosk and screen for order no). But without fail, Hanily is always there patiently apologising and explaining about the situation and providing solutions to minimise inconvenience for all the customers. With her attention to details, she will even go the extra mile to either personally serve the food to waiting customers or inform the correct customers that their order is ready. Hanily makes customers feel valued by creating genuine connection with them - checking if they enjoy their food or if they need anything else to make their meal more enjoyable and always wishing customers a good day with her uplifting and positive smile when we leave.

Hanily is definitely an asset to Soup Spoon. It is commendable how many customers have become regulars because of her her warmth, hospitality, passion for service and genuine care for them. Thank you Hanily for creating such a welcoming and positive atmosphere and also the staff at Tiong Bahru Plaza outlet for making the dining experience pleasant and comfortable for all your customers!
author: V Lim

review_text: The Beef goulash has a lovely flavor with herbs & chunky beef & vegetables. A wholesome meal - ham & cheese sandwich with buttered-up dinner roll and ice lemon tea made the dinner so enjoyable! Comforting & nourishing!
author: Another Big Bite

review_text:
I patronise the Tiong Bahru branch a few times and every time, the quality of food haa been consistent and good. The ingredients tasted fresh and they renew menus often.

Tried Chengdu mapo tofu tomato stew and glass noodles with teriyaki chicken. For $15, it was really value for money for delicious and healthy food!
author: Chow Carole

review_text: Good place for a warm bowl of soup during raining season in Singapore. And a great place for kids too. We ordered the tangy spicy tomato soup, lobster bisque and French onion soup. The soup were rich and full of goodness. They do offer set meals that come with a simple burger and additional buns. Hence for 4 of us, 3 sets was sufficient. Service can be better improved as I had to wait for a while to get the lady’s attention for tasting. Otherwise, decent place for a quick lunch.
author: Sue G

review_text: I always enjoy dining at the Soup Spoon branch in Tiong Bahru. The staff are friendly, pleasant, and consistently provide great service. The food is prepared well and served with care, making every visit a satisfying experience.
author: Amor Muyrong

restaurant_name: Shihlin Taiwan Street Food (Tiong Bahru Plaza)
review_text: Visited multiple times at this store, the lady (never get her name, but she dyed her hair blonde and never wear spec) always being polite, friendly and welcoming. Seldom see f&b staffs being so passionate and consistently offer a smile all times, food is nice but this review is to give her a special shoutout ❤️
author: Juliana Lim

restaurant_name: Shihlin Taiwan Street Food (Tiong Bahru Plaza)
review_text: I would like to give my appreciation to the manager/In-charge and all staff there as order was a lot and they still handle it so well, as today I was suppose to order the rice box with chicken but I accidentally order the wrong one which is assorted mushroom, they was so kind still give me change and additional of the mushroom too. I have been buying from this outlet was quite sometimes already, thanks for giving such a great services and always so kind to us even while they was behind with the hot steamy environment.
author: Jen Tham

restaurant_name: Shihlin Taiwan Street Food (Tiong Bahru Plaza)
review_text: I would have given zero star if I could. I ordered mushrooms cheese crepes via Grabfood and halfway through the meal, I noticed some black fiber looking things in the egg, I started to peel everything apart and to my horror, there's lots of black fiber looking things in the egg. It looks like insects, but I'm not sure what kind of insects. There's like large pieces of it too, I tear those large pieces apart and it breaks like fiber. I'm not sure if it's burnt pork floss that's left on their stove or if it's really insects. I feel very very disgusted and nauseous now.
