restaurant_name: Shihlin Taiwan Street Food (Tiong Bahru Plaza)
review_text: Have been there few times during peak hours (around 1900~1930) although the workers are super busy they are still very polite and kind. Really enjoy the food, everytime its scorching hot 🔥
author: 星

restaurant_name: Shihlin Taiwan Street Food (Tiong Bahru Plaza)
review_text: Food and service were on standard. Chicken was crunchy and juicy. Stall hygiene was well maintained. Shout out to Ms. Shi En for her humble and comprehensive service especially in introducing the new kiosk system, which can give customers more time and options to explore the variety. Keep it up.
author: yixiang hoe

review_text: Succumbed to a craving. Thai Thai was ok, not bad! Looks spicy. Is spicy! Sauce did not completely cover the chicken pieces like the photos. Oh well. Punchy stuff.
author: michael lin

review_text:
I will never visit the Tiong Bahru KFC again. The staff took more than 20 minutes to prepare just 4 orders, they were totally bo chap and took their own sweet time.

This isn’t the first time I’ve had issues with them missing items from my order, which is why I now always double-check before leaving. And yes, it happened again! When I brought it up, the staff were rude and unfriendly.

To make things worse, the chicken pieces were ridiculously small. Just look at this, it’s like a joke for the price I paid. Totally not worth it.
author: Jying Lim

review_text:
The staff are rude — and honestly, “rude” doesn’t even begin to describe it.

My order number was 8793. The display screen was stuck showing 8790 to 8792 for quite some time. I had no problem waiting, but just to be safe, I politely went to the counter to check if I’d missed my number. I even started with a “sorry” — yet the staff completely ignored me, as if I was invisible.

Fine. I stepped away — and moments later, they suddenly called my number. The same staff member who had just ignored me (let’s call him A) then turned to another staff member (B) and in Malay complained about “these people who cannot wait and don’t know how to look at the screen.” B responded by saying, “That’s because they are uneducated.”

That was the last straw. I lost my cool and raised my voice, telling them outright: “The problem is the number is not showing!” Only then did they finally shut up.

I am utterly disgusted by their behavior, their unprofessionalism, and their condescending attitude toward customers. It is completely unacceptable. If I was rude, I can understand why but I wasn’t.
author: Simon Teoh

review_text: The staff were very attentive and welcoming.
author: Chan Vanmy

review_text: Staff Kai An or Kai Yan was super rude when asked if able to get my cheese fries w no spring onion. Please don’t allow staff that has no basic courtesy so serve customers. If it was busy I understand but it wasn’t busy at all. Last time I will visit this outlet
author: Dee Dyana

review_text:
Great disappointment, once awhile, I patronize this branch but I usually buy Ebi Rice burger.

Their packing looks nice but the burger cold and talking about double mushroom what do they mean double mushrooms, there like 6 to 7 slices of mushroom that's all, hmmm you call it double so if not double means I will just have 3 slices mushroom???

My hubby Ebi Rice burger was as usual warm and nice to eat. Corn soup was still hot.

So , I' m sorry to say , do not order their buns burgers, only Ebi Rice burgers or beef rice burgers is ok.

As for their soup it cost me $3.50 , you better buy Campbell soup from the can now ntuc promotion selling 3 cans for $5.20 is way much better than Moss Burger corn soup.

Moss Burger in TBP , I wish your branch all the best and I pray your management read my review.

I won't be surprised, they might close one day if this type of standard goes on.
author: Feliz

review_text: I ordered teriyaki rice burger. Ended up all the meat are black n burned meat. Threw it away cannnot be eaten. So regret buying from this branch.

Aunties and uncles working there are very friendly.

If any customisation of the item, they are willing to help.
Tried the new Wagyu brown rice burger, it’s just simply so nice.

Standard cannot make it now

everything feels very low quality and food feels tepid like microwave vibes

better off going to macs or a proper restaurant at these prices

at least their fries still okay
author: Goh SK

review_text: Please provide plastic straws. Small stirrers are inadequate for iced tea and make it less enjoyable. This feels like misplaced cost-cutting, as consumer straws are a minor part of plastic pollution.

review_text:
Very normal curry puff. Not spicy and the crust is thick.

I prefer thin crust with spicy filling.

restaurant_name: 西得利 Xi De Li You Tiao
review_text: i tried many deep fried foods, this shop is the most of the best in SG

restaurant_name: 西得利 Xi De Li You Tiao
review_text: Have not try the rest. But you tiao is 5 stars.  Not oily and nice salty flavour that goes so well with coffee.
author: Goo Bakmi

restaurant_name: 西得利 Xi De Li You Tiao
review_text:
Just tried the "Butterfly", dipped in coffee. Nice and hot and huge. Everything in this store is priced at $1, including the curry puff. Will try that in my next visit. Redhill food centre is a gem.

Curry Puff - don't like this.

Accepts CDC vouchers.
author: C Irene

restaurant_name: 西得利 Xi De Li You Tiao
review_text: I like carrot cake, and this stall delivers.
author: LP Pua

review_text: The quality of the coffee has plummeted. They seem to have stopped serving specialty coffee, at least not in the form of a flat white, which was more a long black with a thick layer of foam. Even during the circuit breaker, they’d served good coffee with chocolaty/nutty flavoured beans from Liberty. Then, the steak and cheese grilled sandwich tasted nice though there was room for the portion of ingredients to be more substantial.
author: Royal Pears

review_text: Extremely disappointing food and service. They were catering an event at our school and were totally unprepared for the number of people attending. We queued for 40 min with 6 people in front of us to order 4 beef and chicken “steak burgers”. The food is inedible, $35 straight in the bin. Boiled beef meat of questionable origin in a soggy bun, chicken slightly better, all tasted absolutely disgusting. And this was meant to cater a children and parents event. Staff were super unfriendly, service couldn’t be slower if they tried and every single order was packed in a separate plastic bag we didn’t ask for. So disappointed with hungry kids that we still need to feed somewhere.
author: Irina De Sepibus

review_text:
I recommend to try the meatballs burger and the long black.
Fries is crispy and tasty, salad dressing a bit like wafu dressing, very refreshing.
Portion look small but you will feel very full after you finish it.
author: Hong Heee Tan (Jim)

review_text:
not recommend the Mushroom Aglio Olio, dried and hard, ordered two plates and one plate without the Red bell Pepper but 👍🏼 coffee.
check out monthly special dish to avoid disappointment.
author: JL

review_text: we really love these sandwiches, but coffee have to improve..by the way their blended taste likes starbucks, a bit surprise
author: Royen Lock

review_text:
Dear McDonald’s Customer Care Team,
I would like to take this opportunity to compliment your staff member, Xing Man, for the excellent service provided during my recent visit.
Xing Man was very friendly, patient, and helpful. The service was professional and made my experience very pleasant. It is always nice to meet staff who genuinely care about customers and serve with a positive attitude.
Please convey my appreciation to Xing Man. Staff like this truly represent your brand well.
Thank you for the great service.
author: V Resorts

review_text: Came to McDonald's for lunch at Regal's outlet, but was disappointed by the service received. Made an order through the app for table service. Ordered a curry sauce and sundae with my meal. Was missing the curry sauce and spoon for the ice cream when the meal came. Had walked twice to the counter after noticing the missing items, which defeated the purpose of table service. Outlet wasn't very crowded at 1:30pm on a weekday.
author: Jasper Teo

review_text: Super crowded. Insufficient staff. Ordered nuggets at 5.09pm, received SPICY nuggets at 5.35pm. Took order and rushed off. Came home and saw SPICY nuggets which kid cannot eat. Poor Poor Poor in every way.
author: Clayton

review_text:
as someone who goes to a lot of study spots, this is absolutely the perfect spot for you to study at! it's not too far from many primary or secondary schools, and the food is served fast and the staff are super nice towards us, even giving us motivating and kind words when we came to mcdonalds to eat or study after cca or school! i also find it not too crowded most of the time from ard 5-6 , but honestly it varies on the day and it's mostly crowded on fridays :)

growing up around bukit merah, i do miss what this mcdonalds outlet used to look like before it renovated around 2021 or 2022. i come here quite often with friends, and this was my go-to spot to get frappes during exam season 🙏
author: gavandfish

review_text:
I am incredibly disappointed with my experience today. I used the McDonald's app to order a Crispy Mac 'N Cheesy Wrap (Chicken Ham) meal for takeaway. Upon opening it, I discovered I had been given a sausage wrap instead.

I immediately returned to the restaurant to politely request an exchange for the correct item. The staff member NADIA (who I believe was the shift manager) informed me that the breakfast menu was over and they could not make the correct wrap. While I understood the menu timing issue, what happened next was unacceptable.

Instead of offering a solution such as a refund, or a voucher for a future visit she simply took the incorrect wrap from me, threw it directly into the bin, and told me I would have to "come back again tomorrow."

This is not how customers should be treated. The response was wasteful, dismissive, and showed a complete lack of care. McDonald's claims to put customers first, but this action demonstrated the exact opposite: my time and money were disregarded entirely. I left with no food, no refund, and no apology just instructions to try my luck another day.
author: Chan

review_text:
Promising stall with options of fishball and meat BCM. Price Options from $4.00

Looks better than it tastes.. sigh

Mediocre bowl of BCM.
Lack lustre sauce mix. Soup is sweet hmm.

Staff are confusing. Asking same questions over again when taking orders.

author: Robin Sim

Used to be a lot more but shrinkflation of course hahaha still my go to BCM tho cos of distance and price

author: Ariane

Service attitude never change same again. This time round worst mushroom give 2pcs half 🤦🏻‍♂️🤦🏻‍♂️. Reason being PRICE increase LOL

review_text: Very poor, noodles are not cooked properly. Waited for at least 10 mins till my turn to order.
author: goh nicholas

restaurant_name: Happy Oven - Tiong Bahru Main Bakery
review_text: Cakes are nice but staff attitude very bad. Had been waiting at the counter for a few minutes waiting to be served. The lady staff with short hair just ignore and continue to display boxes of cake which I think that can wait but not your customer. Your staff would rather let the customer wait? Attitude is very rude too. Not recommended to go back although cakes are nice. What for as a consumer we buy your products but had to tolerate your staff poor service attitude!
author: Sharonng

restaurant_name: Happy Oven - Tiong Bahru Main Bakery
review_text:
A neighbourhood bakery that’s right beside Beo Crescent Market, & what’s better is CDC vouchers are accepted here!

Bought a few of their signatures such as Ondeh ondeh (packed with coconut), Kaya pandan & chendol cake, which were all not too sweet. The Apple crumble pie’s crust was abit dry for our liking, but I enjoyed the Gula melaka swiss roll.

IG @pingguo301
author: Angel Tan

review_text: Cake texture is good, taste good too. But 1 question is, why they are using hand to mix the batter?( saw from vedio in thier website) I am an imaginary person. After seeing how they used half of the arm to mix the cake batter. It makes me wonder, even they wash their hand . It doesn't mean thier hand doesn't sweat. author: Xue Tan

restaurant_name: Happy Oven - Tiong Bahru Main Bakery
review_text: I found this lovely halal bakery online and ordered some pastries for a company event. They were a hit! The presentation was great, and we loved the variety of options. The prices were also reasonable. I will definitely use them again.
author: Touristmouse

restaurant_name: Happy Oven - Tiong Bahru Main Bakery
review_text:
EmceeRichardStyle Mic Rating
🎤🎤🎤🎤🎤

author: EmceeRichardStyle

review_text:
I was quite disappointed with my recent visit. I ordered the fish and chips, but the portion served was really unsatisfactory – the piece of fish was small and didn’t feel like value for money at all. For the price I paid, I expected a more generous serving or at least something more worthwhile. Unfortunately, the meal didn’t justify the cost, and I left feeling shortchanged.

I hope Common Grill takes this feedback seriously, as portion size and value are just as important as taste.
author: ano chan

review_text: Food is normal, nothing special but the portion is so random so beware when ordering as you may get a small portion instead since they don't weight or portion their servings. Pitiful amount of sauce or dressing on the salad and mushroom soup was so thick that the texture was horrible.
author: koh jun qiang

review_text: Was there ard 1030pm, coffeeshop is about to close, common grills is the only stall left open. The service is acceptable. The food looks good, tastes good. Was satisfied that I only need to spend $30 to enjoy a good meal.
author: Dan Ng

review_text:
Most awful fish and chips i ever had it here.!! The fish itself is totally hard like stone , until the whole plate of food I have to throw away.

author: Leigh

review_text: This is one of my favorite places for a quick snack whenever I am feeling hungry after work. Fried chicken and fish balls are one of my favorite to choose from. Just next to tiong Bahru MRT station and before fairprice finest.
author: Ramesh Sharma

review_text:
Don’t order the mee siam. Bought it for lunch. There’s no fillings, mostly bee hoon, chives, a few strands of bean sprouts and some super dry tau pok. Bee hoon was so dry and rubbery. Wasted my stomach space. Should have ordered Nasi Lemak instead.

Don’t think I wanna buy from them again.

Dry Mee Siam taste starchy wander isn't ........,.....etc

author: 张晶娜

review_text: Bee Hoon not bad
author: Mae Ng

review_text:
Had dinner here this week and honestly, the food hit the spot. The nabe soup was comforting without being overpowering — just the right balance.

Service was warm and friendly, which made the experience even better. My only gripe: the price. You’ll definitely pay a bit more here (around 20% higher than similar places), so it’s not somewhere I’d go regularly… but for a cozy splurge, it’s great.
author: Timothy Leong

review_text:
Came for a weekday lunch with my family.  Sushi Tei is a trusted brand that has been around since the 90s.
The quality of food is still good.
The miso cod is value for many. And so is the grilled kampachi collar and various maki rolls.  Service was prompt and eatery environment relaxed.
Had a hearty meal.
author: YL Wong

review_text:
We are regular customers at Sushi Teh, and every visit has been a consistently pleasant experience. The staff — especially the managers and supervisors — are extremely friendly and attentive. What truly stands out is that they remember their customers and always greet us warmly whenever they see us, which makes us feel very welcomed and valued.

The food is equally enjoyable. Whether we dine in at the restaurant or order takeaway, the quality and taste are always well maintained. Fresh, satisfying, and reliable — it’s a place we’re always happy to return to.

Highly recommended for both the great food and excellent service!
author: alice tay

review_text:
Great for japanese food cravings. The food is up to Sushi Tei's standards.

I am a huge fan of Unagi Don and Soba, and I am happy that it didn't disappoint. Also, the salmon skin, jellyfish, and soft shell crabs are bonus side dishes to add on.
The service may be lacking just a little bit, but overall, it is still good.

Just take note that it may have a long waiting time during peak hours.
author: Nel GTS

review_text: If you are thinking of ordering food delivery or patronising this restaurant, kindly think twice as service is absurd and slow 🐌🐌🐌! Especially for food delivery orders, it is one of the worst Japanese Restaurant! It is extremely slow 🐌🐌🐌(waited for almost 30 minutes)!
author: ピカ ピカチュウ

review_text:
The food was decent overall. The chicken tenders turned out to be made with chicken thighs, but unfortunately, they were quite fatty and not very enjoyable.

The star of the meal, however, was the cheesy loaded fries. We initially thought it would just be fries, but it came with four pieces of meat as well—super worth it if you’re only getting one dish!

The chicken wings were fine, nothing exceptional. Do note that all their chicken items are made using either thighs or wings.

One downside unrelated to the food—the announcement volume was way too loud. It would be much nicer if it were softer on the ears.
author: Orange

review_text: Have lunch on a Saturday. The place is surprisingly empty. But the chickens are really nice. Tasty and succulent. The sauce is also authentic. Meet our expectation. Fries are of superior quality. All are crunchy outside with soft inside. Ambience is great (cos not crowded). Best past is the staff were very polite and friendly. Totally opposite form K*C. Will encourage all neighbours to support so we are. Alternate choice of fried chicken in Tiong Bahru.
author: Liwei Chiang

review_text: Shoutout to the lovely staff (cashier) , so so kind. I requested for the kimchi slaw to be separated & for a little extra & she made it happen. Truly appreciate you ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️ this is what customer service is!
author: Alicia Lee

review_text:
Standards dropped. 4Fingers used to be one of my favourite k fried chicken.

The 6 pieces boneless chicken was super tiny. Due to the super hard fried skin, each piece of the fried food tasted like it was fried many times prior to serving.

The maki rolls most likely used left over chicken from the day before. They all tasted with strong chicken stink.

Oh yea, forgot to add. The sushi was warmer than the boneless chicken bites. Certainly not freshly made.

Maybe it’s not 4 fingers, it’s just this outlet. But be careful when choosing.
author: Evelyn Chen

review_text:
The best Korean style fried chicken with distinct and flavorful sauces. I ordered spicy drumsticks with rice and kimchi sides (as in photos).

The chicken itself is juicy and flavorful with crispy fried skin. So unique that’s why different from other fast food chains.

Quite casual dining atmosphere there and most importantly it offers reasonable price. Really satisfied with quick, tasty meal for my dinner.

One of downside is that some said there can sometimes be mixed reviews about the consistency in cooking or waiting times, particularly during peak hours.

But overall to me, it is a satisfying choice for craving a crunchy, flavorful-bite day🤭🫶🏻
author: Lana

review_text: I got a sandwich 🥪. It costed me $8 😁 the price is not bad. I got a drink, a sandwich and a cookie 🍪 🥤🥪. very healthy. I would come again. the sandwich was crunchy and the cheese was melted just the way i like it. Really good price too!!
author: kyla ho

author: Daniel Lim

review_text: This morning i went to subway to get myself my bulgogi chicken sandwich. however when the employee was preparing it, she put regular plastic cheese. i proceeded to ask her where my mozzarella cheese was, hinting to her that i want it. however,  she  then simultaneously said she only puts it on when customers ask for it while putting it in the oven, giving me no chance to ask for it. This is so ridiculous. the menu LITERALLY says ‘with mozzarella cheese”. NOT 'ask employee if you want mozzarella’. this whole thing ruined my day because i couldve asked for chicken teriyaki if i wanted the plastic cheese. i payed EXTRA. i am a broke poly student. i cant believe subway does not train their employees to follow the menu and do whatever they want. horrible customer service.
author: m

review_text:
The tiong bahru branch by far the slowest and most chaotic branch of subways I've seen, worldwide.
Not just can this hardly be called fast food at this point (even the oven works slower than in other branches I'm pretty certain), I also didn't get the same sort of vegetables when ordering "all except jalapenos" (an instruction I've been using for about the last 10 years now, but i never had corn and carrots before, might be new?!)
Comparably other subway outlets (e.g. 100am are much better, the food looks better, the staff works faster and is less confused). I guess I'll rather go elsewhere in future, if i wanna grab a quick sub.
author: Arne Leonhardt

review_text:
Came here on New Years' Eve with my family looking forward to some good food. Unfortunately, the experience wasn't the best. The selections were pretty small and modest - spanning across Asian and Western food. However, I expected there to be more Indonesian food considering the place's reputation as an Indonesian restaurant. The Asian food that did exist, meanwhile, were random combinations of dishes that didn't pair well with the saffron rice given. Furthetmore, while there was seafood bisque, no bread or whatnot was even provided as a dip for the soup. The drink selection is limited to three different kinds of cold sweet drinks. Desserts were varied and were more balanced in terms of variety of Asian and Western desserts - however, the Western ones (eg. eclaire, cream puff) were soggy and seemed to be like those instant types.

Service-wise, some waitresses were attentive and proactive in clearing plates. I do wish, though, that more tissues/napkins were provided.

To give credit where it's due:
The christmas-themed roasted turkey(?) and beef, as well as duck in mashed potatoes were very nice. Starters such as the burratta salad etc were diverse and also decent. I'm also glad that a prayer room is available.

However, overall, the experience was disappointing because I was very excited to try at least some Indonesian food - even if the menuw as Christmas-themed etc perhaps at least two or three dishes could've been maintained. The service was pretty average and the restaurant's interior was quite bland. I think it's an okay place to just have a filling dinner with your family, but I wouldn't go in with much expectations.
author: Zaki

review_text:
Subject
Feedback on Food Quality and Authenticity
Dear Sir/Madam,
I am writing to share my feedback regarding my recent dining experience at your restaurant. I used to enjoy dining here and always appreciated the authentic Indonesian food that was served previously. Unfortunately, during my latest visit, I found that the food quality was not the same as before.
I was very disappointed as most of the seafood served did not taste fresh, and the dishes no longer reflected the authentic Indonesian flavours that I was familiar with. As a regular customer, this was quite upsetting.
I hope you will look into this matter seriously and take the necessary steps to improve the food quality and freshness. I am sharing this feedback because I truly hope to see your restaurant maintain the high standards that it used to have.
Thank you for taking the time to read my feedback. I hope to have a better dining experience in the future.
Sincerely,
Norlela Noh
author: Norlela Noh

review_text:
Had a lovely dinner for two at Kintamani Restaurant. We were warmly greeted by the front desk officer and shown to our table. Despite being surprisingly crowded for a weekday, the staff made sure we were seated without any waiting, which we really appreciated.
The food was enjoyable and comforting. While a slightly wider variety would have been nice, the selection was more than sufficient for us. We enjoyed the beef rendang, ayam kicap, and sambal prawn — all favourites — and my wife especially loved the crab.
Special mention to Jessica, the part-timer who provided excellent service. She was attentive and thoughtful, clearing our table promptly, preparing dessert spoons without us having to ask, and even reminding us to try the popular durian pengat, which was absolutely delicious.
Overall, a great dining experience at Kintamani Restaurant. Will definitely return, next time with our extended family!
author: affan mohdnoor

review_text:
Food wise ok.. better to buy with eatigo app more worth it for the food = price.

There's is an mrt quite near the hotel.

Chilli crab was given flower crab instead of mud crab.

Desserts hmm can just pass..

Durian penget don't taste like 100% durian.
Kuih lapis is not soft and stretchy kind.
Cakes not bad.
The passing desert would be the 🍮 pudding!

Laksa was not bad.

Prawns - some was soft (not so fresh..?), some firm (fresher kind)

author: Hello Chester

review_text:
I visited Kintamani Restaurant today for a discounted weekday dinner via Eatigo and had a great experience.

The service was top-notch, particularly the gentleman who attended to us and an auntie who even took the time to show my loved ones where the toilet was while I was busy with the reservation. Kudos also to the aunties who were diligent about clearing dirty plates - it's the little things that make a difference.

At 50% off, the price of $24 per pax before GST and Service Charge was reasonable for a hotel setting. However, at regular prices, I'd be more hesitant given the limited variety.

The ambiance was lovely, and overall, it was a nice dinner. I'd recommend trying it out during promotions!"
author: Low Bao Heng

restaurant_name: Creamier Handcrafted Ice Cream and Coffee (Tiong Bahru)
review_text:
Drop by this cozy place in Tiong Bahru, another great ice cream shop that serves unique flavours like Sea Salt Gula Melaka, Pulut Hitam, Blue Pea Vanilla. But their signatures like roasted pistachio, was really good too! Waffles were crispy outside, soft inside, decent indeed.

If you are around that area or want to go for cafe hopping, you can consider this place too!

Follow us on instagram @twospoonsonebite for honest reviews!
author: Two Spoons One Bite

restaurant_name: Creamier Handcrafted Ice Cream and Coffee (Tiong Bahru)
review_text:
We had our regular and fav fix at Creaamier, Tiong Bahru.

The staff are usually friendly, helpful and so kind with their free ice cream tasting, they are so informative and good at promoting their ice cream.

We are here for our regular ice cream and waffles. The ice cream is dense, smooth and creamy. There are plenty of flavours to choose from.

We like the waffles that's crispy on the outside, and warm and buttery on the inside. Come visit when you are at Tiong Bahru.

author: Jyy Jyy

review_text: Waffles is bagus. One of the better waffles I had in ice cream store. Ice cream flavours are kind of mid. The star of the show is sea salt gula melaka. The yuzu sorbet is not bad as well. But the other flavours lose to other ice cream store. Great staff service by letting us try the ice cream flavours without judgement.
author: Truth Fairy

restaurant_name: Creamier Handcrafted Ice Cream and Coffee (Tiong Bahru)
review_text: Creamier's outlet in one of Singapore's oldest estate. Tight and narrow sitting, and definitely a squeeze while savouring the ice creams. Taste is generally ok but leaning towards the overly sweet spectrum.
author: Ee Kwang Han

review_text:
Nice alfresco pet-friendly area with a sizeable number of of seats available. This is in addition to the huge indoor air-conditioned space within which is only human friendly.

We enjoyed the ham and cheese tart and cinnamon sugar cupcake. The pastry for the tart was the right balance of crisp and softness while the cinnamon icing tasted like Christmas.

The drinks, however, tasted diluted to me and nowhere near a quality cup of chai or mocha respectively.

Will return for the deli!
author: MH Tham

review_text: Had a wonderful breakfast here! Got the goat cheese, mushroom, and leek tart, which was fantastic! My partner had the scrambled eggs on toast said they were the best eggs I’ve ever had. We loved the drinks as well! Great atmosphere
author: francesca Olguin

review_text:
Very pleasant atmosphere with aircon or non aircon seatings. Stepping into the cafe, on the right with shelves of souvenirs and handicrafts. QR code menu on each table that has lists of coffee, non-coffee, freshly-baked confectionery, etc.

Further into the cafe is another vibe with nice and peaceful decorations. Known for its muffin, a selection of sweet treats available.

For meal, had the rosti with smoke salmon. Far from the best I had but not any near to average. Worth the try though. Ice matcha latte not too sweet and strong matcha taste. Ice americano not too bad too.

A very nice indeed for all day or coffee breaks.

Ate Tiong Bahru Pau and chatted with the elderly owner of 7 Original Fishball stall. Very friendly, bubbly, energetic 80 years old lady. The stall is now managed by her son & grandson. The fish balls and otah fish cake were a let down. The fish balls were not bouncy and the otah fish cake has no otah flavour.
In comparison to the stall in Bendemeer hawker center, the taste is far from tasty. I would say those sold in supermarkets taste better.
Price range is also on the higher side.
author: Jane Lee

review_text: Wide selection of fried fishballs, fish cakes, otah, bean curd skins and the likes. Very tasty and reasonably priced. Uncle was friendly and e-payment was available.
author: CK C

review_text:
If I could give more stars I would!
Super nice staff, amazing food and a cozy atmosphere.
I’m gluten intolerant and coming here and have the possibility to order everything on the menu made me so happy, haven’t had such good waffles ever! And the sourdough - so good!
For a next visit in Singapore this will be the first place I go to, so if you have the chance you shouldn’t miss this place out, highly recommend!
author: Hanna Holmström

review_text: As a celiac, I find it very hard travelling internationally. Finding gems like these truly make life worth living. This is the first time I’ve ever been able to try KFC “Korean Fried Chicken” since it became popularised, and it truly brought a tear to my eye. I’m so grateful for being able to dine here, the staff are lovely, the food is amazing and being able to eat traditional foods finally is an experience I couldn’t thank this place enough for.
author: Laura Frith

review_text: Breakfast was excellent. Waffles were fluffy and tasty and well loaded with toppings. Bruschetta bread was crispy on the outside and soft in the middle with tomatoes bursting with flavour. Coffee is smooth and gelato was rich and creamy. Overall a great gluten free cafe.
author: Jason Feuerstein

review_text: A cozy place. Wide range of selection even for one with gluten free diet or lactose intolerance. Like the special chicken to share as the sauce compliments the tender chicken that melt on the first bite. Recommend one to share that dish instead of having alone as can be heavy. Like the simple kaya toast. Food serving takes awhile so be prepared for that. The staff are polite but perhaps not enough to serve the busy crowd.
author: laney low

review_text: The café is really great, and there is absolutely nothing wrong with the food and its quality. The service is very attentive. However, the portion sizes are far too small for the prices you pay. If I pay SG$21 or SG$25 for a breakfast dish, I expect a portion size that is larger than an appetizer.
author: Max B

review_text:
Paradox Hotel is a paradox.

We had read that it’s a smaller hotel chain positioning itself as a boutique lifestyle experience — and in many ways that’s absolutely true. The hospitality, the welcome, the personality, and the location in Singapore are all excellent.

We booked an Executive Club room and forgot to mention my wife’s food intolerances. The team handled it perfectly from the very first evening, and the gluten-free options at afternoon tea were outstanding.

But the entire executive feeling disappeared at breakfast.

We were directed to a windowless room and then had to collect food in a massive buffet hall that felt more like a large charter resort or a Las Vegas hotel than a boutique property. It was crowded, chaotic, and almost competitive just to reach the dishes.

Everything fantastic we had read beforehand was unfortunately overshadowed by the breakfast experience.

WE DID NOT GET WHAT WE PAID FOR!

Would I stay here again? Yes, most likely — thanks to the genuinely accommodating spirit of the team. If the breakfast mayhem isn’t sorted out by then, there’s always a Starbucks around the corner.
author: callesteros kanal

review_text:
Overall experience is good but definitely can be better. We booked Pawcation Retreat and the hotel consider as new player for pet friendly hotel.

Package includes high tea and happy hour. For high tea, we can have it outdoor at Ellenbourough market cafe. However, we were told by check in staff not for happy hour as the cafe is not pet friendly. Instead we were told we can just sit at the lobby area with the dogs in the stroller. Not sure if there as miscommunication between the staffs.
However, when we come down the lobby area is full and no place to sit at all. After some talking with the staffs, we are allowed to eat at the outdoor area same as high tea.

I think if the pawcation retreat package offers all this benefits, hotel should give more options such as for example we can choose to have it in our room or outdoor area where we can dine with our dogs.
Luckily our experiences saved by the quick action of Izad and also hospitality of Jia Bao.

One thing that I NEED to mentioned though is the lack of staff during breakfast hours. No one paying attention to people dining outside. I need to ask 3 times to 3 different staffs just to get cutleries and ice.
Overall is a good experience but not sure we will be back.
author: Jeff Jeff

review_text:
We had an absolutely wonderful stay at this hotel! Everything was perfect from the moment we arrived until the moment we checked out.
​The Staff: Everyone was incredibly welcoming, professional, and went out of their way to make us feel at home.
​The Breakfast: The morning spread was delicious with a huge variety of fresh options. It was the perfect way to start our day.
​Cleanliness: The housekeeping team does an amazing job. Our room was spotless and refreshed perfectly every single day.
​Overall, it was a 10/10 experience. We had a fantastic time and will definitely be returning in the future!
author: Mariann

review_text:
Loud shout out to the Entire Hotel team for such a wonderful and comfortable stay.

Hotel is quite premium, a colonial era type architecture refurbished to meet the evolving standards...a very helpful and always available conceirage.. complimentary welcome drinks.. complimentary coffee machine with fully filled amenities...clean and well appointed room. No unnecessary noise.

Only drawback no washer available with WC. Washroom is not that big but good compared to regular singapore standard. Also bathroom is quite slipery. Be careful. Me and my kids both slipped but luckily escaped harmless.

Highly efficient and approachable front office team.

Hotel is located on clark quay river and has direct access to the river side. Pool  is very well maintained with slides for kids and adults. Very well located jacuzzi.

We stayed here from 25th December to 27th December paid 250sgd/per night for premium king (no balcony) category.
We had a wonderful stay..
author: deepika garg

review_text:
Amazing Hotel right by Clarkes Quay. Stayed for a couple of nights on the way to Bali.
All staff are very helpful. Rooms are spacious and clean, the bar area is lovely and relaxing, in-between sight seeing we sat by the pool for a few drinks.
Breakfast was plentiful with lots of options.
A big thank you for my Birthday cake that was left for me 🥰.
It's the little things that make hotels Great.
Would recommend to all, central to all tourist attractions, transport.
Would stay again.
Thank you for making our few days in Singapore amazing 😁
author: Karen Newman

review_text:
I had a couple of meals here- one was the fish dish. Went for the hot and spicy sauce! Was so gorgeous. Another visit was the dumpling soup. Lovely too. Good value for money and didn’t wait too long to be served.

At night it was buzzing both inside and the closed street outside where they were cooking on a street BBQ.
author: Yvette Dorman

review_text:
Lau Pa Sat is an absolute must-visit for anyone wanting to experience authentic Singaporean hawker culture in a beautiful historic setting. The stunning Victorian cast-iron architecture makes it one of the most unique food markets in the city, blending heritage with modern skyscrapers all around it.
During the day, it’s a lively food center offering a wide variety of local and international dishes — from Hainanese chicken rice to laksa and seafood. Everything is reasonably priced, and the variety ensures there’s something for everyone.
At night, the atmosphere becomes even more special when Boon Tat Street transforms into “Satay Street.” The road closes to traffic, tables fill the street, and the smell of grilled satay fills the air. Sitting outdoors under the city skyline while enjoying freshly grilled skewers is an unforgettable experience.
It can get busy, especially during dinner hours, but that’s part of the charm. If you’re looking for great food, local flavor, and a vibrant atmosphere all in one place, Lau Pa Sat delivers. Highly recommended for a true taste of Singapore.
author: Andy Rodriguez

review_text: fantastic place to grab some food and/or beer. Famous for the skewers on the street, especially the chicken satay. Plenty of options to choose from, Indian, Arabic, Chinese, Singaporean, etc. There's something for everyone. Good ventilation and plenty of tables but the place is always packed and noisy (it doesn't take away the enjoyment). A must to visit.
author: Franco Migliorati

review_text: Hugely popular place for both locals and tourists to get some food. This place has an amazing variety of cuisines ranging from Chinese to Indian to Malay and Middle Eastern fares. The quality is generally good. But we feel there should be some system whereby the tables get wiped to maintain a cleaner environment.
author: Cher Lee Kiat

review_text: Lau Pa Sat is a must-visit food haven in Singapore! The variety of food choices is incredible—from local hawker favorites to international dishes, there’s something for everyone. The atmosphere is lively and vibrant, especially in the evenings when satay stalls line the street. The place is clean, well-organized, and perfect for both casual dining and foodie adventures. Definitely worth the stop if you want to experience authentic flavors in the heart of the city!
author: Glenn Reyes

review_text:
Impeccable service, adding this to my favorite solo meal spots! The team was attentive from start to finish.
Cosy Italian spot and I was pleasantly surprised. Decent white truffle prices and pasta dishes were really well made. had their tajarín and the flavours were great, though the seasoning leaned a little strong. The tomino cheese with truffle was excellent — perfect with a glass of wine

The only slight downside was that the white truffle aroma was slightly lacking in comparison to others I’ve had this year …
author: Ms Neko

review_text: Our annual place for white truffle.. They have a good executive lunch set but we are there every year during truffle seasons. Thye have a truffles menu where they recommend some dishes to go with white truffles but we typically go for the eggs for appetizer and either the pasta or risotto for mains. Service as usually is excellent and friendly. Truffle this year (2025) was pretty good but not exceptional. Prices has steadily gone up over the years and is $15/g this year. At these prices, each serving of truffles is almost 2-3x the prices of the dish itself but I guess once a year is pretty good.
author: STEK TAN

review_text:
When I tell you about Otto, I get emotional. This restaurant is not a restaurant, it’s home. It’s everything you didn’t know you need!

It’s hands down THE BEST Italian restaurant in Singapore and one of the best overall in Singapore.

The food here never misses, I trust the chef with my life.

We miss you Michele and Paolo, please open a restaurant in Switzerland. ❤️
author: Sabrina Scherer

review_text: Finally decided to have dinner at Otto Ristorante after passing by a couple of times while trying other nearby restaurants. Nice interior with good ambience. Food quality is superb. We had the lamb shank and the beef tenderloin which were both perfect! The service was impeccable too.
author: Rachel Ng

review_text:
We chose Otto Ristorante for our ROM dinner with family and friends (30 guests), and it was truly the perfect choice.

The service was excellent – the staff were attentive, knowledgeable, and took great care to introduce each dish to our guests while also being mindful of allergies and preferences. We really appreciated the thoughtfulness and dedication from the whole team in making our special day smooth and enjoyable.

The food was fantastic. Every dish in the gourmet course was well-prepared and served simultaneously for all 30 guests without compromising on quality. Many of our guests mentioned it was the best foie gras and Wagyu beef they had ever tasted.

Thanks to Otto Ristorante, our celebration became truly memorable. We’re so glad we chose this restaurant and look forward to returning for future anniversaries.

A special thanks to Linda, who helped us from the very beginning and made the whole experience seamless

Lastly, We would also like to thank Basketcase Florist, recommended by Linda, for the beautiful decoration. The setup perfectly matched our style and made the room even more special.
author: Mm Kh

review_text: This is one of the most historical old food center in Chinatown.  They have many good food such as famous soya sauce chicken, steamed fish head, beef noddle, claypot rice, porridge, China food, Teochew porridge, Fried Kway teow and some Malay and Indian stalls.  There is wet market at B1 , retail stalls mainly at level 1 and the food center at level 2.  You can see more of old residences in their 70s/80s eating here.  Certainly a good place for you to try out …
author: Louis

review_text: 20251120 - one of the nice hawker centres in singapore where you can get variety of local food and drinks in 1 place. Place is not air conditioned and therefore more affordable than restaurants. Ordered hokkien mee, satay, popiah, chendol and iced tea from different stalls. Overall satisfied with all the food and would come again.
author: Frank P

review_text: Great experience exploring Chinatown! The Buddha Tooth Relic Temple is beautiful and definitely worth a visit. I also enjoyed walking around the neighborhood; the streets are lively and full of interesting shops. It’s a nice place to soak in the local culture
author: komang adi

review_text:
There are so may food court in Singapore and This is good place to go for eating out: cheap, good, variety of food.

One of the best food court in Singapore as it is very reasonable and good quality. You can even find a place with Michelin star place.
author: Cou Cou

review_text: I think you can find a wide array of international & local cuisine at pretty decent prices which may be a shock to tourists we can eat out cheap in SG. I personally like the AN JI steamed fish head in sour plum gravy (there are several stalls selling similar), very appetizing as well as fresh fruits juices like Green Apple Yakult and Soupsop ($7 for both) at stall #02-192.
author: Che C

restaurant_name: The Southbridge Hotel Restaurant and Whiskey Bar
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

We had a fantastic experience at The Southbridge Hotel — their lunch promotion was absolutely the best! The meal was delicious, and the deal made it even more worthwhile. The staff, especially Dianara and James, were incredibly attentive and friendly. Their warmth and professionalism made the experience even more enjoyable.

We also stayed at Terra Hotel during our visit, and they went above and beyond to make our stay amazing. The service, comfort, and overall hospitality were top-notch. Highly recommended!
author: Sari Cartagena

restaurant_name: The Southbridge Hotel Restaurant and Whiskey Bar
review_text: Went to their bar, the foods super good!!!  I njoy also The lives band shout out to Kim, Merthon and BJ. super talented. for staff Dee super like her cause very humble and  friendly and always smile to us. !! love her so much.
author: Rasnih Nuil

restaurant_name: The Southbridge Hotel Restaurant and Whiskey Bar
review_text: Went to visit the bar/pub since we are roaming around telok ayer and chinatown. But unfortunately out experienced with the server which is a filipino man was very rude and not friendly at all if you work in an F&B surrounding you should bring a thousands of patients and energy with you to keep up if you don’t want your job then better quite rather than ruining the bar/pub reputation to keep your customers from keep coming back. I will not recommend this bar if come to Singapore there’s a plenty of bar around the corner rather that to ruin your not with rude staff. Definitely will never come back here the service was terrible.
author: cndplumbing rose

restaurant_name: The Southbridge Hotel Restaurant and Whiskey Bar
review_text: Excellent place to go for a drink and food. Service is authentically welcoming and makes you feel home away from home. Would recommend over all the other places around. The team is brilliant and Charles is on top of that. A genuinely welcoming man who will take good and honest care of you
author: Ch Schenk

restaurant_name: The Southbridge Hotel Restaurant and Whiskey Bar
review_text: I have to say I absolutely love this place and its location. I was a foreigner visiting back in August of 2025. My friend and I got stranded in a country we have never visited before and did not know how to get around and unfortunately we had a bad experience due to getting followed by a man who most likely did not have good intentions and we seek refuge in this place. We had a lychee highball (which was delicious) while we waited for our male friend to rescue us from the situation we were in. I will definitely be visiting again!
author: Ari Guerrero

review_text:
February 2026 visit:
I really wanted to try a Laksa and this was a very good first bowl. I loved the creamy soup base and the noodles.

Several people in line when I arrived at the stall - everyone ordered at least 1 bowl of the $5 Laksa. So I did as well (lemming).
Medium sized bowl for the $5. It was a good size to share between 2 adults with other food.

I paid cash, but others paid by some digital payment with the QR code at the counter.
author: Ali C

review_text:
Store is located in the same lane as where the famous chicken rice is, closer to the main road.

Delicious traditional laksa - will be back! Ordered a large and extra cockles - cuz why not. We thoroughly enjoyed it, sorry no pic of food tho cuz we inhaled in.
author: B H

review_text: Delicious food! I came here to have the laksa but I saw at least three people in the queue ahead of me getting a laksa and a rendang chicken, so I took this as a sign that I ought to as well. Having now had both, I can say that the sign was appropriately interpreted and received.
author: Tyler Davis

review_text: Excellent Nyonya laksa with a rich, creamy base. The mild chili adds great depth, and the yong tau foo pairs perfectly with the broth. Highly recommended!
author: Foo

review_text:
Reasonable food but rude staff.

I asked for a $7 laska with yellow noodle. Firstly he misheard me and gave back $5 for change. I clarified. Then he served me with a bowl of rice noodle. I questioned again, the chef said my face looked like yellow noodle. The words were unexpected rude and disgusting.
author: Danyang Zhu

review_text:
Very wide selection on the menu, ranging from a long list of soup dishes to fried chicken.

The highlight for me is definitely the side dishes, everything tasted delicious and felt thoughtfully prepared. The grilled fish with chopped chilli and sticky brown sauce was also very good.

The kimchi soup was just okay, a bit too sour and the flavours did not balance well. The fried chicken wings were also average, with a batter that was more hard and crunchy rather than light and crispy.

Overall, a good Korean place with plenty of options to choose from.
author: Leh

review_text:
It’s been a long time since I last dined here, but the food did not disappoint and has clearly maintained its standard.

I really like the waitresses — they were warm, welcoming, and served me with a smile during my visit, which made the experience especially pleasant.

The complimentary ice cream is also a lovely touch. It’s surprisingly tasty and a thoughtful gesture that I truly appreciate.

The space itself is also quite Instagram-worthy, making it a nice spot to enjoy both the food and the ambience. Thank you!
author: Franciz “SG FlavorScape”

review_text:
Friendly staff in this restaurant with a lady on the first floor to guide you up the beautifully decorated stairs to the restaurant.

Loads of options available on the menu, ensuring there is definitely something for everyone.

The Jok Bal (Braised Pork Trotters) was a popular choice for the whole day. Beautifully braised in a sweet & savoury marinade, the trotter was tender with a nice chewy skin.

Cheese Dak Galbi (Cheese Spicy Stir Fried Chicken) is another favourite and paired well with the rice.

Gyeran Jjim (Steamed Egg) & Sarigomtang Myun was average but the kids enjoyed them over the other spicy options.

Gave the Spicy Boneless Chicken Feet a shot & it was on the spicier side. A good option for anyone who likes chicken feet 😄

All in all, a nice meal for everyone & recommended for anyone who is looking for a nice Korean meal.
author: Jing Jie Ng

review_text:
Possibly the best Korean restaurant in town.
Banchan is very tasty and refillable.
Kimchi so fresh and crunchy.
Beef ribs are full of flavours.
Ate so much until cannot stand up 😃
author: Pukamaster

review_text: Amazing spot with great vibes and delicious food! Tried the bulgogi and octopus pancake  both were super tasty and flavourful. The atmosphere was cozy, and I love that they have private dining rooms, perfect for gatherings with friends. Definitely coming back again!👍🏻
author: Kaylee Tan

review_text:
The dim sum price does not meet the standard that it’s worth.
So probably will not come again.
The pork skin is crispy but have a pork smell..
And the dim sum is push to your table very traditional way and you can select but I think will be better if have picture from menu to select as sometime no wordings to see.
This method will only work for regular old customer.. a lot of elderly people there maybe the food more to their liking.
author: EL

review_text: Red Star Restaurant is a very nostalgic place that feels like stepping back into old Singapore with its traditional push-cart service and bustling, vintage atmosphere. The dim sum is straightforward and dependable; the fried yam puffs had a nice crisp texture, and the custard buns were filled with a decent salted egg yolk lava. We also had the chee cheong fun, prawn dumplings, and braised pork ribs, all of which were standard and satisfying. It’s a reliable, no-frills spot if you’re looking for a simple meal that captures a bit of local history.
author: WK C

review_text:
This restaurant offers a very traditional Hong Kong style dim sum cart experience. The atmosphere feels like stepping back into the 1990s, almost like an old-school Chinese wedding banquet, super retro and nostalgic. Orders are recorded in a small booklet, and every time you take an item from the cart, the staff stamps it. That simple detail really brings back the old Hong Kong dim sum culture, which is becoming quite rare to find these days. I truly appreciate the effort to preserve this tradition.

Service is relatively good. However, not all dishes are available directly from the carts. Some items need to be ordered separately, and the staff will bring them to your table. Also, certain dishes are only available on weekends, so do take note of that when visiting.

As for the food, it was decent but not particularly impressive. The dishes retain their traditional taste and portion sizes, which is commendable, but there is definitely room for improvement. Especially in terms of flavor depth or having a standout specialty. Compared to dim sum in Johor or even Kuala Lumpur, it doesn’t quite measure up yet. That said, with some refinement, this place has the potential to better showcase and elevate traditional dim sum.
author: Jason Chia

review_text:
Came here for the old school atmosphere and was not disappointed.

The restaurant is huge and there were lots of tables and seats so was not surprised that we didnt have to wait for a table. This was a weekday lunch btw.

Once seated, a barrage of trolleys started serving us food. Virtually no wait time to start eating. However as the food are always on the cart, some of the fried stuff had already cooled and lost its crisp.

Food was normal, i would come once for the experience. The authentic HK cha chang tng is definitely more hectic and fun experience.

Notice that most of the staff are quite elderly. Kudos for hiring and retaining the old folks.
author: Ben Teo

review_text:
Tucked away along Chin Swee Road, Red Star Restaurant offers a truly traditional dining experience. With its round tables, carpeted floors, and private dinning rooms for special occasions, the setting feels like a charming throwback in time.

Taking the lift from Block 54 up to the 7th floor feels very much like stepping into style—and you’re greeted by the restaurant.

It was my first visit, and we were seated in a private room, which added to the nostalgic charm. The service was attentive, and the food delectable!.

I have a sweet tooth so my personal favourite was the Yam Paste with Gingko nunts & Cocount cream- creamy and sweet - making it a perfect memorable part of our exclusive Cantonese dinning experience!

You can truly call this a part of Singapore’s culinary heritage. I later found out that this gem is kept alive by Grand Master Chefs Sin Leong and Hooi Kok Wai—two of the remaining members of the legendary Four Heavenly Kings of Cantonese Cuisine.

Do Chilli Crab, Yam Ring, Yu Sheng (Raw Fish Salad), and USA Duck ring a bell? These iconic dishes were created by them. How awesome is that!
author: Kath S.

review_text:
Food was amazing, chilli crab is addictive. The mantou was pipping hot, so crispy and soft on the inside. I think I still think about it everyday, it has been a week since I had cny day 2 lunch there.

The atmosphere is so nice, with a photo section to take nice photos. Really recommend wholeheartedly. Friends were all very impressed.
author: Alex Chan

review_text:
Top notch service, good ambience, great food!
The service staff were friendly and helpful, gave us recommendations and the dishes were so satisfying. The seafood was fresh and dishes were not so salty. The deep fried soon hock was fried to light crisp and the Alaskan king crab was so good! An unforgettable dining experience!
author: Angela Y

review_text: Its located on 2nd floor of 5 stars hotel. I felt that the Staffs were not that warm welcoming us. Dull and boring ambiance. Ordered as per waiter's suggested for Alaskan crab which on promo, great price but i think its not fresh  live crab  and ordered steam prawn garlic, but too bad those menus taste mediocore not reach my expectation.
author: Dee Jessup

review_text:
Hola everybody.

Had Tim Sum buffet lunch with 2buddies @  “.. Red House At The Grand
Copthorne..” recently Aug 2025.

One of the better timSum buffet I’ve eaten so far.

Everything was on point.

Service was excellent. The restaurant Manager Candy was superb in her PR and professionalism. 👍🏽

Likewise for the service staff Esply Michael. Super attentive.

The standout Tim sum dishes for me are …🤔 I think almost everything. 😅

We ordered almost everything on the buffet menu except the grouper fish porridge and the fried bHoon.

Reorder some notable dishes like the poached chk with ginger scallion garnish, mined pork roll (heychor), chicken feet, steam pork ribs, fried carrot cake…etc. Burp. 😅

Their dessert only 3types (cold). The boboChaCha is good. 👍🏽

A fully satisfying meal. 🤗

Hurry come try. Candy mention maybe their timSum buffet promo will end soon probably in Sept.

Not confirm. Depending on the head chef.
author: J X

review_text: We had dinner in a private room. All of us were impressed with the food quality, presentation and value. The service was also excellent (which is quite rare in sg these days). The restaurant even made an elaborate set up for the birthday celebration. The decor at this outlet is also beautiful and makes for great photos.  2 things that made the experience less than perfect: 1) private room was very warm and the door had to be kept open for ventilation. Perhaps they need to place a fan or a mini cooler within the room. 2)signages in the hotel needs to be improved as all of us had difficulty locating the restaurant
author: Yvonne Ng

restaurant_name: Yum Cha Restaurant | Best Dim Sum in Chinatown
review_text:
I had such a blast at Yum Cha Chinatown! The food was so well made and layered, and it was a beautiful visual rendition of what our traditional dimsum can be!

My favourite has to be the pork! It was vinegary and sweet and the meat was so tender. I love the pickled snow pear and the fried shredded ginger ontop, such a palette cleanser!

Thank you Melody for having us! Loved the food
author: Shiny Phua

restaurant_name: Yum Cha Restaurant | Best Dim Sum in Chinatown
review_text: Yum Cha dim sum tea house since 2000 in a shophouse setting brings charm to traditional hand made old school dim sum dishes. We enjoyed the food selection and atmosphere. A robot will deliver the food from the kitchen to the server at the middle of the Dinning Hall and will be served at no time. No services for tea pouring. Nothing fancy just enjoy old school dim sum in old shophouse to bring back nostalgic memories. Buffet available from 3pm approximately $43 including tax per pax. Do visit Yum Cha when around this area. 🥟🥠🍥🍤🧆
author: Clara Poh

restaurant_name: Yum Cha Restaurant | Best Dim Sum in Chinatown
review_text: Six of us had lunch at this restaurant on 21 Jan. The tim sum here is tasty and prices are reasonable. Service is also good and location is just walk from the MRT station. Also a great place to walk around the Chinatown after the meal. Worth visiting while in Chinatown.
author: Jon Ng

restaurant_name: Yum Cha Restaurant | Best Dim Sum in Chinatown
review_text:
Atmosphere rather noisy,Food average, Ee-Fu noodles good, congee both too thicken like glue, Char Siu rice roll poorly texture. Har kow good,Siew Mai average. Service is good. Double boiled Soup overly salt.
We are tourist but we eat what is tasty what is not.
author: Henry Low

restaurant_name: Yum Cha Restaurant | Best Dim Sum in Chinatown
review_text:
Very good service and dim sum. Favoured by locals and tourist
Har gao is very fresh and prawns are huge

Carrot cake is crispy and taste good
Char siew bao is very delicious too
Service is great. Slightly pricey but worth it
author: Sean T

review_text: Overall good experience. The chocolate cake called Crumbs of Curiosity was decent enough and similar to most of other chocolate cakes. The iced caramel latte coffee was nice and good for sweet tooth like me. Overall ambience was good and such a chill place to relax or to socialize in groups.
author: Jonathan Kenichi

review_text: ​The Book Cafe isn't just a place to grab a coffee; it's an institution in Singapore's café scene and truly lives up to its self-proclaimed title as a "second living room." All-Day Breakfast: Their hearty brunch classics, like the Breakfast Steak & Eggs or Eggs Benedict, are fan favourites and are available long past traditional breakfast hours. ​The Book Cafe is a must-visit for anyone in Singapore looking for a genuine escape. It brilliantly merges the quiet inspiration of a library with the warmth of a local diner. If you can snag a prized spot on one of the comfy sofas, you'll find yourself happily losing track of time here, whether you're reading a book, crunching numbers, or simply enjoying a leisurely meal with friends #thebookcafe #quaint #quiet #
author: Neha

review_text:
Visiting here the 1st time on last Sunday . I love the vibe here , where I can sit outside without feeling heat. Thanks to the big ceiling fan .:))
The mocha was so so, but the apple cake is nice , not so sweet . The waiter also came to ask me about that sweetness level , and that’s exactly the thing I intended to say . Definitely I will come again .
author: Tho Nguyen

review_text:
We came at about 8pm and the place was peaceful with jazzy music in the background. Perfect ambience.

We ordered the Crumbs of Curiosity Chocolate cake, chicken-in-wonderland (grilled chicken) and Pulled porky & Bess burger.

Food was absolutely perfect, fries and wedges were fried to perfection with just the right amount of seasoning. Chicken was smoky and juicy, while the pulled pork burger had a lot of meat. The cake was not overly sweet and you can tell that it is made of good quality chocolate.

Service was impeccable and the staff were very polite.

10/10 will come again. Recommended if you wish to hotdesk here as they do have multiple power plugs around.
author: Janelle Yip

review_text: My favourite cafe in Singapore. They play wonderful music, have perfect lighting design, serve good coffee and properly cooked food that’s not overpriced. Everyone is either quietly reading or having their meal. Most importantly, their service is excellent. I was blessed to be served by Avis who takes her job seriously and brings a smile to all of her customers.
author: Tan Chiew Hong

review_text:
I visited this restaurant on my birthday, and it was truly a wonderful experience. The service from the staff, especially Melissa and Alfred, was exceptional. They were incredibly attentive, warm, and genuinely caring, which made the evening feel very special and memorable.

The food was delicious, beautifully prepared, and full of flavor. On top of that, the view was stunning and added so much to the overall atmosphere.

I was deeply impressed. Highly recommended.
author: Florence

review_text: The views from this place are one of the best on the island. Their beers are even better. Their cocktails are okay and the fries didn’t disappoint either. This place needs early reservations for weekend slots. Their wheat beer was wonderful. It’s amazing how they make all that beer up here on the 33rd floor. The service is very good and the waiters don’t mind taking pictures for you. They even have a designated photo spot to get good views of MBS and the vicinity. Would definitely recommend to experience this place at least once.
author: Rajeev Mangaladarshan Sundaralingam

review_text:
Went on a Saturday for lunch and opted for their lunch set — great decision. The beef tartare was fresh and well-balanced, the white fish sashimi was clean and delicate, and both the chicken and salmon were cooked nicely without being overdone.

For dessert we had crispy churros on the outside, soft inside, and the lava chocolate cake. Portions were satisfying without being overly heavy, making it a very comfortable lunch.

The overall experience felt thoughtful and well-paced. Solid spot for a relaxed yet quality lunch — would happily come back again.
author: E W

review_text:
Level 33 provides a solid dining experience anchored by its breathtaking panoramic view of Marina Bay, which is the undeniable main attraction. The food is decent, with notable highlights including a rich and creamy burrata, perfectly balanced with sweet, acidic tomatoes, and an amazing mango-pineapple dessert tart. The well-crafted drinks are a plus, though some dishes, like the surprisingly lean Wagyu beef, don't fully meet expectations.

For the best visit, time your trip for late afternoon to capture the sunset, or secure an evening reservation to watch the city lights come alive. The venue is consistently popular, especially on weekends, so booking ahead is essential to enjoy the vibrant atmosphere and unforgettable vistas, which ultimately make the visit worthwhile.
author: Ribeye

review_text: We booked outdoor seating and the marina bay view was absolutely worth it. The beer paddle and cocktails were excellent, and the food from the cart was tasty. Service was friendly and even helped us take great photos. The only drawback was the repeated reminders about the minimum spend, which felt a bit pushy. Overall, a great spot with good food, drinks, and atmosphere.
author: Li Nh

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (11 New Bridge Road)
review_text:
The soup has a light color, but don’t let that fool you—the peppery kick is strong, and the stewed pork ribs are incredibly soft and tender. From the first sip, you're welcomed by rich, warming flavors that comfort your soul, with just the right balance of spice.🥰
Even though we had eaten earlier in the day already, but the flavors here made us want to keep going. The hearty soup not only warms your soul but also leaves you feeling energized and satisfied.
author: Wayne Star

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (11 New Bridge Road)
review_text:
This place is amazing. Unlimited soup refill and it is boiling hot that warms up your stomach and your soul. Also ordered two other dishes and all came out as happy surprises. The lychee drink is not sweet but fresh and enjoyable. Service is amazing if they are not tooooo busy. Or, just ask.

Tip: make sure you arrive before 11:15am to avoid a long line.
author: Xuan “Shawn” Li

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (11 New Bridge Road)
review_text: The restaurant serves delicious Chinese food. The restaurant is usually crowded so you have to queue to be served. The staff is very friendly and enthusiastic. The prices are reasonable.
author: FrancisP

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (11 New Bridge Road)
review_text: Finally we get to try this Michelin star Bak kut teh!. totally satisfied  and happy!! Ordered the premium loin soup, its is good as advertised! The soup is thick &  flovourful and not salty.  the chicken feet is surprisingly good!! It's so good, nothing left!
author: joseph ng

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (11 New Bridge Road)
review_text: Taste here at this outlet is less impactful compared to other outlets, have a feeling it’s adjusted due to the number of tourists visiting this outlet. Regardless food quality is still good and worth going. Service is exceptional
author: TLBX

restaurant_name: L'Entrecôte Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
review_text: Went on Christmas Eve and had the dinner set, which was really good value for money. As first-timers, I requested a separate sauce for the steak (just in case 🙂), and they happily obliged. Boy, was I wrong—now I know why the meat came drenched in the sauce. It was wonderful! Kannan was lovely and took care of us. It was busy, but the service was quick.
author: yates_111 yates

restaurant_name: L'Entrecôte Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
review_text: We had lunch on Sunday. The restaurant was practically empty, so we were served quickly. The steaks were tender and juicy with a delicious sauce, the fries were soft on the inside and crispy on the outside, and the salad was okay. The tartare was tender and well-seasoned. Overall, a good experience. I recommend it.
author: Daiana Peres Nunes

restaurant_name: L'Entrecôte Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
review_text:
Had a lovely dining experience here! The staff were really friendly and observant throughout our meal. Special shoutout to the dashing Indian gentleman (I think he might be the manager) — he was super warm and thoughtful. Thank you again for the special birthday cake arrangement, and for personally coming over to wish me a happy birthday. That small gesture really made my day 😊 (p.s. we accidentally pressed 3 star on the app, it should’ve been a 5 star)

Food & Environment
The beef steak was decent, though I’d say the prices lean a bit on the higher side. The environment was quite lively and noisy since the restaurant was about 80% full, so not a very good place if you need to share some stuff between your friends and the seating between you and the next customer felt a little tight and close 🥹

Overall, great service and a memorable birthday touch. Would come back for the service and hospitality!
author: yuting

restaurant_name: L'Entrecôte Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
review_text:
The  food feels average for the price.

We ordered the beef carpaccio, foie gras, onion soup, two steaks, and three desserts. Overall, everything was decent,nothing was very bad, but nothing really stood out either.
Will I come bk again, maybe no.

The foie gras, in particular, didn’t quite feel as authentic as what you’d get in France, though I understand that this is fairly common in Singapore. The steaks were fine, not especially memorable. Desserts were okay as well, quite traditional, but without much wow factor.

For 3 people, the bill came close to SGD 300 even without ordering any alcohol, which made the value feel a bit questionable for what we got.

Overall, it’s not a bad place and you won’t leave unhappy, but at this price point, expectations would naturally be higher.
author: hey Xy

restaurant_name: L'Entrecôte Singapore Duxton Hill, The Steak & Fries Bistro
review_text: Steak was pretty decent and I really liked the sauce. The lava cake was good as well. Kannan’s service was amazing, he was very attentive and made our dining experience better. Would come back just to support him ☺️
author: Cherie Lee

review_text:
Your after-work gathering spot just got a MAJOR glow-up. 🍻🔥

We’re back at Harry's for their refreshed menu, and the bites are simply mouth-watering.

Harry's still your go-to for easy drinks and good vibes, but now evolved into a lively social space where hearty plates, bold Asian flavours and classic Western favourites come together. Whether it’s after-work drinks, family dinners or chill catch-ups, Harry’s is serving something for everyone at the table.

MUST-TRY HIGHLIGHTS
🦞 Spiny Lobster Spaghettini ($38) – A playful local twist inspired by Hokkien mee, topped with a whole spiny lobster and housemade sambal belacan.
🐟 Cream of the Catch ($38) – Flaky pan-seared miso cod on spinach with a bright lemon caper cream sauce.
🍖 Herb-Marinated Tomapork ($29) – Juicy, hearty and packed with flavour. Oh and loving how tender the meat is, as it is done sous vide style.

My choice of sharing bites in the following order:
• Crab & Potato Croquettes ($16/6pcs)
• Harry’s Signature Wings ($17/6pcs)
• Salt & Pepper Chicken Poppers ($15)
• Sticky Mirin Sweet Soy Wings ($15)
• Kurobuta Stuffed Pockets ($14)

🍸 DRINKS FOR EVERYONE
From fresh beers from the tap, refreshing cocktails to no-alcohol options like Paloma Fizz and Big Drop alcohol-free beers — no one gets left out.

Good food. Easy drinks. Great company.
Harry’s just gave us another reason to stay a little longer. 😉
author: Kean 《keanmono IG & TT》

review_text: The food, service and atmosphere was fantastic. Food quality was good and what added on more was the 1-for -1 lunch was a fantastic deal. Service was superb. Will come back! Thank u!
author: Winnie Chua SW

review_text:
2026 March First visit to Harry's because of East Coast Comedy show. Enjoyed all the Malaysians comedians and the best of the lineup would be Dr Jason Leong, followed by Keren, then Mikhail and Brian Tan. Harry's good venue and we were surprised the food pretty good. Liked both the beer battered chips and the rendang lasagna. A little overpriced, but the fish was good quality, the flavor good, and the rendang lasagna an interesting fusion dish.

However, sadly Harry's home beer is just average, did not taste the Yuzu at all. The air conditioner was clearly underpowered for the crowd, was on the verge of being uncomfortable for many. Need another one for this venue, or it has to be somehow fixed.

Won't claim that I'm a mixologist or know the exact proportions for a Bloody Harry. But this was so salty that it was nearly inedible. At least 5-8x too much salt was placed within it, clearly an error. After choking down about 15% of it, tried diluting it with water. So it went from almost inedible to extremely unpalatable. Drank about 10% more cuz ADHD hamster-brain while listening to jokes, started idly going through in my mind trying to estimate just how many times the proper amount of salt was added. Ended up with previous figure. Finally totally gave up on it.

The negroni was fine.

Downloaded the Harry's app but it was quite frustrating, badly designed and slow. We ended up ordering from Harry's website only. The food took nearly an hour to come - though I understand that this was because the kitchen was understaffed, it was nevertheless not an ideal state of affairs. Food was pleasant, as previously mentioned.

Nonetheless we enjoyed our Friday night date with the Malaysian comedians and their friendly totally relatable banter. The staff who were present did well, presentable, affable, and efficient.
author: JR FF

review_text: Very attentive staffs and warm service. Foods was nice and portions were big. Special thanks to Chris and Glenn for the complimentary dessert for my son's birthday, appreciate that very much.
author: Justin Law

review_text:
Not our first visit to Harry’s Bar at Boat Quay, and it never disappoints. The food is consistently good, and the draught beer is always fresh and refreshing.

Highly recommend the truffle mushroom pizza — a definite must-try!

The staff are very friendly and attentive, especially Kumar and Christina. Kumar always makes sure we are well taken care of, which really adds to the overall dining experience.

Will definitely keep coming back! 🍕🍺
author: seren po

review_text:
We recently celebrated a birthday at Spring Court and had a truly delightful evening.
The meal was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully executed. The broccoli with scallops was cooked to perfection. The roasted duck was exceptional, easily one of the best we’ve had — crisp skin, succulent meat, and deeply flavourful without being heavy. The roasted chicken was equally well done, tender and not overly oily. The Ee Fu noodles were fragrant and satisfying, rounding out the meal wonderfully.
A lovely highlight was the complimentary longevity buns presented for the birthday celebration — a gracious and thoughtful gesture that added a special touch to the occasion.
Service was impeccable throughout. The staff were attentive, frequently refilling our tea and water. The hospitality was warm, polished, and consistent from start to finish.
A memorable dining experience!
author: K Cynthia

review_text:
impressive food.
most of the dishes were very nicely done.

Had a great meal and will be back for sure.

Attentive service from the staff as well
author: Ars 3276

review_text:
Spring Court is a distinguished heritage restaurant renowned for its traditional Cantonese cuisine, with a legacy spanning nearly a century. Having dined here on numerous occasions, we returned this year to celebrate Mother's Day. We ordered the claypot chili crab, which was fresh, meaty, and delicious as usual. While my mother appreciated the kongbak, I found the gravy slightly too watery, as I prefer a more viscous consistency for the kongbak gravy. The dim sum we had were both flavorful, though the golden dragon chicken was somewhat underwhelming. The cabbage with dried scallops was light and sweet, enhanced by the umami essence of the dried scallops. The fried glutinous rice was a crowd favorite and wasn't soggy.

The worst dish of the meal was actually the melon sago, which was too sweet and probably tasted worse than crappy desserts at a koufu or kopitiam food court. Service was notably slow on this occasion, though understandable given the occasion. The staff graciously waived the charge for the dessert we barely touched.
author: Julius Tan

review_text:
We had a wonderful evening here last night with my work partners. Xiao Chen (小陈） from the “Chrysanthemum” private room provided us with warm, enthusiastic, and professional service. She made us feel very welcome, and my guests couldn’t stop praising her.
The dishes were as delicious as always and the portions were generous. Everyone enjoyed every dish we ordered.
I’ll definitely choose this place again the next time when I have business or family dinner.
author: 淡色绿茶

review_text: We really enjoyed our meal today. Every dish was flavourful, authentic, and beautifully prepared. The staff were friendly and attentive. We will definitely come back again!
author: gskang

review_text:
Came here on a Friday afternoon and had the “Sicilian Journey” 5 course taster menu and was thoroughly impressed. I try not to give too many 5 star reviews but my lunch was faultless. Service was very attentive and ambience was great.

Regarding the food, the highlight for me from the menu in my opinion was the prawn and truffle ravioli, which was creamy without being overpoweringly rich (I could have drunk the sauce like a soup it was so tasty). Also the dessert was an  amazing finish to the meal, the tart having a perfect texture to it providing just the right amount of bite and complementing the other textures on the plate including the beautifully constructed mini Italian meringues which I loved. Also the red berry sauce giving a perfect offset to the nuttiness of the pistachio cream.

Surprised that this place was not so busy given the quality of the food and without naming any names the offering here is far superior than other comparable restaurants in the area. Will for sure come back again with another group and this time try the wine pairing.
author: Dwk Y

review_text:
Every seafood dish was Umami, and the service was warm. Have been to Italy twice, I would say this restaurant is authentic in terms my own understanding on ‘Italian cuisine’. Not Sicilian, though, cause I have never been there before.
The pistachio tart was so ‘pistachio’, love it.
author: Xialing Chen

review_text: My first visit to the one & only Sicilian restaurant in Singapore. Came over for Restaurant week! And of course I had an amazing dining experience. The crew in Gattopardo was lovely and friendly. Loved every course that I had. They were tasty! The wine was lovely as well. They have a great selection of Sicilian wines. Had such a wonderful time dining, I would definitely come back to try different set menu’s next time.
author: Bernie Chin
