review_text: Lovely McDonald's ever! Perfect spot in Gardens by the Bay – grab a Big Mac and chill with epic Supertree views. Super convenient after walking around, air-con bliss on hot days, clean and fast service. Total win for a quick bite! 5 stars 🌟🍔
author: JAO JAO

review_text: We went on a quiet morning with our two small dogs and wanted to sit in the outdoor area which was empty but was turned away by the staff who pointed a sign that says "No Pets". However since January 1, 2025, Singapore law allows dogs to be present at private restaurants' outdoor dining areas. It's a shame that Macdonalds has not updated their rules. Gardens by the Bay is a popular place for dog lovers to bring their pets for a walk and Macdonalds should review their rules on this.
author: STEK TAN

review_text: I understand that the place was rather crowded, but 10 dollars for this? Not worth it. Also, they did not even bother calling out the number, resulting in the food getting cold. Go to somewhere else.
author: LEONARDO ZHANG HAO RAN HCI

review_text: Well, it’s no different from other McDonald’s but since it is close to the Cloud Forest and Flower Dome makes it a nice place to rest and have some refreshments after walking around, especially if you’re here with family. The vacation vibes is strong since all of the visitors are practically tourist.
author: Galih D. Putranto

review_text: Located near to the Flower Dome and Cloud Forest. Good place to eat when not many food places here. Quite small inside though.
author: snk

review_text:
Palm Restaurant Review

*Rating:* 2.5/5

I recently had the opportunity to dine at the Palm Restaurant, located within Singapore Swimming Club. While the setting is lovely, our experience was a bit of a mixed bag.

*Ambiance:* 4/5
The restaurant's ambiance is elegant and inviting, perfect for a special occasion or a night out with friends and family.

*Food:* 4/5
The menu is impressive, offering a wide variety of dishes from local cuisines to Western favorites like pasta. We were excited to try out different options, and the food was generally delicious.

*Service:* 2/5
Unfortunately, the service was a letdown. Because reservations are not allowed, we had to arrive early to secure a table for our large group. However, once seated, we had to wait quite a while for our orders to be taken and served. The waiters seemed overwhelmed and the service was not friendly.

*Value:* 3/5
Given the quality of food and service, the prices were reasonable. However, the lack of reservations and slow service might deter some diners.

*Overall:* 2.5/5
While the Palm Restaurant has potential, the service needs significant improvement. If you're planning to visit, arrive early to secure a table, and be patient with the staff.
author: Chris Family Reviews

review_text:
A friend invited us for lunch here. The restaurant is spacious with plenty of sitting space. It offers a wide variety of food, from local, Chinese and Indian. We ordered our food for sharing.
First was the laksa. It a big bowl which is enough for two small eaters to share. Generous amount of noodles and ingredients. The laksa gravy had good coconut taste and it is not spicy.
Both the chicken tikka masala and the fish curry were excellent and goes well with the garlic butter naan and the briyani rice. The two paneer dishes were ok.
I like the mutton briyani but it was quite gamy. Some people may not enjoy it. Overall, there was enough food for the four of us.
The cakes and coffee were enjoyable.
Service here was good.
author: Jacob TAN

review_text: Food was average but ok value.  Rojak was average, tauhu goreng was good, laksa was too lemak and not enough flavour, the pan fried bee hoon had a lot of carbs/ bee hoon but not much ingredients.  The chempedak cake, yam cake were not bad, soft and spongy and can taste the chempedak/ yam.  The Christmas log cakes we took away were a bit dry.  Service was disappointing, seems rather short-handed and hard to get their attention even though it was not that crowded.  We were there on a Tuesday night.
author: Bugwagen

review_text: Been coming to The Palms, a cafe at Singapore Swimming Club, since I was a child decades ago. So glad this cafe is still doing well all these years! They try to reinvent themselves with their menu that gets refreshed periodically. The staff here are their biggest asset, and although they can get busy during peak hours, they do put their best foot forward to serve the diners. The food is usually quite good here too. Thank you! 🙏🏻
author: Ashley Liew

review_text: Okay it seems they have an Indian chef really skilled. The Indian food we ordered was really good and not too spicy so we could really enjoy it. Check some of the pictures... The only thing is the service that is not really competitive. Quite slow and we had to wait like 15min just to have others garlic naans (Indian bread). Thats the only thing actually not perfect 😅
author: Aud Vianney

review_text:
I had an amazing experience at this Thai chicken rice stall! The chicken was absolutely delicious—tender and juicy on the inside, with a perfectly crispy exterior. The sauce was spot-on, adding just the right amount of kick and complementing the chicken beautifully.

To top it off, the shop owner was incredibly friendly and welcoming, making the whole experience even better. She’s also very charming, which just adds to the warmth of the place. If you’re craving authentic Thai chicken rice with great service, this is definitely the place to go!
author: Max Tan

review_text: Very nice fried chicken & rice, decent price and amazing service! ♥️ would come here again!
author: Mishkan O

review_text:
Been back at least 5 times. The fried chicken is sooooo good, it's very crispy on the outside. The inside is still moist and soft. The chili at the side is very good as well.

Even though the food is fried, it doesn't feel oily or give that uncomfortable feeling after the meal. That's so hard to achieve. Well done. Will be back
author: Melody Heng

review_text: I eat thai food very often and i have to say Ooh Fu Thai standard is REALLY GOOD. I tried the omelette egg with prawn and fried rice and the egg is so fluffy and delicious! The fried rice brings a great fragrance too without being oily. Highly recommend this stall as they the food quality is really of good standard!!!
author: Will Lim

review_text: Char kway teow dry and tastless, no fresh chillies available, only sweet chilli sauce. Good size portion. Thai beef mince was tiny portion for $12. Don't order any of these dishes.
author: MiiaKoi

review_text: The quality of the satay meat is good, although the peanut sauce was a little too creamy and fine grain for my taste. Be sure to order ketupat if you want some with the satay. The otak was reasonable.
author: Elaine C

review_text:
Review of City Satay at Satay by the Bay

I visited City Satay around 9 PM, and despite them nearing closing time, we managed to get 50 sticks of satay for $45, which is about $0.90 per stick. We had a mix of pork, chicken, beef, and lamb, plus two ketupat. The satay was flavorful, and overall, it was great value for money. The only downside was that the satay pieces were a bit smaller compared to other places I’ve tried. Overall, a solid experience with good taste and decent value.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text: Got 10 pork satays. Almost all are charred, you can see them when you flipped the decent looking ones over. Mostly lean meat. Long queue so might have rushed through the barbecuing. Tasted nicer elsewhere.
author: Kate Lim

review_text: Non aircon. Not halal. Standard seems to vary. I ordered a mixture last time and was good. This time I ordered just pork belly satay, and each is $1.80/stick. Not cheap, although they did tell me before I pay. Seems too heavy to only eat pork belly too. My recommendation is to order a mixture, other types of meat are affordable. Disappointed that they burnt the tip of some sticks, like in photo. That is $0.60 that is not going into my mouth!
author: Lim Jaspar

review_text: Located a few minutes from garden by the bay, this satay had a long queue compared to the one nearby. The difference is that this store offers pork satay which the other store doesn’t. However the pork satay is one time more expensive at $1.8 per stock compared to other meats at $0.9.  The wait to order is quite long after which you need to wait to collect when ready. It comes with spicy peanut sauce and cucumber only, no onions. The pork satay is disappointing as the meat is quite stiff.  The others are still ok
author: Susan Tay

restaurant_name: Makan By The Bay Seafood Halal
review_text: Order beef hor fun and chicken fried rice. Meat seems like frozen and uncooked amd taste like rotten meat. Food served cold. Definitely will not try it again.
author: James Tang - Real Estate

restaurant_name: Makan By The Bay Seafood Halal
review_text: $18 for 18 pcs of gong gong and the gong wasn’t cleaned and they were inedible. Would not recommend the gong gong
author: nur aisyah

restaurant_name: Makan By The Bay Seafood Halal
review_text:
Seems to have wider variety of traditional Chinese zichar stall dishes than Boon Tat Seafood stall, in terms of individual rices/noodles.

BBQ dishes starts at $20, instead of $16 at other BBQ seafood stalls.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

restaurant_name: Makan By The Bay Seafood Halal
review_text:
Owner was very mean and told me he is on a break. come back after 15 minutes. I came back after waiting and order something from the menu. He says it’s not available anymore. I ask for the seasonal price on something else and seemingly forgetting he has it on his menu he raises his voice and says ‘you need to follow the menu do not order anything which is not on the menu’ and he kept walking off to use his phone while i was speaking.

I was being very polite.

I kept going through all different menu items I want to order and each one he either tells me he cannot make because it isn’t in stock.

I ask to order a menu item that is in stock and he tells me the price is $50 when the menu says $20.

He just kept convincing me not to order things or telling me they’re not in stock or telling me the price is triple what the menu says. Obviously he can’t be bothered to make food, so why run a restaurant? Just be honest and polite and tell me you can’t be bothered.
author: James Coulson

restaurant_name: Makan By The Bay Seafood Halal
review_text: What is this??? You call this pineapple fried rice??? This is the worst pineapple fried rice i ever eaten
author: Lookilo Toh

review_text: Very Nice food with humble and smiling staff... especially Adana Kabab and Humus with Flafil.. and in the end king of sweets Gulab Jamun.....We enjoyed alot
author: Izcorpion Shah

review_text: Absolutely gross! $12 for hummus and see the amount of hummus on the plate. Falafel wrap with 1 falafel and vegetables slammed with mayonnaise. Truly unbelievable. Don’t even consider eating here. Worst choice ever.
author: Joe Loo

review_text:
Bad experience

Butter Masala tasted nothing like it. Embarrassing for the restaurant

You need to hire someone who can actually cook Indian food

Owner accepted return due to disappointment and gave refund
author: Nicholas Dow

review_text: I wish I'd read the reviews before trying this place (which is now called Turkish Indian, not Turkish Mediterranean). It is absolutely the worst hawker stall I've ever encountered. The food took an unbelievable 35 minutes to prepare and I only had one pide plus two drinks. The pide was doughy and undercooked. The mango lassi, if anything, was even worse. By far the worst mango lassi in Singapore. It was clearly made from powder with milk added. The food was also very expensive. Like, double the price of anything at Lau Pa Sat, which is already on the pricey side for a hawker centre. So, if you read this review before going to Satay by the Bay, please do yourself a favour and DO NOT GO TO THIS STALL.
author: Carbon Malibu

review_text: Tabbouleh salad mostly cabbage. $12 wrap was such a pathetic portion size.
author: Abigail Melis

restaurant_name: DumPrince Dumpling House @ Satay by the Bay
review_text: I wanted to order something light to eat. I decided to get mushroom dumplings. My order was taken right away and was ready quickly, though I was a bit sus at first. Then I took a bite, and the inside was cold and soggy. I went back and told the staff it was cold. She asked if I wanted to reheat it. Keep in mind, this was $11 for 10 dumplings. But, thankfully, the staff was nice enough to let me exchange it for noodle soup without charging me extra.
author: pei chen

restaurant_name: DumPrince Dumpling House @ Satay by the Bay
review_text:
Absolutely delicious dumplings! I always visit when I’m in the area and they are never a disappointment. Great fillings, and so yum! I’ve tried the chicken and the mushroom versions. 🫶🏻
This time I had the fired dumplings with Sambal Mayo - life changed! These are my new go-to choice. Ignore the low rating - this place is fantastic!!
author: Hazel Brinkworth

restaurant_name: DumPrince Dumpling House @ Satay by the Bay
review_text: Tasty dumplings, although a bit on the pricey side, but that's expected of the location. $11 for 10 Szichuan Chicken Dumplings. I liked the taste!
author: Florian Parzhuber

restaurant_name: DumPrince Dumpling House @ Satay by the Bay
review_text: Local Sporean here. Had the Sichuan spicy dumplings and it was yummy. It was slightly spicy, sour and flavourful. I enjoyed it very much. Its abit on the pricey side bit thats expected of this location.
author: EJ Tan

restaurant_name: DumPrince Dumpling House @ Satay by the Bay
review_text:
No idea why this place has such bad reviews. If your review name is clearly from an English speaking country and you're upset about the staff "not uttering a word", maybe consider that you're in Singapore, English isn't their first language and that any communication issues/ignorance is actually on your own part.

Ordered 10 chicken fried dumplings and 10 chicken nacho ones which are the same, just with some squirty cheese sauce and spring onions.

Waited about 10 minutes for them to be cooked fresh while the guy stood finishing making his next batches.

They were so good I went back and ordered another 10 of the deep-fried version, which were just as good.

Ignore the arrogance of my fellow country members and just eat this guy's food. You won't be disappointed.
author: Ben Mowbray

review_text: Ordered sambal stingray and sambal Sotong, total at $30. Tbh, it’s expected to cost this much since it’s in marina Bay Area but the stingray was overcooked and had a funky taste - seemed like it was probably prepared a day before and only reheated upon order since it was out within 5mins time (not achievable for a dish like this if made from scratch). The Sotong was also slightly rubbery and didn’t taste fresh (came out within 5mins too). Don’t recommend eating at this stall.
author: Ah Kay

review_text:
An overhated Hawker style takeaway serving a variety of rice/noodle dishes, omelettes , mains and seafood.

Located a stone's throw from Gardens by the Bay MRT, its a convenient stop for hungry souls. I ordered an oyster & onion omelette ($14.50 each). Not cheap, and took a while, but it did not disappoint. Warning: good luck finding seating at 7 pm!
author: Toy Galaxy

review_text:
Non aircon. Tze char style stall, affordable prices. Tried the yang zhou fried rice. There is a slight wok hey vibe. Can taste each grain, solidly. Quite generous in ingredients. I can see
a number of small shrimps. Quantity is a lot for a small size plate ($8). Service is 4 stars cos they cook so fast! Ready in 5 minutes.
author: Lim Jaspar

review_text:
Menu is on the countertop instead of the signboard [see prices in attached photos). We ordered:

1. Stingray $15, 20
2. Lala $15, 21
3. Kangkong $11 (5 to 6 pax), 16
4. Oyster omelette $13, 18
5. Hotplate beancurd $16, 21

White rice is BIG.

Beeper token will be give after order is placed. Collect food later again from counter.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: We had the pineapple rice, scallops and king prawns. They were all delicious. It wasn’t cheap but was worth what we payed. Lovely setting in the gardens.
author: Marina

review_text:
Ordered the Hokkien mee to go.

Tastes nothing like Hokkien mee. For the tourists reading this, a proper Hokkien mee should have prawn flavour. This version has no flavour at all.

And to make things worse, the noodles have a strong alkaline taste. Makes the whole dish smell and taste bad.

I ate a couple of bites and threw the entire batch away.

Avoid if you can.
author: Chris A

review_text: The servings are large, but both the oyster omelette and the fried daikon cake (chai tow kueh) were mainly omelette and not much oil.
author: Elaine C

review_text: Zero hokkien mee taste. If considering it as fried yellow noodles, maybe 2/5. Fried oyster is even worse, 1/5. Not worth it even if sold at normal hawker prices.
author: EL Ng

review_text:
Overall, the Hokkien mee’s texture was excellent, and the portion size was just right—definitely worth the wait and offering good value for money. The quality and taste are truly commendable, and I would recommend it to anyone visiting the area.

I would like to share some feedback with the intention of supporting the business’s growth and success. I noticed some inconsistency in operating hours between this outlet and information available on food review platforms, which may cause confusion for customers. Ensuring clear and consistent communication about operating times across all outlets would enhance customer trust and reliability.

At the same time, I understand that during festive seasons or busy periods, being flexible with operating hours can be beneficial. Places like Gardens by the Bay and Satay by the Bay attract many visitors, and if there is still a steady crowd, extending opening hours could allow more people—locals and tourists alike—to enjoy the food and the atmosphere.

Such flexibility not only maximizes revenue potential but also builds a strong reputation for customer care. I also appreciate that rental costs can be high, and government assistance can help ease this burden, making longer hours more feasible.

During a recent visit, I was disappointed to find the outlet closed earlier than expected after a long day at work, missing the chance to support and enjoy this local favorite. I share this feedback in the spirit of constructive encouragement, hoping the business will consider adapting to meet customer demand more flexibly.

By doing so, I believe the business can build lasting loyalty, attract a wider customer base, and continue to thrive in the long term.

Thank you for considering these points, and I look forward to seeing the continued success of this establishment.
author: Elizabeth Joyce

review_text: Eh I stupidly thought it’s fine to eat prawn noodles at a tourist attraction as you can’t screw this up. Tasteless squid and prawns that feels like they had all the flavour washed out of them. Noodles are full of alkaline flavour. Sauce has no depth.
author: Raven Tan

review_text: We needed some vegetables to complement other food we had ordered. The three dishes were satisfying and exactly what we needed.
author: Elaine C

review_text: visited satay by the bay to have a quick dinner with my family. ordered some rice and noodles dishes, but found one very very short strand of hair in our lala beehoon. it was nothing much, really, but we just decided informed them and they offered to whip up a small portion to compensate us. they ended up serving us the medium sized portion (our order) and we were shocked. it was really nice of the lady to do that. the food tasted great too!
author: sinyeeo

review_text:
Visit Date 6 October 2024

We have eaten food from this joint over the years. The food used to be good but today we were very disappointed

Food: We ordered Garlic Kailan, Chicken with Dried Chilli, Hokkien Mee, Prawn Omelette and they helped us order a mix of pork, beef and chicken satay from the nearby stall.
The kailan tasted bland and there was no salt in the omelette although with a spash of chilli sauce and soya sauce it tasted alright. Their chilli sauce from the sauce counter was quite good. The Hokkien Mee looked very unappetising and the gravy was watery. We discarded the 2 prawns in it and of course the heads that had come off. There were some slices of sotong but there was no taste when chewed. We found and picked the tiny pieces of chicken from the Chicken with Dried Chilli that was filled with a bed of onion pieces. The chicken sauce was okay-ish. The satays were well grilled and juicy and the sauce tasty

Service: the staff was friendly and gave good suggestion. Food order was taken quite efficiently and the buzzer alert was quick. Their cutlery and sauce station was well stocked

Atmosphere: I am very fond of the open setting and ambience of Satay By the Bay. The rating on ambience is certainly not a reflection of Marina BBQ Seafood.
author: Barnali Roy

review_text:
I don’t usually leave negative reviews for food places, but after 3 consistently disappointing visits, spread over a few months, I think it’s fair to say this stall has issues. Every time I’ve come, the staff seemed disinterested, like I’m bothering them just by placing an order.

The food itself is nothing to write about. If you’re wondering why I came back a 3rd time after two underwhelming visits, it’s because I was with other who wanted to try something on the menu, and I figured maybe I’d just had bad luck before. Unfortunately, this third time confirmed it for me, I won’t be coming back.
author: Lim fui kin

review_text: Overpriced, terrible food that is not fresh!!! $80 for a tiny crab which they said weighted 600-700g. Nevermind it’s overpriced, crab is dead and not fresh with very soft mushy meat. Worst chili crab we ever had. Tastes horrible. Fried rice and fried Hokkien mee terrible too. Avoid by all cost. Tried this only because we were here with tourists friends and waiting for supertree night show.
author: J C

review_text: Got wings and black carrot cake from stall. Food is decent. Owner auto charged large plate and 5 wings without asking. Min order was 3 wings and there’s small portion for carrot cake. Need to be alert when ordering from them. Min 10 satay but auto charged another tourist 20 satays.
author: Kate Lim

review_text: One of the best carrot cake I had. And the service is fast and friendly. I love this place.
author: Jairo Cesar

review_text: The chicken tasted nice but when I cut deep in to it, it was not cooked properly. Staff did not care at all and begrudgingly gave me a refund.
author: Lorcan Wade

review_text: Rude service by the staff, spoke as though we could not understand them and did not bother to take our order timely.
author: Loizen

review_text: Popiqh was great!
author: lina rosquist

review_text:
Had a nice meal at TungLok Seafood at Gardens by the Bay. We ordered a fried asparagus dish which was tender and crunchy and braised house special beancurd with nameko mushrooms and vegetables, which was light and flavourful.

The fried mee sua was well done — tasty and not oily at all. We also had the tangjia braised fish maw soup, which was rich and comforting without being too heavy.

Dessert was our favourite part. The chilled mango cream with pomelo and mango ice cream was mouthwatering. We also tried the black glutinous rice with durian purée and coconut ice cream which was normal compared to the 1st. Lastly, the fresh coconut was surprisingly tender and the coconut water was super refreshing, pairing really well with the dessert.

Overall, a pleasant dining experience with good food in a beautiful setting. Would come back again.
author: Yuki Yumi

review_text:
We had a lovely lunch at TungLok Seafood at Gardens by the Bay, and it was the perfect, relaxing pause after a long day of walking around the area. The miso soup was an absolutely delicious start— comforting, perfectly seasoned, and full of depth.

We also tried the unagi chawanmushi (the egg pudding with eel topping) and it was hands-down the most unique dish of the meal. The silky egg custard mixed with the savory richness of the eel created a flavor combination that was completely amazing.

For mains, we ordered the crab fried rice, the deep-fried juicy prawns, and the calamari. Every single dish was exceptional — fresh, well-cooked, and bursting with flavor.

The service was very polite and attentive, and the overall ambience was calm, restful, and exactly what we needed after exploring the gardens. A truly delightful experience!
author: Sandeepa Dey

review_text: I want to share my wonderful experience at the restaurant, specifically regarding the service provided by Sarah. Despite the restaurant being incredibly busy, Sarah was exceptionally patient and kind to both the elderly members of our group and my children. She even took the time to check in on our dining experience and ensure we were enjoying ourselves. The food was outstanding—the chili crab is a must-try! Thank you, Sarah.
author: You

review_text: This is my second trip to Tunglok Seafood (Garden by the bay). On my first trip, we’re impressed with deep fried marble goby & Chili crab. Hence, on second trip, we ordered the same. Found that the fish (1 kg) is very good but crab’s meat (1.2 kg) had shrunk. Disappointing. We’ve provided feedbacks because we’ve always found that TungLok is a very good restaurant. Thanks
author: hontuck kwan

review_text: We simply loved the entire experience at this restaurant. Not only was the food excellent, but the service staff truly shine. They are friendly and genuinely helpful, creating a wonderfully happy and conducive atmosphere for dining.
author: Jean Yap

review_text:
Excited to learn that they have a vegetarian menu (vegan-friendly)! We loved their flavourful use of seasonings, featuring fresh vegetables and mushrooms - my favourite kind of food.

The staffs are very friendly and helpful too!
author: Josephine

review_text: The sashimi was incredibly fresh with a clean ocean sweetness and buttery texture. Each slice was thick, chilled perfectly, and had zero fishy aftertaste. Definitely one of the best places for high-quality sashimi — worth every bite.
author: Faye Lee

review_text: Excellent and delicious food. Staff were meticulous and helpful.
author: Aster Ng

review_text: It was extremely difficult to find the place at Gardens by the Bay. There were no signs for the restaurant and unknown to us or anyone we asked, this location of Douraku Sushi is inside another restaurant called Tunglok Seafood. Now for the food. The Garoupa in the claypot was from the Tunglok menu and it was very good. The fish was tender and moist, very generous with the protein portion and the sauce was thick and flavorful. The sushi was okay, nothing exceptional but fresh. I was expecting a lot more, since it is touted as a sushi restaurant. The service was slow but polite and gracious.
author: Sam G

review_text: Highly recommend their kaisen don
author: aedan tan

restaurant_name: Shake Shack Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
This Shake Shack in Singapore is one of the busiest, but visiting before or after dinner usually makes it easier to get a seat.

It’s located right in the beautiful Gardens by the Bay, which adds to the lovely atmosphere.

The place has a nice special concrete sundaes from the area too.

Usually, there’s not a long wait, and since people tend to eat quickly and then leave, you shouldn’t have trouble finding a seat. Enjoy your meal!
author: Charles Rezandi

restaurant_name: Shake Shack Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
I had Shake Shack for dinner and it was fantastic. The burger was cooked perfectly and tasted amazing, super juicy and full of flavour. The fries were great — crispy, hot, and the perfect side. We also got the Singapore-special milkshake, and it was so unique and delicious.

Everything came out fresh and quickly. The portion sizes were perfect and really satisfying. The ingredients tasted high-quality, and you can tell everything is made with care. The milkshake was rich, creamy, and honestly one of the best I’ve tried. Staff were friendly and the service was smooth and efficient. Overall, an awesome meal and definitely worth trying if you’re in Singapore.
author: Grace Chizawsky

restaurant_name: Shake Shack Gardens by the Bay
review_text: Ordering was very simple and straightforward at the kiosk. Order was ready quite quick, after ordering it was done in about 10mins, and this was on a weekend morning. The beef burger patty quality was much better then what I imagined. It was worth the price paid. Only small gripe I had was that they do not have meals for a single person, and their combo meal's portion looked rather huge, you have to order your own sides and drinks. Their staff was very nice as well, I was bringing back the baby chair to the spot which I've taken it from and a young staff took it from me. Overall a very nice meal, will patronise Shake shack again.
author: Ron “Ronster” 荣少

restaurant_name: Shake Shack Gardens by the Bay
review_text: Came here after visiting the two domes for lunch, was very busy but managed to get a seat outside. Food was absolutely delicious, we had never had Shake Shack before so this was a novelty for us. Drinks were also delicious. Did not have to wait too long for food as well.
author: Crystal Russom

restaurant_name: Shake Shack Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
French Onion Burger (double patty) $15.70 was the sin, heavily delicious! Caramelized onions always belong in a beef burger.

ShackBurger (double patty) $14.30 was scrumptious as expected and had a “cleaner” taste than the above one.

Fries sprinkled with parmesan cheese $7.50 were ok… garlic parmesan aioli was quite powdery and not refreshing. I prefer the fries topped with cheese sauce.
author: Sophie

restaurant_name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang - Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
It looked really good.
But the fried chicken was so dry and tasteless. You had to put the sambal, otherwise it was really painful to eat.
The fact that they had the option of sauceless fried chicken gave me the impression that the meat would be flavourful like ayam berempah but this was not that kind.
Factoring in the price, which was higher than average, not worth it.
Oh and it was under the Michelin guide, the reason is beyond me.
author: TzeThon Chua

restaurant_name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang - Gardens by the Bay
review_text: I won't trust Michelin Guide ever again. The rice and sambal is okay. But the chicken meat is so dry. The begedil is soggy. Quite disappointed. Other restaurants no need the Michelin Guide but can give the best quality food. How Michelin rate the food? Really i wanna know.
author: Nadhirah Hamzah

restaurant_name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang - Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
Another halal food choices. You can tell from the picture that the food looks great, and it truly was. No wonder they've been featured in the Michelin Guide five times. Kudos!

I ordered the curry rice chicken, and I really loved it. The curry was rich and flavorful, blending perfectly with the chicken. Although for my Indonesian taste, the chicken itself could’ve used a bit more spice, but the curry definitely brought out its flavor.

Overall, I really liked it!
author: Handi Prabowo

restaurant_name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang - Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
We weren't expecting to find a Michelin starred restaurant here (we were only looking for a place to casually dine in before exploring the area), so it was a pleasant surprise. The service was efficient and fast.

At first, I thought the food didn't look too impressive, but when I took my first bite... I think I heard a choir of angels singing. It really lives up to its record. The rice seemed to be cooked in whatever coconut essence (coconut oil?), and the chicken had a very nice texture. So glad to accidentally find this place.
author: Doc B Lapa (skysenshi)

restaurant_name: Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang - Gardens by the Bay
review_text: Chicken is burnt and the meat does not have any taste at all (except the burnt). It failed the standard level of Indonesian nasi lemak. Seriously they do need immediate improvement.
author: Sherly Wijaya

restaurant_name: Tsuta Japanese Noodles - Gardens by the Bay
review_text:
idk what to say... most atrocious ramen I've ever had. i bought their truffle shoyu for $18.80. the soup is tasteless, just like hot water with a bit of truffle taste. no rich pork broth, no fragrance, nothing. the noodles are soso, nothing special. the spring onions are cut ridiculously poorly as if a child did it. one long thin limp strand of bamboo. two flat pieces of pork that's soso.

wow absolutly ridiculous. take down your "michelin star" sign please.
author: chu xuan

restaurant_name: Tsuta Japanese Noodles - Gardens by the Bay
review_text: Honestly I’m disappointed. Very touristic place, not good food and especially very expensive. All the meat was cold, boa didn’t look like cooked, the only one thing I save it’s the gyozas that were acceptable but nothing particular. I don’t advice to eat in this place, if I come back again to this area for sure I’ll never go again.
author: Gerlando Valenti

restaurant_name: Tsuta Japanese Noodles - Gardens by the Bay

review_text:
My wife and I were at Gardens by the Bay and decided to check out Jurassic Nest given all the advertising about "Michelin" star hawker stalls there. It's a short walk over to Jurassic Nest and there are about 7 stalls inside (see my separate review of Jurassic Nest). We saw somebody else who had picked up their order of Pla Tot (fried fish with papaya salad) and it looked good enough that we were persuaded to try the stall.

We ordered the Pla Tot, Green Curry with chicken, stir fried Kailan, and two plates of rice. We've got Friends of the Garden membership so that gave us a 10% discount. You get a receipt with a number on it after paying, and you go back to collect your food once the number pops up on the screens that are displayed in the eating area. The kitchen area is right behind the counter and you can see the chefs at work. I think all dishes cooked in woks and you can see the flames flying high (maybe even in the videos below).

The fried fish was excellent. Very crispy and fresh. Crispy enough to eat the fins and parts of the head. The papaya salad on top was also excellent and gave it a nice savoury contrast (slightly sour and maybe with fish sauce?). It's also a decent sized fish and more than enough for two people. Given that we paid just over S$40 for the three dishes and rice, it's good value for money.

The green curry is similar to what I've had in Bangkok, so more oily and more liquid that what I've had locally. Less ingredients but decent amount of chicken and no complaints about taste. The plate of kailan was also a good sized portion and well cooked. Quite tender as well. Rice plates were small given the $1.50 price/plate.

Overall, the three dishes were good with the fried fish and papaya salad standing out. We'll definitely come back and thinking of bringing friends along to try as well!

review_text:
An enchanting French garden escape with a world-class dessert trolley

My close friend and I enjoyed a lovely lunch here today. The atmosphere is absolutely charming—cozy, elegant, and set in a breathtaking indoor garden filled with lush plants and thoughtful botanical touches. Every detail, from the table settings to the plate presentations, felt delicate and refined.

The food was beautifully presented. The starters were subtle and sophisticated. The main course was good—well-composed and skillful—though I felt it lacked a tiny bit of depth compared to the exceptional starters and desserts.

Ah, the desserts—this is where the experience truly shined. The restaurant offers what might be one of the best dessert trolley services I’ve ever seen. A elegant cart is wheeled to your table, filled with an array of exquisitely crafted sweet treats. Each dessert is plated individually for you, with careful attention to detail. The portions are small, allowing you to taste several without overindulging, and the variety is impressive. This alone is worth a visit.

The coffee afterward was also a delightful surprise—far better than expected and a perfect finish.

What makes the visit truly worthwhile is the complimentary access to the gardens after your meal. Strolling through the landscape felt like a natural extension of the dining experience. If you leave right after eating, the price may feel a bit high, but including the garden walk makes it excellent value.

Other practical highlights: the golf cart shuttle to and from the entrance is a nice touch, and SMS reminders are sent if you have a reservation.

Just a note: when booking online, you must confirm via email after submitting your card details. I forgot this step and my link expired, but a phone call resolved it kindly.

Overall, this is a wonderful spot for a leisurely lunch, especially with visitors. A beautiful French meal, a world-class dessert trolley, and a peaceful walk in the gardens make for a truly memorable outing. Highly recommended for a special yet relaxed experience.

Date of visit. Saturday April 17th 2021 for dinner.

The service was relatively good. 9/10

Assorted bread rolls (rasin, plain white, walnut grain) with butter was good. 9/10.

Mushroom soup was good, 9/10.

Escargots was lacking in garlic and so was the toasted garlic bread. Add more garlic and it should be perfect. Rating 7/10.

The Tomahawk steak 1.4kg was a tad too tough - too chewy. The mushroom, kale and small whole potatoes were very good. Overal it did not impress. Do not think we will order this again. Tasted better ones else where. Rating 7/10 at best.

The Prime Roasted beef was better, soften than the tomahawk. However still too chewy. 7/10 rating at best.  The days of The Harbour Grill (predecessor to Jackson Miller) roasted prime rib was much better.

Sides : Caesar salad was so-so 6/10. Corn on the cob 9/10.  Asparagus was okay 7/10 rating.

Appetizers : French oysters 7/10. We prefer the Canadian or Japanese ones that are fuller & creamery. So 7/10 rating.

One critical feedback, the waitress in black suit Ms Tran packed the left over steak as requested and retrieve the remaining bread rolls (2 of 3) saying no take aways and apparently to be ‘recycled’ into the bread roll plastic bin. That is a hygiene issue especially during this on going pandemic. The club need to explain this odd service. What is wrong having to pack 2 remaining bread rolls (1 was consumed) that was served already, exposed for a good 45 mins though partially wrapped in cloth towel. Strange.

Another odd observation. Ms Tran upon receiving the oysters from the kitchen proper, started shifting the oysters with her bare fingers to make room to place the two dips on the bowl of ice along side the oysters. Perhaps to save an additional trip to our table? SMH.

review_text:

The al dente spaghetti carried fragrant truffle aroma, mushrooms, herbs, and a surprise topping of caviar that added delicate umami bursts. Each bite felt like a little flavour bomb, with smooth noodles and sauce syncing beautifully. The ribeye was cooked between medium and medium‑rare, juicy and chewy, though some edges leaned dry — pairing it with pasta sauce enhanced the taste. For the price, the quality was well worth it.

The Sparkling Lemonade ($3) was fizzy, sourish, and refreshing, a perfect chill to balance the richness of the pasta.

Roasted Delight is a simple stall run by a friendly Chinese national.  I was pleasantly surprised by how delicious their roasted meat and char siew were.  I ordered a mix of both, and they really loaded up the portions.  It was incredibly generous for just $5!

The meat was tender and flavorful, and the char siew had a lovely glaze.  It was a perfect combination of savory and sweet.  The owner was also very friendly and welcoming, making my morning routine even more enjoyable.

It was a great way to start my day, and I'm definitely going to make a point of stopping by again sometime.  I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a delicious and affordable breakfast option in the area.

restaurant_name: Al Sheika Banana leaf Restaurant Pte Ltd.
review_text: This place is very old, and famous, some Hollywood celebrities have had their lunch here. This place is you traditional indian/Malay food.  The main course is steam white rice, that is served on a banana leaf square ( hence the name), and the you choose as many small side dishes you want to mix along the rice. You can choose from fish, mutton, vegetarian, etc...hot curries, to fried vegetables. Then the idea is you serve some portions NEXT to your rice and by using your hand you make a small food ball and then eat it. This traditional way of eating using you hand allows you to measure food temperature and avoid burning yourself. I highly recommend  this place. The only reason I did gave them 5 stars it was due to the fact last time I ate there, my stomach got upset afterwards, which never happened to me. But this can happen anywhere to anyone. I will go back again!!! ..... do nor forget to eat it with a Garlic Nan (Indian bread).

One star for service. Like some of the reviews here, the boss does not seems interested in serving the customer.

Store was left unattended. Thought the boss went to toilet. Stand and queue outside the stall with another customer behind.

About 10 minutes, there was still no show. Until the egg delivery guy come and shout out to the boss, he was standing at another table facing the stall, talking to another customer happily, knowing the fact there is customer queueing infront of his stall...

If you have no intention to sell, don't bother opening the shop man.

But honestly, Oyster omelette is above average.
author: jason Tan

review_text: The cheapest fried oyster in town, price starts $3 and up to $5.
author: Sebastian Tng

review_text:
This plate has the right balance of eggy omelette, crispy bits and soft, gooey starch with smaller briny oysters 🦪.
And dare I say it’s probably the best version I can find in the western part of SG 🇸🇬?
But I guess one thing I know for sure — I’m officially a fan. 🙂‍↔️
author: AC Chan

review_text: The visit started well with fried oysters priced reasonably at $3-$5 and served in generous portions. Unfortunately, the quality didn't match the value. The ingredients felt stale, and the flour had an unpleasant sour taste. Additionally, a significant part of the dish was overly charred (烧焦不是锅气／wok-hei), which made it inedible (see photo). Service was also below expectations. Despite standing at the stall and calling out twice, I was blatantly ignored for over five minutes until the vendor responded dismissively. This experience was notably poor, even for casual hawker standards.
author: Wei

review_text: A decent plate of fried oysters from a stall that specialises in this dish. The eggs part of the dish is fried precisely to a crispy texture. Even for the smallest $3 plate, you get at least 3 juicy oysters. Overall, if I am craving for fried oysters, this would be my first choice around this area. For those budget conscious, I believe we cannot find fried oysters at this price anymore. The famous Newton stall starts at $8. Taste it before the price increases.
author: Alvin Mah

review_text:
Extremely disappointed with the food quality at the West Coast Plaza Toast Box outlet. The soft-boiled eggs were completely overcooked – the yolks were half-solidified, and the whites were rubbery and clumpy, far from the smooth, silky texture you’d expect from a proper soft-boiled egg. As seen in the photo, the eggs looked unappetizing and poorly prepared, almost as if they were just left in hot water without any timing or care.

For a place known for local breakfast classics, this kind of inconsistency is frustrating. It’s not hard to get eggs right, especially when they’re a staple menu item. When even the basics are mishandled, it raises serious concerns about kitchen standards and staff training.

We ordered 2 sets of the Kaya Toast (that came with 4 eggs). First batch was disappointing so we asked for a replacement. We were shocked that the second batch of eggs were served overcooked AGAIN. Total 8 eggs were ruined and we didn’t got to eat any of them.   We won’t be returning to this outlet and hope Toast Box seriously re-evaluates their food prep and quality control.
author: Rachel LIM

review_text:
Staff is very lovely but queue is too long during peak hours n every day only one staff at the counter. Seriously? The other girl should not go for break until 2pm?

Update 07 Nov 2025 :
She always seems to be on break from 12pm to 1pm when we need 2 people to be on duty. The poor Indian guy had 20 grab orders n 3 office staff who ordered more than 10 orders in front of us. We were waiting and waiting n many people left the queue.
author: Michelle Robert

review_text:
30/10/2024
Had 2 coffee and kaya toast ($6.40), was normal. Cashier was quick and friendly. She collected payment and made coffee singlehandedly, much appreciated. Relatively big aircon dining area within the mall. Tables were cleared fast for customers to sit on.
author: T greensake

review_text:
On Sunday Nov 9, 12pm, I purchased from this shop and received bad customer services, which reflect inferior quality control on food and staff.

I was a long term customer of this shop. I was queueing on Sunday lunch hour, with 6 customers behind me. When I reached the cashier counter, there was no greeting from the cashier staff. Instead of taking my order, she standing at the cashier, receiving instructions from her colleague who was preparing drinks. They both understand there were customers queueing outside yet they talked to each others and passing instructions to each others for 4 minutes and keep every customer waiting. When taking my order, the order taking was came from the staff preparing drinks, instead of staff from cashier, with a sudden question and did not look at the customer. As a customer, I expected to having greeting, at least say hello, and described the expected time of waiting if needed, instead of doing their own things. When taking orders, staff should at least look at customer’s eye to start asking the order. The staff’s manner is very disrespectful by doing this to customers.

My order was a piece of banana cake take away. The cashier staff took the cake for me from the fridge. The size of banana cake was unevenly cut and with different sizes. The staff used the knife to push aside two slides of cake that was closer to her and chosen the smallest size of the whole cake. I do not understand the actual reason of her strange act. But to customers, it was a bad quality control in the products by sliding into different sizes, as well as staff’s bad service standards by having discretionary to choose less favourable product for customers which by default should have the same features.
author: Ine Cha

review_text: I tried the roti with chicken curry, it’s pretty good. The roti is crispy, very flaky, which I like. The curry is really good! Very savoury, goes really well with the roti. The toast is good, soft boiled egg is alright. The chocolate cake I got wasn’t that great though, the cream isn’t good.
author: Han Yu Tan

review_text:
Ordered the Fried Kway Teow ($7), Kway Teow Soup ($6), Prawn Noodle ($6) and Assam Laksa ($6).

The Fried Kway Teow had a slight hint of wok hei, which was encouraging, but overall the flavour felt quite muted. The savoury depth and caramelised sweetness you usually expect from a good plate of char kway teow wasn’t quite there, it leaned more towards lightly seasoned rather than bold and punchy.

The Assam Laksa broth was noticeably diluted. It lacked the usual tangy intensity and complexity that comes from a rich tamarind and fish-based stock. There were only a few small bits of sardine in the bowl, and I didn’t notice any torch ginger flower (bunga kantan), which is typically a key aromatic ingredient that gives Assam Laksa its distinctive fragrance and sharpness. Without that element, the soup felt flatter than expected.

The Prawn Noodle was decent, the broth had some sweetness from the prawns, but it didn’t have the deeper umami richness or porky intensity that makes a bowl memorable. It’s passable for a quick meal, just not particularly standout.

The Kway Teow Soup was probably the most straightforward and reasonable of the lot. The broth was light and clean-tasting, with simple, comforting flavours. Nothing fancy, but easy to finish.

Overall, if you’re coming here, manage your expectations, the flavours are toned down quite significantly compared to what you might expect from more traditional Penang-style stalls. That said, taste is subjective, so you might enjoy the lighter profile more than I did. Worth trying once to form your own view.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
Had a satisfying meal at Island Penang Kitchen near West Coast. The highlight for me was definitely the Assam curry fish head. The fruit rojak was refreshing and well-balanced, with that addictive sweet-tangy sauce. A comforting spot for Penang favourites when the craving hits. 🍽️✨

I like the fried kuay teow too. Yum!
author: Heather L

review_text:
Only the rojak and prawn mee is not too bad.
The seafood fried rice, mee tai mak and assam laksa was nothing memorable. Chendol was v sweet and not fragrant. With 1 barley and 1 longan drink the bill is $45.

A tad disappointed since the shopfront gave an impression that they specialise in Penang food.
author: Ling Ho

review_text: Overrated place, though they don’t charge for service charge but prices are already costed in, Penang char koew teow is 7 dollars, they seem to mess up their chicken so badly, pork is damn fatty, not much meat really. I found shards of chicken bones in their egg and their salted egg chicken is really hard on the chew, not sure if it is a bone or hard meat until it is really a bone, even opening at 5pm, their indoor seats are already full, takes about 15 mins to serve, the claypot of pork seems like the best if I had to rate the dishes I ordered. Super oily and fatty meal, I guess it’s cos it’s Penang style?
author: FROSTY

review_text:
My rating on food is just based on 2 dishes, so by no means a holistic review of all the dishes in Island Penang Kitchen.

I had my craving satisfied with the Assam Laksa. The broth had the nice tangy flavour with a fishy taste I love, so 100% approved. Prawn paste is served at the side so you can put it in the broth as how you like it.

I had also ordered Nanyang Fried Rice takeaway. Tasted it at home. It was nice but was slightly on the sweeter side. I would try other Fried Rice dishes next time to compare.

Overall. Nice setting, Efficient service. Taste is good. Need to come back and try more dishes
author: Yogeswaran Gopala Krishnan

review_text:
Reliable place for good quality Japanese food, especially sashimi.

Order the sashimi from the fresh seafood counter, rather than from the menu. You can thus decide how much weight/portion of sashimi you want.

Tempura is great; udon is ok.

Daily lunch specials ($13.80++ - $19.80++) available.

- The wait for the food is quite long though.

Prices below before ++.

Salmon Don ($15)
Chirashi Don ($15)

Crispy Negitoro Maki ($12)

Ebi Tempura Prawn Don 4pc ($14)
Katsu Don (Chicken/Pork) ($14)
Katsu Curry (Chicken/ Pork) ($14)

Plain rice ($2.50) !!
Sushi rice ($3)

Tempura Udon/ Soba ($16)

Ramen ($15-17)
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: Been coming here over a couple of decades and it's still high quality sashimi grade seafood from Japan
author: joe tay

review_text: Decent quality and taste. Giving a 2 star because had to wait 50min for sushi orders. Was informed the wait will be 30min but 50mins is a little unbearable. Food is great and definately better than upstairs.
author: Soda Pop

review_text: A good replacement for the usual sushi tei. Food was fresh. I saw plates of sashimi on other tables but I just could not locate them on ordering menu. Checking in w the staff then got to know I have to pick fr the freezer area for them to chop. This is great as u choose what fish and amount you want to have for sashimi.
author: wen

review_text: Fresh fish and absolutely gobsmacking food ! Loved that you are able to pick your own sashimi cut and fish to be cooked the way you want it. Service and food was amazing. Will be back!
author: elayna chin

review_text:
It's a good budget Korean/Japanese restaurant. Not meant to be fancy. Just good value. I really enjoy the beef. The salmon is OK but don't expect big pieces for the price.
The Kimchi is exceptional and the best deal that I've ever seen.
author: Me Too

review_text: Was there on a Sunday before 5pm for early dinner, place was relatively empty. Food was ordered via kiosk at entrance, they were ready within 5mins. Hot and cold Tea is available via self service. Price has gone up a little over the years but overall good experience at this restaurant.
author: Brandon Wong

review_text:
Delicious food but is it authentic, I'm not sure.

This was my first try of Korean food here in Singapore and I rate and review this based on taste and not authenticity.

Honestly, I loved their food. Ginseng chicken was subtle in flavors while the chicken steamboat was bursting with flavors. Similarly kimchi rice rice with egg was equally good. All at an affordable pricing.

For the food, portion size, flavors and affordable pricing, this place is packed. Definitely worth trying for all the above reasons. Highly recommend.
author: yamuna mohanram

review_text: Located on the level one of West Coast Plaza near the main entrance. This Korean food taste was reasonably good. My favourite was the spicy chicken with Saba fish was priced at a awesome value of $7.  You get to enjoy the best of both worlds. The meal would come with free tea and seaweed soup. Last but not least,  you can order your food via the orange self ordering kiosk in-front of the shop entrance.
author: Alex Liang

review_text:
Very nice place to go to. The lady at the counter is very efficient and friendly. She is always cheerful and bubbly when we order.
Food is generally cooked fast and need to collect at the counter. I would say the quality and quantum are reasonably good for the price.
Price has increased after the renovation but probably due to the higher rental for the new contract. But it is still reasonable.
Atmosphere is ok and has improved after the renovation.
author: Louis Chua

review_text: A cute little KFC outlet located in a shophouse. There were only three tables to sit a maximum of 12 pax inside the air conditioned restaurant. Two more tables of 4 located outside the restaurant. Though small, we always managed to find seats to dine in easily. The taste is expected of all KFC outlets. Tried out some new items on the menu like the mala chicken and ondeh ondeh egg tarts. Both were good and we could accept the taste. But these days, dining at KFC is no longer cheap. Thought the prices have increased substantially. Parking lots right outside the restaurant.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text:
Tonight, I originally came to this KFC in a happy mood to enjoy a meal, but I ended up feeling very disappointed because of the poor attitude of the front counter staff. It was a middle-aged Chinese woman wearing glasses. When speaking to customers, she was impatient, abrupt, and her tone and expressions carried a sense of arrogance. Ordering from her made me feel as if I “owed her money,” and it completely ruined my dining experience.

As an international fast-food brand, KFC should provide friendly and professional service to its customers. However, this staff member’s unprofessional attitude not only spoiled my mood but also damaged the brand image. I strongly suggest that the management reassign her to a position that better matches her temperament, such as in the kitchen or in a role without direct customer interaction, instead of keeping her at the front counter where she seems unwilling or unsuited to serve guests.

The most infuriating thing about this KFC branch is that there's no way to file a complaint or provide feedback. I tried submitting feedback through the KFC Singapore website, but the feedback function seems deliberately designed to be faulty, leaving no avenue for complaints.
author: Shui Luo

review_text: When I come here once in a while, I’m always reminded why I stopped eating KFC for some time. They’re always under-staffed. On this occasion I stood at the counter for 20 minutes without a single staff speaking to me, because they’re frantically churning out online orders. I don’t fault the staff, but at the franchise management level, they need to ensure that they have enough staff at the branch to ensure that they are able to handle the orders. Or else they should just exit the industry, just like many of their other branches, and deservedly so too.
author: Edmund Choi

review_text:
I was very upset with the lady who served me on 8 November afternoon around 2.30pm.
I ordered 1 x 2 pc meal and was eating in the shop. While looking around then saw the KFC promotion. It's buy 1 get 1 free and was not informed during the order.
Went to the counter and asked the lady why, she said normally I don't tell, the board is there.
So I demanded for my other set. It doesn't matter if I'm eating only 1 set, but you should let me know!
author: Tsoi Ka Man

review_text: Kicap Manis Wing must try item, Fast service, Small and Clean ambiance
author: Vashi Vashi

review_text: The service at West Coast Domino's was exceptional. Thumbs up to all è staffs especially for Raja&Rejab! They are very professional and went above my expectations. They are friendly too! Thank you for the great experience.. =)
author: Dyla

review_text:
Third time ordering. Their delivery service is getting from bad to worse. I placed order at 5pm for delivery. The food not ready even at 6.30pm. No point calling as they never answer the phone. I end up driving to the store to collect on my own. Wasted the delivery charge!!. Worse still, they got the order wrong. Clearly, they are lack the capability of managing the orders!
Beware of ordering from this stall!!! Order only if you can wait for at least 1.5 hours with minimum customer service and that you can accept a wrong product after all that waiting.
author: Damien Lee

review_text:
Got their limited-edition ShaWAHma Pizza!!! A delicious fusion of Middle Eastern magic and pizza perfection. Think juicy beef or chicken, loaded with bold spices, topped with signature ShaWAHma sauce and a zingy garlic mayo drizzle. It’s the kind of bold, crave-worthy combo that’ll have your taste buds begging for more.

And if you’re a cheese lover? Ohhh, you’re gonna love the Cheese Volcano ShaWAHma Pizza. Picture this: a molten cheese core in the middle, just waiting for you to dip your slice into. It’s gooey, it’s indulgent, and it’s everything.

Chocolate egg tart was not bad too!!
author: Zozo

review_text: Ordered for self collection, pizza was ready really quickly and staff seemed quite cheerful and ready to help. Have been ordering for collection for a long time and no issues always
author: Debo

review_text: Ordered from this branch several times over the years. Standard has indeed dropped to ridiculous levels. Similar to other reviews, a small order can take 2 hours to fulfill, the outlet does not pick up calls, and food is just left waiting for delivery for at least 30 minutes. The toppings on the pizza is little as well, it's almost like eating just the crust with sauce. Other pizza joints can do a much better job in terms of food quality, customer service, and punctuality, best to avoid Dominos.
author: jinsen goh

review_text:
​The menu is fairly simple with Bak Chor Mee in many variations, and I just went for the #1 Signature Bak Chor Meepok ($7). They offer extra noodles for free, which is a super nice touch.

​My wait only took 10 minutes, despite only one person cooking, as the stall has two other staff dedicated to managing orders. ​Upon collecting the order, I was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion. There was a huge and super fresh prawn, a larger than usual fish dumpling, and chunks of sliced meat.

​I know the noodles are going to be good when they have ti poh and golden lard cubes. Indeed, the noodles are cooked perfectly with a generous sauce mix. The mee pok here are extra thick and very chewy. Note that the vinegar taste is very subtle here, but you can help yourself at the condiments station. I only realised later that this variation has no pig liver or mushroom, and yet the flavours are on point.

​And the soup is one of the best BCM broths I have tried. The umami broth is rich and sweet, thanks to the addition of cabbage.

I only got to know of this place from Alderic's video, and I made a special trip down a weekday morning around 8 am. The coffeeshop was quiet, and only two other stalls were open, but everyone seemed to be here for this stall.
​Overall, this is a solid Bak Chor Mee. 10/10 worth getting out of the way to try.
author: Touristmouse

review_text:
Tried this BCM today 🍜 and was really impressed 👍😋
Everything was well balanced and nicely executed — noodles were springy, sauce on point, and ingredients were generous. What really stood out was the lots of pork lard 🤤🔥 and even a piece of pork trotter 🐖✨.
A very satisfying bowl and definitely one of the better BCMs around. Shiok! 😋🔥
author: Raymond Lim

review_text:
The Singapore national must have meat noodle, BCM Bak Chor mee!
Don’t ever miss this and don’t just order one portion noodle. It is so good you will feel one portion is not enough.

Extremely yummy and I had to chew and eat slowly so that I can savour the portion I bought. The lard, the mushrooms, the soup and pork slices, and noodles were so gooood!! Is damn can!!

The dumplings and 鱼饺 are the best ones I ever had so far, even better than the famous one at Yio Chu Kang.

For sure very happy to be back for more
I just regret not ordering more…
jialat cannot lose weight

PS only taken photos after eating some
author: Lillian Pang

review_text:
They deserve to get 5 star ⭐️

Mee pok cook to perfection, Al dente.

Fish dumplings is excellent

Teochew dumplings is good and give u a good quality large prawn. Prawn paste so so.

Soup is good, of course the tee pok is excellent

Must try if you have not done so
author: King

review_text:
Noodles al dente but the cold blanch step was too long causing the noodles to become barely lukewarm.

Standard noodle portion size is way too little for grown adults. Shop says no extra charge for extra noodles, but the standard portion should be reasonably satisfying. Still feel hungry after the meal.

Sauce is nice and goes very well with the noodles.

Soup is tasty but bordering on too-salty.
author: Spencer M

review_text:
Everything here good food good service good place to dine. Place kept clean and tidy. Servers and cashier prompte in serving or attending even it’s no service charge. Well known not very atas Italian food, nothing to complain at all. Portion not very big portion but decent.

Salmon salad sauce is good, goes super will with the corn. Recommended truffle mushroom spaghetti and bacon mushroom risotto. Super flavorful and goes well with the unlimited Parmesan cheese provided. Mushroom soup, butter corn and sausage recommended too though nothing special.

Chocolate lava ice cream, tiramisu and hazelnut semifreddo are my all time dessert choice here.
author: TNJ Housing Solutions Pte Ltd

review_text:
I visited this restaurant just before the Sunday lunch rush, and the interior was relatively quiet and uncrowded at that time. As is typical with most family restaurant chains, the overall flavor profile is consistent with what you would expect from other locations. However, the Milanese doria was served noticeably cold, which was a disappointment regarding the food's preparation.

The staff's performance was standard for this type of establishment; the service was neither exceptionally attentive nor particularly poor, falling strictly into the "average" category. While the atmosphere remains calm before the peak afternoon hours, the consistency of food temperature could be improved to meet the usual standards of the chain. This spot is a functional option for a quick meal if you are in the area, provided the kitchen ensures dishes are served at the appropriate temperature.
Would you like me to adjust the tone of this review or draft another one for a different location?
author: Yoshi S

review_text: All the food was great, but I found a dirty glass at the clean glass station. Most probably somebody out there accidentally, but still it’s not nice. Thereby 4 star only.
author: Tibor Pesel

review_text: Horrible! Ordered Bolognese in Saizeriya 321 Clementi and the plate came with only a few grams of ground beef. See the picture, u can hardly find any beef after much stirring around. I informed the male manager and just said “It’s like that”.
author: Jason Tan

review_text:
When its very crowded, the noise level can be very high and the sound cannot "get out of the place" so its very noisy inside the place. Try to avoid peak timing if you cannot stand the high noise level.

Sirloin steak on hotplate very hot and nice. Can choose either medium or well. Comes with few pieces of potato wedges and some corn bits.

Chicken wings are the fave. Can order 5pcs or 8pcs. 5pcs pricing is more worth than 8pcs....

Saizeriya will introduce new items once a while, so today we saw new item, asparagus with egg mayo. Asparagus is quite big pieces but too soft.

Bacon mushroom risotto looks like quite small portion, but taste is ok.

Pancakes with ice cream - icecream very small scoop (different from photo).

Egg mayo and asparagus today (03  Aug 2025) is smaller portion too. Today (03 Aug 2025) seems like food portion not normal, seems smaller than usual. Quite disappointed.

Today (02 Jan 2026) $4.90 egg salad is big portion, please keep it this way. Calamari also surprisingly many pieces for $4.90.
author: Lina Lim

review_text:
Finally tried the Michelin-recognised Song Fish Soup at Clementi hawker centre. Surprisingly, there was no queue today. I ordered the large bowl with mixed fish (fried fish and sliced fish). The broth was good — light, comforting, and not overly salty. Ingredients were generous, including fried egg and bitter gourd, which added nice texture and balance.

Do note that CDC vouchers aren’t accepted, but PayNow is available. The chilli comes pre-mixed with salted beans, which might not be for everyone. Personally, I found the bowl comforting and satisfying, though not something I’d consider a “must-eat” or “must-try.”
author: Chia Hau Lee

review_text:
After a long day of work, this hearty, warming bowl of sliced fish soup helps to nourish the body. Boiled fish slices are fresh, firm, and mildly sweet, pairing well with the tangy orange chili sauce or soy sauce with chili padi. Options that include fried fish, fish head, fish maw, prawns, and clams can be ordered based on availability. Customers usually order a meal with a separate bowl of rice or rice noodles cooked in the soup. A larger bowl comes with thinly sliced, crunchy bitter gourd, tomatoes, lettuce leaves, and a satisfying piece of golden fried egg floss which soaks up the soup’s goodness as you eat it.

Adding a dash of evaporated milk to the soup is optional, though it makes the dish more fragrant according to the stall owner. On its own, the soup already has a depth of flavour that resembles those from charcoal steamboat stalls. It is enjoyable to the last drop. Ordering is smooth and easy, and at times two queues can be seen, the right one for ordering, and the left for collection. If unsure, simply ask those in the queue to check.
author: 葉

review_text: Don’t get the hype around this. Had better fish soup at maxwell hawker/arcade fish soup. Think it’s overhyped. But still, the non fried fish slices were fresh and tasty! The fried fish though- super cold and hard. Not good at all- so disappointing! Think it used to taste better a few years back. Now it feels like it’s just hiding behind the Michelin guide stickers which it earned a long time back. Not recommended.
author: Bryan CY Chua

review_text:
I never noticed this stall until I saw that they were on the Bib Gourmand list and gave it a shot though it was near their supposed closing time of 8pm. There was still a queue at that time (and some more after me) so it seems to be very popular.

Tried their fish soup + rice for $6. The fish was smooth, firm, and tasty (though the portion seems small) and the soup was tasty. It's nice but I wouldn't go for it if the queue was too long.
author: Luke Lau

review_text: If you’re in Clementi and craving a comforting bowl of fish soup, Song Fish Soup is a must-visit. Their sliced fish bee hoon is a standout—firm, fresh fish slices served in a light, subtly sweet broth. The addition of bitter gourd and cabbage adds a nice crunch and balances the flavors well. For something richer, the fried fish bee hoon in milky broth is equally satisfying, with crispy fish pieces that soak up the creamy soup beautifully. Don’t forget to try their unique chili sauce with fermented bean curd—it adds a delightful umami kick. The stall has earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand, and it’s easy to see why. Be prepared for a queue, but it’s well worth the wait!
author: Lau Guan Zhen (Sean)

review_text:
The lesser-known branch of the famous Tian Tian chicken rice of Maxwell Hawker Center, occupying a space in an unassuming hawker center away from the downtown. As a result, it doesn't suffer from overcrowding from tourists - usually I got my orders within a few minutes (note I always come before peak hours in weekends).

The chicken is soft even for the breast meat and the poached version, accompanied with flavorful and rich rice - one of the bests in Singapore. Don't miss their veggie sides (poached kailan or beansprouts with fried shallot and oyster sauce), which are freshly made and compliments well the chicken and rice.
author: lontongstroong

review_text:
Biased fan here, can confirm clementi stall same food standard as maxwell stall. Location coffeeshop facing MRT between NTUC Fairprice and Clementi Mall

Unique quality of tian tian: chicken meat and rice were moist, not oily nor dry as most chicken rice. Gravy sauce, chilli, even dark soy sauce were excellent.

Service was quick and accurate.

Small stall in non-airconditioned coffee shop, so i can only give 3 stars for atmosphere. Clean and plenty of tables.
author: Lenon Tan

review_text: We came on a weekday at about 2 pm, the queue was okay and serving fast as expected. We got the steamed chicken back, so juicy and tender! The rice is okay but meat is the best. Prefer other places chilli. Also they give surprisingly a lot of meat. Amazing clementi branch and will eat if in the area again but will ask for less tao gei since they portion a lot. But coffee shop can be cleaner.
author: Pam Lim

review_text:
There are so many good chicken rice places in Singapore, but this store happens to be my favorite. The chicken is so tender and cooked just right, and the rice smells so nice that you can't stop eating it. Their chili sauce is also amazing—I think I drank it, haha.

I would give their chicken rice an 8 out of 10.

However, this store is really famous, so you might need to queue for 10-15 minutes if you go there at peak times.
author: Siriyakorn Tamsangchutti

review_text: Came by for late lunch. Ordered the small portion of the chicken rice. I guess the visible main difference is you get soup along with your rice. Although breast meat is served, it is still tender and juicy. Nicely chopped in chucks and not smashed with gelatinous skin. Signature sauce draped across the chicken with freshly cut cucumbers. Chilli is slightly tangy and spicy. Nice pleasant bowl of soup. The rice that was on my plate is lightly fragrant but a little clumpy which surprised me.
author: Ron Ng

review_text:
Used to love the carrot cake here, but it's no longer available. Sad! There's something to say about keeping basic options available.

The place seems to be known for the fusion cuisine, but upon being denied our hearts desire, my partner and I were ignobly forced to partake of merely mortal fare, such as mee Siam and nasi lemak.

To be fair, they were pretty good. Nasi lemak distinctively above average, mee Siam was wet instead of the expected dry local version, but still alright. That's what she said. The brownie was creamy and rich too.

The decor was put in by a remarkably unfocused out of work design student out of odds and eggs with no particular theme, a lil too eclectic to be truly eccentric. More ADHDesque.

Liked it, may come back if theres a discount.
author: JR FF

review_text:
Nice and chill vibes for brunch. Their food items are actually of quality and really good. Enjoyed the flavoured coffee and salmon.

But I don’t understand why they don’t serve the food to your table which is the con of this place.
author: Fatimah Sajidah

review_text: Love this place on UTown to come inbetween or after classes! Great and affordable food that is fresh and delicious. Highly recommend!! Love how their matcha is thick and they have oat milk and their burger is customisable, like for me no bread! Generous servings and friendly staff! CDC Vouchers are accepted too!
author: LT

review_text:
I stopped by for dessert and was blown away by the flavours. We tried the fudge brownie with salted caramel ice cream, and it was divine. The brownie had a perfect balance—crunchy on the outside, rich and chocolatey without being overly sweet. Paired with the creamy, subtly flavoured ice cream, it created a delightful contrast that felt truly gourmet.

The restaurant itself is a feast for the eyes—beautifully decorated, airy, and spacious, with plenty of seating. The lively atmosphere adds a sense of community to the dining experience.

The staff were warm and attentive, and the food arrived quickly. This spot is a must-visit if you’re in the area!
author: Ong Zhi Yuan

review_text:
This restaurant is located in Utown and offers a pretty wide range of options—they have burgers, pasta, rice dishes, and more.

The prices are quite reasonable compared to places outside, and NUS staff and students can even get a discount. I tried the chicken satay quesadilla, which was quite tasty. The chicken was marinated with a sweet sauce, and the tortilla was nicely grilled.

Overall, a solid place on campus for a casual meal with plenty of variety.
author: Gary Lin

review_text:
A cheap and pretty good grab and go sushi place. Due to the crowd in the evening, sushi are definitely freshly made as it will be gone in a while. Cashier aunty is friendly and nice. Staff are helpful with enquiries and request too.

For delivery, items are nicely packed with freebie. Sushi still came fresh and good.
author: TNJ Housing Solutions Pte Ltd

review_text: Cashier lady was polite and assisted to check with the kitchen crew when I requested for more corn sushi. Waited for a few minutes and left the place happy with my sushi. Keep up the good work. Will support again.
author: Mindy

review_text: Got the aburi salmon🐟🍱 and crabstick mayo🦀 sushi and while I enjoyed the salmon sushi, the crabstick one was a letdown as it clearly wasn’t freshly made (rice was super hard, crumbly and dry🙁 tho the crabstick tasted fine; didn’t finish in the end and threw some away). Was initially concerned about freshness as some reviews mentioned food poisoning after consumption😳 but I guess the cooked ones are safer to try! Price-wise this is definitely much more affordable than other brands😂
author: Rach

review_text: Decent shop focusing on low cost operation and fast in fast out customers. Food was ok and nothing to shout about. Price was competitive vs other brands due to its operational model. Have to eat fast after takeaway to prevent the food from going bad in the hot and humid weather here in Singapore.

review_text: Ate within 2 hours during dinner. Everything tasted ok. All these are just $20. However after few hours I had diarrhea. Next day morning diarrhea again. author: Stella Tan

review_text: The sambal prawn fried rice was really good — fragrant, tasty, and cooked just right. Ingredients were fresh and the portion was generous. A comforting and enjoyable dish made with love.
author: Jesvin Kaur

review_text: Expensive for the serving. Fried rice tastes ok. Good selection of toppings (meat or vegetable). However the serving size is pathetic. author: plcsntfcs

review_text: Great fried rice. You could taste the wok on the rice which was really nice. We were served very quickly and will not hesitate to come back again.
author: Benjamin Reynaud

review_text: Absolutely delicious fried rice -perfectly fragrant, well seasoned and cooked with just the right wok Hei.Easily one of the best I have had
author: Cheshire Home

author: Carrie

review_text:
I had a great experience at Burger King! The food was fresh, hot, and exactly what I was craving. The Whopper was perfectly flame-grilled, loaded with fresh veggies, and full of flavor. The fries were crispy, and the drink station was clean and fully stocked.
The staff was friendly and quick, and my order was ready in just a few minutes. The restaurant was clean and had plenty of seating. I also really like the deals on the BK app — they make it easy to get a good meal at a great price.
Definitely one of my favorite fast-food spots when I want something tasty and satisfying. Highly recommended!

author: Ajay.L14

review_text: very good service, especially the cashier. did not need to take long before food is ready! definitely recommend this place
author: Kayden Ong

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (The Clementi Mall)
review_text:
