author: Wanie Wahidah

review_text:
Had a fantastic meal with friends at Crystal Jade Hong Kong Kitchen in Clementi Mall. This place consistently delivers high-quality, comforting Cantonese dishes, and this visit was no exception.

Everything we ordered was well-executed and delicious.
Scallion Oil Noodles ($5.80) & Roasted Honey BBQ Pork ($14.80): I opted for the simple Scallion Oil Noodles, paired with a side of their signature Char Siew. The noodles had a wonderful texture – crispy, springy and cooked just right, coated in fragrant scallion oil. They were the perfect base for the Roasted Honey BBQ Pork, which was beautifully caramelized, tender, and had a lovely balance of sweet and savoury flavours. A classic combination done perfectly.

Shrimp Roe Prawn Paste Noodles ($13.80): My friend had this, and it looked fantastic. The thin egg noodles were topped generously with shrimp roe and bouncy prawn paste balls. They commented on how good the noodle texture was, and thoroughly enjoyed the umami flavours.

Pumpkin & Yam Porridge with Egg: Another friend ordered this comforting porridge. It looked smooth and creamy, with a lovely golden hue from the pumpkin, studded with yam cubes and topped with youtiao and egg. A very satisfying choice.

Seafood Hor Fun: This classic dish looked hearty and delicious, with broad rice noodles smothered in a silky egg gravy and topped with fresh prawns and other seafood. It received positive feedback from our friend.

XO Carrot Cake (to share): We shared this popular dish, and it was a great addition. The carrot cake cubes were nicely stir-fried with egg, beansprouts, and that signature savoury kick from the XO sauce.

Overall, every dish hit the mark. The quality is consistently high, especially the texture of the noodles and the execution of classic dishes like the char siew and hor fun. For a reliable and delicious Hong Kong-style meal, Crystal Jade Hong Kong Kitchen remains a top choice. An easy 5 stars!
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text:
I visited Crystal Jade Hong Kong Kitchen at Clementi Mall recently. To get a table, I had to scan a QR code and fill in a web form just to get a queue number, which felt a bit cumbersome.

The food was honestly just average. I was previously a fan of Crystal Jade for years, but I feel the quality has gone downhill. The dim sum tasted like reheated frozen items, the noodles were slightly overcooked and lacked the usual springy texture, and the porridge was overly starchy. It also took quite a while for our food to be served, which was disappointing.

What made the experience more uncomfortable was witnessing a heated argument between the cleaning and service staff right in the middle of the restaurant — definitely not something diners want to see.

Overall, not the experience I was hoping for. It’s still a decent option if you’re already in the mall, but expectations should be managed.

The charsiu was nice too.
author: Chi Ling

review_text: Food was great. That’s why I was a repeat customer. However, as a solo diner and seeing the seats were empty. I was told to move once from four seater to two seater. I refused as it was a dark corner that I am uncomfortable with and was allowed my current seat. After ten minutes, my food arrived and I had taken a bite, I was told to move to the deck seats when two guests arrived. There was actually a four seater seats available next to where I was sitting. This is high inflexibility that cause great customer dissatisfaction. will not visit again
author: Shi Min Lin

review_text:
Food was good. Sashimi was outstanding. However, we felt like we sat at the “naughty corner” right up near the entrance, but much neglected by service staff.

Apparently there was a large group inside, but this also caused our order to be very late. It was more than 40 mins before we were served our first dish.

Will think twice before heading there again.
author: Vincent Wong

review_text:
Very nice people and if you have pets the sitting area is outside, with ceiling fans and despite us going at the  hot midday timing, it was nice with the fans,  and the awning definitely shields so  we could  enjoy the delicious food comfortably. There are water bowls and tap conveniently located and there’s a small but nice park just to the right of this place. The doggy received a free treat too.

The waiter bothered to swop a chair with a backing when he noticed my 90 year old mom.

I saw cars stopping by to do takeaways and people popping in to  buy bread too.
author: PHINE

review_text:
Tucked in cosy corner of landed property near west coast area. Cafe has a retro deco vibe with gives a cozy and nice ambiance. Plenty of outdoor seatings, cool and well shaded. Cafe is pet friendly which is a bonus for us as dog pawrents who is always looking out for cafes to dine together with our furkids ! Food was flavorful and well-presented. Staff was attentive and friendly which added to the dining experience. Overall had a great and enjoyable dining experience. They even served dog ice-cream which the furkids love it. I look forward to come again.

Summary of what we ordered

Starters:
Signature crab cakes
Fried Calamari

Mains:
Festive set - meat platter
Crabmeat Rice with Seabass (spicy)
Salmon with baby scallop risotto

Desserts:
Red wine poach pear with vanilla ice-cream
Cakes - Yuzu and chocolate cake
author: jennie cat

review_text: Pet friendly cafe . Outdoor seating only but very cooling with many fans and shade. We did not sweat one bit. The food is amazing, very delicious, drinks were great too. There are also pet food and pet ice cream. Our furkids totally loved it. Will be back and recommend to our Furiends !
author: Adrian Ea

review_text: This place is known mostly to regulars as it is pretty obscure. They are pet friendly, if you don't mind sitting outdoors. Indoors, the place is nicely decorated and air-conditioned which some tables and bar counter seats. I have been here on a number of occasions and found their food nice and tasty. Prices are reasonable and more importantly, the service is friendly and prompt, which kept me coming back. I liked their cakes too and between 6 to 9pm, you can buy them at a 30% discount.
author: Rex Tan

review_text: Food is amazing - everything we ordered were really good! Special shoutout to the Chef’s Special Assam Fish & Fragrant Rice, Crabmeat Rice with Seabass and the Salted Caramel Cake! Staff service were excellent too and outdoor seating were well-sheltered and ventilated. Would definitely come back again to try the other mains and cakes.
author: SY Tan

review_text:
One of the best fried chicken that I had. As my kids take a long time to finished the food, and as the “official food recycler”, had to finished up some pieces of the chicken. Still taste great after a good 20 minutes.

Went for the chicken and waffle. The chicken bits is tasty!

Great place and uncle is the nicest person you could ever meet.
author: Wai Sing Ong

review_text:
Waffletown Wonders: A Chilli Fish Revelation?

My friend, a staunch advocate for Waffletown's chilli fish with rice, finally convinced me to give it a try. Located conveniently near my place, this small eatery with limited seating was our destination. Luckily, we snagged the last available spot.

The menu was a mix of familiar Western fare, but I was slightly taken aback by the waffle combinations. Waffles with bacon, eggs, or chicken? It felt like a bit of a culture shock, as I usually associate bacon with sweet accompaniments like ice cream, honey, or chocolate syrup. Perhaps it's an American thing I'm not familiar with.

The humble and obliging boss greeted us with a smile and took our order. We opted for the black pepper chicken chop, the famous chilli fish, and a side of curly fries. The prices seemed a tad high, but the air-conditioning and table service made it acceptable.

Our food arrived promptly, and we dug in. Everything was enjoyable, but I'm not sure Waffletown will be my go-to spot when I'm craving Western food. My friend vouch the fish was delicious and gave me a small piece to try. I am just glad that I didn't order that for my meal

The real highlight of the meal was the IBC root beer. As a root beer aficionado, it's a rare treat to find it in Singapore. Sadly, my friend wasn't a fan, claiming it tasted like cough syrup! Hehe...

It's funny how different people can have such different opinions on food! Sometimes it's worth trying new places just for the experience, even if it doesn't become my new favorite.
author: troo foo

review_text:
Nostalgic vibes, blast from the past, consistent standards, hot and crispy good food cooked on the spot upon order. Sincere fantastic service with a smile that warms the heart, completed with the same lovely chairs.
It was a full house indoors on a Sunday however There’s a few outdoor seating available.
author: Posh Pearl

review_text:
Time travel back to the late 80s where I frequent Bukit Timah Plaza weekly. Such an iconic restaurant back in the day and brought back so much memories. Anyway the fried chicken is still very good, although the price has more than doubled or tripled since then. Also like the root beer float where the ice cream is in the cup before you pour the root beer over. Coleslaw is also very crunchy and nice old school homemade goodness. Waffles is not that special and I didn't really enjoy the mashed potatoes which felt very pasty and artificial.
Full points for the nostalgia though. Will be back again when I'm around the area.
author: Jack

review_text: Sorta gives off a retro americano vibe.  Fresh tasting fried chicken and their waffles icecream isn't dense and is more on the light side,  on which I prefer, excellent service from the owner and members.
author: Jimmy Nguyen

review_text: Great place to sing/relax, especially at the hall, Very reasonable priced. Would really love it if they separate the dart throwing and not together with the singing hall. Great sound system & great service
author: Benson Tan Life Records

review_text: The atmosphere is great. They have darts and pool table plus KTV. A good place to hang out with friends.
author: Florence Lee Chai Ling

review_text:
Best place to chill and drink after a long day of work! Prices are reasonable and staff are all friendly

If you’re a pool lover, you’ll love the 8 feet pool table!
author: Ivan Woo

review_text: Coolest place for low-key beers, darts, and karaoke
author: Patrick Jason Dimalanta

review_text: The food are all super good. Recommend you to come to this place
author: Ayden Ong

review_text:
I ordered fried without salt and it tasted awful. The texture and taste were like it was double fried. Even my nephew said it was not nice. It was tough and tasteless.
I ordered the chicken burger, the bun was tough and had a strange consistency, and it stuck onto my teeth. I won’t be going back.
author: Jos M

review_text: Order morning breakfast from this outlet McDonald's.. I order two set of breakfast deluxe. Never give me hotcakes syrup !!! Chilli source 2 pack ? Hello ? Do you think 1 pack for each meal is enough ? You guys had spoil my morning mood. I nv wanna order your delivery again ! It happen too offen. Not first time !
author: kelvin koh

review_text:
It's genuinely mad. I mean the service isn't bad, the food is mid and there isn't exceptional service but it isn't bad service either.
One more thing, WHY WOULD YOU PUT A CRANPED AHH SMALL MCD WHEN THERE IS A 4★ MCD LIKE A 2 MIN WALK. No offence but kinda stoobid. Just go to the better one in the mall where koi is. I think this place is only good for takeout/grab orders.
Not bad
Not good
author: Harry Brown

review_text: The burger was poorly wrapped and assembled, which is not the standard one would expect from McDonald’s.
author: hoejhl hoe

review_text:
Hi McDonald's
I use to love your filet o fish burger way back in the 80s, 90s...but how is it that nowadays I have this feeling that the fish filet is fried and refried...doesn't have that softness and light crunch any longer!
Sad:(
Is it the outlet issue? Or islandwide?
Just wondering 🤔
author: Geraldine Khong

review_text: Masala Thosa soso, but sauces with it flavorless. The orange color sauce- see photo- was disgusting. Why serve something so bad when a good sauce is so easy to make?
author: Fab C

review_text:
The taste is average to me.

The worst part is the rude attitude. Regardless what is the reason, zero tolerance to me when I heard  the owner bark to customer.
author: Boba Pon Gaming

review_text: Masala dosai is good. However, found the dahl to be slightly too salty. Creamy coconut chutney is delish!
author: Jane Ang

review_text:
Love the food of this stall, portion is big, staff are friendly. Also, they allowed ordering through WhatsApp.

The must-try are:-
1. Nasi Briyani with fried chicken
2. Rojak
3. Ikan Bilis Fried Rice
4. Roti Prata

Cannot find a better indian muslim stall than this.
author: Selina Koh

review_text: Best service and have been a long-time customer for 4 years their egg prata and chicken curry are the best. Dont know why others give such bad ratings on their other foods. love the Prata there👍👍👍
author: Jia Hao

review_text:
A good and spacious Food Centre that offers delicious food at a reasonable price.
For vegans and vegetarians, there’s a stall serving delicious local Chinese vegan food (V4 Vegetarian) ~ made without MSG, eggs, milk and alliums. It’s 100% vegan and Pay-as-you-wish (one can decide how much  to pay). I sincerely hope more people can come and support this stall, as it’s truly inspiring to see a business put so much heart, love and compassion into their dishes.
There are also stalls that serve good Teh Halia (Ginger Milk Tea) and Teh Pandan (Pandan Tea) at truly reasonable prices.
author: Yellow Bear

review_text: I love eating here. More choice for halal food compared to most hawkers in the west. Lots of drinks stores too. Sadly not too accessible via public transport. Downside is the cleanliness but its alright
author: iskandarex

review_text: This food stall is great — the food is delicious, affordable, and generous in portion. It’s run by an elderly couple, and every time I come, they always serve a lot. Sometimes, they're even worried you might not have enough to eat, so they’ll give you an extra bowl of soup. Truly a stall run by a kind-hearted couple — highly recommended!
author: Vernon tan

review_text: Ayer Rajah Food Center is good, but please please avoid Shawarma Man Stall 23. I waited for 35 mins, and when I asked again, apparently he has not started my dishes yet. But he was already making the dishes of others who ordered after me. My daughter and I were already so hungry. It’s a one-man show who collects too many orders, but doesn’t have the capacity to serve. Too bad.
author: Marvin Joseph Montefrio

review_text: The kunafee was delicious but the wait was 30min. No buzzer given and we had to keep coming back to check if the food was ready.
author: Emily Ho

review_text:
A Halal restaurant which is always full during meal times and is famous for their curry fish head.

Their signature curry fish head is really reasonable for the price and great to the taste buds and has sufficient meat. Proportion  is also just nice so that you won't overeat.

Service is fast and for an air-conditioned place, definitely a
thumbs up!
author: Botak

review_text:
I came across West Co’z Café through a recommendation on Miss Tam Chiak, so I decided to give it a try — and I’m really glad I did.
The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, perfect for a relaxed meal. I ordered the Assam Curry Fish Tail, and it was really tasty. The curry was nicely tangy with a good balance of flavours, and the fish tail was fresh, tender, and soaked up the sauce beautifully.

Portions are generous, prices are reasonable, and the menu features a solid selection of comforting local favourites. Service was friendly and efficient, which made the experience even better.

Definitely a place worth visiting if you’re craving hearty, flavourful local food.
author: Shawn Lourdusamy

review_text: Staffs were friendly n efficient. Ambient were good. Only food i felt so so. Some prawn i felt were not fresh. As the prawn come out green paste. Pandan chicken not really nice. But curry fish was good.
author: Joslyn Lim

review_text: We had a 10 pax dinner set, with probably 8 course dishes (and we added one curry fish head). The serving is plentiful and the taste is well acceptable. The service is surprisingly good and attentive. Also, the set come with drinks and the restaurant is Halal certified.
author: Dave Ng

review_text:
A regular customer at the shop. Food is nice but the level of service has declined. Only friendly staff is the Chinese lady who never fails to remember what I like. The serving staff is OK but the staff managing the cashier, Krystal, has serious attitude. Not only she gave wrong bill and charged me (ended asking the Chinese lady to chase after me when I left and not informing her why need me to come back), she presented an attitude that customer owing her.  While I informed her I needed to check fave app, she simply not patience with attitude like asking me to quickly pay and move on. Not a single smile. Suggest not to put her at a front line position.  Rethinking whether I should continue to patronise.
Though food is nice, I don't think diners deserve such service.
Post review
I realised I was charged twice as Krystal voided the other table customer's payment instead of the wrong charge to my card. Only I reviewed the credit card statement, I realised I am being charged twice. While the manager swiftly refunded me when I called, I would thought that the counter closing would realise Krystal done the wrong thing, instead of me calling to inform.
author: Hammie Devil

review_text:
Taste: Tandoori Chicken Briyani was decent with flavourful rice and smokey protein. Garlic naan could be improved with ghee and more garlic but the texture was great. Mango Lassi was super thick but delicious. Came with raita and curry, which are decent but could be improved further

Cost: ~$21

Waiting time: 15 mins, weekday lunch

Overall: 4/5. Clean and air-conditioned. Extensive menu, will be back to try their thali!
author: Grace Bu

review_text:
One of rare places in SG to get regional *Indian* Indian dishes outside of Little India, with seasonal menu in occasion or festivities.

The Southern Indian options tend to be more authentic than that of the Northern ones. The Andhra veg thali was spot on, with tons of side dishes. Weirdly enough, the North Indian thali includes a few of these, particularly the green chili stir fry and rasam (!) of all places. Don't get me wrong, it's still tasty (been a few years since I had paneer tikka), but I doubt folks in North Indian states are well acquainted with these particular side dish. For the desserts, the jigarthanda (milky sarsaparilla drink) was refreshing and surprisingly not as sickly sweet as what I expected from typical Indian drinks or desserts, which is good.

The price is a bit on the expensive side (but by not that much), which makes sense for restaurants these days, particularly for niche cuisines. Indoor dining space and the airy outdoor patio are both available.
author: lontongstroong

review_text: Wide variety of Indian dishes. Spoilt for choices. Nice and quiet on a weekday evening. The tandoori chicken kebabs, fish curry, fried Aloo Gobi, Palak Paneer are tasty. We can only eat so much for 2 pax. Go in a bigger crowd if you want to try everything there.
author: Junjie JJ

review_text: The food is competitively priced compared to other North Indian restaurants in Singapore. The taste is quite good and overall satisfying. The masala tea has a strong cardamom flavour, which adds a nice touch. The mango lassi is well balanced and refreshing.
author: Anson

review_text: The recent change in outlooks and menu has worked really well. Food taste has improved and staff are very active. Introducing south indian options is a great relief because previously this place had only bland and boring north indian food.
author: kaarthick subramanian

review_text: Had a company team lunch here on a Monday. Place was quite empty when we arrived. Food was good, service was not bad either. The staff asked us if we wanted to order drinks, and again for a second round. Also offered to clear stuff when they were done. Food was served very fast, dish after dish, even though we hadn't finished the earlier ones (in some cases didn't even start yet). Ambience was decent too, it's indoors with aircon. Place isn't very big, less than 10 tables.
author: Sihan Goi

review_text:
yummy yummy! will come back to try their other dishes!

we tried their chongqing grilled fish, sambal kangkong, chye sim, black pepper beef, oats sotong, century egg. chongqing grilled fish was more 麻 than 辣, not sure if that was bc we asked for low spice level

i wna try the 辣子鸡 nxt time 😌
author: inayah yacob

review_text:
Standard drop so much. Food taste average. Curry fish head was not bad last time, but now, standard so-so only.

Sharks fin soup very salty. Salted egg chicken has smelly oil taste and no salted egg taste at all. Oatmeal sotong (squid) also so-so, not flavourful at all. White rice is very small bowl portion on the plate.

Staff also has difficulty understanding our ordering. Seems like only know chinese. For a halal eating place which serves many malays, this is indeed very surprising.
author: Lina Lim

review_text:
The aunty who served us was extremely cheerful and patient. There were 12 of us, and she took the time to carefully listen to our many orders, repeating them to ensure nothing was missed. She even wished our friends a happy birthday, which felt very genuine and thoughtful.

The staff were kind enough to help us store our cake in the fridge and even played a birthday song for our friends. The food was served promptly, and service was efficient throughout.

What I really appreciated was how considerate they were to other customers as well — politely asking us to lower our volume when we got a little too boisterous, while still accommodating our requests with a smile.

Thank you for the excellent service. The aunty truly made our experience special!
author: Dancia Tan

review_text:
Table seating - Got a seat pretty quickly upon entry.
Order - Menu shared instantaneously once we are seated. Order was taken once we are ready.
Drinks - Ordered hot lemon tea, it's a Lipton tea bag, hot water n a slice of lemon.
Food - Arrived 15 mins upon order. Portions are reasonable to me. Ingredients were visible.
Taste - Can taste the wok hei. Authentic food!
1st time trying and quite satisfied with the food. We will be back for other occasions!
author: Mohd Amin

review_text: I thoroughly enjoyed the coffee and experience here. Although the seating capacity is limited, the environment is clean and comfortable. The lady boss is very friendly and make great Chinese tea. The gelato tastes great too!
author: Swee Chee Teo

review_text: Thank you for the Freshly Brewed Peppermint Tea! Soothing for me during this time!
author: Yovanee Appadoo

review_text: The gelato tastes great and coffee gives a punch!
author: Z X

review_text:
Very nice ambience, friendly staff.
Great place to chill!
author: Irah Zafirah

review_text:
Bee Hoon has good flavour, the rest are average.
Curry vegetables is really salty, and I found a piece of plastic in it.
May have complimentary soup.
Not sure how the dishes are priced.
author: JK T

review_text: Delicious thin and crispy pancakes for a reasonable price! Many flavours available and I was able to customise a chocolate + cheese flavor. Will definitely drop by more!
author: Xian You Lim

review_text: Good snacks for young and old. Our favorite is chocolate, ham and cheese. Be prepared to wait if it is very crowded. You can order early but it is nice while hot. If it is cold, you can bake it reheat. Pricing is standard for HDB area. Best time to go is off peak during 3-5pm, timing for your tea break snacks.
author: Danny Kwok

review_text: It is hard to find a stall that makes such nostalgic pancakes after the closing of the Lavender hawker centre. Get your quick fix here.
author: rodneysyx

review_text: Traditional Ming Jiang Kuey with a modern twist to suit our new style of having in many choices to chose from. They are also serving the traditional simplicity of coconut | peanut | red bean. With improvised equipment and smaller size makes this local delight not a usual breakfast item but a quick snack with reasonable pricing anytime of the day. 👍🏻🤩
author: Gra Cious

review_text: Price has gone up since the covid-19.. standard still good and lady selling the pancake is friendly to remind me that pancake cost $1.3 each.. haha.
author: Daniel Sin

review_text:
Chance upon this stall the last time i was here to try the porridge from the same coffeeshop. This stall selling fishball noodle seems to be very popular. Upon reaching the coffeeshop, there were at least 7 people in the queue already. The stall is operated by only an elderly man. Queue moved pretty fast, it took me about 15 mins before it was my turn to order. Fishball noodle price starts from SGD$3.50 onwards, i think there was an price increase from SGD$3.

The noodle was nicely cooked, texture of the noodle was springy. Sauce was well balance and tasted very lardy. it has that  古早味. The bowl of noodle came with ingredient like sliced fishcake, meatball and fishball which tasted like homemade. portion of the noodle was also very generous. You can also add on item but with additional charges.

Overall, the fishball noodle here is definitely above average and would highly recommend.
author: Sean Goh

review_text: Overall not bad. Fishballs are really handmade, which is pleasant surprise in Singapore. Dry meepok noodles did not have enough acidity and oil/lard, but I guess you can always ask for more. Very budget friendly, $4.50 for a decent serving size but heh I don't eat much (serious).
author: Joel Tan

review_text:
Update 9 Aug 2024:

Been a while since I last ate here. Although the prices have not changed since the last increase to $4.00 a bowl, they swapped out one fish ball for a fish stick (see latest photo) and cut down on the number of slices of fish cake. The fish stick is so ordinary and obviously factory supplied. Rather have my fish ball.

Decided to try this relatively new stall in Clementi West St 2. Ordered the $3.50 portion of mee kia dry with chilli sauce. The portion is decent for this price. It came with two fishballs and one meat ball and about 10 slices of fish cake.

First of all the accompanying soup. It didn’t taste solely made with MSG and salt. Pork bones were boiled with water and it became more umami tasting as more fishballs are boiled. The noodles could have been more al dente. Glad I did not order the soup version because the noodles would have been even soggy towards the end. With this dry version, your main focus is on the chilli sauce which was good. Not a lot of heat but fragrant and very savoury. With enough vinegar, it goes well with the noodles. Owner was also very generous with the lard and oil so that helped elevate the overall taste of the noodles

The sliced fish cakes were a joy to eat. They were fried until a crispy skin on the outside was achieved and then sliced. So as you bite down, the crispy skin contrasted against the soft core of the fish cake. But the star has the be their fishballs. Bouncy, irregular shapes and tasting full of saltiness of sea fish, every bite was a pleasure, even without dipping into cut chilli/soya sauce. As for the meat ball, it was more of fish meat and pork cause it tasted as umami as the fish balls.

Very well done as far as fishball noodles go. It’s been a while I found since such tasty fishball noodles. I must come back again soon for their mee pok.
author: Wilson Foo

review_text: Love the handmade fishball from this stall.. it is really hard to find fishball stall still selling the traditionally made fishball noodle at $3 per bowl. Ask for mee pok and their noodle is boiled without been too soft and still have the springy texture.
author: Daniel Sin

review_text: Delicious bowl of fishball noodles with the noodles cooked just right. Fishballs were handmade, bouncy and huge in size, highly recommended to try if you are around the area!😋
author: Chow Gerald

restaurant_name: Hong Kong Street Restaurant - Clementi West st 2
review_text:
Blk 727- I've been to this coffee shop a few times, and while I don't expect exceptional service, I do hope for basic courtesy and a smile. Unfortunately, the server with curly hair and a ponytail consistently fails to deliver on this.

My visit today with my family, was despite the welcoming atmosphere, the server's attitude was again disappointing. This was especially noticeable since I had previously met the boss, who was friendly and welcoming.

What's concerning is that this server's behavior seems to be a recurring issue. Today, I witnessed another customer express frustration with the server's attitude after being informed that a dish was unavailable despite being told it was available earlier.

I hope the management takes these feedback seriously and addresses the server's behavior. A little courtesy and attentiveness can go a long way in making customers feel valued.
author: Jolene Lim

restaurant_name: Hong Kong Street Restaurant - Clementi West st 2
review_text: Order $8 XO fish soup and it only consist of 4 pathetic fish slices, a few strand of leafy vegetable and the soup doesn’t taste of XO. Mind you, You need to add $2 to the Fish soup for the XO. First and last time here!
author: Elyna Wong

restaurant_name: Hong Kong Street Restaurant - Clementi West st 2
review_text: Ordered via grabfood and amazed by its price and quality. Saw no google reviews of this place n decided to create it! Not to be confused w another HK street restaurant at avenue 3
author: Jason Lee

review_text:
Best Mee Soto in Singapore. I tried so many Mee Soto that are highly rated but none can beat this stall. The soup is tasty and the chilli makes it hot and shiok! I will travel 1.5hrs from Punggol for this.
Stall opens 5.30am to 2pm. Don't know why the status says temporarily closed but it's open.
author: Lynn Lum

review_text: Had the nasi sambal goreng, mee rebus and nasi padang (sambal sotong, paru and urap). The price is very reasonable and the food is not bad. Our food however was on the salty side. Nevertheless, will try again!
author: Zaty Roslan

review_text: Food portion was good for 3 pax, we had mango salad fried fish and asked to separate the sauce - fish was real awesome, crispy and fresh. Generous portion of petai in our petai prawn so we really enjoyed it.
author: Antoinette T.

review_text: I’ve been staying in the area for over a year but only tried Nakin Thai for the first time today. Ordered takeaway basil pork with egg — very tasty and the portion was generous. Will definitely be back to try other dishes!
author: Cynthia Lim

review_text:
One of the best Thai food I have had in a coffee shop. This unassuming stall serves delicious and authentic Thai food that is wallet friendly.
I have been there several times, and this time, being a quiet evening, our food was delivered to our table. The Tom Yum Soup was tasty and not overly spicy, just nice. One of my favourite dishes is the Crab Fried Rice, which is enough for 2. The Prawn Cakes were excellent too.
When we couldn't finish our food, they were nice enough to pack the food up for us to bring home, and after packing everything nicely including chilli sauce, they brought them back to our table. Really great service. Highly recommended.
author: Jason Ong

review_text:
A short walk away from West Coast Plaza with plenty of parking.

The prices of this Thai Food in a coffee shop is fair. The spicy lime fish, pineapple fried rice and the fried pork collar are a must order (the grill one is not bad too).

Their basil pork rice and kang kong are nice too!

Will be coming back!
author: Cheng Han Chua

review_text: Good and affordable Thai food in a kopitiam. I particularly liked the fried pork collar it was crispy and meat was fatty and not dry. Phad Thai had good wok hei. The stall has a wide variety of dishes and will definitely go back to try out their other dishes.
author: Gooose

review_text:
Mee pok is cooked nicely, not too hard not too soft. Chilli is ok. The nice part is the tender lean pork and fluffy minced pork. Soup is also not bad
$5. Good bowl, will eat again
author: Taste & See

review_text:
With a name like that, one would not have guessed that this is a noodle stall. But it is. One of the newest in Clementi West Coast area, this new stall is located at the newest Kopitiam, Foodland 713.

And it sells all sorts of noodles. Bak Chor Mee, Fishball Noodles, Ban Mian, Laksa, Kolo Mee and even fish soup!

Ordered their Fishball Noodles, Mee Kia dry with chilli for $4.30. The noodles were cooked right, but not the round thin noodles variety but the thin but flat type. The specialty chilli was good. Savoury with dried prawns, it made up for the otherwise unimpressive fishballs and the equally bland soup.

New stall still getting the hang of things as the boss lady is seen continuously coaching the two employees from how to cook the noodles to how to fry an egg.

Will come back to review their other items some other day.
author: Wilson Foo

restaurant_name: 嗨饭天 Hi Fan Tian (Clementi West)
review_text: Yummy fried rice and succulent pork chop only $6.50 at this newly opened stall at Clementi West. Can try their Mala noodle too. Their chicken wings are huge and flavourful.
author: ronnie chan

restaurant_name: 嗨饭天 Hi Fan Tian (Clementi West)
review_text: Love their fried rice, pork chop and chicken cutlet. It’s really nice and yummy! The 红油抄手 is also delicious! Had a good lunch with my friend! Do give it a try :)
author: Erica Zhao

restaurant_name: 嗨饭天 Hi Fan Tian (Clementi West)
review_text:
Very generous with the amount of egg and shrimps. For $6.50 egg fried rice with shrimps, the portion is sizable. Whilst it cannot claim to have every grain coated with egg, the fluffy grains were well separated from each other, evidence of thorough frying of overnight left over rice.

Very nice. Must return to try their other items especially the spicy wantan noodle.
author: Wilson Foo

restaurant_name: 嗨饭天 Hi Fan Tian (Clementi West)
review_text: Really enjoyed this fried rice. Not too heavy and salty. Can finish it. Plus the toppings are really meaty. I love the wontons too.
author: Alvin Sahagun

restaurant_name: 嗨饭天 Hi Fan Tian (Clementi West)
review_text: Love the fried rice & spicy wantons. Tasty food at a affordable price! Conveniently located at Clementi. Worth the visit!
author: Jasmine T

review_text:
Not sure why this new stall at Clementi West Street 2 is called Yicheng Noodles because it’s a cai png stall.

Variety is limited but portion is large. Steamed egg, sesame oil chicken and tofu  with rice cost $4.00. Not exactly cheap. Taste wise, chicken had a strong unwashed smell and very little sesame oil taste. Tofu and steamed egg were acceptable.
author: Wilson Foo

review_text: We do our grocery shopping nearby every week but have never discovered this eatery! Ordered the nasi lemak with 2 wings set ($7.90) which is not bad value for its portion. The turmeric coconut rice was very fragrant and not clumpy at all. Fried chicken was also well marinated and juicy. Wished their chili was more fragrant and strong, and also provide more. Theirs tastes very healthy. Bonus is their staff are really friendly and the place has no GST / svc charge. CDC accepted too
author: Y

review_text: A few diners rated the white curry chicken noodles good so I tried and being a soupy person myself I don't usually finished the entire bowl of curry cause it gets sickening and heavy halfway. This one here despite the curry texture a little thin but flavourful tasty enough and can drink fully on its own. The place is very clean and cool enough with some aircon and fans to beat the heat here so a very nice place to chill drink and have food.
author: eric lim

review_text: Small restaurant in West Coast-Clementi area which serves a wide variety of Malaysian dishes. Quite reasonably priced with very delicious food. I ordered the chicken white curry noodles. Curry wasn’t too strong and was soaked up well by the noodles. Chicken was tender and well marinated. Very tasty! Staff were very accommodating and friendly. Overall, a very pleasant experience
author: Elijah Lim

review_text: I don't see many white curry noodles in Singapore, so it's worth trying. The Turmeric Nasic Lemak is also very delicious.
author: Wye YO

review_text: The cozy, retro-inspired vibe at ISLAND CAFE 爱人茶餐厅 is a nice change of pace from the usual busy kopitiams — cleaner, more comfortable, and a bit more relaxed. The menu’s interesting and has a good selection. I dropped by for dinner and tried the Pig Skin Curry Rice Noodle Roll, which was decent, though it didn’t leave much of an impression. Service was fine, nothing to rave or complain about. The place had a few customers but wasn’t particularly busy. I’d put it down as a decent option if you’re nearby and want something casual without the usual hustle, but not a must-visit.
author: C

review_text: Authentic Penang white curry mee. We ordered the sea food curry mee, chicken curry mee, chee chiong fun and hakka yong taufu. It is not as crowded as the sister shop a few units away. Curry chicken is authentic Penang taste. Worth coming back again if nearby.
author: Xplorer SEA

review_text: I  tried the nasi lemak and curry noodle from this stall, and it was an absolute delight. The dishes were packed with flavor and the ingredients were fresh and high-quality. The nasi lemak had the perfect balance of sweet and spicy, and the curry noodle was full of aromatic spices that made my taste buds dance.
author: Chomeh Alex

review_text:
Experience from bad to worse. First time had the curry noodles and a few hum was sourish. The pig skin was hard to cook but they did fine. At least it was soft, but it's texture was average.

The dessert at 2.50 was affordable and they were both delicious in their own way. It was thick and well cooked. No gluey parts found.

As for the Nasi lemak set that came with drink. It was $8.90 and considering that this is a neighbourhood, it could be a bit ex.
First time the Nasi lemak had enough curry to go with rice but second round it was pathetic. Did not finish the rice.

It was mentioned that the curry was cooked and portioned with serving. Sounds very stingy. Even if the part is a thigh, lack is curry gravy is a joy kill.

The ikan billis was very little and the ikan is very saltish. Peanuts ok.

Place was aircon and cleaned well.

But lack of curry gravy is a big Nono for me.

It is ok, they can save the curry for the next person. Miserable.
author: Will

review_text:
Came by for a quick coffee stop after our lunch at Island Penang - which is under the same umbrella of companies.

Prices are okay, and the air conditioned environment is a welcoming addition especially in this hot weather.

☕️ coffee was decent, similar to the tea which we had as well

Fishballs were good, my father liked the curry 👍🏻

Definitely will be back for more coffee in future!
author: YY

review_text:
I was pleasantly surprised at the close to authentic Ipoh style curry chee cheong fun at this new place just opposite Sheng Shiong supermarket.

The curry was lemak and tasty (some may find it a little too salty - but just right for me). Boneless tender Chicken pieces made it super convenient to eat.

My sister has the char siew version; the char siew was I guess ok.

My wife had the curry chicken with bread and the chicken thigh portion is sizable. Same curry sauce base which goes well with the french loaf bread.

The fried chicken wing was well seasoned and crispy on the outside and juicy on the inside. No cloying oiliness which is good.

The honey lemon drink was a bit on the sweet side and the I would pass on the soya bean - too small a cup.
author: Leonard Lim

restaurant_name: Teck Hin Delicacies • Chee Cheong Fun
review_text:
2.50 for 2 rolls.
One of the best I ever had and I dont even like cheese cheong fun to begin with! Deceptively simple looking ! Smooth and right balance of taste.
Will close early when they sell finish. Usually by 11am to 12pm
author: Mikki B

restaurant_name: Teck Hin Delicacies • Chee Cheong Fun
review_text: One of the best chee chiong fun, with thin and soft skin.  The sauce is just sweet enough top with toasted sesame seeds Be prepared to queue but it’s worth the wait.  They are usually sold out around lunch time.
author: Esther Teo

restaurant_name: Teck Hin Delicacies • Chee Cheong Fun
review_text: This has to be the best chee cheong fun in town. So long queue. My friend queued for more than 15 mins , but it is definitely worth the wait. Super smooth texture and it is so super yummy.
author: SK Ho

restaurant_name: Teck Hin Delicacies • Chee Cheong Fun
review_text:
I was around the neighbourhood and decided to check out this popular Chee Cheong Fun. I was not disappointed with my high expectation after reading Google review!

The cheong fun is so soft and tender yet does not disintegrate easily in my mouth. 有口感. Reminded me of another good one I had in Ipoh long ago. The dark sauce, sesame and I think some kind of garlic oil further elevate its taste level.

Uncle was nice as well to make sure the dark sauce are poured to the side of the cheong fun so diner can own time own target moderate the amount of sauce they want on the oil/sesame coated cheong fun.

It is so important that the basic cheong fun is made well else anything that is drizzle on it will just be useless.  This stall exceeded my expectation.
author: Riccardo Tan

restaurant_name: Teck Hin Delicacies • Chee Cheong Fun
review_text:
It sells only 1 item which is steamed rice flour roll. Always a persistent queue with a friendly smile.

It is not the thinnest or smoothest as compared to Hong Kong steamed upon order, this is excellently balanced with a nice bite.

Splash of garlic oil, soy mix, bean paste sauce, chili and sprinkling of sesame seed.

The ultimate end product is quite addictive.
author: MNG

review_text: Hidden in 1 corner of an army barrack. Loved the rustic charm and industrial backdrop the moment you stepped in. Toasted bread for the steak sandwich was a bit tough to cut though; latte with biscotti was perfect. Nice place to enjoy a cup of coffee and chill.
author: Chen Li Jannie Lee

review_text: The strawberry iced latte was pretty nice, but the pesto mushroom rigatoni was so disappointing. I think it’s the first I’ve ever not enjoyed a pasta so much. There was no taste of pesto and because of the bowl shape, all of the oil went to the bottom and drowned everything which made it the dominant taste. Really sad considering how much it was.
author: Eve Low

review_text: Never miss to make me feel happy with their coffee tastes. Happened to be at this place after many years and was happy to pick this place for a quick coffee. Could not find the carpark outside and parked at the basement at the condo carpark. You need to inform the guard that you are visiting jimmy monkey to enter.
author: Ravish M

review_text:
Jimmy Monkey Café & Bar is one of my favourite breakfast and brunch spots in Singapore. Tucked away at One-North Residences, it brings a slice of Melbourne café culture to the quiet, leafy surrounds of one-north. Opened in 2011 by Australian native Michael Ryan, it’s known for quality coffee, hearty food, and a laid-back vibe.

Service is good, and the food is both interesting and top notch. My personal favourite is the Cheesy Vegemite Toast Soldiers — buttered sourdough with Vegemite and melted cheese, served with duo onsen eggs. Comforting, bold, and uniquely Aussie. A solid 5 out of 5. Great spot for a relaxed, satisfying brunch.
author: C

review_text:
Visited Jimmy Monkey at PLQ for a casual dinner gathering, as we were looking for a kid-friendly spot.

We were seated at an outdoor table conveniently located right next to the playground, which was great for families with young children. However, do note that the outdoor area had some mosquitoes, so insect repellent might come in handy.

We ordered a variety of dishes to share – the salmon steak, wagyu burger, white clams in white sauce, aglio olio with prawns, cornflake chicken breast, and the sweet & sour cauliflower. They also offer a kids’ menu, which includes a main and drink – a thoughtful touch for families.

Unfortunately, while the food was decent, the service left much to be desired. It appeared that only one service staff was managing the floor, which resulted in a long wait for drinks and multiple reminders needed for cutlery, condiments, and basic requests.

Overall, the experience was underwhelming, and while the location is great for families, we’re unlikely to return given the slow service.
author: мιѕѕувєlα2828

review_text: Amazing food and service, especially the pasta. This is one of the best pasta i’ve had in Singapore! We also had the Signature Wagyu Tomahawk Steak, we ordered the extra small portion but it was such a huge portion. Definitely worth the price for such high good quality food. Highly recommended restaurant and will definitely come back again.
author: Louisa Seow

review_text:
reasonably priced set lunch and dinner of same price!  friendly staffs. nice music. cosy christmasy vibes.
food are good but a tad too salty.  angelhair pasta would be better if served colder.. abit too oily.
author: Peggy Lee

review_text: Literally a hidden jem in the west. It’s a little difficult to find as it is not in the main blocks of the office stacks. It is not a big restaurant however it has seatings indoors and also outdoors. Perhaps it can serve up to between 20 to 30 tables The food selection if you go for the set meals are on attractive prices and by topping up a little you can get more premium main courses and you should do it. The food is on spot delicious, well marinated a delight for most. the servers are absolutely helpful and considerate. In fact, they moved us to a More private table after the seats open up during a packed Friday lunch. Kudos to that. Reservations are recommended
author: Mervyn Phea

review_text: Not too crowded on a Fri night. Had Set A wirh carbonara plus a pint of Guinness. Quality remains excellent since the last time I came here a year ago, the soup and creme brulee were also 💯💯 Keep it up!
author: Eli Yeow

review_text: Really enjoyed this Oven-Baked NZ Rack of Lamb! The meat was tender, juicy, and cooked just right with a nice sear on the outside. Each bite was full of flavor and had that perfect balance of smoky and savory. The veggies on the side were fresh and complemented the lamb nicely.
author: T.R.

review_text:
Very bad experience. One male staff member had an extremely bad attitude and was very rude.
My girlfriend asked a simple question and he responded loudly and in an aggressive tone, as if we had done something wrong. This is completely unacceptable for customer service.
I hope the management will look into this matter seriously because such behavior damages the reputation of the store.
author: Beh Ben

review_text:
Extremely poor customer service

I visited this Subway outlet recently and had one of the most unpleasant service experiences with subway ever. When I walked up to the counter, the staff saw me approaching but immediately turned away and faced me with his back — without saying a single word. I wasn’t sure if the store was open or ready to serve customers, especially since it wasn’t during lunch or dinner hours.

After waiting for a while, he slowly turned back to face me, still completely silent. I stood there waiting for some kind of acknowledgment or explanation (maybe they had run out of bread or were not serving yet), but nothing — just silence for about 10 seconds. It honestly felt like a staring contest.

When I finally gave a puzzled look, he muttered one word — “yes.” That was it. No greeting, no “what would you like to order,” nothing. I continued my order, but it was clear he had zero interest in serving customers.

A very disappointing and unwelcoming experience. Definitely not going back to this outlet again.
author: Cstherine Tong

review_text: Conveniently at the MRT station. The egg mayo sandwich was delicious and crispy! The environment of the restaurant is bad. It’s hot and not cooling. At least there are fans. It’s not very crowded. Would recommend here for lunch sometimes.
Great Affordable Sandwiches.  This outlet is very friendly compare to others.  Service is fast and efficient.  Dining area is spacious with lots of seats.  Sandwiches are consistently good.
author: Logan Chiam

review_text: I have been going to subway for a long time now. Every time I normally praise subway, but this one was purely awful. I was literally searching for the 3 OLIVES and few PIECES of corn that they gave. The sandwich artist wasn't even in a respectful mood. Even the sauce I asked for was half of what I normally get from other branches I usually go to. Maybe i chose the wrong day to come to this branch.
author: Srilakshmi Namini

review_text: I ordered the lechón and grilled chicken. Both were good overall and the flavours were authentic. The lechón was tasty but a bit on the greasy side, and the chicken was slightly dry for my liking. Still a solid experience and worth trying if you’re in the area
author: Vlad Tapia

review_text: First time trying cebu restaurant. I would say it's a unique experience. I think it's quite rare to see such food in Singapore. The lechon meat has got a unique taste. The skin is super crispy. The soup provided is saltish and sourish. One comment is that after chewing the crispy skin for a while, my jaw feels very tired.
author: FF2030

review_text: Great tasting lechon. I ordered the 500g for $24. Skin is very crispy, nice mild smokiness, good balance of fats and lean meat. Aromatics like spring onions, ginger, garlic and lots of lemongrass makes the meat very fragrant. It's lemongrass overload! Actually the lechon is flavourful enough that no sauce is needed for me.
author: Ida Einjaw

review_text: Very authentic Filipino cuisine. Delicious and the serving is just right. We tried their lechon, sisig, adobo, liempo and laing and we say it is really really good. Very near to Lyf hotel and very close to One-North Station too! It is a must-try Filipino cuisine! They are located in Timbre+ where there is a live band or gig every night. You have to try and comment here if you agree! 😊
author: Dennis Teodoro (D Channel)

review_text:
I am an undergraduate student from Nanyang Technological University and a member of the Filipino cultural club. For our end-of-academic-year event, we reached out to Iskina Cebu, and they generously agreed to sponsor a large serving of their delicious lechon along with two trays of flavorful chopsuey.

The coordination was smooth, and their team was incredibly accommodating throughout the process. Our attendees thoroughly enjoyed the dishes—the lechon and chopsuey added a wonderful touch of home to our celebration and made the event even more special.

We are sincerely grateful for their generosity and support, and we definitely look forward to visiting their restaurant to enjoy their amazing food again!
author: Jan Matthew

review_text:
The food is fine, but the workflow here is a mess. You order, queue, and pay, then collect your drinks. For the food, you're supposed to follow the number on your receipt, but they just left the eggs sitting on the side of the counter with zero indication. New customers are just expected to magically know to look there.

No serviette provided, and trying to get anyone's attention is a challenge.

But the worst part was the aunty cleaning tables. She started wiping down other people table while their belongings are still on it, physically moving their stuff to clean underneath. It felt incredibly intrusive and rude. Fix the system and teach the staff some boundaries.
author: Ryan Lim

review_text:
When it comes to kaya butter toast and kopi/teh, Ya Kun is one of the classic go-to.

I’ve visited many outlets over the years, but this Fusionopolis (One-North MRT) branch really stands out. I’ve been religiously patronizing this outlet for about a year, mostly on weekdays, and it consistently delivers that familiar, comforting experience.

The layout works really well: cashier, drinks, eggs, and toast stations are spaced out so the usual morning chaos is minimal. The crew works very much in-sync, and a few even remember regulars’ orders before we can speak. Considering the sheer number of offices and industrial buildings nearby, that level of attention is both impressive and genuinely personable.

The outlet is also clean, spacious, and comfortable, unlike some of their other branches where I practically need to tuck in my stomach just to squeeze between tables, this one gives you room to breathe.

Friendly, efficient, and reliably warm, this branch perfectly captures Ya Kun’s familiar, kinship vibe. Another check-in, another spot I’m happy to return to!
author: Darren Lim

review_text: Our toast was served cold. Mei Lin, the duty manager, was rude and suggested retraining. Her staff members were much more polite.
author: K W

review_text: Great breakfast place near the MRT station. The kaya toast was delicious and crusty, served with two eggs and a hot drink. The set costs SGD 6.70, which is a fair price. During the National Day they also sell special durian toasts.
author: Pui Yu Chan

review_text: The staff were incredibly kind. I accidentally spilled my drink and before I could even react, they were already by my side with tissues and wet wipes. They even replaced my drink at no cost, despite the mess being entirely my fault. Thank you so much for being so gracious and thoughtful!
author: Peggy Soon

review_text:
Pretty good bowl of chicken cutlet noodles. The texture of the noodles was done just nice, soft and springy enough. The dumplings we ordered were huge, probably the largest I've ever ate. Really value for money. The beef brisket was also soft and flavorful.

Last but not least, lady boss super friendly!
author: Choon T

review_text: Definitely deserve the 5 star! Tried this stall across 2 weeks - Wanton noodle (dine-in and takeaway), XL fried chicken noodle! Noodle still maintains its springiness even though it is a takeaway. XL Fried chicken noodle is really nice but it is $5.50. (Wanton noodle is $4 definitely more worth it!)
author: Javin Chan

review_text: Delightfully Tasty Wanton Noodles!  Definitely value for money with the generous serving and huge dumplings.  Noodles are springy and cooked to perfection with different flavours too (tomato and spinach).  At only around $5 definitely value for money.  Service is fast and efficient.  This stall is located in a food court that can be crowded during peak lunch hours so make sure to chop your seat.  Wong Kee is a must try for noodle lovers!
author: Logan Chiam

review_text: Textures of the noodles was nice. The vegetables were really fresh too. But I got overcharged for my bill. Dumplings were huge and clump together (kinda like on steroids). The original outlet at depot road is still overall better in terms of quality.
author: Brian He

review_text:
03/11/18
Overall the wonton mee is one of the better ones you can find in typical hawker centers or Food courts. They give both fried and soup based wonton. Both versions are generous in size and delicious. The Char Siew portion is good as well and the noodle is firm and blend nicely with the sauce. However, beef brisket is too salty and not worth a try. Go for the wonton mee which is their best.
author: Luke Skywalker

review_text:
It’s like hawker food but abit pricy by $1-2

Variety is limited imo. Theres a Thailand, Malay, Chinese, Korean and some food trucks do burgers and fried chicken.

Food is decent but not exactly wow. The space is huge and many seating area, I’d assume it’ll be crowded during lunch hours from the offices nearby

Ambience is lit.. there is a live band too, but it’s pretty loud and hurts the ear. Good if you prefer not to hear each other in a conversation. A lot of alcohol people there, more to chill and enjoy the music.

Interesting vibes but not for everyone
author: elayna chin

review_text: Nice hawker scene near one-north mrt. Good variety of food with some modern healthy options to cater to the younger working demographics. Interesting beer taps, an option for day drinking
author: PD

review_text: Open air food court with live band on Friday evening. A little too noisy for me but can see the crowd were enjoying themselves much and with very good vibes. Highly recommended.
author: Eng Siong Lee

review_text: The food here is underrated. Asia wok and Momo burgers remain the best. Live band is awesome and its not that hot despite being semi open air thanks to the cooler fans
author: zun lee

review_text: One of the best food court / hawker centre in the area. They have multiple outlets serving different cuisines. There is a Vegetarian bowl place as well along with a Kopitam.
author: Shubham Gupta

restaurant_name: Hoodadak Korean Restaurant 후다닥 한국 음식점
review_text: Delicious and worth. In compare to most Korean restaurants, it taste better with others more of a blend in Western taste. The seafood pancakes, the best awesome one I ever had.
author: new4sg

restaurant_name: Hoodadak Korean Restaurant 후다닥 한국 음식점
review_text:
Delicious place but not the kind that blows your mind. But it is a place you wont mind coming back multiple times.
I loved the gamjatang (potatoes and pork bone soup). Spicy pork was pretty normal? Banchan was normal as well. Would come back here to try their other stews.

This place gets really crowded even on a weekday night. Come early to avoid having to wait.
author: Charis Koh

restaurant_name: Hoodadak Korean Restaurant 후다닥 한국 음식점
review_text: Visited on a rainy day and really enjoyed the hearty stews! Tried three different soup bases, and the spicy seafood tofu soup was the standout. The kimchi wasn’t quite to my taste since I prefer sweet and spicy, while theirs leaned more towards sour and spicy. Looking forward to coming back to try the fried chicken.
author: S S

restaurant_name: Hoodadak Korean Restaurant 후다닥 한국 음식점
review_text: I love how casual this place is. Their fried chicken is super crispy yet juicy inside. Highly recommended. The LA beef ribs were slightly tough though. Still very flavourful nonetheless.
author: Bryan CY Chua

restaurant_name: Hoodadak Korean Restaurant 후다닥 한국 음식점
review_text: Being a regular here for the past three years and leaving with a satisfied tummy each time, this is one of the best Korean restaurants in Singapore for their hot food (excluding KBBQ). The tasty banchan sides are served generously and refillable. Nothing has been disappointing so far and portions are huge for most, can't wait to try more from the menu!
author: Kosong Belly

review_text: The place is clean and comfortable, with friendly and fast service. I ordered the beef pho, and the broth was very flavorful and rich — just like authentic Vietnamese pho. The portion was perfect and the toppings were fresh. The owner was very kind and even gave a complimentary dessert. Great spot for a casual lunch or dinner. Definitely coming back
author: Steve

review_text:
Really love their vegetation pho, Buddha rolls and Vietnamese white drip coffee.
Usually 21++ ( slightly over priced). Taste is excellent and ambience is good
author: Gowtham Subramanian

review_text: great lunch spot if you want to come here during lunch hours. their pho is very comforting. would definitely come back here again!
author: Angela Almond

review_text:
I visited shortly after the weekday lunch hour. I had checked the menu beforehand and planned to order the fresh spring rolls, but when I arrived, everything I wanted was unavailable 🙄 The only option left was the salmon and avocado summer roll, which is unfortunately the one I like the least.

The Korean pulled pork banh mi was fairly good, though it leaned more sweet than spicy. i also ordered a noodle bowl, but the rice noodles were completely overcooked and clumped together. The fresh vegetables were nice though. Still, the overall flavors weren’t close to authentic Vietnamese cuisine. If i had known that, I would have chosen another a different place.

There were also many flies inside, and the kitchen didn’t seem to have proper ventilation while cooking, which made the experience uncomfortable.
author: Lena

review_text:
First try on classic baguette, pate and sauce blended well with the generous hams and ingredient, to go with crispy fresh baguette. Recommend!
Self service, poor ventilation due to small enclosed placed.
author: Leno Saw

review_text:
If you are looking for a spot to kick off an early evening in the lush greenery of Rochester, this is a winner for the drinks alone—just maybe plan your dinner elsewhere.

The Good: Come for the Brews
The Witbier here is fantastic. Huge props to the brewmaster (9/10) who clearly knows their craft. They have a brilliant hourly pricing promo where beers go for $5 to $10, making it a "fab" and affordable way to start your night. The vibes and the beer quality are definitely worth the trip.

The Bad: Stay Away from the Kitchen
Unfortunately, the kitchen is where the experience falls flat (Chef: 3/10). The food is passable at best and misleading at worst:
* The Calamari: These weren't actual squid rings but appeared to be breaded, "composed" fish rings.
* The "Bashkir" Pizza: The toppings were incredibly miserly. It felt like the chef had a single piece of tandoori tikka and sliced it paper-thin over the pizza, like they were shaving expensive truffles rather than serving chicken.
The Ugly: Service & "Compensation"
To make matters worse, they tried to compensate for the lack of toppings by piling on chilli padi. It was scathingly hot—to the point of being painful. When we shared this with the staff, they took the half-eaten pizza back to "remove the chillies" (which is an odd fix) and then had the audacity to charge us for the water we needed to cool our burnt tongues.

Verdict: Go for the beer—it’s definitely worth it. Just make sure you eat before or after your visit!
author: A-Cute Hunger

review_text: I loved Picotin’s food but Rochester outlet really is a totally disappointment. Food totally can’t make it, it’s totally unlike cannot even compare to the few other Picotin restaurant which I have visited, eg Katong, Waterboat House and Fairways (before it closed). The worst part is the Calamari is just like Squid Cake not Crispy Squid, it tasted just like Fried Fish Cake. When we informed the service staff about it, he informed us to write a review on Goggle to let his boss see it, what type of service is this !! Really not worth the visit. Only thing unchanged and good is their house brew beer.
author: Honey Tan

review_text: We truly appreciate the restaurant’s outstanding flexibility in catering to our recent corporate event. Despite the last-minute increase in guest numbers, the team accommodated us seamlessly and handled everything with professionalism. The service staff were attentive, friendly and the food quality and quantity were excellent, our guests were very pleased. Thank you Noe Tay & team for delivering such a smooth and enjoyable experience for our event!
author: Michelle GOH

review_text:
Reached at 845pm without any crowd at all.
Please order Mixed grill sausage and nacho, they were great! 😃
However, the rest of the dishes weren’t up to par.. Ribeye was very tough, lamb shank portion is very small & tough 😅 Pizza (pepperoni) is super salty.
But service is warm and nice just like the ambiance.
author: Elainn

review_text: Really a hidden nook....works well for diners who want quiet and good food :) Greens were crispy fresh, the beef was tender and enough, and the seasoning was done with a light hand, which was splendid.
author: G

review_text: Aunty never wear mask, very rude attitude. The veggies were not fresh at all.
author: Bobby Lee

review_text: One auntie very rude. Understand it’s lunch time but if the staff can’t handle crowds, too bad, not our fault. Also , I asked for corn and olives, but I just received less than half a scoop of corn and just 3 small olives
author: Ying En

review_text:
To start of is attitude staff attitude is horrendous ask abit more this and them, tell me "we can't give you more of onions" I replied "huh?" I'm like what do you mean you can't abit more, when I order from other subway's store I can ask for more this and that. Can see there's alot of unfairness. Is it due to budget? Or you see us as students so U can give abit more this and that.

Can foresee this subway won't really improve including the service of it.

Would I recommend anyone eating subway here? No I prefer other places wherever standard
author: Leon Hart

review_text: Staff don't understand English. I called and said "I'm waiting for my order" and they replied "what's the meaning". Order arrived late and didn't update on Grab. Missed my lunch break and had to go back to work. Sandwich was disgusting also, not fresh.
author: Natalie

review_text: It was fast but they mix up the order. The stuff attitude was very bad. If there is any manager please tell her that she speak very soft and have to improve in her attitude towards the customers. It was a auntie with tattoo. Thank you.
author: tharaaa aaa

restaurant_name: CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar
review_text:
I ate dinner at this restaurant a handfull of times now, their food is delicious. The menu does not have a large amount of items but a carefull selection of different tasting dishes, something for everyones liking. Each dish on that menu is perfected by the cooks and has a deliciously balanced taste, a joy to eat.
The serving staff is polite and professional and the restaurant is kept neat and clean.
Finally, the dining area is inviting, complimented with fitting background music, not to loud so you can still have a conversation with table companions.

A very recommendable place to eat.
author: Arthur van strien

restaurant_name: CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar
review_text:
Travelled here for lunch. To put it shortly, food is just superb.

Mushroom stew was superb. You could literally taste each ingredient that was listed in the menu, either subtle or dominating in the dish, while the aroma wafts pleasantly. The generously filled garlic bread compliments well with this stew, which makes this side really filling.

The Beef Bolognese was really crafted with care. From the fine texture of the pasta to the burst of flavour from the sauces that coats the dish, it truly was a delectable meal. For the price, I would say it is absolutely worth it.

This place has a very soothing and somewhat romantic dinner, which acts more like a bar. The service was smooth too, and overall, this is a place that's good for a meal or a drink. Cleanliness was well maintained too. Interior designs were also thoughtfully laid out, which gave it a clean vibe.

Overall, a fabulous place for everyone to enjoy a meal or drink. Excellent restaurant!
author: Everhart

restaurant_name: CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar
review_text: Such a lovely cafe cum restaurant. The food was really tasty and the portions were generous. The staff as always very welcoming and friendly! Great place to chill with friends. Will definitely be back!
author: Janice Lee

restaurant_name: CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar
review_text:
Booked through eatigo with a good discount. The place is a little hidden behind the hotel counter, so took us a while to locate it.

A typical small hotel eatery. It was quite empty on a weekday evening.

Food was acceptable considering the pricing with eatigo discount. Service was basic, but a few occasions, difficult to get the servers as they were not even in sight, not helpful that the shape of the restaurant was a L shaped one.

I don't revisiting for that pricing.
author: Angie Chng

restaurant_name: CALI Rochester Park – Pet-Friendly Restaurant & Bar
review_text:
Great experience. The food was top notch. Lamb shank was tender and came off the bone easily.

Pasta, pizza & ribs were also amazing.
Nice place to bring doggos and chill at the alfresco.
author: A M

review_text:
I recently visited Chibing for the third time, and it never disappoints! They offer a wide variety of Korean dishes, and my family and friends were all very satisfied with both the food and the service.

I’ve tried their bingsu, army stew, chicken, and beef bulgogi — all superb! Plus, they serve unlimited side dishes, which is such a great bonus. They also offer drinks, and their Korean barley tea is definitely my favourite!

All the staff welcomed us with warm greetings and smiles, and they assisted me, my dad, and my friends throughout our stay. Their friendliness made the experience even better.

Can’t wait to visit again — next time, I’ll be trying their BBQ with my friends! 😋
author: Sandra Mae Dela Cruz

review_text:
Authentic Korean flavors with the perfect balance of spice and sweetness. The bibimbop is authentic, the Mango Bingso is my favorite and every bite felt like a trip to Seoul. All side dishes are unlited when you order any meal from them.

The crew is kind and nice.

Worth the price
author: Shie Candelaria

review_text:
They actually serve very authentic Korean food (My Korean colleagues actually were impressed by this restaurant).
For easy decisions, they have 3 sets that include chicken/beef platter, Korean pancakes, side dishes and fried chickens, which is very very plentiful for 3 pax to share!
They also have tea bags from Osulloc which I like a lot too :)
For the sets, we ended off with bingsu! And a lucky draw but I only got 10% of next chicken dish hahaha sad
author: Liau Yuan Wei

review_text:
CHEESE DAKGALBI
The dish was absolutely satisfying! The generous layer of melted mozzarella on top was rich, creamy, and perfectly balanced with the savory sauce underneath. As the cheese melted, it blended beautifully with the tender ingredients below, creating a comforting and indulgent flavor in every bite.
The portion size was generous and great for sharing, and serving it hot on the pan made it even more enjoyable. The combination of gooey cheese and flavorful base made this dish a standout. Highly recommended for cheese lovers! 🧀✨
author: Yt Yt

review_text:
Referring to my order of seafood tofu kimchi soup.... the 2 miserable looking prawns has a mushy texture and are not fresh, the small portion of crab is also not fresh and tasted fishy. When i feedback to a male staff, his reply was that these are frozen seafood. I clarified again that these are not fresh. He repeated that these are frozen items.
Huh? Frozen seafood=Not fresh?
The 2 sotong rings are the cheapo, plasticity and chewy type. Luckily the strong kimchi flavour concealed the flaws. Their sides dishes are also limited in variety although refillable.

If you order their bbq set, there is only one small basket of lettuce, cannot refill.

If you are in the West side and want good Korean food with lots of nice and unlimited side dishes, go to the one at Sunset Way.
author: Ron ni

review_text:
If u want to have good quality soups but hate sweating out eating at hawker centres/ coffee shops… this is the plc.
It offers a variety of good, wholesome boiled soups in a spacious aircon seatings.
Ordered the lotus root peanut soup. The soup was good, and it’s not too salty. (For those want it more salty, can add to taste at your preference)
The pumpkin rice was soft and nice too.

Will be back to try their other soups in future.
author: YL Wong

review_text:
Rated this for the overall dining experience - a cozy spot for Chinese cuisine at reasonable prices. Would definitely come again when craving comfort and a quiet dining environment.

We ordered the National Day set, and I’d say it was worth the bucks. The additional dishes we tried were all lightly warm, which made me guess they were prepared earlier and kept in the bain-marie. Personally, I prefer my food served hot, especially at a Chinese restaurant. The only dish that arrived piping hot was the salted egg lotus root. Overall, the flavours were average and comforting.

Now, onto the most important part - the soup! I was pleasantly surprised to know they offer a one-time refill, which is such a thoughtful gesture for a soup lover like me. But a little heads-up to all soup people out there: this isn’t your typical hawker or home-style soup. It’s boiled for a long time, so it’s thicker and less smooth on the throat. The soups we had were quite meaty and hearty, not exactly light or refreshing, but perfect if you’re looking for something warm and filling!

Oh, and one more thing! The pumpkin rice totally surprised me! I don’t even like pumpkin, but the rice was so flavourful and full of dried shrimp aroma. Dried shrimp lovers, please order this! I finished the whole bowl without even realising it.
author: Nomnomyzm

review_text:
Lao Huo Tang. Franchise with 10 stores island-wide. Set lunch $69 and three tea, with total cost $89.81 (after GST & service charge). Soup was well boiled, with soft meat. Prawn was not as nice. 辣子鸡was good.

Plenty of tables in this restaurant. Arrived at 11.45 am and got a good table.
author: biyan tt

review_text:
I used to visit The Soup Restaurant at their JEM branch, and it’s always been a comforting spot for a simple, hearty meal. One of the standout items for me is their lotus soup – it’s flavourful, soothing, and perfect for a rainy day. I especially appreciate that they offer refills once you’ve finished the first pot, which is a rare and generous touch these days.

The tofu dish was decent – nothing particularly memorable, but it paired well with the rest of the meal. As for the roast chicken, it leaned a little on the dry side, but still tasted alright and was acceptable overall.

All in all, The Soup Restaurant continues to deliver a satisfying dining experience. I’ll definitely be back again!
author: Ming Shen Tham

review_text: Food was above. Operation was not that smooth and not restaurant alike. The lifeline of the operation - credit card payment system - was down. Food was reasonably price.
author: 7eleven

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant | The Star Vista | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Had a satisfying meal at Yayoi Japanese Teishoku Restaurant at The Star Vista. Ordered the Unajyu set and was pleasantly surprised by the generous portion of unagi. The eel was soft, nicely grilled, and coated in a rich, flavourful sauce that paired perfectly with the fluffy rice and shredded seaweed. The set came complete with a crisp side salad and a warm, comforting bowl of miso soup, making it a well-balanced and filling meal. Overall, good value for the price and a solid choice if you’re craving Japanese comfort food. Would happily return to try other dishes 🍱✨
author: Jason Sim Hong Teck

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant | The Star Vista | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text:
Located at Star Vista, Level 2. Price matches serving size. To be honest, the taste is pretty good too. The broth of the Sukiyaka is great, sweet & savory as it supposed to be. The Mabushi is a teaser if you haven't tried. Can be eaten in 3 ways giving a different spice to each level.
If u are a big eater, rice & basic salad is refillable (FOC), same applies for the Miso soup. However, I thought the Miso soup was a little blend.
Service, nothing special. The regular norms you get at most restaurants. Atmospphere, limited indoor seating (Air-con). Outside is under shelter & ve a lot of fans blowing. Tempreature wise, acceptable but can be a little annoying for ladies with long hair.
Damage for 3 pax SGD80+.
Overall, my family was sastified. Will definately return.
author: viking T

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant | The Star Vista | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Open air concept. No aircon but surprisingly not hot. Ordered beef Nabe set and it was quite good. There's free refill for rice, salad, kimchi and pickles. That made it more attractive for me as I wanted more salad. Staff are friendly and helpful. Prices are reasonable by Sg standards.
author: Elaine Quek

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant | The Star Vista | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Nice restaurant. They seem to have changed their menu (I was here in 2024). The salmon in my "Salmon Jyu" was coming apart, worst I've seen from a Japanese restaurant. The gyoza looked and tasted like gyoza I could get frozen from a supermarket. I didn't try the takoyaki, but my friend said it was nice. Overall the food is pretty normal, but 100% not worth the price I paid.
author: Phoebe

restaurant_name: YAYOI Japanese Restaurant | The Star Vista | Teishoku | Tonkatsu | Chicken Namban
review_text: Had our usual family dinner here on 3 Oct. Food is great as always and service staff fabulous and pleasant as with our every visit. Their set meal with the unlimited sides refill is good value for money! Photo shows the mixed grill set with beef pork prawn 👍👍👍
author: kencsr

restaurant_name: Pizza Express | The Star Vista (Buona Vista, Holland)
review_text:
PizzaExpress - The Star Vista is a reliable spot for a casual Italian meal. The pizzas are thin-crust, nicely crisp, and well-balanced in flavour — not too heavy, yet satisfying. Ingredients taste fresh, and the dough has that signature light and airy texture.

The pasta dishes are comforting and portion sizes are decent. It’s a good place for family meals or relaxed catch-ups with friends, especially given the spacious and comfortable setting at The Star Vista.

Service was friendly and attentive, though it can get a little busy during peak hours. Overall, a pleasant dining experience — not overly fancy, but consistent and enjoyable!
author: Boon Siong Goh

restaurant_name: Pizza Express | The Star Vista (Buona Vista, Holland)
review_text:
I’ve always loved PizzaExpress for their thin, crispy crusts and fresh toppings — and their new menu didn’t disappoint!

They’ve just launched:
✨ Overloaded Pizzas – Double the proteins for just +$3. Totally worth it if you love a hearty slice!
✨ 5-Minute Favourites – Hot, fresh pizzas that arrive just when you’re ready. Perfect for quick lunch breaks or casual dinners.

We tried two of the new pizzas and both came out hot, fresh, and full of flavour. Their pasta, sides, and desserts were equally delicious — great for sharing with friends or family.

More flavour, more speed, and always satisfying. 🍴
Highly recommend for anyone craving quality pizza done right — without the fuss!
author: Kimberly Chew

restaurant_name: Pizza Express | The Star Vista (Buona Vista, Holland)
review_text: We had a great experience at PizzaExpress. The pizzas had thin, light crusts but fully loaded with toppings. We tried one of the popular pizzas Hawaii-not, and it was pretty good. Service was quick and friendly, and the atmosphere was casual and relaxed, a great spot for both gatherings and a simple meal. Definitely one of the go-to places for quality thin-crust pizza in Singapore.
author: Nobody

restaurant_name: Pizza Express | The Star Vista (Buona Vista, Holland)
review_text:
