Nestled within the lush greenery of Ridout Tea Garden, the surroundings give off a calm, almost park-like vibe that makes dining here feel quite different from the usual fast-food experience.

The outlet itself is spacious, and the atmosphere is much more relaxed compared to busier branches in malls. What I really appreciated was the ample parking space, which makes it convenient if you’re driving over. It’s the kind of place where you can enjoy a simple meal and then take a short walk around the garden area after, which adds a nice touch to the whole experience.

Food-wise, it’s the familiar McDonald’s menu we all know, but paired with the scenic and tranquil setting, it feels more enjoyable. If you’re looking for a peaceful spot for a quick bite or coffee without the rush of the city, this outlet is a great choice.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: Just visited this estate out of random and chanced upon this very old school restaurant. Ordered from the white hair uncle before sitting down and opening up the Google map review. At first I was scared after looking at the negative reviews that this uncle would not cook what we have ordered from him as he didn't acknowledge or say anything when we told him our orders. To our relief, the food came in about 15 mins time. The Sweet & Sour Fish Rice and the San Lau Horfun taste good to be honest, it has this "wok hey" taste which is quite rare in most of the local tze char stalls. We decided to takeaway the salted egg prawn which we have waited for about 20 mins. The uncle was telling us "不要看我，看外面，好了" when the takeaway is ready and made us LOL. Overall the salted egg prawn taste good but it is a little too spicy and pricey at $18. Would recommend if you don't mind the eccentric uncle's attitude but I guess food is decent enough to attract some people back.
author: Whatever You say

review_text: The food here is really good and value for money! :) We especially love their lotus leaf fish, black butter chicken and tofu with emoji mushrooms! We're return customers and will definitely da pao their food again:)
author: Rosemarie Lim

review_text: Love their salted egg chicken rice, uncle is also friendly - not sure why everyone says otherwise
author: Flo Tiffany

review_text:
Food is good (ordered from Grab before). But the In-dining service is appalling. I see several stories here with the white haired uncle, so i’m not the first to experience his “service”.
I arrived a bit before my friend, so I ordered a soup first. White haired uncle refused to take my order, he says must order all at once, otherwise the paper is too expensive.... huh... joke?
10min later my friend arrives, then we order additional dish. After 40 (!!!) minutes of waiting (and i see other people who arrived after us already been served), i asked him where our food is. He says must wait, or you want cancel? I was so furious, i said cancel it. And left to go to a much nicer resto.
author: Hans Y

review_text: The old white haired uncle is very very rude! Make customers wait and doesn't want to take order. And keep shouting at customers all the times. Horrendous attitude! I ordered fried rice with egg for takeaway. They collected the right payment but left out the egg. Won't go back again and highly discourage anyone to.
author: Esther Leung

review_text: I saw some reviews saying that Edmond is "no ____"/"despite being halal" (which is about the most backhanded compliment I can think of.) Well, hard disagree, or perhaps, agree. Edmond is in a class of its own with very fragrant and savoury rice (he doesn't try to puff up the grains with water like some sellers), tasty chicken meat that is never dry or tough (I don't know what this other 1-star rater ate), and a special soy sauce that makes clever use of subtly infused fried garlic, among other things. On top of that, the portions are big, although prices start slightly higher than a typical hawker chicken rice stall. The end result is always very satisfying, and instead of just getting any old chicken rice, Edmond is actually something you treat yourself to. Sure, you can go for more expensive chicken rice that is "branded* and maybe even tastier. But why be such a slave in capitalism's maw? When the trials of this materialistic life get me down, I just go to Edmond's. Try it too, there's literally no comparison.
author: TH Tan

review_text:
I came on a Friday and it was sold out at 3pm.
I came back on Tuesday 11am, and finally got to try it. Probably one of the best chicken rice on my list! Extra chicken and add-on chicken gizzard total of $7.50 worth it!!
author: AJ

review_text:
A Solid Halal Chicken Rice Option, But with Room for Improvement

It’s rare to find a good halal chicken rice, and Edmond’s certainly stands out as one of the better options I’ve tried. However, it does fall short of the high standards set by other Hainanese chicken rice stalls. If you plan to visit, be sure to arrive early to avoid the long queues and the possibility of them running out of chicken.

The set is great value, offering generous portions of vegetables, rice, and chicken. The roasted chicken is juicy and flavorful, the vegetables are well-seasoned, and the soup even comes with two wanton dumplings—a nice touch. However, the rice was overcooked, which was disappointing given the quality of the rice brand used. It also lacked the rich flavor typically associated with this dish.

Overall, while there’s room for improvement, Edmond’s offers a satisfying meal for those seeking halal chicken rice.
author: Mimo Eats

review_text: Long queue but worth the wait. Chicken is nice and rice is as good as it can get.
author: Syed Muhamad

review_text:
Edmond Chicken Rice.. is one of my favourite local chicken rice stall.
The rice is flavorful, toasted chicken is nicely done and the soup i can say is tasteful..with dry onions in.. makes it better .
The chilli sauce with the chicken rice is not hot and also not blant.. just nice..
They also serve steam chicken.
Overall i give Edmond chicken rice.. 10/10.. even the price is reasonable.
Extra rice n extra chicken.. would cost u only between $6.50 to $7.0...this is for an UPSIDE portion of rice n chicken .. not the normal size..

Location: Tanglin Halt food stall. At the wet market.. opposite the old police post..opens morning to 3 or 4 pm.. depends of chicken availability..

If you love chicken rice.. you should try it out when your nearby... You wont regret it..

Enjoy...

Aman .😘 🐔
author: Azman Koozy

restaurant_name: Guangzhou Mian Shi Wanton Noodle (广州面食)
review_text:
Order wanton mee + dumpling. Decent amount of portion. Requested for less oil and less salty.
Overall pretty old school slightly better plate of wanton noodle. Decent size wanton and dumpling too. One of the better stall for wanton mee at late night. +1 for the very polite service and getting the order right from the guy preparing noodle and orders.
author: zack zack

restaurant_name: Guangzhou Mian Shi Wanton Noodle (广州面食)
review_text:
Good place to go at night of your craving for a decent wanton mee. Slightly on the sweeter side.

Ordered a large bowl @ $5.

Do recommend to request more chilli of you like spicy, as I didn't feel the any heat from the chilli paste.

Plump wanton. Still on the look out for the traditional wanton with chestnut
author: Thaddeus Zheng

restaurant_name: Guangzhou Mian Shi Wanton Noodle (广州面食)
review_text:
Eat at Tanglin Halt Market (Singapore).
Went for a small wonton mee, added extra char siew and wonton ($5.00). Noodles were springy enough, char siew decent, but sauce a bit plain—nothing too exciting. Can eat, but won’t make you shout shiok.
Food rating: 6.8/10 🙂
author: Jinghorjiak

restaurant_name: Guangzhou Mian Shi Wanton Noodle (广州面食)
review_text:
Noodles were nicely seasoned, with a nice tanginess.
Wanton and soup complemented each other well - flavorful.
Charsiew was a slight letdown - a tad dry.
Overall, still an enjoyable meal.
author: Stephen Chan

restaurant_name: Guangzhou Mian Shi Wanton Noodle (广州面食)
review_text: I find the noodle texture particularly stands out here, but not really for the char siew and wanton. The best part is they offer anyone who craves a good wanton noodles for dinner or supper as they close at 12am.
author: Dunnowhattoeattoday

restaurant_name: Delifrance Singapore - Queensway Cheers 1 Express Corner
review_text: Delifrance pastry is not of good quality. Pain au chocolat uses chocolate emulco instead of real chocolate. Ewww :/
author: Jane Ang

review_text: Nice experience though some dishes were slightly overcooked like the prawn or the duck. The bird nest crab meat soup was great and appetizers too. Perhaps it’s the crowd so quality control was slightly off. Service is great and decorations were nice. Good to try at least once.
author: Ah Kay

review_text:
+The calm and luxurious interior gives off good vibes.
+The clerk is kind and professional.
+The food isn't usually too seasoned, it's pretty mild.
+It's my first time having Beijing duck, and it's super tender with no weird smells.
-a bit expensive.
-You gotta order Beijing duck ahead of time.
author: Harry HM

review_text:
Had a really enjoyable meal here. The Chinese dishes were well-executed, flavours were comforting yet refined, and everything tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared. The environment is also a big plus , bright, clean, pleasant, and comfortable, making it a nice place to sit and enjoy a proper meal.

Service was attentive and staff were quick to respond, which I appreciated. However, the knowledge and recommendations could be improved. When we asked for suggestions, the staff didn’t really explain the dishes properly and mainly pointed us to order what was on the pictures, which wasn’t very helpful.

The tea experience was also disappointing , when I asked about about a certain white tea, the explanation was simply “white tea,” and there was a little snigger, as if we wouldn’t understand what white tea is. It came across as unprofessional.

Overall, I’d still return for the food and ambience, but I hope the team can improve on product knowledge and how they guide customers.
author: Mikki B

review_text: Went for a bday celebration - food was good, albeit not spectacular for value. Felt duck was a tad dry, but we had salted veg soup as a second dish and it was really yum. Highly recommend chefs appetiser platter and turbot fish done 2 ways.
author: B H

review_text:
Had dinner here during the cny period. The person doing the lo hei for us appeared to not be very familiar with the things to say or the sequence of items to be added. To make things worse, she dropped the abalone on the table and threw it back into our lo hei..... Perhaps try not to do that?!!

Anyway, the food was abit of hit and miss. Very disappointed with the peking duck served here. It was quite small and more like a roast duck. The amount of skin they could carve out was pathetic as most of it was stuck to the duck. The one at imperial treasure super Peking duck was definitely much better. Lobster noodles was alright and the homemade tofu in spinach (?) and crab was very good. Prices are reasonable but service was quite poor. I think they were quite understaffed and it took a long time for them to refill our tea.
author: HL

review_text:
Walked in on a weekend night so naturally it was really crowded. You can tell all the servers are trying their best to get food on to our table fast. Everyone was attentive, helpful and smiley. Atmosphere was really nice. We were seated outdoors, our server offered us fan and even mosquito repellent upon seeing me scratching myself.

Food was good just that the fried rice was a tad too healthy for our liking. But would definitely recommend this place to someone visiting Singapore.
author: Summer Lee

review_text:
Came here for lunch to celebrate hubby’s birthday. We chose this place because there is lots of vegetarian options for us! Menu were mainly chinese food but we love it that they give it a twist to all their dishes! Sharvin attended to us and was very attentive to our needs.
Love the patio ambience too, definitely come back to try other dishes!
author: Claudia Chew

review_text:
First visit to Chopsuey and enjoyed the food, service and atmosphere.
Prawns were fresh and huge but the surprise was the sauce that enhanced the dishes we ordered.
The Lychee Granita dessert was truly refreshing and perfect for ending the meal.
Special shoutout  to Eileen's attentive service and food recommendations, it was a truly enjoyable Saturday lunch.
author: Yang Eu

review_text:
3 Stars - Great Ambiance, Creative Food, But a Very Poor Start with Staff

​Chopsuey Cafe at Dempsey Hill has a charming, cozy ambiance and a beautiful setting. The colonial-style decor and lush setting make for a wonderful atmosphere for a meal.

​We were looking forward to the creative Chinese/Asian cuisine. We opted for a shared dining experience to sample more of the menu, and the dishes we had were acceptable and unique, though they didn't quite reach the "fantastic" level we had hoped for, making the premium pricing feel a bit high for the overall quality.

​Unfortunately, our visit got off to a truly terrible start with one of the tall staff members. We had two infants (3 and 8 months) and simply asked for a quieter corner in case they got fussy. His reaction was to literally say "huh" and roll his eyes. When I arrived later with my partner and our 8-month-old, and requested a baby chair/booster, the same staff member said, "another huh! One more, walao"—a completely unprofessional attitude that almost made us leave before ordering.

​The rest of the staff were courteous and friendly, but the dining floor and kitchen appeared understaffed, which resulted in noticeable delays in food/drink preparation.

​In summary, while the atmosphere is lovely and the food is creative, the overall experience was significantly hampered by the very poor attitude of one staff member and the service delays. Given the high price point, the food and service standards need to be more consistent to justify anything above a 3-star rating.
author: Elaina Poh

review_text: Our visit was during CNY and we had Yuzu Yusheng. Raphael is so fun, helped us with the Yusheng and used his best to cite all the CNY auspicious words. Next Jot was very attentive to our needs. We are so lucky to have both of them serving us. We will recommend this restaurant to our friends.
author: Pamela Lee

restaurant_name: Ippoh Tempura Bar by Ginza Ippoh
review_text: Have never had better experience of tempura’s . Had a private dinning room and chef explained everything so well. Food  was great, yummy and amazing.
author: Sundeep Sikka

restaurant_name: Ippoh Tempura Bar by Ginza Ippoh
review_text: Not a big fan of Tempura so will unlikely return again. Kudos to the incredible team of service staff who explained every dish served clearly. The dish that I liked most was actually the handmade soba in cold sauce. It was the best soba I’ve ever had so far. Ambience was not great as the bar next door was quite noisy as they are open concept & linked. For $250++ per pax, I’ll prefer a more conducive dining experience.
author: Kelvin Wee

restaurant_name: Ippoh Tempura Bar by Ginza Ippoh
review_text: Really enjoyed the dining experience here. The set menu was extremely worth it. Saw many reviews saying that they were unhappy that the tempura was served in batches but that’s because they chose to sit at the normal tables. If you prefer for your tempura to be served piece by piece, I recommend you sit at the counter tables. You can even see the chef frying each piece. Will definitely come back again!
author: Kimberly T

restaurant_name: Ippoh Tempura Bar by Ginza Ippoh
review_text: The tempura was decent, but not memorable enough to warrant a return visit. For $125 per set lunch, I expected much more. There are definitely better options out there for tempura at a far more reasonable price.
author: Chewielicious T

restaurant_name: Ippoh Tempura Bar by Ginza Ippoh
review_text:
Excellent tempura place. Took the biggest course for lunch, plenty of tempura, ends off with rice or noodles and some dessert.

Overall, it's pretty nice, not heavily seasoned, with very fresh ingredients for that 'clean fried taste', it's hard to explain but I think you'd know once you try. Very high quality tempura.

Excellent table service.
author: Lionel

review_text: Food was great. Ordered the salmon and crispy chicken. Salmon was fresh and the chicken breast was really tender and juicy. Ordered apple pie as dessert (was great too), chef gave a complimentary ice cream dessert for the long waiting time. Service staff Camille was very attentive too. Overall awesome service and food!
author: Joyce Wai

review_text:
8/10.

Got quite a few meals so I’ll just write what I liked and disliked.

Liked:
• The Crispy Salmon Sushi was great, with the crispy fried exterior of the rice but still chewy and soft interior. The Chipotle mayo gave some tanginess and the salmon had no off-smell.

• The Pepper Crusted Wagyu Beef Tenderlion was very well-cooked. Despite it being a thick cut, it was still extremely tender. The pepper crust gave it nice texture and the sauce complemented the beef well. The carrots were well-cooked too and were sweet to balance the richness of the beef. However, the beef was not very juicy.

Disliked:
• The Fried Crackling Chicken uses a half chicken so you’ll get both breast and thigh meat. While the thigh meat was tender, the breast was not as tender and formed a hard skin from the fry. Both meats weren’t that juicy as well. That said, I really enjoyed the Buttery Hot Sauce and spinach that came with it, it really helped with the richness of the dish and the spinach gave much-needed freshness.

• I think presentation could have also been better.

• Atmosphere is also not that great. Because the building is shared with 2 other restaurants, it lacks a sense of identity. Those looking for a quiet experience may also not receive one as it can get quite loud due to the poor acoustics.
author: Caden Tan

review_text:
Do like this restaurant, so does my 5 year old 👧
We ordered one brunch set and two entrees, I would say portion is generous and tastes are all good.
Oven roasted tiger prawn is a bit spicy but still very nice, pork chop is tender.
Coffee is also nice.
author: Cindy S

review_text: A lovely, unhurried dining experience overall. The food was pleasant and well prepared, the ambience serene and soothing, and the service impeccable. Particular kudos to the server who attended to my family’s table– she was warm, attentive, and helpful.
author: Ivan Yap

review_text: Exploring a new Kris+ dining place for the wifeys birthday. Loved the atmosphere and service provided. We had x2 set dinners and were satisfied with the yummy mains and sides. Would recommend although a tad pricey
author: Glen Tan

review_text: Great teriyaki chicken bento. Meat is well-grilled, flavourful, and tender. Japanese rice is just the right level of sweetness. And you get a dollop or various veggies (pickles, wakame) and sweet omelette (tamagoyaki). Plus a cup of piping hot green tea to boot!
author: danielchen87

review_text:
Ordered this platter via GrabFood around lunch time and it arrived so messed up with the sauces stuck on the insides of the lid. One side of the platter is squashed and some of the sushi toppled.
For delivery handling issue, i had sent in my feedback to GrabFood.
On the other hand, all the items are present in the platter as per photo except for the scallop sushi. The staff replaced it with crabstick sushi… in the end there were 4 pieces of crabstick sushi and 0 scallop sushi. If there is no stock please replace with at least something of the same value, NOT with crabstick this kind lar…..
You go chicken rice stall ask for drumstick rice they dont have and they give you braised egg rice you willing to pay same price or not???
The sushi rice is not flavoured well enough, rice is also not cooked well enough… tamago egg sushi tasteless…. There’s this something mixed with mayonnaise, tasted spoilt… a big waste of money spent. Never ever again will i buy from umisushi.
author: Benson Tan

review_text:
good food 🍱 yummyy🥰 I always come here for lunch.
They have good lunch set starting from $7.90. With main dish, veggies, mash potato and miso soup.
All taste very good.
The staffs are also friendly especially the cheerful Louis(?). 😄
author: Indah

review_text:
Probably one of the best udon I ever had in SG. Portion and ingredients were generous and the soup is piping hot! 👍🏻

Really loved that the udon is soft and the soup tastes so so good. The ingredients used (oden) is fresh and well cooked. Only spent $9.80 on the udon and $2.50 on a pink lemonade beverage that is refillable. Super good deal!!

Staff is polite and very helpful, food was served fast too! Kudos to all staff 😊 The outlet can be a little hot due to poor air conditioning but that should be MRT’s central aircon issue.
author: Jessica

review_text:
The moment when we stepped in at 8.07pm, 21 October 2024 and we said we want to claim our Shopee voucher, Oyako Don, the aunty showed an unhappy/rude face. We claimed 2 bowls. First bowl taste ok but the second bowl taste sibeh salty, my friend felt like eating “Pao Fan”/ porridge just like the images shown.

Definitely will not recommend this place to others! Worst food and service! Bad experience!
author: Jean Tan

review_text:
Tried the food at Pepper castle for first time last weekend and we loved it. A bit spicy for me and the chicken tikka masala was a bit different; but the food was very tasty and they do a really good naan! Will be back to try more!
It's not much of an ambience as such, but you can sit on the tables and watch the buzz of HV :)
author: Sonal Sathe

review_text: It’s in Hollande village . The food is good but the place is not promising. Still the prices are as high as the air-coned restaurant. But they absorb the service charge n gst in price which is good. We had sahi paneer n Manchurian.. the quantity is definitely good enough for 3 person so that makes the pricing worth.
author: Sane

review_text: I love the garlic naan and mutton curry! While not every dish is a hit, I find their butter chicken to be too buttery and rich. Overall, I would recommend trying it if you’re in the area.
author: Empress Ker

review_text: Enjoyed this place for a curry.  Recommend, around 100 Singapore dollars for 4 people main courses, 2 drinks naans & rice. Outdoor dining area.
author: Chris Weatherburn

review_text:
1st time ordering home delivery from here. Arrived within 20 minutes, hot & well packaged.

The chicken biryani portion is very generous — enough to share. Chicken is boneless breast meat, tender & easy to eat. The biryani is aromatic, topped with cashew nuts & fresh pomegranate seeds. Meal came with a gajar ka halwa (carrot halwa) dessert
author: L Chan

review_text: Got my salads here twice in a recent week and I have to say that it is a unique option compared to other salad bars. Following Australian style, the salads here are pre-mixed. Every salad mix has a different personality and more importantly tastes flavourful. Not to mention that the boxes are filled to the brim which is bang for your buck so the servings are really filling. Recommend anyone to go for the Tandoori chicken, egg and potato and pesto pasta if you are looking to try.
author: Marcus Phua

review_text:
Not my first time having Sumo Salad in Holland Village. The ingredients were always fresh and portions were generous. The highlight for me was definitely the potato salad, creamy, well-seasoned, and super satisfying! Overall a healthy and tasty option, though prices are a little on the higher side for salads.

Rather generous serving. Mini (2 choices) , medium (3 choices) and large (4 choices). We went with the medium, each was 11.50$ if I recall correctly. Was very filling!
author: Yun Yi Thiam

review_text:
Sorry to hear about Jane’s demise 😢
Ordered the medium take out… super greens, Thai spicy tofu and avocado chicken. For health, longevity and still so yummy!
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
author: Edwin Soh

review_text: Don’t know why the review is so high. This is one of the worst bowls I’ve ever had here in Singapore. $13.50 for a bowl of brown rice, some chicken with a bit of leaves. Tasteless and expensive. Don’t bother with the preset bowls
author: Doppelgriff Ganger

review_text:
My mother recently bought the pesto chicken & avocado salad from Sumo Salad and the experience was incredibly underwhelming. Do not be fooled by the photos on their menu. What she received was nothing like what was advertised: just one thin slice of avocado, an almost laughably small amount of chicken, and barely any sauce to bring the salad together.

For the price they charge, this felt like a complete letdown. The portioning simply did not justify the cost, and it left us feeling short-changed rather than satisfied. Based on this experience, I would strongly advise others to think twice before spending their money here.
author: Lemon Tea

review_text:
If anyone has ever wondered what happens when Italian food loses the will to live, this place provides the answer.

The Caesar salad arrived swimming in dressing, completely overwhelming the greens and masking any nuance the salad might have had. The only flavours detectable were salt and Caesar dressing. When I politely pointed this out, the supervisor simply said, “That’s how we prepare our Caesar salad.” If that truly reflects the house standard, it may be time to reconsider the recipe.

The Bolognese pasta was overcooked and soggy—far from the al dente texture I had expected from an Italian restaurant. The aglio e olio was no better, consisting mostly of oil and salt, with barely a hint of garlic or any sense of balance.

To round off the experience, we were charged $3++ for tap water, which was never communicated beforehand. Being surprised with a charge for something so basic only added to the overall disappointment.

Overall, this was easily one of the worst Italian dining experiences I have had. When fast-food chains manage to produce better pasta, it really says everything that needs to be said.

Based on this visit alone, I would suggest diners temper their expectations. If this is their idea of Italian cuisine, Italy deserves an apology
author: Shayn K

review_text: Great Lunch with Great Buddies! Enjoyed a delightful light lunch at Madrinaa Italiano in Chip Bee Gardens. The thin-crust pizza was well-seasoned and crisp, complemented perfectly by fresh salads and a comforting soup. A simple yet satisfying spread that made for a wonderful lunch with peers. A great spot for relaxed dining and good conversation. #MadrinaaItaliano #ChipBeeGardens #ItalianFoodSG #ThinCrustPizza #LunchDate #CasualDining #FoodieSingapore #CafeHopping #christmas2025 #gathering #italiancuisine
author: Ivy Eyu

review_text:
I’ve been coming to this pizza joint since a decade or more ago, and the quality has always been consistently excellent. The staff are friendly, and the owner is incredibly welcoming — always up for a friendly chat, which makes the experience even more special.

The food is amazing: great flavours, perfectly thin and crispy crusts, and a wide variety of pizza options as well as pasta dishes. Definitely worth a try, whether it’s your first visit or your fiftieth!

Bonus- Is that they have gluten free pizza crusts upon request!
author: Joanna Zhan

review_text: Good restaurant with friendly and competent staff. Excellent specimen of thin crust pizza. Some fusion options (e g., I noticed one with tandoor chicken topping, though we didn't order that). There's happy hours too
author: Hui-chieh Loy

review_text: The food here is really disappointing for the price. The risotto was watery, overly soft and slimy, and the seafood didn’t taste fresh at all – it seemed like frozen or glass prawns were used. Truffle fries were charged at a premium, but the quality was no better than coffeeshop fries. Overall, very average food at an expensive price point. Definitely not worth it.
author: E Heng

review_text: This place is a great family dining place especially in the evening. Nice ambience. The kids can go roam around the coloured ligtsy fountain area nd play ground while waiting for food. The steaks are good. I love the T none to shared, the onion soup is rich and not salty.. The kids meals too popular that most time not available. I suggest better after service staff (cleaning and washing) though. We asked for extra bowls . No more..  Glasses for water... Pper cups given. Staff attentive and friendly
author: Henry Hsu

review_text:
Was my first visit. It was amazing to taste the quality meat from the bistro, am sure these are selected quality from their butchery.

Was recommended sausage of the day, this was really good stuffs,  nicely grilled and tasty with good texture and flavour.

Steak was thin as per recommended doness by the service team, it turns out amazingly delicious.   It is definitely a place for steak.

The service team is so attentive and pleasant to share their recommendation, not a sales talk, they really feel proud of what they are serving. Even in a busy sat lunch crowd.

Am sure this will not be my last visit

Portion is generous for that price, it is quality stuff.

Bread can be better.
author: joe fong

review_text:
Huber's Bistro is the perfect family dining destination! The environment is incredibly kid-friendly, with a playground right there so the little ones can play while we enjoy our meal—it makes for such a relaxing experience.

The service was great, but the real surprise was the value. We bought a bottle of wine next door at Huber's Grocery and only had to pay a very reasonable $10 corkage fee to enjoy it with our meal. Plus, parking is free, which is a huge plus these days.

As for the food, everything was good, but we absolutely loved the pork collar—it was cooked perfectly and full of flavor. Highly recommend for families and couples alike!
author: OB1

review_text: Huber’s Bistro never fails. Always constantly churning out good quality, delicious food with beautiful presentation and warm attentive and good service. The beef rib remains my favourite but the rest are all ranked 2nd equally. We finished every bit of it every time we dine here because it’s too good to resist.
author: Posh Pearl

review_text:
Food is good. Service is very good.

Ordered 3 steaks & 2 desserts.

The steak orders have an option for either fries or potato with cheese. And 3 types of sauce: pepper corn, garlic butter & au jus.  The au jus was the best, followed by the peppercorn. The garlic butter was too buttery & thick; it did not go well with the steak.

The crème brûlée was good enough to order a second one.

Overall a positive dining experience.

2025 December

=========================

Very good service. Mr Monty, Ms Celine & rest of the crew members were prompt & efficient; above all pleasant with their interaction.

Food was also very good. French Onion soup, mushroom soup, German sausages & sauerkraut, beef rib brisket, beef burger with bacon & fries. And the beer was good too.  Will be back again to try other dishes.

Indoor seating is very limited so we had to take a queue for about 15 min before we were seated. There are outdoor seatings which is available right away.

2025 August
author: John Tango

review_text:
This is an amazing hotel! The rooms, food, facilities, are all outstanding. But, the staff is even better! We were greeted at the front desk by Suzy, and she is simply wonderful. That set us off towards a great stay!
Also, the breakfast is simply outstanding, not to be missed. A shout out to Yeti in the dining room. She is so sweet and took time to make us feel so comfortable and to help us plan our short stay in Singapore. We can't wait to return!
author: Doug Davis

review_text: Booked via a third party service (Agoda). Hotel definitely caters for business traveling guests, but not limited to tourist. Great in terms of location, directly next to Orchard Boulevard underground train station which has shaded path connecting to the hotel, and rental bicycle available within the hotel. Connecting directly to Tanglin mall but the mall does not have much going on for a tourist visit, just for some quick needed shopping. Hotel experience wasn't great. No greetings but instead of unhappy stares from the staff. Check-in was fairly quick but could only say it feels extremely robotic despite having a staff-to-guest check in. Was given non-functioning key card twice and having to go up and down the hotel just to get it right. Concierge were not intuitive in providing guest the hotel experience or any assistance but mostly just there until guest approach them. It is almost not obvious as the concierge desks is just next to those of reception. Only positive was that they are able to lend us umbrellas when there were heavy raining. Definitely not happy with the security check for when I left my "Do Not Disturb" on for too long with the front desk attendant and security entering my room while I was having a nap, understood that it may be a concern but could have been a call or a longer, louder knocking instead of a couple minutes of knocking and direct entering the room. Have to get up quickly from a drowsy nap to check who opened the door and was given an apology and them explaining they closed the door when they heard my friend showering. Not a good experience if hotel attendant can enter the room while no one was available to answer despite putting on "do not disturb".
author: HYong Gan

review_text:
★★★★★ Excellent Stay – Highly Recommended for Club Members
As a club member, my stay at JEN Tanglin Singapore was consistently impressive and well worth it. The hotel strikes a great balance between comfort, convenience, and thoughtful service.
The club benefits really elevate the experience. Check-in was smooth and efficient, and the lounge access was a definite highlight—quiet, well-maintained, and perfect for both relaxing and getting some work done. The food and beverage offerings were generous and well presented, especially during evening refreshments.
The rooms were clean, modern, and comfortable, with good soundproofing and all the essentials you’d expect. Housekeeping was attentive without being intrusive, which I really appreciated.
Location is another strong point. Being close to Orchard Road and public transport makes getting around Singapore easy, while the hookup to Tanglin Mall adds extra convenience for dining and shopping.
Most importantly, the staff were warm, professional, and genuinely attentive throughout my stay. As a club member, I felt recognized and well taken care of, which makes a big difference.
Overall, JEN Tanglin Singapore delivers excellent value and a consistently high standard of service. I would definitely return and highly recommend it—especially for fellow club members looking for a reliable, comfortable stay in Singapore.
author: Czariiina Sison

review_text:
Dear Hotel Jen Tanglin Team,

I would like to extend our sincere appreciation for the excellent catering service provided for our recent company yacht event on 5 Feb 2026.

Despite the heavy rain that day, your team demonstrated outstanding professionalism and commitment. The food was delivered punctually and arrived in excellent condition — warm, well-presented, and ready to serve.

The quality of the food was truly impressive. The beef was perfectly prepared, and the seafood thermidor was absolutely outstanding — both received wonderful feedback from our team.

We truly appreciate your partnership and look forward to working together again in the future.

Jessie Zhou
Senior HR Manager
Moet Henessy Diageo Singapore
author: Jessie Zhou

review_text:
I have severe nasal allergies, staff did their best to accommodate me by arranging a suitable room. They even provided an air purifier in the room, and they were very attentive and smiles.

The hotel room was designed to be tidy and of adequate size, though I felt the windows were a bit small. During the rainy season, it can feel a bit humid. The gym is well-equipped with a variety of exercise machines. While I'm not particularly fond of swimming, I really enjoyed the hotel's pool—it was a lovely spot to sit and breathe in the fresh air. The hotel facilities are comprehensive.

All the staff at the front desk, concierge, and housekeeping were excellent and highly efficient. Oh, and I almost forgot—they also offer bicycles for borrowing and provide a great complimentary shuttle bus to Sentosa!
Also, the uncle at the noodle station during breakfast was particularly cheerful and seemed to really enjoy his work.
author: Peggy Lau

review_text:
Hospitality services that go beyond regular duty. Team at front desk helpful especially Sebastian. Royal Lounge team also friendly and attentive. Made us feel very welcome.

Super value for money to stay on executive floors with the extra perks included. Food is splendid especially breakfast and afternoon tea.

Our room is spacious and comfortable. The shower with consistent flow of hot water is perfect. One of the rare occasions the shower cubicle glass door doesn’t leak.
author: Alice Yong (AliceJomMakan)

review_text:
Exceptional Family Hospitality – Truly a Home Away from Home!
​We are currently halfway through our stay at Royal Plaza on Scotts (Jan 24–28, 2026) with my wife and our son, Daniel. I am so impressed that I felt compelled to write this review even before we check out!
​A huge thank you to Melrose Thomas, who was incredibly helpful and responsive to my emails before our arrival. Thanks to Melrose's coordination, everything was perfectly prepared for our little one. We were greeted with a complete baby setup: a cozy baby cot with a pillow and blanket, a baby bathtub with a dedicated toiletries set, and even a sterilizer for our baby’s gear—which is a total lifesaver for parents!
​The warm welcome didn't stop there. We were touched by the beautiful welcome card written by Farly, and the room was festive with balloon decorations and delicious snacks. These thoughtful, personal touches made us feel so special and welcomed.
​We still have 2 more nights to enjoy here, and we are already convinced that this is the best family-friendly hotel in the Orchard area. The attention to detail and genuine care from the staff are top-notch.
​Highly recommended for anyone traveling with a family. 5 stars well-deserved!
author: I Goh

review_text: Hotel room is clean though it has aged a little. Location is A+ and Staff service has to be A++++. I checked out and realised that I left an important item in the room. The staffs looked twice and located the item for me. Not only the service was great whilst I was there but that same standard of service persisted even after I have left. This is rare!! HIghly recommended. This is a great honest hotel!
author: Andrew Lau

review_text:
Royal Plaza on Scotts is always my go to hotel whenever I am in Singapore. I honestly cannot remember how many times I have stayed here, and that alone says a lot about how reliable and comfortable this hotel is.
The location is perfect, right in the heart of Orchard Road, making it very convenient for shopping, dining, and getting around the city. The twin room is ideal for a family of four, with enough space to move around comfortably without feeling cramped.
One thing I really appreciate is that they provide a drinking water tap inside the room, which is very practical and eco friendly. The check in process was smooth and efficient, making arrival stress free. The room itself was spacious, clean, and well maintained, which always makes the stay pleasant.
Overall, Royal Plaza on Scotts remains my top choice in Singapore and I will definitely continue coming back.
author: Yessie Tanuwidjaja

review_text: It was my first time staying at a five-star hotel in Singapore, and I was not disappointed. The staff were incredibly kind and even upgraded my room to one with a bathtub, which was a pleasant surprise. The bed was exceptionally comfortable, and although the hotel offers a selection of pillows, the standard one was already perfect for me. The TV didn’t have Netflix access, but with screen mirroring available, that wasn’t an issue at all.
author: Berntrieseverything

review_text:
The food was really bad. Fried dishes were limp and soft, felt like they microwaved instead of fried (imagine microwaved potato wedges!). The staff were blur and couldn't really answer questions. They couldn't or couldn't be bothered to explain how we should be cooking the beef after putting a charcoal grill in front of us.  We didn't expect to cook ourselves in the first place given that place was not set up with any ventilation system and they just put a fan on the table for the smoke which doesn't serve the purpose! Aircon was down and they had to open the door.

We did free flow alcohol but the sake was lousy, felt like it was opened for too long... Only the highball was nice.

Very horrible experience. We definitely won't be back!
author: Nic W

review_text: While it said Closed on Google Map, I went into the place during lunch hours and they were servinc sets. I had the wagyu beef don set and it was delicious and substantial. I came away quite full, with the soup salad and matcha tea all in. Service was good, as the lady would come by to top up the tea. Think owner is Japanese? And atmosphere feels authentic too, like places I've been in Fukuoka and Osaka. In fact, eating next to me were 2 Japanese salaried men.
author: Y H L

review_text:
I love the atmosphere here and the vibe.
Though I am alone today. I can totally see my friends and I enjoying the night away here.

Staff is friendly.and the price is very reasonable. Totally recommended the free flow drinks.

Will be bringing  friends back here on my day off.
author: DuirEbelaar

review_text: This Japanese restaurant serves really authentic food, feels just like being in Japan! Prices are a bit on the higher side, but it’s a great spot to unwind and chill after work. Worth it for the quality and vibes!
author: iamjess

review_text:
I came on a weekday using J passport promotion.
Food portion was adequate for the price . We ordered an additional tofu salad .
Overall enjoyable , but the yakitori could have a bit more charcoal burnt flavor. Will come again if in the neighborhood
author: YF Poon

review_text: Not been to Hard Rock for a while, I love their ribs and it's good to go on a night with live music, check their website if your keen on music, or not. The ribs are wonderful and a plate full, very filling. Music was entertaining and not too intrusive as you could still easily hold a conversation so good balance. We had booked but there were still places available throughout the evening, we went on a Tuesday. Service was a little slow but not overly so, could have just needed 1 more staff to match the number of tables.
author: Andrew P (Highlight Photography)

review_text: This was my first visit, and the place has a lively bar-and-live-band setup with a good mix of performers, worth checking their socials to see who’s playing. The atmosphere was fun, and the service was generally friendly. The food was decent, with the ribs standing out as the best dish. Portions were fair for the price, and happy hour offerings were standard. Overall, it’s a solid spot for casual dining with good vibes and live music.
author: Yordan

review_text:
First time in my life, pretty standard Bristol and Bar live band setup. If this is your thing, it is your thing. They have quite a range of artists so do check out the socials for the type of live performances you prefer.

Food is okay, nothing really jumps out and is generally good. Portion is right for the price. Pretty standard alcohol happy hours offering, come early and order first type!
author: Andrei Jedidiah

review_text:
Hard Rock Cafe Singapore absolutely surprised me in the best way! It was my first time here and I came with a group of friends for a Thursday night chill-out session.

The food was a total standout. I have to shout out the nachos. hands down the coolest twist I’ve seen. Instead of minced meat, they serve it with whole beef cubes, cooked to the doneness you like. So juicy, so flavourful. We shared a spread of dishes and everything hit the spot. And please, don’t leave without trying the hot fudge brownie… chewy, warm, rich — dessert heaven. 🍫

We were extra lucky to catch the live band that night (apparently every Thursday!). It’s a duo singing English hits, super engaging, super fun, and they know how to bring the whole place together. The energy was great without being overpowering — music loud enough to enjoy, but you can still talk comfortably. Perfect balance. 🎶

What really made the experience complete was the service. The Hard Rock staff are consistently warm, friendly, and make you feel right at home the moment you walk in.

Highly recommend for anyone looking for good food, drinks, good vibes, and a great night out. Whether it’s friends, team dinners, or just a mid-week pick-me-up — this place delivers. Will definitely be back!
author: Health Coach - Dina Sim

review_text:
Had made the reservation way ahead of time but the restaurant doesn’t seems to bother us though I added I’m going to celebrate my son’s birthday a day early. Maybe they were too busy with other customers actual birthday. My husband ordered a Stout but waiter doesn’t even know what is STOUT 🤣
What a disappointment
author: Diana Low

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Had a wonderful dining experience at Sushi Tei! The food was fresh and delicious, but what really made our visit special was Sally’s warmth, friendliness, and enthusiasm. She made us feel genuinely welcome and added such a pleasant touch to the meal. Great food and even better hospitality — thank you, Sally, for making our visit so enjoyable!
author: de

review_text:
Stumbled upon this cozy Japanese restaurant while shopping with friends in the area, and we were craving something tasty—so glad we walked in! We got a window seat with a lovely view overlooking 义安城，which made the whole experience even better.

Maybe we were just really hungry, but we devoured everything in no time—it was that good. The beef in the sukiyaki was especially flavorful, and the sushi was fresh and delicious. Can’t wait to come back and try more of their sushi rolls next time! 🍣

A special shoutout to the lovely auntie who served us—she was so warm and kind. When we wanted to take some photos, she even suggested waiting until all the dishes arrived so the picture would look nicer. She helped us take photos so patiently, and you could really feel that she genuinely wanted us to enjoy both the meal and the moment.

All in all, a wonderful experience!
author: Judith

review_text: food was served fast, staff constantly refilled my green tea as well. everything was perfect
author: boom

review_text: Used to be regular there. But because the price keep raising, don’t think is worth to eat there. Service was bad compared to last time. Not sure the management know this. But I might not go again. Goodbye Sushi tei 👎👎👎
author: Middayjoy Jan

review_text: Excellent service and really good sushi! Everything tastes fresh and well made. I especially love the view of Orchard Road 🙂 perfect spot to enjoy good food and relax.
author: Ksenia K

review_text:
food are tasty but there are some disappointment mainly due to the lack of pictures to substantiate the description is menu. in short, the menu descriptions sounded overly exciting but some dishes when served can be underwhelming in expectations (while taste wise is ok).

eg. the salmon hot n cold smoke, caramelized onion yada yada, when served, is just bagel with smoke salmon scrambled eggs. so in mind I'm expecting something sophisticated worthy of $30, but was disappointed.

this is my second visit after few years. and I made the same wrong choice as before in drink 😂. the drink honey+ cinnamon+vanilla I always thought would be something creamy (vanilla) but it's unlike my imagination and is quite acquired taste.
author: William Toh

review_text:
I've been twice, once for lunch and once for dinner, and I would go back again. This place is really great. The food is excellent, the drinks are high quality, and the service is friendly.
The Reuben Sandwich is absolutely incredible. I order the sauce on the side because I do. The meat is the best and not greasy at all. It's so amazing. Yes, I ordered it both times I went because it was so great. My friends also tasted it and were impressed.
My companions preferred different meals. Sadly, I can't remember what they were. One was a chicken that was spicy and my friend enjoyed it. He ordered 3 different drinks and he especially enjoyed 2 of the 3. The 3rd one was a bit boring (seasonal sangria), but I think it's because he expected a red wine version, not white. My drink was spectacular. Perfectly balanced. I can't remember what it was called, but it's the pink one in the picture.
Definitely go here for a meal, again and again.
2 notes:
1. It's a little challenging to find in Mandarin Gallery, but don't give up. Floor 3, towards Orchard road.
2. It serves breakfast and lunch all day. Don't be discouraged because there are plenty of amazing, viable dinner selections.
author: Donna Cashore

review_text: Was served by Maxx on a Saturday evening, had dinner with my parents and Maxx took amazing care of us! he took our order, checked in on us, and ensured the food arrived in a timely manner and the drinks that we requested to be served after the meal, we did not even need to ask him to come over, he noticed and took the initiative to ask us before we could even request it. absolutely stunning and stellar service! perfect timing on everything!
author: Cas Lam

review_text: This restaurant has one very important difference from many others: here, they can prepare dishes from the menu without salt, for example, according to your order. Or feed those who follow a gluten-free diet. You must agree that this is very important for those who want to eat safely. Otherwise, it is simply a pleasant restaurant located on the third floor of Mandarin Gallery. Please note that the elevators to the third floor are located at the back of the elevator hall, so pay close attention to the signs on the elevators.
author: Drew Esa

review_text:
This brunch spot is honestly such a pleasant surprise. The portions are really generous, and everything I tried tasted great. It’s one of those places where you actually feel like you’re getting your money’s worth.

The iced latte is the highlight for me. They freeze the coffee into ice cubes and serve it with hot milk, so as the cubes melt, it slowly turns into the perfect iced latte. It’s super unique and fun to drink.

The atmosphere is cosy, the staff are friendly, and the food comes out quickly. Definitely a place I’d recommend if you want a good brunch with something a little different.
author: Master Ji-Ning

review_text: PS.Cafe near St. Regis has great food, drinks and a lovely atmosphere. We especially loved the truffle fries — always a favorite! The meatball mafaldine was really delicious, and we also enjoyed the pizza and salmon. The environment is calm and not noisy, which made the experience even better. Special thanks to Chew, who was incredibly friendly and welcoming and made us feel right at home. We’ll definitely be back next time we come back!
author: Masaki Lady Imagawa

review_text:
Beautiful PS cafe, great vibes and a perfect place to catch up with friends. Service was friendly and pretty quick.

Food was decent and portions were decent, although on the pricier side. The truffle fries are always a hit, but it was the first time I was having the calamari and was delighted by the light and tasty batter.

Reservations recommended as it gets pretty busy.
author: Sarah S

review_text: P.S. Cafe at Palais Renaissance is a masterclass in posh design, offering an elegant, high-ceilinged escape. It’s perfect for groups thanks to the plentiful, spacious seating. While the ambiance is stunning, the food is the real star—especially the amazingly decadent double layer chocolate cake. It’s a sophisticated spot that never fails to impress.
author: Henry Goh

review_text: Absolutely beautiful venue and the staff was so incredibly kind and attentive. Mr Chew, our server was very considerate of my dietary needs, he was also so lovely and continuously checked up on our table.  Thank you so much for an amazing experience.
author: Baes Bae

review_text: PS.Café at Palais Renaissance is a really nice place to chill. The vibe is great - bright, airy, and relaxing, with lots of fresh air. Food portions are generous, so you won’t leave hungry, and everything comes out nicely done. Service is also good, with staff being friendly and attentive without being over the top. Overall, it’s a solid spot for a casual meal or a relaxed catch-up with friends.
author: Kamille Nazareth

review_text: Delicious alcohol, smoothies and shakes. High quality, fast to serve, and the staff there gave me complimentary peanuts and anchovies 😍. Great experience and impression!
author: Kuru Prakash

review_text:
Oasis Bar nails the food and ambience, black pepper prawns? Chef’s kiss. Mango sago? Probably the best dessert I’ve had in a while. Perfect place to chill and eat well.

But the service… let’s just say it’s not as memorable as the food. Friendly enough, but a bit slow and inattentive. Still, worth coming back for the flavors.
author: Nanda (Nseptember)

review_text: We visited Oasis and ordered the BBQ sharing platter, fried soon hock and lobster noodle. The food was delicious, and the ambiance was warm and welcoming. Excellent service from Loraine and her team Highly recommended.
author: Mae Anne Fernandez

review_text:
Just had a wonderful dining experience at Oasis Bar & Restaurant. The food was absolutely fantastic — fresh, beautifully cooked, and full of flavour. The grilled prawns especially were perfectly seasoned and so delicious.

The service was equally impressive. The staff were warm, attentive, and made the whole meal feel effortless and welcoming.

A great spot for a relaxing meal with quality food and genuinely good service. Highly recommended.
author: Jane Foo

review_text:
🔵 Oasis poolside restaurant & bar
The Grand Hyatt Singapore
Level 1 ( Terrace Wing)

🔵 Location = 🔵 Oasis restaurant & bar is set in a corner of the beautifully landscaped forest garden at Level 1, Terrace Wing.

🔵 To get here, use the guest lifts at main lobby area and press Level 1.

🔵 Level 1 = Oasis restaurant, Damai Spa, The Pool, The Garden & Lawn.

🟢 Ambience / Decor
************************
🟢 Oasis at The Grand Hyatt is a dedicated poolside restaurant and bar located by the hotel's swimming pool deck. It has both alfresco seats and indoor ( air con) seats too.

🟢 We came here for the ala carte menu as I prefer eating local Singapore dishes.

🟢 The Oasis restaurant is set in the midst of this spectacular rainforest landscape & lush waterfall area.🌿🌳 The entire garden lawn and the lush verdant flora and fauna are so astoundingly beautiful. ➖️  In the middle of concrete Orchard Road, you suddenly find yourself in an Amazon-like rainforest. So amazing!

🟡 The Food = Dine in dishes
______________________________
🟡 Laksa Singapura SGD28 - The Filipino staff attending to us was kind enough to ask the kitchen to spilt the laksa bowl into 2 bowls for my husband and myself. ▪︎I also requested deshelled tiger prawns, and the chefs kindly peeled the prawns for us. So grateful. 🙏🏻

🟡 The Laksa at Hyatt Hotel reminded me of the delicious Nonya Laksa my late Peranakan mum used to cook for us. The laksa broth was creamy and full of umami flavour. The prawns were fresh and succulent.

🟠 Mee Goreng / SGD28
**************************
🟠 The Mee Goreng here is simply scrumptious — an upmarket, refined take on our familiar hawker classic. The noodles were springy & well tossed in a fragrant, savoury-sweet sauce, with a deeper, more balanced flavour profile and less greasiness than the usual street-style version.

🟠 Ingredients tasted fresher and more premium, giving the dish a cleaner & lighter finish. Familiar in taste, yet elevated and restaurant-style.

🟣 Service = A shout-out to Ms Sujeong, the Korean Senior Team Leader.➖️ She attended to us during payment time and I had a short chat with her. ▪︎Sujeong informed us about the changes to the poolside and restaurant area at ( Level 1 Terrace Wing) when Hyatt hotel was being renovated for 3 years from 2022 till mid-2025.

🟣 Sujeong was gracious, affable and polite. ● It is really nice to meet staff like that who are genuine in their demeanour and you can tell the Hyatt Oasis staff all takes great pride in their work.

🟣 I will be back soon to dine at Oasis again. Because I truly love the rainforest dining experience! 🌳🌳🌿 The whole setting felt almost surreal — like stepping into a tropical garden oasis right in the middle of busy Orchard Road.

◼️19th Feb 2026 / Thurs / CNY 3rd day, 初三。
author: Florence Leow

review_text:
Saw their $10 chicken cutlet lunch promo and decided to give it a try. There were plenty of seats available, and the staff were friendly and welcoming.

We ordered the $10 chicken cutlet lunch promo. A nice touch was that they also serve free water.

The food came fairly quickly and the portion was huge. The chicken cutlet was as big as, or even bigger than, my palm. It tasted really good and wasn’t oily at all, unlike some places. The batter was nicely seasoned and crispy. It was served with potato wedges and purple cabbage coleslaw, which I really enjoyed. They were also generous with the mayonnaise, which paired well with the dish.

Will definitely come back again!
author: June Ang

review_text:
Came here expecting a fun Irish pub atmosphere, but the live band completely ruined the experience. It honestly felt like they didn’t practice at all , they kept tuning their instruments. Instead of music, it was a cycle of awkward pauses, random noise, and constant stopping and starting.

A pub can be loud and lively, sure , but this was just messy and frustrating, and it killed the vibe for everyone trying to enjoy a drink or have a conversation.

The only saving grace was the Guinness, which was solid and probably the only reason I didn’t walk out immediately. If you’re coming for live music, skip it. If you’re coming purely for Guinness… maybe sit far, far away from the stage.
author: Mikki B

review_text: I drink kilkenny on this bar. Taste is very good! I will surely be back. Food is also commendable. The service is highly rated.  However, furnitures inside looks quite old. But i will surely be back for its draught beers.
author: LumenGentium

review_text:
Loved the vibes and the friendly staff! Reminded me of my time in London.

We got the three course set ($35 nett!) - the lobster bisque was amazing, beef roast and Yorkshire pudding was decent and the apple pie was delightful. Enjoyed our time!
author: KW Yoke

review_text: Would like to give a special shout-out to Grace for her thoughtfulness and initiative. Even though my wife and I only ordered a single portion from the Christmas menu to share for our dinner tonight (as we had a late and heavy lunch), she proactively prepared two serving plates and utensils for us, which was a very nice touch. The service was attentive without being intrusive, and the mashed potato was absolutely amazing!
author: WS

restaurant_name: The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens
review_text: Finally tried this restaurant although it has been around for more than 20 years. For appetizers we had the burrata which was very good. Tried the barramundi (salmon sold out). Surprisingly it was very good. I didn't quite care for the couscous salad. I didn't enjoy the chili crab pasta which was on the sweet side. The lacto chicken breast was soft and silky but for me the sauce lacked a punch. I feel the chicken was neutral tasting hence needed something stronger than the vinaigrette like sauce. The dish came with a few slivers of octopus which was good. The star of the night was the artichoke and mushroom salad which was divine. We finished off with two desserts - the chocolate and the peanut butter one (forgot the exact name). Both were good but the chocolate one was decadent and had mango puree and a sour cherry filled chocolate ball. Yumz.
author: Aminah Hussien

restaurant_name: The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens
review_text:
Ambience especially at night is really great. Not that ideal though if celebrating anniversary or romantic as the place is rather small.But service top notch, anniversary cake to celebrate our wedding anniversary

Food wise definitely halibut is good (similar to Chinese wedding fish dish) and lamb rack is soft tender. The vegetable serving was a bit weird (half an empty plate). The mint drink was definitely refreshing
author: Ryukooh

restaurant_name: The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens
review_text:
Randomly popped by The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens and went for the set dinner for two. The dishes recommended to us were spot on in flavour, presentation and portion, and made the whole meal feel like a well-curated experience.

Special shout-out to Ms Zuhaidah, who was very friendly and took the time to walk us through the set menu, explaining and recommending each dish with real pride. Her warm, attentive service elevated the evening and made us feel very well taken care of.
We were sad to learn that The Halia will be closing in March, which makes this visit even more special. Thank you to the team and to Ms Zuhaidah for the wonderful experience and exemplary service — a memorable meal in a beautiful garden setting.
author: Spidey

restaurant_name: The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens
review_text:
Ordered a 3-course set meal dinner for $60 before GST and service charge.

Starter: Burrata served with chilli was a weird combination. Scrapped away the chilli. Brocollini had a few grains of popcorn and ikan bilis that felt out of place. It was supposed to come with parmesan and chicken but only a few thin strands of chicken was served.

Main: Salmon fillet skin was crispy but too salty. Gado-gado salad had too much coconut milk and was too salty. Served with fish roe which was a weird combination as well. Inconsistency in food presentation of the salmon for both mains.

Dessert: not bad, the only saving grace of the set meal. But popping candy with the chocolate dessert felt very extra and unnecessary.

Tea: tasted like lipton tea. Served with UHT milk. Would expect higher quality tea and milk for this kind of price.

Overall disappointing experience with subpar food quality for a $72 3-course meal (after gst and service charge). Will not reccomend.
author: Rose

restaurant_name: The Halia at Singapore Botanic Gardens
review_text: Fantastic dining experience at Halia restaurant. Celebrated my hubby's birthday and our anniversary here. Ambience is very apt for the occasion. Good for talking and catching up. And food and service are great too! Forgot to take the picture of the paperbag halibut. Love it! ❤️ and the waiter after knowing it's our special occasion, served us a cake which was lovely and delicious. Fantastic service 👏
author: flora soh

review_text:
A true hidden gem of Singapore right inside an expensive neighborhood

Came here while on business to renounce foreign citizenship, a great place with wonderful prices. People say it's probably for the workers nearby since you get additional discount if you have a worker card.

I sometimes order a second serving not because the portion is small but because the food is too powerful. Eat till you explode 11/10. Be aware that menu changes(rotates?) every two weeks so what you see in the pictures may not be there.

Oh yes the milk tea is great.
author: Jiayou

review_text:
Monday special- always loved the fried fish soup. Fish is cooked well, not too oily or salty. Soup is tasty , does not have the preservative taste at all. Set comes with a drink only for $8+, so worthy.

Fruits, kuehs & other delicacies can be found here,

The hot milk tea (teh tarik) is one of the best tea i had.
Tasted like a local coffeeshop.  Please try it :)

Generous portion and very affordable given it's location.
There is also a wide range of daily menu that is updated on their telegram page, reservations of food are allowed as well.

Clean dining area, not too crowded, indoor & outdoor seating available. Will always come back here for comfort food, everything here taste home made which is amazing.  Staff are friendly and do not rush us to order.
author: Shaf Jay

review_text: With the opening of more stations along the Thomson-East Coast mrt line, this is a gem of a place that I have come to treasure. Almost did not want to recommend as I would like to keep the tranquility to myself. Food reminds me of days gone where my parents brought me to RELC building or Sloane Court Hotel for lunch. I would say,  food is not pretentious and it's hearty. Fills one's stomach and the milk tea is to die for.
author: Olivia H.

review_text:
I have been visiting this Bistro for almost a year, it has been well only until recently these few days (June 2025), . Back then i remember that i tried their fried bee hoon breakfast set, taste was great.

Lately, the food standard drop. I had the Fried noodle set, it was so dried, noodle were tasteless, sticky together.

I hope there can be some improvement.
author: Thong Steven

review_text: OMG.. this is a quintessential little cafeteria on the ground floor of STB catering to the nearby working class at one of SG's most expensive district. I don't see much review on their breakfast but boy, I am certainly impressed with the breakfast that they serve. Toasted wholemeal bread with loads of vegetables, ham n fried egg and a cup of local kopi. It's nutritious, filling and extremely affordable at only $4.50.. considering the locality!!
author: Lau Cherie

review_text:
Had a fantastic time celebrating a special occasion here. The Rajasthani festival menu was delicious, especially the Dal Banjara and Gatte Ki Sabzi.

To top it off, the service was excellent—attentive without being overbearing. Highly recommended!
author: Dhanesh Shah

review_text: We had a lunch wedding reception at Yantra on 28/2  and it was a wonderful experience. The team headed by Senthil and supported by Manu, Gupta and Chef Shafaq Husain was simply spectacular. They were sensitive to our needs (a group between India and Singapore) and curated a menu for us from their menu and their Rajasthani menu festival. They gave us a tasting, configured the room setting and were accommodative on our need for flowers and cake. They served the immaculate food on cue with precise timing professionalism and service. Very attentive the food was of great quality and guests asked for takeaways. Overall a great experience, reasonable expenditure but more importantly a great group to work with
author: Jayant D'Mello

review_text: Outstanding Indian cuisine. Everything we ordered was simply divine. The flavours were so refined and seasoned just right. The ambience of the restaurant was cozy. The service staff was so professional yet warm. We will be back again.
author: Jenny Kang

review_text:
We had a great time with my friends here. Visited the 2nd time and the team is very friendly warm like family. Ambience is cozy and comfortable, tasting menu is flavorful I like the small portions so we can try many flavors.
Love the special bespoke cocktails. Be sure to ask for an any customized cocktails or mocktails with the friendly bartender. Senthil is very kind. Thank you team Yantra for making our experience so memorable
author: Frankie Wong

review_text:
The finest Indian restaurant in Singapore and competitive with the best Indian fine dining I’ve sampled globally (including London, Hong Kong and Mumbai)

Service is consistently polished and authentic

Rajasthani menu was a hit (especially the Bati) - looking forward to more special menus in the future!
author: Ross Vinten

review_text:
Had a dining experience at Carousel, and the buffet spread truly offers an impressive variety of food. There’s something for everyone — from fresh seafood on ice, sushi and sashimi, to local delights and Western selections. The seafood station was a highlight, with fresh prawns and shellfish replenished regularly. The carving station and hot dishes were also well-prepared, with good rotation to keep the selection interesting.
I also appreciated the mix of international cuisines, including Mediterranean and Asian options, making it easy to go back for multiple rounds without feeling repetitive. The dessert section was equally attractive, offering a nice spread of cakes, pastries, and local sweets to end the meal on a satisfying note.
The ambience was lively yet comfortable, suitable for family gatherings or celebrations. Service staff were attentive in clearing plates promptly, which made the dining experience smooth and enjoyable.
Overall, a solid buffet experience with wide variety and good quality. 4/5.
author: Ewe Keat Huan

review_text: Vv large selection from multiple cuisines. Options were alright, generally quite decent and wel executed. Stars for me were the sashimi, roast beef and chicken, and roast pineapples. Sadly no smoked salmon/ hams though. A lot of Asian singaporean options like kuehs and chicken rice.
author: Sarah Constance

review_text:
This buffet used to be pretty good, if halal. It's still halal, but prices have risen a lot and quality has fallen. Sunday to Thursday dinner was $92++ & even with $11 off it wasn't good value. A free flow of 6 local drinks was included but really at this price you're approaching free flow alcohol territory.

The cold seafood looked impressive but the lobster was only alright, though the prawns were great.

Beef striploin was dry & overcooked though pretty tasty. Papaya soup was an unusual dish but so spicy it was unpleasant. Chili crab was not fresh & the sauce was a bit off.

Chap chye was good though it had little cabbage. Lamb Stew with truffle mashed potato was a bit dry. Okonomiyaki was mislabelled as egg paratha & wasn't fresh.

Laksa had no Laksa leaf or cockles & was on the sweet side but good. Other dishes were generally decent if not particularly good.

Desserts were the biggest letdown. They used to be awesome but were only decent. Coriander ice cream was better than it sounded & was decent. Bandung ice cream was good & surprisingly very light. Mango yogurt ice cream was good but with some ice crystals. Durian Pengat was good.

Service was functional. They didn't ask if we needed carpark coupons.
author: Gabriel Seah

review_text:
Somehow the food quality taste went down abit. I go there every year and always look forward to the seafood Paella, however, the paella this year was kinda meh.

The tomato paste tasted more like diluted tomato paste. Seafood however was alot more than last year.
author: Hello Chester

review_text: I came during their grand launching of the Korean japanese theme night. First time and love it already. All food prep fresh. Delicious. Even have live tuna carving. The chefs willing to share their experiences too
author: Simson Lee

review_text:
place our family has been following for a very long time, and it still carries that same charm. This is one of those rare spots where traditional Hokkien cuisine is preserved in its authentic, old-school form.

The setting itself feels nostalgic — no flashy décor, just that classic Chinese restaurant atmosphere that reminds you of family gatherings from years past. The food is hearty, traditional, and cooked the way it’s always been, which is exactly why we keep returning.

It’s not about modern twists or trendy plating here, but about consistency and comfort in every dish. A true heritage spot for anyone who appreciates authentic Hokkien flavors.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text:
As crowded n noisy as always :D
It has that nostalgic vibes that elderly relatives in my family love.
Food is good, esp oyster omelette and braised pork w steam buns. Dim sum items are ok.
author: Berlinda Goh

review_text: We were there for their buffet dim sum. It was surprisingly value for money. The menu is not that extensive but good enough for the price and quality. Quality of food was good especially the known ones. Some of their original dishes are so so. Some hits some miss but generally, value for money.
author: Kymn Yee

review_text:
I was recommended to try this restaurant so I decided to try it after discovering they were on Quandoo. We ordered the fish maw crab meat soup, yam ring with scallops and their signature Hokkien noodles.

The soup was quite tasty and we had to wait quite a while for the noodles, as they had to simmer it. The taste was not bad. Yam ring was also decent, and I think they had more yam than flour within.

One improvement though, would be for the staff to actually ask if certain things should be done. I wanted to take a picture of the entire yam ring, but once it was set down, the staff started portioning it with the spoon.

It was also fairly crowded which really surprised me. We also heard from the staff that they would be moving soon.
author: Alvin Choo

review_text: This is a traditional dim sum restaurant with a cozy atmosphere. It’s perfect for small groups of 2-3 people, but also spacious enough to accommodate larger parties. I primarily visit for the dim sum, and I’m always satisfied with both the taste and value. If you're a fan of dim sum, I highly recommend the dim sum lunch buffet. The price is reasonable, and you can truly enjoy the homemade, hand-crafted taste. I hope this place continues to operate for a long time, and I look forward to visiting often. Thank you.
author: S J

review_text:
We had a 20+ pax gathering and we've enjoyed ourselves. Many praised the wide selection of food & beverage, the quality of the food and the ambience. The staff were attentive and accommodating. After hearing a neighbouring table celebrating birthday with staff singing the song, we asked if we could also have one for one of our guests. They agreed and we enjoyed the "it's your day ah ha ah ha, happy birthday ah ha ah ha" birthday song. The staff looked a bit shy while singing but we want to let you know it has livened up our mood among the team and brought us much laughter as we tried to sing along. Thank you all, esp to Stephanie and Evangeline, for helping me with the arrangement.
Btw, would suggest that you provide individual food labels in Indian food and dessert selection, instead of one A4 sign listing the food selection. For those who are not familiar with food, at least they can tell what dish they are looking at. Also perhaps considering serving kueh pie tee instead of popiah which is good but huge. After eating one Popiah, we already started to feel full. 😅
author: Sze Mui

review_text:
Came here for a work function. It feels like a fancy buffet of Singapore hawker food. I loved that the was a very wide variety of different food available and that all were really truly local food. Hence it is a great place to bring guests/visitors from overseas.

I really enjoyed the live stations. Such as the noodle station where you have 4 different varieties of soups (laksa, prawn noodle, wonton soup and vegetarian). There was also the roast duck and Hainanese chicken station. You will find food from the different cultures of Singapore (Malay/Chinese/Indian).

What was somewhat disappointing was the cold station (minimal choices of cold seafood) and desserts (once again all local desserts only).

Overall, I found it expensive for the type of food offered as most were street food. But a good experience especially with overseas visitors.
author: Sharon T

review_text:
Reservation made. Table ready upon arrival. Staffs very friendly. Seating arrangement was good.
Wide spread of foods choice. I love the gado gado. Sauce was thick. Basically i love the buffet spread. They have juices and teh tarik peng is wonderful.
author: Eddy Muhamad

review_text:
Full marks.

I dont usually eat to my full at buffets but this place kept me going, filled to the brim. Dont underestimate the local cuisines. Quality of food served and the wokhey glassnoodle stole the show. Can nvr get to try all the dishes. Will be back for more.
author: Lynn S.

review_text:
Straits kitchen was refurbished when Grand Hyatt was renovated recently. It is also a Halal certified restaurant, so you could come and enjoy the food and company of friends who can only have Halal food.
The different cusine is arranged in section. There are Chinese chicken rice, noodles. Indian nasi briyani, nan, tandoori chicken and different curry dishes. Malaysia nasi parang, satay, grilled chicken wing and side dishes.
Other sections include, ice cream, fries fritters, rojak, popian, kueh kueh and more.
The food are tasty and the setting is cosy.
author: peter liew

review_text: We celebrated our reunion dinner at Jiang Nan Chun for the first time and it did not disappoint. The setting was elegant and festive, creating a wonderful atmosphere for family celebration. Each course was nicely executed with reasonable portions. Service was attentive and warm, making the entire experience smooth and enjoyable. Definitely a place we would return to
author: Jamie Lee

review_text:
We dined here on Saturday, 21 February at 8pm, booked by friends visiting from the US who were staying at the Four Seasons. Unfortunately, one of our friends fell seriously ill and was unable to attend the dinner.
The service was the main disappointment of the evening. One of the waitresses — possibly the manager — appeared visibly impatient while taking our order and gave the impression that she could not wait to be done with us. She also commented that we had ordered “too little,” which felt unnecessary and came across as condescending, leaving us uncomfortable as diners.
In addition, when we asked about credit card promotions, we were given a flat “no” without any explanation. After later noticing promotions advertised on the DBS website and probing further, the response shifted to a vague verbal comment that “maybe Chinese New Year, no promotions,” with no clarity on terms or conditions. The lack of a clear, courteous explanation — and the dismissive manner in which the query was handled — suggested either unfamiliarity with the promotions or a lack of willingness to explain. A more informed and polite response would have been appreciated.
The food, however, was excellent and ultimately the saving grace of the experience. The dishes were refined, well-executed, and fully deserving of the restaurant’s strong reputation. The kitchen clearly operates at a very high level.
For a restaurant of this calibre, service should match the quality of the food. While the cuisine was outstanding, the service fell short of expectations, resulting in a mixed overall experience.
author: Glenn

review_text:
The restaurant has warmly welcomed back Chef Alan, who has been leading the kitchen for almost three months now. His new menu is fantastic, with plenty of exciting dishes that clearly show his personal touch.

The food is comforting, served hot, full of flavour, and beautifully presented. Every dish we tried was tasty, satisfying, and made with great care. The menu is also very extensive, with lots of options and attractive set menus,  definitely a reason for me to come back and try more next time!

Highly recommend to anyone looking for a great dining experience,  Chef Alan and his team are doing an amazing job.
author: Patrick
