review_text:
Peking duck served with caviar, first time trying and it was exciting. This is definitely the better Peking duck you can get in Singapore.

Other dishes taste pretty average here and price is on the higher side. Service is great though and the restaurant has a very nice Chinese decor.

Other than the duck, their complimentary birthday cake impressed us too.

If you are looking for Peking duck and celebrating a birthday, this is the place to go.
author: Alan

review_text: A very cosy and posh place for Chinese cuisine. Tried their famous Peking duck with caviar which made it really special. The duck skin was crispy and was nice to go with their original sauce. The fish maw soup was think with broth and the lobster with glass noodle was 👍. The fried noodles with duck meat was my fav with wok taste.
author: Blue Angel

review_text:
Bistro Du Vin is a cosy, no-frills French bistro that does the classics well.

We started with the French onion soup, which was deeply flavourful and comforting, with a good balance of sweetness from the onions and richness from the broth. The steak was nicely done, juicy, nicely charred and satisfying, paired well with crisp fries. The frog legs were a highlight for me- well fried, light and fragrant, not too greasy.

Dessert was excellent. The soufflé was airy and warm paired very well with the vanilla ice cream, ending the meal on a high note. The wine selection is solid and reasonably priced, making it a pleasant place to enjoy a relaxed meal without feeling rushed.

Overall, a dependable spot for classic French comfort food in a casual, welcoming setting.
author: Evon Tan

review_text: Went there in one of weekday, surprisingly pretty pack at peak hour; humble restaurant ran by a nice and cheerful chef. The food was so great, loved their French onion soup to the max! The braised duck was scrumptious, the gravy was so nicely done. Chocolate mousse was made of 75% dark chocolate and it’s light and less guilty when you have it.
author: C

review_text:
First time at this restaurant for me. I used to patronise Sebestien's years ago, as part of the Les Amis group.

I will say that the atmosphere was a good recreation of a french bistro. Service was attentive without being overbearing. :)

As for the food, we enjoyed every dish. The mussels were great: not too big in size and consequently very tender and sweet. The duck confit was great too. I have read that it is very salty. Well... I can't say I feel that way. Very much on par with other duck confit I have had in french places. ;) Of course, YMMV.

We loved the cheese platter! and the chocolate mousse too!

All in all, we enjoyed the lovely meal. and the tables are not as close as some reviews suggest...
author: Kiat Lee

review_text: Had lunch for two at this excellent French restaurant near Orchard and it was a real highlight. We went for the lunch set, which is fantastic value and highly recommended. Everything was spot on—from the rich onion soup to the perfectly cooked pork chop, finishing with a classic crème brûlée. Consistently excellent throughout. Would definitely return, especially for the lunch set.
author: Barney

review_text: Excellent food and service by the team here, they are efficient and very attentive to guests needs. Visited BDV after a few years and the food still tastes fantastic, probably even better than we can remember. We had duck confit and mussels and soup. All of which were delicious, the mussels were surprisingly sweet and delightful. The desserts - soufflé and Crepe suzette were very nice too, all of us loved it. The grand marnier soufflé was very delicious! You can feel that care and thought were put into ensuring the food is of highest standards. One side note is that the potatoes with the duck was a little on the dry side, I wish it can be creamier. Overall we had a wonderful time and will definitely visit again soon!
author: YY Lee

restaurant_name: Taste Paradise 味之楼 at Ion Orchard
review_text:
Lunch with visitors to Sgp. Chose Taste Paradise as location is central. However, at times it is difficult to make booking for lunch.
Food wise, dim sum is very good and selection is wide. Enjoyed the Chai Tow kueh-Radish cake that’s fried with bean sprouts and eggs, very delish. Most delicious and wholesome is the Fishmaw soup served in heated stone bowl and a long twisted ‘cigar’ made from frying popiah skin. My family thoroughly enjoyed this. Making it a must order dish whenever we patronised.  Service wise, we were pampered by staff Hui Chie and Siew Ying who had given us most attentive service, checking on us that all is well and what can be done to help us? Keep up the good work!
Just  a comment on need to create a better restaurant ambience.
author: Fe Chf

restaurant_name: Taste Paradise 味之楼 at Ion Orchard
review_text:
My favorite restaurant in Paradise Group: Wanted to order the signature shark fin soup but friends no longer eat shark fin so we chose the fish maw soup instead. Though menu said the soup is for 1 pax, I think it’s good for 2-3 pax to share. We ordered 2 fish maw soup, 1 clear and 1 thick, the fish maw was soft, no oil smell/taste.

This is a treat for a birthday girl but I guess she might afraid we spent too much, so she ordered the sweet n sour pork instead the chef recommended pork cubes dish.

I think we can have better chef recommended dishes than these but they are equally good.
we love the fried carrot cake, it has the work hey and XO sauce taste.
author: JJ T

restaurant_name: Taste Paradise 味之楼 at Ion Orchard
review_text: Intro by friend, pop by to try the dim sum. Freshly made dim sum is of good quality ingredient and serve piping hot as it should be. Had ordered half of Peking duck which was crispy n juicy. Definitely a place to try out if you feel rich. Food quality A+ quantity A Service A+ RTE 4/5
author: Ed K

restaurant_name: Taste Paradise 味之楼 at Ion Orchard
review_text:
4.5/5 The taste and quality of the dim sum here is definitely a notch up compared to the dim sum offerings in their more casual restaurants like Canton Paradise or even Paradise Seafood. Most of the dim sum were well made, with the different prawn dim sums generously filled. The seafood porridge had ample ingredients, silky and delicious. The scallop cheong fun is smooth and flavorful, while the Cantonese roast platter is commendable, with the roast duck being the highlight among the three meats.

However, the cheong fun with crispy netting and shrimp was less appealing due to the inclusion of a vegetable I found unpalatable, likely celtuce or a type of bean. An enjoyable dim sum meal at taste Paradise located inside Ion Orchard.
author: Julius Tan

restaurant_name: Taste Paradise 味之楼 at Ion Orchard
review_text: A solid dim sum spot with prices that are reasonable for the location, quality, and service provided. Food is nice overall, and it’s a good place to come with a bigger group so you can try more varieties. The XO carrot cake portion is quite generous. Remember to make reservations during peak hours
author: RACHEL NG

review_text:
The food here delivered by Chef Jake Lee & Team is at an exceptional level, worthy of 2 Michelin stars at least and looked visually stunning in photos too! There was a lot of finesse and passion that you could see on display from the team at the open kitchen. Came here for the first time for a Valentine’s Day celebration with my wife and we were delighted by every course with spot on flavor balance and perfect interplay of textures. Some misses that marred an otherwise outstanding meal:

1) Table assignment which was confirmed 15 days ago was not fulfilled and I had to show my WhatsApp conversation with the team to reconfirm, was initially seated just beside kitchen.

2) There was no table crumbing service and I had to request for it after a few courses were served and the table was untidy. Last photo as example. This is a basic professional service standard let alone at a Michelin establishment.

3) I was presented final bill for payment and since I was asked to pay a deposit beforehand to reserve table, I wanted to confirm deposit was going to be deducted from the full amount since there was no record of deposit on the bill but both staff who handled my bill told me the full amount was correct and they had no idea about the deposit and I had to show them my PayNow (see last screenshot) and WhatsApp message as confirmation that I paid the deposit. This process is unusual. I was told later by another staff to trust the process as they would’ve deducted the deposit when I made payment. Most places would give you a final amount less deposit before they proceed with payment.

Clearly the kitchen & menu is managed at the highest level as for the rest of the operations there is hope that one day they can reach for the 2nd star. I wish them all the best.
author: Adrian Yeo

review_text:
Really cosy and smooth experience. Food was delicious and I loved the cold inaniwa dish with the amazing wine-like tomato.

I don’t take alcohol so wished they had a more extensive drinks menu to cater to that.

Special mention to the hot and crispy ginger madeleines that made the menu feel more festive. The other table also gave their compliments to the chef for it.
author: First Virtue

review_text:
Food 8/10
Service 11/10

Had a fine meal at Iggy's.  Had some stumbles at the start but finished strong

The snacks/amuse bouche looked exciting but was a major letdown.

Bafun uni on yam. The uni looked so fresh but was immediately was overpowered by the yam. The combination did not work at all. What a waste! I should have eaten the uni separately.

The tuna tartare on hash brown was so so. The hash brown was very oily.

The last was a cold pumpkin soup with tofu. That was excellent.

Inaniwa udon that followed was  good - smooth , silky enhanced by the tomato consomme. Very fresh and light dish.  But It came with shreds of snow crab which was dry and hard causing disharmony to the overall taste.

Carabino salad was good in its parts but didn't come together. Felt like one piece of prawn with a greens on the side.

Things got better from here,
The foie gras was buttery and smooth

The cappelini was a beautiful fusion of japanese umami and italian finesse. Loved every bite

The tennen buri was gorgeous.  The applewood gave it a smokey richness that complemented the buttery and fresh sweetness of the fish

The tenderloin was good but nothing exceptional. A good piece of meat cooked right.

Dessert was good and so was the madelines. I always remember them having a great pastry chef

Service was spectacular. I walked in without prior reservation and requested some mix and match to the menu and they did their best to accommodate with a smile.  Service was attentive. Kudos to the team!
author: Kwong Chee Choo

review_text: Amazing experience start to finish. Service was impeccable and completely unintrusive - it never felt like they were anxiously hovering around, yet they're immediately there when you need them. Perfect. Food was also top notch - one of the few Michelin places that I actually felt was deserving of its star and status. Not a single bad dish on the lunch tasting menu. The fish was a revelation - exactly what a good fish steak should taste like. Full of natural flavour. Best thing was that the staff also wasn't pushy about beverages - a true testament to good hospitality. Will definitely return.
author: the5thcellar

review_text: I had lunch at Iggy’s recently. It felt like seeing a good friend I hadn’t met in a long time. Not much has changed in terms of aesthetics but that is more than made up for on the plate. Iggy’s menu consists of familiar fare, dishes which are simultaneously delicious and comforting. It doesn’t try to be overly uncomplicated but it is no less delectable. Each dish is a testament to the freshness and quality of the ingredients, the skills and techniques of the chefs and their ability to showcase this without the eye watering price that sometimes accompany these kinds of meals. Speaking of accompaniment, the Pouilly fumé and Savigny-les-Beaune by the glass make for a wonderful pairing!
author: hernie m

review_text:
I’ve lived in Vegas for many years, I have seen great buffets and I have seen not so great buffets. I can honestly say this is probably the best buffet I have ever eaten in my life.

Yes, it’s expensive. But there are definitely high-end items on this buffet that you don’t get other places. There is a huge variety of everything from Boston lobster to snow crab legs. There is sushi and cold cuts. There are Asian dishes that I’m not sure what they are, but tasted good.  Of course, great desserts. Basically, everything in the world.

One thing I loves - they don’t try the trap of lots of filling, but empty foods like starches and breads. There is a large variety of quality protein.

The service was excellent. They keep your table clean and your water full.

I slightly down grade the atmosphere because, regardless of the quality, variety and quantity of the food it’s still a buffet. So, it’s bright, crowded, busy and loud.

Don’t come here often or you will have to get a new wardrobe with much bigger clothes.

Enjoy!!!!
author: John - Explore Asia with V&J

review_text:
The Line used to be one of the best buffet restaurants in the city, but alas, it has fallen from grace.

I went for their claypot specialities lunch buffet, which looked incredible as there were many live stations, with food all cooked in claypot, such as claypot rice, curry fish, XO fish soup etc. Most of the food was decent, but there were quite a few misses.

The tempura station was awful. I was lucky enough to take from a freshly fried batch, but the prawns were completely soggy.

The dessert spread looked amazing, but most of it tasted like cheap cakes that were mass produced (they probably were).

What was most annoying was that the restaurant doesn’t refill the food promptly. Check out my photo of the Indian station. I went back three times at intervals of 10-15 minutes to get the garlic naan, but there was none (pun intended). There was also no one at the station for me to ask.

Similarly, they ran out of nonya kueh at the dessert station very quickly, so I didn’t get to try any.

I also had a very unpleasant dining experience, but I shall not bring it up because it was handled by the restaurant manager, Jason. Notwithstanding that, this is no longer The Line that I remember it to be.
author: Chester Chua

review_text:
The food and experience was average. I believe The Line should be aiming for higher than that. We came for the festive dinner at 98++ pp and while the food was passable and some dishes more delicious than the rest, it didnt hold a candle to The Colony at the ritz. There were personal touches missing. At the colony, a staff member would bring you around the whole buffet spread to introduce each section. Here, you sit down, and they pour you water without offering other beverage options. The interior feels shabby too. I think it’s due for a renovation. The table we were sat at had blue scratches.
The carvings were really good! Props to the chef. Turkey drumstick was tender. Indian naan was great. Cold seafood was nothing to shout about. Crab legs should be served cracked.  Finger bowls only appeared upon request. Sushi was mostly tasty! Christmas aesthetics on point but the very appealing Christmas dessert selection didn’t taste as good as they looked. Churros and waffles were left out for a while. Hard and inedible.

Final bill came to $470 for 4 of us. I don’t see myself coming back.
author: Ruby Chan

review_text:
ig: @lifetogether97
———————————————
came by for a buffet dinner on a weekday and can we just say we were really impressed by the spread of the food 😍 food was actually AMAZING. quality was there, contrary to what some of the other commenters are saying. we absolutely demolished the sashimi live station and the seafood- especially the lobsters. there were just so many options to choose from but we made sure to save space for dessert, which options were endless too 😋
———————————————
p.s. get their iced milo!! it’s so good and tasted like milo van milo. also, only served upon request but they have really nice teh tarik too 🤤
author: lifetogether97

review_text:
Very impressive buffet spread 👍👍

We can request for fresh salmon belly sashimi 😋

Almost all the claypot specials were delicious.  The Indian station too.  Must try the laksa soup.

The desserts and ice cream section looks nice but taste just so so only.

Pretty crowded for a Friday evening.

There is a current promotion for weekday dinner @ $98 per pax one-for-one deal.  Very worthwhile.
author: Teck Chong Law

review_text:
I had the privilege of dining at Les Amis for lunch last October, and although this review comes a few months later, the experience remains vivid in my memory.
Holding three Michelin stars, Les Amis truly delivers an extraordinary level of refinement and consistency. From the moment I arrived, the service was polished yet warm — a seamless balance of professionalism and genuine hospitality. The team demonstrated deep knowledge, attentiveness, and grace throughout the entire lunch.
The cuisine was exceptional — precise, elegant, and beautifully composed. Every course reflected technical mastery while maintaining soul and clarity of flavor. It was a lunch that flowed effortlessly, each dish thoughtfully progressing to the next.
As a wine professional, I must highlight their wine program. Since 1994, Wine Spectator has recognized their wine list, and it is easy to understand why. The depth and breadth of the collection is remarkable — one of the most comprehensive and impressive in the region. The curation, maturity of vintages, and overall selection speak to serious dedication and passion.
Four months later, I can still say this was one of the best dining experiences I’ve had. A true benchmark for fine dining in Singapore.
Highly recommended.
author: Vikneswaran Koonnusagaran

review_text: Had a lovely dinner last night - my only complaint was that the main course of venison was a tad underwhelming in terms of size and flavour - but presentation and thoughtfulness in all the other dishes still left an overall positive experience. It’s the perfect place for an understated yet traditional french experience for special occasions or anytime you just want to treat yourself. Special thanks to Catherine for taking care of us!
author: C Crumbs

review_text:
Recently went to try out Les Amis in Singapore at a stopover. Food was on par as what a 3 star Michelin restaurant should be, but in between courses, we were served with a wide choice of viennoiseries, delicious yet full of carbs and in fact made us so full that it affects our appetites for the main and dessert. Service was superb and our serveuse Ms Catherine, was warm and welcoming. The whole Les Amis Team was very professional, all dishes were served at precise timing. At the end of our meal, my husband and I were both presented each with a warm orange butter cake wrapped in parchment sealed with the signature LA sticker to take back to our hotel for afternoon tea, a continuation of the Les Amis flavour. Perhaps our only complaint in this aspect would be the very rushed explanation of the dishes. We had the impression that this was a well rehearsed description that was put on repeat over and over which became robotic.
Ambience was elegant and quiet. Would be happy to visit again when we stop over Singapore.
author: Ali S

review_text:
Sometimes, Perfection doesn’t need to be over-the-top, pompous, or shockingly extraordinary. Sometimes, it is about lovingly crafting a meal using the experience of more than 30 years and the finest ingredients Mother Nature has to offer on this planet. Cooked cleanly and purely, every course incorporates balanced seasoning and more importantly, is thoughtfully served with authentic smiles. Ms. Catherine, Mr. Murugan, Chef and the Les Amis team created an experience for us that couldn’t be a better way to conclude the year of 2025, and to look forward to a happier, brighter one in 2026. Our heartfelt thanks to the Team for taking us on this journey of French culinary excellence that we will never forget.
⭐️⭐️⭐️
😌🇫🇷🇸🇬🍽️
author: 葉

review_text: This place is remarkable at so many levels. I am going there since 20 years now and quality of the service and food have never ever changed ! Most probably one of the highest standards in the world of haute gastronomy. After 2 years , all the staff recognised me from even the door step and calling me by my name  ! Just amazing! Well done guys ! Of course food is the the top of the top ! Well done and see you soon
author: Christophe Bourrie

review_text: Akashi is my go-to spot for a quick Japanese dinner. I’ve been coming here for over 20 years — from Tanglin Shopping Centre to Orchard Parade, and now Orchard Rendezvous. The food is consistently good, service attentive, and the atmosphere very comfortable. Pricing remains affordable for the quality. A dependable favourite I keep coming back to.
author: Clara Lee

review_text: Have been patronising Akashi since they were in the basement of Tanglin shopping centre. My family has never been disappointed and always have a great meal when we come. Definitely on the pricier side but it’s one of the very few Japanese restaurants that we bother to dine at in Singapore.
author: Esther Chiang

review_text: Great atmosphere, a taste of Japan with it's interior and food. There were lots of options to choose from. And each one was tasty. It is on a pricey side and best to make reservations. The location is a little out of the way from the mrt if you're traveling by this mode.
author: Annabella Lam (Annafanza)

review_text: Was a regular about 20 years ago when Melvin was running the place himself. Haven't been back for a while. The place now has an "atas" feel to it and I could see that the establishment still have many regulars who were enjoying their meals at the counter, having drinks and chats with the chefs. Food was good, though on the pricey side. But given the location, that's expected. The service crew was exemplary though - always on hand to attend to your needs. Amongst other orders, the service staff recommended the iwashi (in season) which was very good. Had my favourite grilled fugu as well.
author: Chee Leong Ang

review_text:
Didn’t really enjoy our meal there. People always say 一分钱一分货. But felt that the $72 wagyu beef that was highly raved about  seems very meh. Perhaps Aston one would be better. Slightly pricey for the whole me and thought for the money spent, we could have eaten sth else. The pilan tofu also looks super different from what was in the menu.

Sushi generally fresh. Wouldn’t complain much about that. Customer service wise yes good, cos they kept coming over to help us top up tea. Very prompt too. And nicely serve us with our birthday cake on a plate.

Overall, the atmosphere is nice. I enjoy the green tea the most. But may not return for another visit.
author: Eileen Neo (Sgsohotleh)

review_text:
The food is generally nice and on point. Peking duck is good but the second cooking style was ok only. The pro is that it was deboned. Dong po meat was good, melts in the mouth. But one piece is enough, so fatty!!

The service is superb. Attentive and friendly.
author: Jennifer Teo

review_text: It was an impromptu last minute decision to get dim sum lunch on Saturday 07032026 at St. Regis. It was my first time! We reached around 2pm so we did not get to try the weekend dim sum buffet. We like the food and the service! Thank you Ann and Bruce!! Hope to see you next time sooooon!
author: zelig official

review_text:
This Chinese restaurant has one of the best cuisines in town. The service is great, ambience is nice and friendly, and the food tastes really good.
Their peking duck is a must try.
The place is also very kids friendly and is suitable for a family dinner with kids.
Their corn soup was outstanding.
They salads are great too.
The panna cota  in coconut shell is amazing 👌🏽
author: Jamal Al Suwaidi

review_text: The food here has sparked so much joy… They may look a little less flashy or trendy as those newly branded dim sum places, but good food is good food man! You gotta trust aunties and uncles sometimes. Even the simple jelly desert is so refreshing and satisfying. Wish I’d be back soon with some friends so that I get to order more. 🤤
author: Candia Tang

review_text: Dining at Chinese restaurant Yan Ting on a cold rainy Chinese New Year’s Day culminated in an unforgettable culinary experience for me  . I  certainly did enjoy feasting in comfort and luxury amidst comfy armchairs and banquettes in an elegant ambience . With the fancy tableware set up , I found myself brimming with satisfaction having indulged  in a trio of irresistible robust flavours of the  hearty corn crab soup , pan fried crunchy radish cake ,exquisite roasted chicken , simmering spinach prawn ball broth and not forgetting the lusciously smooth yet texturally lively mango pudding with the tender sago pearls to finish off the meal . The Cantonese culinary art at Yan Ting is certainly one that titillates one’s tastebuds, treating one to an opulent spread of beautiful crafted Chinese cuisine abundant in flavour and finesse . Having said this ,the roast chicken is my perennial favourite as it deserves the accolades for my continued patronage of Yan Ting.
author: jia ling Guo

review_text:
We recently dined here for the lobster buffet and had a truly wonderful experience. The buffet spread was impressive, with a wide variety of dishes and sauces like Black Pepper, Kam Heong, and Percik. There was no shortage of lobsters, and the dishes were always replenished promptly. Plenty of drink options too. The Teh Tarik was especially good! The ambiance was pleasant, tidy, and the seating arrangement suited us perfectly.

A special mention to Lian Poh from the restaurant floor, who was exceptionally attentive and friendly. She always asked politely before clearing our table and even sang a birthday song for my wife, all by herself! Her sincerity and cheerful attitude really stood out.

Shasha, at the cashier, was also amazing. She patiently explained the ongoing promotions and was friendly and helpful throughout our payment process.

Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed our dinner and felt genuinely welcomed by the team. Great food, great service, and great people. Highly recommended!
author: Mohammad Azry

review_text: Very spacious layout. Even though a lot of people, the table space is good and not too near to another table. The food was fantastic and there were many choices to choose. The salmon were well cooked, the beef tender, the lobster in abundance. Even the pengat durian were very delicious. A number of cold and hot drinks available. Lots of desserts and fruits available. Sushi was very fast snapped up. Server were very attentive and friendly. There's prayer room for muslim people located on 4th floor. It was very clean and spacious. Will go again next time.
author: Noorzidah M N

review_text: We had reunion dinner here on Chinese new year eve. Place seems small because most tables are full. Wheelchair friendly. Food is good except for dessert. Service is friendly.
author: Alicia Hock

review_text: The food quality, customer service and atmosphere is good. Halal certified. Most dishes were flavourful and perfectly spiced. The staff were attentive and friendly, making the overall experience very pleasant. The location is easily accessible. Exit 1 from Orchard Boulevard. Sheltered and very short walking distance within a few minutes. The ambiance is cozy and inviting, perfect for a casual meal or a special occasion. A must-visit spot!
author: Jimmy G

review_text:
Serena Chow provides great and friendly service. She understands what customers need and helps very enthusiastically!
The food is delicious and clean.
It’s a place with an excellent atmosphere.
I will definitely come back next time.
author: Tammi

review_text:
Attended a wedding at Basilico in Conrad Singapore, and everything about the experience was excellent. The venue itself is elegant and spacious, setting a great tone for a special occasion

The food spread was a real highlight — an impressively wide selection that catered to different tastes, from fresh seafood and cheeses to well-prepared meats and desserts. Quality was consistently high across the board, and everything was well presented
author: Loki

review_text: The food quality was good and the selection was fantastic. The cheese room was truly awesome with the selection, i have never seen so many cheese in a buffet before! The salad section was great! As it was Xmas season, they had Xmas desserts like panettone, logcake and stollen! The cakes were good and so were the mini cups. It was truly a fantastic buffet meal. I would highly recommend this place for family and friends gathering!
author: Jane Lim

review_text:
Basilico at Cascade Road completely exceeded my expectations! The buffet spread was absolutely insane, easily one of the most impressive Italian buffets I’ve experienced in Singapore. Every corner of the restaurant seemed to offer something special, from the beautifully presented antipasti to the fresh seafood, pasta, and roasted meats.

The cheese platter deserves a special mention, a true highlight! The variety and quality were top-notch, featuring everything from soft and creamy burrata to aged Italian cheeses that paired perfectly with the homemade bread and honey. You can really tell that attention to detail and authenticity are key here.

The dessert section was another delight. I especially loved the sorbet, light, refreshing, and bursting with real fruit flavor. It was the perfect way to end such a rich and indulgent meal.

Service was warm, attentive, and efficient, making the whole experience feel seamless and relaxed despite the busy crowd.

If you’re looking for a buffet that’s not just about quantity but true Italian quality and flair, Basilico is definitely worth the splurge. I’ll be back again next time with an even bigger appetite!
author: Yvonne Chou

review_text:
Basilico is a well-known buffet restaurant in Singapore, specialising in Italian cuisine and especially famous for its impressive cheese room. I visited for both breakfast and lunch, and the food was consistently excellent. The quality and variety really stand out, particularly when it comes to the cheeses—there are plenty of options available even during lunch, despite the cheese room itself not being in use at that time. During breakfast, the cheese room is instead transformed into a pastry section, which is equally delightful and offers a great start to the day.

The pasta and pizza are definite highlights, with everything tasting freshly made and full of flavour. Desserts and ice cream are also must-tries, and you’ll want to make sure to save some stomach space for them as they’re surprisingly good for a buffet spread. One small drawback during lunch is the limited selection of fruits, which felt a bit lacking—though this may simply reflect Italian dining culture rather than an oversight.

Overall, Basilico delivers a high-quality Italian buffet experience with standout cheeses, excellent mains, and satisfying desserts, making it well worth a visit for Italian food lovers.
author: Wesley Wong

review_text:
Brought the family out for a start of festive season buffet, buffet's go down well with them as they love the ability to choose and keep going back for more. Food was fresh and well prepared, it was an international buffet with a wide choice of food from seafood, to meats, pizzas, breads, cheeses, puddings all you could imagine. Staff were very efficient and friendly, keeping our table free from used plates and generally helping where needed. We chose not to have alcohol but for a supplement you can also have free flow alcohol.
Really good venue for buffet lovers.
author: Andrew P (Highlight Photography)

review_text: Very disappointing dining experience right from the start of making reservations. Had to prepay for Christmas Dinner, which was not an issue with me. The big problem was that after payment was made, instead of a confirmation email, received an email advising to disregard the previous email. Administrative glitch? Had to call Voco to straighten things out. Then came day of dinner, we ordered a bottle of red wine. Service staff was not confident and kept pouring much of the wine on the table. Then came the “Italian food”, which was pretty mediocre for an expensive Italian restaurant. Risotto was like eating porridge (see photo attached). The mains and dessert were just so-so, with nothing to shout about. Service Captain had to check if we had been served our various courses. There were barely 15 tables. Overall, I rather spend my money elsewhere, restaurants that have provided better service and better food.
author: Ern Lau

review_text: Everything was excellent—from the warm, friendly staff to the prompt service. The food was top-notch in both quality and presentation. We especially loved the generous shaved truffle slices, which complemented every dish we ordered beautifully. There were no issues at all when using the Eatigo promo. Will definitely visit again. Highly recommended.
author: sky tan

review_text:
Ordered the Burrata Campana, Tagliolini al nero di Seppia and Linguine al Granchio and they were visually appealing and tasted great. Nice balance of flavours.

The restaurant was empty on a Friday evening with just my table and 1 other from 5pm to 6+pm.

Service seemed very curt and cold. There was a poster at the entrance for some drink promos but when I asked about it, the staff said there was no promos.
It was only on the second time that I asked to confirm that they mentioned the promo is for dining outside.

To make things more confusing, there was a sign within the restaurant that said Jim Beam highballs were available for $10++. But that was never offered or mentioned when I asked about drinks offers.

I had just dined at Opus Bar and Grill at level 1 of the very same hotel where Il Cielo a week prior and the service was so different.

Upon being seated the staff informed us about the menu limitations of using the Eatigo app and would later ask how our meal was and if we had any other requests or feedback. They quickly cleared anything from the table that wasnt needed and when we were done with them.

Staff were warmer and so much more friendlier at Opus than at Il Cielo.

The stark contrast in service levels really stood out and it kinda killed the vibe.

I stayed on to have drinks at Opus but decided to go elsewhere for drinks after eating at Il Cielo
author: Uncle Chan

review_text:
It's a second visit. Decided to host my friend's birthday lunch there.
Started with a cold reception by the senior staff, that borders on being curt and dismissive.
Unfortunately it was too late to change venue.
The junior staff that took the orders were approachable and has room for improvement.
Food was tasty but served less than warm.
Decided to adjourned to Opus Bar for dessert instead.
Thankfully the food saved the day.
Should services improve and food serve warmer (as preferred) , might consider going back.
author: Jc Chong

review_text: Was there to celebrate a birthday. Service team was very lovely to extend a discount because am an ihg member too. They also gave us a birthday surprise. We ordered a mixture of pizza , meat and soft shell crab / prawn fritters appetiser. Was very disappointed with the pizzas and appetiser, felt that it was nothing special for the price paid as well. Taste was mediocre. Visually speaking, did not look the best too. Meat dishes (beef and pork ribs) were tender and good. Overall, for a dining experience at a hotel with the price value, it was a very underwhelming experience.
author: Janice Loh

review_text:
food is consistently very good and always delicious at din tai fung, but it’s pretty obvious the portions have shrunk quite a bit over the years.

tried the crispy duck fritters for the first time and loved it! just wished there was more filling though.

the chilli oil dumplings were delightful as always, and our favourite egg fried rice with pork chop was absolutely delicious as always! tried the prawn cake too, it was a bit of a let down and portion was very small.

service here is excellent and shoutout to the staff for being so attentive and prompt!
author: Marc Singh

review_text: Din Tai Fung at Paragon continues to impress every time I visit. The service team is consistently friendly, attentive, and efficient, even during the busiest lunch hours. Food arrives fast and always tastes fresh and well-prepared. The xiao long baos are delicate, juicy, and full of flavour, while the pork chop fried rice remains one of the best comfort dishes you can get in Orchard. The restaurant is clean, organised, and well-run, making the entire dining experience smooth and enjoyable. Easily one of the most reliable and satisfying places to dine at when shopping around Orchard Road.
author: The Travel Hunter

review_text: Went there on a Tuesday afternoon, no wait, I like this one better than the one across the street.  Scan the QR code and order, they charge pretty much everything, including hot or cold water, I ordered the hot tea with unlimited free refills.  I enjoyed the food, they still hold high standards and that is reflected with the pricing.  No restroom inside the restaurant, you have to use the mall restroom which is about 2 minutes walk,  after you finish with your food, take the little clipboard to the cashier and pay.
author: Ex miuwu

review_text:
Had a delightful (and slightly dangerous-for-the-waistline) Valentine’s celebration at Din Tai Fung — doing a strategic lunch-cum-early-dinner move to avoid both the lunch crowd and the romantic dinner chaos. Smart planning means more peace, less queue, and more time to focus on important matters… like dumplings.

⸻

We started with the Hot Jasmine Tea — smooth, fragrant, and classy enough to make you sit up straighter like you suddenly remembered your table manners. Free flow means you think you’ll sip politely, but somehow you end up drinking like you’ve just trekked across the Gobi Desert.

The cold dishes marched in like the opening act of a concert:

🥗 Oriental Salad in Special Vinegar Dressing
Super refreshing with a tangy kick that wakes up your taste buds faster than your morning alarm. Crunchy, zesty, and dangerously addictive — the kind where you say “just one more bite” about 27 times.

🥚 Century Eggs with Diced Ginger
Creamy, rich, and paired beautifully with the ginger that cuts through the intensity like a well-timed joke. If you’re a century egg fan, this one hits the comfort-food sweet spot.

🍗 Original Shanghainese Drunken Chicken
Tender, chilled chicken soaked in aromatic wine goodness. Fragrant, silky, and elegant — basically the chicken version of someone who speaks softly but commands attention.

⸻

Then came the flavour bombs:

🥟 Oriental Wantons with Black Vinegar & Chilli Oil (Dry)
These wantons don’t just walk onto the table — they strut. The black vinegar gives a sharp tang while the chilli oil adds a cheeky kick. Each bite is like a small party happening in your mouth.

🍲 Special Braised Beef Soup
Deep, hearty, and comforting — like a warm hug from your favourite relative who also insists you eat more. The beef is tender and flavourful, and the soup has that slow-braised richness that feels like it simmered with patience and love.

⸻

Now… the stars of the show 🌟

🥟 Steamed Pork Xiao Long Bao
Classic, delicate, and executed with surgical precision. The skin is thin, the soup inside is rich and savoury, and the whole experience requires careful handling unless you enjoy soup explosions on your shirt (Valentine’s Day outfit protection is very important).

🦀🥟 Steamed Crab Meat & Pork Xiao Long Bao
A luxurious upgrade. The crab adds a natural sweetness that blends beautifully with the pork. It tastes like the regular XLB decided to dress up for Valentine’s Day.

⸻

And finally, the crunchy showstopper:

🐟 Fried Salmon Skin
Crispy, light, and ridiculously snackable. Once you start, you’ll keep reaching out “just one last piece” until suddenly… plate empty. Perfect salty crunch to round off the meal.

⸻

Overall verdict:
A fantastic Valentine’s meal — peaceful timing, great company, and a well-orchestrated spread balancing refreshing starters, comforting soups, legendary dumplings, and sinful crispy snacks. Love was definitely in the air… and possibly inside the Xiao Long Bao too.

Would absolutely return again… maybe next Valentine’s, maybe next week. 😄
author: Mark Lim

review_text: The Din Tai Fung chain in Australia has become over-franchised and lost its quality so it was a relief to have a delectable dinner in Singapore like last night. Super friendly service and the waitress Kelly was amazing. The food was fresh, hot and so tasty!
author: David Maddison

review_text:
I was in Orchard Road and thinking what lunch could I have with a budget of $20/-. It was a Sunday and Ding Tai Fung Wisma Atria wasn’t too crowded. I decided to dine there as I didn’t have to wait.

The service staff asked if I would prefer order online or pen & paper (hard copy). I was quite charmed by their thoughtfulness.

I had a good & satisfying lunch under $20/-!

Guess what I ordered..photos tell it all😊

I enjoyed my lunch👍
author: l k

review_text:
Lunch at Din Tai Fung — Day 3 in Singapore

It’s the third day of my mother-in-law and niece’s visit to Singapore. My husband and I are residents here, and we’ve always wanted to bring them to Din Tai Fung, one of our favourite places for comforting and reliable food.

We ordered Xiao Long Bao and century egg, and for my mother-in-law — who’s very selective with food — she decided to try the dry noodles with pork cutlet, since there wasn’t much else on the menu she thought she’d like. We asked to remove the pepper because she can’t handle spicy food.

To our surprise, the meal turned out to be another wonderful success! Despite being extremely picky, my mother-in-law finished all her noodles and even said that if she had more, she would’ve finished the pork cutlet too! She also tried the century egg — which, as we know, not everyone dares to try — and actually liked it more than we expected.

The Xiao Long Bao was as delicious as ever — perfectly juicy and flavorful. It was so good that we ordered another basket! My husband doesn’t usually eat much, so my niece and I ended up sharing and finishing both sets. I also had fun teaching her how to eat them properly — poke it first, sip the broth, then eat it. My husband, of course, told her to just eat it whole 😅. She tried it his way once but quickly switched to mine — and she loved it! It was adorable watching her carefully poke the dumpling, sip the hot broth, and enjoy every bite with a little chili on the side.

When we were paying, the cashier/server asked how our experience was, and I shared how impressed we were — especially since my mother-in-law enjoyed everything so much. The prices were also very reasonable, which made the experience even better.

We ended our meal with the Christmas chocolate bun, which they described as an “Asian lava cake.” My niece and mother-in-law, both being European and quite particular about chocolate, absolutely loved it — rich, gooey, and perfectly sweet.

By the end of lunch, my mother-in-law said she wanted to come back again just to eat the noodles — and for us, it will always be for the Xiao Long Bao.

Thank you, Din Tai Fung, for another heartwarming and delicious experience! ❤️
author: Leicht 2017

review_text:
I love this restaurant chain!
I visit every time I see one & they never disappoint!
The variety & quality of their food is wonderful!
author: Beatriz Cóbreces

review_text: Ordered a number of items such as Dan Dan main, sweet and sour pork, black sesame buns, hot and sour soup, spicy dumplings, fried rice, diced mushroom noodles and limited edition noodles with scallion. Notable mentions are the usual hot and sour soup, and sweet and sour pork and noodles with scallion.
author: Bosch Xie

review_text:
Had early dinner here (around 4+). It's pretty quiet with lots of seats.

There were  3 of us of which one does not eat pork.
The server highlighted there's limited items served without pork, but was able to make recommendations, including the noodle cooked in a vegetarian way. It smelt good though looked plain, and it went very well with its chilli sauce 👍

Had two other typical highlights of the restaurant - happy dining :)
author: Loh Kwai Yin

review_text:
We walked in without reservation on a Friday evening.

The place was half filled. Service was good and basically attentive. Some tables were slightly too close though, and you could hear other's conversations.

Numerous birthday celebrations held there, so they gave free cakes and you get to hear many rounds of birthday songs being sung.

Food was scrumptious, the steak was good of course. Will not recommend the salmon though. Can definitely get better ones elsewhere. Salad was interesting. A little pricey.
author: Angie Chng

review_text:
Wonderful place for all your prime meat needs. Decided to dine on a well done ribeye steak and this place lived up to my happiness and provided me with a sense of satisfaction and completeness. Was not starving in case this would place a bias to my review. The staff were attentive, went above board with a bit of a twirl and dance to the rhythmic motion of mixing my salad, and served my food within an admirable time of less than 15-20 minutes of waiting.

I was sat next to a view of orchard road, their window view, and that made it all the more pleasant since I did not make reservations.
author: Symeon Chiam

review_text: The roast beef today  was very tender and cooked to perfection. We ordered the English cut. Together with with the spinning salad and Yorkshire pudding, we barely finished the food. Remember to sprinkle the special Lawry's seasoned salt and pepper which made the beef super savoury. We will definitely return again.
author: Choong Leong Tan

review_text:
Finally tried Lawry's after many years of waiting! Had the weekend brunch set for an occasion and it was quite value for money.

Started with the salad which was a spectacle on its own. Salad was lovely!

After that was the soup, which was accompanied by bread (suspect the butter was house butter).

Opted for the prime rib (came in 120g) along with accoutrement (yorkshire pudding, mashed potatoes and creamed spinach). Partner ordered the steak and egg (180g). Both were good!

The set came with a spritz (alcohol and non alcoholic option) and cake.

Since we were celebrating, the restaurant also gave us a free cake and we just couldn't finish 3 cakes to ourselves.

Came at 12 so it was quieter on a weekend, got more crowded at 1.30pm.
author: Natasha Tjahjadi

review_text:
Came here to celebrate my birthday bc they have a good promotion for birthdays, i saw on thesmartlocal.

For Couples / Party of Two*

Order 1 Main Course and enjoy 50% off 2nd Main Course
Complimentary Birthday Dessert
Instant Photo Print

We got an English cut, Ribeye, Mac and Cheese and 2 mocktails for $283.56.

Pros: english cut is very tender. I love the yorkshire pudding. I love the special seasoned salt. The chef cut the beef into 2 for us despite how it traditionally is cut into 3.

Cons: the 200g english cut is alot. In fact, my sister couldn’t even finish 100g. The strawberry slush taste v bad, sour and melt v fast all over the table :(
author: Ember Shen

review_text:
Atmosphere is great. Service is great.

I came for the dimsum but it is surprisingly disappointing especially for its price.
Siewmai is not fantastic.
Porridge is just ok only.
Chicken feet is having a spicy aftertaste.
Carrot cake is normal.
I won’t come back for dimsum again.
Thanks for the experience.
author: Hanshi.Nancy Wu

review_text: First time here and I enjoyed it alot. Lohei was nice, wagyu beef was succulent, 3-colour nian gao dessert was yummy too. Service is prompt and atmosphere was conducive for a good chat with the business partners.
author: Jan

review_text:
Shang Palace at Shangri-La Singapore delivers a consistently elegant dining experience that reflects the brand’s timeless commitment to excellence. The atmosphere is refined and serene, setting the perfect stage for a relaxed yet sophisticated meal.

The service is attentive and polished, with the team demonstrating a quiet confidence and genuine care that makes every visit feel special. The food quality is equally impressive thoughtfully prepared, beautifully presented, and rich in flavour.

What truly stands out is the restaurant’s ability to maintain exceptional service standards and culinary quality over time. A place of reliability, grace, and refinement, one I would definitely return to again and again.
author: S LeBlanc

review_text:
We got a variety of dishes and not all were great, and many lacked oomph to separate this Cantonese restaurant from cheaper alternatives.

The dim sum was definitely the best food had there. I particularly enjoyed the truffle mushroom dumpling; the truffle was not overwhelming and there were a variety of textures. The softness of the mushroom, the crunch of the watercress, and the chewiness of the dumpling. However, I believe that it could have used more pickled olives to provide more complexity to the dish.

Many dishes were like this - they were definitely refined and skilled but weren’t daring enough to explore beyond the common taste palette.
author: Caden Tan

review_text: My friends invited me to a vegetarian lunch here at Shang Palace and we had an early Loh Hei too !! The vegetarian lunch here is so delicious that one of my friend wishes she could have this everyday !!! Not only the food is good but the environment is also suitable for lovely long conversations as well. Their service is always polite and pleasurable. We had an enjoyable lunch here today !! 👍👍👍💗💗💗
author: Lynn Yap

restaurant_name: 潮州发记 Teochew Restaurant Huat Kee
review_text: first course yusheng was already a disappointment. frozen salmon stuck together (round circular things in the photo). even a fork couldn't separate them cleanly. waitress said "it's like that". instead of getting more pekchek with the to-and-froing, our host decided to send the yusheng back without touching the salmon. no attempt at service recovery to comp or give a discount on the dish. the rest of the dishes were so-so. not particularly cheap either for the quality.
author: J. Kew

restaurant_name: 潮州发记 Teochew Restaurant Huat Kee
review_text:
Advance booked 3 tables for a birthday dinner that turns out to be the worst restaurant taste. I wonder if the boss or the chef taste himself if he accepts this standard of food. Started with longevity bun that dough was still hard, obvious that these frozen stuffs were steam with a time too short. Next the cold platter that was served together with the braised duck dish at the same time. I think chef is rushing home! The ngo hiang on the platter is slice thin and fried till hard n dry, it is also extremely saltish that make me wonder if this is a teochew restaurant. Mini popiah, fied oyster taste worst than a hawker ngo hiang bee hoon stall though most of them came from factory. Another worth the mention is the prawn with white chives. Chives is obvious older than me that I had a hard time chewing. The oyster omelette (orh lua) is hard that is obviously fry with strong fire and lousy blend of tapioca starch. By then none of us are looking forward to the dishes served but to mingle around.
Nevertheless, only the crab meat fish maw soup and steam fish is acceptable that accompanied by the waitress good service throughout the dinner. I think being a chef or a restaurant owner there has to be a certain level of pride and etiquette to serve tasty food to the table. If the chef eat such standard of food he shouldn’t be one and if he does, he should not operate f&b biz.
author: Don Lim

restaurant_name: 潮州发记 Teochew Restaurant Huat Kee
review_text:
The servers serving us are very friendly. That is why I give 5 star for servicing. The food is way too low standard given the high price. The seating is like we are sitting in the corridor, it feels really bad. And on Sunday afternoon, I can hear clearly some church group singing in a rented room. This is exacerbated by the fact that we are seated along a corridor. I ordered the set menu that cost me 600 plus for 6 person,  but the food quality is just bad, and I even suspect some of the things are not fresh.
Eventually after adding all the tax, it cost around 900 SGD
author: gfishball

restaurant_name: 潮州发记 Teochew Restaurant Huat Kee
review_text: Very bad food, we order Loh Hei, they gave us a plate of frozen salmon. When we inform them of it, the reply was oh it’s like that we take it out for u … I told them better u take it back. Waitress told the boss and came back with two forks trying to pry the salmon apart.  Other food was mediocre, not worth a $600’lunch.
author: Khim Tay

restaurant_name: 潮州发记 Teochew Restaurant Huat Kee
review_text:
May 2025: We ordered several dishes, and the total bill came up to ~$980.

The best dish that we had was the double boiled chicken soup with shark's fin. The soup has a rich texture with deep flavours because of the high-quality chicken stock. Shark's fin has a crunchy bite, but otherwise, it is bland in taste.

We also like the candy heart abalone with sea cucumber (must have).  The sauce has a delicate,  caramelised flavour. Both abalone and the sea cucumber were tender in texture.

The next highlight for me was the promfret fish (must have). It was fresh and full of flesh. The thinly sliced salted vegetables and tomatoes gave it a tangy taste. I highly recommend this dish.

The fried oyster omelette was delicious,  not oily compared to hawker centre version. The braised duck tasted ordinary, and I can find better versions from the hawker centres.

The stewed Chinese mustard in claypot was delicious, too. The signature stir-fried kueh tiao was average in taste.

We ordered 2 different kinds of dessert: ching ting and yam paste with pumpkin and gingko biloba.  The yam taste is very delicious.
author: Justin Tan

review_text: This was our first time dining at Chatterbox to celebrate a special occasion, and we’d love to come back again to try other dishes with our family and friends. The rojak, heritage set meal and premium set meal pictured here were a delectable treat and we thoroughly enjoyed their variety of flavours. The service crew’s attention to our needs was impeccable. I appreciate Xuan’s care shown to us since setting up our table. She ensured that our food arrived on time, our glasses never ran empty, and thoughtfully replaced our cutlery so we could enjoy each new dish with refreshed palates. Thank you!
author: Kelvin Su

review_text:
My family and I visited Chatterbox for a late lunch, and it was exactly what we needed after returning from our Hong Kong vacation. We were craving local favourites such as steamed chicken rice, satay chicken, curry chicken, and Seafood Hokkien Mee and Chatterbox did not disappoint.

From the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by the service crew. In particular, Manager Karen truly impressed us. She noticed that the table reserved for us felt a little tight and immediately offered to move us to a larger, more comfortable table. Her attentiveness and thoughtfulness made us feel very well taken care of.

The food was, as always, delicious and consistent in its high quality and standard. Every dish was satisfying and perfectly hit the spot for our cravings. Just as I was about to settle the bill, Manager Karen surprised me by presenting a specially prepared birthday dessert. This complimentary and heartwarming gesture truly made my day. 🙆🏻‍♀️

A big thank you to Chatterbox for the wonderful meal and excellent hospitality. Special thanks and a heartfelt shout-out to Manager Karen for her outstanding service and dedication. We will definitely be back again! ♥️
author: Xiao Ting

review_text:
We had a family gathering and birthday celebration at Chatterbox, and the experience was excellent from start to finish.

The food was consistently very good — we especially enjoyed the rojak, satay, laksa, chilli prawns, and beef hor fun. Everything was flavourful and well executed, and the dishes were perfect for sharing.

Service was also a standout. One of the waiters, Leslie, was particularly impressive — he gave thoughtful food recommendations, was very attentive to details throughout the meal, and maintained a warm, positive attitude that really enhanced the experience. He made our celebration feel special without being intrusive.

Overall, a wonderful dining experience with great food and genuinely good service.
author: Vivian Tay

review_text: After a local recommended this place, we made a reservation (reservations highly recommended). It was a little disappointing. The famous chicken rice wasn't as good as we anticipated because the flavor of the sauces weren't that strong. The other dishes we had were good but not amazing. The best thing we got was actually the coconut shake. Service was friendly, but prices were high. The restaurant is beautiful, but I probably won't come back.
author: Nancy

review_text: Overall the food is okie (Assam Barrumundi and Lobster Laksa is nice) but the chicken rice set is a bit disappointing. Chicken is not as tender as expected. Atmosphere is typical restaurant vibes. Staffs are friendly and approachable, but at times they will get abit overload when the crowds are there. Please make a reservation before going down.
author: Alvin Teo

review_text: Love this restaurant and conveniently located just in front of escalator leading up to Level 2 from the street.  Serve contemporary menu. Ideal place to have a coffee, light bites or full meal. Ambience good for gathering or to chill. They occupied various shoplots across a corridor. Have outdoor seating (partially sheltered) as well.
author: EveC

review_text:
I recently stopped by this charming brunch and bistro spot, and it immediately stood out for its welcoming atmosphere. The space feels bright and cozy — the kind of place where you could linger over a meal with friends or simply enjoy a quiet moment to yourself. The service was attentive without being rushed, which added to the relaxed vibe.

Their menu offers a thoughtful variety, from fresh-baked pastries and hearty brunch plates to lighter options for those just looking for a quick bite. I picked up a croissant, a warm chai, and a loaf of sourdough bread to go, and everything was delicious — the croissant was buttery and flaky, the chai had the perfect balance of spice and sweetness, and the sourdough was baked beautifully with that satisfying tang.

It’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back and explore more of the menu. A wonderful little gem for anyone who loves good food in a pleasant setting.
author: ELIZABETH DAO

review_text:
The cocktails here are pretty good overall, one of them was a bit overly sweet, but the weekday promo (2 for $20) is definitely a nice deal. The atmosphere is just okay, nothing too memorable.

Service could use improvement. It was a bit slow, and the staff felt quite neutral and not very warm. The waitress seemed a little lost and overall came across as cold and uninterested, which made the experience feel a bit less than great.

There’s potential, especially with the drink promos, but the service and vibe need some polishing.
author: Reina K

review_text: The foods are wonderful especially chicken with roasted chestnut and butter prawn with clam skillet , enjoy the atmosphere with friends and seating arrangement at the restaurant just nice for friend gathering. Service crew Eezy was helpful and friend, he also recommend us to try their beef ribs when visiting next time
author: Loh San

review_text:
I had a wonderful experience at this restaurant thanks to Miss Hailey’s outstanding service. From the moment we walked in, she greeted us warmly and made sure we felt welcome. Throughout the meal, she was attentive without being intrusive, checking in at just the right moments.

Miss Hailey was knowledgeable about the menu, gave great recommendations, and made sure any special requests were handled smoothly. Her friendly attitude and genuine care really elevated our dining experience.

Thank you, Miss Hailey, for making our visit so pleasant — we’ll definitely be back!❤️
author: Jamie Wong

review_text: We used to come every year in the 2010s for the Penang hawker buffet. Back then it had a wider selection of hawkers and definitely more people. When I came back around X’mas 2025  period, the crowd was less and I thought the food was still as good! Loved the dry kway teow with soup and char kway teow. Their nasi lemak was good too. Highly recommended!
author: Bryan CY Chua

review_text: First time trying it and I must say the food is legit good compared to other Penang theme buffet, here each dish is freshly prepared by a chef who specialised in that item and probably cooks the same dish back in msia. Staff are very polite and nice variety but they didn’t have wanton mee from Penang considering how much Singaporeans love their wanton mee as much as as ckt, I’m sure it would be a banger if they bring it in future. Hope they do!
author: Star Carter

review_text:
Penang Hawker fare buffet in a hotel,  white rose had been known for it's Penang food.. really good..

Many stations serving nasi lemak, Royal, Penang prawn noodles, assam laska, pan cake, Chendol,  Penang fried kway teow......

The food served when you ordered so the fried kway teow had a Que always, because it is really good.. I can say even better than the ones I had in Penang.

Food is top quality , chef had made it well no short cuts.

Price is worth, hawker food in a very comfortable setting.

Will be back again.
author: joe fong

review_text: Annual pilgrimage to York hotel Penang hawker fare, served by friendly host & yummy Penang dishes. Praise White rose maintains its hawker standard.
author: H Ngim

review_text:
Came for the Penang Hawkers' Fare.

From the tangy, spicy goodness of Penang Laksa to the savory delight of Oyster Omelette and Penang Prawn Mee, every dish is made à la minute. But that’s not all—watch in awe as hawkers work their magic before your very eyes. Marvel at the sizzling sounds and aromatic clouds of steam as they fry up Char Kway Teow, whip up crispy Roti Canai, and assemble the perfect plate of Pasembur.

Lastly, a big shoutout to all the staffs at Penang Hawkers’ Fare! Despite the place being so crowded, their service was absolutely top-notch, making our dining experience even better. all the dishes we tried were fantastic especially the Char Kway Teow, Penang Rojak, Roti Canai, Pasembur, Oyster Omelette, Penang Laksa, and Cuttlefish Kang Kong. Truly enjoyed every bite!
author: Zozo

review_text:
Tried this branch recently, but won’t be returning.
Perhaps you can try their other goods and stuff like ice cream or other merchandise as a gift but it’s hard to dine in for the price with that quality.

•	Wine (own label) $48++
Sourish, off taste, and very limited variety. Not recommended.
•	Tiramisu (good for 2) $19++
Dry, lacking coffee flavour compared to before. Disappointing.
•	Truffle Fries  $18++
Acceptable taste, but portion far too small for the price.
•	Service, Okay, attentive and friendly enough

Overall: Steep prices, underwhelming quality. Will give this place a miss.
author: dian bearwith

review_text:
Came here for breakfast. It’s awesome! Grilled mushrooms and iced matcha latte are some of the best I’ve eaten. The mushrooms are really nice and flavorful and juicy/oily and the iced matcha latte was really thick with nice matcha and milk flavors. Sourdough bread and scrambled eggs are pretty nice. I didn’t like the sausages. I hated the salad.

I would recommend only coming here for breakfast, as their lunch food is pretty mediocre.
author: K S

review_text:
Absolutely the best pasta ever!
Da Paolo truly knows how to do pasta right. The flavors are rich, balanced, and clearly made with high-quality ingredients. The pasta was cooked perfectly, and the sauces tasted fresh and authentic, not heavy or overpowering. Portions were generous without feeling excessive, and everything came out hot and absolutely delicious.

The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, making it a great spot for both a casual meal and a special night out. On top of that, the service was friendly and attentive too!

If you’re a pasta lover, this place is an absolute must-visit. I’ll definitely be coming back to try more dishes!
author: Muhamad Shafiee Abdul Khalid

review_text:
Hidden Gem at Paragon B1 – Da Paolo is actually one of the oldest Italian restaurants in Singapore, with a 35-year history! Came here for brunch and completely fell in love with their croissants and coffee! 💘

🇸🇬 National Day Special – Coconut Gula Melaka Croissant 🥐 | 💰$7.90
✨ So flaky it crumbles! You can literally hear the crispy crackle when slicing it open!
✨ Toasted shredded coconut on top adds a golden crunch, and the buttery coconut aroma is irresistible – I already want a second one!

Almond Croissant 🥐 | 💰$5.50
✨ Topped with a rich, creamy crumble and crispy almond flakes – each bite is super satisfying!

Caffe Latte ☕ | 💰$6.90
Creamy and slightly sweet, comes with two mini cookies – so thoughtful and adorable!

Cappuccino ☕ | 💰$6.90
A must for coffee lovers! Rich crema, bold flavor, and a lingering finish.

🌟 What makes this place special
✅ Open all day from 8AM to 10PM – perfect for breakfast, brunch, or dinner
✅ Authentic Italian chefs in the kitchen, no canned or frozen ingredients – just real Italian flavor
✅ Besides brunch, they serve handmade pasta 🍝, pizza 🍕, tiramisu 🍰, gelato 🍨 – lots of variety!

🛍️ Don’t miss the retail section!
Right next to the restaurant is a lovely little corner selling imported Italian goodies – think chocolates 🍫, wine 🍷, pasta sauces, and more! Great for souvenirs or gifts!

If you’re shopping along Orchard Road, definitely swing by for a taste of authentic Italy 🇮🇹
author: Ivy Hu

review_text:
🎉 Salted Egg Lava Black Gold Croissant – Da Paolo’s National Day Special!

🖤 For all the salted egg lovers out there, this one’s pure fireworks!

The outer crust? A textbook-perfect French croissant – flaky, buttery, and golden. But the real magic is inside: a rich, flowing salted egg yolk lava that’s iconic to Singapore.

Savory, creamy, and oh-so-satisfying, it bursts with flavor in every bite without ever feeling too heavy. A true local twist on a French classic – indulgent yet refined. Don’t miss it this National Day!
author: Miaoji Miaoji

review_text: We had a great time at the afternoon tea session. The service and ambience were superb, staff were so smiley and friendly, making you feel so happy and welcomed too! The selection of teas are great, afternoon tea set includes 2 drinks, I suggest you skip the coffees and take the teas. The food were really good with a relatively good mix of savories and sweets. As I indicated that we are celebrating a birthday, they prepared a complimentary chocolate dessert for us! Such a nice gesture, makes us want to return for future special occasions!
author: Carmen Huang

review_text: Booked for 3pm weekend hi-tea and when we arrived at 2.55pm, we were told that the lounge opens at 3pm. They could have let us take our seats first and come to get our drink orders at 3pm. The lounge was comfortable and they offer an interesting range of tea.
author: Josephyne Ho

review_text: We love the peace and comfort here. Celebrated my friend's birthday and also celebrating year end together. The spread was great and quality! Buffet spread came with 2 drinks. Staffs were very prompt. We will be back!
author: Rebecca Tan

review_text:
Tea Lounge at Conrad Singapore has long been one of my dependable weekend high tea spots, so when they introduced a special Chinese New Year themed edition, I was naturally curious to see how the experience would be reimagined.

The Spread: Comforting Familiarity with Festive Twists

The generous variety that regulars appreciate remains intact. The selection is extensive without feeling overwhelming, striking a nice balance between savoury classics and playful creations.

Highlights That Stood Out
•	Seafood Congee : Easily one of the stars of the afternoon. The broth was deeply flavourful, infused with the natural sweetness of seafood, and generously topped with prawns and fish. Comforting yet refined.
•	Kurobuta Pork Char Siew : Not part of the free-flow selection, but worth every bite. Exceptionally juicy and tender, with beautifully caramelised edges that delivered a delicate crispness and smoky sweetness.
•	Quiche : Above average, featuring an impressively thin, crisp crust that avoided the heaviness many hotel versions suffer from.
•	Chicken Satay : Juicy, tender, and paired with a rich homemade peanut sauce that tasted freshly ground rather than mass-produced.

Creative Touches That Keep It Interesting

Both the sandwiches and desserts continue to be where this high tea differentiates itself from others.
•	The sandwiches showcased unexpected ingredient pairings that somehow worked harmoniously, offering pleasant surprises rather than gimmicks.
•	Desserts were particularly strong, more imaginative than those at many other hotels. The combinations of flavours and textures felt thoughtfully composed, often unconventional but consistently enjoyable.

A Small Miss
•	Singapore Laksa : Slightly underwhelming compared to the rest of the spread. The coconut milk ratio leaned too heavy, resulting in a broth that felt diluted and lacked the punchy depth one would expect.

Value for Money

At $82++ per person, it sits on the pricier end of the high tea spectrum. However, considering the quality of ingredients, execution, and the creativity shown across the menu, it still offers solid value—especially for those who appreciate a high tea that goes beyond the predictable.

Final Thoughts

This festive edition proves why I keep returning. The experience stays true to its strengths—variety, quality, and creativity—while introducing seasonal elements that make it feel refreshed rather than repetitive. It’s a reliable indulgence that still knows how to surprise.
author: forever.hungry

review_text:
food-wise, i feel that some of the savouries are quite salty. the scones was a bit hard, but the cempedak cream tasted good. the other sweet desserts taste good. per pax price inclusive of svc charge and gst is $74.40, do note that only 2 drinks included and not free flow selection.

service-wise, 6 of us had to squeeze at a coffee table, drink orders taken and served wrongly but quick to react and serve the correct drink. there were 4 service staff, but attention was not given to the customers, our teapots went empty for very long and no one came to refill hot water till we asked for it. also, the male waiter needs more training, couldn't understand our questions so we had to repeat, answers he gave sounded uncertain as well.

all in all, wouldn't come here again for high tea, their lobby lounge at conrad marina bay was a much better experience.
author: pattyhaha

review_text:
We celebrated my birthday and Valentines’ Day here because my husband has been talking about coming back to Shinji for years since he first ate here 4 years ago.

It did not disappoint. Each dish looked deceptively simple but you can taste and feel the care in everything that was presented. I wish I took a picture of that amazing looking tamago. (How was it so smooth with a uniform color???) The sushi rice was warm and slightly salted so you don’t eat it with shoyu. Even the seaweed was something different.

The staff makes sure to clean the table with every dish served and constantly changes the cups of tea to make sure it’s always hot.

I would recommend this place if you love sushi and sashimi and want to enjoy an elevated twist on what you already know and love.

Unless the price tag is a drop in the bucket for you, I would not recommend this place if you don’t care much about distinguishing the flavours of each type of fish. (Or, if you don’t eat seafood….)

The experience was only marred by a excessively obnoxious bunch of people next to us, which was unfortunate, but not something that the restaurant can control………

I’m not sure if I’ll be able to come back but it was an unforgettable dining experience. :)
author: R's Main

review_text:
Totally enjoyed an exceptional omakase at Shinji by Kanesaka, St. Regis. Every dish, from pristine nigiri to delicate chawanmushi, was a study in balance, texture, and seasonal finesse, presented with understated elegance.

The chefs worked with efficiency and mastery behind the hinoki counter, serving each piece of sushi immediately after it was made. This created a particularly memorable culinary experience, where the warmth of the rice, the freshness of the fish and the timing of the bite all come together in perfect harmony. Shinji absolutely deserves its Michelin star — this is Edomae sushi at its most refined!
author: Josephine W

review_text:
Amazing night and experience! Dishes were immaculate and best we have ever tried here in Singapore. Quality, service and the chefs made sure our anniversary dinner went perfect. Even surprised us when they dressed up.

Highly recommend. Worth every cent!
author: Ian Santos

review_text:
The food is so unbelievably bad that I have to give this review in the middle of my meal.
The service staff were so weird and kept looking over our food ( to see if we finished), cutting our conversation and served the next course even when my course was unfinished . Plus they told us at least twice shoyu is for the sushi . ( yes., that’s how intrusive they are).

But what’s really astonishing is the food. Have been to many omakase and even basic Japanese food to feel this isn’t even don don donki standards. Presentation was ugly , flavor was flat and the ingredients were so normal for a $480?! Meal . My Otoro had veins in it , another sashimi meal earlier also had veins . The place was noisy . If this is Michelin star, I suggest the judges maybe try eating sakae sushi first to recalibrate their taste palette.
author: Bellachic

review_text: Lovely, memorable experience at Shinji! Each dish was so beautifully presented and thoughtfully executed. The flavours of the dishes were both subtle and bold, I've never appreciated the varied flavours and textures of fish so much before!
author: gillian chan

review_text:
Celebrated sister birthday here and boy, the food was good!
Mushroom soup was slightly watery but taste was great!
Burrato was 5/5 and it was huge!
Both pasta was flavourful and ingredient tasted fresh!
Pizza was light and great too!
author: Ron Yip

review_text:
We visited CIBO Italian Restaurant for New Year’s Eve after a friend—who’s a regular here—highly recommended it. And wow, did it live up to the hype!

We ordered:

· Burrata (250g)
· Calamari Fritti
· Tiger Prawn Aglio Olio
· Vongole
· New Zealand Ribeye Steak (250g)
…along with a selection of their wines.

Everything was fresh, flavorful, and delicious. The steak was cooked perfectly to our requested medium-rare, and the burrata was creamy and delightful. The tiger prawns in the pasta were huge and so fresh!

What made the night even more special was the warm, family-run atmosphere. The whole family was helping out, and they were incredibly attentive—even refilling our ice water without us asking. All the staff made us feel so welcome!

We loved the celebratory ambience—they stayed open late for New Year’s Eve and counted down with us. The food was amazing, and the wine list offered a wide variety. As someone who often buys wine directly from suppliers, I was impressed by their reasonable markup and great selection. Tim, the owner’s son, gave us a fantastic recommendation too!

They also seem to have a BYO policy with one-for-one promotions—definitely check with them for current offers.

Highly recommended for fantastic food, wonderful service, and a genuine family hospitality vibe. We’ll be back!

(The price quoted below is without wine.)
author: OB1

review_text:
Awesome! Have been looking for a replacement for Valentino’s and I have tried around 10-15 Italian restaurants! This is it boys and girls!

The crab meat aglio olio was really nice, as was the bread starter with olive oil. The margherita pizza and tiramisu were pretty good too! I liked it more than d.o.c., fortuna, l’antica which were my previous favorites.

The waitstaff were very accommodating and let us sit inside even though they had reservations (although we had to vacate the table by a certain time). The food was served lightning fast (probably less than 5-10 minutes after we ordered). It was kind of crazy. We were in and out in less than an hour! Amazing!
author: K S

review_text: think we ordered the best 2 things on the menu... burrata was so huge literally every piece of pizza i had was fully covered in burrata HAHAHAHA so worth it. Pork and potato was so yummy too!! ended off the night with a lemon tiramisu and wow we will definitely be back here. Staff are really hospitable and service was great! 10/10
author: Germaine

review_text: We celebrate my husband's birthday here. Food and service were fantastic. Pasta cooked al dente, pizza with the right amount of toppings, a perfect steak, and an amazing limoncello to end. They paid attention to the details and were kind to us during our celebration.
author: Constanza Suarez

review_text:
Was recommended by friends - didn't know what to expect. Ordered tre porcellini pizza, papardelle con salsiccia e funghi pasta and fettucine ai frutti di mare.

The star was the tre porcellini pizza - was afraid that it'll be too cloying to have three types of pork but the pizza was fluffy, light and delicious.

The pappardelle meat sauce was so good! Highly recommend. Pappardelle could be better - it's sticking to one another, slightly overcooked.

The seafood salad was fresh and interesting, as it's not oil based - rather tomato base pasta. Not a favourite, just needed something lighter as the rest are meaty dishes.

The profiteroles really shone. Thank goodness sizing was okay, otherwise would be really too rich to finish. Cream based profiteroles covered with chocolate sauce. Yum.
author: Natasha Tjahjadi

review_text: Been here 2 times. Vongole was great. Pasta here is always al dente unlike some places with same price but overcooked. Calamari was ok but marinara sauce tasty. Apple crumble was good as well, ice cream was super smooth.
author: Amanda H

review_text:
Ordered Tortelli with Pumpkin and Butter Sage… looks so so sad. Like frozen pasta from the supermarket that was reheated. Pasta was overcooked, too hard.

Needless to say the quantity is………  for kids?
author: Aidan Li

review_text:
Everything was perfect !!!!!

Valentine's Specials - The Pizza Viola & Golden Fried Bread was absolutely delicious, good portion size & excellent service.

Home-made pasta - The pappardelle was fresh, the sauce was well-seasoned, and the portion was just right 😊
author: Checy Low

review_text:
Fantastic pizza’s and arguably the best carbonara I have had.
This place is a must if you’re a pizza lover. We only had one pasta dish but if the others are as good as the carbonara then you can’t go wrong.
