My only regret is not taking more pictures of the pizzas. No excuses either as we ate here and had takeout 3 times 😂.
author: masonhope

restaurant_name: Morsels Restaurant & Gastro Wine Bar | Morsels Private Dining
review_text:
We celebrated our dear friend’s birthday at Morsels and it was such a lovely experience from start to finish. The restaurant has a cosy, rustic charm — intimate without feeling cramped, and perfect for a relaxed celebration.

The canadian manila clams in lemongrass broth with laksa leaf oil and bread was an absolute standout. The broth was fragrant and layered with flavour, and that bread was perfect for soaking up every last drop. Another favourite was the fisherman iwashi maruboshi assam thick rice noodle — comforting, punchy, and beautifully balanced with that signature assam tang.

Special shoutout to moses, who was a star throughout the evening. Friendly, attentive, and genuinely helpful — he made the celebration feel even more special.

A warm, charming spot that’s perfect for meaningful gatherings. Would definitely be back.
author: Janice Ng

restaurant_name: Morsels Restaurant & Gastro Wine Bar | Morsels Private Dining
review_text:
Organised a corporate dinner at Morsels for 30 pax. Intimate and cozy location if you’re looking for place that isn’t too stuffy and overly formal. Worked with Moses who was a great contact point, and guests thoroughly enjoyed the line up of specially curated and on-theme dishes that were planned by chef Petrina, cooked up with care and meticulous detail from the kitchen staff. Definitely on the slightly higher end budget-wise (for food and drinks), but you get great quality.

Will look into for future events, and even coming in my personal capacity 😊
author: Charlene Goh

restaurant_name: Morsels Restaurant & Gastro Wine Bar | Morsels Private Dining
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

An amazing meal at Morsels — every dish was a creative explosion of flavor and technique! The Toriyama steak was exceptional: beautifully marbled, perfectly seared, and melt-in-your-mouth tender with a deep, umami richness that lingered.

The duck noodles were a comforting yet elevated delight, combining smoky duck, chewy noodles, and a broth so layered it felt like a warm hug in a bowl. The oysters were fresh and briny, dressed with just the right touch of acidity to lift their natural sweetness.

The steamer crab puffs were little clouds of joy — light, crisp, and packed with the sweetness of fresh crab, an absolute must-try.

And then, the showstopper — the Bak Chor Mee Carbonara. A genius creation that truly embodies what Morsels does best: bold, inventive fusion that still feels soulful and familiar. Creamy, umami-packed, and impossibly addictive — it’s the best of the best, a dish you’ll dream about long after the meal ends.

To finish, the Milo Tiramisu and Horlicks Tiramisu were nostalgic bliss — both desserts cleverly reimagined with local childhood flavors and a touch of indulgence. The Milo version was rich and malty, while the Horlicks one had a comforting, creamy depth that rounded off the meal beautifully.

With impeccable food, warm service, and inventive flair, Morsels continues to be one of the most exciting dining experiences in Singapore — every plate tells a story, and every bite leaves you wanting more.
author: Rodney Loh

restaurant_name: Morsels Restaurant & Gastro Wine Bar | Morsels Private Dining
review_text:
I had walked past this restaurant many times but with no big signage I’d never thought to give it a try. Luckily by chance I found an excuse to visit and was surprised to find a hidden gem.

A nice cosy interior supplements the interesting menu … something different than the regular fare you find at most mid-range restaurants in Singapore. Friendly and flexible service and an interesting drink menu made the experience complete.
author: Andrew Shuttleworth

restaurant_name: Morsels Restaurant & Gastro Wine Bar | Morsels Private Dining
review_text:
Absolutely loved my experience at Morsels in Dempsey. The ambience is stunning — it feels like stepping into a European rustic cottage tucked away in the lush greenery of Dempsey Hill. Super cozy, intimate, and full of charm.

The food was equally impressive. Each dish was thoughtfully curated, with a creative use of quality ingredients, fermentation techniques, and house-made sauces that really elevated the flavors. You can tell a lot of heart and craftsmanship goes into the menu here.

A beautiful spot for anyone who enjoys unique, ingredient-driven cuisine in a warm, welcoming setting. Highly recommended!

@cheechin.chew on Instagram
author: Chew Chee Chin

review_text:
Had a great time at Brewerkz Singapore. The food overall was really good — especially the wings, fries, and mains — everything came out fresh and well-flavoured. The staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel welcome from the moment we walked in.

The atmosphere was very nice too — relaxed, lively, and perfect for hanging out with friends or family. Prices are reasonable, slightly on the higher side, but still fair for the quality and portion sizes.

The only downside was the dessert — it didn’t meet expectations — but I really appreciated the way the team handled it. Once we mentioned we didn’t enjoy it, they kindly made it complimentary, which shows great customer service.

Overall, good food, great service, and a pleasant place to spend an evening. Would definitely visit again.
author: Amila Kankanamge

review_text: Came here for dinner and had the Cesar salad, beer and fish and chips. The beer is very well poured. First time seeing a beer with good foam. Salad was fresh and tasty. Fish and chips were good except the fish was a bit too oily.
author: C K Leong (Ah Leong San)

review_text:
Dropped by for a relaxed drink and was genuinely impressed. The local craft beers were excellent, well-balanced, fresh, and clearly brewed with care. A great range for both casual drinkers and craft beer lovers.

The food was solid and well-executed, perfect to pair with the beers. Portions were good, flavours were on point, and everything came out timely.

What really stood out was the service. The staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel very welcome. Special mention to David, the manager, who was warm, professional, and clearly takes pride in running a great place, it shows in both the atmosphere and service standards.

Overall, a great spot for good food, quality local brews, and excellent hospitality. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be back.
author: Stanley Lee

review_text:
We have now eaten here twice and the food has been outstanding both times!
From kids fish and chips and kids pasta, to the wagyu beef bowl, Portebello mushrooms, satay skewers and now the Laksa. You cannot fault the food here! It’s well worth it :)
author: Karina Young

review_text:
I only ordered 2 glasses of craft beers but my service person (PRATHIP) is superb and excellent!
He is an excellent frontliner… he is the epithomy of good human being!
I should recommend him for a salary raise!!!
Excellent service, Prathip!!
author: pete jimenez

review_text: The place is well-decorated and welcoming. The staff are warm and friendly as they serve food with a bright smile on their faces. They are open, polite and proactive. The food is delicious, each bite a mouthful of flavour and joy. It is also presented extremely well and the food looks appealing, which definitely suits the taste of the food. I would definitely recommend coming here as I had an amazing omakase experience here.
author: Amie Notts

review_text: $58++ for high quality, and fresh sashimi and food! Super worth and cute desserts. Blue cocktail (bubble bath) was $25, appropriate portion but I feel more alcohol can be added! We also got the banana matcha tiramisu ($13.5) which was good! Overall, super worth and really delicious.
author: kim

review_text:
Came in for a birthday dinner and we took the Best Seller Menu set. Definitely worth the value.

The service is great as the service staff clearly explain what you are eating with the sequence of every dish.

Although seated at the main dining area,  the restaurant is not too noisy and we can enjoy the food peacefully.

Will be back to try other menu set.
author: CL Lim

review_text:
My 1st time, was recommended by my colleague, visited Hana Restaurant. To my unexpected expectation,  the food were presented Wonderfully,  every dishes "Pops" with level of Great Taste, Freshness and Quality. And if coause with the compliment of the Sake were had. Every moment feels like wonderland like if feel. Not Forgetting the team are so great and shared every dishes presented... it was Lovey,  will be back again.

Had a Great time dinning @Hana Restaurant...

Happy New Year...
author: Anderson Liew

review_text: I had the $58 per person omakase, and my wife had the $88 per person omakase. Each one of us thoroughly enjoyed our meal. There wasn't one thing that I didn't love, and the service here is fantastic as well! I especially liked the steak and the unagi out of mine, but again, everything it came out very quickly, and the food was super fresh. We definitely come here again!
author: Jarrett Lau

review_text:
Overall we had pleasant time staying at this hotel. The food, room, and services are great with very strategic location in Orchard area.

There is a bus stop in front of hotel that can bring you almost everywhere in Singapore and near to MRT station also (Somerset).

Even though it’s not a brand new and luxury hotel, it’s still very comfortable and well maintained.
author: Rafael Rakyan

review_text:
I experienced a series of unacceptable issues during my stay at
Concorde Hotel Singapore.

First room:
•	The room had a spider,
•	And a strong fresh renovation smell.
When I reported this, the front desk astonishingly told me “just use an air freshener”, which is not a proper solution at all.
They even added that the “other rooms might also have spiders,” which was shocking and unprofessional.

So I requested a room change.

Second room (even worse):
•	There were used socks left on the floor from the previous guest.
•	Then a male staff entered my room without permission, after pressing the doorbell for less than one second.

At that moment I was only wearing underwear, this is a major privacy violation, completely unacceptable in any hotel.

Worst part – hotel management attitude:
•	The manager is never available, almost impossible to meet.
•	Everything is pushed to the front desk, and the staff were impatient and dismissive.
•	Despite all the issues, they offered no real apology and no compensation, and acted like it was nothing serious.

This entire experience shows a complete breakdown in hygiene, privacy protocol, and management accountability.
I sincerely hope the hotel reviews its standards and trains its staff properly.
author: Steve Leung

review_text: Special thanks to Vivian (reception staff) for being so accomodating to us and Rita (spices cafe) for being so nice to our 4 year old. She loved it and it made us feel very welcome as a family. The location of the hotel is super convenient with lots of dining options around. I recommend it!
author: ash joysury

review_text: Well I have a mixed feeling about this hotel. At one side they have this amazing location right in the heart of Orchard and making it easy accessible to shopping center and center city attractions, bit the hotel is quite old altho they maintain it quite well. They have big breakfast buffet selection and strict dress code where you should not wear PJ or room sandals, instead proper attire and shoes. Value for money considering location and apparently it’s quite famous for neighborhood countries. If you are not that picky with old building and simple room, and prioritize location more, this is a good choice to stay when in Singapore.
author: Arti Soejitno

review_text: First time in Singapore and we thought that Concorde Hotel would be a good choice. We were not disappointed. We were looking for a central place within easy reach of shopping, and Orchard Road is packed with shopping malls. We also wanted easy public transport and a bus stop directly in front gets you quickly and usually without change to all the spots you will want to get to. Buses are easy with CC tap on and tap off. We chose to stay in the hotel Premier Club rooms which includes access to members lounge open daily 7am to 11pm. Here you can breakfast away from busy restaurant and enjoy evening snacks and cocktails. We were very happy with the service here and we would like to acknowlege Kirssen, Kimberly, Faridah and others for their excellent service. Room services including limited free laundry and minibar are available. We were very happy too for room housekeeping, particularly Melody who was friendly, efficient and happy to help at all times. We were unable to use the swimming pool due to cough/cold illness, but maybe next time.
author: Sandy Middlemas

review_text:
Hawker fare.
Tried the mutton soup. Too bland for me. Though there is some heat level to it, there is no rich spice and milky mutton soup that I normally associates with mutton soup.
Meat taste bland as well.
Overall is ok but not for people who need stronger flavour.
author: Kt Goh

review_text: One of the worst mee gorengs. Extremely disappointed. Costs $5.00. Just pay a dollar more could have enjoyed the best briyani instead at one of the 2 famous stalls there. Mee goreng was dry. No wok hei unlike reviews. Beansproughts (taugeh) still raw. Totally spoilt the dish. When was the last excellent review ???
author: gary chan

review_text: Their mee goreng is easily the best in tekka market food centre. It brought me back to the olden days authentic taste. Highly recommended!
author: Citran Jai

review_text:
Tourists must try!

Better than any briyani here the taste is so good. I ordered kway tuew and seafood fried rice. Both outstanding with lots of meat for $5 each.

Fusion of Indian/Malay/Chinese food that I didn't find anywhere else.
author: Myles

review_text: Best Mee Goreng I had in a long while despite the noodle lacking wok-hei. In fact the look of it already tells you that it would be nice. Unlike lots of the modern 'kosong' mee goreng, each mouthful here was packed with some crunch, there were even some meat in the mix though they were very small pieces and rather chewy.
author: Simon Y

review_text:
Came here for a cozy CNY Eve dinner with my kids. As usual, the fishhead curry was our personal favourite and the staff was so kind to offer dissecting it for us. Rice and veg top-up was prompt and efficient too.
The highlight was really the staff, especially Mr Mani and Trisha. 👏
Overall, thanks for the great food and experience!
author: Cheryl S.

review_text: Some of the best Indian food we've tried. Ordered the tandoori chicken with garlic butter naan, the chicken was packed with flavour and cooked well. The lamb biryani was generous and tasted very authentic. My mum approved too! Jit provided great service, we felt welcomed and will be back
author: Brando The Pig

review_text:
Googled “Best Indian Fish Head Curry” - it led me to this restaurant and it definitely lives up the raves.

Our family really love the fish head curry - fragrant & flavourful!

And it goes really well with their in house homemade prata - crispy & not oily at all.

They accept CDC vouchers too.

We approve.
author: Kelly Chong

review_text: Came here for a gathering. Food and hospitality were good. There were great varieties of food and options for vegetarians as well. Pls see the photos taken, although some photos were missed out. Location was easy to find too. Of course nothing is complete with alcoholic drinks.
author: Chan “Toffees” Allen

review_text:
Gayatri restaurant is a Cosy spot in Little India for hearty North and South Indian food, with standouts like biryani, fish head curry and tandoori items that are full of flavour and spice.

The air‑conditioned dining room feels homely yet modern, with banana‑leaf style plating and an open kitchen adding to the lively ambience.

Portions are generous and prices are reasonable for central Singapore (around S$18 per person), making it good value for families and groups.

We tried chicken tandoori, fish head curry. Both were good options for a group.

Service was attentive and fast.
Prices are at par location and nearby options.

Its a must visit if you are fan of Indian cuisine in Singapore.
author: Hrishikesh Deo

review_text: once you come here, you can never get used to treatment @ other Subway! The team here is responsible, accommodating and always trying their best to give us as much veggies as possible (hard to find in other subway especially msia) look at the amount of greens, how generous, we love the subway here pls RAISE THESE PEOPLE PAAAY the it’s always the same awesome 2 ladies 🩷🩵
author: Hailey Khor

review_text: Writing a review about (i guess it is the same) the Filipino staff named Maries(if not wrong). She really seems unhappy to work at such timing. I was dining at around 10:30am. Usually staff would ask the usual questions like may i have your order, what bread would you like etc, but she came out of the kitchen and just look at me, and say nothing. Yes, we  are expected to know what to order but that's not how you work in a service line right? I searched the reviews here and now I'm not surprised why there are so many 1 star reviews, all about the same person. 💀 usually i dont write bad reviews but this staff is another level
author: Christopher Wong

review_text: Came around 3pm today and I received excellent customer service from the crew today! they greet customers with a smile and positive attitude and serving them promptly in a friendly manner. They cleaned the tables immediately after the customers left. They have maintained cleanliness well. Atmosphere was relaxing to have a meal.
author: Rifa Zeera

review_text: If i can give negative stars i will, youre staff the big guy whatever his name is, he is impatient and just screamed at me, he was rushing me like there was a long line, i was the only customer. Also when i got there i was at the counter, insted of entertaining me he only looked at the woman behind me. HE IS SO RUDE.
author: Carl Sustiguer

review_text: Went to get breakfast 2 times in this subway, always met this women with bad attitude. No more next time
author: S. Sow

review_text: One of the legendary Indian restaurants! We visited with a small group for dinner, and the food was absolutely amazing. We enjoyed every single item we ordered, and everyone was very happy with the experience. The dishes are highly recommended, this is a must-try Indian restaurant in Singapore. The place is always busy, which shows how popular and loved it is!
author: rena nura

review_text:
Dear Banana Leaf Apolo Management,

I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding the unacceptable food quality from my takeaway order purchased on 24 February 2026 from your Race Course Road outlet.
The condition of the food was extremely disappointing. The curries were excessively oily, with a thick layer of oil visibly floating on the surface, making them unpleasant and effectively inedible. The briyani rice was soggy, clumped together, and lacked the expected texture and standard one would associate with your establishment.

This order was specifically purchased for breaking fast, and it was both frustrating and upsetting that the food had to be discarded due to its poor quality. For the price charged and given Banana Leaf Apolo’s longstanding reputation in Singapore’s food industry, this standard of preparation is unacceptable.
I have attached photographs taken shortly after purchase for your review.

I request that your management investigate this matter seriously and provide:
1. A clear explanation of how such substandard food was served.
2. The corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
3. An appropriate resolution for this incident.

I trust this matter will be handled with the seriousness it warrants. I look forward to your prompt response.
author: Sophian

review_text:
Excellent Service & Warm Hospitality By the two staff members, Mr Rajasekar and Mr Ashok who took care of us during our visit. Their service was attentive, friendly, and genuinely warm without being intrusive. They were knowledgeable about the menu, quick to respond to our requests, and made sure we were comfortable throughout the meal.

It’s service like this that truly enhances the dining experience. We left feeling well taken care of and will definitely be back. Well done to the team at Banana Leaf Apollo!
author: Ranj Rk

review_text: One of the best places for hosting small scale events (120 to 150+ pax) and the food is very delicious. Guests could not stop praising, especially the Mutton Mysore which ran out very quickly. Love the decorations and ambience of the event hall. The staffs and managers, Mr.Karthick & Mr.Raghu, were very cooperative and made our reception a success. The customer service is highly commendable and hope we get more opportunities to host more events in the future here.
author: Lava Ravina

review_text: The food is towards the spicy side but it’s still delicious. The mutton dim Briyani is flavourful without the gameyness from the mutton. That’s the highlight for me!
author: Amanda Woon

restaurant_name: The Song Of India temporarily closed for renovations
review_text: Easily located lovely black and white house along Scotts Road. Was here for the Sunday brunch buffet with friends for the first time. There was a private event happening on the grounds, so I was expecting the staff to be pretty busy that day. The restaurant manager was in a pleasant mood and showed us to our table. The service staff were attentive enough to make sure our glasses were full and clear off the used plates. The spread of food for the brunch wasn't exactly expansive but definitely it was more refined to what I am used to in other famed restaurants or eateries. The manager was nice enough to come round our table to check if we had an enjoyable meal. This might just be a brunch service but overall I was truly expecting more out from a Michelin restaurant.
author: Matthew Lee

restaurant_name: The Song Of India temporarily closed for renovations
review_text:
The experience feels authentic.
Paintings of people dancing on the walls are beautiful. The table arrangement and the service feel old-fashioned thus nostalgic.
5 classes of set menus are available including vegetarian version for each.

There was one same staff attending us and checking how we liked it through the meal.
He talked with us in detail and gave us good recommandation based on our preference. That is very helpful to us whole are not so familiar with Indian cuisine.

In general, it is outstanding with food presentation and service among Indian restaurants, which makes it a good choice for people want to try Indian food. But it still has way to go to achieve an inpressive taste, and a really fine experience.
author: WEI HUANG

restaurant_name: The Song Of India temporarily closed for renovations
review_text: Nice ambience, good Indian food. Servers are very helpful and gave great recommendations. Star of the dinner was sarson wali Cod (Cod fish marinated with mustard paste). We tried a lamb dish cooked in ginger gravy which was also very tasty. Overall a big thumbs up to this Michelin Star studded restaurant.
author: Rusha Chakraborty

restaurant_name: The Song Of India temporarily closed for renovations
review_text:
Lets start with giving it due credit for the ambience and staff worthy of a Michelin Star restaurant.  The staff is professional, polite, accommodating, they explain you in great details every cuisine served infront of you.

We were not willing to be very explorative so went for the course meals, and the quantity is justifiably good. It fills you up. However, in the curries, I couldn't find that succinct flavor I was looking for. Some of the curries did have a unique punch lurking around in the background, but I guess the quantity is too less for one to actually enjoy or feel it. Maybe they should consider serving more of a curry and reducing the number of items from Sets.
Overall, an expensive meal for an experience worth it, not quite the flavor wise a winner.
author: Amar Akshat

restaurant_name: The Song Of India temporarily closed for renovations
review_text: This is a nice restaurant and I'd love to give it 5 stars but can't quite. The food is all excellent and very interesting. We enjoyed each course of the Degustation menu. The service is very attentive, though there can be disconnects (we asked for the "after-dinner drinks menu" and they didn't understand, just to name one issue). The real downfall is the wine. We asked for the wine pairings, and it was just three glasses, each from their by-the-glass list (as opposed to a tasting serve with each course). And the wines on that list are fairly mediocre. How can a Michelin-starred restaurant have such bad wine? They also do the smallest pours of spirits in cocktails I've seen in a while. When they brought out the cognac it barely had anything in it. Also, the entrance has stairs and they don't have an alternative, so if you have strollers, wheelchairs etc you will have to carry them up stairs. And the price is pretty high for what you get. Again, a lot to enjoy here and it can be a special evening, but expect to pay a lot too, don't expect good wine, and make sure you can navigate stairs.
author: Joanna O

review_text:
A wonderful place for a classic Singaporean breakfast. They serve all the local staples, and each one is done with care and attention to detail. The coffee was freshly brewed, aromatic, and robust, with that familiar slightly bitter edge that pairs perfectly with breakfast.
The kaya toast was excellent—thin slices of bread toasted until golden and crisp on the outside, slathered generously with fragrant kaya and a slab of cold butter that slowly melted into the warm toast. The balance of sweetness and richness was spot on and incredibly satisfying.
The soft-boiled eggs were cooked just right, with silky whites and rich, runny yolks. Seasoned with a splash of soy sauce and white pepper, they were comforting, savoury, and simple in the best way.
Everything came together beautifully for a nostalgic, no-frills breakfast that really hit the spot. We enjoyed it so much that we returned again—definitely a place we’d recommend for an authentic and satisfying Singapore breakfast.
author: Li Nh

review_text:
Always looking for the OG 🥹.

Soft boiled eggs, Singaporean coffee and butter kaya toast.
Nice place to have some breakfast and chilling with some locals, who also known as one of their favorite places
author: Mike Wong

review_text:
Nostalgic place to eat at since the brand started here. Can’t go wrong with the popular kaya butter toast. We also enjoy their French toast ($2.80, served with kaya), & chicken curry with bread ($7.50). Mee rebus ($5.40) was average.

If you are sensitive to cigarette smoke, avoid sitting near the entrance. Smokers light up at the tables by the roadside.

Not a night-time spot
author: Cheen the Curious

review_text:
One of those familiar names you’ll probably bump into more than once in Singapore. The menu is classic: toast, soft-boiled eggs, nasi lemak, mee rebus, curry mee, Siam noodles, and etc. Basically all the local picks under one roof.

Dropped by around 2 p.m. for a late lunch and was surprised it was still quite packed! Ordered the mee rebus and a lime juice. The broth was thick, though it could use just a *tiny* pinch more salt (or MSG magic) to really round up the flavour, and to hit that full, flavourful punch. The noodles came with basic condiments - bean sprouts, bean curd, egg, and a few green chilli slices.

Lime juice was refreshingly zesty (though I can taste the lime cordial), did its job on a hot afternoon. Nothing mind-blowing, but a reliable spot for a quick, local fix.
author: Nomnomyzm

review_text: Uhh call me crazy but $1.2 for one hard boiled egg should be illegal! Adding on an extra egg for $1.2 (normal toast set) would’ve brought the total up to $8! Pretty damn steep imo 🥴 lots of tourists tho! Toast is good & they sell hot food too if you’re not in the mood for eggs & toast.
author: foodieboba

review_text:
It’s really noisy from all the nightclubs? Karaoke? In the building. I’m not sure what those places are but some of the characters going in and out of them seem quite dubious.
The McDonalds is fine. Maybe the seating is a little rundown but I think that’s the building, not the McDonald’s.
Food was fresh and staff were helpful and efficient.
I’d rather eat here any day over the Bugis Village store which is dirty with rude staff.
author: Luke

review_text: This outlet is really not bad but limited numbers of seats. Service is good and staff are friendly. Just perhaps it’s Parklane. Tried the smoky beef burger but not impressed sorry!!
author: Gary Ng

review_text: Came close to closing time at midnight and staff were still prompt and courteous. The quarter pounder was delicious with plenty of chopped fresh onions and pickles. Plus the fries were fresh out of the fryer. Good supper after a tiring work shift. 👍 Take note though that this outlet is surrounded by many nightclubs.
author: Cheryl S.

review_text: Cozy And Friendly Mc Donald’s!  This branch tucked inside Parklane and is a great place to dine as its not crowded.  Service here is amazing specifically from the friendly auntie who is both efficient and helpful.  I love how she interacts with every single customer and makes this fast food chain feel like a proper restaurant.  Food is of course consistent.  You should try the Laksa Prawn Burger!
author: Logan Chiam

review_text: Do not come to the McDonalds here. Their service very slow as per usual. And their customer service is very low. This worker in the picture was cursing at us and calling is names. This is very unprofessional and she was having an argument with another worker. Please do not allow such people to work. Thank you.
author: Mika Humayl

review_text: Visited this Burger King location recently and had a great experience. The food was fresh and served hot, and my order was prepared correctly. The staff were friendly and the service was quick even during busy hours. The dining area was clean and comfortable. Overall, a reliable spot for a quick and tasty meal. Would definitely come back!
author: Zhenhua LIU

review_text: they have some value for money things and some really SCAM things like look how small this peanut butter choc cake is. $4!!!
author: keefe

review_text:
15 Jun 2025.  Came here to redeem two sets of chicken fries.  A new product.  Texture wise was crispy.  We were also given curry sauce to dip in.  Both the sauce and the fries were too salty.  It would be best to eat with rice or lettuce.  Also dipping in tomato sauce might help to balance the taste.

This location was rather small with limited seating area

Thank you BK for launching this product in a big give away campaign
author: Sean

review_text: Nice quiet place. Foods was delicious except the fries 🍟 texture. Staffs was nice. Ordering of foods at kiosk was easy
author: Mimikuku Mimi

review_text: It was our first night for this trip in this area of Singapore, and most of the food shops were closed (we're not alcohol drinkers, and it seems like those places were the only ones open). We couldn't decide where to eat, so we ate here. To be honest, hawkers are waaay cheaper, but sinve we were super tired and hungry, we made do. Contactless kiosk was super handy, and I like that they have more juice options than the BK branches in my country.
author: Doc B Lapa (skysenshi)

review_text:
The food here is super sedap, huge shoutout to Mr Yusril 🔥
He made my pepperoni pizza and it was next level — perfectly cooked, generous toppings, and packed with flavour. You can really tell care and skill went into it.
Definitely coming back again 👌🍕
author: luxeskh

review_text:
Dear Domino’s Team,

I am writing to express my extreme frustration and disappointment with my recent order.

We ordered 36 roasted golden drumlets, yet only 26 were delivered. On top of that, the New York Crust with Volcano Nacho Cheese was not wrapped properly, resulting in the contents spilling out and making the entire pizza a complete mess.

To make matters worse, when we tried to call your outlet to rectify this, no one answered the phone. This level of service is absolutely unacceptable.
author: Athena Koh

review_text:
Ordered delivery and the food was disastrous. Just look at the photo — which part of the mac and cheese pizza even resembles the advertised image? I get that “images are for illustration purposes,” but this is way off.

As for the pepperoni pizza… the amount of pepperoni is pathetically few, and the sauce is just a thick layer sitting on the dough. Where’s the balance? I used to think pizza could never go wrong. Well, I was wrong. Very wrong.

You’d think the kaya banana pizza might save the day? Look at the photo — it speaks for itself. OMG. What is going on with Domino’s??

“Edited portion: I just realised. There’s no banana at all on the banana kaya pizza!”

Side note on the delivery service. It’s marked delivered wayyyyy earlier than the time it reached me.
author: Simon Teoh

review_text:
Placed an order for 6 X large pizzas for a kids birthday party the previous day for 7pm delivery the next day. At 6:45pm, the order update said the pizzas were ready and at the store.

No sign of delivery and I tried 25 times to reach them - no response on the phone number listed.

We finally gave up at 7:35 and drove to the shop and were casually dismissed by a staff that the delivery person had just left. And 5 minutes later, the app update still said the order was at the shop.

The delivery was finally made at 8:10 and we got 6 cold pizzas and half the kids had left by then. I should have seen the google reviews before I took a chance - mistake going by the Domino's name.

Edit: Their auto answer has popped up for the review asking me to give feedback via the website. They could have checked I have already done it and no one has contacted me yet. I will update here if they call
author: Karthik Ramanathan

review_text: We sat down and placed our orders. It’s quite fast! The inside dine in area is pretty small, only 6 chairs. The pizza was delicious as usual. I always eat dominos & it tastes really good 👍🏼 the staff were friendly too.
author: Kai

review_text: Good omakase with a great selection of sushi to try. Premium and fresh! If you want to experience a different fish texture, aburi is the way to go. Recommend to add on shirako and uni! Trust is having 1 for 1 promo for birthday month which is an even sweeter deal~
author: MF

review_text: Used to go to standing sushi bar but decided to give it a try. From my last visit felt average. The sushi rice feels different from before where it tasted harder and doesn't seemed as seasoned with as much vinegar? Love the Foie gras chawanmushi, tasted really good.
author: Tarcisus Ho

review_text:
I’ve visited many times and always have an enjoyable experience, especially when coming for their famous daily promotions. If you can make it on a Monday or Thursday, the deal is unbeatable, you get 5 thick, fresh pieces of salmon sashimi for just $3.90 with no order limit, which is incredible value for money. I paired mine with the $6 umeshu promotion.

Beyond the sashimi, the rest of the menu holds up really well. The ochazuke is a personal favorite, offering a rich, satisfying flavor.

What really sets this place apart, however, is the service. Even during busy periods, the staff are warm, attentive, and genuinely sincere, making the entire meal feel much more pleasant. The food arrives quickly, so it’s a great option if you want a fuss-free meal that still feels high-quality.
author: Jeffrey Ng

review_text: Located with Odeon and quiet area for catchup. Ordered a salmon sashimi don and sashimi was fresh, but thought the rice could be warmer, it was quite cold and chewy. The sushi roll - salty sweetie, was made well with balanced flavours. My partner loved his set meal and finds it value-for-money. Food looks well-presented and is pretty nutritious as the set had protein, veggies and carbs.
author: Melissa Leong

review_text: Fantastic omakase!! Every dish was very tasty and well executed. I've had omakase experiences that were twice the price and not even half as good! They only use high quality fish imported directly from Japan. Highly recommended!
author: Khim Y

review_text:
This is a lovely spot if you’re after comforting Chinese + Peranakan halal food with authentic and satisfying flavors. The ngor hiang and grouper with their special sauce are truly fantastic; rich, well-seasoned, and clearly made with care. Still, the real star of the table is the chicken rice, which stands out for its fragrant rice and perfectly cooked chicken that hits all the right notes.

Don’t leave without trying their longan ice drink. Refreshing, lightly sweet, and the perfect companion to the meal. Overall, Rex MacKenzie delivers a warm, friendly dining experience that feels casual yet memorable, making it an easy place to return to.
author: Teddy Hendra Z

review_text:
Hor fun was not hor fun, plain no egg type gravy.

Hotplate and claypot chicken are the same dish except for different type of placement! Cheated my feelings!
author: Hello Chester

review_text: Taste wise is good, the quality is there. But the quantity , look how pathetic and stingy the portions of beef and rice were . The rice is less than a bowl.  Here’s the main absurdity, The Beef with Kailan. Costing at $15, yes they loaded the whole Kailen farm in my order, but look at the Beef! That’s not a handful, just a pinch of Beef! It’s more like Kailan With Beef rather than Beef with Kailan! The first mentioned ingredient should be more than the second! That’s basic culinary understanding! Double up the beef to justify the cost for goodness sake!
author: Md Ariff

review_text:
- The food tastes authentic and the portion sizes are just right.
- Cozy atmosphere, great for dining with friends or family.
- Friendly staff, quick to respond to requests.
- Prices are reasonable for the quality and flavor.
- Convenient location, easy to find and access.
author: Irfan Al Hamdi

review_text:
Hidden at the end of the road, this is a gem to be at.

Lets dive in!

Food:
The food options were similar to those like 'Tang Tea House'. Its a 5 star for us and nothing of negative came up when we had our takeaways.

Service:
Would have been 5 if the staff was more smiling.. but probably tired since there could have been alot of orders earlier.

Atmosphere:
The area is well known for pubs and bars but having a halal eatery here is really a great addition.

All in all, its an overall 5 star and we recommend highly to all to visit.

Cheers!
author: Sten (Piqued Wanderer)

review_text: Came in here for a family gathering. The staff were very friendly to usher to our seats. Authentic Cantonese food, served with exquisiteness. My favorite is probably the chicken soup, simple but refreshing start of the meal. Overall enjoyed our meal here. Food is very good but for the price I have raised my bar much higher.
author: Wing Seng Chan

review_text:
Welcoming the Year of the Fire Horse, Carlton Hotel Singapore presents a thoughtfully curated Lunar New Year experience centred on heartfelt reunions, auspicious flavours and timeless traditions. At the heart of the celebration is Wah Lok Cantonese Restaurant, where heritage Cantonese cuisine meets elegant festive dining.

A cornerstone of Lunar New Year celebrations, the reunion meal takes centre stage at Wah Lok. Known for its culinary legacy and refined Cantonese craftsmanship, the restaurant offers eight auspicious Lunar New Year set menus, starting from $88 per person, available from 9 February to 3 March 2026.

Each menu is meticulously designed to symbolise abundance, harmony, health and prosperity, making it ideal for multi-generational family gatherings and meaningful festive reunions. Set within a warm and elegant dining environment, Wah Lok continues to be a trusted choice for traditional celebrations elevated with finesse.

Debuting this season are two standout offerings:
Abalone Eight Treasure Duck ($208)
A luxurious centrepiece featuring slow-braised duck with abalone, sea cucumber, conpoy, pork, chestnut, mushroom and lotus seed. Rich in flavour and symbolism, the dish embodies unity and prosperity.
Sea Cucumber White Bait Lo Hei ($108 / $148)
A refined interpretation of the festive classic, bringing together auspicious ingredients and layered textures for joyful tossing and shared moments.

For celebrations beyond the restaurant, Carlton Hotel Singapore presents a refined range of Lunar New Year takeaways, thoughtfully crafted for home reunions and premium gifting. Pre-orders run from now to 10 February 2026, with collection and delivery available from 19 January to 16 February 2026.
author: fatspoting

review_text:
📍 Wah Lok Cantonese Restaurant
Level 2, Carlton Hotel Singapore 🇸🇬

We recently made a reservation for 10 persons, and the restaurant handled the group smoothly and comfortably.

Our orders included a good spread of Cantonese favourites:

🍜 滑蛋炒粿条 — medium seasoning, flavourful and satisfying
🍝 星洲米粉 — with added curry powder, aromatic and nicely balanced
🥢 萝卜糕 — very good, crispy outside and soft inside
🦐 Prawn dim sum — fresh prawns with bouncy texture
🥩 三拼烧肉叉烧鸭肉 — crispy roast pork, juicy char siew, and fragrant roast duck
🥐 Polo bun — must try, crispy topping and soft inside ⭐️
🍚 海鲜炒饭 — acceptable, decent flavour and texture

We noticed that many dishes came with prawns, and overall the taste was acceptable, leaning towards classic Cantonese flavours.
💰 Total bill was around SGD 440+ for 10 persons, reasonable for a hotel-based restaurant.
author: The Lost Forest Mum

review_text: Probably we made the wrong choices when ordering and should have stuck to dim sum. The seafood fried noodles were quite tasteless, and the soup had a strange flavour with an unexpectedly thick consistency for a Cantonese restaurant. The stir-fried radish cake and siu mai were alright. I would still give it another try for other dishes on the menu if I have the chance. Service was quick and friendly.
author: Leh

review_text:
I've been a loyal fan of this dim sum spot for decades, and the overall experience has consistently impressed me.

The food quality, service, and ambiance all come together to create a solid, classic dim sum experience with traditional flavors. The emphasis on quality ingredients and traditional preparation methods really shines through, providing a straightforward and satisfying experience.

The service staff are always prompt and attentive, ensuring that our teacups are always filled. The consistency of their service standards is truly commendable.
author: I.Y

review_text:
We had such a wonderful experience at Sakunthala’s Restaurant, thanks in large part to our amazing waitress, Hiruni.

From the moment we arrived, she made us feel so warmly welcomed. She surprised us with a generous serving of papadams right away, and when she noticed we had finished them, she topped them up without us even needing to ask. That attentiveness really stood out.

What made the experience even more special was her thoughtfulness. On her own initiative, she offered to bring us mint chutney, explaining that it paired especially well with the papadams. She was absolutely right. It was such a simple but delightful touch.

Hiruni also recommended the Chicken 65, and it turned out to be delicious. Crispy, flavourful, and perfectly spiced. Her recommendation did not disappoint at all.

Exceptional service, genuine care, and great food recommendations. Hiruni truly elevated our dining experience, and we will definitely be back.
author: Madeline Wong

review_text:
Not my first visit here. The food is usually good, but this time I felt the fish curry had a slight off smell, and the puri puri tasted different from before. The style also seemed to have changed, I remember there used to be a sauce we could drizzle over it.

For drinks, I tried the fresh lime juice with salt, which was really refreshing. I also had the version with sweet and salt, but personally preferred the one with just salt.

Overall, still not too bad.
author: Jeena Hey

review_text: We chanced upon Sakunthala’s Restaurant while getting our phone repaired nearby. The place was clean and comfortable, with nicely presented food and good, satisfying flavours. We were served by Dinesh, who made us feel very welcomed from the start. He took our orders carefully, checked that all our dishes arrived, and even kept topping up the papadom since it’s free-flow. He served everything with a warm, friendly smile and even offered to pack our unfinished food as the portions were quite generous. His attentiveness really stood out. We’ll definitely consider this restaurant again whenever we’re in this area.
author: Rahuda Rahman

review_text: Szechuan Vegetarian noodles were good! Would've been better with tofu cubes or soya chunks added! Vegetarian mysore mutton was little hard otherwise taste was perfect with cashew nuts!
author: TravelWithMo

review_text:
Service here is better than the fish head curry. Usually Singapore suffers manpower crunch in F&B sector.
Fish head curry was fresh and fabulous.
author: Regu Pillai

review_text:
Overrated, Overpriced, and Not for Indian Taste Buds

Visited this place purely because of its sky-high Google ratings, but the experience was a major letdown. The food was outright mediocre, the flavours felt flat, and the prices were far higher than what the quality justified. It genuinely felt like a place running on hype rather than delivering good food.

Based on my experience, foreigners might enjoy these meals since the flavours seem toned down for a global palate, but Indians looking for authentic, flavour-forward food will likely be disappointed.

Tourists, a quick heads-up: Don’t rely solely on highly rated reviews here. There are plenty of better and more authentic options around that offer far superior taste and value. Explore a bit — you’ll definitely find better spots.
author: rosh

review_text:
I’ve been visited Khansama occasionally since the last 3 years and their taste is consistent and good. Although it’s a little highly priced compared to the surrounding restaurants the taste is worth it.
They have different tandoori options - hariyali, tikka, reshmi etc among which hariyali is my favourite.
There is level 1 seating - non AC and level 2 has AC with more seating options. The serving time is fairly quick and the waiters are very responsive as well.
Though it’s mainly non vegetarian, they have a plenty of vegetarian options. They also provide catering services.
author: Charan Shetty

review_text: Day 2 of our Singapore 🇸🇬 trip. 2nd stop of the day 'little india' 🇮🇳 (exactly what it says on the tin!!) However,  if you enjoy your Indian food, and you have a European pallet,  you will love it here. We didn't need a beer, but there was a good selection. The gentleman serving us, I'm guessing was the 'Boss'made us very welcome 🙏 we ordered egg fried rice and a mixed chicken titka grill. OMG..THE best fried rice we have ever had, nicely spiced, very aromatic with a nice kick  👌 plenty of chicken on the grill platter, different flavours. Good value for money.
author: Maxine Strugnell

review_text: We wanted to order 4 dishes but the waiter recommended that we stick to two mains. Very considerate of him. Fish Marsala, butter chicken and mixed raita with garlic naan as carbs. Marsala tea was good! We even ordered samosa to go 😆
author: Alvin Wong

review_text:
I absolutely loved this Indian restaurant! From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm and welcoming. The staff was incredibly kind and attentive, Brahma is amazing staff.

The food was simply amazing and full of flavor, perfectly.

Every dish we tried was delicious, but the butter chicken and chicken korma were definitely highlights!

Highly recommended!
author: Elaine Telles

review_text:
This hawker center was the first place I visited right after I landed in Singapore. Personally, I cannot say that this was the best in Singapore since I have not yet tried other places at the time.

As a first time traveler, Newton Hawkers were so welcoming! I had a great time with the vibes by the uncles and aunties offering their products to me. Majority of the crowd are also local, which is a plus for me. This specific stall (in the picture) was the best (service-wise).

In the photo, I have made friends with Auntie Nico and Uncle John. I don’t know their relationship or if they own the store but they treated me so well and even offered to show me how they cook their food (I told them that I own a restaurant and was curious about how they cook their food).

In the end of the night, I asked them to take a picture with me and they did. Auntie Nico also used her phone to get a selfie with me lol. Fun times!

There’s always something beautiful about hard working people and everytime you get a chance to talk to them, do it!

WILL ALWAYS VISIT HERE EVERYTIME I GO TO SINGAPORE!
author: Mitchell Cody Torrejos

review_text: One of the most popular hawker centres among tourists and locals. Been visiting here on and off for 30 years for esp for oversea friends gathering. Most people come here for the famous satay, bbq seafood, chicken wings and local delights.  Spacious clean with lots of parking. I like to visit this stingray shop because the owner is more friendly and the bbq stingray chilli is decently good. The sliced fish porridge is very good too. Simple clear soup with fresh fish slice. This corner is less crowded. More comfortable for me. Kim Keat Sarah very clean good satays. The chain braised duck yew kee also has a other here. Weekdays not much people but weekdays can be hectic. Price here can be higher than neighbourhood due to proximity to the city.
author: Asia Apparel

review_text:
A Rite of Passage in the Singapore Food Scene

Ok,context first. Newton Circus is a food center that has been around for decades. It has been able to pass the test of time for good reason. This food haven offers some of the most delectable local dishes like, satay, chilli crab, noodle soups, barbeque chicken wings, among many others. It reflects the diversity of Singaporean culture and cuisine. Moreover, it reflects how differences in taste and flavors can be appreciated by everyone, leading to a harmonious existence as a people rather than a divided one.

Some people may say it is touristy and overpriced and to a certain degree, I must agree. Prices are definitely higher than the average hawker center and it is often visited by many tourists. Despite comments from other reviewers like "there are so many better and budget friendly places", I still recommend visiting Newton Circus for the following reasons

1. It is conveniently located near the city center and is perfect for those who dont have extra time to visit more local and off the beaten path hawker centers

2. The place is so lively at night. You can see families, teens, tourists, locals, professionals, couples on dates having a good time, digging in to their plates, conversing, having good laughs, sipping on tiger beer. The high energy and positive vibe sets the mood for a wholesome night out.

3. The place offers a wide variety of food. My family and I sampled many dishes from different stalls and we were not disappointed. We enjoyed the chilli crab, satay, shrimp BBQ, cereal prawns, oyster omelets and a seafood soup. Food was cooked well, flavors on point, fast and friendly service.

4. I would dare say that the place is almost historic in a sense that it has been a staple of the Lion City's food scene. As a person who spent many of my childhood years in SG, I recall our family entertaining visitors and family friends by bringing them here and our guests would always leave high praises about the dining experience.

5. I know there are a couple of stalls here which have garnered Michelin recognition so for those who believe in the Michelin list, dining here might be a good proposition. ( I trust local reviews more than Michelin, when in SG, do and eat as the Singaporeans do)

To conclude, I'd say that Newton Circus is definitely worth visiting. It is a great way to sample various local dishes and enjoy the lively vibe that the place offers. You could dine in the more posh restaurants in the City but you cant say that you've scratched the surface of Singapore's food scene if you have not been initiated through this culinary rite of passage.
author: Jesus Franco

review_text:
Newton Food Centre is a must-visit in Singapore. Lively, authentic, and packed with incredible food options, it’s everything you want from a classic hawker centre.

The variety is outstanding — from local favourites to late-night comfort dishes, there’s something for everyone. Prices are very reasonable, portions are generous, and the flavours are bold and authentic. It’s the kind of place where you can try multiple dishes in one visit and still want to come back again.

The atmosphere is busy and energetic, especially in the evenings, but that’s part of the charm. Despite the crowds, there’s plenty of seating and the space is well laid out. Being open 24 hours is a huge bonus, whether you’re after a late supper, early breakfast, or anything in between.

Great spot for travellers wanting a genuine local experience, groups with different tastes, or anyone keen to eat well without breaking the bank. Casual, vibrant, and full of character — exactly what a Singapore hawker centre should be.

🍜 Huge variety of food
🌶️ Authentic local flavours
💰 Affordable prices
⏰ Open 24 hours
🎉 Lively atmosphere

Highly recommended.
author: Nicole Syriotis

review_text: A must-visit for food lovers. The location is very convenient and the atmosphere is vibrant. Great variety of local dishes—the seafood and satay are outstanding. Everything was served fresh and full of flavor. A perfect, straightforward spot for a great meal in Singapore. Highly recommended!
author: Rizky Bagus Oka

review_text:
maybe my favorite restaurant in the world.
wish i could give more than 5 stars. i came back after 7 years just to have their szechuan dumplings and they were as good as the first time. love the way they operate, and they’re open late 🥹🙏🏻 you can see them making the food fresh from scratch but everything still comes quickly. you can be there by yourself relaxing and they won’t bother you/make you feel rushed. great service if you need anything too, xtra sauce or something
author: Alyssa Hartzell

review_text:
A local delicacy place well known for their snacks and dim sum. Heard a lot about this place from friends and decided to try it out.

Tried their carrot cake, felt a bit oily but tasted good. It’s a typical local snack and doesn’t have carrot but made using radish. Also liked their yam fritters.

The best of this place is their har gao dim sum. They serve it pipping hot right from the steam. The dim sum has a rich prawn flavour with 2 small pcs of prawn inside which is soft & juicy. The layer over the dimsum is very thin and doesn’t overpower the flavour prawn unlike some places. A must try dish here.

Take away price is less when compared to dine in as they charge service charge in dine in. Definitely worth trying when in Singapore as they have different branches.
author: abijith munikannan

review_text: Last came here was many years back, mum wanted to eat so I bring her here, we reach around 4.30pm there was seat inside the air conditioning place, ordering through the scan QR code with menu, some of the dish are available after 5pm. Food was generally good. Except for some was a turn down such as the onion pancake, taste and feel like roti plata. Nearest mrt is jalan besar mrt walking distance. They have service and GST.
author: vin takahashi

review_text:
Swee Choon is, quite simply, the best dim sum place in Singapore. From the first bite to the last, every single selection we ordered tasted superior to any other dim sum we’ve tried in the city. Each dish arrived fresh, beautifully prepared, and bursting with flavour—classic favourites executed to absolute perfection.

The service deserves special praise too: quick, efficient, and impressively smooth, even when the place is buzzing. Plates appear almost as fast as you can think of your next order, making the whole experience feel effortless and joyful.

This is dim sum done right—no gimmicks, just consistently outstanding food that keeps you coming back for more. Come early, because word is well and truly out. Swee Choon isn’t just popular—it’s legendary, and for very good reason. Highly, enthusiastically recommended!
author: Pete Klimek

review_text: Less of a queue these days and reservations now allowed. The fried bean curd is very yummy. Other dishes typical of a good dim sum.
author: A T

review_text:
First visit to this multi years  Michelin Star award restaurant. Dinning area is not big with simple decor. The Aircon was very cold but they are thoughtful to provide a blanket if needed.
Simple food, nice plating and presentation. Overall the food was consistently good and delicious, none has a WOW impact. To a person who does not enjoy seafood, their Seafood Lor Mee was pleasantly good with absolutely no fishy smell. It is a place worth visiting again.
author: Kesmond Kwek
Heng fs

review_text: Overall food is good. Must give a praise to the service team and Miss 亮. Minus - Oyster egg too much flour and beef is better without the batter.
author: WeeTeck Chaw

review_text:
Had a wonderful dining experience at Putien (Kitchener Road), and a big part of it was thanks to Jing Jing (and Yun). She is truly an impeccable person whose warmth and attentiveness completely changed the atmosphere of the restaurant.
Her service was easily one of the best I’ve received in Singapore’s dining scene — sincere, thoughtful, and effortlessly professional. She genuinely made my day.
The food was great as always, but great food paired with exceptional service takes the experience to another level. Thank you, Jing Jing and the entire team, for making our visit so memorable.
author: Philip Wong

review_text:
Easily the best Fujian food I’ve eaten. Putien’s Kitchener Road outlet has a record 7 year consecutive ranking as a 1 Michelin Star restaurant.

The food is a gastronomical delight, the presentation is visually appealing and the service personifies the best in Fujian hospitality which is savouring the very best food served unhurriedly making for a wonderful dining experience.

As a vegetarian I didn’t have a problem finding dishes to order and the pics prove it :)

Don’t go without a reservation.
author: Bon Appetite

review_text: Subway remains the top sandwich chain due to their consistency and variety. I always admire the artist doing up my food. Go for set meals to get a drink and cookie combo
author: Jon Wan

review_text: It’s 2/8/2025. Each time I visited this Subway outlet during the weekend, the service staff has always been great. Today is not surprising. I wanted to eat in initially, and was making the payment. Abruptly I told him that I decided to take that sub away. He quickly bagged the cookies and sub for me, and told me that the sub needed a sticker on it to seal the wrapping since I was to take it away. The little details. ❤️ melts my heart.
author: MABEL KHIEW

review_text: We had the best experience at Subway City Gate! Jason and Amer, was incredibly patient and friendly. They were professional, efficient, and thorough in their service! Wil visit again. Highly recommended
author: Watie Zamri

review_text: I would like to recommend this subway they have a good staff and friendly specially jason and nice environment must return 👌
author: Darrell Ang

review_text:
Just a regular Subway shop. They dont really publicize the $6.8 Value Meal anymore but it's still there if you ask the staff. Add on $0.5 to get hot americano instead of the soda dispenser drink.

Place is clean. As expected from Subway shop anyway. Staff are usually friendly too.
author: William

review_text:
I tried the famous Paper Chicken near Netrie India.
The chicken, cooked inside the paper with a rich garlic flavor, was incredibly juicy and full of taste.
It was so delicious that I would love to come back again.
author: Catherine

review_text:
We enjoyed our family lunch at Hillman - chosen for nostalgia against a backdrop of chinese restaurant chains taking over our malls. Parking in the area was a challenge, and we ended up at City Square Mall before walking over.

The paper-wrapped chicken was absolutely outstanding — juicy, flavourful and perfectly seasoned. The tofu dish was silky and comforting, and pork ribs were tender with a rich, savoury sauce. Most dishes felt like a taste of tradition done right. Great food, friendly service, and a nostalgic atmosphere — worth revisiting again!
author: Daniel Goh

review_text:
This is an interesting and longstanding restaurant that offers authentic local Singaporean and Chinese (Cantonese-style) cuisine. The food is flavorful and well-prepared — definitely worth trying if you're in the area. It's quite popular among Japanese visitors and has even been featured in Japanese magazines, which speaks to its reputation. While the prices are on the higher side, the quality and experience justify the cost. Overall, a hidden gem that's worth a visit
It was a bit noisy during my visit, as some customers were quite cheerful and loud, which made the atmosphere a little less relaxing.
author: Behnam Nikouei

review_text:
I would not have come here if I hadn’t recalled a neighbour’s recommendation from five years ago. Unfortunately, the experience turned out to be thoroughly disappointing and well below par.

The so-called signature duck, which required pre-ordering, was a letdown. It became almost painful to watch when the initial server had to be replaced midway because he was practically mutilating the duck while attempting to carve it.

Adding to the unpleasantness, the atmosphere was anything but professional. What kind of eatery allows its cooks and serving staff to sit among the dining tables, chatting loudly, while guests are trying to enjoy their meal? In a space this small, the number of staff loitering around far outnumbered the diners — hardly the environment for a peaceful dining experience.

Even basic knowledge about the menu was lacking. When asked how a dish was prepared, the server had no idea, and the owner’s vague response of “we use oyster sauce, etc.” only underscored the lack of culinary thought or care.

Mediocre food and careless service are inexcusable. If this is the standard they aspire to, I believe their days are numbered.
author: Samuel C

review_text: If you are looking for dishes with Wok Hey   This Zi char store is the place to go.  Amazing food great taste and good varieties of dishes.  Service is good.  Always seeking feedback and prompt.  Price is good n many sizes to choose    Things to look for or try is. Paper wrap chicken, fried pork chop., stir fried veg.  The bee Hoon and fried rice with salted fish.  Swing by check it out  u would not regret it.
author: TSage

review_text:
This Halal stall next to Ashes Burnnit, fried delicious Kway Teow Goreng. The noodle is abit moist if anyone like it fried this way. The prawn is cut in smaller size & fresh too. Portion is good for heavy lunch at S$4.50, however is a little chilly, so prepare a cold drink in hand.
I had try their Laska Johor before which is creamy & different from SG laksa.
Stall mainly served seafood dishes, No beef & mutton.

Jan’26, revisited the stall and managed to photo the stall name. Ordered the Mee Goreng also Kway Teow Goreng and she take time to fried it. The taste remain same as last eaten but this time less spicy. The Mee Goreng is slightly on a wet/moist dish that differs from traditional Indian mee goreng with potato.
author: Thomas Saw

review_text:
Like most food centers in Singapore, Golden Mile food center doesn't disappoint given the abundance of choices they offer.

It's rather well ventilated seatings make it a big plus.

You can almost find any food you desire here and at an affordable price.
author: Lee Kah Lok

review_text: A 40 minute treck to this place was well worth it! Please find this stall on the second level, the claypot gongpao was unbelievable. Friendly locals kept the night entertaining.
author: Ian M

review_text:
Do support this new hawker.

The curry had great texture, a uncommon lemongrass taste, chef was generous with the sauces. Meats are freshly re-fried upon order (hence do expect some waiting time), egg was perfectly cooked, items were decently priced.

I would recommend the chicken cutlet set instead, please skip the red beancurd skin pork - its nice and crispy but made me feel like im eating vegetarian (zero meat)- it was enough to keep me away from returning to the store.
author: Agdoron Gemaildotcom

review_text: A popular food hangout with office workers who work around Kallang area.  The hokien mee and fried cockles kuay teow are the favourite stalls with the locals .  There are many other traditional foods that one can find to suit ones tastebud . Stuff like chicken rice, char siew roast pork rice, pig trotters rice, law mee, bak chor mee, pork porridge, strong kopi, curry puff n pasteries. One is split for choice here.
author: Cheong Loong

review_text:
Came here on a weekday at 7.30pm. The restaurant was completely empty except for two other patrons at a table who were not eating but talking non-stop to the waitstaff.

We ordered 2 plain rice, one mysore mutton (not even 4 pieces for $12), brinjal, a hot lime and a milo. Also took away a chicken biryani. Total came up to $58.

Portions are very very small. When we ordered a mysore mutton, staff informed us that for 2 pax we should get a large portion as the small would only be 4 pieces of mutton. Looking at the photo, I cannot even make out 3 pieces of mutton.

We asked for extra mutton masala on the rice and staff obliged. However the service is quite poor. One staff was just talking to the other table throughout, even sitting with them at the table. The staff who served us did not even give us menus.

He asked us, “What do you want? Only biryani we have”.

This is not my first time coming to Islamic, I’ve been coming for years and sad to say the standard has dropped. The empty restaurant is testament to this.
author: Sk Sk0311

review_text: This place has been our go-to spot for years, but our latest dinner was a real shock-fest. The meat was so bloody, it looked like it just came from a slaughterhouse! And the staff's response? A casual "yeah, that's just how we serve it." Um, okay...Blacklisted!
author: Ira Norris Othman

review_text: Took Lamb shank biryani. But was quite disappointed. Outside the lamb meat was hard, and some part is burn. Rice are average potion and some part of the rice is hard and oily. Not worth the price as the taste consider normal. Can try at Mr Biryani or Al Mubin stall are much better than this. The fish biryani are average but can make it (a little salty) but not worth the price. Mostly the foods are on the high prices. If the foods is good l definitely will add into my lists but was regretful disappointed as my first time there.

review_text: An institution. How many places can claim to be a grandfather of a product? Now in the 3rd generation of family. The food delicious with flavour, portions big. Good service overall in cosy seating environment
author: Jon Wan

review_text: I don’t know why the restaurant’s rating is so low, the owner seems really kind and nice. The food we had was chicken biriyani, it tasted pretty delicious. Definitely recommend 👍
author: sarah

review_text:
Service was amazing! Staff were friendly, and food was served really quick too!

Loved their kebab platter, so juicy and tender! 🤤
author: Hamid Nawaz

restaurant_name: Copper Chimney Syed Alwi Road Singapore
review_text: Iftar buffet was good and the food was amazing too! Definitely worth the price! Will come back for sure!

restaurant_name: Copper Chimney Syed Alwi Road Singapore
review_text: The food is really good. It’s my second time here, but my first time trying the iftar buffet. Highly recommended.
author: Nur Alisha

restaurant_name: Copper Chimney Syed Alwi Road Singapore
review_text:
We were a big group of 30 pax for their iftar buffet. I must say that Baljeet, Dean, & Tamilian Gentle Man( Sorry forgot the name), these guys were on their toes providing utmost hospitality and quick response to replacing plates, refilling water and the buffet items.
I was very happy with their proactiveness which was great as we’re managing our guests.

review_text:
Rating: ★★★★★

restaurant_name: Nando's Bugis Junction | Flame-Grilled PERi-PERi Chicken
review_text:

Service was good but staff behaviour could be more friendly.
author: Fazal Mahmud Roni

restaurant_name: Nando's Bugis Junction | Flame-Grilled PERi-PERi Chicken
review_text:
Ordered the Peri-mac & cheese Chicken Bowl eith a lemon-and-herb level spice, a side of fully-loaded chips, and a bottomless Soft-Drink and bottomless Froyo. The mac and cheese pretty well balanced, and the chicken just blended into the flavour and texture of the mac and cheese, making for a pretty tasty dish I would order again. The "chips" (they were fries btw) were pretty dope, but tasted even better when the Nando's sauces were added in. There were a variety of options for the free-flow soft drinks, from Fanta to Coca-Cola and "Sky Juice". The bottomless Froyo never arrived as the machine was broken right as I was about to get my helping. The staff didn't seem to know how to fix the machine (when it was clearly visible thst it was empty) and spent at least 20 mins troubleshooting (nothing was coming out of the machine btw). It was probably another 15-30 mins until I requested for a refund, of which they finally decided to allow me to choose another dessert of my choice (I went with the chocolate chip muffin).

Overall food was good, service was not.
author: thelevitator

restaurant_name: Nando's Bugis Junction | Flame-Grilled PERi-PERi Chicken
review_text:
Nando’s Bugis Junction: Peri-Peri Perfection on a Budget!
Tucked away in the bustling heart of Bugis Junction, Nando’s never fails to deliver that fiery fix I crave. The star of the show? Their legendary peri-peri chicken—juicy, smoky, and customizable with just the right kick of spice. I went for the lemon and herb grilled half-chicken with sides of peri peri wedges and mild wings, and it was a flavor explosion that hit all the right notes without overwhelming the wallet.
Service was quick and friendly and the casual vibe makes it ideal for a solo bite. Portions are ok, its unbeatable value for that bold, tangy satisfaction.
If you’re wandering Bugis and need a reliable, delicious pick-me-up, Nando’s is your spot. Can’t go wrong—I’ll be back for more! 🔥🍗
author: Yim James

restaurant_name: Nando's Bugis Junction | Flame-Grilled PERi-PERi Chicken
review_text: I love Nando’s!!! Definitely recommend, best chicken in town, the place also comfy, it’s not that affordable but worth to try. The staff also very friendly and helpful…
author: They call me zoe

restaurant_name: Nando's Bugis Junction | Flame-Grilled PERi-PERi Chicken

author: Idrus Yusof

review_text:
Stopped by McDonald’s at City Square Mall Singapore for dinner, and it delivered as expected—fast, reliable, and convenient. The food was fresh, and the fries were hot and crispy, just the way they should be.

Service was efficient, even during the dinner rush, and the self-order kiosks make things move faster if you want to skip the line. The dining area was clean and had plenty of seating, which is a plus in a busy mall.

If you’re looking for a quick, affordable dinner while shopping, this place gets the job done without any fuss.
author: Benedict Correya

review_text:
Came here for lunch with a friend visiting from the US who wanted to try nasi padang. We arrived early and had no trouble getting seats, but the place filled up quickly as lunchtime approached—clearly a popular spot.

Service was friendly and fast. The staff were attentive.

We ordered two single rice servings with a variety of dishes piled on our rice so we could sample more items. Here’s my take on what we tried:
Rendang – The beef was tender but slightly dry. That said, the gravy was bursting with flavour, with a well-balanced blend of spices that delivered a rich umami taste.

Fried Fish with Sambal Ijo – The fish was fresh and fried until crispy. Unfortunately, the sambal ijo was quite sparing and lacked the punch one would typically expect.

Paru Sambal – Thinly sliced fried beef lungs topped with red chilli sambal. Nothing particularly memorable here, and as with the fish, I wished they were more generous with the sambal.

Sotong Sambal – The squid was tender, and the sambal had a slight sweetness that worked well. One of the better dishes we had.

Tempe Ikan Bilis – The standout for me. The tempe was crisp, well-seasoned, and paired beautifully with the ikan bilis sambal. Not spicy, but extremely moreish.

Terung Sambal – Fried aubergines with the same red chilli sambal used for the paru. This would have benefited from lightly seasoning the aubergines themselves and perhaps pairing them with a different sambal for variety.

Achar – Tasted homemade, with a lovely balance of flavours. The cucumber and carrots were crisp and refreshing—really enjoyable.

Tahu Telor – Loved this dish. The sweet, mildly spicy sauce poured over the tofu omelette made it a definite recommendation.

The total came to $36 including two lime drinks for two pax. Not an everyday lunch, but a reasonable price for the variety, reasonable portions, and heritage flavours. A solid spot for nasi padang, especially if you enjoy sampling multiple dishes.
author: Yasmin Abdeen

review_text:
❤️ Food sharing IG @ jkgourmets
😋 美食分享尽在 IG @ jkgourmets

This local eatery was one of the famous and popular restaurant specialize in Indonesian cuisines. Strategies location, great attraction to tourists and locals too.

In fact, their foods was very similar to local Malay Nasi Padang, variety of dishes, selection from protein meat like chicken, beef, lamb etc, to seafood like fish, prawn, squid, cutterfish etc. And a lot of vegetable dishes and some carbs too.

Similarly like Malay cuisine, Indonesian foods are also focused on great flavours with spices which savory met spicy flavours. It was really delicious and flavourful, especially those with coconut cream like curry or spicy dishes.

Unfortunately, their serving was not so great and yet pricing was quite high. Perhaps, the strategy touristy location causing them to charge more. Honestly speaking, this wasn't a air-conditioned restaurant, yet charging at such high price, this probably a big disappointment for some tourists who already can't tolerance of Singapore hot and humid weather.

As seen on the photos I shared, my plate of rice which contains of 1 piece of red spice chicken (Ayam Merah) and 2 vegetables includes of sweet potato leaf, and eggplant. This plate cost me $9. Not that affordable for daily meal as local. Perhaps once a while for craving satisfaction.

Overall, if you loves local Malay foods or specifically Indonesia style cuisines. I really recommend all to try. Unless you are local who know where to find good Nasi Padang, you may skip it. 🤗
author: Josh Kuek (#jkgourmets)

review_text:
Food was ok. Seems plain bit taste is there. Self service unless u sit on 2nd floor but forks, spoons, and drinks are self service.

review_text: honestly, the food was alright, but the price range was slightly on the expensive side — one dish was $11 and another was $8, which was a bit shocking. the beef and chicken were on the dry side, but the ayam gulai was alright and more enjoyable.

author: Milk and biscuit

review_text: Picked Ya Kun because it’s listed to close at 10pm. The drinks we got were just standard Ya Kun stuff (though they were out of barley by then). If they want takeaways only or early dine-in shutdown, just say so instead of the 10pm sign.

review_text: As far as ya kun outlets go, this isn't the best. Queue was very long and slow moving. A single person takes orders and prepares the food and drinks, while a few more aunties worked in the kitchen dunno doing what. Ordered a kopi c kosong ice, it was just OK. review_text:

The Turkey was nice and tender, served with great sides like the duck fat spuds.

review_text: Unique ambience with windows overlooking the streets and fine dining style setting. Food was good especially the sous vide lamb shoulder rack and desert. Chicken was slightly rubbery though. Attended a Penfolds wine event which was fantastic at Flutes.

review_text:

review_text:

review_text:
Excellent service.

Sambal Kangkong

author: Muhammad Iskandar

review_text:
Bumbu has always been our go-to place for meetups because it’s halal, the food is decent, and the ambience is charming. I’ve always liked their tahu telor and beef rendang — both were usually rich and flavourful.
However, when I visited recently, I noticed that the flavours weren’t as strong as before. It’s a little disappointing since this place used to be consistently good.
That said, because of its nice atmosphere and good track record, my friends and I will probably give it another try the next time we meet.

review_text: Food some good some not good. Staff not welcoming. Doesn't want to give us seat that we wanted , said it's reserved but nobody came. Chicken dish very bland. Thai tea is good. Lemon grass drink is good. Decor is really nice. Food is overpriced.
