review_text: Well decorated and much like the traditional Peranakan style. Upstairs aircon is a little weak. Staff may be a little forgetful but still polite. Food wise, much oil and its taste isn’t strong or as salty. Overall is still pretty good.
author: SuzseQ “RedDotter” Ng

review_text: Food and service are excellent. Mesa Tabagi is a perfect starter. It goes so well with the fresh baked bread. Grilled meat and seafood platter is exceptional. The lamb is very tender and tasty. The fish is soooo fresh. I highly recommend this restaurant.
author: Mona Seto

review_text:
I recently went here and had such a wonderful experience. The lamb chops were perfectly cooked-tender, flavorful, and absolutely delicious. The appetizers were fresh and beautifully prepared, and the baklava was the perfect sweet ending to the meal.

A special thanks to Nicol, the Filipino staff member who served us. He was very attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was perfect throughout our dining experience. His warm hospitality truly made our visit extra special.

Highly recommended! 😊
Shukran! and Godbless for everyone!
author: Don Ant

review_text:
I had one of the most delicious lunches I’ve enjoyed in a long time at a quaint little restaurant tucked along the bustling lane of Bussorah Street. The moment I stepped through the doorway, a tranquil calm washed over me, and I was warmly greeted by the cheerful service staff.  Lunch was thoughtfully curated by the manager, and while waiting, I wandered around to admire the walls adorned with delicate watercolour paintings of the very ingredients used in their dishes. These simple yet soulful artworks were soothing, almost meditative, and added to the charm of the space.
When the food arrived, I couldn’t resist tearing off a piece of the fragrant, steaming hot lavash before it was even properly served. Having skipped breakfast, I was determined to savour this single meal without restraint. Then came the meat platter—an impressive spread that immediately caught my attention. The smoky aroma mingled with the rich scent of spices, and each bite was utterly delicious. As I savored the meal, each bite revealed the care and craftsmanship behind every dish. It was clear that a great deal of passion went into its preparation. By the end, I was left completely satisfied—content, satiated, and delightfully full.  I’ll certainly be back. The ambience and the food truly reflect the soul of this little restaurant with a big heart.
author: Kathryn Ho

review_text: Came here because of Krispay and we were a little skeptical because the restaurant seemed empty. But this is definitely one of the best Turkish restaurants around the stretch. The babaganoush was smoky and perfectly balanced with the pops of sweetness and acidity from the pomegranates. The classic platter was also delicious and the meats were well seasoned and well cooked. Definitely not the tourist trap that it looks from the outside
author: Karen Liu

review_text: Very nice and delicious food. Taste are suitable for our asian buds. We order Ispanakli pide, Alaturka musakka (choose lamb or chicken), Fileto somon, apple tea, and kunafa for dessert. Will come back for sure
author: Juliana Sanjaya

review_text:
We visited McDonald’s Bugis Junction and had an average experience overall. Like many other visitors have mentioned, the food quality was okay — the classic burgers and fries were familiar and tasted fine, but nothing exceptional. Service was a bit slow during peak hours, which made the wait longer than expected.
The seating area can also get crowded and a bit noisy, especially around lunch or dinner time. It’s a convenient spot if you’re already at Bugis Junction and want a quick, familiar meal, but nothing stood out to make it a great experience.
Overall, fine for a standard McDonald’s visit — 3 stars ⭐⭐⭐.

Humne McDonald’s Bugis Junction visit kiya aur overall experience average raha. Jaise kai logon ne bhi bola hai, food quality theek tha — burgers aur fries familiar taste mein the, lekin koi special ya outstanding nahi lage.
Service thodi slow thi, especially peak hours mein, jis se wait lamba lag gaya. Seating area bhi crowded aur thoda noisy ho jata hai lunch/dinner time par.
Agar aap Bugis Junction mein ho aur quick familiar meal chahte ho toh theek hai, lekin kuch khaas nahi mila jo experience ko 4 star banaye.
Overall standard McDonald’s experience — 3 stars ⭐⭐⭐.
author: varun kumar

review_text: Had their latest mandarin orange McFlurry and honestly it tasted more like mango. Still delicious and smooth! Refreshing as well. Service is a bit slow as I waited 5min for the McFlurry but the restaurant was super packed even at 9pm. Come with expectation to wait for order and seats.
author: Aven T.

review_text:
Dear McDonald’s Singapore Customer Service Team,

I am writing to formally lodge a complaint regarding an unpleasant and humiliating experience at one of your outlets.

During my recent visit, my group spent over $100 on McDonald’s food. One member of our group, who is currently facing financial difficulties, decided to purchase a small item from a nearby shop instead. Despite our group having already made a substantial purchase at McDonald’s, your staff verbally singled out and embarrassed this person in front of others because they brought in rice from next door.

The way your staff handled the situation was unnecessarily harsh, insensitive, and completely lacking in compassion. Instead of addressing the matter discreetly or politely, they chose to call out one individual publicly, causing them significant embarrassment. This treatment was heartless and unacceptable, especially considering the circumstances—and the fact that we had already supported your business with a sizeable purchase.

We expect a higher standard of professionalism, understanding, and empathy from McDonald’s. This experience has left us deeply disappointed.

I request that you review this incident seriously, provide appropriate staff training to prevent similar situations, and inform me of any actions taken in response.

Thank you for your attention. I look forward to your prompt response.

Sincerely,
Todd Mawdesley
author: Todd Mawdesley

review_text: Prakarsh, one of the manager at this McDonald’s, provided truly outstanding customer service. Even when it was busy, he stayed friendly, calm, and very attentive. He made the whole experience smooth and welcoming, and you can really tell he cares about both his team and the customers. Great leadership and a fantastic attitude!
author: Tik S

review_text:
Stopped by McDonald’s at Bugis Junction for breakfast, and it did the job. Went for the Big Breakfast—fluffy scrambled eggs, a warm muffin, sausage patty, and crispy hash brown. Everything was fresh and hot, exactly what you’d expect.

The place was busy, but the self-order kiosks made things smooth, and the food came out quickly. Finding a seat can be a bit of a hassle during the morning rush, but the staff kept things moving efficiently.

If you’re in the area and need a no-fuss breakfast, it’s a reliable spot with all the classics. Fast, convenient, and hits the spot when you’re craving a quick morning bite.
author: Benedict Correya

review_text:
This is the BEST FOOD i have had in my entire life! I have traveled to over 30 countries and tried 1000s of restaurants and this ranks at no.1 for me. I will be back for more forsure!
The garlic sauce and chilli paste on the Pide is amazinggg
author: TradeSphere Innovations

review_text:
Thank you for the wonderful meal, speedy service and warm hospitality. Even the music was perfect! We will definitely return.

Recommend: Falafel, mezza platter, feta and spinach pide, mixed grilled kebab platter, kebab kofta, kunefe.
author: Valerie M Pura

review_text: Food was great and portions were big for the price. Staff were very friendly and welcoming and would like to give special mention to the manager. She checked on us often to see if we needed anything and even had a conversation once we finished our food. It was good being indoors with the AC and not too busy during the time we went around 12:30pm. Would recommend to try this place out.
author: Barbecue sios

review_text: Went there to celebrate a colleague’s promotion and service was great. Food was pretty good too! I love the dessert so so much.
author: Jenn T

review_text: Came here for weekday dinner with group of 12. Made reservations at this cozy place, good selection of veg and non-veg. We mostly have the place to ourselves. Great hosts and service👍
author: Timothy Teo

review_text:
I’ve been a regular here for two years, which honestly makes this review extra disappointing to write.

I ordered my steak medium rare. What arrived was closer to rare. It was not warn in the center, mushy in texture, and genuinely SLIMEY inside. Not just “a little under,” but clearly undercooked. Anyone who eats steak regularly knows medium rare should be warm with a tender pink center, not cold and gelatinous.

What really ruined the experience wasn’t the mistake kitchens mess up sometimes, it was how it was handled. I was asked to speak to the sous chef, who proceeded to argue with me and insist I didn’t understand steaks, while the manager stood by and said nothing. Being talked down to over a simple, reasonable request to correct an order is honestly wild, especially as a long-time customer.

Good hospitality means listening to guests, not debating them into submission.

I used to recommend this place often, but after being dismissed and made to feel uncomfortable over a clearly undercooked steak, I won’t be returning anytime soon. Really disappointing decline in service and professionalism.
author: kaelan johnson

review_text:
It's a Mexican joint on a street famous for evening out with friends and family, loads of Turkish, Lebanese and other cuisines are served in the restaurants in the area.

Piedra Negra has good Mexican food, popular Mexican / Latin music playing and staff is quite attentive and efficient. They were able to suggest food and drinks for our group, served us quickly, made seating alteration for us to acomodate our group and were more than happy to click pictures for us whenever we asked for it. Prices are affordable and the whole area, including this restaurant, has good vibes.

I'd recomend one evening here in this area with friends, if you are visiting Singapore.

review_text: The only redeeming quality was the amazing band they had playing there. The servers did not want to be there at all and I could not finish my food as it was not great. The entertainment was probably the best I have seen in a long long time…. The band deserves a 5 star review though 😍.

review_text: Took myself out on a date to haji lane and tried the food at this restaurant. The food is good but service could be better as I had to look around for a staff to ask for serviettes after the meal was served. Loved the deco btw.
author: Dolly Reavathi

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ 5/5  Fantastic Experience at Peidra negra  Singapore

I had an amazing time,their happy hour deals are genuinely one of the best I’ve seen  great prices and even better quality. The cocktails , especially margaritas were especially impressive, crafted beautifully and full of flavour.

The environment is vibrant and welcoming, with a stylish yet comfortable vibe. The team there is incredibly friendly; the servers were attentive, polite, and made the whole experience even better.

If you’re looking for a perfect spot for happy hour or just want to enjoy top-quality drinks in a great atmosphere, Definitely a place worth visiting!

review_text: Amazing place to have Italian. The ambience was lovely, food was excellent, drink options were plentyful. Its one of the best quite place to have lunch. Absolutely recommended. Be prepared to for out at least $50 per person though as the price is quite steep.
author: Aldo

review_text:
Truly an experience dining here. Celebrated my birthday here today, I enjoyed it so much. Both food and service was amazing.

Highly recommend the Capellini with snow crab caviar and add on sea urchin!! Everything else was very fresh, well prepared and presented too. Thanks to Nove for being so attentive and also helping us take many nice photos!
author: rui 1

review_text: Lovely dinner at Garibaldi. Beautifully plated dishes with standout flavours. The prawns were fresh and juicy, and the fish was well‑seasoned. Desserts had just the right richness without feeling heavy. Service was friendly, warm and attentive. The space is quietly elegant and perfect for an unhurried conversation with friends or family.
author: Josephine W

review_text:
Had a truly lovely lunch at Garibaldi today. The ambience was perfect for a quiet, relaxing afternoon — elegant, calm, and ideal.
We opted for the 3-course lunch, and every dish was beautifully prepared and well-balanced. The flavours were refined yet comforting — exactly what you’d hope for from a quality Italian restaurant.
A special mention to K Sandhu, who was incredibly professional and attentive. He made the entire experience feel smooth and welcoming. He also has excellent wine knowledge — his recommendations were spot-on and complemented the meal perfectly. 👍🏼
Great food, peaceful setting, and outstanding service. A place I’d happily return to and recommend!
author: G

review_text:
A Truly Perfect Experience

Ristorante Garibaldi in Singapore is an absolute benchmark for Italian fine dining. From the moment you walk in until the very last detail, everything is executed to perfection.

The quality of the ingredients is outstanding, with authentic, beautifully balanced dishes that fully express the soul of true Italian cuisine. Each course is presented with great care and served at exactly the right pace.

The service is exceptional: professional, attentive, and genuinely warm, making you feel welcomed and looked after without ever being intrusive. The wine list is simply endless, offering an extraordinary selection that can satisfy even the most knowledgeable wine lovers and perfectly complement every dish.

The atmosphere is elegant, refined, and inviting, ideal for a romantic dinner as well as for special or business occasions.

In short, a restaurant without a single flaw — everything was outstanding. A true reference point for Italian cuisine in Singapore. Highly recommended, and I will definitely return.
author: Don Amesh

review_text: 🤤 The taste is absolutely incredible! The fish was perfectly cooked—crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, with a sweet, savory sauce. The curry vegetables with tofu were also great, and the Ikan Bilis was the perfect crunchy addition! For my spice lovers, you MUST try their Sambal Belacan, but be warned, it is seriously spicy, yet so fragrant you can’t stop! 🏠 Despite the crowd, the restaurant is kept very clean and tidy. The ordering section and a small seating area are on the ground floor. If it’s full, you can head up to the second floor for plenty more seating options! 📍 Find it here: 11 Jln Pisang, Singapore 199078 (About a 10-min walk from Bugis MRT or Jalan Besar MRT). Final Verdict: 💯 Verdict: Long queue and slightly pricey, but for this level of authentic Malay/Indonesian flavor, I give it a perfect score! Definitely one of the best Nasi Padang meals I’ve had this year. If you’re in the Bugis area and craving local food, go for it!
author: 一言天成

review_text:
When you want a home cooked type of food, Hj Maimunah will be the answer. I am a regular customer and i can say the quality is consistent. It's halal, every dish is burst with flavour and it's considered value for money for daily meals.

Do notes that during lunch hour 12-2 will be busy so expect to see long que. But if you can come early at 11.30 that's even better!
author: ic kh

review_text: Get ready to taste the best Nasi Padang you have ever had in Singapore. Opened in 1992, this famous Nasi Padang restaurant has a ton of accolades including a Michelin bib gourmand.  Go early otherwise expect a looooong queue. Favourite dish beef rendang and their curry squid cooked in squid ink. Yum!!!
author: M4l2K T4N

review_text:
We ordered the platter, quite delicious and full of flavour. The portion can actually serve 4–5 people, depending on appetite — it’s very generous!

The queue was quite long, and there were even tourists dining there, which shows how popular the place is. Overall, a tasty and satisfying meal, definitely worth trying.
author: Crystalynn Chai

review_text: Here for a brunch and get a surprisingly big portion of nasi rawon. The best one is the beef skin. Not crowded at arrival. Lots of traditional cakes for try next time. Outside and inside seating. Upstair seating is also available.
author: L Sam

review_text:
I have been visiting this stal on and loff for over 30 years, and it remains a family favourite. Today, I brought my children along to enjoy a meal, and it’s heartening to see that the quality and taste are still as good as ever.

The food is incredibly tasty and authentic. We had the classic HingHwa Bee Hoon, the signature noodle soup. Everything was seasoned perfectly and served hot.

One of the best things about the current setup is the air-conditioning. Believe many people like the hot soups noodle, and as anyone knows, you usually perspire a lot while eating them! Having a cool, air-conditioned environment makes the dining experience perfect.

I wouldn't call it "cheap," but the pricing is very reasonable given the quality of the ingredients and the portion sizes. For the heritage and the taste you get.
author: Donut

review_text: Authentic Putian type of dishes. Very delicious and freshly prepared after order. Traditional seating arrangement reminisce of the older days. Value for money
author: Jon Wan

review_text: You'll get authentic Xing Hwa cuisine here. The food is not very salty and their dishes are well prepared. Look out for all the marked popular dishes and you won't go wrong.
author: Simon Ong

review_text:
I ordered 3 dishes (signature dishes) to be picked up at 1230pm on Saturday 13dec. Total bill was abt $45.
Was extremely disappointed to discover that the sambal kangkong I ordered didn't come with cuttlefish which was displayed on menu (look at pictures). Overall, I wasn't impressed with the standard of food. Kangkong was soggy and overcooked, prawn paste chicken wasn't crispy and fried beehoon wasn't flavourful or savoury.
On top of that, when I arrived earlier to pick up food, I was shocked when realised there was only a tiny miserable tub of chilli packed in bag. When I requested for more chilli, lady staff told me she could only give me one more and anything more would be chargeable. I said my food cost $45 and I am only entitled to 2 tiny miserable tubs of chilli? Is amount of chilli also limited if I had dined in? Apparently not (look at picture, free flow on table). I only needed another 2 or 3, not like more than 5. She unwillingly gave me just one more, so total 2 tiny tubs to be shared by 4 people. Customer service left a lot to be desired here. Staff were unfriendly with bad service attitude, and with no sense of flexibility.
It was a disappointment and a bad experience.
author: Phoebe Lim

review_text:
One of the oldest restaurants in Singapore, dating back 1933 and the very few Henghwas offering its dishes.

The dishes are no-frill and very much homecooking-like which were of good quality.

The appetizers were roasted peanuts and signature dried seaweed which the latter was mind blowing.

Trio golden platter consisted of prawn fritters, prawn rolls and prawn paste chicken which were freshly prepared and of great tasting.

Steamed fish was perfectly cooked, fresh and tender. The accompanying soy sauce was balance with a mildly sweet note.

Sweet and sour pork could do with more sauce as it was unevenly coated.

Flower clams came with its homemade chili sauce which overwhelmed the sweetness of the crustacean. A light soy garlic would be preferred.

Stir fried kailan and beancurd skin was a simple dish, well executed.

Lor Mee was starchy and a splash of vinegar lifted the overall taste. I missed the dried seaweed in this dish.

Peach gum as dessert, which was not too sweet. Refreshing and a great way to end the meal.

Portions were generous and represent good value.

Service is prompt and friendly.
author: MNG

restaurant_name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
review_text:
I have been to Mustard countless time over the years. Sandwiched between 2 bigger restaurants, it's easy to miss this cozy shophouse. It's a great place to bring a date, the place always seems to be filled with office workers hanging out with friends after work.

Their famous Chingri curry served in a coconut is a must have. You usually see that on every table. We tried the Murraya fish , which was beautifully flavoured and tasted really fresh. Being a Bengali restaurant, we will definitely be back to try the other fish dishes.
author: Faraz Hussain

restaurant_name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
review_text:
A true gem in Little India! Mustard is Singapore’s Bengali-Punjabi restaurant and it nails both cuisines perfectly. The Chingri Malai Curry and Damodar Chicken served in a coconut shell are absolute standouts—rich, fragrant, and bursting with authentic mustard flavour. Everything tastes fresh, homemade, and perfectly spiced without being overly heavy.
Special shoutout to Vijay for his outstanding service – super knowledgeable, gave spot-on recommendations, and made the whole experience even more enjoyable with his warm and attentive hospitality!
Portions are generous and prices are very reasonable. The cozy shophouse vibe makes it extra special.

If you want real regional Indian food instead of the usual butter chicken, this is the place. Book ahead—it gets packed for good reason! Highly recommended. 🇮🇳🍛
author: Naj K

restaurant_name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
review_text:
I found The Mustard through the Michelin Guide and visited for lunch. The restaurant opens at 11:30am; it was initially quiet but began filling up around 12:30pm.

The interior is air-conditioned with terracotta-coloured flooring, black-and-white sketches on the walls, and oil lamps used as ambient lighting. There is a bar on the far left and two tables outside. Inside, most tables seat four and are set with colourful runners. Overall, the décor is pleasant and themed, though not especially striking.

Food
•	Rice: Standard, nothing notable.
•	Aubergine in clay pot: Average. The dish was more of a paste and, despite the name, was served in a regular dish rather than a clay pot.
•	Kosha Mangsho (mutton special): Again, average. Thick gravy but lacked depth and richness. Found the meat dry rather than soft.
•	Doi Maach (Rohu fish): Dry, with many bones. Acceptable but not memorable. Odd sauce and a lot of it. The fish quality was poor!
•	Pure: small, oily otherwise Fine, no issues.

The meal started reasonably well but declined in quality as the restaurant became busier, suggesting some inconsistency once service ramps up.

A significant issue arose during payment. My credit card was taken away to be tapped and returned inside the bill sleeve, meaning the transaction was not visible to me. More concerning, my card was accidentally kept by the restaurant. I only realised this at Little India MRT station and had to call them and return to collect it.

Additionally, the route to the toilets offers a partial view into the kitchen, where kebab meat was seen hanging openly. This appeared unhygienic and detracted from the overall experience.

While The Mustard benefits from Michelin recognition albeit a gourmet bib and a pleasant setting, the food was largely average and the service and hygiene issues were disappointing. Given its Michelin Guide status, higher standards of consistency, transparency during payment, and kitchen hygiene would be expected.
author: Travelling Doc

restaurant_name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
review_text:
My recent visit to Mustard restaurant was a delightful exploration of rich and robust flavours. The restaurant promises a culinary experience inspired by the cuisines of Eastern India and Bengal, and for the most part, it delivered beautifully on that promise.

We ordered a mix of classic favourites and a house specialty, and here’s the breakdown:

The Unforgettable Star: Damodar Chingri (★★★★★)
If you take one recommendation from this review, let it be this dish. The Damodar Chingri was an absolute masterpiece. The prawns were cooked to perfection—succulent and juicy. But the real magic was in the gravy. Describing it as "tangy" doesn't quite do it justice. It was a complex, vibrant symphony of flavours where the tanginess (likely from mustard or tamarind) cut through the richness beautifully, creating a dish that was both bold and incredibly moreish. This is a must-try and worth the visit alone.

The Solid Supporters:

· Murgh Tikka (★★★★☆): The chicken was impeccably marinated and grilled, resulting in tender, smoky pieces with a lovely char. It was a classic done right, making for a perfect starter.
· Paneer Butter Masala (★★★★☆): A comforting and reliable classic. The paneer was soft and fresh, and the gravy was luxuriously creamy and mildly sweet, just as it should be. It provided a wonderful, soothing counterpoint to the more assertive flavours on the table.
· Daal Makhani (★★★★☆): This was a rich, slow-cooked delight. Creamy, buttery, and with a deep, smoky undertone, it was the ultimate comfort food. It paired perfectly with the fluffy naan or steamed rice.

The Ambiance and Service:
The restaurant has a warm and inviting ambiance, with subtle touches that hint at its regional focus. The service was attentive and knowledgeable, happy to explain the dishes.

Final Verdict:
Mustard restaurant offers a fantastic dining experience. While all the dishes were executed with skill, the Damodar Chingri truly stole the show and is a testament to the chef's expertise with regional specialties. It’s a dish that will have me coming back for more. I highly recommend Mustard for anyone looking to enjoy both classic Indian fare and some truly exceptional, flavour-packed regional gems.

Definitely ordering the Damodar Chingri again!
author: Dev008

restaurant_name: Mustard Singapore - Flavours of Bengal & Punjab
review_text:
Coconut curry with shrimp is the best!!
Others are great too, but this is their specialty!! We were 8 people and ordered a lot but all served very quick.
author: Eunji Emily Lee

review_text: Best subway outlets all day everyday. Very impressed w the cleanliness and friendliness of staff. The lady with the scarf led by example w good customer service. Well done to the team! Also the black pepper nuggets are really good; should be a staple combo!
author: Sharina Bynes

review_text: Excellent service from the chinese lady serving today late lunch, good energy, polite and attentive, please give her a raise.
author: Bebe

review_text:
Hi morning
I"m here for my breakfast the lady  Ayu service me is so friendly & patient .
I will be back again for her service.
author: Sharon Sim

review_text:
Both staffs were very friendly, hardworking and have strong customer service skills and a positive attitude.
Marco greeted us as we entered and prepared the sandwiches according to our order whilst Liyana processed the payment and at the same time giving Marco some pointers on wrapping the sandwiches securely. Liyana was professional and very pleasant towards customers and co-worker.
author: M Lee

review_text: For all those of you guys who haven’t been here in a year, the place has changed but just opposite of the OG location in the hallway. The Place has just become better, a new vibe, much more comforting seats but the same vintage drink dispenser. Mr Ali who was working at about 4:30 on 24/12/24 was so nice and friendly. Like usual great service and great food. Loved it!
author: Aviv Mathur

review_text: Old Airport Road Food Center is one of popular places for breakfast and lunch.  There are many nice food around such as Lor Mee, Hokkien Mee, Prawn Noddle, Chicken Rice, Roasted Pork and Duck, Western Food, Wanton Noddle.  There is also a new NTUC at level 2.  This food Center can be quite packed during peaked hours.  If you are around Kallang area, I will recommend you guys to drop by …
author: Louis

review_text:
Old Airport Road Food Centre exceeded my expectations with a great variety of Singapore heritage dishes. I also loved the creativity behind many stall names referencing places like Chong Pang, Kallang, and Blanco Court — adds local charm.
•	Old Airport Road Fried Hokkien Mee (#01-99) – 4/5: Wet-style Hokkien Mee with decent wok hei, generous prawns, good value.
•	Famous Old Airport Fried Oyster (#01-101) – 3/5: Soggy omelette, overcooked prawns, not worth $10.
•	Chong Pang Huat BBQ (#01-90) – 3/5: Expensive, small portions, hygiene issues.
•	Jin Fried Rice (#01-63) – 5/5: Fragrant mala fried rice with pork chop — excellent, must-try.
•	Chuan Loo Bee Hokkien Food (#01-111) – 2/5: Tough pork ribs, odd sauce, disappointing.
•	Whampoa Soya Bean (#01-68) – 4/5: Solid traditional desserts; soya drinks slightly diluted.
•	Unkai Japanese Cuisine (#01-88) – 5/5: Generous salmon bowl, wallet-friendly, satisfying.
•	Western Barbeque (#01-53) – 3/5: Chicken chop okay but lacks flavour; queues are long.
•	Famous Kallang Airport Fried Oyster (#01-55) – 2/5: Oily, overwhelming, still hunting for a better version.
•	Salt (#01-128) – 4/5: Aglio Olio with teriyaki chicken — decent but slightly pricey.
•	Yi Ji Fried Prawn Noodles (#01-73) – 3.5/5: Carrot cake decent, noodles not outstanding.
•	Xin Mei Xiang Lor Mee (#01-116) – 4/5: Double Fish Lor Mee decent; broth mediocre, some service issues.

Overall, a must-visit for variety and heritage flavours, though some stalls are hit-or-miss. Will keep exploring and updating!
author: WanderWithWit

review_text: One of my favourite food centres. Great selection and food. Easy to get to via Bus 36 from Changi. Due for a nice power cleaning though.
author: FTS

review_text: Finally, I managed to taste the famous kway chap here, and it is time to review this food centre. The quantity is there, and the quality? Well, its pretty much there, although most of the stalls there do not impress me. The crown of the jewel here is probably the To Ricos Kway Chap. Long waiting times, short opening hours and no lack of michelin bib gourment awards. There is another kway chap stall here, but i seriously do not recommend it. The char kway teow here? Nothing really impressive either. And I mean both stalls. There is a ngoh hiang here that is rather cheap and has no lack of customers.Taste wise, I feel that it is a little lacking. There is also a hand made chee cheong fun here that I really like. This stall also serves a modest portion of congee which i feel is worth the money. You can pretty much find all of Singapore's local fare here. From hainanese curry rice, mutton doup to chicken rice. The variety available here is staggering. Most of the food here is at least of average standard, and this is why it gets a 4 star rating. This is hands down one of my favourite hawker centres is Singapore.
author: Hatsune Miku

review_text:
Great hawker centre but it can get a little stuffy. Try to grab one of the round tables by the entrances or near the ventilation areas for more space and cool air.

Loved the lor mee! Char koay teow and prawn mee we’re decent too.

If you’re getting ais kacang or cendol, get it from the popular stall in the middle to avoid disappointment!
author: Andrew P

review_text: Food was served to us efficiently. Crinkle cut fries were chunky delicious and goes well with chilli and ketchup. I like that the whipped butter is concealed    and have the option to put my preferred amount of butter into the corn. Generous amount of tartar sauce in the fish fillet burger.
author: Lisa T

review_text: We just ordered a mc nuggets meal via drive through. We got 4 nuggets in the box instead of 6 nuggets and we got curry sauce when we specifically asked for barbecue sauce!! It’s not even a crowded day. There weren’t even cars after us.
author: Karen Koh

review_text: Among the many McDonald’s outlets in Singapore, this one is exceptional for its generous space and pleasant atmosphere. It never feels crowded, making it an ideal place to enjoy a calm breakfast. I regularly had my breakfast here during my stay in February 2026 and always had a good experience.
author: Deshani Bandara

review_text: They have always kept their standard and this is something I appreciate as I know where I can get my comfort fix :)
author: Ann Teo

review_text:
Booked their party package for kids (15 pax min) for my daughter's birthday on a Saturday. Added on the cake and balloon sculpting. Party room is located away from the main area near the indoor playground. Environment was clean, cooling and private enough with a basin in the room convenient for handwashing. The room accommodated 13 kids and around 20 adults comfortably standing, and around 20 pax comfortably for eating. Bill came up to $600+ inclusive of food for the adults, balloons, happy meals and a party pack for each kid (Drawing Pad, Illustrated Book, McDonald's Table Mat, Minecraft Toy), and the session was for 1h 45m.

Only comments I have is that the games played are more suitable for ages 6 and up (Charades/Musical chairs), and the toilets are limited. I would also recommend bringing your own cake as well as the McDonald's chocolate cake was basic.

Jiha, Friya and another lady supervisor (didn't get her name unfortunately) were assisting us and facilitating the party. They were accommodating with our requests, friendly with the kids and pleasant in our interactions!

You can't go wrong with the food (they take your orders and it's brought out to you), there's ample parking, the location is easily accesible and there's a baby care room just beside. I'd definitely recommend having a party here for a no-frills experience!
author: kevinnihc

review_text:
This is sensational dimmy!

It may have been a combination of the time of day and there only being a few occupied tables; because the food came out fast and piping hot.

My client and I came here for a late lunch and it was so good that we are both looking to have another meeting so we can return ASAP.

Normal dim sum gets wheeled around on a trolley in endless laps of the restaurant - even though everything is sealed and steamed it isn’t always hot; but Joyden brought everything hot straight to the table.

Sui mai, char siu, BBQ pork buns and prawn dumplings were all standouts. The showstopper though was the Lobster noodles; we shared half the lobster each and both had gorgeous noodles underneath.

The staff were also fun and friendly with good banter!
author: Dan P

review_text:
Came here for their Lobster Porridge as it was highly recommended by one of our friend and also wanted to patronize this restaurant after i had a rather good lunch experience at Joyden Canton Kitchen in Hillview.

Well, their Lobster Porridge was overall ok, Lobster meat was tender, firm with slight seafood food sweetness but broth for the porridge was abit too bland… lacks sweetness (Lobster broth should have) and could do with a little bit more salt.

The rest of the dishes that we ordered (Trio Of Eggs And Wolfberry With Seasonal Vegetable In Superior Broth, Beancurd and Black Pepper Beef Tenderloin) were Average but were more well balance than the Porridge.

I personally liked their Yam Ring with Sweet and Sour Pork as the Yam Ring was Crispy on the outside and inside packed with smooth creamy Yam… Sweet And Sour Pork had also crispy outer crust and tender inside.

Their Signature Braised “Tai-O” Fish And Seafood Vermicelli was the next good dish. Its well cooked and flavourful.

Overall, Service staffs were friendly, patient and attentive, but would prefer them not to have more than 2 staffs clearing the table, as its rather overwhelming and uncomfortable, when we just finished our last bite, sipping hot tea and wanted to chit chat for just awhile.
author: Bernard

review_text:
Had Mothers Day dinner celebration here and was quite a pleasant dinner. Most of the dishes were really good.

The braised chicken dish was so flavourful, and the chicken has absorbed all of the essence in its meat. The lemongrass pork rib in the yam ring was mindblowing.

The pork ribs had a slightly fragrant lemongrass taste, and combined with the yam ring, it was such a delight.

Every dish that came up continued to impress, and I must say it was a very, very scrumptious dinner.
author: SL Wong

review_text: Restaurant is spacious and can host big tables and families. Food is good and classic, not the best but classic enough. Famous for their crab beehoon but we found the beehoon abit too hard that day, have had better ones so could be a hit/miss depending on the day itself.
author: J. L.

review_text: We never even knew that restaurant was there. Lunch time and total surprise. What we had was delicious. Service was good too … atmosphere could be a bit more… warmer and restaurant like. Will come again to check out more dishes
author: GA YA

review_text:
Date: 15 Feb 2026
Time:6.30pm
Person: 4pax
Crowded: No queue required.

This is the old restaurant, initially located at 2nd floor of Kallang Leisure Park mall, now they moved down to ground floor.

Overall food taste still good, no crowded during weekend too. Suitable for family lunch and dinner.

Do note the dim sum only until 5pm.

Environment also good, but I think they don't have vip room.

Price are consider acceptable. Average sgd 30 to 40 per pax
author: William Tan

review_text: The five stars are thanks for the memories. As a long time customer of the Joyden brand since their West Coast days, I have decided to stop patronizing them after this. The prices now are exorbitant, four dishes and three drinks adds up to close to $200. And of course the portions have all shrunk, and the food has lost its flavours. Neither is the fish ‘live’ fresh. Consolidating your business after so many closures and this is the end product - nothing but utter disappointment. Thanks but never again.
author: Clement Ng

review_text:
We have been patronising Joyden Seafood for more than a decade but this is closed.

This review is for Joyden Canton, a new outlet, and is our first visit.  We ordered four items of dim sum and it was pretty bad.  The dim sum was served hot which is good but the food is too salty especially the har gao and lacks flavor.  The steamed pork ribs is out of tangent, super oily and 90% pork fat and the pieces are not properly sliced.  Look at how the siew mai is presented.

On checking out, the cashier said the chef is from Hong Kong.  Rather disappointing and far from the excellent Hong Kong dim sum.
author: Y Teo

review_text: Food is not good and expensive. Outlet is newly decorated so ambiance is ok. Won’t come again. Bean curd roll has a layer of flour coated. Xo carrot cake is worst than hawker center with no xo taste at all, not crispy just put together. Service is so so, meat ball porridge is really plain porridge with meat ball added. The is no taste to the porridge and meat ball  is hard
author: eve.koh @ascendmktg.com

review_text: Was here on Mother’s Day weekend and the food took quite a while to be served. Every dish we ordered was delicious except the olive fried rice. It was too oily and salty for us.
author: Wong

review_text: Very friendly and quick service. The chicken was soft and tender and the rice was the stand out, full of chicken flavour in the rice. The only complaint is the amount of meat is too little.
author: Derrick L

review_text:
I ordered the chicken rice set. Chicken + rice was decent, but they didn’t give me breast meat as requested instead the drumstick and wing which is full of bones. The quality of their work is questionable as I had charsiew stains on my chicken and some of the veg looked abit old.

I think the worst part is probably the attitude, the lady did a rude “what?” and walked off as the man took over. They also gave attitude as they served me, I’m not sure why as i went on an off-peak time and there was no other customer pressure. Just a bad experience overall for me and I think it might be better to have my chicken rice fix at another stall next time.
author: c lex

review_text: Not my favorite, but definitely my go-to chicken rice spot in this neighborhood. It's a no-frills, above-average plate of chicken rice—good enough to bring your foreign friends for a taste our Singapore Chicken Rice standard. Be prepared for a regular stream of customers and a bit of a wait.
author: Steveo 88

review_text: Charsiew Wonton Mee ($4) Charsiew was on the meaty side but still tender and delicious. Wonton was okay. Generous portion of noodles and the sauce they were tossed in (say yes to the chilli!) was quite delicious. Overall, for this price, wouldn't mind coming back regularly for a good and affordable meal. Minus points for atmosphere as there were a steady stream of birds terrorising the area.
author: Darren

review_text: decent chicken rice. ordered the roasted drumstick and roast pork for $6. meat was ok sufficient but be full. but felt that the rice was a lil plain and dry. it was served with soup so that helps a lil.
author: Mao

review_text:
Thank you again for a wonderful end to end experience with Fortville. This is by far one of the best temporary stay experiences we have.

From initial apartment viewings, checking in, stay and checking out, everything was seamless and easy.

The environment is clean and staff are friendly. I’ll highly recommend to friends and families should they need accommodation.
author: Cindy P

review_text: Fortville (@ Fort Road) offers well-maintained, comfortable accommodation options at a very competitive price point. The staff are also very approachable and helpful. I enjoyed my stay here and would certainly return when I’m back in the country.
author: Alston Ng

review_text: Visited to inquire about longterm stay and was welcomed warmly by their male staff. The rate is reasonable and near bus stop and new train. Location is near a lot of good cafes, few bus stops away.
author: Keena Ivane

review_text:
Very pleasant 9 day stay. Helpful, friendly staff and clean, comfortable room with 2 AC.
Kitchen was well equipped and we were pleased to have a washing machine too.
The pool was a great extra.
author: ja h

review_text: This is my first time to stay in a Serviced Apartment and I must say it exceeded my expectations. Fortville’s location was great, close by the metro station and bus stop. Travelling to any where in Singapore is a breeze. The rooms are spacious and it is much better than staying in a hotel. The room is well maintained with housekeeping too. You just need to bring your own toiletries and make your own breakfast but hey it’s very convenient. On top of that booking and check in/check out process was easy. All the staff were very friendly. It made my week vacation in Singapore awesome. Highly recommended and would definitely book again.
author: Ed Ereno

restaurant_name: Café Melba at Goodman Arts Centre
review_text:
Big thank you to the team for making my daughter’s birthday celebration such a success today! Guests loved the food and kids-friendly environment. Mushroom soup and pizza were a huge hit, Caesar salad was fresh and crisp, and the roasted pork was great!

To the always-smiling Sufyan, a lovely and helpful gentleman who helped with the event planning and great food recommendations. Even assisted us with the additional bouncy castles we brought for our guests whenever required in view of the weather.

To the rest of the front and back of house team, thank you for being attentive, hospitable and on point with the food.

Highly recommend this venue. Good food, superb service, kids-friendly, and value-for-money.

I’d only recommend more fans or air-circulation when guests are seated in front of the kitchen, as it can get too warm.
author: Valerie Khoo

restaurant_name: Café Melba at Goodman Arts Centre
review_text: Had their 1 for 1 pizza weekday promotion. We could not finish the pizza. Was larger than expected 14 inch. I enjoyed the truffle pizza the most. We also order the nacho which might have been too much. The area was kid friendly with playing area overall atmosphere was good.
author: Daryl Nonis

restaurant_name: Café Melba at Goodman Arts Centre
review_text:
We tried all the mains from the festive menu and thought they were all well prepared.

They were delicious, and well plated.

The children loved their pasta and pizza from the kids menu. they had 2 orders each because they were tasty.
author: sooyun teng

restaurant_name: Café Melba at Goodman Arts Centre
review_text:
I was here as a family with a 3yo & an infant. We were here after our activities at Goodman art center. We were seated outdoor with reservation on a weekend lunch. The first impression is that this place is extremely under staff. From what we see, there’s only 2 serving staff on the ground (for both indoor & outdoor). The staffs however are trying very hard to keep up the service, however it’s lagging due to headcount. Kudos to them.
1. The chairs outdoor… oh my goodness are littered with bird droppings. They are extremely disgusting & unhygienic. It affected me about the cleanliness for kids.
2. The food came all at once after 25-30min wait. However I ordered a starter, came with the mains too. And you can tell sweet potato fries were left out waiting for the mains as it’s cold & lost the texture).
3. I ordered C.A.T. Sandwich. I was really surprised the toast was burnt & the avocado in it was really bad! It’s honestly the worst smashed avocado sandwich I ever came across. The quantity exceeded my expectations, however the quality is so unpleasant that I wish there’s less of it!
4. My husband ordered the chicken katsu burger & he was looking forward to it because he had it before at the other outlet. However he said that this time it’s such a disappointment & the only good part of it was the buttered bun.
5. The cups for drinking are not maintained at all with tons of residues & chips.

We are really saddened because we really enjoyed the outdoor experience here. However everything else is really creeping me out.
author: Eileen Boey

restaurant_name: Café Melba at Goodman Arts Centre
review_text: My hubby and I come here for dinner sometimes after BFT and the food never fails us!! Good vegetarian options too. It’s quite chill and not crowded on weekday evenings so that’s a nice experience.
author: Leandra Chee

review_text:
My family and I had a wonderful dining experience at this restaurant. The food was absolutely delicious, beautifully presented, and clearly prepared with great care and quality ingredients. Every dish we tried was flavorful and satisfying.

What truly stood out, however, was the impeccable service. The staff, Sheedah especially, were warm, attentive, and highly professional, making us feel genuinely welcomed from start to finish. They were knowledgeable, efficient, and always ready to help with a smile.

Overall, it was a fantastic experience with excellent food and outstanding service. I would highly recommend this restaurant and will definitely be returning again.
author: Nabilah Eddy

review_text:
This is clearly an above average venue, but I’m rating it 4 stars mainly because of how poorly reservations are handled. We tried calling 5–6 times with no answer and eventually had to contact head office, only to be told they don’t take reservations at all. For a restaurant of this caliber, that’s disappointing—especially for large groups. They should seriously consider allowing reservations with a deposit via a payment link for diners who are genuinely committed.

We were welcomed by Linda, who was very accommodating given that we were a large group of 11 there for a surprise birthday celebration. Be aware that the restaurant will not seat you until your entire group has arrived, which made things a bit stressful. That said, Linda relented and we were eventually seated in a back corner that offered some privacy.

Service was mixed. While the food was served promptly, the tone and manner of some of the serving staff came across as curt and unfriendly, which detracted from the overall experience.

Food-wise, the rotisserie chicken, beef pot pie, oxtail stew, salad and other dishes were good, with a special shout-out to the seafood stew, which really stood out.
Chilled flavored drinks were refreshing too.

Ambience was great and allowed us to enjoy a semi-private celebration without booking a private room.

review_text:
Visited A1 Porridge for the first time on Lunar New Year's Eve, and the experience was a mixed bag of pleasant surprises and slight letdowns. Here's a breakdown:

👅 Taste:
The highlight of the visit was undoubtedly the taste of the food. Everything we ordered was flavorful and satisfying, living up to the expectations one would have for a special occasion like Lunar New Year. It's worth noting that despite the holiday period, the prices remained reasonable, which was a pleasant surprise.

🍽️ Ambience:
Here's where things began to diverge from expectations. Given the significance of the date, we anticipated a festive atmosphere, complete with Chinese New Year songs to complement the dining experience. Unfortunately, the place was devoid of music, leading to a rather subdued environment. This, coupled with the fact that only 2-3 tables were occupied, contributed to a quieter ambience than expected. While some may appreciate the calm, it felt like a missed opportunity to elevate the festive mood.

⭐️ Service:
The staff were polite and friendly, which added a nice touch to the overall service. However, there were moments of forgetfulness, such as missing out on our drink orders despite the restaurant not being busy at the time. These lapses were minor but noticeable, especially considering we were the only table at that moment.

💰 Price:
At $36 per person, the meal was priced on the higher end, but considering the occasion and the quality of the food, it felt justified. The restaurant managed to keep the pricing fair even during a high-demand period, which is commendable.

Overall:
Despite the minor hiccups in ambience and service, A1 Porridge offers a good dining experience, especially if you're in the mood for tasty food at a reasonable price during the festive season. While the lack of festive music and occasional forgetfulness in service were drawbacks, the quality of the food and the friendliness of the staff make it worth visiting. It's not every day you find a place that maintains reasonable prices during Lunar New Year without compromising on taste. I'd recommend giving it a try, at least once in a while, for a decent meal that won't disappoint taste-wise.

review_text:
Genie Go’s Classic Kuehs at Old Airport Road! A Taste of Tradition!

In a hawker center as legendary and sprawling as Old Airport Road, it can be easy to overlook the simple, unassuming stalls. But to do so with Genie Go would be a genuine mistake. Specializing in traditional handmade snacks, this stall offers a beautiful, comforting bite of Singapore's culinary heritage.

I managed to snag their very last box of the day—a wonderful medley of mini Ku Cai Kuay and mini Soon Kuay. This smaller size proved perfect for sampling and affirmed the high quality of their craft. Let's be clear: while I wouldn't call them the absolute, hands-down best kuehs I've ever tasted, they are unquestionably good and deserving of a high recommendation.

The Star: Mini Ku Cai Kuay (Chive)
The mini Ku Cai Kuay truly shone. For chive lovers, this is a beautiful rendition. The small size was a flawless two-bite snack, but the most striking thing was how the filling retained its vibrant green colour and surprising crunch. Often, the chives are overcooked into a limp, dark paste, but Genie Go ensures they keep their fresh, slightly peppery kick. This freshness is key! The skin was thin, delicate, and just sticky enough to hold the generous filling without tearing—a true mark of skilled craftsmanship. Paired with a dab of their chili, it was an addictive balance of fragrant spice and herbal brightness.

The Classic: Mini Soon Kuay (Turnip)
The mini Soon Kuay was equally satisfying. The filling of shredded turnip (jicama) was sweet and savory, perfectly seasoned with dried shrimp and perhaps a hint of oil to give it that essential, comforting umami depth. It’s a very clean-tasting kueh, not overly greasy. While I've had versions with perhaps a more aggressive smoky wok aroma, this one excels in its textural softness and harmonious balance of flavors, especially in the delightful mini format.

What makes Genie Go highly recommended is their consistency and quality. These are not factory-made snacks; they are clearly handmade with care. Every miniature piece held its shape perfectly, the skins were thin and translucent, and the fillings were generous. Tip: Getting the mini assortment is fantastic for sharing or just trying both flavors in one go!

In a competitive market like Old Airport Road, sometimes "unquestionably good" is more valuable than trying to be an erratic, one-hit wonder. Genie Go delivers a reliable, delicious, and authentic taste of Teochew and Hokkien snack culture. If you're craving traditional kueh in the East, this is an excellent, solid choice that will leave you feeling warm and satisfied.

Highly Recommended!

review_text:
Review of Salt @ Old Airport Road Food Centre

Salt is a western-style stall at Old Airport Road Food Centre offering a mix of dishes such as spaghetti, chicken chop, herbal chicken recipes, and fried chicken wings — a slightly different lineup from the usual hawker western fare.

I tried the Sous Vide Grilled Chicken with Aglio Olio. The aglio olio was done well, with decent garlicky fragrance and a clean, straightforward flavour that didn’t feel greasy. The chicken chop, however, stood out in an unexpected way — instead of the usual black pepper or mushroom sauce, it was glazed with teriyaki sauce, giving it a sweeter, Japanese-style twist that sets it apart from typical western stalls.

That said, while the execution was acceptable and the concept a little different, the price point of $9.90 feels steep for a hawker setting, especially when portion size and overall complexity don’t quite justify the premium.

Overall, Salt offers an interesting variation on western food, but at this price, it may struggle to compete with other value-for-money options at Old Airport Road.

restaurant_name: Imam Banana Leaf Restaurant Pte Ltd
review_text: Indian curry fish head. Seen this a few times and finally tried it. Portion is huge, this is a whole fish head, enough for a good 3-4 pax though not difficult for me to finish it alone. Only setback is no ladyfingers, brinjal, taupok and taukee. It's a very good curry fish head.

author: Ed K

restaurant_name: Imam Banana Leaf Restaurant Pte Ltd
review_text:
I visited Imam Banana Leaf Restaurant on 14th Dec 2024 @ 10.30pm and had a very disappointing experience. The kitchen was visibly dirty, and I saw the staff handling food with unwashed hands, including picking up sunny-side-up eggs from one plate to another with no gloves or thongs. He used the same unwashed hands to pick up the ingredients and the ladle to continue cooking, simply no hygiene measures.

The staff member, Veera, insisted that 'Daging' (beef) was actually 'Kambing' (lamb), despite the fact that it was clearly beef after we tasted it. My friend is Hindu and he not suppose to eat beef due to religious reasons. When we questioned this, he claimed they only sell "Daging which is lamb" and they have the necessary certificates to prove that is Lamb/Mutton. Come lah even the signboard got put "Daging", "Ayam".

We had to wait more than 30 - 40 minutes for simple Maggi Goreng, Nasi Goreng Kampung and Kway Teow Goreng  and despite being told our food was next to be served multiple times.

When the food arrive, its so high in sodium which is salty. None of us took more than 2 or 3 bites. Not only unpleasant to consume but also concerning from a health perspective.

The restaurant was stuffy and poorly maintained, and there were no clear systems in place for managing orders. There is no menu cards nor pricing of the food stated anywhere on the shop boards.

Overall, it was a frustrating experience, and we left hungry and dissatisfied.

DINE AT YOUR OWN RISK! DON'T SAY WE DID NOT WARN YOU!

review_text: Convenient to order via the QR code and pay at the counter using PayNow. The desserts weren’t too sweet and the chrysanthemum tea was honestly refreshing. I came on a weekday so there wasn’t any crowd

review_text:
It's not cheap, that's for sure! A small serving of dessert costs more than the average economy rice plate, but some of their desserts are worth it.

I highly recommend their yam paste, the steamed milk pudding (oh it's so smooth, and every mouth is a delight), as well as their milk tea guilinggao. Their yam paste is thick, with enough ginko nuts, and it's flavourful to boot. Personally not a fan of their guilinggao on its own, but my partner loves it. It's good, but pricey. However, the milk tea guilinggao is a different beast altogether so I can recommend that.

Though I'll recommend avoiding their other hot desserts like the sesame paste, almond / walnut paste etc. Those are definitely not worth the price charged here. Just go with the few recommended ones. About 10-12mins walk from the MRT, though there's parking spaces nearby, but those fills up fast around dinner time since there's a lot of good food in the area.

review_text: This is a must-visit every time I’m in Singapore. The frog meat is always fresh, tender, and perfectly cooked, with no gamey taste at all. The sauce is rich and aromatic, pairing beautifully with the smooth, comforting porridge. I personally prefer this place over Eminent, the flavors here are more balanced and satisfying. Simple, local setting, but consistently great food. I never skip this spot when visiting Singapore.
author: Mimi

review_text: This is where I often go to eat the famous Singapore frog porridge. I just came back and felt the taste of the dish is still great. The service is very fast, professional, reasonable price. The restaurant is clean and the staff is quite enthusiastic.
author: FrancisP

review_text:
Servers were readily available and took orders rapidly. The porridge smooth, had a claypot taste to it which was unique; higher end restaurants sometimes use milk to smooth out the texture.

The frog was really fresh, springy and chewy, with the cartilage still crunchy.

Bad part is for flavours wise, it is be-your-own-chef and add your own amounts of soy sauce and ginger. So you do not really get to know the chef’s skill.
author: Benedict Chua

review_text:
Ordered the ginger onion frog legs (2 servings - $22) and porridge ($11) which was enough for 2 people. The frog legs are tasty and the muscle fibers are slightly shorter than chicken and have a flakiness like fish. Meat falls off the bones easily. I enjoyed it.

Prefer to eat the porridge and frog legs separately because the sauce of the frog legs will make the thick porridge more watery.

Fast service - ordered and paid soon after we were seated. Staff was helpful in her reccomendations which helped as it was my first time trying frog leg porridge.

Seated outside which was quite windy that night. Good vibes and breeze.

Crowded at 7 but still got a seat outside
author: Ellen

review_text:
1. The outdoor space is airy but the hot and humid climate of Singapore makes you feel a bit stuffy when sitting outside.
2. The best sellers of the restaurant are frog porridge and oyster fried eggs. Frog porridge is cooked differently from Vietnam. Not too many spices but very hot.
3. The staff is very enthusiastic. Please bring dry tissues and wet towels to wipe your mouth after eating. The restaurant does not have them.
author: Trịnh Minh

review_text: It is Michelin recommended place, hard to image the place is still with so many people during the middle of the night. Food is ok and a little too salty for me but the whole place and its surrounding environment are very interesting and charming in a way. No wonderful it can get Michelin recommended.
author: Daniel Wang

review_text:
Terrible service with a wrong order.

We were a group of 6 adults (only 2 of us eat frogs) and we ordered as follows:

1. The 3+1 frog promotion, cooked into 2 claypots, including 2 spicy frogs and 2 non-spicy frogs (25 SGD – Buy 3 Get 1 Free = total 4 frogs).
2. 2 portions of porridge (Large size 4 SGD per portion = 8 SGD).
3. 1 small portion of fried squid with salted egg sauce (15 SGD).
4. 1 small portion of seasonal mixed vegetables (10 SGD).
5. 1 Water chestnut drink and 1 coconut. The other 4 drinks would be ordered later.

After waiting more than 30 minutes outside and more than 20 minutes at the table, we received the following:

1. They served 5 coconuts and 1 water chestnut drink. I told them that it was incorrect — we only ordered 1 coconut and 1 water chestnut drink. The rest would be ordered once everyone arrived.
2. Next, they served 2 claypots of frogs with quite a large portion, so we assumed the serving size was simply big.
3. However, when it was time to pay, they charged us for a different package: Buy 6 Get 3 Free – Total 54 SGD — meaning one pot had 5 frogs and the other had 4 frogs.
4. Although we had confirmed at the beginning that there would only be 4 frogs divided into 2 pots, when the bill (plus VAT) came out, they insisted that we had to pay because we had already eaten the frogs.

We were very disappointed because the service felt like a scam. We hope the owner can better train the staff to reconfirm orders clearly. Hopefully this review will help others be more careful when placing their orders.

Regarding the food quality, we really liked the smoky flavor and the combination of oyster sauce mixed with hoisin sauce for the frogs.
author: Anh Nguyen

review_text: Had the frog porridge with garlic & pepper and frog with chicken essence — both were amazing! The garlic & pepper version was fragrant and slightly spicy, while the chicken essence one had a rich, herbal aroma and super tender frog meat. The porridge was smooth and comforting, perfect for mixing with the sauce. The tofu side dish was crispy outside, soft inside, and drizzled with a tasty sweet-spicy sauce. Portions are generous, service is quick, and everything came piping hot. Definitely one of the best spots for frog porridge in Singapore! 🐸🍲🔥

review_text: Food-wise, I would give it a 4 out of 5 stars. The portion is generous, and the price is very reasonable. The cold appetizers were very well seasoned, with the exception of the slightly salty cucumber. However, hygiene standards must be improved. During our meal, we were greeted by two rodents. One was roaming inside the private room we reserved, while the other was outside. Understand that it’s a old shophouse and the restaurant did their regular checks, but it just wasn’t a pleasant experience.
author: Lauren Tan

restaurant_name: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup 陳生成山瑞补品
review_text: My family and I visited Tan Ser Seng Herbal Restaurant in Singapore, and it was a unique experience. The atmosphere is traditionally Singaporean-Chinese, very communal and focused on sitting down to enjoy a hearty meal. The food was lovely, with large portions. We tried the black chicken soup and the turtle soup—both were interesting, and the herbal elements are said to help if you’re feeling under the weather. Overall, the food was enjoyable, and it was definitely an interesting dining experience!
author: Joshua Lee

restaurant_name: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup 陳生成山瑞补品
review_text:
A continuous stream of customers usually signals great food, and this place is no exception.

The Soups are the main draw! Indeed the Cordyceps and Ginseng chicken soups are rich, robust, and incredibly soul-warming. We also loved the Turtle soup—it’s loaded with ingredients and has a soothing, herbal finish.

Don’t skip the sides: the Chai Poh Omelette is fluffy with a perfect crunch, and the Spinach Tofu gets a "zesty" upgrade thanks to a Thai-style chili relish. Whether you choose plain or yam rice, every bite is an umami bomb. Definitely worth a return visit!
author: milestone check

restaurant_name: Tan Ser Seng Herbal Soup 陳生成山瑞补品
review_text:
🍜 I have ordered a few of their signature dishes
🌟 Nourishing Claypot Turtle Soup (S$28/Small) - The small size is HUGE—more than enough for one person!  Sweet, smooth, and the herbal taste is just right—not too overpowering.  They are generous with the meat! The best part is the turtle skin, which has a super Q and jelly-like texture, almost like sea cucumber! So much collagen!  You MUST try it with their chili sauce! It’s spicy and slightly sour, the perfect complement to the meat and skin. 🍳 Aged Preserved Radish Omelette (S$10) Fried to perfection! The salty aroma of the preserved radish with the fluffy egg is an amazing combination. Super addictive! 🍚 Yam Rice (S$1.6) - A classic! Fluffy rice mixed with yam and mushrooms, topped with crispy shallots. A great side dish. 🍵 Homemade Ginseng Chrysanthemum Tea (S$2.4) - A refreshing and light floral drink to cleanse the palate after the rich soup. Highly recommended! 💰 Price & Value - My meal cost around S$40++. Considering the generous portion and incredible taste, the price is definitely reasonable. It explains why they are crowded from the moment they open!

author: Sylvia Ang

review_text:
​If you are looking for an authentic and reliable spot for crab in Singapore, look no further than No Signboard Seafood in Geylang.
​First off, the pricing is completely transparent—everything is clearly listed on the menu, so there is no need to worry about hidden costs. The Sri Lankan crabs we ordered were incredibly fresh and meaty. We chose the Chili Crab and the Black Pepper Crab, both of which were spectacular. The chili sauce had the perfect balance of sweetness and spice, and mopping it up with mantou was a highlight of our meal. The black pepper sauce was equally impressive—aromatic, bold, and perfectly seasoned.
​The service is thoughtful and professional. They provide boxes for your bags and backpacks to keep them clean, along with aprons, gloves, and specialized tools to extract every bit of meat from the crab.
​However, what truly stood out was the kindness of the staff. As we finished our meal, a heavy rainstorm started. Being tourists, we were caught unprepared without umbrellas or raincoats. One of the staff members noticed our predicament and kindly gifted us a raincoat and an umbrella. We were so touched by this gesture! It turned a stressful moment into a wonderful memory. We highly recommend this place for both the incredible food and the genuinely caring staff.
author: Hoàng Vũ Trịnh

review_text:
My husband and I were very satisfied with the meal. The chili crab and bamboo clams were very fresh and delicious. The staff were friendly and enthusiastic. I was impressed that they proactively offered to take pictures for us when the crab dish was brought out.

The meal was a bit pricey but worth it
author: Thư Bùi

review_text:
This is the locals preferred spot over JUMBO.

The crabs are big and incredibly meaty, definitely choosing the best ones for their chilli crabs!! We chose a package which included both the chilli crabs and the white pepper crab, both nice, but my preference would be the OG chilli.

My favourite dish was the egg yolk lobster (not sure the official name), perhaps my personal preference, but for me Singapore is the king of egg yolk flavoured anything.

The other side dishes were nice accompaniments to break apart the flavours of the sea food, but it’s clear what their specialty is.

If you want to try chilli crabs, this is a great spot.
author: David S

review_text:
I had no idea there was a seafood restaurant located in the middle of Geylang road. The alfresco dining area basically feels like road being fenced with a cover and a lot of floral decorative lights around. So one may like it if he is reminiscent of the older Singapore.

We started off with Yu Sheng. We were distracted with a sudden recording being played. When the waitress served the yusheng, she poured the ingredients and asked us to just listen to the recording, which is totally robotic and not in sync. We told her this is the first time we have yusheng in this manner. Without the live spoken greetings is half the experience gone! Her face turned black and replied that if she had to do this, she would lose her voice very fast! The yusheng price is similar to that of a restaurant so we did not think it was something that we should not expect. We feedback to another female staff on this matter. Especially we were having our foreign friends who are visiting Singapore for the first time and we wanted them to experience louhei during the CNY period. We gave our feedback to another female staff who immediately apologized and gave a brief explanation for the greetings.

The star dishes are the crabs. The ginger white pepper crab tastes better than the chili crab. Though the chili crab sauce is always good with the deep fried mantou. Another nice dish is the drunken prawn and the prawns taste sweet.

The claypot tofu, 3 eggs spinach, yam paste are decent. I did not like the sweet and sour pork.

#nosignboardseafoodatgeylang
#traveliscallin
author: Ying Ying Chan

review_text:
Excellent food. My partner and I came here randomly.

Fresh ingredients, great ambience and perfect presentation. The staff was enthusiastic and very engaged.

We will be back!
author: Justin Alejandro Lladoc

review_text: Came here for lunch as a group, and I have to say that this place's atmosphere has largely improved compared to the last time I came here. Lights became brighter, increasing the vibrancy of the place. Not to mention that there is also music playing in the background. The waiters had a very good attitude and were very enthusiastic. Moreover, the food is equally nice. The lamb skewers were tender and well-seasoned, easily one of the better lamb skewers that I have eaten. The cereal prawn is fragrant and incredibly succulent, also being well-plated. Shredded potatoes were savory with their sour and spicy flavor. Their grilled fish is unique in flavour, different from other restaurants', also being grilled to its finest, crispy on the outside, soft and delicate in the inside. Overall, an excellent experience and definitely recommended to others looking forward to a conducive dining experience.
author: Jason Tan

review_text: ABSOLUTELY AMAZING! The roast lamb was juicy with glossy skin, and the crispy barbeque ripped perfectly with each bite. It is authentic and focused on incredible flavor. A must try for BBQ lovers.
author: Cooper Wan

review_text: Amazing food and menu. Mostly Chinese speaking staff but it was fine. Love this place! The plates are so cute and we got some delicious spices to eat our food with. Lots of great drink options too. Love the art in here it’s got a lot of character

review_text: Able to bbq lamb leg on coals is special. Good size leg of lamb, bbq and carved at the table. So very good, please look photos. Good atmosphere, Owner looked after me, I felt special, thank you.
author: Ben

review_text: Fast and good service. All dishes very tasty. We liked the sprinkle powder and condiments. Meat skewers were really tasty w fats between it for flavour and moisture. Lamb leg was really good and glad they cut it for us once we're don't carving on the grill. Side dishes were good too.
author: Dean Aw

review_text:
1st time to Skewer Bar. Simply fell in love with the place n vibe. A Japanese styled Izakaya bar. The owner n chef recommended some unique dishes like bacon tempura and ngoh hiang maki. The bacon tempura was crispy but not oily. You wouldn't even notice it's bacon. Goes so well with beer. The ngoh hiang maki rolled with prawn s also light n flavorful. A playful change from e usual mski roll. Love it! Monday n Friday offer 1 set for 1 set free oysters. We had e Canadian oysters. Yuzu n Ponzu tastes.
The Bar has a good list for drinks. I like it that they serve e beer ice cold in a iced glass. Thumbs up. This s how beer should be. Drinks r reasonably priced. So are the food menu.
U can choose to sit indoor or outdoor. Outdoor is great especially after November rain with e cool weather.
This place s gem. Near to Aljunied mrt. No drink n drive 😅
Sure to come again.

review_text:

Foods are really tasty and unique! Strongly recommended chawanmushi as owners added quail eggs, century egg and salted eggs.
Basically i love all their foods on the menu! Potatoes salad, ngoh hiang maki, otah egg roll...
etc...
Service are really good as well... Sake, highball and beer are fantastic too! Reasonable price!

review_text: 1st time visiting this lovely place. Some interesting items such as bacon wrapped lychee, grilled avocado and taopok. You can choose air con or outdoor dining.

review_text: Doesn’t disappoint. Great place to chill and hang out, doesn’t quite too noisy or rowdy. Good food, good drinks.
author: Dennis Yeo

review_text:

Service was ok, but i hope the young lady server can be friendlier. Price was ok, paid $69 for 2, but ordered no alcohol.

Overall, I will come back! This place is a hidden gem.
author: Willdy Cheng

review_text:

The prata quesadilla is very interesting and the ranch burger superb. The mee siam is v nice.

Really like the pet meals too!

review_text: Brought the missus and furbaby for dinner.  Indoor was cooling. Food was a lil long because of the crowd but manageable. Overall very pleasant experience. Rigor and Jimica were very attentive and portray very good customer service. Thank you for the great evening!
author: Kwee Woon Chua

review_text: Nice ambience and good food. Very creative in reusing instruments as furniture. Service was excellent. My puppy also loves the food. 👍

review_text: Dog friendly restaurant both inside and outside! Ample amount of parking both at the restaurant compound or just across the road. Lovely to sit outside on a cool evening. The common bar food like chicken wings, fries etc are really good. Some of the main course menu items can be hit or miss but overall still a really nice place to be at for dinner when it’s not too warm.
author: Teck Boon

review_text:
This is a dog friendly cafe and also along the Marina Bay park connector walking route. So can stop by for a meal before continuing or end the walk here.

There is outdoor and indoor sitting. We opted for indoor. Very warm service staff who explains the menu when asked.

I had the salmon and avocado sandwich and it was a good and hearty one.
author: Trotting Horse

review_text: This is the closest to an American style thin crust like Blaze pizza that I've had in Singapore.  The proportion of sauce and cheese and sauce are a bit the sparse side but good for a crisp crunch and clean taste. I wish we could have a quieter environment to eat in but in the atrium of a hdb you really have little choice. I would recommend if you want to quench that Blaze fix.
author: Ning An

review_text:
Honestly…. Really wanted to enjoy this little hidden find.

Pizza’s are homemade but that’s really the only good thing I can say about it. Can imagine it’s a nice hangout/convenient spot for residents to get their pizza fix but other than that… will give it a miss.
