author: jeremy tang

review_text:
I used to go Penang frequently for biz trips…and I missed their Penang CKT.
And thru fren recommendations… came here to try their Penang CKT.
I was blown away.  This is one of the best Penang CKT in Spore.  (Better than Penang Kitchen at Far East Plaza). Here, this dish has wok hei, generous pork lard bits (that’s freshly fried not kept overnights), and rice noodles were flavorful and not too oily.
If only Spore allow duck eggs, then this is as good as one gets in Penang (where the latter use duck eggs to fry)
The other dish I had is the handmade prawn roll.  This dish is quite common in Spore, so nothing special to me.
I will be back to try other dishes…!!!
author: YL Wong

review_text: It was a delightful experience! The prawn was irresistible to eat and the flakes on it were crispy too! An extra bonus. The volcano chicken made everything better! The jaw-dropping show made me fascinated ! The flames rose to the very top and created a smoky smell. The fire was ENORMOUS! The chicken was juicy and crunchy at the same time! It was also air conditioned which made cooling breezes of air flow around my family and I like the breeze.
author: Whiskers Ruffles

review_text: Food is value for money at this restaurant setting. Chilli and other condiments are on self service. I hope the restaurant could provide a box of tissue on every table. May need to reserve table for weekend. The toilet requires revamping.
author: H26

review_text:
Went at about 1245pm on a Sat afternoon. Didn't make any reservation and staff indicated we could be seated indoor.

Ordered medium portions for assam laksa, char kway teow and nan ru fried pork. The char kway teow had some smokey wok flavour. The taugeh was firm and crunchy, there's lap cheong, pork lard, egg, prawns and tiny cockles. I liked the assam laksa more as its broth was so appetising. The nan ru pork was well fried but not too strong of a flavour.

Overall, food was tasty and staff that attended to us, was friendly.
author: purple taste

review_text: The assam laksa was so delicious, with huge pieces of makarel and a scrumptious sour broth. Sooo good! Worth the 8 dollars. The char kway teow also had a lot of wok hei and hum! Great!
author: Tania Koh

review_text: No crowd when I came on Sunday morning before 10am, it’s like 10% occupied. Ordered the local recommended pork rib prawn noodle, I selected soup version. Inside the restaurant it’s clean and considered comfortable. On the table a container is provided for pran shell and bones, I found this very well organized. For tourist, beware that it’s not a common practice that the restaurant provide tissue paper or napkin so bring your own especially when you come to this kind of food place where potentially you use your finger to unshell the prawn. Outside the shop at the front entrance there is a big garbage bin when I walked passed i can smell the odor. I came from the back and left from the front, if I came from the front with this smell, it would probably affect my appetite. But from the back was much better as I saw crows bitting dead rat just right in front of me on the pedestrian path. The noodle taste average for me (for malaysian please don’t expect the same taste like our prawn noodle), the broth has some umami but can taste the sweetness was not from the bone or prawn but rather sugar or rock sugar. The broth is lacking the “spices kick” if to compare with prawn noodle from different countries in the region. The prawn texture was good, probably it’s boiled before putting into the noodle. The pork rib was tasteless and texture a bit too lean in my opinion, not recommended. Afterall if you haven’t tried Singapore prawn noodle, it’s ok to experience it but my suggestion just take the prawn noodle, pork rib is not necessary it’s not adding any positive element to the dish.
author: siauhwa tew

review_text:
> Fresh and firm prawns with a rich, flavourful soup that isn’t too heavy. Classic, satisfying bowl of prawn mee — portions a little small but taste makes up for it.
Chilli wise, not quite the level I like n prefer.
Less crowded as I came on a Sunday afternoon.
author: Ars 3276

review_text: Update on their prawn mee, ever since their michellin awarded last year the taste still taste the same very scrumptious. Very deep prawn flavor & peeled for you if order small.  Their Pig tail especially delicious can't wait to go back 🫡
author: Timo

review_text:
That umami-heaven of a prawn broth is what customers would come here for - rich and full of depth and prawn flavour, there are options to have noodles and bee hoon served in it or prepared dry with a mild chili sauce. Both soup and dry versions are garnished with fried shallots, bits of pork lard, crunchy bean sprouts and some kang kong vegetables.

A variety of protein combinations and sizes can be opted for, whether it is only with prawns, mixed with pork ribs, or the more premium Sultan prawns that are larger, meatier, and sweeter than the regular ones. Some of the Sultan prawns also had trails of orange roe in the tails, which has a taste similar to the prawn butter in the heads. 🦐

Further back into the open-air restaurant, one would find a booth selling ngoh hiang prawn crackers by Hock Lian Huat. A variety of ingredients can be chosen, then fried, cut, and served with sweet and savoury dips. Drinks are also available beside the noodle ordering counter. Special thanks to the uncle from the service crew who watched over the food at our table when we were ordering other items, preventing hungry birds from stealing our prized prawns.
author: 葉

review_text: Prawn mee was actually delicious but the pricing was confusing and almost ‘scammy’ (mainly due to the difference between Tiger and sea prawns). The ngoh hiang was mediocre. Place was spacious and breezy.
author: CK C

review_text:
One of the best dim sum place reccomended by my wife. Her last time here was 29 years ago where she tried the HK Char Siew Bao. 29 years later, the bao taste the same as before.

We tried the fried large intestine, juicy and tasted so much like suckling pig. The cold dish pigs ear also taste terrific.
author: T0m2y Ch00

review_text: New and improved menu. Digital online order. Large variety of dimsum available. Opens 24 hours! Hakka Olive congee was nice! Worth a visit if you’re staying in the area. Leave a review for a free drink! ✨⭐️🌟
author: PY Ting

review_text: Probably had my first dim sum over here some 30 years ago, used to be a really old school and nostalgic place but it has since changed to a generic looking shop. Not the best dim sum but still decent, can try if there’s no late night supper choices. I like the chee cheong fan the best, the porridge feels like it’s full of msg but I’m not 100 percent sure.
author: Derrick L

review_text:
126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi (Geylang): Still a Dim Sum Gem, Even with a Modern Makeover! 4.5/5 Stars

Ratings:

• Food Quality: 4.5/5 (Delicious Dim Sum, Fresh and Flavorful)

• Ambiance: 4/5 (Modern, Bright, and Spacious, but Less Rustic Charm)

• Service: 4/5 (Great Overall, Minor Hiccup with Order)

• Value: 4.5/5 (Good Value, 15% Discount with Grab)

• Overall: 4.5/5

126 Dim Sum @ Geylang, also known as 126 Dim Sum Wen Dao Shi 揾到食, is a new place to me. Donkey has been coming here since younger. It's always been a Hong Kong style dim sum cafe, the kind of typical dim sum shop you'd find all over the streets in Hong Kong. I came with Donkey for supper, and it wasn't too crowded.

Donkey remember it used to be incredibly crowded. But when Donkey and I arrived, it didn't seem so busy anymore. The place has been renovated, and it's much brighter and now fully air-conditioned. It was air-conditioned in the past, but it used to be a bit cramped. Now, it's more spacious, and there was plenty of sitting space. No waiting at all. The bright lighting and vibrant color scheme give it a more modern feel. It still has some traditional touches with the murals of dim sum preparation and Chinese artwork, but the rustic charm of the past is definitely less prominent.

They have a huge menu with tons of dim sum to choose from. Donkey and I ordered a selection of chef-recommended dishes and some of our favorites: Signature Tofu, Crispy Radish Cake, Scallop Congee, Spare Ribs, Char Siu Cheong Fun, Chicken Feet, Honey Yuzu Tea (hot), Traditional Coffee, and a Signature Big Bun. We enjoyed all the dishes a lot. I even mentioned that the dim sum here somehow tastes better than some of the other dim sum places we've tried in Singapore. They also have a special sauce and homemade chili that goes perfectly with everything. However, there was a small hiccup. We ordered the fried carrot cake, but they accidentally gave us the fried yam cake instead.

The service was great overall, and the food was good too. Even though it has a more modern look now, the essence of a good Hong Kong dim sum experience is still there. They even have a 15% discount if you pay via Grab.

I would definitely recommend coming here if you're craving dim sum, especially late at night. If not for the slight mix-up with the cake, I would have given this place a full 5 stars.
author: oXRYSTALo Ong

review_text: Very disappointed for the dim sum. The chili peppers were sweet, and chili peppers are the most important ingredient in dim sum. The shrimp dumplings weren't fresh. The xiaolongbao (steamed buns) hadn't been refrigerated for who knows how long; they were very unappetizing. 👎
author: Jessica Chan

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata in Singapore
review_text:
Recently visited Siam Square Mookata at Golden Mile Tower, and it was a great experience! The marinated meats were fresh, flavorful, and grilled perfectly. The dipping sauce was the real star—super tasty and complemented the BBQ so well.
I like that they have multiple outlets, making it convenient to enjoy their food in different locations. The vibe is casual and fun, perfect for gathering with friends or family over a hearty meal.
author: Ying Yong

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata in Singapore
review_text:
Had a decent experience dining here. Food prices aren't expensive and the portions are reasonable, except for their pork belly that cost between $2-3 and only comes in 4 small slices, that was the only dish that I felt was quite pricey.

I just want to point out that this establishment has quite a few cockroaches. While I was dining here, I saw a few baby cockroaches roaming around on the table. I'm guessing they were hiding between the cracks on the table. Towards the end of my meal, one cockroach also went into one of my dishes and I did not finish it after that. It would be great if management could do a better job of up keeping the place and enforcing a more clean and hygienic eating environment.

My favourite item from their menu is the sliced lamb. Great flavour and decent portion. The rest of their meat selections are alright. Their soup is nice too. I usually like to wait till the end of my mookata meal to drink the soup because that's when all the meat juices have mixed with the soup.

If you don't mind dining with a few cockroaches, this place is fine, but I'll stick to other mookata establishments.
author: Bryan Lon

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata in Singapore
review_text:
Would recommend to those who came in pairs to try the Ala carte mookata instead of it's buffet. Some of us may not have a big appetite and yet can have a taste of it. 2 pax may cost about $40+.

The pork meat were well marinated, and we love the pork lard. Besides that, I like to mix the special sauce with the chili sauce to dip with.

I preferred their Lemongrass drink as its refreshing and not too sweet. And lastly one free scoop of ice cream after meal.
author: Euphorie Liew

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata in Singapore
review_text:
Our favorite mookata place! Siam square has several outlets in Sg and the golden mile one is the one we'll go if we want mookata in aircon with the thai vibe!
Friendly staffs, fast service, affordable food with generous portion. Love it more now that they have free ice cream even for non buffet customers!
Love their thai milk tea tower and their special chilli sauce!
author: Cindy Ong

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata in Singapore
review_text:
Walked pass here quite a few times during lunch, decided to check out this place for dinner tonight with a friend. Reached the places slightly passed 7pm and the place was pretty crowded but we didnt had to wait long to get our seats.

Ordering is pretty straight forward. There is a ordering sheet on the table, majority of the dishes on the menu are between SGD$1.80 to $2. Noticed that there are premimum items that goes up to SGD$10 per portion. Our food came shortly after ordering. The marination for the chicken was pretty good, so was the soup. Portion of food was acceptable,room for improvement in terms for service. Staff could be more friendly.

Overall, pretty good dinning experience.
author: Sean Goh

restaurant_name: Sik Bao Sin/Desmond Creation 吃飽先
review_text: First time patronise this homely eating house, the lady boss and staff were friendly. The menu is simple and the dishes we ordered were well executed and served piping hot. We had black chicken soup, sweet and sour pork, steamed pork salted fish and stir-fried kailan. All dishes shone but the star dish would be black chicken herbal soup. Very hearty and black chicken was tender. Sweet and sour pork was meaty and ratio of batter to meat was just right. Definitely so much better than most zi char stalls we had. Stir-fried kailan was beyond my expectations because this type of vegetable is usually bitter but this restaurant did justice to the vegetables. Very crisp and wasn't bitter at all. The steamed pork salted fish was cooked to perfection and not overly salty. We will definitely go back to try other dishes! Kudos!
author: Isabelle Shen

restaurant_name: Sik Bao Sin/Desmond Creation 吃飽先
review_text:
Been wanting to visit this place for some time and a friend from overseas visited and we decided to head to the place.
There is no reservations just walk in, had to call and check and was told most likely would not have to queue but there is an hour dining limit.
Visited on the day the restaurant was partially filled we were able to get a table immediately.  Ordered a few dishes and have to say the wait for the first dish was a little longer than expected. The table next to us came later but got their dish first, and we realized they seem to cook in batches so generally the same dish would come out serving a few tables at one go.
Ordered 5 dishes. Would say we enjoyed the food. Everything was good, but if I have to say the weakest among the 5 dishes probably had to be the ginger chicken. There wasn't any ginger taste, but there was a surprise when we saw cubes in the dish which we thought was potatoes and it turned out to be the ginger! It was quite soft and the taste was quite mild hence the reason why there wasn't much ginger flavor.
Of course for me the star was the sweet and sour pork and the tofu prawn. Even the foreigner commented the dishes had the wokhei and it was good. Our foreign friend loves the beef on the kailan the most as the beef was so juicy and tender.
We ate slightly more than an hour and no one chased us away. I believe though its a "rule" they have leeway if the dishes take longer to be served or we still have food on the table.
Now to the issue of cash payment only. It caught us by surprise as well we only saw it on a note on the wall.
However the auntie mentioned it was their tradition and there is totally no issue with it because there are a few ATM machines just a minute walk away. Very pleasant and nice lady had some small talk with us.
Pretty good food, one of the places with good wokhei and definitely need to bring a group to try out more dishes.
author: Matthew Lee

restaurant_name: Sik Bao Sin/Desmond Creation 吃飽先
review_text: Was recommended this place by a friend. Was surprise there is nice eatery at geylang area.  Ordered a kailan beef, black chicken soup and tofu prawns. The soup was very tasty, kailan fresh (the beef is a little hard), and tofu prawn very good.  Place can be crowded as seats are limited.  Note, cash basis only.
author: teh andrew

restaurant_name: Sik Bao Sin/Desmond Creation 吃飽先
review_text:
A shophouse restaurant serving Cantonese cuisine. No reservations allowed, be ready to queue, eat and go kind of place.

The streamed fish head was very good value for money. At $31, the flesh was tender and the tau cheo gravy yummy. Minced meat with salted fish would have been perfect with porridge but was still great with rice. The beef in the beef with kai lan was genuinely tender and had "wok hey". Prawns with tofu were big and fresh.

Only cash accepted here
author: George Khoo

restaurant_name: Sik Bao Sin/Desmond Creation 吃飽先
review_text:
千万别来吃！😡😡😡
AVOID THIS RESTAURANT AT ALL COSTS. The food is ridiculously salty, and you'll wait at least half an hour for your meal. The entire place is filled with elderly customers, and it's CASH ONLY! Don't be fooled by the Michelin stickers on the door—it's all a marketing gimmick. The fish had a disgusting, muddy taste, like eating dirt, and the fishy smell was overwhelming. I hope no one else has to suffer through this!
author: Potato

review_text: I personally think this is a better pick than Swee Choon. The dim sum and tzi char here far exceeded my expectations. Prices are reasonable and the food is served fresh and piping hot. Staff are overall friendly and the place is pretty clean, and the place has decent space which makes dining inside and outside pretty comfortable.
author: Timothy Khoo

review_text: 1st time here. It’s reasonably priced and delicious. Porridge was perfectly seasoned. Carrot cake and prawn fritters were crispy. My favorite was the Har gow and Siew Mai. Very satisfied. 👍🏻if can’t finish, you can ask styrofoam to pack.
author: Lisa T

review_text:
The food and overall experience were fantastic! It’s a great spot if you’re craving authentic dim sum flavours without breaking the bank. The open-air seating adds to that true local vibe, making it feel casual and familiar, just like the old-school dim sum places.

The porridge was delicious, warm, comforting, and full of flavour. Definitely the dish I’d recommend trying! The portions across all dishes were fairly generous, and everything we ordered tasted fresh and well-prepared.

Prices are reasonable, especially when compared to Swee Choon, offering great taste and good value for money.
author: Jeffrey Ng

review_text: We passed by this place one night and we immediately dined in for lunch the next day. The dimsums were so good. I also loved the pork cutlet with fried rice. Service was fast and we took our time to savour the delicious food. I will definitely consider staying along Geylang and eat at Mongkok again. We spent SGD 59 for food and drinks (4 pax).
author: Charisse Reyes

review_text: Training takes, time, patience and money. I took my time ordering what I thought were going to be 5 total pieces. I had patience while I was questioned about my ordering of my 5 pieces. I was asked to pay before my 5 piece order was presented to me. $27. My 5 pieces turned out to be 17 pieces!!! All very delicious and will be for lunch and dinner later today. My training is complete, on how to order at this fine open air restaurant. The cold Thai milk tea is fantastic!
author: Scott La Bee

review_text: The restaurant is clean and atmosphere is good with polite staff. The food is nice and delicious especially the vegetables sushi. They have new dishes such as bacon wrap asparagus  in some occasion. Overall is good.
author: tienci yang

review_text: When feel like eating vegan food, this the place . Food is nice , not oily n healthy . By the way am not a vegan but their food making is good.

We had the tomyum (not too spicy), fried eggplant (crispy and sumptuous), and olive fried rice (wok-hei taste) and the coral harvest nest (refreshing and yummy). Will definitely be back!

review_text: The food gets a 3.5⭐️ because it was unnecessarily too sweet. I prefer cooking that actually pays attention to detail. The gravy is thick and spiced but in spices and not in the capsaicin way.
author: Farhanah Ross

review_text: One of the better Tulang we’ve had in Singapore - rich, flavorful, and satisfying. We also ordered mee goreng and beehoon goreng. The mee goreng stood out with its bold, well-balanced flavors, while the beehoon fell a little flat and felt like it was missing something. Unfortunately, the mutton chop was a disappointment. The meat was tough, overly sweet, and served cold. Despite that, the Tulang and the carb dishes made the meal worthwhile overall.
author: TTT

review_text: Amazing mee goreng, kway teow goreng and meehoon goreng. I love the cheese fries too..thick cut potatoes. Just amazing. My only shop to visit at this place ever since working nearby
author: BH

review_text: Their lunch special (Monday to Friday) is high in value and quality. Generous portion of lamb and noodle for just 6.90. It also comes with free plum juice and ice cream. The soup is yummy.
author: James

review_text:
Staffs are extremely attentive. My kids always leave happy, they enjoy the red sugar glutinous fried sticks a lot.

Very helpful to elderly who have walking difficulty as well. Staff comes out to the parking to assist.

Food is also value for money. Taste good and look good.
author: amanda toh

review_text: Enjoyed the food very much. Soup was nice and clean and very comforting. Sides and dishes also affordable. Highly recommend
author: S. Tan

review_text: Had the good dinner with friends and the price is not very expensive. The lamb shanks and grill ribs are delicious. Good place to chill and enjoy good Chinese food. Not very sure this delicacy is from south or north China. However, the servers are fast and even we have several rounds of ice cream. Their ice cream taste like Mixue.
author: Serene Goh

review_text: A place to have your Mutton fix. Food is pretty good.
author: Joel Tan

review_text: Our very first trip to this branch as we rarely move around that area.  Love love love the service from the young lady who speaks with a PRC accent.  She was very nice, helpful & patient when we couldn't  find the grab rewards from our phone.  She waited very patiently for us to surf through the maze of information in the grab apps while we stood at a corner in the shop so that she could serve other customers.  When we finally found the 2 reward vouchers, it was really so nice of her to introduce the types of puffs she had in her shop.  We observed that there was quite a constant flow of customers even though the shop has been unfortunately, blocked by the huge pillar supporting the MRT tracks.  If the shop has been located in one of the more conspicuous neighbouring units, we believe that business would have been even better for this branch.  The sardine and chicken curry puffs were delicious.  Highly recommended!
author: Barbette Strauss

review_text: Although their operating hours until 9pm, they stop entertaining customers at 845pm. The staff said that she needed time to count the money for accounting sake算帐. When I finally purchased the curry puff two days ago, it was really tiny and no longer value for money. If this was from central kitchen, it shows that the standard has dropped tremendously and the management is only interested in making more profits with lesser ingredients.
author: MrA

review_text: Friendly and competent staff (super sweet Indian auntie) at the counter last weekend. Help to cut the chicken wings, packed into a box. And also packed curry puffs nicely. Thank you for great service!
author: Karen Ng

review_text:
The food quality at this specific outlet is subpar. I have often experienced several instances esp  weekday mornings, where I received cold nuggets and other fried items. they were consumed immediately upon order

Besides the service, this outlet probably needs a refreshment of look as well

author: Derrick L

author: Yap Kelvin

- soup was very flavorful
- very tender beef slices
- chili adds on to the flavor
- gravy wasn’t too thick and was able to coat nicely with the noodles
- owners were very helpful and courteous
author: Calvin Woo

review_text: Good portion for $7 mixed beef noodles with delicious broth. Would recommend if you are in the area. 8.5/10.
author: D. Lim

review_text: I had the mixed beef soup set meal here and it was absolutely delicious! The broth was rich and flavorful, and the beef was so tender. The lady boss was super friendly and welcoming — her warmth really made the experience even better. Highly recommended!
author: lyon Feye

review_text: KFC located at 190 Stadium Blvd, Singapore 397800. They are newly renovated with super cold aircon and environmental are clean and importantly not so crowded.  But definitely service wait time need to be improved but I would like service staff overall improved.  No more handwashing sink for customers and inconvenient to go toilet to wash especially there is only 1 small sink.
author: Eileen

review_text:
Great service from Manager Jessie — very chirpy, friendly and all smiles. 👏 Keep it up!

The other cashier seemed a little lost and I assume she’s new. Ordering was a bit slow as she wasn’t familiar with some items, but she eventually got everything sorted.

The newly renovated space looks great. It’s spacious with plenty of tables, and the crowd shows it’s popular.
The chicken was excellent — flavourful, tender and well-spiced.

My kids and I had a really good Sunday lunch here.
author: Ars 3276

review_text: Ordered the zinger meal. Burger came very neat. Didn’t much care for the bun, but the rest was good. Chicken juicy on the inside and crispy outside!
author: michael lin

review_text:
🍗 La Zi Ji is next-level crispy, spicy, and aromatic

review_text: Had an incredible dinner at Katsuya with my husband. The space is cozy with warm, welcoming hospitality and great vibes. Chef Kervin truly masters his craft—every dish was flawlessly executed. The ebi was impressively fresh, wrapped in an ultra-thin, crispy batter that let the sweetness of the prawn shine. The unagi was soft, tender, and literally melted in the mouth, packed with deep, savory flavor. The Jeju tomahawk tokujyo was the star of the night—beautifully tender, juicy, and cooked to perfection. An unforgettable meal that we’ll absolutely be coming back for and recommending to fellow food lovers ☺️
author: Wanting Yau

review_text:
Had a lovely time here. Had the tomahawk and hire for us, dory for our kid. The Katsu was fantastic - the best we have had in Singapore! The chef was very friendly and the staff were very accommodating to our young children. We had the most lovely time! Will be back for sure. :)

author: Jamie Kee

review_text:
Popped in today for lunch with a last minute reservation for 2. Ordered the wagyu and rosu and they both didn’t disappoint. Meat was pink on the inside yet cooked to food safety standards. One could see the dedication of the chef to his art in his fastidious preparation. The crunchiness on the outside of the meat met with a succulent core for a perfect mouthfeel. We also added a raw salmon (lightly aburi’ed’) over a cold tofu. That was equally delicious.
Overall, we enjoyed the experience, excellent service and of course the food and left thoroughly sated.

Not the biggest place, but this allows for more intimate service, which was great.  The food was also great, we enjoyed everything we had.  (The lean pork katsu was our favorite.  Was like butter)

review_text: The fish soup was super salty or msg filled, actually pleasantly surprised and found it delicious. Their porridge here wasn’t really porridge but rice with soup, so not my cup of tea. The other dishes were legit good though.
author: Javier Tan

restaurant_name: Hong Qin Fish and Duck Porridge
review_text: Been a customer with my family at this stall for 30 years, ever since it was just a small stall in a small corner coffee shop in its original location. The new location is a lot more spacious and airy. This is by far our preferred fish soup. Don't be fooled by its clear soup - it is tasty without any overpowering meat taste like some other fish soups. The fish portion is ultra generous - no frivolous side dishes to make it appear that the bowl is full of ingredients (the clear soup makes it abundantly obvious just how much fish there is.) Extremely reasonably priced. Never had any experienced of being pushed or pressured to buy their braised items - they ask once, and leave you alone if you decline. Thank you for the heartwarming meal each time we patronise your stall!

review_text:
Punggol Nasi Lemak is always the one we keep coming back to whenever we are in Singapore. It is hawker style, simple and no frills, but somehow it hits the spot every single time even after trying so many other nasi lemak places.

The rice is fragrant with a lovely coconut aroma, the chicken wing is a must, and my favourite is still the ebi chilli with their sambal. Everything just comes together so well and you can pick your own sides which makes it even better.

There is always a queue even for a late dinner but it moves quite fast and it is definitely worth it.
author: Blenda

review_text:
The East Coast branch offers a much better experience compared to the Jalan Besar outlet. The service is faster, the staff are friendlier, and the overall atmosphere feels more comfortable.
I’ve visited both locations, and the East Coast branch stands out. The food quality and service are noticeably better than at Jalan Besar.
author: Tracy Tan

review_text:
I takeaway at least 2X per month from here coz nasi lemak is my favourite.

Service
The staff here is very efficient and fast so even if there’s a queue, it’ll clear pretty quickly (customers need to decide what they want earlier to facilitate this).  They’ll also accommodate any reasonable request (eg:separate pack the chicken wings).

Food
Love their rice (very fragrant and fluffy) and their chicken wings is insanely crispy (really shiok).  The Ngoh Hiang is also very good, but I don’t see much customers ordering this.

Conclusion
A little ex, but worth paying the premium coz it’s nice.  The must order stuff:
1) Chicken Wing - Mac shiokkk
2) Ngoh Hiang - bite into the chestnut and feel the crunch.
3) Egg - ask for runny and let the yolk seep into the rice.
4) Silver Fish - crispy and best combo with the rice & chilli.
author: Eric Lee

review_text: When it comes to Nasi Lemak, it isn't far-fetched to say that everyone in Singapore knows about Ponggol Nasi Lemak. They do a few things consistently well: the coconuty rice, the sambal, and the crunchy fried chicken wings. Among their outlets, the Serangoon and Tanjong Katong locations always attract snaking queues. It is a meal that feels both heartwarming and hearty every single time.
author: CP

review_text:
Ponggol Nasi Lemak Centre sits tucked in the everyday hustle—unassuming frontage, open windows, and the comforting aroma of coconut rice, sambal, and fried goodies welcoming you in. Inside, it’s a blend of hawker energy and family rhythm: metal tables, plastic stools, lunch crowds, and the occasional diner asking in Malay for extra ikan bilis.

They do what they do with no frills but serious care. The nasi lemak arrives with fluffy, fragrant rice, each grain carrying creaminess but not sogginess. The sambal has a measured heat—not numbing or flat but soulful, slightly sweet with a hint of smokiness, picking up complexity at the edges. You’ll find crispy fried chicken with skin that snaps under your fork, ikan bilis that crunch, peanuts toasted, and custard egg just soft enough to ooze without chaos.

What stands out is how the flavours balance—nothing overpowers. The sambal, the rice, the sides—they hold their own but also support each other. It’s not gimmicky; it’s the kind of plate you taste room-by-room, noticing little things you’ll want again.

Service is hawker speed but with care. The workers are efficient without being robotic—tea top-ups come without asking, and they’ll clear tonight’s empty plates to make space for more. Prices stay kind, making this place as satisfying for daily habit as for those occasional cravings.

If you’re around Punggol or passing through and want a solid plate of nasi lemak that hits both heart and hunger, this is one you’ll keep coming back to.
author: Chong Tee Lim

review_text:
New-ish shop. Lok lok is their specialty... but we wanted to try their ala carte M'sian dishes. Friendly boss lady. Free crackers whilst waiting for food.

Ordered KL Hokkien Mee, Penang Fried Kway Teow, BKT (dry), Herbal chicken, Muar Otak, Braised Lobak.

Generally pretty ok. Hokkien Mee had a nice smoky taste. Fried Kway Teow didn't quite have the wokhei but still acceptable. Otak was nice, quite authentic. Lobak quite close to Penang ones. Dry BKT and herbal chicken were so-so, nothing to shout about.
author: Jimmy Liaw

review_text:
Borders close but you can consider dropping by this place for some Malaysia Lok Lok! I feel it’s quite authentic. They offer fried and steamed Lok Lok dishes. Thumbs up for their fried Lok Lok dishes, it was delicious.

Crowded but the staffs were still very attentive to every request of customers. Lots and lots of selection, the prawns were really huge, and it’s peeled! Favorite items included fried crab stick, sliced abalone, luncheon meat, enoki mushroom, cheese tofu and satay! Occasionally, the staffs will also go around serving fried items like seaweed chicken, satay, nuggets, chicken wings, fried tofu skin and etc.

Very satisfied after eating and 3 of us in total drank 9 cups of drinks!! For the buffet, it includes free flow of drinks, from hot beverages to canned drink, and even home made drinks like ice lemon tea and lime juice.

Note: Buffet is for 2 hours! Ice cream is also served at the end. 👍🏼
author: Eileen Neo (Sgsohotleh)

review_text: Comfort Food ! Love the simplicity both of the restaurant and the food. Quality is good and clean. Occasionally Chef will serve you satay and chicken wings and some happening pork strips all deep fried ! Yummy! Buffet served at $25-26 per pax, comes with free flow drinks, ice cream, coffee and also crackers! You can choose your items and just let it boil or put a white peg on the plate to note that you want them deep fried . Look for Kelly who manages e restaurant there. Totally cheerful and nice. Wish there were more outlets like these. Pure and simple everytime !
author: Hua Mulan

review_text: Food was okay, not too bad. Price was actually okay for buffet style for 2 hours. Quite a few variety of food and drinks, even have ice cream, chips and alcohol sold separately. Service was good just that the place was a bit warm and when you leave you will definitely have BBQ smell on you. Overall not too bad.
author: Gabriel Ignatius

review_text:
Tried the KL Hokkien mee and Penang Char kuey teow. They charge a 10% service charge but service can be a little slow.

CKT is not bad, but no wok hey.

Hokkien mee has a lot of pork lard, but it’s too sweet, not fragrant and no wok hey.
author: Benjamin Cheng

review_text:
Absolutely outstanding experience from start to finish. The food was truly marvelous. Deeply flavorful, and clearly prepared with fresh, natural, high-quality ingredients. You can genuinely taste the care in every bite.

The service was exceptional, especially from Akash, who was attentive, welcoming, and made the entire experience even more special.

The Malai Rabri… the best I have ever had in my life.

Highly recommend.
author: Marinna Baretta

review_text: Found this gem, excellent food and services. Love how they introduce the food and type ingredients they use. The Rohan Josh is a must try dishes, they use Australia goat with gamey taste.
author: Achel T

review_text:
I had such a wonderful experience at this Indian restaurant. From the moment I walked in, I could feel the warm and welcoming atmosphere, which made me instantly comfortable. The food was beyond expectations—every dish had so much flavor and was clearly prepared with care. You can truly feel the owner’s passion and dedication in the details, from the way the dishes are presented to the rich, authentic taste.

The highlights for me were definitely the mango lassi, the chicken curry, and the naan. The mango lassi was refreshing and perfectly balanced, the chicken curry was rich, flavorful, and cooked to perfection, and the naan was soft, fluffy, and paired wonderfully with the curry. Together, they made an unforgettable meal.

This was honestly the best curry I have ever had in my life, and it left me with such a memorable experience. I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for authentic, delicious Indian food with a cozy atmosphere. I’ll definitely be coming back again!
author: キムソク神

review_text: A most delightful dining experience. The Northern Indian food was amazing, and warm service especially by Akash of Mumbai was impeccable. Helmed by chefs from India, the kitchen whipped up amazing traditional dishes with heartiness yet with a touch of class....not fine plating a la Masterchef (this is not a fine dining place), but certainly with thoughtfulness. The Malai Chicken Tikka was a family favourite being totally tender, juicy and aromatic...for me, the Vatan Se version was especially memorable as it leaves a unique lightly fragrant aftertaste. The Chicken Dum Biryani was possibly the second favourite dish. I personally love the Tandoori Stuffed Mushrooms being a fan of the fungus, I haven't tasted this in many places. I am told that the chefs use fresh (not frozen) ingredients prepared anew every day - this certainly shines through in every dish. I am not much of a dessert person, so I cannot comment too much although I loved the simple lasso art. For people who drive there, you can actually park in front of the restaurant although places are limited. Otherwise, go to the large carpark nearby...off-street parking requires much chance and skill.

Senior couple are very friendly and always serve with a smile and lots of patience.
One of all time favourite for HKM. The portion is generous! The flavor is rich and really umami! HKM is saucy and served piping hot. Love the chili too! There will be a generous topping of crispy lard pieces.
Best is able to order kosong/plain with no meats.

review_text:
Hoe Fried Hokkien Mee @ North Bridge Road Market & Food Centre

Recently tried Hoe Fried Hokkien Mee at North Bridge Road Market and Food Centre, and I’ve got to say this is one of the best wet-style Hokkien mee I’ve tasted. The noodles are rich, flavorful, and perfectly soaked in savory broth, making every bite really satisfying.

The portion is generous, and they add a sprinkle of crispy fried pork lard on top just before serving, which really elevates the dish. What makes it even better is the friendly and appreciative owner—it’s always nice to support a stall with such great service.

Highly recommended for anyone craving a comforting plate of Hokkien mee!
author: K Tan

review_text:
Good plate of Hokkien Mee - flavourful, not salty, lots of gravy, generous portion and well worth for the buck! It doesn’t have much wok hei but that makes it a very clean and palatable dish for me.

Friendly folks as well!

Tried this pizza self-collection outlet in Tanjong Katong and was really impressed. Ordering was smooth and hassle-free, and the pickup was quick and efficient — perfect if you don’t want to wait around.

The pizza itself was the highlight: freshly baked, generous with toppings, and the crust was nicely done — crispy on the outside yet soft inside. Everything tasted fresh and well balanced, not overly greasy.

Staff were friendly and organized, making the self-collection process very easy. Great option for takeaway nights or when you’re craving good pizza without the delivery wait.

Definitely a solid go-to pizza spot in Katong. Will be back again!

In America, any regular pizza would have a good amount of sauce you can actually taste and gooey stretchy cheese all over.

What really stood out was the staff: cheerful, helpful, and very welcoming throughout our visit. Definitely a place I’d come back to again.
author: Din Lee

review_text:
Marrybrown Forest City is a convenient and dependable option in the area. The food quality is just okay—nothing exceptional, but consistent and acceptable for a quick fast-food meal. The fried chicken is reasonably crispy and filling, though flavors are fairly standard.

What works well here is the overall experience: the outlet is clean, seating is comfortable, and it’s usually not crowded. Service is efficient and straightforward, making it an easy stop when you want something quick and familiar.

Overall, a solid 4-star spot for convenience and value rather than standout food quality. Reliable, but not memorable.

Ordered the "stir fried belly silk" as a  side dish, which was served in a cold-cuts fashion, with a mix of carrots, parsley, tribe meat. The taste of the parsley in that dish was very well paired and uniquely flavourful making this spicy cold-cut dish a favourite of mine! Will come again for it. Next visit will try out the hotpot.

review_text: Will give 0 stars if possible. I visited this Chinese restaurant and endured what felt like a culinary marathon (1 hour wait) for a simple bowl of beef noodles. The noodles were overcooked and the beef tasted like it had been marinated in disappointment. Despite the lack of customers, the lady boss managed to ignore us and maintain her impressive level of rudeness. She clearly missed the memo on service recovery, as no apology or compensation was offered for the torturous wait. Save yourself the agony and find a more hospitable dining experience elsewhere.

author: marilyn Dass

review_text:
If I were to rate the entire meal with stars 🌟:

👉Tom Yam ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - The most delicious Tom Yam I've had in Johor! The rich, spicy, and tangy flavor with the perfect balance of creaminess makes it a standout dish. Truly authentic! 🍲🔥

👉Pandan Fried Chicken⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - Crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, with the aromatic infusion of pandan. It’s a dish you wouldn’t want to miss. 🌿🍗

👉Salted Fish Stir-Fried Kailan ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - The perfect fusion of greens and salted fish. You get the right amount of flavor and saltiness in each bite. 🌱🐟

👉Thai Milk Tea⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - Smooth, perfectly balanced, not too sweet, just like the ones you get in Thailand. A refreshing and satisfying drink! 🧋💛

👉Egg Omelette⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ - A must-have pairing with Tom Yam, fluffy and just right. It complements the spiciness perfectly. 🍳💛

Such an amazing experience overall, every dish was flavorful and delicious! Highly recommend. 😊

review_text:
Missed the Peking Duck at the old Meisan restaurant in Hotel Mutiara, so when I heard abt the Forest City outlet, I was excited. But, excitement turned into huge disappointment.

Reached there and was told no more Peking Duck, coz they only prepared 3 ducks per day. 1st red flag, coz which restaurant prepares only 3 ducks per day?But I decided to stay, since I missed the food there.
I was so wrong.

We were the only ones in the restaurant at 7pm on Fri,  which was dinner time.
2nd red flag.

The lady captain recommended a special pumpkin based soup with fresh Soon Hock.
she did not show us the weight or size of fish before cooking.
3rd red flag.

The soup was nice and the fish meat was fresh.

Also ordered a veggie dish not listed inside the menu and the portion was so small, though it was medium size and ordered a ma po toufu.

The shock came when I went to pay. The total bill came up to RM462, which was a shocker, as I never expected the fish soup alone costs more than RM300.

So sadly, this would be my last time at Meisan.

The hand - grasped mutton (RM48) was tender, and the sweet and sour squirrel fish (RM29.9) had a perfect balance of sweet and sour. The nourishing soup (RM9.9) was comforting too. Definitely coming back!

restaurant_name: Wan Soon Lai Bakuteh & Fried Porridge
review_text:
Unfortunately, there aren't that many fried porridge outlets in Singapore. Plenty of Teochew, Cantonese, Taiwan congee, frog porridge etc, but precious few that actually serve fried porridge.

Apparently originating from Malaysia, the ingredients are first stir fried in a wok under high heat before adding the porridge base. When done correctly, the wok hei aroma permeates throughout the porridge, adding an extra dimension to a dish that for many represents the epitome of comfort food.

My favorite example of this porridge however doesn't even make it to Google's list of fried porridge in Singapore (again, you get plenty of porridge that isn't actually fried). Add to that, WSL is located in an industrial area not easily accessible by public transport (the nearest MRT being Joo Koon which is a 15 min walk away).

You don't have to worry about eating cold porridge here. The thick flavorful porridge is served piping hot in a claypot that takes a long while to cool down. Even at $6 it still represents fair value given how generous they were with ingredients. They keystone of this dish however,  is the wok hei and it's front and centre in WSL's porridge. Honestly, worth the trek out into the industrial heartland for this simple dish!

review_text:
Donkey, Aerin, and I visited Kokoro Izakaya based on a TikTok recommendation praising its vibrant atmosphere and quality food. The restaurant has warm, cosy decor with a dedicated band area, which likely livens up in the evenings with live music. However, during our afternoon visit, the place was very quiet, with few patrons and staff mostly sitting idle.

We arrived with high expectations but found the lunch menu quite limited, with many desirable dishes available only at dinner. We wanted to try the beef cubes, so we asked if they could prepare them outside the regular menu. The staff kindly agreed. When the beef cubes arrived, the portion was small for the price, and the beef was overcooked beyond our preferred medium rare and not top grade.

We also ordered the seafood ramen, which was decent but lacked excitement, and the California Maki, which was presented untidily with unevenly distributed fish roe and an odd taste. The Chawanmushi was watery and lacked proper egg consistency. The sashimi portion was acceptable but the wasabi lacked a real kick. The Beef Don was cooked perfectly and was the highlight of the meal.

The yuzu mochi was refreshing and sweet, making for a pleasant end to the meal. We initially planned to order garlic fried rice but decided against it after trying the other dishes. Donkey ordered a Highball, but the ice was regular cubes instead of spherical, and the alcohol-to-mix balance was off, making the drink less enjoyable. We noticed the restaurant remained largely empty during dinner hours, with staff sitting around idly, which was disappointing.

Despite the nice decor and potential lively atmosphere, the overall experience did not meet expectations due to small portions, inconsistent food quality, and quiet ambiance. Aerin also mentioned the food was not particularly enjoyable. Considering all factors, I’d rate Kokoro Izakaya 3 stars—a cosy spot with promise but lacking vibrancy and consistent quality during our visit.

Ratings:

- Food Quality: 3/5 – Some decent dishes but inconsistent overall
- Service: 3/5 – Staff were polite but somewhat inattentive during quiet periods
- Ambiance: 3/5 – Nice decor but lacked the lively atmosphere expected
- Value for Money: 2.5/5 – Portions felt small relative to price
- Overall Experience: 3/5 – A cosy spot with potential but needs improvement in food and vibe

review_text:
Kitty, Aerin, and I visited Kokoro Izakaya based on a TikTok recommendation, which praised its vibrant atmosphere and highly rated food. The restaurant features a warm, cosy decor and has a dedicated band area, which I believe makes it lively during the evenings when live music is performed. During our visit in the afternoon, however, the place was very quiet, with only a few patrons and the staff sitting idly.

We arrived with high expectations but soon realised the lunch menu was quite limited, with many of the dishes we wanted only available at dinner. Kitty and Aerin were keen to try the beef cubes, so we asked the staff if they could prepare them outside the usual menu. They kindly obliged. However, when the beef cubes arrived, we were surprised by the small portion relative to the price. The beef was not of top grade and, unfortunately, was overcooked beyond our preferred medium rare.

We also ordered the seafood ramen, which was decent but lacked the ‘wow’ factor, and the California Maki, which was presented somewhat untidily with unevenly distributed fish roe and a strange taste that was hard to identify. The Chawanmushi was watery, more like a soup, with the egg insufficiently cooked. The sashimi portion was acceptable, but the wasabi failed to deliver any real kick. The Beef Don was cooked perfectly and was the most satisfying dish of the meal.

The yuzu mochi was quite nice, refreshing and sweet, providing a lovely ending to our meal. We initially wanted to order the garlic fried rice but decided against it after sampling the other dishes. I also ordered a Highball, but the ice was not the typical spherical shape and consisted of regular cubes. The drink’s alcohol-to-mix ratio felt imbalanced, making it less enjoyable. After our meal, we noticed the restaurant remained largely unoccupied, even during dinner hours, with staff sitting around idle, which was quite disappointing.

Although the decor was nice and the atmosphere appeared promising, the overall experience did not meet our expectations due to the small portions, inconsistent food quality, and the quiet ambience during dinner. Aerin mentioned that the food wasn’t particularly enjoyable either. Considering all factors, I would rate this place 3 stars, a cosy spot with potential but lacking in vibrancy and food consistency during our visit.

Nandhana's Restaurant @ Joo Koon Circle
The Place

What I had:
Stuffed naan with vegetable ($4.50): The stuffing of minced vegetable (tasted like pumpkin) was rather sweet, which did not go well with the curry - perhaps I should have ordered the plain naan.
Chettinad Chicken Masala ($10.90): The curry was delicious and redolent of aromatic spices. I would prefer it to be a bit less salty though. The chicken pieces were not too dry, although they were rather bony.
The service
The junior staff was enthusiastic and friendly, although seem to be overwhelmed with work. A serious looking older gentleman (the manager, I presumed, since he was not wearing uniform) who came to take the order, however, seem impatient and hurried.

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $10) @ Crave Nasi Lemak.
.
Descended from the famous Selera Rasa Nasi Lemak when it was founded in May 2015 by 2nd-generation owner Doctor Abdul Malik Hassan, this modern homegrown chain is among the most accessible and ubiquitous, with nearly 50 outlets across Singapore.
.
Consistent in quality and taste, their fluffy loose long-grain white rice carries distinct floral earthy grainy sweet flavour. The crunchy deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies carry fishy salty savoury flavour, the firm roasted salted peanuts have nutty savoury salty flavour, and the wobbly soft fried chicken egg with runny yolk releases pleasant eggy savoury sweet flavour.
.
The soft otak-otak / otah / spiced mackerel fish paste is decent with fishy savoury spice flavour, and the tender springy breaded fish surimi fillet has sweet savoury flavour. The deep-fried turmeric marinated chicken wing, while smaller in size than their parent brand, is tender and juicy with smoky meaty savoury salty spice flavour, best eaten when piping hot. Their grainy sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste has a bigger sweet salty spice flavour kick compared to elsewhere.

restaurant_name: 803 Thai Food (803泰国小吃 @ Upper Jurong Road
review_text:
Undoubtedly, this Thai Zhi Char stall in the west can be considered as one of the finest establishments of its kind. I had the pleasure of visiting it for the second time, this time accompanied by my family, and it truly left a lasting impression. The sheer quality of the food served surpassed our expectations, leaving all of us thoroughly satisfied.

One standout dish that captured our taste buds and brought us immense delight was the Tom Yum soup. Its tantalizing blend of flavors, combining the perfect balance of spicy, sour, and savory notes, was a true testament to the chef's skill. Each spoonful of the aromatic broth was a burst of culinary excellence that left us craving for more.

Additionally, the fired Hor Fun with wok taste was an absolute masterpiece. The skilled craftsmanship displayed in its preparation was evident from the first bite. The flat rice noodles were expertly stir-fried in a scorching hot wok, imparting a delightful smoky flavor and a slightly charred aroma. The combination of tender slices of meat, vibrant vegetables, and the tantalizing sauce made this dish an irresistible symphony of textures and flavors.

Not stopping at these highlights, we also had the pleasure of savoring other delectable dishes that further enhanced our dining experience. The Thai Pandan Chicken, with its fragrant pandan leaves wrapping succulent pieces of marinated chicken, was a delightful fusion of aromatic herbs and juicy meat. The Garlic Chicken, on the other hand, delighted our taste buds with its rich garlicky flavor that permeated every bite, leaving us wanting more.

To complete our feast, we decided to try the Thai Cockles, and they did not disappoint. These plump and juicy shellfish were cooked to perfection, highlighting the unique briny taste that makes them a sought-after delicacy. The accompanying sauce added a delightful tanginess, elevating the dish to new heights.

All in all, our visit to this exceptional Thai Zhi Char stall in the west was nothing short of an outstanding culinary adventure. The food quality, attention to detail, and the overall dining experience were truly remarkable. We left the establishment with contented smiles on our faces, grateful to have discovered such a gem. Without a doubt, this place has earned our highest praise, as there was absolutely nothing to complain about.

Well, 5 stars review must be longer than 1 star review! Swee bor?

restaurant_name: Xi Yan Seafood Restaurant 禧宴海鲜酒家
review_text:
“Fantastic” wasn’t the word I expected to associate with this restaurant when I first heard about it. So, when my family decided to dine here for Chinese New Year’s Eve, our initial amusement was more about the funky decor than the food.

Upon arrival, we were pleasantly surprised to find a private car park right outside. The wait staff greeted us warmly, cheerful and sincere despite the relatively quiet crowd. This was a refreshing change, especially during the festive season, when some places have waitstaff with expressions so sour like mandarin oranges that they would be considered inauspicious for a celebration.

Service was seamless. Food arrived almost immediately, and the staff thoughtfully checked in on our tea preferences. We kicked off with an authentic and well-seasoned Lo Hei, and throughout the meal, the pacing was never rushed nor slow.

Then came the real surprise, which was the food. Dish after dish impressed us, with seafood that was fresh, high quality, and generously portioned. A special mention would be the fruit garnishes. Most restaurants use stale or tasteless fruit purely for aesthetics, but here, they were fresh, juicy, and actually edible.

Our favourites were the excellent lobster cold dish and vegetable platter, but the highlight was the Mao Tai Alaskan King Crab. The liquor eliminated any fishiness while enhancing the crab’s natural sweetness and springy texture, being flavorful but never overpowering.

Portions were beyond generous. We left both full and satisfied, with plenty of leftovers, which is an auspicious touch to end a festive meal.

I would recommend this place especially for celebrations. Just be prepared to embrace the quirky decor which stays true to theme, even as you dine.

review_text:
**After repeated eating at this place, I must say the craft of the roast master clearly shines.

It's now a 5 stars for me, and the rating for meats are as follows

Roast Pork: 3.5/5
Char Siew: 4.5/5

Always order the noodles and my only gripe with the Char Siew (which honestly can easily be a 5/5) is how small they cut it. But yed after repeated eatings, this roast place is honestly super solid - even better than some other famous, more well known places iykyk

--------------------

Second time: 12 starts the long queue. Morning is better cause you skip the whole queue

Ordered a Char Siew Shao Rou Noodles , add noodles for ($5.50).

Honestly a great bowl of noodles. Black sauce style with the very small kind of noodles. Coated with a layer of oil so it gives that nice slippery texture. I also love the chew of the noodles. While the black sauce is flavourful, I only wished there was more black sauce for my (added) bowl of noodles - some parts were seemingly dry. Overall, there was also a nice smokiness to the noodles.

To Roast Pork and Char Siew

Roast Pork (3/5)
Char Siew (4.5/5)

Roast pork is normal, didn't really like the texture but taste was there. The crisp skin was also nice. Char Siew is way better. I don't really like how they cut it (very small). But their char siew is super super fatty. So it feels like biting into gelatinous bites of oil burst - honestly I enjoyed it. Also char siew is very sweet kind.

Soup was amazing - they have a huge pot and uncle told me to take myself. Was Salted veg and duck soup for the day. Pretty decent soup, really enjoyed the choice to self-service soup and its not the usual kind. Also available for people taking away os thats a plus.

Oveeall, a decent bowl of noodles with highlights. As a while, its good but not perfect. Definitely worth travelling to this ulu spot imo if you craving some black sayced, roasted meats noodles.

restaurant_name: Poon Kee Traditional Roasted Duck Wanton Noodle
review_text:
ordered the 叉烧烧肉面 (char siew roast pork noodles) for $5 on a thursday morning (~9.45am). there was no queue!

i'll start with my favourite part: the char siew! this was phenomenal! thick slabs of melt-in-your-mouth char siew. it seemed to be around 50-50 fat-to-meat. i'm usually not a fan of fatty char siew because of the greasiness and taste, but this was amazing.

the roast pork was not bad. a little salty on some bites (but that's the appeal?) and sometimes the crispy skin was a little tougher. the meat was tender, not dry at all! it also didn't have the porky taste i dislike about most roast pork :) disclaimer: not a fan of most roast pork but i enjoyed this

the noodles were typical wanton mee noodles. in my opinion they were cooked just right and also didn't have the ki taste (alkaline bitter taste) which was great! disclaimer: i'm not a fan of wanton noodles so i could've done with less noodles but i could still finish it :)

the soup was peppery soup but didn't fall flat! seems to have some stock and maybe sesame oil? can't quite tell but it was good soup

the chilli sauce was great! slightly spicy and slightly sour

the actual location itself is really out of the way unless you work in the area but i would say definitely worth a try if you enjoy char siew, roast pork, and wanton mee

review_text:
**Moderate Review of Jack's Place, SAFRA Jurong**

I recently visited Jack's Place at SAFRA Jurong and found the experience to be quite mixed. The location is convenient and offers a pleasant ambiance, ideal for a casual meal or a family gathering. The decor is warm and inviting, adding to a comfortable dining atmosphere.

The menu has a good variety, featuring a range of Western dishes, from steaks to pasta. I ordered the sirloin steak, which was cooked to my preference, though it lacked a bit of seasoning. The accompanying sides were decent but nothing exceptional. My dining companions had mixed feelings about their dishes; some found them satisfactory, while others felt they were a bit underwhelming.

Service at Jack's Place was another area where the experience was mixed. While the staff were generally polite and attentive, the service was somewhat slow, especially during peak hours. This wait time can be a bit frustrating if you're hungry or in a hurry.

Pricing at Jack's Place is reasonable, considering the portion sizes and the overall quality of the food. However, given the inconsistencies in food quality and service, it may not always feel like great value for money.

In summary, Jack's Place at SAFRA Jurong offers a decent dining experience with room for improvement. It's a good spot for a casual meal, but there are areas, particularly in food seasoning and service speed, that could use some attention. If you're in the area and looking for a reliable place to eat, it's worth a visit, but don't expect to be blown away.

review_text:
First time having a Bengali meal after some years (first time since relocating to Singapore). The stall is located pretty much out of the way in an industrial area, where many Bangladeshi folks work in the area. Perhaps we can assume it's authentic since it caters to the customer base with the same taste as the owners and cooks?

Tried their duck stew meal ($7), which was pretty delightful. The meat was very boney (beware, none of their meat dishes are de-boned), but the meat fell from the bone easily due to the slow cooking. Due to the such cooking technique, the meat became tender and well-marinated. Surprised to see the accompanying rice wasn't just a white rice - more like a spiced rice (pulao) type.

Their mutton briyani is pretty much a standard trade with its own twist. Seems to be not as strong in terms of spice compared to let's say Southern Indian briyani and much of its 'kick' came from mustard. Usually Bengali briyani is often characterized by some potatoes tossed here and there, but seems it wasn't the case here. It's also priced more affordably ($6) compared to other briyanis in Singapore. On the flip side though, I hope they practice better hygiene in handling the side raw veggies (cucumber and green chili), at times they just handed them over bare-handed.

review_text: At the recommendation of my colleagues who swear by this soup stall, I braved the blazing heat of the wild west which is Yuan Ching and wandered into Jurong Superbowl with colleagues in tow in search of this legendary soup. What greeted me was a sauna of a food court somewhat of a cantina vibe just alot more chaotic. Anyway, the stall has a slew of soups, not being much of a fan of it i opted for the Lotus root with peanut soup with an order of Olive Rice, braised pork trotters (yes, again), and stuffed Tofu. Now I must say the soup was hearty, with lots of feel good nourishing stuff inside. The taste was robust, sweet yet savory too, very home cooked type of taste thanks to the generous helpings of pork ribs, peanuts and of course lotus roots. The olive rice was extremely fragrant had chunks of olives in it  that contrasted perfectly with the soup. Dunk the ribs into the cut chillis with the soya sauce and this is borderline BKT but with a more satisfying aftertaste. The trotters were average, but I did enjoy the stuffed tofu, just make sure to cover it in the topped chillis for a good kick. I tried my colleague's Buddha Jumps Over the Wall and it packed a massive kick of unami, now I understand why this stall is so highly recommended. If ever I make another Journey to the West, I might actually pop by again to try out more stuff from this stall.

author: Kai Jun

restaurant_name: Tien Lai Rice Stall (天來飯店)
review_text:
Absolutely amazing establishment, it truly lives up to it's name!
Id go daily if I didn't live in punggol XD
The rice is fragrant and flavorful, cooked in a special way, the taste is simple yet exquisite.
All the meat was tasted excellent, the shao rou skin was extremely crispy while the meat remained tender, the char siew was soft on the insides and just the right amount of crisp on the outer layer, the duck was moist and the skin just amazing to bite into, both textures and taste pairing to create something absolutely smashing.
The egg pairs well with the meal although it sells out fast I'd suggest going in the early morning, I find the yolk pairs with the rice well and the whites the meat.
While the sauce has a rich and in depth tasting flavor that can't be found anywhere else, believe me I've tried.
The owners are extremely nice people and get stuff done quickly and efficiently while maintaining excellent quality, theyre truly friendly people and it especially shows in how they interact with their regular customers.t
The environment gives a nostalgic childhood hawker experience and the flavors of the food take you there, especially for me.
Prices are as friendly as the people, truly a wonderful establishment as shown in their many achievements.

author: Cheow Mong Chan

review_text:
Just an 800-meter stroll from my accommodation, Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre is a convenient and practical hub for shopping and dining. Anchored by FairPrice, it’s a go-to spot for fresh produce and groceries. The market also features a diverse range of stalls selling hardware, household items, personal care products, and toiletries. A bargain shop offers items at significantly lower prices, while bread and baked goods stalls, small appliance shops, salons, and barbershops round out the offerings, making it a one-stop destination for daily needs.
The food court is a standout, serving a variety of affordable dishes that cater to different tastes, all at budget-friendly prices compared to other dining options. Unlike busier markets, the atmosphere here is calm and relaxed, providing a pleasant environment for shopping and eating. The combination of convenience, variety, and low prices makes Taman Jurong Market and Food Centre an excellent choice for locals and nearby residents looking for quality without the hustle and bustle.
author: Romeo Jr Matula

review_text: Came before the lunch time crowd. Try out the SG Prawn noodle. Soup was sweet and savoury. Quite popular with the queue not stop
author: Willy Chng

review_text:
Tried this stall at level 3, #03-169, in the morning. Pocket friendly and surely a hearty meal. Surprised that I could not find anything regarding this stall. Owned by a pair of sweet and nice early couple. Visited there around 6am, before heading for some morning walk.

They do have some special dishes like pig's tail, chicken feet, duck wings. Dint order those as I'm not into it.. but for people who wanna try, this place absolutely deserve your visit. Im unsure of how much a pig tail costed elsewhere, but this stall sells at around 2 dollars for a big one. Chicken feet is 3 for 2 dollars as well.

They does have the regular dishes like fried eggs, chicken wings, luncheon meat, chap chai, fish fillets...etc. Order a plate of fried beehoon with egg+chicken wing, costs $3.10. The red chill is really spicy with a hint of pleasant sweetness. However the green chilli is always my to-pair with for the beehoon. They does have sets as well, but I like to choose my dishes on my own.

restaurant_name: 德记潮州鱼汤 Teck Kee Teochew Fish Soup
review_text:
Came here for lunch and honestly, the food was pretty normal. Nothing particularly memorable, but not terrible either.
The ban mian soup was slightly flavourful, but it didn’t leave much of an impact. It’s decent enough for a simple lunch, just not something I would specifically crave for.
The fish soup tasted good when it was hot. However, once it turned warm, the flavour seemed to disappear. There was also quite a lot of bitter gourd in it, which made the soup a bit too bitter for my liking.
The steamed fish was unfortunately not that good as it had a slight muddy taste. That was a bit disappointing.
One thing I did enjoy was the chilli sauce for dipping the fish. One of the versions was sour and spicy, which I really liked. It added some excitement to the meal.
Overall, I think it’s still a decent place for a simple meal, just don’t expect anything mind blowing.
author: Ming Shen Tham

restaurant_name: 德记潮州鱼汤 Teck Kee Teochew Fish Soup
review_text:
Pretty pricey for a bowl of fish soup, but I thought since it’s a proper restaurant, maybe it’s worth it. I figured the food must be so good that it commands this kind of price. Sadly, that wasn’t the case.

I ordered the sliced fish soup, and the fish was really fishy, usually a sign that it’s not very fresh. It was also overcooked to the point of being dry and almost powdery. My Ee Mian was extremely soggy too. Just pulling a bunch of noodles out of the bowl, I could see them snapping because they were so soft. The fried fish batter was also strange. It reminded me of you tiao batter, which doesn’t go well with fish inside.

The saving graces were the raw chopped garlic condiment (which helped mask the fishy smell), the tissue box on the side (always appreciated), and drinks that weren’t too sweet.

But since price and food quality are what matter most in a restaurant, I’m sorry. I have to give it a -2 stars.

review_text:
Heading down to this corner of the food court after learning from a friend that this Indonesian Grill & BBQ serves a good bowl of Mee Soto.

Besides the lighted menu that was displayed on the stall, they have a paper menu on the ordering counter too.

While my friends had introduced the noodles dishes we somehow got carried away from the Nasi Set and ordered their Ayam Penyet and Ayam Penggang. Each plate comes with meat, raw vegetables, Tempeh and a small piece of Tau Gua. The Ayam Penyet was big, meaty and crispy.

Ayam Penyet - $6.80

The chilli is the bomb and elevates the dish giving a fiery kick to it. Ayam Penggang was sweet and delightful coated in the dark sauce.

Ayam Penggang - $6.80

We added Bagedil on top of the $4 bowl of Mee Rebus. Their style of Mee Rebus was decent with hard-boiled egg, beansprouts and chopped Tau Gua. The gravy was more an orange color. Overall, this bowl of Mee Rebus was not too bad too.

Mee Rebus - $4

A stomach-comforting bowl of Mee Soto was recommended. It was pretty decent with a handful of shredded chicken meat, not too bad but I'm still searching for a good bowl of Mee Soto.

Mee Soto - $4

Food is pretty decent and there were also a long queue during lunch hours. I do not mind going back again for other dishes.

review_text:
Just finished the fantastic dinner set at Bali Thai IMM and it was a superb experience! This set is truly the best of Thai and Indonesian cuisine, offering amazing value for a full, delicious meal.

The Lime Steam Fish was the absolute star of the show. The fish was incredibly fresh and tender, swimming in a broth that was the perfect balance of zesty lime, spicy chili, and pungent lemongrass. It was bright and addictive!

Next up, the Chili Kang Kong was spot on. Perfectly stir-fried with just the right amount of sambal kick—crisp, flavourful, and a great pairing for the rich fish and meat. The BBQ Chicken was equally impressive; marinated beautifully and grilled to smoky, juicy perfection. It was tender and had that authentic charcoal flavour.

Finally, the Dessert of the Day was a delightful and sweet end to the meal. Today was Mango Pudding—a refreshing palate cleanser.
author: Candy Tan

review_text:
I’ve been to the Bali Thai outlets at Suntec and Ngee Ann City, but this is my first time at the IMM branch.

We ordered the Tahu Telur, Crab Meat Omelette Fried Rice, and Kang Kong. Everything was delicious, though I do wish that for the price of $23.80++, there had been more crab meat in the fried rice.

Overall, a great meal.
author: P Lim

review_text:
This restaurant truly exceeded my expectations. From the moment I walked in, I was impressed by the warm and inviting atmosphere. The space is clean, beautifully decorated, and comfortable, making it a perfect place to relax and enjoy a meal.

The service was exceptional—friendly, attentive, and professional without being intrusive. The staff made sure everything was just right, which made the dining experience even more enjoyable.

Most importantly, the food was outstanding. The ingredients were fresh, the flavors were well-balanced, and every dish was thoughtfully prepared and beautifully presented. From the appetizers to the desserts, everything was delicious and memorable.

Overall, this is a restaurant I would highly recommend. It’s perfect for gatherings, dates, or simply treating yourself to a wonderful meal. I will definitely be coming back again.

review_text:
This Thai restaurant offers a very authentic dining experience. The Tom Yum Goong stood out with its strong lemongrass aroma and bold flavours—spicy yet refreshing.

Service was friendly and efficient, and the food arrived quickly even during peak hours. Overall, it’s a great place for comfort Thai food and good value for money. Highly recommended.
author: chua guo xiong

review_text:
Paofan Paradise lives up to its name, offering a comforting and satisfying dining experience. The friendly staff and prompt service made us feel welcome. The highlight of our meal was undoubtedly the large lobster hot pot. Generously portioned with three large lobsters, each cut in half, it was perfect for sharing. The broth, while undeniably delicious, was a touch salty on its own, but easily balanced with the other dishes.
The sides were equally impressive. The cai pu omelette was cooked to perfection. The sweet and sour pork was a hit with the kids, a testament to its well-executed flavors. The hotplate beancurd, made with homemade tofu, was a pleasant surprise – soft, flavorful, and a clear indication of the chef’s commitment to quality. Finally, the stir-fried dried shrimp with French beans was a savory delight, adding a nice textural contrast to the meal.
What truly sets Paofan Paradise apart is its affordability. Despite the generous portions and quality ingredients, the prices were surprisingly reasonable. If you're looking for a delicious, hearty meal served with a smile, Paofan Paradise is definitely worth a visit.
author: E’leen Liew

review_text: We came  here for dinner, and since there are only two of us, we can only order ginseng chicken rice and lobster hot pot. The total cost is $78. The ginseng chicken rice is hugh, and we could not finish it. The lobster hotpot is tasty, and we have the option to add vegetables or noodles to the soup but at extra cost. Recommended.
author: Jason Tan

review_text:
We were excited to visit your stall for the first time after seeing the promotion for 5 small lobsters at $38. However, we decided to try the 4 medium lobsters for $49 instead. Unfortunately, our experience did not meet expectations.

Firstly, we were served 5 lobsters instead of 4, but they appeared smaller than the advertised medium size. Secondly, the lobsters did not seem fresh, which was quite disappointing. We were charged $49, but the quality and portion did not feel justified.

Overall, we spent $83.30 on a dinner that did not feel worth the price. What started as an exciting visit turned into a disappointing experience, and unfortunately, this will likely be our last visit. We wanted to share this feedback in hopes that you can address these concerns for future customers.
author: franco teo

review_text:
It's unbelievable! A lobster pot of this level is only $38! I'm sure this is the only place in all of Singapore that offers this!

And it's not just one or two lobsters, but 5 whole lobsters, and they're not small either! The highlight is not just the freshness, but also the incredible taste. The lobster is served with a flavorful la la (clams) broth, and the sweetness of the lobster pairs perfectly with the broth, making it a dish that's both delicious and filling!
Their herbal chicken paofan is also an absolute must-try! The chicken is tender, juicy, and full of herbal flavor, and when paired with the paofan, it's simply divine! I love it so much! I'll definitely be back to visit them again, and you shouldn't miss out either!

But wait, the real magic happens now – you get to pair the pot with meat, seafood, veggies, and other hotpot must-haves!

review_text:
Swagat Indian Vegetarian just performed the culinary equivalent of a Jedi mind-trick on my taste buds. One chapati thali in, and I’m already drafting a heartfelt apology letter to every chicken wing I’ve ever met. The fluffy-yet-toasty chapati is a warm hug from a carb-loving fairy, and the spread of curries, veggies, rasam, and papadum turns the humble metal tray into a full-blown flavour amusement park—no roller-coaster lines, just pure spice joy.

Highlights:
• The dal? So comforting, it practically asked about my day.
• The veggie korma? If velvet had a taste, this would be it.
• The rasam? Imagine tomato soup got a PhD in sass and decided to party.

I left 100 % satisfied, 90 % convinced I could live happily ever after on plants alone, and 10 % wondering if chapati-scented cologne is a thing. Carnivores, beware: one visit to Swagat and you might find yourself Googling “how to break up with bacon.” See you on the veggie side!

**some food contains alliums, hence not suitable for those vegans/ vegetarians who don’t eat them for religious reasons.

review_text:
The food is scrumptious and mouth watering. They have exclusive deals such as their buffets and discounts. Their food is authentic Karnataka cuisine especially coastal Karnataka. They change their menus every Saturday and their food is fresh and hot.It is also a pure vegetarian restaurant.
I recommend the methi parata and paneer.
They also do deliveries.

I recommend the amazing rava masala dosa. It was heavenly and I absolutely enjoyed its pairing with madhur vada which is a flat vada that is filled with flavour. So decadent and rich absolutely divine. The vada Pav is beautifully prepared with chutney of various flavours and a melody of the potatoes as it melts into your mouth- just like in Mumbai!!
Overall, an amazing place which I definitely recommend.
