The lamb is slightly tough but chicken is not bad. Oxtail stew is one of their signature and is pretty good. This is tender and sauce is good. Comes with veg and mash potato, both yummy. Seated outdoors but not hot. Better to make reservations especially if you want indoors. Set cost abt $26, oxtail stew as well. Set is quite worth but not considered cheap for hdb area. Reminds me of the ship at shaw.
author: Loo Zheng Rong

review_text: Mariners Corner Restaurant serves hainanese and western food, and I recommend the sirloin steak on a hot grill, with the garlic brown sauce. The steak is tender and a good portion. Pork chops wasn't available when we wanted to order. Fried pork cutlet and chicken cutlets were not too dry. Topping up $5.80 gives you a choice of hot tea or coffee, a soup of the day, garlic bread, and a swiss roll dessert. Service was great here.
author: Shaun Chen

review_text: Mariners’ Corner Restaurant serves some of the most authentic, old-school Western dishes in town. The steak is cooked to perfect doneness, and the brown sauce hits all the right nostalgic notes. However, there are a few shortcomings — the baked potato comes without bacon bits, replaced instead by garlic crunch, which feels like a downgrade. Additionally, the dining environment could use some improvement due to noticeable mosquito presence. Still, for those who appreciate traditional Western fare, it’s a place worth experiencing.
author: Sammy Soong

review_text:
Service was ok. We called abt 30 mins in advance and managed to get a table outdoor. Atmosphere was ok for a restaurant below the block. I think they tried to make it as good as it can be.

Tried a few dishes nothing v impressive for the price that we are paying. Overall 200+ for 5 pax (inc GST & Service)
Oyster - not very fresh and there was some funny smell for the piece. Informed the server and they changed it, a bit better. But not the best tt we eaten.
Escargot - not bad, one of better dishes
Steak - also not bad, considered the better dish
Lamb shank - well, it was soft, but not well seasoned. Seemed to be a sauce dribbled on top instead of braised whole. I think secret recipe sells it ard the same price, with much better taste.
Fish - ordered fish and chips style. Again same, seasoning is the issue, its was also
overcooked. fresh thou.
Chicken - same, not seasoned.
Pork rib - same not seasoned. Can taste a bit of the fridge taste, maybe frozen pork.

Not sure what the chef was thinking. This will be the first and last time we will visit.
author: Cheow Mong Chan

review_text: This restaurant has a nostalgic style and atmosphere is very nice, I like it very much and the music is not too loud just nice to enjoy it while and chatting with my family. The service staffs are attentive and also very courteous and friendly. The food is great and portion is very generous. I had the chicken chop and lots of source which is how I like it. The salad is also very fresh. I will definitely recommend to try this restaurant when you are in the Clementi area. My family and I had a very good experience having lunch here.
author: dennis giam

review_text:
The lala beehoon is highly recommended. Always order this whenever we visit. I loved the fish head curry as well. Those are my favorite and plenty of good choices for entire family.

This is the place we always go for a good comfortable zichar dinner. Reasonable price and very comfortable seating - not super crowded like some kopitiam places.

The service was great despite being a busy night - and a couple of service staff checked back a few times to see how we find the food.

Overall a great zichar restaurant
author: Hk

review_text:
We had a fantastic family dinner at JB 101 Seafood in Bukit Batok! I really appreciated the lady who took our order for being so considerate. When I was about to order one more dish, she genuinely suggested we might have ordered enough already. That kind of honesty and care for the customer is rare and truly commendable!

Overall, the food was excellent and the service was incredibly fast—our dishes started arriving within 10 minutes, which is impressive!

Here are the dishes we especially enjoyed:
• 南乳炸肉 (Fermented Beancurd Fried Pork): Deliciously marinated and crispy.

• 四大天王 (Four Heavenly Kings): A great mix of vegetables. Not too spicy which is good for children.

• 自製海鮮豆腐 (Homemade Seafood Tofu): Smooth and flavorful.

• 菜埔河粉 (Chye Poh Hor Fun): The wok hei (smoky aroma) was outstanding, and it pairs absolutely perfectly with their special chili!

The free-flow ice cream was a nice treat and a great way to end the meal!

The only minor disappointment was the 甘香啦啦 (Kam Heong Lala/Clams), where some of the shells were unfortunately broken.

The restaurant itself has a windy, comfortable, and very family-friendly atmosphere. They even have some kids' rides near the seating area, which is brilliant! It kept the little ones happy and entertained while the adults could relax and enjoy the food.

Considering the quality of the food, the speed of service, and the pleasant environment, the price is very reasonable. Highly recommend!
author: OB1

review_text:
Visited close to Chinese New Year, so the place was very crowded. There was a staff shortage, but everyone was clearly doing their best. The chefs were cooking non-stop, and although there was a delay in food service, the manager later explained there was a system error that duplicated orders, adding to the chaos.

Despite this, the team remained professional and friendly. More importantly, the food was good. We had the sambal stingray, fried tom yum glass noodles, yam ring with pork ribs, hot plate sotong, and curry vegetables. Loved the sambal — flavourful and well done. Even during the rush, food quality was well maintained. Worth a try if you’re nearby 👍

Only managed to take 2 photos cause we attacked the food the moment it arrived. 😆
author: Samantha Lin (Sammie)

review_text:
Not sure if it's overrated and decided to try.
It’s a zi-char style restaurant serving a mix of Malaysian/Singaporean-inspired local dishes at Bt Batok area in between building.

The menu is quite broad: various noodles, rice, seafood, meats and more — from hor fun and bee hoon to prawns, fish, pork ribs, etc.

Some dishes are particularly popular, such as crab bee hoon, seafood, and “wok-style” noodle/meat/seafood dishes.

Not worth to order vegetables as too expensive.

There is also a guy asking if you like to see his magic tricks (but he was in a mask and looks scary)

Only 1 male and female so can be a queue.
author: Peter

review_text:
Tried JB 101 Seafood / Famous JB Firewokz — overall the dishes were sumptuous and really solid. The lala was fresh and flavourful, the broccoli was crunchy and nicely cooked, and the onion omelette was great as well. The deep-fried fish with soy sauce was the highlight, crispy outside, tender inside, very shiok.

We also tried the garlic pork rib, but that was the least to our liking compared to the other dishes. Still, overall the food quality and flavours are strong. Open space, comfortable for big groups. Will come back again.
author: Raymond Beh

restaurant_name: Evertop Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice Pte Ltd
review_text: Absolutely delicious chicken rice — tender, flavourful, and cooked to perfection. The side dishes were just as impressive, especially the crispy tofu, prawns, fried wanton, eggs, and fried sweet and sour fish. The boss was warm and accommodating, even with our last-minute reservation. Great food, amazing service!
author: Chomeh Alex

restaurant_name: Evertop Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice Pte Ltd
review_text:
Been patronising this shop when they are still in tanglin Halt.

Their Steam Chicken rice and Fried wanton is still the best for me. Only thing that is different from back then the aca portion becoming smaller and smaller. The challenges running FnB in Singapore.
author: Rusdan Lee

restaurant_name: Evertop Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice Pte Ltd
review_text: Had Iftar at Evertop Clementi on 1 March, made reservations and pre-ordered earlier in the afternoon as advised by the staff over the phone. My family was really impressed with the operations team, their planning and execution for the buka puasa crowd was amazing! Believe everyone there had a good iftar!
author: Jasmeen Lim

restaurant_name: Evertop Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice Pte Ltd
review_text:
A place where excellent service and delicious food meet. My family esp my 5 year old daughter had craving for chicken rice so we thought why not go to Evertop in Clementi for some good chicken rice as we haven’t eaten there for quite awhile.

The food as usual was awesome and their service still top notch after so many years. A little pricier then your normal chicken rice stall but for the excellent food and service, I’ll say it well worth it.

We ordered Roasted Chicken rice, Lemon Chicken Cutlet rice, Mayonnaise Chicken Cutlet rice, Thai Style Tofu and Chicken Sausage Omelette. The chicken rice dishes came with soup which was tasty but mild, not those where tons of msg is used or some which tastes like hot water. Their soup had the chicken essence in it.  The roasted chicken rice came with a side of cucumber and pineapple pickles which was a tasty. Chicken was soft and tender, nicely soaked in their own tasty sauce. For the cutlets, it was surprisingly juicy and not dry like some other stalls. The chilli I find, could be improved but still not too bad. The Thai tofu was a little crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, just the way it should be. The Thai sauce was tasty and not too spicy. Lastly the omelette, was fluffy and had a good amount of chicken sausages in it. Overall, the portion is pretty decent. Dining here was enjoyable as the restaurant is clean; attentive, fast and excellent service.

Highly recommended 👍
author: Ryan Fernandez

restaurant_name: Evertop Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice Pte Ltd
review_text: My Most favourite chicken rice shop ever! I can eat this everyday😋🤭 Highly recommended to all chicken rice lovers out there! 💯✨
author: Kin Sakinah

review_text: One of our favourite place from Clementi neighbourhood! Always frequent their roasted stall for charsiew/roasted meat rice abc/white raddish/watercress/lotus root soup😍; thai stall's seafood fried rice/sambal kangkung/tomyum/brazil minced meat (some dishes so so); collins mixed grill and aglio olio. And newly tried bbq stall's seafood fried rice big portion! The other stalls either never tried before, or so so. When we don't don't know where to have our lunch/dinner, there we go/dabao.
author: loli sit

review_text:
This Food Loft coffee shop has spacious seating area, the seating outside the coffee shop is airy.

There is a vegetarian stall 品味素食，serving nice vegetarian foods. As early as 9 am, they too serve fried Ho Fan.
author: Cheng Min

review_text: Tried the Thai food place. Food rating - fried pork 3/5, prawn omelette 3/5 and mango salad 3/5. Price is reasonable for Thai food. Place is not too crowded and not noisy.
author: CS Lee

review_text: Just your regular neighbourhood coffee shop. What's special is that there is a Thai food stall here instead of the more commonly found Zi Char stall.
author: Tony MY Ching

review_text: I feel so cheated. The senior Cantonese auntie at the drink stall wasn't honest — she charged me $1.60 for just a bottle of mineral water. That’s ridiculous. It felt like she was being cunning and taking advantage. Please don’t buy drinks from them. The provision shop nearby sells cold mineral water for just 70 cents — much more reasonable
author: lekc lekc

review_text: 😋 I've ordered the Honey Glazed Chicken Thigh Banh Mi ($5.80). The bun was crispy and the chicken was tender. Really tasty. There's some special sauce with chili sauce and mayonnaise. Maybe they can reduce the sauce a bit coz it was dripping much when I'm eating. So a bit messy. 😆 Overall, it was a good meal. ☺️ I'm looking forward to trying the other Banh Mi.
author: Lili Ang

review_text: Delicious and affordable Vietnamese food (Banh-Mi, Pho etc). As stall is One-man-operation, might need to wait but quality is there and worth waiting.
author: Wilson Tan

review_text: decent banh mi if u are in the area! i can taste hints of vietnam
author: Jared Choa

review_text: Incredible food. For $5.80
author: Beng Yang Tan

review_text: Honey glazed chicken thigh
author: BK Low

review_text: Food is delicious. Better than restaurant. It's good to have good, yet affordable japanese food in the west. Definitely recommend this stall. The curry was spicy enough and not too salty. Pork cutlet was perfect, not too tough to chew on. My favourite is the danban chicken don, love the onion sauce!
author: Emily Ho

review_text:
Pork katsu curry and chicken nanban.
Very flavourful and both protein are well cooked, tender and not dry!
Both bowls come with a bowl hot miso soup!
Better than some restaurants indeed!
It's a coffeeshop in HDB, ample parking.
author: Lin Lin

review_text: Super good quality Japanese food you can get at affordable pricing! Enjoyed their katsu curry the most. Fries is not really a stand out for me, will try the tamago next time. :) totally worth a visit. 😆
author: Chu Lin

review_text: I was lucky enough to find this hidden gem located in a small HDB estate coffee shop. The chicken nanban ($6.50) came with six thick juicy pieces of karaage thighs, topped with creamy, tangy tartar sauce. There was an onsen egg too and some tempura bits which went so well mixed into the rice. It was such a generous portion and so so delicious. I will definitely be back to get this again or try other items!! Came back another week for the chicken teriyaki don added mentaimayo sauce (+$2). Owner super generous with mentaimayo and it was as delicious as always!
author: Y

review_text:
One of my favourites for Japanese cuisine! Having visited weekly for a few months, their dishes are consistently tasty and well-made, and all run by a one-man show!

The Chicken Nanban Don is a must-try, with its crispy chicken, great flavour, and beautiful presentation.
Portions are generous and prices are reasonable. Highly recommended!
author: thomas rodrigo

review_text:
$5.20 for mixed veg rice in a kopitiam On the signboard $2.80 for 2 veg and 1 meat. but my 2 meat (1 is egg with very small portion 1 mouth can finish) and 1 veg cost me $5.20.

confronted them. small portion and bland meat. too expensive. avoid
author: Professional Tummy

review_text: There’s a new stall banh banh that sells really good banh mi!!! My kids and I enjoy the banh mi! Freshly toasted bread and ingredients
author: Esther Yeo

review_text:
+ The stall seems to also own the entire coffeeshop previously.

+ Located in quiet hidden corner of the estate. Less hot and expensive compared to the other nearby coffeeshop at 209B Clementi Ave 6.

+ Ample sheltered MSCP parking next door.

- Few other stall options in this coffeeshop if your companions want to try something else.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: Amazing banhmi!!! Vietnamese sandwich! We tried the honey glazed chicken and the crispy shrimp! Am coming back!
author: angela anthony

review_text: Zhichar quality at mixed rice price , I love it!
author: GOH Philip

review_text:
Had a lovely lunch at Jovis Cafe while celebrating Christmas, and it was absolutely perfect! The food was delicious, beautifully prepared, and so satisfying. The cozy atmosphere made it feel extra festive, and the staff were warm, friendly, and attentive throughout.

Such a great spot to enjoy good food and celebrate special moments. Highly recommend Jovis Cafe — especially for a relaxed and joyful Christmas meal! 🎄☕️✨
author: Tracy Ngeow

review_text:
the steak is good!

baked rice also decent, so were the fries, nice and thick cut fries. carbonara not bad too, but is the very creamy kind

the beef stew was a bit bland so it wasn’t really to my liking, but meat was really tender

very homely dining atmosphere
author: Michelle :D

review_text:
cosy cafe great for friends meetup or gathering. food here is great, nothing to complain about.
ordered the pizza, spagetti,  cod fish and desserts.

portion and prices reasonable here. food was served swiftly and the staff here are friendly and helpful.
author: Bimbles

review_text: Went there for lunch on a Sunday afternoon. Was pleasantly surprised by the cozy environment. A few selections of the main and side dishes. Food came promptly and was tasty and yummy. As the restaurant was not filled up so it was a enjoyable and peaceful meal. Recommended
author: Han Seah Sim

review_text: Here for the first time. What a gem found! They have such a cozy ambience with great food. Even have a small kids area. Kid definitely well entertained! Will be back!
author: Melissa Yam

review_text: Really ordered a lot of variety and all taste not bad. Authentic Taiwanese food be it the vermicelli or lu rou fan. Salted chicken is good. Location is not the most accessible. Not crowded on sun afternoon. Slightly on the pricey side i feel but place has aircon.
author: Loo Zheng Rong

review_text:
I’m Taiwanese, and this is hands down the most authentic Taiwanese food I’ve had here.
The crispy fried chicken, braised pork rice, and tofu are all SO GOOD. highly recommend!
The owner is super nice too. Whenever I’m missing Taiwan, this is the place I come to eat 💗💗
author: Davina

review_text: One of the most authentic tasting Taiwanese food I’ve tried in Singapore. The staff are warm and attentive. Cosy environment and pet-friendly. Must try’s are their signature beef noodles, minced pork rice, fried chicken chop!
author: Serene

review_text:
Food is tasty but portion is less than ideal.
For the price, I am expecting more ingredients. The mee sau texture is unlike those I had in Taiwan.

Service is friendly. Nothing more to add.

Atmosphere is clean, quiet and good to gathering.
author: Leon Lee

review_text:
Lee’s Taiwanese · Singapore ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️

Stopped by for a quick lunch and enjoyed the Taiwanese sausage — flavorful, nicely grilled, and satisfying for a light bite. The place was quiet on a weekday, making it an easy, relaxed stop for a casual meal.

Lee’s Taiwanese captures the nostalgic warmth of Taiwan’s street food culture, with homely décor, hearty comfort dishes, and familiar night market-style snacks. Whether you’re craving a simple bowl of lu rou fan or just a quick snack, it’s a solid choice for authentic Taiwanese flavors in a cozy setting.
author: C

review_text: The food was good. Had basil stir fry and fried mama noodles. But the portion size was way too small. You would need 2 or even 3 orders for a normal meal.
author: Felix Michael

review_text:
Yummy thai food! Food portions were also decent. Their thai milk tea is also really one of the best and thickest i’ve ever tried.

The only downside is that they’re a home based business and have no dining space, but it’s worth the delivery!
author: Theodore Ang Yong Hui

review_text: Delicious Thai food. Ordered the basil pork rice and boat noodles. They packed the soup for the boat noodles separately so the noodles don't become soggy
author: Stephanie Ang

review_text: Cannot find the 'restaurant'. I drove here in vain.
author: David

review_text: Good food and amazing Thai Tea
author: Danny Hinde

review_text:
Lovely place! Have never tried jokbal before and didn’t understand why they like to order this in k dramas and variety shows. Saw this on social media and decided to give it a try. And no regrets! Stepping into the restaurant feels like you are teleported to korea! Got the jokbal set and everything (including soup, bibim noodles and sides) were very nice! Got seafood pancake as ‘service’ and their strategy worked, coz next time i will definitely be ordering that. The pancake was a work of art, fluffy on the inside and crispy on the outside. It doesn’t feel heavy like the usual seafood pancakes we had.

Do give it a try! It made me miss travelling to Korea though….
author: Fiona Lin

review_text:
Authentic Korean Feast at Jang San! 🇰🇷✨

✔️ Jang San’s Signature Jokbal Set
✔️ Seafood Pancake
✔️ Stir-Fry Glass Noodles
✔️ BBQ Pork Jowl
✔️ Spicy Cold Dry Noodle
✔️ Mild Spicy Beef Soup

Every dish was incredibly good, but the Mild Spicy Beef Soup truly stood out — rich, flavorful, and perfectly balanced. The Signature Jokbal Set is huge, mouthwatering, and comes with generous side dishes that make it a must-try! The Seafood Pancake and Stir-Fry Glass Noodles were equally satisfying and delicious.

Big thanks to James & Van for their warm welcome — humble, friendly, and truly made the experience better.
Highly recommended if you’re craving authentic Korean food!
author: luto ni kuya levi

review_text:
$77 for this spread is damn worth it!!! 👍🏻

I always come for the pork trotters here. It’s the QQ skin with good bite, thick slices.

Got the Jokbal Medium Set which comes with noodles and soup too, not stingy at all when it comes to the portion. Could easily feed 3-4pax.
author: T L

review_text:
First of all, I really liked how they welcomed us, and their service was excellent. When it comes to the food, my number one favorite was the mild spicy beef soup. I'm not really into spicy food, but I was able to tolerate this one because it wasn't too spicy and the flavor was delicious.

Second is the Jang San’s Signature Jokbal Set, super tasty and definitely worth it.

Thanks so much to James and Van for the warm welcome; they were incredibly humble. I truly recommend this Korean restaurant.
author: Ayiesha Belmonte

review_text: It’s always heartwarming to come to this restaurant after work - for one, the food is legit (who can resist jigae?), the service (the boss gave me free food, saying “service” like I hear in kdrama) and the cosy, homey atmosphere. It’s so much better than the chain restaurants! sorry for my half eaten pork knuckle (jokbal) photo. It’s very flavorful and not oily. Indeed “king of Jokbal” LOL
author: C Low

review_text: Honestly, I didn’t expect to come across such a skilled and engaging salesperson here. The cashier did an outstanding job explaining and promoting the membership without being pushy at all. Service was impressively fast — within five minutes of making payment, our drinks arrived, and just a few minutes later, the food was served. Best of all, everything tasted absolutely delicious. The quality and standards of this place clearly haven’t dropped one bit. Huge kudos to the chefs for the great food and to the entire crew for the efficient and friendly service. Overall, it’s an excellent spot for supper, and I’d give it a solid 10/10. I’ll definitely be coming back again.
author: Glenn Lee

review_text:
Glad to have Springleaf Prata in the West Coast area! Food was consistently good — prata was crispy on the outside and soft inside, just how it should be.

Special mention to Carol, the cashier. She was very patient, friendly, and took the time to recommend signing up for the membership since we come here quite often. Really appreciated her service — made the whole experience more pleasant.

Definitely a go-to spot for prata in the neighbourhood. Will be back again 😊
author: WONG SAY TIAN

review_text:
Many times here, first time reviewer. Thank you carol for the good service. Apart from that, always enjoy having their cheese and okonomiyaki prata. But remember to order in advance :)

Though sometimes I wish the cleanliness can be improved abit!
author: Teo Jun Jie

review_text: Like to come here as it's usually not as crowded as other outlets. I think the Otah Prata would have been better without the hollandaise sauce, especially if you are those who definitely have ur pratas with curry.
author: Mr Yang

review_text:
Springleaf prata at Newest is my favourite go to place for prata at any hour of the day.
When ordering prata, ask for “more crispy”!
Service is always prompt and friendly
Fathima in particular goes out of her way to greet customers
author: Winston Lee

restaurant_name: Bombay Grill - Authentic North Indian Restaurant
review_text:
Had a fantastic meal at Bombay Grill, made a reservation with Eatigo app and gotten 50% off.
Pleasant experience with the front facing staff, he recommended me dishes to try which were amazing. I really like the mango lassi and the mutton biryani!
Kind of a hidden gem in this area for Indian cuisine, I highly recommend to visit and try!
author: Ze Kai

restaurant_name: Bombay Grill - Authentic North Indian Restaurant
review_text:
Ordered 150 $ worth of food and this is what I get for almost 120 $ out of total.  The portions are smaller than Food court where this would have been 1/4th the price. I think these guys are flying their goats and chicken directly from India and charging for it accordingly. Taste also not that great that i would pay so much for.

Highly disappointed with my order. Think before you order.
author: akee sharma

restaurant_name: Bombay Grill - Authentic North Indian Restaurant
review_text:
I had been a regular to this place; visited 1-2 times/ months for the last year.

Very nice food. Lots of selections and different tasting dishes. I had tried many dishes and there are lots more to try!
author: albertong76

restaurant_name: Bombay Grill - Authentic North Indian Restaurant
review_text: It was a slow and relaxing Sunday dining experience for us. Food was served quickly and tasted rich and flavourful. The owner was friendly and service oriented... He was kind enough to offer the baby in our group 2 plain pani Puri to try. Place is kids friendly. We enjoyed the lunch session very much.
author: Linda Srichat T

restaurant_name: Bombay Grill - Authentic North Indian Restaurant
review_text:
Vegetarian Only Review:

Food: One of the bad Veg Biryani I had. The vegetables used are frozen one's and the rice also doesn't tastes good in terms of their flavor. Probably one can get better elsewhere for the price.
The veg gravy given for biryani is also a frozen one and not prepared fresh on the day as I felt it cold while having it.
The onion pakoda isn't good too, I felt that the flour used probably is a freezed one and didn't taste good, I had good one's before so this isn't good.

The carrot halwa is not that bad and not super nice either. It is just ok.

Good: The lime soda was perfect 👌, it was one of the best lime soda I've had recently.

Staff: I placed a grab takeaway order and the staff was kind enough to allow me have the food in the restaurant.

Ambience: It's like any other typical restaurant, nothing fanciful.

You can read my other contributions. So to say this is totally an unbiased review.
author: Pavan Kumar

review_text:
Had a lunch here to celebrate my mother’s birthday. We enjoyed the service, it has the atmosphere of relaxed neighbourhood restaurant. All the food were really good. We ordered garlic pizzetta, clams, beef short rib fettuccine, grilled Iberico pork, pizza magherita, tiramisu and cheesecake. Family enjoyed every dish, totally no complains.
Only thing i could feedback is that restaurant did not give any complimentary for birthday, but I guess they didn’t remember that this table was for birthday. Overall I would highly recommend.
author: Junwen

review_text:
Had a wonderful birthday celebration here with my family and friends. Managed to arrange for table for 16. All the staffs are very friendly and accommodating. I searched a couple of places and Italian food is one of my favorite. The food they served were all well liked and delicious. Even kids said it was great. Yummy hot pizza, truffle fries, Comparing to other restaurants like Etna, Lino can be well compared and maybe even better especially with their pizza, king prawns, chicken wings, mussels, clams, pasta, braised beef cheek, many more and wine (CARPINETO CHIANTI CLASSICO). Wine was good! Overall I enjoyed their food, quiet environment and service.

I had a very good arrangement for them to allow me to hold on to my card so I can foot the bill instead of my love ones, and they had to bear the little earful when actual payment was trying to be made. I thank you for holding the fort and what a wonderful experience.

Highly recommended.
author: Alan Morghan

review_text:
Pizza was definitely one of the best I've had in Singapore.
The other dishes... Not so much. The prawn in the soup had a weird funky taste and the soft beef ribs pasta didn't wow us.

Staff service was great tho, very attentive and friendly.

Would return to try other pizzas.
author: Victor

review_text: Beef short rib fettuccine was delicious, depth of flavour and textures were great - worth the mention. Other foods we ordered we alright
author: Denise Lee

review_text: First time dining at Lino. We had tuna as a starter, followed by pizza for our main course as recommended by Subra. He was very customer oriented and made sure we were satisfied with our meal. We ended with a cheesecake for dessert. Overall, it was a good dining experience.
author: Alice Bok

review_text:
Tucked inside Pandan Valley Condo, The French Ladle is one of those rare places that immediately makes you feel at home. The moment you step in, the cosy, intimate atmosphere sets the tone — warm lighting, friendly staff, and a charming, homely French bistro vibe that makes you want to linger just a little longer.

The food is absolutely comforting in the best way possible. Portions are generous and hearty, the kind that truly reflects the spirit of rustic French cooking. The salmon dish was beautifully done — tender, perfectly seasoned, and served over a colourful mix of roasted vegetables and tomatoes that soaked up all the lovely flavours. The duck confit was equally impressive: crispy skin, fall-off-the-bone meat, and plated over a bed of soft vegetables and golden jus that tied everything together. Even the simple bread basket felt thoughtful and freshly prepared.

What stands out most is how sincere and unpretentious the food feels. Every plate comes across like it was prepared with genuine care, and every bite is satisfying without being overly heavy. It’s the kind of place that reminds you why French comfort food is so beloved.

Whether you’re here for a relaxed family meal or a quiet dinner for two, The French Ladle is a cosy, heart-warming spot that consistently delivers delicious, comforting French cuisine. A wonderful little treasure in the neighbourhood — we’ll definitely be back.
author: Casper K

review_text:
It's hard to find a neighborhood resident French restaurant what more in a nearly 50 year old elegant Ulu Pandan condominium.

The menu rotates on what's available and this round it's a choice of NZ Hoki (a white fish) or Waghyu steak.

The mushroom soup with truffle oil is an excellent starter. I didn't fancy the escargot as much but the waghyu tri-tip steak is excellent. Rounding it up was a warm chocolate berry topped cake.

Highly recommended.
author: David Fu

review_text:
This review is long overdue. My friends and I have been visiting The French Ladle at Pandan Valley for a while now, and it has consistently been one of our favourite spots for a reason. This place is a true gem, serving up incredibly delicious, authentic French food in a cosy, unpretentious setting, with service that is always warm and wonderful.

​Our most recent dinner was, as usual, a perfect 10/10. We started with the complimentary bread and butter, which was simple, fresh, and delicious. It was the perfect opener for what was to come.

​Every single one of us (a table of six!) ordered the French Onion Soup ($18 each), which is a testament to how good it is. It's a non-negotiable must-order every time we visit. The soup is rich, deeply savoury, and topped with that perfect, bubbling crust of melted cheese.

​For our mains, the table was a showcase of their best dishes:
​Three of my friends had the classic Duck Leg Confit ($38). It was, as always, executed perfectly—the skin was beautifully crisp, and the meat was fall-off-the-bone tender.
​Two of my friends opted for the special of the day, the Hoki ($38). The fish was cooked beautifully, with flaky, moist flesh and crispy skin, served over a bed of fresh vegetables.

​I decided to have the Pan-seared Foie Gras ($28) as my main, and it was pure indulgence. A generous, thick-cut portion, perfectly seared on the outside, creamy and decadent on the inside.

​We also shared a basket of Truffle Fries ($14), which were crispy, fragrant, and a perfect side for the table.

​The French Ladle never fails to deliver a 5-star experience. It’s a place you can always count on for fantastic, hearty French food, friendly service, and a wonderful, cosy meal. We will, of course, be back again and again. Highly, highly recommended!
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text:
Quaint French outfit in an old condo.

Interior was small and it can feel a bit claustrophobic. Furniture seemed old and rickety as well, but you could say they have true French character.

Food was great, no complaints there. Free bread basket was generous.

1. Beef cheek was rich and fatty, with a luxuriant red wine sauce.

2. Duck confit was cooked perfectly, with crispy skin and fall-off-the-bone meat. The veg stew that it came in was nothing to write home about though.

3. Pork tenderloin was the black horse - tender and juicy with little porkiness.

Serving sizes could be larger for the price, but I'm greedy.

Got the apple pie and lemon tart for dessert. They were okay, not bad.
author: Derek Hum

review_text: We have been here twice. Quaint and cosy French restaurant in an old condo. It’s charming the atmosphere  and the food is delicious. Highly recommend escargot, French onion soup, duck confit, pork or beef is nice too. Foie gras was delicious as well.

review_text: One star for the price n zero for food.  It is near lunch time but the dishes r cold!!  The beehoon, curry chicken n veg all r cold with no hint of warmth

review_text: Had an enjoyable dinner at One Holland outlet. Food is great as usual. Jasmine is especially attentive to us. Her friendly attitude makes our dining experience so much better.

Definitely a great spot for good Japanese food and excellent service. Will gladly return again.
author: Mindy Tan

review_text:

I had Udon, Maguro Natto and Mekajiki sashimi. The picture says it all, it was too delicious. The chef made it a point to make sure the mekajiki is soft and delicious, it is always my favourite.

I want to call out to Treslin, Janice, Chee Mun and the service team - always with a smile.

restaurant_name: Le Rida (Mediterranean. French. North Indian).Bukit Timah, Six Avenue
review_text:
My family and I went there for lunch today since there were so many good reviews and to our surprise, it was a huge disappointment. We ordered the chicken tikka, fish tikka, chicken shirazy kebab, mushroom soup, creamy salmon with rice and margherita pizza. With the exception of the salmon dish, every other dish was EXTREMELY salty. Especially the mushroom soup, which we didn't even finish. The chicken shirazy was also extremely burnt all around as shown in the photo of all the burnt bits I had to cut off. The pizza which we also didn't finish was very doughy and had no traditional pizza/tomato/cheese taste. Basically everything was either very burnt or extremely salty.

I mentioned this to the Indian staff who was present and he didn't even look apologetic or sorry that the food turned out like that. He offered me a return voucher which I declined because we'll never come back ever again to even use it. If customer service was top priority, I think much more could have been done to make it right.

I think this place is trying to do too many cuisines at once. Decor also looks all over the place. Overall not worth the price and food is definitely not worth coming back to. We left the place feeling extremely thirsty throughout the day due to the very high salt content. Customer satisfaction? Non-existent.
author: Wes K

restaurant_name: Le Rida (Mediterranean. French. North Indian).Bukit Timah, Six Avenue
review_text:
just discovered this little bukit timah neighbourhood hangout

always walked past but never ventured in because of the odd assortment of mediterranean, french and north indian food, but having tried once, i will definitely be back!

lamb wrap ($12) and beef kebab ($24?) were also really good. meat was tender, juicy and well seasoned. beef kebab portion was perhaps a tad small so lamb wrap was better value imo.

happy hour drinks available.

really satisfied with my meal esp at this price point

review_text:
The pizza was delivered on time, as per the requested delivery time placed on the website. The pizza was also still hot when it was delivered.

review_text: Came on Valentine’s day, ordered their ala cart dishes. Food was really good, really got standard. Friendly & helpful staff, particularly Joyce, kelvin & Edward. Will come back again.
author: Sandra Galistan

review_text:
Prior to going to see the eye doctor, we popped in for lunch at this cafe

We ordered the Thai tom yam bee Hoon with fried chicken, chicken chop with black pepper sauce and a lemon meringue tart.

The beehoon was very flavorful and excellently cooked , and the pieces of fried chicken paired well with the beehoon.

The chicken chop was also nice and tender.

The star of the show was the lemon meringue tart. It tasted heavenly!  The lemon filling was also done very well and the lemon flavor was not overpowering. The crust was just baked firm and nice and not crunchy like in other places.
author: Gopi Bala

review_text:
You know how sometimes you go far off looking for something and then you realize what you wanted was always close to you. Got that feeling after visiting here.
We've been staying close to this for years now and hadn't visited such a good cafe. And I've visited half the cafes in Tanjong Pagar and east ..
Anyway this is set in King Albert Park mall. Slightly cramped but the good food makes up for it. Oh and they have seating on both sides.. one near the bar and another near the patisserie section.
I ordered a Build your own Breakfast with Sunny side up, croissant, sausage. Avocado and Mushrooms and Potato hash. And my wife got a Kaya butter croissant.
I must tell you they nailed the breakfast.. Eggs were great, sausage was cheesy and juicy.. I'm not sure if they actually had added cheese. And croissant was amazing. Flaky and crispy, it was just perfect.
I got a caramel macchiato and just felt bad at not coming here earlier. Fantastic coffee !! At the end of the day good coffee is non negotiable for a cafe and this place took it seriously..
We're going to be coming here more often...
author: Sairam Subramanian

review_text:
From my many instances of patronage I've never gotten the chance to try the food, but the valrhona brownie is good enough to return for multiple times and definitely one to put on the bucket list. Such a moist and rich texture, but without nuts (personally this is a huge plus to me as a nut hater), certainly one of the, if not the best, I've had, to the extent that I've gone back for it three days in a row at one point. However, it must be noted that the gelato portion, while the price is lower than others at $3.90 a scoop, no price reduction when added onto desserts like waffles or the brownie and a noticeable reduction in portion has made it a less desirable addition to me.

Service staff have always been friendly and knowledgeable who are sure to make for an enjoyable dining experience.

P.S. The atmosphere is good but do not be fooled by the first photo on Google - that is not a picture of the public dining area that is the focus of this review

review_text:

Horrendous food. Tastes very bland.

Its unauthentic flavour made us dislike this place along with its sky rocketed price. We ordered the tom yum soup which was incredibly bland. It was sweetish and really felt like dessert more than tom yum soup. The Thai Green Curry was incredibly thin in texture. It was bland and there was no spice. Exorbitant price was also charged for the small portion they gave. 14 dollars for that pile of unseasoned food was not worth it. The tempura was   not even seasoned well. The chendol was horrible and an insult to Thai cuisine. It did not even have shaved ice. There was just plain solid blocks of ice.
The servings is small, the service is inefficient, the taste is horrendous and the cost was exorbitant. They do not have much vegetarian options too.
I will never visit this place again for sure.

Authentic, aesthetic, and absolutely delicious, this Spanish restaurant nails the vibe and the flavor. From the warm, rustic decor to the genuinely great service, it’s clear they care about the full experience.

A standout spot for real-deal Spanish food. Will be back.

author: Escilpe

review_text:
I recently visited Peperoni Pizzeria in Singapore and had a generally pleasant experience. The staff were very friendly and welcoming, which created a nice start to the meal. The atmosphere of the place is decent—nothing spectacular, but comfortable enough for a casual dinner.

I ordered the Prosciutto di Parma pizza, which had good flavor and quality ingredients. However, the dough was noticeably too thin and a bit dry, which took away from an otherwise enjoyable dish. With a slightly thicker and softer base, it could have been excellent.

Overall, Peperoni Pizzeria offers friendly service and tasty toppings, but the pizza crust could use some improvement.
author: Bernhard R.

review_text:
Lively atmosphere with delectable pizza 🍕 in between NJ, RJ and ACSi, it’s prime location! Food comes fresh hot but the chairs’ legs have no soundproofing so it gets disruptive at times. Thankfully the staff have good manners to walk without dragging their feet 👍🏻

Price of items could be lowered if they saved on aircon electricity by closing the doors to the kitchen and toilet. Not a big deal but drinks menu is inaccurate using UK sprite for illustration but serving Malaysian sprite 🤔 overall, it’s worth checking out if you live near Dunearn Road or simply have an occasion to celebrate :) Better than Astons and Saizeriya for sure!

review_text: The pizzas are of good quality and enjoyable. However, the overall service could be improved. The bartender, Irina, deserves special mention for her cheerful, helpful, and understanding attitude, which made the dining experience much more pleasant. In contrast, the manager appeared rather stern and unapproachable, which was unexpected, as one would usually expect the person-in-charge to set a warm and welcoming tone for the team.
author: K Ng

review_text:
9Aug 2025. We came here after some highs of NDP parade. The kitchen made a mistake with the order and we got pizza on the house.
The service was really commendable. Upticked to 5 stars !

Aug 2025. Hey, there was a SG60 promotion where we could order an XXL pizza and 2 pastas and a jug if lemon tea at price of $60 only.
The manager was so friendly and sweet.
It was really a deal !
author: L.G. Wee

review_text: Brought my significant other here for a birthday meal after watching zermatt’s video and boyyyyyyy, we really love this place! The meat and food were awesome, everyone was very friendly and best was the vibes! The place looks very nostalgic and original, nothing pretentious. Just pure good food and great service! I am soooo gonna come back again! Thanks for the awesome meal today! 😋
author: Amanda Chong

review_text:
Coming here was the best thing I could plan for my valentine's date with my partner.
The ambience was amazing, not too bright and each table is nicely spaced out that it gives the feeling of privacy.

The service is top notch with its servers checking on us whenever our plates goes empty. since it's a buffet, it's amazing to see the frequency of the meat servers walking around.

Now comes the food, there's a whole central area for the sides and my goodness the egg mayo and potato salad was to die for. There's a beef stew which was amazing and the aglio olio was el dente.

The meats however, aside from the amazing beef and lamb, the chicken and fish seems to be lacking. With the fish being a bit too seasoned with the lemon and the chicken being too dry. The chicken parts such as the liver or heart was amazing and the beef, well, it's amazing.
The dessert was so good and not overwhelming. My partner didn't like chocolate but the lava cake was surprisingly good. Must try for sure.

Would definitely come here again.
author: Nuh Jamal

review_text:
Went there for their Sunday brunch offer which is priced at $58++. Was informed ahead of time that certain cuts and meats would not be available which is understandable since this is a lower priced offering.

The manager was extremely friendly and hospitable, giving us a rundown on how the buffet would work once we were seated.  Everyone is given a small circular puck which indicates to the waiter whether you want to continue being served meat or not, green being yes and red being no. The salad bar was self-service, and the waiters would bring the meats directly to the table.

The salad bar was surprisingly very impressive, with a wide variety of dishes available. The different cuts of beef and meat were also great although the quality of the cook can be a bit inconsistent. I enjoyed the chicken and the picanha the most, but there were also some misses such as the chicken liver. While the overall experience was mostly positive, I do have some gripes about the way some things were handled.

Since my group was seated towards the back of the restaurant, the meat was served to multiple tables ahead of us which I have no complaints about. What I do have a problem with is that when the meat on the skewer ran out halfway through serving our table, the waiter never returned with another skewer to ensure that everyone had a portion of that particular meat. Sometimes a particular skewer of meat doesn't even make it to our table, and we wouldn't have a chance to try what was being offered.

It wasn't until the manager came to check up on our table where we requested for specific dishes to be brought to our table to be served. Kudos to the manager, but this was towards the end of the meal, so we didn't get to enjoy some of the dishes as much as we liked.

Overall, generally good service and good food, just that the total will definitely be on the pricier side. I personally feel that it was worth trying but I'm unsure if I'll be back again.
author: Sean Phua

review_text: Loved the huge variety of meats and the amazing salad bar! My fav by far was the picanha steak, lemongrass fish and the grilled pineapple. The pao de quiejo was so nice and chewy too. From the salad bar - my favs were the cold tofu, grilled shrimp, burrata tomato salad and the pickled mango. Amazing service and so worth it. Can request for a certain meat if you know what you’d like. Super worth!!
author: Sarah Constance

review_text: Visited the restaurant for my son's birthday and we had an amazing time. We were met with excellent service by kuya Bobby. He made sure that we were taken care of throughout the evening. The meats were to die for. Seasoning is kept basic but thats all you need because of the quality of the meat. My favorites were the picanha, the beef hump, garlic steak, and the tenderloin 👌
author: F L

review_text:
This is definitely a 5-Stars Nasi Lemak! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟 Easily top of my list for my favourite Nasi Lemak in Singapore.

What's important in a Nasi Lemak is the chilli. Their chilli is very nice and well balanced with the right amount of sweetness.

I agree with some of the reviewers mentioning the battered fried chicken is slightly tough on the outer layer. But I can understand why is the stall owner doing so, I've seen a lot of customers ordering takeaways. This type of batter will remained crispy for a long time, so even if you eat 2 hours later, it is still crispy. And it is very well-seasoned too. If I really want to pick some flaws, it will be the chicken is slightly overcooked to me, I will prefer the chicken to be more juicy. But I do understand that for it to be halal, our Muslim friends have to cook it sufficiently.

The coconut rice is fragrant and fluffy. A real good coconut rice shouldn't be too moist, you must be able to see distinct grains of the rice, not mushy soggy rice. For those who prefer their rice being less oily will love this stall's Nasi Lemak. But personnally I prefer it slightly oilier for added fragrant. I think you can't have an exceptionally fragrant coconut rice with too little oil.

Next, is the otah, can taste a well mixed of spices, very fragrant! The begedil is well made, can taste the use of 'dhal' in it. Ikan bilis-peanuts is very fresh and crispy. Even the fried sunny-side-up is well done, not overcooked.

Overall, I truly think this Nasi Lemak deserves a 5-stars rating and when you eat their Nasi Lemak, you can feel the efforts and hardwork behind the stall owner's preparation. With that kind of effort and hardwork, I think this meal is very very affordable. Easily one of the best in Singapore! Well done! 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
author: Desmond Lim

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $7) @ Selera Rasa Nasi Lemak.
.
Established in 1998 by couple Hassan Abdul Kadir and Aminah Binte K. Omar, this legacy brand is amongst the most well-regarded in Singapore, counting Southeast Asian royalty, dignitaries, and heads of government amongst their customers. Today, it remains family-run by their descendants, including founder of Crave Nasi Lemak and their eldest son, Doctor Abdul Malik Hassan.
.
Their rendition features a bed of long-grain basmati rice infused with coconut milk, lemongrass, and pandan / screwpine leaves, resulting in a fluffy loose soft moist texture with beautiful grainy earthy floral sweet herbal milky flavour. The deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies with roasted peanuts are crispy crunchy firm in texture, shattering with fishy salty savoury earthy nutty flavour. The thin cucumber slices are crisp and juicy in texture with vegetal sweet flavour, while the fried chicken egg is soft and wobbly in texture with eggy savoury sweet flavour.
.
The otak-otak / otah / spiced mackerel fish paste is pliant and soft in texture, carrying fishy savoury spice flavour. The turmeric marinated and battered chicken wing has a lovely crunch to the exterior, a warm tender juicy chew to the interior, and lovely meaty savoury salty spice flavour. Their grainy sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste has a bigger sweet salty spice flavour kick compared to elsewhere. Additional crispy bits of batter lend an addictive crunch.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text:
Good deal. Great service. Fragrant nasi lemak (coconut infused rice). Otah good. Fried chicken batter a bit too hard but chicken wing meat freshly good so it was tender. Friend egg good. Ikan blis okay. Cucumber fresh & nice bite sizes.

A repeat better than its next door stingy neighbour LOL. Will be back.

2025 November.
author: John Tango

review_text:
Better than average nasi lemak! I had the royal rumble, which include all the ingredients, chicken, fish, otah, bergedil, egg. The stall holders were friendly as well, so a big thumbs up to them.

Waited for about 15 minutes before my turn, and I'd say it's worth the time queuing.

However, I personally feel that their rice and sambal could be improve. Even with basmati rice, couldn't get the beloved clumpy feel of the nasi in nasi lemak and the sambal was slightly on the sweeter side, which I'd prefer it to be on the spicier side. But to each their own taste buds.
author: Mohammad Fathullah

review_text:
Ordered the full house set of chicken wing, otah, egg and ikan bilis for $6.

Summary
Chicken wings : great
Others : average

Chicken wing is the highlight. Crispy other layer and juicy and tender for the wing parts. Drumettes part not quite. Nor is it the most crispy and quickly

Others are mostly okay. But dun expect it to be spicy. Otah and sambal are sweet more than spicy.

review_text:
It could have been 5 star for food but because the Vongole was slightly saltish, it didn't taste well. The texture of the gravy is okay. There was generous portion of the clams. Thank you.

The beef rendang shepherds pie was good. The cube of beefs just nice tender. Pretty awesome taste. I love it.

The dessert wise, the cake was delicious. Chocolate cake with cream. But the blue berry muffin was a bit too dry.

Overall ambience is cozy. I will still return to dine in again. There are plenty other foods I haven't tried.

Thank you guys. Nice time dining.
author: Lisa Alias

review_text:
Ordered the fried onion rings with curry sauce — a great side dish. Crispy and flavorful, and the curry sauce paired very well. 4.5/5 for the sides.

The Wild Rocket burger was amazing, likely featuring their in-house sauce which really enhanced the taste. However, the doneness could have been better — I ordered medium rare, but it came medium. Still enjoyable overall.

The atmosphere was great and comfortable, though there was a slight kitchen smell of cooked food at times. The cold long black was just on par, but still a good cup of coffee.

Overall, a satisfying dining experience with good food and ambience.
Overall rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐½ (4.5/5)
author: Ewe Keat Huan

review_text:
I had their onion rings years ago and never forgot them, so I couldn’t pass up the chance to try them again when I was nearby. Though I think the batter has changed, it still tasted really airy and crisp, and continues to be made with real onions which can be so hard to find these days!

For mains, I had their oyster omelette pasta. The bite was great, and the overall flavor was very addictive although I wished it was abit more fragrant? True to its inspiration, the pasta also came with thin slices of eggs and fried oysters.

Highly recommend the Sng Buey drink as it was really easy to down and tasted like its namesake.

Overall, I would return again as there are still a couple more interesting menu items that I would love to try, including the Hae Be Hiam spaghetti, as well as, the beef rendang Shepard pie!
author: Sandra Tam

review_text:
sadly, we feel standards have dropped here since the last time we came.

we got here for early dinner around 520pm, so it was pretty empty. we had the beef bolognese and the pancetta.

the beef bolognese was a major let down. the sauce was surprisingly sweet and just doesn’t go together. adding chilli flakes helped, though. also, portion size was also quite little.

the pancetta was pretty average too, to be honest. again, adding some chilli flakes definitely helped add some flavour.

service wasn’t great this time either but they were probably just having an off day.

personally, i would still come back because i’ve had some good experiences here and this was hopefully just a one off.
author: Marc Singh

review_text: A nice spot along Bukit Timah for a healthy lunch - used to be focused on burgers but they have expanded menu with some lighter and more healthy options. Staff were friendly and attentive and place was super casual allowing for nice chats and catch ups.
author: Winston Khoo

review_text: Regular hangout place of expats and pets. Mostly outdoor seating and not ideal for big group meat ups. Came here on a weekday and there was a quiet buzz amongst the patrons, chilling after their walk / run or just passing the time
author: Timothy Teo

review_text: Full service charge, even though we self order from the QR code. Lemon pond cake is under average, will not eat again. The americano Bristot brand is okay.
author: Sarah Soong

review_text:
This has been one of our favourite Italian for years. The eggplant is real cheesey and tomato sauce rich.

The coffee is nice too
author: Henry Hsu

review_text:
Accidentally found out this hidden gem while me and my husband went to botanic garden last weekend. I really enjoy the atmosphere of the restaurant — it feels like being abroad, not like I’m in Singapore.

The food is a bit on the pricey side, but you can tell a lot of effort went into it. The ingredients are fresh, and the serving speed is quite fast. I ordered a 'balanced bowl' with a lot of choices to choose from and the portion was quite big and it was the best choice for me during fat loss period.

Overall, it’s a place that makes you want to come back again, perfect for weekends when you want to try something different and relax in a restaurant with an exotic vibe.
author: Qiau Qian Ang

review_text: Great for a lunch, very competent staff and no wait times at least at the time I visited. Food is good but this is not a place for delicacies or specialty items. Located steps from the botanical gardens, it's probably the best place to unwind after a long walk in or out of the gardens.
author: CR Ruan

review_text: My go-to place for a hearty plate of mutton dum biryani! Added a serving of vege for a balanced meal. The mutton is tender and rice flavourful. Mopped up everything as you can see. Come try it!
author: Dawn Lim

review_text:
The mutton served in big chunks.

Surprisingly, the meat is not as hard as you would think. Very flavorful and tasty, the mutton. Hopefully I will request mutton curry sauce next time.

However, the biryani rice is not as fragrant as I expected. Its good not oily and the masala not too "overpowering"

It's still good to pair with the mutton.

The given sauce is very ordinary, not my favorite.

The price and portion are okay - $7 SGD for mutton biryani.

Overall, I will patronize it again if I come to Farrer Road, but it's not the best biryani mutton in my book, just slightly above average."

2nd visit is a nightmare..

The briyani rice disappointed..

The worst chicken I ever had (tasteless) .. the portion disappointed.. they use the biryani to cover the chicken to make it look bulky or a lot..
author: Darren Cheong

review_text: Thoroughly superb Prata. The Prata’s texture was a perfect blend of crispy and soft. It was crispy enough to give it texture but also soft enough such that it didn’t suffer from the issue of being too oily and starchy as other crispy Prata do. The curry was aromatic and flavourful, not too spicy yet it got the job done giving one’s tastebuds a heavy dose of spices when paired with the Prata. The cheese in the Prata wasn’t too melted and also not too firm, really adding depth to the taste of the Prata. At $2.00 a piece for cheese Prata. I found the price highly reasonable compared to the usual Prata shops and I do not regret purchasing food from this stall.
author: Elijah Lim

review_text:
I really like the prata here.  The curry sauce is very tasty, and I usually order the plain prata which is nice and a bit crispy but they have lots of choices with the fillings for the prata.  Also serverd briyani rice, either with chicken or mutton.

Usually has a short line for breakfast but otherwise quick service.  Very reasonable price.
author: Saifu Angto

review_text: Bunga Raya Prata at Empress Road Market is a must-try! 🔥 Fluffy, crispy prata paired with killer curry dips - the OG Singaporean street food experience! 🍴 Open late, budget-friendly, and totally finger-lickin' good! 👌 #pratalove #hawkergrub
author: kevin mun

review_text: A quaint Peranakan eatery which, based on their decor has been serving good food for a long time. Service is prompt and the food is fresh and cooked well. Went there twice within a week: one was for lunch and another for dinnet. Ngoh Hiang is of a good size and the mince meat is minced and well-blended with spices and very diced carrots. I enjoyed the Ayam Buah Kaluak where the gravy is mashed up with the flesh from the seeds while the chicken pieces are so tender. The fish maw soup is so filled with fresh q-q pieces of fish maw tay have been cleaned well. I also enjoyed the tauhu telur where the tauhu is fried so perfectly with the eggs that the combination leaves fragrant crunch of the fried eggs and the softness of the beancurd in your mouth. Fo dessert, it was chendol and the ubi baka ad kueh dadar: all cooked with freshness.
author: GK T

review_text:
Bumbu offers a, in my opinion, a strange mix of Thai-Indonesian-Peranankan menu. For my lunch I did not order their Thai dishes and went for just Indon/Peranankan fishes. I had some vague memories of eating at their restaurant at Sultan Mosque area that served just excellent Indonesian food but that was probably 15 years ago. Anyway I digress but the dishes are a mix of decent and good. The good are the crispy kangkong and the tahu goreng. The decent are the ayam buah keluak and the beef rendang. The excellent are the desserts that we find so good especially the kueh kosui.
The staff are quite attentive and polite the place has some old beautiful furniture at the entrance and good ambience.
Overall decent food decent prices and good service and great ambience.
author: Gooose

review_text:
This is one of those restaurants where not all things were perfect but considering the price point and overall experience it is 5 stars.

Food is really tasty- tamarin prawns, Kang kong , etc all yummy. Rendang was good but meat was a bit tough. But overall a solid meal.

Service is a bit grumpy but in general we were served quickly and had no real issues

Interiors were beautiful and really felt like a Peranakan home.

Overall this is a lovely neighbourhood restaurant, so if you are in the area - check it out
author: Pratyush Rastogi

review_text:
$17.90 - ayam buah keluak
$12.90 - tahu telur
$12.90 - sambal brinjal
$1.90 - white rice per pax

Bumbu has some really good and authentic Peranakan food. They have thai and indonesian dishes too but I feel like the Peranakan here is the best. Rice is free flow per person and you should also try the $1.50 sambal that they sell. Had it during a previous visit and it was great too.

The place has a really old school and quiet vibe so it's really good for intimate discussions but also large family dinners. Really a gem and I'd recommend foreign friends if they wanted an authentic taste of southeast asian cuisine.
author: Yap Seng Ang

review_text:
Great food and service from the restaurant :) kueh pie tee shell was very crunchy and satisfying to eat

Antique retro decor themed too, lots of potential photospots

There's also a washroom in the restaurant
author: kyh

review_text:
Avoid this station — especially if you use a corporate fleet card.
The machines malfunction, the staff makes mistakes by pressing random buttons or giving wrong informations, and they expect you to pay for their mistakes.

First visit:
I clearly told the pump attendant I was using a fleet card. He insisted to go for V-Power, saying it was the same price as 98 and that the corporate card would work. But It didn’t. When I asked the cashier, he claimed it wasn’t his problem. If I had known, I would have gone to SPC near my home where I have membership.

Second visit:
My company card had a remaining balance of S$58.91. I was going to do the self-service pump because of my awful experience in the past, but the same uncle came over and started pressing random buttons on Pump 5. The screen reset, numbers disappeared, and the machine kept running until it exceeded the limit — S$61.

1. My fleet card showed zero balance,
2. The uncle told me to pay the extra amount,
3. Cashier said there was no 'unpaid balance' at their record. What should I do?

I refused to pay with my personal money because I had clearly stated from the start that I would only use the remaining fleet balance.

Later, when I tested my fleet card at another pump, the balance went back to S$58.91. I offered to pay the exceeded (due to uncle's mistake) amount out of my pocket after deduction of requested amount from my fleet card, but they said it is not possible.

After leaving my contact, they called saying they would allow it — but even when I returned, the payment still didn’t work with my fleet card.

Every visit here turns into an exhausting, incompetent mess.

Avoid this place unless you want to waste time, argue with staff, and risk paying out of pocket due to their own errors.
author: Kushi

review_text:
BEWARE OF LETTING A MALE STAFF WITH LONG HAIR AT THE COUNTER HANDLE YOUR TRANSACTION. He has made me and others lose Uni$ and entering wrong amounts countless times.

The manager should seriously review this employee.
author: Clotted Fudge

review_text: The pump attendants will not assist with my diesel van. Only Shell I have experienced this poor service. Therefore I will not use this Shell ever again for my other vehicles. So you lose my business for our company Alphards, Roll Royce Phantom and my personal Lexus RX350.
author: Francis Higgins

review_text: Only at Shell, Dunearn Road, Eng Neo. I thought all shell stations are similar, but really proved me wrong. Only one staff who is professional and courteous enough to help me with re-fuelling diesel for my van. The rest of the staffs only approached big and expensive cars.
author: Darren Tan

review_text: There's an Autoserv station here and the staff was very helpful in helping us with our puncture tyre.
author: Xian You Lim

review_text:
No parking on site. Small eatery with limited seats. Find a table and order at the counter. No pay wave payment.
Char mee was tasty but a tad expensive at sgd$11. Rojak was average and the nutmeg juicy was just sweet with a tinge of nutmeg flavour.
Might return if in the area to try other dishes.
author: VP

review_text: Great for people on Keto or Low-carb, but it is pricey. The Penang char kway teow with konjac noodles was $13 if irc. It was tasty and had wok hei. You can also swop the rice dishes with konjac rice.
author: Paepae S

review_text:
my honest review based on my experience.

Service :

1. U need to walk-in to the counter to place order and they expect you to pay immediately after ordering.
It's kind of weird for a restaurant type setup.

2. Unhappy expression while giving the food. I wonder why the service person keeps the face angry...lol

3. Food comes to your table less than 5 mins ( so no waiting time ).

Food taste :
1. Honestly nothing special or extraordinary

2. char kway Teow - 4/5
Prawn noodle soup - 1/5
Loh bak - 2/5

Ambiance:
1. Decent place with Aircon - 4/5

Price :
Very expensive 🫰
author: Naveeth Nausath

review_text:
Great service from staff, they took the criticism from other reviews and improved their service. Now they do table service and you can pay after you finish your food. Service was fast and prompt, and seeing them work hard is amazing.

Food was great and affordable if you come in a group. Portions are big and the food tastes like traditional Penang food. 10/10 will definitely come here again
author: Edgar Ong

review_text: The restaurant has a somewhat dated ambiance, but the food is reasonably good. We chose to dine here primarily because they accept CDC vouchers. The service was attentive and prompt, thanks to the staff member taking our orders. However, the kueh pie tee had a somewhat lackluster, non-crispy exterior, and the rice cracker was a bit soggy. On the positive side, the nasi goreng had good flavor. The place was relatively crowded, and overall, the experience was average.
author: Abraham Lee

review_text:
HIGHLY Rated But Deeply Disappointing (4.2 Stars Misleading)
​After seeing the 4.2-star rating from 300+ reviewers, my husband and I drove 30 minutes specifically to try this "old school" wanton mee. Unfortunately, we were thoroughly disappointed. We won't be back and do not recommend a special trip.

​The Noodle & Sauce:
The noodle was indeed "Q" (springy), but it had a very strong, distinct alkaline (lye water) smell that overpowered the dish. The sauce was just normal and leaned heavily toward the sweet side. The chili offered nothing special to balance it out.

​The Meats - A Firm Skip:
​Char Siu: Do not bother. It was hard, dry, and had an overly sweet aftertaste.

​Wanton: The wantons had a very strong, noticeable "porky" smell. We each tried one and ended up binning the rest—that’s how strong the smell was.

​Braised Chicken Feet: These were not to our liking. They were chewy, and the braising sauce was also too sweet.

​Final Thoughts:
We gave it two stars purely for the good effort from the three generations running the stall (Grandma managing orders, daughter cooking and grandson managing next stall). While they seem adored by the neighborhood crowd, this place is just not worth driving for. If I had to drive here and queue, I would definitely say skip it.
author: Elaina Poh

review_text:
An old school with long traditional. The Ah Ma is friendly and still helping at the front. To be honest the Wanton Mee is ok but nothing to shout about. The noodle is nicely cooked but do have a little alkaline taste, very mild and hardly noticable.

A fair deal at $4 a plate. Not something you would travel across the island to eat though.
author: Nixon Neo

review_text: The noodles is nostalgic and my family has had it for more than a decade. Now ran by 3 generations together. A very nice family. Alot of comments about the 2 aunties but definitely because they do not understand the 2 aunties. Generally loud but they are actually very friendly and accomodating once you get to know them better. Business is so good there is always a queue so be early to avoid the crowd. Pork rib noodles is very nice and not commonly found in singapore. It is actually braised in dark sauce and i think it is definitely a must try. Prices are also reasonable.
author: Christopher Tan

review_text: The old-school wanton mee, priced at $4, delivered a comforting nostalgic taste. While not particularly exciting, it had that familiar "comfort food" feel. The soup stood out as especially tasty. They accept PayNow for payment.
author: LP Pua

review_text: Heard about this stall from someone & decided to give it a try. Long story short, it is not worth the hype. We got the wanton noodles & chicken feet noodles. Portion was quite small. Char Siew was too dry & bland. The chicken feet was too salty. Texture of noodles was good though. The mother & daughter pair was insistent that the old lady (ah Ma) would arrange the prepared food on a tray with picked chili, they didn’t want us to do it. I thought that they were unfriendly but when she handed the tray over to me, she made some jokes with me in a friendly tone.  It was quite an unique experience !!
author: Merryheart

review_text:
Homemade pastas were amazing. Pictures don't do it justice, looks fairly simple but the flavours where sublime

Was there for lunch and ordered a 2 course set lunch with a salad and mussels pasta. The salad serving size was HUGE (could be shared by 2-3) and the flavour was complex. Something about the bacon tasted unique and delicious

The pasta was perfectly seasoned with a  flavourful seafood sauce. My friends ordered the non-set pastas which were both homemade. Some pasta types I've never seen before!

Would come here again just to explore their huge menu. Food is delicious

Edit: visited again and enjoyed more dishes and desserts. Scoglio pasta was top notch
author: Bryan Lim

review_text:
Skip the sides and go straight for the pizza, pasta and tiramisu!!

The handmade pasta was cooked perfectly al dente and paired beautifully with the lamb ragù.

The gorgonzola pizza was rich and creamy, yet somehow still felt surprisingly light — and the crust hit that perfect balance of chewy, crisp, and savoury.

The tiramisu was excellent too: the mascarpone was soft and creamy without feeling too heavy, and the ladyfingers had a great balance of sweetness with that slightly bitter coffee kick.

And for the record, the sides weren’t bad - they just didn’t blow me away like the mains and dessert haha. I’ll definitely be revisiting to explore the other items on their menu!
author: lynn

review_text: Been here multiple times and Caruso never disappoint us. The food was consistently great. We highly recommend the La Burata, Ravioli Porcini, Controlfiletto Di Manzo & the Tiramisu. Looking forward to try other items from the menu next time. 😄
author: Sheila Ela

review_text: absolutely excellent. our go-to italian place. we love ordering the calamari (if you like the springier type of squid it may not be your cup of tea), eggplant parm, ravioli, gnocchi, seafood pasta, gorgonzola pizza, lamb chop, veal chop, meat platter, ribeye steak, florentina, the seafood soup and the branzino. the service is attentive and atmosphere is nice and comfortable. just note that the pasta portions are smaller, but all other dishes are generous with the portion size. nonetheless, i will still order the pastas because of the excellent execution.
author: Kit Ng

review_text:
Since we were in that area, my teenage son suggested we grab dinner and randomly search for an Italian restaurant. I told him not to "hammer" your mum's pocket! 💸This restaurant was next to the one  I used to patronise..see my previous post. When we got there, we only saw one table with two customers. I was thinking, should we even stay? hahaa... After placing our, we saw guests pouring in, and the first floor filled up! My son's choice was great. Besides the awesome food, I had such a good time bonding with him. He usually dun talk a lot or start conversations. Like most teenagers (correct me if i m wrong),  u asked they answered! So I was surprised this setting gave us a comfortable space to chat while enjoying our food. I rewarded him with his favorite dessert.
The service overall was good, but I did see two times where staff personal hygiene needed a reminder.
author: banana man

review_text: I love to eat chicken chops, this shop is very reasonable price and taste very good. Comes with coleslaw and mash potato. Even tabao, and cool off did not change the food quality much
author: little dot

review_text:
my go2 place whenever im craving hawker western food!!! the chicken chop is so tender and juicy u don't even need a knife. the skin is crispy with a lot of the fat rendered off. and the brown sauce super savoury and flavourful

coleslaw and corn are my go2 sides, but i was craving carbs and decided to go for the fried rice. i was a lil skeptical since it doesn't really look that appetizing but wow it is a super comforting plate of egg and ham fried rice with smoky flavour. i wiped the plate clean even though it was a mountain of rice (u can't tell from the picture cus the chicken chop is also huge)

PSA quality control is not the best - sometimes the chicken chop is a lil overcooked / tougher (but still decent)
author: Nic

review_text:
The 2 guys attitude really cannot make it, rude and can’t be bothered. I ordered the “Go Golden Crisp Fish”, and selected my 2 sides.

When I asked, “Can I add mentaiko sauce to the fries?” (Because they have mentaiko fries) the 1st guy just flat out said “no”. When I pointed out that their menu states that we can add the mentaiko sauce. He replied, “ya that one is alacart. So why not just say “Yes, but it’s alacart charges” as I was willing to pay. Finally he added it in, and I paid my bill.

When I came back to collect, the 2nd guy served me “Mushroom Grilled Fish”. Which was totally not what i ordered and I told the 2nd guy it was wrong. So we both check the receipt and order chit at the same time and found that it indeed states “Mushroom Grilled Fish”. All he said is, “The order is correct” and walked off to leave me with the food. I was willing to accept the mushroom fish, but he didn’t even make any attempt to check with the 1st guy or apologize for their mistake.

My mistake is not checking the receipt as it seem like something that could not go wrong, also the price Keyed into the register was the same as the Go Golden crisp fish.

Anyway the food was very bad as well, it was a waste of money. The fish was so thin and the sauce was water flavor, there was no taste whatsoever. The fries was rock hard as if fried then cooled then put into microwave oven. The coleslaw is just coleslaw nothing wrong, nothing special.

I do not recommend this place, not worth the money or time to visit. Also not worth to see the 2 rude guys. Shameful.
author: Nissan Skyline GTR32

review_text: It's a classic coffee shop western food outfit, at the heart of 6th avenue. They do cheap local pastas and chicken chops, and french fries. Don't expect too much out of this stall. Just see them as a place to fill the hunger pangs, or to getting some bar snacks for your wines if you're drinking across the road at Straits Wine.
author: Flo Yeow

review_text: Decent western food and affordably priced. $7.30 for chicken chop and two sides. I I usually Chose corn and onion rings. The chicken cutlet is total comfort food.
author: Cookie Monster

review_text:
Atlas Coffeehouse Review ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4.4/5)
Atlas Coffeehouse is a great spot for Western-style comfort food with a relaxed café vibe. I tried their Smoked Brûlée French Toast, and it was excellent — fluffy on the inside with a nicely crisp exterior. The smoky brûlée flavour paired really well with the berries, balancing sweetness without being cloying.
The long black was a solid choice too, clean and well-brewed, making it a good match with the French toast.
Overall, a satisfying experience with good food and coffee. Definitely a place I’d return to try other items on the menu. ☕🥞
author: Ewe Keat Huan

review_text:
Went for brunch on a Friday late morning. Place was not crowded like it usually is on weekends.

Staff gave a warm and chirpy welcome. Customers were manly adults when we were there and the acoustics made chatting comfortable.

The coffee and food were above average. Portions are “healthy living” size. 😅
author: PomChatChat

review_text:
Indoors can get pretty packed but managed to snag an indoor table to escape the heat.

Service was good & hospitable.
Food was wonderful, and the rosti/eggs were done beautifully. Rosti with a crispy exterior and fluffy middle & runny yolks on the eggs.

It is a good spot for brunch whenever you are in the area.
author: Jing Jie Ng

review_text:
Was here on a sunny Saturday afternoon. Thankfully, we only had to wait about 10–15 minutes for indoor seats and with an insanely hot weather, the air-conditioning was a lifesaver in the heat! The vibes were decent, and service was relatively fast with food arriving shortly after ordering.

We tried the Wurst Rosti, which had a nice crisp exterior with a moist centre. The sauce complemented it well, and the spicy chorizo add-on was an okay choice, did help to fill my stomach more but felt that the sausage skin was too tough to chew…. The Steak Hash was alright — decent but nothing particularly memorable plus the meat portion wasn’t justify for the price… There were more potatoes than steak that’s why it kept us full. Both sunny side ups were done wonderfully, makes me happy seeing such pretty eggs!

Didn’t order coffee because tables around us were lamenting how the coffee didn’t taste as good, hence we skipped.

Overall, a decent brunch spot, if you are around botanic garden area and you have a pet, this is the place though not quite exceptional enough to rave about..
author: Yun Yi Thiam

review_text:
First time at Atlas coffeehouse. Shoutout to the honeybutter tater tots- so good! Idk how they infuse each piece with the honeybutter flavour. It’s so addictive and I really enjoyed it.

I think the pancakes I got were alright though (there are better ones out there). Loved the butter and maple syrup on their waffles.

My gf got the new french toast with smoked butter and I found it kinda weird as it had a savoury smoky bbq taste which confused me. Still not too bad as the french toast was soft and pillowy inside which soaked up the sauce well.
author: Bryan CY Chua

review_text:
One of the best ribs ive ever eaten. Bourbon and hickory are good!
