Here for ribs but don’t expect too much for steak I guess 😅 reasonably priced.

Good old cozy place. Will be back again.
author: Miao

review_text:
EDIT: Meat n' Chill has ceased operations on 2 November 2025. A terrible shame.

Went there on a Sunday evening for dinner with friends. Place is relatively small and cozy, with the seating divided into a lower and upper floor area. We were seated upstairs as our reservation was for a bigger group, the lower area seemed to be packed as we were leaving so its probably best to make a reservation ahead of time if you're intending to come during peak dinner hours.

We ordered a selection of sides which included the Fried Calamari and Chilli Cheese Fries. Both were decent, although the fries felt like regular fries that you can find at NTUC.

Despite the relatively weak start, the pork ribs were a complete 180. They were quite literally "fall off the bone" tender and were simply delicious. I personally found the honey mustard flavour to be a tad too sweet to my liking and honestly preferred the Signature Original and Hickory flavours more. Nevertheless, if you're looking for a plate of excellent ribs, I can wholeheartedly recommend them.

Wanting to end off the meal with a dessert, we ordered a variety which included the Bro Bruce Browned Butter Brownie and the Belgian Waffles. The brownie was great, the waffle on the other hand was quite disappointing.

All in all, I would definitely still recommend this place just on the strength of the ribs alone.
author: Sean Phua

review_text:
Ribs are great meat falls off bone. .sauce excellent.  8.5/10

New York strip $24 tender medium rare but some gristle.  Juicy too.  8/10.  Very good value for money.  Cheap and good.

Quesadillas pulled chicken 7/10.  Not bad.

Vanilla bean milkshake 5/10.

Angus Ribeye $45 was excellent.  Tender. Little fat juicy almost perfect.

Crab cakes had too much crumb.

Restaurant feels old.  Free flow water.
author: Porter KHOR

review_text:
22/06/25
Excellent ribs and steakhouse, definitely better than typical chain restaurants. The pork ribs were tender, with meat so soft it fell off the bone. The Angus ribeye steak was flavorful and juicy, though the medium-rare doneness was inconsistent, with some portions slightly overcooked. The side dishes were delicious, especially the mashed potatoes, which had a rich, buttery taste.
author: Luke Skywalker

review_text: Went down to meat and chill for dinner and it was really good! Ribeye steak was cooked perfectly medium rare and the sauce went really well with it. Spicy mayo sauce with spam fries was a really nice snack. Not forgetting the truffle Mac and cheese that was super cheesy and tasty as well. Overall portion was huge for the price and taste wise was great.
author: Cheong Fu Sheng

review_text:
The name fat belly gave me the impression that the steak will be fatty. I was wrong. Both cut were lean, not what I expected.

We ordered Rump cap and dry age. If you're into marble steak, this is not it.

If the manager had not prepared us what to expect, I would have been disappointed.

Lucky, she when it was served she explained how it should be eaten and what to expect.

The rump cap has a natural sweetness, the dry age ribeye has more bite and gamey. both were lean and chewy. The edges of the ribeye were tough.

The veggies were ok. The cream sauce paired well with steak.

Asked for the chefs cut. It may be better.
author: Alex Lim

review_text:
Came for lunch. As we didn't make reservations, only outdoor seating was available. It was breezy and as that day was cloudy, it was nice and cool. Traffic wasn't heavy, so it didn't intrude allowing us to have quiet conversations.

We had the F1 Wagyu M2/3 Bavette (medium rare) with Grilled Maple Corn Ribs and Creamed Curly Kale as sides. The beef was tender with just the right amount of beefy flavour. The roasted garlic that came with the steak complemented the beef very well. The sides were equally delicious.

Service was good.
author: Le Rock Steady

review_text:
Had a quick and early lunch here on a Friday. There were already 4 tables seated at 11am+. We had a (temporary) dietary restriction and the lady manager was helpful about it. She has a professional yet also a chill vibe if that makes sense. Did not feel pressured to get apps.

We had the steak frites from the lunch menu which consists of the flat iron and a few dollars more for a good portion of fries and salad. Had a side of brussels sprouts also which did not taste that unhealthy. The steak had a smoky flavour and aroma with a nice crust.

Saw someone order the bolognaise. It looked delicious with a generous amount of meat sauce and it is blow torched. Should’ve tried it.

It is nice to see the chefs do their thing.
author: lion_doge

review_text: Definitely worth going. I heard about this place from an online post recommending steak places in Singapore. We went during lunch time, not many people, we booked bar seating but were able to get table seating when we get there. Food takes a while to serve, about 30 min from ordering. Their steak did not disappoint, it was worth waiting for. I ordered their 200g Full Blood Wagyu steak, it’s cooked to perfection. I love the pairing with garlic as it gives a special kick to the flavor. Burger is ok, nothing too special from other places I’ve tried.
author: KellyZ

review_text:
Super tasty and satisfying rice bowls. For lunch, we ordered sourdough with truffle and nori butter, the angus steak and iberico pork rice bowls and creamed curly kale. The portions were generous (except perhaps the serving of truffle and nori
butter - which was very yummy but gone too fast). The meats were tender. I especially love the deep fried brussel sprouts.
author: Anna Lee

review_text: Awesome Italian pizza 🍕 place with even better appetiser. However prices are close to high end pizza places but without the wood fire oven. Pizzas here are cooked in conventional electric ovens. There’s no smokey flavour but pizzas are still tasty.
author: Kelvin Wee

review_text:
The Pizza bar serves a good selection of thin crust pizzas 🍕, along with Italian beers and wines.
Both their air-conditioned and Al Fresco settings are relaxed and casual, suitable for dates and family events.

Service is brisk, with bottled/ tap water being served before orders are taken.
Good selection of wines and sides for some happy hour and for the price tag for Italian fare, I’d say it’s decent and worth my every visit.
It’s a pity I always miss out dessert as there no more room after all the antipasti and pastas.

There’s great deals throughout the week, check them out before visiting.

Service charge and GST applies.
author: desmonik

review_text:
Tried their seasonal specials menu which comprises of:

🦑Cuttlefish Squid Ink Croquettes ($18+)
Combination of creamy cuttlefish and squid ink, coated in panko crumbs and deep-fried to perfection. Elevated with a refreshing house-made dill aioli.

🐚Hokkaido Scallop ($28+)
Seared scallops served with a velvety cauliflower puree, offering a delightful textural contrast. The addition of pickled cauliflower and savory Ikura pops brings a burst of flavor to this elegant dish.

🍝Smoked Sardine Tagliolini ($35+)
Squid ink tagliolini pasta tossed in two complementary sauces: bagna cauda and piquillo. The bagna cauda sauce, a rich blend of anchovies and garlic, pairs perfectly with the subtle sweetness of Spanish piquillo peppers. Elevated with umami-packed smoked sardine slices, making it a true seafood lover's delight.

🍕Artichoke & Cantabrian Anchovy Pizza ($45+)
Da Paolo's signature artisanal thin-crust base topped with creamy artichoke purée, savory Cantabrian Anchovies, piquant salsa verde, caramelized balsamic onions, black olives, sliced artichoke, and a touch of heat from sliced red chili. Sprinkled with Parmesan cheese and Pecorino Romano, delivering a symphony of flavors.

🍨Pistachio & Mascarpone Chiffon ($20+)
This exquisite dessert features three variations of pistachios: a delicate and airy pistachio sponge, house-churned pistachio gelato, and crumbled pistachios, all beautifully complemented by rich and creamy mascarpone.

Some hits and misses, but highly recommend their pistachio gelato!!
author: fatspoting

review_text: I can’t believe I’ve never reviewed this place as we’ve been here numerous times. I just love Da Paola everywhere as food quality is consistently good and never disappoints. This pizza outlet of course, serves great pizza. Hubby’s fave is the 5 cheeses. Mine is the white mushroom and truffles oil (I normally avoid truffle oil as many restaurants overdo it but this one is fine). The meat lover is a bit of an overkill for us but great for meat lovers! So the pasta is also excellent a la da Paolo. I was first smitten years ago with their veal sauce ravioli at Cluny Court. Now we both like the creamy crab meat pasta and it’s a returnee. Oh the Mediterranean salad (HUGE) is also a favourite. Oh dear almost everything is a favourite. I must say, though, we often skip dessert as we get too full. So I can’t comment on dessert.
author: Nicole Yeong

review_text:
We were a group of 6 with elderly. Staff were friendly and helpful.

Nothing too fancy about this restaurant. However, Pizzas were very good and Spaegatti Carbonara was great too.

A nice little eatery to chill and grab a bite with family and friends.
author: S C

review_text:
One of the smaller but popular hawker center, perhaps due to its location just across the road from the Botanical Garden. Aside from a few hawker centers in places like Little India, this is perhaps one with the highest concentration of Halal (Malay, Indian Moslem, with one or two Javanese) stalls in SG. There are also a few non-Halal stalls as well, such as the chain chicken rice and Hokkien mie.

Went there a few times during visits in the area for breakfast and lunch. The nasi lemak stalls seem to be always having long lines in front of them. Tried the Sutra (?) Nasi Lemak, the rice and otah were well-spiced and marinated, although the ikan bilis was somehow wasn't as crunchy as what I expected. The Indian rojak was pretty nice, with spicy peanut sauce.
author: lontongstroong

review_text: We queued for Nasi Lemak from Adam's Nasi Lemak but was disappointed when the owner announced that they were closed as the food was sold out. Bought from Siti Nur Liyana instead - turned out good - for $5! We enjoyed the Indian Rojak from Adam's Indian Rojak. The 'paru' (lung) was really tender! Found that the Tray Return counter was clean & well-maintained. Toilet was nice & clean too!
author: Normawati Selamat

review_text:
So many halal stall still open, time now is 9pm on friday night.
Also the food that i bought  mutton ribs soup, taste soo delicious.
And youbadd on some white pepper powder and soy sauce (kicap)  make the vroth taste heavenly.. (not exaggerating) 😉
author: sulhi mohd

review_text:
Nice, clean and airy food court. Food is majority Malay/Muslim/Mamak. Little variety; many stalls offer similar items; nasi lemak, fried rice and fried noodles. Well patronised by Botanic Gardens weekenders.
No comments on the food; I only had teh tarik and curry puff.
author: Aaron Chung

review_text: Some empty stalls or sold out early not plenty options. They have section for halal and non halal food. Price is similar to other hawker places. It has open air in the middle but for those who concern about catching bad smells on their clothes or hair not advisable to come by. Otherwise within this area you dont really have lots of choice for local food. Dont think its worth coming for tourist.
author: Ryan Toqueen

review_text:
Definitely one of the older Nasi Lemak stalls in Adam Road Food Center. I decided to try it out instead of Selera Rasa because of the super long queue. The Makcik also was very friendly.

(Honestly, because Selera Rasa's chain of Crave hasn't been fanstastic in my opinion and actually sub-par.)

This was actually quite decent in terms of flavor, but a little pricey I feel in terms of portion at $5 for the chicken set.

The rice had the lemak taste, and I liked the little triangle egg omelette, but I thought a whole sunnyside-up would have been better for the price (like Mizzy Korner and Changi Village Famous Nasi Lemak). The chicken was warm and actually quite tasty.

Overall very normal.
author: Bryan Chihan

review_text:
Horrendous! Utterly unethical. Bought 2 Chicken Wing Set for family for lunch as today is CNY, am deeply disgusted and utterly pissed off.

They have the audacity to be selling uncooked coconut rice with very clear visible coconut yet to be cooked and fully infused with the rice. Rice is hard, totally inedible. Chicken wing is overcooked, taste of burnt.

I am amazed how the owner can serve such food. Totally ruin my family’s mood and have to waste this food as it is totally inedible!

I will suggest all to avoid this stall and totally not patron them. This is utterly disappointing and disgusting!

Never ever am I going to ever buy from them even if they are the only stall open. Pissed off.
author: Jovan

review_text: The nasi lemak is very above average cos the rice is very lemak. Fragrant but a bit inconsistent so you go on different days and it doesn’t taste the same. Fried chicken is decent enough. But the biggest problem is they charge FIFTY CENTS for take away, on the higher end of takeaway charge at hawker centres. But their takeaway materials are styrofoam and paper (for the fried chicken). I understand the plastic containers costs money but they’re are between 20 to 30 cents in most hawker centres. 50 cents in this case when they’re using regular takeaway materials seems like taking advantage of the customer.
author: Angela Lau

review_text:
Always go to this Nasi Lemak rather than the one (I had it once it was horrible - the egg was cold and oily and the otak already sour) beside it which spots a super long queue. I understand it is the crowd effect - everyone queues for this so you think this is the better one!

But No. 1 is much better in terms of freshness of ingredients, the heart to do good nasi lemak can be seen from how they prepare each item. The long grain coconut fragrance rice paired with the nicely fried condiments and slightly sweet sambal chilli adds up a simple quality nasi lemak.

Overall, not the best in Singapore, but a must-go-to for nasi lemak when I am in the area.
author: Hao Yang Fu

review_text: Totally love the Nasi lemak, rice is fluffy, chicken is crispy, chili goes extremely well with the dish! Wish that aunty could have speed up in her serving as it’s nasi lemak and I queued for 20 mins to get the bowl of rice, fried chicken that’s readily fried and egg all done.. the queue was “ not extremely long”
author: Empress Ker

review_text:
The Living Café is a nice spot if you’re into healthier-style desserts and pastries. Their menu focuses on clean, wholesome ingredients, which is a plus for those with dietary preferences or restrictions.
The coffee was okay—nothing particularly outstanding, but decent enough to pair with the desserts. Prices, however, are on the higher side, which might feel a bit steep considering the overall experience.
I tried the lemon pistachio cake (dairy-free). It was good and not bad at all, though it didn’t really stand out or leave a strong impression. Still, a decent option if you’re looking for dairy-free desserts.
Overall rating: ⭐ 3.9/5
A good place for healthier treats, but the pricing and average coffee keep it from being exceptional.
author: Ewe Keat Huan

review_text:
A excellent place to get great tasting organic, vegan food options. We especially enjoyed the drinks!
The coconut curry dahl was a huge serving which we hadn't expected. But it was so good we polished off the entire bowl!
author: Darren Siow

review_text:
Quiet and cosy place for wholesome desserts.

Check in rewards for a free ice lemon tea. Great place to chill and relax.

Desserts were tasty and could taste the ingredients. Definitely different from the mass produced type of desserts.

Establishment accept CDC and Grab as payment.

Cafe is located just beside six avenue mrt exit.

We had the Raw Lemon Pistachio tart and the Chocolate Avocado Mousse 😋😋
author: WH

review_text: this place is a godsend to me! i am gluten free dairy free and soy free. there are so few places i can dine at comfortably and this place is not just safe for me, but creative in how they make lagsana, or “goat cheese”. i am so satiated and happy to have this option. definitely returning :)
author: Cho Tofu

review_text:
At this cafe, usual ingredients are swapped out to create a “healthier” version of the food. I ordered the Goat Cheese Quiche ($14) and it’s gluten-free. The filling is light and soft, and the tart is very crumbly. Won’t taste as rich as your regular quiche, but it’s a nice alternative.

Some items on the menu can be quite pricey, but you can use CDC vouchers here.
author: M N

review_text: The tacos are really authentic, especially the fish taco, fresh, flavorful, and perfectly crispy. Highly recommend pairing it with a hard shell for extra crunch. Staff were friendly and attentive. Will definitely be back!
author: Sylvia Fan

review_text: I love this Mexican restaurant and have been a regular from years ago. The food never disappoints, I always get the pulled pork chimichanga, along with a side of loaded nachos. This time round I got the calamari and it was crispy, savoury and zesty. The service is also quick and attentive, every dining experience has been nothing short of fantastic. Highly recommend!
author: Dan O

review_text:
My family and I came by here, we tried the Quesadillas with Pulled Pork, Fish Tacos, Chimichanga with Shredded Chicken and Nachos with Beef. They were all delicious with each dish being served with Guacamole and Sour Cream, with onions. Staff here were also really friendly and nice!

Will definitely come here again!
author: Matthew Chuang

review_text: Not many places sell Fajitas, and this is one. It was not as nice as it used to be, but then again it's been a long time since I was here. The Chimichanga was very good. Deep fried just right, crispy, and tasty.
author: Jason Ong

review_text:
Located in Holland Village.

Excellent Mexican cuisine here. Friendly, patient and attentive waiters provide pleasant service here. Very filling quesadillas with lots of cheese, meat and dipping sauce like sour cream and guacamole. Good nachos too with generous amounts of cheese. Chipotle wings came out very hot and were crispy and well marinated. The dipping chipotle sauce was very strong with both sweet and savoury flavours. Overall a very satisfying experience
author: Elijah Lim

review_text:
Love the chocolate H2O as it was so rich and delightful! Amazing blend of salty and sweet taste from the caramel sauce and the chocolate. Didn’t go for the pairing but it’s nice place for a (artistic and expensive) sweet treat. It used to be darker the last time I visited years ago, and now it’s brighter so it’s great.

Excellent service staff who were polite and professional.
author: Paepae S

review_text: Desserts were beautifully crafted and tasted so good. Although the service crew were busy on a Saturday night, they were efficient and patient. They celebrated my mom’s birthday with complimentary chocolates as well. Thank you for the great service!
author: Michelle Tan

review_text:
The moment you enter there's a very bad smell. We were 'welcomed' by this staff and the first thing she said after asking is if we have a reservation was , each person has to spend minimum 20 dollars today. It didn't feel good hearing that. (I spent way more than that per person lol). It simply felt like "if you don't spend more than 20 dollars per person then you are not welcome." Why is that something to tell?

The service wasn't great either. The good part, they explain very nicely which is nice. They even show the food with lights after serving which is a nice touch. They also recommend what's good. They were also nice enough to recommend us non alcoholic stuff which was nice.

The bad part, we dropped a spoon, so we asked for another. We literally asked 3 times. Twice to the same person once to another. Both of them forgot. Had to wait for quite a while.

Food wise. Desserts were actually awesome. Loved them. So was the drink. The taco was good too! I'd go back for the food, but didn't really feel welcomed here. If we did we would have gotten more food too.

Hope you improve on your service, because the food is great.
author: Tashfique Niloy

review_text: Went there on a weekday night, vibes was great. Really lovely and chill atmosphere. Had a dessert along with a cocktail and both are amazing. Love how there's an introduction given about the dessert and instructions/directions on how to enjoy the dessert fully. Would 100% go again
author: Xuan

review_text:
After 10 years, we are still amazed that @2amdessertbar is rockin their dessert craft.

🍫 I had the Chocolate H20 - which was a chocolate dessert (inaya chocolate?) drizzled with salted caramel and paired with a refreshing yuzu sobert; it came with chocolate soil, yuzu calamensi gel and caramel bavarois.

I don't recall ever having yuzu with chocolate and this combination was surprisingly good! The inaya chocolate was layered and molten in the middle. I love the rich chocolate soil when dipped with the yuzu calamansi gel.

🍷 I had it with the drink pairing - a (red) Coppi Siniscalo Primitivo. It smelt very fragrant when introduced but surprisingly the notes weren't pronounced when drank. It was however smooth and light.

My friend had the Sticky Date Pudding that was vegan and dairy free. It surprisingly tasted like dairy! It was served warm and enjoyable on a cold day.

Service can be improved but we were amazed that the price for the desserts are more or less the same as 10 years ago. For this craftmanship, this is definitely value for money.

Would love to try their other desserts in the future when we are back to Holland V!
author: Ruth

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Bukit Timah
review_text:
We ordered the mahi mahi with a charcoal-grilled cooking style. However, it turned out a bit fishy and not fully cooked.

The lobster was tender, and the truffle cream sauce was great. The seafood soup was also great. The king crab lobster was just average — we couldn’t taste much freshness, and it simply didn’t hit the mark. The pasta was quite tasteless.

The total bill came to $493, including one bottle of white wine ($79.3). We don’t think it’s worth the price given the food quality.

Overall, the service was excellent, but the food definitely needs improvement.
author: Alice Wang

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Bukit Timah
review_text:
Went there to celebrate a birthday.

- The oysters were fantastic!
- The sashimi wer thick and delicious!
- The hummus was great, but I'm not a fan of the dough fritter that came with it. Doesn't go well.
- Pull pork pizza. (If you like pull pork, it's very sweet, lots of cheese, decent pizza base/dough)
- Sweet Potato Mash (avoid it. It was sour...we were offered to change it to Truffle Fries. It was really good)

Highly recommend if you are here for seafood and the oysters.
author: Abigail Tan

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Bukit Timah
review_text:
Greenwood Fish Market is hands down one of the best places for seafood lovers, especially if you’re an oyster fan. The oysters are exceptionally fresh, clean, briny, and bursting with natural sweetness. Each one tastes like it was just shucked straight from the sea, and the variety available makes the experience even better.

Beyond the oysters, the quality of the food here is consistently top notch. The beef burger is a pleasant surprise, juicy, well seasoned, and cooked perfectly, with a satisfying bite and great balance of flavours. It holds its own even alongside their seafood offerings. Everything is handled with care, clearly fresh, and prepared simply to let the ingredients shine.

Service is knowledgeable and friendly, always happy to recommend oysters or explain the differences between them. It’s a place you can trust for quality food, and between the fresh oysters and the excellent beef burger, it’s easy to see why this spot is a favourite. A well deserved 5 stars.
author: Shawn Chua

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Bukit Timah
review_text: Food is alright, relatively fresh seafood - although one of the pieces we had tasted awful nothing like what we ordered. Thankfully the staff agreed to swap it for us at no cost so allsgood. Burrata was really creamy.
author: Sarah Constance

restaurant_name: Greenwood Fish Market | Seafood Restaurant & Market in Bukit Timah
review_text: Atmosphere was good with the restaurant bustling with filled tables and Christmas songs in the background. However, it'd be better if the volume of the music was softer as we had to raise our voices to hear each other across the table. Quality of food was good, taste wise was ok. Would recommend the white wine mussles from France and lobster bisque.
author: Sherlyn Peng

review_text:
Visited Two Chefs Eating Place at Commonwealth and it absolutely lived up to its reputation for honest, flavourful zi char. We ordered their famous coffee ribs and the XO fish slice hor fun, and both dishes were standout favourites.

The coffee ribs were fragrant the moment they arrived at the table, a perfect balance of sweet, smoky, and slightly bitter notes from the coffee coating. The meat was tender and came off the bone easily, with a caramelised glaze that made every bite addictive. It’s clear why this is their signature dish; it’s unique yet comforting.

The XO fish slice hor fun was equally impressive. The wok hei was strong, the hor fun silky, and the XO sauce added a beautiful depth without overpowering the dish. The fish slices were fresh, thick, and perfectly cooked, complementing the savoury gravy so well. My only gripe is the fish has a 土味. It’s one of those dishes that feels simple but is executed with real skill.

Service was fast and efficient even though the place was busy, and the overall experience felt very local, lively, and satisfying. Prices are reasonable for the quality and portions. If you’re looking for classic zi char with standout flavours, Two Chefs at Commonwealth is definitely worth the trip. I’ll be back!
author: Yvonne Chou

review_text:
Definitely one of the better Tze Char places around. All the more better due to relatively inexpensive pricing likely from the non-loading of heavy rental from evil landlords.

I hadn't been back here for a long time; since before they opened the SinMin branch. Still good. My minor grumble (because I'm grumpy) is the Si Hum being served in a plastic container. 2nd minor grumble is that the Har Cheong Gai flavour is less intense than I recall it.

Butter pork ribs and cereal prawns all good. Beer price is reasonable too! Never did ask whether BYO is acceptable here.

Note: Cash, CDC Vouchers only. No PayNow.
author: Benjamin T P Tan (btptan)

review_text:
The first time I was there last year, food was good. Last night however was a total disappointment. Lohei was a tad too sweet. Fish maw soup and dried shrimps either long beans were acceptable but I was expecting better due to their good reputation. Prawn paste chicken has no taste of the prawn paste. San Mee was not crispy before mixing. Chef’s recommended tofu with enoki mushrooms was nothing special. I could easily cook this myself at home. The worse of all, chili crab. One piece of crab costs $70. We wanted to enjoy the sauce with fried mantou, but the failure was in that sauce. It was sour! The reason given was to lessen the spiciness, hence the chef added more ketchup. Perhaps they should change the brand of the ketchup if the chef has no skill balancing out spiciness and sourness. Not a single cent was discounted on that dish. Service recovery was bad on this part.
Had made an advanced reservation for next week’s dinner with colleagues. I am definitely not coming back.
author: Chris Cross

review_text: Pretty good zichar place in Singapore. Quite affordable too. I heard about the highly raved butter pork ribs which came with condensed milk powder on top of perfectly fried pork ribs. So sinful but bloody good! We also got their signature tofu with mushrooms and the spinach with eggs. Both were decent, nothing mindblowing. Fried rice had wok hei and was decent too. Total damage $37.50 for 3 pax. Super worth it!
author: Bryan CY Chua

review_text: We order their recommended dishes. The food is delicious. You can come earlier than the operating hours at about 15 mins earlier they will start already. Environment is okay, sheltered eating place. Cash or CDC Vouchers only.
author: L A

review_text:
Fantastic restaurant and we are extremely happy to pay premium for really good sashimi. The staff members were hilarious and really entertaining. Gary had always been the lead man and had served us really well, giving us the best cuts and slices.

Thomas and Anna were fantastic as well, constantly making sure our glasses were full and have received all our orders.

This is the only place we run to for our Japanese comfort food in Singapore. Highly recommended!
author: Leah Keh

review_text: Best dinner experience we’ve ever had! Not only was the food absolutely delicious, but the service made the night even more memorable. A special thanks to Anna and Thomas— she was professional, fun, and gave us great recommendations for both the food and sake. We had such an enjoyable night with her. We’ll definitely be coming back for the amazing people and food!
author: Penny Phoon

review_text:
For diners seeking a satisfying Japanese dining experience that offers excellent value, Shin Yuu delivers with its impressive à la carte buffet. The restaurant stands out for its quality ingredients and diverse menu options that cater to both traditional and contemporary Japanese cuisine preferences.

The sashimi selection was a particular highlight - each slice of fish was served at perfect temperature with that unmistakable freshness that melts in your mouth. From the buttery salmon to the clean-tasting tuna, the quality rivaled many dedicated sushi bars.

Another standout dish was the stir-fried beef, which arrived sizzling with just the right balance of tenderness and smoky wok flavor. The beef was thinly sliced and well-marinated, making it one of the more memorable cooked dishes of the evening.

The sake experience elevated the meal further. The servers demonstrated good knowledge of their selection and recommended bottles that complemented our food choices beautifully.

Service throughout was warm and attentive, with staff checking in regularly without being intrusive. The only drawback is the limited seating space, so reservations are highly recommended, especially during peak dining hours.

For those looking for quality Japanese fare at reasonable prices, Shin Yuu offers one of the better buffet deals in town. The combination of fresh sashimi, well-executed cooked dishes, and good sake makes it a spot worth returning to.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: Not one for reviews but this was great! Had an amazing experience celebrating my mother's birthday here! We had omakase for 9 pax and were given the private room, which rly heightened our experience here :) Service was great thanks to Thomas and Ana, they were patient and efficient! Gary the chef was hilarious as well. Really appreciated the special touch of the birthday cake as well :) would definitely come back here again! Food was 10/10 amazing, please try the omakase if you're here!
author: Hannah Lim

review_text:
This place left me confused my first time on a weekday lunch buffet.

It has the potential. Can come back for another try.

Came back a second time.

Another weekday lunch buffet.

Better this time!

Saba fish was excellent.
author: 4vi31t

review_text: Ordered 2 pizzas for takeaway under the 1 for 1 promo. I think the pizza is quite decent and offers great value at around $28 for 2 pizzas after gst. Personally, i still think its best to have the pizza when its fresh out of the oven, so maybe consider to reheat the pizza if you order takeaway.
author: Jason Soh

review_text: Famed wood fire pizza joint with tons of topping choices & variety! Loved their crispy calamari and rich iced chocolate. Whole meal dough options available too. Cozy spot for pizza and chill vibes 😋. Perfect for foodies and friends gathering!
author: Ian Sarah

review_text:
Service is quick and serving of food was really quick. Of all the dishes on pictures, my favourite is the pesto pasta.

Pizza is thin crust and authentic.
author: Alex Lim

review_text:
Very nice Italian restaurant in Balmoral plaza. East access by public transportation.
Food is great and they have some good deals too. Staff is very courteous and service is very quick. Awesome range of pizzas and good other food options.
author: Rajeev Kapoor

review_text: Nice pizza and on weekdays they have 1 for 1 for all pizzas and pastas. I love their fried chicken wing. Piping hot, crunchy and good tasting battered wings. A 'must order' with their pizzas!
author: Amy Leong

review_text:
Nice Japanese restaurant at RTC. Service is good and the staff recognises the members by name.

Would come here for meals compared to the western n Chinese restaurants.

Gonna miss this spot when it is on en bloc next year :((
author: elayna chin

review_text: I was invited by a friend who insisted that I taste this special set lobster menu at the Raffles Town Club. The chef in attendance was creative in preparing his dish with  fresh ingredients like salmon, lobster, wagyu beef he had in hand . The meal started  light with veg salad , prawn fritters, the salmon platter,  garlic fried rice  and  miso soup. Then came the main course of  the butter garlic lobster,  fried rice with the marinated cube beef . The course was a delightful treat to the palate as each dish was prepared with care by the chef n presented hot in beautiful plating. A fabulous lunch that leaves one fully contented enjoying the different flavours of japanese crusine in one sitting. Worth the Indulgence if one is thinking of enjoying a well balanced thought out menu , which I fully agreed with my foodie friend . The service was above par as staff were attentive to the needs of the diners. Heard that the club would be closing its door in a year time and sad to see another hidden gem that has great food gone. So support  the culinary skills of these chefs as they are rare to find today.
author: Cheong Loong

review_text:
Making the best of an old building with minimum of upkeeping by management and owners of the private club that Miyabi is located in, it makes up for the delicious food & service by chef & staff.

I was almost 45 mins late for my reservations, however the manager was all smiles and kept saying ‘no worries, no problem’ while showing us to our table.

We had booked specially to try the Wagyu Beef set special for August - but was disappointed to realise that it was sold out as there were more diners than expected that Sunday!

We ended up a bento set of beef sukiyaki & grilled cod, which turned out very nice indeed.  We were surprised with a chawanmushi each, and a choc tiramisu dessert that we did not order.  A pleasant offer to make up for the disappointment.

Service was brisk & efficient, tea & water top-up was unobstructive.
author: Adeline O

review_text:
Very busy restaurant with value set lunch and dinner.

Best teppanyaki Restaurent in SG. We often visit this place for our teppanyaki fix and the seat meals are value for money.

Beef is something which is a must order every trip and we manage to try their Boston Lobster.

There was a lot of meat compare to other joints and it was comparable to having steam lobster at a chinese seafood restaurant.

Quality is also consistent and sometime wait time might be long due to how popular it is.
author: WH

review_text: Come here pretty often when I eat out with my grandparents as they are members ! The food here is not bad and it doesn’t take that long to come ! Have tried quite a few items on the menu and they were all pretty good !
author: pam

review_text: Visited this place on a weekday during lunch. Was the only patrons at noon, so for a table for two, we were waited on by three staff members. Despite the high staff to customer ratios, refilling of water requires a degree of effort, which marred the dining experience. Food wise was decent, the trio of pork being a good value, but probably would not be sufficient for two big eaters. The serving of the course were well timed, and clearing of the dishes prompt. Overall, quite comfortable a place to dine, but could be perfect if staff could be more proactive in topping up of the water.
author: Derrick Tan

review_text: A small restaurant, slightly dated feel but you can argue the other way and say that there is some old world charm here. Delivers mainly angmoh food with a tapas menu, and for October they have an Oktoberfest promotion. During covid times there are a number of takeaway promotions. This is the flagship angmoh restaurant inside of RTC, not as posh as Churchill room at tanglin but also easier on the wallet
author: Crème Brûlée

review_text:
Appallingly poor food and service for the price, looks like all the staff worth anything must have jumped from the sinking ship.

Waiter didn't know what a rare steak was. Kitchen didn't know what a medium steak was. Pork rib was tough and leathery.

Eat anywhere else.
author: Ryan Martin Ang

review_text: Quite good! Enjoy the food well.
author: C.W.

review_text: Had a birthday dinner with wifey & son, both falls in April, 2 days apart. Small restaurant with private dining feel. Kudos to the crew who were attentive & prompt with their services.
author: Michael Tay

review_text:
Came in during lunch time with my mother…
Menu surprisingly limited to local fare, western selections, pizza, drink and dessert.

Ordered a pork chop and chocolate sundae… both of which were really good… extremely hard to find places that don’t overcook them. Ma’s black bean beef hor fun marginally better than Changi Village’s…

But PLEASE take note to not eat here unless you’re a member or a guest of a member to the Raffles Town Club

For their part though, the waiters were fairly understanding, as it was almost the end of lunch time. If I’ve a membership or a friend who has membership, would go eat again imo. 4 stars !
author: Justin Wong

review_text:
I rate the majority of the staff for their warmth, flexibility & caring attitude to me & my 33 guests while we were there for thirteen days, daily breakfasts, some lunches & dinners.

Organising the space so that the group can be managed effectively, changing a few items in the menu as the students were not familiar with the food, and advising me on reducing or increasing certain menu items helps in minimising any food wastage.

Chef was open to cooking a S’pore favourite dish a bit different to ensure that it did not look ‘uncooked’ to the diners.  He was helpful in cutting up pineapples for the group when we brought in a few to treat the group.

The cafe was open, casual & spacious.
Food was standard cafe fare with local & western favourites, prices were on par as outside for some items.
author: Adeline O

review_text: Chicken rice was very nice. Place is under utilized. Come for a peaceful relaxing time.
author: Jason Chung

review_text: Food is ok. Tried the fish and chip, batter and fish are fresh. Services on the slow side but the service crews are friendly. This place is for members only
author: Backyard Xplorer

review_text:
Definitely a refreshing change from the environment outside - it's like I've stepped into another world.

From the good smells to the good spacing and the excellent food. Highly recommend to drive in rather than taking the disgusting train.
author: Lunch Chiao

review_text: Came here for a weekday lunch. The restaurant was pretty quiet when we first arrived and more people coming in towards 1pm. They had set lunch promos and I highly recommend to take this option as I find it quite value for money. A starter, a main and a dessert/coffee. I knew from their days in AMK park to be famous for their har cheong gai waffle (prawn paste chicken waffle) and I ordered it again after so many years. It still tasted good. The mushroom was stick (not the watery type) and pretty decent sized. Overall, a good experience here.
author: Alan Tan

review_text:
Everything was absolutely delicious, and the service was truly exceptional from start to finish. The staff were attentive, friendly, and made the whole dining experience very enjoyable. I especially loved the drinks and special thanks to Vicco for crafting such delicious and well-balanced drinks and for the great service.

Overall, it was a wonderful experience with great food, excellent drinks, and top-notch service. I will definitely be coming back again and would highly recommend this place to family and friends who are looking for a great spot to dine and unwind.
author: Amberlynn Chng

review_text:
We celebrated our son’s 100-day milestone at this restaurant, and the experience was wonderful!
The staff were incredibly patient, friendly, and supportive, helping us with every detail of the celebration.
Thanks to their thoughtful assistance, we were able to enjoy a smooth and joyful event with our family.
We truly appreciate the team’s effort and would be happy to visit again! ✨
author: Yingya Huang

review_text:
Wanted to get a quick bite after checking into my room and settled for GRUB. I'm not new to GRUB so I didn't expect much on the food. Personally I'm not a fan of open kitchen concept in an enclosed environment as you will get an oil smell after your meal. My pasta was alright but for the price tag I wouldn't fine it fantasic.
I would definitely order more if there is a discount for hotel guests since this is one way to attract hotel guests to patronise the eateries within the hotel precinct.
author: Ben Lau

review_text:
Ordered 2 sets lunch, starters and mains were decent.
(Mains were served as regular portion but starters & dessert were not the usual portion )

I was quite disappointed that the dessert was served as a half portion (on the menu it doesn’t state half portion cheesecake). The server asked me to feedback to them. But after that, none of the staff members or manager bothered to give me a proper resolution from the time I raised the issue till the point we settled the bill. (just feign ignorance)

I thought it could have been very reasonable for the staff members to do an immediate service recovery by changing both our half-thinly sliced cheesecakes to 2 full slices, or the staff member or manager could've given us a proper explanation & label their menu clearly so other diners wouldn't find this misunderstanding in the future.
author: Ray Heng

review_text:
The best Japanese restaurant with affordable price in Singapore for my family.
A wide variety of set meal (Gozen) are very worth for money. Fishes are very fresh. Japanese western food such as Tonkatsu, Steak, Grilled chicken are also very very well cooked. Kids meal are very attractive for Children too.
Their seasonal menu is 'must try'.
Atmosphere is sophisticated and quiet. Maybe family with baby is not preferred.  　But kids are OK as long as they understand the situation.
author: RYKAYOYU

review_text: An exclusive members-only Japanese restaurant—prepare for an authentic experience that delivers exactly what you expect and more.
author: Andrew Tan atomi Singapore

review_text:
In the ever escalating contest for over-the-top Japanese experiences in Singapore, it’s great to enjoy an authentic meal that isn’t ostentatious nor relies on the freshest and/or rarest ingredients or spiky sea creatures to delight diners. We’ve thoroughly enjoyed each visit, be it for a chirashi bowl or a set variety of cooked and fried dishes.  The tempura is especially notable - the prawn heads may be the best I’ve ever had anywhere.

Unfortunately, Akane is a members-only restaurant, so our visits here are far less often than we’d like =(
author: Wen Huang

review_text: Great place to have a private dinner. Great food with great service.
author: Lim AS

review_text: Had the biz dinner in the private room in this Japanese restaurant, enjoyed their excellent service with the good taste of all the dishes
author: Ben Lin

review_text: Quiet, large, spick and span restaurant, popular with members and guests. Have great choice of Japanese food with set meals, soups, sashimi, ramen, and ala carte meals
author: Victor Wong

review_text:
A great authentic family restaurant nestled within the Japanese Association. Maybe it’s the Japanese families dining around you, but it feels exactly like Japan in this place. Although the food isn’t the best, there is a warm homely flavour to the dishes. Had the seasonal special Hamburg rice with demi-glace sauce and was pleasantly surprised by the huge portion, with the beef being tender and not too gamey. Special shout-out for the salmon head which also comes in a generous portion for a very reasonable price!

Do take note that only members may gain entry or bring guests to dine at the restaurants within the Japanese Association.
author: Brandon Louis Rozario

review_text:
The service and taste must be good because it’s the Japanese restaurant in the heart of Japanese Association... did look fine to me.

The dishes like set menu, donburi, and assorted sushi are around $20 should be good pricing. I actually felt like ordering Unagi Bento with a free drink bar for $27 or so...

The problem is, only the Japanese Association members or the escorted guests can dine there and I had to leave the place just before ordering like a guy in a wrong place.
author: Xiro Ar (Alphonz)

review_text:
We adjourned here for desserts and coffee after lunch at Akane.  The staff here are friendly and helpful.

If possible, request for the private room at the end if you are a large group.  There is a $10 surcharge but this can be waived.

There are special offers which include free flow beverages for $3 each if you order a mains or dessert.  It was well worth it, as we could try their cold brew coffee, cappuccino, mango juice and teas etc.

We enjoyed desserts like matcha ice cream, coffee with vanilla ice cream, mochi and cheesecake cup.

You need to be a member or signed in by one to enter Akane or Donguri.
author: steven lim

review_text: Members only exclusive - donguri family restaurant
author: Andrew Tan atomi Singapore

review_text:
Celebrate CNY here, and had a wonderful experience. The highlight was the God of Wealth walking around with a pot of gold coin chocolates and giving blessings to the diners. It felt very festive and joyful. Everyone was smiling and taking photos. It really brought a strong New Year atmosphere.
Another lovely surprise was that during this New Year period, they gave each table a mini “盆菜.” It was such a heartwarming gesture and made us feel special and welcomed.
There was a good variety of food, and everything tasted delicious. The venue was beautifully decorated with festive decorations, which made the celebration even more lively. Although it was crowded because of the New Year season, the staff were still very attentive and provided excellent service. Thumbs up!
author: Cheiro Theorem

review_text:
The high ratings of this hotel buffet is no scam or coincidence. For starters, 4.4 stars (as of 21 Feb 2026) is very high for buffet, where food quality is often compromised for quantity and variety.

Not at the orchard cafe. The variety is considerably higher, especially when compared to other similar priced buffets. The food quality is also great. Special mention to the grilled live stations. Room for improvement is the snow crab legs, where the texture of the legs is not very firm.

In the comments below, you'll see specific mentions praising specific staff member. The restaurant doesnt offer benefits or perks in exchange for reviews. In other words, the service is genuine and good enough for many people to leave good reviews and praise for the staff. Special mention to Tina, who was very diligent and warm in ensuring that we got the food we wanted and following up with us without becoming disruptive or overbearing (I.e. good sense of space). During CNY, the restaurant also gave use a free pack of bak kwa to take home. I also saw staff members singing birthday song for persons having their birthdays without causing a ruckus.

Overall, probably the best buffet experience I've had in Singapore.
author: shao yan

review_text:
I had lunch at Orchard Café to celebrate my birthday with my friends, and we had an amazing experience. Ms. Tina Soh welcomed us with a warm smile and genuine hospitality. Her team — Amy, Lawrence, and Minah — were incredibly attentive and helpful throughout our meal. They were quick to assist with anything we needed and answered all our questions with patience.

We ended the lunch with a lovely complimentary birthday cake, which made the celebration even more special. Thank you to the wonderful team at Orchard Café for making my birthday lunch truly memorable! Highly recommended.
author: Jameszedrick Bautista

review_text: I never thought the buffet here is great until I was searching for one with chocolate fondue as it was the wish of my kid for her birthday. Upon early arrival, they allowed us to enter and did a one Quick Look at their spread. It is AMaZing! Ranging from local, Christmas festive, desserts, Indian, and good mix of varieties. If I were to rate this with the hotel 5 mins drive away, this is an amazing find! The quality of food was way off expectation, tasty and very well prepared. Lots of desserts and drinks stations as well. Must also highlight great services of the staffs plus the two smiley managers Evelyn and Catherine who provided the warmest of hospitality. I will return again!
author: Alan Morghan

review_text:
Had a wonderful Christmas lunch buffet and our family was very satisfied with the whole setup. Before we entered the restaurant, there was staff dressed up in santarina costume and help us take nice photos of the Christmas setup in hotel lobby. And while waiting to enter restaurant, we were served a drink with rosemary and a raspberry. It was unique and nice.

The food selection was good and we were not disappointed. Roast suckling pig, roast lamb, roast wagyu beef, gammon ham, whole salmon, lamb chops, foie gras, bbq prawns, tempura, lobster, crab legs, various shellfish, roast duck, roast pork, laksa station, sashimi station, cheese station, bread and the wonderful dessert section with my favorite logcakes and durian pengat. Oh they even have live slicing of a leg of prosciutto and a mulled wine counter. (The only thing we feel that can be improved, the on ice lobster and crab was bit overcooked)

We were blown away by the taste and the service of the staff. Everyone was so friendly and so accommodating. Like to specially mention Sam, who I think is one of the managers, who took care of us very well. Always with a smile and engages us during our lunch. Although it was a busy service, he took time to share with me the wine offering and offered me a tasting glass. That made my mind to order more. The wine was nice and went well with the various meats.

Overall, I will come back again and definitely 2026 Xmas will be our 1st choice!
author: John Cheong

review_text:
Singapore’s Ultimate Mexican Experience! 🌮🍹 (5/5 Stars)

Skip the restaurant chains where you pay a premium for average tacos and watered down margaritas.

Mexico Mama delivers perfection every single time! From the first bite, you’ll know why this is the gold standard for Mexican cuisine in Singapore: bold, authentic flavors that keep you coming back for more.

But here’s the kick; it’s not just the food. Jeff and Shavs bring a level of hospitality that turns every visit into an unforgettable memory. Warm, lively, and downright infectious, their energy makes you feel like family from the moment you walk in.

Cocktail lovers, brace yourselves: the margaritas are sinful, Long Islands dangerously good, and the beer selection including stellar IPAs is nothing short of spectacular.

Whether it’s mouthwatering Mexican food, killer cocktails, or just an unforgettable vibe, Mexico Mama is a non-negotiable 5-star experience. Head to Mexico Mama Now!
author: Bhuvana Asokan

review_text: Delicious! I'm from Texas and did not expect to find such good Mexican food on the other side of the planet. Highly recommend the guacamole. Appreciate that the tortilla chips were freshly made and not from a bag.
author: Robert Sebastian

review_text: Yummy authentic Mexican food with suchhh great vibes all around! Really enjoyed the pork and beef tacos - goes perfectly with a pint of San Miguel!
author: Elizabeth Tan

review_text:
Since coming back from the US, I’ve been disappointed with every Mexican restaurant in Singapore, that’s until my friend introduced me to Mexico Mamma!

Honestly, the best and most authentic Mexican food you can find here in Singapore. Jeff also made the whole experience better by being so welcoming and chill.

Definitely my go-to spot for tacos in Singapore from now on!
author: Adelene (Adele)

review_text: Food here is not bad, though after a while it can get quite one dimensional. Not sure if it’s just me?? Their normal spicy is tolerable for me, but if you can’t take spice pls don’t go for it haha. You can try their medium spice instead! Took quite a while for them to churn out orders, but there was only 1 guy cooking so completely understandable. The ambience is great too so that can be your distraction? :’) Overall price point is rather high, but I feel it’s def worth it to a certain extent. Highly likely will dine here again, esp when craving for fish tacos and guacamole!
author: JM

restaurant_name: The Lobby Lounge at Shangri-La Singapore
review_text: Lovely food and great service by everyone except one short Indian man who is bald and does not smile. The management should fire him and replace him with someone polite who smiles. He brings down the quality of the place and undermines the efforts of all the staff all of whom are wonderful. My partner had the chicken rice which was very good and I had the Hokkien mee 100% best in Singapore
author: Dementia Beat

restaurant_name: The Lobby Lounge at Shangri-La Singapore
review_text:
Absolutely excellent food as always, with the kitchen maintaining its prestigious high standards, now enhanced by a lovely renovation featuring new leather furnishings and updated lighting.

I visited Shangri-La Singapore during Christmas week, the first hotel of the renowned Asian hotel chain, which opened in 1971 and pioneered the tall, gold-decorated lobby now synonymous with Shangri-La hotels.

The atmosphere was buzzing, with a gigantic real Christmas tree, complemented by genuinely warm service. The staff were courteous, efficient, and unfailingly polite at all times.

Since my last visit a year ago, the lobby has been refreshed with new furniture, lavish leather sofas and lantern-style chandeliers. The space now feels brighter and more inviting, giving it a fresh new feel. The menu remains very reasonably priced.

The food was well done and every dish was generously portioned. I caught myself saying “Wow!” more than once, especially with the chicken curry and the chocolate cake decorated with gold flakes.

Up first was the carrot cake, lighter in colour, refined, tasty, and well-sized.
The chicken curry was simple yet full of flavour, with a right balance of coconut milk and spice. The asam pedas was aromatic and hearty, with a tamarind sourness that paired beautifully with the hot rice. To drink I had a soothing chin chow, served with petite sago pearls, and suited to contrast the mildly spicy curry and asam pedas.

Desserts were excellent overall, with the chocolate truffle standing out for its rich, dense chocolate intensity. The mango-lemon tart, also finished with gold flakes, was equally brilliant. I seriously could not put my spoon down.

Shangri-La’s F&B standards remain consistently high and offer excellent value for money. Tranquil and timelessly elegant, it’s a wonderful place to slow down and spend quality time with loved ones.
author: Honest Makan

restaurant_name: The Lobby Lounge at Shangri-La Singapore
review_text: Dropped by the restaurant for a quick lunch on a Saturday, and it provided a quiet oasis in the midst of a busy weekend.  Service was attentive without being intrusive, and the food was really good. I had the hainanese beef noodles and it was exquisite. The broth was flavourful, the beef tender, and the noodles were nice and springy. The beefballs were delicious too! It was a most delightful lunch.
author: Jk l

restaurant_name: The Lobby Lounge at Shangri-La Singapore
review_text: Had an amazing dinner at The Lounge! It is my second time here and still amazes me. The vibe is calming. Special thanks to Karen, Liz and Alyssa for the great service. Will definitely go back there again.
author: Nicholas Lim

restaurant_name: The Lobby Lounge at Shangri-La Singapore
review_text: A perfect spot for a relaxed yet professional business meeting. The lounge is spacious, elegant, and offers one of the most comfortable seating areas in the city. The kopi tarik is excellent — rich and authentic — and the calm atmosphere makes it easy to talk without noise or distraction. Service is attentive, and the overall setting strikes the right balance between casual and classy. Highly recommended for both meetings and leisurely catch-ups.
author: Faisal Abbas

restaurant_name: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips - Balmoral Plaza
review_text:
I came here looking for authentic English fish and chips, but it was a big disappointment.
The chips were some of the worst I’ve had in my life: soggy, undercooked, and with a very strange color. Absolutely no crispiness at all. What made it worse was that nothing was seasoned — not the chips, not the fish, not even the batter. Zero salt across the board.
The fish itself was decent quality and tasty, and the batter texture was okay, which is the only reason I’m giving this place three stars. But seasoning is basic, especially for a dish this simple.
Service-wise, we were seated at a table and left waiting, only to later realize we were supposed to order at the bar. No one bothered to explain this.
To top it off, there’s a sign explaining “what a great chip should be,” which honestly felt ironic given what was served (see attached photo).
I wouldn’t come back, and I’d strongly recommend avoiding this place if you’re craving proper fish and chips. It’s really not worth it.
author: Bobby Green

restaurant_name: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips - Balmoral Plaza
review_text:
This place absolutely nails the classic British Fish and Chips! The star of the show is the fish, encased in a nice batter that is perfectly crispy and light. More importantly, the fish itself tasted awesome—incredibly fresh with no hint of that "fishy" taste you sometimes get. It was a clean, pure flavour that was simply delightful.
​I also tried the fish cake, and it was equally impressive. It was a perfect size—not too small, not overwhelming—and had a clean, tasty flavour profile.
​Rounding out the meal were the potato fries. They clearly use real potatoes, cut and cooked to absolute perfection. They were just what you want in a chip.
​If you're looking for superb, high-quality Fish and Chips with fresh ingredients and perfect preparation, look no further!
Don't forget to complete the perfect meal with a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc! It offers great taste and a great price—the perfect way to upgrade your order! 😉😋
author: joanna chia

restaurant_name: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips - Balmoral Plaza
review_text: Dine here before but years back and came back today because they are the only place that have variety of fishes plus its fresh and really really good chips!! Staff is always nice and  friendly. Love the outdoor seating.  Definitely a place for authentic fish and chips.
author: Faezah Bujang

restaurant_name: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips - Balmoral Plaza
review_text: Very nice and fresh fish and chips! The fish really melts in the mouth. The chips are a bit thick too my liking but it's still very nice. But the onion rings are the best. Don't know how they do it. But I'm obsessed. One of the best I've had in Singapore.
author: Mariah Boon

restaurant_name: Smiths Authentic British Fish and Chips - Balmoral Plaza
review_text: A proper English chippie feel and service, fish and batter was crunchy but soft, only little less seasoning for my liking in the batter but still a very good fish, proper hand cut chips but we're not cooked well enough and still many hard potatoes, great size portion. Wanted Pickeles onion but was out of stock today, had beans and these were not Heinz but a reasonable alternative although cant ever beat Heinz Beanz, kid cooking fish was excellent in service gave me choice of fillets and took his time to do a good job nice one. Definitely worth a try when in Singapore
author: Javed Malik

review_text:
Lovely members exclusive pocket pouch with birdie, fries, grimace and burglar

The toys were so soft, will definitely hang on my bag! Super duper cute.

The burger is A VERY GOOD ONE!!! Will order the burger again.…
author: Cherrlyn Lim

review_text: Most delicious McDonald's ever had. The aromatic journey that begins with first crispiest bite to the spicy tinge at the very end of bite ,Ahh what a mouth watering treat it is. I tried their Double Mc Spicy burger together with their oh so crispy fries and caramel frappe. One who comes to singapore must try Mac Donald's which is located at the Orchard road at the heart of bustling city. Interestingly it's a 24-Hr service.
author: Sajjad Rasool

review_text: It is open 24 hours that’s good. There are no enough space to sit separately. Tables are so close each other.
author: Erdem

review_text: McDonald's (Forum The Shopping Mall) has one of the worst management with no sense of urgency from my point of view! Received an order to pick up from the restaurant by Deliveroo! By the time travel to the restaurant to pick up the order is already past 15 minutes and order has not even started preparing! Waited another 10 minutes, order still not ready for collection for just 1 set of breakfast meal! For goodness sake, can you imagine this is food delivery (FAST FOOD) and what the staff is doing the whole time for the past 25 minutes? Even walk in customers order is faster than food delivery! End up, refused to wait any longer and cancel the order.
author: ピカ ピカチュウ

review_text: i ordered take away a beef burger. gave me chicken instead, i only found out after i took a bite. ofcourse i wouldnt make a fuss as i already bite it. however, the service they give me was horrible. i understand that it was a busy day, they might have mistook my order for having here. but i showed them my receipt that i am taking away. and this one girl showed me irritated face. she shouted “eh give this one paper bag” and this one kind malay that was wearing a black shirt served me so nicely. the manager was there but didnt even acknowledge the situation. i came on sunday, 12 october, at roughly 1.20 plus
author: rihannaa

review_text: Tohoku sashimi was super fresh, and the Iberico pork collar with yuzu miso was lovely. The spicy salmon ikura mentai roll recommended by staff was okay, while the unagi avocado foie gras roll was better. The Hokkaido crab meat and mushroom donabe was alright, more suited for those who enjoy raw flavours and minimal seasoning. Overall, a solid spot for Japanese cuisine, though slightly on the pricier side, with some standout dishes.
author: Astralis

review_text: Our second time here. Good place to have premium value set meals at decent prices. Set meals  are only available during lunch time, and there’s a choice of either $30 or $48 lunch set. For an added appetizer, we ordered their foie gras roll, which is delicious.
author: S Law

review_text: Might honestly be the best Jap food in sg. There was not a single bad bite of food. Sounds strange, but we could taste the attention to detail in every single dish. Even the potato salad thing was fantastic. Highly recommend the dinner set and grilled chicken. Service was fantastic, ambience good, food unbeatable. 10/10 wld go again
author: Lai Zi Iun

review_text:
Had a great lunch at Ishinomaki Orchard Road. The food was excellent — we had the Iberico Pork Yuzu, Beef Shogayaki, and the Wateishoku set. Everything was well-prepared, flavorful, and nicely presented. Portions were generous, and the quality matched the price.

Special thanks to Kar Ming for his outstanding service. He was attentive, friendly, and very professional throughout our meal. His warm attitude made our dining experience even better.

Overall, delicious food + great service. Highly recommended and definitely worth returning!
author: Gary Hadi

review_text:
We had a dinner gathering here
The sashimi platter was pricey but really amazing, super fresh and tasted just like in Japan!
and matched perfectly with sake
We brought two bottles of sake, and the staff were friendly and helpful
I had a great time here!
author: moon Luan

review_text: I ordered the beef and mushroom  and was told I cannot add my choice of vegetables. Why is there a change now and it’s not written on the ordering board . It’s a waste of I don’t eat the vege they choose n throw .
author: JO Sze

review_text:
The staff at the Subway in Novena Square are really friendly and adapted to everyone’s unique requests. Even though many customers had last minute changes, they accommodated without any fuss. I especially liked the constant smile I got from this young server.

The staff is also constantly wiping down their station after making each order and I noticed they change their gloves after each order.

Everything is so fresh, they bake the bread and prepare the ingredients every morning.

I know Subway outlets is catered for Halal and Vegetarians.

Come and try their Rendang Prawn, Chicken or Beef.
author: Ricka Dagger

review_text:
Don't want to come anymore.
Really ridiculous.
I didn't eat anything.before take a pic
