review_text: Waitress recommended steamed fish head with fermented bean. Gave it a shot and wow it tasted so fresh! Sadly it is not available every time, so good to ask beforehand. Chicken rice (chicken and rice) are both good compared to other outlets
author: Indie Jun

review_text:
The moment you walk into this restaurant, you know that you are ensured of quality food. We ordered their famous Chicken Rice, Fried Tau Fu, Vegetable Soup and Dark Sauce Eggplant.
As expected, the chicken rice is the best turn up. The chicken is smooth and secullent and mostly deboned. The sauce is well balanced too. The rice is ok. One of the better Chicken Rice in Singapore. Public parking is  ample behind the restaurant. Can pay a visit.
author: Wong Timothy

review_text: I love how old school this restaurant is. The chicken was so tender, chicken rice fragrant and the stir fried zichar dishes spot on. Shoutout to the fried homemade beancurd too- crispy on the outside and so silky smooth on the inside. Coffee pork ribs were good too! Garlic kailan was alright
author: Bryan CY Chua

review_text:
An old school and famous steamed chicken rice outlet at Whampoa or rather at Boon Leng MRT vicinity.
Overall the food was good and service is normal. Downside is the dishes menu prices are relatively on the high side and been increasing over the years but the portions remains the same... :(((
author: Andrew Ho (何德财)

review_text: The steam chicken and fragrant rice is very good. Side dishes is not as good. Just go for the stream chicken and rice, surely satisfactory. Must add another bowl of rice.
author: Edward Koo

review_text:
The salt-baked chicken tasted slightly better than the version from the stall at Waterway Point. However, the experience was let down by the very poor attitude of both the cashier and kitchen staff, they stared aggressively without reason and even dropped the coins when handing over the change. On top of that, the chicken leg portion was really small and not worth the price.

The one star is solely for the cleaning uncle, who noticed I didn’t receive any soup with my $8.90 rice and kindly informed me that I could go and collect it. He was genuinely friendly and attentive, not just to me but to other customers as well.
author: S

review_text:
More than 30 years ago , use to be the top of BCM, even tai Wah not as famous as ah Lam when he is at lavender street.

When they move to race course road, still have standard, the shark fin soup and the BCM is one of the best especially the soup , very very tasty.

But today I go and try, it is worse and definitely not better than any hawker center BCM, now the soup is very dilute,
And the teowchew dumplings is missing, very disappointed and feel sad that the legendary is gone, accept it still call themselves Ah Lam😰
author: King

review_text: Ridiculously pricey. Taste mediocre. Noodle texture normal. Fish ball like any other frozen. The slithers of meat is like pathetic. Sauce is just loads of vinegar and chilli spicy  nothing else. Compared to when I last ate this 10 years ago…..won’t recommend unless you are really desperate like me today. But if you do wanna eat take the mini wok noodle more worthwhile than then mince pork version.
author: SooJin Wee

review_text:
Great options to go with the salted baked chicken.
Do try the otah carrot cake. probably the most flavourful carrot cake in town.
author: Stan Ley

review_text: Noodles are bouncy and goes well with the chilli / vinegar. Soup wasn’t so full flavour.
author: Sze Wee Tan

review_text:
Have eaten here twice, I think considering the price food is not worth it. Its just okayish. Staff are really just indifferent, not greetings or anything. I once asked one to parcel our food, he got a pack and asked me to put it myself with a straight face. Its as if they just want to be here for the money and that's all.

Have masala tea previously not that good. On other occasions, we had Bhelpuri, dahi valla etc, which were okayish but not worth the price.

[Update: Since the childish owner has responded to this review, first time we went there to only have snacks and the staff attitude were still the same. Basically not giving a shit. The second time, we were trying to find veg food closest to laxmi narayan Temple and this came up on google - its not some love affair for average overpriced food that we came back.]

PS: learn to accept constructive criticism, most people who go here are tourists and cant differentiate overpriced food. Stop acting childish. What a pity!
author: manas nag

review_text:
A great place for vegetarian Indian cuisine. The service is quick and atmosphere is very Indian. They have full variety of chaat if you are craving for Indian street chaat food. Tried their Pani puri and honestly it was ok, the water and very cold and sour, bud as it goes with Pani Puri, when you want it, you gotta have it.
They have huge menu from chaat, to Biryani to Paneer curry and naans.
They have variety of Indian sweets including Rajasthani sweets like Ghevar.
You can visit this place to satisfy the cravings for Indian food.
author: Shubham Gupta

review_text: Great food. Quick service. Atmosphere is OK but not an experience. Balaji Bhawan was my alternative restaurant after nobody feeling responsible to offer me a seat at Sara Anna Bhawan. So in the future Balaji gets my money spent
author: Khun U

review_text:
Stopped by this restaurant for a light meal last evening. This restaurant has a very pleasant vibe. It was well ventilated and the aircon was working, the attendants met and greeted me and were quite welcoming.
The buffet was available although I did not opt for it.

I had a dahi Puri and it was quite well prepared and yummy.

I think the hygiene standard requires some improvement since I was seated at a table and  noticed litter below the table. The manager happily had the table cleared and I continued to enjoy my meal.

Pricing was also quite nominal and affordable.

Overall I was satisfied and had a reasonably good experience.
author: Savio D'Souza

review_text:
Pure vegetarian restaurant located opposite mustafa centre. Ambience was family friendly, service was good and food tasted exactly like how we get in india. Mix veg sabzi was delicious and tandoori rotis came fresh hot and perfectly cooked.

They do have variety food options like Gujarati thali, Rajasthani Gatta curry, poori bhaji, north indian thali and dosa.
author: apeksha gupta

review_text:
Dec 2025:
Return visit and the food offerings did not disappoint.
Tried their BBQ pork, kimchi soup, GGJ pork and kimchi pancake this round and all were delicious!
New variety in the banchans too. Well filled and satisfied meal.

Oct 2025:
Very decent korean offerings here.
Tried their BBQ chicken and tofu soup, both were enjoyable.
Portion size and amount of ingredients are very reasonable at their price point too.
Worth a return to check out the rest of their menu.
author: Sharon

review_text:
Authentic delicious Korean food - really hidden gem at ct hub!

The chives pancake is crispy yet fluffy, bibimbap really mixes well n the pork is sooooo well marinaded.

Tofu soup is v nice! Must order.

Must eat!
author: Han Lee

review_text: Dined on a Sunday. Not too crowded. Food is ok. Also ordered Korean coffee but I don’t know what makes it korean. The korean pancake is better than the free side dish. So if you want a better pancake just order it. The rice on kimchi fried rice is soso.. the Bulgogi soup is sweet.
author: Jo G.

review_text: Three of us came here for lunch on 14 Dec (Sunday). The ginseng chicken is not bad but the kimchi pancake is a bit oily. They only provide 3 free side dishes here. Plus another 3 bowl of white rice, total cost is about S$39, which is quite reasonable
author: Jon Ng

review_text:
Good place to get your Korean fix. Hot and spicy and satisfying when hungry and craving for good Korean cuisine.

Nothing revolutionary, the drinks were served quickly and the food also came out right.
author: JR FF

review_text:
I recently visited A- One Restaurant and had such a wonderful experience! As a Chinese customer, I wasn’t sure what to expect at first, but everything truly exceeded my expectations. The service was absolutely five-star, the staff were warm, welcoming, and very attentive. They made me feel comfortable right away and patiently explained the different dishes on the menu.

I was honestly surprised by how delicious the Indian food was. There were so many varieties to choose from different curries, breads, rice dishes, and sides — it was hard to decide because everything sounded amazing. When the food arrived, it was rich in flavor, perfectly spiced, and cooked so well. Every dish was satisfying and authentic.

Overall, it was an excellent dining experience with outstanding service and incredible food. I’ll definitely be coming back again and highly recommend A-One Restaurant to anyone looking to try delicious Indian cuisine!
author: Ryan See

review_text: South Indian non vegetarian restaurant at Birch road. All non vegetarian curries and dishes like chicken, fish, prawn, mutton etc are tasty. Service is very good and rates are cheap compared to the quality of food in that area. Located near the Farrer metro station and Mustafa mall. Highly recommend for the Indian tourists to visit this restaurant for the quality non vegetarian food.
author: Gopi Nallaiyan

review_text: Simply the best! Tried chicken and mutton briyani. Well cooked and tasty! Try Masala chicken and curry mutton if opting normal rice. Less oily and yummy! Will go again once they reopen from reno in Feb.
author: Chandira Punchihewa

review_text: Very nice food. Friendly customer service by the uncle who serves food he will tell what items they have. Been coming here few times.
author: Sar R

review_text:
Excellent South Indian food served on banana leaf. The mutton curry is really good, so too the fish cutlets which are really a fish and potato pasty deep fried. The local flower crabs are excellent too but can be messy to eat.

The protocol is to order the mains which tend to be meat and seafood. Rice is served as a matter of course, also papadoms. The vegetables are part of the sides and don’t have to be separately ordered. Do ask for curry gravy which the waiter will slop on your rice. It’s part of the whole experience.

Careful, it’s right spicy. Not toned down for tourists, or indeed many a Singaporean.
author: Bryan Goh

review_text: huge portions!!! 2 people can share :> they use rose water for their biryani so it’s very different, not spicy at all but has a very clean and fragrant feeling, you will be able to eat a bit more.
author: The Eating Shrimp

review_text: Not full 5 stars for service and atmosphere as they do not charge 10% service charges. Road side restaurant not much atmosphere to talk about but there is a homely, warm feel to it. Food with family and friends-no need anything else. Or a quick filling and delicious meal on your own. No need much else.
author: Mark Ang

review_text: Absolutely Very delicious authentic Briyani that my Bangladeshi friend treated me too. According to them it’s authentic and this restaurant is well known in Bangladesh. It’s a no-frills air-conditioned restaurant that serves just a few dishes but they are all their specialty. I really enjoyed this unique version of Briyani which is different from the local Singaporean Indian or Malay kind. It’s not overwhelmed by spices and condiments yet so flavourful and aromatic with a Twist of lime and green chillies and potato. Reminds me of the similarities with Lebanese or Iranian kind that is aromatic and not spicy or drowned in curry. A nice change from the usual. Was advised to consume with the famous green coloured drink Bohrani which is made of fresh vegetables and herbs and a dash of green chilli so it has a slight punch but not too spicy. This drink apparently helps with digestion and prevents heartburn and indigestion. A perfect compliment to the main dish. I had the Mutton briyani , generous portion of meat, tender succulent and packed with flavour. And if you are lucky you also get the tulang (bone marrow) They do have fish and chicken options. I recommend to Singaporeans and tourists to try. Yes they do provide cutlery. It cost me around S$15 in total for a plate of mutton briyani and drink. I will definitely return for more when I crave this version of Briyani.
author: Steven Chee

review_text: This is a unique and different biryani that I had compared to I had experienced. It’s dry but rich in flavours, the marinated chunky lamb meat is cooked with the rice, but still remains moist and soft, strong lamb fragrance but in pleasant way. The rice was so flavourful, slight oily but acceptable.
author: Yong Siew Wong

review_text:
Aircon is surpringly strong and super comfortable. Clean and hygienic zero flies. Full house of regulars even at 3pm on Sunday.

Most friendly staff.

4/5 cuz for SGD13 I prefer a punchier briyani with more tender mutton like Nazeer at Mandai or Samy's at Dempsey. and also I still prefer basmati rice. But I appreciate the difference in style and at least this briyani isn't greasy at all.

Trivia ... Did you know Bangladesh was part of Pakistan before they seceded in 1971?
author: T Tan

review_text: I love this place! Reasonably priced buffet (hopefully they won’t raise prices).. and good service! Quality of food is so good, and I absolutely love their chai tea! ✨
author: lala

review_text: Awesome place with delicious 😋 🤤 and mouth watering food.
author: sumbul saleem

review_text: Best place , nice and hygienic, affordable buffet but few varieties
author: reddy revathi

review_text: Nice lunch buffet. Not so much diversity but good quality.
author: Sangmin Lee

review_text: Food good, price reasonable and good ambiance.
author: hurly wu

review_text: Staff were absolutely warm and welcoming. But food is becoming bad to worse. Its horrible to be paying $122 for 5 people with this kind of standard. Satay was literally fried cubes of dried chicken! Fried rice was just with peas and carrot. Carrot cake was tasteless and unappetizing! Nasi Ayam Penyet was with nasi lemak rice! Absolutely unacceptable! Will not be dining here anymore. Totally disappointing!
author: Faezah Bujang

review_text:
Just had our dinner here. We took HK Beef Noodle Gravy (👎🏼), Nasi Goreng with Chicken Satey (👍), Cheese Backed Rice with Sea Food (👍), Sichuan Dumplings and Fruit Tea Cooler(👍). However, they have a very good and large menu.

Staffs were very attentive. Order needs to be placed using QR. Food served on time.
author: Fazal Mahmud Roni

review_text: A decent place for a meal with not much crowd. I got the  Indo goreng with satay and I like the noodles as it’s not too oily yet flavourful. Satay wasn’t too bad but could be warmer. They do have some deals even during dinner time.
author: Kah Wang Tan

review_text: Decent quantity n price of weekdays lunch promotion. I like the kwayteow n seafood slightly lesser but fine. Tom Yum is not very spicy, decent spice level. Satay ok. Dessert is ok (but am a very low sweet tooth person).
author: Cindy Cin Chua

review_text: The bespectacled manager always remembers us and our boys, and always warmly welcomes us with a genuine smile. Our go-to location for our boys' favourite curry chicken. Probably not the cheapest food around but you get what you pay for.
author: Eric Lim

review_text: I seldom eat Indian food. Their food was quite flavourful so it is solid 3 stars. Their service slow, it took very long to serve the food and drinks for 7 people. I hope it is because they freshly make the naan so it takes time??
author: Li Yen -

review_text: 24 hours indian restuarant for prata, mee goreng etc. I am here for masala tea, which is quite ok but prices on higher side as compared to other places i went for masala tea
author: Backyard Xplorer

review_text:
Date of visit: Tue 18 June 2024
Time : 8.45 pm

Regular at this restaurant here.
Ordered fried bee hoon and 1 ginger tea.
Quality remains good. Bee hoon is spicy so you could ask for less spicy.
Priced at $5.20 and $1.70. GST is charged.

Date of visit: Thurs 21 Dec 2023
Time : 8.45 pm

Ordered the usual pratas and 1 mutton mee goreng.
The mee goreng is generous spicy and mutton is good.

Date of visit: Thurs 23 Nov 2023
Time : 8.45 pm

This time ordered a fried mutton bee hoon and masala thosai.
Portions are generous. Both pretty good.

Date of visit : Thurs 16 Nov 2023
Time : 8.50 pm

No queue. Came here again for our favorite pratas. Always freshly made. 👍👍

Many people ordered thosai. Will try that the next time.

Date of visit : Sat 14 Oct 2023
Time : 6 pm

Came here for loti prata. Nobody queuing for food.

Ordered 2 plates : 1 onion and 1 plain, 1 onion and 1 egg.
Ordered 1 tea Tarik and 1 ginger tea.
Priced at $11.25.

Prata is freshly made and good.
Ginger tea is still slightly sweet despite asking for less sugar.
author: Sunny M

review_text: Staff were friendly. Foods quite pricey but it is very tasty & spicy. 🤤
author: dewi abiha

review_text:
I visited Ariff's Restaurant around 8:50 PM for a takeaway order and was quite disappointed with my experience. I ordered 1 egg prata, 1 plain prata, 1 chicken biryani (specifically requesting the drum part of the chicken), and an ice Milo.

Despite the server nodding and acknowledging my request for the drum part of the chicken, I didn't receive the part I wanted, which was quite frustrating. Additionally, the ice Milo was far too sweet and thick, showing little to no effort in its preparation. To make matters worse, I was given a burnt papadom, which should not have been served.

Overall, it was a disappointing experience as I had expected better quality and attention to detail. I would recommend ordering at the hawker centre behind, which at least has quality food and drinks. I hope Ariff's Restaurant can improve their service and food quality to provide a better experience for their customers in the future.
author: halyssa fatiha

review_text:
So good ,its nice and quite restaurant with fresh bakery products too
We ordered two layer cake and it turned out so delicious ,according to theme,kids like the taste  its soft,moist and fresh....definitely reordering from them only ,also packaging was good and price reasonably.
author: Shruti Dubey

review_text: Very nice and quiet place on a Thursday afternoon. I enjoyed the thali, the masala tea and the quiet space. The thali portion is so huge that I had to take away. Love it here. And super affordable. What I love is there it’s all veggie. Lots of flavour
author: eesock

review_text: I am probably not an expert in Indian food, but I have been patronising this restaurant for the past 4 years. Recently they renovated and is brighter and cleaner!  Have not been posting previously. Love their samosas which I always ordered 10 to takeaway 😂.  Ordered my favourite Masala Dosa again. I love all the dips they served. A mix of flavours to my liking. Prices are really affordable for an air-con shophouse!  However was abit disappointed that we need to cancel our order for Gobi. Will be back again.  ❤️
author: A T

review_text: Food is very good, tasty and delicious. Service is good with nice cafe decor. Food price is affordable and they play nice tamil songs in the background. Definitely will be back again 😋👍
author: Morier Juliet

review_text:
Our first visit to this pure veg Indian restaurant, Sangeetha Bhavan, operating since 2002. Its long history is testament to its good food and popularity! Located at a different side from City Square mall, it is surprisingly near to Farrer Park MRT Station (NE8), at just 200m away.

We had the following dishes:
1. Mutton Kofta Briyani
2. Sze Chuan Noodles
3. Paneer Prata
4. Cashew Dosa
5. Tandoori Gobi
6. Hara Bhara Kebab
7. Dahi Puri
8. Desserts - Ras Malai, Gulab Jamun

Our favourite mains are the cashew dosa and briyani, and we love all their sides. Their cashew dosa is crispy and fragrant; tastes good with or without dips. Their briyani is nice, although I would prefer my briyani with lots of thick curry.

Next on the sides, the tandoori gobi is very well-grilled and flavourful. The dahi puri delivers a crispy exterior and an explosion of flavours in your mouth. The kebab is made from finely chopped fresh vegetables and spinach marinated with indian spices, dry fruits and cooked in a clay oven. All are enjoyable and essential to your gastronomic experience.

Lastly, their desserts, Ras Malai and Gulab Jamun, provided a sweet ending to our experience.
author: Kelvin Ngo

restaurant_name: Chung Ping Chicken Rice 众品鸡饭
review_text: Was curious at the long queue so gave it a try. Ordered half a chicken for 2 to share, rice was dry and no fragrance, while the chicken was the worst in a different way - I dint realise how you cut the chicken mattered until today, each piece was as large as a prime rib, eating it actually produced a weird overall texture that left us feeling disgusted somewhat.
author: Jin Chaw Yew

restaurant_name: Chung Ping Chicken Rice 众品鸡饭
review_text: Wandered into Bendemeer food centre hours past dinner time, with most stalls closed, and discovered a chicken rice stall with long queue. They were almost all sold out, and we ordered a half chicken (white) with some sides. The portion was really generous and price was very reasonable at around $12 for half chicken. The meat was tender wand skin was silky smooth, with a wholesome amount of sauce. Perhaps due to the last batch, we wished the chicken meat could have been more succulent with a springier texture. Else a simple fare with decent taste! :)
author: JK Ong

restaurant_name: Chung Ping Chicken Rice 众品鸡饭
review_text: Decent Chicken Rice but in a really affordable price range. It's only $4.90 for my plate of White Chicken+Roasted Pork+Braised Egg Rice, which comes with complimentary soup as well. Really worth it, and it open until late evening, which not much other chicken rice shop does that.
author: Jayon See

restaurant_name: Chung Ping Chicken Rice 众品鸡饭
review_text: Ordered 3 packet of Roasted Chicken Rice for takeaway. Price was decently cheap at $3.50 per packet. Service was very fast and friendly. You might notice the chicken meat is pretty nice but the rice is a tad bland. But it is the Chicken Rice stall with the longest queue in this Hawker Centre and lots of old folks patronise them. Reason is because it is more healthy due to less fat in the Chicken Rice. Will recommend this stall to people with dietary restrictions.
author: Ryan Tay

restaurant_name: Chung Ping Chicken Rice 众品鸡饭
review_text: I always give up trying because there’s always a long queue on weekdays lunch time! I was glad I managed to try this fragrant chicken rice. The firm flavorful rice   & lovely chicken texture. Valued for the generous servings. Will perserver on the Q to reach my turn next time. Highly recommend!
author: Another Big Bite

review_text:
I ordered the grilled chicken, fried fish, mushrooms & ham pizza... and we are all disappointed... very disappointed ☹️.

Firstly, the grilled chicken is nothing fantastic coming from a restaurant kitchen.
2ndly, the fried battered fish was double-fried, it was hard and dry...
3rdly, the pizza... the dough doesn't raised at all, esp around the edges, hence it was dry, hard and cold... not hot at all. I hv to cut the pizza into small pieces to chew...it is that tough..!
4thly, The pasta spaghetti that come with it is also cold and bland.... I suspect that it is cooked in batches and place aside waiting for orders, that's all. The portion is miserable.

Other westerns in food court or kopitiam serves better food than this. We used to order from Collin's kitchen from time to time in the past... but this is the last time. Take a look at the photos.

I actually want a refund.
author: MinfuWong

review_text:
Quality has dropped. To my surprise the fish and chip for lunch at 9.90 has shrunk, not just in size also in volume. Had it takeaway... Pls see pic. The fish sliced is around 0.3mm thick, it was chewy, dry and hard.
I understand that times are tough but I'm sure that by slicing the original fish piece into a half size will not gain you further customers. I'm so disappointed when I received my lunch, that I lost my sense of grammar.
author: IT

review_text: In a convenient Coffee shop, great option for western food especially for children. $10.90 for this margarita pizza. Even the  Kirby’s fan is so in love with it. Felt expensive in the beginning but think half size is around $5. Okay, that’s cheaper than some places for that portion.
author: Smelly Techou

review_text:
This is one of the stalls where the picture is actually smaller than the portion. Food was decently cooked!  Very amazed and impressed. The staff was extremely friendly and price was not too expensive! Definitely buying again.
Came back and the staff was still as friendly! For the price, the food is decent but not to die for!
author: Javier Tan

review_text: The food is fantastic! The price is worth as well for its huge portion. suggest everyone to come on weekday, as weekend is usually crowded and have to wait longer than usual. We waited for 15 mins for Our meals so I believe is still acceptable on a Friday night.
author: Michelle Lim

restaurant_name: Cheng Hoo Thian Teochew Restaurant OSL 清壺天潮州餐馆
review_text:
My go to place for good Teochew food.
In particular you must order the following- liver roll, oyster porridge, pork trotter, braised goose, oyster egg, orh nee.
I like the taste of these dishes, especially the Orh Nee whixh is done differently from others.
The only downside is the prices which is on the higher side. However you should still pay and eat at this Cheng Hoo Thian to experience good Teochew food.
author: Stam

restaurant_name: Cheng Hoo Thian Teochew Restaurant OSL 清壺天潮州餐馆
review_text:
If you grew up in a Teochew household in Singapore, the food here will be deeply nostalgic. The flavours are old school and comforting, reminiscent of childhood family dinners. I cannot put my finger on it but it is slightly different from Teochew food in other countries. Maybe it’s the accompanying sauces, the braising liquid or the seasoning. My husband pointed out that they use dried mushrooms in the steamed fish (no pictures, we started eating too quickly), which is different from Teochew steamed fish in Hong Kong where we lived for awhile. My favourite is the 三拼 platter where the ngoh hiong, hae zhor and pork trotter jelly (and their respective accompanying sauces) really brought back the memories. We also ordered the nai bai fried in garlic which was excellent.
We came to celebrate a birthday, but really, this should be a regular thing where we move forward as a society but do not forget where we started out.
author: LR Lim

restaurant_name: Cheng Hoo Thian Teochew Restaurant OSL 清壺天潮州餐馆
review_text:
09/September/2025
Had lunch here, was good! Friendly and warm service. Had the opportunity to try authentic Teochew cuisine. Besides the main dishes, don't forget to leave room for desserts.
author: T greensake

restaurant_name: Cheng Hoo Thian Teochew Restaurant OSL 清壺天潮州餐馆
review_text:
Authentic Teochew food.

All dishes we ate today is to the point !  I am impressed that each dish and item has its special sauce to go with and the waitress will introduce to you when they are delivered to the table.

Everything is freshly prepared and plated nicely. The service is top notch too.
author: Samuel C

restaurant_name: Cheng Hoo Thian Teochew Restaurant OSL 清壺天潮州餐馆
review_text: Old school Teochew restaurant. Why didn’t we discover this place earlier? Finally found our long lost favourite Teochew dish: Crayfish with onions and eggs! And their version was fantastic, the crayfish was cooked to perfection and they were meaty. The eggs and onions have wok hei and slightly spicy (with sambal chilli). That’s not all- we found goose here! Other famous Teochew restaurants in Singapore serve only duck because of the government ban (Avian flu) Only Hungarian geese are allowed (don’t ask me why) in Singapore. And so they served the goose here in 2 flavours. Being so used to the braised version, we were sceptical when they offered the deep fried version. CHT proved me wrong…this version was delicious. Tender and full of flavour, we were bowled over. Let me shorten this essay: all dishes were yummy. I particularly liked the oyster omelette. Glooey inside and crispy outside. Also the meat ball soup. Was it beef? The beef ball had the bite to it where you can’t find if it was factory made. QQ, surely you can bounce it off the floor. Chye por kway teow is a must in any Teochew dinner. Here, they made it clumpy until the texture was like carrot cake. I preferred the dish to taste like noodle but dining companions loved it a lot. Finally, I felt that the yam paste here was the best I’ve tasted in Singapore, ever. The yam was so fine and syrup was thick. Only complaint was that the pumpkin was too little. Lastly, there were 6 of us all adults. For each dish the portion was about just a bowl full. For example a piece of crayfish each. A small quarter of omelette each. So the smaller portion were complaints in other reviews. For me, it was alright. We get to taste more dishes…and we’ll definitely be back for the starters and desserts. Oh, service was great with the woman captain. She was friendly and patient to explain the dishes. And all the dishes were served fast despite the crowd.
author: HC L

review_text: We ordered the $15.80 set lunch, which consists of 4 choices of roast meats, either with rice or noodles, a drink and dessert. The star is of course the char siew, perfectly caramelised and not fatty but moist texture. Their roast pork ranks second with a thin crust and soft chewy layered meat. Can’t say the same for the roast duck, but still decent. Two side dishes we had were garlic crushed cucumber, not quite to our liking. That said, the mushrooms tofu was tasty. Overall a nice quick lunch, we’ll be back to try the other dishes.
author: S Law

review_text: Good Hong Kong–style Chinese food that’s worth every penny. The char siu pork is nicely caramelised, tender, and flavorful, while the roasted duck is juicy with crisp skin and rich taste. Portions are satisfying and the quality really shows. The shop is also very clean and bright, making it a comfortable place to enjoy a proper roast meat meal.
author: nina e

review_text:
Staff was friendly and extremely accommodating to us 4 - staying open on CNY Day 2 even though we came late. We were even fortunate enough to be given free charsiu to clear the remaining stock before they closed for the Lunar New Year.

Thank you to all the staff for taking great care of us despite given the opportunity to leave early to head home for celebrations. Greatly appreciate and wishing you a bountiful new year filled with happy customers and full bellies!!💰❤️
author: Kai Xiang Kuah

review_text:
Tried their promotion 4 items platter at $30. I find the charsiew a bit fatty, the roasted pork is ok. Chicken and duck is just average.

Went at 11:30am when they just open, and we waited for about 20 mins to get the platter served, kind of slow, consider they should have their items ready when is opened.

Staff is friendly, and helpful, and they do apologised for the slow serving.

The restaurant serves free ice water, which is good.
author: Chris

review_text:
My family went here for the first time last night and we're pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food.

The char siew were soft and delicious without being too oily. The beef were tender and delicious.
author: TH Too

review_text:
Good atmosphere and authentic Thai decor.
Ordered the Thai Claypot sharkfin soup which was a let down. Although served in a claypot, it was not hot, you don't even expect any bubbling popping when it was served to the table. The soup based was thin and mildly tasteful, can still get some sense of fishiness of the shark fins. Not woth money.
Contrary the fried kang kong was excellent and steamed Seabass was good. The bamboo clams were also fresh and crunchy .
author: WT Wong

review_text: Service is good. The basil pork rice I ate is tasty and flavorful, cooked to suit local taste buds, I think (as one who now spends half the time in Thailand. I am quite accustomed to eating truly local food). Nevertheless, my first impression of this place is good - the set lunch is worth coming back again.
author: GL

review_text:
Every dish we tried was thoroughly enjoyable — flavourful, well-prepared, and satisfying.

The service was excellent and attentive, adding to the pleasant dining experience. We also appreciated the clean and well-maintained toilets, stocked with proper soap, hand-drying napkins, and a large dustbin, showing attention to detail in both food and facilities. Overall, it was a great experience from start to finish.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text: Came during lunchtime so was not crowded. Food was great, drinks were not too sweet. Prawn vermicelli was on the peppery side, squid was cooked well, garlic pork was great, green curry spice was well infused! Thai style orh nee was great as well with a sugary take on it. Very reasonable prices as well! (maybe not the prawn haha)
author: J N

review_text: Came by for a celebratory meal as I saw that they sold a wide variety of seafood at an affordable price. They're having a promo for their crabs and we got 2 mud crabs for $48, and topped up $40 for the Tom Yum Mama pot. The pot was chock full of fresh prawns, squid, clams and noodles, though I thought the price was a lil bit steep. Crabs were great and decently sized for the price, and the tomyum soup was on the lighter side (though you can add chilli flakes for a spicier kick!). We also got the sambal kang kong ($12) which was delicious, and Iced Green Milk Tea ($3.50) to wash everything down - pleasantly surprised that the syrup is provided separately so you can dial the sweetness to your liking! Ended off with a Mango Glutinous Rice ($9) which was so good and the mangoes were so sweet, though I felt they could be more generous with the sticky rice. Overall, a great meal at great value, and at a convenient location too! Would definitely return!
author: Darren

review_text: The Home Bar and Kitchen offers a delightful fusion of Indonesian and local flavors that feels just like home. The food is incredibly delicious, making it a great spot for gatherings.
author: Irene Tin (TinTin)

review_text:
Very cozy decor and the atmosphere is a nice place to chillax. Good yummy food and the prices of drinks are reasonable.

Staffs are very attentive and displays a warmth friendly approach, especially Gary taking the lead (the cool boss)❤️

Will highly recommend anyone who wants an after work chillax time with friends, colleagues and even family.
author: Neil Nicholas

review_text:
Firstly, the ambience was great. You are able to speak to your friends without even shouting across tables. It was a cozy feeling and you will automatically make yourself at home.

Secondly, service was great. Gary approached my group in a friendly and welcoming manner, and it is not about 'get your order and done deal'. On the contrary, he ensured everything goes smoothly by checking in occassionally, and asks for tips to improve client servicing.

Third and lastly, the food tastes exceptionally delicious, and the portion is indeed WILD!

Thanks Gary and team.

Appreciate it!
author: Clarence Chua

review_text: We tried many dishes today and I would say most were disappointing, for me. The portions were rather small. The owners (a couple) run this all by themselves and they serve mostly regulars and I'm sure they have their fans.  There were only 3 tables occupied on a Friday night.
author: Kelly C

review_text: Nice ambience at this bar tucked in a small street. Although the location is not prominent there were crowds in the evening and it was almost full. The furniture were made of teak wood and you can see the owner made efforts in the design including the toilets. We only had drinks that night hence no comments on the food. Will be back again for food next time
author: Cecilia Xiao

review_text:
A lovely little stall at quite a hidden location. The staff owners are very friendly and the prices are truly affordable.

A surprising take on classic Chinese favourites as each item was fresh, rich and packed with flavour!

The green vege was crunchy, coated with a sauce that was light and tasted like something you would find in a fine-dining restaurant!

Wanton Noodles contained char siew, dumpling and was tossed in a delightful albeit spicy sauce ensuring each noodle was coated very well. This made for a very palatable dish. The dumpling was stuffed with mock meat and mushroom perhaps. This was not too heavy and made for a great addition to the dish overall. A crispy side item was also give which was alright.

These dishes stayed fresh for many hours which signifies the pride the couple has when it comes to their food.

*Do head down soon as she conveyed that she may close on 26/2/2025. What a delectable place to check out! With enough patrons, there’s hope that the stall will continue running*
author: Starlight Whispers

review_text:
Went on 21st Feb, uncle charged another additional $1 for each plate of wanton mee, claiming is CNY surcharge (but pls, it’s already 5th day of CNY).
The wanton mee are so-so.. (it could be due to uncle cooking instead of auntie). Nothing like the picture that others posted
Forgot to give me veggie until I asked .
I also ordered the blanched veggie, ah. Taste bitter instead of savory
So, should be the last trip for me.
author: Kath Chin

review_text: Warm and friendly elderly couple that prepare their food with passions. Very nice wanton mee, the noodle is so q n yummy.. Triangular tofu, polish goes so well with their special chilli sauce 😋 Fried rice and chicken rice smell so good too.. 👍
author: S L

review_text: Very unassuming looking place with very friendly owners and good food!Tried the wanton noodles - noodles were QQ (springy) and the dumplings were chunky and good! Uncle even gave me a sampling of his chicken rice chili which tasted special and unlike the usual chili. And he even gave me some sweet oranges as “dessert”. Certainly recommend this place!
author: Janice Peh

review_text: Have been wanting to check out this noodle stall after reading great reviews about it but it’s kinda out of the way for me. Was in the area so decided to check it out. We were not disappointed! The noodle was extremely well done! Perfectly cooked with the right bounce and texture. I like that the portion of vegetables is relatively generous. Definitely a must try if you like dry wonton noodle.
author: Rae L

review_text:
This mee siam is a no frills old school style that brought back a lot of childhood memories. The stall is run by an elderly couple. The bee hoon was pre-cooked, upon order, instead of just assembling everything and serving quickly, he chose to warm the rice noodles in the sauce several times before adding the topping. The final touch, a squeeze of lime was by his wife who controls the queue and takes orders. The scent of tau cheo or fermented soybean first hit my nose, the mee siam was sweet and savory with a little hint of spice. Tip- crush the egg yolk and mix it into the sauce for an added unami.

I went before the lunch time crowd and there was already a queue of 4-5 persons. The toppings included spring onions and one whole hard boiled egg cut into 2. For $3.50 (a price hard to find nowadays even at hawker centers), the portion is considered generous. They do not open daily so do check before going.
author: Jenn Wong

review_text:
Old school Mee Siam at Whampoa Food Center.

This stall draws a constant queue of several people waiting for their Mee Siam.

The noodles have been seasoned and tossed to a nice orange, but the boss will dunked each order into a boiling cauldron of tangy soup with half cut boiled egg to heat the noodles up and plate it up and adding the soup. This means the ‘seasoning’ for the noodles all end up in the soup pot!

The aunty will squeeze the calamansi lime into your mee Siam and add the chopped chives and belachan chili onto your plate. This saves customers the hassle of squeezing the lime and needing to clean up.

Taste-wise, I would rate it 3.5/5. Soup was tangy but mild tasting. Mix in the sambal chili for better taste.
author: Winston Ho

review_text:
Another one of those overrated stall. That is my own opinion of course.
I remembered there used to be a mee siam stall with the same name located in AMK estate. I am not sure if it’s the same.

Anyway, the old couple front this stall and it seems that they are popular with the residents there. The old gentleman is the one preparing. Inside the stall there is a weighing scale. And believe it, he will weight your bee hoon. If it’s over the scale, he will remove some. Maybe he just wants to be fair to every customer.

The gravy is a bit watery. It’s a little sweet but the calamansi balanced it well. I would say it’s not bad but it’s not great too. Depends on your taste. No queue so it’s ok. And if you want to ta bao back, you can choose to put in plastic bag or pay extra 20 cents for a plastic container. (Just use the plastic bag) or if you are a big eater, add another 50cents for more bee hoon.

This stall also have many off days so do check out their operational readiness before heading down.

Enjoy!
author: EatSleepChyll L

review_text: 3⭐️ (average dish) something new but not to my tastes. This mee siam is quite simple, with just soup, noodles, and a boiled egg. The soup is the only element with flavor—a sweet and sour profile. The noodles are pre-made, and the egg is hard-boiled. While it may appeal to some for its simplicity, it didn’t quite work for me.
author: Luke He

review_text: The mee siam gravy was flavourful and delicious, and the vermicelli waa very soft.  The chives were very nice.
author: Chin Zhi Hui

review_text: Childhood memories since eating their branch at Kovan Road 30 years ago. Their Chicken wings are my favourite simply because their turnover is so high. You literally eat the wings out from the oil the entire time I was there. Chilli sambal is just nice and the coconut rice is fragrant. The other sides are mixed in terms of taste.
author: jeremy cho

review_text: Yes, it’s more expensive than a hawker center, but the food is higher quality; the chicken is more succulent and the sides are better. Plus it’s air-conditioned, a big plus in Singapore. My go to place for nasi lemak.
author: Herc World

review_text:
Correct me if Iam wrong .
The chilli is different from the one in pungol .

The price here is more ext compare to other branches .

The serving is not that good maybe is old uncle doing .

Ask for additional chili willing to top up money but still did not give till I leave over lots of rice .

The chicken is over fried very crispy hard . The meat is also like over fried dry .

Overall I like is because of aircon and short queue . Other than that I think it’s not worth it .

Serving preparation look nice but for that amount for $8 2 wing and one egg and some ikan belis I still think is overrated
For $8 I think another small fish or fillet added will justify the price .
author: admen Lim

review_text:
Incredible to me. Been there years ago and led to visit this place again recently. It has only got worse.

Over the years I know of lots of people from all over the island who rave over this stall in a very old run down coffeeshop and I can never understand, given the elevated prices and the below par food portions and quality. It didn’t help too that the service by those old aunties behind the stall is consistently shabby.

Come on, there are far superior food options along with more comfortable setting than here - with the same prices you pay to this food operator.
author: Lynn Lee

review_text: At yesterday about 8:30PM, I was having my dinner here before work. Everything was OK until today morning when I felt the urge to vomit and had nausea when I was driving home, later on when I reached home, I had a severe diarrhoea which was consistent and I was in a lot of pain. Do note that I had not eaten anything else other than this nasi lemak.
author: yihao

restaurant_name: Fo You Yuan 佛有缘素食馆
review_text: Had an early CNY reunion dinner here. The Yu sheng is really tasty and flavourful, they didn't skimp on the ingredients. We loved their signature beehoon too. The best part was that the service was amazing! They were professional and detailed and responded promptly to each of our requests despite being very busy. Thumbs up to the staff! Thank you for the wonderful service and making us feel so welcomed. Would definitely visit again!
author: Kaya bun

restaurant_name: Fo You Yuan 佛有缘素食馆
review_text: Excellent quality vegetarian food. Great taste & fresh ingredients. Heard from boss that they’ll be closing down in June 2026 when the lease ends. So do hurry & try the food if you are looking for vegetarian food. Don’t miss them.
author: Karin Chan

restaurant_name: Fo You Yuan 佛有缘素食馆
review_text:
Highly recommend the food. Authentic and traditional.
Many good choices to choose from but my top 3 are the white beehoon with chilli, mock shark fin soup and mango roll.
author: Eugene Chua

restaurant_name: Fo You Yuan 佛有缘素食馆
review_text:
I recently had dinner at this restaurant with my family, and it completely exceeded my expectations! The food was not only delicious but also superb and amazing.

As a full-time vegetarian, I'm not a fan of mock meats, so I was thrilled to discover that this restaurant uses high-quality, healthy ingredients instead. Their dishes are unique, flavorful, and, best of all, they don’t have that MSG-heavy taste.

The presentation of the food was stunning—it felt like I was dining in a five-star hotel! LOL! The service was thoughtful too, and the owners were incredibly friendly and welcoming.

Overall, I would definitely organize another family dinner here, despite the tricky parking and challenging traffic. Highly recommended!
author: Ada

restaurant_name: Fo You Yuan 佛有缘素食馆
review_text: Nice food & good atmosphere. Good for vegetarian family for gathering.
author: Mavis Quek

review_text: True Ipoh food nestled in the heart of whampoa next to st Michael’s interchange ! Must try the curry pork rice for a true authentic taste of Malaysian cuisine!
author: Dr Samuel Lee

review_text: This is one zi char store worthy of promoting. The wok hei is good. Food is cook very fast yet the taste is not compromise. A very good portion is given too. I have tried many dishes, and most bring me enough joy to be back again and again whenever I need some zo char for a meal.
author: HP Tan

review_text: Fish head curry and stir fried chicken were nice. The Pork rib was way too tough. Generally above average standard. Keep it up, guys.
author: Isaac

review_text:
This was a surprise for me today as I was looking for something to eat late afternoon.
It looked good and tasted good. At $4.50 a plate laden with wok hei rice noodles and ingredients aplenty, this was heaven sent. I normally like hor fun like this with sliced red chilli. The taste is well paired.
Got to try the others next time when I go to that outlet again.
Maybe a steamed fish and stir fried dishes next?!
The price is right for me.
author: Gabby Fantasy

review_text: I got to know of Golden Sands after seeing @immichellechong share her meal on Instagram. Found out that they were near me and I love tze char so I thought, why not give it a try and support our local businesses during this time. (They deliver islandwide, but I prefer nearby places 😊) I was not disappointed, prices are reasonable and food was tasty with generous portions. Service was very pleasant as well - both the person who took my order on Instagram and the delivery personnel. I was thinking of paying in cash and checked if they accepted it - they prefer PayNow, but they were willing to accommodate just for me. I did PayNow eventually as I didn't want to trouble them and it wasn't a hassle to me actually. My grandma really liked the fish head set we ordered (pictured) and she got me to order the same set to my other relatives as well, so I just ordered again from them. ❤
author: Kimli

review_text: at about 1900 on 18/12/2025. one of your staff, an elderly lady. was incredibly rude, there was no one behind me and when i paid. she said “faster take and go”. i’m sorry? what’s the rush? i just did my payment. a fellow customer infront of me wanted to pay via qr code but was forced into paying with his card. completely uncalled for, i’m not from around here and i’m residing in the north region. i love old chang kee but this has never happened to me before. everyone at other outlets was so friendly, warm and kind. this particular staff, my goodness. hope you guys will take action.

review_text: The side dishes, peanuts, salted vege are small in portion and pricey at $6. And it's not that it's yummy. The pork rib soup is just ok, smells quite funky when piping hot. When it cools down a bit it's ok, but still not the kind where I would ask to top up more soup
author: Taste & See

review_text: The service was excellent, and the soup base was just right—not too peppery or overly seasoned, which could make you thirsty. Nevertheless, I will still return!

author: Jes Jassi

review_text:
One of the best bak kut teh experiences I’ve had in Singapore. The soup is rich, peppery, and full of flavor — absolutely comforting and satisfying.

I highly recommend their Sliced Lean Meat Bak Kut Teh — the meat is tender and perfectly cooked, pairing beautifully with the aromatic broth.

Service is impressively fast and efficient, even during busy hours. The staff are friendly and make sure you get your food piping hot in no time.

If you’re looking for a hearty, authentic bak kut teh with great service, Legendary Bak Kut Teh at Rangoon Road is definitely worth a visit!
author: Justin Ngui

review_text:
I was looking for a place to have bak kut teh nearby and found Legendary Bak Kut Teh. It’s a mid sized restaurant with a decent amount of seating. The space is clean and tidy and the staff were polite and welcoming. I was shown to my seat and one thing I appreciated was that they soaked the utensils in hot water before use, a nice touch to ensure cleanliness.

We ordered the sliced lean meat bak kut teh ($8.50), pork rib bak kut teh ($9), salted vegetables ($6), you tiao ($2.50), barley drink ($2.80) and a soft drink ($2.50). The meats were absolutely tender, unlike some other places where they can be tough. The soup wasn’t overly peppery but had a really nice, balanced flavour. The salted vegetables were well-prepared, not overly salty and tasted fresh with no odd aftertaste. The you tiao was served hot, not oily at all and goes perfectly with the soup. Best of all, the soup was refillable. The barley drink also was not too sweet, just nice to my liking.

It was a very satisfying meal with good quality food, friendly service and a clean environment. Definitely worth a visit if you’re craving bak kut teh in the area.
author: June Ang

review_text:
Was hungry for lunch and passed by this restaurant and happened to see their set lunch promo for $9.90. Decided to take settle lunch at this restaurant. Count my blessings, for $12.90, I ordered Fish and Chips and the Chicken Chop set meal which offers salad free-flow and mushroom soup free-flow.

The mushroom soup was delicious, better than some restaurants out there.

Chicken chop was fragrant and flavourful, really delicious. Fish and chips, the fish was soft, batter was not too thick and was easy on the palate.

On top of both salad and mushroom soup, there was ice cream free flow.

Really worth coming here when you're nearby and looking for something value for money.
author: Kai Ang

review_text:
This cafe is located on the ground floor of the Aqueen Hotel along Lavender Street.

This cafe serves very good tasting and large serving of westren food come with soup of the day, dessert and tea/coffee/soft drink at only SGD9.90 per person.

If you come in a group of 4, the 4th person is basically free!

Picture left to right Mushroom Soup, Grilled Chicken Chop in Black Pepper Sauce with Salad and Fries, Lamb Chop with Onion Sauce with blanched Cauliflower & Broccoli and Mashed Potato, Pan Fried Salmon with Salad and Mashed Potato.

These are the few dishes from their menu.
author: SKEC SKEC

review_text: Located next to hotel Aqueen Lavender. Went here on sunday noon. Tried set lunch for $9.9++. Choose main dish from few options, comes with soup of the day, and free flow ice cream. Professional service and friendly staff. Highly recommended!
author: Hartono Harjono

review_text:
I found this unique piece of amazing and good food in the middle lavender. Located next to the Aqueen Hotel.

I had the set chicken shop 9++ buffet salat bar plus drink of your choice and ice cream bar all options refill just no the main dish.
Worth the price and food was good and good amount. Totally recommend this place
author: Norman Barrantes

review_text:
Went for weekday lunch set at 9.99

Small sitting area but comfortable, total seating space should be about 40pax

For set lunch of 9.99, you get a main course to choose from 5-6 choices (range from chicken chop, lamb, steak, salmon, and 1 more), a soup, and ice cream.

Add 3.99 will give access to salad bar and a drink (coffee n tea need to add a dollar)

Overall food quality is not bad, spread of salad bar is good. Considering all are refillable except for main dish, it is worth the price tag. Portion is good also.

Recommend to try out for a lunch if one is working near by.
author: Stephen Chan

review_text:
A very retro vibe, casual and homely restaurant. Love their retro decorations in the restaurant. They have quite an extensive food menu of western food and staffs are friendly and helpful. We tried their course meal that came with a sample size soup, regular main course, drink and a small dessert at $39.90. A pretty good deal and a good meal. My hubby topped up $10 for Wagyu steak, $5 for Red wine, whereas I topped $2 for lobster bisque soup. We paid less than $100 for 2 sets meal and 2 glasses of wine. The second glass is priced at $11.50 ( regular price). I love black pepper sauce that came with the pork chop and mashed potatoes were soft and tasty. Pork chop was nicely grilled but some part were difficult to cut due to the tendons, will be good if can choose meat with less tendons. Wagyu beef was decent and nice.

Overall, food were decent and delicious. We were there on a Friday night, so get to listen to enjoy live music and songs sang by Gilbert.   Live music is only available on Friday and Saturday dinners. Seats are very limited, do reserved your seats if you have a bigger group of 4-6. Have a great night and will definitely come back again.
author: May Soon

review_text: This was my first visit, and I was impressed by the warm hospitality from both the owner and the staff. The place has a unique setup, filled with nostalgic items that give it a special charm. Live performances add to the overall atmosphere, making the experience even more enjoyable. The food is tasty and the prices are very reasonable. We were even given a pair of small horse plush toys. Highly recommended.
author: Yuan Sharon

review_text:
My family and I had a wonderful time at Brunches Café!

Every dish we ordered was absolutely delicious and cooked to perfection. From the Pan-Fried Seabass and BBQ Chicken Quesadilla, to the Truffle Fries, Portobello Mushroom Fritters, and the beautifully done Christmas Set with Wagyu Beef Steak.

We also loved the Honey Orange Yuzu Soda and ended our meal on a sweet note with the Molten Lava Cake and a single scoop of Chocolate Mint Ice Cream.

The service was exceptional. It was warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly. The owner is incredibly friendly and hospitable!!

The café itself has such a cosy, homely vibe, filled with charming vintage furniture, and an impressive collection of antiques that give the place so much character.

The highlight of the day was getting to dine at the Mini Cooper–converted dining table. It was such a unique and memorable experience!

We thoroughly enjoyed our time here and will definitely be back again in a heartbeat!
author: Jason

review_text: Christmas decor with special Christmas menu. Given the “car seat”1st visit to this place and find it a pleasant experience. Food wise my daughter’s choice was nicer(risotto with beef stew). I find the seafood risotto abit too salty for me. Soup and drink were good!
author: May Long

review_text: Blast from the past with great hospitality and passion for both their food and service. Yet, definitely with modern vibes in terms of atmosphere and food tastes. Yums...and as usual, when it comes to a restaurant where I totally enjoy the food,  there are no food pics as they make it to my stomach faster than the snaps! author: Sarah Lim

review_text: Buffet food is okay for one time try. Not bad. Costs 20$ per person walking dinner. Veg options available. No starter though
author: Prateek Pandey

review_text:
Our Dinner experience at Spice Grill Restaurant was the worst in entire Singapore trip.

When we reached the restaurant we were greeted saying that we’re sorry but we only have vegetarian food today and being vegetarian we got excited with we’ll have more options for us compared to situation when you have both veg and non-veg food. So we said yes, we’re fine with it.

The staff said wait for few minutes while they still setup for food. After 5 mins this whole big group came in 2 coaches and it became overcrowded in just 2 mins from entirely empty room. And also the crowd was literally behaving in such a way that you wanna leave the restaurant immediately.

Ignoring that, we thought at-least the food would be better but not a single item was tasty. Each and every item was such you’d feel you wanna stay hungry but not eat there. Paneer subji was sour, naan was not well cooked, masala chaas was very sour, not a single item was such where you feel satisfied.

I’d highly recommend to skip the dinner here and instead go to Riverwalk Tandoor for dinner as it was our best Indian food experience in Singapore in restaurant.
author: Yash Zalawadia

review_text:
A Flavorful Journey at Spice Grill
Spice Grill in Singapore is a culinary gem that has captured my taste buds and left me craving more. From the moment I stepped inside, I was greeted with a warm and inviting atmosphere that perfectly complemented the delicious aromas wafting from the kitchen.
The menu is a delightful exploration of authentic Indian cuisine, offering a wide range of dishes to suit every palate. I opted for the butter chicken and naan, and I was not disappointed. The butter chicken was rich, creamy, and bursting with flavor, while the naan was soft, fluffy, and perfectly cooked. The combination was simply divine.
The service was impeccable. The staff were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu, making my dining experience even more enjoyable. The ambiance was also perfect, with soft lighting and soothing music creating a relaxed and enjoyable atmosphere.
If you're looking for a truly authentic Indian dining experience in Singapore, I highly recommend Spice Grill. It's a must-visit for any food lover!

review_text:
Had an absolutely wonderful dining experience! The food was fresh, flavorful, and beautifully presented. Every dish we tried was cooked to perfection, and the portion sizes were just right. The service team was warm, attentive, and made us feel very welcome without being intrusive.

The ambience is elegant yet cozy, making it a great spot for both casual meals and special occasions. What stood out most was the attention to detail – from the plating to the quick service and even the small gestures of hospitality.

Highly recommend this place if you’re in Singapore and looking for a restaurant that combines excellent food, great service, and a lovely atmosphere. Definitely looking forward to coming back!
author: Wilson Dsouza

review_text:
Went there yesterday (Sunday) for a late Lunch at around 2pm. Samantha, who was serving us was not only friendly & helpful, but also very perceptive of us as the customers. Like when she brought a dish & was quick to ask if we needed small sharing plates. She was the extra "oomph" that gave the extra touch of good customer service! 👍

We had ordered the following food:

1) Chilli Crabmeat Linguine
- A unique fusion of Italian pasta with a local delicacy flavor, which was delicious but can be a little too spicy for some folks.

2) Almond Butter on Toast
- Got this because I've not heard of Almond Butter & wanted to try. Liked it that it was flavor-rich without being too sweet.

3) Enchanted Scrambled Egg Burger
& Lychee Soda
- This was quite a big proportioned dish with a delicious chicken & sumptuous scrambled egg. The French fries were also flavorful too.

4) Açai Bowl
- My first time trying fruity delight of blueberries, strawberries & açai. We also liked it especially when the chia & sunflower seeds were "crunched" together in our mouths.

5) Waffle with Gelato
(Rocky Road, Golden Pistachio, Belgian Dark Chocolate)
- Loved it that the waffle was crispy & complemented well with the 3 large scoops of gelato

6) Latte
- Simple yet done & delivered nicely.
author: franz1c

review_text:
Went planning to have standard breakfast platter. But turns out they don't have it on their menu any longer.
Infact the place is quite small and the menu is quite limited compared to the older menu you see on Google reviews.
Music was all recent familiar pop music at the right volume.. ( many places mess those up, either the choice of songs or the volume)

Initially disappointed at lack of obvious choices, decided to be a little experimental. Ordered their Crabmeat linguine, and Damn it was good. I don't normally like red sauce pasta but the egg and Crabmeat made sure the red sauce doesn't stand out as much.
My wife ordered veg linguine which had Mushroom and broccoli. And sweet potato fries.
Oh and also an Ezekiel bread toast for the pasta.
While portion size looked small it was quite filling.

And we finished with a Sundae with Pistachio asked hazelnut ice cream. Because it was almost lunch time and why not. Pistachio icecream was top notch. Surprised it was this good, I didn't expect this especially considering this wasn't a speciality ice cream place.
Finally the hot Crem brulee intrigued me so I had to try that. It was interesting, but too sweet.

Overall worth a visit..

author: Amirah Arnuar

review_text:
Fayidha Restaurant, open 24 hours, is a hidden gem for those seeking a late-night bite or an early morning feast. The cozy atmosphere welcomes diners at any hour, making it a popular spot for locals and travelers alike. One of the standout dishes at Fayidha is their roti prata, which strikes a perfect balance between crispy and flaky. It’s served with a side of rich curry that complements the flavors beautifully.

The tosai is another highlight, with its thin, crispy texture and delightful taste. It’s evident that the chefs take pride in their preparation, as each serving is fresh and flavorful. While the drinks menu is not extensive, the beverages offered are refreshing and pair well with the meals. Whether you opt for a classic teh tarik or a simple iced tea, they provide a satisfying accompaniment to the dishes.

Though the food is good, it’s the round-the-clock availability that truly sets Fayidha apart. Whether you’re craving a midnight snack or a hearty breakfast, this restaurant has you covered. Overall, Fayidha Restaurant is a reliable choice for those looking for comforting Malaysian cuisine at any time of day!
author: Mackaz Sajiaos Tan
