author: Raveen Shahdadpuri

restaurant_name: Druggists | Craft Beer Taproom Restaurant Singapore
review_text:
Druggists | A hidden gem in Singapore

Located at 119 Tyrwhitt Road, this place offers a unique and delightful experience for craft beer enthusiasts and food lovers alike.
One of the standout features of Druggists is their impressive selection of craft beers on tap. With 23 rotating craft beers, there's always something new and exciting to try. From the flavourful Jaipur IPA to the indulgent Naughty & Nice Stout, the variety is remarkable. The beertenders are knowledgeable and friendly, always ready to recommend a beer that suits your preferences.
The setting of Druggists is equally appealing. The bar is housed in a building that was once the headquarters of the Singapore Druggists Association, giving it a unique historical charm. The atmosphere is casual and welcoming, making it a great spot to hang out with friends. Whether you prefer indoor seating, alfresco dining, or lounging, Druggists has got you covered. The staff are friendly and efficient, adding to the overall enjoyable experience.
In addition to their fantastic beer selection, Druggists also offers a range of bar bites, casual food, natural wines, cocktails, and handcrafted sodas. It's a place where you can relax and enjoy good food and drinks in a laid-back setting.
Overall, Druggists is a must-visit spot in Singapore for anyone looking to enjoy a great selection of craft beers in a unique and charming setting.
author: Nikhil Pendse

review_text:
Overall, this is a quality spot that truly elevates the freshness of its seafood.

There were two stellar standouts:
The Seabass: Don't let the unassuming looks of it fool you. It was extremely tender and flavorful, with that delightful fattiness you typically only get from cod. It was executed to perfection, with crisp skin, easily the best seabass we’ve ever had (had to ask them for the secret formula). It came with pickled starfruit, which was a first for us. It oddly tasted a bit like plum, while we couldn't quite decide if we liked it, it was definitely an interesting flavor profile.

The Panna Cotta: I loved the tea base here, a very unique take on the dessert. Everything complemented each other well, don’t break the meringues if you aren't a fan of heavy sweetness. The other components hold their own perfectly.

The Miss:
The fried calamari fell short, especially given the high expectations for a seafood centric restaurant + being pricey. It felt like an amateur mistake, the squid was perhaps too moist, causing the batter to crumble off rather than stay crisp. The presentation was also subpar. That said, the sauce was fire!
author: Xanxus Reef

review_text: This is another interesting fusion seafood joint. If you’re a seafood lover then you need to step in. All the items are really fresh. The shell fish, squid, prawns. Didn’t get a chance to try out any fish items, maybe on the next visit. Loved the way the seafood was done. Curry mussels, Assam sambal clams, grilled prawns with salted kombu. Grilled squid with spiced cumin potato. The flavours were bursting and complimented each other. The place deserves its rating it seems. Matter of time this gets on some gourmet list I’m sure. Worth a try. Small seating area but they do have tables at the back for parties of 6. Enjoy.
author: david chong

review_text:
I recently dined at Scaled @ Hamilton, and it was an exceptional experience from start to finish! The highlight of the meal was undoubtedly the seafood, which was incredibly fresh and flavorful.

The *Soupy Sambal Lala* was a standout dish—rich and aromatic with just the right amount of spice. Paired with the garlic bread, it was a heavenly combination perfect for sopping up the delightful broth.

Additionally, the **roasted prawns** were perfectly cooked, showcasing the natural sweetness of the seafood, while the **prawn aglio olio** was a savory delight, featuring the perfect balance of garlic and olive oil.

The ambiance was charming, and the service was attentive without being intrusive. I highly recommend Scaled @ Hamilton to any seafood lover looking for top-notch flavors and freshness. Can't wait to return!
author: Zackery Goh

review_text:
Wonderful experience! We particularly enjoyed the Seabass Puttanesca - the fish was super fresh, perfectly cooked, and the pasta was a nicely seasoned staple to complete the dish.

Got the curry mussels on everyone else’s Google recommendations. While the mussels were very fresh, we couldn’t get much of the mussels’ taste as the curry was pretty strong. Also felt like the sour dough from the Seabass pate dish was a better match to dip the curry sauce as opposed to the slightly sweet mantous.

Seabass pate and the fried squid were pretty good, but we felt could do with a bit more seasoning.

Service was prompt and helpful with recommendations.
author: Ellise Lim

review_text:
Celebrated Mama’s 74th birthday here. The space felt romantic (read: dim lighting), modern, and minimally styled. Since it leans Western fusion — more Western-forward — each dish came with a thoughtful explanation of how best to enjoy it.

Most, if not all, of the seafood is locally farmed, which is quite a feat for a small country like ours. And they were delicious. We had plenty of prawns (as you can probably tell from the photos) — plump and juicy. I’d love to try more of their fish next time, and probably go lighter on the starters since they were quite carb-heavy.

Also thought it was funny when my mum commented on how young one of the female staff looked and wondered aloud if she was even old enough to serve us. Classic mum moment.
author: yingers11

review_text: Started with Mushroom soup. Dense with flavour. Crab cake was surprising good. Meat tear off the lamb shank. Finished off with a warm pizza. Highly recommend. Would come back again.
author: Dennis Ang

review_text: Escape Restaurant serves a nice mix of local, Western and Chinese dishes, with elevated touches like Singaporean Chili Crab Mac and Cheese and Satay Chicken Brioche Roll. The desserts are creative and tasty too. The setting is relaxed and not too noisy, though seating took a few minutes as no one was at the reception initially. A pleasant spot for comfort food with a gourmet twist, and worth visiting when there’s a deal.
author: Yordan

review_text:
I would like to commend the two wonderful servers (Hardeep and the lady server) at Escape Restaurant for their outstanding service during our recent visit. Their attentiveness, professionalism, and warm smiles truly elevated the dining experience. From the moment we were seated, they made us feel welcomed and well taken care of, ensuring every detail was thoughtfully attended to, from refilling water promptly to checking in on our meals at just the right moments.

The food was equally impressive, the Angus burger with truffle fries was juicy and flavorful, the lamb shank was tender and rich, and the miso salmon was beautifully cooked with just the right balance of flavor. Every dish was a delight, and it was clear the service team took pride in presenting the best of what the restaurant had to offer.

Kudos to the team at Escape Restaurant, especially the two servers who went above and beyond. Thank you for making my wife's birthday enjoyable one!
author: Kim Wui Chee

review_text:
The restaurant is a tad small, it's on same level as the gym & pool. Simple deco. It wasn't crowded...

The bread was nicely warm (fluffy inside) and served with individual butter & vinegar serving to each pax.

The food quality is quite excellent... Miso salmon was nicely done and served with a delicious salad! The tandoori chicken was marinated with fine indian spices and was aromatic. It goes well with the naan and side dips. The prawn paste chicken burger was quite an innovation of blending a local flavor into a fusion dish. The taste was just nice!

We didn't have stomach space for dessert. Will come back again and try!
author: Cool Dragon

review_text: Highly recommended to come to this restaurant ! Cosy ambience and good food. Excellent service standards and very pro-active. Hardeep and Janice has made my day exceptional as I am here to celebrate my birthday. Food-wise was good as well, especially the lamb shank. It was very tender, off the bone and well flavoured !
author: Hugo Ho

restaurant_name: PastaMania - Italian Casual Dining @ City Square Mall
review_text:
Tried the festive menu at PastaMania and here’s my take:

Truffle Porcini Smoked Duck Pasta– Creamy porcini sauce with shimeiji mushrooms and cherry tomatoes. The truffle adds a nice aroma and the smoked duck goes well with the dish.

Pistachio Honey Baked Chicken Ham Aglio – A mix of nutty, savoury flavours with roasted nuts and honey-baked ham. Something a little different from the usual aglio style.

Peppermint Pomegranate Tamarind Fizz– Refreshing and festive, with a blend of sweet, tangy and minty notes.

For dessert, I tried both the Coffee-misu and Wildberries Panna Cotta. The panna cotta stood out for me—light, creamy and nicely balanced with the berry tang.

Overall, a nice festive meal with a good variety of flavours.
author: Edwina Pariwono

restaurant_name: PastaMania - Italian Casual Dining @ City Square Mall
review_text:
The vibe is casual and unpretentious, making it perfect for a quick lunch or a relaxed dinner after shopping. It’s a great value-for-money, hits the spot for comfort food every time.

Their menu is quite diverse— the current Gong Xi Raya festive set is a interesting taste to try from the usual, which comes with colorful "福 [full] of pasta" red packets.
author: The Genesis Family

restaurant_name: PastaMania - Italian Casual Dining @ City Square Mall
review_text:
Food was pretty good.
My kids were happy and we had a great meal.
All were nicely done and pretty reasonable prices.

Will be back to eat it again.
author: Ars 3276

restaurant_name: PastaMania - Italian Casual Dining @ City Square Mall
review_text:
We recently brought our K1 children for a pizza-making field trip with Rina from Doughworkz, and it was such a wonderful experience!

Rina was incredibly patient, warm, and engaging with our young learners. She gave clear, age-appropriate instructions and ensured that every child felt confident and involved throughout the session. The pace was just right for preschoolers, and she managed the group very well.

Our children were so excited to spread the sauce, add their toppings, and see their pizzas come to life. Beyond the fun, it was also a meaningful hands-on learning experience that supported their independence, fine motor skills, and confidence.

Thank you, Rina, for making it such a memorable and enriching session for our K1 class. We highly recommend Doughworkz for preschool field trips!
author: Shulaiha Sapani

restaurant_name: PastaMania - Italian Casual Dining @ City Square Mall
review_text:
My kid enjoyed the whole process of pizza-making. Simple and clear instructions for 3 years old children to follow. Host Alya is awesome and her hospitality shines through.

Worthy workshop for parents and children.

#DOUGHWORKZ
author: Fairuzana Anna

review_text: I had a meal at Saizeriya recently. The main dishes were okay — decent flavor and portion for the price. However, the tiramisu was quite disappointing. It tasted frozen and lacked the soft, creamy texture you’d expect from a proper tiramisu. Overall, a good place for a quick, affordable meal, but I wouldn’t recommend the dessert.
author: Tina Love Painting

review_text:
Noisy place when crowded and quite family friendly seeing babies and kids so kudos to this.

Food quality match the price point, you pay what you get and they don’t use fresh ingredients.

It is a cozy hangouts that is budget friendly, it’s quite similar to hawker prices.

For $3 you get freeflow soda drinks for that is best good deal if you want sugar rush.
author: Danny Tan

review_text: Located at B2 of Farrer Park MRT, Saizeriya is a convenient spot for affordable and tasty Western-Italian food. The BBQ pork rib and steak are nicely done — tender, flavorful, and great value for the price. Service is quick and the place is clean, making it a good choice for a simple, satisfying meal with family or friends.
author: viet linh

review_text:
Went during dinner peak; was crowded but managed to get seats. After placing our order, we enjoyed our drink bars.... Food came in rapid order, mussels were delicious! Butter corn serving was generous and buttery...we added a dash of cheese on it. The seafood marinara was good with generous seafood! There were lots of kids and students running around, dashing between drink bar and their seats.

Service by crew were struggling to cope, hope management either increase some help as they looked overwhelmed.
author: Cool Dragon

review_text: Been here countless times for at least once a week. Fuss free, quick service, nothing much  to complain. One little suggestion if I can, please wipe the table with a clean cloth. Although the food is delicious for the price we pay, but the chairs and especially the tables are mostly greasy from the previous diner. I think that will be a better experience for many people. Though they may get too overwhelmed with the few staffs that they have, I think diners will be more than happy to wait few minutes longer for a cleaner, grease-free table and chair. Budget Italian food makes kids and everyone happy.
author: yilih chia

review_text:
First time tried Din Tai Fung. Really not disappointed. We tried the Xiaolong Bao, Wantons in spicy sauce as well a noodle dish (cannot recall the name). Everything was DELICIOUS.

It takes some time for the dishes to be served as they are made to order I believe. The portions are enough for one person and if you are sharing, might have to order more dishes.

The service was impeccable and the atmosphere was nice. Not at all crowded.
author: Acetyl CoA

review_text: The kitchen took 30 mins for my pork fried rice to be served. We had finished all my other dishes before the fried rice finally came. I noticed that the other tables were being served before mine. The servers were too busy clearing tables and under-staffed to notice us. Poor service. Will not visit again.
author: Han Meng See

review_text:
Staff was not attentive, guess not enough of manpower. The price was above average but better than other restaurant in the mall.

Have try out most of the dishes, all of well prepared, flavorful and tasty. We will always order the spicy soup soup which is a must to order in every visit as well the salted egg bun.
author: Audrey L

review_text: Last day of Chinese New Year, whole family happily gathered for a dinner at this restaurant. We ordered our food way before the restaurant got crowded. Despite checking with the waitress multiple times, 2 of us waited for almost an hour for our dumplings, yet they never came. We felt the waitress was just paying us lip service and never informed the kitchen at all, or the kitchen didn't bothered. To stop feeling dumb sitting inside the noisy restaurant and waiting for nothing, we decided to cancel it. 2 of us went home with empty stomachs as we could not order more because likely they would never come. We also understood from the children that the noodle soup was plain and disappointing. Reading the reviews here, missing orders were actually very common at this restaurant, yet the management was happy and seems to have done nothing about it.
author: Cheese

review_text:
Went in for a quick dinner almost at the time of closure of the day.

We were allowed and ordered Vegetarian Dumplings , Vegetarian Fried Rice and Lemon Grass Juices.Everything was Good.

My Kid loved the Dumplings.

Previously I have tried their branch in the Jewel too.

Please don't miss out their Dumplings if you come across the restaurant.
author: Balamurugan M

review_text:
Subway got to Educate a staff of the name ZHANG.

The food was great as we dined in, but the experience was ruined by an extremely rude staff member named Zhang. He asked us to choose our vegetables, but when we selected more than five types, he bluntly remarked, “All vege?” in a disrespectful tone. While we were choosing our sauces, he turned his back on us entirely.

Subway should address this type of behavior. If an employee is not in the mood to work, they should not take it out on customers and ruin their day.
author: Dd Yn

review_text: It’s not really surprising that most recent reviews are all ‘⭐️- one star’. It seems like the recent bad experience was with a male young staff member who was ‘unfriendly and rude’. We ordered  simple and it was not a peak hour ‘around 8pm something ‘but it seems he didn’t listen well or maybe he just didn’t hear us. It’s like he was having a bad day or something. Overall, we had an unpleasant experience which is pretty typical with fast food chain staff.
author: Holidays Traveller

review_text:
I was purchasing a sandwich at the Subway outlet in SingPost. When I approached the counter, a staff member named Liza asked me to wait as she was attending to other matters. I replied, “Okay, no problem.”

However, when she was ready to take my order, her tone was rude and she appeared unwilling and unfriendly while serving me. I felt uncomfortable and confused, as I had been polite and patient throughout the interaction. I am unsure why she seemed unhappy or reluctant to take my order.

I hope this feedback can be taken seriously, as customer service is important and such behavior affects the overall experience.
author: jason loh

review_text:
Not even Feel giving like half a star today. I have been coming here for more five months, but one of the employees didn’t listen carefully to me, What veggies to put. After that unnecessarily put extra mayo, which I didnt want, not listening, carefully to my requirements. Felt like just swallowed trash.

Never visiting this outlet again.
author: Ratul Gumber

review_text:
Check out the sandwich that I packed home. Almost inedible looking,isn’t it. And This isn’t even the sandwich I ordered! Cashier boy gave me wrong order! It’s a off peak timing somemore. It’s not even lunch time yet. When I went back to subway to tell them they gave wrong order, none there even apologise. They did made a new sandwich and the black polo shirt Filipino lady who gave to me had this stern face and without saying a word. What a lousy attitude for a problem resolution.
Anyway,this is such a horrible customer service place,avoid this outlet at all costs.
author: Sorin G

review_text: Excellent Teochew food. Must try their steam soon hok if you are a fish lover. Even better than those 5star restaurants. Very reasonably priced restaurant that I visit almost every week.
author: S Sim

review_text:
Liang Kee Teochew Restaurant offers a classic Teochew dining experience. The menu features traditional dishes, and while the flavors are reliable, they don't necessarily stand out.

The restaurant itself is quite small. Inside, there are only about four air-conditioned tables. The majority of the seating is outdoors, which gives it a more casual, open-air feel.
author: WK C

review_text: A place to come if you want to have Teochew food. The braised duck sauce is too light in taste, you can't really taste it. You don't really taste the oysters in the fried oyster omelette, it's almost tasteless.  The pig trotter jelly is meaty and flavourful. Leather jacket fish is pretty good. The traditional garlic, chilli vinegar dipping sauce is also very light on taste. Prefer if the vinegar is slightly stronger. Sweet potato porridge is good, perfect to go with the dishes. The steam vegetables with dried scallops is flavourful, goes well with steam rice. Overall had a good lunch.
author: WTR Works

review_text:
I recall visiting this place at Havelock a long time ago, but a casual drive recently made me notice they had moved to MacPherson. Goot thing too because MacPherson is closed to home.

The family dropped in recently to catch a quick dinner before some drinks nearby.

In the words of my wife, the food tastes clean, unadulterated, and doesn't overwhelm with seasoning, and I totally agree with her.
Then again, aren't these the hallmarks of truly traditional Teochew cuisine? To not over-season the food so that the natural taste shines through?

Well. The food tastes Good here, and you don't come away after a meal feeling parched and dry in the mouth.

The candle on the cake has got to be the really nice wok-hei infused Chye Por Kway Teow! Just the right amount of preserved radish, and fried rice perfection with burnt ends to boot.

Ok. You may be wondering why 4 stars if that good ya?
Well. One of my favourite dishes in any Teochew place is fried liver rolls, but they don't have these here. Whenever I eat anything Teochew, and this dish is missing from the menu, I go home with a tinge of disappointment, because I simply Love It.
The sambal crayfish was good, albeit missing the punch you usually get with a stronger whack of sambal and chilli, but I guess for those who auccumb easily to numbing spices, this is a welcome relief.

In all, we had a good meal, and will likely be back for more.
author: Teck Chye Yeo

review_text:
I recently dined at Liang Kee Teochew Restaurant and was truly impressed! The fresh steamed fish was a standout—perfectly cooked, flaky, and full of flavor. It’s clear they prioritize quality ingredients.

The braised duck was equally fantastic. Tender and rich with a delicious sauce, it was a dish I won’t forget anytime soon. Both dishes were beautifully presented and paired perfectly with rice.

But what truly made our experience memorable was the exceptional service. When some tea was accidentally spilled on us, the staff immediately apologized and offered us a complimentary yam paste dessert. It was a thoughtful gesture that turned a minor mishap into a delightful moment.

Overall, I highly recommend Liang Kee Teochew Restaurant for its delicious food and outstanding service. I can’t wait to return for another meal!
author: Zackery Goh

review_text: Customise your beancurd with more than 1 options and believe it or not you can try out D24 Durian beancurd, and unique toppings such as black glutinous rice too! I had a plain original Beancurd which was smooth and refined in texture. They had some pastries to offer too. A walk at Geylang brought me to this pleasant beancurd  stall!
author: Reiko H

review_text:
Not the normal soya or beancurd shop. They have elevated for enthusiast who crave for midnight soya n beancurd. Menu offering is wide enough for a light snack aside from their soya n beancurd.

I have to agreed with some comments here that their beancurd n soya drink are on a light side.  I too prefer more of the soya bean taste. Beancurd smooth but lack the taste. Sugar is on extreme sweet. Nice if the sugar sweetener infuse with pandan leaves.

Price is a few cents more than your normal soya bean stall in a hawker center. Hey.. this is not a hawker. I think they have balance out the selling price well enough to call it affordable.
author: SD D.

review_text:
24 hours beancurd and light snacks. Price is on the hight side maybe due to 24 hours biz. Beancurd drinks and beancurd are flavourful. Best is can have it anytime.
On 22-10-25 try the pudding beancurd and beancurd drinks. The beancurd drink is as usual but the pudding beancurd is not my liking as is more watery than the beancurd.
author: Daniel Aiden Leo

review_text: Friendly good service by the shop owner. This fried banana thingy first time try, very nice. Recommend.
author: Zhenwei Peh

review_text:
The beancurd dessert was smooth, silky, and comforting. The syrup was gently sweet and complemented the softness of the beancurd well.
However, the pearls were still hard inside and lacked the chewy texture.
author: Kate

review_text: The dishes we ordered were nice, and we really liked the side dishes, especially the salad, which was fresh and tasty. However, the mobile ordering system could use some improvement — it’s quite laggy and the member registration doesn’t seem to give any real benefit when ordering. Other than that, the place has a nice and comfortable environment, and the staff are friendly and helpful. Overall, still a pleasant dining experience.
author: Dillon Tan

review_text:
Poor first experience. Ordered & Paid at 2.16pm, 26mins for my fish and chicken combo meal to arrive on a no crowd weekday late lunch.

No pre-empt about waiting time window yet, after 25mins of wait and watching me start taking photo of receipt, dish came in a few seconds. They could have at least serve me side dishes first & manage expectations isn’t it?

One young lady staff was just standing there at the counter and manager at the drinks counter not being observant with the needs of customers. Disappointed with the service. Food wise, was okay, as usual like other outlets.
author: Fion Koh

review_text: Came with family on a weekday night. Meet expectation for price. Steak was nicely done. Friend chicken was surprisingly very nice. Crispy outside. Succulent inside. Would recommend this combo. Mushroom soup can past. The environment was a bit noisy but that is expected too. Will come back if family looking for steak.
author: Liwei Chiang

review_text: Haven’t been here in a few years but still as good and affordable. Value for money. I always go for the grilled chicken and it remains juicy good. Usually have the hickory chicken but I tried the black pepper for the first time and it did not disappoint. For the amount of money spent to have a hearty main with 2 sides, enjoying it in the comfort of a clean, air-conditioned place - wonderful!
author: everlydaydream

review_text: I ordered the Prime Ribeye Extra at medium doneness and it was perfect!! So good that I forgot to take picture of it and enjoy every bite that’s so tender and juicy. Astons’ price is very reasonable for such good steak at $27.90 which comes with 2 generous side dishes of your choice from the selection. Service were prompt and professional. Keep up the good work!! F&B is tough to survive but we want Astons to be around for a long long time.
author: Jasz C

review_text:
Absolutely delighted to find freshly made delightfully mouth watering and delicious pani puris!!! Loved the perfect size and texture of puris (very essential when one is a fan of the dish). All components of the dish were tasty, made my heart sing!!
I also had the pleaure of savoring other snacks like papri chaat, churmur, bhel and pav bhaji, all of which were delicious and felt light and full of flavor. Would highly recommend these Indian snack dishes from Panipurizz!!
author: Ulupi T

review_text: Hands down some of the best pani puri I've had in Singapore! You can really taste the freshness in every bite. The fillings were generous and the spiced water was perfect. If you're looking for a 5-star snack experience at home, this is it.
author: Shirshendu Bhattacharya

review_text: One of the best pani puri I've had in Singapore. Their quality of puri is hard to find here and the spiced water is tailored to different tastes as required. Great service, too, at an affordable price.
author: Anubhav Mishra

review_text: This panipurri is really one of the best I've had in Singapore! It is both crispy and crunchy. I really suggest giving their full set a try, and the stuffing is really delicious :) What you might end up regretting is not getting enough for the first order!
author: Song Fengyang

review_text: Legit golgappas. Stumbled upon the website accidentally but so glad I did. Really wish I discovered them earlier. The taste and flavours are just right, authentic. Placing another order with them after yesterday. Prompt service and replies. Trying out dabeli and sev puri for my next order. Thank you Panipurizz
author: Niharika S

review_text: I went for the pump at around 615pm yesterday. Great service recejved from the cashier, senior with spec. She is friendly and pleasant to greet, suggest and verify my appl entitlement the rice and oil. It is rare to receive such excellent service this day, compliment to shell for this. The uncle that served me at pump 2 is polite too. Thumb up.
author: Mdm Yong

review_text:
The night-shift lady cashier displayed a poor attitude when I enquired about the rice and water bottle rewards. Her replies were blunt, unclear, and she appeared impatient during the interaction. This resulted in an unpleasant customer experience.
I believe Shell should enhance customer service training to ensure staff communicate clearly and serve customers with courtesy and professionalism.
author: Mikezhang Chong

review_text:
Good carwash service. Went the extra mile to remove a very stubborn grime and gave advice on car maintenance.

Found out it’s a new carwash tenant. Good job, keep up the service!
author: Nicole T

review_text: I want to commend Uncle 'Siva' (not sure if I spelt his name correctly) for his concern and help towards my annoyance earlier. I was trying to drop off a parcel as 259 Shell Macpherson was one of Singapore's drop off locations and the website stated they are open every day from 9am to 9pm. I came at around 715pm and the Chinese uncle at the register told me their manager had already left, so obviously I was annoyed because I lug my parcel around the entire day and made my way after work only to find out I cannot drop off my parcel. Uncle Siva noticed I was clearly upset and distraught that he told me to wait and he will call the manager. She promptly called the other Uncle to try to guide him through the issue/process. I am still disappointed that I am unable to sort this out properly and swiftly but nonetheless Uncle Siva made my evening better with his kindness and concern. So I would like to thank you very much and Shell please give Uncle Siva the thanks he deserves. The only reason I am giving 4 stars is because of him. Once again, thank you Uncle Siva 🙏🏽
author: Abigail LeonoraLim

review_text:
I normally pump at Esso but decided to give Shell a shot and I did not regret it. Ayisha was very careful to explain how to use the vouchers in the Shell App, with a really cheerful disposition. The service staff outside was also very friendly and went the extra mile to bring a box for me to throw my trash from the vehicle. Great job to the team here at Shell MacPherson!

I came again and Katherine and Ching were really awesome! Did all the good service staff go to Shell? Wow!
author: Samuel Goh

restaurant_name: Soon Lee Lor Mee Stall 順利滷麵攡
review_text:
Possibly the worst tasting Lor Mee I ever tried in Singapore.

Ordered a Small bowl ($4) and added $1 for extra ingredients. Either I got scammed or the portion is truly pathetic. The 'lor' is also too sweet, and the chilli isn't spicy enough to provide the "kick".
author: Jason

restaurant_name: Soon Lee Lor Mee Stall 順利滷麵攡
review_text: My favourite Lor Mee! Love it since I first tried it 16 years ago - good taste & value-for-money.
author: Adrian Lee

restaurant_name: Soon Lee Lor Mee Stall 順利滷麵攡
review_text:
A lor mee that's value for money, and with a soup that's not too starchy/viscous. This is also the first time I finished the soup as though it was a bowl of ramen!

They offer 3 sizes of $4, $5, $6 for the portions. My picture shows the $5 portion. I loved the great noodle firmness and texture. Flavours are awesome and you can adjust the flavour by adding as much vinegar as you want.

Will definitely return for more!
author: Glen Ho

restaurant_name: Soon Lee Lor Mee Stall 順利滷麵攡
review_text: Lovely and tasty lor mee that is thick in their gravy. A popular lor mee stall among the residents and regulars. Highly recommended.
author: Tengcc Ng

restaurant_name: Soon Lee Lor Mee Stall 順利滷麵攡
review_text:
Located near the extreme right end of the Circuit road hawker center (last 2nd to be exact).

Ever since exposed to this when I was working at Ubi area, occasionally when time permits, I'd take bus to Circuit rd hawker during lunch. Just to eat his lor mee. A pity would be in the past, the operating days are kinda inconsistent.

Although slight increase (now at $4/ 5/ 6) of price, the quality seems to taste better. And I'll definitely go for the large one. Regardless $5 or $6, any day.

Uncle is always friendly. Always in a jovial mood everyday.

The ingredients he used is fresh (just look at the beansprout, man). The Lor in the Lor mee is the main star. Subtle hints of spices yet not too overpowering. Consistency of the Lor works for my palate. Pair it with a cooked-just-nice flat yellow noodle, that's your comforting bowl of lor mee. Works even better on a cold rainy day.

Highly recommended for dine in for the optimum shiokness.
author: ʍɾɴ

review_text:
good old school wantonmee that i like. ordered additional fried dumplings to try , fresh prawns in these dumplings!!
lady boss served the fried dumplings to me after i took my noodles, friendly lady boss.

before coming, i read from a couple reviews that the wantons were bland, but after tasting, realised they made adjustment and i liked the whole meal! businesses that take feedbacks definitely deserve a mention!

noodles were springy and charsiew was the lean type (my preference) . will definitely be back!
author: adelin lin

review_text:
15/02/26
Honestly, the wonton noodles are overrated. Ordered without chili, the noodles came simply tossed in dark soy sauce with some pork lard, which tasted quite plain. The char siew was also rather bland and lacked flavor. The only standout item was the wonton itself bigger and tastier than what you typically get with standard wonton noodles.
author: Luke Skywalker

review_text: Tasty wontan noodle at hawker. Noodle is cooked to Al dente and both fried and soup wanton and char Siew are also tasty and of reasonable size.
author: Charles Lim

review_text: Finally found a really really tasty wanton noodle stall. The chilli sauce is spicy without burning one’s tongue and it’s a very balance of salty and sweet. Theres a generous serving of char siew too. The noodles were springy and chewy (not overcooked or undercooked). I love the wanton (not the fried type) - the meat is flavourful. For $4.00, I had a good serving of the noodles. Like most stalls in this food centre, the stall closes at about 2 pm.
author: Jee Nee Lim

review_text: Ordered a $5 fried wanton mee. Taste was nothing to harp about. Soup was bland. Pretty underwhelming. Char siew, noodles and fried wantons all fell short of expectations. Disappointing.
author: Hatsune Miku

restaurant_name: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
review_text: I went with a group of colleagues as our plan was lunch at old Airport road end up market was closed for washing. I feel disgusting after I finish my meal and I witness this myself. 1st soup was diluted, meat not so tasty, the salted vegetables taste horrible too and totally tasted different and not as good as previous stall we have at Jalan Besar. After our meal, I'm shocked to see the stall helper digging his nose and worst is after doing that he didn't wash his hand! Less then 5min, he went to smoke 🚬 at the walk way and came back to the stall didn't wash the hand and proceed back to cook for the customer who ordered. Omg! Never in my life, I will go back again! This is super disgusting and horrible unhygienic! Hopefully, SFA can visit and access the stall! I seldom give such review and would said this is the 1st time I see such thing! Regret having meal there!
author: Eileen

restaurant_name: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
review_text: Despite the vendor's notably brusque demeanor, this stall earns its reputation through impeccably cleaned pig organ soup. The offal—whether liver, intestine, or stomach—arrives without a trace of that gamey aftertaste that plagues lesser versions, a testament to rigorous washing that borders on artisanal. Where they falter is portion control: servings lean modest, making the automatic inclusion of meatballs and three-layered pork feel like filler rather than value. Truthfully, I’d prefer an organs-only option to savor their star ingredient undiluted. Come prepared for old-school transaction rules—cash is king here, with digital payments firmly off the menu.
author: Mr Wang Wang

restaurant_name: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
review_text: Pig organ soup ($5.50) has quite a bit of ingredients, but the only organ is liver, coupled with lean pork, pork belly, pork ball and tofu. No intestines, stomach or any other organs. Additional order of salted vegetables was tasteless. Can ask for additional soup re-fill, which is a plus.
author: Jerald Ici

restaurant_name: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
review_text:
One of the famous Pork Organ Soup in the area.
Ingredients were fresh, the portion is pretty big for its price as well.
However, the soup has a bit of porky smell, and their Kiam Chai (Pickled Veggies) is not tasty.
To me it’s just average, plus the uncle is pretty sarcastic toward his other customers, not really friendly.
author: Jayon See

restaurant_name: Cheng Mun Kee Pig's Organ Soup
review_text:
Nice portion for SGD 5.50
Add 50c for a bowl of rice
Chill sauce is spot on, suitable for most taste buds. The salted vege is strong, so its suitable for those prefer their soup on the salty side of things.
author: MrJayquak

review_text:
The bryani and the prata had spicy curry. They did give quite a huge portion of bryani rice, so it's value for money, though the taste needs improving. Old shop, with a slightly confusing ordering system.

But it has a old school kind of charm, even if I don't think I'll ever eat here again. The teh tarik peng is very sweet, with more sugar than tea taste. Good for a sugar rush, bad for the waistline.
author: Drew

review_text:
i always come here for a prata and maggie goreng after i do my lashes next door. the prata is always made to order and comes out exceptionally hot and nice.

the owner and staff here are always friendly and always ensure that the food is good(:
author: Mar

review_text: Prata were fluffy and soft inside and crispy on the outside, unlike many of other stalls in Singapore that have crispy but dense and tough pratas. Curry was of perfect consistency, flavourful and nicely tinged with assam give a nice spicy and sour kick.
author: Wayne

review_text: Ok la not bad. Chairs could be cleaner. Can also ask smokers not to smoke right outside.
author: Ramzi

review_text: best curry for prata ive tasted in SG and the prata is not so oily compared to others, def recommend everyone to try
author: Elroy lim

review_text: Curry fish head are not bad, taste good reasonable size. The rest of the dishes pricier. If you don't mind the price that's no reason to not to go. Just pay more. Please note that you will still need to pay for GST and service charge. 2022 boxing day I go there with my family again. This place are good with their zhi char, so nice didn't disappointed me. Excellent service. The foods also taste good. We order crabs which are good highly recommend.
author: LWF SL Leong

review_text:
Located just 5mins+ walk from Potong Pasir MRT, Gu Ma Jia serves a decent varieties of local 煮炒 that are simple yet delicious.

The Assam Groupa Fish Head was quite spicy and goes very well with rice. Kyoto pork ribs were very tender with appetising sweet and sour sauce. Salted egg prawns were very fresh but otherwise pretty normal. What surprise me was the ying yang kai lan which was served with deep fried shredded kai lan leaves and crunchy kai lan stems.

Staff were very prompt in service and  friendly as well. Recommended to make reservations during Friday night and weekend to avoid not being able to get seats. Pricing were reasonable as well.

Overall definitely one of the better zi char restaurants option in Singapore.

There are plenty of dessert cafe and bar next to it for after meal chilling sessions as well.
author: Genesis NΞO

review_text:
Updating my overdue reviews and had came here at least 3 times today as of writing.

The food is tasty and the staff are very friendly. We love the assam fish head and the white bee hoon. The asparagus with seaweed is special. Overall me and my family like this establishment!
author: Quak Yong Sheng

review_text: Friendly and attentive staff. Nice cosy environment. Food is good and delicious. We especially love the assam curry fish head, quite spicy yet taste good. Do try their dessert as well. Overall worth coming again for dinner.
author: Kelvin Chye

review_text:
My family and I came to Gu Ma Jia on Saturday for dinner. As it was a last minute decision, we did not make any reservations. Nevertheless, we had a table within a minute of arrival.

The lady boss and her daughter were extremely friendly and service-oriented. The menu they provided were very clear and informative on the dishes they have.

So we ordered 2 of their signature dishes - the Assam Fish Head and Kyoto Pork Ribs. As I do not like to eat fish, I ordered an additional Prawn Paste Chicken Wings, and wrapped up with a Stir Fried Garlic Broccoli.

The dishes came fast despite many tables at the lower level being occupied. The Assam Fish Head was sourish and mildly spicy, perfect to go with rice. The gravy was delicious!

The Kyoto Pork Ribs was a bit too sourish for my liking, but the meat was extremely tender. I ate at least least the dish myself.

The Prawn Paste Chicken Wings and Fried Garlic Broccoli were of a decent standard.

All the food were finished rather quickly despite the adults being not hungry, an account of how tasty the food were.

Finally, ordered 2 mango puddings for the my kids and the my in laws shared the lady boss recommended Kefir Jelly dessert. Not sure what was the name of the dessert, and did not managed to get a picture of it. But my mother in law loved it! My wife and I tried a spoon of it. The texture was like aiyu jelly with some citrus elements. This dessert would be perfect after a very filling dinner.

Highly recommend this place to everyone. And we will be back soon for the tasty food again!
author: Eviltrap Choi

review_text: It’s my first time to Singapore and I knew I had to try Kaya toast and I’m glad I picked this spot to try it! Definitely a locals shop but the cashier was friendly and didn’t make me feel unwelcome, it is cash only though! I got the breakfast set and it was delicious, lots of Kay and butter on my toast, my kopi was delicious, and my husband got some sort of stir fried noodles with an egg that he loved also. I was a little surprised that the eggs were soft boiled but I enjoyed eating them with my toast! The seating was very full but a nice couple at a big table was nice enough to let us share with them.  I’d definitely come back for a breakfast set!
author: Sarah C

review_text:
Really one of the better traditional breakfast around SG. The bread was well toasted and their Kaya is unique which you know it’s home made. Coffee was good too and I think for $4.20, it’s really worth it.

What I also like is the vibes here that made you feel like you are in JB. Just chilling and vehicle watching.

They have other stalls too and I tried the $3 mee siam which reminds me of the primary school meesiam.
author: Kah Wang Tan

review_text: Delicious kaya toast with a generous serving of butter. Coffee is fragrant. Egg is well done. Nice relaxing atmosphere. Their pastries such as cream puffs are freshly baked on site.
author: Su Hui Lee

review_text: Hainanese Kopi Gao Siew Dai. Kaya Butter Toast. Charcoal Toasted Bread. Old School Taste So Good. Delicious . Great Combination ❤️. Love The Coffee And Toast. Hainanese Cuisine.
author: Tan Meng Geok

review_text:
Good traditional wanton noodle, VFM economic rice (home style) and fresh baked buns and pastries.

An old school kopi-tiam that sits at the corner of a terrace shop houses. Likely a go-to spot for the neighbouring business and residents.  Liked the small eclectic mix of stalls. Tried the wanton noodle, and it's the traditional type. Noodle is QQ, decently spiced chilli, and home-cook char siew. Pretty value for money for its location.

The kopi o kosong is strong, and burnt well. The way I like it. The drink stall also sells fresh baked buns and puffs, baked with happy Uncle Wong, with long experience as a baker, restaurant owner and a colourful history to boot! Love the fresh old style sugar sprinkled doughnuts, their version of ham-chim-peng, custard puff and sausage bun.

Economic rice is decently good and value for money. Home taste type, the dishes are not strongly flavoured.

Supposedly the toast bread and half-boiled eggs are good. Will try that next. Update: Toast is yums! Although not the charcoal type but electric toasted. The sifu got the kungfu to make a savory kaya-rich crispy toast! Half boiled eggs is of the right consistency to rival those from the more established Singapore brands!

The place can get a bit crowded during lunch time and can be rather warm.
author: David Oon

review_text:
For an authentic Thai dining experience near Jalan Wangi, I highly recommend a spot that offers both great value and exceptional flavors.

Be sure to try their Steam Seabass with lemon garlic source and Tom Yum Soup – both dishes are absolutely delicious , big position and full of authentic taste.

You'll find that the pricing is quite reasonable, making it a perfect choice for a satisfying meal.
author: wayway Lim

review_text:
Chance upon this eatery when I was scouting for late breakfast.
Ordered boat noodle and bak chor mee which the prices were reasonable. The boat noodle broth was a little sweet for me but with chilli flakes, it became fine. The bak chor mee meets expectation and for $5, the portion is big.
The kopi siew dai was good n cheap at $1.30 during breakfast hours. The toast however was so so. The usual bread toast you get at coffee shop but nothing to complain when the set costs $2.50
The elderly lady serving us (not sure if she is the lady boss) was very friendly and nice. Our bill was wrong and on checking refunded us the difference. We ordered through QR code and the coffee price is different but we did not realize at point of payment.
Will go back to try the Thai menu which the prices were reasonable. Saw set meals below $13 with one drink.
author: Jane Lee

review_text:
Worst bcm ever
Order for breakfast but the noodle is legi tasteless.Order with chill but no taste at all noodle does not have any sauce at all also
Soup taste kind of salty. Liver is overcook and very hard. Not worth the 5 buck to eat. Topping also very little. Eat once not coming back again
author: Wei

review_text: Delicious and yummy Thai food with good service from the staff, reasonable price for the taste and portion ⭐️🌟💫✨
author: Darjs

review_text: Second time here! They serve up a wide selection of yummy Thai food at good prices. We loved their omelette and lemongrass drink! The prawn in the clear tom yum soup could be fresher, but everything else was great. Cozy, comfortable place to dine in and the staff are nice too. Definitely worth a try
author: J H

review_text:
Staff cashier was friendly. I would come again and refill petrol here, not really near where I was staying or working though but recommended to refill here.

Did car wash here, just so so.
author: William Lu

review_text: Just want to give my gratitude to one of your staff named Crystal. My husband fainted and unconscious today. Now my husband is safely reached to the hospital brought by the ambulance. Thank you for your help and kindness. I appreciate it alot. Hope to see you soon 1 day.
author: Anna

review_text: The staff are friendly n helpful. There is a small cozy and relaxing area to allow consumers to consume their purchased coffee before travelling.
author: Samantha Khor

review_text:
Car wash over charging customers.
Driving a mini bus and yet charge for a big bus/ lorry.
And they're charging extra for "Chinese New Year" on the 2nd February onwards. This is absurd!
author: Feroz Ghulam

review_text:
New management at the car wash!

Very detailed clean very friendly.

Love the antics.
author: Dave Ang

review_text:
I saw the banner and went up to purchase. I was blown away when the guy started making and assembling the brownie right infront of me. Taste amazing with all the chocolatey taste. Will come
Back more to purchase !
author: Axen Lee

review_text: P.OSH has always been my childhood favourite and drop by all the way just to get it again for a friend's birthday. The 2 lady staff that attended to me were very friendly and nice, and the brownie toppings are made on the spot for you. I hope more people will know about this and have it nearer to town!
author: Alicia Chan

review_text: Best brownie ever!! Thick and good. Not overly sweet. Many favors. Been buying for over 15 years.
author: Daph

review_text:
Favourite brownie since schooling days!!

Chewy, decadent and rich brownie. Even nicer when warmed up or paired with ice cream!

They have a lower sugar option that is slightly tougher but still a great dessert option!

Great for gifting and for self consumption.

Please support them!!
author: DH

review_text: Have been living posh brownies since 10 years ago and quality has not changed over the years. The shop is abit out of the way located in MacPherson mall on level 3 with no seating area, but anything to get the brownie fix
author: Deng Yimin

review_text: Small Delifrance counter within Fairprice Express. Good to pick up a couple of pastries.
author: Patrick Teo

review_text: Nice cafe
author: Goh Francis

restaurant_name: Ji De Chi Dessert @ Paya Lebar Square
review_text:
At Paya Lebar area, many would come here for a dessert after meal. Usually crowded and need to wait for seats from 8pm onwards (usually on Fri and weekends).

Overall not bad but I would recommend to go for their cold / shaved ice desserts. Hot desserts probably lacking a bit of punch. The pumpkin pancake also a bit average. I like their durian desserts.
author: Lee Wayne

restaurant_name: Ji De Chi Dessert @ Paya Lebar Square
review_text:
When I saw half a bowl left of another customer’s black sesame paste, I instinctively thought that it could be personal preference of sweetness.
But then I realised on my first taste that this is a bowl of sesame paste without the sesame taste.
The mango sticky rice roll was ok but the ‘skin’ texture seemed a little thick and ‘plastic-y’
- could be improved I guess. Just my personal opinion. I left the bowl of 芝麻糊 untouched - so sad
author: Linna Tan

restaurant_name: Ji De Chi Dessert @ Paya Lebar Square
review_text:
While the taste of the two desserts were alright, you can tell they do not put in effort or heart in their food or maybe they just don’t give a damn about their food. Durian Mille feuille came frozen and rock hard and definitely not that texture I was expecting for a slice of cake. Durian sago also came frozen and the sago were all frozen solid.

If the eatery can’t take pride in its offering, it’s better to close down their shop.
author: Julius Tan

restaurant_name: Ji De Chi Dessert @ Paya Lebar Square
review_text: Nice place to grab traditional and new desserts at an affordable price. With many different choices, from warm to cold and sweet to sour, there is definitely something that can satisfy your dessert cravings. Prices here range from about 3.50 to 10 dollars depending on the item, and special add ons are available. Overall, it was very well portioned. The environment here is peaceful and quiet with a simple interior design. Service here is fast, however tray return is self service.
author: Elden Teo

restaurant_name: Ji De Chi Dessert @ Paya Lebar Square
review_text: Huge variety of desserts. Sweetness level is mild, suitable for those who love desserts but not at 100% sugar. Prices are very competitive, I'd say even cheaper that other dessert shops.
author: Peipei Peipei

restaurant_name: Saute Sushi | Paya Lebar Square | Paya Lebar | Vegetarian Vegan Halal | Japanese Cuisines
review_text:
A great place to enjoy plant-based sushi, if that is what you are looking for.
Food served on mini toy model trains on conveyor belts ~ bring all the excitement for the kids,and us adults too, as it was our first visit.
We loved the Volcano rolls and the ramen. Other sushi were good too. We didn't get the donburi (it had limited choices).

Will definitely come back.
author: Veronica Chan

restaurant_name: Saute Sushi | Paya Lebar Square | Paya Lebar | Vegetarian Vegan Halal | Japanese Cuisines
review_text:
Vegan food isn’t usually my first choice, but this restaurant completely changed my perception of it.

Initially, I found myself looking for flavours similar to meat or seafood. By the end of the meal, though, I genuinely enjoyed the vegan ingredients for what they are. Come with an open mind and you’ll understand what I’m trying to share.

A special shout-out to the staff who served us — they were friendly, attentive, and very helpful, which really added to the overall dining experience.
author: Franciz “SG FlavorScape”

restaurant_name: Saute Sushi | Paya Lebar Square | Paya Lebar | Vegetarian Vegan Halal | Japanese Cuisines
review_text: Visited Sauté today with a few friends and I was very impressed with the plethora of vegan sushi options they had. Everything tasted really good and high quality, and I love how they utilised vegetables in their normal form versus resorting to mock meat for every dish. I would definitely give this place a try if you’re on a plant based lifestyle.
author: Amrita Bala

restaurant_name: Saute Sushi | Paya Lebar Square | Paya Lebar | Vegetarian Vegan Halal | Japanese Cuisines
review_text: I really like the spicy tomato ramen, it was delicious although a-bit oily. The fried battered black mushrooms was really juicy (not oily). The hot Genmai tea is free flow (do-it-yourself with the hot water tap at the side of your table). Order your food and beverage via the QR quote placed at your table and the food will be delivered to you via the conveyor belt beside your table as it’s a vegetarian sushi place that’s why. Service is very good. Although there is a time limit of 90 minutes (mentioned on small signages at our table), we arrived rather late for dinner service and everyone let us stay there to chitchat until closing. We wouldn’t have stayed so long during normal dinner service as this place is really popular.
author: XY C

restaurant_name: Saute Sushi | Paya Lebar Square | Paya Lebar | Vegetarian Vegan Halal | Japanese Cuisines
review_text: Great spot for families with kids! The sushi train is such a highlight—my kids couldn’t wait to collect their food. Everything we tried was good, but I especially recommend the soup noodles—the broth is rich and well made. Sushi is creative, delightful, and there are lots of selections to choose from. It will be perfect if the rice texture can be improved. Service is friendly and efficient too. Will definitely come back!
author: Josephine

review_text: Today this is my second time eating pizza from Pezzo . I really love it 🍕. Tastefully also the stuff, India guy are friendly and helpful. Will buy again ..
author: April Cho

review_text: Thumb up to the manager, Mdm Tay on her awesome service. She assist me to mix n match to save cost. She offer to cut into 2pcs for each slice so that easy to eat and suggest to pack 3 slices in each box to make up total of 4 boxes, plus additional sides that I bought, so that I’m able to carry them back. She is very patient in explaining and giving me a lot of suggestions n recommendation. Thank you Mdm Tay for your time and service, my family enjoyed the food hot, nice and neatly packed.
author: Winnie Tay

review_text: Went at about 8:20am for their advertised breakfast sets but only 2 items off the bfast menu were available hahaha so I got the chicken mayo rolls. On the brightside, they were nice and hot. Service was alright, staff were busy getting started. Overall quite average but not bad for the price ($4.50 for 2 rolls and a drink).
author: mushroom soup

review_text: The Malay guy name khai so helpful and help me with patience to choose pizza and some more give a good slow talk with me fast service and I didn’t need wait too long over here just few second the pizza is ready. Really love your pizza and your work 👍👍👍👍👍
author: Qinobizz 135

review_text: Selling simple pizzas at a price of gold with Horrible packaging that doesn’t travel well. No wonder the brand is dying. Sooner the better. Awful
author: hamza shahid

review_text:
Saw that they won the taiwan beef noodle award for 2025 when i visited today. Congratulations!
---
This is my favourite Taiwanese food restaurant - I've been going frequently since more than 10 years ago when they were at vivocity, then when they moved here until now when they expanded their tables to the shop beside.

Their beef noodle is a MUST eat - melts in the mouth like the best beef noodles in Taiwan! All the Taiwanese snacks like 盐酥鸡，卤肉饭, 面线 tastes authentic too. Oh and the bubble tea too!

Highly recommended if you love authentic Taiwanese food too!
author: Collin Ng

review_text:
If you come here, you must try the Braised Pork Rice , which taste quite nice and cheap. It is $4.9 and taste good with meet ,egg and veg. If you like eating Yoshinoya,  you will find it as another easy, affordable and worth choice.

Tried four different dishes today, and every single one of them was good.
author: Echo Cheng

review_text:
Poped by for a quick dinner twice. Same staff on two occassions. She was very attentive and approachable, very good service attitude.

Had plain rice, beancurd skin and black fungus (cold dish) on first visit. Had beef noodles soup for second visit. Food were all good. Beef were tender (cant find this standard elsewhere other than Kings Noodles in Richardson, Dallas). Soup was flavourful. Only shortall is noodles not enough to fill my stomach. Overall very good experience on both visits with good standards of food. Nice ambience hidden in a basement. Though dinner hour (6.30pm) on both weekdays but no queue required.
author: Christofer

review_text:
Visited 5 Little Bears for a quick solo dinner. The place had a nostalgic street-style charm with vibrant lanterns and travel posters lining the corridor-style seating area—though a little cramped during peak hour.

Ordered the Taichung Braised Pork Rice set ($7) which came with green tea and added crispy shiitake wedges ($3.50). The braised pork rice was hearty and flavourful with a good mix of pickled veggies, greens, and a braised egg, though the meat could be more tender and fatty in balance. The fried mushrooms were a nice touch—crispy and seasoned well.

Service was fast, food was warm, and value for money is fair for a quick casual meal. Nothing mind-blowing, but a satisfying fix if you’re craving Taiwanese comfort food.
author: Jeffrey

review_text:
They have quite a cute shop name. If you do not take a closer look, you might not know they are actually serving Taiwanese food.

Their food are actually very affordable and the portion is absolutely generous. The braised pork rice is a big portion. Very comforting to eat, slightly sweet, but it taste well.

Big chicken cutlet is great. Not too much flour and you could have a mouthful of chicken in every bite. The chicken is really big and alone can be a full meal for some.

However, i find the chicken can be quite salty and if you are eating the whole chicken by yourself, it can become quite Jelak. I strongly recommend sharing the chicken.

Overall, good place to go on a cheat day.
author: Clarence Ow

review_text: Service very attentive and pleasant, drinks reasonably prices. But the food/snack is definitely not recommended. Very over priced for the portion given. $12 for 10 pieces of potato wedges. Is a joke, this was not indicated either on the menu.
author: HonShun Wan

review_text: Super cool ambience by the river! We were super late visitors as they are the only place around open until 5am, but service was amazing. Kitchen was no more open at that time, so we brought some take away food from the place beside - and the barman gave us plates (normal, not a single-use ones)! Also allowing and encouraging us to play our own music and in general feeling like being in a friend's bar! Highly recommended, will come again!
author: Tomas

review_text:
Was pleasantly surprised with the quality of food.  I ordered a lamb chop, chicken chop and fish and chips, all of which tasted great, especially the lamb chop.
The gentleman serving us was very friendly.
Al fresco dining concept.
author: Hou Seng Tan

review_text:
Came here thinking to try out the 1 for 1 mains on Chope, but honestly like the other reviews, the food is really bad and not worth your time and money.

The "fish" from their fish and chips is basically the same kind you can find at NTUC in the frozen section. The lasagna is extremely soggy and it tastes microwaved. The sides of the plate is not wiped down and the sauce is splattered everywhere.

We are the only table on a friday evening, and the food still took almost 30 minutes to come. It looks like there is only 1 person running the restaurant. Her service is good but I would say the poor standard of this place is attributed to its management, the poor girl is just doing her best. The tables are outside too, so unless you really like the Singapore weather, it's not what I would consider comfortable. Would not recommend and would not come back again.
author: Zheng Songhua

review_text:
A chill bar near the river. We came here for the 1 for 1 deal from entertainer hsbc.

From the looks itself, it definitely looks quite sad, but it actually tasted quite special. The taste is not what you would get in the typical western food store.

But well, i had to admit that it is not worthwhile to have their food and drink at the original price, it is really expensive and absolutely not value for money.

Nevertheless, the server that serves us is meticulous and patient. He immediately gave us the insect repellent after he realize that we might have seen some bugs around the table.
author: Clarence Ow

review_text: Very pleasantly surprised by the nice food, excellent service and not so noisy atmosphere. The sesame chicken portion was good and delicious, plus free top up of soup base. The pork belly really nice. Staff are super friendly and nice. 👍🏻The inner space is actually less noisy than outside. Suitable for chats
author: Jason Lee

review_text:
Definitely loved my experience here! Frequent visits back to the restaurant. Highly recommended to give this a try.

The chicken hotpot was incredibly flavourful — drinkable broth, tender chicken, and fresh ingredients that made every bite satisfying. Boneless chicken meat made it even better, no frills! Can eat without worrying biting onto any bone scraps. I’ve always added on plenty of dishes. You can too, to your own liking!

The crushed garlic pork belly is a dish that I will definitely order whenever I visit! The crunch of the cucumber wrapped with the pork belly is very refreshing. The crushed garlic adds additional layer of flavour to the pork belly too.

Another recommended dish is the egg fried rice with pork chop! The fried rice is filled with the fragrance of the egg. The pork chop is flavourful as well, with a hint of sweetness on its skin.
author: Nicholas Goh

review_text: One of the best chicken pots I had. Quality of chicken is good; tender and moist. Comes in a mini claypot with a fire below. You can ask to add more gravy and add side dishes. Fantastic lunch deals at $10.90. Will be back.
author: Joel Tan

review_text: Great value for money. I came alone for dinner and ordered a chicken pot, fried egg, jasmine rice and iced water. The food was served in less than 5 minutes, and I finished them in under 20 minutes. A testament of how good the food was. Payment process is pretty fast too and the staff asked to double check the order before finalizing the payment.
author: antoni zhu

review_text:
Hot and sour fish pot(M) 酸辣鱼锅
Chicken pot(M) 鸡肉香锅
Stir fried Baby Spinach 蒜炒箥菜
Pork belly with Crushed Garlic 蒜泥白肉

🍜 Food wise:
It should be very good to start eating the Hot and sour fish pot, the soup was so refreshing and was very appetizing. The fish was pretty firm and delicious, and dip it with their chilli sauce for an additional spicy kick! Good for sharing between 3 or more people!

Next, the chicken pot was saucy, the bubbling of the gravy by itself looked very appetizing already. Taste wise was not bad, the meat was pretty tender and nice chewy texture. Other ingredients were fresh, crunchy and sweet. In my opinion, the meat size was slightly small, if only the meat was a bit thicker, and throwing in a bit more dried chilli then I think would be perfect. It still tasted quite nice in general! Good for sharing between 2 or 3 persons given the portion of meats, the chunks of fish from the fish pot was more satisfying and sufficient.

Stir fried baby spinach was fragrant, fresh and savoury. Quite good, veg lovers might appreciate it more!

The pork belly was nice, coated with aromatic minced garlic sauce along with fresh crunchy cucumbers. Overall taste wise still has room for improvement though.

✨ Ambience wise: Felt slightly like Song Fa Bak Kut Teh or Dian Xiao Er restaurant, Chinese restaurant vibe!

🤵🏻 Service wise: Great!

💵 Price wise:
Hot and sour fish pot(M) 酸辣鱼锅 $23.90Chicken pot(M) 鸡肉香锅 $21.90Stir fried Baby Spinach 蒜炒箥菜 $8.80Pork belly with Crushed Garlic 蒜泥白肉 $7.90
author: Wei xiong Wang

restaurant_name: Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King (Paya Lebar)
review_text:
Frankly the ramen taste pretty gd. However, there were two major no no

1) it was a gd gesture to have free flow eggs, however, the batch we had were really hard to peel, the shell stuck to the egg and not a single egg came out nice n intact. All were broken or barely left 70% after removing the shell with the egg white stuck to it.

2) the place though small could be bearable if the aircon was working nicely. However , this was not the case. When u enter a restaurant and u see many fans around, it is a red flag. Imagine eating a bowl of hot soupy ramen in a cramp stuffy hot restaurant, we were sweating even bef we could finish our meal. Very unpleasant experience. If you are someone who cannot take the heat esp on a hot and humid day, I suggest you skip this place, do takeaway or wait for one rainy day to dine in the restaurant
author: Super Bunny

restaurant_name: Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King (Paya Lebar)
review_text: A good ramen spot if you’re in the area. They offer unlimited bean sprouts and hard-boiled eggs, which I think is their unique selling point and a nice bonus while waiting for your ramen. There are many varieties to choose from, but I always go with the classic tonkotsu ramen — tasty, flavorful, and not overwhelming. Price is reasonable for the quality, and service is quick even when it’s busy.
author: G A

restaurant_name: Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King (Paya Lebar)
review_text:
Great broth and noodle texture. Would order spicy black sauce the next time.

The tonkotsu king branch specialty is the choice that is more worthy here. The amount of meat is good.

Taste:
Tonkotsu niku king ramen 4/5
Tonkotsu niku king spicy black ramen 5/5
Tonkotsu ramen 3.5/5
Miso Ramen 3.5/5
author: Kai

restaurant_name: Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King (Paya Lebar)
review_text: Found this hidden gem tucked just outside Paya Lebar Square, serving up authentic Japanese ramen and gyoza. Tried all three of their soup bases: 1) the tonkotsu was rich, creamy, and deeply satisfying, 2) the miso was salty, umami-packed, and incredibly comforting, and 3) the shoyu had a light sweetness with bold soy flavor—clean and refreshing. The gyoza were crisp on the outside, juicy on the inside, and bursting with savory goodness. Portions are generous, noodles cooked to al dente perfection, and each bowl comes with huge, tender slices of pork. Bonus points for the free flow of hard-boiled eggs and crunchy bean sprouts. A solid spot for a hearty, satisfying meal that hits all the right notes. The only downside? Expect a short wait during peak hours—but it’s well worth it.
author: Gin Lee

restaurant_name: Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King (Paya Lebar)
review_text:
Ramen Keisuke Tonkotsu King Niku King is situated at Paya Lebar Square and one of the many branches under the Keisuke Group.

Visited around 6pm and ordered the Niku King Shoyu Ramen for S$13.90(S$16.65 after GST and Service Charge), toppings include 3 pork slices, menma, negi, and a piece of narutomaki.

Chose the normal flavor strength(saltiness level) for the ramen broth but I did find it more salty than expected for a normal level. The menma has a nice crunch to it and the pork slices was good in flavor.

Complimentary hard boiled eggs and bean sprouts are available for customers who dine in, each table also comes with a condiment rack which is convenient.

The interior aesthetics was traditional styled with manga panels used as a wall art deco which is nice. Service was mostly limited to being led to our tables and the serving of food so I am neutral with regards to service.
author: ShinoCoffee

review_text: Weekday have 20% off if you are not using any discount. The food was served shortly and the service staff uncle and auntie are friendly. All the food was tasty and delicious. I will definitely go back again. They are having promotion for 2 crabs for $48. The crab was expectedly small for the price but was good enough to ease if you have craving for crabs.
author: BMWGal

review_text: Came to this place at a whim after deciding that our previous dining reservation was not for us. For the food we ordered, the pork ribs, curry fish head, prawn roll and bean curd were all good, just that the drink was too sweet and the prawn dumpling skin was falling apart. Other than that, would recommend those looking for Chinese zhi char.
author: Kenneth Goh

review_text:
We ordered the 2 for $48 chilli crabs promo. Crab meat was fresh and firm and the chilli sauce delicious. We also ordered the set for 2 pax with a choice of 3 dishes (we chose salted egg chicken, trio egg spinach and cai poh tofu) and an additional sweet and sour fish. All these were enough for 6 adults. I didn't like the salted egg chicken, felt it was oily and too much batter, very little chicken. Cai poh tofu was very salty. So ate tofu without the cai poh. Crabs good & the other dishes were ok.
We had dinner on a Saturday at 5pm. The restaurant was empty and service was fast and attentive. Uncle was very patient in explaining their membership promo which we did not sign up for.
author: Avril Teo

review_text: Food taste okay and seems freshly cooked ones not pre cooked ones. Honestly price a bit emmm… Coz don’t find the service’s fee goes to… the bill ends up with a 10% service fee a bit shocked lah, am I having a Michelin restaurant ==
author: Annie & Carrot

review_text: Curry fish head and salted egg pork ribs are good. If they keep it up this stand and the price, I think will have more customers come over for dinning.
author: Rosalind Tan

review_text: Absolutely love Smol! The food is always incredibly fresh, healthy and consistently high quality. You can really taste the care that goes into every dish. The staff are super friendly and welcoming which makes the whole experience even better. I always leave feeling energised and genuinely good after eating here. So grateful to have a spot like this! Highly recommend!
author: Kai Xin Khoo

review_text: Glad they moved to have a whole unit with indoor and outdoor seating from PLQ mall. Food was a hit as I last remembered it from 2024, with delicious protein packed options for your gains. Now comes with a loyalty membership.
author: Isabelle Koh

review_text:
smol’s been a favourite haunt of mine to get healthy and delicious  protein bowls since they were at PLQ1. They’ve relocated a few blocks away, to PLQ Parkside now, to a bigger and brighter unit.

I love that their menus are flexible and allow for you to build your own bowls. Price is very affordable for the quality served.

Macros wise, they could be a little more transparent with the breakdown of each item. There’s a table for the breakdown of macros for proteins, not the base, supplements and toppings, so if you’re looking to track macros/calories, it might be easier to order the best sellers.

The best thing about smol is definitely the staff. They are always cheerful and make you feel at home. Janu, especially is always there to greet you with a smile,  and I’m amazed at how they remember all their regulars. Right down to which gym you are with.

Also love that it’s a woman-owned business and supports various minority groups.
author: Jo T

review_text: Food was tasteless, bland. Almost no seasoning for the beef. Rice was too wet. Broccoli tastes ‘raw’. Only positive was the beef was tender and not overcooked. Disappointed with the lack of flavour given the price point.
author: Wei Wen L

review_text: Tried the fun with black (tofu) during their $6 promo, though I initially wanted the salmon one, I was informed that it was sold out. I was pleasantly surprised by the big portion size. The taste was also not bad, the tofu had more flavour than expected, though the dressing didn't really suit my palate. I still think I would probably prefer some form of meat as the protein, so I'd probably go for other options if I'm back again. Not sure if I'd purchase this at their usual prices though, as they are quite steep.
author: GG K

review_text: Food was better years ago when it was the old shop. There were many orders and the guy in front was very busy. Ordering through the QR code pasted on the table was convenient but I did not know that the number being called was the table number and not the queue number! I was waiting so long, even the counter guy who saw me looking and waiting at my table while the food was on their counter, did not bother to call for me. Ended up my noodles were clumpy and did not taste good. Coffee was realllyyy sub-par, tasted like 3in1 packet. fried shrimp dumplings filling was not seasoned well too. Tasted better at many other places.
author: J Low

review_text:
I ordered Ban Mee soup. Quite a generous Portion. Smooth noodles & nice poached eggs. Like the veg Soup based ikan bilis. There's Chilli & pepper powder on table . Can imagine dry one should be nice too.
Can order via qr code at table, pay at counter paynow. Serves food to table
author: Cha “Cha Ye” Ye

review_text:
I like the fish ball soup with bee hoon kway.

The fish balls are delicious and do not have the fishy taste.

Bee hoon kway is very smooth.

On my second visit, I tried combo ban mee. It includes three fish balls, three fish dumplings, two meat balls and onsen egg. All the ingredients are of high quality and are very delicious.
author: Fairy

review_text:
The taste of the ban mee here is quite good, especially when paired with their signature chili. If you're a chili lover, this place might just be your kind of heaven. One great thing is that you can customize the spice level by adding as much (or as little) chili as you like, perfect for those who enjoy a bit of control over their heat.

The portion size is on the smaller side, especially considering the price point. It might not be the most filling meal if you're really hungry. Another downside is the ventilation, since they also serve mookata, the space can get a little stuffy.
author: Neo Zi Xin

review_text: Not quite like KL but decent enough for a tasty meal. The additional Thai garlic chicken goes well with the al dente noodles. Crispy prawn dumplings and ngoh hiang were average. Soup not very nice though. The star of the show here is definitely all the 3 superb chili sauces that completely elevated everything it touches. Powerful stuff. Shiok.
author: Case Woo

review_text: Convenient location and food is reasonably priced and quite filling. Just pay a little for some side dishes. For the prawn hotpot, can ask them to separate the fries if you dont like soggy fries. The side dishes are good to complement the hotpot. Can refill the soup too, will go again to try other flavours.
author: YF

review_text:
Chicken Hotpot offers a fun and dual-concept dining experience that starts as a rich claypot dish and ends as a mini steamboat.

We ordered the 2 mini pot, chicken and fish.

Taste wise good
Pot size mini, have to keep top up the soup, hard to cook the Maggie noodle, have to break it.
author: Hary Luo

review_text: Tender chicken and savory sauce! Not too salty and few MSG thirst. Staffs are warm and considerate! I left my headphones there. When I went back to check a few days later, I found that they had been well taken care of, so warm..:)
author: Joyance Jiang

review_text: Good family package of $60 for 2 big chicken & fish or prawn pots + 4 drinks. The portion was too big for 2A2C. Kids who were trying this for first time could not get used to the taste. Do not like the type of Fish they use inside 酸菜汤 (feels like tasteless fish fillets) but overall good value of money.
author: Shermaine Wee

review_text:
CHICKEN HOTPOT 鸡公煲
☆☆☆☆☆

Tender chicken served on the bone in a pot of famous soup. Choose from three levels of spiciness and add as many fresh vegetables and additional meats as you wish. And keep eating, the more you eat, the more flavourful the experience.

We choose the SMALL spicy.

This has to be one of the best tasting hotpot for me!
The soup is flavourful and you will never get enough with the numerous top up of the soup!
The soup goes so well with rice!
You can even finish a bowl of rice just with the soup!

We can also order ingredients to go with the Chicken Pot.
We ordered some quail eggs, spinach, enoki mushrooms.

FISH IN A POT 酸菜鱼
☆☆☆☆☆

Catch of the day (Snapper or Grouper) specially marinated and cut into fillet strips. Served in a simmered broth of preserved picked vegetables.

Generous servings of fish slices and the soup is as equally flavourful too!

Overall 4.8 / 5

3 to 3.5 - save the calories cos bo ho jiak
to 4 - can try if no queue cos ay sai lah
4 to 4.5 - highly recommended cos ho jiak
4.6 to 5 - Must Try cos jin ho jiak! Mai Tu Liao!

However, I felt a bit unfairly treated. Even though I arrived first, the server attended to other customers who came later, possibly because they knew each other. It doesn’t feel good when you’re waiting, but someone who comes after you gets served first.

review_text:
The food were generally acceptable.

The eatery is generous with the vegetables and carbohydrates. Proteins? Quite skimpy.

The lamb rack was pathetically little. A huge contract from what was seen on the menu.

The BBQ stuff like lamb skew, chive, golden mushroom and egg plants were fantastic. Savoury and flavourful.

The noodles in mala and gravy version, were above average. The noodles was al-Dante and the flavouring was acceptable.

The sweet and sour pork is cooked with maltose and the meat was extremely crunchy. A little too sweets

But the ambience was really bad - air con was non existent and customers were smoking inside. Might consider a return if we are nearby but definitely not making a trip to forest city just for this.

review_text: We stayed in Regalia Park Forest City for a relaxing weekend and base to visit JB. We ate three dinners in a row and very happy with the spicy food! Cool funky place and fun and lively. Boss and family staff are very chill. I could order my favorite Szechuan dishes and they were very authentic and delicious!
