review_text: The experience was quite mixed. The food was excellent, with most dishes being enjoyable. However, the ambiance left much to be desired; the lack of air conditioning and indoor smoking by customers were significant drawbacks.

review_text: Best place to dine in Forest City. Their BBQ lamb is my favourite.
author: Edmund Chan

review_text:
Restaurant CGP is open 24 hours, which is very convenient, and they have many staff working, so you would expect the service to be fast. However, the service is still quite slow, especially when it gets busy. Even so, the taste of the food is quite nice, and we enjoyed most of the dishes.

One thing we were not satisfied with is the Nasi Goreng Pattaya. It came with only egg and rice, nothing else inside, so it felt incomplete for the price.

But what truly stood out was the old staff wearing a cap, as shown in the photo. He was very polite, very kind, and extremely respectful. Even though he is older, he has better manners and attitude than many younger staff. It made us really happy to be served by him, and he gave a very positive impression of the restaurant.

The environment and seating here are surprisingly good, almost like 5-star seating. The chairs and layout feel very high class compared to other mamak-style restaurants nearby. It’s a nice place to chill, relax, and have a meal.

I really hope they can maintain the quality of the seating and environment over time, because it’s one of the things that makes CGP stand out.

✨ Overall: Nice taste, beautiful seating, slow service, but one very polite staff who made our visit meaningful.

author: Yves Burri

review_text:
Raffles Marina used to be a vibrant, safe, and well-managed place. Since YCL took over and installed a weak CEO, it’s all cost-cutting, with no reinvestment.
The bowling alley is gone. The Discovery Pub is always closed. The bistro now serves only Western food, with Chinese rarely available, after the Indian chef was fired. The squash court, gym, snooker room, and tennis courts are all deteriorating. Members are improvising just to salvage some activities.
All sailing activities for 2026 have been canceled. Regattas, championships, and community events that once made this marina thrive are gone.
Security is down to two people. Non-members roam freely, even in the swimming pool, and standards have collapsed — people were washing their feet in the hotel lobby pond.
The staff below the CEO, however, are outstanding. They are working tirelessly to stop the decline, but it’s a battle they cannot win alone — hats off to them, truly great people.

YCL’s relentless cost-cutting, combined with a powerless CEO, is destroying what was once a great marina. Without serious investment, safety and quality will continue to slide
author: Rudi Johnson

review_text:

author: CP

review_text:
Went during Christmas and surprisingly it wasn't too crowded and we reserved a table just the day before! Go there earlier to get seats nearer to the wharf so that y'all can get a clear view of sunset 😜

The food was better than expected (we read reviews and alot of people were commenting that the food's average but we thought otherwise) but of course, it's a little pricey ($19.80 before gst and service charge for a plate of pork chop and $20.80 for a plate of fish and chips. Thankfully the food portion was pretty huge! The fish felt firm and is not your cheap mushy type and they give you 3 pieces of it. The pork chop wasn't dry nor too hard on the teeth and there were 2 huge pieces so I think it'll be good for sharing too!

It's semi-outdoors so maybe spray some insect repellent. The furniture's kind of old as well so don't expect a posh environment but it's like those retro diner places where it's not easy to find in Singapore anymore and moreover, the view's great 😃👍
author: kopiandmilktea

review_text:
Staff was friendly and the view is amazing - catch it at sunset. However, the food is not worth the drive here. We had the Laksa and Black Olive Dancing Fried Rice; both are signatures. The laksa was rich and creamy, save for the stray piece of shell that I bit too hard into.

The fried rice, however, failed to meet expectations, especially considering it was more expensive than the laksa. I mean, we live in a country where fried rice is everywhere, so if you must charge $20 for it, it had better be amazing - no, perfect. There was a hint of olive, and a hint of wok hey. But, other than that, what else justifies the price? The presentation, too, was non-existent. It’s mind-boggling that something so basic can be done so wrong.

Other than the fried rice, I’d say do pay a visit for the atmosphere, but please order something else.

author: Pascal XXX

review_text:
disclaimer: they’re a little understaffed, so service and food may be slower for this place. I don’t mind as I like to take my time with food!

Wonderful place to have dinner at - the sunset views are stunning at the correct hour.

Fish maw soup: Very balanced. Just the right saltiness and texture. Have a little sip first before adding in (just a little bit of!) vinegar and pepper to taste the difference.

Stir fried scallops with asparagus in truffle: interestingly good! In many dishes I’ve had, the truffle taste is stronger (and after a while it gets overpowering), but in this dish it was just a hint - a really delicate highlight to compliment the dish as a whole. Asparagus texture was just right - easy to chew but not too crunchy.

Stir fried kurobuta (black pork) in black pepper sauce: very tender!

Peking duck: must order in advance! Make a reservation and order in advance due to the preparation the kitchen must make prior to the meal. I really love the “pastry” they use to wrap the skin for the meal, it’s thin and fragrant. They’ll serve it half with cucumber and half with spring onion. For the second round, you can choose to have it one out of several ways (if I remember correctly : fried rice, stir fried with e-mian, salt and pepper stir fried, ginger/garlic and onion stir fry, or just chopped up and served).

Mango and pomelo was nice and fragrant, not too thick but also not too watery.

Deep fried Red bean pancake: MUST ORDER. Can’t stress this enough; this was actually so good. Exterior was wonderfully crispy without being too oily, and the red bean paste in the middle was fragrant and delicious. Got a “not too sweet” of approval from family members! (ps: you should probably order this dessert slightly ahead of time, not at the end of the meal but maybe before your second last or last dish arrives since it takes time to prepare by hand.)

Star of the whole meal was service staff Simon, who also did the table side Peking duck serving. Very charismatic and charming. Will definitely come back again!

Total was around 300+ for 5 people.

(Do ask them for parking ticket discount coupon if you’re dining in without membership. Gives a 4 dollar discount, equivalent to two hours of parking I think!)

review_text: was initially in a good mood. wanted some sweet tasty ice cream to beat the heat. waited 44 mins for 2 ice creams. staff claimed it was normal to wait 20+ minutes, told me that I should have just told them I was ordering ice creams. BLAMING THE CUSTOMER IS CRAZY IM SO FED UP LITERALLY JUST DO YOUR JOB PROPERLY AND CHECK THE ORDER??????????? there was No order number display big enough for people sitting and waiting to see the next order number. the staff said she called my order number twice but how am i supposed to hear that????????? literally if im gonna have to wait so long u CANT blame me for going to sit down and do other things 🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩🫩 TIME IS MONEY WHO DO U THINK U ARE!!!!!!! and the place is SO DISORGANISED. all the order numbers are jumbled and not in order????? how is that fair to customers when they cant receive their food  in the order they ordered it? ????????? SO DAMN LOUSY IF I COULD PUT NEGATIVE STARS I FREAKING WOULD. WORST SERVICE EVER. HOW CAN $2.30 WORTH OF ICE CREAM COST ME A FURTHER 44 MINS OF MY PRECIOUS TIME.
author: cherry

review_text: Long queue and clearly they need more manpower and be organised. Ordered McCrispy and instead of thigh and drumstick got two drumsticks instead. Have to remind the staff that I ordered a McFlurry as well.
author: zy

review_text: It's always fast and fresh. But I wish the fries were crispier.
author: west Mac

review_text: Very good service. Staff are very helpful and sincere. This outlet is spacious with friendly and lively vibes. One of the best McDonald's branches in SG.
author: Chen Wan Ting

review_text:
Horrible outlet with rude staff. Very disorganised. The queue numbers on the screen are only there for show.

I ordered my food, stood in front of the counter, and watched the staff preparing lots of mobile orders. I saw my order number under “Now Preparing” on the queue screen so I waited. Then it disappeared. It was not under “Serving”, and no one had called my number (which I do not even understand since isn’t the point of the screen is so no numbers need to be called)?

So I approached this male staff at the counter and asked if my order was ready since the number was not on the screen. He glanced at my receipt and said rudely and sarcastically, “Ma’am please wait it has only been 3 minutes”. Even had the cheek to glare. I tried telling him that I ONLY asked because my number had disappeared from the screen and he replied loudly and impatiently, “I will call the number when it is ready” - as if I am supposed to be familiar with their messed up system. So much for the screen alert advising you to “Please watch here for your number”.

The patty on the cheeseburger was too salty, and the ice in my drink was already half melted.

Based on the reviews I’ve seen here, McDonald’s should do something about the staff and system at this outlet.
author: Samantha

restaurant_name: Good Fortune Seafood 福满海鲜
review_text: Slightly on the salty side. Dishes r quite unique and taste not bad. Nett price. Pork rib can be softer and chicken can be in bigger piece. Lots of seats.
author: Loo Zheng Rong

restaurant_name: Good Fortune Seafood 福满海鲜
review_text: For 5 people the small portion should be enough.The seafood hor fun was very good.love the cereal prawns most as very fresh and meaty.Prawn Paste chicken wings were a bit smaller size though.if one order the Chili Crab then prepare to pay a lot more.
author: teck huay lim

restaurant_name: Good Fortune Seafood 福满海鲜
review_text: Ordered fried Kuey teow with chicken cube. Regrettable. The chicken is hard. Looked like has been fried , kept inside fridge and refried. Flavour of kway teow not up to standard. Cashier girl asked me to sit and wait. Don’t bother to ask me what chilli type I want. After telling her the food was served without the chilli. Still want to ask me to go back table and wait for chilli? lol I went to take myself.. Better improve your service and manpower . They looked too stressed . Not recommended food and service. Will never come back for sure.
author: Calvin Tan

restaurant_name: Good Fortune Seafood 福满海鲜
review_text: Price reasonable , taste doable, vibe makable
author: Mcenroe ng teow ee

restaurant_name: Good Fortune Seafood 福满海鲜
review_text:
Tried this Zi Char stall at Jurong West last night, and I was impressed! The Hor Fun stood out the most—smooth texture with a strong wok hei that really elevated the dish. Also ordered prawn paste chicken, broccoli with Bai Ling gu, four-season beans, and prawn-stuffed beancurd (all in small). All dishes came hot and fresh, and the flavors were on point. The total bill was around $66.

The only downside was the dining environment—it was quite humid as there were no fans around, and last night was particularly still with no wind. Otherwise, a solid Zi Char spot worth checking out! Will be back for the Hor Fun again.
author: Pauline Wee

review_text:
New Western Food in NTU. Chicken chop is their best seller🥰 today  I had late lunch the Grilled fish with brown sauce free 2 sides fries & mashed potatoes 🥔 and the ice milo very nice
My fren had the aglio E olio pasta with bacon.
author: Jeanie Lee

review_text: Had a Double Chicken Chop with black pepper sauce for $12.50. it's quite value for money in the university. Food wise can't compare to real deal cafe but it's okay.
author: Jacksonfoong Foong

review_text: fast and good food, very reasonable price. Fried rice is especially good
author: Amberlie Yap

review_text: amazing food at an affordable price!! one of the best chicken chops in town
author: Ruo Lin

review_text:
Try the fried rice, it is a must.

The chicken chop is amazing, very filling.
author: Kwong Kok Zeng

restaurant_name: Yew Kee Specialities @ NTU North Spine Plaza
review_text: Standalone store at North spine beside crowded bowl (the landmark on google maps is wrong). Was originally from south spine. It’s combined with a chicha store. Service wised, it’s very crowded during peak hours from 11am-2pm. No seats and long queue. Only can order with machine. Since it’s very crowded, the staffs feel very irritated and short fused and will just shout at you. Food wise, tastes like other outlets. Recommend you come during off peak hours for better service and seats.
author: Truth Fairy

restaurant_name: Yew Kee Specialities @ NTU North Spine Plaza
review_text:
Takes 15 minutes to prepare a simple duck rice dish with nobody in the stall

Don’t bother if you’re in a rush
author: brad _

restaurant_name: Yew Kee Specialities @ NTU North Spine Plaza
review_text: Rice is the wet kind, really satisfying. Cheapest set starts at 3.50
author: Jin Wen Thai Low

restaurant_name: Yew Kee Specialities @ NTU North Spine Plaza
review_text: No point getting the specialty. The side is quite pathetic. The amount of peanut is so little that I can count it and is is only 4 peanuts. The strand of veg is so little and same too I can count on it. Feel disappointed that you kee has become like this.
author: Oh Yu Rong Jeffrey

restaurant_name: Yew Kee Specialities @ NTU North Spine Plaza
review_text: Food is good and cheap, staff is very friendly! I always come here to eat.
author: Lawrence

restaurant_name: Fu Xiang Seafood 富香海鲜
review_text: Put off ordering seafood white beehoon but given DIRTY end stalks of vegetables that I wouldn't even feed my pet rabbit with. Disgusting if authorities hasn't come checking on quality of food for good money we pay for. Woman quote different price from menu and had to correct her. Served without any kind of chilli but have to ask and still give wrong type. No words when it's empty in the afternoon lunchtime afternoon.
author: SuzseQ “RedDotter” Ng

restaurant_name: Fu Xiang Seafood 富香海鲜
review_text:
THANK YOU for the amazing catering experience. Have been patronizing this stall for few years now and decided to approach them to cater lunch for my baby’s birthday. We were honored to be their first catering customer, all the setup was done professionally, food served was amazing as usual, and my guests were all raving about their food.

Highly recommend their Mongolian pork, salted egg french beans, cereal prawns (SUPER fresh)

The lady boss is always so kind and friendly, will definitely be catering from them for future parties 💯
author: Suzanne Tan

restaurant_name: Fu Xiang Seafood 富香海鲜
review_text:
My family all time dinner option.. We are staying nearby so easily one week twice ordered our dinner from them. Fast and nice food ,even there's lots of ppl their service is still quite fast waiting time about 10 to 20mins or sometimes lesser.
My daughter's favorite cereal prawn ball , prawn paste chicken and slice fish beehoon soup.
author: Jocelyn Quek

restaurant_name: Fu Xiang Seafood 富香海鲜
review_text: Well done and nice zhi char.. Ordered the lala soup, fried squid and salted egg bittergourd& pumpkin. Lala soup is herbal type... Shiok... The fried squid is those large type.. Crispy outside soft and chewy inside. The best is the salted egg b&p... Will come back again to try other dishes.
author: ericchia23

restaurant_name: Fu Xiang Seafood 富香海鲜
review_text: 5.50 for a dry fried horfun with only beansprouts and egg, real messed up. Go to the Indian shop or buy buns from the coffee shop instead to get actual meat and feel full
author: bakedsquirrel

restaurant_name: A & I Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text: Top 3 best chicken rice in Singapore I ever tried. Even the white chicken breast is so tender. The skin melts in the mouth. Juicy. Rice is cooked just right pretty big bowl. My white chicken breast + roast drum stick with rice is only $7.00. Expect long queues taking away 10 packs for home, schools and factories nearby. 9:30am come already very busy shop. Ample parking as pretty tuck away in the far west of Singapore.
author: Asia Apparel

restaurant_name: A & I Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text: Chicken is fresh and rice is well cooked. Char siew is average. Service is average. Place is clean enough.
author: Alicia Hock

restaurant_name: A & I Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text:
Ordered half steamed, half roasted chicken ($14 each). Not bad at all, chicken was tasty and tender. Portion size is super generous compared to most places, maybe because they use bigger chickens? Even the rice they give is a lot.

Price is really decent, quite rare to find this kind of value nowadays.

The auntie might seem a bit grumpy at first, but she’s actually really nice. I asked to change one half to roasted, and she helped check if there was any ready at the back, had to walk all the way around the stall to do it too.

Just note: cash only. I almost didn’t have enough, but managed to scrape through lol.
author: Melvin J.

restaurant_name: A & I Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text:
Extremely tender chicken with really legit chilli. Soup was nicely seasoned and the salted veg and chicken broth is a nice additional to the meal. We arrived at 11.15am and didn’t have to wait, but there was a constant queue after 11.30am. Line moved pretty fast though.

Note that this place is cash only.
author: SH K

restaurant_name: A & I Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text:
Read pretty good reviews about the chicken rice, and as was in the vicinity, decided to takeaway half steamed chicken and half roasted chicken with 4 packets of rice for the family.

The rice was very fragrant and I can smell its aroma in the car even though I put the rice in the boot.  They were generous with the chili and soy sauce.  However, I find the chili too spicy for my liking but the 'sweet' soy sauce is good enough for me.  We were pleasantly surprised that the roast chicken was so tender and juicy.  I haven't eaten roast chicken for a very long time because among the many stalls that I have tried, the roasted chicken tends to be dry, so naturally I'm impressed with this roasted chicken. The steamed chicken is equally tender and some collagen can be seen nicely coagulated on some of the pieces. However, it can be observed that at the bottom of the box, some of the chicken blood has mixed with the chicken juices and leaving a reddish liquid at bottom of the box with the cut chicken in it and that sort of affected my appetite.

But overall, I love the rice and the roasted chicken very much. I will definitely come back for it again! However, expect to queue for a bit though.
author: FIVE-A-DAY

review_text: Best Hainan chicken you can find in the world. From famous local family farmed chicken with succulent juicy tender yet firm meat, and soaked to perfection. The rice cooked in chicken broth that kept all the essence of the chicken, can't help thinking about a second serving...
author: Victor Chao

review_text:
Super good have been over 30 years last time at
966 now 907 believe me must try 👍
author: Andy Tan

review_text: very nice chicken rice. my breakfast everyday
author: Patrick Wan

review_text:
This is a chicken rice specialty restaurant, or rather just a pho bar, but unless you line up from around 11:30am there's no guarantee you'll be able to eat there; it closes when stock runs out.
The chicken is incredibly delicious (the rice is average), and perhaps it's spread by word of mouth, as the number of customers seems to be increasing every time I go. The mustard is also delicious; I wish they would sell just that.
It's astonishing to see so many people flocking to this off-the-beaten-path location, which to be honest is difficult to get to even for the first or second time.

Chicken rice is a culture.
author: K M

review_text: Delicious chicken rice! It's always packed at lunchtime! Arrive early or call ahead to order!
author: Thew Guat Hoon

review_text: Food was acceptable. Taste is not bad actually. But really disappointed with how the staff is. Went to get my food when it was ready but staff was too busy to see my reciept. So I left it in the receipt tray and collected my food. Staff suddenly ask to check my number in a rather rude manner. Eh. You think I nothing do, come and steal food? Or you think I poor, cannot afford ah. Want to see transaction again? This is unacceptable. Other food establishments don't react that way.  Also there was no container for chilli sauce. When I asked for it. He passed me a stack. I took one and he raised his voice at me, semmingly ordering me to place it all at the chilli sauce receptical area. Does he really think I am his colleague?! Pls don't work in F&B if you can't handle stress.
author: Lim Andre

review_text: The food is pretty nice and average filling for the price. Wok express allows you to pick your ingredients but if you do not know what you want, you can always order from their pre-select menu. The shop has dine in and the vibes are ok but the fried smell from the kitchen and the aircon don't really make you want to seat there for long. Worth a visit for those who need a quick convenient lunch in a box that's not fast food 😆
author: Nick

review_text: Portion is too little for the price. $7 for a set of fried rice with 2 meat 1 vege 1 egg but it's not even filling. Food doesn't taste good either.
author: CheShin Chew

review_text: Taste is really bland and egg was over cooked. $7 for the small serving. Place wasn't well cleaned and have a lot of flies around
author: Joshua Loh

review_text:
Wok Hei strong here.
Fried rice is nice.
May be dry so do add eggs.
Its a Yum. Get their XO for more flavours.
Many people queue so please have patience.
author: Yang

review_text: Sorry if we have different taste but I love their nasi lemak so muchhh!!!🫶🏻🫶🏻🫶🏻 it was tasty, the spices didn’t overpower the whole dish, the coconut cream (santan) was cooked well, the oil blended well. They cooked properly really! But i feel like it would be better if they added herbs into the rice coz it was not fragrant as it supposed to be. I wish the chili paste would be spicier as well, but it was okay tho.
author: Annisaa Hayya Arundati

review_text:
Cafe inside NTU campus.  Cafe deco and ordering system looks interesting among the usual fastfood
option in the same dining hall.  Food serving was rather large on the carbo but unfortunately taste was below expectation. Kolo noodle fried dumpling was quite tough.  Nasi lemak lack the fragrance and curry chicken also seemed tough. Milk tea and chendol were better. Relatively value for money dinner but as the dining hall has no aircon it is rather warm even on evening.
author: Ken Tan

review_text:
First time here. Last time also la.

Food: Ordered the signature curry and nasi lemak. What a big letdown really. The curry is very watery, and the nasi lemak really so so only le. The rice totally no flavor, machiam white rice and the ikan billis and peanut so little like feeding ants. OMG the expectation totally don't match at all. Kopi peng similar to your kopitiam standard. Really not worth the price tag. How can, and they are supposed to be famous with their nasi lemak right? Taste worse than Ananas.

Service: What service really, all self service le. And hor, supposed to have credit card payment on their screen. However when you tap on their kiosk, it is just qr scan payment... Seriously... Why bother having other payment mode when you don't support it in the first place.

Skip this, kopitiam kopi and Ananas so much better.
author: Ken Peh

review_text:
Not the best thing, but not as bad as what others say. Perhaps my review is a bit biased since most of the negative reviews came from those who ordered the toast sets and so far I haven't tried that one just yet.

The noodle set (kolo mee?) was cheap (if my fuzzy memory serves me right, around $4?) and tasted alright. The portion might be a bit too small for hyperactive uni students though. The nasi lemak was pretty mediocre relative to the price (somewhat north of $5) - too little of everything but the rice for the price.
author: lontongstroong

review_text: One star.  Avoid this place. The curry chicken was bland, the chicken itself tasteless. The egg in the nasi lemak was stale, with an enlarged yolk indicating it was old.  The rice was just plain, lacking any flavor.  The only redeeming quality was the kacang nuts.  The photo shows what I left off without eating much. Disposal quality in my opinion. I would not recommend this to anyone.
author: Klair T

review_text:
Halal Food. The food is good, and you can add $4 for a set that includes an additional soup and drink. The normal set costs $12.90. The staff mentioned that NTU has its own menu, which is different from other branches.

For the main course, I highly recommend the salmon (an additional $2). It is much meatier and more flavorful than at other places in NTU, but it tends to run out quickly. The sides (2 out of 3 from french fries, broccoli and corns) are served in large portions. For the soup, the mushroom soup is the safest option; tomato soup could be sour to some; pumpkin soup could be weird to some. The tea is freshly made on the day itself.

The staff are very friendly and patient, willing to answer any questions you have about choosing your meal or the free membership.

Regarding membership, you can collect points but cannot use vouchers because the prices are lower than at other branches.
author: Jerry

review_text: Ordered the set with 1 main, 1 soup and 1 drink. Main comes with 2 sides; either fries, pasta, broccoli or one more option (can’t remember). The pasta is truffle based (30 cents extra), the taste is great, strong truffle taste, the pasta is well cooked as well. Salmon is small portion but the tenderness was just nice, won’t crumble into pieces and not too tough. Spent 30 cents to change to mushroom soup but felt like the soup can be better. Felt that the soup was slightly watery that day.
author: Raine

review_text: I ordered their hot meal seat $12.90, took the chicken lasagna, roasted pumpkin soup with drink. The food is warm, the drink is cold just like what it’s supposed to. Will definitely have to come back for the food.
author: Nor Hafizah Abd Hamid

review_text:
Super hot meal @$12.90 is a good option for  lunch that come with a main dish,a soup of the day and a drink. Fried chicken wing is nice.
Place is quiet and cozy, not very crowded.
Staff is friendly.
author: Kris Ng

review_text:
Being a grad student at NTU, I have at least 3-4 meals in a month here at The Soup spoon. Being a vegetarian I mostly stick to the meatless minestrone soup. I do miss the wraps option they use to have earlier. I do like their salad,pretty simple. Wish they could increase the serving quantity slightly though. This outlet is priced lesser than the outlets outside NTU. So make the most of it.
I was also wondering if they can serve the drinks in non plastic containers when one is not taking away the drinks.
author: Chinmayi Prasanna

review_text:
date of visit: 2025-11-10 mon

spicy pork bimbimbap - taste great!

tteokbokki - sauce v diluted, quite bland

tofu soup - taste great!
author: M Yeo

review_text:
MUST TRY!!!

So far the best and relatively more authentic Korean delights inside the campus.

Service is good — the aunties are welcoming. The chicken bibimbap and the spicy chicken soup are highly recommended. I usually buy either one of these. Fried chicken is also gd if you’re looking for snacks. Plus one point for the clean environment.
author: Nomt Narmandakh

review_text: It's a hit or miss really. I had pretty decent bibimbap here before and I quite like the fried dumpling and rice cake. However, today I had a lunch set with sad looking veg noodles and grossly soggy rice cake. I wasn't even asked what sides I would like for my set and the staff was rather curt throughout the communication we had. When I was here a year or 2 ago, service was pretty good!
author: L X

review_text: I am a Paik Bibim fan and had visited every Paul Bibim branch in Singapore. NTU branch is always the best one to visit. It is so much better than many other branch. The food is very nice and so fresh! The staff are all very friendly and always provide very good service!
author: Benson

review_text: Reasonable food quality, noting how I can see food preparation being monotonous and standardised across orders. I liked their iced coffee, though I find their fried chicken a tad too hard.
author: Nobita C

review_text:
Nice noodle dishes from a part of China that is near North Korea. Ordering is easier if your Mandarin is better though.

Beef noodles with mushroom soup: 7/10. A bit salty, but the portion is decent.
author: Zachary Lee

review_text: Nice noodles restaurant. For a bowl of cold or hot noodles. Portion has reduce though.
author: Margaret Ang

review_text: I used to like this restaurant and went there for 10 plus times. However, the new waitress there wearing glasses is basically a fierce monster that yells at everyone ordering there with least politeness and patience. She acted as if everyone owes her 1 million or what. I wish her a very unpleasant future. Will tell friends never eat there again because of her.
author: Kaka 3120

review_text: Beware if you’re paying in cash the balance returned might be torn notes, and the waitress refuses to exchange it (saying it’s inconvenient to open the cash register) if you cannot notice it on the spot. It’s unbelievable this could be happened in SG school canteen.
author: Yu Qing Song

review_text: Must try at NTU. Life changing experience.
author: Kim Seng Tan

review_text:
always my go-to in NTU, loved their scrambled eggs and the protein balls are good. however i do recommend frying with lesser oil as it defeats the purpose of advertising as a salad place (supposedly to be healthy) but the oil used to cooked the dishes are …. plenty.

the younger servers are just meh, the portion they give is really less. But the sweet auntie that have been working there since 3 years ago?? Really nice and friendly! Portion she give is good too.

just that the price kept increasing hais.
author: i love food

review_text:
Not a bad healthy option. It says $4.90 on the board + $0.30 for takeaway, and mine was $6.90. Not sure where that price came from.
The vegetables taste fresh. The lettuce is just romain so nothing too substantial. The rice is a bit oily.
The tofu was good but there wasn’t much of it added.
You choose a few sides and a main. The base is salad and rice or pasta. I think that’s how it works…
No credit but they take cash.

If you’re looking for a healthy option on campus with lots of vegetables, try the Yong Tau Foo in south spine (fine foods).
author: Cass

review_text: Tried The crowded bowl many times from other outlets Biopolis, RP, NCCS food court were of good experiences. Heard that NTU has one outlet and decided to give it a try. Pasta was salty, food so so. Broccoli look overcooked. Service need to be improved. staff look like I owe them million. I am totally fine that you charged me for the take away bowl. But you charged me a normal hawker centre takeaway transparent plastic bag for $0.20 when I mentioned take away. What a rip off. I don’t remember your other outlets charged for plastic bag. Even Starbucks coffee charges their paperbag with logo for $0.10…
author: Tina

review_text:
Mains like olive rice, chickpeas, pumpkins and potato salad are available. Dressings include sesame and [balsamic?] vinegar. They also have a couple of tofu\mockmeat options. The scrambled eggs go great with all of these.

My favourite part is that I felt great after eating this meal. Very natural and soothing meal. Thanks to the owners!
author: Shamima Banu

review_text: Fml the price increase like no tomorrow. Inflation rate 10%… few years ago, it was $4.5 for small bowl, now it’s $4.9. The staffs here are also not very generous with their portion. Lunch time queue waiting time can get up to 30mins. Take away add $0.3. I would recommend to just get the eat in bowl if you are going to seat somewhere near northspine.
author: Truth Fairy

restaurant_name: Bottle tree cafe restaurant by sembawang eating house seafood restaurant
review_text:
Ordered an ice Milo from the self-order kiosk at 4:10pm and no movement for a prolong period. No one was making drinks and two chefs in the kitchen ignored my ringing of the bell at the counter. Also spied a fried rice on the table that has been there since I arrived at the cafe and no one serving. Terrible service.

A second customer also experienced the same thing. The cafe only had 3 customers all trying to order food.

Only got my drink at 4:50pm when a staff passingly went to the counter. Discovery Centre needs to do better than to have a cafe with no service to customers.
author: MatthiasTay

restaurant_name: Bottle tree cafe restaurant by sembawang eating house seafood restaurant
review_text:
A decent local cuisine that is halal. It is located at Singapore Discovery Centre itself.

Pretty alright for it's affordable price, nothing to complain about.
author: Mohammad Fathullah

restaurant_name: Bottle tree cafe restaurant by sembawang eating house seafood restaurant
review_text:
The signature pan fried bee hoon is good!
The dining environment is also very cool and breezy..
Price is reasonable..
Worth dining here
author: Food lover

restaurant_name: Bottle tree cafe restaurant by sembawang eating house seafood restaurant
review_text:
Literally the ONLY place for food and drinks in Singapore Discovery Centre. SDC truly felt like a relic from the past, hardly anyone drop by to this place and also the marketing of this place seems to have been on cheap movies $10/pax with no other push.

However, despite this I still enjoyed my time at SDC and had fond memories here. 3 stars rating for my salted egg chicken because the food came cold…
author: Jie Ying

restaurant_name: Bottle tree cafe restaurant by sembawang eating house seafood restaurant
review_text:
The best cafe ever had in SDC. Didn’t even realise it is halal until my wife told me. Tasted just like any Zi Char stall outside.

But the down side is to enjoy the 10% member discount, need to order over the counter. Self service kiosk doesn’t support member discount
author: Donny Yong

review_text: Medium steak was ordered. It came medium well. Requested for steak to be redone. Cane back medium well. Chef was insistent it was medium. Do order rare if you need your steak medium.
author: Kevin Chai

review_text: Absolutely love PEN & INC NTU Cafe & Bar! The vibe is cozy and stylish, perfect for studying, catching up with friends, or just relaxing. The food is delicious – their pasta and snacks are always on point, and the drinks selection is great too. Staff are super friendly and attentive, making every visit enjoyable. Definitely my go-to spot on campus!
author: Lotus keye Dy

review_text:
Hidden Gem at the far end of SG found in NTU, very chill and simple place to enjoy food 😀

Ordered items: Peach lemonade (tad sweet more like mango), truffle fries - chunky and serving is enough for sharing, salmon mentaiko - best item ordered!
author: Nagamie KusaKo

review_text: The ambience was cosy, and suitable for couples and families. The menu offers a variety of dishes that are very interesting - such as the Salted Egg Fish & Chips, which we ordered. The Salted Egg sauce completed the dish very well! Seafood Marinara was delicious as well but the Mexican brownie stole the show. It was very chewy and rich, which went very well with the ice cream! Overall it was a delightful dining experience.
author: Cheryl Chua

review_text:
After discovering PEN & INC through Google reviews, we decided to visit the restaurant located in NTU. Following the signage and direction boards, we easily located the establishment. Our visit took place on a weekend late afternoon, and we were among only three patrons at that time.
We thoroughly enjoyed the restaurant's vibe and the background music. Our order included the Slow Cooked Beef Cheek, Fish & Chips, Honey Mustard Chicken Leg, Meat Beef Ragu Pasta, and the highly recommended Lava Torte for dessert. All dishes were impeccably prepared, with each item reaching the perfect level of tenderness and harmonizing well with its respective sauces. It's challenging to pinpoint a single "Must Try" item, as every dish was truly worth sampling.

Among our favorites was the Chocolate Baked Lava Cake, exuding a delightful fragrance of chocolate and mild milk. Served piping hot and paired with cold vanilla ice cream, each bite resulted in a satisfying melding of flavors that melted in our mouths.

The waitstaff and entire crew were not only friendly but also deserving of a double thumbs up for their excellent service. Our visit to Pen & INC proved to be a delightful and memorable experience, making for a wonderful afternoon.
author: C’estLaVie

review_text:
i have been a fan of encik tan for a long time now. in fact i was extremely excited when they decided to open a branch in NTU, i brought friends there for most of my lunches and many students like me enjoy encik tan - evident from the long  snaking queues during peak hours that last for nearly 30 minutes each time.

however, my experience today (3 september, wednesday, 1pm) frustrated me deeply. i queued for approximately 20 minutes and ordered my usual set A (curry rice with chicken cutlet). i have known from patronising the stall for about 3 semesters now that the size of chicken cutlets has decreased over the last 1.5 years (thats okay/slightly sad, but the variation and shrinkflation is understandable).

BUT TODAY!! TODAY!! THE SIZE OF MY CHICKEN WAS THREE FINGERS THICC. 😭🤏 AND DA CURRY. DONT GET ME STARTED. THE CURRY. WAS LIKE 1TBLSPN of curry mixed into 500ML OF WATER. 😭😭

i was so upset. because what happened to the delicious thick gravy that i love from encik tan?? i walked away sadly, with my plate of food that i paid $5.30 for. in fact, when i ate it, the rice was clumpy and compressed — nearly like a kueh. but i was already upset enough.

i am pretty certain that my experience would differ greatly if i ordered from a different branch! I understand that in NTU, the queues are long and the serving is pretty systematic and fast-paced. but that cannot excuse the strongly watered down gravy and rice quality. afterall, we are paying the same price for the same set.students deserve the same standards as any other branch, if not better. ❤️ i truly hope Encik Tan NTU takes this feedback seriously and upholds the brand’s reputation, instead of letting students walk away disappointed and disillusioned.
author: Natalie

review_text:
Fast food version of typical Singaporean Peranakan Chinese cuisine. Don't know they opened an outlet in NTU campus until just recently. Predictably, the price is more expensive than comparable non-chain versions by $1-2 (most noticeably the noodles), especially considering such normal-ish portion.

The curry rice is alright, crunchy chicken cutlet size and taste are just fine, but the rice is too soggy especially when paired with the curry gravy. I'd say purely quality wise, the fishball noodle would sit in the middle of the pack compared to similar items elsewhere. For $5-6, I wish there's a bit more substances in it, for example more fishballs, mushroom, or dried anchovy.
author: lontongstroong

review_text: Went to Encik Tan at NTU north spine canteen today and order chicken cutlet curry rice. Request for more curry gravy on rice and staff told me extra curry will costs additional $1. I was stunned. I did not expect a full bowl of curry but extra gravy to cover the rice as I like my rice soaked in gravy (see pic that the rice is clumped together and not every grain is covered with gravy). I mean it is personal preference and others may request for lesser gravy so they should not be loss. Will vendor charge less if asked for lesser gravy? In addition, it is common that most stalls usually more than happy to provide extra curry gravy. Further this stall is located in NTU where majority are students who are not working and the additional $1 for extra gravy is unjustifiable and ripped off. If there is miscommunication like the cost refers to separate bowl of substantiate amount of gravy, this should be communicated but the staff did not mentioned anything or clarified what I am asking for. Very bad experience and will never patronise this stall. A ripped off and unethical business model in NTU. Beware.

review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience at Tenderbest. The service was appalling from start to finish. The cashier was curt and dismissive, showing zero interest in engaging respectfully with customers. Staff behind the counter were equally indifferent, with no sense of urgency or basic courtesy.

To make matters worse, the food was served carelessly — portions were sloppily thrown together with no regard for presentation or hygiene. This is not what I expect from a brand that positions itself as a reputable F&B establishment.

What truly added insult to injury was the payment process. A QR code for online payment was clearly displayed, yet when I attempted to use it, I was abruptly told it was cash only. No signage, no warning — just a blunt refusal and poor attitude. This kind of miscommunication reflects very poorly on the management. It’s 2025 — cash-only operations without proper notice are unacceptable.

This outlet needs serious retraining on customer service, basic professionalism, and operational clarity. Until then, I won’t be returning — and I wouldn’t recommend it to anyone expecting a minimally decent dining experience.

review_text:

Ordered the medium $6 portion. This is certainly the wettest version I have eaten. Serves with 1 whole prawn and 3 half prawns? Couple slices of abalone, pork lard and chilli on the side. There are hints of wok hei, but the broth does not have strong umami taste. Not sure why the prawns are a mixed of whole abd and halves, i prefer the whole prawn. Also unsure the replacement of abalone over pork belly. Chilli is pretty decent. Pork lard is chunky and well fried.

review_text:
We steadily decided to visit this very old time HKM stall. We visit around 11am and there's not much queue but after that the queue started to boom!!

We share a plate of $5. It's super duper wet style hkm but if you look closely the gravy was ultra thick & very brownish. A little let down at first as there's no squid nor pork slices. Just prawns, but just one mouthful I understand it's ok without them. And the fresh and crispy pork lard and 2 pcs of abalone more than made up for it.

I think they are very focused on the prawn stock. It's heavenly good, very prawny & unami taste. Noodles were well cooked, portions great and there's really nice wok hei. Every mouthful goes perfect. Worth our long trip there.

We will be back!!

restaurant_name: Lu Heng Kee 盧興記 Hokkien Mee
review_text:
HKM is prepared in cauldron size so it may take a while if you are in line for a new batch.

The largest order was $7 which came with 4 mid sized prawns and mock abalone. No squid or pork.

It was very moist, almost soupy. The broth is of pork bone and crustacean base, offering deep flavor. Egg wash gave it another depth. A good mix of yellow noodle and white vermicelli.

A squeeze of lime uplifted the dish. Lard was large and crisp while the chili was potent and went well with the overall dish.

Almost 80% of the tables were having this dish. A great find in a far flung corner.

review_text:
We had a truly satisfying dining experience at Swensen’s Jurong Point and it definitely deserves a 5-star rating. From the moment we were seated, the overall ambience felt welcoming and comfortable, making it a great place for both family meals and casual gatherings with friends.

We ordered a variety of main dishes to share, and every single one was well prepared and enjoyable. The Duck Baked Rice was a standout — generous in portion, flavourful, and well-balanced. The duck was tender and juicy, paired nicely with the baked rice and cheese without being overly heavy. It was comforting and satisfying, perfect for those who enjoy hearty baked dishes.

The Fish and Chips was another highlight. The fish was fresh, crispy on the outside, and moist on the inside, while the batter was light and not greasy. Served with fries and tartar sauce, it was a classic dish done right.

We also tried the Seafood Pasta, which came with a good mix of seafood cooked nicely and coated in a flavourful sauce. The pasta was cooked al dente, and the dish did not feel overly rich, making it easy to enjoy till the last bite. The Fisherman Baked Rice was equally impressive, packed with seafood and baked to perfection with a deliciously melted cheese topping.

Overall, the food quality was consistent across all dishes, portions were generous, and everything arrived well presented. The service was attentive and friendly, adding to the pleasant dining experience. Swensen’s Jurong Point is a reliable choice for good food, a comfortable setting, and a satisfying meal. We truly enjoyed our visit and will definitely return again.

I am lodging a serious complaint regarding the unacceptable and extremely disrespectful conduct of one of your staff members on the morning of 22 February 2026.

I was the first customer to arrive at the outlet that morning. The manager personally saw me and invited me to take a seat while waiting for operations to begin. At approximately 11:00am, I was clearly the first person in line at the ordering counter.

After waiting for about four minutes, a woman in her 50s blatantly cut the queue and even attempted to grab the menu from my hand. I chose to remain calm and avoid physical contact. I politely informed the staff at the counter that I had been first in line.

Instead of managing the situation professionally and fairly, the staff member rudely snatched the menu from my hand and proceeded to serve the customer who cut the queue. This was completely unjustified and demonstrated a shocking lack of professionalism and basic respect.

The situation worsened when I received my takeaway order. No utensils were provided. After I reminded her, she threw the utensils into my bag in an aggressive and dismissive manner. Furthermore, I noticed that my sauce container was only half-filled, while other customers were given full portions. When I calmly asked whether mine could be filled to the same level as the others, she responded with an unfriendly expression and said, “Bring yours over,” in a tone that was clearly annoyed and unwelcoming.

As a paying customer, I expect to be treated with fairness, courtesy, and respect. What I experienced was the complete opposite. The staff member’s behavior was rude, dismissive, and unacceptable in any service environment.

I request that management investigate this incident thoroughly, take appropriate disciplinary action, and provide proper service training to your staff. I also expect a formal apology for the way I was treated.

This experience has seriously affected my perception of your establishment, and I hope this matter will be addressed with the seriousness it deserves.

Ichiban Boshi · Jurong Point · Singapore ⭐️⭐️⭐️

Each outlet features a slightly different concept, with menus curated around regional Japanese flavours — from sushi and sashimi to donburi and teishoku sets.

The upside is the restaurant’s large, comfortable space, making it easy to find a table even during peak hours. A convenient choice for a quick Japanese meal, though not one that stands out for flavour or experience.
