review_text:
I dined here about a week ago and recently came across the photos of my meal, which reminded me how much the food quality has declined compared to a few months back. It’s disappointing, especially considering the higher prices, as the restaurant used to maintain much better standards.

I ordered the lunch set, which I now wouldn’t recommend. It felt like the set was made with lower-quality cuts or leftover ingredients — perhaps that’s why it’s offered at a lower price. I found a hair on my steak but decided not to make a fuss, thinking it was a one-off issue. However, the steak itself was more raw than medium rare, and much of it was inedible due to tough ligaments, making it hard to cut through.

The crispy chicken aglio was also a letdown — about a 2/10. Some pieces tasted like they’d been double-fried, and the bonito flakes didn’t complement the aglio flavor at all.

Service, as always, was friendly and attentive, but unfortunately, the food didn’t live up to expectations this time.

BTW after recent renovations. we got a cockroach visit us at our table when we finished eating. :)
author: Claudia

review_text: Very good western fare served in the heart of Jurong Pt mall. Our first time here & it didnt disappoint. Ordered beef mafalda pasta, seafood pasta, burgers, fish & chips & pasta. My mother-in-law who rarely comments on western fare said the food is good, which means something! We ordered 2 types of pizza, some spicy salami w jalapeno & carbonara pizza- v.yummy slices! For an 8 pax gathering, we overordered slightly & everything was abt $200. Worth the price, service was prompt & generously gd portion. Would repeat!
author: Zaza Md Taat

review_text:
Restaurant deco is quite nice.
Food portion is reasonable vs price but taste is not very tasty and require further adjustment or improvement.
Didn’t get much service as the place is a bit under staffed.
Overall a 6/10.
author: Tom Lee

review_text:
Best and personal favourite place to eat Udon, one of my favourite Japanese restaurants ever!
I highly recommend Kinoko Pork Udon, and Pork Kimchi Udon, as they always taste amazing throughout the years. Good alternatives are the Niku Pork Udon, or Niku Beef Udon too. For the adventurous, Mentai Carbonara Chicken Udon is also a must-try!
Dry udon with egg / Ontama Bukkake Udon was pretty good. The soup udons do taste better.
They have a huge variety of tempura! One of my favourite tempura is the Kaikage / fried vegetables, as hardly anywhere else has them as an option let alone such a generous serving. I added a bacon tempura to one of my meals, and it was tasty but quite expensive.

Free-flow tempura sauce to accompany the chosen tempura, along with other condiments like chili padi, japanese radish (daikon), and tempura flakes that I will always add to my meal.
Currently it has a free upsize offer and can be applied to any dish! Recommend, you add free upsize to your meal.
You can even request to add kimchi, onsen egg, or extra meat to any bowl but at the cashier. You can request additional free wakame seaweed and spring onions too.
Self-service, cheerful Japanese music with a calm atmosphere, clean tables. 100/10
author: Amelia Crowe

review_text:
Visited Idaten Udon for the first time and was pleasantly surprised! We ordered the Nuri Udon (Pork) and Mentai Carbonara Udon. There’s also a condiments bar with fried tempura bits and dipping sauce, which was a nice touch. The fried tempura added a satisfying crunch to the udon dishes.

The udon itself was really smooth and springy, and true to what they advertise, it’s served from Japan. The soup base was really flavourful, and the pork slices were thin, soft, and tasty — with a nice balance of fat to meat. The Mentai Carbonara Udon was not bad too, though it would have been even nicer if it was creamier.

Prices were pretty affordable, and there’s also an ongoing promotion with free upsizing for dine-ins, which makes it even more worth it. The restaurant has plenty of seating with free seating available. We went in around 7+ pm and it wasn’t too crowded, making it a comfortable dining experience.

Highly recommended! 👍
author: Zoey W

review_text:
Passing by and decided to give it a try for their Udon. Hence we ordered Black Garlic version & Spicy version, together with a few fried dishes. Preparation was pretty quick. And they have free upsize of Udon! The price is considered cheap for a bowl of quick Udon.

The bowl material is quite heavy, one have to be careful if you have ordered a lot to carry them to your table. Udon portion was really big, whereby Udon is on the softer side rather than chewy. The soup base was kinda salty which makes you quite thirsty after having it. Pretty like the tamago and chashu was not those fatty type. The fried vegetables was very crispy even though it has been placed there for a while.

There are many tables and easy to get one during lunch time.
author: Euphorie Liew

review_text: Dropped in for lunch. I prefer to order the plain udon and add-on tempura. The tempura was not as warm as expected. It was more expensive than expected, but I will occasionally eat here when I'm in the mood for it.
author: Neo Chuan Cheng

review_text: If you want to get a quick and simple Japanese food, I would recommend this chain restaurant. The quality of the udon that you can get and the price you pay is very reasonable. We went to the Jurong Point branch today and the place was not crowded. While I didn’t expect a Japanese quality of service, I still believed that the tone of the staff could be a bit friendlier. A good spirit of hospitality and gratitude should not be dependent on the price of the food 🥰
author: Flying Molen

review_text: Light broken, aircon no cold, coke machine inside have mosquito when i take ice it drop it down. Refill water is not unlimited need pay extra (Get stop by stuff when try to refill). Wraping also very horrible all vege split it out. Dirty wont come again thanks.
author: Su Wei Lee

review_text: My personal experiences ordering from Subway at different outlets differ most of the time, depending on the service staff on duty manning the outlets. Generally it’s more uncommon these days to meet F&B service crew who make an effort even to appear friendly, helpful and accommodating to customers’ requests if any🥹; shout-out here to the young staff - Harshini who made my day (and my delish sub haha) with her warm and personable service🙂. Thank you!👍🏻💯
author: Rach

review_text:
Hi, i like to bring to your attention because is not the 1st I had experienced.
The 2 crews are new n they are still not familiar with the products. They nearly gave me a wrong meats on the order.
One of the dressing bottle neck was too narrow to pour. The staff ask me if I can change my choice of dressing. Only I told him to open the cover n then pour over it
I then order a nancho bowl, then he gave me a packet of nancho.
They seem to have any clues wat were they doing, as such it delay all orders coming in.
Please have an least 1 x experience staff around so that they are able to guide them.
When I get home I realised the nancho noel was nancho chips with salad n Caesar dressing.
No salsa, no jalapeño, no melted cheese.
I am telling you, there is a serious problem happening at your outlets
author: Richard Ng

review_text: Staff not sure of what they are doing. Wanted to shortchanged me of portion of tuna. And the other was corrected by another staff. Wore gloves and contact everywhere with the gloves and touching your foods. Very poor hygiene. Will report to sfa!
author: Terence Tan

review_text: went there during 6pm so many things were no longer available ??? pickles, mixed greens, jalapeño cheese, multigrain bread?? idk why they are not refilling it?
author: Jieling Teo

review_text:
Good tasing food at reasonable price. Standard from stall to stall may differ a little due to cooking skill.
Portion and ingredients fairly consistent.
author: Marcus Goh

review_text: This is always my only choice whenever I feel like eating bak chor mee. The noodles are cooked just nice, not too soft and not too hard. The sliced meat and minced pork are fresh and tasty, can really tell the quality is good. The braised mushroom is my favorite part, very rich and full of flavor, you can taste how long it is braised. Everything comes together very well in one bowl. Simple, comforting, and very satisfying. I keep coming back again and again because it never disappoints. Definitely a place I trust for good bak chor mee.
author: Tian zun Tiam

review_text: Had the fishballs noodles meepok dry. Food wise was nice, fishballs were chewy and fresh, noodles were just nice and chewy. She asked if to add noodles, I said ok and with 50cents topup, I don’t mean to offend anyone but it didn’t seem to have added noodles 😅 overall taste still good 👍
author: Steven Ho

review_text:
Great coffee shop and stall for a late night supper! The auntie manning the late night shift is very friendly and nice.

Tasty noodles that brings me back to my childhood!! 😍
author: Rex Tan

review_text:
Been eating here for years, food is decent but 9 out 10 times order have issue while on take out.

And today takes the cake,
ordered 2 laksa with no blood crockles at around 6pm+.
Actually started eating at 8pm+ and there are crockles inside went to exchange but was rejected due to cause not the staff shift. Asked for more info for the other staff number or boss number she said she doesn't know any of em.

Tried online calling their company and to no avail.

Luckily i am only sensitive to blood crockles not allergic. Regardless wasted money on food that i can't eat.

Basically got scammed for food.
author: evolutionkin

review_text: One of the better Chinese Nasi Lemak stalls in Jurong. The food quality is good, but I feel a bit pricey as I paid $5.50 for fish, luncheon meat, curry potato, and a chili fishcake.
author: Sheringham Zhou

review_text:
One of the very few best nasi lemak in Singapore, and definitely the best in west area.

There’s a good variety of food and dish. Very healthy food proportions and value for money. Food stall aunties are very friendly and nice. Always felt welcomed and greeted when I order food.

Nasi lemak chilli is another magic that makes the food irresistible. They have earned a loyal and returning customer in not only me, but also my family and colleagues.

👍👍👍👍👍
author: Kelvin Tan

review_text: I found a gem! Visited Boon Lay market after the renovation, saw the queue and decided to try too, the food is amazing and the price is very affordable. Prices are listed so we can get to know how much before hand. My favourite is their fish and chicken wing.
author: Anna Wong

review_text:
Long wait. Decent portion. Food is OK. Price ok

Don't expect much selection as the store will keep serving mass orders of more than 20 packets. They will not prioritise those dining in or small orders.

Have seen a single person takeaway more than 40 packets. End of the day not much options left for the rest queuing in line.
author: Jordan

review_text: Their nasi lemak is very delicious, many varieties of dishes but my favourite is obviously the mermaid (mei ren yu).. it’s so fresh! definitely worth to make the trip all the way there just to have this for lunch! ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
author: Huifen Teo

review_text:
Authentic and traditional fritters !
You tiao salty and red bean Ham Ji Png. Butterfly fritters , sweet potato fritters etc
All freshly made from dough and fried immediately !
No unpleasant oily after taste at all.
Really nice taste of nostalgia
author: J T

review_text:
This stall serves up standard fried fritter fare, operating from early morning until everything is sold out, often before noon. High turnover of products so the items are often fresh.

Although a variety of options tend to be readily available, securing a youtiao frequently involves a significant wait time (you’d need to preorder and come back 30 mins later).

I’m not sure what’s stall owners’ strategy for this but getting a youtiao from this stall feel akin to capturing a rare Pokémon.
author: CG

review_text: Great delicious snacks! A bit of queue in the morning. But was clear within 5 mins…
author: Marlene Lee

review_text:
If you have plenty time and a penchant for standing in line, this is the perfect place. Snacks here tastes good and tastes even better when you've finally satisfied your intense hunger from having stood so long in line. Some might be perturbed by their serious lack of respect for patrons' time though. For the few times I've purchased from here, I realised that queue cutting is normal and welcomed by the stall personnel. I didn't find it socially acceptable to be a queue cutter so didn't plan to try it out at this stall. So I thought today I can get a snack (butterfly bun) from here quickly as there were only 3 people ahead of me. But wow I was so wrong. The stall personnel let a lady cut the queue. He moves really slowly. Like... He ambles? Objectively, perhaps being physically big in mass limits movements and probably dispenses more energy? I was contemplating to leave the queue but since I'm already 2nd in line, I should just get my snack. But after watching the man's movements for some time, I realised that I have only 14 minutes to buy & eat my snack & walk back before my lesson starts.
Alas it was my turn! He told me "I'm selling the youtiao first". Then I watched him in slow mo, getting the fritters, getting payment etc. I finally figured I will be running real late if I'd decided to wait. So I cut my losses and left.
Shall not be going back anytime soon. Complete waste of time.
author: L.J.

review_text: Youtiao (aka dough fritters), butterfly bun, etc always great ... Worth the queue   ?!
author: J.K. Chua

review_text: It was raining heavily & my colleague & I decided to order Pizza for lunch. The counter staff is a tall young man, he served me politely & guide me on how to place my order. I’m very pleased with his wonderful service.
author: Tay Valerie

review_text: Had a great experience here! The service was amazing and the staff were so kind and helpful. I kept changing my order and they were super patient and sweet about it. I’ve been coming here since I was a kid and it’s still my favourite pizza place till today. Highly recommend!”
author: Afrin Noor

review_text: Mira is always helpful and accommodating. She makes every customer comfortable and she serves in a high customer care manner. She is respectful and she deserve to be promoted.
author: Jhing Ladrillo

review_text: Pizza hut comes out buffet promotion. And the manager can’t even take care the queue. Left everyone outside, while the table is empty. Priority to 4-6 person.
author: Yigene Lim

review_text: The person has given a good service & the food was amazing
author: Esta Esta

restaurant_name: Ho Huat Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee 和发福建炒虾面
review_text:
​In my opinion, this is one of the best fried Hokkien Prawn Mee stalls in the Jurong area!

​I also noticed that 正志文记猪什汤 has moved into this food village, taking over the old Tian Tian Xiang Mixed Rice (天天香) stall. I'll definitely be back soon to give it a try!
author: Sheringham Zhou

restaurant_name: Ho Huat Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee 和发福建炒虾面
review_text:
I was in the area looking for food at this hawker centre and noticed this stall had many good reviews, so I decided to give it a try. Despite the pretty long queue, the stall was efficient — I was served almost immediately and the total wait was under 15 minutes. A plate costs $5, which is quite reasonable for the portion size.

However, the noodles were undercooked, which left them slightly hard and unable to absorb the broth well. They also carried a noticeable alkaline taste, which affected the overall flavor. Unfortunately, it wasn’t to my liking, and I wouldn’t return for another plate.
author: yenney lee

restaurant_name: Ho Huat Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee 和发福建炒虾面
review_text:
We made our final dash to Boon Lay Place Food Village this weekend before the hawker centre takes a 3-month rest for repairs and a fresh new look.
This stall always draws a queue and their wet-style Hokkien mee may be a little light on the wok hei [a.k.a. smoky aroma], but it more than makes up for it in nostalgic taste.
author: AC Chan

restaurant_name: Ho Huat Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee 和发福建炒虾面
review_text: Reopened with the newly renovated hawker center. Bought $10 but was surprised by the small size of it. Such stingy amount of prawn and squid. NOT WORTH my $10 at a HAWKER CENTER that's hot as hell. Will never come back again. Feel so cheated!
author: Happy Lucky

restaurant_name: Ho Huat Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee 和发福建炒虾面
review_text:
Home cooked Hokkien mee but your mum worked in a restaurant before.

Long queue during lunch time, but cleared pretty fast. One round could clear about 10 people. Really big hawker centre with lots of selection.
author: Derrick L

restaurant_name: Bok's Kitchen by Hidden Chefs - Singapore
review_text:
It was our first time dining at Bok’s Kitchen, and overall we had a nice experience. We ordered freshly brewed iced lemon tea, truffle carbonara, chilli crab pasta, and crispy pork cheek.

The crispy pork cheek was fantastic, especially when eaten hot, as it tends to lose some of its texture once it cools. The chilli crab pasta had quite a strong level of spiciness, so those who are less tolerant of spicy food may want to take note (not sure if a less spicy option is available). The truffle carbonara was enjoyable, though my husband would have preferred a slightly thicker sauce.

Overall, it was a pleasant dining experience, and we enjoyed trying the dishes
author: Cindy

restaurant_name: Bok's Kitchen by Hidden Chefs - Singapore
review_text:
This place is a new gem! Definitely deserves our 5-star review.

The char siew rice is a must try! The mushroom soup comes with two pieces of toasted garlic bread. Probably one of the most garlicky breads I have ever had. If you are not a fan of garlic, you might want to skip it, but I personally loved it!

Will definitely be back to try more items on the menu. 😊
author: Berniceee

restaurant_name: Bok's Kitchen by Hidden Chefs - Singapore
review_text:
Visited Bok's Kitchen upon a recommendation by a colleague. If you are driving, it might be a bit hard to spot the place. It's located on the extreme left hand side of the building (when you are facing the building).

For the main dishes, we ordered:
Spinach Mushroom Aglio
Truffle Carbonara
Char Siew Rice Bowl
Salmon Teriyaki Rice Bowl

We prefer the pasta dishes over the rice bowl ones. Portion is considered small but the quality of food is definitely good. Question of quality over quantity 😊

For the side dishes, we ordered:
Bok's Garlic Winglet
Crispy Pork Cheek

Both side dishes are worth trying. Crispy and tasty.

We wanted to try the chili crab pasta that many customers are raving about but it wasn't available during lunch.

We will be back to try the other dishes in the menu. Recommended place to visit if you are in the vicinity.
author: Eric Loong

restaurant_name: Bok's Kitchen by Hidden Chefs - Singapore
review_text:
Delish VF$$ Fusion Dishes to die for

Had a Sunday dinner and ordered the crowd favs of garlic winglets, cheesy meltz, beef bowl, grilled chicken bowl, rendang chicken bread bowl, deep fried beef cheek, carrot cake fries, mango fizz and home made onion rings. And ooh lala... All of them were simple delish! The rice is not the usual white rice but an aromatic buttered-herb moist rice that goes so well with the proteins.

The meats were well executed, well grilled flavours and tender. The winglets, with garlic bits and fried laksa leave is yums! Crispy, tender and full of garlic goodness!

Onion rings is authentic onion cuts, sweet and not oily! The messy cheese is also so so good. The fries that came with it... Is packed and doesn't taste like it's the frozen stuff. The carrot cake... So well executed... Each bite is crispy and with moist inside that packs a punch of a typical carrot cake, with taste of the shrimps and rice!

What is clear... Their frying skills is top!

The rendang bowl... Yums too!

Will definitely be back to try the other stuffs on the menu!

Great service, as in it's fast

Only complaint is the noise level. The hard walls of the interior can be soften to reduce the reverberations.
author: David Oon

restaurant_name: Bok's Kitchen by Hidden Chefs - Singapore
review_text: Been here a few times since this café is in my hood. You will be surprised that this quiet, tucked-away spot is always quite busy. Prices are reasonable, portions are huge, and the food tastes homemade. They also have some off-menu items worth trying. We always takeaway their homemade curry puff which is super good!
author: S S

review_text:
We had a fantastic experience here! There is no service charge and no GST, which makes the already reasonable prices even better. The food is delicious, and the staff are incredibly attentive.
What impressed us most was the honesty at the counter—the cashier double-checked if we used the wet tissues and proactively deducted the cost since we hadn't.
Highly recommended for great food and even better service!
author: Sheringham Zhou

review_text: Was at Putien Jurong Point. We were welcome warmly by the friendly staff. Our food was served promptly. All dishes were delicious and fresh. We were very happy with the staff, Lan Ting who was very professional in her service. Other staff were also polite and accommodating. Will surely recommend family and friends to patronise this restaurant.
author: Magdalene Koh

review_text: I went to Putien at Jurong Point to have my dinner.  I was being served by the store manager Ms Lan Ting who was very polite and friendly.  She recommended me their signature lychee pork and Ca Fen dish which I enjoyed very much.  I also tried their pomelo which was sweet and refreshing.
author: Cherry

review_text:
Visit during lunch time.  Not really crowded.  Placed order at 12:28pm and waited for 33 mins before
first dish to arrived.  Ironically the “6 min”
baked croaker dish arrived exactly 36mins later…
author: Ken Tan

review_text: At first, I was disappointed by the menu choices. But everything turned out so well at the end of the day. We asked for opinion on the portion of food for 4 and the person gave very accurate info (portion just nice, not like some restaurant which purposely made your order big portion to earn more). Good service. The dishes we ordered were all so tasty and delicious. My family certainly enjoyed the meal. Best of all, no service charge, no GST.
author: J Chua

review_text: Every dish is good, but the flavours may not be very kid-friendly, as the food tends to be on the heavier side. Other than that, there’s nothing negative to say about the restaurant, except that since it’s teppanyaki, the area can be quite oily, and some utensils may not be completely clean.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text:
Been here multiple times over the years.
Their complimentary appetisers have gone from tuna(?) dips with cut veggies to just cabbage with some dressing over it. The scallops that come with their scallop fried rice seem so scammy. They used to be fine, but now they're so thinly sliced they look like scallop bacon?
The service has really gone down the hill too... apart from one more senior lady, they seem so reluctant to help customers.
The staff was even eating chicken rice at the next table.... at first, they didn't want to let us have the corner table for four (we're two people), saying that they're worried more customers would come in... but maybe it's cos they wanted that table to eat their break time meal?
For this price, it feels like the service should be at least a little better...?
author: Bren A

review_text:
The food was enjoyable overall — ingredients were fresh, and the flavors were well-balanced. However, there’s still room for improvement, especially in terms of seasoning and overall presentation, which could elevate the experience further.

One notable downside was the waiting time. The food took longer than expected to be served, which affected the overall dining experience. A faster turnaround would certainly enhance customer satisfaction.

Looking forward to seeing improvements, as the concept and potential are definitely there.
author: Jamie Tan

review_text:
Delicious teppanyaki lunch set meal @ $14.90 consisting of (tried chicken and white fish options), bean sprouts, salad, pickles, miso soup.  Upgraded to garlic fried rice which tasted  great. Overall good value and taste as the dishes were freshly prepared.
Amazing service the staff provided complimentary yuzu iced drink after meal and also extra appetiser for me and wife though only sharing a set.
author: Ken Tan

review_text: Good variety of teppanyaki food. Enjoyed the nice cod fish and sukiyaki beef, washed down with red plum wine while watching the skilled chefs cooking and serving delicious food. Limited seats and expect to queue during weekends.
author: J Acksee

review_text: Tried the new breakfast bagel meal at McDonald’s.  Selected the corn side and add on 2pc hotcakes. Warm firm and chewy texture of bagel tasted delicious with savoury mushroom egg filling. Weekday breakfast crowd is less with many seats available.  Consistently good food quality.
author: Ken Tan

review_text:
literally ordered spicy nuggets and gotten nuggets for god sake? called the hotline multiple times and no one picked up. 2nd time gotten the order wrong. cant check before giving out?

came another day before 12am closing. reach at 1120pm and everything was cleared?!
author: Joan Lee

review_text: i got mobile order and when i arrived i checked that my fries was exceptionally LESS so i politely asked them if i could have more ofc i upsized for a bigger portion it literally looks like the small one ? the staff said okay after i askex if i could have more he came back with the same  amount or at most he added 2/3 more fries… wth
author: Tan Meini

review_text: Came in at around 3am since was hungry at night, there was barely anyone and the place was very quiet and peaceful, would come again for late night meals when i get the chance!!! Food and service was amazing
author: Lwin Thant Maung

review_text:
I regularly order all ice cream sundae from this branch. Today I ordered strawberry sundae with strawberry ice cream, it came out so short, way below the brim of the cup. Requested for a change, it's just touch the brim only. Staff said the ice cream is very soft, it collapsed until like that. She kindly replaced for me. Please refer to picture for the replaced sundae.

Mgmt, please check if ice cream too soft is a result of refrigeration problem or formula problem.
author: Cindy C

review_text: We ordered two Family Fest meals for about 8–10 people. When the order arrived, we noticed a few items were missing. I managed to reach out to them, and Andrew was the one who helped resolve the issue. He asked me to list the missing items and arranged for a redelivery. After checking, it turned out to be a delivery fault, but he still ensured the items were sent over. Thank you for the great help, Andrew!
author: J Wen

review_text: It’s officially back. Just had my first bite of KFC’s ondeh ondeh egg tart and we’re officially obsessed — soft, wobbly pandan custard, a light flaky crust and molten gula melaka at the bottom, topped off with bits of shredded coconut flakes.
author: AC Chan

review_text:
During my visit on Xmas eve morning...
Clean and tidy restaurant. Friendly Staff at front counter.
Ample seating space.
Hand wash area with soap is available on site.
author: Siah Hx

review_text: tell me why my mashed potato is bigger than my soggy fried chicken??? if i could post a video i would show a 360 of this tiny chicken
author: Jonathan Lim

review_text: KFC Mofusand plushie launch day where the queue for plushie ends around 930am when the staff announce they have ran out of queue tickets to give based on queue length.  Reached there 5 mins earlier and were one of the last to get.  Took 3 hrs from queueing to getting my food with plushie.  The staff was managing the queue well this round as most were seated before 11am.  Cereal chicken was quite ok though most customers were not really for the food and the restaurant was probably only quarter full with customers during lunch.
author: Ken Tan

review_text: Went here at 140am, barely customers and ordered a filet o fish set but it took 20 mins to do. I walk to ur counter i see 10-12 people in kitchen, malay guy preparing food was throwing food on counter he looks so done. Then indian lady at counter never say thank u and glares at customers, i dont get it bro u got so many staff so little customers…. why u look like the world owes u money? also what is this filet o fish lol, cannot even put HALF a slice of cheese properly.
author: Amelie Sim

review_text: Worst experience ever, malay lady who was infront of the counter packing at 9.50 pm night on 20 October. keep telling me wait just for a freaking pack of salt. She also packed half packed fries to my order and kept telling me to wait for a plastic bag, a salt, and a freaking ice cream of the same order. Do NOT GO. If you're grumpy please do not work. Just look at this fries. And Look at the ridiculous spicy tomato sauce, honestly just close down this unit.
author: Wong Wei Wei

review_text: The Mcchicken chicken patty became thinner, Crunchy like biscuit ... Today brought and get half of the tom yum sauce for the burger, must be right handed...then wrapper triple the size of the tom yum(sauce) burger itself...20cents more pay for a larger wrapper.
author: Patrick Zhang

review_text:
My friends and I regularly visit the McDonald’s at Pioneer Mall after our daily workouts, and we have consistently been impressed by the excellent service provided by the staff at this branch. In particular, we would like to commend the Customer Experience Leader, Soo Kheng, for her warm and outstanding service.

Soo Kheng and her team have done an exceptional job in creating a welcoming and memorable experience for customers. She always makes us feel at home with her friendly attitude, efficiency, and attention to detail. It is clear that she takes great pride in her role and is genuinely committed to ensuring that every customer has a pleasant and enjoyable visit.

We understand that the Pioneer Mall branch is consistently busy with a high volume of customer orders, especially during the period when the Gek Poh Shopping Centre branch was closed. We have also noticed that some reviews mention longer processing and delivery times. However, from our own observations, the team at Pioneer Mall is already working extremely hard to manage the heavy demand and ensure orders are processed as quickly and efficiently as possible. Credit should certainly be given to the team for their dedication in handling the challenging workload.

We truly appreciate the hard work, professionalism, and positive atmosphere that Soo Kheng and the entire team bring each time we stop by. Their dedication reflects the high standards of McDonald’s and makes this outlet one we are always happy to return to. Kudos to Soo Kheng and the team.
author: ah chan

review_text: ordered an mcchicken and nugget set to deliver at 2am, cuz we have a break then. the kitchen was ‘preparing the food’ since 2am to 6am, from sun down to sun up. what are the mcdonald’s employees doing, are you sure they preparing food or sleeping. if they can’t do it why would they accept the order and not cancel immediately. got me checking my phone waiting, even the driver went to the mall itself and left to go boon lay 😭 it literally shows open 24hour
author: Vannsss

review_text:
Imagine getting so pissed that i had to give my 1st google review. Look at the timing from order to receiving and decide if its reasonable during off peak hours that you have to wait for almost 30mins just for some fries, 2 pieces of chicken and 2 prawns ! The staff had the "common sense" to put the coffee before the food was ready, and ending up cold by the time it was ready. When i asked for a replacement of said coffee, the staff neither apologised nor provided any word of followup on the replacement and left me waiting there for a few mins like a fool ! Seriously i wouldnt miss it if long john silver was gone with this sort of standards, especially when you look at the full bins of trash that no one cares to clear during non peak period.

Clearly the outlet manager doesnt delegate, not interested in running the place, nor care about the turnover or the daily revenue takings. If the top management is reading this, I suggest firing the manager and redeploying the staff elsewhere. Its obvious the work culture in the branch has gone amok and only a fresh brood of caring workers can bring up the standards.
author: aa bb

review_text:
I paid a total of $8.40 for the Golden Deal (1 piece Alaska Pollock and 1 piece chicken) with a sour cream and onion sauce. I chose the spicy option and honestly, the portion sizes have really shrunk. The fish was thin and almost the same size as the chicken. The chicken was over-fried, making the outside leathery, and I couldn’t even cut it properly with the plastic knife. The fried loose batter was minimal, just one forkful.

I’m not sure if the spicy option was the problem, but looking at other reviews, the Alaska Pollock seems larger if you get the original flavor. The spicy flavor I had was saltier than spicy.

It’s been over a year since I last had LJS, and with the small portions, poor quality, and relatively high price, I think I’ll skip Long John Silver for at least another year.
author: J

review_text: It appears there may be a significant resource allocation issue or a shortage of staff at this branch. When I placed my order, there was only one outstanding order, which led me to believe service would be prompt. However, the staff prioritized fulfilling delivery orders, and after approximately 15 minutes, there were still 10 customers waiting for their dine-in orders. My order was received about 20 minutes after it was placed. Additionally, I've noticed that the food portions seem to be considerably smaller than they were previously. I respectfully suggest that management seriously consider investigating these concerns.
author: Beaumont Sim

review_text:
A reliable choice for a quick and affordable meal. The outlet is conveniently located inside the mall, making it an easy stop for shoppers and commuters alike.

The food was served hot and fresh during my visit, and the portions were generous for the price. Seating is comfortable, and the outlet is usually kept clean even during busy hours. Service was decent, though it can be a little slow during peak times.
author: Benedict Correya

review_text: Portion has shrunk over the years but still delicious … will be crowded during peak dining hour
author: poh wei kiat

review_text:
Love a great break after driving for so long...

Lets dive in!

Location:
At one of the corner at a traffic junction. Very prominent and easy to reach here.

Amenities:
EV charging, car wash, repair station, convenience store and more! We bought ourselves latte which was made over the counter as well!

Operations:
Open 24hours a day, 7 days a week, this place is a definite stop.

We enjoyed our petrol top ip and the amenities offered here as well.

Cheers!
author: Sten (Piqued Wanderer)

review_text: I used to patronise this car wash when the old team was here. Super quality wash but now it is one of the worst carwash I have been too. After vaccuming there was still debries.He had to redo the vacum again.
author: mel roy

review_text:
Washed car end up with deep scratch on paint
Used sponge one shot to wipe never rinse at all
author: Ming

review_text: The kiosk to pump air into the tyre doesn't work. Always happens at a few Shell stations I tried, Bukit Timah area one similar problem
author: Ray

review_text: Had car wash, its basic.. no big issues just not super clean. Dont expect magic and you wont be disappointed!
author: zeppe linz

restaurant_name: Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao
review_text: Crystal Jade is one of the rare chinese restaurants in Singapore that despite they are around for decades, they still deliver very delicious, high quality food. They remain creative and innovate. Constantly updating their menu to keep up to trends on popular choices. Every dishes we ordered were delicious. ALL. I have no feedback at all to pick on. Good selection of dishes that cater for young, adults and elderly.  Environment is nice and staff friendly as always. Always love to visit a crystal jade. Reservation is recommended but walk in will be fine too.
author: EveC

restaurant_name: Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao
review_text:
Came to JP because the man wanted to visit this camera shop,SLR Revolution.

After checking out what he needed, we decided to go dinner. Walked around and we settled for here.

It was not crowded and hence didnt have to wait and we were ushered to our table quickly. Scan QR code to order and I ordered:
1. Drunkard chicken with sour plum(chilled)
- sour plums were infused with alcohol
- if you don't opt for chicken thigh, mostly breast meat which won't be tender
2. Chicken soup
- tasted good and feels nutritious
3. Chilli Oil Dumplings
- tasted mild and isn't spicy or sour from the vinegar
- didnt appreciate the fried garlic as it is hard and spoils the texture when eaten with the dumplings. At times they stuck to my teeth.
4. Prawns
- batter was light
- prawns were firm and crunchy
- mayo over killed as it can get cloying
5. Xiao Long Bai
- skin was thin but wasnt juicy enough
- taste wise ok

Will I go back to this place again? Maybe not..
author: Nana

restaurant_name: Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao
review_text: Pretty disappointed by the food at this branch though service is really very good. The cha siew standard is not there. The rice is dry and not nice. Paid premium for low standard food.
author: J Chua

restaurant_name: Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao
review_text:
Walk in on a weekend afternoon and waiting time is less than one minute to be seated.

Member can enjoy 50% off the Crispy Duck served with Egg Crepe and the taste is quite good.

La Mian with Scallion Oil, Wuxi Deep Dried White Bait, Deep Fried Beancurd Skin with Prawn and Signature Pan Fried Scallion Pancake all taste nice and delicious.

The Dong Po Pork Sesame Pocket Bun taste pretty awesome.

The portion of the dishes is quite small but quality is good.

Overall experience is pleasant as good customer service with tea refill a couple of times.
author: Robert Robert

restaurant_name: Crystal Jade La Mian Xiao Long Bao
review_text:
My family and I used to frequent Crystal Jade for their noodles with minced meat & mushroom. Came again in June 2025 and to our disappointment, this dish is no longer on the menu.

The menu has been updated for what is currently popular - mala, sour fish, etc which I personally think is not a very smart move. If I wanted to eat mala & sour fish, I would head to a China chain where they are established experts on that flavour profile.

Nevertheless, we tried the sour fish la mian. It's okay. It's not bad but it's not good either - fish is dry, although soup is flavourful and spicy.

Thankfully their dim sum has remained the same, quality and enjoyable although not the best out there. The dishes were served very quickly, although it took us almost 15 minutes to get seated when there were several empty tables.

The staff are pretty good and are trying their best, but the truth is this place is understaffed and you can feel it. Thankfully the kitchen doesn't seem to be understaffed.

After their menu revamp, the best part of this Crystal Jade outlet is the atmosphere and the place. It is comfortable, spacious and neither too bright nor dim. It will be a good choice for dim sum & if you are not too hungry.
author: Wei

review_text:
It is not that bad as the other commenters .

They were kind and not bad service.

The soupe is simple but tasty.

The braised pig trotter  was not that bad. It was very tender and tasty.
We really enjoyed the food. The quantity is also good.
author: Cou Cou

review_text: The food is good! I’ve been patronising for awhile now. The prices are very affordable and I especially like the 梅菜扣肉饭 and the 台湾卤肉饭 😀
author: Brannon Oh (Brannon)

review_text: Foods sucks, the braised meat not even soft and hard as rock. The soup tasteless and Luke warm. Boss attitude sucks as if you own him a living.
author: Joe Chan

review_text: The watercress pork rib soup was just so-so.
author: Repent less

review_text: This outlet in JW50 no good! Aunty is RUDE and slow. Noodle nothing special.
author: Jermiane Tay

review_text: Noodle is tangy, generally standard is maintain at this outlet. noodle portion reasonable. Stall located at second level, infront of escalator.
author: Siah Hx

review_text: I got the item #1. Only gave me 1 wanton :( why so stingy. Noodles are qq tho
author: Kathleen Salazar

review_text:
Super small portions for the price paid, and overall quite disappointing.

Ordered the saba fish, but the sauce was too sweet and it only came with two small pieces instead of a whole fish like the photo suggested. The bibimbap hardly had any meat, making it feel quite empty and not worth the price. The salmon omelette was alright, but it only came with two thin slices of salmon and egg.

For what you are paying here, the value just isn’t there. If you top up just 50–80 cents more, you can get a larger and more satisfying portion from the Koufu stall right beside.

Wouldn’t return.
author: Yun Yi Thiam

review_text:
This was probably the best Saba Fish Set I’ve ever eaten till date. They were very generous with the sauce given (not like most other places), which was the key to make this dish delicious. Both kimchi and sliced cabbage (below the fish) were given, and the soup was ok. It was a very satisfying meal. 😋👍🏻👍🏻

By the way, when I was being presented with the meal, I was surprised by the amount of fish given! I asked them and the cashier said it was because the particular fish was not big enough, so they gave me another half portion. Wow… how big is your normal fish size man? 😅🥰💕

Hope you keep up with the good standard. Will come and eat more often. 😋😋
author: Alice Wong

review_text: I've been a regular at this stall and it's one of my go-to foods in JW Hawker. Their saba fish is the best I've ever tried in SG. It's always very fresh, huge and grilled to perfection. The sauce is great as well. I keep coming back because it never disappoints!
author: Rlyejayn

review_text: We came here to check out the newly renovated hawker centre, and we were ecstatic to see very affordable food prices at this stall. The food portion is worth it for the price of Hotplate chicken which was only $5.80! It is very difficult to find such a cheap price and the food is very delicious too. Queues are quite short too. Highly recommended!
author: Joshua Chew

review_text:
Cheap and good food! Worth the price given the inflation of the current situation. Ordered set 1 salmon and chicken teriyaki bento. Portion is same as outside. Taste great as well, can compare with restaurant and food court. Worth the money.  Their preparation time is also not long,  around 2 minutes to get my bento set done.

Rice is sushi rice so they did not skimp on ingredients. Thank you very much! I will come and try out other dishes when possible. There are other stalls to try though. 😁😆😅
author: Bloody Toad

restaurant_name: 联邦肉骨茶 Lian Bang Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Herbal style (aka Malaysia style) bak kut teh. Meat is tender and fall off the bone easily, friendly staff. I dig in and finish the entire broth within minutes.
author: Kok Xiang Teh

restaurant_name: 联邦肉骨茶 Lian Bang Bak Kut Teh
review_text: My go to Bak Kut Teh spot in singapore. It’s rare to find dry bak kut teh but this place have it and it’s taste amazing and the price was reasonable.
author: Vanbotinner Chan

restaurant_name: 联邦肉骨茶 Lian Bang Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Today is Monday and quite a number of stalls are closed. Reached around 2:30pm and ordered the Herbal Bak Kut Teh & Kampong Braised Pig’s Trotter with one bowl of rice. Total $11.50 Taste great and trotter is soft. Boss also friendly. Didn’t take pictures of the food because I was very hungry. Before leaving, I told the boss I will take picture of his stall and give him a review.
author: Heng Nam Ong

restaurant_name: 联邦肉骨茶 Lian Bang Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Very friendly people so I gave 5 stars. I love to eat braised pork trotter but this store gravy is too sweet for my liking. Usually I pour gravy to my rice but cannot as sweetness empowers the taste of the skin and meat that even I dip it with chilli it’s still sweet. It’s a pity as they are really very nice people and really like to support them💪
author: yang fan

restaurant_name: 联邦肉骨茶 Lian Bang Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Ordered the dry Bak Kut Teh. I didn’t order rice, so it turned out a little too salty for my taste, though the flavor itself was really good. The portion was generous, definitely good value for the price. I also appreciated the small bowl of herbal BKT soup that came with it, which balanced the meal nicely. Overall, a satisfying dish, but it might pair better with rice to offset the saltiness.
author: Wong

review_text: Rude service and overpriced. Tau pok was priced as a type of meat? Ridiculous.
author: Isaac C.K. Tan

review_text:
Ordered the prawn paste chicken scrambled egg rice for $5.90.
The portion is really generous, the chicken is seasoned and fried nicely.
The egg is nicely cooked as well, not overly cooked or too runny.
It comes with a small bowl of egg soup, although I'll have preferred it to have more pepper in it.
Overall, a very good experience. Will definitely order from there again.
author: Sion Toh

review_text:
Decided to give this new stall a try, and was impressed by how delicious the prawn paste pork cutlet with scrambled egg tasted!

The pork cutlet was tender and crispy on the outside, with a nice prawn paste flavour. The scrambled egg was creamy and fluffy, just the way I like it! Very yummy and satisfying meal~
author: Rlyejayn

review_text:
Delicous scrambled egg served with prawn paste chicken cutlet. Fried fresh upon order.

Aromatic prawn paste that’s juicy and tender. Great value at just $5.9 with generous portion. Can also order other sides as add-on. Service crew is friendly as well. Highly recommended!
author: DS

review_text:
Have tried the salmon 3 times already. Safe to say this stall offers a generous serving of salmon chunks that are crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, far from the typical salmon that just crumbles apart and I appreciate the light taste of prawn paste since I'm not a big fan of prawn paste. Egg is soft and creamy.  Rice portion is also good but standard rice.
Bonus point for the good egg soup although for dine in only.
For $8.50 (dine in), this is value for money especially for those looking to eat "premium" fish and honestly the 2nd best salmon i have had so far (the best costed me 7 X the price at MBS :(    )
author: Yue.q

review_text: Ordered the prawn paste pork cutlet rice and added on prawn paste chicken wing. I think the prawn paste flavour tasted better on the chicken wing. The pork cutlet was quite tough. Scrambled egg was rly yummy!
author: Wong

review_text:
Newly opened Mala stall. I decided to give it a try. Approached by a malay lady (surprised!  First time served mala stall by a malay! ). IT seems this stall is halal? (I did not check whether they has the logo)

Picked my ingredients (7) of them,  no pork so I chose chicken. Handed over for her to calculate price. Came up to $21... Costly for a medium portion, but I did add quite an amount of chicken meat.

They accept CDC voucher,  but was not ready and wifi connection was down when they tried using it to scan. No choice. Cash payment it is then. She then passed me change with electronic tab.

Cooking - the lady put the ingredients onto what look like automated cooking machine (interesting), after that I did not go kaypo further. It took around 6 minutes before my buzzer signalled me to collect.

Packaging - Good quality plastic container with good quality chopsticks and disposable wooden spoon. Packed nicely and no spill. Nice.  Good quality,  but bad for environment 😅

Taste - I ordered mild spicy. They put quite a lot of dried chilli and peppercorns. They also added some spices which I usually did not find in other mala. Star anise, bay leaf and somewhat olive lookalike but do not taste like it. (Google internet picture one similar is either it's nutmeg,  or another spice named "cashew ") They also added orange peel! Interesting!  Taste wise,  it did not have the wokhei, and I find it not as aromatic, but for those who wanted to try out the added spices you are welcome.

Conclusion:  taste and price should improve. Must remember this is hawker,  not restaurant.
author: Bloody Toad

restaurant_name: Yunnan50 Fishball Noodle 云南鱼圆面
review_text: First time, and probably last... My main problem with this Laksa... is that it's "Hum-less"! The gravy was decently lemak, but c'mon... No cockles?! A hint of cockles blood is absolutely necessary for the right taste, else it's just NOT Singapore Laksa... Noodles of the Bak Chor Mee had ok texture, but the fishball was wrong for me... it's not the white and bouncy type, but more the Yong Tau Fu type... Taste so salah... Might as well use meatball better.
author: Y Nailah

restaurant_name: Yunnan50 Fishball Noodle 云南鱼圆面
review_text: Ordered fishball noodle and the Mee pok has good texture and flavour. Only the fishballs were disappointing.
author: Benito Linus

restaurant_name: Yunnan50 Fishball Noodle 云南鱼圆面
review_text: Arguably the best cooked mee pok in this region. Soup reminded me of childhood street hawkers' taste. Fishball texture needed further improvement. Laksa was without cockle, but gravy taste was acceptable. One of my favorite stalls in this hawker centre.
author: Repent less

restaurant_name: Yunnan50 Fishball Noodle 云南鱼圆面
review_text: 5.50 for the portion not worth to me, taste is okay.
author: Kyp Teh

restaurant_name: Yunnan50 Fishball Noodle 云南鱼圆面
review_text: curry taste normal , xiao guo mee not bad, the portion is just enought for lady
author: Boon

review_text:
Was told the rest of the fish dishes sold out (on a Sunday night) so only the whole fish was available. Ordered suan cai soup base at $29.90 including the so-called four side dishes which were added into the pot with the fish to heat up—potato slices, wong bok cabbage, fried & boiled bean curd skins, and luncheon meat— and 2 rice.

1) the whole fish did not taste fresh and feels flat maciam "buey buey" in hokkien - it was fried before adding it to the soup. 😔
2) the potato slices tasted bland without the potato fragrance - wonder what type of kantang they used! 😔😔
3) mediocre luncheon meat quality 😔😔😔

I was excited to try their fishes but were met with these disappointments 😔😔😔

Realising after finishing the food, there are 2 more stalls selling whole fishes (SG Chinese steamboat style and Malay/cina style). So you'll just visit this stall if you want China flavours such as mala and sushi cai fish dishes which I supposed it's popular among the younger folks. 😂
author: Fyn

review_text: Ordered HK steamed fish king grouper head but got back home to realise I got asam head seabass fish instead. Taste wise is okay but the eggplant is under cooked. Pls compensate the difference that I was shortchanged!
author: Pinzheng Zhang

review_text: excellent taste and meal.. great value for the dollar too.. had the steamed Seabass with Nyonya Assam Sauce.. found the sauce on par with any restaurant i have tried, in various cities in Malaysia.  This stall is a real hidden gem
author: RotiJohn

review_text:
Amazing fish at an amazing price. I dont think you can find this anywhere else in Singapore. The curry sea bass is also delicious!

Hope more people can find them!
author: Curtis Neo

review_text:
Steam Fish YB offer affordable steam fish at a hawker setting

You can’t go wrong with Assam fish and a bowl or white rice the assam gravy is sour and tasty and very appetizing
author: Kenneth Choo

review_text: Located in a new generation hawker centre that is very modern looking. The stall was closing when I wanted to order so the boss was feeling generous and gave me loads of ingredients for my lontong. The food was served piping hot so it's super delicious. Will return to try other dishes!
author: Sandra

review_text: Located within the newly revamped jurong west food centre. They have good chinese breakfast, taste wise, it was pretty standard. Priced was around $5, which was kinda expensive.

review_text: The price is ridiculously pricey. Noodle, lady finger, zai er and take away box was $4.80. Not recommended at all.

review_text: I won’t say the food looks fantastic but taste is not bad. Not to mention the stall owner is generous. For the commenter below, you can order their $4 meal and you can select any 3 dishes. She gave quite big portions of zai er and curry veg for me. Cheap enough for their stall rental price.
author: Jiabin Tang

review_text: My favourite vegetarian food! Friendly services and reasonable prices! I am not fond of vegetarian but I make sure to eat here daily :)

review_text: They served me lukewarm hor fun, and it didn’t even take them long to cook it. It honestly felt like they might have just given me someone else’s food.

review_text: First time ordering mutton tulang pizza and it did not disappoint. Sauce was spicy and mutton was well marinated. We ordered 2 hawaiian, garden veggie and mutton tulang. All pizzas were buzzing! Delivery also came 2 mins early👏👏👏
author: Yasotha Jayabalan

review_text:
We had an amazing experience celebrating a birthday at Canadian 2 for 1 Pizza! The service was top-notch - friendly, attentive, and accommodating. Our server went above and beyond to make sure our party felt special.

And the pizza was delicious! We loved the variety of toppings and the 2-for-1 deal is a fantastic value.

But what really made our experience stand out was the partnership with the next-door coffee shop! They allowed us to use their tables and chairs to accommodate our large group, which was incredibly kind and convenient. We were able to enjoy our pizza and coffee in a comfortable and spacious setting. Thank you to both businesses for making our birthday celebration so special!

Highly recommend Canadian 2 for 1 Pizza and their neighboring coffee shop for any occasion. They truly made our celebration memorable.
author: Kong Ming Loh

review_text:
Ordered pizza for a party of 10 and the pizza came 5 mins earlier than the expected time. Speed delivery!

Delicious pizza and a convenient, fuss-free option for parties and/or events. Definitely will order again.
author: Samantha Suliyanto

review_text: Tried the garden veggie pizza and loved it! fresh ingredients, flavourful sauce, and a perfect crust. It’s not always easy to find something that fits my diet and still tastes amazing. friendly boss! definitely swing by to try :)
author: louie life

review_text:
Canadian Pizza in the west sideeee! 🙌🏻

Had pizza delivery for my family and it was good - the food delivered was still hot, the crust was great and the portions were generous! It is definitely worth re-ordering again! 💖

IG - @adblehs / @at.foodcrawls ✨
author: Amanda Tay

review_text:
The food was really good and tasty! Thought it would be a normal cafe but it exceeded our expectations. The music playlist was a total vibe as well. It was quiet and this cafe needs more attention for the quality it’s offering. I live at the east and came to Chinese Garden to visit and was happy we made the choice to have our food at Canopy. The service was also really nice and warm.

We had smoked duck , fish and chips, Caesar Salad , calamari , chicken pesto and margarita and tea
author: Hueing L

review_text: Pretty good, I must say, despite being pricey. The smoked salmon salad was good. And the crispy chicken starter was great (loved the sauce). Was it because I was hungry after birding? 🤣. Came back here for beer-battered fish and chips on 18/Feb/26. They make good stuff, really.
author: Vinchel Budihardjo

review_text:
Arrived late evening for dinner and was pleasantly surprised by the restaurant's stunning design and spacious layout. The ambiance was soothing and relaxing, with nice background music – although a slightly toned-down volume would enhance the vibe.

The pasta dishes were all delicious, though the chili crab flavor was a tad too spicy for my taste. Overall, it's a fantastic spot to dine, with friendly and cheerful service that adds to the welcoming atmosphere. Kudos to the service team!
author: Viny W

review_text:
Food is decent and the ambience was pretty good. Though sitting beside the purple light was a bit distracting and uncomfortable.

Really liked the crispy pork, it was juicy and tender on the inside, didn’t feel too oily as well. The wait for the food was a little long considering the groups of people around us. Staff were nice as well.

Overall a pretty good restaurant in located within chinese garden!
author: Junyi Wu

review_text:
We were pleasantly surprised by the food quality. Price is on the higher side but for the quality, it's worth it... Except for the overpriced drinks. Good place to dine after a leisurely morning walk/jog around the serene water features and greenery.

I had the spicy soft shell crab pasta and I was definitely not expecting the softshell crab to be done so well. Most places mess this up by making it too soggy oily. Theirs were light, well seasoned and fried at the correct oil temperature. Resulting is a crispy light batter while remaining juicy insidem the pasta itself has quite a bit of heat which compliments the crab well. My friends commented that their mains were also delicious.
author: Fel Ong

review_text: If I can give 0 star, I will. The auntie is extremely rude and she keeps screaming at customers.

review_text:
346A Kang Ching Road. The fat Chinese lady has an attitude problem, have bought from this stall many times because we live nearby. This fat Chinese woman will show attitude when placing your order, the way she ask you is as if she is unhappy to take your order. It’s like you’re making her work and she can’t rest. review_text:
Braved more than an hour long bus commute for a satisfying early BKT breakfast. Located in a laid back neighbourhood that's a 4 minute walk from the bus stop. It's along the same row as Richie's Curry Puff and is around the corner from the Yuhua Market and Food Center.

The stall was founded in 1985 and I first had a taste around 2004. The broth was still rich and delicious but not as peppery as I remembered. Meat was fall-off-the bone tender and I liked their preserved vegetable which wasn't salty, sour or oily. Soup was self-serve refillable up to two times. All in, the meal was wallet friendly at $9.90. Give this heritage food business a try.
author: Pretty Catmint

review_text:
Ordered pork rib for $7, rice 70¢ and preserve vege for $1. Wait time was around 20min.

Pro

Pork rib. Reasonable off the bone not the most disintegrative but plastic spoonable. Can also taste the pork due to mild soup.

Meh
Soup. Erm too mild man. Barely peppery I can see people who will like this mild taste but not up my alley.

4 pieces of rib cost $7 is kinda steep preserve vege amount was good though.

review_text: Joo Siah Bak Koot Teh. Famous For Their Prime Ribs Bak Kut Teh.Have To Be Early, The Prime Ribs Always After 11.00 Am. The Braised Pork Knuckles Is Another Must Ordered Dish. Braised Tau Kee. Served With White Steamed Rice. That Will Be A Great Combination. Old School Taste . You Can Refilled The Bak Kut Teh Soup. Yummy😋. Singapore Local Favourite Place .
author: Tan Meng Geok

review_text:
Bak Koot Teh or pork ribs soup is a great example of creating comfort through minimal but impactful ingredients. The warming pork bone broth harmonises with garlic and crushed black pepper, keeping customers going back for bowl after bowl. The meat on the ribs is tender and moist, lifted further by dipping into dark soy sauce with chilli padi for a hint of sweetness, umami, and spice.

Premium loin ribs soup or 龙骨茶is only available in the mornings. Often combined with rice or mee sua (wheat vermicelli), getting a side of dough fritters to soak up the soup is also delicious. Braised pork leg and preserved vegetables are also commonly ordered together with the pork ribs soup.

review_text:
I was quite disappointed with my visit today. Upon arrival, I was informed that there was no dine-in available, and only takeaway was allowed. There were only four tables open for dining in, which wasn’t mentioned anywhere on your Facebook, Google, or Instagram pages.

On top of that, I had to place my order through the app, meaning CDC vouchers couldn’t be used since payment had to be made online. Even the tap water was disabled, so there wasn’t anywhere to wash my hands before eating. When I asked about this arrangement, the staff mentioned it was due to a lack of manpower.

Taste wise, it was also disappointing this time. The Shanghai steamed chicken dumplings tasted sour, as if they were spoiled, and the porridge was very bland. It would’ve helped if pepper and soy sauce were available, but there was nothing on the tables, just empty chairs and tables left for diners. The lemon sour plum drink I bought was literally cordial lime juice with 1 slice of lemon and 2 sour plum. $3.40 for that.

I’ve visited a few times before and found the food to be moderate, but after this experience, I don’t think I’ll be returning.

YTF: ingredients are decent and would say pretty fresh and you get to add your own condiments

LCR: opted for brown rice without the green soup and add bittergourd+egg plant(both were yummy). Ingredients of tofu, different variety of vegetables were on the bland side which makes it healthier. Asked for chilli and it was some dark brownish looking dip that was meh. A chilli that enhances the flavour of rice+ingredients, that would be great!

After eating, there are shops for one to explore around the neighbourhood.

author: Honest Review

review_text:
Visited WellSmooch recently and absolutely loved the experience! It’s such a perfect spot for vegetarians, with a menu that’s thoughtfully curated and full of flavourful options. The café has a warm and inviting atmosphere: cozy, modern, and perfect for a relaxing meal or dessert date.

I tried the Kaya Pandan Ice Cream with Waffles, and it was simply divine! The combination of the fragrant kaya pandan flavour with the crisp, fluffy waffles was perfect, comforting, nostalgic, and delicious all at once. Every bite had the right balance of sweetness and texture, making it one of the standout desserts I’ve had in a while.

We also ordered the Pizza, and it was fantastic! The crust was light and crispy, with toppings that tasted fresh and well-seasoned. You can tell a lot of care goes into how each dish is made everything felt wholesome, satisfying, and crafted with attention to detail.

The overall experience at WellSmooch was wonderful. The food, the atmosphere, and the friendly service all made it memorable. It’s definitely a must-visit for anyone looking for great vegetarian-friendly food and amazing desserts. I’ll surely be back to try more items from their menu, especially their ice creams!

They used to have an amazing hazelnut chocolate ice cream but I think they no longer make it. I guess they opted to do more Asian and local flavours (e.g. durian (maybe only during CNY period) and matcha too). We had their pandan ice cream which was refreshing and peanut butter cookie ice cream (w waffles of course) yesterday. So good.

They use cashew cream instead of store-bought processed fake cheese, which tastes better than fake cheese imo. Glad they have survived COVID and the harsh economy which hit the FnB industry pretty badly (even worse for vegetarian/vegan places). Hope they will continue to stay around for as long as I live haha.

author: Mervyn Lim

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text:
Terrible service despite decent food.
I’ve been to Siam Square Mookata a few times and the food is generally good, but my recent experience was unacceptable. We ordered a normal plate of garlic chicken, but they served a large plate instead. When we checked the bill, they had changed our order in the system and charged us almost triple the price.

When we raised this to the cashier, she didn’t care at all. Her exact attitude was basically, “so what, you guys already ate it.” No apology, no explanation, nothing. Just pure rudeness and zero accountability.
author: Li Xinwei

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text:
Absolute rubbish of a place. Worst mookata place. Burner is stupid slow, so I asked for a gas change but dude showed me some casino sleight of gas burner hand. Plate remained not hot. Food quality is terrible, the beef shabu smells off like left for days. It has some strange aftertaste and even if just cooked a little it bricked up. The pork liver is really bad, I don’t know how to describe this. It’s hard and tasteless and comes in too many small pieces, lots to flip. The veggie platter has really unfresh vegetables and the corn comes scattered onto the basket like salt bae was back in the kitchen. And the bowl just couldn’t hold that much and the corn would roll off anytime so I had to pour them over the hot plate and chopstick them into the gutters. Honestly the experience is really bad I hate it. I wonder if anybody actually ate and run over here. The only saving grace is the mama noodle which we have at least some control of. If I could write a hundred review of this mookata outlet I would. This place needs to stop giving such bad food and service. Also their sauces looked fermented in their bin.

You see I’m no food gourmet or Gordon ramsey’s godson I’m just an everyday guy who decided to eat mookata once every 2mths and I’m just absolutely destroyed. I worry if my stomach gonna ache.
author: Harry Rettop

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text:
Disappointed with the service here. We came with 9 pax and were told to squeeze into one table, which made no sense, so we requested 2 tables — 4 and 5 pax. The cashier auntie already seemed unhappy about having to set up another mookata pot and gave us a really bad attitude. Later when we asked (politely) about the free ice cream promotion — which we know is usually available with a minimum spend — she completely ignored us, black face, and acted like she didn’t hear. Honestly, if it’s not available anymore, just say so. No need for that kind of attitude. We’re paying customers, not asking for a favour.

To top it off, another staff member who lights the pots decided to clear our table without a word — just told the cleaner to remove our bowls and utensils and let another group sit down, without even informing us first. That’s not how you treat customers.

Food is okay, but the service is really off-putting. Not sure if I’d return. Staff need serious training on basic courtesy.
author: Precious

review_text:
The fast food here is exactly what you want when you’re craving something quick and satisfying. The service is fast, the staff is friendly, and the food comes out hot and fresh most of the time. The burgers are juicy, the fries are crispy, and the portions are decent for the price.
The menu has a good variety, making it easy to find something whether you’re in the mood for a classic combo or a quick snack. While it can get busy during peak hours, the wait is usually reasonable.
Overall, it’s a solid choice for a quick meal when you’re on the go. Reliable, tasty, and affordable—just what fast food should be.
author: Jennifer Joy Desullan

review_text:

I can guarantee you that her sole of her feet will never feel good after 8 hours of standing and it’s gonna ache for a long period of time due to the weight exert to her legs thus I truly feel heartache for her.

So I am very impressed with  own customer service skills & never give up working attitude thus this is highly recommendable especially when Burger King have so many people during dinner timing which is around 745pm thereabout on 6.2.26 (Friday evening) hence Saleema is a very awesome and good staff to have as she is willing to go the extra mile to serve their customers at the shop which is a rare gesture nowadays as I do not see any Burger King staff who will do such a caring gesture when come to serving of customers.

Most importantly is that she did not show any sign of impatience body language when she face so many different customers over at the ordering counter hence this small gesture already deserves my utmost respect.

So I am very confident to comment and compliment that Saleema is a very responsible, attentive and detail oriented lady because I work from a very small role in my finance career until only 3 years ago I got promoted as a Director of Sales when I start working in finance industry at age 26 and till now I am 43 years old already.

I have my utmost confidence that Saleema is very capable and competent for her work and job duties from the way she serves me.

Henceforth, she definitely deserve a pay raise and promotion for her effort in serving clients and going the extra mile for servicing me and making me feel so happy and fully satisfied and literally will want to patronise Westmall Burger King outlet more.

If not, please kindly arrange a session to compliment her in front of all the staff for her awesome and splendid customer service cause she truly deserved it and all other employees should literally take her as a role model to learn from.

Lastly I sincerely hope the higher management will take serious consideration on my feedback written especially for Saleema. Thank you.

review_text:
Wa. This is the kind of food you look at it and wonder why is it $5, until it tasted like $15 on your first bite!

author: HR Lim

review_text:
Fei Fei Wanton Mee serves one of the most satisfying bowls around. The char siew is extremely tender, juicy and nicely caramelised — easily one of the best parts of the meal. Their duck is also very tasty, soft and flavourful without being too oily. The noodles are cooked perfectly with a good springy texture, and the wantons are fresh and well-seasoned.

However, be prepared for a long queue, especially during peak hours. The service can be quite slow, so waiting is expected. That said, the food quality usually makes the wait worthwhile. Even with the slower pace, the staff still try their best to handle the crowd.

Overall, if you don’t mind queueing, Fei Fei Wanton Mee is worth a visit for its tender char siew, tasty duck and perfectly cooked noodles. It’s a solid bowl that keeps people coming back despite the long wait.
author: M S

review_text:
Having tried the one at Orchard which tasted really good, we wanted to find out how the original one tasted so here we are!

⏰ arrived on a Wednesday morning at 0838, and got our food at 0857. The queue was significantly longer once we started queuing, very lucky indeed. But 20 minutes for half the alley puts the total queue time beyond 40 minutes once it stretches out of that small alley, something to consider when spotting the queue.

🍝 I ordered their traditional wanton noodle option, with roast pork on one and roast duck on the other, to see how those “miscellaneous” meat tastes.

Char siew 5 stars, no doubt their signature, as good as the one in Orchard, with bits of char that adds to the flavour. Wanton 5 stars, definitely will opt for the combination of these 2 in future. Roast pork 3.5 stars, good but not one that i’m fully sold, had better ones. Roast duck 3.5 stars, the skin did have some flavour but not perfect, and i requested for breast meat but wasn’t given that so some points off that too.

Overall, I would be most willing to queue 30-40 minutes tops for their amazing wanton mee, but nothing more in terms of time and meat.
author: YY

review_text:
The sio bak isn't just crispy - biting it is a tectonic event. It has a distinct, airy crackle that tastes like pure, salted indulgence. One bite and you’ll understand why the queue is so long everyday. Then there’s the char siew that’s been charred to a sticky, smoky, caramelized perfection. And don't forget the duck too! Go for the three meat combo with noodles - it's the best thing that's happened to Jurong, other than the MRT.

I’ve posted some tips on visiting this stall on my Instagram @iamgettingfat. Do check it out :)
author: I am getting fat!

The small little pieces of pork lard was really good and flavourful. Nice umami taste of the soup but just a little too salty for me. Conclusion : The char siew and roasted meats are the drawing factor. Else don’t bother
