Highly recommend for anyone looking for nice and affordable satay. The portal to order is easy to use and staff are prompt to response to your order.
author: Lionel Lim

review_text: Chicken and mutton satay is well marinated and taste awesome but the satay gravy is too diluted. I opt for self collection. Friendly staff but driver is kinda rude. Payment can be done in cash or paynow. Overall experience is good.
author: Wee nee Tan

review_text: Delivery was on time and cake in good condition. The macaroons maintained their usual standard. Only one thing is they did not read or bother about the instructions. I have requested for words to be written on the cake. Based on some photos of the same cake across the media, this can be done. There was no contact number to check if the special instruction will be done. No one contacted me as well. So if you have specific instructions, it is best to contact them and ask before placing order.
author: Shuzhen Lai

review_text:
We got the cake exactly the same design we requested. The eat is light and not very sweet that kids able to enjoy.
Thank you for such lovely cake.
author: Crystal Low

review_text: Thank you, Annabella Patisserie, for being flexible in changing our order and making my son’s school birthday celebration go smoothly. The children loved the cupcakes — they were so cute and delicious! Highly recommended for birthday parties and as gifts.
author: Hay Dary

review_text: The macaron cupcakes were picture perfect and yummy! It was great for preschool birthday celebration as were easy to give out by the kids. Great customer service and timely delivery too.
author: Xinyi

review_text: Ordered cookies n cream dino bday cake for my boy. Its sooo yummy, cream is not heavy , cake is moist ! The brownie n financier too . definitely will repeat order
author: Jessica k

review_text: Dropped by Ajisen Tanjiro and had a pleasant meal. Interesting to note that it shares staff with Mama Klang, so service was smooth and familiar. The ramen was enjoyable — comforting broth, decent noodles, and satisfying portions. Also tried the dumplings, which were nicely pan-fried with a good balance of juiciness and crispness
author: Loki

review_text:
Visited Ajisen Tanjiro on Tuesday, 09 Dec 2025 for dinner with my partner. The place was quite empty, with only one other customer. They offer free boiled eggs, which is a nice touch — I ended up having two.

My partner ordered the Volcano Ramen. It wasn’t as spicy as expected, even after he asked for chilli powder. The noodles were decent and the flavour was alright, though the texture lacked the springiness you’d usually expect from good ramen.

On the bright side, the meal was very affordable — $39+ including GST for both of us. For that price, it’s hard to complain.

Overall, Ajisen Tanjiro is a decent option for a simple, casual meal when you don’t feel like spending too much. Just don’t expect high-end ramen standards.
author: Yiling Lai

review_text:
Visited Ajisen Tanjiro for dinner and the place was pretty packed, which shows it’s still a popular spot. They offer free boiled eggs, which is a nice touch, though I personally didn’t eat them since I’m not a fan.
I ordered the Volcano Ramen, and while it’s still spicy, it’s definitely not as intense as it used to be about 12 years ago. The noodle quality wasn’t great — the texture felt weak and lacked that springiness you’d expect from good ramen.
On the bright side, the meal is very affordable. At $21 including GST, it’s hard to complain too much. They also give a portion of mentaiko to pair with the noodles, which was an interesting addition. Not mind-blowing, but a fun twist.
Overall, Ajisen Tanjiro is a value-for-money ramen option, good for a casual meal when you don’t want to spend too much. Just don’t come expecting high ramen standards.
author: Ming Shen Tham

review_text: Good service. Not queue during weekend lunch. Service was prompt. Food wise mostly above average. Dry style Ramen was quite unique. Serving size was above average. Set meals were value for money.
author: 7eleven

review_text: Ramen is delicious and it comes with free eggs and fish roe for this period!
author: nick yee

review_text: Very good portion of food for 10 pax. Savouring and not greasy Teochew dishes. Love their cold platter as well as how well they steamed fishes. Staff is super friendly too. Definitely worth going back again.
author: Jennis Ng

review_text: been here afew times which i find their duck not bad. but sadly today the staff actually recommended a pot of fish porridge with 20% off promotion which cost $100+. the fish is horrible with the typical fishy smell. very disappointed… for those who encounter their promotion next time please dont order that.
author: Murphy Chng

review_text:
I would not advice anyone to specifically travel down the area to eat here. If you’re nearby and want some teochew fish porridge then sure, it’s an okay bowl, but I think kopitiams or coffee shops would be a better deal than this restaurant. Plus point, is that they don’t charge service charge, maybe that’s the reason why the service was so horrible 😂

Other than their teochew porridge, we ordered some alacarte sides: seafood spring roll and teochew ngoh hiang. Please don’t get them. They turned up lukewarm and bad.

All in all, they got worse over the years.
author: scrap sd

review_text: Decided to visit this restaurant due to out of idea of where to eat and the location is near to my home. Their service was ok but their staff quite "hard sell" when taking our order. The portion of food is fair enough but the taste, foods were too oily, greasy, served in warm condition and it's overpriced ($220 for 5 dishes). Definitely would not visit this restaurant again.
author: Huan Choon

review_text:
Apologies for the lengthy review, but much needs to be considered before a 3-star is justified.

The atmosphere and decor is shabby for its restaurant price, resembling the nearby heartland stores.

When we were seated, the expensive, not-worth-it (based on other reviews) set menu (the only one at that point) was already on the table. A single ala-carte menu was provided to the table of 4 at request. The waitress never left post "menu delivery". A 2 second pause before the aggressive upselling began as she repeatedly asked if we'd like to order their fish (likely most expensive) and other seafood dishes (dingdingding! Service 2, max). When we asked her to give us a while, we were given about 10 seconds before the process was repeated. Had to ask her explicitly to return at a later time. I wish some of the other servers who deserved at least a 4 didn't have to be dragged into this bad review, but giving any more than a 2 is inaccurate to the experience.

FOOD: Nice rice, has a good bite. Meat platter was of good quality, at normal price of $24 for that quantity. Oyster egg was a bit heavier  than what I'm used to, a little like biting into an oil-soaked sponge, but still good. Stir fried kway teow was a little tasteless but the noodles had a good texture. The "Haa Zhor(?)?" wasn't disastrous, basically fried fishcakes with sriracha mayo. Steer clear, it's the same price as the meat platter!!!!

Recommended? No. Would I return? No. Apologies to the restaurant for this stinking review. I would much prefer the food at the many hawker centres in the very nearby Bukit Batok West Shopping Centre.
author: Brandon Yeow

review_text:
Overall, we had a pleasant experience at the restaurant. The restaurant was in a ballroom, with a cozy atmosphere. It was a Monday lunch and we were the only family there and the restaurant was empty. Honestly, we felt it was a little awkward but the food made our time worthwhile. The ala-carte buffet they offer has a wide assortment of vegetables, meats and delicacies, some of which can be ordered once only. There were crabs, cod fish, prawns, desserts and many more were served quickly when ordered. The birthday person (which was me) could eat free.

However, service could have been improved. When asking the waiter regarding the birthday discount, she could have been friendlier and gave a smile or perhaps wished me well. The serving of food was a little unprofessional and the waitress could have been more proactive in clearing plates, pouring drinks since there was nobody else and they were free. More effort could have been put in to make the extra mile to make our experience an even memorable one.

Other than that, the food is certainly commendable. The price is attractive and the restaurant is recommended.
author: Joshua Chew

review_text: Veryy good banquet service , had my graduation here at HillTop Garden. The Banquet servers here were very nice and gave us a full jar of Fruit punch for our table. They were very nice as well.
author: Lwin Thant Maung

review_text: I was there yesterday for the dinner buffet to celebrate one of my friend's birthday. 3 of us plus FOC for the birthday person. The taste of the food are okay but some dishes are cold and some are too dry after deep frying. The portion are small but just right so we can order a variety to try. They served the dishes quite promptly after we placed our order but to get their attention was a tad bit difficult as the tables are fully seated with customers but they're were only like 5 waiter and waitresses, except for the bubble soya which I have to keep asking for it when other tables can get theirs right after they were seated.
author: Zyin W

review_text:
Went there for a weekend buffet lunch for $34.80 per-pax excluding gst and service charge fee of 10%.

Ordered almost the entire menu lol! Some hits and some misses but mostly good. Just to name a few of the good ones, e.g. fried rice, mee suah, smoked duck, garlic pork belly, char siew, teriyaki fried fish, chilli crab, cordyceps prawn, salted egg prawn, sweet sour pork, etc.

The cod fish, roasted chicken, sambal kangkung, buddha jump over the wall, thai fried chicken, wasabi roasted pork, braised pork in steamed bun, and fried spring roll, not so great.

The setting and dining environment is in a wedding restaurant. The props and deco are still there. Just something to take note of. Not a romantic setting that you would bring your gf unless you plan to get married after the meal.

They also offer free dining for birthday month, just show them your IC and that will do.

Overall happy with the experience, service is quite fast despite full house as they do not have shortage of waiter and waitress.

Book in advance to avoid disappointment.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
Writing the review now as
I have collected all feedback from family and friends.
Had our lunch wedding early this year, in March25. The only awesome thing is the food was great. All the guest loved the food. But alot were offended by the service. BQT staff were ALL late, even an hour after our contracted time. We had to turn on the aircon, set up the location ourselves. There were no snacks or drinks served to our guests upon arrival as the BQT staff were not ready. So our guest sat at empty tables, without beverages as they waited for the wedding to start. Our lunch was abit rushed through by the staff and I (bride) was shocked the main table was cleared even before I realised it. We hated the music for the food walk in, we actually had our selected music that was not played. Again, the food was great. But the courses came too fast. Nearing the end of our lunch, according to our guests, the staff told them to leave as they needed to clear the room. However, we had another 1&1/2 hour to the room as per contract. So we were surprised people were getting up and leaving. And in-front of EVERYONE, they were clearing the tables, removing table cloths, etc
Overall, my family and I am upset at the lack of professionalism and hospitality provided. We did enjoy the food, and I personally really like the fish and dessert course.
author: Baileys Kreme

review_text: Waking up late morning and went over for lunch . Ordered Chicken rice that came with a delicious Radish soup. Still the same taste and portion was good 👍 👍
author: Philip Kung

review_text:
Not trying to be a karen, but this happens everytime I visit this branch. Clearly those other dine in orders fries are filled to the brim, meanwhile,  my fries are always shortchanged.

One staff had to be very rude when I told her about the fries issue, not sure her name but without specs, still can tell me fries will reduce in size after its not hot so will go down. I understand fnb staff are underpaid but don’t bullshit me like this okay?

The other malay staff with specs was kind enough to actually give me my portion back, credits to her for really being nice.
author: Rawr Only

review_text: The worst customer service ever experienced at a McDonald's in Singapore, don’t care whatever your order is express but you still need to wait more than 20mins to collect the order and this supervisor attitude very rude and impolite a very contemptuous attitude towards customers. She doesn't deserve the title she's receiving.
author: thanh ngoc nguyen

review_text: Breakfast at McDonald's is no longer packed not because we are lucky on a Sunday morning but because of the generosity.  What was in the picture is the "BIG" breakfast w/out the hash brown.  Guess it's now under kids meal section with adult prices.
author: Leethal Ho

review_text: The worst customer service ever experienced at a McDonald's in Singapore. Messed up my order and then still argued about it very rudely and never apologized at all. Was just passing through and wanted to have a nice time with my son. Such a pity this is what you have to put up with. For the record my local McDonald's is absolutely lovely and I'm greeted and dealt with like part of the family.
author: Wayne Rice

review_text:
Hidden Gem.
Didn't know about this place until I brought my child to Kids Stop
Very nice mutton brayani
Mutton is soft, chunky meaty and yummy.
Gravy is very good. Mix well with the brayani.
Serving looked small at first. As I dig in then I realized portion is big.
Good environment to sit down a chill for few hours waiting for my child 😁
author: Tony Too

review_text:
We went yesterday, Ms. Chithra provided excellent service. She was very welcoming and attentive.
We ordered biryani rice, naan, and paneer masala, and everything was delicious.
My children enjoyed the food very much.
Thank you, Ms. Chithra, for your warm hospitality.
This is the best restaurant—h
ygienic, with great flavors in their food.
author: Geetha Kalyan

review_text: Pretty decent Indian food if you're at science center! Cheese and keema naan is very good. There's kids meal with nuggets too
author: Colin Tan

review_text:
Butter Naan was so good. We finished every bite. Also ordered the butter chicken, mango lassi and masala tea. Grateful for a good meal and table service after all the tiring fun at Science Centre.

Comfortable and clean dining area, personal wet wipes provided too!
author: B W Y

review_text:
We had lunch for 5 pax. Dishes that we tried:
Basket naan: ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Combo of 3 types of naan. Value for money. Definitely a must order if you are having gravy dishes.

Gobi 65⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Crispy outside, soft inside. Packed with flavor.

Butter chicken ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Good balance of creamy, sweet and tangy.

Black lentil⭐️⭐️⭐️
Hot and tad bit spicy for our liking.

Lamb Briyani ⭐️⭐️⭐️
Rice cooked with perfection. But not very generous with protein.

Mango lassi⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Best Mango lassi

Ice Masala Tea ⭐️⭐️⭐️
I prefer hot masala tea

No service tax !!
author: Steven Tan

review_text: A big organisation should know better. The takeaway plastic bag was poorly designed and caused the drinks to overflow. This is not good service, especially when other chains like Burger King provide proper drink-holding bags.
author: David soh

review_text:
Ordered today at 18:17pm 12 Feb 26

As you can see my fries amount are only given halved..
Contacted McDonald Customer Service and it seem it doesn’t compensate and required 3-5 working days just for fries issue….

Food prices went up and i expect the services to be better but guess it becoming poorer. Let see if it become as bad as KFC 😂😂
author: Teck Beng

review_text: Fries should be hot and crispy. This fries is obviously pre fry for couple of hours before serving to customers. So disgusting. Cold fries 😡
author: Lina Tay

review_text: This outlet never ever will deliver the order in full. They will definitely miss out an item or two. It's been years. Today, right now I have an missing item again. Order a sundae and they only deliver a spoon. To the staffs, please handle your order properly. You have not been doing your job all this years. As for the manager, your team is not efficient, not alert all this years. Do something!
author: Andy Chee

review_text: Had dinner at McDonald’s Bukit Batok. The space was clean and comfortable, and the food was good as always. However, the service was disappointing—we waited over 20 minutes for our meal. Order receipts were just stacking up, and nothing was being called out. Only after we approached the counter did the crew check and hand over the food. Definitely needs better order handling and faster service.
author: Benedict Correya

review_text: I was here today to meet a friend for lunch. It has been a very long time since I visited this place, and I was greatly impressed by it. The restaurant is not just your usual Indian Muslim restaurant, but IMO a multi-cuisine place, offering South and North Indian food, Western food and also - and this is where it's more than the usual Indian Muslim restaurant - Nasi Padang and Western-style cakes. My friend and I had an Indian rojak platter here - TBH I was drawn to (I have not seen before) blue-coloured flour ball with bean sprouts. The Indian rojak was very good. The service here was also very good - very professional and very attentive. The dining ambience was comfortable for a non-airconditioned setting as it was very well-ventilated. I highly recommend this place - in particular because it's open 24/7.
author: edtayjb

review_text: The nasi lemak is horrendously artificially dyed. Real pandan leaves won't stain rice green but slightly turn the rice yellow and fragrant.The nasi lemak paste and other ingredients are great. Healthier options are available for drinks upon ordering if you like less sugar. Great place for meals. Nice and helpful staff.
author: Chew

review_text: The restaurant stays open until late at night and serves Malay, Thai, and Indian dishes. We tried the North Indian chicken, Maggi mee, and prata — all were delicious and reasonably priced. If you live nearby, it’s definitely worth a visit, though not something I’d travel a long way for.
author: Forest House

review_text: Food was average. Service was quick, orders were served quite fast. However, gotta agree with some of the reviews that the ordering system is not the most desirable. It'd be best if we could order and make e-payment through the website, and not need to go to the counter to settle the bill. Also, there was a very strong sewage smell during our visit, which made our dining experience less enjoyable.
author: Rlyejayn

review_text: Always a delightful experience here… a customer since 5-10 yrs ago… Alhamdulilah food & drink is off quality served hot everytime … this is chicken afghan, naan butter & nasi daging merah … the teh tarek sedap… silky smooth… Masya Allah alhamdulilah
author: Sofia Cullen

review_text:
Solid Comfort Food – But Be Ready for the Q!

​Satay Bee Hoon is my go-to comfort meal, and this stall does a consistently solid job. It's not the absolute best I've ever tasted, but it is definitely above standard, thanks mostly to the sauce.

​Their satay sauce is perfectly executed—it's just the right consistency, not too watery or too dry, and the crushed peanuts are spot on. I also really appreciate that the accompanying ingredients are perfectly blanched and not marinated, letting that sauce be the main star.

​The downside is purely logistical: they're only open about four times a week, and the queue is infamously long.

​My recommendation is balanced: If you are nearby and the queue is short, absolutely give it a try. But if you have to drive a long distance and wait for more than 15 minutes, you can probably skip it. Jia you (keep it up) to the owners!
author: Elaina Poh

review_text: Hawker centre setting so there isn't air con but very windy as the place seems newly renovated. Queued for almost 30 minutes before the lunch time crowd kicks in. Ingredients are fresh and cooked on the spot. The gravy for both satay and cuttlefish kangkong bee hoon are spot on. Glad we ordered tabao together with eat in. Most patrons seem to eat this satay bee Hoon when we walked about to explore other stalls.
author: Patrick Goh

review_text: Not usually one to gravitate towards satay bee hoon, but this dish completely changed my mind; really delicious, with fresh and generous ingredients. Good satay bee hoon is hard to come by in Singapore, so it’s definitely worth the queue.
author: ms __

review_text:
The satay bee hoon was great. The sauce was great and $5 one came w a prawn and a slice or 2 of lean pork too.
However will give the Kang Kong cuttlefish a pass as I am not a fan of sweet sauce . It was Served w ah-cha thus when mixed felt not compatible too imo.
At one price of $7, serving was huge thou w lot of cuttlefish too. Overall not my favourite.
U can use QR or CDC voucher to pay.
Super long Q at lunch time but Q moved very fast.
Stalls closed at about 2:30pm or earlier.
author: Dan Wuang

review_text:
My favourite food since Ngee Ann Poly days over a decade ago. Been craving for it but it’s really out of the way for me. Finally was able to conveniently eat it after enrolling to SUSS evening classes but timetable had to set it on their off days.

Maybe one day I’ll just decided to be late for class and have it! Hopefully still taste as good! To be updated..
author: Kong Wen Sheng

review_text:
In the same coffeeshop as Yi Pin Vegetarian Stall, Delisnacks sells vegan/vegetarian pastries and fried foods like fried dough sticks ( You Tiao ), curry puffs, butterfly buns, red bean buns, salted buns, sesame balls etc.
Cheap and delicious, great if you don’t want a heavy meal.
author: Yellow Bear

review_text: Add meat and egg only, $9.10?! I even asked twice to confirm double. The worker was being tone-deaf and gave me a unreasonable attitude, but I gave the benefit of the doubt because the surroundings were kinda noisy.
author: Teo Jia Le, Tonny

review_text:
Auntie is moody, can’t be bothered to take order

$4.80 for century egg and minced pork congee.. I barely can find minced pork.  A total ripped off haha! Won’t ever eat this stall again.

Cant be bothered to replenish their chili sauce also. Lazy to max

The cost price of the congee is at most $0.50 excluding Labour

Damn. I have to order extra dishes from the CaiFan stall to mix with the congee.

Haha what a joke!!! 😂😂😂
author: Chia Zhenli

review_text: Chicken rice is good, but recently price had increased. Extra meat now is $7.80 vs previously only $6.50. Original price is $4.80 now.. $3 for extra meat which the chicken slices are so thin. Not coming again.
author: Tidus T

review_text: Requested for breast meat and it was super tender and nice. Rice has only slight fragrant but they are very fluffy. Overall I find it not bad! Portioning was just nice for me too.
author: Benito Linus

review_text: I hate brands who treats their online order more important than the customers who are physically there to queue for their food. All the customers behind me waited 20 mins just to process their online orders. Know your priorities! What the hell is wrong with them? How is this good for your stupid brand??? Over priced food $17.50 for 3 packets of chicken rice???? Seriously??? I DO NOT RECOMMEND THEIR CHICKEN RICE TO ANYONE
author: Alvin Tan

review_text: tucked in the corner of a residential area un Eng Kong is thus great Pizza hut takeout outlet. the place is conveniently located with lots of side street free parking to stop to order your pizza. everytime walked by there are someone stopping to order their food. it is also convenient location for the grab food delivery and Food panda guys to pick up their order. it makes a lot of sense.
author: Sam Goh SE

review_text: Really impressed with the service here. The team was welcoming and efficient. Food came out faster than expected and everything tasted amazing. Thank you for the great experience!
author: Patrisha Bitangcol

review_text:
Pizza's arrived cold, (I believe) under-cooked & and also made incorrectly with the wrong pizza delivered.  We supplied photos via the support process.

We could see while tracking the order, the pizzas had been made, then sat in the store getting cold and soggy, waiting for the delivery (this was a pizza hut direct order so no excuses blaming Grab). It was probably 30 mins they sat there, dying.

Customer support reasonable in fairness, offered to replace, but they wouldn't arrive for another 1 hour.  I stress the lady who called me back was lovely, certainly not her fault.

I have no idea how this chain is still in business, it's staff doesn't even bother to cook or check they're sending the right pizza, deliver  it promptly so it's not cold, or even cook it so the base isn't soggy.

Oh, the delivery rider who delivered the original order didn't bother knocking or ringing the bell either, just dumped it and left.

An extremely poor experience, unlikely to order again.  Worst pizza delivery I can remember.

Edit: For the record, I opened a support ticket, as per the feedback here, the ticket was closed with no action, feedback or anything.  Closed without even a comment or apology from the business.  Make of that what you will about this business and the way they treat their customers.
author: Scott

review_text: The pizza is freshly baked and very delicious! It's close to home, so we often come back to eat here! My friend and I both love it very much!
author: shenyi cheng

review_text: I recently walk in and ordered a Pizza at this outlet, and the service was exceptional! Nora was friendly, courteous, and ensured our order was accurate. The pizzas were hot and delicious, and the entire experience was seamless. Highly recommend Pizza Hut and Nora's excellent service!
author: Muhd Harry Hamzah

review_text:
Came on Sunday 12pm, waited for the restaurant to open. Not very easily accessible, have to walk from the nearest bus stop

Service was okay, managed to sit at the front table, with the food cooked infront of us.
Okonomiyaki size is about 6 inch, loaded with cabbage ($18 each)
Can choose 3 toppings of choice including seafood, poultry and vegetables
I feel that the okonomiyaki is not cooked till crispy type, they set a timer for each side, serve right on the dot. Inside was slightly mushy(?) may get abit jelak if u are eating the whole by yourself. Can add unlimited bonito flakes, so feel free to request!
The fried rice was very oily…. The bottom of the bowl was coated with oil. It was full of wokhei though but really too oily.
The torched scallops were delicious, but I would say for this four piece, it’s kind of not worth it.
Hot sake was smooth and nice
Would I come again? Maybe not… it was a good experience tho
author: Xiao Xuan

review_text: It’s a cozy and authentic okonomiyaki experience where you can cook your own pancakes right at the table. Everything at Ajiya was excellent! The potato mentaiko was absolutely addicting — creamy, savory, and full of flavor. The pork was damn good, tender and perfectly seasoned with their special sauce. The yakisoba were tasty too, with just the right texture and seasoning. I definitely be back the third time.
author: Hiang Ar

review_text: Visited on a Saturday around 12+, not much people yet and didn’t need to wait. Ordered the Okonomiyaki combo with tako, pork belly and grilled onions. Pretty good though size is not too big. The garlic fried rice was garlicky enough but could have been a bit saltier. Pork gyoza was not bad, can’t go wrong.
author: Vicky

review_text:
A nice spot for okonomiyaki if you prefer lighter flavors. The yakisoba and okonomiyaki are not overly flavorful, which makes them easy to enjoy without feeling too heavy. Everything tastes balanced and comforting.
Don’t miss their fried chicken — crispy on the outside, juicy inside, and surprisingly the highlight of the meal. Definitely a must-try 👍
author: Ken Lim

review_text:
The okonomiyaki tasted like something I could get at a pasar malam for a fraction of the price. It lacked soul. The rest of the dishes were mediocre at best. The real offender was the grilled mackerel, which tasted like cheap chopped canned fish soaked in vinegar.

I really wanted this to be a great meal — it was my one and only meal of the day, and I was brought far from my usual locations.

But alas, life had other plans.
author: yingers11

review_text: A lovely gem in the west! Ordered the sea prawns, patatas bravas, squid ink paella and tiramisu for dinner and was very impressed. The sea prawns stole the show with the amazing bisque and garlic, which provided so much flavour and umami. The patatas bravas were a surprise (we ordered this as there were many reviews about how good it was) as the potatos were soo crispy. Leaving the skins on was such a good touch as they added a great texture. The squid ink portion was really good for the price, we ordered the small portion and managed to finish everything. The tiramisu was then a great way to add the evening, my husband loved it and is even thinking of popping by to takeaway the dessert already, and even considering the tiramisu party portion for future gatherings. Will definitely be back to try more of the menu!
author: Melissa Tham

review_text:
The restaurant was lovely, had indoor and outdoor seating, wasn’t too huge. The Seafood & Squid Ink paella we had were fantastic and delicious at the given price point. The clams were generous in the Seafood Paella! The croquettes were good as an appetiser, however I would give the wok hey cauliflower a miss next time as it was quite bitter so we didn’t finished it.

Overall, it’s a good experience with the food! There are plenty of parking opposite and there are 2 bus stops as well so it’s convenient. I would love to return next time to try other dishes!
author: Jonas Ng

review_text: delicious spanish food! i loved the tapas and the paella. portions were decently sized, and everything was so flavorful. my only complaint is that it’s somewhat outdoors (indoor seating is still open air) and it could get hot sometimes. staff were also super friendly and attentive. definitely a must try if you are in the area! will be coming back for sure!
author: Francesca Teo

review_text: First time eating here and we were not disappointed. Dining is open but plenty of ceiling fans and air-con. Decor fairly modern. Lighting was good and bright. Went as a family of four and asked the chef what he recommended. All very good suggestions and was also willing to accommodate us. We had an array of tapas. Burrata with prosciutto, roasted potatoes with aioli, lovely focaccia bread and the oysters were fresh and prepared well. Our main course was the seafood and the chicken meat paella. Delicious although the seafood one was more to our liking. Red sangria was very nice too. Our water bottle was constantly refreshed. In all a positive experience. Would definitely go again. Although car parking is limited but there is surrounding HDB parking.
author: Alice Lee-MacAry

review_text: Really good Spanish food. All the dishes we had were a solid 💯 prawns were fresh. Grilled chicken was tender juicy. Squid ink paella was just so flavourful. My fav was the crispy potato w fried eggs!
author: Crystal Ho

restaurant_name: KOON Bak Kut Teh 坤肉骨茶
review_text: Came in without much expectation as it was a random stall that we jus wanted to quickly stop by for dinner after a tiring hike at bukit timah hill. The BKT soup was surprisingly not bad. It was a fine balance between being over powering in flavour and pepper. The prawn noodle and braised pork noodle was also rather decent. Would come back again if am craving for both BKT and prawn noodles.
author: Gabriel

restaurant_name: KOON Bak Kut Teh 坤肉骨茶
review_text:
My point of view and experience it got from here.
Steam egg is very salty. A lot of pepper in mee suah, make the taste spicy and bitter. Beancurd skin and tao pok gravy very little, feels like the gravy is expensive to give more. Traditional prawn noodle taste below average. I got a 5 year old kid with me and doesn't serve utensils & kid chair for us. (Need request then will provide or self service). The service here is 2/10, NOT RECOMMENDED to fill your stomach.
author: Aaron Koh

restaurant_name: KOON Bak Kut Teh 坤肉骨茶
review_text:
Clear soup and peppery type of ba kut teh with pork ribs that look clean. Taste is ok, more peppery than savoury.

Signature Seafood Mee Sua is pretty good. Soup is rich and flavourful. Don't expect a lot of seafood for $8.90 - lots of fish slices and one prawn cut up into 6-7 mini pieces.

Chicken feet, which came as part of the set, is the cold, tangy type but the chicken feet was very tough. Not enjoyable for me.

Prawn paste chicken is richly coated on the outside, but lacking prawn paste flavours on the inside.

We ordered other dishes like the Sesame Chicken and Fried egg, which were ok. Sambal Kang Kong was very spicy and fried with pork lard, which is quite shiok.

Came on a weekend afternoon and there's only one wait staff on duty. And they didn't switch on the aircon, even though most tables were occupied inside. Pretty stuffy and made us feel sleepy after food.

Overall, it's ok for the price, not  outstanding, acceptable for a simple meal.
author: Andrina Loo

restaurant_name: KOON Bak Kut Teh 坤肉骨茶
review_text: Ordered the premium prawn noodles with pork rib. See the size of the prawn? What a joke. Ordered white pepper pork intestine soup, soup not very peppery and tastes quite diluted. You tiao was crispy. Lu rou fan comes with pork belly was not bad although i thought that lu rou fun suppose to be mince meat? Won’t patron again.
author: Khai Xin

restaurant_name: KOON Bak Kut Teh 坤肉骨茶
review_text:
Here are some of my feedback from our first visit:
1. No English -- perhaps it would be nice to hire someone who can speak in English since it took awhile for the staff to understand what i was asking
2. Vegetable with less green -- i ordered the Seasonal Vegetables in Oyster Sauce. But when the food came, it is totally different from the image in the menu. I received 90% stem and 10% greens 😅
3.  Bah Kut Teh -- perfect blend. The flavour is just enough and not so strong like the one from Song Fa.
4.  Peanuts -- i loved it.
5.  Ambiance -- it's cozy and good view of the street while enjoying dinner
author: Diogy

review_text: This "Lei Cha" or Thunder Tea Rice stall in Bukit Timah Interim Market and Food Centre is my go-to for Thunder Tea Brown Rice. And I have been faithfully "following" this stall since it first opened years ago at its previous location at Bukit Timah Market and Food Centre that has since been demolished. Today (16 January 2026) I ordered my usual Thunder Tea Brown Rice Set that was as always excellent in terms of taste and texture and in the case of the latter, there's a lot of different textures to savour when one is eating Thunder Tea Rice. Service here and as always was very good - friendly and courteous and generous (when I asked for extra peanuts gratis). The dining ambience here was nice enough for a non-airconditioned setting.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
The vegetarian Thunder Tea sits with a calm, understated elegance. The pale green tea broth is smooth and velvety, almost jade-like, its surface serene and inviting—light yet deeply nourishing, promising freshness before a sip is even taken. It feels cleansing just to look at.

Beside it, the bowl is a celebration of texture and care. Finely chopped greens form a soft, leafy base, topped with golden tofu cubes that look gently crisp on the edges. Crushed peanuts scatter across the surface like warm, earthy notes, while sesame seeds add a subtle sparkle. Dark beans, preserved vegetables, and fresh herbs are neatly arranged, each ingredient clearly respected rather than mixed into anonymity. It’s rustic, honest, and thoughtfully balanced.

Together, the meal feels wholesome and grounding—comfort food without heaviness, nourishment without excess. Lovely not because it shouts, but because it whispers calm, health, and quiet satisfaction.

#YummyForMyTummy
#Vegetarian #Vegan
#NoOnion #NoGarlic #NoAlliums
author: Juwin Ho ERA

review_text: Brown rice lei cha. Clean taste, not too salty, mellow balanced flavours. Tea broth is mild, could be stronger. Fresh veggies, generous portion. A bit pricey but supports good health so it's worth the price.
author: Ryza Jake

review_text: At $7.30, I would not say it is value for money. Quantity is a little too little, especially the tea. I like my thunder tea soak in tea but this stall gave so little it can hardly drench half the rice. Taste-wise, it was ok. I still prefer the Margaret Drive one.
author: Rex Tan

review_text: Food taste ok but 7.30, check out my photos. I didn't expect so little rice. I definitely need 2 portions, so now I need to go out and eat another portion for lunch. This is too expensive for a hawker center takeaway! The sauce also very little as in picture. I asked for abit more she said it is very thick but it is very watery. And she asked for 2.20 but I did not go for it. Lousy way to do business for sure
author: Amanda Tan

restaurant_name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
review_text:
I don’t usually leave 1-star reviews, but this experience was very disappointing.

I ordered 2 chicken rice and was asked which parts I preferred. So I requested for 2 chicken thigh rice. After making payment and asking for a receipt, I was only given the order slip. The same staff later came back and said there were no more thighs and asked if breast meat was okay.

Not wanting to make things difficult, I asked if at least 1 packet could be thigh meat. She checked with the kitchen and came back with a no.

Out of curiosity, I walked over to take a look and could clearly see chicken thigh portions still available, yet they refused to serve.

I requested a refund. The refund was processed, but the last 4 digits reflected did not match the card I used. When I asked the cashier, she mentioned it was processed according to the payment system.

After all the time wasted, I even asked again if I could proceed to buy 2 packets of chicken thigh rice. The reply was immediate, no more thighs, only breast meat.

After checking Google reviews, I realised there are similar complaints about refusal to serve thighs and poor service attitude. This is not my first time at Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice, which makes this outlet’s service quality even more disappointing.

Service transparency and consistency really need improvement.
author: Chen Yanming

restaurant_name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
review_text:
Our go-to spot for chicken rice in the Upper Bukit Timah area. While there’s also Boon Tong Kee at the other end of Cheong Chin Nam Road, we always come back here. The rice here is softer and it comes with soup — because no meal feels complete without soup.

I have my own three steps to enjoy chicken rice:

First, mix the rice with dark soy sauce,

Second, take a mouthful to savour the flavor.

Third, pair the rice with the chicken meat — ideally with the skin, because the skin really brings out the fragrance of the dish.

Apart from the chicken rice, another dish worth trying is the 滑蛋河 (silky egg hor fun), which has just the right amount of “wok hei.”
author: a_b_c_t_w

restaurant_name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
review_text: We've been coming here for years and the quality has sharply declined. Today, we ordered half a chicken, and it mostly comprised bones with extremely little meat (the attached photo shows the entirety of the half chicken). Would not recommend.
author: Darren Lim

restaurant_name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
review_text: I love chicken rice so much, best Singapore food. Roasted chicken was nice, tender and juicy, goes really well with the chilli sauce that is provided. Nice to come with a bigger group to try their other dishes. I liked the cereal prawn, and the hometown tofu is also usually really good too!
author: Julian Seow

restaurant_name: Five Star Kampung Chicken Rice & Kitchen
review_text:
I really enjoyed the set meal ($15.91). It is valued for money and so tasty.

My favourite part is the side house-made tofu, so soft and umami with minced meat gravy.

The chicken thigh is tender. It contains a bit of soft bones but no issue for me.

The chilli sauce is good too, enough kick but not overly spicy.

I would definitely eat here again if I am in the area. Recommended!
author: Kennigrace

review_text:
My sis wanted to have dinner here, so we did. Waited 5 mins for a table on a Sun evening.

I honestly don't know why it's so popular and crowded. Found the food heavily seasoned. For a restaurant, I was expecting food to be cooked more delicately, not fast food style.

Probably comfort food to most.
author: Nicole Tan

review_text: Went back after a few years. The food, although not bad, had dropped in standard. Used to be one of the best affordable Korean food but not is just average or slightly above average at best. The beef ribs stew $18 was disappointing. There's no unami from the ribs, only can taste seasoning. Fried chicken was so so. If you are into Korean chicken, you'll be happier somewhere else
author: tj tan

review_text:
Do not trust the Google reviews! One of the worse Korean restaurants I've been to in Singapore :(

We ordered the kimchi pancake, kimchi stew for sharing. The kimchi pancake was alright, but the kimchi stew was... bad. The restaurant is extremely rundown and dirty, and you could see accumulated dust all round the area especially near the cashier counter.

♿️ not wheelchair entrance accessible as there is steps at the entrance and not able to fit the wheelchair. Area is pretty cramped as well.
author: Angie

review_text: I’ve ordered from this restaurant several times and have also dined in on a few occasions. The food is consistently excellent, and the quality never disappoints. It has become one of our go-to spots whenever my family is in the mood for Korean cuisine. The flavors are authentic, the portions are generous, and the service is always warm and welcoming. This place truly holds a special spot on our list of favorite restaurants.
author: OJH

review_text:
There is always a queue during dinner period. Only managed to try on a Saturday at 2pm.

Prices were affordable with delicious ban chan. The spicy pork bibimbap is generous in portion and not that spicy.

Service is friendly and prompt.
author: L. c.

restaurant_name: NO.5 Bukit Timah Live Bull Frog Claypot Porridge
review_text:
Food was decent, but the pushy sales tactics and questionable practices left a bad taste in our mouths.

First, the wet tissues cost $0.90 each, which is about double what most places charge. If you’re not comfortable with that, do not use them and remember to return them after the meal.

When the staff member took our order, she repeatedly tried to push us to order more food, particularly the expensive dishes like fish. We had already ordered more than enough food for four people, so it wasn’t as if we were under-ordering.

After failing to force us to order more drinks, she informed us that we weren’t allowed to drink plain water from our own bottles, which felt unreasonable.

Lastly, we ordered fried chicken skin, but what arrived didn’t quite match what we expected. The pieces were unusually large, thin and crumpled, and lacked the small feather follicles typical of chicken skin. We suspected it might have been frog skin served as chicken skin. When we raised this with the staff, they defended it and offered to show us the raw chicken skin. However, even if we had seen it, it’d be hard to verify if that was what was served to us, so we declined.

The food wasn’t even good enough to justify the bad experience. There are better places to satisfy your frog porridge cravings. I personally recommend the one at Chinatown.
author: Joho

restaurant_name: NO.5 Bukit Timah Live Bull Frog Claypot Porridge
review_text:
Flavorful frog leg porridge! Recommend also getting their signature tofu!

2 pax and the service lady recommend 4-5 frog set, which we did not manage to finish and had to takeaway. Takeaway box 0.4 and wet tissue 0.9/each had additional charge.
author: Chocodimples

restaurant_name: NO.5 Bukit Timah Live Bull Frog Claypot Porridge
review_text: When the going gets tough, the wife and I go for our comfort food. Frog Leg Porridge at Sinma. Fresh, tender meat that melts in your mouth. Tried so many stalls and theirs stand out above the others. We get our cravings satisfied even past midnight. Fantastic for busy couples with young kids after putting them to bed. Reward with some frog legs.
author: WDG Dingguo

restaurant_name: NO.5 Bukit Timah Live Bull Frog Claypot Porridge
review_text:
The frog was fresh and the vegetables were decent. However, the service of the Chinese lady was horrible. She gave us a black face when we didn’t order the special expensive dishes she recommended. She kept forcing us to order more as well, which was so awkward.

Furthermore, she also forced my mother to buy a drink even though we already bought two. Even at a restaurant to relax and eat, you need to face sales tactics. I would much rather go to another stall than come here again.
author: Hui

restaurant_name: NO.5 Bukit Timah Live Bull Frog Claypot Porridge
review_text:
July 2025
Their cooking of Frog legs improved and other dishes we ordered were tasty except the small white fishes 白饭鱼 which still not up to standard. Next time shall try other dishes. Servers were attentive and food was served quickly (late dinner at 8.30pm), not crowded.

.......
~ 2022
Used to patronize frequently before covid. Now has more selection but quality is not as good as before when they were named G7.
author: L Wong

review_text:
O.BaJjijang & BBQ
Ordered the Pork Set and it was seriously satisfying. 🥩🔥
The pork cuts were fresh, thick, and beautifully marbled, especially the pork belly and collar — super juicy once grilled. Every slice cooked evenly and stayed tender without being overly greasy.
Loved the variety in the set — from rolled pork belly to sausages and mushrooms, everything complemented each other well. The side dishes and sauces were flavourful and paired perfectly with the meat, enhancing the overall BBQ experience.
Portion size was generous and definitely worth the price. Great place for a casual BBQ meal with friends or family. Will definitely be back again for another round!
Highly recommended 👍
author: Joanne Ang

review_text:
My go to when craving for Korean dishes. Generous banchan, nice bibimbap, decent kimchi jjigae.
The jajangmyeon is also one of the best I've had and this coming from one who doesn't eat it often. Their bbq is average nothing fantastic.

Cleanliness could be better.. the table and menu is grimy and has an off smell.

Toilets used to offer mouth wash, great for after bbq,  but think they removed due to budget cuts.

However above all, their service is friendly and helpful...a cut above the rest👍🏻
author: Melanne T

review_text:
Update: came again to try the bbq set #1, the beef is super good and the pork paired with the spicy sauce is so good, came on a weekday and didn't need to wait long.

Came here after looking high and low for a place seeking tangsuyuk. The set is great value and the sauce is super nice. The smell of BBQ is amazing, will try that next time
author: Krystle Tan

review_text: I had an amazing dinner at O.BBa Jjajang & BBQ! The food was absolutely delicious—their Korean BBQ meats were tender, flavorful, and perfectly grilled, and the jjajangmyeon was rich and satisfying. The service was top-notch: the staff was attentive, friendly, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout the meal. The atmosphere was warm and inviting, with a cozy vibe that made the whole experience feel special. I can’t wait to come back and bring my friends next time！
author: jiaxin zhang

review_text:
This has been pur family's go-to going out restaurant for years! We highly recommend the set menus. When the fancy strikes, we get the BBQ sets sometimes. They service is always amazing, as the staff are accompdating and attentive to our needs. They are also very good at cooking meat, which is always a plus!
Definitely will be coming again :)
author: Kim Raphaela

review_text: Since i revise all Review,  can't  believe it?This is most favourite Chicken Rice, in Singapore! （ 给顾客写得很难听！）My daughter tell me about the detail, make me  confuse? She say Service is OK, but their things look very disapointed,  the price OK! Hope all the Outlet must inprove the skill !🤔
author: Annie Yeo

review_text: Signature chicken is still the best dish to order here. The other dishes are subpar.
author: Lisa T

review_text:
I am writing this with a heavy heart. There is nothing wrong with the chicken and rice itself—on any day, this should easily be a five-star review. The chicken is a good-quality kampong variant, and the fragrant rice is above average. However, they forgot the essentials: a proper ginger chili and a bowl of hot soup to accompany the meal. This is the basic package for any chicken rice set, and some places even offer free-flow. At BTK, each person only gets one small saucer with half chili and half dark sauce, both of which tasted mediocre.
The soy sauce for the chicken is poured from a jar on the spot, which I find unnecessary and only adds extra work for the elderly aunty (I’m not sure why this outlet has so many senior waitresses). She mentioned it was a special blend, but to me, it tasted like any other soy sauce.
It also seems they are trying too hard to promote their Tzi Char dishes, with the “paper-wrapped chicken” positioned as the anchor of the menu instead of their famous chicken rice. I understand they are probably trying to boost sales, which is fine, but it should not come at the expense of their star performer.
I just moved in nearby, but I’m not sure I will return, as there are better Tzi Char options and equally good chicken rice around. I can’t rate them lower because the food quality is there, but I also can’t rate them higher because, to me, bad chili and no hot soup are inexcusable for any chicken rice meal.
author: Yong Desmond

review_text:
I can't believe their standard has dropped so much!!! Good BKT is use to be my favorite and this branch is one of the 2 (besides River valley) I often visit. I am greatly disappointed by their food presentation now compare to previously.
Also, the chicken meat is not as tender as previously too! I I have voiced this out to one of the waiter who claims bcos is breast meat ! I told him I have eaten here for more than 20 years and I could easily tell whether the standard is on or Off. Poorly trained staff who don't know how to manage CS.

Luckily the fried tofu maintened it's standard.
author: Amous Lee

review_text: Well poached chicken, tender and flavourful in every bite, I love the puffy soft rice, appealing at first sight and delightful as you chew on spoonful of these well seasoned rice. Given both my friend and myself are small eaters, we only ordered add on side dish, Thai style fried tofu. Despite dining during peak lunch hours, the restaurant was not as crowded as I expected. Service was fast and atmosphere was peaceful for diners. I gathered that parking can be an issues for some drivers as there were limited parking lots along the stretch of this dining places. Overall a pleasant experience for first timer like myself! 👍
author: Reiko H

restaurant_name: Jew Kit - Bukit Timah Shopping Centre
review_text:
Jew Kit Hainanese Chicken Rice @jewkitoffical hits you with that old-school, nostalgic flavour from the first bite.

I went for the Lovely Meal ($10.30) — tender, moist chicken paired with rice, kai lan and a comforting bowl of soup that just feels like home.

The Hainanese Pork Cutlet ($18.80) was another highlight, crispy on the outside, juicy within, and nicely balanced with its tangy sauce.

Don’t skip the Homemade Crispy Prawn Roll ($14.00) — golden, crunchy, and packed with savoury prawn goodness

📍Jew Kit Hainanese Chicken Rice, 170 Upper Bukit Timah Rd, B1-/17/18,  Bukit Timah Shopping Centre, Singapore 588179
author: MightyFoodie

restaurant_name: Jew Kit - Bukit Timah Shopping Centre
review_text:
Chicken rice in a old school nostalgic taste and decorations. Bring you back to the olden days.
The chicken is slimy and soft, however a little bony. The chicken gizzard is chunky and nice to bite, the rice isn't that fragrance however will be perfect when you put a good decent amount of their homemade chilli and ginger on the rice.
author: jayden

restaurant_name: Jew Kit - Bukit Timah Shopping Centre
review_text: Good service. Chicken rice and fried ngoh hiang is ok. But very very thirsty after the meal. Too much msg. Will not return.
author: M D

restaurant_name: Jew Kit - Bukit Timah Shopping Centre
review_text: Food is really nice. Ordered the Valentine Meal and the Tofu is actually better than the chicken !! Most impressive is the service attitude , the staff brought soup and plate for our additional person without asking 👍👍
author: William Lim

restaurant_name: Jew Kit - Bukit Timah Shopping Centre
review_text: Chicken rice is good, electronic order and fast. Something it's expensive but I think their portion is healthy.
author: Xiaoming Lim

review_text: Best You Tiao in Singapore! Takeaway for your ba kut teh or soya bean drink. The rest of the menu are good too. They quite an expert in frying. The you tiao can run out fast in the weekend, so join the queue early.
author: Timothy TM

review_text: My favorite You Tiao in the mornings! Crispy and hot. Totally Yummy 🤤
author: Luc

review_text: Please reply where the vendors have relocated. I can't find you at the interim hawker.
author: Elena Jane

review_text:
I can’t remember when was the last time we had Korean food at home...... so we decided to ‘tapao’ (takeaway) some kimbap to have a change of meal option.
These healthy and enjoyable seaweed rolls is a welcome change for my folks and each roll is stuffed with ingredients including ham, egg, crab stick, cucumber, radish pickle, burdock root and carrot. My dad loves the variety of vegetables that give a good crunch and toasted sesame seeds sprinkled on top which lend a light fragrant to it.
author: AC Chan

review_text: Come in the evenings. Relax and watch the sun set over the neighbourhood. They've got the best fried chicken! Crispy batter over hot steamy flavorful meat. Service is wonderful. So friendly! Even though I'm there alone, the lady boss made sure I was comfortable.
author: Grace Tan

review_text: Loved their BBQ pork belly, so tasty and perfect wrapped with lettuce and garlic! The lady boss was super friendly too. Great service 👍🏻
author: iamjess

review_text:
Friendly n efficient service
Food are nett price.
We like: Honey Fried Chicken Wings, Beef Hotplate, Kimchi Pancake

Felt kimchi fried rice lacking smokiness n flavours from frying.
author: Berlinda Goh

review_text:
The BBQ was delicious, and the atmosphere was decent with a breezy, open setting. However, the service was a bit slow.
•	BBQ Set: $39.90
•	Spicy Rice Cake: $12.90
•	Seafood Pancake: $19.90
•	Cold Noodles: $13.90
author: Planet Mars Exploration 2033

review_text:
I purposedly went to Beauty World Food Centre just to try this ramen stall. I read that this stall is one of the 'must try' in the list. I went through the menu and saw that the ramen called BLACK KING (GARLIC) has 3 thumbs up sign. I ordered a bowl costing $9.90. It did not disappoint me. The broth is tasty with rich umami flavor while the noodles are al dente. The thing that I liked most is the barbecue slices of pork with nice  charred flavor while maintaining the tenderness of the meat. It also comes with cabbage, japanese style soft boiled egg, and generous topping of bonito flakes. I would definitely recommend this stall. An affordable ramen that is only a fraction of cost than a normal ramen would be.

BUTA KIN CURRY RICE - It's been 2 years since I visited the stall. The dish is a mixed of fried crispy goodness of ebi (prawns) tempura, and tonkatsu of pork and chicken.  Served with short-grain Japanese rice and a bowl of curry. I appreciate that the curry gravy is served separately in a bowl instead of poured over the dish which makes the dish gooey. Every scoop and every bite is definitely worth it.
author: Miguel Esesjay

review_text: I have always wondered about this long-standing Japanese cuisine stall at Beauty World Centre Food Centre. It has been there for as long as I have known this Food Centre and its stall frontage seems worn out over the years. Anyway, as it was a dark and gloomy day today, I thought I try something hot and spicy from this stall. I ordered a "Red Ramen (Spicy)" for $6.70 without any further add-ons. And I must say that the picture of this Ramen on the stalls menu board is almost exactly what you get "in real life." I must also say that this Ramen was exactly what I expected and what I needed - the "soup" was hot as in temperature hot, and spicy with a "kick." And the noodles, "Chasu" and shredded black fungus were all very good. Service at this stall was very good - very friendly and helpful. As for the dining ambience, those familiar with Beauty World Centre Food Centre know better. WINK WINK
author: edtayjb

review_text: My daughter choose it because the photo shown it comes with corn. End up is only veg. $5.50. She doesn’t like the taste. Still preferred clear soup type.
author: Franny GOH

review_text:
Spicy Miso Rice with Mentaiko Pork(Cutlet) @Buta Kin

I occasionally visited this hawker center for the great western, but opted for something a little less heavy(just abit). Found an interesting dish of Miso Rice. It’s like an earthy kimchi fried rice, being spicy, savoury and a little umami. It felt like a dish you would have in a chinese restaurant in Japan, which I’d say is a good thing.

The ajitama on the side was also great, while already delicious on it’s own, having it with the rice makes it even better. The cutlet tasted alright, but of a good size so I’d say it’s pretty worth it for the variety of flavors you get!

The soup the meal comes with is a tonkotsu broth, likely from the same pot the ramen comes in. As a result, it’s rather thick, with a thin fatty layer forming on the top if you leave it untouched for abit, you may or may not like it over Miso Soup, but I’d prefer Miso Soup, or Tonjiru

Overall, quite a satisfying meal with an interesting taste profile, takes the favourite parts people like and puts them onto a plate(mentaiko, ajitama, flavoured rice), never tasted anything quite like this in Singapore.

8/10
author: TheSoloDiner

review_text: Love the Ramen, they are delicious, especially the black garlic ramen. The food are all value for money. The curry rice is not as nice as the Ramen because it is too salty.
author: Teresa Leong

review_text:
Came on weekday late lunch hour.
Best korean pancake we have had in a while. Especially after a terrible one at vivocity, the chives pancake here was superb.
The surface was crispy n the middle is moist n full of ingredients.
We also had cold noodle which taste good but the bulgogi pork was on a sweeter side.
Very nicely done banchan too.
author: P Tan

review_text:
Chanced upon this place for a birthday celebration and we weren’t disappointed.

Lucky for us, we got in before crowd started forming and we didn’t make a reservation beforehand since this was a last-minute decision.

Though the four of us came with half-empty stomachs, I think we ordered quite a substantial amount and managed to finished them all since their food was awesome.

We had a Pork & Beef BBQ platter for 1-2 pax (consisting of Boneless Beef Short Rib, Pork Belly & Marinated Pork Collar), Kimchi Stew, Seafood Spring Onion Pancake, and Cold Noodles. All the dishes were delicious, thanks to the waitresses’ expert grilling + others served pipping hot.

The only slight disappointment we had was that the marination could have been a little less sweet. Probably I’ll go for plain meats without marination the next time.
author: Bylur Xu

review_text: I think the most notable point for this shop is the $19 cold noodles. No meat, no veg. Nothing. Totally overpriced. Food was fresh but the taste did not meet expectations. My  advice is that you can enjoy much better Korean food overseas.
author: 虫でんでん

review_text:
I’ve been eating here since my first taste of Korean food about 17 years ago and I’m glad it’s still going strong. The soups are the draw: soondubu and kimchi jjigae have deep, rounded broth with plenty of tofu and ingredients, perfect with rice.

The banchan is the star with a big, varied spread and everything well seasoned. Crunchy cucumber kimchi, beansprouts, braised potatoes, fishcake, and pickled veg keep refills fun. Portions are hearty, the vibe is old-school cozy, and it still feels like the OG of K-food in SG.
author: edwin

review_text:
I had a fantastic dining experience at Kim’s Family Restaurant! I tried the hotpot along with the BBQ pork and beef—both were incredibly delicious and full of flavor. The BBQ came with an impressive 12 side dishes, which were all fresh and complemented the meal perfectly.

We were pleasantly surprised with a warm porridge starter, which paired beautifully with the side dishes (and yes, they were free!). The hospitality stood out—especially when the kind owner offered us complimentary hot steamed egg and their signature Bali beverage.

The food was amazing, and the warm, generous service made the experience even more memorable. Highly recommend for anyone craving authentic Korean BBQ with heartwarming hospitality!
author: Rennis Cecil

review_text: Opens very early(5.30a.m) to serve customers who may need to go for work..or have some sustenance in the form of Vegetarian food after early meditation and prayers. Many Hindu, Buddhists and Jains living around this area refers to this restaurant as a place to go for good food. But often it's closed early around lunch time
author: G A

review_text: Great food at reasonable price. Stall owner is very kind too. Food portion is generous
author: Dylan Chong

review_text: The vegetarian here is expensive. I ordered brown rice with 1 vegetable dish and it costs $3.00…
author: Sharon Ho

review_text:
Flavorful & Colourful dishes.
Nice curry vege to go with mee hoon.
author: OngOng Journey

review_text: Been eating here for months as it’s near my workplace. There is a wide variety of dishes to choose from and they have other cooked noodle options too.
author: Tracer Bullet

review_text:
Found Hair in Food – Serious Food Safety Concern

I was very disappointed with my recent visit to Subway at Bukit Timah Plaza. In the middle of eating, I discovered a human hair in my sandwich. This is unacceptable and raises serious concerns about the food safety and hygiene practices at this outlet.

As a paying customer, I expect proper handling of food and adherence to hygiene standards. I hope the management will investigate this incident and take immediate action to ensure such contamination does not happen again.
author: Lam Xin Ye Cindy

review_text: I used to visit this Subway outlet here on a weekly basis. Then I took a "break" and had my Subway fix at its other outlets. However, returning to this outlet today was very rewarding - although I had to wait a while to get a table to dind in, as there was a big crowd at Bukit Timah Plaza today, on a Saturday. Anyway, I ordered my usual Tuna Wrap and added a Small Meal Deal to it - and I was highly satisfied by the service at the counter, the taste and mouth feel of my Tuna Wrap, the Zero Sugar drinks option available here (I had a Fanta Orange Zero), and of course the Subway macadamia cookie. The only thing that I felt let down by, was the dine in situation - there were just too many who either had already finished their meal, but proceeded to linger and do other things at the table, or those who were lone diners, but occupied a table for four. Perhaps, staff here could do something about this when genuine dining in diners are in need of a table.
author: edtayjb

author: Josh k

review_text:
A good place to have a hearty meal. There are limited vegetarian options.
I went here for dinner. I really liked the sandwiches they serve here. I also love the value meal where you can get 2 sandwiches,cookies and a drink. Absolutely delicious.
The sandwich was soft,delicious and had a slight crunch due to the veggies. I really enjoyed the soft and fudgy cookie as it melted and crumbled in my mouth.

author: Anikaz Travel

review_text: My wrap and other sandwiches are very nicely wrapped by this female staff. (15th Jan 2023 at 11.23am) Easy to open and hold, and eat. Well done. Place is also clean and neat. Keep it up.
author: Alice NTN

review_text: This is our 2nd time here at their Bt Timah Plaza outlet. The dishes we ordered were delicious and we appreciate that the portions’ big! Lady Boss was around, she was really friendly and warm. We will come back again!
author: Audreyyy

review_text:
For someone who is not a fan of Korean food, this stall nearly made me a convert!

The cold noodles had that tint of sourish taste (not spoilt), which made it very refreshing to eat and their kimchi appetiser was good in my opinion.

Difficult to get seats on a Friday night and price of food was a little on the high side but the pancake which was the highlight..had right amount of crispy-ness for me.

Definitely worth eating!
author: Botak

review_text:
Have been here multiple times and the food never fail to disappoint. My favorite is the soy sauce fried chicken, samyetang and seafood pancake. The free side dishes were amazing too.

The staff here are super friendly and hospitable as well. Highly recommended if you want authentic and high quality Korean food.
author: Teo YR

review_text: ratings should be higher in my opinion!! was lucky to have met the owner (who is one of the most humble & down to earth owners i’ve seen in sg) :) my friends and i had a really good dining experience here. we ordered the sundubu jigae, seafood pancake and tuna kimbap. amazing service 🫶🫶
author: Pearlya Preandra

review_text:
Come here almost every week, the food is amazing, the staff are very friendly and nice.
Our favourite Korean food place hands down.

Also, the appetisers are amazing!
author: Li Yan Koh

review_text:
One of the better halal restaurants offering fusion cuisine. We chose Sumac to celebrate a colleague’s farewell.

Despite arriving 25 minutes late, the staff were kind and accommodating in holding our table. The restaurant was almost full for a Tuesday lunch. Impressive, given its elusive location.

The first thing that stands out is the view. Overlooking the swimming pool, it is beautifully complemented by the lush greenery of Bukit Timah hill.

Service was warm and efficient, and we were offered a larger table as we over-ordered.

The food arrived promptly, with bold and well-balanced flavours. While the grilled meats felt slightly under-charred for my preference, this allowed the marination to stand out, something the rest of the group enjoyed but me.

Portions are generous and prices are competitive, making it great value overall. Highly recommended for hearty meals and gatherings.
author: MH Tham

review_text:
An exceptional dining experience reflecting true five-star standards. The cuisine was exquisitely prepared and served in generous portions. Although slightly premium in pricing, the experience fully justifies the cost. The service was consistently prompt, attentive, and highly professional.

While the restaurant is discreetly located away from the main road, a complimentary shuttle service from Bukit Timah Plaza ensures convenient accessibility.

Thank you, Sumac. I look forward to returning for another memorable dining experience.
author: Zahir Jumaat

review_text: Love the ambience and the pace. It had a tranquil and chill vibe with large glass windows facing the green forest. I had the burger which tasted great! The kebab was seasoned well but a bit dry IMO. Overall the price is slightly above average but still worth to come.
author: Rashidan Shane Tian

review_text: Great food, love their Lebanese grills, very well cooked and seasoned, great views and ambience. Will definitely visit again, shuttle bus provision makes the trip convenient and comfortable. Ideal birthday celebration restaurant too!
author: Chong Pei Wen

review_text: Previously known as Spize. Decor has been kept the same. Place is still immaculate.  Mediterranean food and plenty of local cuisine choices. Good quality is still as good as before. Service can be challenging to get considering only seeing 3 crew covering the entire floorspace. Still they manage to get the dishes out pretty much in record timing. So kudos to them. Will definitely be back again.
author: LAM CHUAN

review_text:
An exceptional dining experience! The ambiance exuded a tranquil European vibe, with the perfect blend of soothing music and attentive yet not overbearing service. The generous portions and high-quality food truly elevated the experience. Highly recommended! (But also worried if too popular it’s hard to book a table next time 🤭) They offer a 5-course tasting menu and sharing platters. We opted for the sharing platter, which included a 600g steak, and several sides, we ordered another side of burrata. We also enjoyed sparkling water and a bottle of wine. To top it off, they surprised the birthday boy with a complimentary dessert! Huge thanks to the attentive waitstaff for their exceptional service, even remembering the details from my reservation comment. Incredible!
And all this for less than SGD100 per person – truly worth it! 🥳
author: Grace Shan

review_text:
We enjoyed our dinner at Swiss Club with our friends from Switzerland. Surrounded by lush greenery, its rustic architecture provided a homely atmosphere.

We ordered the Orecchiette Pasta, the Steak Frites and Veal with Rosti. The pasta was light and flavorful, the steak was succuluent but alittle too fatty, and the rosti was cripsy.

While the price point is high, the unique al-fresco fine dining experience suits a warm gathering of friends and family.
author: WS

review_text: Fav steak house. It wins with the whole package. Not just the taste
author: Elon .H

review_text: My hubby & I had a great 16th wedding anniversary celebration at Arbenz restaurant for the first time, attended by a very attentive and professional restaurant Manager called Mr. Yusri. We truly touched by his great service as well as his team positive attitude. Food & Beverage was so great! We appreciate their kind service and definitely will introduce this place to our friends and families!😍
author: Janette Seetoh

review_text: Great place and great food. Love it
author: Mark

review_text: Delicious food (the veal and masala kulcha were highlights!) and warm, friendly service. We had a great time — thank you!
author: MICHELLE LO

review_text: Located within the Swiss Club and is open to non members. Nice ambience, surrounded by greenery and overlooking the pool. Kudos to the attentive and friendly service throughout our meal! We had the barramundi fish, gnocchi, meat loaf and chicken wrap which were all good and reasonably priced. Only the milkshake was not cold and not thick. Highly recommend to try this for a different location and environment!
author: Chong Peng How

review_text:
As a frequent visitor to Switzerland, I’ve become accustomed to the local food. Unfortunately the classics at this restaurant were nothing short of underwhelming. The fondue seemed to be more like a cheesy sauce than cheese itself. With its flour-like flavour it did not even behave like cheese. It remained liquid even once cooled which is most uncharacteristic of fondue.
The veal sausage was not at all meaty. It was a low grade sausage made from reconstituted meat mixes - the ones that have a foamy texture rather than bits of meat. No different to a chicken sausage.
Finally, the staff had as much character as a teaspoon!
author: Ray M.

review_text:
I had called the place twice to check if they allow non-members. And I was told by the lady staff that they do allow non-members except on a weekend.

So I booked a cab and went happily there. Once I reached I was told it is only for members. It was a bit embarrassing 🙈.

I was standing near the temperature check zone and called up the restaurant again to be sure it was not a mistake from the person taking the temperature. This time a male staff picked and he dint give proper ears to even understand what I was saying/giving feedback about.

Anyway it was a not a great experience and I had no other option other than to book a cab again and drive away to some nice place to have my dinner.

Do take my feedback - Pls ensure your staff doesn’t give wrong information to any potential customer. It doesn’t leave a very good experience.
author: Gitika Singh

review_text: The food was excellent. The service was ok. The ambience was better than expected. Overall, it was a pleasant and joyous adventure worth every penny and journey. Will definitely go back there when I have the chance. Keep up the good work.
author: Simon Vijay

review_text: The Windsor at the British Club always brings back fond memories of growing up in the neighborhood. The fish and chips and apple crumble are timeless favorites that our entire family loves! Many of the staff have been there for years, offering a warm, familiar sense of hospitality that adds to the charm.
author: Eva Cheung

review_text: Had dinner with an ex-colleague who had a membership here. The British Club has an old school charm about it and the food at Windsor Arms was pretty good! Loved the Beef pie!
author: Eric Lee

review_text: The British restaurant has some nice fish and chips, but not as good as the Indian food. The portion of the food is big as well.
author: Wesley Wong

review_text: Good ambiance and friendly waitstaff. There is a wide variety of food choices from Western to Asian. As the club is relatively tucked away and quiet, it's a good place for a quiet night and ideal for having conversations.
author: Prashaanth Rajandran

review_text: Nice range of western pub food. In fact Gordon Ramsey would have a nightmare since there are so many food options..! Menu includes Indian and local food. All delicious.
author: Mark B

review_text: I have always visited Mountbatten Bar & Grill whenever they change their menu. Been here since a long long time, I think my earliest memory of dining here was in 2015-2016. Food & service never disappoints. I love their sourdough so much, it tastes really great with their butter. I have also always loved their lobster bisque, it is a must-try. Their latest menu is by far their greatest, yet. I enjoyed the scallop & my partner – their special’s for that day: the Foie Gras & Crab. The ambience is terrific for people who prefers a less rowdy environment.
author: lydia bae

review_text:
The Mountbatten Bar & Grill at the British Club is an excellent restaurant that combines refined dining, warm hospitality, and a peaceful atmosphere. It’s quiet and elegant, making it an ideal spot to enjoy a relaxing meal. The staff are exceptionally friendly and attentive, always serving with genuine smiles and ensuring every guest feels well taken care of.

The food is consistently outstanding, from starters to desserts. The MBT Signature Truffle Focaccia is soft, fragrant, and infused with the rich aroma of truffle — a perfect start to the meal. The Traditional French Onion Soup is another highlight, deeply flavorful with a rich, slow-cooked broth and topped with Emmentaler and Gruyère toast that adds just the right balance of saltiness and creaminess. The Grilled Ibérico Pork Neck is beautifully cooked — tender, juicy, and full of natural flavor, showing great attention to detail in preparation.

The true showstopper, however, is the Crêpe Suzette. This dessert is not only delicious but also a delightful performance. The staff prepare and cook it right in front of you on a rolling cart, explaining each step and ingredient along the way. The orange juice used is freshly squeezed from real oranges, giving the sauce a vibrant, natural sweetness and aroma. Combined with butter, sugar, and liqueur, it creates a thick, glossy orange sauce that coats the delicate crêpes perfectly. The result is fantastic — warm, fragrant, and bursting with citrus flavor.

Overall, the Mountbatten Bar & Grill offers an exceptional dining experience within the British Club — delicious food, attentive service, and a serene atmosphere. It’s a wonderful choice for both special occasions and quiet, indulgent dinners.
author: Wesley Wong

review_text: Was hosted here for dinner. Had the French Onion Soup, Beef Wellington, lamp rack, pork iberico. For dessert the lava cake and crepe sauzette was acceptable
author: Sze Wee Tan

review_text:
Had a most lovely dinner. Well looked after by their front of house manager and staffers in the dining room. The kitchen whipped up a storm with so many delectable classic. Walked out of the place a very happy satisfied man.

Looking forward to their reopening.
author: Matthew Lee

review_text:
The Mountbatten Room at the British Club Singapore exudes an air of refined elegance and historical significance. Named after Lord Louis Mountbatten, the last British Viceroy of India and a key figure in Singapore's post-war history, the room pays homage to its namesake with a tasteful blend of colonial charm and contemporary sophistication.

The upmarket restaurant serves as a versatile venue, hosting a myriad of events ranging from formal dinners and business gatherings to cultural celebrations. With its panoramic windows overlooking lush greenery, the Mountbatten Room seamlessly integrates the club's British legacy with Singapore's tropical landscape.

Whether savoring a traditional British high tea or engaging in lively conversations during social events, visitors to the Mountbatten Room experience a curated blend of nostalgia and contemporary luxury. It stands as a testament to the enduring connection between the British Club and Singapore's historical tapestry, providing a distinguished setting for both reflection and celebration.
author: Mayuresh Godse

review_text: Came back here to try their food after many years .... Before they renovated the place and scale down the shop from 2 to 1. Food prices has also got up to keep up with times. We had the rendang beef, sayur lodeh, chilli lady fingers and the meat balls soup (comes with 5 large meat balls). Quality of ingredients are good. Taste is average and typical perenakan.

review_text:
Kind of disappointed. The ayam buah keluak serve with heavy chicken skin and fats. Not sure forget to trim off or cook that manner. But very unpleasant to eat. The sotong hitam is thinly sliced.
