review_text:
Tried this place many years ago before it renovated. Miss the old (and cheaper) extensive menu, but the food tastes still as great! Four of us ordered the Set B and added on an Ayam Buah Keluak. Portions are big, spices were on point. Babi ponteh was on the saltier side but goes really well with rice.

Love the desserts too! Will definitely come back!

review_text:
Been a while since i’ve been here and it’s totally changed. much cosier, quieter and aesthetic after redesign. review_text:

review_text: The pork and lamb chops were cooked to perfection (tender and juicy). The fish and chips are authentic and crispy. The proportion of the foods was large. And the prices of the foods are reasonable. Their service is good, friendly and welcoming atmosphere environment
author: vicki chong

restaurant_name: Buddy Hoagies Steak & Grill Restaurant (Bukit Timah Shopping Centre)
review_text:
We found ourselves here two days in a row, trawling the upstairs mall for a transfer helper. It's a tiring business and Buddy's offered a welcome respite at lunchtime. It's a large restaurant with both an indoor and outdoor option. The indoor can be a chilling experience if seated directly under the aircon.

The clientele appeared to be made up of three groups; people such as ourselves in need of sustenance in the 'helper' quest, workers from the mall or local businesses and an influx of students from neighbouring schools.

The menu is quite extensive and it whilst you can order by QR scan the staff are happy to key your order in themselves.

Across the two days we tried the Korean ribs, fish and chips, rosti with chicken chop and vanilla ice cream and you can order a set with a soup and beverage "free'.

A standout is the service, which is excellent, attentive and incredibly quick to serve the food. The food itself is hot (not the ice cream!) tasty and large portions. Simple yet fulfilling and feels like good value for money.

An enjoyable tea or coffee at the end caps off a great experience and we walked away both days happily nourished ans recharged.

Would recommend and will return if in the vicinity. 👍
author: JT

review_text:
Went to McDonald’s at Beauty World Centre for lunch and tried the returning Prosperity Double Beef Burger set 🍔✨

Paired it with Twister Fries, a Peach McFizz, and topped it off with an add-on of 4 Garlic Pepper Chicken McNuggets for just $2 (with curry sauce).

💛 A meaningful touch this year — with every Prosperity Special Meal purchased, $0.10 is donated to Ronald McDonald House Charities Singapore (RMHC) to support families with sick children.

Taste test:
The Prosperity Double Beef Burger was served warm with its signature pepper sauce, though I felt the peppery kick wasn’t as strong as previous years. Still enjoyable, but slightly toned down.

Twister Fries stayed consistent — curly, crispy, and always satisfying.

The Garlic Pepper Chicken McNuggets were a slight miss for me. I still prefer the classic nuggets, and the curry sauce felt a bit more watery than before.

On a brighter note, the Peach McFizz was refreshing and delicious — definitely one of the highlights of the meal 🍑🥤

Overall, a mix of hits and misses, but still a comforting seasonal meal I look forward to every year.

review_text: Came here for staff lunch. Food was great, teochew steamed fish was very fresh. I particularly enjoyed the homemade toufu with minced pork. Parking is a real problem tho extremely limited in front of the premise. Roadside parking is available along the road in the surrounding private estate.
author: Glenn Tan

restaurant_name: Bukit Timah Wet Market & Food Centre (Interim)
review_text:
Nice Environment, well ventilated. Good strong local Coffee and Tea.

Best Wanton Noodle with well charred deeply seasoned Char Siew, tender umami Pig Leg Noodle and Chicken Feet Noodle. The braise has a dried seafood taste and thickened with collagen. Noodles are seasoned with that braise sauce from the pig leg taking the noodles to the next level.

Wonderful fried Beehoon with Ngo Hiang, the secret is in the sauce which I believe is infused with limau purut.

One of the best Lala Prawn White Beehoon at affordable prices, large prawns plenty of Lala and Umami Soup. To be eaten with the complimentary crispy lard. Mixed Vegetable rice is generous and generally freshly cooked.

One of the most popular Hainanese Style Mutton Soups in Singapore. Generous portions at affordable prices. Great tasting herbal soup, just the right amount of herbal infusion, not medicinal tasting.

Two stalls selling Fried Carrot Cake, Black and White. Both are possibly ranked amongst the top in Singapore.

Fish Soup is excellent, generous portions with super fresh fish!

Overall, one is spoilt for choice!

No longer the narrow aisle like the old site, I found myself enjoying coming here again as many of the OG stalls had moved over here while also exploring other stalls for new food gems.
author: Mr Yang

restaurant_name: Bukit Timah Wet Market & Food Centre (Interim)
review_text: Always a place for good hawker food. Lots of stalls! spoilt for choice. Mostly close or sold out around 830pm. More parking than their original location. Pretty cozy interim place.
author: Asia Apparel

review_text:
We visited Daisy’s Dream Kitchen for their Christmas set dinner and were truly impressed by the warmth, authenticity, and heart behind every dish. Daisy’s is known for its Peranakan flavours, but this festive set really showcased the depth of their craftsmanship.

We had the Nut-Cracking Nonya Meal, which came with a beautiful spread of classic dishes — each portion generous and thoughtfully prepared. The Nonya achar, emping belinjau, and bakwan kepiting were delightful starters, full of familiar home-cooked comfort. The homemade otak-otak, ngoh hiang, and tek tim were standouts, with flavours that felt both nostalgic and refined.

The star of the night was definitely the Babi Buah Keluak — rich, earthy, and cooked with the kind of depth only true Peranakan kitchens achieve. The rendang, assam batang slice, and Nonya chap chye completed the meal beautifully, each dish balanced with just the right acidity and fragrance. The 3 Wise Men vegetables (sambal lady’s finger, brinjal, petai) added a spicy, aromatic punch that we loved.

The homemade lemongrass lime and longan ginger drinks were refreshing and tied the meal together perfectly.

Service was warm, attentive, and genuinely heartfelt, you can feel the pride in their food. Daisy’s remains one of the best spots for authentic, soulful Peranakan cuisine. Highly recommend for festive gatherings or any day you crave true Nonya comfort.
author: Yvonne Chou

review_text:
We had a lovely family dinner (6 pax) at Daisy's Dream Kitchen at Temasek Club, a place known for its solid Peranakan and local delights. We ordered quite a spread, and while the food was consistently very good, a couple of dishes truly shone.

​The absolute standouts of the night were the Ngoh Hiang and the Buah Keluak Fried Rice. The Ngoh Hiang (which came as unique, plump balls rather than the usual rolls) was packed with flavour and texture. The Buah Keluak Fried Rice was incredibly aromatic, with that distinctive earthy, savoury taste infused into every grain – a definite must-try.

​We also ordered the Assam Batang Slice, Beef Rendang, Babi Buah Keluak, Kueh Pie Tee, Otah Otah, and the 3 Wise Men (a stir-fry of lady's finger, brinjal, and petai with ikan bilis). Every single dish was well-executed and tasty. The fish was fresh, the rendang tender, and the sambal vegetables had a nice kick.

​We finished off with a refreshing bowl of Chendol, which was the perfect sweet ending.

​Overall, while not every dish was "exceptional," the standard was consistently high across the board. It's a very reliable spot for a comforting and satisfying Peranakan meal with the family. A solid 4 stars!
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text:
Authentic atmosphere peranakan restaurant tuck in a quiet corner besides the swimming pool of Temasek Club.
Food up to par for a authentic peranakan, it has all the flavour you expect from peranakan food. Only the chendol needs to bump up as it lacks the classic gula melaka flavour.
Our first visit but the staff did not promote nor introduce to the free drink offer for new member!
Order was also wrongly taken as we ordered only one soup but two were served.
Price range on the upper end for the casual restaurant.
author: WT Wong

review_text:
Sunday with Daisy’s Dream Kitchen, right in the comfort of home. ☔️

I love Peranakan food, so I was excited to try Daisy’s Dream Kitchen after hearing rave reviews from Bibi. Out of the seven dishes we ordered, the Ngor Hiang and Assam Fish were my favourites. Daisy surprised us with a complimentary Achar which came fresh and really tasty. Me likey!

The meal portions were rather small, but luckily we had backup sides from Dian Xiao Er, some cheesy pizza, sushi and cake for the hangry kampung.

I can’t comment on the atmosphere till I visit Daisy’s Dream Kitchen in person. 😁

#tiramisoooo #tramisoooojiaks #jiakjiakjiak #daisysdreamkitchen #temasekclub #peranankanfood
author: Tiramisooo Tiramisooo

review_text:
The Peranakan dood was like home-cooked food. The ladies fingers & buah keluk were good. Staff were courteous & helpful.

I made the reservations through Google and it gave me only 2 options at 6pm or 8.30pm.  I picked the former. I stayed for about 1.5 to 2 hours but the restaurant never filled up. I think if you require other timings, it's best to call the restaurant if not you are limited to unpopular timings.
author: Jacqueline Cheong

restaurant_name: Bar Bar Black Sheep @ Cherry Ave
review_text:
Naan (SGD $9) @ Bar Bar Black Sheep.
.
With 3 independent kitchens, including a North Indian focused kitchen, this watering hole is a relaxed night-time dining spot.
.
Their rendition is soft fluffy chewy in texture, tearing apart easily. While the plain version exudes smoky bready sweet savoury flavour, the garlic version studded with minced garlic and fresh coriander exudes smoky bready savoury vegetal bitter herbal spice flavour.
author: Ivan Teh

restaurant_name: Bar Bar Black Sheep @ Cherry Ave
review_text: An easy place to relax outdoors with a beer and some food. They do have some German beers on tap but unfortunately a lot were out like the Gravenstein. The service was great, friendly and prompt but the food could be improved. I had the chicken kaladi and garlic naan but both were quite salty. Overall a decent place to relax on the way home for a nice beer.
author: matt wood

restaurant_name: Bar Bar Black Sheep @ Cherry Ave
review_text:
This is a nice, casual neighbourhood gastropub for residents staying in Bukit Timah Road area. It is equally well patronised by diners from further away. Its open-air premises has a rustic atmosphere, with dining tables and high tables. Adults and children are welcomed here.

A variety of cuisines is offered to accompany beers, homemade lemonade and drinks. As credit cards of customers are held by the operator, we felt more comfortable to pay as we ordered to avoid unnecessary hassle of disputed charges.
author: Jeff Leong

restaurant_name: Bar Bar Black Sheep @ Cherry Ave
review_text:
Decent option for casual drinks and it has a reasonable range of tap beers. The seating is all covered but it's open plan and semi-outdoors (ie, no walls). That's ok though because the location is set back from the main road so it doesn't get too much traffic noise and ends up with a nice breeze.
The food is from a separate (but connected) Indian kitchen and is good but it's a little annoying you can't just order it all at once with the drinks.
Fun, relaxed place for a beer.
author: Howard

restaurant_name: Bar Bar Black Sheep @ Cherry Ave
review_text: (The Indian chef who made this great food is gone and so is the quality, likely same with Thai - very sad)) Can’t go wrong any night of the week. Perfect Indian fare, burgers for kids, and authentic Thai... all of it with perfect pint of Carlsberg or whatever beer you have in mind including some choice IPAs.
author: Raphael

review_text: Best fish soup store in the area! Fish slices are thick and fresh. They have the best chilli as well! A lil pricey but value for money imo. Nice uncle and auntie too, been my family’s go to for years :)
author: Lynn Cheah

review_text:
6 Dec 2025
My 2nd visit. I ordered the batang fish slices with rice and with mee sua on separate visit.

There’s always a queue.

The fish slices were fresh. The broth was normal and plain to me but it doesn’t affect me since I usually eat dipping into the balachan chilli, so hot and so good!
author: Jessie

review_text: Leng Kee Fish Shop is my go-to for fresh fish – cheap and good! Always very fresh, perfect for cooking fish soup at home. Standard never drop over the years. Uncle very friendly and honest. Highly recommend for those who love a good bowl of homemade fish soup!
author: Hazel Ng

review_text:
Recommended by a friend and it's definitely 5 stars! The fish slices were so fresh, so sweet and tender. The soup tastes very natural too, not overly salted. Generous portion of fish slices.

Ate the fish beehoon and takeaway 2 bowls of fish slice soup. Super yummy. Will definitely be back (even tho it's across the island for me)
author: Xuan Lin T

review_text:
Visit Bukit Timah Food Centre on a Monday past lunch. With most stalls closed and my stomach rumbling, fate (or maybe just hunger) led me to the unassuming Leng Kee Fish Soup. I got the smallest bowl ($6) and added bittergourd and rice (+ $1).

Don't underestimate this simple soup – it's a flavour bomb! The broth is rich with the delicate sweetness of batang fish. The fish slices are fresh and cooked to perfect tender texture. I finally get why this stall is always buzzing, even on Mondays!

The popular side, pig trotters, were sold out, but the kind folks drizzled their heavenly braised sauce over my rice upon request.

I should have tried this place ages ago, and you bet I'll be back for more of that amazing soup and, hopefully, score those legendary pig trotters next visit!

Update Dec 2024: revisit the stall and they are now located at the interim market. I had the $6 fish soup and added braised tau pok for $1. The quality and portion remains the same and I realised they are using You Mak Cai. It's no wonder the soup has a natural sweet fragrance. Pig trotters were unfortunately sold out again but it gives me a reason to visit earlier next time.
author: Touristmouse

review_text:
Was quite blown away by the quality of BBQ beef and their home made sauces. They have Jeju interior decos which made me felt like I have been transported to Jeju. Their owner is Korean, and customers are also Koreans. There are many Korean shops in this same mall, but Joomak was the best. The staff also BBQed the beef for us and dipped in their own sauce, and served us, it taste really good. The salt is homemade and imported from Korea, it was unique and good.

I'll recommend my friends definitely 😁
author: Jamie Goh

review_text:
This place is a hidden gem for Korean food in Singapore. I've been on the hunt for authentic Korean pancakes, and many places felt lacking, but the Seafood leak pancake here is delicious. It truly reminds me of the food quality a Korean grandmother used to make back in childhood . The pork soup was also incredibly flavorful. And we both really loved the teokbokki.
My wife wanted to try this korean restaurant and I must say she's also not disappointed at all. The service is great with free flow of side dishes. Though the staff is bit less. But both the boy and the waitress were nice. The couple friend set is really worth the money, especially the set A. The service from the lady Nan is really good. She is very thoughtful, thorough and grill our food to almost perfect satistifaction. It is so nice that finished barely so we takeaway a lot. Come at around 6 pm where there is not many dinner crowd and u will get undivided attention. Really a great place will come again
author: Icotifica

review_text:
The gukbap was really good — comforting and flavourful, definitely the highlight of the meal. Customer service was top-notch: attentive, friendly, and made the dining experience very pleasant.
BBQ meats were above average, but the great service and solid gukbap & banchan more than made up for it. Overall a nice, fuss-free meal. Would come back.
author: Lee Angeline

review_text: It's a great place for authentic Korean meal, I really liked their Pork soup, Kimchi pancake, steam egg(it comes with the set if you order one), also they have their own signature beef soup "Joomak Gukbap". And the fried chicken is so damn good, my friends really order 2 times😂. The only drawback here is the staff otherwise it's a great place with soothing music. Will come again.
author: Alexander

review_text: This restaurant serves authentic Korean dishes and is extremely packed on weekends. The scrumptious and crispy pancake which comes with lots of scallions, squids and prawns is certainly one of the best Korean pancake I have ever eaten.
author: AC Chan

review_text:
Local fare in great variety at affordable prices. Love the nasi kunyit, rendang gravy was just right for me.
Curry chee cheong fun was also satisfying.
A lot more things on my list to try.
author: Kai Ling

review_text:
They definitely know how to do food WELL. Nothing pretentious, just good food. I don't understand why there are so many 1 star reviews but I would totally disregard them. Of course the ambience is not super fancy, and yes they serve food with disposables, but hey it works for them!

I got Nasi Lemak with Chicken Rendang. The rice was so fragrant, but not too heavy on coconut milk. Super fluffy and tasty!! Ikan bilis was so crunchy and flavorful too.

For dessert I got the Barley Beancurd Gingko - this was not too sweet! Very pleasant to keep slurping on it.

So happy to have Le Tian Tian near my home and hope the shop flourishes and stays long long!!
author: Ji Young Lim

review_text:
The negative reviews are MISLEADING.

3rd time eating here and the standard holds up. You can taste the lemak in the Nasi lemak and the white beehoon is properly infused with the stewed pork, might be underwhelming for individuals with stronger/higher threshold tastebuds but you can be sure that your arteries are not clogged here.

Tastes like another Sunday back at home lunch typa situation. The one star reviews are quite extreme and skewed, so don’t let it deter you. TBH some of those reviewers are chronic one star reviewers so I wouldn’t take them seriously 👀
author: Jian Kai Pang

review_text: I don't really understand the low reviews. Can't rate the atmosphere and service as I've only eaten their food getting delivery but their food is old school and tasty. Another reviewer said it's unpretentious and I think that's exactly why it's so good. I've tried a lot on their menu - their nasi lemak (Chinese style), noodles, French toast, desserts are all good but the real stand out is their white bee hoon with stewed pork, so good especially when you get the extra soy chips. I also often crave their ikan bilis porridge, and homemade soy milk cos it's not sweetened and thick - makes a great local breakfast. Be sure not to miss their hawthorn (San-cha) jelly - the one and only place I've been able to find this.
author: Jeannette James

review_text: Tried Le Le Tian at Bukit Timah for the first time via GrabFood after seeing their good ratings. Unfortunately, it didn’t quite live up to expectations. A few of the desserts were decent, but the main dishes we ordered were below average. I was hoping for something that would impress based on the reviews, but honestly, the food fell flat. Maybe it's better dining in, but for delivery, it just didn’t hit the mark.
author: Pauline Wee

review_text: Myeongdong Korean Food - this smallish Korean restaurant in Bukit Timah Plaza is amongst several such cuisine restaurants in this shopping mall and after more than a year in business therein, it has certainly stood its ground in face of such competition. My wife and I had a meal at this place ordering a "Pajun" and a "Jjanjangmyeon" and both orders were very good; especially the "Pajun" that was delightfully crispy. And the food here came with a free flow of banchan and Korean tea. Service here was good - friendly and courteous. And the dining ambience here was nice enough in air-conditioned comfort.
author: edtayjb

review_text: Exceeded my expectations but to be fair, I had none to begin with, as I went along with my friends and walked in not knowing what to expect. I’m not a meat person but the meats were amazingly and tenderly cooked and simply the star of the dinner. We ordered some sides too, seafood stew, pancake etc which were all okay. Sides were very generous and there’s a nice seaweed soup provided. We paid quite a bit for the meats but it was worth it. Great easy Saturday dinner.
author: Jamie W

review_text:
It was our first time visiting last night, and we had a fantastic dinner. Deep was incredibly helpful right from the start, recommending the perfect set for us since we weren’t sure what to order.

The service here is top-notch. Their aged meat is incredibly flavorful and grilled to perfection. I specifically requested my meat to be extra crispy, and since the staff takes turns grilling, the waitress was very attentive in relaying that request to the next waitress who came to attend our table.

Deep was the main person looking after our table most of the night, and he made us feel very welcome. Great food and even better service—we will definitely be back!
author: mmonita1234

review_text: Very good food here! Highly recommended! Dep was very friendly, introduced us to these wonderful meat. Cooked it for us and told us to pair with which sauce. Love his services! Thank you for the good meat! We will be bacon highly recommend!
author: Ricky rick Phua

review_text:
Had an amazing meal at GO! KBBQ, and it’s easily one of the best Korean BBQ spots I’ve tried in the area.

First off, the side dishes were awesome—fresh, well-seasoned, and constantly refilled, which already set a great tone for the meal. But the real highlight was the aged pork and beef. The cuts are a generous 3cm thick, beautifully marbled, and incredibly juicy. Each bite was packed with flavour, tender on the inside with a perfect sear on the outside—super delicious and very satisfying.

What really elevates the experience is the service. The servers are extremely friendly and attentive, and best of all, they insist on cooking the meat for you. You can really tell they know exactly how to handle these premium cuts—timing, heat, and doneness are all spot on—so you get the meat at its absolute best without any stress.

If you’re looking for quality aged meats, great banchan, and warm, professional service, GO! KBBQ at Bukit Timah Plaza is definitely worth a visit.
author: Nicholas Chong

review_text:
Had Dinner here on Christmas Eve, situated within Bukit Timah Plaza upper level.

Service was quite good, very attentive to our eating speed while they cook on the bbq plate. We dont need to lift a finger on cooking.

Ordered Beef set and ala carte pork belly. Cooked very well by the staff. One of the side dish is call Chinese Salad was incredible.
author: Da Jun Woon

restaurant_name: Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice
review_text: I’m glad that this store has survived the test of time through the many iterations of renovation this “food court” has gone through, and deservedly so! Solid choice and I especially love the herbal soup that comes along. Portions are also very generous for the price. Most striking of this store is the service and the friendly smile that always comes along from way back.
author: Abraham Lee

restaurant_name: Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice
review_text: Tucked away in a corner in the mall but so good! The yam rice had chunks of yam and nice mild flavour but the soup was packing the herbal flavour. They are very generous with the meat, super value for money. Will definitely go back.
author: S Elan

restaurant_name: Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice
review_text: The duck rice chilli and chicken rice chilli were bomb. So glad my bf insisted that we eat there even though we’ve already had lunch. Albeit I wish the duck had more than just one piece of skin on it 😗
author: Rei Miyazaki

restaurant_name: Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice
review_text: I'm a long-time fan of Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice. The owners are super humble and friendly, often staying open past dinner time to accommodate late customers. The serving portions are generous, and their duck noodle and rice dishes are simple yet incredibly delicious. A true gem in Bukit Timag Plaza.
author: derek neo

restaurant_name: Zheng Wang Chicken and Duck Rice
review_text:
i could eat this duck rice everyday... it is so damn good!!!

feels very comforting like home cooked food, because there's not too much oil and sodium! and yet, so big on flavour!!! duck is deboned and tender, and the yam rice super fragrant. don't leave out the sambal too

even the duck soup is super tasty
author: Nic

review_text:
Service was great! Generous portion of beef and love the cucumber slices to give a twist and crunch to the sandwich which does blend well with the beef marination. Beef was abit too flavourful for me but overall was yums! Good to share for two!
Tofu was good, simple but yummy with its seasoning! 💯 looking forward to healthy high protein meal, this is one of the places to get it!💯
author: phyllis tan

review_text:
Tried the beef sandwich and mushroom cheese sandwich, both are very delicious and fillings were generous for this process! Can tell that the owners had put in a lot of effort into thinking through the menu and taste profiles of the sandwiches. Portions are great for sharing.

It was crowded during peak hour on a weekend but the food was worth the wait! Highly recommend to visit this shop!
author: Lee Zheng Fen (LZF)

review_text:
I visited on 2 occasions so I managed to try a few of the different sandwiches. Tried the Christmas festive special in early Jan before it was taken off the menu. Subsequently also tried the popular Big Beef Theory and CNY festive special with the Brocc n Roll (broccoli) and tofu sides.

The sandwiches were really big! Each sandwich is filled with generous fillings and the different ingredients in the sandwich really complement each other. Loved the fluffy focaccia bread as well! The sides were unique and yummy too!

It was great that gloves were provided so I did not get my hands dirty at all :)
author: Rachel L

review_text:
Couple owners are so friendly and generous with their portions! Ordered beef and ham sandwiches, which both were super rich and flavourful! took my gf here for lunch and now its bookmarked in maps for future dates

i braved the rain for this. 10/10 would come again
author: timothy choo

review_text:
Went for lunch and was really impressed. I ordered the beef sandwich and it was delicious - tender, flavourful, and nicely balanced without being too heavy. The bread had a great texture and held everything together perfectly. I also tried the broccoli side, and it was refreshing, tasteful and addictive!

Overall, it was a satisfying meal with quality ingredients and great execution. I’ll definitely be coming back to try the other sandwiches on the menu!
author: J L

review_text:
Had lunch at Mita Sushi today and overall enjoyed the experience. I ordered the mentai salmon set, along with salmon and salmon belly sashimi.

The sashimi portions were generous — the slices were thick and large — but the texture felt a little soft, and the salmon in the mentai dish was slightly watery, which didn’t pair perfectly with the mentai sauce.

The restaurant is small but very new and clean, and the service was friendly and attentive. I especially appreciated that they offered complimentary black coffee after the meal, which was a nice touch.

Overall, it was still a pleasant meal, and I would come back to try other dishes next time.
author: Angela Chen

review_text:
We came for lunch at around 1–1:10pm and were surprised to find that there was only one other table, as I expected the place to be busier during lunchtime.

We ordered two lunch sets:
- Chirashi Bakumori Teishoku – $30 (-10%)
- Otsumami Teishoku (Half Set, Pork Belly Slices) – $16
Subtotal: $46
After discount + service & GST: $51.60

Both sets came with miso soup, potato salad, a small salad with sesame dressing, and a choice of iced or hot coffee (we skipped the coffee since we were already full and went with water instead).

The set sides were enjoyable. The miso soup was a little different—lighter in taste, but in a good way. The potato salad was excellent; it had carrot and cucumber bits that added a nice crunch, and the potatoes were mashed just enough to keep some texture. I’ve always liked sesame dressing for salads, so that was a nice touch too.

For my main, the Chirashi Bakumori Teishoku definitely lived up to its name—the sashimi were fresh, thick-cut, and piled high like a little hill. Very generous portions. That said, I’m knocking one star off because the rice was unfortunately too soggy and sticky. I’m not sure if it was because the sashimi’s moisture seeped in or the rice was packed too tightly, but it made it hard to enjoy. I only managed around a third of the rice. The rice that came with my partner’s teishoku set, however, was perfectly fine, so it might just be how the don was plated.

My partner’s Otsumami Teishoku (Pork Belly Slices) was a winner though—flavourful and comforting. The gravy was a bit salty but went really well with the rice, and she even finished all of hers!

Overall, Mita Sushi offers a good-value lunch with fresh sashimi, hearty sides, and attentive service. A solid four-star experience—I might come back and give it another try, especially to see if the rice issue was just a one-off.
author: Joey K

review_text:
Found this little gem here.

Ordered the deluxe bakumori don. At first I thought it would only be a layer of ingredients layered on top of rice but I was wrong, the ingredients took up half the bowl, it's basically stacked. The ingredients is fresh and fatty as well and the meal comes with a bowl of miso soup which is very tasty as well with seaweed and beancurd skin.

Is very impressed by this shop.

Highly recommend.
author: Sion Toh

review_text:
Good food cooked with heart & thoughtfulness. Edamami was prepared just right- warm, seasoned with just the right amount of salt & cooked just nice to allow the beans to pop satisfyingly into your mouth. The beef Otsumami was in a small bowl just right for a smaller appetite- the broth was tasty, not too salty, and the potatoes, onions & carrots boiled to a nice softened texture. The 4-5 chunks of beef were just the right bite-size & cooked so that it was soft but not soft enough to lose the fibrous texture, chewiness & taste. The green tea was prepared with care and the taste was not too dilute nor overpowering. The Unagi set was of moderate healthful size, the rice and eel were cooked to a delicious texture and extremely satisfying. The miso soup that accompanied it was rich and flavorful.

Prices are in the moderate to high range, what you would expect for good quality Japanese cuisine in Singapore. So if you factor in the quality and passion, it represents good value. No need to travel all the way into town.

The restaurant itself is almost Singapore's version of a "hole in a wall", so seating is limited. No reservations accepted as far as I can tell. So time your visits well.

A special place.
author: Colin O

review_text:
We had a wonderful dinner at this humble hidden gem! We ordered from their weekday deals menu (that had some discounts), and got the maguro don and nishiki don.

We were pleasantly surprised by the generous portion size for the fish!  So much fish that we barely had enough rice to eat with the fish 🤤.

Highly recommend giving this hidden gem a try next time you have a sashimi or don craving!!!🥹
author: Thomas Krellstein

review_text:
Fantastic!
Stumbled onto this place for lunch.
The portions were so generous that we ended up over ordering.
Not only were they generous but they were also tasty!
The original chicken was great, as was the kimchee udon. The Korean hotdog was an interesting surprise! Will definitely be back to sample more of the menu.
Oh also the lady who was serving us was very nice and made my family and I feel very welcome!
author: Shane Mardjuki

review_text: Staff were so friendly and willing to answer questions, food was piping hot and cooked to order and so so yummy. definitely recommended to come here for delicious food without breaking the bank! My favourite is the seafood pancake, one of the best i’ve had!
author: estelle oei

review_text:
Ice cold draft beer. With nice BBQ chicken rice set.
Taste pretty nice. Will try their fried chicken next round.
Staff is friendly and cozy place.
author: Play with SY

review_text: Fried chicken and ice cold glasses to go with their beer on tap!!! Glad to see a cool new addition to the neighborhood. Will definitely be back to try the other menu items!
author: Arvin Isabelo

review_text: Chanced upon this place after cycling. Amazing food and beer!!! Fried chicken is tasty, though can be juicier.
author: LQS K

review_text:
Love the atmosphere and environment of the store. Clean and well organised, everything was neat and tidy.

They don’t charge GST or service charge, so you’ll just have to order and pay from their QR code on the table, collect your meal in front and return your tray after you’re done.

They offer self service water, and there’s an array of condiments for you to use at your table.
I would say it’s good for customers looking for a fuss-free meal, especially solo diner friendly.

Ordered the regular broth Hokkaido ramen ($12.90). It came with bamboo shoots, black fungus, seaweed, half an egg and 2 slides of char siu.
Decent bowl of ramen, but nothing outstanding. Enjoyed the addition of bamboo shoots and the char siu was so tender.

Soup was slightly too salty for me unfortunately.
author: Joey

review_text: Rare and wonderful find in Bukit Timah Plaza. The heavy broth is a bit too salty for me (they did warn you in advance on the saltines) so I usually go for the Black Garlic Oil Ramen. Absolutely tasty! Staff is friendly and the place is cozy and clean. I'll definitely be back again!
author: Yen Trinh

review_text: Order the original Hokkaido ramen and gyoza. Authentic taste and service is really excellent! Chefs are friendly and helpful!
author: Ryan Ng

review_text: Had the spicy hokkaido kare miso ramen here. The broth was rich and flavourful, and the chashu portion was very generous. Service was also good.
author: Ong Ray Yi

review_text: Noodles are broken. Its a taboo. Gyoza generally taste ok. But seem from commercial brand.
author: Sean Weng

review_text: Huge chunks of sashimi in my kaisen don! Biting into them was pure glee, especially since I had been craving them for a while now! The service staff were also very friendly, hospitable and prompt in manner. Overall it was an enjoyable experience eating here!
author: Chee How Kwok

review_text:
truffle chirashi don was worth it - $15.90 for a generous portion of really fresh cubed sashimi. (however the truffle oil fragrance was quite light)

unagi don was great! for $15.90 the unagi was thick, flavourful and teriyaki sauce was tasty.

overall a great atmosphere tho there aren’t many seats, so the waitresses may rush to clear your table immediately once you’ve finished the soup/salad/main.
author: Us The Creators

review_text:
[BEAUTY WORLD, SINGAPORE] Having tried @tsukijikaisendon, I had to try @zushishou knowing that they are from the same owners. Undoubtedly, their sashimi quality is similar though I find myself liking the seasoned sushi rice from Tsukiji more.

Their Kaisen Don 🐟 ($20.90) is really a sight to behold. Incredibly thick sashimi slices of hamachi, salmon and scallops is really the dream of every sashimi lover. Their hamachi is probably my favourite, due to its sweet, clean and fatty flavour. I don't think I need to say much given the visuals of the bowl 🤣 really worth it considering how much sashimi you're getting!

If you like variety, their Irodori Chirashi Don 🐟 ($19.90) might be your go-to. The sashimi here is chunky, and you get tuna, mackerel and a tiny bit of uni in addition to the ones mentioned above. The uni is my favourite, as it was like a shot of seafood flavour that was intense but clean.

Somehow the rice here seems under seasoned as compared to that of Tsukiji, but still good! My only other gripe is that their using some kind of wasabi paste, not the freshly grated one but I guess it's difficult to achieve that given the affordable price point.

Definitely coming back for more!
author: Jason Ng

review_text: This is probably the more popular chirashi don place at Bukit Timah Plaza. The prices are very reasonable and it comes with free salad and miso soup. The seafood is fresh and nice. Overall it is very good at this price point. I would have preferred the rice to be a bit more flavoured. Service was good and the vibes are great.
author: Ban Heng Choy

review_text: Really bad experience which shocked me cos I tried this before. This time the food was not fresh… The maguro consistency was gross. Don’t know how they can serve this… and the boss was really rude which shocked me and my family. Then afterwards we got food poisoning… Not sure how it got the good reviews, but quality has really gone down. Be careful on visiting this place, there’s really no quality control and they don’t admit it too. I would not visit anymore sadly. For those looking for chirashi or kaisendon, would instead recommend Kei Kaisendon that has consistently good quality over the past few years.
author: Jonathan L

review_text:
Came to this mall for the bank and decided to have lunch here. It wasn’t crowded when I arrived and there was plenty of seating. The place has a homely feel and the uncle at the counter was friendly.

I ordered the chicken cutlet noodles and a hot barley drink. You’ll need to add the chili yourself, it’s not mixed in for you. The food was average for the price, portions were small, and the cutlet wasn’t really to my liking. The noodles were alright, nicely cooked. However, the chili containers were empty and hadn’t been refilled. The barley drink was also a little too sweet for me.

Overall, it’s an okay spot for a quick meal if you’re nearby but not something I’d go out of my way for.
author: June Ang

review_text: Simple home cooked food and its simplicity is the attraction.  Quite expensive but yet popular among the frequent visitors to this mall.
author: derek neo

review_text: This snack bar has been our family’s favourite. We sometimes come to Bukit Timah Plaza just to order something here for lunch. We particularly like the noodles here. The wanton noodles is highly recommended. They now have a seating area in the open atrium which certainly heightened the dining experience. Try it and you will come back again!

review_text:
Went to Zzang Korean Food at Bukit Timah Plaza for lunch — one of my regular spots since it’s close to my office! 🍽️🇰🇷

They’re located at the highest level of the mall, and I’ve honestly lost count of how many times I’ve visited.

What keeps me coming back?
✨ Free-flow side dishes
✨ Free water
✨ A wide variety of comforting Korean dishes
✨ Friendly service every time

This round, I ordered their Vegetarian Japchae — stir-fried glass noodles with assorted vegetables. Light, flavourful, and perfect for anyone looking for a vegetarian-friendly option. 🌱🍜

If you’re around Bukit Timah Plaza and craving good Korean food, Zzang is definitely worth a visit!

review_text:
Went to Zzang Korean Food at Bukit Timah Plaza (Level 2) with my students — it’s been a while!
Heard they’ve got a new menu, Dwaeji Gukbab (돼지국밥),
so we just had to try it!

The soup was so rich and milky,
with tender pork slices that just melted in my mouth.
Paired with fluffy white rice — wah, so comforting and clean! 🤍🍚
Felt like a real, authentic Korean-style gukbab!

And honestly, the price is super reasonable! 💸
If you like Bak Kut Teh or Chicken Soup,
you’ll totally love this one too.

Perfect for a cozy lunch or when you need a bit of a body boost!
Zzang Korean Food — truly 짱! 😋🇰🇷🍲
author: Xina Park

review_text:
We were looking for a quick lunch spot in Bukit Timah Plaza before grocery shopping and ended up at Zzang Korean Food on the top floor (first to the right of the escalator). The place had a few empty tables while most eateries downstairs were packed, so we decided to give it a try.

Prices were reasonable, with no service charge and even a 10% student discount. We ordered one of the sets for 2 and paid at the counter (they accept cash, PayNow, and cards). The meal came with 3 complimentary appetizers and hot tea, and the food was served quite quickly in generous portions.

Taste-wise, the food was OK. Nothing spectacular, but not bad either. Friendly and fast service overall. I wouldn’t make a trip just for this restaurant, but if I’m already in Bukit Timah Plaza, it’s a decent option for a quick, fuss-free meal.
author: Ivan Loh

review_text:
This was my first visit, and it proved to be an extremely disappointing and unacceptable experience.

To begin with, I was incorrectly overcharged on my credit card. The error was only rectified after I raised it with a staff member who appeared to be the person in charge. This incident raises concerns about billing accuracy and transparency - whether this was a genuine mistake or indicative of a recurring dishonest practice of overcharging customers.

I placed an order for just one pancake at 12:19pm. Despite observing that other tables who ordered after us were served earlier, my order was repeatedly delayed. I had to follow up several times before any action was taken.

My single pancake was eventually served at 12:59pm - a 40-minute wait for a simple item. Such a prolonged delay, coupled with the billing discrepancy, reflects poorly on the stall’s operational standards and service integrity. This experience has significantly undermined my confidence in this stall.
author: Chris Chris

review_text: Nothing fancy but a nice place to grab some Korean food. Prices were fair. The staff was flying, it was busy! The food was good for the price. Try a pancake. There is limited seating and it was full constantly. I saw a lot of take out. Thank you for the good experience. The chicken and pork bulgogi were enjoyable. The chef is cranking it out from a super tiny kitchen!
author: Tyler Dixon

restaurant_name: Baan Chadar Thai Cuisine Pte Ltd | Best Thai Food In Singapore
review_text:
Pretty mediocre food actually. Ive been to Thailand multiple times and my partner has grown up there and this is definitely NOT it.

I suspect the other reviews are paid for or biased? Beef was dry and rubbery, pork was dry to and the tom yum seafood soup was mediocre at best. The food is pretty expensive too.
author: Joshua

restaurant_name: Baan Chadar Thai Cuisine Pte Ltd | Best Thai Food In Singapore
review_text: Best tomyum fried rice I ever had, very rich with spices and perfect with the aromatic Thai tomyum. Portion is big, tastes yummy, very authentic Thai food I would say, recommended.
author: Siew Ean LIM

restaurant_name: Baan Chadar Thai Cuisine Pte Ltd | Best Thai Food In Singapore
review_text: I passed by this place twice around lunchtime and saw that it was full house, with diners seeming happy. So, I made a trip down today to try it. I ordered the Pineapple Fried Rice, Tom Yum Seafood Clear Soup, Grilled Pork, and Kailan with Oyster Sauce. The grilled pork was the best, and the rest were okay. Overall, good but not wow.
author: LP Pua

restaurant_name: Baan Chadar Thai Cuisine Pte Ltd | Best Thai Food In Singapore
review_text:
Small Thai resto that’s big on taste! Authentic tasting Thai food tucked away in Bukit Timah Plaza. We found a seat immediately at around 6pm but a few minutes later, there was a queue. Food came quick and service was alright - can’t complain.
For spicy dishes like tom yam soup, you can specify the level of spiciness. Normal is pretty spicy if you’re not into chillies. More spicy means you might have tom yam shooters later 😅.

Loved the taste of the red ruby desert but the ice was pretty rough.  Otherwise, I highly recommend this place for your Thai food fix.
author: iaMR_Skye

restaurant_name: Baan Chadar Thai Cuisine Pte Ltd | Best Thai Food In Singapore
review_text: The coconut soup was chock full of ingredients and chicken. Very flavourful and slightly spicy. The omelette was fantastic, crispy and deep-fried. Best eaten while it’s fresh out of the oil. We also had the pineapple fried rice which was tasty. Thai milk tea was not overly sweet. There might be a wait during peak times but worth the wait!
author: S Elan

author: Chin Serng Siew

author: Greg Blackwood

review_text:
My go-to Korean restaurant whenever I crave for Korean food. Weekends always busy, but they have 2 kitchens so food served quickly. Service also very prompt & friendly. Sajangnim very hospitable, went around giving Korean yogurt drinks to diners.
As usual the seafood pancake is very crispy & generous with seafood. Super love their kimbap because very little rice and full of ingredients (I don’t like those with too much rice). The soy garlic fried chicken is must try, moist and super crunchy with addictive sauce. The kimchi soup is seasoned just right and soothing to go with the dishes. First time trying bossam, the pork belly is flavourful and melt in the mouth.
Chat with Sajangnim, everything is handmade in their kitchens including the banchan, kimchi & chicken-mu.
Highly recommend 👍🏻
author: dreamersloft17

review_text:
We visited Myung Ga II with a group of 6 and had a very satisfying dinner. The first thing that stood out was the service—the staff were incredibly attentive, meticulous, and considerate throughout our meal.

​The Highlights:
​Fried Chicken: We shared the Yangnyum and Soy Garlic chicken. Both were excellent—crispy wings coated in very flavourful sauces.
​Seafood Pancake (Haemul Buchu Jeon): Texture was on point—crisp on the outside, soft on the inside, and it paired perfectly with the dipping sauce.
​Kimchi Stew (Kimchi Jeongol): Served bubbling hot! It was comforting, packed with pork belly, and had a great deep Umami flavour.

​The "Be Aware":
​Donkatsu: The portion is genuinely HUGE—I almost couldn't finish it!. It was very crispy, though I found the pork a bit leaner than I usually prefer. Also, note that the sauce is a distinct Korean style (savoury, sweet, slightly tangy); it’s good, but if you are a die-hard fan of Japanese Miso Katsu sauce like me, it hits differently.
​Cheese Tteokbokki: My daughter tried this. It was decent/ok, but didn't stand out as much as the other dishes.

​Overall, the portions are incredibly generous (we spent about $185 for 6 people and were stuffed). We will definitely be back to try the noodles next time!

review_text:

author: Pearl

review_text: This is our 2nd time here at their Bt Timah Plaza outlet. The dishes we ordered were delicious and we appreciate that the portions’ big! Lady Boss was around, she was really friendly and warm. We will come back again!
author: Audreyyy

review_text: Very good restaurant serving authentic Korean food for years now. The sides were great especially the kimchi very different from others. Signature soy sauce chicken were excellent. However the cold noodles were a bit too bland. Gimbap was also good though.
author: Jack

review_text:
Very solid nasi lemak shop, ran by friendly folks behind the counter, with a good selection of tasty food!

💵 it definitely is pricey though, at $6.60 for 1 fish fillet and 3 “vegetables”, comparable to a nasi padang shop which typically is pricier.

🍚 that said, they do have one of the best begedils i have had, the rice itself was lightly fragrant too, paired with an amazing chilli which didn’t overpower the ingredients.

🪑 there’s limited seats though, and definitely a lot of table sharing during lunch time like we did - the corner seats near the fridge was definitely too warm for more than 5 minutes, something to note if you are coming here.

Definitely one that i would like to return to in future 👍🏻
author: YY

review_text: The food is delicious. However I find it overpriced for what I have ordered. I would only go here when I am desperate for good Nasi padang at the area around Bukit Timah Plaza. I paid $9.80 for my takeaway.
author: M V C

review_text:
One of my favourite malay rice stall. Limited dishes, but everything I've tried is very good. Highly recommend the beef rendang, chicken curry and black ink squid (if available).
Limited seats unfortunately.
author: Mihwa Lee

review_text:
I come here to tabao and makan quite often. The food is yummy and brings back a lot of nostalgia! Really feels like home-cooked food.

I’m from Thailand, and sometimes when I miss that comforting, homey taste, eating here makes me feel so happy. You can really taste the love in the cooking ~ it’s different in a good way, very heartwarming.

The folks at the stall are always super sweet and helpful too. Will keep coming back to support for sure! 😊
author: Titisa Jeamsakul

review_text:

On the whole, would recommend this place.

author: Merlynn Tan

review_text:
This was my first time visit here to celebrate my friend’s birthday.

The valet service was excellent as we were assisted by a very friendly young indian parking attendant on where to park our car. He had also recommended us to must try the pizza and cheese cake. We ordered cooked ham & mushroom pizza, it was indeed very delicious and was well received by everyone. The cheesecake was nice and delicate. For the mains, l ordered lamb chop, it was tender and not dry though well done.

However, there was a point that I would like to share. As we were seated next to the door opening, the door had been opened/closed frequently which produced a little irritated sound when it repeatedly hit onto the door knob. I think by adding a small foam on the door knob can help to reduce the sound effect so that the whole dining experience can be improved.

Overall, the ambience, food and  service were great. Highly recommended!
author: Christina Tan

review_text: Complimentary fresh bread was a nice touch but the olive oil provided in the dip looked very thin and tasted very diluted, maybe it’s not olive oil but something else… lasagna was great with ragù and bechamel but would be a little better if were provided with some parmigiano to sprinkle on. Porchetta wasn’t dry and seasoned well, baked potatoes were great but mustard is a strange pairing for me and I would’ve preferred something brighter and more acidic like salsa verde. However the complimentary bowl + a scoop given with the Porchetta of boiled vegetables is something I didnt like, it was just a bunch of unseasoned bland boiled vegetables, would’ve been better if it were not served. Fish with tomato sauce was decent and cooked well. Pizza with prosciutto and mushroom was done great albeit in a thinner crust style. Limoncello cake however had a grainy texture which I didn’t really like, but the vanilla gelato was great. Portion sizes were excellent and value for the money. Really loved the free corkage service on Tuesday, enjoyed my bottle of recioto di Soave in the great environment. However perhaps there are some things with regards to the taste which could be considered.
author: Chua Mingxiu

review_text:
La Braceria Pizza & Grill offers a refined take on Italian comfort, where the charcoal grill (the "braceria") takes center stage. The "Chef’s Specials" are the clear stars, featuring a succulent Wagyu Flank Steak with chimichurri ($38).
For a standout starter, the Portobello mushrooms—oven-baked and smothered in a silky parmesan cream sauce—are practically mandatory. It’s ambiance, it’s the kind of spot where a glass of red wine feels like a requirement, not an option.
author: Bruce

review_text: A hidden gem!! Everything was so good I can see why it’s packed even though the location is so uluu. The sea bass was too die for literally melted in my mouth. Burrata oh so creamy. Steak was good too. Sadly way too stuffed for dessert. Relatively affordable too. Will be back!!
author: Sarah Constance

review_text:
it was a full house on Saturday night but the staff were fast in delivering food.

Food was okay. The roast beef was the best dish and tasty.

the pasta was average. the pizza is heavy loaded with ingredients which the dough cannot handle.

Atmosphere was very nice. Worth going on a date or night out with family and friends.
author: Chris Quek

review_text: Horrible experience. Waited almost 1hr for the first salad dish to come. Don't order their seafood, they probably had to defrost or head out to catch for them. The revamped menu does nothing to enhance the dining experience when 4 of us, and 3 other tables, have to wait a very long time for our food. Some of the other diners wanted to leave after waiting more than 45mins and suddenly, they brought out some complimentary bread for every table in the restaurant. It was not even full house, mind you. Looks like they only have 1 cook in the kitchen. Think you are better off going to Pasta Mania for quicker service and portions. P.s. The sword fish dish at almost $40 is not worth getting as fish is hard and over cooked.
author: jo tan

review_text:
Always a good time here.

author: Emmanuel

review_text:
This is my first visit in years. The pasta is still good, u can choose from a wide variety of pasta to go with the sauce of your choice, and that is always welcomed. Though I do think that it is a bit overpriced, hence the 4 stars.

The pizza is good too. They serve the thin crust type, which I like. Crust was crispy with generous toppings :)

If u're looking for a cosy pasta place to spend some time with your family or friends, this is a good place. I would recommend it, but it is not a place for the 'budget conscious'.
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text:
First time trying!
Food was decent, steak was rather thin, but pastas were huge. Drinks were good, especially the margaritas. Service was not that great though.
author: I Kuan

review_text:
Lazy Lizard at Sixth Avenue is a true neighborhood gem. The atmosphere is cozy and welcoming, perfect for casual dinners or drinks with friends. The staff are consistently friendly and attentive, which makes every visit feel relaxed and enjoyable.

The nachos are a standout: crispy, generously portioned, and served with tasty dips that pair perfectly with a cold beer. It’s the kind of snack that sets the tone for a great evening.

Portions are hearty, pricing is fair, and the drinks menu offers a solid range of beers and cocktails. Whether you’re popping in for a quick bite or settling in for a longer night, the service and quality stay consistent. No surprise they’ve earned nods like the Singapore Food Master awards (2020–2022).

Overall, Lazy Lizard delivers on its promise of being a cosy neighborhood spot with hearty Western fare, friendly staff, and a warm, welcoming vibe. Highly recommended if you’re in Bukit Timah and craving good food with good company.
author: Jiak Pa Liao

review_text: Tried the pork rack, beef sirloin and aglio olio with prawns. All dishes tasted great, the pork rack was tender and juicy and prawns were big in size and delicious.
author: Eunice

review_text: We went quite late I. The afternoon. Place was quiet and the food came out really fast. Really appreciate the food. So yummy! 😋 Will definitely be back again 😍
author: Jayasri N

review_text:
Had Wine clam pasta and rack of pork, along with half a dozen of cheese oysters.
Especially enjoyed the rack of pork, oysters were delightful as well.
author: Vivian Tan

review_text: Been here twice for breakfast and it's one of my favourite cafes. The black coffee is just perfect that we even bought the beans. Brunch is delicious with good portion.
author: Emily Ho

review_text: Came here for a quick and light breakfast on a Saturday morning with wife. Had a matcha latte, a café latte, and a pastry. Also ordered another pastry to go. Total came up to over $20, which we paid with triple plus points and vouchers. Service was polite and professional. Ambience was quite good as well.
author: Sihan Goi

review_text:
Was within Greenwood landed estate… came for a caffeine fix in during weekday’ afternoon.
It has both indoor and outdoor seatings. Decided the latter as the weather was overcast.  I usually have their sourdough breads… but was too full. So a nice long black will do.
Good plc to do some reading/ catching up with frens. And free parking along the street.
Do expect this plc to be crowded during weekends!
author: YL Wong

review_text:
Had brunch here with friends after hiking at Bukit Timah. Ordered a big breakfast with a cup of iced black coffee.

Big breakfast is really good and the environment is nice. It was quite packed with customers at this location, that we decided to leave after finishing our food and drink.

Overall, the food is better than I expected. Pricing is a little too high. Will go back once in a while to enjoy the food here.
author: Keith Wong

review_text: Nestled at a quaint new neighbourhood, it’s quiet and amongst greenery. Went twice. Yesterday went during weekend night and the crowd is manageable. We sat outside and order a pizza, a prawn aglio olio and a bbq pork ribs for sharing. With three coffee priced at $6.50 each the bill came up to $97 for three persons. I think it’s decent pricing. The cafe offered us three small cups of earl grey tea on the house. As well as three cookies. Service is very good and attentive though we were seated outside. The cafe also has very nice artisanal bread if you are a bread person. Go for its fruit sourdough. It’s yummy and healthy.
author: Swanie Paddles

review_text:
R Italian Kitchen and Smokehouse brings authentic Italian flavors together with a warm, modern charm, creating a dining experience that feels both comforting and refined. Their hot starters are the perfect way to begin, the Fried Calamari is crispy and tender, the Burrata Pizza and Truffle Mushroom Pizza offers an earthy indulgence that’s hard to resist. Each dish highlights the freshness and quality of ingredients that make Italian cuisine so loved.

The pasta dishes are equally impressive, with the silky Pasta Carbonara, flavorful Crab Linguine, and the showstopping Seafood in a Bag showcasing the kitchen’s skill and passion. Love the smoked Beef Brisket. To end on a high note, the Tiramisu is a must-have, light, velvety, and perfectly balanced in sweetness.

Overall, R is not just a restaurant but a true celebration of Italian cooking, ideal for cozy dinners, special occasions, or simply indulging in authentic comfort food.
author: Angie Tan

review_text: We over ordered for this meal. The pizza , pasta and calamari is great. The shared platter came last and we were too full for it, ended up taking away most of it. I should be coming here again but focusing on the sides , pizza and pasta vs the mains.
author: Escilpe

review_text:
This restaurant is 500m in the side road off Dunearn road surrounded by the Atas private residential, recommend to drive there instead.

Want to dine there for the past year and today lunch happens family are available😊 to make this food trip.
Simple starter fried calamari is chewy and goes down with a beer 🍺 on a hot day.

Mushroom soup is delicious not too creamy and the Hawaiian pizza 🍕 is thin crisp with sweet juicy pineapple slices, eat while served hot.

Ricotta Ravioli has 3 big pieces with blue cheese cream sauce wraps in spinach is well boiled & tasty too.
Smoked Wagyu beef brisket with meat tenders soft, fresh green & potatoes are good. This dish is good for two sharing.
author: Thomas Saw

review_text: Had my first time to Rubato to celebrate anniversary with my husband. We ordered beef bolognese as one of the dishes. The waiter gave us a scornful and rather arrogant “lecture” of how we should correctly pronounced “beef bolognese” He further added on to say “Please don’t say it like this anymore, people who understand beef bolognese won’t pronounce it this way” and implied that it’s very low class to not know the true way of saying these two words. To be honest, we felt that was quite demeaning and unnecessary to us customers. Well we may not have gotten the right pronunciation of “beef bolognese” This certainly was a very unwelcoming and unforgettable encounter to this “high class” restaurant, it left a very bad taste whenever we passed by this place again.
author: Helen Tan

review_text:
Valentine Day set is disappointing. Totally not worth the $400+

The total price for each item ala carte is still cheaper than the set and you can definitely get more quantity. Only difference is the Antipasta course - which they bundled with the first course and add only 2 small pieces of Uni and 1 piece of scallop.

Their classic Angel Hair is still nicer by the way with more scallops and less marked up. The staffs even tried to smoke me that ingredients used in this set menu are special and not possible to order them ala carte..... as if this is my first time here. But well, this will probably be my last if the food I had under Rubato before the rebrand is their "special highlights" like what they said.

PS: It is marketed as a 4 course which includes Amuse Bouche (which is just a spoonful of appetiser). It will be less misleading if they say it is a 3 course meal.
author: Chong Shao Siong

review_text: Haven’t had breakfast here in a while but wow, the sour dough with eggs & mushrooms are very well done plus good strong coffee.  I also think their croissants are excellent. A simple place with freshly prepared food done on site, regular go-to for those living in the neighbourhood.
author: Winston Khoo

review_text:
Casual stop overto have some me time after lunch. Quite a few bread options to choose but I just ordered the croissant to try and a cup of cuppuccino.

The croissant is normal, nothing to shout about. The cuppuccino was a disappointment, overly bitter. Overly extracted probably. Maybe try other bakes next time, croissant might be too high a bar for most bakers.

A homely place to chill out though the air is abit "stuffy" because its open to the kitchen. But still a nice place to spend some quiet time.
author: Nixon Neo

review_text: My 1st visit to Simply Bread @Guteria House, which was recommended to me. The cafe is no-frills but the bread & pastries selection was vast. Everything looked good and was reasonably priced … really appreciated that.
author: Josephine Tan

review_text: Nice little spot but the food was very average. The French toast was too eggy and tasteless in particular. The omelette was not bad though. Staff are friendly.

author: KARIN

review_text:
We hosted our team Christmas dinner at Yi Residence and had a wonderful experience.

Terence was very easy to talk to and always quick to reply, which made the whole arrangement smooth and stress-free. When we arrived at the venue, we were warmly greeted by Carmelle, and the Christmas music playing immediately set a lovely, festive mood.

Chef Joseph Yeo prepared truly exquisite food! He was incredibly knowledgeable about the produce and had a wonderful way of telling a story with each dish he presented, which made the dining experience even more special.

The place itself was beautiful and perfect for hosting guests. We were a group of 8, yet it felt very spacious. There were also karaoke and games available, although we didn’t get a chance to use them.

Highly recommended :) We’ll definitely be back!
author: Nicole Sy

review_text: My first time at Yi Residence with friends was an intimate birthday celebration with great food and service. Big thank you to Chef Joseph Yeo and the team for their attention to tiny details like tabletop birthday decor and accommodating our drink & dessert requests.
author: Charlene Sng

review_text: Yi Residence exceeded all expectations. The venue is stylish, spacious and comfortable, with great attention to detail in both decor and service. The food was exceptional from canapés to dessert, everything was perfectly cooked and beautifully presented. Truly an outstanding venue for any special occasion!
author: Jo Jo

review_text: A cosy private dining space set the perfect homey vibe for our gathering. We savored the chef’s delectable dishes, paired with several bottles of quality sake, and wrapped up the lovely session with two lively hours of KTV fun!
author: Cons C

review_text:
No rating for food as we didn’t opt for their private dining options, but went for pure venue hire instead.

The place is gorgeous, as per what the images show, and the staff Carmelle was a great help. She’s always willing to assist us and we truly appreciate her responsiveness.

The house is spacious, able to fit more than 20 pax easily. The modern interior design made us feel like we were visiting someone’s new house.

There’s plenty of facilities in the house - you have a karaoke room, a mahjong room, and a cigar room even, along with a huge hall and a very good sized kitchen.

Personally we would have preferred the karaoke to be on level 2, which is also where the main living and dining hall is at. This would have been a bit more convenient for us to mingle and enjoy the karaoke at the same time.

Lastly, do note that as it is still a private residence, there are neighbours staying next door. Do remind the host to shut all windows (which it wasn’t for our event), and I would propose to the host to also install acoustic blinds. Otherwise, it may be slightly challenging to avoid disturbing the neighbours, particularly when we were truly enjoying the company and having laughters through the night.

Nevertheless, this is a place that I would still recommend others to book, and I would be open to book the venue for myself again in the future.
author: CeeKay

review_text:
The tables were carefully setup, place was cosy. No loud music so we can have a good time chatting.

Servers Ms Chini and Ms Magdalene were great too, very friendly and helpful;)

The pork dish, crabby pasta & bread were good.. Clams could have been bigger/better quality.  Overall good experience, will be back.
author: Dash T

review_text:
Came here on a Friday night and was surprised that the restaurant wasn’t very crowded.

The food portions were generous, which was a nice plus. However, I felt there is still room for improvement in the taste of the fish and chips.

Overall, it’s a decent restaurant for families, especially considering the large portion sizes, though the food quality could be improved.
author: Toast

review_text: I had a fantastic time at The Little Lizard! The food was delicious, and the atmosphere was perfectly laid back. It’s rare to find a spot that is this kid-friendly while still having a cool vibe for adults. It's the perfect place to chill out with family and friends. Highly recommend!
author: Roy Shao

review_text: Nice atmosphere and very family friendly. I always come here with my kid for the Kid meal and also enjoy a quiet Lunch by myself. The pricing is reasonable and food is good. Decor is cute with the lizards scattered around. The mushroom soup was super thick and creamy and I savoured every drop.
author: Teh Bee Fah

review_text: I had such a fantastic time here! 🤩 The food was absolutely delicious, and the atmosphere was really lovely and inviting. 🍝🥗 I truly enjoyed my experience and would highly recommend this place to everyone! 👍✨
author: Peishan Yu

review_text:

review_text: Very good Indian food. The naan and Dal Takha are very good, better than a lot of places :). The restaurant staffs are very friendly. Highly recommended!

review_text:

author: Jake Morris

review_text: The atmosphere compliments the spectacular food amazingly, this is all due to the service and pure excellence of this restaurant. I recommend to anyone!

review_text: Celebrated Kong Kong’s birthday here last weekend with the family. For a Saturday morning it was completely empty so we had the restaurant all to ourselves. We ordered a range of timsum, braised duck, truffle beef cubes and of course birthday noodles. All were excellent, especially the melt in your mouth beef cubes and tender duck slices. Service was also exceptional and the staff waited on us hand and foot and even gave us a tour of the function rooms for future visits. Will definitely come again for dinner one day.

restaurant_name: Soi Thai Soi Nice @ Sixth Ave
review_text:
This outlet offers both indoor & outdoor seating.

🥘 Royal Thai Hotpot (choice of Tomyum Red, Yam Fish or Tomyum Clear) $39.80
🐷 Jellied Pork Trotters $11.90
🐟 Thai Style Steamed Seabass $36.90
🦀 Stir-fried Fish Maw with Crab Claw $28.90
🍤 Breaded Prawn Donuts $8.90

The Royal Thai Hotpot is good for sharing, and you can even add on fresh fish slices for just $12. Our favourites were the stir-fried fish maw and the crispy breaded prawn donuts. The jellied pork trotters were wonderfully well-made and had that delightful jiggle. We ended on a sweet note with their Snowflake Yam, a sugar-coated addictive yam dessert that is a tasty alternative to the usual mango sticky rice or red ruby.

restaurant_name: Soi Thai Soi Nice @ Sixth Ave
review_text:
We visited Soi Thai Soi Nice at Sixth Avenue for their opening and had such a great experience. The food was delicious across the board — the Signature Royal Thai Hotpot was rich and comforting with just the right level of spice, the Thai Style Steamed Seabass was fresh and perfectly seasoned, and we loved the Breaded Prawn Donut and Braised Pork Belly with Yam for their unique flavors. The Jellied Pork Trotters were surprisingly moreish, and the Snowflake Yam made for a lovely dessert. Drinks like fresh coconut and Thai milk tea paired so well with the meal.

On top of that, the Thai dance performance was truly charming and made the celebration feel extra special (only for the opening day). Overall, it was a memorable dining experience with authentic Thai-Teochew flavors and a warm atmosphere.

restaurant_name: The Sixth Noodle House @ Soi Thai Soi Nice
review_text:
Lovely vibey place to chill at Sixth Avenue! Atmosphere Bistro & Bar has a warm, laid-back ambience — perfect for casual catchups or winding down after a long day.

The menu is impressively extensive, offering a mix of Thai, Western, fusion dishes, and even all-day breakfast. We were spoilt for choice and ended up trying quite a spread:

Grilled Pork Neck – juicy, flavourful, and perfectly charred

Breaded Prawn Donut – fun, crispy, and addictive, a bestseller here according to the staff

Seafood Tom Yum Soup – spicy, tangy, and full of ingredients, the prawns and squids in it are very fresh

La Zi Ji – fragrant with that satisfying Sichuan kick (this is done by their Thai chef btw)

Mega Platter – great for sharing, ideal for variety lovers, there're sausages, nachos, chicken wings, fried white bait, fried pork cutlet & lemongrass pork popcorn, an intriguing combo served with sauces

Garlic Butter Mussels – aromatic and buttery, love how they serve this western classic with a crispy prata on top. The prata pairs so well dipped into the sauce!

Truffle Bacon & Mushroom Pizza – this is easily one of their most popular pizzas, great for families & kids

Tom Yum Seafood Pasta – East-meets-West done right! The pasta was perfectly al dente, with fresh seafood + the tangy mild spicy sauce

Thai Kaya Custard Soft Bun Bread with Local Kopi + egg set – comfort food with a nostalgic local twist, the pretty coloured Kaya makes it so Instagramable! Serve all day till ~5pm so you can have this set still even if u woke up late haha

Overall a great spot if you're looking for variety and chill vibes all in one place. Will definitely be back to try more! Also shout out to Steve for his impeccable service this afternoon!

author: Kevin Ang

author: Dawn Lim

author: kenshinjeff 躍洋

review_text:
A very decent Indian Muslim stall in this corner coffeeshop.  The briyani is usually ready around 1100 hrs and before that there are the usual breakfast offerings of roti prata in all its glorious variations!  The chicken briyani served here is a fried version instead of the curried version.  The flavors are good and the rice has a pleasant deep umami and is aromatic.
The texture tends to be on the slightly moist side.  I always enjoy the briyani here although I've had friends who've said their chicken was less than absolutely fresh.  Still worth a go!

review_text: great food, very slow service, ehh atmosphere… could be better it is very overpriced 😔
author: nathaniel

review_text: Carving for Nasi Lemak this morning..... Decided to go to this stall. I have fond memories of their Nasi Lemak. But this time, I left with disappointment. All the ingredients were salty, taste like they have seasoned generously with salt. Even the sweet chilli has a pronounced tone of saltiness. $8 for my order is probably on the higher price range. Overall, not a pleasant dining experience. I remembered them to be better.
author: Rick

review_text: A good friend recommended to us 2 weeks ago and we decided to try this for lunch today. Noted their closing time at 1pm which is an indication of popularity and selling out early. So we headed down slightly after 11am and by the time we ordered, the otah option was out. The rice was selling out fast too. We ordered 2 chicken wing sets and added a bergadil to share. The rice was basmati rice. Generous with ikan bilis and ground nuts. Great if they also gave more chilli. We have friends that commented that its slightly more expensive ($5.8 per serving) compared to the average hawker centres ($4-5) - but I guess we have to consider that this is the "Bukit Timah 6th Avenue" private estate locality. Overall a very enjoyable meal.
author: Mark Yeo

review_text: Old-school nasi lemak done well. Rice is fragrant with a nice texture, and the sambal has that roasted, slightly sweet flavour that keeps you eating. Chicken was a great add-on too. Simple comfort food — would recommend coming early.
author: Pio Win

review_text: Crispy chicken, nice fragrance fluffy rice, sweet-spicy sambal — this nasi lemak hits all the right notes. No frills, just pure comfort. 🍗🍳🌶️”
author: martin

review_text: Nasi lemak that opens early and closes around noon. While the nasi lemak is generally above average, it is not outstanding in all aspects. Long grain rice can do with a stronger coconut punch. Chicken wings, while tender, are not marinated enough to hit it through. The sunny side up egg is decent, without overcooking till it's leathery. All in all, a decent plate of nasi lemak but may not be worth queuing for too long.
author: Ee Kwang Han

review_text: Noodles are cooked to al Dente but the taste is below my average expectations. Maybe they are not using pork lard but vegetable oil. If this is the case, then the healthy option is not for me.
author: Michael TAN

review_text:
initially wanted to try another fishball noodle stall from a neighboring coffeeshop but unfortunately they were already closed for the day. I stumble upon this stall by chance while walking back and decided to give it a try. Apart from fishball noodle, they also sells laksa and lor mee. Price for the noodle starts from SGD4.5 onwards.The aunty behind the stall was very friendly.

The noodle was nicely cooked, texture of the noodle was springy. She added quite quite a lot of vinegar, as a result the sauce was quite tangy. The bowl of noodle came with ingredient like meatball, sliced fishcake and minced meat.

Overall, a decent bowl of minced meat noodle if you ask me.
author: Sean Goh

review_text:
Average bowl of noodles portions are small 2 fish ball 1 dense salty meatball and slices of fish cake, sprinkled mince meat on top.

Not worth $4.50 for portion & taste.

Off to find another food to fill my hunger.

review_text: A super consistent bowl of great fishball noodles. Not a huge serving but perfectly cooked noodles, perfect amount of sauce.  Mdm Eng has been doing this for 21 years! Always friendly and cheerful. Love it!
author: leslie goh

review_text: Nice and clean tasting bowl of fishball noodles with vinegar. My favourite in the Bukit Timah area. The aunty is friendly and smiles. $4.50.

Ordered takeaway - the dishes are ALL WET AND OILY!!
Deep fried crispy squid is soggy!!
Sweet sour pork is soaked in oil!!
Yam ring is soggy !!

All the reviewers are dead wrong!! The poor quality is not due to delivery (the restaurant cannot shift the blame to delivery person)

author: Jonathan

The Garlic Fried Chicken was fragrant and crispy, definitely a must order. The Salted Egg Prawn tasted really good too. I got the Fish Bee Hoon was normal and didn't feel like it was worth the $6.

Overall and enjoyable meal. Coffeeshop so don't expect any amazing ambience. Was told this was the best shop (along 6th avenue) amongst the chain.

Fried pretty well and beef was tender according to my sister.

XO fish slice bee hoon ($10) - 2 stars

author: N T

restaurant_name: Sixth Avenue Porky Prawn Noodle | 第六道豚蝦麵 (Flagship)
review_text: Yummy prawn noodle with flavourful soup and pork ribs. Their special sauce tastes like a good mix of taucheo, chilli and lime... goes very well with the pork ribs. Prawns are fresh and comes right off the shell.
author: Stephanie Tan

restaurant_name: Sixth Avenue Porky Prawn Noodle | 第六道豚蝦麵 (Flagship)
review_text:
Getting a parking lot and a seat at this coffeeshop is a huge challenge, and you will still need to brave the lunch queue for this incredibly popular prawn noodle.

Normally, such a wait would be off-putting, but here, it is worth the wait. The broth bursts with rich and satisfying prawn essence. The noodles are springy, generously portioned, and perfectly coated in chilli for the dry version. Though I’m not a fan of pork, my colleagues swear by the pig liver and pork ribs, paying extra for that tender, juicy goodness.

Still, I wish the queue moved faster. The elderly uncle can only do so much, but perhaps going cashless could help speed up the ordering process.
author: MH Tham

restaurant_name: Sixth Avenue Porky Prawn Noodle | 第六道豚蝦麵 (Flagship)
review_text:

Soupy bowl of prawn yellow noodle with prawns n pork ribs were also yummy-RM10 per bowl

author: Lyla (ZL)

review_text: 5 stars for their siew yoke. Crispy skin with the perfect ratio of fat & meat and perfectly salted. It's so hard to find this level of siew yoke in Singapore because most stalls use lean meat. Siew Yoke is not meant to be a healthy meat dish!! The duck rice was ok, the siew yoke is definitely the star of the show for me.

review_text: Don't let the unassuming stall fool you when the prawn noodle is actually the mediocre one here! The roasted pork meat when dining in is super crispy amd good ratio of lean and fat meat. skip the dry pot cauliflower... the fatty
