author: Andy sim

restaurant_name: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh, located at 58 Seng Poh Road, is a beloved breakfast spot serving traditional Teochew-style bak kut teh. This iconic eatery is famous for its flavorful, less peppery soup and tender pork ribs. Enjoy with you tiao and sambal kangkong.
author: 웬케빈

restaurant_name: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh
review_text: The Bak Kut Teh in the morning is different but not the most flavourful. In the evening, this converts into a Chinese eatery and the food is fantastic. Love their stir fry beef and lamb skewers.
author: Jeffrey C

restaurant_name: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Newly opened bkt and Chinese restaurant. Love the extensive menu and very yummy meat skewers. Food is generally good and service is prompt. There's an opening promo 20% discount for cooked dishes. Bkt is available until around 3pm.
author: Zhuo Yan Lim

restaurant_name: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Ordered the BKT and mixed platter. The pork is a tad overcooked And the ribs were hard "tough" and half "tender" Mix platter was ok while the BKT soup was robust and peppery.
author: Cookie Monster

restaurant_name: Old Tiong Bahru Bak Kut Teh
review_text:
food is really good
my favourite meat option is the long dragon bone. the meat is very soft and tender. flavour is superb.

this is the third time i’ve been to this restaurant and they never fail to suffice

the soup is flavourful and has a peppery aroma

the youtiao is better than most bakuteh stores

i like the xiancai and the tofu in braised sauce

the service was wonderful

definitely will keep on coming here for many years to come.
author: julius bean

restaurant_name: 6th Avenue Fishball Noodles by Auntie Sally
review_text: Surprisingly good fishball noodle! Ordered a mee pok dry, was cooked by a young guy in his 20s. Was doubling him thinking he is too inexperience thus it won't b nice. When l was home , mee pok was juz nice surprisingly. Usually noodle is over cooked when u packed home by the time u eat it will b too soft but he is able to do it juz nice n best part the pork lard oil n chilli sauce was juz nice too. When l stir to mix erythg tgt it tasted perfect 👍 This is the first time l packed noodle home n it taste so good 😊😊😊 Thumbs up ! Last but not least he is so detailed to even asked if l wan spring onion in my pack of soup. Asked for pork lard he gave me 2 big spoon, super generous. Service no.1. I seldom give 5 stars in my review esp not for noodle, this is one of the best l hv tried so far!
author: Joyce Lim

restaurant_name: 6th Avenue Fishball Noodles by Auntie Sally
review_text:
This is actually my 2nd visit to this stall inside a coffeeshop at Sixth Avenue. I came a little late on my first visit, thus wasn't able to try their food. Just so happen to pass by this area again and decided to give this place a try. This time round, I came around late morning. Quite surprised that there was any queue, I was able to order immediately. The price of the fishball noodle starts from SGD5 onwards.

Noodle was nicely cooked, texture of the noodle was springy. The sauce has that old school taste to it but a little too much for my liking. The bowl of noodle came with ingredients like fried wanton, sliced and minced pork and fishball.,

Overall, an above average bowl of noodle for me and would definitely highly recommend if you happen to be at the coffeshop and not sure what to eat.
author: Sean Goh

restaurant_name: 6th Avenue Fishball Noodles by Auntie Sally
review_text: Fishballs fresh and bouncy, taste like they’re made with fish and not just flour. Pork and noodle texture were great. Prawn sat in the baking soda a bit too long, noodle sauce and chili average.
author: Jonathan

restaurant_name: 6th Avenue Fishball Noodles by Auntie Sally
review_text: I actually like this bowl of fish all noodle. Have an old school style cooked by a young lad. The soup I feel could be less saltier. The fishball and minced meat was good along with the qq noodle.
author: DIn

restaurant_name: 6th Avenue Fishball Noodles by Auntie Sally
review_text: On the 13 Oct 2025 I visit sixth ave fishball noodles the fishball tender nice cook by a youngster their vinegar must put yourself so far is recommend to try
author: Ong Kianpeng

restaurant_name: Feng Wei Mixed Veg Rice Xiao Chao 峰味什菜糜小炒
review_text: My neighbourhood instant gratification.....best place to come when you are hangry. Food is always fresh (they sell out every single day) and very well cooked. Never too salty or bland. Steamed egg is a big favourite of the regulars. So to snag that, you have to be early (before noon and 6pm for lunch and dinner respectively)
author: leslie goh

restaurant_name: Feng Wei Mixed Veg Rice Xiao Chao 峰味什菜糜小炒
review_text: They open early here , very friendly and plenty of dishes to choose from
author: Princess Floss

review_text: Located within Good Good Eating House . Very respectable roast meat and for us - a high protein low carb meal complimenting the fish soup we’ve ordered
author: Elna Tan

review_text:
i don't know why there isn't more hype over this roast meat stall

the char siew and sioba r worthy competitors of hk88.... super tender meat, crispy crackling skin, good char/caramelisation
author: Nic

review_text: Decent roast meat. They have an oven. Another option as the other stalls are over rated with long q
author: chengann tan

review_text: Bought roast chicken rice with extra chicken ($6.50). Rice is good. Roast chicken is acceptable but considering we asked for extra chicken, the portion provided looked less than expected. Chilli is spicy but seems to miss something.
author: P Loh

review_text: Chicken rice and roast pork was fantastic! Set value for money. Steamed chicken and char siew (roast pork) is always sold out so go early.
author: Nicholas Ong

review_text: 5 Jun 21  - went there today, I am assuming they are COVID affected. Rice half cooked, roast chicken tasteless, chili - not sure what was that red mess. Overall - For a person that loves chicken rice, I must say, my school canteen is better. Hopefully you guys will have better days.
author: Henry Low

review_text: Horrible service. Went there a couple of times and the person serving was always grumpy, impatient with no eye contact. Will never ever buy from here again.
author: Stephanie Ong-Thomas

review_text: Attitude is bad and overcharged me too.
author: Fairy Tail

restaurant_name: 小馥苑 Fu Yuan Teochew Dining Greenwood
review_text:
Hui Ming , Hui Xuan , Lesles and Ah Kuan have a good service.

Great dining experience!

The food was delicious and nicely presented. Every dish was fresh and full of flavor. The staff were friendly, attentive, and provided excellent service throughout the meal. The restaurant atmosphere was comfortable and welcoming. Definitely a place I would come back to again. Highly recommended! 😊
author: Shu Yun

restaurant_name: 小馥苑 Fu Yuan Teochew Dining Greenwood
review_text: It's no exaggeration to say that the food here looks exactly like the pictures in the menu and tastes just as good. From what we tried, there were no misses and even the more common dishes like the stir-fried kailan and pan-fried oyster omelette were done to an excellent quality. The most unique dish tried was the marinated raw roe crab which was served with a healthy dose of roe. Surprisingly, the soy sauce marinate was not too overpowering and balanced out the rawness of the crab. Another standout was the pan-fried fish served with shark cartilage soup. The soup was rich and keeps you going back for more, while the fish was very fresh, and when fried, goes well with the soup. It was like a very high class version of fried fish soup with milk. Overall, a very nice place with a unique Teochew style zi char menu.
author: Ian Li

restaurant_name: 小馥苑 Fu Yuan Teochew Dining Greenwood
review_text:
Outstanding cooking execution by the chef. Each dish was done just right—good wok hei, proper textures, and clean flavors. A solid Chinese restaurant that focuses on technique and quality.

Very fresh seafood with excellent cooking technique. Flavors were clean and well-balanced. Dessert was just sweet enough and a lovely way to end the meal. One of the best Chinese restaurants in town. Would come back again.
author: Yan Ming Tan

restaurant_name: 小馥苑 Fu Yuan Teochew Dining Greenwood
review_text:
Had a really great experience at Fu Yuan Teochew Dining (Greenwood). Everything we ordered was excellent and well-executed.

The Pumpkin Cream Boston Lobster was nicely balanced and not too heavy, the braised duck and abalone platter was flavourful yet not overly salty, and the Salted Egg Prawn Balls were crispy outside with juicy prawn meat inside. Even the simpler dishes like the preserved radish hor fun stood out with good wok hei. The crispy eggplant was also a pleasant surprise.

Desserts were just as good — the yam paste was smooth and not too sweet, and the peach gum soup was light and refreshing.

Overall, a very satisfying meal in a quiet, comfortable setting. Definitely a place I would return to.
author: SB Lee

restaurant_name: 小馥苑 Fu Yuan Teochew Dining Greenwood
review_text:
Great Teochew cuisine tucked away in a cosy corner at Greenwood. It’s really hard to find authentic and well-executed Teochew food in Singapore, so this place was a pleasant surprise.

The staff were attentive and the overall service was excellent. Special thanks to Kaiyue, Hui Ming, Ah Kuan and Leslie for their warm and thoughtful service — they made the dining experience even better.
author: lai waiyan

restaurant_name: Nami Korean Grill House by Hanjip
review_text:
If there's additional category to rate: ONE Star for marketing team.

I made a lunch reservation at Nami Korean BBQ via Grab Chope. The restaurant sent a WhatsApp to confirm, which was appreciated. However, there was no indication on Grab or WA that Valentine’s Day set menus ($258 and $298) would be served or minimum $258 spend. The only menu on grab and google reference was the Nami Signature set at $188, which gave us a different expectation.

We were only informed about the Valentine’s Day menu and the $258 minimum spend upon arrival. While they allowed à la carte ordering, the minimum spend still applied, which was disappointing since this was not communicated beforehand.

We were seated near the entrance. We overheard conversations of a handful of others  who came in with reservations. 1 out of 5 left the restaurant as ALL were unaware of the minimum spending or special menu. 4 out of 5 seems hesitant and took some time to ponder but end up dining in.

Thought the marketing could have done a better job by a simple communication beforehand on the updated menu/minimum spending.

That said, the food was good. We had the Nami Signature Meat Platter, Ginseng Chicken Soup, and Nami Kale Salad, and everything was flavourful and well-prepared. Overall, the food quality was solid, but the lack of transparency regarding the menu and minimum spend dampened the experience.
author: Yummy Shalala

restaurant_name: Nami Korean Grill House by Hanjip
review_text: Excellent Korean BBQ experience. We booked through Chope and received complimentary Australian wagyu, which was a great bonus. We also tried A5 wagyu, pork collar, and pork jowl — all were high quality with great flavor. The staff grilled everything perfectly and plated it for us, so we could just relax and enjoy the meal. Not only was the BBQ great, but the other Korean dishes were delicious as well. Would definitely come back!
author: Milly

author: Iris

restaurant_name: Nami Korean Grill House by Hanjip
review_text: Great service and food! Really fresh soy marinated crab and meat quality, cooked by John who was so kind and friendly! The side dishes also had really authentic flavours! Highly recommend!
author: Keatyin Chin

restaurant_name: Nami Korean Grill House by Hanjip
review_text:
We celebrated our anniversary over lunch at Nami, and it was a wonderful experience. The restaurant has a very nice and cozy atmosphere, making it perfect for a special occasion.

We had the Christmas set lunch, which featured a BBQ selection of Wagyu beef strips, pork jowl, and prime strip loin. The meat marbling was impressive, and every cut was tender, juicy, and full of flavor—I absolutely loved the meats.

We also really enjoyed the anchovies with peanut side dish and the seafood stew, which complemented the BBQ perfectly. The staff were attentive, and they helped grill the meats to perfection.

Overall, it was a memorable and enjoyable dining experience. Highly recommended!
author: Evangeline Tan

review_text:
Best indian cuisine in the hood! Highly recommended for westies. They offer a wide range of food so you’ll definitely be spoilt for choice 😋🤤 The sizzler is a must try! Besides that we got garlic naan, biriyani and chicken patiala.
Plus point would be the place and friendly crew. Love the cozy environment here with beautiful lamps at every table. Will be back again :)
author: Wendy Loke

review_text: Delicious meal at Omar Shariff! We ordered the naan basket, Malabar fish curry, and pudhina gosht, everything was flavorful and well-cooked. The fish curry was rich and comforting, and the gosht was tender with a refreshing mint kick. Will definitely come back!
author: Princess R

review_text: The food was amazing and very authentic. Enjoyed every bite of it and will definitely recommend to my friends and family! Staff were friendly too and atmosphere was great with very colorful lamps at every table.
author: Kinston Herald

review_text: Fantastic Indian food, best we had our entire week in Singapore! Highly recommend for a great mix of North and South Indian cuisine, with some special dishes like the Fish tikka which was AMAZING!! Huge variety to choose from too. Can’t go wrong.
author: Christopher Schott

review_text: Had food delivery today for son's bday. Food was amazing. Butter Chicken was cooked to perfection. Rogan Josh had balance flavours. Tandoori Chicken n Chicken Tikka were so juicy. Too many dishes to mention ☺️ Been a customer since many years. No regrets as food is consistently outstanding. Highly recommend this restaurant. 😋
author: Maria Rafie

review_text:
It's our first time here but we're so impressed with the quality of the braised duck that we are ordering a whole braised duck for our party tonight.

The duck is skillfully braised with a rich tasty sauce. It is soft on the outside and tender on there inside.

The sauce has a hint or herbal essence but not too overpowering.

The soup also has an herbal taste and on the sweet side.

They also serve other local dishes on different days and local breakfast before 10am.

I tried the broth of the pork rib  prawn noodles (Wed & Thurs) and it was rich and full of the aroma of prawns but again not overpowering or overly salty.

I would say the chef is really skillful with his noodles.

They have different types of chilli sauce for the different dishes like chicken rice. buck sambal, green chilli... Etc.

This place is definitely worth a visit if you're a prawn noodles fan or braised duck fan.

🤞🤞🤞
author: Alvin Quah

review_text: A surprising find right in the heart of Greenwood. Where can one find a comfortable eatery, air-con, serving local delights and kopi/kaya toasts at such reasonable prices? We ordered kweh chap & 1 cup of kopi for about $12. Taste good too. Tissue is also provided! Nice touch. Will be back.
author: WilsonW

review_text:
Amazing value for money and comfortable ambience! Clean, air conditioned and food here is good. For those who don’t eat meat, they have plenty of meat-free side dish options.
Very hearty kuay teow soup and generous portions 😋
All these just $5! Hot coffee is $2 and iced coffee is $2.50. Super worth. Do support them!
author: Elizabeth Mok

review_text:
Braised duck value set B (braised duck, intestine, beancurd, egg, peanuts) ($8.80) - Good.

From an earlier order:
Braised duck rice with extra duck, large intestines and egg - Boneless duck and good gravy with rice.
author: Royal Pears

review_text: Really cute concept ! Love the modernisation of this classic singapore food. We tried the braised set and also the duck porridge and it was so good. Yummier than the famous market stalls and no long wait plus theres AC! 1000% would recommend.
author: Kara H

review_text: We simply LOVE these pizzas! The texture of the crust, the generosity, freshness and quality of the ingredients are unbeatable. We polished off every single pieces plus crumbs! Yumz! Highly recommend everyone to try!
author: Phoebe Yee

review_text: The pizzas are light and delicious with a variety of good quality toppings. You can taste the difference in the ham, pepperoni, mushroom, cheese which they used. Happy to support our sweet neighbours in their quest and passion for good,, honest food!
author: Karen Lim

review_text: Great pizza! The sour dough thin crust was delicious and the flavor of margherita pizza toppings was so well balance and yummy. Simply love the cheese and the tomato sauce. Looking forward to the next opening for orders.
author: A Oeij

review_text: The first bite of the pizza got me hooked! The texture and you can taste the quality ingredients. The owners are also approachable and friendly! My favs are the Hawaiian and pepperoni and the rest are really good too!
author: Jon Soon

review_text:
Pretty decent pizza.
Had a generous amount of pepperoni on chewy pizza dough.
Will definitely have it again!
author: Jing Jie Ng

review_text:
Disappointing Experience

I visited this restaurant for the first time. The unclean toilet was a major turn-off. Things didn't improve with the food - the Indian chicken briyani rice lacked the authentic flavor I've come to expect from even the simplest prata shops.
The only good is the service.
Anyway, the attached picture speaks for itself.
author: yeo clare

review_text: East or West superfamous prata is best !!🫶🏻
author: Harshit Sharma

review_text: Too expensive. You will get these for 1/3rd price in sixth avenue. Food is so so, nothing to rave about.
author: sanjeeva kumar

review_text: They got my takeaway order wrong despite me checking before leaving the restaurant.
author: Eugene Lim

review_text: It's a small outlet inside Mt Alvernia hospital. Looks for the directional signs to find it. Service staff is helpful and meal at Subway has expected certain since they have a systematic way of preparing the meals. I had the 6 inch breakfast set - Sausage Ham and Cheese. Taste good.
author: Winston C

review_text:
Ordered triple cheese rotisserie chicken.
Was informed that I could not customize the subway as it was a signature sub.

Did not fill the signature with correct vegetables.
author: Aaron

review_text:
worst subway experience and outlet i've ever been to. i've been eating at subway for the past decade or so and their quality/customer service has genuinely and objectively degraded.
first and foremost, i asked if the $6 fiery chicken 6-inch sub was valid and the staff (Seva) said yes. the first issue i encountered was being told that i was not allowed to choose my own vegetables and sauces because i had to follow the "recommended" choice on the poster. if something is recommended, it implies that its just what they think is a good choice, no? NOT something we HAVE to adhere to -- i couldn't even choose my own sauces and bread💀
Back to the $6 sub (second issue). upon paying, she charged my sub for the a la carte price for $9+ instead of the $6, arguing with me and saying that it was always $9 and pointed at the poster DESPITE me clarifying with her BEFORE ordering that it was $6
lastly, did not even receive a receipt.

terrible service and terrible experience

DO NOT dine here unless there's genuinely no other alternative/unless u want to overpay and let people choose your veggies for you
author: Oliver Lim

review_text: Justin is a true sandwich artist. Thanks for making our morning better
author: Andy Lines

review_text: Super friendly and fast service. Food was nicely wrapped. I was staying at this hospital and because hospital food was terrible I asked my mom to buy Subway for me to eat. After I got discharged my appetite was slowly gaining back so I decided to order subway again for my lunch. Friendly staff great service.😃👍🌟
author: Merlynn Koh

review_text: Below average golf terrace food. I had the drumstick chicken rice and my fren had the lala bee hoon. Both are mediocre at best. Chicken used is frozen and does not live up to the Singapore Chicken rice standard. Rice is mushy and soft. Chilli served is a mouthful serving size. Two dips and it's done. For the price charged, really? Hopefully it is just an off day for the cook today. 😔
author: Rick

review_text: A pleasant find in an unexpected location.  Very nice restaurant serving delicious local food. Service was good. The signature fried chicken wings are a bit overrated with the high price. The chicken rice with breast meat tastes very dry. The rest are good. Restaurant overlooking the golf course. Outdoor and indoor seating avail. Very nice flowers ceiling design.
author: EveC

review_text: I patrons teetop restaurant and they have good food like satatys, fried rice and specially they launched the Christmas lunch set
author: Shirlin Lim

review_text:
this is an excellent place to meet friends and enjoy a wide variety of exotic food.
next to the central water catchment area，the restaurant is close to nature， serene and tranquil.
author: Heng Yi Koh

review_text:
Nice, relaxing setting, although there isn’t a good view of the golf course. Open to public.
Tried their stir fried laksa which had a mix of yellow noodles and thick rice vermicelli, 3 prawns, squid rings and tofu puff slices. Quite a moreish dish but I would think a bit more protein and a bit less carbs would be ideal. Didn’t like that the prawns weren’t deveined.
author: JATHL

review_text: Food n ambiance is tip top! Definately worth every calories increased. Japan Oysters- pork tomahawk- Yakitori Sticks all damn power. I think they might have put some magical powder in their homemade togarashi chilli too, spicy n super goes well with everything. Meats marinated on point. Kudos to the team of charcoal Gill experts!
author: mark lim

review_text: Izakaya style, yakitori was not bad, went well with red wine. Good dining ambient in a quiet and remote area with fresh air. Nice place to chill out.
author: J Seng

review_text: Food is soooo good!! Ribeye steak was cooked to perfection. Must try their bacon lychee and pork tomahawk! Service was pretty fast, I highly recommend this place. Will definitely visit again.
author: Danica Tan

review_text: Awesome experience with good service and the food was served very quickly! Love the ambience and chill vibes of the place as i chose to dine alfresco. Must get the pork tomahawk which is so juicy and tender, and the smoked duck which comes with super crispy skin!!! Kushiyaki must gets are the bacon mushroom, pork belly and teriyaki chicken thigh. All pairs super well with beer too 😍 Super value for money and will definitely be a returning customer!!
author: melissa ang

review_text:
they told us we had to be out by a certain time as there was another booking. tat was fine, but food took a long time to come. when it finally came, couldnt really tell wat we were eating as the lighting was dim, but the yakitori sticks looked charred n burnt. told the server, he said to try it first n so we did.  but i spat it out as it was really chao ta n couldnt b eaten. asked for replacement but the replaced skewers looked fewer than the first round. as it turned out, they gave us the wrong order so we had food we didnt order.

we also ordered the kurobuta pork tomahawk as recommended but there was nothing special abt it. on the other hand, the pork belly yakitori was juicy n succulent.

to their credit, staff were polite n did their best to salvage the disastrous situation. but its highly unlikely i'll ever return.
author: Meifang Huang

review_text:
V near my office. The food overall is good.  2nd visit this time.  First visit have v good impression .
Opening special 10%discount plus food is hot n delicious, not to mention reasonably priced for the lunch set.

1st visit ordered their daily lunch set, chicken katsu with sides of vegetables plus lava eggs at only $9.9, Addition orange drink at only $1. Complementary appetizer of mini popiah n watermelon.  Super value for money. 😁

Second visit decided to try their premium - Garang beef bowl.
However, this time I waited v long for my lunch.
It is not acceptable as this is industrial / office area where we only have an hour. And when the food finally came, I do not have time to enjoy my meal because of the rush.
The beef bowl wowed me with the fried rice. 👍👍💖💖
It is so delicious to the lay mouth, but, disappointed with the beef cause it is too raw to my liking.  Surprised they did not ask me how I preferred my beef to be done. Waited so long n do not have time to return it to kitchen already so I left the beef there.
The meal would be perfect if the beef is medium to well done. :)
Coffee does not taste good .
This cost $14.90 for the rice bowl plus $1.50 coffee
author: SH Y

review_text: The beef and pork rendang is good and spicy with olive rice. Yet it’s cheap and good for a quick lunch if you’re near Bukit Merah. Perhaps the entrance and steps within restaurant is a bit difficult for handicapped or senior citizens. The car park is at 2nd entrance not the first entrance !
author: Samuel Ng

review_text: the burgers arrived - they are sliders size. totally different from the pictures on the menu. the worst part is when i’m ordering the burger i told them that i can’t take any spicy at all because i have gastric. it arrived spicy. i sent it back. won’t be back again.
author: Rene Tan

review_text: Come view and taste awesome food from Incredible Hulk and Ironman, super hero ovens 💪 from this kitchen !
author: James Peh

review_text: Food is excellent, but rather pricey. Ambience and service is very good too.
author: Raied

review_text:
This place is a bit hidden and hard to find, but totally worth it. It’s quiet and perfect for a chill beer. The mussels were especially delicious!
I happened to be wearing my Celtic FC jersey that day and was pleasantly surprised to spot something Celtic-related there—made the visit even more special.
author: LILLY

review_text: 1st time trying. Most of the food are nice, except the beef is over cooked, the grilled egg plant is also over-cooked and taste bitter. Else, the rest of the food are good. They have both indoor seatings  and outdoor seatings. Parking will be a bit challenging, and we have to park along the roadside.
author: Chris

review_text:
Far from the crowds, this little bar is located in lush greenery and sports a very laid back, old school pub/ bar kinda vibe. Staff is chilled and helpful and bar bites are good.
It has both outdoor and indoor seating. Ample parking spot outside the place. Beer and food is reasonably priced. Highly recommended for a quite evening or a gaggle with friends
author: Harsh Saxena

review_text: Had our engagement/pre wedding party here recently & dined multiple times prior to that. Thanks Alvin and team who helped organise, being a great host, and spoilt us with their scrumptious food and drinks.
author: Jolene Chua

review_text: Great service. The owners were really nice, P.S: didn’t get their names(stripes blue and black Ts), thank you for the herbal quail eggs. The food was really nice and fresh. We also had a lychee martini, bartender pour it at our table(nice touch). Sadly I drove, can’t have my Guinness so will be back soon!
author: Gerard James Rozario

review_text: Destination dining at its best! If you’re looking for an exotic, quiet, hideaway, cozy spot with delicious (Thai) food — this is it. Quite unwilling to share this dear spot because it’s such lovely escape from the hustle and bustle of city life but the food’s really great and service top-notch. It’d be a pity and disservice to them not to. Authentic Thai cuisine with excellent ambience and impeccable service. We thoroughly enjoyed ourselves. Prawn cake was amazing. Love the Thai sauce fried fish. And seafood Tom Yum goong was a delight. Definitely worth a visit even though it’s a little off the beaten track.
author: everlydaydream

review_text:
I was ordered a lot of Thai food here. Authentic taste and all delicious!
The owner was very friendly and kind.
Her mango sticky rice is the best in Singapore 👍 👍👍
Dine in and take away
author: Naklapas Watcharapariyapas

review_text: Super good. Firstly the coconut ice was really good. First time I had it and it was so refreshing while not being heavy. Greta surprise. Food came fairly quickly (15 mins) and there was a good selection which enabled all to eat. Space was a bit quirky but suited it well.
author: Bradley James

review_text:
Visited this Thai restaurant with really nice vibes—loved the environment, and the food was decent too. But honestly, the service could use some improvement. The staff couldn’t communicate in English or Chinese, and one of them accidentally dripped some dark soy sauce into my bag (which was on the empty chair next to me).
I asked for a wet tissue to clean it, but they didn’t seem to understand me!
author: iamjess

review_text: Had dinner around 8pm on a Sunday. Restaurant was quiet and not crowded. The outdoor seating area was fantastic (it had just rained). Prices are on the higher side for thai food, but the food did not disappoint. Prawns were incredibly fresh!
author: Tze Yee

review_text:
RiceDrive has proven to be an invaluable tool for managing and transferring files across multiple cloud storage services. One of its standout features is the seamless integration with various platforms like Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, and more, making it extremely versatile. The interface is intuitive and user-friendly, allowing even beginners to navigate file transfers with ease.

Another key advantage is the speed and efficiency of the transfers. RiceDrive handles large files and multiple tasks effortlessly, which saves both time and hassle. Additionally, the scheduling feature allows you to set transfers at convenient times, ensuring that data synchronization happens even when you’re not actively monitoring it. The tool's reliability and minimal downtime make it a dependable choice for both personal and professional file management needs.

Overall, RiceDrive simplifies cloud file management significantly, especially for those dealing with multiple accounts. It’s a powerful solution for users looking for speed, reliability, and ease of use in cloud transfers.
author: Rina Lewis

review_text: With $10USD one-month only subscription I transfer 0.8TB in about 36 hours from Onedrive to Dropbox resulting in about 50 transfer errors (out of 250k files=0.02% failures), but the error log didn't include paths for file names, so we had to laboriously find and check every instance of every file name that failed to transfer to find and manually to fix the transfer error. I belatedly learnt that the 'restart' icon is misnamed, as it doesn't restart the transfer, rather it only re-tries the files that failed to transfer in the errors logs. We didn't try the function because from the name we thought it was going to restart from scratch and potentially just create a different set of problems and errors.
author: John Brown

review_text: Because I was taught to look for food
author: Icca Piica

review_text:
Had dinner with the family here recently, loved their brocolini and brussel sprouts, as well as the organic mushrooms! The mushroom dish comes with a runny egg, which combines the two things the family loves. Well executed dishes and we'll be back to try more tapas from their menu!
The service staff were also wonderful and accommodating to our needs especially with a curious toddler running around and exploring the place.
author: Christopher Leong

review_text:
Daughter chose this restaurant for her birthday dinner.

We ordered a selection of starters and tapas plus a steak (I have a steak weakness). Food came promptly and was thoroughly enjoyable. Because they were mostly small plates, we were able to order extras. The highlight for us were the mushroom croquettes, chorizo, and the tacos.

The steak had a nice char on the outside paired with a nice spicy sauce but felt the doneness was under done.. we ordered a medium rare (as we always do) but the middle was deep red instead of a brighter shade.. will remember to order medium to medium rare, which I think will the correct for our taste. But still very nice.

Then for our deserts, as most of us were filled to the brim, we just ordered the chocolate something w mango sorbet (hahaha I didn't pay attention as was too full to eat anymore).

Will return for future meals. Parking was challenging tho.
author: Kenneth Low

review_text: I've found my go-to Spanish restaurant in Singapore! The ceviche was heavenly and the mushroom croquettes were incredible! I think the only slight miss was the churros, because I like mine a bit more fluffy and these had more crispy shell. But such a delightful dinner in a quiet neighbourhood. Already planning another visit!
author: Daniel

review_text:
1st time here was for Xmas. 2nd time here for a birthday celebration. Service, food and atmosphere were impeccable on both occasions. Staff were attentive and approachable - helping to refill water, wine, and in phototaking. Squid ink paella, bikini sandwich, and fish tacos were our favourites. Desserts (apple and chocolate tarts) were a little sweet for our liking but would be great for anyone looking for a decadent treat.
Looking forward to be back!
author: Phyllis Yen

review_text: The food is Great !! Outstanding dishes are the Rota Heuvos - potato, jamon, eggs- and the Lamb Ribs !!  This was AWESOME ! Done very well. Granted it was a little fatty, perfectly chargrilled, and the meat was dropping off the ribs.. so much flavour.
author: MingYao Tan

review_text:
After 10k run. Feel hungry. So i ordered curry rice. Surprising delicious. Inside curry have lots of carrots and potatoes.
Will come to eat again. Pls support them too.
author: Eric Ng

review_text:
Brisk short walk in the hot 3pm afternoon sun at the MacRitchie Reservoir Park. Saw a rooster strutting away. A monitor lizard about a metre long languid in the hot humid breezeless air.  A troop of young long-tailed macaques feeding on what looks like unripe mangoes 5-8 cm diameter.

Seeking refuge from the weather, wandered to Gink-Go, a delightful snack bar located at the Amenities Centre of MacRitchie Reservoir Park.

First attractive feature: a small 10 seater air conditioned snack room: the view is most pleasant from here: lush tropical greenery.

There was a vase with branches of the fan-shaped epynomous “ginkgo” leaves. Ginkgo biloba leaves are green in the spring and summer, turning a vibrant yellow in the autumn before they fall. This color change is a key characteristic of the ginkgo tree, making it a beautiful addition to landscapes.

Between the service counter and staff “retreat room” hangs a noren. (Japanese door curtain with vertical slit to gain access.) The design on the noren are sprigs of yellow ginkgo leaves, explained the lady boss, a young energetic ernest lady who was happy to espouse things Botanicals. She relates to the ginkgo ability to grow from a small nut to a big tree, and its aesthetic related to the unique, fan-shaped leaves, vibrant yellow fall color, and enduring presence in art, culture, and nature

Gink-Go serves a carefully curated menu of healthy food options, catering to nature enthusiasts, fitness joggers, and anyone looking for a quick and wholesome meal in the tranquility of nature.

I had a coffee hot, served with available evaporated milk and yellow lump rock sugar syrup.
Wife had cold chin chow (grass jelly drink)

After chatting with the kiosk owner/staff and downing my caffeine fix, I did a quick potentate postcard.
Sailor Fude Peni
Rembrandt Watercolours
author: Su Min Lim

review_text:
Had a chat with the owner. It’s was a lovely chat. She made her food from scratch. And very passionate about food.
It’s my favourite place around here. It’s peaceful and quiet here.
author: Wee Peng

review_text: Great little snack shop on the McRitchie Reservoir trail. We enjoyed bottles of water with ice and hummus with veggies. There is a small air conditioned room to cool you down before continuing on the trail
author: Rhonda Handley

review_text: Nice small place for a meal when you are trekking at MacRitchie.  They serve healthy food and are mindful of the ingredients they use.   I had the potato salad and curry rice with chicken.
author: Soh

review_text: If you're in the mood for delicious smoked meats and fresh seafood, Black Bear Craft Meat Smokers is the place to be! Located at 2 Greenwood Ave, this spot serves up mouthwatering flavors with a great vibe to match. Whether you're digging into their perfectly smoked meats or savoring the fresh seafood right off the grill, every bite is a treat. The drinks are spot on too—perfect for unwinding after a busy day. It's definitely my new go-to for good food and good times! Highly recommend checking it out if you're a seafood lover or a fan of smoky goodness.
author: Anne

review_text:
A nice surprise to chance upon Black Bear BBQ & Smokehouse whilst considering what to have at Greenwood area. Black Bear had taken over the very short-lived Dan’s Steaks outlet which in turn was previously Roots Mediterranean Restaurant.

The beef brisket was superb and the way I like it. Well balanced smokey flavor, super tender and juicy. Had more than average amount of fats but I like it that way. The Beef rib was also very good, spot on in terms of flavor, char and juiciness.

The Dirty Fries was atypical as the key ingredients   were separated and you had to mix it yourself according to your liking which was kinda DIYish fun in that aspect. The Apple pie that was done in a French way was yummy and had 2 generous scoops of Vanilla ice cream, albeit it had a lot more raisins to Apple slices. Feedback to the chef was positively taken and we expect this item to be improved. Decent selection of wine and reasonable prices. 4/5 in my books!
author: Ed Seng

review_text:
I never tried the black bear, because it’s too many western cuisine surrounded this area.
First tried the Prata, I felt it’s delicious, but the curry is not the local style. It’s more sour.
Love it very much, we enjoyed the food, price is affordable. Will visit again.
author: Chin Kang Teh

review_text:
Was recommended to visit this place from a resident. It has collaborated with Super Prata to include some local dishes, and man, it hit the right spot.

Firstly, the attentive, friendly staffs were inviting enough that we decided to take a risk. Hey, what could go wrong with such friendly and warm hunks right?

Secondly, the atmosphere, environment were great for a couple with good seating, lighting.

Finally, the food. We ordered a Greek salad, a super murtabak with beef brisket and 2 calamansi drinks. The drinks were weak, but the murtabak was simply heavenly. Soft, wet mutton in a soft warm bread. Topped with melt in your mouth beef brisket.

We were so in loved with the super murtabak with beef brisket, we even considered having seconds!

Give this place, and the folks a try. The prices are extremely reasonable in a place like Greenwood.

Will certainly be back there to try the rest of the menu.
author: Chun Teck Ong

review_text:
Brought my family here for dinner and it was a great experience. Food was tasty, well-seasoned and oysters were extremely fresh and well priced.

Could tell that the waiters were extremely busy but still provided great service. The waiter gave us some good recommendations. Brisket and chicken wings were definitely the stars of the night 🤌🏻

Complimentary oysters were a nice touch too. Thanks for having us, we will be back.
author: Nicolas Koh

review_text:
Food is slightly different than most other Italian restaurants.

Good and delicious! One just needs to slowly eat and enjoy here.

We had the anchovy starter, a meat Ravioli, the seafood aglio, a burrata pizza, the Bacalao Fillet and a tiramisu.

Had a beer, a rośe wine and a medium bodied red cab.

We enjoyed. Just wished I had more time to slowly enjoy the night.
author: Samuel Lam

review_text:
A cosy restaurant (30 seats) in Greenwood and it can get packed during dinner.

A beautifully curated wine list is available at Bacaro that pairs wonderfully with the food.

They have a unique deep fried dough pizza base (not greasy at all) that went well with the spicy Calabrian salami & burrata cheese.
The calamaretti & zucchini fritters were excellent as well.

The seafood aglio olio with peperoncino was done perfectly and we enjoyed it immensely.
The Milanese deep fried veal was tender came with a trio of sauces. The basil sauce was outstanding and freshened up your palate.

At the end of the meal, we were served a glass of complimentary Italian liqueur.

The generosity and friendliness of the staff really elevated our experience in Bacaro.
author: Jing Jie Ng

review_text:
Bacaro Italian Restaurant signals its commitment to authenticity. A quietly confident celebration of Italian conviviality, channeling the spirit of Venice’s bacari—neighborhood wine bars where food is honest, flavors are bold, and conversation flows as freely as the wine. It’s the kind of place where a casual weekday dinner can effortlessly stretch into a long evening.

However the steak, while expertly cooked, leans slightly too far toward tenderness, losing some of the textural resistance that gives a great cut its character.
author: Sammy Soong

review_text: I traveled to Singapore for work and had the opportunity to dine at Bacaro several times. I'll start by saying that I'm Italian and frequent many restaurants for work. At Bacaro, I found Chef David's dishes to be meticulously prepared, with a focus on quality ingredients and attentive customer service. The wine list is alternative, carefully curated and expertly explained by Elena, a professional sommelier. The spirits selection is also excellent. A fantastic experience.
author: Gabriele Conte

review_text:
Came here on a Saturday lunch date, the restaurant was quiet and homely. My partner and I shared the deep fried pizza with spicy salami and burrata, and the meat stuffed tortellini with a creamy sauce.

The sommelier served us, and he was very attentive and informative. He replaced our utensils and plates with every dish, and even divided up the tortellini into individual portions when we mentioned that we were sharing the dish.

We finished off the meal with a tiramisu, which were delicious. We loved the deep fried pizza a lot, the fried dough was airy and not oily at all.
author: Julia Tay

review_text: The Hunan Barbecue is definitely worth trying. The spice and chili make every skewer so savory and fragrant, I honestly couldn’t stop eating. The quality of the food and the decor are absolutely worth the price. Definitely recommending this place to my friends. Heard they have another outlet at Bugis, might go there next time.
author: Sam

review_text: This restaurant is the premium version of Scallion ForFree (Bugis). The food remains exceptional, adding an Omakase element to the original teppanyaki menu. Open until 2 AM, it's a perfect place to enjoy delicious food and drinks in the area.
author: JIMIN LI

review_text: Very delicious food with good ambience. Suitable for all ages. Will make you come back again.
author: darren toh

review_text: The food was good and the ambience was pleasant. Enjoyed the overall experience and will definitely return
author: hanzhou wang

review_text:
The scallion oil noodles are fragrant and very addictive. Simple ingredients but full of flavour.
Great value for money, especially with the generous toppings.
The noodles have a nice springy texture.
Fast service and perfect for a quick lunch.
The scallion aroma really stands out.
Portion size is satisfying for the price.
Affordable and tasty comfort food.
I love how customizable the toppings are.
Definitely worth coming back again.
author: Lew Kimyong

review_text:
The ice kachang at Adam Road is a delightful treat, especially on a hot day. The combination of shaved ice, colorful flavor syrups, and sweet corn topping is yummy.

This dessert offers a refreshing escape from the tropical heat, a good portion for the price. It's always a challenge to eat the shaved ice mountain without it falling on the table, but it is highly recommended. :)
author: kenny choe

review_text:
Tried their 清汤 and it was surprisingly good!  Light, not too sweet, and generous with ingredients.

Hubby highly recommended it so since I was here I gave it a try.

Love it :-)
author: 阿宝

review_text:
We ordered the ice kachang from Adam’s Desserts — super refreshing and really delicious! 🍧✨ The shaved ice was smooth, the syrup was just right (not overly sweet), and all the toppings added great texture and flavor. The boss is very generous with the condensed milk, making it even more shiok. 😋😋😋 Perfect on a hot day! ☀️👍

Highly recommended if you’re in the area and craving a good dessert. Will definitely be back to try other items! 💯👏
author: Raymond Lim

review_text: Adam’s Desserts really hits the spot on a hot day. Their ice kacang is super refreshing — finely shaved ice, generous with the toppings, and the syrup isn’t overly sweet. Loved the balance of textures with the corn, jelly, red beans, and a syrups. For a humble food court stall, they really deliver. Affordable and satisfying. Don’t miss it if you’re around!
author: Lau Guan Zhen (Sean)

review_text:
Best ice kachang, ice jelly, Ching Tng and deserts!!!!!

Friendly couple and great service. Makes it more satisfying to have a good desert.
author: Samuel Lam

review_text:
Decided to help this aunty one day and got her watermelon soursop juice. Was so disappointed that she used syrup. Never had such a bad juice in my life. It tasted like liquid bubble gum.

Was not going to write a bad review until the next day i returned to get juice from a neighbouring stall instead - and the aunty just shook her head at me and gave me black face.
author: Sarah Lye

review_text: I ordered mango juice. Paid $3. Then I saw the stallholder open the fridge door and took out a box of mango juice. It is not blended on the spot. I totally lost faith. Didn’t want to create a scene.
author: Jonathan Koh

review_text:
One of the best Avocado drink around.. suitable for this hot weather. The boss use the real Avocado 🥑. At only $2.50, what a bargain. Thank you boss 🙏🏻

Love it!  Going to take out another cup

15th June 23 - Come back to revisit. The goodness is what makes me return again.

Bought 1 and takeaway another 2 cups. Taste superb as always!!
author: Keify Toh

review_text: Flies all around their fruits in their display upfront with no attempt to get rid of them. I paid extra for no ice but juice was extremely diluted. There was grains of dirt in the juice, indicating that they didn’t wash their fruits. Do not recommend.
author: An Ting

review_text: We used to get juices here for 4 months now. It's not the easiest  Singlish, especially if it's the assistant, but the lady is fantastically positive person and will do everything in the best way - just make sure to communicate properly your wants.
author: Oleksii Pasichnyi

restaurant_name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
review_text: Ordered the prawn noodles with pork belly. Taste is decent, but compared to other places I’ve tried, this one is not as good. The noodle sauce is on the sweet and oily side, and the soup is just okay. The pork belly was sliced very thin. They also don’t allow adding extra noodles or topping up the soup. The price has gone up as well, so overall I think there are better options out there and I won’t specially go there to eat.
author: Freddy

restaurant_name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
review_text:
Singaporeans take prawn noodles seriously and with many options and several good ones dotted across the island, this stall is one of those that draws a queue and is one of the more frequented stalls at Adam Food Centre.

The noodles and thick bee hoon are cooked al dente with a nice bite, the sauce is lighter than some other stalls, though the lard oil that coats the strands make them slick and smooth to consume. For the more affordable option, the prawns are smaller but are still fresh and succulent. The unassuming bowl of soup with its brown hue contains the richness and sweetness of prawns and is  balanced.
author: 葉

restaurant_name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
review_text:
Ordered a Large pork ribs noodle soup at $10.

Soup is very tasty and rich with prawn flavour. I really like the taste of the soup but it made me slightly thirsty after drinking it. But the soup is still very tasty IMO.

Pork ribs are soft and tasty and portion wise is not bad.
author: Justin Oon

restaurant_name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
review_text: Seemed promising, but lacked the depth of flavour one would expect from good prawn noodles in SG. Underwhelming as a whole as the stock forms the base of the whole dish. Not too deserving of its ‘Michelin’ status. In hindsight, the lack of aroma was a big telltale indicator.
author: Dylan Chia

restaurant_name: Adam Rd Noo Cheng Big Prawn Noodle
review_text:
I’m a big fan of hey mee and always thinking is this stall a hype. It’s not. I just ordered a normal one $7 small. What amazed me is the soup and the portion of prawns are not bad too in today’s climate where $8 -$10 ones from those “famous” stalls gives u a bit only.

The only thing is they are pretty slow. So if u see a short queue 3-4 pax in front it’s gonna take you 10-15min.

It’s a stall with a lot of clearly stated rules and practices too which I think over the years they must have encountered countless demands and complaints and requests so they now upfront clear w you. The “not happy don’t eat” kind of stall.
author: Cl Ang

review_text:
The lady is super nice!!
Even brought my food over when she saw i was busy at the drinks stall.
However, really disappointed in the hokkien mee. This has to be one of the worst hokkien mee in the whole of SG.
In hindsight, should have gone for the white carrot cake maybe? Looks better and i noticed other diners eating that.
author: Bren A

review_text:
Randomly came here to try the white carrot cake. Only word - yummy😊 and the portion was big for S$4.
Must also mention the toilet here is really clean 😬
author: Tsoi Ka Man

review_text: Hokkien prawn Noodles not well cook, no wok hey. Photo shown with squid but replaced by fish cake. Prawns  blend and tasteless.  Most disappointed HKM that I have.
author: Yong Heng Quek

review_text: The kueh tiaw is not my preference... not that kind of wok hey style...$5sgd.. but portion ok la..ingredients not bad.. got prawn
author: Darren Cheong

review_text: My first time trying this store. The fried Kuay Teow taste ok but lack of Wok Hey, kind of watery, soft was not oilly, the color was a little pale and not appealing. Their version of Fried Kuay Teow comes with fresh cockles and prawn from S$4 to $6 is reasonably priced. They also serve Hokkien mee, oyster omelette and fried carrots cake.
author: Kesmond Kwek

review_text:
Agree that the (taller) person taking the orders is not the friendliest at the hawker centre. I look past that, focusing on getting a serving of their tasty braised duck meat :-)

My usual order is duck meat noodles ($4) dry. I enjoy the meats dipped in both their citrusy & dried chilli sauce. Soup is more savoury than herbal. A bowl is served with lots of vege.
author: Cheen the Curious

review_text:
Standards have indeed dropped at this place. I usually like to support hawkers but not when food standards as well as service standards have dropped. It’s now just an ok braised duck stall for me.

I don’t usually write negative reviews but
What gets me most is how standoffish and rude the person manning the stall was when I patronised it. I admit, I haven’t eaten here for a couple of years but still…
And when I ordered a simple duck rice, he added an egg and charged me for it when I didn’t ask for it. Then he smirked at me as if challenging me to make a fuss. I don’t like making a scene so I left. Never will I come back to this stall again.
author: Gary Sim

review_text:
For a place that sells ‘开心鸭饭‘ (happy duck rice) the people tending the stall are totally not ‘开心’ at all serving you.

At least the poor service was consistent to everyone else in the queue.

Food is decent but let down by the service, would not recommend a visit.
author: Ryuta Teo

review_text:
I must say this stall has a lot of haters for having such a low rating. Why bring in roast duck to compare when it’s all braised here? Don’t rate if you don’t know how braised ducks taste in the olden days. If nothing better to say, 🤫🫢🤮

This simple plate of braised duck rice brought me back to the 80s growing up to this nostalgic taste. From the tender duck meat to the rice that is a little sticky and with the sauce drenched over but not too much. The sambal chilli is homemade and has that taste that I love as a kid growing up to my size. Really good and thanks for keeping this legendary taste.
author: Big Roy [eatwithroy]

review_text:
Came here on Sat morning but disappointed that my favourite Nasi lemak stall was closed. Guess the owners were taking a break.

Decided on a whim to go for this braised duck stall without reading reviews.

Ordered a large sized duck soup with kway tiao. Was shocked when I found the kway tiao was cut into small string. The portion was also not what I expected for a big bowl.

However I found the taste to be above average especially the soup which I slurped up entirely. The duck was ok but again portion wise was too small but that could be due to inflation n shrinkflation going around in Singapore lately...

What was really nice though was the chilli oil which had a distinct dried shrimp taste and it was good enough to eat on its own even.

Overall wouldn't agree that it's 1-2 stars but 3-stars is the most I would give the stall.
author: LexTeo8888

review_text: Had the tauhu goreng and a plate of nasi lemak w/ chicken wing. Taste is fine. Tauhu goreng sauce is thick and rich — can use more beansprouts and cucumber for more textural and flavour contrast. Chicken wing is a little tiny and rice could use more santan as it wasn't as rich as I would like. Chilli leans towards the sweet side.
author: Sg Hungry Ghost

review_text:
the mee soto is good, i alternate between this and the other store because they are both great. super fast ordering time and good opening hours

Update: the mee soto was not as nice in the morning, think it was better in the afternoon

The nasi lemak was not that good, the chicken was very oily and flavourless and the rice not fragrant enough. The sambal is okay. Wouldn't order the nasi lemak again
author: Tania Koh

review_text:
Eat at Adam Road Food Centre, Singapore.
I’ve been here a few times, usually just for the famous Adam Road Nasi Lemak. But today it was closed, so I decided to try something else. I randomly picked a Malay stall and ordered the seafood mee goreng. To my surprise, it was excellent. This version felt more like a Malay-style Hokkien mee—slightly wet instead of the usual dry mee goreng, and it even had a nice touch of wok hei. I also added some mee soto chilli from the stall, which elevated the flavor to another level. Definitely a dish I’ll come back for.
Rating: 8.0/10
Horjiak 😀👍👍
author: Jinghorjiak

review_text: Famous for their lontong but this mee rebus is so good especially if you crave for it for supper. They still selling at after 9pm. $5.00. Fast and efficient.
author: Asia Apparel

review_text:
28/10/2024
Had Nasi Lemak Chicken Wing set ($4) for dinner, was quite good. Portion was generous. Chilli slightly on the sweeter side.
author: T greensake

review_text:
The quest for Michelin hawker took me to Adam Food Center today. The queue was about 10 pax in front of me and I think I queued a good 20 mins before getting Mee Rebus and Mee Soto.

The chicken Mee Soto that I ordered had a very savoury stock and the chicken was fresh and tender. Wasn’t a big fan of Mee Soto prior to this visit but this bowl definitely changed my impression of this soup dish.

The Mee rebus was accompanied by the robust and thick gravy. It was slightly spicy to me. It came with one full egg.

The queue was long, even at 1030am on a weekday morning but it’s well worth the wait!

Both dishes were great but if you asked me, I will pick the Mee Soto over the Mee Rebus!
author: Damien Wong

review_text:
Warong Pak Sapari serves one of the best, if not the best, mee soto in Singapore. The broth is incredibly rich and flavourful, and the noodles are always cooked to the perfect texture. Every bowl is consistently satisfying.

They do sell out pretty quickly, so it’s best to go early to avoid disappointment. I’m not usually someone who would wait in line for food, but I happily queue for this mee soto. The line moves steadily, so the wait isn’t too bad.

Absolutely a must-try!
author: Ivan Loh

review_text: My bestie queued for 20 minutes to get two bowls of noodles. The Mee Soto was excellent; I wish the chili had been spicier. The soup was savoury, with great-tasting chicken and no unpleasant smell. I loved the soup, and the mee rebus was decent.  Still, I will still choose the Mee Soto! Will go back again!
author: Empress Ker

review_text:
This humble stall at Adam Food Centre serves Michelin-recognised Mee Soto and Mee Rebus. Coupled with recent media coverage in a documentary, it is no wonder the queue is perpetually long and the stall stops business a couple of hours before its official closing time, when the food is sold out. We were fortunate to have tasted the legendary Mee Soto and Sup Kaki Ayam (chicken feet soup), and let’s just say any other Mee Soto we have in the future will have a challenge meeting the bar this stall has set, in terms of depth of flavour and cooking techniques.

The soup is the star with its myriad ingredients and spices that meld together with the essence of chicken for that distinct, Mee Soto profile. A teaspoon of dark sambal is added by choice to provide a lingering heat to the taste buds, without numbing or overpowering the soup - adding a layer of complexity. The chicken meat is tender and flavourful, not bland and dry as can be encountered elsewhere. The feet, on the other hand, are gelatinous and soft, easy to separate skin, meat, and cartilage in the mouth before discarding the bones.

If you’ve missed out on the operating duration to get your hands on these coveted bowls of noodles, visit their franchised stall at Lau Pa Sat, which the chef would drop by from time to time to check on quality and consistency.
author: 葉

review_text:
Tried the new Century Square outlet today and wow—the portions are huge and the food is so good! The gravy isn’t overly thick or jelak, just nicely balanced. I had the Mee Rebus Kaki Ayam (added babat too), and they even gave a full boiled egg. Received 5 pieces of kaki ayam and 3 big slabs of babat 🤯. I’m plus-sized, and even I found the portion really generous—love it! Also added a lil bit of sambal kicap for a tiny kick.

I also spotted the owner in person, which felt a bit surreal after seeing him on YouTube interviews (haha!). Overall, everything was delicious. May Allah bless the owner with endless rezeki and success.

Next mission: trying the Mee Soto! 🔥
author: Nurulhudah Yusoff

review_text: So yummy better than the one next door and it’s cheaper. Fried chicken taste super good. Rice is fragrance. Chilli is sedap! It’s my first time trying after knowing there is the Famous one there but I decided to have a try and no regrets.
author: Alan Morghan

review_text:
There are a few Nasi Lemak stalls in this hawker centre, and I chose the one with the longest queue—about three people. I ordered the $4.50 chicken set and asked for less rice. To my surprise, the stall owner also reduced the price—something most, if not all, other stalls wouldn’t do.

The Nasi Lemak was pretty standard, but both the chicken and ikan bilis were crispier than usual. The chilli leaned spicier than the typical sweet type but wasn’t overly so.

Overall, a decently good plate of Nasi Lemak made and served by a very friendly stall owner.
author: LP Pua

review_text: Their nasi lemak was SO GOOD. Fried chicken was fresh and well-marinated (had to buy another 2 for takeout) and the rice and sambal was like home-cooked. What a lovely meal.
author: Nat Nat

review_text: Near to the more famous Nasi Lemak stall but that queue was slow moving. This stall serves as tasty for Nasi Lemak and price is cheaper by comparison. Enjoy the food with lots of sambal provided.
author: Hrmgr

review_text: It was my first time trying nasi lemak, and it was a really pleasant experience. Rice with gentle coconut scent blended really well with red sambal sauce. Chicken was fried like pro, and other components of dish like fried anchovy and fish pudding also went well with the rice. Loved it!
author: sunsik kim

restaurant_name: Fried Kway Teow Prawn Mee Oyster Carrot Cake (Adam Road)
review_text:
Decent Hokkien mee served by friendly aunty and uncle. Enough wokhey taste and evenly coated noodles. Noodles were also fresh and springy. I ordered the small portion and it came with three sweet albeit small peeled prawns.

Note: they don’t have sotong despite the menu’s image.
author: Nicole Quek

restaurant_name: Fried Kway Teow Prawn Mee Oyster Carrot Cake (Adam Road)
review_text:
Fried Oyster ($8)
This is highly recommended for its good amount of fresh oysters, which are perfectly complemented by a well-balanced mixture of egg, flour, and starch.

The dish stands out for its light, non-greasy texture, making it a satisfying choice without overwhelming the palate. This dish is a definite highlight, and I would gladly revisit the stall for this or other dishes whenever I'm in the area.

Also, I completely agree with others who have noted that this stall is underrated. It deserves more recognition.
author: T WP

restaurant_name: Fried Kway Teow Prawn Mee Oyster Carrot Cake (Adam Road)
review_text:
Sort of a second choice given that the famous stores weren’t open, but it turned out to be really good!

The dry Hokkien mee was flavourful, pretty rare to find a dry version, but I do love both variants after trying the dry one for the first few times 👍🏻

Prawn omelette was slightly salty though, but thoroughly enjoyed it since we don’t eat the oyster style one and this has the starchiness cooked within the eggs 🥚
author: YY

restaurant_name: Fried Kway Teow Prawn Mee Oyster Carrot Cake (Adam Road)
review_text:
This store is underrated because it don’t have a proper stall name.
First time patronise this stall. Can’t believe white carrot cake can be fried till one side is crispy while the other side is soft and moist while not charring it.
Chili and savory is just right. Perfect balance.
Will try their other dish.
Will definitely come back to Adam hawker just for this stall.
author: Ronnie Seah

restaurant_name: Fried Kway Teow Prawn Mee Oyster Carrot Cake (Adam Road)
review_text: The fried oyster very big, very fresh. And generous serving. I order a $6 small one, got 7 oyster. The egg was alot too. Chili also very nice, savoury, sour and sweet tinngy.
author: Alan Thong

review_text: Owner came to our table and I ordered an ice milo for $2.50. I went to the stall to pay by PayNow and he told me off for not telling him earlier as he would have charged me more for PayNow. And made it seem like it’s my fault? What kind of logic is this? (Especially in this day and age where barely anyone brings cash around anymore)
author: Jared

review_text:
Date of visit: Mon 24 June 2024
Time : 9.45 pm

The Chinese desserts stall is closed on Mondays so we opted for cold drinks from Taj Mahal.
Ordered ice tea halia and ice chendol. Priced at $2.50 each.

The chendol drink is incredibly good.
author: Sunny M

review_text: Menu put Horlick ice $2.50 , that guy charged me $3 ! 👎👎👎
author: Samuel Ho

review_text: Friendly service. Teh halia was too sweet even though we requested it to be less sweet, overpowering the tea and ginger tastes.
author: CK C

review_text: I wish I could give zero star. Probably the worst experience. Kept asking if I want any drink. Die hard salesman, cannot take no for an answer and Mumbling to himself "everything also no".  I also noticed a lot of other shops doesn't have pricing here. He colleague also came and asked us again.
author: Clarence Loh

review_text: Got the Ayam Penyet for $7 and it was quite delicious. Rice is very flavourful and the portion is good. Definitely cooked with some kind of chicken stock. Chicken is crispy and perfectly salty, although I would like it to have been hotter. Perhaps they were making a new batch. Tofu and vegetables are a nice side touch. Be careful of the chili if you can't take spice. But I love how it is sweet and spicy and is very delicious. Pairs well with the rice and chicken. If you can take spice add loads of it! The chicken soup also pairs well with the entire dish. While $7 is slightly steep in my opinion, I would definitely get this again. I went at 1pm on a Saturday afternoon and it was one of the few stalls without a queue. Would definitely get this over Nasi Lemak which always has a long queue.
author: Kenneth Huang

review_text: One of the best chicken rice I had eaten recently. The rice is very fragrance with yellow rice. First time I have tried. The roasted Chicken are very crispy outside and soft inside...perfectly done. The chilli is very nice not too spicy. Just nice. The vendor is very friendly and welcoming. Prompt service. For $6.00 is worthwhile going to the hawker centre. Well done 👏
author: syed Ibrahim Yusoff

review_text:
Quite fiery spicy fragrant chilli.
Rice quite fragrant.  Fried tofu nice.
Half chicken on the dry side, with yummy crisps.  Soup tasty.
author: Stanley Teo

review_text:
Chicken is still nice & crispy even after it reached my dinner table at home. Word of caution, watch out for the chili and use it sparingly because jt is extremely spicy. Food portion is also acceptable for the reasonable price.

However, I still don’t understand the use of raw cabbage.
author: J

review_text:
$6 for Ayam penyet. Had it as an early lunch. Soo delicious and no queue. Crispy chicken and flavourful rice that was just nice to match the chicken. Sambal belachan was the winner. It's fresh, very spicy, and fragrant with pungence- exactly what you want out of your sambal belachan.
I dont understand why this stall has such a low rating, it definitely deserves more!
Owner had a friendly smile too!
author: Mindy Tan, Photographer

review_text: Lovely service delivery today. Received a call to remind about my order pickup and when I was there, the lady at the counter took the initiative to have my order converted into a value meal for cost savings. This extra mile to ensure that the customer gets a better value was unexpected, and worth a shout-out. Thank you for making my day ♡
author: F A

review_text: Delicious Pizza! One of the best in Singapore! We got 3 Pizzas - Canadian Supreme, New York Deli and Chicken Alfredo. All of them were different but they have one thing in common - they all tasted amazing! People should get pizzas from Sarpinos, they are much better than Pizzahut or Dominos!
author: Ethan

review_text: Kiosk in the shell petrol station. Service is good. The pizza flavours is good but lacks of good quality of mozarella cheese. No stretchable or pull cheese from the pizza. Price is ok.
author: Epal Hijau

review_text:
One of the worst online ordering experience. This is the 2nd time that online has screwed up the order.

First your app is not even working. Are you even aware of it?? First screw up the order placed and paid did not arrive and only upon calling then I knew that order was not accepted but you collected the payment??

This time again had to order from website again cos your app is not working….

I key in the address using shortcut which I have used for so many other order but it screwed up the block number and my contact number.

Will not be ordering from them again…👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻👎🏻
author: Kelvin Lee

review_text:
Very friendly staffs and nice pizza!
Located in Shell,
A little bit small but it’s okay they are having 50% discount!
I am going to visit again soon
author: Haily Zett

review_text: If you want a refreshing and delicious drink PLEASE go here!  The guy that worked here was super honest, friendly and just a great human being!  The freshly squeezed lime juice is true to its name and FRESH!  This is now my favorite spot to get one and I can’t wait to go back!  If you get a chance to try this I guarantee you’ll want to keep coming back!  Thanks for the great experience and I hope to see you soon! 😊
author: Mark Monstroski

review_text: What's more inviting to counter scorching climate change than a cuppa Sugarcane Plant's fresh sugarcane juice... Apart from its signature item, the Lime and Soyabean are hot favs with nearby residents and Botanic visitors. Any of these would be perfect to go with ur meal at Adam FC .. bon appetit =)
author: Tonto Lim (Tonto)

review_text: The "boys" are always woth a smile and are so accommodating.. service is great. This is what service is all about . I'd recommend sugarcane lovers to this stall anytime . refreshingly awesome.  Drinks and those big smiles .thanks guys .
author: roberto de costa

review_text: Hands down the best sugarcane juice I've ever had. Fresh, naturally sweet, not watered down at all, and great value. Excellent service too!
author: Shannon Low

review_text: Solid customer service ! Refreshing and super shiok sugarcane with lime 🍋  LOVE IT ! One for the hot weather 🥵
author: devan srigaran

review_text: Ordered the power avocado premium which cost $5.5 (apparently it comes with 1.5 avocados hence the steeper price) but was disappointed when I drank it. It was creamy but icy and didn’t have any taste of gula melaka in it😅 Had better ones elsewhere!
author: Pamela Lam

review_text: The avocado juice was incredibly creamy, rich, and velvety-smooth. It struck the perfect balance—it was satisfyingly decadent without being overly sweet. You can tell they use only the freshest, highest-quality avocados, resulting in a vibrant, natural flavor that is both refreshing and surprisingly filling.
author: Harris

review_text: The uncle serving us was nice and honest! You can use your CDC vouchers here as well! The avocado drink was nice and thick it is highly recommended to get this drink! But if you are looking for a refreshing drink, you can get the lychee soursop snow drink which is highly addictive! Couldn’t stop drinking it after I started!!🔥🔥
author: Athanasius Ooi Xiehui

review_text:
this was their avocado & banana smoothie ($3.90)! surprisingly, the banana was strong but not TOO strong so it didn’t completely erase the taste of avocado!

great price and great quality, i’ll definitely have to come back!
author: penny

review_text: The avocado 🥑 drinks here are great and reasonably priced. I bought the avocado with strawberry option and it is a mixture of sweet and smooth rich creamy taste. At around $4, it is a steal!
author: Keng Cheong Tan

review_text: Ordered a large stingray for $22, but we were shocked when a small-to-medium portion was served instead. It felt like daylight robbery. The taste wasn’t great, the sambal was overly sweet and didn’t complement the stingray at all. Definitely not worth the price. I’ve gotten the same portion for only $12 at Satay by the Bay. Wouldn’t recommend this stall.
author: CM C

review_text: Very poor stingray n rice for 19 $. Just tail bone  almost. Felt cheated. Sambal Sauce is also very bad looks like chili powder mixed with ketchup.. My last time to try this hawker. Please stay away until they improve or u see better n real reviews.
author: SD

review_text: Adam’s seafood bbq is one of our favorite dinner option. Always the same order: bbq stingrayx2, sotong & kailan.
author: Pauline Ng

review_text:
Repeated visit for their BBQ dishes. Would usually order their leather jacket grilled fish and their stir fry Kai Lan.

Love that dried shrimps are added in the stir fry Kai Lan elevating that umami-ness.

Ordered their sambal sotong - excellent doneness; sotong not overly cooked, nice bite to it.

Love their chinchalok which compliments the sambal seafood.
author: YP Soo

review_text: Uncle was friendly and sent the order to our table. Unfortunately, the food was rather disappointing. The belachan of the stingray was too sweet, and tasted like it contained ketchup. The kangkong was well fried but was extremely salty. Everything served in disposables.
author: CK C

review_text:
The Mutton Meat Soup was really delicious and one of the best I have tried. Mutton meat were tender and flavourful. Every mouthful of the soup with mutton meat was a timeless journey to wonderland. Kinda warm though, since we are eating hot soup in a warm environment, so enjoyment level minus 5%.

Suggestion: Bring your own bread to dip in the soup for enhanced enjoyment. The bread they provide is decent, but there are better options to pair with the mutton soup.

The portion size of Lamb Shank Briyani was huge and more than enough for 2 pax. The Briyani rice and sauce was delicious, but we found the lamb shank meat could be softer.
author: C Y

review_text: Tried the super popular mutton soup, waited 45min in the queue at 2pm! its the longest queue in this place. the food was v good, strong mutton smell and taste but not as rich tasting as i expected. almost tasted too diluted. so it was a good dish but not a great one. however the meat is cook to perfection, thats a standout. All good but the v tiring queue... theres also v good alternatives like nasi lemak.
author: Timothy TM

review_text:
Purposely drove here to eat the michellin rated Mutton soup.
Soup is at most average only.
( hiag rd or upper boon keng has better mutton soup)
Biryani rice is room temperature and stick together,  not much flavours.
Mutton is dry.
The good things is: the staffs is friendly and portion is a lot for $8.
One more, achar is good.

Personally, won't come back again.
author: Nick Neo

review_text: We saw a video about this place and went last Saturday for lunch. We reached pretty early so there wasn't much queue. The mutton soup is super tasty! I would definitely go back for more. It is more like a curry but very mildly spiced so you can have it plain as well. They do serve it with bread, but better take your own as you need more :)
author: Sonal Sathe

review_text: A hearty, beautifully-balanced bowl of Indian mutton soup that produces a symphony of meaty, aromatic flavours in the mouth from the first spoonful to the last drop. The varieties of meat parts are prepared well without gaminess, and cooked to retain the taste of spices and herbs from the soup. The stomach is slick and smooth, while the meat on the ribs are soft, tender and fall off the bones. Queues can be long and food can be sold out by the evening or earlier.
author: 葉

review_text: The vendor use plain white rice and she told me is chicken rice’s Rice
author: Johnson Ng

review_text:
This is gonna be a super funny ordering experience. The charm is in the shopkeeper who doesn’t really speak English but who has a great smile and follows it up with his thumbs up sign.

We got teh tarik siu dai. Our “less sweet” orders were still pretty sweet. I think the only way to get “siu Dai” is to tell him kosong. But all in all, 5 stars cause of the shopkeeper
author: Daniel Bok

review_text:
Best Teh Tarik and Teh Halia we've had in awhile....
Most recommended  👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻
author: Muhammad Amir Sathiq

review_text: 🥤 Adam Drink Stall is actually open  they must have forgotten to update in Google search 😅 one of the favourite crowd with long queue of hungry workers buying & great spot for tourists & locals, highly recommend as their drinks sells at reasonable price with machine secured wrapped so you not worry the spills, very good 👍🏻 service, mutton & potato curry puff look 👀 super fresh at 5pm 🕔 on 15 June 2023.
author: Sarah Yeoh

review_text: Great service and tasty teh tarik served with joy and a twinkle in the eye.
author: Elaine C

review_text: Teh Halia iced for $2.50- not too sweet and the Halia is definitely strong enough. Good stuff!
author: Max S.

restaurant_name: Kelly Jie Seafood 凯莉姐龙海鲜 • Formerly TPY Mellben Seafood
review_text:
The seafood is very fresh and well prepared. Appreciate the enthusiastic n warm service of the team.
We lunched at KellyJie Seafood restaurant specifically to appreciate Aunty Alice’s yusheng rap!  She and the team are amazingly good at celebrating the Lunar New Year with many auspicious sayings or greetings!  All of us enjoyed this 2026 Ren Ri lunch very much - food is great! Atmosphere is great! And overall it is reasonably priced for the quality of the food.
author: Olivia Chua

restaurant_name: Kelly Jie Seafood 凯莉姐龙海鲜 • Formerly TPY Mellben Seafood
review_text:
First time to Kelly Jie Seafood.
Was impressed with their food presentation as they are not a fine dine restaurant yet the presentation was fine dine standard.
Applaud to their dishes.. it was indeed as they claims unique sauces that handmade which else where can’t find.
Food was not oily not salty.. suitable for elderly or those with health concerns.
Atmosphere was on the downside we are seated on level 2 may be due to the concrete and glass bouncing back through and flo all the voices from all table causing echoing effect. With more fabric may help to absorb some of the sound from the surrounding.
author: tan eve

restaurant_name: Kelly Jie Seafood 凯莉姐龙海鲜 • Formerly TPY Mellben Seafood
review_text:
The only "good" thing was how fresh and meaty the crabs were. I highly recommend ordering based on personal knowledge of your own portion sizes, as the staff kept trying to recommend "more" or bigger crabs, and upsized dishes. The rest of the menu we had felt very normal, and quite honestly a little overpriced. The whole family still prefer Jumbo after trying this. Also would NOT recommend the ice cream as the artificial flavouring was so off-putting.

Staff were very snappy (not the owners, who were quite sweet), and the noise was not great for dining either.
author: Crystal

restaurant_name: Kelly Jie Seafood 凯莉姐龙海鲜 • Formerly TPY Mellben Seafood
review_text:
This place offers a variety of Chinese-style seafood dishes. We ordered the signature crab bee hoon soup, bamboo clam, black pepper crab, cold fried pork, and one vegetable dish. The only two items I didn’t like were:

1. Crab bee hoon soup – the only good thing was how fresh and meaty the crab was. The soup was overly sweet, almost like it came from canned cream.
2. Bamboo clam – the flavor just wasn’t there.

The other dishes were good.
author: nina e

restaurant_name: Kelly Jie Seafood 凯莉姐龙海鲜 • Formerly TPY Mellben Seafood
review_text: Their famous louhei atmosphere is energetic n impressive. Worth its value for e performance by the auntie n kelly jie n staffs. Great crabs dishes as always. All the other side dishes are decent too.
author: Edwin Ng

review_text: Feb 2026, dim sum is good and all the dishes taste good. The service is excellent. The only thing is the price. I not sure is it Chinese New Year a coke cost $7.50++.
