author: LWF SL Leong

review_text: I was quite disappointed that the usual dim sum menu was not available during Chinese New Year. It would have been courteous to inform customers beforehand, as many of us visit specifically for those items. Unfortunately, the service standards also seemed to have dropped compared to my previous visits. I used to patronise this outlet regularly, but this experience has made me reconsider returning in the future.
author: Valerie Hwang

review_text:
Following a great dim sum experience a week ago, I returned yesterday with my sibling and a large group of over 10 people to take advantage of your Value Lunch promotion.

It was the perfect choice for our big party. The food was excellent—delicious, well-prepared, and the portions were  generous, which is so important when dining with a crowd. Everyone left feeling satisfied.

A special mention must go to your staff. They were exceptionally helpful and friendly from the moment we arrived, managing our large booking smoothly and ensuring everything ran perfectly throughout our meal although the initial request to partition for our big group to avoid talking too loud 😀Their attentive service made the experience even more enjoyable.

Thank you for another wonderful dining experience. We will definitely be back, whether for a family celebration or another value-packed lunch!
author: Sim Sebastian

review_text: It was a very nice experience lunching at Peach Garden Thomson Plaza. We were well taken care of by Alvin who was very knowledgeable of the menu. He gave us some good recommendations. The dim sum were fresh and yummy and we also particularly enjoyed the Spinach with Trio eggs and the sea cucumber casserole.
author: clarissa then

review_text:
Our group of 6 visited the restaurant specifically for its $52++ (ala carte-buffet) dinner (50% off).
We ordered 18 food-items (some with repeats), in varying plate-sizes and portions, as well as 2 desserts. The food was mainly satisfying and fulfilling, some would even say: good "value-for-money", aside from some truly delicious dishes.
Serve-staff (a mix of young and senior-years) were very helpful, attentive and friendly.
Ambience was comfortable, although sometimes noisy from the big groups of diners.
author: Sim Simon

review_text: Food here is great! Even though the bread doesnt look nice (who cares?!) it tastes great! I like how patient the staff are. When i chose my vegetables, i pointed at the lettuce and the staff helping me confirmed before putting it on my sandwich. The cookie is perfect!
author: TheLight

review_text:
On 13 Feb around 10:20am, I visited your outlet and was the only customer in line. I ordered a 6-inch wheat sub and forgot to mention avocado until after the vegetables were added. Your staff member Esswari was visibly annoyed and remarked that I should have informed her earlier. Her facial expression and tone were unprofessional and made me feel unwelcome as a customer.

I personally told her that her behaviour was disrespectful and that as a service staff, she should not be speaking to customers in that manner. She eventually apologised, but only after initially being defensive about it.

I understand that adding items after vegetables have been placed may be inconvenient, but that is part of the job. There is no excuse for showing annoyance or speaking to a customer in that manner, regardless of what kind of day you're having.

I would appreciate it if Esswari could be sent for customer service training. Service staff should be able to handle simple order changes without making the customer feel like a burden.

Thank you.
author: Andrew Tan

review_text: I was served by James on 4 Dec at around 4:30pm and he was extremely helpful. He is very dedicated and also made my order with lots of care. Thank you for the great service James 😊
author: Elisha May

review_text:
I have been eating/buying at Subway J8 for years and realised that the amount of lettuce that they give nowadays are pathetic.

Bought (takeaway) a footlong chicken teriyaki flat bread on 18 Sep 2024 for $14.60. The amount of lettuce that I got is less than half of what I used to get (photo attached).

The prices of their sub have gone up quite a bit over the years, and I understand that it's due to inflation, and I can accept that. But at the same time, they are also cutting down on the amount of vegetables that they are giving us.

I'm really very disappointed and felt shortchanged. I'm not sure whether this only happens at J8 outlet or it's across all as I seldom buy from other outlets. Hope the Subway management can look into this and be fair to their customers.
author: Yeow Hwee Goh

review_text: “I had a really disappointing experience with your staff. They were quite rude and displayed a lot of attitude. It felt like they lacked basic manners when interacting with customers. They didn’t listen properly, added the wrong vegetables, and when I asked to correct it, the lady gave me a very unpleasant look. Is this really how your staff are trained? I expected much better service.”
author: Abhirami Gireeshkumar

review_text:
Decent family restaurant. Food is not fantastic, but good enough for the kids. Desserts are a crowd favourite too. Ordered the fish baked rice, mac & cheese, and an OG Ultra burger. Kids loved the baked rice and mac & cheese, though the latter got a bit jelak after a while. The burger was surprisingly good. Loved the caramelised onions and the sauce, and even the patty was better than I remembered. Desserts wise, we got the mint ice cream and the sticky chewy chocolate. I didn't try the mint, but the sticky chewy chocolate was pretty darn delicious.

Service was quite slow though. The dishes arrived quite far apart from one another. First the baked rice, then the mac & cheese, and finally the burger. By the time my burger arrived, my kids were done with their food. Also, staff didn't look friendly. In fact, they looked like they were forced to work, and everything was a chore.
author: Sihan Goi

review_text: Had a great dining experience at Swensen’s Thomson Plaza. The food was served fresh and tasted excellent, and the overall service was very good. The staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel comfortable throughout the meal. Definitely one of the better Swensen’s outlets — will be back again. Highly recommended!
author: Cash Loke

review_text:
I had a wonderful dining experience at Swensen’s! The food was delicious, served fresh and quickly, and the atmosphere was warm and welcoming. I would especially like to compliment the staff, particularly Shi Jia, for her exceptional service. She was friendly, attentive, and made sure we had everything we needed throughout our meal. Her cheerful attitude truly made our visit memorable.

Thank you, Swensen’s and Shi Jia, for the great service! I will definitely be coming back again! 😋🍽️✨
author: Miki Lew

review_text:
🟧 Swensen's
301 Upper Thomson Rd,
#03-23, Thomson Plaza,
Singapore 574408

🟡 Location = The Swensen’s at Thomson Plaza is nestled at a corner of the 3rd level, adjacent to a children’s educational learning centre.

🟨 Visited with my hubby and ordered two items to share, as we were not very hungry.

● Creamy Mushroom Soup — SGD9.90
◼️ Strawberry Sundae — SGD8.80

🟤 Food wise = The mushroom soup was thick, creamy, and delicious.

🔶️ The Strawberry Sundae was a lovely treat and brought back nostalgic memories of me as a teenager dining at Swensen’s in the 1980s.

🟢 Decor / Ambience
*************************
🟢 This is said to be the very first Swensen’s restaurant in Singapore, which opened in 1979 at Thomson Plaza.

🟢 The beautiful stained-glass Tiffany lamps are a classic decor element that harks back to the 1980s and 1990s. 🟢 There are booth seats too, which make dining comfortable and cosy.

🟠 The restaurant isn’t too crowded on a Monday, allowing a peaceful and relaxed dining experience.

🟪 Mr Rafiq, the floor manager in charge, was very pleasant, affable, and polite. We had a short chat with him and found him to be warm and amiable.

🟨 Overall, today’s simple dine-in at Swensen’s truly brought back wonderful memories of the past. ●  A timeless restaurant that continues to serve comfort food with warmth and nostalgia — Swensen’s at Thomson Plaza remains a sentimental favourite after all these years.

🔵 6th Oct 2025 Monday evening.
author: Florence Leow

review_text: Last minute we came in to have dessert near to last order time and the manager and service crew welcome us. The dessert was fresh well presented and all ingredients were fresh. Good Job
author: Lia Mezelf

review_text: Best banana fritter in Toa Payoh, maybe Singapore. Their turnover was very fast so no matter what time you buy, the fritters were still hot. Maybe their bright lights helped too. I loved their banana fritters and the green bean. Chempadak was special but there’s a big seed inside. Would be so much better with the seed removed. Coffee at this coffee shop was decent too. Good pairing.
author: HC L

review_text:
Not as crispy as last time. Batter seems to have changed.

Oil not that clean. Has a weird taste/smell.

Cash only.

- Count your pieces and count your change before leaving.

Pisang Raja ($1.50)
Curry Puff ($1.50)
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text:
This stall specializes in Goreng pisang and other fried delights.

They are located at a coffee shop along Toa Payoh Central, and is a 2 mins walk away from Toa Payoh National Library.

I got the following:
- Goreng pisang, which was freshly fried. It was big and mildly sweet.
- Fried sweet potato: this was a huge piece of sweet potato 🍠 that was coated with crispy batter. Not too sweet though.
- Chempedak: this was a huge specimen, and I had a hard time chewing the fibers and swallowing it.

Not too bad, but we didn’t get to try the other items, as they were sold out and being replenished.
author: Winston Ho

review_text:
Do note they accept cash only. Not even Paynow yuh.

Have been buying goreng pisang here (on and off) for over 30 years. Not consistently good goreng pisang so there will be days it’s better than others.

They start making the items from their opening time so some of the items may only be available some time after the opening time.

Only the pisang is a 4/5 inconsistently (+-1). The other items are 2-3/5 impo. Ref pix of the red bean which had toooo much pastry.
author: Raphael Too

review_text:
Simply one of the best, if not it’s the best Pisang Raja in Singapore!🍌🍌🍌

Translate to “Fried Banana”, it’s found in most hawker centres in Singapore 🇸🇬. Traditionally a Malay snack, what is rare here, is a Chinese Chef to master cooking this snack. Toa Payoh Lucky Pisang Raja has got to be in business for well over 50yrs, ever since I was a kid and the stall has been operating at the same coffee ☕️ shop.

What’s good? What’s special? 1️⃣ Firstly, it’s the whole banana not the cut into half type type. So full banana….. super sweet! 2️⃣ Secondly, the batter they use has gotta be one hell of a special!! 🤣💪💪💪 Fried till super crispy and yet the banana inside is still not burned and super juicy? How? You gotta ask yourself how on earth did they do it? 3️⃣ Thirdly, everything else in the store is just as yummy! Nobody goes there and buy just 1 x Pisang! 🤤

Pro Tip : All orders are take away orders. So it comes in a paper bag 🛍️ and then a plastic bag. NEVER tie up the bag! The minute the heat gets trapped inside the bags, they will go soggy 💦. (Guarantee) if they just finished frying it, air it as much as you can and try your best to avoid getting the paper bag wet. (Or you can walk back and queue again 😂😂😂)

Sick Tip : Bring it home and pour hot chocolate or condense milk over it! 😋😅😂😘 don’t say “Bo Jio!”

#kingofpisang

review_text:
Dear Management,

Order Date: 28.11.25
Order Time: 2:11 PM
Requested Delivery Time: 8:45 PM
Actual Delivery Time: 8:10 PM

I would like to provide feedback regarding a very disappointing experience with your store manager.

When I highlighted that the pizza we received was noticeably thinner than what we have ordered from Pizza Hut in the past few years, and that the ingredients were clearly less than before, I asked the manager to check our past order records. Instead of assisting, he told me not to make comparisons. If customers are not allowed to compare, how can we know whether the quality is consistent? His response was unprofessional and left me very upset.

We spent $45.10, and the order was meant for my brother’s birthday celebration. Yet the pizza arrived cold, looked like it had been left aside for a long time, and the overall quality was unacceptable.

What made the situation worse was the manager asking me to go down to the outlet so he could “do the pizza in front of me.” As a customer, is it my responsibility to go to the store just to check what should have been properly prepared and quality-checked before delivery? Why wasn’t the food quality inspected by the manager before handing it over to the delivery rider?

This entire experience was extremely disappointing, especially considering it was for a special occasion. I sincerely hope the management will look into this matter seriously and take the necessary actions to ensure better service and quality in the future.

Thank you.

review_text: The stall offered a really wide selection of 酿豆腐！ Most of the items were very decently-sized and came in two selections- fried and ‘boiled’. restaurant_name: Hup Chong Yong Tau Foo Blk 203
review_text:
I’m usually not a fan of yong tau foo, but I recently tried this stall as I was in the area and completely fell in love with it. Their ingredients clearly taste freshly made in-house, very different from the mass-produced items you get at supermarkets or many other YTF stalls. I especially appreciate that they separate ingredients meant for deep-frying from those for soup. That alone shows the extra effort and care they put into their food.

Their pumpkin rice is another highlight, generously packed with ingredients like yam and mushrooms, and full of flavour. I usually order five ingredients with the pumpkin rice and it comes up to around $7.20. It’s extremely filling and I often struggle to finish it.

Despite the long queues, all the staff are consistently friendly and patient, which is refreshing compared to some popular hawker stalls that come with unnecessary attitude.

I genuinely don’t understand how a STOMP journalist ordering nine ingredients for $9.20 can consider that “expensive.” Did she even finish the food? More importantly, how can one claim to critique food when unable to distinguish between factory-produced ingredients and freshly handmade ones?

The stall has clearly put up a notice that they will be closing in January 2026 and thanked customers for their support. Knowing this, why intentionally patronise the stall only to publish a malicious article that undermines a hawker’s hard work and rubs salt into the wound?

Final words to the journalist: what goes around comes around.
author: Jolene

restaurant_name: Hup Chong Yong Tau Foo Blk 203
review_text:
If ever someone asks me, I'd recommend to go for bee hoon (dry version) if you are at Hup Chong. The bee hoon is cooked to perfection, not soggy at all, and tasted like fried bee hoon after being tossed in fragrant scallion oil.

While the usual healthy yong tau foo items were expectedly good, the fried items here are the bombz! Rare, novel and delicious. We enjoyed the mozzarella wrapped in ham (yes, there was cheese pull) and the fried enoki mushroom wrapped in ham (seemingly). Honourable mentions are the fried eggplant with meat and another rendition of fried eggplant with fish paste.

We also liked that the fried items were separated from the non-fried ones which were meant to be in the soup. And they even went through the trouble to fry those fried items again on high heat which makes it less oily actually. It was speedy though, we got our food right after making payment. "A" for effort and efficiency.

Do remember to grab the chilli sauce. Definitely has a kick! It goes very well with the fried yong tau foo.

The coffeeshop can get somewhat crowded during mealtimes so the tip is to beat the crowd and secure a table under a ceiling fan!

review_text:
I’ve been eating this chwee kueh for over 40 years, starting from their original stall in Tiong Bahru, and to me they still serve the best-tasting cai po (preserved radish) condiment in Singapore. Yes, it leans on the oilier side, but the umami depth is unmatched—likely from the addition of fried and powder 扁鱼 or ikan bilis. The touch of toasted sesame adds a lovely fragrance, and when paired with their proprietary chili sauce, the flavour is truly unrivalled in my opinion.

That said, ever since they expanded through franchised outlets, the consistency hasn’t quite kept up. Quality can vary, and service standards differ across locations.

I really hope they preserve the standards of this heritage dish and not let Jian Bo fade into oblivion.

Gourmet Paradise where the stall is located is extremely crowded during lunch time so definitely come early before the lunch peak hour.

The waiter brought the bowl of calamari into the kitchen and immediately came out with it, and told me that his peers in the kitchen said it was "supposed to be like this". I very painstakingly peeled off the burnt areas so that we could eat the calamari. It was very upsetting. Couldn't believe I was paying money at Saizeriya to do this. When I paid my bill, I told the cashier what happened and showed him pictures of the burnt calamari. I was glad that at least he had the decency to say that "we should never serve customers food that is burnt like this"!

This was such a bad experience, and such an upsetting one!
author: Allison Loo

review_text: The food is stunning, chicken chop is juicy and combined with their black pepper sauce which is delectable and spicy, makes a feast to remember for. review_text: Mixed experience today. The fried glass noodles were quite oily and lacked flavor, though the omelette and green curry chicken were decent. author: SP Gan

review_text:
This isn’t about the money — the prices are reasonable. But the food was honestly terrible.

The long beans were completely undercooked — hard and raw. Even my kid refused to eat it and said we should never come back again. That says a lot.

The green curry was acceptable, which is the only reason this place gets 2 stars. But even in that dish, the long beans were still undercooked. It feels like basic cooking standards were ignored.

Having lived in Thailand for many years, I can confidently say this does not represent authentic Thai food. They should seriously reconsider calling themselves “Maya Thai” if this is the standard they’re serving.
author: Low Roy

review_text:

Portions were good, food court prices but taste was delightful. We asked for spicy for every dishes and loved it. Recommended mango salad, basil minced chicken, steamed squid in garlic and lime. We will definitely checkout other outlets/ne back again.

review_text:

review_text: Always my to go place for western good! Very nostalgic ambience with good service and food! We have a CNY special today with two mini cupcakes served! Thank you again to the service staff!
author: Irene Seah

review_text: I come here regularly for meals. Had a Christmas dinner with family and was very happy with the service. Manager Krishna was such an excellent host and went over and beyond to make the occasion specials

review_text: Only had dessert here. Lava cake with ice cream was alright. Ambience and service was that of a neighbourhood eatery. No frills and simple. If not for rain, would have gone to other dessert options along upp thomson cafe stretch. Might be back to try their mains.
author: Joyce Lim

review_text: Pocoloco really stand up to their title as the best Italian restaurant in Singapore and I dont really understand what's there to hate 🫤. It started one day when I was craving pasta when I saw Pocoloco. When I reached the place, the atmosphere was silent and with music playing in the background. I ordered the mushroom soup and it came after some time. In the menu they said their mushroom soup is homemade and it is really true, I could see the chuncks of mushroom inside the soup, the soup was not too thick and not too light just perfect and it is so creamy with the chewiness of the mushroom in the bite. Next I ordered the manzo ( a truffle cream base with beef) and is also the second picture right next to the mushroom soup, for me I am a truffle fan and the manzo satisfied me. With just one bite, I could taste the rich truffle with the creamy sauce and the al dente pasta, making it not chewy but just right, the beef was succulent and just right not too chewy and not too hard. Lastly for desert I ordered their their lava cake, once I cut inside the cake rich chocolate oozed out of the cut and amazed me at first sight when I took a bite my mouth exploded the flavour of the rich chocolate filled my mouth and with the side of the vanilla ice cream balanced the taste of slightly bitter with sweet. Overall, Pocoloco is very good and really does not deserve hate, it can be pricey but let me tell you this it will be worth every cent, even though you look st their food it may look like a small portion but it is really heavy, as I said it is about the quality not quantity and all the food has great presentation. Staff is also very kind. Please just order what you like and don't try anything for the first time and leave a bad review saying it is bad 🫠. Everything there is good but I really recommend the pasta. However, please do not hate the parking it really is not Pocoloco's fault my advise just park at the landed properties up the hill anyways there is no harm to walk. But beware they close at 9p.m. . Everything has great quality and great taste.
author: Gerard Yan

review_text: Friendly service and nice cozy vibe! Was recommended the pork chop from the dinner set and it didn’t disappoint! The set came with a pasta and meat dish, and appetizer. Very generous portions - 1 dinner set meal was just nice for us 2 ladies, and we added a salad just to see some greens.
author: Joo Chin

review_text:
I only patronised this place because I saw a TikTok video by Food Truths SG calling them the “OG affordable pastas” (from multiple outlets now down to just one). Honestly, there’s a reason why they’ve closed so many.

Pescatora – bland beyond belief. Light tomato sauce so weak I had to ask: was tomato even in the room? Partner (not picky at all) finished it, but even he said it was tasteless. 2/10

Vongole – smelled like flour, tasted like plain boiled pasta. I had to drown it in Tabasco just to eat a few bites. 2/10

Funghi Trifolati – dry, salty, lifeless mushrooms. I usually love the natural juiciness of portobello, but this had none of that. Anyhow sautéing mushrooms at home with garlic, butter, olive oil could taste better. 2.5/10

Gamberi – finally a dish that was seasoned properly. Decent flavour, nothing mind-blowing, but at least enjoyable. 6.5/10

Seafood Tomato Soup – seasoned and comforting, thankfully. 6.8/10

Filleto di Manzo – the best dish of the night. Sauce was the star. 7/10

The so called “2/10” pasta ratings are really just for the ingredients; the pasta itself is a zero. I don’t know how anyone in the Tiktok comments or Google reviews said their pasta was good. HUH? What did they eat? Did I get a stand in chef? Or was the head chef on MC today?

This wasn’t “health-conscious bland” it was absolutely no seasoning bland. Really, really disappointing.

review_text: Great Granchio & Vongole Bianco to kick-start the week! Rich and creamy pink sauce coats every single strand of tagliatelle pasta along with bits of crab meat. The delightful clams in white wine were juicy and plentiful tossed with copious amount of sautéed chopped garlic and spaghetti. Love it!

restaurant_name: 饗好吃 Xiang Taiwanese Desserts and Food
review_text: I come here every time I’m in the area. The flavours meet my tastes perfectly. I especially love the fried chicken scallion noodle set. Really cripsy,  juicy and tender chicken. They have a wide variety of dishes to choose from and their desserts are so good as well!! Really love this place, do come and try it out!
author: Regina Yap

restaurant_name: 饗好吃 Xiang Taiwanese Desserts and Food
review_text:
Ordered braised pork rice for $8.80 plus combo with mala enoki for $2.50. Total cost $11.30.

Rice: poor
Onsen egg: excellent
Braised pork: okay... Not authentic
Sour vege: good
Mala enoki: great
Amount for money: poor

I actually have the choice of egg and i went with onsen egg. Honestly it was top notch in term of doneness hence runniness. However, PARTLY due to me asking for less ricr and their rice being cooked in a wet way, the rice became too watery, taste was okay but texture was not good. However i would say main problem was the rice was already damn and doesn't absorb the egg well... Cooking rice with braised meat, it should been harder/dryier, while partly due to lesser ricr, i doubt it will help that much given the starting state of rice. But nevertheless a very well cooked egg.

Braised pork was tough and not melting. More lean than those I had in Taiwan and certainly it is more catered to local dinner than being authentic taiwan... Because from the old reviews there were complain of it being too salty... But that's generally how they are in Taiwan tbh.

Sour vege was good to prevent the meal from getting too gela. The mala enoki was very well done, managable ma and la to give that kick without bringing tears... A good balancing act.

Amount for money is not very good since braised pork already cost $8.80 as RELATIVELY not alot of braised pork were in it. It might be just nice for the meal but for $8.80 it is not a lot. My wife's drunken chicken was a lot though.

Having say that do check out their lunch which cost just $5.80, i assume that will be value for money.
author: Super Fragrance

restaurant_name: 饗好吃 Xiang Taiwanese Desserts and Food
review_text:

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text: On CNY Eve we prepared a feast for our family but was missing the butane fuel canister to cook the hotpot. FairPrice and Shengsiong was closed, 7-11 and other convenience stores didn’t carry any. I walked by this restaurant and asked to buy 2 canisters, and the 2 sweet Thai staff gave it to me without question and refused to take my money, effectively saving our reunion dinner. They honestly made me feel lucky! I came back days later with 2 canisters and a small gift to them (one of the sweet staff was out buying stuff). Seriously we need to see our migrant workers as the backbone of our society, and a blessing to all. Thank you!
author: Sun Koh

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text:
One of the best mookata but today a bit disappointed with the pork collar. Almost all fat n no meat.
But staff helped to cancel my pork collar order. Will still come back cos it’s tasty n price reasonable.
author: sandy chua

restaurant_name: Siam Square Mookata - Best Mookata Restaurant in Singapore
review_text:
We planned to get a late-night mookata snack on a whim, just the two of us. We thought it’d be a cheap and cheerful meal—we were told the buffet was over $30 ➕➕
per person, but the final bill came to a whopping $130 total 🥲

We asked if they had an à la carte option when we walked in, and the staff said yes. Then my husband decided to switch to the buffet instead.

First, they handed us an à la carte bill for $112. I was shocked and pointed out we’d had the buffet, not à la carte. The staff looked dismissive, then reprinted a buffet bill—which was even more expensive at $130. And they refused to switch back to the $112 bill, claiming they’d printed too many receipts already.

To make it worse, the buffet didn’t include all dishes—some items were extra charge, and the staff never bothered to mention that. I even had to ask if water was included with the buffet because they didn’t say a word about it. The staff spent most of the time on their phones since it was quiet late at night, with zero proper communication.

And when I checked the receipt at home? They charged us for 3 bottles of Coke Zero when we only had 2. Seriously, what were they even doing at work?

This was our first time here, and it’ll definitely be the last. For $130, we could’ve had way better hot pot or BBQ with actual service. Lesson learned with buffets: ask every single detail before you order. Sure, we could’ve been more thorough—but the restaurant’s service and staff accountability need a massive upgrade.

Avoid this place at all costs:
SIAM SQUARE MOOKATA (UPPER THOMSON)

Din Tai Fung never goes wrong. The atmosphere is comfortable, though it’s usually quite crowded, especially during peak hours. Service is efficient despite the crowd. The beef noodle was great — rich broth and full of flavour — and the brisket was impressively tender. Overall, a reliable spot for quality Taiwanese cuisine.
Overall rating: 4/5 ⭐⭐⭐⭐

review_text:
We frequent this branch as it is near our place. We love the food. Kudos to the kitchen and service staff.

However, recently the smell of the table (we thought it was from smelly table cloth) got to us. Even after asking the staff to help us wipe another time, i tried wiping with my wet wipes too but the smell lingers. It affected the enjoyment of the food as every mouth took in a whiff of the smelly sweaty table smell. Feedback to the staff but they say they already feedback to the management to do something about their 8yrs old tables that have absorbed the smell. I appreciate their honesty and i look forward to see them able to secure a budget to change those old tables.

The vegetable noodle soup was light yet satisfying, and the steamed vegetable dumplings were delicate and tasty. We also enjoyed the pork chop fried rice, which had just the right amount of seasoning, and the classic xiao long bao, which never disappoint. Service was prompt, polite, and efficient despite the busy crowd. Always a reliable spot for a comforting and delicious meal. Highly recommended!

author: DeeSee

review_text: Pretty decent thai food around the neighbourhood! Just feel that the meat is a lil less on the rice dish! Would be a 5 stars if the portion is increased! Would come again in e future!
author: Louis (ahluu)

review_text:
One of my long time favourites in Toa Payoh!
Food is consistently yummy. Used to eat so regularly and tapau home when I was living in Toa Payoh. Came back today after a year's absence to find new items in the menu. Food is as yummy as usual!
Happy that they customised my rice to half portion (in case anyone thinks the rice portion is small)!
Cozy environment.
Come on weekdays if you wanna avoid the crowd 😋 otherwise, be ready to tapau or queue awhile.
author: Lye Yoong Tan

review_text: Good value for money.  Loads of food for almost 90 bucks for 5 of us.  Enjoyed crab meat yellow curry 7/10.  The rest a decent good tasty.
author: KC PSbackup

review_text:
quite good especially with grab dine in deal

tomyum soup is yummy but im not a fan of the vermicelli not wokhei enough
author: Justin Chong

review_text: Super chill corner in Toa Payoh to enjoy Thai food. Ordered the vegetarian green curry and it was surprisingly good as I tried the chicken version and the chicken meat tasted “frozen”. The Tom yum seafood was okay but hot, a bit on the salty side. There’s a chill out corner at the side of the restaurant. Service was good and prompt.
author: Derrick L

review_text:
Sent in a pickup order via online website for collection at 615pm. When I reached the restaurant at 620pm there was a long line outside. I overheard a lady that is collecting her order for 545pm and the food wasn’t even ready

Waited for over 50mins to collect 3 pizza. Food collected at 705pm

Order at your own risk!!!

Why take orders when you can’t even deliver a preorder on time?
author: Low Heng Yin

review_text:
Well it arrived on time, but no other saving graces. That might’ve been our worst pizza experience. So bad we couldn’t stop laughing about it while eating. The biggest problem was the dough which was traumatizingly thick (we ordered the classic) and felt like eating bread and calories. Second, equally disturbing problem was the cheese. We understand processed cheese is inexpensive already, but they managed to find and use the most flavorless processed cheese. We ordered 2 pizzas and finished half the order before giving up. Serious improvement needed here and hope the business tests try their food to come to their own conclusion.
Added thought: the advert in YouTube did its job and one of the pizzas we ordered was the beef shawarma. In fact the pizza “looks” just like the video! but taste and texture fell way short.
author: Gordon Lau

review_text:
Delivery. 26th December 2025. 2 large pizzas. 1 carbonara, 1 simply cheese.

Delivery:
- Delivery was quick and pizza was warm.
- Delivery man was polite.

Food:
- Carbonara pizza was ok. Average. 3 stars.
- WARNING. The simply cheese had a strong stale pungent smell similar to a dirty towel used to wipe tables and not cleaned for days. It's as though the water from that towel was squeezed to make the pizza. Lowest rating possible - 1 star.

Never buying from dominos again. Not even worth the 2 for 1 offer as it totaled close to $50 for this standard.
author: Ken

review_text: got it for delivery, ordered at 6:20pm, arrived at 7:46pm. pizza is cold, little sauce. called this branch about 8 times, no answer. seems like whoever is working doesn't even pick up calls nor even know how to work. checked how busy they were on the live update on google, and it tells me they aren't even busy. hella poor management, got zero serive. also, delivery person doesn't even bother to knock on the door. all they do is send a message saying the pizza is here. no sound, nothing. shut down at this point, y'all have been going downhill since last year
author: Sung min Won

review_text:
When I first entered the store to ask about my order. I was attended by a lady who served me with a good attitude. However, when she cannot find my order, she called someone who I believe was the manager to attend to me. When he spoke to me and ask on my order details, it felt like as if I owe him  something. I do not expect a very 5 star service as this is just a pizza shop, but perhaps at least basic manners to talk and not talk like a gangster.

Food: This is dominos pizza, one of the famous pizza shop in Singapore. However what I see today is an uncooked cheese stick and the way they prep the pizza was quite disappointed.
author: Zi Bao Ng

review_text: Tasteful & yummy Beehoon with lobster 🦞, prawn 🦐, crab 🦀, seafood. Fresh seafood with tasty Mee Hoon. Price is cheap with big portions also. Highly recommended. Toa Payoh mrt take bus 238 then reach this location. Location at Toa Payoh Lorong 8 market there.
author: August Zin

review_text:
Food: Very flavourful white bee hoon soup; with wok hey taste. portion is large for 1 person.
Service: Good and fast service.
Atmosphere: Warm and got birds around.
author: J “Nobita” O

review_text: Seafood White Mee Hoon: Superb! I highly recommend the Seafood Vermicelli (Mee Hoon). The dish was incredibly flavorful and complex, coated in a thick, savory gravy that was just bursting with fresh seafood essence. The noodles were generous and loaded with fresh prawns and clams, topped with those wonderful crunchy fried shallots/lard.
author: Ooi SB

review_text: Last Saturday,  I came across this White Mee Hoon at Pasir Ris Central Hawker Centre, managed by Foodfare. It means there is at least one dish selling at $2.80. White Meehoon (Veg/Lala) at $2.80. My wife and I went for Crayfish Lala Prawn Meehoon $15. The portion was large, enough for 3 adults. The stock of meehoon was deliciously rich with flavours. The crayfish, prawn and lala (clams) were very fresh. The stall holders were friendly and honest.  I initially ordered $20 , but he said $15 is more than sufficient for 2 adults. The meehoon was dry fried to give the smokiness aroma before adding the stock. Heavenly taste. They have pure fish version for those who have prawn or crayfish or clam allergies.  Value for money. I like the white meehoon so much that I went back in the evening to buy another two tubs of $20 each for my whole family to try. 👍👍👍😋
author: Ngee Wah Ng

review_text: Love this white mee hoon which has a very clean taste to it! So it tastes quite healthy to me. My first time trying this tonight and it was delicious, even though mine was takeaway. Lots of options too, I went with the sliced fish option. Thank you for making my night! 🙏🏻
author: Ashley Liew

review_text: Good chicken rice restaurant. Famous easy dish of Singapore. This restaurant are really good. I love the chicken which is juicy and tender. Rice are not oily. Stir fried vegetable are also good. You need to order first then they will assigned the seat for you. Cash only. Please bring your own napkin. Enjoy!
author: Supakij Khomvilai

review_text:
Famous for its kampong chicken rice, Chicken House serves tender, leaner cuts of Kampung Chicken with fragrant rice and a light, flavourful soup. The chilli and ginger sauces complement the chicken perfectly. I thought the standard as dropped slightly over the years though. Their blanched beansprouts add a nice crunch, while the prawn rolls are crisp, juicy, and a great side to share.

Service is quick and efficient even during busy periods, though parking along Upper Thomson can be a bit of a hassle. Simple, no-frills coffee shop setting — great for a satisfying and comforting chicken rice meal.
author: Xin Hao

review_text: Serves kampong chicken with its unique yellow skin, pretty juicy skin along with fragrant rice and soup. Saw some reviews about a rude cashier but my experience was good. Shop closes quite early around 7 as soon as chicken runs out so if u want to eat for dinner don’t come too late
author: Jason Z

review_text:
My friend and I went there for the first time and when we walk inside thought of we can just sit and order. She shouted at us let us to queue up and order. Till now it is fine. When I just finished eating without any rest, LITERALLY JUST FINISHED MY LAST BITE. She say, ay, can I collect, a lots people out there queueing alr. So, I quickly finish my drink then we walk out. BUT there is no one queueing for sit at alllll. We get so disappointed after this meal, we were so happy to try out but this was very bad experience for us.

Food: Just OK, the experience make it worse
author: Jerry Yin

review_text:
Decent plate of chicken rice. Saw a lot of raving fans for this place.

Probably unable to identify this from a decent hawker stall, but when paying for food court or big brand price then, probably have other options better.

What I appreciate is the flavor of the nice chicken soup.
author: Thaddeus Zheng

review_text: Celebrated my birthday here. Thank you so much for the service 😊 we’re here while ramadhan for iftar. All foods are good. I love the bubur/porridge. So tasty! Salmon here also very nice.
author: Asmarani Ran

review_text:
Location- situated at the Aloft Novena east wing

Food- Ample spread of delicious dishes, be it, meat or seafood. There was cold dishes, sashimi, roast beef, satay, etc The replenishment of most food, were done promptly except for the large lobster. Water is free flow but you have to self service and it's only one small dispenser.

service- The dishes were cleared quite promptly. Just that when we arrived early
we were told that the restaurant was fully booked so we couldn't be seated by ourselves, had to share those 2 seaters located closely to one another. There were some still empty tables throughout the buffet time. The closeness, led to my spouse and myself, being splattered with crab juices when the adjacent table were eating crabs/lobster.

Value- booked the hotel and got this buffet under SG60 package.
author: Richard D Lee

review_text:
Cooked food spread is alright. But good value especially with the one for one lunch deals.

They charge for still water. But you dont really need this since they've a wide range of teas and coffee options. Dessert soread is good too with pastries and fruits and a fondue
author: Colin

review_text:
Went for Lasa Pilipinas weekday lunch buffet on Oct 31 2025.

Good selection of food & Bangus and Palabok tasted authentic. Other selections were quite good as well but sadly, didn’t get to try Lechon Manok.

Price is acceptable as they were having an offer for “2nd dinner dines for $2”

Service staffs were very attentive especially Carrie & Natasha as they were constantly checking if we were enjoying the food & need any refills.

Carrie also noticed that I was checking my Bonvoy app & told me that I can get points after payment.

Overall, the service & food was very good and will definitely be back for more.

Thank you to the service team & the cooks and chef behind the kitchen 👏🏽
author: Alfred Oreta

review_text: Had a company dinner at the venue. Food was great everyone enjoyed the various spread of food made. The seafood spread was generous and fresh as you can see from the pictures. The satay was amazingly tasty too not those sweet kind found at many satay stalls outside. The turkey is due to christmas is just round the corner. Turkey was well marinated and is flavourful, the lamb is fresh and juicy certainly a must try for diners. With a good spread of desserts, variety of sweet cakes,chocolate fondue and ice cream what more can we ask for. Totally worth it dining experience. Thanks 21 on Rajah you were wonderful!
author: Hafiz Nor

review_text: Unexpectedly, our favourites from this pizza place were the pastas! Pastas were very yummy and cooked to a perfect al dente. Our favourites were the pesto chicken pasta and the carbonara - lots of ingredients and very flavourful. The all-day Mon-Thurs set set deal is very worth it as well. Panna cotta was tasty, could see specks of the real vanilla bean.
author: Lextherex

review_text: Had our farewell team lunch at Peperoni Pizzeria and it couldn’t have been better. The food was amazing, the vibes were great, and the staff were incredibly friendly, they really made the whole experience feel warm and memorable. Special shoutout to Lidia she was damn kind, super friendly, and made the whole experience feel extra warm and memorable. Thank you for making our farewell lunch so special!
author: Syrena Tang

review_text:
It was a day for pizza and pasta, so we decided to try this place. There was no queue when we arrived and the staff were friendly and efficient. We ordered the truffle fries ($13), a half and half large pizza with smoked farmer’s ham with kale and egg and funghi ($27), and a carbonara ($24).

The truffle fries were hot, fresh, very flavourful and they came with a truffle mayo dip that went well with them. The pizza was a bit disappointing. We didn’t know it was thin crust and it would have been better if there was an option for normal crust since we prefer something more filling. The carbonara was so so, a little too creamy and would have liked it to be a bit more cheesy.

One thing to note is that plain water is not available and you have to order drinks instead, which I felt should have been complimentary.

Overall, the food was okay but it’s not exactly cheap for the taste and portion.
author: June Ang

review_text:
The pizza was a bit burnt on the base n so could taste quite bitter. Otherwise, Average food.
Environment was good for a family gathering.
Clean and quiet.
Service could be improved. We ordered the xxl pizza and they just came with it without first making sure that there is room on the table. We had to scramble to remove and make way for it.
author: Mikki B

review_text: Decided to give it a try since the review looks good. Found it very misleading . For the price, the pizzas are rather disappointing compared to others available nearby. Pizza is thin but even the cheese is spreaded too thin that you feel like eating just the thin crust . The salami used also weren't as good as the ones used by other pizza orders I've done. I wouldn't order this again honestly.
author: HiroM

review_text: Curry puff was average. Can’t beat the more established Brands. But the discovery of the day was the fried banana. Really sweet on inside and light crispy batter on outside.
author: FoodieDirectory

review_text:
Tasty curry puff with solid filling. Pastry is crispy. Giant fishball is nice and juicy. Goreng pisang is good too! Definitely a must to try.
There's another branch at Blk 349, Jurong East Ave 1, #01-1201
author: Joey Low

review_text: The mutton curry puff is the best imo. I love having prata next door then come here to get curry puffs. The price point is lower than ock and it is more homemade flavours. Nice packaging for a box of 10 and good to bring to gift. Very polite staff!
author: Sue Asff

review_text: We have been frequenting this shop since almost 10 years ago. They sell one of the most delicious curry puffs in Thomson area, thin and crispy crust with generous fillings of meat and egg. Highly recommend to try if you are around the area. Definitely deserving of 5 stars!
author: H

review_text: nice curry puffs with thin flaky crust.  value for money as the fillings are quite substantial.  Love the strands of onions inside sardine puffs and the chunks of chicken meat in the chicken curry puffs.  Love that it is not oily.
author: Sharon Chua

review_text: The beef with fried garlic and the fried chicken with cashew nuts were tasty and well cooked. Their fried egg was surprisingly delicious, and the chilli padi with fish sauce paired perfectly with the rice. The Tom Yam soup was alright, but overall the food was tasty, affordable, and consistently satisfying. Always a great place to come back to for a reliable Thai meal.
author: John

review_text:
If you’re looking for a solid Thai meal without the chaotic crowds, Jai Thai is a hidden gem worth visiting. The food is consistently good—not necessarily life-changing, but authentic, flavorful, and hits all the right notes for a satisfying lunch or dinner.
The most striking thing about the restaurant is how peaceful and quiet it is. Because of its slightly tucked-away location, it avoids the frantic energy of more central spots. This makes it an excellent choice for a focused catch-up with friends or a solo meal where you actually want to hear yourself think. It’s a reliable, low-key spot that deserves a bit more foot traffic than it gets!
author: FF2030

review_text:
Display and setup was well done. Food came on time and as usual taste great. Every guests enjoyed it very much.
Throughout the order, Boss was really helpful and responsive. Thanks once again for making our CNY gathering such a memorable experience
author: Lina Teo

review_text: If u love thai food, u hv to try this place! I order fish basil, tomyam clear soup, baked prawn tanghoon and seafood pad thai. The tomyam hits u with the perfect spicy and masam combo, wallahhhh really satisfying! Portions are generous, service is fast 15-20min and staff are super friendly. Highly recommended for anyone craving for authentic thai food👍🏻
author: NURUL NAJWA GHAZALI

review_text: Food standard varies, some days good some days not good. I ordered ผัดกระเพราไก่ basil with chicken and fried kangkong. I asked for less salty but the foods were still too salty for me. However, the fried egg was dripping with oil and overly deep fried with charred edges. Foods here are reasonably tasty but not exactly the best or authentic Thai food as most reviewers claimed.
author: Mandy

review_text:
Visited a second time and the mutton biryani has become even better and Fish Tandoori is very nice and generous in portion.

Previous visit :
Very fast and efficient, mutton biryani is very fragrant, like the rice. Mutton can be more flavorful but is tender. However given that it’s $13, I rated 5 stars relative to the price as  well. Overall most items are quite good.
author: Sarah Soong

review_text: The dishes are very good especially the pani puri, tandoori chicken, aloo gobi and dal tadka. We like their basmati rice more than their tandoori roti. The meal arrived quickly and the service was good. Will return especially for their pani puri for sure.
author: Anthony K

review_text:
was superb food was goated
tasted like actual authentic north indian food
but service charge was too much $10
and only two people ate. and the service was avarage
and pani puri was mid.
and food arrived quick
author: Banu Hari

review_text:
Been coming to Daawat Tandoori for over 15 years, and it never disappoints. The butter chicken is creamy and flavorful, the naan is always fresh and fluffy, and the aloo gobi is beautifully spiced. Their tandoori chicken is another must try, smoky, tender, and packed with flavor.

This is easily one of the best spots in Singapore for authentic Northern Indian cuisine. Consistent food, warm service, and a place that truly feels like a gem in the neighborhood. Highly recommended!

From the moment I stepped into the restaurant, I was transported to the vibrant streets of North India. The ambiance was a perfect blend of tradition and modernity, with the aroma of spices wafting through the air, promising an authentic dining experience. The service was impeccable, and the owner was knowledgeable about the dishes and passionate about their craft. They recommended the perfect pairings and ensured that my dining experience was nothing short of extraordinary.

This restaurant isn't just about food, it's about an experience that stays with you long after you've left.

In summary, for anyone seeking the best of North Indian cuisine, this restaurant is a must-visit. It's a place where every dish tells a story, every flavor is a memory, and every visit feels like coming home.
author: Akhil Rana

review_text: If you're around Toa Payoh and need your caffeine fix, this spot is a solid choice. Be prepared for a bit of a crowd, as the ordering process can be a little messy at times. However, you can count on a consistent cup every time, and the staff does their best to keep things moving. It’s a dependable local staple.
author: Flo Yeow

review_text: New product at Ya Kun! Roasted Golden Chicken Leaf Bun!! The tiny crisps had added crunch to the buns! The taste would have been better if it were to be a little less salty! But I still enjoyed the buns with the hot ginger water.
author: Janice Tan

review_text: Came here courtesy of a birthday voucher from our brother’s insurance agent, and got ourselves a typical kaya butter toast set meal. The toast was good as usual, though the coffee was really small for the price, and slightly bitter too. Tough to give it 5 stars for the price, and especially so when it’s a tight space too.
author: YY

review_text: Toast is inconsistent, one side is crisp and the other is soggy like a used diaper. It’s not even busy yet it felt that the toasts were rushed out so the one making it could relax and chat. What a pity, yakun’s standards have really gotten drastically low over the years.
author: Lancelot Armstrong

review_text: Always enjoy the steambread and softboiled egg. I accidentally made the wrong order today and Wenhong is so understanding and accommodating to allow me to make changes to one set - at least my friend got the correct order! Really appreciate her great service attitude and flexibility. Really made my morning!
author: Koby Poppy Lim

restaurant_name: Long House Soon Kee (Boneless) Duck Rice(长屋順記(起骨)滷鴨飯・粥・鴨面)
review_text:
Tender and succulent duck plus well marinated with the braising sauce. I like the fattiness of the skin that is supper. Best part, they are boneless 😋😋😋

The giblets and heart are crunchy, but the liver is just too hard. A bit wasted.

Both the rice and noodle are very good. It comes down to your preference.

CBK verdict: definitely worth a repeat visit for their braised duck. 😊😊🐨🐨
author: N Hence (Chubby Botak Koala)

restaurant_name: Long House Soon Kee (Boneless) Duck Rice(长屋順記(起骨)滷鴨飯・粥・鴨面)
review_text:
Went to try with my family today. All of us really enjoyed it and agreed that it is one of the better duck rice in SG. Recommend everyone to try
