author: Jia En Liong

restaurant_name: Long House Soon Kee (Boneless) Duck Rice(长屋順記(起骨)滷鴨飯・粥・鴨面)
review_text:
Highly recommended sumptous duck rice.
$5 Portion small but taste good
author: HIN HOE CHEW

restaurant_name: Long House Soon Kee (Boneless) Duck Rice(长屋順記(起骨)滷鴨飯・粥・鴨面)
review_text: Braised duck was truly fantastic. Moist, tender, not greasy. Everything on the platter paired so well together with the egg, braised Tau Kwa, peanut, sauce and chilli. Not forgetting the  herbal soup. I enjoyed this so much that the next visit, I ordered to takeaway for the family to enjoy at home. The owner was really friendly and patient. Do take note that they only accept cash, so prepare this in advance!
author: Mel K

restaurant_name: Long House Soon Kee (Boneless) Duck Rice(长屋順記(起骨)滷鴨飯・粥・鴨面)
review_text: The boneless duck rice was tender, juicy, and full of flavour. The rice was fragrant and soaked up the delicious sauce perfectly. I also tried the duck porridge, which was smooth and comforting with generous chunks of duck. Both dishes were hearty and satisfying.
author: Helena Quek

review_text:
I had a bad experience at Old Chang Kee Toa Payoh branch on 11 Feb 2026 around 8.20pm.

I asked the staff what curry puff flavours were available because I saw different markings (green, red and normal). The staff only mentioned two flavours and did not explain clearly what the markings meant. When I politely asked again to confirm, she raised her voice at me.

I understand retail work can be frustrating, but I did not ask any offensive or unreasonable question. I was simply asking about the product before buying. Being spoken to in a raised tone was unnecessary and disappointing.

In the end, I still completed my purchase, but I bought fewer items than I originally intended because of this experience.
author: B. L.

review_text: First time trying out this salted egg chunky chicken pop IMO, this was very spicy. OCK should specify the spiciness of item
author: Elisa

review_text:
Very convenient place to get a quick bite. Love their fried sotong, my all time favorite and must eat whenever in the Lion City.
The curry puffs are also huge and filled with potatoes and chicken.
author: Jac Yim

review_text:
Since 1956, @oldchangkeesingapore has been a household brand, especially for their signature curry puffs and a wide variety of delicious, high-quality finger food.

It's delighted that Chicken Satay'O is coming back after its inaugural launch during SG50. The puff pastry is filled with tender juicy chicken and onion with a pinch of spice coming from the satay gravy peanut sauce.

Only $2.30.
author: Jeffrey Yeo

review_text: The lady who takes the order for the breakfast at the side is all smiles. She is the definition of customer service. Always visit this outlet to grab breakfast. The porridge and youtiao is popular and  gets quickly sold out. Today tried the mee siam. The portion is great and tasted delicious. I wish more old chang kee outlet could open up and serve breakfast as demand is there.
author: Aziana Nana

review_text:
The food at Omote has always left a good impression on me and this was my first time visiting the Thomson outlet. Food-wise, it was generally good, but the service was a little lacking. When you order hot green tea, the staff usually refill it proactively — but I had to ask twice. And considering we didn’t order very little (the bill came up to about $230 for 4 pax, which isn’t cheap for lunch), I expected slightly better attentiveness.

I also ordered the hamachi tartlets, and while the waitress was serving them, one of the tartlets toppled and the filling fell out. She saw it, pretended nothing happened, and still served it to me — even though I was clearly taking photos. I honestly didn’t know how to react. Isn’t this basic service 101?

On a brighter note, the salmon sashimi salad was the highlight — we liked it so much that we ordered a second portion. The truffle tako was the next best dish. The least impressive items were the beef tataki and the hamachi tartlets.

Overall, food is still reliable, but the service at this outlet could definitely be improved.
author: Angela Hoi

review_text:
We were the first to enter the restaurant without a booking at 5:30 pm, and within 10–15 minutes, about half the restaurant had already filled up. I’d definitely recommend making a reservation before coming.

The food was generally quite good with a decent variety, though the price point is on the higher side. It’s a cute concept that clearly appeals to a younger crowd and the idea of selling merchandise adds a unique touch.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text:
8/10
I had such a fantastic experience at Omoté! The food was truly outstanding, easily an 8/10 for deliciousness 😋. Every dish I tried was bursting with flavor and perfectly prepared. The service was also top-notch, incredibly attentive and friendly staff who made me feel so welcome. ✨ The atmosphere was simply delightful, creating a wonderful dining ambiance. Highly recommend! 👍
Just price wise a bit ex but u pay for it
author: Bryceps

review_text: Went with a group of five and were pleased with the variety on the menu. There were plenty of options, prices were fair, and everyone found something they enjoyed. A few dishes took longer to arrive and we had to follow up a couple of times, but overall we had a good experience.
author: Letícia Ventura

review_text:
One of the best japanese food chains in Singapore.

Love the chirashi don. Lots and lots of sashimi to go with the rice. Added the premium set for the rest of the side dishes.

Will definitely be back.
author: Jason Deng

review_text:
Review of The Roti Prata House @ Upper Thomson Road

If you are a fan of crispy roti prata, this is a place worth visiting. Their prata is pan-fried till nicely crisp, with a satisfying crunch on the outside while still enjoyable on its own or dipped into fish or chicken curry.

Personally, I still enjoy prata the childhood way — with sugar. Simple, nostalgic, and surprisingly addictive. Prices here are also very reasonable:
•	Plain prata at just $1.00
•	Egg prata at $1.20

What I like about prata is that there are almost 100 ways to enjoy it. Beyond the classic styles, modern variations are available too. One popular option is tissue prata, and my favourite version has to be the condensed milk tissue prata, where condensed milk is drizzled generously over a thin, crispy crust — sweet, light, and very addictive.

Apart from prata, I also fancy their Mee Hoon Mee Goreng and Nasi Goreng, which are comforting choices when you want something more filling. We sometimes order the Ayam Murtabak, where the chicken filling is wrapped with crispy prata, making it hearty and satisfying.

But my number one favourite here?
👉 Bomb Kaya Cheese — sweet, cheesy, indulgent, and honestly… just try it to know 😄

A solid spot at Upper Thomson for classic prata, modern twists, and comforting mamak-style dishes — whether for breakfast, supper, or a prata craving any time of the day.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text:
Overall - A great restaurant super cheap, good food, and good service. A bit crooked (literally) but still good. I have been going here since I was a young child great food.

Food - Overall the food is very good you can buy a Roti Prata for very cheap and the curry sauce is free. Though I have to admit the curry is not very complex but it is still delicious.

Service - Service is very attentive and whenever you need something you can get the attention of any server fairly quickly and they will bring what you request fairly quickly.

Atmosphere - The atmosphere is okay. It is not the most decorative restaurant and they are fairly open air but it is not necessarily bad it has a bit of a charm but that could be nostalgia talking. The outdoor seating is located on an incline so it can be a bit awkward sitting there.

Still overall pretty good restaurant would recommend.
author: Simon Beaubien

review_text:
Competent prata place, nothing stand out. Compared to the Leaf, i prefer the Leaf's egg prata, and complimentary curry. But prefer Prata house's kosong prata over the Leaf.

I'm quite biased towards the curry determining the quality of a prata place and
unfortunately their curry is more average, the chicken and fish curry here is more herbal. Also got their mutton curry, and it's quite nice, but is an extra cost side dish.

Egg prata ($2) is more fluffy than crispy, and the prata becomes abit like a fluffy bread, which is ok, quite average.

The cheese prata is also quite normal, the cheese inside becomes melted and ur eating dough covered cheese (which is great). It is not crispy and abit bready, so it's really quite average.

Migoreng is pretty good, but i wouldn't order it for one, as the oily, egg noodle flavour becomes abit much after about a quarter in.

Crispy plain prata ($1!!! wow) is quite good, slightly better than the Leaf. Inside it is fluffy and fine with a very lightly crisp outside compared to the Leaf's hard crisp and big chunky insides.

Also my teh O cup was straight up cracked and slowly dribbling a small puddle of tea on the table as my meal went on lol.
author: Cath Palug

review_text:
This shop existed for a long time. Used to be quite good but it no longer holds it’s uniqueness.

Teh tarik quite milky but still not bad.

Plain prata i have tasted much better ones from elsewhere.

Cheese prata doesnt have much cheese to it.

Mushroom cheese egg is huge but the prata is abit gelak.

I have decided to leave this place alone and visit my top 2 favourites instead.
author: Jason Deng

review_text: Tried both plain and egg version. Prata was super crispy and flaky outside while soft and fluffy inside. It was served very fresh, hot and not overly greasy. Service was also very great and prompt. Will definitely come back again.
author: ZZ

review_text:
Ordered a Teh O With Lemon, only 1 slice of lemon. 🤷‍♂️

Toast Box did better , at least can get 2-3 pieces of lemon. Even HDB coffee shop better.
author: jlky Loke

review_text:
I went only to try thier Kaya 🧈 toast.

Crunchy bread 🍞 toast was nice to try here.

Loved it .

Also ais coffee was good here.
author: Sharad Kumar

review_text: Always very good soft boiled eggs and very nice, thin and crispy toast. I love their set menu where butter is replaced by peanut butter: a tastier and healthier version of the classic kaya toast.
author: Mimo Eats

review_text:
This outlet is the lowest quality so far;
toast ordered arrived late (>15 mins) and customers arriving after me had their order arrived earlier.

And after my order arriving late, the toast came out untoasted; you can barely see the toast marks and the slices looked so clownishy bare. (ignore the two bites i took out of the left toast slice)

Tables are also cleared late, environment is pretty haphazard.
author: Chua Yi Fang

review_text: Yakun's food and drinks always got standard, but quite ex for such small cups. Silky barley nice too, but very watered down. Love their steamed bread, and their soft boiled eggs has very orange, healthy yolks. Passable service and depends on which outlet. Their own cherish app allows you to earn points for rebates on future purchases but so far we haven't earned enough points yet, despite patronising yakun quite often. Tables are small and area is cramped. This outlet also leaves piles of stuff around seating area, which is unsightly. Still four stars because food is tastier and place is brighter and cleaner than competitors in the same mall.
author: Joyce Lim

review_text:
Used to support OCK alot. Their taste has never dropped. Unfortunately a recent incident has put me off with this franchise.
In the curry puff was a strand of hair..I took photo and gave my feedback to the store. All I got was just stares and say its factory issue. I told them if they wanted the photo to report to their manager or office..they couldn't be bothered and said once I complain online it's done. So here I am . Sad customer experience ..
author: HiroM

review_text: nothing much to say. i can see her back name only “yayan” is rude when serving a customer. pls OCK thompson plaza take some action with your staff. pls. so many complaint already with your rude staff. tq
author: Melati White

review_text: Bought the deep fried chicken wing earlier this afternoon. The meat inside had this very strong blood smell and weird taste like as if its not cooked properly. Very disappointing!
author: Hui Ling Wong

review_text: My mom went today 17 March 2025 at around 10 am and asked the staff about chicken wings and was shouted at that wings only ready at 12 noon. I was rudely waved away by the same Chinese lady previously.
author: Wai ling Ho

review_text: I didn't have my glasses and I was looking for the price of a spring roll, I can't find it, and asked the staff.  She said prices are there, you can't see?  Wow what a rude reply, if she is attentive,  she should have seen me stood there for a few mins trying to look for the price myself.  I went on 6 Oct at about 3.45pm.
author: Lui

review_text: I always enjoy a meal at Boon Tong Kee and will definitely bring my guests from overseas here to try their famous chicken rice. I cant help but to realise that they use kampung chicken now and not the fat white chicken that it used to be, so the chicken meat is slightly tougher now. Nonetheless, it was still a good eat. Many of the other dishes we ordered were also nice. Service was prompt and nice. Friendly too. Helped us take photos with my guests.
author: Rex Tan

review_text:
We had a hearty lunch at Boon Tong Kee and loved how comforting everything tasted. The boiled chicken was tender and juicy with a light flavour that paired so well with the sauce. The crispy beancurd had a golden crust with soft tofu inside and the bai cai with gluten was fresh with a nice bite. The chicken rice tied everything together and made a simple but tasty base. A satisfying meal and great for sharing.

📸 Follow @ayaalan.foodie for more foodie reviews!
author: Ayaalan.foodie

review_text: Boon Tong Kee on Balestier Road offers a cozy, well‑served dining experience with attentive service and flavorful, well‑balanced chicken dishes that over all provide solid value for casual meals.
author: Theng Seng Tan

review_text:
Had a lovely delicious meal this evening at Boon Tong Kee restaurant in Balestier Rd  Long queue as usual but worth d queue. We Always go for the watt tan bee Hoon  hor fun- full of flavour n wok Hei - Has meat , prawns , liver, pigs stomach, sotong etc. The broth ( kwah) was laced with egg n so yummy tasty😀. We had a clean sweep of this dish- taste like Penang watt tan horfun  stye
The half chicken we ordered was tasty but meat slightly tough   The chicken skin was not fatty even though imported European chicken ( I guess). Generally boon tong kee steamed chicken was good/ we finished ever bit of it.👍
author: TPH

review_text: The poached chicken is good but the stir fry pig liver dish is really bad. The liver was marinated with a sweet and slightly savory sauce based on soya bean sauce, the sweetness totally altered the taste of liver. The liver was quickly fried in high heat, in the traditional Chinese way, but the chef either did not drain the oil from the liver before stir frying it with kailan, or he just dumped everything in oil at one go. You can see the residual oil on the plate after we finished the food. Don't order this dish.
author: Dora La

review_text:
Back after the revamp!

Tried the
- Nasi Lemak (green spiced boneless chicken)
- Nasi Lemak (classic fried chicken wing)
- Laksa with wanton skin
- Kaya Butter Toast
- Garlic bread
- Teh Siew Dai

PROS:
All were generally good and served hot, serving size big. The fried items were well fried and crispy / crunchy.
Toast, garlic bread were good. Teh was thick enough.

NEED TO IMPROVE:
the fried chicken seasoning and laksa gravy were too salty. Need to reduce salt by 30%. The laksa gravy before revamp was perfect, management should look into that!!
Teh Siew Dai was too sweet, also should reduce sugar by 20-30%.

Service:
Very fast service. Polite enough.

Environment: More tables now - can fit more people and spacious enough for my liking. One of my favourite places to chill.
author: linteoh

review_text:
Nasi Lemak is good, the begedil is very good!
Top up 1.50 for Hot/ Ice Drink and $0.70 for upsized of drinks!

Good lunch, very affordable at $7.70!

Will definitely eat again when I'm not monitoring my calories 🤣
author: Michelle Lu

review_text: Came with my colleagues and the new garlic butter bun was so savoury and comforting! I tried the Sambal Balado Nasi Lemak and the chilli was damn good 🌶️🔥. I also loved the Kopi-O Affogato — the coconut ice cream has real coconut bits and pairs perfectly with the Nanyang kopi-o. And it’s only $3.80! I’ll definitely be back to satisfy the cravings!
author: Pearly Teo

review_text: I love the friendliness with the staff. They patiently explain the meal set. The food is above average. Due to off peak, less people here, we can chill here.
author: Yi Lin Tan

review_text: Come here often. Love the food. Will keep coming back. Izuan was really good. He was patient and helped us with the ordering. Appreciate that he could help us in English. Thank you!
author: Shayna Wong

review_text: Loved their food here! I come here every time I crave for Indian food. Mango lassi is the best. And serve it quite fast too. Their chutney is the best I tasted as it suits my palate.I brought my pregnant friend here and she approves of all the food we ordered. The atmosphere is quite cozy as they have both indoor and outdoor dining. They serve alcohol as well.  The service staff has great attentiveness and takes good care of their clientele. Definitely one of Balestier’s best restaurant.
author: Camille

review_text:
Excellent North Indian food along Balestier Road.

Went for lunch - for food quality and level of service was excellent. The Bryani rice was done just right. Next came the meats - they were well cooked and marinated. The naans were also warm and fluffy when served. The spinach and cheese was my favourite - absolutely tasty with the right texture.

Highly recommended and I’ll be back for more! Thumbs up!
author: Ron Yang

review_text:
Amazing place with great ambiance,  the food was great for me. As a chinese with picky taste buds, this place is fantastic and the flavours were not overwhelming.
The food was very delicious and definitely beyond my expectations. The server here gives great recommendations and is very friendly and accommodating.

15/10 will return to try other dishes.
author: Xavier Tay (XaviTay)

review_text:
Our all time favourite got to be the tandoori lamb chops and butter chicken with a distinct smoky umami. Mutton bryani is also a delight with really tender chunks of meat in full flavoured spiced rice.

When i could not get food panda to confirm delivery for a really delayed order with no resolution, i called the restaurant and they immediately told me they will deliver it to my house themselves having prepared the food and waited for a rider for a very long time themselves too.

Great good even more amazing service.
author: Angela Lim

review_text: I absolutely loved this place! Everything was top-notch, the food was delicious, the ambience was warm and inviting - the interior? Beautiful! the team were just brilliant—total pros, but also the friendliest people you could ask for. Definitely coming back!
author: ELY M

review_text: First time here was 18 years ago. Nostalgic hehee. Curry puff $1.70. 2 for $3.20.
author: Lim Ray

review_text:
Truly is one of the best and unassuming curry puffs!

💰 got 2 for $3, as my wife and I bought this as a post lunch snack to eat on the way home.

The crust is super well layered and crispy, fillings were generous, and it was very warm still when we got it at around 1pm in the noon!

Manned by an old couple at those shops along the HDB block, I’m hoping the sales is enough for them to sustain a living and I will be back for more in future 👍🏻
author: YY

review_text:
Saw the high ratings and bought 2 chicken curry puff. Too oily, but seasoning was pretty decent.

Male owner only provides transparent bag without handle (probably expecting me to eat on the spot), which makes it difficult to carry home.
author: Mao Kun Goh

review_text: Tasty curry puff by an old couple. $1.50 per piece for 2 piece and above.
author: Alex Soo

review_text:
Superb curry puff! The dough was  almost crispy rather than crusty. Beautiful folds and perfect even after air-fried.
The sardine version was flavoursome with onions added and a touch of spiciness.
I would love a slice of egg to complete the experience, together with a cuppa. But for $1.30, nothing to complain.
author: MNG

review_text:
Super smooth soya bean curd.

I recall eating this at the Serangoon outlet 2 decades ago. Back then, I thought it was one of the best bean curds around.

After all these years, it was only recently that I chanced upon this outlet and I dare say N&B has upheld the standard.

5 stars for the soya bean curd. I haven’t tried anything else.

The dine in experience is pretty cramped and not very comfortable. It’s an eat and go kind of place.
author: C Lau

review_text:
Don’t buy takeaway beancurd
Spoons are cheap and can cut ur children’s lips

Bought takeaway tauhuey.

It’s yummy, definitely fresh and distinctively better than other soybean curds

Got cut by the sides of the spoon, $3 tauhuey but cheap spoon, not acceptable.

No one picks up the phone either, what’s the point of having a phone number?

Sorry I won’t come back again
author: Ming Jin Soo

review_text:
Went for the experience, left with curiosity satiated with no huge motivation to return.

Overall food was alright - beancurd was nice and smooth, milk was not grainy. Croissant is said to be made without egg and very little oil, and i can tell. Its served heated up and is nice and crispy but also tasted very healthy and a little dry. Tangyuan was quite chewy.

Disappointed that there seem to be no pie in sight, despite the storefront listing pie as an offering.

Pricier than huge chains but that's the literal price of supporting smaller shops, so no biggie! I can justify spending $4.90 on tangyuan and beancurd since gelato shops charge $6 and up for a singular ice cream scoop anyway.

Tangyuan beancurd with soymilk: $4.90
soyabean milk cold: $3.90
plain croissant: $3
author: mushroom soup

review_text:
WOW. This place is a gem and should be protected at all cost. Came across someone who recommended it on Reddit and decided to check it out since I was nearby.

I am a self professed soy bean fanatic and can’t believe this is my first time trying. The beancurd and soy milk here are extraordinary and one of the best in Singapore. Just pure and simple soy goodness with soy being the main lead and doing all the talking. 25% sugar level was perfect for my not so sweet tooth. Tried their apple croissant and I love it too.

The prices are slightly higher than your traditional hawker outlets but hey, they are using Canadian beans!!! I am more than happy and all for it when business uses good quality ingredients.

The old school vibe at N & B smack is just amazing and like a dream. You can see elderly couples and students enjoying healthy bowls of beancurd as their afternoon snack in this cosy little air conditioned shop.
author: TF

review_text: Small and cosy snack shop that serves soya bean and croissants. I enjoyed the Tang Yuan (peanut) in Soya Bean with Bean Curd. It was lovely. The staff was friendly. It's a little pricey but their stuff is fresh and they are not a chain, as far as I know. Can support if you're around the area.
author: Jason Ong

review_text:
After many times visiting this hawker centre (like Liu Bei visiting Zhuge Liang), I finally got to eat the turtle soup I used to have since young.

Originally a stall inside a nearby coffeeshop, my family has been patronising them for decades.

Other than the smaller servings (of course this is normal), I still love the claypot turtle soup and the yam rice that the owners prepare.

Wishing them good health so that we all can enjoy more years of such delicious food.
author: Alwin Woo

review_text: Soup damn tasty! Although price on the higgher side! Yam rice was generous with ingredients as well!
author: Louis (ahluu)

review_text:
I think their herbal chicken soup is done better than their turtle soup. Don't get me wrong, the turtle soup is decent, but far from great. It was light on the turtle meat, though they cooked it til it's soft, and the cartilage / joints were nice to chew on. However, the taste of the soup is too light, bordering on the blander side.

Not my favourite, but OK in a pinch. It's in a hawker centre, so don't expect an upscale ambience or anything. But they do close early, so maybe they do have a steady stream of customers.
author: Drew

review_text: If compare to Fu He Jalan Besar, this soup lack a bit richness. Turtle Meat wise is the same. But the chilli is very nice. Service also good help bring to ur table.
author: xinwei

review_text: Nowadays hard to find this traditional turtle soup stall, surprise to see it today! Try the $8 one, it was well boil and good portion. The soup fragrance stay for a long while. Highly recommend. The Chinese name is 国记山瑞。
author: Gregory Goh

review_text:
Eating there is ok, food is good and portion is reasonable.
But look at my takeaway for ginger fish rice $6.50
Did i just paid $5.50 for the rice? Joke!
No fish at all! Pathetic, my family member only got to eat rice and spring onion and ginger. Am i eating vegetarian? Worst than eating cai fan (at least cai fan i get to eat meat and vegetables)

My table is table number 4, reserved for 7 adults and 4 children at 5pm on 16 Nov.  We spent $176 on eating there and we took away just one box of ginger fish rice (luckily we only took away one item - enough of disappointment)
author: Cheryl Leong

review_text: Best zichar store. Food standard always good for big group or small family.
author: Yew Kong Ng

review_text: Tried the crab at Yi Jia – absolutely worth it. The crabs were big, fresh, and full of sweet, juicy meat. You can really taste the quality. The price was super reasonable for the portion and freshness. $88 for 2 and their have 9 free mantou and two free desserts. Definitely a hidden gem if you’re craving seafood without burning your wallet.
author: Bon Ang

review_text: Ordered salted egg butter crab the salted egg butter was nicely done and tasted very good with the juice and fresh crab. The fuyong egg was done well with softness and not oily
author: Shirleen Tay

review_text: Got tzechar for a weekday evening. Crowd was at an average . We ordered sweet and sour pork , sambal tapioca leaves and hotplate tofu. All of them were tasty and sweet n sour pork was still crispy when served. However hygiene on the other hand could be improved. Quite alot of flies were flying around too. Will come back to dabao though
author: Louis (ahluu)

review_text: La Pizzaiola is a secluded Italian restaurant nestled in a residential area. They have a wide variety of pastas, pizzas and other mains. Their cheese garlic foccacia is unlike other puffy breads, but rather a thin, almost pancake like dish full of gooey cheese and a delicious garlic flavour. The pizzas are well-sized, thin crust and have almost no oil on the underside. The carnivora meat pizza was full of succulent ham and tender chunks of meat, along with spicy and salty salami slices. The tangy sauce cut through the richness of the cheese and pizza. The diavola pizza was simple but well made, with spicy salami and rich cheese. Their homemade chilli flakes also packed a punch. The sausage and mushroom pasta, accompanied with a pink sauce, was fantastic. The pasta was cooked to a perfect al dente, and the pork sausage was juicy and full of flavour. The carbonara was very very creamy, and had no truffle oil flavours. The lasagna was also very well made, with layers of pasta and tender meat. However, the serving size for the carbonara and lasagna were a bit small. The desserts were all tasty and well-made. The tiramisu was the clear winner among the three we had, being creamy, sweet, slightly bitter and full of coffee flavour. They have a wide variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks, which were reasonably priced. Overall, this is a great place to come and eat authentic Italian food with good service.
author: Ashok Sankaran

review_text:
Food is really good and authentic Italian here. Love the pasta very savoury and good texture overall and you be hard pressed not to clear every drop of sauce which is very generous.
The pizza is good too and we went for the safe choice signature roasted beef. Crust is thin and beef is very tender. However it's quite difficult to serve will suggest better to cut evenly especially hard to cut through the beef.
Tiramisu is also nice and the beer is also surprisingly smooth and easy to drink. Price is slightly on the higher side and it's rather crowded for dinners.
author: Jack

review_text:
Ingredients were fresh, which were super important to me. Pizzas and pastas were great. Desserts were delicious.

Service was very good.

Weekday deals for seniors are available (do check if they are though).
author: Ann L

review_text: Went to La Pizzaiola at Jln Riang for lunch, trying their senior 1 for 1 deal, which is only valid for pasta n pizza n weekday lunch only. The wife ordered the seafood pasta n I, my favourite Hawaiian pizza ($24.90 n $23.90 respectively b4 ++). The pasta was good, with lots of seafood. The crust of the pizza was thin but not the crispy kind. The edge of the pizza has a nice chewiness. However, I wud prefer the toppings to b a little more intense in taste. We added chilli flaks, which was very spicy. Anyway, we were warned. I must say the pizza was rather big (cut into 8 slices) n the wife helped me with one n a half slices (her pasta's portion was not too large)  Finished off with a cup of cuppacino to share ($4.50). The cuppacino was sufficiently intense, tho not very big cup considering the price point. Overall, a filling meal n good value for money, with the 1 for 1 deal. Wud want to come again n next time wud try other pizza.
author: David Ng

review_text: Food is super delicious! Especially the pizza & TIRAMISU!! Red wine selections were also amazing! Totally recommend this place as service was also super excellent. Kudos to Laura & Natalie for the excellent service you provided! Will definitely be back again with or without CDC vouchers 🥰
author: Singapore Girl

review_text:
Have been to a few other popular Thai eateries and most of them are either too sweet or too salty for my taste. This taste quite authentic to me , plus the HDB setting gives a different feel to the food. Additional stars goes to the wide menu and they even have a special thai breakfast menu. The best part ......no gst and service charge!!
$25
author: c k

review_text:
Decent and authentic thai food.

Ordered set A which included kangkong, minced basil pork, tomyam soup and fried egg. Can share about 4 people for small eaters. Also ordered salted egg squid on top of that. But maybe should have added one more dish for sharing. Total was around $85 for 6 people, so around $14 per person.

Kangkong: Decent
Minced basil pork: Decent
⭐️ Tomyam soup: Everybody liked this. Asked for less spicy and still yum.
⭐️ Thai milk tea: This never goes wrong.
Salted egg squid: Not too salty so is good.
Fried egg: A bit too oily but still nice

Overall had a good meal. Not disappointed with the food or drinks. Very friendly service.
author: lean

review_text:
The most authentic Thai food experience!🤌🏻✨✨✨
Every dish was bursting with bold, rich flavors — absolutely delicious from the first bite to the last. Everything was so good that we literally cleared every plate. Truly one of the best Thai meals I’ve ever had. Highly recommended!🤌🏻✨
author: Ming Yi明宜

review_text: The restaurant was bright and not too cramp. Food was great, not too salty and not too oily. The pad thai and mamee tom yum were delicious. The fried rice portion was huge-very value for money. The green noodles was a little mild on the spice and flavour though, but still a rather good meal.
author: elizabeth goh

review_text:
Ran an errand nearby Serangoon broadway, decided to try out this place after looking at the recommendations by TikTok.

Ordered a couple of dishes, the best was the green curry with rice. Pork and century egg is a unique combination can try too.

Pad thai and Tom yum soup is not the best that I had.

However, given that the place is accepting CDC vouchers and the atmosphere is quite ok, you can still consider to visit to try out the food.
author: Zi Liang Ng (Zi Liang)

restaurant_name: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (Serangoon Road)
review_text:
First time trying this place after hearing about them for the longest time.
We came around 8pm and was able to get seats immediately.
They ran out of fillet so we went for their fish head instead.
Also ordered nai bai & har cheong gai.

The dishes came very fast & we were really delighted with how delicious the fish soup was! Love that it came with very generous serving of vegetables too & the lady came to top up our broth without us requesting.
The fish head was really meaty too paired with this delicious vinegar chilli it was perfect!

The nai bai dish although looks deceptively simple was very delicious too!
The only dish we felt was ok and could be better was the har cheong gai. Although it was piping hot and crispy it seem to lack a bit of the prawn paste flavor .

But all in all we had a wonderful dinner & will certainly look forward to coming back to try the other dishes
author: sok tuan t

restaurant_name: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (Serangoon Road)
review_text:
We were there for dinner on a weekday at 5.30pm. The place started to get crowded from 6pm. And was almost full by the time we finished our dinner.
Dishes were promptly served after ordering. The chilli prawns with tofu was flavorful and prawns were flesh. The steamboat had thick slices of fresh grouper, generous serving of spinach and yam. Soup was salty. There was unlimited soup topping up.
The meatball roll was served as chunky big pieces, fried in thick batter. A little too heavy to our liking. The dried squih with Kang Kong was normal, no wow factor.
Dinner was a little disappointing to us though the food pricing was good
author: Bian Lee

restaurant_name: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (Serangoon Road)
review_text:
The red grouper is super fresh—thick slices, no fishiness, tender enough to melt. Pre-fried taro and sweet cabbage in the pot, taro soaks up the broth, soft and fragrant. Soup’s sweet with a hint of white pepper, lovely.

Tofu Prawns: Silky Japanese tofu + big fresh prawns—bouncy! Rich sauce pairs great with rice.

Ha Zao (Prawn Fritters): Crispy outer, generous size, sweet and tasty with layered texture.

Not crowded at night, no queue. Worth a try!
author: Andy

restaurant_name: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (Serangoon Road)
review_text:
My favourite fish head steamboat in Singapore. Despite the cost of everything going up, this eatery has kept its prices largely unchanged. We went at 7pm on a Tuesday and there were parking lots available (though not many). The shop wasnt crowded and our food was served in under ten minutes.

The usual stuff I'd order include the grouper steamboat, prawn fritter, prawn paste chicken are still great. Since it was a relatively slow evening, the lady boss helped us with the soup refill which was super.

Highly recommended for folks who want a piping hot steamboat and chinese zichar fare
author: Gh Wu

restaurant_name: Tian Wai Tian Fish Head Steamboat (Serangoon Road)
review_text:
It is still going to be my go to for fish steamboat.

Their broth is fantastic.

Their zi char dishes good too.

Personal favourites are their fish steampot for sure, and their Har Cheong gai, oyster omelette
author: Ed T

review_text:
Had a very satisfying dining experience at Dian Xiao Er (NEX) recently. The restaurant has a warm, rustic Chinese village-style ambience that makes it comfortable for family meals and gatherings.

Their signature herbal roast duck is definitely the highlight — fragrant, tender, and well-marinated with a nice balance of herbs without being overpowering. The skin was slightly crisp and the meat remained juicy.

Besides the duck, the Chicken cooked with Marmite is highly recommended — rich, slightly sweet and savoury with a nice caramelised glaze that makes it very addictive. The Mongolian Pork Rib is another standout dish, tender and flavourful with a well-balanced sauce that goes perfectly with rice.

Service was attentive and efficient even during busy hours. Staff were polite and responsive, which made the experience more pleasant.

Overall, a reliable choice for Chinese comfort food in NEX.
author: Leonard Lim

review_text: Visited Dian Xiao Er outlet located at NEX yesterday. Wait time was about 15min due to weekend Dinner crowd. The sever offer us to take a sit inside while waiting for our table as there is about 4 group waiting infront of us. For family of 4 and we paid about $160 for the dinner. The menu offered many different variety of dishes, and we decided to try the signature herbal roast duck, which was absolutely delicious, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, but about 3 to 4 was really too much fat and unable to chew well. We also ordered the char siew wow really too fattening when we're chewing and kind of full of fat. Their soup was awesome and our children love it. The rest of the dishes was really great. Overall, the restaurant was clean and well-maintained, adding to the overall pleasant atmosphere lovely deco and cool environment. 😎 Definitely, we will visit them again.
author: Eileen

review_text: My family and I celebrated my Aunt's 80th Birthday. The food was scrumptious and full of flavour. I throughly enjoyed the  Roast Duck with dang gui Duck Roasted with Angelica Herb, Fish Maw Thick Soup with Crabmeat and Conpoy & Ee fu noodles. On the whole a very enjoyable meal.
author: Teoh Beng Eu

review_text: Never realy ate at Dian Xiao Er till now and boy was i missing out. The food is actually really nice! Service is generally good too. Didn't get pics of every dish but the Mongolian pork ribs were really nice. We also had some tofu dish and assam prawns which goes suoer well with rice. Will definitely be coming back
author: randall

review_text:
I was really impressed with the roasted duck here! The meat was tender, juicy, and perfectly roasted with a beautifully crisp skin. Easily one of the best dishes I’ve had at a Chinese restaurant.

The waiting time was only about 5 minutes, which was pleasantly surprising given the quality of the food. Ordering was also extremely smooth thanks to their fuss-free ordering system — quick, simple, and efficient.
author: Ling Low

review_text: the waitresses were really kind and attentive to my needs. the food was really good, and the set meals are exceptionally good in my opinion. the atmosphere is really good as the place looks new and very well maintained, not a single speak of dust can be seen. really a 150/100!!!!!
author: john doo

When I arrived, I was told the same. Having dined at the Geneo branch recently, I insisted on the a la carte menu as I knew it was available. It was eventually provided, but the staff member’s tone became noticeably rude.

When we ordered a small Yu Sheng, we were asked to upsize it to match our group size many times by the same staff. We reiterated that we preferred the small portion as we had ordered several other dishes. I really don’t understand the staff’s insistence to push the CNY menu.

The food was consistent with Putien’s usual standards. However, the persistent steering toward the CNY menu made the experience unpleasant. It gave us the impression that staff was incentivised to push the festive set menu at this outlet.

Given the poor service experience, we are unlikely to return to this branch.

review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience at Putien NEX on 23 February 2026 (Ren Ri, Day 7 of CNY).

I purchased a small yusheng portion stated to serve 4–6 pax, yet it contained only four pieces of abalone. For a festive dish during Chinese New Year, this is already below reasonable expectation. From a cultural standpoint, serving four pieces (an inauspicious number in Chinese culture) on such an occasion reflects a surprising lack of sensitivity from a Chinese restaurant.

When I approached the staff, I was told that I would need to purchase additional abalone as an add-on. There was no attempt to address the concern meaningfully.

The quality was equally disappointing. The abalone was tasteless, stale, and overcooked to the point of being rubbery. The entire yusheng lacked flavour despite the sauces and condiments added. It felt rushed and far below festive standards.

I have since emailed customer service which has left unanswered. I have also been unable to submit feedback via the website for the past two days as the form does not go through.

Overall, the experience fell far below expectations — not only in terms of food quality, but also customer service and post-purchase response. For a brand of this reputation and pricing, this is unacceptable.

With that said, being a long time customer of Putien, I will no longer patron this establishment.

review_text:
I wasn’t too excited when proposed with the option of having MOS burger for dinner, as prices for MOS were never wallet-friendly despite its fast food outlook, and food tasted, for a lack of a better word, dull.

To my great surprise, they offer a rather innovative menu with Singaporean-infused flavours such as chilli crab mantou and prawn soup nowadays, which is definitely a welcome change.

First impressions when the food arrived was that every single item was so well-packed (RIP environmentally-friendliness) and you can see where most of the expense went to.

Next, the chilli crab sauce and mantou puts many local eateries to shame. The sauce was on point and the mantou was so well-fried without the reused-oil taste. The prawn bisque was superb and tasted like a strange yet likeable mix of local hae mee broth and industrially available prawn bisque. Nevertheless, much better than any “lobster bisque” offerings from mid-tier restaurants here.

The chicken burger seemed to be MOS’ rendition of a nasi lemak burger, and it was very strange that they only allowed the ordering of matcha with the burger. But having been to Japan, that’s how they roll I guess. The matcha was actually decent to be honest, and many local cafes should take note, instead of serving sugared green tea milk as “matcha”.

All in all, I surprised myself by enjoying this meal a little too much. May order again soon.

review_text:
26 Jul 2025 update
Being a Chilli Crab Sauce connisuer has literally forced my hand at trying every fast food iteration of this local dish and I must say MB has got the taste and egginess of the sauce down right on par with LJS, edges out KFC for heat and trounced McD abysmal collab with Jumbo. However, MB will have to take a take back seat to LJS and KFC as these two have worked the sauce into proper meals and not just as a condiment for 4 mini mantous. MB could have done better like incorporate the CC sauce into their rice burger or just do the mantou burger bun but with yakiniku beef or anything fpr that matter. But nope, they got some prawn noodle turned into a burger which I didnt like the smell so I skipped that. I did dip my MB fried chicken into the CC sauce and it was nice - missed opportunity there.

Previous Review
Tried the new burger which they just launched this week and was quite disappointed, lack of sauce ensured that the Tsukune patty, beef yakiniku that were combined into one meal was dry, tasteless and overall quite sad. I had to use the plain white rice bun and meats to try and mop up whatever sauce that was on the wrapper tp get a semblance of taste. Also tried the spicy seaweed shaker fries and this is nothing like my fav McD ones. Even though the seasoning was abundant, they season it for you, but all I tasted was a somewhat salty BBQ taste with barely any trace of seaweed - missed opportunity as I actually quite like the chunkiness of the chips. Perhaps the only safe option of the day was having the comforting corn soup that npw features grains of corn at the bottom of the cup.

Oct 2024 Update
Decided to try Mos Burger again as I was craving teriyaki burger but Mac was way too crowded. To my surprise, front line staff service improved tremendously. The burger was pretty good too, while the meat was suitably coated with the sauce, the rice bun was nor. I had the fried chicken fillet and that was very nice, with a crisp crust and juicy inside. Finally the corn soup is the main reason why I keep coming back to Mos.

Got a reply from the GM of Yoshinoya SG on map. Very steady and gung-ho for a management to read a nobody's review like me, so this part really inspired and they gain a lot of respect from me. I'm so looking forward to visit them again at NEX very, very soon. 👍👍👍

Just came back from Japan and have a craving for Yoshinoya gyudon, decided to come here and have a try. These are my reviews.

Food: Definitely nowhere near Japan standard. But it is as good as it gets. Standard Yoshinoya style. Still passable and ok overall.

Service: Again definitely nowhere near level of Japan. Serving is very slow. If you are saying I'm not comparing apple to apple, let me tell you that in Japan, there's even lesser staff working in any yoshinoya branches, but they serve within 5 minutes, no matter what's your order and it's always full house over there.

Atmosphere: Very bad indeed. The reviews were true. What's going on with the Aircon? I'm basically sweating while eating. Clearing of used utensils are very slow too.

Final verdict: Got a lot to learn from Japans HQ operational SLA. Keep it up guys 👍
author: Ken Peh

review_text:

author: Brendan Leow

review_text:
Opted for a light dinner at Yoshinoya NEX and ordered their smallest portion. While the meat looked plain and bland at first glance, it was actually well-marinated with just the right balance of saltiness and flavor. However, the rice quality doesn’t quite match up to Sukiya’s standards.

Overall, it's a good option considering the price and pleasant dining environment.
author: K Tan

review_text:

What I liked most was that everything was quite affordable, making it a great place to enjoy a satisfying meal without spending too much.

review_text:
I visit this outlet regularly, and the food quality has always remained consistent. The salmon miso soup is a must-order every time! I also tried the Zermatt salted egg abalone — surprisingly tasty and definitely worth a try.

The staff here are always attentive and friendly, especially the aunties — shout out to them for their great service! I wouldn’t dare say it’s the best outlet in Singapore, but it’s definitely above average and one of my favorites.
author: Benjamin Chen

review_text:
Most not steady marketing in Singapore #1

Your marketing has been really inconsistent.

I understand that price increases are due to inflation — that’s fine.

But previously, the salmon sashimi used to come with 3 pieces. Then you changed it to 2 pieces, saying it would be “thicker.” In the end, the two pieces were still as thin as before, even after the price increase.

Then you introduced the 1-for-1 salmon promotion on Tuesdays, which I believe attracted quite a few customers. But after a few weeks, the same signboard was still there — only the day had changed. Many customers went on Tuesday and only realized after their meal that the promotion was no longer valid that day. Nice trick, by the way.

Now you’ve brought back another 1-for-1 offer, but with a tiny line at the bottom saying the bill must exceed $20 and somemore the sushi rice portion came with HALF portion.

Come on, Sushi Express. Be a bit more steady. Such a great food place, but it’s becoming disappointing because of these marketing tricks. Dont treat your customer like an idiot.

restaurant_name: Muslim Delights Malay Food and Noodles
review_text:
Tried Muslim Delights and really enjoyed it! The food portions are generous and definitely worth the price, which is quite reasonable. The stall has a nice, chill ambience, perfect if you come slightly after lunch hours when it’s not too crowded.

One small downside is that parking can be tricky since there are limited slots around the area, but if you’re willing to walk a little, it’s worth it for the good food. Overall, a great spot I’d recommend!
author: Shah

restaurant_name: Muslim Delights Malay Food and Noodles

Best Padang food in SG & the beef rendang maknyus. Tender, so soft it falls apart in your mouth and doesn't leave bits in between your teeth unlike other places. Plate cleaned in no time👍🏻

review_text: Absolutely woeful experience. I placed an order at 11am for delivery at 12:30pm...I know, it was xmas eve, might be a bit busy ... THAT'S WHY I PLACED THE ORDER 90 MINUTES EARLY!!! We duly waited for our 2 large pizzas and 2 portions of chicken wings, by 12:45 I couldn't find a phone number, so I walked round (it's only a 6 minute walk from where we wanted the delivery, which makes this story even worse), I walked in and asked, "Where is my delivery?" The guy took my phone number and then just said "another half hour" as if this is perfectly normal. By the way, that was not the delivery time, that was when it would be ready in store 1:20pm so delivery would actually be 1 hour late. Not good enough, not by a long shot. I told them to cancel, oh woe is me, apparently it will take 7 to 10 days to get your money back, about the same amount of time it takes these jokers to deliver a zza. Anyway, I cancelled, I videoed the episode for my safety and then walked next door to Pizza Hut and 13 minutes later was walking back to my office with 2 large pizzas and 2 portions of chicken wings. My lesson learned here is that Dominos staff are incapable of managing time and haven't a clue about customer service. I am afraid that from now on I am a confirmed Pizza Hut man.

Service is absolute. Good manners, fast service and warm people.  Love it.

Atmosphere wise, we sat outside after a rainy session and it was as cooling as it could be. The only downside are the flies flying around which i dont really fault the restaurant. The table is beside a small road which is beside a main road with cars and buses driving past.

In Summary, highly highly recommend. It is very popular with long lines.

review_text: Their curry fish head is superb! They don’t take reservations, but we were lucky to be given a VIP room for our group of six. It was a full house on a Saturday dinner, and almost every table was ordering their curry fish head. Dishes were served quite fast and arrived together, which made the meal even more enjoyable. Highly recommended!
author: PHENG

review_text: It’s our first visit and we love the fish head curry! It was lovely especially since we like ‘tau kee’ and there were plentiful. The chilled sweet sour pork was a twist from our usual tze char standard. But it was delicious with the mango and dragonfruit on top. Service staff were attentive and they were served with a smile!  We will be back for more!
author: Cheryl Sng

review_text:
We ordered their famous curry fish head and it absolutely lived up to the hype — rich, flavourful, and perfectly cooked. The taste was excellent and very satisfying.

The restaurant is pet-friendly (outdoor seating), which made the experience even better. Service was prompt, polite, and very accommodating. Would definitely return. 🐾
author: Phyll Czh

restaurant_name: Grain | Meals On Demand and Catering
review_text:
We engaged Grain for our church wedding lunch (~150 pax), and the entire experience was seamless from start to finish.

The delivery, set-up, and tear-down were all promptly coordinated and handled with professionalism, which took a huge load off our shoulders on an already busy day. Everything was on time, well organised, and ran smoothly in the background, exactly what you want for a wedding.

The food was a hit across the board. Our guests had only good things to say about the selection and the taste, and we received multiple compliments throughout the day. We also ordered two live stations; popiah and kueh pie tee, and they were incredibly popular with the crowd. The stations were constantly busy and added a fun, interactive element that our guests really enjoyed.

A special thank you to Seraphina, who was our coordinator throughout the entire process. She was consistently responsive, clear, and reassuring in her communication, and made coordination effortless from planning to execution. It was a real comfort knowing we were in such capable hands. Thank you for taking such good care of us and our event.
author: Benedict Ng

restaurant_name: Grain | Meals On Demand and Catering
review_text:
Feb 2026:
Repeat customer. Ordered for 45 pax for CNY. My guests love the delicious Chai Po Bee Tai Mak!! The chicken and prawn were wiped out very quickly. The Teochew Steamed Sea Bass tasted fresh and were definitely a great hit with the seniors. The 2 young men who set up and tear down were professional, friendly and polite. Perfect catering experience!

Dec 2025:
We’ve ordered Exclusive Christmas buffet for 40 pax. Portion was generous and everyone had more than 1 serving. Except for the mussels that was a little tough and chewy, the rest of the dishes were well-received. The salmon was especially delicious and was the first to be wiped out. Cream and all. The pasta was also very popular. Even one guest who don’t usually eats pasta commented that it was good. The log cake was so adorable and taste delicious too. Special mention to Joshua and Zhiyang who were in charge of our dinner tonight. Setup/teardown was fast and efficient and they are a warm and friendly duo. Overall a great catering experience and I will recommend them to my friends and family.
author: Calbee Cracker

restaurant_name: Grain | Meals On Demand and Catering
review_text: Catered for my daughter’s 18th birthday with no regrets! The service was great from the start. Sherlyn was very responsive and when she heard it was a birthday party, she even asked for the theme so they could try to match our decor and they even presented her with a gift! The service staff who did the set up, Solaris and ZY, were also highly commendable and very helpful. They communicated with me every step of the way! And of course the food was liked by everyone. Would definitely use them again, and recommend them!
author: Charmaine Kwan

restaurant_name: Grain | Meals On Demand and Catering
review_text: Awesome dishes from Grain for a teenager’s BD party. Loved all the dishes that we chose!! Although the dishes came in disposable containers but the presentation and colour of the dishes were exactly as shown on Grain’s menu! Does not only look appetising and full of colour, but tastes good too!! Would love to try the other dishes in their selection next round! Many thumbs up!
author: Deanna Chan

restaurant_name: Grain | Meals On Demand and Catering
review_text:
Ordered from Grain Weddings for my ROM to feed 35 pax, their menu is extensive and was a joy for me and my husband to choose from. After our order was confirmed, we received emails from Seraphina (their wedding sales rep) who followed up before the ROM on if there were any changes to the order to ensure all was ok before the actual day. On the actual day, we were in contact with their rep,Elvin- who is actually the driver + the set-up man for the buffet. He was a little delayed due to the heavy rain but thankfully managed to set up before our ceremony began.

Food was wonderful and delicious, we heard compliments from all our guests and truly the food is a good restaurant quality. I was so pleased and thankful the food was good as we were unable to try it beforehand. In particular the fish in cream sauce, mac&cheese and egg tarts were a crowd fave. The blue pea lavender tea was a bit too sweet imo. They provided ample plates and cups and their plates are a good quality- not flimsy plastic. It gave a more refined feel. There was also some  table decor (flowers in vases) which I appreciated.

After 2 hours, Elvin came back to collect the food and pack up. A very fuss-free experience and absolutely no regrets on having Grain be a part of my wedding/ROM. Would rate the food a 4.5/5
author: Megan Lee

This place is near Tai Seng MRT and it is convenient. It’s surrounded by pubs so be ready to inhale some smoke before you could step into the restaurant.
The place is coz with some floor seats. However it is not a conducive place to chit chat with lots of echo.
Food wise, it is vegetarian and you do get a very wide variety of food for a Korean vegetarian. And they are all very tasty. Do get them to introduce the dishes to you if it is your first time there.
author: Live2eaT

review_text:
No frills dining!! The food was great.

Sorry for the nondescript descriptions, but if you’re looking for vegan Korean food, then just come here. Bc this is Singapore and not Korea, but still some places do offer the cold water flasks, this place does not. They charge fifty cents for an iced water.

There’s also a dining limit of 1h15 mins if I remember correctly at peak dining periods.

The perilla noodle soup (perilla guksu) was comforting and very brothy. It had a good mix of noodle to ‘liao’ or vegetable ratio so that was much appreciated.

The kimchi pancake was also crispy and thin. Not too spicy too. The banchan was also great. The radish one is sweet, cucumber spicy and the lotus root the most balanced of all.

Thank you friends for the birthday meal treat!

No pictures of the steamed egg though. It was the best imo bc we all finished it 😭
author: megan

review_text: Delicious food and the service was great! We arrived tired and just close to 9pm on a Saturday and their service was very polite. Appreciate it!
author: VRC

review_text:
Authentic Korean Vegan Delight!

We had an amazing lunch today at this hidden gem of a Korean vegan restaurant. The place was spotlessly clean and the food quality was top-notch. Everything we tried tasted incredibly fresh, flavorful, and truly authentic.

The standouts from our meal:
•	Yubu Kkaennip Kimbap – Light, savory, and bursting with well-balanced flavors.
•	Dolsot Bibimbap – Served sizzling hot in a stone bowl, packed with perfectly cooked rice, veggies, and bold gochujang flavor.
•	Mandu Guksu – Comforting noodle soup with delicate dumplings—perfectly seasoned and so satisfying.
•	Yachae Jeon – Crispy, golden vegetable pancake that hit all the right notes.

Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for clean, healthy, and incredibly tasty vegan food. Definitely coming back!
author: Sivakumar M

review_text: Definitely can’t miss this if you are a vegan or vegetarian visiting Singapore. Service was very quick, food was extremely flavorful and there were so many options we wished we had bigger stomachs to try more. Being vegetarians, it gave us an opportunity to try many new Korean dishes, and if I’m ever in SG again I will definitely pay them a visit. Note that they can make most vegetarian dishes vegan on request.
