author: Danesia Lai

review_text:
I love it here!

The Kyushu Tonkotsu Ramen broth is flavourful, sashimi are thick and is a good match with the soya sauce and wasabi. Grilled salmon belly is the melt-in-the-mouth kind. The Pork Shabu broth is umami and the pork pieces are easy to eat.

The ice cream is creamy with the favourite evenly spread out. Crepe cake is a little bitter but has a tinge of refreshing sweetness, together with fine cream. Both are compatible with coffee.

Ambience very relaxing, and staff are so efficient and friendly. Nice to come here for lunch 😁
author: Sherlyn ONG

review_text: Fun and fulfilling experience with Kushi! The team were attentive and prompt in their service. For a buffet feast, food is pretty good and each of the sashimi cuts is thick and filling. Will come back again!
author: Kezzendra Quek

review_text: Positively very good Jap and Izakaya place. Menu is quite extensive. Had dinner with family, ordered ala carte although they had buffet option. The cooked food from appetizers to grilled choices, definitely done very well. Also had sashimi which taste fresh. Ordered some recommendations plus others (See pictures for some of stuff ordered). Staff is friendly and attentive.  Will come back again for sure.
author: William Ngoh

review_text:
Affordable Japanese food, especially:
- Daily Specials at 50% off!
- Everyday Lunch Sets that starts from $11.90++!

We enjoyed the tender shabu shabu meats, fresh sashimi and sushi, moist grilled salmon belly, comforting ramen and indulgent desserts!

They also have wide variety of sake to choose from! Coffee lovers can check out their exclusive Enliven crafted coffee!

Spacious and comfortable dining environment. They also have private rooms that can be booked with a minimum spend.

Kudos to the helpful staff and kind manager who gave a sticker book to my friends’ son. ☺️

📣Check out my IG/Lemon8/Tiktok @samlivestoeat for more detailed foodie reviews! 🥰
author: samlivestoeat

review_text: I had a really enjoyable dining experience. The food was fresh, well-presented, and full of authentic flavours — every dish we tried was thoughtfully prepared and satisfying. The cold brew is really enjoyable too. The atmosphere was cosy and welcoming, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a proper meal. Service was attentive and friendly without being intrusive by Summer and their staff. Overall, a lovely spot for quality Japanese food, and I would definitely return again.
author: Charmaine Lee

review_text:
I’ve been to the Hei Sushi outlet at Tai Seng several times, and while the food is acceptable, the service definitely could use improvement.

The variety of Japanese dishes is ok, and the food quality is consistent. Everything tastes average and well-prepared. However, it’s strange that they’re so stingy with the wasabi; for a Japanese restaurant, that’s quite unexpected.

What brings the experience down is the service. The same group of staff, mostly older ladies, have served me on multiple visits, and they’re not particularly friendly. There’s no greeting, no smile, and they seem more focused on assigning seats than welcoming customers. Even when the place is empty, you don’t get to choose your seat — which feels unnecessary.

Overall, the food is average, but the service lacks warmth. Honestly, I’ve met friendlier and more polite servers in coffee shops. A little smile and hospitality would go a long way in making the dining experience match the quality of the food.
Lastly this is the only halal Sushi outlet closest to my place, but I don't think I will come back here again.
author: AFY_NLH

review_text: I brought my friend here for the first time to this outlet because the food quality here is better to other. They patiently answered our questions and made great recommendations. Sushi is fresh and the tempura we ordered is not greasy and very well fried. Overall, a very pleasant dining experience.
author: Jumayah Sd

review_text: Used to enjoy coming here to eat occasionally. Miss the hot stone beef bowl but too bad it is no longer in the menu. The food tasted pretty bad, all the sushi has too much rice, especially the maki.. the genmai cha is bland too. The only thing that tasted nice is the chawanmushi and salmon roll. Not a fan of their service too as they are always in a rush even if the shop is quite empty, they simply serve us without saying anything when serving the food and taking the empty plates away, and rush us to “settle” the bill. Feel it is a bit rude. But still acceptable.. overall I feel this is such a disappointing experience. Will not come back again.
author: Sheep Monkey

review_text:
Have tried a few sushi places, and this one stands out for its consistent quality. There’s a good variety on the menu, and everything we tried was good. The sashimi was fresh, and the spicy chicken karaage wasn’t oily at all.

They have a wide selection, so there’s something for everyone. My mother-in-law and our kids really enjoyed the meal as well. The staff were friendly, and the overall dining experience was comfortable and relaxed.

Our kid accidentally spilled the noodle soup, and the staff ( wasn't able to get her name ) still came over to help clean up despite being busy. Really thankful for that.
author: Muhammad Halim

review_text: This is probably one of the worst Japanese establishment we had gone to. We went for lunch, and we tried a wide variety of food there, and we were overall very disappointed. Seems there is no foot traffic, and the staff did not seem motivated/interested. Although the ambiance seems nice in the pictures, the seating layout is odd, and the call button is also placed in the corner, allowing for only one person to reach.
author: Maya See

review_text:
Dear Management Team,
I am writing to complain about a service delay during my visit.
At approximately 5:10 pm, the food was already prepared and ready for steaming but was left unattended for about 20 minutes. The ground staff on duty continued to cover for the kitchen instead of addressing or escalating the issue, resulting in unnecessary waiting time.
Please review the CCTV footage at around 5:10 pm to verify this incident. This delay was avoidable and reflects poor coordination and service standards.
author: Jenson Nil

review_text:
Ordered a few dishes. The outstanding one was the spicy noodles. The rest were so so. We came here quite often, usually they have a complete menu but this round a few that we usually ordered regularly were sold out.
We love Din Tai Fung so we hope they will work to maintain their standard high.
author: Chim Mei

review_text:
My girl had DTF xiao long bao craving 😂 haven’t had for quite a while as she had been busy studying for exams 🙏🏻 it was fantastic! She absolutely loved it! 😍 Thanks DTF!

Managed to also sort out the BT app to get my birthday wings 😅 batter was light and not oily 👍🏻 yums!!

Perhaps both of us prefer the garlicky taste of 红油抄手 at another restaurant so the ones here didn’t quite give us the ‘oohh’ 😝 maybe can tweak the menu option to add garlic? 🫢
author: Liz

review_text: Love this branch of Din Tai Fung! Not so crowded and staff are super attentive and friendly. Of course food was yummy!
author: Jo-Anne Tay

review_text:
Ding Tai Fung at its HQ! Must try out it's standard here...  Was really packed despite it's a weekend afternoon!

We didn't have to wait to get our seats! Food was served pretty quickly.

Quality of food is undeniably consistent...Good quality!

Service was quick and here it seemed to be well staffed compared to some other outlets at times. Hot Chinese tea was regularly refilled without asking as compared to some other outlets.

Noise is a bit high for any decent chat. We were seated near the kitchen door which can be noisy and dangerous... Thus the stars.
author: Cool Dragon

review_text:
SCAM SHOP!!! STAY AWAY!!

They lure you in with a false sense that the food will be cheap with the price of nasi lemak.

But when you go & order cai fan style YOU WILL GET SCAM.

Ordered mee goreng with nuts , 1 chicken & 1 fish fillet & got charge $9.10.

TOTAL RIP OFF
author: ben ben

review_text: Seeing all the bad review. Mayb I’m lucky cos my experience with them is ok. Order the $2.90 set nasi lemak with chicken wing and add $0.10 for takeout. This price in a aircon mall I think is very cheap. Chicken wing is very nice. Nasi lemak rice so so but acceptable for this price. Next time will go order more chicken wing. Saw many pple eating there.
author: Teng Andrew

review_text: If you are looking for food that’s within the range of $2 plus and not very particular, this is the place to come. They have 3 sets and the Set A is only $2.90 and you have a chicken wing, egg and cucumber and not forgetting a good amount of rice. May look simple but it’s actually delicious. As the seating area is limited, you may have to wait or grab one for yourself fast once the other person leaves. All in all, as long can fill your stomach happy already. How often can you come across food that’s below $3 these days in Singapore? Unless food that’s good but little or expensive, could still accept but will not eat too often. Least you tried! Come here when you’re at Nex Serangoon.
author: Ivan Tan

review_text: I recently had an unpleasant experience with the Malay staff handling food takeaway. I understand that mornings can be busy, but I was taken aback by the rudeness. I'm sure it's not the first time you've dealt with a demanding crowd, but a simple acknowledgement and polite response would go a long way. Most customers, like myself, just want to order their food quickly and leave. I'd appreciate it if you could remind your staff to be more humble and courteous, as it's not too much to ask for respectful service. The numerous negative reviews about this place seem to echo my experience.
author: Elmi Nurfiqha

review_text:
DO NOT take the mixed vegetables and meat, as it is SUPER EXPENSIVE, unlike normal mixed rice stalls.

Don’t be cheated by the cheap set-meal posters — only the set meals are affordable; everything else is EXTREMELY RIDICULOUSLY EXPENSIVE.

I recently bought three dishes: char kway teow, sambal tempeh with bean curd, and red-sauce fried “meat” (but it tasted like fried vegetarian bean curd/chicken skin), and it cost me $8.10.

I was shocked at the price, and because of the long queue, I did not ask the cashier on the spot how the total was calculated.

The sambal tempeh was listed on top $2.00, and takeaway cost $0.10.
After reading the bad reviews, I believe the char kway teow was $2.50 and the fried vegetarian meat was $3.50 (can you believe it?).

I was too angry while eating the meal and did not take any photos.
RIDICULOUS PRICING. DO NOT BUY ANYTHING EXCEPT THE SET MEALS.
author: Rainie Fang

review_text: I ordered 4 sticks ala carte with the addition of rice (generous seaweed and pickles). I feel that the chicken taste better than pork, while the fried item (karaage) is abit cold. Overall still a very good bento with their variety and taste
author: PD

review_text: Always a long queue if you come after work hours. Still my go-to place to hit my protein intake.
author: Elo

review_text: I took 3 stick, shoyu karaage(1.70), chicken ball(1.70) & chicken with green pepper(1.60), total cost $5. All the food are cold. Taste so so. Suggest maybe they can add numbering on the food, make it easier to order. (Eg: order 1,3,8) instead of pointing which one/ took the wrong one/ reconfirming order. I saw a customer point to the pepper chicken but the staff took the one next to it.
author: Yee Yee

review_text: Tori Q has always been one of my favourite Japanese Yakitori stalls. Especially their chicken balls. Simply delicious
author: FF2030

review_text: Grilling meats on a stick till they are slightly charred to bring out out that smokey flavour while coating them in an umami rich teriyaki sauce is the perfect comfort food when you can't decide what to eat. Let the staff know to spam the sauce, seaweed and pickles on your rice for a sensory overload!
author: Jechtto

review_text:
Just order delivery from this outlet. Due to the high turnover, this is top tier McDonalds.

Also, due to the high volume of delivery orders, you would be very much taken for a ride if you order drive-through. Can go home and take a bath and your car will still be in line. Have kena a few times. Just sit back and relax at home while the food reaches you.

The fries stuff from this branch is good. Fries are well-salted like old days and not the super tamed version that you get nowadays. Had a surprisingly great quarter pounder, which actually felt like a real cheeseburger from the past, from this branch.
author: MH Tham

review_text: Best mcd fries in whole of sg. Always consistently giving HOT fries that’s crispy and so addictive. I love this outlet the most. Never an episode of soggy or cold fries!
author: P O

review_text:
If POSSIBLE, DO NOT ORDER FROM THIS OUTLET!
Our company had made big order of happy meals for children day but outlet cannot cater properly and short give 6 packet of happy meal fries. When checked and asked for them, staff argue instead of ensure that we get the correct quantity. Manager stepped in and same thing, argue!
We, customer will greedy for 6 packet of kid's fries or not? Come on! We just want school kids to have happy meal, not meal with missing fries!!

Have given this outlet 2nd chance yet attitude still same. The 1st bad encounter is I'm being refused grape/straw jam when I buy MCD breakfast. What is wrong??
author: jasrine Leekhaw

review_text:
Made an order through app for delivery, item was out of stock, and requested to cancel. They never delivered but still charged the amount. One month passed with phone and email, no refund was done still. Very bad service!!!!

______

Very quick drive through experience here. No queue at lunch time here and also quick to get the order. Payment counter was closed and paid at collection counter as well as collect the order.

Didn't really like the fries here. A bit dry but beside that Mcd as usual, I am lovin' it.
author: William Lu

review_text: Even the app shown delivery in 30 min when order, it stuck on the first step without moving more than 1 hour. Phone the Mac hotline, after 10 min people in charge of this store called over. Was told there are lot of pending order no rider picking them up when asked for estimation time can't provide it. When ask for solution was told I can cancel the order instead. What can I say? Waste my time... The reason I writing this is because this is not the first time I encountered this. Really disappointed on how thing are being handle.
author: Peter Teo

review_text: This is my go to pizzas especially when I'm expecting a large group of people. The dough is thin and the toppings are generous. I love how Angela & Anna accommodate to all my requests every time I ordered the pizzas.
author: Ash “Qurataq A'yun” Asmawi

review_text: Called in for takeaway. Ordered the Medium Combo for 5-6 pax, 2 medium pizza and bites platter for $51.8 which is super worth!! Will definitely order again!!
author: Peizhen Wang

review_text:
Read some good reviews so decided to order the pizzas(Double happiness set) for self pickup. However on reaching home, was disappointed to find both the pizzas we were given weren't the ones we ordered. Instead of the Super Meaty and BBQ chicken which we have ordered, we were given seafood Fantasy and sunshine Fantasy. The seafood pizza tasted ok but the Sunshine Fantasy had sliced hard boiled eggs in it and I really hated it, I think it tasted weird. My family didn't really like the boiled eggs in the pizza as well.

On top of that, we ordered fried chicken wings, and 4 out of the 5 wings were undercooked, the flesh was still pink  within and a couple of them, especially the bigger pieces were still bloody.

Fortunately, there was a chicken lasagna which I ordered and that I could eat. Even then it tasted just average and nothing special.

I hope the kitchen could get all the orders correct before they hand it over to the customers, otherwise it is very troublesome to bring both pizzas back to change for the right ones. I do not encourage the restaurant to let customers open and check the pizzas and to have them put back if it weren't theirs for it will be too unhygienic. Doing it right the first time should be the way to go.
author: FIVE-A-DAY

review_text:
Ordered the Lady Rose Pizza on the phone and self-collected it from the shop. Friendly owner.

Overall the pizza was okay, love the tomato base. The Lady Rose felt lacking in artichoke but the cheese was adequate.
author: Tarcisus Ho

review_text: Nice sunshine pizza. It was freshly made. The ingredients are suffice. I do prefer the dough to be thinner. It is more of asian-styled pizza rather than italian.
author: LANCE LEE

review_text: This is a hidden gem place. Wish not to tell anyone as I think it will be hard to get a reservation next time. Shark fins portion is really huge and delicious. Perking ducks is awesome and sweet and sour pork on ice?!? Did you hear that before? It was my first time trying this and the pork is still hot when served! Truly amazing experience and place. Private room is very spacious. A table for 10 people should not be an issues and there is 2 big tables! you can sing ktv if you want as well.
author: Jamie Sim

review_text: The dishes are so delicious with many of them unique and not seen in other restaurants before. There are many configurations of the rooms such that you can get your own private room to sing karaoke, perfect for a 20 pax gathering. The waitresses were so attentive and professional. The only knock on this place is that it's location is a little "ulu", otherwise it's amazing.
author: Jush Chen

review_text: Highly recommend - One of the best Chinese restaurants in town - fresh, value for money.   Deduct one star because it is at local area and not really new place - otherwise, everything is nice
author: Anita Yiu

review_text: The 避风港虾球is more than one big mouthful and is really delicious! The fishball with mushroom gave me a surprise, the fishball is extra extraordinary!
author: Angel Cheong

review_text:
Was craving for seafood porridge which lead me here. Was surprised by the unique dishes available. I absolutely love the ice sweet&sour pork and ordered twice.

The seafood porridge & soonhock  is 10/10 for me. Porridge comes in a big portion. Ingredients are very very fresh, It is so good I had to dabao home for round2!!

The best thing about the whole dinner is i didnt feel thirsty at all!  Thumbs up for this hidden gem. Must try!
author: hong ng

review_text:
Neighborhood food with VVIP treatment!🆘🆘🆘

Been to many turtle soup stall .

Nothing beats this Tai Seng ever so friendly Mr Gary Tan herbal soup .🍲

Was told to sit down and he shall deliver my orders . Was rather apprehensive 😬

Will he ?
Then my soups came …
Together, he provides tissues and bottled Martel - brandy ?
Omg 😳

Tell me which other coffee shop stall in Singapore provides u free tissue 👍👍👍

My first thought 💭
Will I get drunk 🤭

Now the climax .. it’s cheaper than TanSerSeng in Aljunied road and without the extra GST 💥and the snobbish atmosphere .

Revisit 311225 🆘

Revisited 30/1/26
Omg - vip treatment with upgrades !
Ordered small soup given a larger portion ,
Thank you Gary !🙏
author: OneLord XXX

review_text: Honestly one of if not the best turtle soup in Singapore. They're really the OG stall that has lasted the test of time. Been eating here for the last 20 years and it's still just as good. The owner might even share some martell with you to add a dash if flavor to your soup. Highly recommended place. The soup literally warms you up from the inside! Perfect on a cold cold day
author: randall

review_text:
amazing soups, nourishing but not overly heaty!

had the crocodile and turtle soup, not too thick/ strong so it was a great balance. crocodile soup is a little more on the savoury side whereas the turtle soup is more herbal .

friendly uncles working here as well! heard from my friend its a family owned business, definitely can support!!

will be back to try the other claypot dishes and other soups!
author: Puppji

review_text:
My Dad brought me to this place 30 years ago and during this 30 years I have tried many Turtles soups all over Singapore.

This one still THE BEST hands down!! Nothing comes close.
author: Leonard Lim

review_text: Very authentic taste and friendly boss. He will top up soup without additional charges.
author: Mike Low

review_text:
Pretty meh prawn noodles for the price you’re paying. But if you’re staying nearby, this is probably the best you’ll get in the area

Typical bowl will cost you $8 on average.
author: Casey Choo

review_text: Pretty good, didn’t have to wait long for seats and for the food. The prawn was a bit hard to peel off the shell though. Saw a lot of ppl eating their wuxiang too, will try it next time.
author: TW

review_text: Great bowl of prawn noodles with pork ribs. Generous portion of protein but comes with a price of $15. Broth was not too strong in flavour (went in the afternoon) but still contains umami flavours from the prawn. Noodles is slightly on the sweet side which is towards my preference but some people may not like it.
author: Siah Rui Heng

review_text: Brought 2 friend from Britain to try this. They both like it a lot. Finish the whole bowl. The pictures and numbers on the wall made it very easy for them to understand what they will get. (Picture not just for reference. They did come out like that) the range of variety was also very pleasing. Ngor Hoong went very well with the noodle. The dip sauce, however, seem to be more to us the local’s liking. Staff also help us open the table outside to accommodate 5 of us.
author: Liwei Chiang

review_text:
Best option to be number 1, $9 add prawn.

Soup refillable!  Super recommended!

Unlike other famous prawn mee stall that is shitty, non refillable soup, super tiny prawn.

This deserve more good ratings!
author: WEI HAO

restaurant_name: Guan Chee Hong Kong Roasted Duck
review_text: The atmosphere can be quite busy due to its location in the center of the mall, but everything is well organized and tidy. The food perfectly suits my palate, which is rare, as I often find it difficult to discover authentic flavors as an Indonesian  I would rate the food 10/10. The service is excellentbevery staff member was genuinely friendly and professional. I was especially impressed with the level of security  I had accidentally left my ATM card behind and when I returned the manager had kept it safe and personally returned it to me. I truly appreciate their honesty and professionalism Thank you so much🤍
author: Putu Dessi

restaurant_name: Guan Chee Hong Kong Roasted Duck
review_text: Guan Chee have a few outlets around. I have ate at 4 of their other outlets. The only outlet that excites my tastebuds is the one at 106 Hougang … you won’t be disappointed here I feel. Meats are roasted in store. 👍🏻
author: Captures Immortal

restaurant_name: Guan Chee Hong Kong Roasted Duck
review_text: Serving staff was very helpful and polite. Generally the roast duck and pork are ok. Chilli sauce can be improved to be stronger in taste and thicker. Easy choice for any meals if you are nearby to eat.
author: Lim Frederick

restaurant_name: Guan Chee Hong Kong Roasted Duck
review_text: Really good roast duck in Hougang! The skin of the duck was crispy, the roast pork was pretty good as well! Pricing is also as usual, same price you would get duck rice anywhere else. Overall, would recommend for anyone living not too far from it.
author: Wilfred Loy Yong Kang

restaurant_name: Guan Chee Hong Kong Roasted Duck
review_text: The char siew was very tasty it is definitely a must-try! The food was affordable and they gave a large portion of meat. The service was fast, we got the food within 2 minutes.
author: Yve Tan

review_text:
Yes, this place had lived beyond it's commercially useful life ...aged equipment n facilities...

However, the roast pork which I tapau, was still cracking crunchy..

One piece was badly charred n yet the guy still have the guts to put into my box.

This worth's my visit there as a secondary place.

Primarily, I was there because of the popular HK cafe with nice dim sum a few doors away
author: David Wong

review_text:
This shop really feels like it’s past its prime. The food was honestly quite meh — the meats lacked depth and flavour, and the noodles were overcooked and mushy.

What bothered me more was the state of the kitchen. From what’s visible from the seating area, it looks cluttered, messy, and not very clean. The floor was wet, equipment looked worn out, and overall hygiene didn’t seem properly maintained.

Plenty of better options around nowadays. Wouldn’t return.
author: Chuckie Siow

review_text:
Food is mediocre, like any other random roast meat stall.
Environment is very dirty.
Saw the staff using hands to handle cash and getting hard boiled eggs from the fridge to put into the simmer to coat the egg with the sauce.
author: max

review_text:
Had a super delicious char Siew rice lunch at Kay Lee roast meat.
Just $5.80 for one serving.
And the meat has caramel smokey flavor and rice portion is generous.
Meat cut could be more pleasing to the eye, but no complains.
Taste just as good from last visit more than 5 yrs ago.
Quality and taste is maintained.
Highly recommended.
author: K Tan

review_text:
It's been a while since I had the Char Siew and Roasted Pork at Kay Lee. The place is quieter now, but the food remains tasty. The char siew has a balanced fat-to-meat ratio.
The roast pork's skin is fragrant, crisp, and crunchy.
Bitter gourd soup pairs well with the roast meats.
author: ERIC CHAN

review_text:
Take note that they have shifted to the condo opposite the old stall.

Service
Friendly and accommodating, will oblige to requests.

Value
Ordered the $7 plain pork rib selection.  What I got was just that, afew pieces of pork ribs with noodles and nothing else. Not exactly good value.

Taste
There were not a lot of the pork lard/shallot/garlic topping that many prawn noodles stalls provide. For me, taste -wise, did not make the cut. The soup that came with it was a tad too peppery for me and if refill is wanted, it’ll cost $1 which I obviously wouldn’t want to pay for it.

Conclusion
Not likely to return anytime soon.
author: Eric Lee

review_text:
The google pic is misleading. They are actually moved to opposite the road and is now air-con. Refer to picture for the correct location.

Ordered pork rib big prawn noodle big for $12. First impression was it was just okay. Noodle was slightly over cooked and lack that al dente. Taste wise it gotten better with the oiliness, chili wasn't anything special and i have to add quite a bit of the chili powder. It is really more on the savory side and pairing with soup might not enhance the taste so don't need to soup dip it.

Speaking of soup it was average. I always feel that the decision not to add prawn into the soup for dry prawn noodle is questionable. Soup was indeed average. So in the prawn goes. I beheaded some in the soup while others in the noodle to spread the prawn paste. Head was later added back into the soup.

Prawn was suprisingly easy to deshell but another issue i have with stall that don't half or devein their prawn is the intestine are still inside. But at least the prawns are great. Sweet, firm and fresh.

Pork rib is more of a miss, pretty tough while it taste porky some might be turn off by it. Personally i feel that it is inconsistent. Some pieces was alright but one was too strong.

On another note, the place is quite dirty. I know they absorb gst etc but they really should wipe the table, most of the table are stained to a degree with spilled coffee on the floor.
author: Super Fragrance

review_text:
Flavorful brooth, not too oily but weak prawn taste, and no thin bee hoon in selection.
Pork slices are super hard, small prawns are super small. Pig tail is pretty good and soft.
Noodles a little hard and undercooked.
Starts at $8, serving size slightly lesser than hawker stall norm.
The use of mini prawn looks awful and weird, iust limit to a few slices of normal sized  prawn feels better.
Taste: okay
Value: Nah
author: A T

review_text: Located opposite of the old kopitiam it used to be at 3 years ago, the eatery includes prawn noodles and 5 spice (五香) bites to order from. Ordered dried version. The white beehoon is of the thicker type, but works well with the yellow noodles. Hits the right spot for me. Enjoyed the bowl and the soup. Very nice.
author: WilsonW

review_text:
It’s been a while since I last had Hoe Nam prawn noodles back at their old location across the street. Their new outlet at The Venue shoppes is now air-conditioned, offering a more comfortable dining environment. The ladies taking orders are polite and friendly, which adds to the pleasant experience.

Portions are decent, though I find the taste rather average. The soup leans more towards a porky flavor than the rich prawn broth I was hoping for. Overall, it’s still a decent spot to satisfy the occasional prawn noodle craving, but not one I’d go out of my way for.
author: K Tan

restaurant_name: Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert 順發冷熱清湯
review_text: We wanted to buy cold desserts but the stall owners said they were all not available. We chose a hot dessert but the stall owners again said that it’s not available, only the ones in display are. So we chose an item on display and during payment, the stall owners charged us more than what was stated on the menu. We asked why and they said adding a little more coconut is chargeable. The stall owners were not friendly and understanding even though we wanted to just find out the reason. They started bickering. It was unpleasant to buy from these stall owners.
author: Dione Goh

restaurant_name: Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert 順發冷熱清湯
review_text:
11/November/2025
Had hot red bean soup ($1.70) for snack. Not overly sweet, soup was lukewarm.
author: T greensake

restaurant_name: Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert 順發冷熱清湯
review_text:
Honey Sea Coconut And Nata De Coco (SGD $3) @ Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert.
.
This humble stall has been operating even before 2012, with locals returning time and again for their tasty desserts, friendly service, and affordable pricing.
.
Their rendition has slippery smooth honey sea coconut with a slight bite, springy nata de coco / coconut water jelly cubes, and juicy longan, paired with some calamansi lime juice over fine shaved ice.
.
Carries lovely honeyed floral earthy fruity zesty sour sweet flavour, yum.
.
Ice Jelly Fruit Cocktail (SGD $3.50) @ Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert.
.
Their version differs more than any other, with the fig seed gel (derived from the seeds of the awkeotsang creeping fig) moulded into an accordian-shape rather than the traditional slices.
.
This wobbly aiyu jelly is then placed over, rather than under, the smooth shaved ice, drizzled with lime juice and a simple sugar syrup. The juicy diced fruit cocktail (pear, pineapple, peach, cherry, green grapes, nata de coco) sits around it.
.
Carries enticing honeyed earthy floral fruity sweet sour zesty tangy flavour, yummy.
author: Ivan Teh

restaurant_name: Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert 順發冷熱清湯
review_text: Cheng Tyng syrup taste like plain water.  Ice is coarse.  More red jelly than any other ingredients.
author: R Ho

restaurant_name: Soon Huat Cold & Hot Dessert 順發冷熱清湯
review_text: Wide variety of dessert. Good quality too. Value for money !
author: WT Wong

review_text: food is delicious & very reasonable, highly recommended. the best among the best
author: Mohd Dzaimy Yosof

review_text:
This is the place where you can enjoy kampung  style food with affordable price. Little bit of "thai " taste also available.  Plenty of seats available

Aunty is very nice tho, gave me the rice for free

author: Yizhou Wu

review_text:
Si Chuan Xiao Chu is a newly opened restaurant that offers authentic chinese dishes at very reasonable prices. Vegetable dishes are typically priced around 6–8, while meat dishes range from 8–12, making it a good option for casual dining with friends and family.

The flavours are impressive and taste quite authentic. One thing to note is that the dishes can be slightly oily, which is quite common for Sichuan cooking. If you prefer lighter flavours, it would be a good idea to request less oil when ordering, as the chef tends to be quite generous with it.

Overall, this is a promising addition to the quiet canteen.
author: Tan Ee Fhong

review_text:
I don’t stay near Hall9 but order Cates on a daily basis. Can9 food forms at least half of my Cates order.

Lan la mian is as good as JP’s she jian jian, half the price w premium quality soup base and beef. Must try pickled vege soup, so heavenly good.

Jiang Lai’s lamb rice, bbq and potato chicken are incredible, not just the taste, but also the meat used. I can taste its quality and freshness.

Chun Jiao Luo Si fen serves authentic luo si fen. What a pity it doesnt accept Cates order any more.

review_text:
I have tried this place multiple times and honestly NEVER AGAIN.  The first time I tried at around 8pm where we ordered plain prata. it took 30 min for my 4 plain prata to be ready, and it was COLD. The wait is always insane, even if the restaurant is empty.

Once, I ordered on Cates for pickup. The restaurant accepted the order and took my money, and when i went to check if it was the ready, the man at the counter simply said "no cates" and refused to answer any other questions. I had to cancel it on cates myself and the only refund I could get was in cates credits. review_text:

The taste of the soup is not as tasty as YGF and Zhang Liang. But maybe it is more healthy and sinful. If it is really so, can explain in a poster so we know the lack of  taste is indeed compensated by healthier ingredients.

The deep fried lotus roots is quite new concept but not well implemented as it is not crispy.

The parking is also more expensive than most malls and downtown @> $2.40 per hour.

The loud music likely is meant for noisy lunch crowd. But today is quite a quiet afternoon since it is Dec 30.

Should pay more attention to small flies. Spotted them on the vegetables near the top shelf. I did avoid those vegetables.

The staff were quite friendly and very very united. Saw them having a nice meal together. Like this homely spirit between the staff.

review_text: Overall quality is poorer compared to ygf, zl and gy. Even pricier than the more well known brands and the soup base is not as nice. Additional price for soup base unlike other brands. The supposed highlight - fried luncheon and potato slices were not well executed and overly soggy with a lot of oil. Felt like they should have left it frying for a while more. review_text:
Had been ordering from them these years (though not regularly). Two weeks ago, due to schedule I had to cancel my order (only one dish) as it was taking too long and the food was not prepared yet.

The cashier was upset which I understand as she had to do a refund. I apologised to her a few times for the inconveniences.

Today I went back and before I told them my order, they immediately informed me if I cannot wait, this time they would not refund me. I asked about the waiting time and was told it was about 25mins. As I am not in a rush this time, I proceeded with the order. Eventually the wait was only less than 15mins.

I am not sure if the 25mins was to manage my expectations (due to what happened two weeks ago) or to discourage me from ordering. However, the front staff attitude was rather rude and hostile. Out of the many times over the years, that was the only time I had to cancel my order, and they "remember"!!

Definitely an unpleasant experience.

Their duck meat is braised nicely, tender in texture, quantity is ample, and the thick gravy that coats the noodles simply delicious. Throw in a lu dan (marinated egg) and dou gan (marinated tofu with a firm texture) and you have the makings of a satisfying lunch.

He told me that it is not possible and came up with some logic I still don’t understand. He told me like McDonald’s like that - “you order this set meal, where got can change one item to the other set meal?”

If the duck is said to be the main, and the rice is the side, then McDonald’s allows me to change to many different sides. Not to mention that McDonald’s and an apparent struggling coffee shop store have almost nothing in common.

Other stalls serving braised duck OR kway chap allow for you to order just a kway chap (but duck) set and vice versa. Not sure why this stall wants to have a god-complex and think that it’s utterly absurd customers make simple requests in polite manners.

Either way, this coffeeshop has aplenty of better choices to patronise. Perhaps that’s why there’s no business for this stall.

Korean food is a good start. Tasty, and super reasonably priced.

review_text:
Na Oh offers a 4-course prix fixe seasonal menu $78++ for a set which includes 2 appetisers and a jinjitsang (진짓상), well as a variety of banchans (반찬). The appetisers and banchans are the same across all sets , you only need to choose the jinjitsang.

For the appetisers we had the
- Jeon platter.
Squash, mountain yam and sablefish coated with maesaengi seaweed.
- Acorn jelly and beef tendon salad in icy kimchi broth

Main No.1
Grilled Jeju Beltfish with Golden Queen’s Rice
Spicy Winter Seafood Stew with Pollock Roe and Cod Milt
Yuja and Cabbage Saengchae, Bellflower Root Muchim

Main No 2.
Galbijjim Finished Over Charcoal
Hanbang-Style Beef Short Ribs Braised in Aged Soy Sauce
Chestnut and Thistle Sotbap, Maesil Dongchimi

The beltfish was nicely grilled , still moist on the inside and the best part, its boneless. The broth of the seafood stew was made from the fish bones and wasn't that spicy. Super love the Pollock Roe and milt which is a winter delicacy. No comments on the beef cos I didnt get to try it but the chestnut and thistle sotbap that came with it was pretty interesting, the server will add the beef broth to the rice pot and u get nice pao fan after 15 mins.

We ended off our meal with a refreshing pear sorbet and an Injeolmi Cake loaded with candied nuts and seeds. I was wondering where's the Injeolmi, turns out its INSIDE the cake. I don't usually fancy desserts but this has the right amount of sweetness and the nuts and injeolmi provided different texture when eaten together.

review_text: Managed to book this place for lunch 1 month ahead and it is indeed a good experience. The food is fine and tasty. We had the winter set and I chose the beef while my friends had the pork and fish. The banchan were delightful and the taste is not overwhelming, preserving our taste buds for the mains. The beef was tender and well marinated without being too powerful. A worthwhile experience that can be repeated with their changing season menu
author: Patty Palmer

review_text:
Dinner at Na Oh was such a good one — modern Korean set menu, but executed with real finesse.

We ordered the pork + crabmeat soup set and the fish & seafood soup set, and both were excellent. The fish was super tender and not fishy at all, and the seafood soup came with big, plump cockles which made it feel really generous. The crabmeat soup was thick, rich and so flavourful — perfect with rice. The pork was also done really well: savoury, comforting, and just… satisfying.

The jeon pancakes were nicely pan-fried and not oily, and the Cameo makgeolli was slightly sweet and really refreshing.

Big shoutout to the cake dessert — mixed grains and nuts with this caramel-y chewy centre. Honestly soooo good. Service was also amazing, proper fine-dining level.

review_text:

Tulang Merah Power($10)(4pcs)

The main highlight in this dish is the soft, melt in the mouth bone marrow inside the bone.
There are several ways to eat this dish with Hands of course.🤗
- Sucking the great essence out of the bone.
- Knocking the bone with impact onto a hard surface or with enough force to let the bone marrow slide out on its own.
- Use the back end of the spoon to scrape it out.
- Use a straw if you have to suck it up.
Overall, is a tastisfying dish but if the meat(not the main point) can be more tender will be great.
4 pcs is just too little to satisfy my crave.😬
.
Next up, all time comfort food, Maggi Goreng($5.50), which is stir fry with diced vegetables and minced mutton. Decent soft noodles with the right balance of spicy and savoury. Just lacking a fried egg here.🤭 Otherwise, all izz well.

review_text: this coffee shop is not bad, just the 菜饭 stall really cannot make it. the portion of the meat lesser than other stall but yet the price still charge the same.
author: sean ong

review_text:
This was a disappointing experience compared to other cze char stalls in Singapore. The food arrived lukewarm and lacked the freshness typically expected from dishes cooked to order. The flavors were rather underwhelming as well. Definitely not worth the price.

I wouldn’t suggest making a special trip here unless there are no other options available.
author: Ken Tay

review_text:
Hua Long Fishhead Steam Boat
ZiChar Restaurant is a vibrant neighbourhood gem that serves outstanding and mouth-watering dishes. A highlight is the Steamboat, paired with a whole Red Grouper for around $60, offering an incredibly rich broth and delectable Mince Meat Tofu with rice. The perfectly cooked Kang Kong and tender sweet and sour pork further elevate the experience. Notably, Ms Ah Bao's exceptional service at this local eatery shines through.
Many thanks to the kitchen Chef and the service personnel for the great food and service
author: Stephen Lim

review_text: Don't recommend the mix veg stall! They are very stingy, give you very less and charge so much.  1 chicken and just a few pcs of  brocolli , $5. Do take note the zhi zar don't return change for those using CDC voucher
author: vin takahashi

review_text: Generous serving of free chicken with my prata order! 👍👍👍
author: Stephant S (stephant_s)

review_text: Good price, generous portions, and great taste - would come again
author: Sina Mueller

review_text: Sugar and salt don't know difference m🖕🏻
author: AMV Loveline Kingline

review_text:
The chicken rice place to go to, when out in the west.

Good portion. And good price, especially if you get the veggie set. They do sometimes run out of veggies, so do go early.

It's in a coffee shop, no aircon, decent fans, clean. And with a smoking section. Hdb multi storey parking beside.

Also, closed on Mondays (more a note-to-self)..
author: Potentry

review_text:
amazing food, beehoon perfectly seasoned. sides freshly fried, chicken very crispy and hot. spring roll is one of my favourites! crispy and delicious.

actually one of the best beehoon stores in singapore.
author: kennis huang

review_text:
The place seems to be only selling bee hoon and rojak these days instead of satay. No idea since when they stopped selling the satay.

The bee hoon and fried toppings are...typical neighborhood food court bee hoon stall which I visit only when I occasionally crave fried stuff. The sambal is pretty nice though, with smooth consistency and right acidity.
author: lontongstroong

review_text:
Damn good , beehoon so fragrant and price of the food is considered decent priced.

Recommend to come !!
author: Cursedxian ツ

review_text:
Went yesterday at about 6.20pm for takeaway. The Beehoon was super duper salty, as well as the TauKwa. We didn't appreciate cutting up the Taukwa before frying, if I had known this before hand, would have stopped him.  Total cost for 2 pcs twakwa 1 long fishcake, 1 ngoh hiang,  fishballs n 2 pkts beehoon cost $8.20. The husband paid $10. Did not check change of 80cents until we got home.  Too much of a hassle to drive back for the dollar.

The stall was only managed by a young couple, and both were multi-tasking with the heaps of orders and multiple menus.  On top of frying, cutting, costing of the ngoh hiang stuff, he also had to grill satays and taking care of the sides..all at the expense of the waiting patrons.

Not impress.  Not worth the drive.  Not going back.
author: G Y

review_text: The owner is very kind. He always gave us lots of Bee Hoon and it's super delicious. Their fried stuff are awesome as well!
author: Anne Anne

review_text:
Damn bad. Waited for 30mins for 3 simple dishes. When all my food was ready, they were just sitting there at the counter. The guy in charge of serving glanced at it and went on to take rice to cook. I looked at him and my food, he didn't even have the awareness and went off. Asked another lady and she confirmed that they were all mine. After so long, order was still missing an egg. Super poor system.

Beehoon soup was bland. I'm not picky but trust me when I say it was like water. We had to add all sorts of seasoning at home but it was still just bland. Soy sauce with the chilli was also super diluted. No I'm definitely not exaggerating. Other dishes were meh and this is the last time ordering
author: Ng Wei Jiang

review_text: This place serves Chinese cooked food (locally called 煮炒) and it isn't impressive. My family ordered, amongst other dishes, a 1.3kg steamed fish ($70) that tasted stale, a plate of stir-fried baby kai lan which was undercooked, and marmite pork ribs that were just horrible. Service was slow, servers were pushy and wanted to get you to order everything. Overall, it wasn't a good experience here.
author: Jeslyn Lim

review_text: Spent $6 for a salted fish fried rice. Initially was $5.50 but I wanted red chilli to be fried along hence have to pay an additional $0.50 for red chilli. Food was done and was not informed even though I was sitting in the middle of coffeeshop. Taste is average definitely not a $6 worthy fried rice.
author: low weijie

review_text:
Ordered 1 plate of beehoon and waited for 20 mins plus. Other customer that ordered later was served first yet I'm still waiting. When I went over to ask, the service lady told me with a very impatient tone, "now cooking, cannot wait ah." This is very rude. Regardless, food is so so only.

Not recommended unless you have a lot of time to wait.
author: Jackie Foong

review_text: Was collecting GrabFood order, it took a horrendous 1 hour just for them to prepare the food. Bad experience. Other GrabFood riders also waited for almost 1 and half hour for their order as well. When promted, they say there's alot of order, well that's isn't the deliveryman's problem. The cook can still went out for a smoke break in the midst of preparing the food order!
author: Nrl Asyxqxn

review_text:
Had the Spookuloos Potion (less sweet, with oatside oat milk) at their Curbside Crafters pop-up, and it was the best flavoured matcha drink I’ve had! Will definitely be back. Hoping they’d do a pop-up in the east at some point! :D

PS: Owners (Two Goose) were super sweet and friendly too! Thank you so much for this amazing experience and drink!
author: Phyllis Chua

review_text:
Got 3 drink from them. Matcha latte, Hojicha latte and Uniquely Singaporean (MiloXMatcha). I am not a matcha fan, I was looking for a matcha fix for my cousin that’s was visiting from abroad and is a mad matcha fan. FYI, I got these drink in less sweet and with oat milk too!

Quick summary:(my opinion as not a matcha lover, taste wise)

Matcha latte: 3/5⭐️
Taste like any other matcha beverage but somehow you can taste the slightly more premium matcha taste compared to St*rbucks (👎) But according to my cousin this drink did it’s job perfectly and actually got her matcha craving fixed.

Hojicha latte: 5/5⭐️
Had never tasted Hojicha so i had no expectations. KID YOU NOT, I finish the drink within 2 minutes cause IT WAS DELICIOUS 💯💯 definitely tempted to get more after I finished this one.

Uniquely Singaporean: 4/5⭐️
Mainly was just curious honestly. Weirdly it actually compliments each other. First sip, you will taste the milo which makes it familiar and the aftertaste hits you with the matcha taste.

Honestly they should be expecting more orders from me cause now even without my cousin’s craving I might just come back for the Hojicha Latte. Price-wise perfect,it’s definitely affordable for it’s quality. Location-wise perfect for me too cause I live at the west side. Altho the BEST PART is the service. Obviously cause my cousin came from abroad and suddenly had the matcha craving, it was last minute. Literally, ordered 2 hours before I went over to pick it up.(in the morning too) Owner were soo sweet and nice literally made the experience better.
author: Desy Nurazura

review_text: Decided to drop by this nearby home-based cafe to pick up the biscoff matcha drink for my daughter who loves matcha. She said it was very nice, and the biscoff compliments the matcha well. For its quality, it was cheap compared to other cafes nearby, and my daughter also liked the smiski sticker they gave out with the drink. The owner explained their drinks very well. I am impressed by their service. Parking at the carpark was easy and the order was quick. Good surprise for kids who love matcha. 👍👍
author: Dylan Leong

review_text:
Recently my go-to matcha cafe. Bought from them twice now, and they have been great! A summary of what I have tried so far:

Uniquely Singaporean: 9/10
The name speaks for itself. Never have I seen a combination of milo and matcha, and yet it was surprisingly delicious! Would recommend this drink to milo lovers that are not superfans of matcha.

Hojicha Latte: 10/10
My go-to drink! Just read the other reviews and try it. It really IS that good.

Frosty the Foam-Man: 9/10
A seasonal item on their menu. Not a fan of caramel to begin with, but it does not remove the deliciousness of the matcha it goes with! Really like the presentation of the drink (photo attached), though I did not capture it well as I sipped it within minutes.

Their hospitality is exceptional, being incredibly understanding when I had troubles with my order, also giving out free stickers along with their drinks (which my nephew really loved!)
author: Julius Ng

review_text: got their limited blend morihan-b for my matcha latte. first thoughts was that it looked really gao and layers were really layering but cup was a little smaller than i hoped. nonetheless, the matcha was whisked till very smooth and the taste was super prominent. the blend was not bitter or astringent just the way i liked it and with a mild sweet aftertaste. will def head back for another cup if in the area! thanks 😬
author: ANNABELLE LIM

review_text:
Just had our reunion dinner tonight n was not going back again to this restaurant.

Location: similar to senior citizens corner under the hdb but it was glass up.

Service : the lady boss was friendly but they are too busy tonight.  Same utensils used throughout the dinner.

Food : big disappointment.  No display for all the dishes served n they are all served immediately after the yusheng.  Yusheng was plain n insufficient shredded radishes.  The scallop half cooked n they microwaved it too long till the scallop tasted rubbery.  I thought we ordered roasted chicken but it was actually fish cake served w a pair of chicken wings?  Ice cream was served as dessert?

We arrived at 6pm n left the restaurant before 730pm.  That was the quickest reunion dinner experienced.

The restaurant catered mostly for rc senior citizens group lunch.
author: Shalli Ang

review_text: I'm so glad to have found a great neighbourhood restaurant that serves delicious food at an affordable price! The rib was incredibly savoury, and the satay was also a hit with everyone. The kids absolutely loved it, and it was a huge bonus that our big family of 13 could be seated together comfortably. For the price, the food quality was more than reasonable - it's a great value spot for a family meal. We'll definitely be back!
author: Manson Luo

review_text: Yummy Assam fish and Sotong, nice Chilli and sauces too especially the Sambal! ☺️
author: TheOilyGoose Studio

review_text: We absolutely reccommend this place. Came with family of four, food was delicious, place was comfortable, view was stunning. There is an aircon room for those who prefer to be indoors. Our server, Eka, was friendly, bubbly and accommodating. We enjoyed our dining experience in Seafood 88.
author: zai zai

review_text: This is our 3rd time visiting.  very comfortable and the food tastes great with a wide variety of options! Particularly like the satay! and today we had the assembly fish head, sambal stingray and the fried calamari which were hot favourites too! Our family has grown to 14pax and luckily we can still fit around 1 big round table. 😊
author: Cheryl Tan

review_text:
Good kway teow goreng, good milo, fresh prata, yummy. Always come here for supper. Staff is friendly.

Wanted to take pics when the food came but forgot, so here's our empty plates
author: Prismatique Skylla

review_text: Been here many times ( at least once a week if am in town) The bryani is kinda of disappointed.  Will never order it again.  The curry sources lost the heavy taste of spices.
author: alex lim

review_text:
24-hr heartland prata place which is pretty popular among the locals. Sometimes go there to grab a prata supper in the weekend. The roti prata is always freshly made, warm, and crispy, served with some kind of South Indian acidic fish curry. The other meals are also generally good, for instance, the chicken kuzhambu (curry) comes with a flavorful and pretty thick gravy. Surprised they also served chilled Shams, which is a non-alcoholic malt beverage from Iran, which means this rare stuff is imported twice from Iran to Malaysia, and later across the causeway to Singapore.

The place is airy, with a lot of ceiling fans and some tables located in semi-outdoor setting.
author: lontongstroong

review_text:
Nice comfortable place. Food was good too. Quite many people during the weekends. Their roti prata is pretty big.

Update: sometimes their waiting time gets long, because they don't operate smoothly.  They get messy between taking orders in person, taking delivery order, giving out orders... just messy.
author: Teng Yan Wen

review_text:
1st time eating here after they opened a week ago. Staffs are friendly. Can hold abt less than 50pax. Place looks neat n tidy.
Tried afew dishes...mee hoon goreng had a lighter but decent taste. With various meat added, price will change. Roti John was good. Mutton Kuthu Prata was value for money. Plenty of meat. Portion was alot. Chicken/fish biriyani was ok. It was cold when served so asked it to be reheated. Reheating took its time thou. Chicken/fish was soft.
Bru coffee tasted abit light.
Teh o limo was good.
I request for 6person sitting & was told by staff he will get back to me but didn't.
Had to settle for 4seater table with extra chairs.
No issue.All's well.
author: Mohamed Haniffa

restaurant_name: Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Restaurant
review_text: Super local, super fresh, and full of flavor. The only downside is the location — it’s in Jurong, so if you stay in the east it’s a bit of a journey. But once you’re there, it’s totally worth it. Portions are generous, prices are very reasonable, and everything tastes amazing. The crabs, curry fish head, and even the simple noodles and rice are packed with flavor. Nothing feels careless or rushed. If I were staying in Jurong, this would easily be my go-to place every day hahaha — it’s just that good.
author: Katherine Lau

restaurant_name: Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Restaurant
review_text: Not sure why the rating is low but personally I think they deserve a higher rating .  Food is nice and many parking around the area too
author: Simon Leung

restaurant_name: Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Restaurant
review_text: Fantastic food & reasonable pricing. Don't always trust Google reviews' system, they definitely worth more than 4.5 stars.
author: Zern Ang

restaurant_name: Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Restaurant
review_text: Yi Jia Le serves tasty food that reminds you of home cooked food. The portions are generous, and we always go there for our family gathering.
author: Juan Sim

restaurant_name: Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Restaurant
review_text:
I recently dined at Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Zi Char, and I must say the dining at 华仔 was an exceptional experience. The standout feature of this place has to be the generous servings – they are truly enormous! You definitely get excellent value for your money here.

It's not just about quantity, the quality of the food is equally impressive. Every dish I tried (Assam fish head, Har Cheong Gai - Fried chicken dish) was bursting with flavour, and the freshness of the seafood was undeniable, especially 麦片虾. The flavours were perfectly balanced, and I was particularly impressed by the skillful preparation of their dishes.

It was an ideal spot for a casual meal with friends or family. The staff were attentive and helpful, providing recommendations and ensuring our dining experience was enjoyable.

In conclusion, Yi Jia Le Wah Chye Seafood Zi Char is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates delicious food and sizable portions. I left the restaurant with a satisfied palate and a desire to return for more. This place certainly lives up to its reputation as an awesome dining destination.
author: Brenda Chong

restaurant_name: 好釆盈香手工面粉粿 Hao Bian Ying Xiang Handmade Mee Hoon Kway
review_text:
This hawker and this stall reminds me of childhood. Like time has paused and stood still here. Thought his noodles can be cooked shorter as they were slightly soggy. But the broth was very aromatic.

Tried the mee pok next door too. Very good also. Many customers asked for his laksa but sold out.
author: Sheryl Zeng

review_text:

I love banmian 板面 so much and this did not disappoint at all💯. Noodles were springy and qq😍, soup was light but really flavourful without being too salty - I wasn’t thirsty after finishing my meal. Cleared my bowl. Will definitely come by again for this! At $3.50 (+ $1 for more pork), it is simply worth your money😊
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
author: Rach

review_text: ABIT hard to find this place, but worth it. Yummy bowl of Mee Hoon Kway! Hand made (like the messy square pieces haha) Got a bit of budget to add prawn and cuttlefish was a good choice! author: We the Flyers

restaurant_name: 好釆盈香手工面粉粿 Hao Bian Ying Xiang Handmade Mee Hoon Kway
review_text:
Came here to try my childhood food! Located pretty near, we came here at around 1-2pm on a weekend  and there wasn’t a lot of people!

Ordered the soup and dry Mee Hoon kueh and I’m surprised at how fast the service is! Mee hoon kueh is very chewy and thicker than the ones I eat in other stores, portion is alright but if you order the dry one might not keep you full

Will honestly come here again to eat :) really affordable ($4 a bowl) and good!
author: Cherise

review_text:
This is actually my third trip here. The previous 2 times they were closed. Decided to try my luck this time round and glad they were open. Heard alot good reviews and decided to give this stall a try. They have 7 different type of porridge to choose from with prices starting from SGD3.20 onwards.  I choose the lean pork and century egg porridge which was SGD3.70.

Portion of the porridge was generous and comes with lots of fried you tiao. The porridge has a thick texture. Good flavours as well. It comes with generous amount of century egg and pork. I love the contrast of texture of the you tiao in the porridge.

Overall, the bowl of porridge was hearty and substential. Would definitely recommend.
author: Sean Goh

review_text: Big portion of porridge. Definitely sharable between two small eaters. It was well-seasoned, though a bit too peppery for my taste. The crispy fried fritters gave an additional texture to the bowl. The ingredients were generously portioned, making it a hearty meal. Be prepared for a long wait, as the queue moves slowly.
author: CG

review_text:
Was chirpy and anticipating to taste the porridge which looks good when observed from other tables. Queue was slow moving too but if it is for good food, why not?

Then came the bad ass attitude from the rude stall owners which kills everything - the uncle from the porridge stall itself plus the aunty from right next door shop - Xin Yi Vegetarian. Both looks connected anyway.

Asked for an additional spoon, the uncle ignored then seeing he might be busy, I wanted to pick a spoon from the tray and was scolded by both the aunty from Xin Yi Vegetarian and the uncle simultaneously. Told off to not to touch their things and the porridge that they sold is very cheap, don’t ask for anything else in a harsh manner that is totally not warranted.

Will never return again 👎 Yes, it is cheap and big bowl but it is also very salty too plus blood boiling 🔥
author: Joanne Lee

review_text:
The tastiest porridge I have eaten. Portion is big and full of ingredients. Totally worth the value u are paying for.

Your food will take a while as he is giving all the love into making a wonderful bowl of porridge, one bowl at a time.
author: Chris Ng

review_text: Hidden porridge place in the west which only these in the known will know. Am a regular at this porridge place. Don’t be put off by uncle’s attitude as he just want to cook the porridge well. He is actually quite nice if there is no crowd. The pork porridge cost $3, extra $0.50 for egg. Porridge is full of ingredients and crispy youtiao. Uncle is quite heavy hand with the sesame oil and pepper, so be sure to tell him in advance if you can’t take pepper. Note tho that uncle will get irritated as he get confused easily if there is too much instructions on the porridge.
author: Willow Q

review_text:
My type of Mutton Briyani!  Taste excellent and generous portion of mutton at only $6.50.

Great varieties.

My empty plate is a good testimonial of how delicious it is, isn't it?
author: Keify Toh

review_text:
Chanced by this prata stall and gave it a try. Made on the spot, unlike usual prata stalls which have mountains of pre-made cold pratas at the side.
Prata was served hot, taste was quite ok, just that not crispy (-0.5 star) (might have to ask for more crisp). Vegetarian curry (Dal) was too watery (-0.5 star), thou taste wasn't too bad. I have tasted better pratas but this was decent.

review_text: Tastes of the food is beyond my expectations.. very well flavoured . The cook seems like a professional in bringing out authentic tastes . I highly recommend this food place to enjoy Ur food
author: prakash jagathalan

review_text: Nice and affordable prata. Worth trying if you're nearby.

review_text:

author: Charles Tiu

restaurant_name: Xin Yi Vegetarian Food 欣意素食
review_text: It was delicious!
author: Monica Zen

review_text: The fried chicken wings and cutlet were crispy and flavorful. I also loved the coleslaw as it’s rare to find it done this well. Perfectly sized portions, too!
author: Sheringham Zhou

review_text:
Absolutely phenomenal! 96 Western has truly outdone themselves — this gem is a must-visit for anyone who loves classic, satisfying western fare with a nostalgic twist.

First off, the triumphant return of the Spring Chicken to the menu is cause for celebration. Golden-brown, perfectly seasoned, and fried to crispy perfection, this full bird is juicy on the inside and crackling on the outside — it’s no wonder it became an instant hit the moment it reappeared. One bite and you’ll understand why people have been raving about it!

Then there’s their Signature Chicken Chop, a true hallmark of old-school western delights. It’s tender, generously portioned, and smothered in that unmistakably savory brown sauce that instantly transports you back to simpler times. It’s comfort food at its absolute finest.

And we can’t forget the Crispy Fried Buns — oh, those glorious, golden pillows of crunch! Crispy, airy, and utterly addictive, they are the perfect accompaniment to every dish. You’ll find yourself reaching for “just one more” again and again.

Whether you’re a longtime fan or a first-time visitor, 96 Western is firing on all cylinders right now. With incredible flavors, generous portions, and unbeatable value, this is one spot that’s definitely not to be missed. Run, don’t walk — your taste buds will thank you!
author: Teng Chun Jian

review_text:
I love it.

The pork chops are not dry, slightly salty and with some crust. For 8 dollars, you cannot ask for more.

The sauce is on point, kinda thick and a bit sweet. The coleslaw is OK though.

The rice is one of the better rice I’ve tried in SG so far, soft yet not stick together.

This whole meal gives me some sort of nostalgia feeling, and I am not even from SG. (perhaps Taiwan is kinda close lah)

I am not saying this is the best in SG, perhaps not even in Jurong, but I love the vibe and will definitely go back again.

And if you live or plan to go near the area, might as well give it a try. It’s the kind of Singapore experience you will not get from somewhere else. (Maybe other old style western hawker stalls, haha)

(PS: be aware of the mosquitos, I got bit twice in like ten minutes, how?)
author: Jason Huang

review_text: Super shiok old school tradition western fare! The fried buns are to die for! Chicken wings were crispy on the outside and juicy inside.  Highly recommended to get their mixed grill and fried fish, my top 2 fav!
author: Angeline Chua

review_text:
Overall all are Nice 👍🏻

Chicken chop have the old school feel👍🏻
Pork chop was not as hard compare to others
Although chicken Cutlet was not those thick and juicy kind but it’s still as 👍🏻

Especially the bun !!
You won’t have the oily feel which is very important 👍🏻👍🏻
author: Frederick Low

review_text:
We found out that this chicken rice stall in this hidden old school zi char coffeeshop serves rarely found chicken rice balls! So we had to give it a try. Walkable from Lakeside mrt.

We had steam chicken rice balls @$5 & 'budget meal' shredded chicken hor fun @$3.50. Chicken is boneless, generous portions and tender. Rice rolled into perfect balls, very compact, soft & flavourful.

And does it look like shredded chicken in the hor fun? It’s actually big portions of chicken meat. Sauce is good too.

They also serve zi char in the afternoon and they got some reunion dinner offer going on. The zi char offer & price looks quite reasonable.

We will be back for more chicken rice balls!!
author: Jodeci Fine

review_text: Went there for the chicken rice but they were already closing. So we tried the tze char instead. The dishes turned out to be pretty good and tasty. Prices were also reasonable.
author: Jason Ong

review_text: honestly a super delightful experience👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻 staff were super efficient BUT also super polite at the same time! not your average zi char experience. food served pretty fast and delicious 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻 will def come back for more 😁😁 (and yes priced very reasonably)
author: Neo Jun Wen

review_text: No service charge. $68 set meal for 3-4, v reasonable. Curry fish is good. Salted egg prawn also nice. Coffee pork ribs however so so only.
author: Orange

review_text: Our 1st time trying this zichar place at jurong west, surprisingly all the dishes was good 👍🏼👍🏼 especially the curry fish head and salted egg sotong. Can say this is one of the better zichar 💟🤗 The guy who attended to us was friendly, we didn’t have to wait long maybe was still early at 5:30pm, it’s also not exp at all. Will definitely dine here again!
author: Gina Joy

review_text:

restaurant_name: Thai Makan by Thai Dynasty - Jurong West
review_text:
Thai Makan Singapore Airport : I have been trying for years at Singapore airport to some Thai food. Pre Covid, there were few places in the terminals but they were closed down. Last few years at the Singapore food street was the only location for some variety of Asian cuisine, but the way it was operated was not very customer friendly. I could never order any food from there.
Surprisingly, when I visited there again today, it has changed a lot. Now the customer can go to their favourite food stall and order at the counter, using the kiosks. Very simple and straightforward approach.

Special mention to the Thai Makan food stall, where I could enjoy the Authentic Thai dishes : Tom Yum Seafood soup, Mince chicken with basil and herbs, and Thai Green Mango Salad.

It is located at Terminal 3 at Changi Airport, Singapore. Will definitely visit again and recommend to anyone who wants some authentic Asian cuisine.
author: Jyju Jossey

restaurant_name: Thai Makan by Thai Dynasty - Jurong West
review_text:
Thai Makan is another brand creation by Thai Dynasty which serves authentic halal Thai Food at affordable pricing. They pride themselves to provide genuine and yummy Thai street food to their customers. Thai Makan was created to provided our Muslim community in indulging in the amazing taste of Thailand.

A little background: Their Staff are Thai and Thai-Muslim which makes them proud to say they make real Thai Food. They are launched since 2018 and has established themselves as an icon of quality and authentic halal Thai Food.

We had their signature Pad Thai (Seafood), Tom Yum Soup (Seafood) with Rice and Signature Mango Salad.

Pad Thai is a beloved stir-fried noodle dish that is a staple in Thai cuisine. It features a delightful combination of sweet and spicy flavors, with prawns as the star protein. The dish is complemented by chopped peanuts, which add a satisfying crunch and enhance the overall texture. The balance of tamarind, fish sauce, and lime creates a vibrant taste that makes Pad Thai a favourite for me.

Although I'm not typically a fan of thick red tom yum soup, this particular one surprisingly opened up my appetite. The broth wasn’t too cloying, and instead, it was light and perfectly balanced, making it irresistibly appetizing.

The vibrant and refreshing Thai Mango Salad strikes the perfect balance between sweet, tangy, and spicy flavours. It features thinly julienned green mango, which is firm and slightly tart. The salad is typically tossed with finely sliced shallots, fresh cilantro, and chopped peanuts for added crunch.

review_text:
Mee Goreng (SGD $8) @ Mr Teh Tarik Eating House.

.

.

.
Completed with a fried egg and sliced cucumbers. Their version veers towards 'wet' in style.
.
.
.
Chicken Masala (SGD $9) @ Mr Teh Tarik Eating House.
.
Tracing its history back to May 2004 when it was founded by Hassan Bin Abdul Kadir, this casual chain eatery is a reliable place for South Indian dishes.
.
Their North Indian style rendition has bone-in chicken chunks, tender and chewy, simmered in a thick rich tomato and masala spices curry gravy. Ample use of turmeric and cumin here.
.
Carries mild but tasty meaty savoury spicy salty earthy herbal flavour. Best when paired with flatbreads or rice.

review_text: One of my favorite chee cheong fan place in this area. Tried some of the offerings, not impressed. Ok for price.
