restaurant_name: The Coffee Bean & Tea Leaf - The Rail Mall Fuyong Estate
review_text:
Super weird attitude of staff. Is it normal I was ordering breakfast and I was told of 60 min sitting time. Really?! Will you count next to me? There were only 3 tables occupied and the whole cafe was empty.
I understand in peak hours, but why to drop these statements when no one at all is here.
From a pleasant time to a rush. Not customer care at all.
author: Liliya P

review_text:
26 Jan 26
Just sharing my personal opinion — everyone has different taste preferences.

I’ve visited Assumption Restaurant for Training (ART) a few times. What makes ART meaningful is that it provides students with real-world F&B and service training. Dining there feels purposeful, knowing that you are supporting their learning and development.

On my recent visit, I ordered the fish and chips. The portion was generous and reasonably priced. The batter was crisp without being overly greasy, and the fish was fresh and moist. Overall, the dish was above average, especially considering the value for money.

I would also like to highlight their pastries, which are one of the main reasons I return. The pandan cake was moist, light, and fragrant — not overly sweet, and well-balanced in flavour. For the quality offered, the pricing is very fair.
Service may occasionally reflect that the staff are trainees, but they are generally polite and sincere, which makes the dining experience pleasant.

Overall, ART offers good food at reasonable prices, while supporting a meaningful training initiative. I would recommend giving it a try, especially their pastries.
author: Wayne Toh Bun Chin

review_text: This monthly buffet is a fantastic way to enjoy authentic traditional flavors. The porridge is comforting, and the variety of side dishes is impressive—especially the tender braised duck and flavorful prawn paste chicken. It’s not just about the food; the event supports student training and community, making every visit meaningful. Highly recommend booking early as it fills up fast.
author: Randomstuffsg

review_text: Wonderful food. Spacious & clean seating. Friendly & attentive service. Lots of (free?) parking. Social enterprise. Likely will visit again & again !
author: PM Kwong

review_text:
I had a very good experience here. The students took really good care of my group and I left feeling well fed. I ordered the baked herb chicken with black pepper sauce ($11) and as a set meal ($5) which included a soup, a slice of focaccia bread, dessert and hot tea with a cookie! It was an affordable, well balanced and tasty meal.

The restaurant is bright, spacious, clean and welcoming. I see this as a wonderful initiative that empowers students, keep it up!
author: C Lau

review_text: First time visiting this cafe for lunch. Had the chicken burger ($10) with an add-on of $5 for the set (incl. bread, soup, cake with ice-cream and tea) which was totally worth it. Filled my belly to the brim. The bun of the sandwich was nicely toasted with cheese. Enjoyed every bit of it. The bread and pastries were quickly wiped out by 1230pm so do come early when they open at 12pm.  Highly recommended. Will definitely come again 😊
author: NonoP

review_text: As a nearby resident to this 24/7 eatery at The Rail Mall, I am thankful that this place is still going strong, because of its nonstop operating hours and offering very decent food at very reasonable prices. Today, I was here for lunch and I ordered a Minced Meat Noodle Dry with Mee Kia that was very flavourful and very satisfying gastronomically speaking. My order was taken in a very friendly manner and it was served to me over the counter in the same manner. The dining ambience here was comfortable enough with the seating area laid out spaciously and in air-conditioned comfort.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
Save yourself the trip here- food is bad, service is better at an ordering kiosk, aircon is switched off when we came for supper at 10pm.

Curry rice was disappointing - hardly came with any pork gravy, the curry itself was of a thick texture, as though thickened with corn starch.
The vegetables were sour for some reason.

Laksa- they ran out of cockles for the day. Tried it anyway but should've read the reviews beforehand. Has zero chili, staff gave a pitiful amount of soup barely enough to cover the noodles. Too much coconut milk and lacked any spiciness.
Staff flat out turned us down when we asked for a little more soup.
author: Milo

review_text: I ordered a $6.80 laksa as shown in the picture. For this price, you get a hot beverage and your standard bowl of noodles. I asked for a teh C, and to be honest, it didnt taste very good. The noodles weren't much of an improvement either. Most laksa have a spoonful of sambal chilli in it to enhance the broth flavors, but we have none of it here. No egg either. What you get are 3 small cockles, some fishcake, 3 small pieces of tau pok and a beancurd roll(豆腐卷). Like most mediocre laksa, the broth isnt lemak enough and the absence of sambal chilli is a disservice to the customer. For once, I have to agree with the google ratings. The food here just isnt good enough. The tray return corner was also swamped with trays, and the staff did not bother to clear the area. The fact that it was 2 am in the morning did nothing to appease my displeasure in standing there looking like an idiot. For once, I contemplated on leaving my tray on the floor. Unless you are dying of hunger, this isnt a good place for you to be in.
author: Hatsune Miku

review_text:
I think Eat! Is one of the most standard places for mee pok kind of food. We tried it at railmall. Now, the venue is abit lacking cuz it was hot even though there was suppose to be air con running.

The food was alright. We ordered mee pok and a platter of the fried items. I think overall the food was alright. It wasn't something that will blow you away. But the whole setting is a little underwhelming especially considering how other outlets along the stretch of railmall is like.
author: Ming Hui

review_text: The ultimate sign that requires no further explanation 😂. I mean, who wouldn't obey a sign that simply says "EAT" when it leads to a delicious bowl of noodles and fragrant coffee at a steal? 🤤 It's like the universe is telling you to refuel!
author: Steven Tan

review_text: Came here for the first time and after trying, I found them nice! Being Halal, they are a favourite with our Muslim friends but I was especially taken in by the flavourful dishes. Will definitely come back for more. Service was prompt and friendly.
author: Rex Tan

review_text:
Food is good, flavorful. I use grab dine out deal, really worthy with additional discount. Highly recommend curry fish head and slippery lobster.

Service by Haziyah is fantastic!

Quiet and cosy restaurant.
author: ah siao

review_text: Service was quick and pleasant. Food taste was average but portion is good. Ordered set for 4 and the set was enough for 4-5 small eater. Place filled up quickly after 6.30pm.
author: H26

review_text: I don’t usually comment badly on food. Fooled by the pictures outside. Ordered Hokkien mee, prawn paste chicken, lemon chicken, black bean la la, broccoli and scallop, fuyong egg, and mango sago. Out of all these dishes, only lemon chicken and fuyong egg are acceptable, the rest of the dishes aren’t nice at all, very disappointed
author: Charlotte Tay

review_text:
Managed to walk in on a Sunday night! Place is usually pretty packed for dinner so we were surprised to be able to with one last seat. We were moved to a bigger table midway through to accommodate for more space for our ordered dishes as suggested by the staff which was much appreciated!

Good standard of zichar food as its name suggests and could see why they are a main stay within this hillv2 area. Would probably be back to try out other dishes.
author: Abraham Lee

review_text:
Had a rare opportunity for lunch with my 85-y.o. mum at the local Wine Connection today and was delighted by the superb service by Liz, who looked after my frail mother with so much kindness and care. The food was good and good value, as usual, but the service today was impressive and beyond expectations.
Well done, Liz!
We hope to be back again soon.
author: Lee Y

review_text:
Our evening at the restaurant was exceptional from start to finish. The ambience was inviting and we had a great dinner.

A particular highlight was our server, Nisshha. Her gentle smile radiated genuine warmth and sincerity, and her attentiveness was impressive. She was not only attentive to our table but also clearly cared for all the diners as well.

We loved the delicious Black Angus sirloin steak and the BBQ pork ribs.  The Black Angus sirloin steak was cooked to perfection, and the BBQ pork ribs were fall-off-the-bone delicious.

Nice ambience + excellent service + delicious food = 5 stars rating. Cheers.
author: Richard Tan

review_text: Patronised this outlet several times. Love the food items like fish and chips, steak frites and Iberico pork chop. Staff are friendly and attentive. They are able to recommend wines to complement the dishes. I usually request to chill the red wine and even decant. Will definitely patronise again.
author: HyperNinjaNerd

review_text: The gambas were good!! Although a tad oily. Pan seared cod was pretty good and moist as well. Not a fan of the steak though, cooked ok but maybe abit overdone? Felt quite dry and rubbery
author: Sarah Constance

review_text:
I always have wonderful drinking and dining experiences at Wine Connection. The staff delivered exceptional service — attentive, meticulous, and always anticipating what I needed without ever being intrusive. Their warm and genuine hospitality made me feel completely at home.
A special shout-out to Bareth, Michael and Jeff for going above and beyond to make the dining experiences memorable.
Good food, good vibes, exceptional service. Highly recommended! 🍷✨
author: Xaye Lee

review_text: BLACK FOREST CAKE. Had a pre-ordered 9” cake directly from Cedele online, not fm this kitchen.  Unfortunately no way to give reviews for their online service so I’m just picking to air my views here.  Cedele used to make 9-layered Black Forest Cake a few years ago. It looked and tasted amazing.  Look at what it is now.  Never mind it’s no longer 9-layers but look at how SLOPPY their baker is now at their work.   Am I eating cream or cake?  Look how thick the cream is and how bad the sponge layering is.  Uneven, thin sponges and slap on thick cream to make up for the bad bakes.  Literally a juvenile chef’s work, anyone at home can do this.  No respect for customers.  Paid $102, you tell me if this is worth it?!
author: Jen W.

review_text:
Reasonable variety, good taste, quick service. What's not to like. Can't go wrong with this place... I love their Rosemary chicken sandwich and beetroot burger. Have had it in their older Raffles outlet which is closed. Decided to try something else so I got a breakfast sourdough bagel - scrambled eggs, smoked salmon and avo. With greens on the side.. Pretty standard stuff. Their service was pretty quick, and bagel was pretty good. Crispy on outside and soaked with avo salmon on inside.
My wife loves their sweet potato fries so we got a plate. Right amount of Crispy and a refreshing departure from the usual boring potato fries..
Dessert was lovely. Pistachio cheesecake was sinful. Finished with an Oatmilk latte.. Note to self - should come here more often.
author: Sairam Subramanian

review_text: Ordered the same meal from this branch in Sep 2024 and Jul 2025. Portion shrank drastically while  price either remained constant or increased. Advise you all not to support a business that evidently lacks respect for its customers.
author: geepeetee cat

review_text: Best Cedele outlet (HillV2) I’ve visited, to date. Well-managed by the great customer service of Hanafi who understands the customers’ needs and requirement. And he brews good coffee. Keep it up!
author: Hazel P

review_text: My visits to Cedele HillV2 are always a highlight! It's rare to find a place that so perfectly blends delicious, healthy, and affordable food with such a warm and inviting atmosphere. What truly sets Cedele HillV2 apart, though, is the exceptional team. A special shout-out to JOAN, whose friendly demeanor, helpful deal advice, and attentiveness to dietary requests make every visit feel personal and special. Thank you, Cedele HillV2 team, for consistently delivering such an exceptional experience!
author: Michelle P.

review_text:
Great place to chill! Great food and service.

This place serves western and Taiwanese Cuisine. Ordered a seafood pasta previously, got beef noodle this time.

Atmosphere is great too with a literal hut built within the restraurant. Servers are very friendly, chatted about the same water bottle we had.

Carpark is quite limited at rail mall. You can choose to park along the roadside, but at your own risk!

Recommend to come!
author: Da Jun Woon

review_text: Overall food was ordinary, howeverlamb chop was good. Ambience is quite noisy but cosy. Price is quite expensive ... although family had a good time there. Went on Fri evening and able to have seats without waiting. Maybe next time can try their TW food.
author: c tzehow

review_text:
I was quite satisfied with the food and service offered at this place, at expected prices. The double cheeseburger (sorry no pic) patties had a delectable full-bodied flavour that went well with the surprisingly nice coleslaw. However, the cajun seasoning on the fries felt a little tasteless to me and only contributed to adding a slightly undesirable, powdery texture to the outside. The pork dumplings were really nice with a pleasant gentle flavour, bouncy supple texture and satisfying ratio of meat to skin, and the dip deeply enhances the experience. Personally don't like nuts in brownie but this one had a pleasant texture with a light vanilla ice cream to pair. Not bad but a little pricey given that it didn't feel very exceptional.
Unfortunately one major complaint is the atmosphere. I'm not sure how close I was to the speaker, but it was really really loud and piercing, honestly quite hard to have a conversation even without other many patrons.
Bonus free water at the end of meal though! Still recommended if in the area.
author: Brandon Yeow

review_text:
Went on a Friday night — pleasantly surprised it wasn’t fully packed, and service was quick. Food-wise, it was average and slightly on the pricier side. But I do appreciate their happy hour that runs Monday to Friday till 8pm — definitely a plus!

The nachos were a little underwhelming; missing some punch in flavor and would’ve been better if they were served warm. The half-shelled mussels looked rather sad and uninspiring, while the jumbo sausages weren’t exactly “jumbo.” I requested to switch to criss-cut fries for an extra $3, but honestly, not worth the top-up. The sauce on the sausage is too salty.

A pity there wasn’t any live band that night — it would’ve added a lot more vibe to the place. Also, parking is really limited, so it’s best to come early if you’re driving.

✨Overall: decent for a casual night out, but don’t expect to be wowed by the food.
author: Orange

review_text: Went there yesterday with a group of 12 people. Tried the taiwanese food and it is as good as you can get in Taiwan! Most important is the service! As most of them have special request due to diet and Manager Kelly was very attentive to all their request, she is also very friendly. And the owner Fiona if I did not get her name wrong is also friendly. 😁
author: Jing Hong Chan

review_text:
It was a wonderful experience dining here. 🤩

We were welcomed warmly by the teacher, who guided us to our seats. The students were attentive and served us well, and they were able to provide explanations for the menu.

The food was of a high quality and I was pleasantly surprised with the red wine braised beef. The portion was generous, and the flavour reminiscent of a French restaurant.

The other dishes and the mocktails were great as well. For the appetiser, main dish, dessert, coffee, mocktail, water and bread, the price of $20 was really worth it.

I would recommend to come and give this a try. 🥳
author: Hui

review_text: Food was delicious and service was great. Personally really enjoyed the dining experience. Will recommemd to give it a try if you are around the west!
author: Tracy T

review_text: First visit to Amber West for lunch. Located within the ITE college West campus in Choa Chu Kang, it's a 'fine-dining' restaurant where students are trained and supervised by mentors by their side. They had just revamped their set lunch menu at the start of the new term. They offer a 2-course meal at $18 and a 3-course meal at $20 which comes with an appetizer (soup or salad), Mocktail, Main Course, Tea/Coffee and Dessert. It is certainly not the best of quality given the affordable cost but it's gratifying seeing the students giving their best trying to serve the customers. Well done 👍🏾😊
author: NonoP

review_text:
A training restaurant for the campus' students. Located on the 4th level overseeing the estate.

A conducive environment with students who are eager to please. Students are competent to their tasks.

There are options of 2 or 3 courses which are priced reasonably which includes a mocktail.

Quality of food is excellent.

Reservation highly recommended.
author: MNG

review_text: Quality food at a very affordable price. This is a training restaurant operated by ITE students from school of hospitality. The quality of food is great, and the presentation of food is excellent! For 3-course meal, it only cost $15. However, do exercise some patience as students serving are still in training. We can provide valuable feedback after the meal, so that they can improve on their training.
author: Chris

review_text:
We were introduced to this Italian restaurant and went there for lunch. It’s a cozy restaurant and we’re greeted by the lady boss who was friendly and know the dishes well. She introduced the dishes to us politely.

We ordered carbonara, squid ink seafood pasta and prosciutto Parma ham pizza, and calamari for appetisers. All the dishes were on point and tasted really really good. Thé carbonara is cooked the true Italian way ( pecorino, Parmesan and egg yolks), without the cream! Tasted so good. We will definitely be back for more!
author: hey jojos

review_text:
We were recommended by a friend who said they have the best carbonara. So we came to try. Amazingly, not only was the carbonara good, but we found our new fave pasta - seafood linguine in a bag. Sooo good. Also love their vongole spaghetti, risotto, mushroom soup and pizza!

Oh, their molten lava cake + tiramisu are delicious too!

We will keep coming back for authentic Italian fare, the homely atmosphere and personable service!

Do come and try for yourselves! You will be wowed! 🥰
author: Chomel Lim

review_text:
When I think “hole-in-the-wall”, Cacio e Pepe fits the image. Hidden gem in the Hillview residential estate. Our family has been coming back (since 2015) whenever we crave homely Italian fare. It helps that owners Bee & Jackie are ever-smiling & hospitable hosts.

Our family has probably tried everything on their menu. Pizza is thin crust style. Ask for daily specials. And don’t forget to save space for molten lava cake (with alcohol & nuts option) & tiramisu. House wines are always dependably good.

Roadside parking around the nearby roads. Reservations recommended.
author: Cheen the Curious

review_text: This local and authentic Italian restaurant is very great for me. I always take a bus more than 1 hour from the middle of city to Hillview to have dinner in this place. The owner and staff is nice and kind. The taste is delicious especially cacio e pepe that same name with this restaurant.
author: KK

review_text:
Cute little neighbourhood Italian restaurant. The food was decent with the pasta being really delicious. The pizza and calamari were a little underwhelming to be honest.

The service was fantastic and had that really homely/family run sort of feel.
author: Ali Jumabhoy

restaurant_name: Acqua e Farina - Italian Pizza & Pasta Restaurant . Rail Mall
review_text: Welcoming staff, consistent level of service amongst three staff. They were all very polite and accommodating. They give notice if food gets a little delayed, but duration was quite acceptable. Food is amazing. All recommended dishes, double thumbs up! Our pizza was especially made with two flavours, thank you! Highly recommended. Ambience was romantic and the place is neat.
author: Aj3y

restaurant_name: Acqua e Farina - Italian Pizza & Pasta Restaurant . Rail Mall
review_text:
The space is extremely unassuming but the food was excellent and priced on the slightly high side for an Italian restaurant nearby our home area with excellent food that is originally from
Italian Chef himself .

We order burrata, clams in white wine, folded pizza, ravioli n 1 seasonal dish (oven baked chicken), scallops and crayfish spaghetti which tasted flavourful yet not too salty, almost as if it came out of a fine dining home kitchen.

The pizza had a nice doughy texture and fresh ingredients and the 2 dishes I added which is scallop and pasta is my favourite with the Tiramisu when I am never a dessert person but I tried this time as it is not too much for sharing. We were also served bread and after dessert as complimentary.

Definitely worth a return as we came here for a couple of times already and saw the chef this time as we ordered 2 bottles of wines and stayed till closing.

He is really nice and friendly to come out to check with us on the food and services. We are surprised that this gem is opened for 21 years so thumbs up for him for the great effort in this business.  Seating is limited but it was full house on Sunday night otherwise, rather quiet.
author: Silver Tan

restaurant_name: Acqua e Farina - Italian Pizza & Pasta Restaurant . Rail Mall
review_text:
Came here with a friend who highly recommended this place as it’s quite well known. We tried a few dishes, but didn’t manage to take photos of everything. The pizza was a must-try as we noticed many tables ordering it, and it did not disappoint. We ordered a white-based pizza with mushrooms and other toppings, and it was really nice.

We also had main dishes, wine, and a dessert platter where we got to try a variety of desserts. Everything was well prepared and enjoyable. The overall bill came to around $220 for two people, which felt reasonable for the experience.

The restaurant has a classy and cozy atmosphere, great for coming with a partner or friends. During our visit, we noticed several birthday celebrations with staff singing and bringing out cute little cakes, which added to the warm vibe. Overall, it was a lovely experience and a good memory. I would definitely come back, especially for a relaxed meal or a special occasion.
author: Jitya M.Topaz

restaurant_name: Acqua e Farina - Italian Pizza & Pasta Restaurant . Rail Mall
review_text: We only recently discovered this gem. The food was excellent, especially the special spanish red prawn pasta and Insalata that came with goat cheese on bread. The chef Roberto was very friendly and came out to chat. Would highly recommend, 10/10 would come again!
author: Clare Nyam

restaurant_name: Acqua e Farina - Italian Pizza & Pasta Restaurant . Rail Mall
review_text:
Delightful place. Pasta was delicious, calamari excellent and four cheese pizza great. They gave free little donut snacks with our dessert.

Overall a nice but pricey place that has interesting Today's Specials.
author: Probably Satan

review_text: A cute little nautical themed pub. Its a bit cranped for space but the atmosphere is friendly and easy going. There's a free pool table which is always fun! Drinks are pretty expensive but that's probably just Singapore in general
author: Oceeyy Gray

review_text: Has been quite long not patronize this pub. Saw that the pub owner has been changed a lot. The pub owner and waiters and waitresses were all very friendly and professional. Still misses the finger snack made by the lady boss she specially cook for me the large wastburg sausage fried with the hoegarrden and thai chilli padis. Taste nice. Hope i still can have the taste when i patronize the pub 1 night.?
author: Remus Lee

review_text:
Chanced upon Jolly Rogers when we were driving around.
Good neighbourhood bar to hang out. Great food.Food portions are a good size too.
Have visited quite a few times already.
It's now our go to bar.🙂
author: Asha Naidu

review_text: We had mixed feelings about Jolly Roger. The place gave us a warm welcome, but we noticed that many items on the menu were not available that day. We're not sure if it was because of the time of day or if the chef was absent. We ordered a few items, and the food was okay, but the options were quite limited. The drinks were reasonably priced compared to other bistros. Despite that, the environment was good, and we enjoyed meeting new people and chatting. I'm not sure if I would come back unless they upgrade the menu and offer more food options. If they do, then maybe I would consider returning.
author: Jitya M.Topaz

review_text:
Used the Entertainer 1 for 1 mains.
Very nice and cosy English pub feeling. Most people come to have drinks but we had the mains. Food was tasty and flavourful and while some might find it too strong tasting, I was delightfully pleased by the taste.
Staff are very friendly and also interact with their regular customers.
Will come back again if there are offers!!
author: Daniel Seah

review_text: My wife and I were here this morning for brunch. It was my second time here year in many years, but my wife's first time here. We ordered the following: an Onion Prata and a Teh Tarik for my wife, a "Sarang Burung" and a Coke Zero for me, and we shared a Plain Prata prepared in a crispy way. For starters, the food and beverages here are all reasonably priced. The Pratas in general were very good - and you can ask for it to be done in the way you want it. The "Sarang Burung" or "Bird's Nest" in the Malay language was both very good and very "pretty." The Teh Tarik here was also very good. Service here, for first timers, might seem to be too presumptuous, but that's because the boss and the crew here are the kind of people who treat all their customers as if they are regulars and friends of the place. The dining ambience here was comfortable and "rustic" as it's set in a quiet neighbourhood off Hillview Avenue.
author: edtayjb

review_text: brilliant food, ive been coming here since I was a child. Friendly owner and very welcoming. Prata is very crispy and the fish curry is the best ive tasted in singapore - for real. Quality ingredients and friendly staff. Good location aswell
author: FN4022026 SEHAJ DEV SINGH

review_text:
Nice tranquil kampung vibes...
The boss and staff are very attentive, warm and friendly..

$10/- Mutton murtabak (ONLY BEFORE 12NOON AND AFTER 4PM) tasted very flavourful. Better than Zam Zam. Much much better than Springleaf. The curry wasn't really required. 5/5

$9 Mutton biryani.. super good quality basmati that is lighter in ghee but still super aromatic from the spices... Mutton was very flavourful. Better than Zam Zam.

$1.50/- Teh Halia impressively strong and robust tea taste. Very consistent 5/5

Come here if you wanna relak one korner with free parking good food and good vibes... Away from stuffy malls and over-rated places.
author: T Tan

review_text:
Recommend the Maggi Goreng Thai Style. It is slightly wet but always flavorful and good to slurp. I always come back once in awhile.

In my latest experience though, the staffs are a little less friendly as compared to how it used to be. The lack of acknowledging you when you made eye contact and just walking away... but of course this could be a one-off or a bad day for the said staff. I hope management would also care for staff if they are not feeling well to be serving.

Will continue to support for the great Maggi Goreng.
author: Aason Than

review_text: Appreciate the deco. It's nice to find a good prata place in a relaxing cafe vibe. Great food. Total enjoyed the Tsunami Prata. The smoothness of the egg coupled with the tangy curry all soak up by the prata. The eggplant and veg provided a good balance.  Sweet, tangy and eggy all provided in 1 dish. Good for brainless weekends when you don't want to decide what to eat and yet you want everything 😂
author: angelin teo

review_text:
We visited to try the chilli crab promotion (2 for $68). Upon entering the private room, there was a slightly musty smell, possibly from the carpet, though it became less noticeable after a while.

We ordered a variety of dishes, which were generally average. The crab size was about average and not overly small. However, some portions of the crab meat were limited and slightly dry, which may be due to the condition of the crab or the preparation. That said, the chilli gravy was quite enjoyable, and we were pleased that one of the crabs had roe.

Overall, I would still recommend giving this place a try, as taste preferences differ and others may enjoy the experience more than we did.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
Highly recommend this place!! Would have given it 6 or 7 stars if it was possible.

To be honest, I had very low expectations as this place was a little remote. I happen to know this place because it's in the same building as shopee collection point.

We ordered the crabs ($90 for 3 good sized ones!), noodles, har Cheong, prawn rolls and fried mantou. All were fantastic.

The crabs were also bigger than I had thought.

I have been to more highly rated seafood places and this is on par, if not better! Please come to support!
author: Selina

review_text: Food was quite good. Wait was slightly to the longer side. Will definitely come back again!
author: Carmen Lee

review_text: Very value for money and cozy restaurant , my family had a memorable time thank you ! Giant lobsters at great pricing , everyone was impressed !
author: rebecca goh

review_text:
Room was very cold, told the staff, can't do anything as it was centralised but I think everyone else dinning felt the same way so should have just adjusted either way. One group even went outside to sit instead.

Food was bad and we waited so long for the food. We ordered around 7pm but only left close to 9pm, more than half the time spent waiting for food.

Never had such bad zichar especially at their price point. Only the crab promo was worth it and at least edible. The rest not so much. We paid for a steamed red grouper for $80 before taxes but the fish was tough and not tender.

Other than the two, we ordered tequila chicken, dragon chives, pork ribs, XO fried rice, drunken prawns, caipoh beancurd. Only the XO fried rice was good. Others was the worst I had comparing to other zichars.

During payment, we were even charged additional fried rice which we didn't order. Was lucky I spotted it if not we would have been charged for it.

Will never go back.
author: Rachel Chua

review_text: Extremely salty. You have been warned.
author: Arun Ratnaa

review_text: Miniscual amount for $30 plus. Prawn biryani had 6 pieces of small Shrimps.. small piece of mutton enough for 3 mouthfuls.  Undercooked rice.  Containers half full. Never again.
author: TRIDENT Group

review_text: hi just recieve my chicken biryani and it is not good rice are uncook and less quantity i spend 36.47$ for this sorry to say it was bad experiance will nt order again thnx
author: Virk Dharamvir Singh

review_text:
Why so much hate in reviews??? 🙄
The food is ok. Eatable la broooooooo.. if u want to know the real taste , try 7/11 butter chicken rice.. This briyani same taste with that.
author: Rathi M Nair

review_text:
Whoever Milind Sovani is, he sure has a huge ego to put his name on food this bad. Dryest, least flavourful Biryani I have ever eaten before. Serving size was okay, but the rice had nothing to it and only four smallish pieces of mutton for 16 dollars. The restaurant called to say they were out of a side dish and offered to replace it with the most authentic of Indian side dishes - deep fried cheese fingers. They tasted okay but I question the authenticity of this restaurant.

EDIT: Looking at other reviews and pictures, it seems my Biryani was supposed to have come with a pot of curry to fight the absolute dryness of the rice. Guess what didn't come with my order? :)
author: Kitsune Risu

review_text:
I ordered 4 biryanis and 4 tandoori chicken pieces today. Ordered around 9am for delivery @1pm, food reached to me @2pm. The delivery guy had to wait for more than one hour for pick up order.
Food quality - Tandoori chicken was spice less and not cooked properly. Chicken biryani was not really dum biryani, they cooked chicken and rice separately and just put 3-4small pieces of chicken on top of rice.
Mutton biryani was same but with 2 small pieces of lamb.
Recommendation - Food court biryani is way better than this, don’t recommend.
author: Niranjan Biswal

review_text:
I placed a scheduled pickup order at 4pm for 5pm collection, ordering a total of 6 pizzas. I arrived at 5pm despite the heavy rain, collected the pizzas, and went straight home.

When I reached home, I realised I only received 5 out of the 6 pizzas. I understand that mistakes can happen, but when we opened the boxes, almost all the pizzas were incorrect.

I ordered Hawaiian pizzas with hand-tossed crust, but received thin crust instead. The large BBQ pizza was supposed to be stuffed crust, but I was given a normal crust. My Classified Chicken and Prawn Sensation pizza was completely missing. Instead, I was given a Vegetarian Lover and a Pepperoni pizza, which I did not order.

This was extremely frustrating as the order was meant for someone’s birthday, and it completely ruined the celebration.

I called the store and was told that a full refund would be processed within 3–5 working days. I sincerely hope they honour their word. I will update whether the refund is received.
author: Mr Chill

review_text: I order in store for takeaway and they give a pizza box with one slice only. Very disappointed with there service and when call them they angry and didn’t apologise. Very disappointed with their service. I ordered 2 small pizza 1 large pizza and 1 crispy fries. Large pizza with only 1 slice inside and didn’t give the crispy fries.
author: Abid Hussain

review_text:
I am genuinely shocked by the level of mismanagement at this location. The store was visibly unclean, poorly maintained, and operating far below what any reasonable customer would expect from an established brand.

Basic hygiene and operational standards appeared to be neglected.
Even more concerning was the behavior of the employees. The staff were rude, dismissive, and displayed a complete lack of professionalism. Customers were treated as inconveniences rather than valued patrons. This reflects either a serious lack of training or a management culture that tolerates indifference and disrespect. Honestly don’t know where you find these utterly incompetent employees, the level of ignorance, laziness, and blatant disrespect they display is beyond embarrassing for any business claiming to be professional.

Management must immediately address both employee conduct and cleanliness standards. If corrective action is not taken, it is only a matter of time before regulatory authorities step in and address these issues themselves!!

For anyone considering visiting this location: if you value professionalism, basic hygiene, and respectful service, I strongly advise avoiding this place under any circumstances, even if you are extremely hungry.
author: soheil haddad

review_text:
I would like really to compliment Cheryl Soh, kitchen staff at Domino's Hillview Outlet!

On February 19, being 3rd day of Lunar New Year, I was very surprised when I visited the outlet to witness Cheryl Soh as the only kitchen staff managing the entire outlet all by herself!!! Besides having to prepare and make pizzas to meet the huge order demand, she also had to attend to walk-in customers as well.

I was really impressed by her good service attitude even though she was up to her neck trying to churn out as many pizzas as possible to meet all the orders. There was virtually no other help around for Cheryl Soh. Why was there a staffing issue during the festive rush?

Domino's is fortunate enough to have such an efficient employee.  Cheryl Soh crushed it all by herself to meet every demand and fulfill every order and yet was able to service her customers with her smile.

Kudos to Cheryl Soh. You have left a lasting impression on me! I hope I can be served by you when I return to the outlet again soon!

Best regards
Angie
author: 安琪ンーじ登辉

review_text:
I just don't understand why they never pick the phone? I ordered pizza from official website, waited 2 hours without any notice. I had no option to even cancel the order on the website, the store never answered the phone. Only thing I could do is just waiting, reading reviews here and got angry..
Why do you run business like this? Pick up the phone or simple text for lateness would be fine.
By the way, our pizza was so cold that we had to heat up in the oven... I don't know how long those set on your counter until it got finally picked up..
author: 늘지금처럼

review_text: Wang Family Kitchen - this Korean family-run restaurant has been in operation for quite a number of years at Hillview Community Club, and its enduring presence thereat is testament to its no-fuss, no-nonsense, comfortingly delicious Korean meal sets served daily as a "Day Plate" and at a reasonable price. My wife and I have dined here on a number of occasions and we have always been satisfied with the place. As we sort of live "just across the road" in the Dairy Farm area, choosing this place for a Korean meal is a no-brainer. Service here is nice enough, and the dining ambience is comfortable. I recommend that you try this place for its home-cooked style Korean food, if you are in the Hillview area.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
My go to Korean restaurant in SG to satisfy my Korean cuisine cravings, something that is hearty and value for money to me.

Have been coming back here many times and it never disappoints as the consistency is always there. I like that they have a fixed menu everyday and you just have to show up and have it served to you, without thinking much about what to eat.

My favourite dishes would be the Bulgogi (generous amount of meat) & seasoned fried chicken! Honourable mention goes to the homemade waffle for dessert 😋  Although it’s a very small piece, i really like the texture of it because it is the chewy kind, similar to mochi, served warm.

The friendly male boss is also very dedicated to his job & can give this place a try if you’re around the area! Can use CDC vouchers too ~
author: Valencia Wong

review_text:
Repeated visits for the hearty meals that feel like homecooked food in a cosy Korean home. Wide variety of banchan that comes in the set. Can check IG for daily menu options that are available.

But some of the cups and and bowls felt sticky. Hope cleanliness can be improved.

Sheltered parking available in basement of Hillview CC.
author: J T

review_text: The price point is overpriced for the quality of food. Paid $41 for a 2 set but the quality of food doesn’t justify for such price and it is more like food catering standard. Korean stew served in a bowl, it tasted diluted more like Korean food court kind. The food is also not hot enough. Suggest to go to other authentic Korean restaurant with the same price and with better quality food. Try once and nv go again.
author: TheCraftWork Ace

review_text:
I stopped by a Korean café at Hillview Community Centre. The staff informed me that pork was the only option available as they were about to go on their lunch break, so I went with that. Unfortunately, both the pork and the soup were only lukewarm rather than hot, which made the meal less satisfying. The pork portion in the main dish also felt a bit small for the price of $19.50 per set, though it did come with a mochi wafer and a small slice of watermelon.
The banchan (side dishes) were served together with the main dish instead of being free-flow, which is something I usually expect from most Korean eateries. My child even commented that the meal looked like a Korean office lunch set.
Overall, the food was decent, but I was hoping for better value and a more enjoyable dining experience.
author: T Y

review_text: Food is good but would have been better if it is less salty. Service is good too. We had 2 elderly in our group who needed warm water. They don't serve warm water in their restaurant but made an exception.
author: J J

review_text: I ordered the mushroom minced meat claypot rice for delivery, and the rice was badly burned with lots of black charred pieces that taste bad, and are likely carcinogenic. So this is a public service announcement: to the chefs, please avoid burning the rice. To customers, avoid eating it if your rice is burned.
author: Ji-Jon Sit

review_text: Newly opened and overall id say it’s a great f&b addition to Hillv2. There isn’t much changes to the previous place with regards to furnishing but overall comfortable and clean environment. Good and wide array of dishes to choose from and many good claypot choices. Some items within the menu are also great value for money such as the fish soup. Staff were prompt and efficient. It was slightly packed on a Sunday evening but we were able to walk in without any reservations.
author: Abraham Lee

review_text:
This Zichar restaurant in Hillview specializes in traditional Chinese dishes fused with flavors and finesse.

Searing claypot and sizzling hotplate dominate here.

I had the fish maw soup with crab meat in claypot to start.

Splashed multiple rounds of black vinegar and added several shakes of white pepper.

Hot, decadent, and tangy.

My favorite.

For the mains I had salted egg yolk prawns with no rice.

The prawns were fried so delicately producing crispy batter, then coated  with fragrant, thick, salted-egg sauce.

Excellent.

Large restaurant.

Beautiful view.
author: 4vi31t

review_text: New restaurant recently opened in Hillv2. Overall the sauces on each dishes are great but could be improved in meat freshness. Will recommend for family gatherings!
author: Kenji Ng

review_text:
their basil is pretty good sia! spicy! pairs so well with their creamy omelette yum would def buy again

their staff are very friendly and outgoing. also provide water. unfortunately idk why my deep fried garlic pork took like 25 mins to come out... everyone else around us were seated later but had their food coe before mine >
author: chu xuan

review_text:
We asked for more sauce for our papaya fish and was topped up immediately. Good service
For the raw oyster , the raw green leaf yod kratin is not included.
The portion for the papaya somtum is too little for $7++; and there is no enough of the fish sauce.
The food is good and served fast .
author: Benson Foong

review_text: 20/10/2025: a kids friendly restaurant for a simple Sunday lunch. Greeted by Thai speaking staff upon arrival and felt like we were transported straight to Thailand! Food was served fast and delicious. Prices were decent. We had a nice time. Will be back to try out the other items in the massive menu.
author: Stella Tay

review_text: Staffs were friendly and kind. Food were delicious and authentic. Must order is the Iced Thai Green milk tea and Thai Deep Fried Garlic Chicken. Better to make a reservation before coming down to the restaurant.
author: Shannon

review_text: Extensive menu, pretty authentic flavours and generous portion. Our faves - the ' heavy wok hei' kangkong and appetising salmon salad with thai sauce. Would be great if the chilli lime dish used a whole squid/ bigger sized squid for a better bite and stronger seafood flavour. Overall, would revisit!
author: Liyan Ho

review_text:
We had lunch at IO Italian Osteria at HillV2 and were really impressed by the quality of the food. The ravioli was beautifully made with great depth of flavour, the braised beef cheek was tender, and the truffle schiacciata was aromatic and addictive. Every dish felt carefully executed and comforting.

What truly elevated the experience was the service. Mega and Jit were exceptional — warm, attentive, and genuinely hospitable. They checked in at just the right moments and made sure we were well looked after throughout the meal, and topped up our water regularly.

All in all, a wonderful lunch with excellent food and standout service. A restaurant well worth a visit.
author: Xuanming Huang

review_text:
Traditional stuffed roman schiacciata (truffle one) is fantastic, crispy and flavourful. Amatriciana (bacon & tomato, this is non-spicy) pasta is simple but done really well.
Dolce salata (mixed salad) is yumny and refreshing
Skip the prawn & asparagus taglioline though, nothing special imo.
Also skip the buttered & fried cod (not pictured) as the batter was way too thick.

Place is huge and suitable for groups. Feels like an authentic Italian place. Lovely natural lighting in the daytime.
author: Sabrina

review_text: Great food, amazing service. Staff were prompt and friendly, helpful and also very kind in accommodating to our requests. The pizzas and flatbread were crispy and flavourful, the carbonara was authentic (egg-cheese mix instead of cream) and served al dente, the roasted chicken was wondefully seasoned, very tender and juicy, the burrata and parma ham were very appetising, the mushroom risotto was perfectly done, and the pistachio tiramisu was one of the best we had - it's not too moist, and you can taste the aromatic coffee in the middle. As an avid fan of Italian cuisine, this is one restaurant not to miss. One of the servers also gave my little boy a nice cookie to take away and some complimentary breads during the meal. Except for the part that the place is a little cramped (I don't mind it as I find it rather cosy), everything was great. It's our first dining experience there and definitely not the last. Highly recommended!
author: Agares

review_text:
First time here, amazed by the food and service.  Head waitress is very attentive and friendly.  The seafood stew is astonishingly well done - seafood is very fresh and the soup is flavourful.  Truly enjoyed our meal.

The place is very popular so better to make a reservation.
author: Kenneth Ho

review_text:
Rajes & Siva were attentive to our needs throughout the dinner experience. The starters (eggs & cod fish) were really good, esp the eggs that had a nice truffle flavour with juicy mushrooms. Taste and flavour of pasta and stuffed bread were on point too! 💯

Even though they were closing in 10mins, Rajes reassured us repeatedly and even brought plates along with our birthday cake :) thank you for making our wonderful night even lovelier! 🥰
author: poromomo

review_text: New Nanyang at HillV2 - my wife and I were here today (27 January 2026) for brunch. It has been a while since we were last here even though we live "just across the road" in the Dairy Farm area. We ordered the following here today: two Handmade Yong Tau Foo Dry Noodle with beehoon for my wife and yellow mee for me - and a Barley with Winter Melon Hot for my wife and a Coke Zero for me. The Handmade Yong Tau Foo Dry NoodleS were (as we have had in the past) very good - with very good yong tau foo pieces all nicely fried and stuffed with flavourful proteins, and the noodles were nicely coated in a dark moreish sauce. Service here was very good - friendly and accommodating, which in the case of the latter, one could place an order at the counter instead of online. The dining ambience here whilst comfortable and spacious, sadly leaves you with cooking smells lingering in your clothes after you depart from the restaurant.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
After a refreshing morning walk on September 27, we decided to stop by New Nanyang at Hillview for breakfast. The menu looked very enticing — especially the Yong Tau Foo Laksa and Nonya Mee Siam with prawns. For just an additional $1.50, you can enjoy a big cup of Kopi O, which was smooth and aromatic — a great way to start the day.

The Nonya Mee Siam brought back fond childhood memories — mildly spicy, flavorful, and so well-balanced that I finished the entire bowl with satisfaction. The Yong Tau Foo Laksa portion was generous and filling, though a little oily for a morning breakfast.

Ordering was convenient with a self-order QR code system. Although we had to wait a while for the food, it was served warm by a friendly server who also helped to clear the dishes and utensils after our meal.

Overall, it was a pleasant dining experience with tasty food, good coffee, and attentive service.
author: N. Gan

review_text: ordered 2 sets of breakfast ($15) which was rather pricey. the french toast with cheese was really nice - thick, soft, cheesy. while the kaya toast set was pretty average.
author: Us The Creators

review_text:
I had breakfast at New Nanyang at Hillv2 on 20th Dec Sat morning.  It was quite disappointing because the breakfast set (ham and cheese toast with egg and kopi c) wasnt served until I reminded the staff (apparently because they didn't receive my online payment though the app showed was successful) and the food quality wasn't worth the amount  I paid.

I will not visit this outlet again, or other branches, as I am not sure of the quality.
author: Yuen Chuan Ho

review_text:
I love their Babi Pongteh (come with chap chye and white rice), its delicious and comforting.

The ham and egg cheese toast is also tasty. The scramble egg is perfect with a good toast.

The teh halia is strong, I seldom get a strong teh halia in Singapore. The pandan milk tea is unique, balanced sweetness and refreshing.

The service attendant was a bit not friendly though, she didn't even want to answer when we asked what food/beverage that she served to us.

Plenty of seats for saturday morning and the ambience is relaxing. Easy to talk environment.
author: Agus Wiwanto

review_text: Our favorite grilled fish joint in Singapore. Serving of the fish here is huge for the price with lots of ingredients without any additional cost unlike the other joints, go for the Wanzhou Grilled Fish. We’ve frequented this outlet for numerous times which we lost count. Fish is fresh and service is good. They have promotions for the beers and skewers as well. Only cons is that the restaurant can get a little packed during weekend meal hours.
author: Joanne S

review_text: Their lunch set deal is so good! The fish tastes really good & their servers were super friendly & attentive as well.
author: lydia bae

review_text: We tried the spicy grilled fish and it was super fragrant and full of flavor. The other dishes were tasty too, nothing to complain about. Service was friendly and the China beer was surprisingly affordable. A satisfying and easy meal overall
author: iamjess

review_text: Chong Qing Grilled Fish offers a bold and memorable dining experience, perfect for groups craving authentic Sichuan flavors.
author: Christopher Ho

review_text:
Chong Qing Grilled Fish is one of the better grilled fish restaurants. I've been to the one in town several years ago, and this is my first visit to this particular branch.
I like the various types of soups that you can choose, and for each option, you can also choose the hotness (spiciness) level.
There's more than enough for 2 pax, including two starters as well as the fish. We opted for the pickled cabbage soup, which had a very nice sweet and sour taste.
Another thing I like is that the fish was filleted and hence, was boneless. The fish was well grilled well and was tasty too.
This is recommended and is good value indeed.
author: Jason Ong

review_text: This Indian restaurant at the second level of HillV2 "mall" is, in my opinion, famous and popular for its "Chaat" or northern Indian street food. So I would come here for that when I need a change from my usual Indian food favourite of either south Indian vegetarian breads or banana leaf rice. And I always love the tastes and textures of the various "Chaat" available here, which are almost always very moreish and more importantly, very delicious. Service here is good - friendly and courteous. The dining ambience here is nice and in air-conditioned comfort.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
The food was decent and enjoyable overall.

That said, the dessert options could really use some improvement, as they didn’t quite live up to the rest of the meal. Desserts are usually a nice way to wrap up dinner, and this felt a bit underwhelming.

The place also feels a little cramped, with limited space to move around, which slightly impacts the overall experience but this is not serious concern though.
author: Arvind Kannan

review_text: I tried their garlic naan and it was so fragrant that I couldn't resist but to order more. Definitely nice food here. However, the pricing can be a little high but it would be worth it. Service was nice and friendly.
author: Rex Tan

review_text:
(Feb)My updated review/reply to the restaurant:

I was not aware of your reply until now. I would like to clarify a few points with the Google Review Words Limits as below.

As adults, we understand whether placing an unused chair beside our table would obstruct anyone. As mentioned, the restaurant was nearly empty. The supervisor simply said “no” and told us to put the bag on the floor, without further explanation. That felt unnecessarily rigid.

Regarding the supervisor’s attitude, she did appear unfriendly. If you prefer not to comment on this, does that mean you agree with the way the situation was handled? Professionalism is not just about enforcing rules, but also about how those rules are communicated.

As first-time customers unfamiliar with Indian cuisine, we trusted the staff and naturally began eating it. To suggest that we “fully enjoyed” feels unfair. Being charged for a dish served by mistake, without apology, was disappointing.

Clearing unfinished dishes without asking also felt rushed.

Your response seems more focused on defending your position than understanding the customer’s experience. Unfortunately, this makes it difficult for me to visit again or recommend your restaurant.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
It was New Year’s Eve, so the restaurant wasn’t  crowded.A friend wanted to eat here, so we agreed.

At the very back of the restaurant there were about four to five tables, and only our table was dining there. We borrowed one chair from another empty table to place a bag. Unexpectedly, a female supervisor coldly told us that we were not allowed to do that. I said, “But no one is using it.” She still refused. I then asked if they had a box or place to store bags. She said no and told us to put it on the floor by the window.

I  couldn’t understand why they were being so strict. Aside from our table, the restaurant was almost empty. Judging from her unfriendly expression, my enjoyment of the meal had already begun to fade.

Another female waitress who served our food looked quite young and inexperienced. When we asked her questions, she didn’t seem very confident in her answers. When the female supervisor spoke to her, her attitude was still unfriendly.

Since we weren’t very familiar with Indian food names or ingredients, and it was our first time here, we began eating once the a few dishes arrived. The food itself actually tasted quite good.

However, after eating some of one dish, we realized it seemed unfamiliar. The female supervisor then came over and said the dish had been served by mistake. There was no apology, nor did she explain whether it would be removed from the bill.

When we were almost finished eating, another male waiter came to our table and tried to take away one of the dishes without any indication or asking us first. We had to awkwardly say, “We haven’t finished that yet.”

When we paid the bill, we discovered that the wrongly served dish had been charged.

My friends said, “Forget it, it’s New Year’s Eve—let’s just enjoy the meal.”

Later, when friends asked me where I had dinner on New Year’s Eve, I said we went to this restaurant. The food was fine, but the service wasn’t very good.
I then started to wonder—was it just us who felt that their service is disapponting?

I checked the restaurant’s Google Reviews, and sure enough, some customers shared similar experiences about the unpleasant service.

Compared to the food, the service attitude of the female supervisor was far worse.

I remember a piece of drawing on the wall that said something like cooking the finest dishes to the highest standard. There were also some beautiful Indian-style artworks hanging inside the restaurant.
But does the restaurant’s “highest standard” apply only to the food? Doesn’t a high-quality dining experience also include making customers feel welcomed, respected, and happy?

The food here makes me want to come back, but the service makes me hesitate.

Perhaps next time, I’ll check the reviews again to see whether anything has changed.
author: ps k

review_text:
A Culinary Masterpiece of Indian Flavors! 🌟

Prepare to be dazzled by the undisputed #1 destination for Tandoori, Tikka, Seafood, and Kebabs! Each dish is a symphony of authentic spices and bold, unforgettable flavors. The tandoori selections arrive sizzling and tender, infused with the perfect hint of char. The tikka is succulent and bursting with rich aromatics, while the seafood delights with exquisite freshness and masterful seasoning. And the kebabs—oh, the kebabs—are perfectly grilled, juicy, and melt in your mouth with every bite.

The ambience combines warm, inviting decor with a vibrant atmosphere that elevates the entire dining experience. Service is impeccable: attentive, friendly, and genuinely passionate about sharing the magic of Indian cuisine. Every plate is presented with artistry, turning a meal into a feast for both the eyes and palate.

If you crave authentic Indian food prepared with skill and soul, look no further—this restaurant is a shining beacon of culinary excellence. A must-visit for every food lover! 🎩🔥
author: Acquin Linston Pinto

review_text: New restaurant at HillV2 that’s definitely worth a try. I came for the weekday lunch set and was pleasantly surprised by both the quality and the price. The food is tasty, portions are just right, and the set comes with everything you need for a satisfying meal. Staff were friendly and service was quite fast, which is great if you are on a lunch break. The place is clean and comfortable, with a nice casual atmosphere. Overall, very good value for money for weekday lunch in this area – will come back to try other dishes.
author: Dominikus Brian

review_text:
First time here and I’m impressed! 🍖 We missed out on the pork rib soup (lunch only—bummer!), but the Don Set did not disappoint. The prime beef rib was the star of the show—so soft! The pork belly and collar were also super high quality.

Don’t sleep on the cheese steamed egg; it’s silky, sweet, and delicious. Plus, you can get it for free right now just for reviewing your meal!

The staff are pros and will help you cook your meat to perfection. It’s a little pricey, but definitely worth it for the quality and service.
author: Mike Ngen

review_text: meat is great quality and yummy though a little pricey! ventilation in the restaurant is also good
author: emma tang

review_text:
Decided to try as we saw some good reviews and we found out it's because they are giving free drinks in exchange for reviews. Didn't partake in it as I wanted to share my true opinion and honestly, I would not recommend this place at all.

We ordered the pork belly and for $27+, there were only 9 pieces and the pork was tough and I've tried a fair share of kbbqs and this was definitely priced way higher for meat quality which was lacking. Sides were provided but midway through the meal, we realised that they didn't provide lettuce even though we were having grilled meat and maybe it is only served upon asking but every kbbq restaurant in sg and kr that i've been to always served it immediately or will let us know where the free-flow bar is.

Kimchi fried rice was another huge let down because it tasted nothing like kimchi and we had to keep asking for kimchi refills so that we could pair every bite with kimchi so we can get the kimchi flavour. For $15+, the portion and taste was not worth it at all.
author: Eunice Pang

review_text: It’s our first time here and we really enjoyed it. The meat is fresh and good quality, and the ambience is nice and cosy. Service was pleasant too. Will surely come back again!
author: Esther Hong

review_text: The restaurant's Christmas decorations are beautiful and create a wonderful, happy and comfortable atmosphere. There was a Santa Claus that went up and down tbh it was very cute❤️ plus the lights and Christmas tree were pretty
author: joyce

review_text:
Had a really pleasant experience at Burger King HillV2! The ambience of the store is clean, modern, and very comfortable. The seating area is spacious and well-maintained, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a meal with friends or family. The lighting and overall atmosphere feel calm and welcoming, not too noisy even during peak hours.

What impressed me the most was the fast service. The staff were friendly, efficient, and handled orders quickly without compromising on quality. My food was prepared fresh and served hot within just a few minutes. Even during busy periods, the team managed the queue smoothly and professionally.

The restaurant also maintains good hygiene standards, and the tables were cleared promptly. It’s definitely one of the better Burger King outlets I’ve visited in Singapore.

Overall, great ambience, fast delivery, and excellent customer service. Highly recommended if you’re around the Hillview area and craving a satisfying meal! Will definitely visit again. 👍🍔
author: Shafiq Mohamed Ayoob

review_text: Visiting Burger King today and had a good experience. Food was served hot and fresh, and the staff/manager were friendly and efficient Overall, a satisfying meal…I like the restaurant very clean
author: Owen Wen

review_text: Stopped by burger king after work and had smooth experience , service was efficient,staff were polite and food quality was consistent.The environment was clean and comfortable, making it a good sport for a quick breakfast
author: Sulekha Manikhandan

review_text: Seriously the worst breakfast service in decades. Ordered for take away at the counter but to my horror, BK staffs not only make on-site customer wait till they served finish their takeaway queue, but short give customers on the set meals. review_text:
We ordered a variety of dishes from Asia Wok at Timbre+ Hillview via GrabFood today, and it turned out to be a very satisfying, above-average meal. While not every dish was perfect, the overall quality and portion sizes were commendable.

​We tried:
​Spicy Chicken with Rice: The chicken itself was tasty, coated in a sauce that leaned more towards sweet and savoury rather than being particularly spicy. A pleasant dish, though the rice was a tad soft for my liking.

​Shrimp Fried Rice & Luncheon Meat Fried Rice: Both fried rice options were decent and had a noticeable wok hei. However, similar to the spicy chicken dish, the rice texture in both was slightly on the softer side. The flavours were agreeable but quite mild.

​Sin Chew Bee Hoon: This was enjoyable. The bee hoon was cooked well, not too firm, and had a decent amount of ingredients mixed in. Again, the flavour profile was pleasant but mild.

​Fried Beef Hor Fun (Dry): This was the clear winner of the meal. They used the very broad type of hor fun, which held up really well and had a fantastic, slightly chewy texture – definitely not soft or mushy. It had good wok hei and was the most satisfying dish of the lot, even with the milder seasoning.

​Across all the dishes, there was a consistent presence of wok hei, which is always appreciated. The flavours generally seemed geared towards a lighter, perhaps healthier, palate, as none were heavily salted or strongly seasoned. Portions were very generous for the price.

​Overall, Asia Wok is a solid 4-star choice for a zi char style delivery. It's reliable, offers good portions, and while the flavours are mild, the cooking is competent, especially the excellent Beef Hor Fun. Definitely worth trying again.

review_text:
UPDATE (31 Oct 2025):
I'm so glad I decided to return! I visited the stall again and ordered almost exactly the same thing: the dry version with kway teow.

I am happy to report that the order mix-up from my first visit was just an unfortunate one-off. This time, the order was perfect from the start, and the kway teow was excellent. It was not overcooked at all and had that smooth, elastic, and slightly chewy texture that I was looking for.

With the noodle component now matching the high quality of the YTF pieces, this was a flawless and delicious meal. The ingredients are still top-notch and flavourful. Upgrading this to a well-deserved 5 stars. This is a top-tier YTF spot!

PREVIOUS REVIEW (4 Stars):
I decided to try Zi Jia Yong Tau Foo at Timbre+ Hillview, and my experience was a mix of highs and lows. The quality of the yong tau foo itself is fantastic and definitely a highlight.

Let's start with the best part: the ingredients. Each piece of yong tau foo I selected was fresh, flavourful, and expertly cooked. The fried items had a wonderful savoury taste, and the stuffed pieces were delicious. In terms of the core product, the quality is easily comparable to other top-tier YTF stalls I've enjoyed.

Unfortunately, there was a mix-up with my order which affected the final dish. I had ordered the dry version with kway teow, but I was initially served the soup version with the YTF pieces on the side. To their credit, they were quick to rectify it. However, the method of correction—simply pouring the soup away from the noodles and then combining everything into a dry bowl—seemed to have an unfortunate side effect.

I'm not sure if this was the direct cause, but the kway teow ended up being overcooked, soft, and mushy, lacking that smooth, springy texture that makes the dish enjoyable.

Despite the disappointing noodles, the meal was saved by the sheer quality of the yong tau foo pieces. For that reason, I'm giving it a solid 4 stars. I would definitely be willing to return, as the ingredients are clearly top-notch. Next time, I'll be sure to double-check my order and perhaps try a different noodle option.

review_text:
Our family has been loyal fans of Jew Kit at Bukit Timah Shopping Centre for years; it's one of our favourite chicken rice spots. I was so glad to find out they had opened a branch at The Rail Mall and decided to visit for a late lunch today (3.15pm).

The good news is that the quality is absolutely there. The restaurant itself is beautifully decorated, with lovely Peranakan-style tiles and comfortable seating—a proper restaurant setting, not a food court.

I ordered the Steamed Drumstick with Rice ($8.30) and a small Thai Style Fried Beancurd ($9.00). The chicken was classic Jew Kit: incredibly smooth (with their signature collagen), succulent, moist, and tender. The rice was also perfectly cooked—fragrant, plump, and with distinct grains (粒粒分明). The chilli and (my personal must-have) the thick, dark soy sauce were all of high quality. The Thai Style Fried Beancurd was also a great side dish, with a crispy exterior, soft inside, and a refreshing, tangy Thai sauce with shredded vegetables.

Now, for the reason I'm giving this a 4-star instead of a 5: the price. I fully understand that the overheads for a beautifully renovated, full-service restaurant at The Rail Mall are high. However, at $8.30 for a single plate of chicken drumstick with rice and $9.00 for a small side of tofu, the pricing feels very steep and does impact the "value for money" aspect.

It's a bit of a dilemma. The food quality is 5-star, but the value is what holds it back. This is definitely a "premium" chicken rice experience, and while delicious, the high price makes it more of a treat than a regular go-to.

The viscous consistency did not really work in their favour, as I found the soup tasty but not the most appetising. Its temperature was lukewarm at best, would have been much better if it were hot.

Taste wise, the soup's got it. However, the texture and temperature did not make this a desired dish when talking about Mee Soto.

They had a whole pile of chicken, which for $4 was very reasonable. Yet, it was mostly chunks of breast meat, and an occassional one piece thigh meat with the nice skin.  The meat wasn't a huge plus.

Overall, wasnt the most pleased with their Mee Soto. Also the spiciness level is pretty high so be warned.

review_text:
Stepping into Tu Chefs feels like being welcomed into a space where culinary artistry and genuine hospitality meet in perfect harmony. The experience is defined not only by the sophistication of the menu but also by the warmth and passion of the chefs, who clearly take pride in what they create and in how they share it.

The menu at Tu Chefs is impressively diverse, weaving together influences from multiple cultures in a way that feels both seamless and intentional. Each dish demonstrates a mastery of technique and a refined palate—flavors are layered with precision, balancing creativity with a deep respect for authenticity. What stands out most is the restraint and refinement; the food is never overdone, but instead highlights the natural character of the high-quality ingredients at its core.

This is fine dining at its best—an elegant yet approachable experience. Each plate feels thoughtfully composed, from the artistry of presentation to the subtle nuances of seasoning. You can taste the quality of the produce, the freshness of the seafood, and the richness of carefully selected meats, all elevated by globally inspired flavors that speak to the chefs’ creativity and skill.

Equally memorable is the atmosphere fostered by the team. The chefs themselves are not hidden behind the scenes but are friendly, engaging, and genuinely eager to share their passion. That personal touch—paired with the meticulous execution of the food—creates an experience that is at once refined, heartfelt, and unforgettable.

Tu Chefs is more than just a restaurant; it is a celebration of culinary diversity, craftsmanship, and hospitality. A meal here is not simply eaten, but savored, leaving you both satisfied and inspired to return.

review_text:
Delightful place for Indian vegetarians to enjoy Mala!

Although I'm non-vegetarian, there are too many vegetarian friends who skip Mala since there's non-veg in the broth or utensils/ingredients get mixed.

Green on Earth is your answer- fully veg restaurant which offers Mala, with the best variety of noodles and veggies (including capsicum!)

This is one of the few places which still achieves that signature Mala peppercorn numbness on the tongue. A lot of other places now just blast it with chillies for spice instead of flavour.

The restaurant is spacious and well lit. The staff are prompt and no main details (cutlery, napkins etc.) are missed out.

Highly highly recommend your next Mala meal to be at Green on Earth!

restaurant_name: Springleaf Prata Place - The Rail Mall
review_text:
Visited Springleaf Prata at Rail Mall today, and it was one of the better experiences I’ve had there. The prata was impressively crispy—light, flaky, and cooked to the perfect golden brown without being oily. Just the kind of texture that makes you want to order a second piece.

The curry was also on point. It had a rich, full-bodied flavour and, importantly, wasn’t watery at all. Instead, it had the right thickness to cling to the prata, making every bite satisfying.

Overall, both the prata and curry were really good today. Definitely a worthwhile stop if you’re craving a solid prata fix.
author: ar_kanji

restaurant_name: Springleaf Prata Place - The Rail Mall
review_text:
⭐ Springleaf Prata (Upper Bukit Timah) – Solid comfort food, great flavours, and no-frills satisfaction ⭐
Had a really good experience tonight at Springleaf Prata’s Upper Bukit Timah outlet. We came for a simple supper and ended up enjoying every dish.

The Dosa was beautifully crisp on the outside and soft inside — exactly how a good dosa should be. The trio of chutneys and dhal were surprisingly flavourful; the sambar had a nice warmth without being overpowering.

The Kothu Prata was the highlight. Generous portion, well-spiced, and full of flavour. You can really taste the wok heat in every bite. Paired perfectly with the curry served on the side.

Drinks: Their Teh O and Teh Tarik were both well-balanced — not too sweet, and the froth on the Teh Tarik was just right. A proper comfort drink to end the meal.

Service was quick despite the crowd, and food arrived hot and fresh. It’s a straightforward, relaxed supper spot — exactly what you expect from a reliable prata place, and they delivered.

📍 Upper Bukit Timah Springleaf Prata
If you’re in the area and craving something hearty, tasty, and comforting, this outlet doesn’t disappoint.

Will definitely be back.

PS: we were here at 2am; Friday morning

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ The Rail Mall
review_text:
Gong Yuan Ma La Tang offers a straightforward take on the popular Sichuan-style mala soup, but unfortunately, it doesn’t quite hit the mark.

Soup & Ingredients

The broth was decent, carrying the expected numbing and spicy kick, but nothing particularly stood out. The ingredients were fresh, though the overall experience felt quite generic—comparable to any other mala tang chain.

Condiments

The peanut sauce was a letdown. Instead of the rich, creamy nuttiness that enhances mala flavors, it was overly diluted and lacked depth. If you’re looking for that signature thick and fragrant peanut dip, this won’t satisfy.

Egg Bomb

This was a disappointment. It was excessively oily, which took away from the enjoyment. A good egg bomb should have a crisp yet slightly fluffy texture, but this one leaned too much on the greasy side.

Overall Verdict

Nothing fantastic. It’s an okay choice if you’re craving mala tang in the area, but there’s nothing particularly memorable about it. With better mala spots around Singapore, this wouldn’t be my top pick.

⭐ Rating: 2.5/5
