review_text:
We have been members at Fu Lin Men (Temasek Club) for over a year, but this is my first time writing a review. We chose this spot for our first family meal of 2026, and once again, they delivered.

​The Dim Sum:
The standard here is consistently high. The kitchen executes the classics very well:

​Steamed Items: The Xiao Long Baos were excellent—delicate skin with plenty of soup inside. The Steamed Prawn Dumplings (Har Gow) and Siu Mai were also fresh and bouncy, just as we like them.

​Fried/Baked Items: The Pan-Fried Meat Dumplings deserve a special mention for being perfectly golden and crisp on the bottom while juicy inside. We also enjoyed the Crispy Beancurd Skin Prawn Roll which was fried to perfection.

​Mains & Others:
If you need carbs, the Fried Noodles with Supreme Soy Sauce is a must-order; it has great wok hei and isn't too oily. The Century Egg and Pork Congee was incredibly smooth and comforting. We also tried the Crispy Eggplant with Chicken Floss and Salt and Pepper White Bait, both of which were addictive appetizers.

​Verdict:
Reliable, high-quality Cantonese food in a comfortable setting. We will continue to patronize them as long as they maintain this standard. Highly recommended for family gatherings.
author: Wiz Yeo

restaurant_name: Fu Lin Men Cantonese Dining (Temasek Club)
review_text:
We had an early reunion dinner at one of our favourite restaurants Fu LI Men,  and this is the first time we asked for a room with a table for 13 pax.
We had pre-ordered an 8-course Set-menu called Greatest Robustness Set. The food was so good and also pleasing to the eyes, I was too busy enjoying eating to have taken photos.

The LoHei had sun-dried fish maw and salmon and we had super long chopsticks, no backache to toss and retrieve, hehe.
Then followed by double-broiled Buddha Jumps Over The wall soup ( so flavourful), sized 5H Abalone with shiitake mushroom & asparagus spears, baked Lobster with creamy pumpkin sauce, steamed Star Garoupa (so fresh), fengsha Chicken with honey glaze, lotus leaf flavoured Rice (i finished my bowl of rice; normally avoid carbo at dinners) & individual-orders of preferred  dessert.

Attached the photos from a cousin  of the abalone and the lobster; it was most tender and very delicious.
I would say the flavours and texture of the food were exactly what they ought to be. Crisp for the bite, soft and tender when it was meant to be and excellent  flavours in the different blends for taste.

The desserts were  individual preferences and among us 13 persons, we had ordered the full variety available and it was all good.  My favourite dessert here ( I often picked the same ) was the “palate cleansing and good on the indigestive system after an 8-course dinner” lemongrass jelly with sherbet.

The team led by Zhang Ping; were  Kimmy, Helen  and Lily.
Zhang Ping even took note of our 91 year old mom what she likes, Chili padi, topping up an ice bucket ice as she likes her tea with lots of ice, cut up the food items which are harder for her to manage, de-shell l the lobster etc.. it’s the little niceties that add to the pleasantness, small things like differentiating the teapots with a rubber band.

We are familiar with this team and they have been always so welcoming and their service is top notch.

So what’s not to like, good food and wonderful staff ❤️❤️
author: PHINE

restaurant_name: Fu Lin Men Cantonese Dining (Temasek Club)
review_text:
Came on a Sat morning and was not crowded. Chance upon this when I was googling for Dim sum around the west and was totally blown away. The dim sum was very tasty and not too salty….good variety of dim sum. The only thing they do not have is Cheong Fun but all is good.

The staff are all very attentive and friendly. Ambience is really nice and cosy. Highly recommended for a dim sum brunch with family. Thank you very much for the really pleasant dining experience!
author: Celia Liu

restaurant_name: Fu Lin Men Cantonese Dining (Temasek Club)
review_text:
🍽️❤️Not thirsty after the meal!
Highly reputable Cantonese restaurant, tucked away in a peaceful environment amidst the bustling city, making it a must-visit for those who love Cantonese cuisine.

The restaurant offers a spacious and comfortable setting with elegant decor, creating a warm atmosphere that is perfect for family gatherings or special occasions. In terms of food, whether it's dim sum or main dishes, they showcase a high level of culinary skill. The classic Peking duck has crispy skin and tender meat, paired with crispy bean curd skin, spring onions, and cucumbers, creating a perfect balance of flavors. The duck drumsticks are cooked with a special sweet sauce, offering a unique taste.

As for the dim sum, the mini egg tarts, radish cake, and char siu pastry all stood out with exceptional texture and flavor.

Overall, Fu Lin Men not only preserves the authentic taste of Cantonese cuisine but also offers excellent service and thoughtful details. It is truly a top-tier Chinese restaurant that you’ll want to return to time and time again.
author: bear zucca

restaurant_name: Fu Lin Men Cantonese Dining (Temasek Club)
review_text:
Went to this Chinese restaurant on a weekday with my wife to celebrate her birthday. The manager 张平 was very attentive. Presented their various dishes, the current special offers and tea.
He even presented 寿包 in decorating.
The Peking Duck is a must to try.
Fried rice with the duck meat is also great.
张平's recommendation to try the Chinese tea using snow chrysanthemum was really good.
They also have nice desserts to end with.
author: foxplayz 132

review_text: Having a private room made it a comfortable and relaxed lunch, where the kid can run around freely. The live singing was a special added touch and lifted the atmosphere. Food-wise, it was delicious and there was plenty. Everyone left full and happy. Big thanks to Zijie for letting my nephew try the drum set, which he was eyeing since the start. Thanks for a great experience!
author: Kai Y

review_text:
This is the 2nd private dining I tried. The first at Cairnhill was disappointing as you're force to pay for 6 pax even though we've only 3 pax and they serve food for 3 only. But not for Pudgy Grill, he said min. 4 pax and I only have 3 pax again and food is very average. Happy to pay for 4 pax and he did prepare for 4 pax portion and allow us to takeaway. The food is A LOT. The wagyu A5 is too fatty for me. But the cod fish and unagi are very good. I love the octopus, can't touch the pork at all as is just too much. I ate a lot of their delicious Japanese rice as I was so hungry (mistake).

They can improve by display more different types of wine glasses before we arrive (knowing I'm bringing champagne and wine). Ice should be plenty for us. Dessert ice cream is cute but the flavor (soursop) is not everyone's cup of tea. Maybe a very good Vanilla will suffice.

Overall the setting is perfect as we are in a big room with ensuite toilet just for us. I would go again but must ensure I choose 3 super big eaters who love MEAT.
author: Ohayo Oreo

review_text: The food was scrumptious and the attention to detail was amazing. The portions are so generous and I cannot tell you how much my wife and I enjoyed your food! Best fine dining experience we have ever had. Would come again for your amazing A5 Wagyu and Cod fish❤️❤️❤️
author: M Z

review_text: Really friendly couple paired with really good food. To quote my family member: "can cook, can sing, your wife is so lucky." Would recommend anyone to come try this amazing private dining experience.
author: Uber LZM

review_text:
We just had the most incredible private dining experience, and it was absolutely fantastic! The highlight for me was undoubtedly the Wagyu steak – it was so unbelievably tender and truly melted in the mouth. Even my mum, who isn't typically a fan of steaks, absolutely loved this one, which says a lot!

Beyond the steak, all the other dishes served were equally amazing. My personal favourite was the cod fish, which was perfectly cooked and incredibly flavourful.

What truly elevated the evening were the hosts. Service was great, and we were even treated to a lovely song! It was such a warm and personal touch that made the experience even more memorable.
author: M Quek

review_text:
Inori Japanese Dining is a quiet neighbourhood Japanese restaurant with a peaceful setting. The food was decent and nicely presented, though prices are on the higher side, especially for the special fish. The set meals felt more reasonably priced and are probably a better choice for value. The chirashi dons were a definite highlight — packed with fresh, generous portions of sashimi and seafood.

Service was attentive, perhaps a little too eager. The waiters introduced the special fishes even before we were properly seated and hovered around the table, trying to clear plates even after we said we were still eating, which made the meal feel a bit rushed.

Overall, it’s a calm place with good food, especially the chirashi dons, but the dining experience could be improved with a more relaxed service approach

Will we come back again? Maybe
author: Yahui Lin

review_text: Had a wonderful lunch at Inori Japanese Restaurant! The service was excellent and the ambience cosy, perfect for any occasion. The fish was incredibly fresh, flown in directly from Japan twice a week and can be served in many delicious ways, from sashimi to grilled dishes. Head Chef Steven is truly an expert, every dish was prepared with great skill and attention to detail. Special thanks to the restaurant manager for the great recommendations on side dishes. Their sake selection was impressive too. We will definitely be back!
author: Cathy Fong

review_text: Had a really great meal at Inori Japanese Dining. The food was fresh and well-presented — especially the sashimi and sushi rolls. Portions were satisfying and the prices are very reasonable for the quality. Service was also friendly with staff checking in at the right time without being pushy. Will definitely come back again 👍
author: Calvin Hooi

review_text: It is truly a gem in the west. Tucked inside the St Francis Xavier church grounds, it has a nice and quiet ambience. The decor is simple and modern but the quality of the food is what stands out. We had the premium and Inori chirashi dons, and teriyaki chicken don. The chirashi dons were packed with fresh and generous portions of sashimi and seafood. Whereas the teriyaki chicken was juicy and tasty. Service was very good where the servers were keen to recommend other items not in the menu, and yet not pushy. Overall a very good experience and would definitely come back. Great value.
author: Meng Yau

review_text: Great service, excellent food. I had the chirashi don, it was above and beyond sushi tei standards. It was so good I had to pause and enjoy the flavours. My friend had the salmon mental don which was great. However, I feel that the monkfish liver wasn’t impressive. Nonetheless still love it. Also, lots of free ample parking in the Catholic Church compound. Amazing. Highly recommended.
author: Karen

review_text:
This place serves undoubtedly the WORST salted egg chicken rice ever. Instead of a salted egg sauce, they serve a plate of gluey, pathetic dry chicken bits that has NO salted egg in it at all. And why are there small bits that look like tofu in it??
The entire plate was a starchy mess and no salted egg taste at all!
Paid extra to add a sunny side up and the egg came half of it hanging OUTSIDE the plate. The server said sorry n started blaming the kitchen. I can only say both the kitchen and server take no pride in their work because none of them bother to put the egg back into the plate. They both chose to serve it knowing that this is not presentable. When feedback was given to the lady boss(?), she didn’t even apologise and just simply walked away.
Hello, customers are not beggars ok!
The photos n bad reviews say it all. Regretted not reading up the on reviews before choosing to dine in.
For sure this will be my first and last time there.
Both food and service attitude 👎🏻
author: JLT

review_text:
Impeccable service :)

Ordered the cereal chicken - felt that the cereal wasnt enough - asked for a top up. Store generously topped up for us.

Sambal kangkong was too spicy. Staff saw us sweating and offered us iced water + tissue FOC. Will def recommend to friends.
author: Dave Chan

review_text:
The worst ever Zichar stall, wonder how they are still operating for so long. Salted egg chicken didn’t taste like it, dry beef horfun looks like char kway teow and taste bad. Regretted not looking at the review before patronising.

Photo as shown, is what we had and we left the cafe for other food as it is really bad to even continue eating.
author: flyfly

review_text:
Like what others said, this is truly the WORST salted egg chicken rice ($6.50), if it is, ever. Probably the worst thing i have ever had. Not even joking. I laughed to myself because it is so bad.
First, it isn't even salted egg. There is no element of salt or egg in it. It is just mushy gooey taste mixed with water. It's repulsive even.

Do not ever buy it. Don't even try.
Second, the attitude of the service staff is just bad. It's as if we owed her a business. Will not return.
author: Lee JI

review_text: The salted egg chicken did not taste like salted egg at all and also there was a weird aftertaste. First and last time, expected to be better then this. I was still hungry so i popped by next door The Grumpy Bear to eat more.
author: E M

review_text: Fabulous place to get local fare for a relaxing breakfast. The curry for the roti was excellent; the sambal balacan exceptional for the cheung fun and in the nasi lemak; and the kaya authentic. The panoramic view of the golf course and gentle breeze did not hurt.
author: Elaine C

review_text:
The food at The Lookout is always very nicely prepared and caters to the healthier palate. Not too oily or salty, just right for our family.

On weekends, service can get a little hectic due to the crowd, but during weekdays and off-peak hours the team is very friendly and cheery. Veteran staff will always make sure you are well-taken care of.

After a recent overhaul, it is more airy and breezy. On lazy weekdays, it is a nice place to just let the mind slow down and enjoy a cuppa.
author: YT Teo

review_text: Nice ambiance with cool breeze on a hot afternoon. We ordered Braised Duck Rice, Ham, Cold noodles and Ice Kachang. The cold noodles is under Japanese menu but it is actually Chinese cold noodles with mala flavour. It is quite misleading and we have feed back to the restaurant.
author: Carol Yuen

review_text: A great place to chill and relax, tried the local delight. Laksa, fried beef kway teow, beef hor fan and the chendol. Must try. If the Chendol ice can be more fine, it will be perfect.
author: Thomas Ng

review_text: Good local food with great wine/whisky selection/price. View is great. A bit hot though for the outdoor.
author: Bryan Wang

review_text:
Air conditioned bistro n bar. Service was attention n efficient. Has a mixture of local, western which includes pasta, soup, grills, burgers. Kids menu
Available. Good range if alcohol n non alcohol beverages. Unfortunately its payment can only be made by members. Ample open air carparks
author: Denis Nyam

review_text: Wah this Bistro @ SICC quite shiok leh. Went there last weekend for lunch after golf, weather hot until cannot tahan, so aircon dining room really save my life sia. The place very chill one, not too noisy, can relax and makan properly. I ordered the grilled salmon, medium doneness just nice, skin crispy, meat soft and juicy. The mashed potato smooth smooth, got buttery taste somemore. My friend took the wagyu burger, wah the patty thick and juicy, cheese melt until steady. Fries come hot and crispy, not those soggy kind lor. We also shared truffle mushroom soup; can smell the truffle from far already, quite power but a bit salty lah. Service quite fast, staff friendly and keep refilling water without asking. Price a bit on the high side, but for club standard still okay lah. Parking free somemore, so can. Best to book in advance if you going during weekend lunch, always full one.
author: Acacia Chua

review_text:
Came to check out the Miyazawa A5 Wagyu special for the month. The Miyazawa Wagyu beef fried rice was outstanding. The short grain rice took on bits of char after we mixed in the sauce and egg, and left in the hot plate for abit. Wok-hei-ious!
The braised Miyazawa beef was resoundingly the highlight! The meat was tender with just the right amount of grilled smokey surface. And the pepper sauce complemented it very well. We shared a cendol to finish off this wonderful meal. OMG this cendol brought back memory of Penang with the pandan cendol that’s kueh-like soft. Together with Gula Melaka in the coconut milk and fine shaved ice, it was the best cendol I had in Singapore.
We’ll be back 😁
author: M L

review_text:
My family has been eating here (and at the sister outdoor Lookout cafe with the same kitchen) for many many years, and we've seen the food quality go up and down and back again.

In the last couple of years, they've tried to improve the menu and bring in specials, some of which work better than others. In this case, they're having a Japanese Miyazaki beef special and the offerings look good so we decide to try.

I was there with my wife and mom around 11:15am. Not crowded at that time even on Saturday, and we had out pick of tables. We got one next to the glass walls overlooking the ponds, so quite relaxing view.

Foodwise, we were there for the beef so we had the Slow Roast Crusted Miyazawa Wagyu Brisket, the Miyazawa Wagyu Hamburg (medium rare) and the Miyazawa Wagyu Beef Fried Rice, with an Energizer salad to start and a chendol (shared three ways) to finish.

The beef fried rice came first. See the picture (and video) for how it's served on a hot plate that you add a sauce and mix. If you leave it for a while, the hot plate gives everything a nice char. They use the medium grain rice so has a beautiful crust and tastes amazing. The beef is a bit lost in the sauce but likely the fat from the beef contributes to the overall taste.

The Energizer salad has lots of spinach leaves, blueberries, other veges, quinoa and root vegetables and comes with a purple dressing that is very thick. This is obviously on the healthy side of things and it tasted great. Could do with a bit of lemon juice and olive oil (personal taste) to balance the spinach but we asked for more dressing and it was okay.

The Hamburg was a disappointment. It's layered starting with mash potato, then a very strong tasting portobello (overwhelmed all the other tastes), then the beef burger (seems to be pure beef with no fillers or anything to hold it together) and topped with a deep fried cheese ball. Tastes didn't blend together and I think we should have asked for the beef to be well done.

The Brisket on the other hand was excellent! Lots of fat in layers and the slow braise brings out the flavours. It's accompanied by potatoes and a sauce but the beef is amazing just eaten by itself.

Lastly we just had space to share one chendol between the three of us. Good gula melaka, lots of coconut milk and the chendol tasted fresh and home made; soft with pandan flavours rather than what you get from hawker centres. As good as any chendol you'll get in M'sia.

We'll definitely try and come back before the beef specials are over. Try a few more dishes, maybe round 2 on the Brisket but definitely avoid the Hamburg again!
author: Mun Kew Leong

review_text: Food here is good. Great variety between local and western fare. Local food is hawker fare, and is authentic enough, while being much healthier (for E.g. the fried carrot cake is not oily and not salty). I love the ambience too. You're nestled in greenery surrounded by trees, and it's definitely very away from the hustle and bustle of the city.
author: Kenny Y

restaurant_name: Delifrance Singapore - Windsor Cheers Express Corner
author: Kevin Yoong

restaurant_name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
review_text:
Came here for their signature Bijin Nabe, and overall it was a satisfying and comforting hotpot experience.

The chicken collagen broth is the highlight — rich, silky and clean-tasting without being overly greasy. You can really tell it’s been simmered properly, and it becomes more flavourful as the ingredients cook. The white fish and prawns were fresh, sweet and cooked beautifully in the broth. The mushroom platter was generous and well-selected, adding natural umami depth to the soup.

I also liked the option to add beauty noodles at the end — light, springy, and a good way to soak up the remaining broth without feeling too heavy. Portions were adequate for sharing, and the meal felt balanced rather than indulgent.

The restaurant itself is bright and comfortable, though it can get quite busy during peak hours, which makes the space a bit noisy. Service was generally attentive, but timing between items could be smoother when the restaurant is full. Pricing is on the higher side for hotpot, but understandable given the quality of ingredients and concept.

Overall, a solid choice for Japanese-style collagen hotpot — comforting, well-executed, and ideal for a relaxed meal with friends or family. Would return, especially when craving a nourishing broth.
author: Jeffrey

restaurant_name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
review_text:
Tbh I’m quite impressed with Tsukada Nojo! I’ve been wanting to try so I went on a weekday lunch for their lunch item - ramen! They use the same broth as they do in the hotpot, so you can get to try it without having to order a whole hotpot menu.

There’s 4 types of broths to choose from and 3 types of noodles. The signature shio broth is a must try! It’s rich and flavorful, without being too heavy/gelat. I really enjoyed this one and finished almost all the soup. We also tried the spicy one but I found that the chili covered the yummy taste of the collagen broth.

The noodles also comes with a plate of ingredients! Ramen egg was good, but what impressed me was the chicken! It’s actually served slightly chilled, but I rly enjoyed it. It’s lean meat but marinated so well. Super flavorful! Not fatty but still tender enough to eat!

The lunch set $1 add on is a must get! Onigiri was rly good! Flavorful and served hot!

Overall, we were really happy with this meal! Would return again!!
author: Rennie Lee

restaurant_name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
review_text: Thick and rich collagen soup, with one free refill of the base included in the price. Original was nice, and the tomato was good to have a different taste but could be more flavourful. Good quality veges and meat, but they don't provide any condiments/chilli which was a major disappointment. However, the surprising hit was the Chicken Nanban which was so delicious! Atmosphere-wise, not sure if the air conditioner wasn't working or something, as we felt pretty warm after some time.
author: Darren

restaurant_name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
review_text:
Konnichiwa dear loveliest Sakura, MJ, Kai & Jo

Arigato many thanks for your excellent services you gals rock keep it up, Happy Lunar New Year & otanjoubi omedetou means Happy Birthday to all of you, have a great CNY's lunch & dinner with your loveliest families always kiotsukete means take good care dears....^-^....

Best regards
Yukiko Kaneshiro
author: Coco Tay

restaurant_name: Tsukada Nojo || Japanese Premium Hotpot || Collagen-rich Chicken Stock || Thomson Plaza
review_text: Went for dinner at the Thomson Plaza branch. Popular for their collagen soup. Was nice but prices aren't cheap. Items were fresh & nice. Opens daily 11.30am to 3pm, 5 to 10pm.
author: Rosalind Lim

review_text: Fuss free cafe with super speedy service. Food arrives really fast. Great if you're in a hurry. Portion is big & generous. Pastas are nice, localised home style so don't expect Italian version cooking. I've been back at Zeppin twice with my colleagues. Service is 5 stars.
author: Amy Leong

review_text: I am writing a review on the 2nd visit. I enjoy the cozy atmosphere and service feels attentive and caring. The food is very varied but I get a Taiwanese cafe style vibe from it. Food-wise, although they may not hit the mark of Japanese and Western food authenticity, their fusion style is delicious enough to be good on their own. I recommend their ramen and dry ramen.
author: Chocs N'Socks

review_text: Friendly and fast service, and the food is reasonably priced. Our food and drinks came within 5 minutes of ordering. The aglio olio is very flavourful, and my girl loves the chicken nuggets, they taste fresh and not like the usual frozen kind.
author: S S

review_text:
Was shopping at Midview City with my SO when a sudden heavy thunderstorm hit 🌧️⚡️

Totally stuck inside the industrial building, we quickly Googled and found a café located in the same building — perfect excuse to slow down and wait for the rain to pass.

Ordered a few items to pass the time:

🍵 Matcha Green Tea Frappé
Ice-blended and refreshing, but a little too sweet for my liking. Could still taste the matcha, though the sweetness slightly overpowered it.

☕ Mocha Frappé
This one was nice — very similar to the ice-blended mocha from big coffee chains, but priced slightly lower, which is always a plus.

🥟 Vietnamese Fried Spring Rolls (4-Piece Combo)
Freshly fried and crispy! Two of them were prawn spring rolls, and they were really yummy.

The café has a nice, cozy environment, great for sitting down, reading, and enjoying drinks while waiting out the rain.

Good food, comfortable space, and a perfect hideout on a rainy day. 🌧️✨

If you’re nearby, do drop by and give it a try!

author: Mealsphotos

review_text: Tried this place by chance as I was nearby. Ordered ramen, seafood noodles and fried rice. I am pleasantly surprised that all tasted good. Price wise is also very reasonable. The staff is very genuine and friendly. I would return again to try the other dishes if I am near here again
author: Patrick Chia

review_text:
So good! The chicken was succulent and well roasted - the breast wasn’t hard. UFO oyster omelette was surprisingly good and creative.

Black Hokkien Mee and Ngoh Hiang not my style but my family approved.

Would be back! Parking is quite savage on Sunday evenings because of the older restaurants nearby which appear popular for multi generation family dinners involving wheelchairs, strollers and children tumbling out of multiple doors everywhere.
author: Kiku C

review_text:
1/10/2023
Back here again, food and service still as amazing!!

2022
Great restaurant. Great service, food was great and their portion is big. Would definitely recommend to all! Celebrated my uncles birthday here! Thoroughly enjoyed ourselves! Staff was accommodating as well! :)
author: Zatarie Hoe

review_text: The food was really good, especially the crispy omelette with chili sauce and oysters, chicken and fish. All were fresh and tasty. The dishes were different from usual Chinese restaurants and I really enjoyed the meal there. Service was prompt and place was clean, great for family meals.
author: Jan

review_text:
Pretty good Hokkien delicacies. But as other reviewers had mentioned, the service can be slow and lacking. They have no service charge or GST over here though. How about a fair bit of give and take?

It wouldn't be a pleasant sight if most we get are standardised same tasting food across big F&B chains. We don't actually have alot of such small restaurant establishments left in Singapore, more will disappear if we gonna be all that harsh. Give them some time to improve. ;)

My favorites from this meal were Xiamen oyster omelette, Beijing roast duck, orh nee with gingko, qing long cai and gong fu chicken.

Can't wait to try more next time!
author: Fluffy Jing

review_text: Nice Hokkien restaurant serving traditional dishes. Try their version of UFO which is the deep fried bun with oyster. Love the traditional Hokkien Mee also with thick gravy and that flavour that only comes with pork lard, love it! Must try!
author: Chong Peng How

review_text:
This Sembawang Hill Food Centre have about 2 dozens of stalls. Small but sufficient fill your belly.

Since it's breakfast time, ordered my usual breakfast set. The bread is well toasted, eggs are perfectly half boiled, coffee sweetness is on spot.

There's no rush and pressure in toasting and spreading the breads. With a cool head and heart, come the perfect crisp toasted bread.

Ordered an additional kopi O, it's a good cup of kopi, with perfect sweetness and not compromising the coffee aroma.

Highly recommend this stall for your favourite coffee.
author: Terence Tan

review_text: came on a saturday morning around 9.30am and there was a snacking queue here! tried their traditional kaya toast set & taro toast. kaya toast was thin & crispy with the right amount of kaya. eggs and kopi were all right, appreciate if the egg yolks could be runnier. taro toast was a letdown - taro spread tasted like a blend of coconut & white chocolate..? not a huge fan. props to them for the innovative idea though!
author: Joy Ong

review_text:
here bright and early at 630am — overall great value for the quality

- tea c kosong was warm and rich with subtle sweetness
- half boiled eggs were perfect, not undercooked nor overcooked, imo better than Yakun
- bun was good (toasted for you)
- lady at store was polite and patient
- turnaround was quick, there were two folks infront of me but i got mine within 5 mins (needed to toast the bread and warm the eggs)
author: My2Cents

review_text: If you like traditional kaya toast and soft-boiled eggs, then you should visit this cafe. Toast was crispy and loaded with generous amount of kaya butter. Half boiled eggs were really soft and runny. Definitely recommended and worth a visit.
author: Stanley

review_text: Definitely the best tea at Sembawang Hills Food Court but disappointing that the teh peng, emperors bun and peanut butter toast came on polystyrene plates and with disposable cutlery even thigh we dined in
author: Lindsey Ong

review_text:
I had a wonderful experience at this coffeeshop. The food was absolutely delicious—fresh, flavorful. Every dish tasted thoughtfully prepared, and you could really tell the ingredients were high quality.

The service was just as impressive. The staff was friendly, attentive, and made sure everything arrived quickly and exactly as ordered. They created a warm, welcoming atmosphere that made the meal even more enjoyable.

Overall, it was a fantastic dining experience, and I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for great food and excellent service.
author: Min Yeo

review_text: Pleasant dining experience here. Plenty of tables which minimised waiting time. Food was served extremely quick and most dishes are in affordable price range even during CNY period. Great variety and enjoyed the meal very much.
author: Travis Lim

review_text: A decent zichar store near Brighthill MRT! Overall dishes were not bad Tried their signature butter pork ribs, which was good. Surprisingly the ribs itself were rly tender!! Fried rice and fried noodles were not bad, flavorful! Tofu and vege dish was okay. Fried yam was nice but would be better if they cut it slightly smaller!
author: Rennie Lee

review_text: Might be partial because I love Zi Char but the Butter Pork Ribs lathered in milk powder was delicious- tofu and french beans were also great when paired with white rice. Not sure if this outlet beats the original, but it was certainly good enough for me.
author: Francis Ethan Wee

review_text:
Revisit Two Chefs after a long while.
Food is still good, especially their signature butter milk pork ribs (actually it's milk powder ribs lah). Food was served relatively fast as we went during off peak period. Glad that they can customize some dishes to accommodate some food allergies.
Do support them as they are being blocked by the construction of new MRT line.
author: Ben Lau

review_text: Quite pricey for the portion that was served. Platter for 2 for about $40, and it feels like platter for 1. As a small eater, after eating, my stomach can take another platter for 2. If you are a big eater and a small spender, you might want to choose another mookata place.
author: Truth Fairy

review_text: not crowded and we enjoyed ourselves! my friend, Louie Cyril, came all the way down from Philippines just to try mookata for the first time and he was taken aback by how delicious the meat was!
author: Jarryl

review_text:
There's a change of menu and the chilli sauce.. the signature spicy chilli doesn't taste the same anymore.
They also removed the big bottles of mineral water, which was easy to serve for a family.
author: xtine x

review_text: Great, fresh food at reasonable prices, with the comfort of air-conditioning. This outlet truly stands out from the rest, the quality and flavors are noticeably better. I’ll definitely be coming back again, especially to this branch whenever I’m craving mookata.
author: Alex Pang

review_text: Used to passby this restaurant a few times while on the way to having desserts on the same stretch of shops. Have noticed it is always very crowded with many patrons waiting outside for their table. Finally, I had craving for Mookata and I came to this shop, arrived early around 6:40pm and there was only 1 other table occupied. Was surprised by the reasonable price and quality of the food. The taste is great, love the chilli sauce and when asked for more, the refill was superbly generous. Love the American beef, taste really great! Will definitely be back again! Highly recommended
author: Sebastian Teo

review_text:
Not the best in Singapore but...

I have eaten so many braise duck that I have lost count. We kept coming to this place, because of my Teochew friend. He loves to patronise this place.

Now for the truth... the braise duck is good, though a little salty for my liking. I do prefer their braise pork, but usually by the time we arrived, they will sold out. The white rice are basically cheap grain rice but the taste will improved when drown with the gravy. The porridge will be far better if it is still available. It is so smooth and with a little sauce it tasted amazing. We usually ordered half a duck (if there are more than 4 of us, a whole duck) with gizzards.

The most outstanding dish in my opinion is the salted vegetable,and peppery double boiled duck soup. The is appetising and satisfying.

For service, we were impressed with the friendliness of the store owner despite being so busy. One of the ladies who served us is living calculator. One occasion, a customer challenges her as he has doubted that she is able to give the total price almost instantly as he had bought so much, dine in and also takeaway. He whipped out his handphone and used a calculator apps to calculate. That lady patiently breakdown each item, and she was right eventually. I was standing behind the customer and saw the whole ordeal and was totally amazed. That make customer did not apologise for his behaviour... wahlau.

Anyway the place are industrial area so atmosphere is rowdy and dirty. The standard of a great ambience or cleanliness must lowered.

A video clip I saw on Facebook claiming this is the braise duck in Singapore... no way!

Ps. We ordered Char Siew and Roast pork from another stall... the Char Siew (fatty ones) is absolutely heavenly.
author: troo foo

review_text: One of the best duck rice in town. The duck is braised in such a manner that the meat is tender and flavorful. The salted vegetables duck soup is also a must order. The queue at the stall is never ending. Be be prepared to queue for your food. Strongly recommended
author: Jason Tan

review_text: Once you get famous, you have an attitude that’s life, seen the owner or the lady owner telling people off when they ask for more sauce n stuff. . She refuse to give extra source even the guy ordered a lot food. I think it could be better last time now still a little bit tough not as soft it used to be, but it’s tasty Atmosphere not the best industrial Park the old place. Coffee shop is better but still a famous place for duck
author: TSage

review_text:
Located in an industrial park area, this stall serves up hearty, satisfying duck dishes. We ordered a plate of braised duck rice for two and a bowl of salted vegetable duck soup.

The duck soup was the clear standout — rich, deeply flavorful, and wonderfully comforting. You can really taste the essence of the duck in every spoonful. The braised duck rice was tasty and well-executed, though it didn’t particularly stand out with any unique twist or flavor note.

Still, with the generous portions, satisfying flavors, and honest cooking, it easily earns a solid 5 stars from me.
author: Kwong Fei Yee

review_text:
The duck was beautifully stewed—soft, tender, and comforting with every bite. The braised pork was a standout for me: rich in flavor, melt-in-the-mouth, and without any overpowering porkiness. But the true star of the table was the salted vegetable duck soup. Peppery, hearty, and soul-warming, it’s the perfect bowl to chase away the chill on a rainy day.

Be sure to come early though—the lunch crowd descends quickly, and long queues are part of the experience at this bustling coffee shop.
author: KC Wong

review_text:
Not a big traditional food centre, but it is clean and well maintained.

For vegans and vegetarians, there are stalls serving delicious food such as Pawon Vegetarian (Indonesian/Malay cuisine) and Delisnacks, which offers traditional local snacks like You Tiao (fried dough sticks). Other stalls also provide meatless options, including fried carrot cake and traditional toast sets.

Prices in this food centre are reasonable and not expensive.
It’s a great place for a satisfying meal or simply a nice coffee break.
author: Yellow Bear

review_text:
Visited this hawker centre on a Saturday morning around 9.30am and it was already pretty crowded! It’s a small, cosy hawker centre with just two rows of stalls, but there’s a surprisingly good mix — noodles, rice dishes, and plenty of breakfast bites like curry puffs, popiah and fritters. There’s also a clean, well-maintained washroom and lots of sinks, which is nice.

I originally queued for Jing Ji Fishball Noodles, but the line barely moved... after 30 minutes, it only went from 12 people ahead of me to about 7–8, so I gave up. Ended up trying Hui Wei Fishball Noodles (Unit 01-04) instead and honestly, no regrets! Their signature soup plus dry mee pok combo is one of the best I’ve had :)

Also tried the popiah, carrot cake, kaya toast set and taro toast from various stalls. All were decent, nothing particularly memorable; but the fishball noodles? I’d definitely make a return trip just for that ☺️

(Taking 1 star off for how inaccessible this hawker is if you don't drive 😭)
author: Joy Ong

review_text:
Food- Constant Taste
If you are seeking for traditional braised items, here is the place.
The in-house made chilli sauce is awesomely thick and tangy. 40 years experience.... no joke. 😘💪🏾
author: Hackson Lim

review_text: About half the stalls were closed today but we had this tasty Signature Noodle + Soup for lunch. Very hearty and umami. Stall owner was friendly.
author: Pearlyn GYT

review_text: This legendary place often no patrons . Which is sad cause they have Good food and drink . There's this noodle place facing main road. Left side. Very good and cheap. Big portion.
author: Arvi Da Mayo Wow

review_text:
Delicious food. The Chinese cuisines are done really well. From their porridge to dim sums and even local fares, we loved it all. Can also get the chef to make something less salty and oily for your little ones too! Service is great!

Remember to wear long pants and collared shirts!
author: Daniel Bok

review_text:
Dinner - Fri 12 Sept 2025
Silk Restaurant @ SICC
Perched on high ground in the Singapore Island Country Club, Silk offers scenic views of the golf course and nature reserve, making diners feel far from the city.

Serving traditional Cantonese cuisine with fresh ingredients, highlights include Suckling Pig, Fried Frog leg, Peking duck, truffle mushrooms, sea cucumber dishes, and bee hoon with grouper. The food is tasty, served very hot, with attentive service in a clean, refined setting.

A members-only restaurant, it’s ideal for business meetings, family gatherings, or fine dining. Reservations are recommended. VIP room with minimum spending.
author: Yiling Lai

review_text: Sumptuous family lunch with a stunning view of the golf course. Attentive service staf too.
author: Doreen Leong

review_text: Comfortable place with delicious food. The view overlooking the golf course during sunset was amazing. Servers were very helpful too !
author: D Y

review_text:
Superb food!!!

We enjoyed the Peking duck, the beef cubes and the patin fish.

Service is so prompt and good.
author: Samuel Lam

review_text: Food is fresh and well-prepared, and pricing is good. Ambience is casual, staff are warm and friendly. Great place to dine. Need to be member or guest of a member to eat here.
author: peregrine

review_text: Good Japanese food for club members
author: Suan Pin Foo

review_text: Food was good and service is impeccable
author: Goh Wee Kia

review_text: Food is great
author: Yeung Gin

review_text:
This is a Japanese restaurant with good value for money.

The food is neat and tastes good.

The corkage fee was also reasonable.

However, it is a shame that card payments are not accepted unless you are a member, and they require you to use PayNow.
author: Ken Lee

review_text: Comforting taiwan porridge. The sweet potato porridge is just the right mix. The braised pork was supposed to be the star but it was tough. Standard dropped ? Hope not, will give it another try next time. Other dishes weee good
author: Mikki B

review_text: A Taiwanese porridge place but also able to order dishes like tzechar. The menu is quite extensive! The dishes were actually all pretty good. FYI, rice and sweet potato porridge is refillable is you ordered those!
author: Rennie Lee

review_text: Our go to when we crave for porridge. All dishes are consistently well prepared with the freshest ingredients. Love it! Love their tofu with pork floss - light and yet tasty at the same time, minced pork with salted fish is moist and tender, chai po egg is fluffy and not oily, sweet sour pork is a delight to have ! Service is great too. Super attentive and helpful. A joy to eat at every visit.
author: KYChingS Y

review_text: One of the rare few places that still uses table cloth. Soft relaxing music, clean and well maintained restaurant. Food is served fast and executed so well. It’s fresh, delicious, high quality and simple. For the service, comfort and food quality, their price is reasonable. I highly recommend this restaurant for family meals.
author: Cadbury

review_text:
Cravings of Taiwanese porridge sets in on a late night and we decided to head for some supper at Upper Thomson side for some good old white porridge and really good side dishes.

At 9pm, the place is still with a lot of diners with takeaway orders and dine in, we opted for the white porridge for us, and chose chai po egg omelette, hot plate beef slices with ginger and onions, and also a popular dishes judging by the reviews, egg plant with mince pork sauce.

We ordered also a braised peanut to munch on while waiting, and the food actually was served very quickly. The hotplate beef was served sizzling, it has been a while that I actually see restaurant serving it this hot, the beef slices were tendered and the sauce goes so well with the porridge.

The chai po egg omelette was only ok for us, we wish that it was thicker and with more chai po in it, but it goes really well with the fast finishing chili sauce at the table.
The highlight for us was the eggplant, it was the weirdest experience for us because the egg plant without the gravy tasted like goreng pisang (fried banana) and it was so sweet and juicy, and when you mix it with the mince pork sauce, that’s a winner, we polish this dish so quickly.

Overall, the meal was fantastic and we will definitely go back there to try out other dishes that they have. There is a parking on the opposite street near the Bangkok mokata if you can’t find a parking there.
author: Lorelai D

review_text: Klara has quickly become one of my favourite restaurants, and my only regret is that I didn’t discover it sooner! What a hidden gem. The interior is eclectic and perfect for an intimate dinner. The food is innovative and unique. They are certainly skilled with their flame grilling - every dish seems to have a flame grilled component and tastes SO good. The drinks are great too, and very reasonably priced!
author: Vanessa Khoo

review_text:
Celebrated my friend's birthday at this cozy restaurant. The staff, I think his name is Shu, was very friendly and warm. The food was really good! The lady chef really put her heart into preparing the food; every dish we ordered was very delicious. Thank you for the good food!

The signature drinks were okay. The lychee osmanthus drink has room for improvement; I could not taste the lychee, and it was quite bland. The restaurant was slightly warm.
author: Ally

review_text:
This is a small and cosy restaurant that has a layout to serve a maximum of 20 pax  with excellent ambience. The staffs were attentive and prompt.

We reserve for a group of 10 for a Saturday lunch and was provided a pre ordering online link a day before which allows prompt serving of food once we arrive at the restaurant. Giving the size of the restaurant we sort have a private dinning experience being the only group at this time.

The restaurant serves a fusion of westeran and asian cuisine that has very nice platting as seen from the photos.

However, the food while good, wasn't something that would entice me to travel back to have a meal again. Personally, there are better food option at this price point.

I would recommend trying the iberico pork chop which is very well grilled as well as mushroom pasta.l which is quite different from traditional aglio olio.

As this restaurant is tucked away at a quiet residential area, parking is extremely limited. Recommend to park at the nearby Thomson plaza if you don't mind walking around 5mins.

Overall, this is an excellent place for a decent meal for a date and small group gathering with near private dinning experience but might not be the best option if the food is your only priority.
author: Genesis NΞO

review_text:
Somehow managed to find this spot while browsing Google Maps.

It’s located in a landed property area beside Thomson plaza, with pretty limited parking. The restaurant is quite small but intimate and cosy, so definitely make reservations in advance. When we arrived, we noted that all the tables were already reserved.

We went with 2 starters and 2 mains. Everything was fantastic and the dishes were all pretty unique in some way, with a lot of heart and soul put into each dish. The prices were also very reasonable for the quality. Service was also prompt and fast, although there was only 1 front of house staff delivering food and making drinks on top of processing the bill.

My only gripe is that the exhaust from the kitchen could reach the dining area which resulted in our clothes having the oily smell. Otherwise I enjoyed every bit of our evening. Favorite for me had to be the squid ink oyster omelette, which was served with their own chilli as well!
author: Kenny Yap

review_text:
Delicious food, cozy ambience, lots of small thoughts and details went into this place. A very rare gem in cut throat Singapore where everything is going corporate.

Menu was vert well written with a good balance of creativity X comfort, drinks were not overlooked as well. Iberico pork chop with porcini mushroom was an amazing stand out, served medium well, it was absolutely perfect!

Will be back very soon!
author: Anotation

review_text: Ordered through food panda app. Ordered at 8pm, app show delivery time will br 25-30mins. Waited till 10pm... but pizza still not delivered.  Call the thomson branch but no one pick up.  Can't cancel the order as its still showing rider on the way...and I live like 15 mine away from Domino's.. super crappy experience. Will never order from them again!!! Feels like a big scam !!!!!
author: Amy Tan

review_text:
I can really imagine why everyone scores this outlet so badly. Looks like they regularly have the practice of marking the order delivered on the app without delivering it.

My order marked delivered at 8.50pm even though it was not delivered. I called the store at 8.55pm & was told by customer service lady that order is with delivery person & will be delivered soon. It wasn't delivered even at 9.15pm.

During my second call at 9.15pm a different staff mentioned about further 45 min delay. He blatantly lied stating they tried calling us to inform about the delay when we placed the order at 8.45pm. I  received no call on my phone & he didn't even realise I placed my order at 7.55pm; clearly showing they never tried calling me. My phone was available since I placed my order. My worst ever experience with Domino's till date in the last 15years.
author: Muralidharan Ramakrishnan

review_text:
Disappointing experience from start to finish.
Ordered through the Domino’s app thinking it’d be faster (despite the $5 delivery fee). The app showed “delivered” — but nothing had arrived. I called the outlet five times before anyone picked up. A guy answered, passed the phone to a lady who clearly didn’t want to be there, and I was told it was “on the way.”

Thirty minutes later — still nothing. I live 5 minutes away on foot. Tried calling again, but now the phone seemed to be off the hook.

Eventually, I got an SMS with a Foodpanda tracking link — turns out they outsourced the delivery anyway. I could’ve just ordered directly from Foodpanda and saved myself the $5.

And the final insult? The pizza arrived with burnt crust, and some slices didn’t even have crust — it looked like the dough wasn’t properly spread.

Totally unacceptable from a brand like Domino’s.
author: Will Chin

review_text:
I am extremely frustrated with this experience.

I deliberately scheduled my order for 11:00 PM delivery so the pizza would arrive hot and fresh when my girlfriend got home. This was intentional, not a suggestion. However, the pizza was delivered an hour early, despite the website not even showing that the order was being prepared at the time.

Delivering food that early completely defeats the purpose of a scheduled delivery and shows a clear disregard for customer instructions. Why offer timed delivery if it is not followed?
author: Linus

review_text:
This outlet is by far the worst Domino’s branch in Singapore and should be shut down immediately. A few months ago, I ordered two pizzas, both supposed to be chicken. The delivery fee was already high, but fine, when you pay for food, you expect quality and accuracy. The order arrived late, despite the outlet being only 10 minutes away, by the way the order itself took a long time to cook, was not the drivers fault. I was monitoring it very closely after the 40 minute mark we were all starving and annoyed. (we ordered in because my friends and I were busy with uni work).

When the food finally came, one pizza was chicken, the other was beef. I’m Hindu and do not consume beef, so this was extremely offensive and disrespectful. To make things worse, we initially assumed it was chicken pepperoni, only to find out after tasting it that it was beef.

Outraged, I drove to the outlet to ask why such a mistake happened and requested a replacement. The manager laughed at me. Imagine that... first, they mess up the order, then mock the customer. When I asked for a refund, he said, “Oh, you can get a refund, just return the pizza.” I handed it back and waited outside while checking the app for confirmation.

After waiting 15 minutes, nothing happened. I went back in and asked... only for him to say, “Actually sir, the refund is not guaranteed.” Excuse me? You promise a refund, then backtrack and act clueless? Completely unacceptable.

This outlet is a disgrace, rude staff, poor service, and zero accountability. I’ll be reporting this to the Singapore Food Agency because this kind of negligence and disrespect should not go unchecked. With an average 1.4-star rating, it’s clear this outlet has no business staying open.
author: Cudiya Madachode

review_text: Visited Sushi Tei at Thomson Plaza on 23 Dec 2025. The quality of the food was fantastic as always – fresh, flavourful, and beautifully presented. The staff were friendly and helpful, making the dining experience even more enjoyable. Highly recommend for anyone who loves authentic Japanese cuisine!
author: Thomas Jolene

review_text: Had the Katsudon while the Mrs had the pork salad and we shared the Tuna Carpaccio. Raisin was well cook while the egg are still easy and wonderfully well seasoned, as for the Pork salad, it was well balanced to perfection, lastly the tuna was fresh and had the tangy taste sweet sour which helps a lot to cleanse the palate. A good place to go for a quick bite.
author: Roger Heng

review_text: Always came for the sashimi salad with bits of raw fish and tangy house salad dressing. Rainbow Roll topped with eel, avocado & cucumber sushi roll topped with yellow-tail, tuna, salmon & swordfish. First time having the delicious & comforting Unagi Hitsumabushi - premium eel on rice with 3 ways of eating. Tuna maki is one of our fav but wasn’t cut neatly. Ingredients fresh. Good to try.
author: Another Big Bite

review_text: Really delicious and authentic Japanese curry.  The curry portion was enough for the ramen.  Ebi tempura was good but the carrot one was so-so.  Regretted taking the counter seat as the staff was using the table soace next to me to clean the cutlery.  They were talking at the same time so it was really noisy even though i had my noise-canceling earbuds.  I felt that it was an working corner and not suitable for any customers to be seated there.  Alternatively those seated there should receive some 20% or 30% discount for the food.  Otherwise, i wouldn't consider paying a $20+ meal for such an experience.
author: Joslovesfood

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐
Glad to be back after a long time!
Dropped by Sushi Tei at Thomson for dinner on a Saturday — there was a long queue, but the wait was worth it. The food is still as good as I remember: fresh, well-prepared, and satisfying. Service was warm and attentive despite the busy crowd, which made the experience even better. A reliable spot for Japanese food — just be prepared for a wait during peak hours.
author: Blessed Irene

review_text:
For my first try of Hokkaido white curry, the overall experience is mixed. On one hand the curry gravy is quite nice -- flavourful while having a light mouth feel. On the other hand the potatoes are quite blunt in taste, with a little grassy aroma. I believe Japanese cuisine does not fry potatoes before stewing them in curry, unlike many local cuisines here do, but there ought to be some alternatives to make the potatoes taste better.
The pork cutlets are fairly good. Although no dipping sauce is provided, the curry gravy is sufficient to wet them if you prefer having them dry.
author: Kai Ming Hew

review_text:
A place get a quick meal with some standard but need to pay a bit.

The ramen with butter is always the item to order - Hokkiado Butter Corn Chasyu Ramen. Taste of the soup is good and the Chasyu is soft and tender even it’s thick. (SGD13.90)

The rice item looks big on the menu but note that it’s the size of the smaller rice bowl (like those used in Chinese restaurants for rice). So for those big eater.. take note. To me, I like the Salmon Oyako Tarta Don. Love the freshness of the salmon and yummy fish roe and crispy rice that mixed with the usual sushi rice. (SGD15.90)

So.. I will usually order the rice set if I’m not hungry as the sashimi is fresh and I like it. If I’m hungry.. I will order the ramen.

You can always make it a “Set Meal” by adding $3 or $6.

If you are around and everywhere is packed.. can try out the food here!
author: Tan Chee

review_text: First try at this outlet, I didn’t even know it’s related to Sushi Teh. I agree with the good reviews… the rice bowl is indeed small but fresh. The beef ramen and pork belly don are good. The best part is the $3 add on, salad is great. And U only pay GST since U self-service. Will be back to try the white curry. I will prefer to dine here over sushi teh due to the lower price and casual and open setting, where U can hear everyone else.
author: Leow Een Tiong

review_text:
I just visited Hokkaido-Ya's 2nd Outlet at Thomson Plaza for the 1st time. Served by Elemor (Cashier), Sam Sheng Keng Hwee and Sai Dik.

This restaurant is self-service only. 1 of a few Japanese restaurants to have self-service only which the majority of the restaurants who have a self-service only are mainly western restaurants or fast food companies.

What I got here is a bowl of Salmon Tamago Mentaiko Don, a set containing Lemon Tea, Miso Soup, and Tori Karaage. All of which are in generous portions.

Overall, I give it a 5 star. I would like to come here again anytime soon!!! Thank you Elemor, Sam Sheng, and Sai Dik for an excellent service!!!
author: Matt Siegfried

review_text: We had lunch there today, and the food quality was decent. Nothing too fantastic, but not bad at all. Prices are very reasonable as well. The seating area is small, and it's free seating, which can be quite unpleasant because solo diners and couples occupy the 4 seaters, and families with children and larger groups have nowhere to be seated during peak meal times. What's worse is that these solo and couple diners don't leave after they finish their meal. While we were there, the solo diner continued to occupy a 4 seater table to watch videos off his phone. The couple diners continued to have a chat at their 4 seater table after their meal. The food portions were quite small at first glance, but I was definitely full after my Bara Chirashi Don meal. Another comment is that the ventilation is bad, so try to avoid the tables nearest to the kitchen if you don't want your clothes and hair to smell like deep-fried food.
author: Ivan Loh

review_text: Excellent Kway Chap set ($6.50) with an authentic traditional taste. The herbal broth was served hot and flavorful. And, the chilli is nice too. I’ve tried other outlets from this same brand, but this specific location is definitely better in terms of quality and execution.
author: Sheringham Zhou

review_text:
Dinner tonight at Yew Kee Specialities 友记家传鸭饭 at Thomson Plaza.

We ordered the Teochew Braised Set with a bowl of Kway 潮州卤味套餐, along with an extra serving of Braised Beancurd Skin 卤香焖腐竹.

The kway was soaked in a lightly herbal, comforting soup, paired with a richer and thicker lor chap. Ingredients like the braised duck meat, fish cake, tau pok and more came together really well with the silky kway. Every mouthful felt hearty and satisfying.

My SO especially loved the warmth of the soup, perfect for a cozy dinner. The braised beancurd skin was flavourful too, soft yet structured, and absorbed the braise nicely.

A simple, comforting Teochew-style meal that hits the spot. 🍜✨
