Arrived 2115hrs
Food arrived cold

Pressed that the delivery has arrived around 2100hrs. But in the end came at 2115hrs

Called them about the messed up order
No one pick up my phone
author: Seet Xinwen

review_text:
My brother placed an order at 5.30pm on 16/11/25. The estimated delivery time was stated to be 6.04-6.20pm. At 7pm the status update is shown to be "still making". At 7.20 the status is being updated to "being delivered". If your estimated delivery time is not even accurate then dont even put it there.
Tried calling the hotline multiple times but the line was busy. If the line is constantly busy as seen from other reviews, then why do you even have a hotline?
Why do customers have to wait almost 2 hours for food delivery? Im a regular at the gym at the CC, everytime I walk past the store is empty.

The review for this outlet is so damn bad, yet the management only gives standard replies, without doing anything to even brush up the service/speed of the store. Had my family know that the review is so damn bad, we would not even order from this outlet. Have already submitted an online feedback.
author: Jun Yao

review_text:
I’m a regular customer here and visit this coffeeshop/zi char about 2–3 times a week. After many instances of unfriendly service, I feel it’s time to leave some honest feedback.

The auntie with short hair and glasses has repeatedly shown poor service attitude. This has happened not just once, but many times. I hope the management will take note of this.

Today, I also learned that customers are expected to collect their own food. I asked when this change started, and she simply replied that it has been this way for a long time. I have never come across a Zi Char place where customers need to collect their own dishes, so this was surprising.

I’m sharing this feedback because I do believe this place can do better, especially for the regular customers who support it. Thank you.
author: Fred Chan

review_text:
Deep fried chicken wings and shrimps were great and very juicy.  Other dishes are okay to fair.  The restaurant was quite empty on a weekday.

Crab needs to be preordered, which is a bit disappointing.  It was used to be crowded many years ago.
author: T Lo

review_text:
I’ve been here two to three times a week, long enough to know exactly what this place used to be — and long enough to see how far the service has slipped.

The lady with short hair and glasses hasn’t just been unfriendly. She’s been consistently rude. Visit after visit. Same tone. Same attitude. And at this point, it’s impossible to pretend it’s accidental. It feels intentional. It feels personal. And it leaves a bitter taste before the food even arrives.

Today was the final push. Suddenly customers are expected to collect their own dishes. No notice. No explanation. And when I asked about it, the response I got wasn’t information — it was a brush-off. “It’s been like this for a long time.” That’s simply not true, and saying it like it’s common knowledge just added insult to inconvenience.

I’m not a one-time walk-in. I’m someone who chooses to spend money here every week. But lately it feels like regulars are treated like we’re a nuisance instead of the reason this place stays full.

This isn’t about high expectations. It’s about basic respect and a service standard that doesn’t drop the moment no one’s watching. If the attitude doesn’t change, regular customers will — and that’s a loss no coffeeshop should take lightly.

This place can be better. But right now, it genuinely isn’t acting like it wants to be. 🌹
author: Steve Lee

review_text: U'll some really good dishes but the rest are so so. The fried chicken was a hit. It was crispy and juicy. Do try. The rest of the dishes were lackluster. Nothing special.
author: Vtigaa Vtigaa

review_text:
I came to place my order around 7+ PM, and I understand it was peak hour. I was told there would be a short wait, which I accepted. However, I waited from 7+ PM all the way until 8:31 PM, and my food was still not ready.

What felt really unfair was that people who arrived later than me and dined in were served much faster, while my takeaway order was still not prepared. It doesn’t make sense that dine-in customers who came later got their food earlier than takeaway customers.

I even had to walk over to the waitress to ask, “How much longer do I have to wait?” She panicked and told the chef, “You never cook the order?” and the chef replied, “What takeaway order?” At that point, it was obvious the receipt had gone missing.

Despite the long wait and the mistake, there was no apology or explanation given. Ridiculous.
author: Felicia Ong

restaurant_name: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
review_text: Expect to queue. Laksa gravy is rich. Price on the higher end. As many commented, the stall holder attitude is not very good. Nice to try but will not return again.
author: C Lim

restaurant_name: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
review_text: Food generally ok, but request to seperate the carbs with ingredient, carbs will be charge $1.50. Price is good for the size of ingredient. But this ball is a disguise, I thought it’s meatball like I had at any stall. But this is hard like stone. Also they deep fry everything except vegetable.
author: Shan Ng

restaurant_name: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
review_text:
There's a queue for a reason! The prices are quite good, and the flavors really hit the spot.

But the true star here (or maybe an acquired taste for some) is definitely their chilli! You can even request it separately from your noodle bowl. This chilli is packed with an incredible "wok hey" flavor – I'm talking 11/10 kind of smoky, almost burnt perfection. It's unique, and probably something you'll either love or find a bit too intense. Definitely worth trying if you're into bold flavors!
author: Zac (Zakku)

restaurant_name: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
review_text: Chanced upon this ytf and decided to join the queue. Hands down one of the better ytf I've tried. Ngioh heong and brinjal is very good! Chilli and sweet sauce is well balanced. Surprisingly affordable too given the quality ingredients offered
author: Y&S

restaurant_name: Xi Xiang Feng Yong Tau Foo
review_text: The laksa is curry and operator put a lot of curry powder. Thick gravy and not edible. Standard drop all way down. Sigh. Not eating again. Lucky no queue that day.
author: luciole tan

review_text:
❤️ Food sharing IG @ jkgourmets
😋 美食分享尽在 IG @ jkgourmets

Didn't notice this Mamak restaurant especially when the hawker centre with variety of food selections just in front of them.

Owner said they have been there for more than 6 years, they already brought over the place, and can enjoy worry free high rentals.

I am trying to take away a freshly cooked Briyani chicken, told the owner I wish to have dum-chicken, which chicken was  cooked together with the Briyani rice, so it is like pure steamed chicken. Unfortunately, he is not listen my order carefully and just wrap a green curry chicken for me.

Fortunately the green curry chicken was not bad, the curry base was delicious and have it own unique special recipes. As usual, Indian foods was always very heavy spices, salty and spicy.

Briyani chicken with one hard boiled egg in the rice, and a basic curry gravy, and cost me at $8.50. Although the rice given is pretty big but I felt it was expensive due to the small piece of the chicken meat.

Popular Mamak restaurant they usually charge $7.50 and with much larger chicken meat, this AL Zouq restaurant simply too expensive.

Believe their foods was quite delicious and have decent good standard, no competition surrounds them make them popular and business sustainable.

Nevertheless, if you craving for Indian foods, you may try, otherwise, you have lots of foods selection in front of them.
author: Josh Kuek (#jkgourmets)

review_text:
Mee goreng at first Mouth is quite nice…but at the end it’s quite greasy…

The butter chicken is quite nice but I find the tikka masala chicken is nicer. Both really call to eat with naan though I didn’t order

Note that it’s quite pricey but location n hours is convenient
author: M P

review_text:
The food here is scrumptious. Very generous amount of food that will surely fill you up. Bought similar food from this store and another just down the lane.

Ordered a full chicken piece from both sides, similar sized. The other side cut the chicken in half and served.

Al Zouq gave me a full piece. Every customer at his store received a huge lamb shank, or chicken piece. Price difference was $1.50. Worth it!

Will definitely recommend this store. 👍🔥🔥🔥
author: Avriel Peter

review_text:
Update Apr '23: The place has changed:  More process oriented, less friendly, smaller portions.  Food is still good but will be finding a new fave for this cuisine.  Loses a star to 3.

Nostalgic old school feel to the place adds to the good traditional flavours. Pay after eating. So far only tried and like in order of preference byriani with butter chicken ($6), curry chicken ($6), lamb shank ($12.9). Byriani rice is light and separated well, not clumped together. IMO the prata is also good - my goto place now for prata for taste, portion and price ($1/pc for plain).  IMO sufficient portion for the price across the menu. Place appears to struggle with volume though... did I say old school. Hope they keep the taste, qty and ingredients if/when they do modernise the sales system.
author: cybertrot

review_text: Never knew Mutton can be so tender. Had the mutton hot plate and the naan was the best I’ve had-garlicky, fresh and warm! Chicken tandoori too sweet for my liking. $17.50 including lime juice for 2 pax. Very filling but a bit salty for me
author: Shirley Odelia

restaurant_name: Bangkok Street Mookata - Ang Mo Kio
review_text:
yummy mookata at a super reasonable price! shop has been here for some time and glad to be able to enjoy mookata here. plenty of fans so dining experience is good not too stuffy.

marinated meat is yummy, veggie and ingredients are fresh too. will drop by again
author: Bimbles

restaurant_name: Bangkok Street Mookata - Ang Mo Kio
review_text: Better than a lot of Mookata places I’ve tried. The meat is nicely marinated and super tasty. Price is affordable and worth it. Will come back for sure.
author: Jay Tham

restaurant_name: Bangkok Street Mookata - Ang Mo Kio
review_text:
been here twice at this point, but it never disappoints! prices are generally really affordable, with around $10 per pax.

it’s in a coffee shop under hdb blocks, and it opens till 2am, which means you’re able to get your late night supper fix here.

they block the fire with aluminium foil so the wind would not blow it out, which i think is really smart to do.

we ordered 6 meats and we were already full by the 3rd plate. if you want more bang for your buck, do not get the mookata set unless you’re an avid seafood lover or you prefer not having to pick everything on your own. it’s more costly to get the set as compared to getting ala carte honestly.

the broth is vegetable based and mild in taste. get the thai noodles if you want a tom yum seasoning packet to add to the broth, or maybe 2 because 1 didn’t feel like it was enough after refilling the broth a couple times.

overall, my partner and i felt extremely satisfied and happy from the meal! very delicious, will come back again for sure. 😋
author: carmen l.

restaurant_name: Bangkok Street Mookata - Ang Mo Kio
review_text:
Value for money. Gets Crowded fast so come early.  Beef is tough so I will skip for next visit. We ordered too much as some items portions for 2 are quite large.

Update on 03 sep 21
Food quality has improved with new items.
author: Kelly Ng

restaurant_name: Bangkok Street Mookata - Ang Mo Kio
review_text:
Went on a Friday evening & was really crowded. Lots of other stalls were opened too & the coffeeshop has been recently re-renovated.

Portion for 2 pax was ok. Meat was well marinated but could be improved. I love the sliced chicken thigh the most. Beef was so so. Still prefer the mookata before they renovate.

Excellent service from one of the elder lady staff. She was very caring, paying attention to details & warm towards us. She also revealed that the broth uses sweet corn for a natural sweetness. A delicate staff is hard to find nowadays. For this we give 5* to their service.

The atmosphere was a little messy. Crowded with lots of customers, probably due to the recent re-renovation where there's lots of new stalls. You will have to queue outside the coffeeshop (under the shelter) for the mookata.

Hoping my next try would be a 4*
author: munchwithvienna

restaurant_name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
review_text:
Coming back from black!

So glad they have open another outlet after closing the other.

Better location than the previous one.

Tried Original and Black. Although my preference is black usually, for only this, Orginal is better.

Black sauce adds sweetness which make it overly sweet for the wanton mee. Including the sausage which is also sweet. It ruins the depth of flavor.

Just order the Orginal one.

They have other options, but who am I kidding? I'll just order Wanton whenever I come here.
author: Thaddeus Zheng

restaurant_name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
review_text:
Went to their old place at Blk 151 AMK Ave 4. Checked & realised might b moved to blk 159 AMK Ave 4. Hope it’s the same stall.
Ordered 1 bowl of original & 1 bowl of black sauce Wanton Mee.
The noodle cooked well. Tho there’s no chilli sauce added in the original bowl but it taste great without chilli too.
Love the generous amount of pork Lard they give & the fish sausage taste so yummy.
Will definitely come again and bring my other family members to try too.
author: kay ng

restaurant_name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
review_text:
I think this just moved over from block 151. Anyhow i ordered original thai wanton mee. Costed $5.80.

It is weird. Another of those without any chili sauce noodles. But it doesn't have sambal chili. It has Thai sour chili and pad thai chili flakes. It was pretty dry and starchy. Definitely would need some sauce or soup or the chili.

Char siew is typical low grade wanton mee char siew while the fried hot dog is sweet and unique, something i would find from cai png store.

Maybe i would try some other version and see how it goes. But ghe original one is something you need to add seasoning to make it nice.
author: Super Fragrance

restaurant_name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
review_text:
Soi 19 wanton mee started as a humble stall at Ang Mo Kio Ave 5, blk 151. The owner even had the thought of closing it down for good.

We 1st tried it years ago and wrote a blog about them. Soon, many food bloggers, newspaper articles started appearing.

The queue started to form, till the point i had to wait for an hour for the bowl of thai wanton mee. Branches soon multiplied and the uncle can no longer be seen at the stall.

I consider them as a family business as all their stalls are helmed by their family members.

We used to eat it so often. Ever since not cooked by the uncle, we eat less and less.

This weekend we went back to eat again, hmm the fish lup cheong is still good. Noodles i feel alittle soggier than before, the soup is still good.

Can try if you are in the area.

#soi19
author: Jason Deng

restaurant_name: Soi 19 Thai Wanton Mee (Ang Mo Kio)
review_text: This stall which has numerous restaurants all over Singapore shifted here after the previous coffee shop it was in was repossessed. Still the same taste.
author: Nicodemus Chan

review_text:
Was walking past Blk 722 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8 coffeeshop and noticed a queue forming at 925 Yishun Hainanese Chicken Rice. With such a prominent display and steady crowd, curiosity got the better of me and I decided to give it a try.

Ordered a steamed chicken rice, with extra chicken meat and a side of mixed organs. Unfortunately, all the chicken parts served were breast meat. On its own, the meat felt rather bland — it really depended heavily on the sauce poured over it. Without the sauce, it would have been quite tasteless.

The rice itself was nicely cooked, fluffy and well-textured, but it lacked that fragrant chicken aroma and flavour that I usually look forward to in a good plate of chicken rice. Eventually, I couldn’t quite finish the rice.

That said, one thing truly stood out and redeemed the meal — the soup. Instead of a basic chicken broth, it came with peanuts and lotus seeds added in, giving it a comforting, slightly nutty sweetness. Honestly, it was so good I should have asked for a bigger bowl 😂

My SO also pointed out that their dark sauce leaned more towards plain salty, rather than the sweet-savoury balance many might expect. Perhaps a tweak in the sauce could help elevate the overall experience.

Not the best chicken rice for us this time, but that soup definitely left an impression.

📍 925 Yishun Hainanese Chicken Rice
Blk 722 Ang Mo Kio Ave 8

Have you tried this stall before? What do you think?

review_text: We always order half a steamed chicken and a bowl of rice to share. The boneless chicken was superb—tender and succulent. The soup wasn’t oily, either. The only downside was the cashier aunty. She was incredibly rude, unfriendly and harsh. She talked to me as if I was an annoying idiot.
author: Unki Sng

review_text:
The steamed chicken is very tender and the texture of the chicken skin is good. The soya sauce over the chicken is nice but missing sesame sauce which would have enhanced the flavour. Chilli sauce is nice but quite spicy.
The soup is flavourful.
Service is ok.
author: Jacob TAN

review_text:
This store is located in Ang Mo Kio, though the store name is stated as 925 Yishun.
There was a short queue when I was there because a customer ordered quite a few packets.
The price was reasonable, you could choose either small ($3.50) or big ($5) size.
For the small size plate, the quantity of the food was just nice for me.
The soup was quite flavourful, one of the best soup, I ever had.
Overall experience was good.
Would definitely go back again soon!
author: DR DAVY GOH

review_text:
Chicken Rice $3.50

Nowadays you don't get to find it at that pricing la! You look at the portion, so decent also. Worth it.

I taobao it home and ate it a few hours later and it was still good lei, not dry the sauce was still there, just that their chili was not that shiok la but everything was on point for me. I remember having it years ago at Yishun Central but couldn't remember the taste of it, just so happened to see it here at Ang Mo Kio had to buy la.

I will always remember this bad experience I had buying a chicken rice from a stall at the Kovan Market & Food Centre, the signboard put $2.50, so when I ordered it the uncle will be unhappy and will ask you want $4.50 or 5.50? 🙄 Then you put $2.50 for what, might as well just put the pricing you will be happy people buying it at.
author: S.Y

review_text: Best Mee Jiang Kueh I had. I personally love the peanut paste flavour, and if you are lucky, you can get them fresh off the grill. The other items are usually very popular, especially the carrot cake. They also sell desserts like cakes and muffins as well.
author: Nahshon

review_text:
Always will have a pancake if I dine here.
Love the coconut most as I somehow always got it hot.
Black sesame is slightly more pricey but the filling is solid.
This is the place for my to go pancake and my benchmark against any other pancake.
Tried their scone and muffin before but nothing amazing
author: Zj

review_text: I walked past this place and decided to check it out. They’ve got a nice variety of cakes like carrot cake, butter walnut, earl grey, chocolate walnut, muffins, and more. Prices range from $3 to $5 per slice. I tried the carrot cake for $3.80 , it was moist and not too sweet, which I liked, but honestly, it felt a little pricey.
author: Daisy Luu Hong Loan

review_text: Tucked at the corner of this coffee shop, this meejiang kuehs aka traditional pancakes, are light and fluffy, void of strong flour taste. Of the 3 flavours, traditional peanut, sesame and matcha charcoal, matcha charcoal is the best!
author: Gabrielle Lew

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Absolutely loved this peanut pancake! The texture was perfectly crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, with a generous amount of flavorful peanut filling. It has the perfect balance of sweetness and crunch. I don’t understand why some people claim it’s not good—this is honestly one of the best I’ve had in a while. The service was okay, nothing to complain about, but the star of the show is definitely the pancake itself. Highly recommended for all pancake lovers!
author: Benjamin Toh

review_text:
Little Farms at Serangoon Gardens is my favorite spot for premium, high-quality groceries! The produce section is exceptional — always bursting with super fresh, organic fruits and vegetables that look and taste amazing. They have an outstanding selection of imported pantry staples from Australia, Italy, and beyond, plus top-notch meats that are consistently fresh and premium.Everything here feels thoughtfully sourced and of the highest quality — it's clear they prioritize excellence in every aisle.

The store has a warm, welcoming, and vibrant ambiance, making shopping a real pleasure.What truly elevates the experience is the outstanding service.

The staff are friendly and helpful, but I especially want to highlight the store manager, Janet. She's incredibly customer service-oriented, patient, kind, and always takes the time to thoroughly answer my queries and help me find exactly what I need. She makes every visit feel personal and enjoyable!Highly recommend for anyone seeking the best in fresh and quality groceries.
author: Lynn Brunkard

review_text:
❇️  Been to MyVillage mall many times over the years. ● Nice mall, small and compact, Toilets are clean.

🌳🌳 This mall has a lovely roof-top wooden deck garden where I always like to take photos of the sunset from here.

● They have the basic amenities here. A premium NTUC supermarket + Little Farms supermkt, hairdresser, cafes and bakeries, ice cream shops etc.
author: Florence Leow

review_text:
A quaint mini mall that sits on a small road, or u can call it a picturesque mall, or whichever u define it, as it is has that alluring feel to it. 😀

It has quite a few restaurants in it and has concierge at level 2, which sits facing the escalator leading to the rooftop. A very well maintained mall despite the looks and many aesthetic works of art around. All u need to do is jz slowly walk and breathe while observing everything around. U will realise that there are creative simple designs that makes the place pleasing to look at.

The layout is simple with 4 floors to boast at the very least. There are practical and creative designs of art outside as well. Walk along the walls and u will realise this, something that some may not have realised. Talk a slow walk n chill with friends on d coolness of this mall. It is definitely not the best of malls, but it serves the purpose fully.

Worth a visit at least once.. Cheers
#piquedwanderer #famwithsten
author: Sten (Piqued Wanderer)

review_text:
A tiny yet charming mall right in the heart of Serangoon Gardens. Well it certainly serves the immediate needs of the residents in the neighbourhood.

The anchor tenant here is Fairprice Finest and rightfully so considering the upmarket neighbourhood.

A couple of restaurants like iSteaks adorn the mall.

Is the mall worth a visit ? I would not make my way here if only to visit this mall. Like i said earlier it serves the immediate needs of the neighbourhood and it is a nice mall.
author: Dr. Reviews

review_text:
Small mall around the serangoon garden. It has few eateries inside and few small shops. There is fair price finest here and indostop where you can buy Indonesia's stuffs here. The shop was in the corner at fairprice, I only noticed it after I went for fairprice to shop.

There are few restaurants at second floor but iSteak seems good because there was quite a number of people queueing at there. Didn't manage to try it. Maybe next time.

I tried korean chicken stall at b1, it was crispy and good. The staff was friendly and patiently explaining me about the food on menu. Order the garlic taste and it was good. Might try again other taste next time. Came twice to the store before and after shopping my groceries, still remember what I asked for the first time not to put chili on the food which I forgot to mention when I ordered.

Here also has coffee shop which caught my attention, only sell coffee related stuff like the machine, grinding, etc.
author: William Lu

review_text:
I ordered double prosperity beef buger set

author: Wi sH

review_text: Grab order came without my double cheeseburger, called the customer service to ask for my burger. The driver came with very good customer service 5 stars 🌟 for the driver who delivered my food!
author: Soh Xuan Ping

review_text:
Utterly shock and disgusted with this outlet, came around 1120pm, wasn't full house, the "kids party" place was still quite empty however was utmost disgusted by the environment and hygienic issues this outlet is having.

No words to explain, do see from the photos itself, to be frank we were very hungry already and at this hour we just wanted to eat and go home which is why we continued to eat over here, however I felt sick after eating with the amount of thrash and toilet condition.

author: jayden

review_text: Order by grab and took almost an hour to recieved the order. And when the food recieved its so embarrasing coz its not newly cooked!  The chicken looks like they re fry it!!!!!
author: Ton Camp

review_text: Nice quiet place to have to rest in a sub urban area in a lazy afternoon.
author: Chris Neo

review_text: Sells a large variety of soya bean and cincau related drinks. Taste good. Ordered 1 soya bean drink ice cold at $1.30. highly recommended. This stall is tucked away behind the location, opposite the famous kway chap stall.
author: Ken Peh

review_text: Nice and cheap soya bean and bean curd. Very thick and have a strong soya bean milk taste. They make their own soya milk and still selling for $1.20. 👍
author: Bee Choo Cheng

review_text: Loved my soybean grassjelly drink for $1.30. Good prices and everything is really fresh.
author: Cass

review_text:
Good to have soya bean curb and drink after a meal .
Reasonably priced !
author: WT Wong

review_text: Serangoon Soya Bean offers smooth, silky beancurd and refreshing grass jelly at affordable prices. A popular spot for light, tasty desserts in Serangoon.
author: Peter Tay

review_text:
My wife and I were here today (13 DECEMBER 2025) for an early lunch - it has been a while since we were last year and we have forgotten how very good the food was here at this well-established restaurant in Serangoon Garden. We ordered the following here: a "Chicken & Roast Pork Rice", a "Chicken & Char Siew Rice", a Watercress Soup and a "Barley Hot." The aforementioned rice meals were both very good - the meats were tender and the rice was fragrant and flavourful. The soup was served pipingly hot and flavourful. And the Barley drink was not overly sweet. And all of our ordered items arrived at our table "super fast." Service here was very good - friendly and courteous.. The dining ambience here was very nice and in air-conditioned comfort. I highly recommend this place for its reasonably priced Hainanese Chicken Rice and also its zi char dishes, which I have tried on previous occasions.

UPDATE OF 25 DECEMBER 2025
I was here with my wife and our son to try the following zi char dishes: Sweet and Sour Pork, Pow Sing Famous Bee Hoon, Chinese Spinach with Preserved Egg, 8 piece Nonya Ngoh Hiang, and Fried-Dry Beef Hor Fun. Overall, the zi char dishes were good - with the best being the Fried-Dry Beef Hor Fun and the passable only Sweet and Sour Pork.
author: edtayjb

review_text:
3.5/5 Have eaten here many times in the past and the last visit before this one was many years ago during Winter Solstice. On that occasion, we felt the standards have dropped quite a lot and wasn’t as good as before.

For this visit, we already had food in the area so we took away two dishes for dinner. The crispy squid (crispy, tangy, savoury with a little heat) is still one of their best dishes and is my favourite from Pow Sing. The cabbage with otah was quite pricey with 6 small pieces for 20 dollars or so and it was definitely not as good as before. It’s sad when restaurants you used to patronise drop in quality like this.
author: Julius Tan

review_text: Classic looking with classic vibe. Soup & chicken rice's still great. Only issue is peak hour traffic & wait for car park
author: Yoke Fei Phan

review_text:
Pow Sing Kitchen is probably the most ungenerous (or stingy if bluntly put) merchant I have encountered.

The half chicken (S$19.62; photos 1 to 3) was suspiciously tiny. (Yes, it was a half chicken. A half chicken that looked like a quarter.) review_text:
Reach 8.25pm but was told they close at 9 sharp, not last order at 9, go home at 9pm. author: Jy Jy

review_text:
I’ve been enjoying Tian Jin Fong Kee’s dumplings since I was a child, and after decades of loyalty, I can confidently say they remain the best dumplings in Singapore. Every bite carries the same handmade perfection: thin yet springy skin, juicy flavorful filling, and that unmistakable balance of taste that only comes from decades of craftsmanship.

It’s not just food, it’s heritage. Tian Jin Fong Kee has been part of my family’s dining memories for generations, and till today, their dumplings continue to set the benchmark. Truly a timeless treasure in Singapore’s food scene.
author: K W

review_text: This pan Fried Dumplings is very flavourful 10 pcs for $7. One thing the store owner can do better is to put the Dumplings nicely on the plate.
author: Daniel Aiden Leo

review_text: The steamed dumplings is excellent!!! I used to order 30 pieces of them for my gatherings. Those get all eaten up and my friends asked for more. Then I ordered 50 and that turns out to be not quite enough too. So it has since been advanced to 70 pieces. All eaten up as usual. When I don’t bring that for my gathering, my friends would ask for them. That says a lot isn’t it :) oh yes! The vinegar that they provide with it is of excellent quality too :) another plus point.
author: Rose Chua

review_text:
The homemade pork dumplings are delicious. The filling is juicy and well-seasoned, with nice flavor in every bite.

The fried handmade noodles are light yet satisfying, with a pleasantly chewy texture that adds depth to the dish.

The dough skin soup is another nice dish. The dough skin is thin and slightly chewy, complementing the rich, flavorful broth. Every component tastes freshly prepared with the comforting essence of homecooked food.
author: J Seng

review_text:
锅贴(guo tie) is a food that is well-liked by many chinese. They are also known as fried dumpling to many non-chinese speaking community.

In Singapore, there are many stalls and restaurants offering this snack to patrons. So which is the best of the best? Debatable yes, but my favorite is a stall located at serangoon garden hawker center.

The 锅贴has a crispy skin and the filling within is fresh and tasty. Dipped together with the vinegar and ginger, this is just amazing.

By the way, the photos were taken before heightened alert period. Words alone cannot describe how good this dish is. If i were to visit the stall again, i will probably gobble them up in the car.

Must eat when you are at the hawker. Won’t ever regret, unless you cannot take pork.

Enjoy!

#dumplings
author: Jason Deng

review_text:
Attracted by the wide variety of dishes from this cai fan stall and decided to give it a try. The server was very generous with the servings of the dishes. We like the sambal sotong and the curry vegetables. The pig trotters and chicken feet were tasty but not soft enough and cold.
Service was acceptable.
author: Jacob TAN

review_text: Jabo Japanese and Korean Cuisine. $5.80 for Bibimbap
author: J

review_text:
There are quite a lot of stalls I like at this place.

Satay very nice, satay sauce is very rich in peanut butter taste. Western food is very original and nice.

Korean food quite nice also for simple lunch. Roast Chicken stall have very nice 叉烧烧肉。

煮炒Stall not bad, I like their 招牌豆腐 （海鲜豆腐）
author: Chung Chan Lee

review_text:
Great Thai Food

Thanks to William' recommendation below decided to try Pad Thai here.

- Good wok hei, portion and fresh ingredients at affordable 6 dollars!

Definitely returning for more and also friendly stall owners too.

Hoping this review can encourage more people to try out so I can still have my Thai food craving fixed.
author: Gwen K

review_text:
Roast meat stall
Very customer friendly guy behind the roast meat stall as he asked if I would like the boiled chicken feet in my soup and I naturally said yes. It is my favourite. The big bowl of soup was nice.
The char siu was that dark roast kind which was delicious to a D! Hahaha my own legit jargon here!
The serving of sliced cucumber was generous and the plain rice tasted good.
I was hungry but still fair to tasting of my meal.

Satay stall nearby located within the same coffee shop
The operator looked professional behind the hot grill and took my order fast. My satay was delivered in 10 minutes to me whilst I was enjoying my char siu rice. There seem to be regulars who ordered the satay and went to the stall to replenish the gravy.

Five stars for good food and good service.
author: Gabby Fantasy

review_text: Delicious food and excellent value! The Tonkatsu was amazing, and I loved that the set comes with free-flow rice and cabbage. They also provide complimentary Japanese tea and water. The staff were friendly and very attentive.
author: Joseph Y

review_text: I absolutely enjoy having the premium pork loin set. It’s hands down the best tonkatsu I’ve ever had in Singapore. The rice and cabbage that comes with the set are free flow too. The staff is incredibly friendly and even refills the free tea without me having to ask.
author: Kris

review_text: Superb value for money with great portions of really nice tonkatsu! The deeply savoury and acidic pickles were also a nice touch as was the vinegrette for the cabbage which lightened the meal as opposed to the usual sesame sauce (also available if you prefer)
author: justin goh

review_text:
The Tonkatsu ramen didn’t quite hit the mark, with the ramen arriving a few minutes before the tonkatsu, which was a bit disappointing since the whole idea was to enjoy them together.
I had a sip of the soup and a bite of the noodles but decided to wait for the meat.

The broth lacked the depth and richness you'd expect from a tonkotsu base. The heat came from a generous splash of layu chilli oil, which overpowered rather than enhanced the flavour. The steamed cabbage was odd, and the bamboo shoots, while still crunchy, didn’t carry much taste.

The tonkatsu itself was decent but on the dry side. The breadcrumbs had a nice ratio but didn’t bring much aroma or flavour from the frying process.

The premium pork loin fared better-juicy and well-balanced in fat and meat but shared the same underwhelming crust.

As for the miso ramen, it was surprisingly mild. The tamago that came with it was slightly overcooked for my preference, lacking that gooey center.

The service was attentive and quick, which definitely stood out in an otherwise uneventful meal.
author: Ferdi

review_text:
August 2025
Here for lunch for the second time, and it was still as good. We loved the pork tonkatsu and the deep fried prawns.  Great that the rice and cabbage was still free flow.

Staff were friendly and the chef smiled and gave a small wave as he walked by.

June 2024
Had lunch here with the family and it was a good meal. Most of us chose the pork tonkatsu  and they were delish.  They came with free refills of sliced cabbage and rice, with soup as well.

The pork was fresh, well battered and tasty.   The char siu ramen was also great, and my wife loved the broth.

Staff were friendly and topped up the cabbage and drinks without being prompted.
author: steven lim

review_text:
One of my favourite stalls to get delicious cakes, especially chocolate walnut and sugee cake. There's even Earl Grey cake for those who love the tea flavour. Easy to find among the stalls at this popular hawker centre.

There's no pork nor lard, so it's good for vegetarians though not for vegans. Service is efficient and any queue moves fast. Have been coming here for donkey years and the standards are consistent.
author: Avril Atkeg

review_text:
Had lunch here, and still abit hungry, cane arias this stall.
Didn’t try their famous peanut pancakes… instead I opted for their in house bakes banana cake.
Cake was dense and moist.  Not much banana smell (I guess they don’t use artificial banana essence… that’s why).
So I guessed it’s more healthy!
author: YL Wong

review_text:
I've mixed feelings about their pancakes. Tried two flavors this time: coconut and peanut.

Had their coconut and it was truly awesome. Piping hot, crusty and fluffy.

Had their peanut though and it felt almost tasteless and powdery.

Portions have reduced by at least 30% too, though prices are maintained.

review_text: I tried their banana cake ($2.7) and decadent chocolate cake ($5.5) and I thought both were pretty decent in terms of taste and portion but would be much better if served warm (esp. the chocolate cake).

review_text:
3/August/2025
Had fried carrot cake, fried hokkien mee, fried oyster omelette & sugarcane juice for dinner, was good! Closed from 27 October 2025 to 26 January 2026 for renovations and upgrading works. This is a great food centre with a diverse selection of hawker food. Been eating here when i was younger and living in Serangoon Gardens. My current fav char kway teow is located at this food centre and they have quite a few good stalls serving BBQ sambal stingray.

On my last visit I was surprised to see that Chomp Chomp isn't as crowded as it used to be back in the day. On the bright side, it’s way easier to get a seat now.
author: Julius Tan

review_text: Ate the satay jawa from The Warung. Not bad. Delicious mutton satay. Spicy soya sauce and peanut gravy was given. Tahu goreng also recommend. If you like spicy, please do try.
author: Wan Sam

review_text:
Food is superb. Ordered delivery with the delivery tea time deal. Despite the huge discount, we were shocked by the $8 delivery fee despite living within the vicinity.

Despite the shocker, the food is something that we will return to again, but perhaps having it there in-person as the delivery and platform fees are just not worth it.

Thoroughly enjoyed the butter chicken and manchurian gobi, which is one of the more flavourful renditions we have had in a while.

See you soon!
author: MH Tham

review_text:
Fish head curry, lamb, and the butter chicken. Briyani rice was awesome too.

Full head and not those half heads bs in other restaurant.

It is a very delicious dinner!!

Highly recommended if you want to have a sumptuous North Indian meal
author: Alex Chew

review_text: We were craving for Indian food and chanced upon this Indian restaurant at Serangoon Gardens. The Chicken Tikka Masala, Butter Vegetable Masala was perfect served with hot naan. Highly recommend!
author: Zoe Xu

review_text: Amazing food - very refined taste, high standard. Service staff is also very friendly and highly responsive. Casual setting - comfortable for a low key dinner with friends or family!
author: Tiffiny Yang

review_text: Finally went to this hidden gem after living in the area for so many years. Restaurant had a nice, vintage feel. Servings are generous - the butter chicken and fried lady's finger were delicious. Will definitely come again!
author: Grace Goh

review_text: Garden Grill offered a comfortable and stylish ambiance. It wasn't overly fancy but had a nice feel for a special occasion or a more relaxed dinner. The seafood dishes were particularly impressive. I tried the lobster, crab, and scallops, and all were cooked well. The seasoning complemented the natural flavors of the seafood without overpowering them. It seems like a good choice for a quality seafood meal in a comfortable setting. The service was attentive, and the food was fresh and well-prepared.

review_text: First time eating at Garden grill based inside the SGCC club, the nice little restaurant upstairs is cozy, though a bit old.  Promotion pricing for meals was quite affordable.  $30 for 3 course, $40 for 4.  Definitely worth the price. Wine was also not marked up too high.  Food was good.  Shoes required.
author: Vinny

review_text:
The service staffs were very friendly and approachable. The atmosphere is friendly and cosy. The food is devious. The beef medium rare was cooked to perfection. The pork chop was soft and juicy
Very good value indeed!
author: John Koo

review_text: A cosy place for family and small group of friends to gather. The service staff all did a great job from welcome to preparing and serving the food. An old English setting but filled with warmth. The food is all great and will definitely be back again next month.
author: Han Emily

review_text: mushroom soup okay. mushroom chicken tender and juicy with really good roasted potatoes. brownie really good
author: natalie lim

review_text: Above average fishball noodles with bouncy fishballs and QQ meepok. Fried dumplings were freshly fried but not much meat filling. Overall, a nice place to have a leisurely weekday lunch.
author: Jerald Ici

review_text: A place to go if you’re craving for noodles or a late-night supper. You know you won’t go wrong. Noodles are tasty. Serving just right. Always to go-to for comfort food. 小锅面 extra nice on a rainy day, belly warming and comforting.
author: everlydaydream

review_text:
After cycling to a nearby bicycle shop, kitty and I decided to visit Ming Fa Fishball Noodles, a 24-hour establishment in Ang Mo Kio that I had saved on my Google Maps.

We were intrigued by their Fuzhou fishball noodles, so I ordered the Fuzhou fishball kway teow (dry), while Kitty opted for the fishball soup. We also ordered the prawn Wu Xiang platter. The Wu Xiang was quite nice. The Fuzhou yu yuan, the Fuzhou fishballs, and their regular fishballs were very flavorful.

The Fuzhou fishballs even had a soup filling inside. Unfortunately, Kitty discovered this the hard way, biting into one and spilling hot soup on herself, an occupational hazard with this particular dish. However, both the Fuzhou fishballs and regular fishballs were delicious, especially when dipped in the provided vinegar sauce.

My kway teow, on the other hand, was a bit dry. I had to add two teaspoons of soup to get the texture just right. It also lacked a prominent taste of vinegar, so we added some ourselves. Kitty suspected that the limited vinegar was a deliberate policy, allowing customers to adjust it to their own preference.

We also ordered two barley drinks, which tasted homemade and were quite refreshing. In total, we spent S$17, and the queue never seemed to stop, which is a testament to its popularity in this neighbourhood. Overall, the fishball noodles were okay, but the real stars of the show were the fishballs, especially the Fuzhou variety.

Impressed by the fishballs, Kitty even purchased some frozen fishballs and Fuzhou fishballs from their fridge section to cook at home, along with other items sold in the shop. It's a great option if you want to recreate the experience at home.

The service was fast and the staff were friendly. The price for the fishball soup and Fuzhou fishball noodles was reasonable, but the prawn Wu Xiang was slightly expensive, though tasty. The location was easy to find using Google Maps.

In conclusion, Ming Fa Fishball Noodles is a great place to visit, especially if you're a fishball fanatic. It has good ingredients and has a great menu to explore.
author: Doraemon

review_text:
25/01/2026

review_text:
Came for a weekday lunch. Maimon Nasi Padang is situated in Serangoon Garden Market, opposite Chomp Chomp.

Queue was already long, even at 1145am, but it's pretty fast moving. Malay uncle taking order was super friendly, always joking with his customers. Menu wise is non cluttered as they are listed in a number order. Ordered set 1, the ayam merah set, i.e. chicken cooked in a red colored gravy, for $5.50 which is very affordable.

The chicken used is definitely the fresh variety, not frozen. Chicken was lightly fried before finished in the red gravy. Gravy is tangy and slightly sweet, very flavourful, like the nice ones you get to sample in Malay weddings.

The accompanying sambal goreng comes recommended (reading from the reviews). Though nice, am not able to rate it as not exactly a fan of sambal goreng. Rice quantity served is just nice, and it was cooked fluffy. The bagedil (potato fritters) is definitely home made and is packed with flavor. Potato content is generous.

Lastly the homemade sambal, is the right blend of sweet and sour, and of the watery and not thick variety. Note: it also packs a punch, i.e., very, very spicy.

Separately, also had the Indonesian tahu telur as a side order. Size wise is just right to share for 2-3 pax. The tofu cake, the size of a human palm, is coated with an egg batter, cooked crispy on the exterior while keeping the interior tender and bouncy. The accompanying peanut gravy is splendid, with the right amount of sweetness to make it decadent. The tahu is topped with vegetable shavings of carrot and cucumber and an accompaniment of small Indonesian crackers.

Overall, Maimon Nasi Padang though listed as Indonesian Padang dishes, is more tuned/catered to a local Malay palette. This is not to be taken as a negative slight however, as the dishes still stands out for being very flavorful. Definitely recommended.
author: Martin Tan

review_text: Very delicious food. Ordered ayam merah and sambal goreng but the ayam was a bit tough and the sauce can be improved.  The sambal goreng was over cooked. The cabbage was very delicious though. Hub ordered mutton briyani and he said it was very delicious. The tahu telur with peanut sauce was very delicious and enjoyable too. Yummy! 👍🏻

Both of us had four side dishes each, and the total cost was $15, which is slightly pricey but acceptable for a coffee shop setting.
author: Lyla (ZL)

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $11) @ Ponggol Nasi Lemak.
.
Founded in 1979 by husband-and-wife team of Ang Chye Choon and Madam Koh Ah Tan, the latter being the 1st sister (and eldest) of the Koh Family behind the equally famous Mount Faber Nasi Lemak and Bali Nasi Lemak brands. Known for being the most accessible yet commercial entity amongst the 3 brands, with crowd-pleasing dishes.
.
Their short-grain jasmine white rice is gently infused with coconut milk and pandan / screwpine leaf essence, fragrant and fluffy with mild grainy earthy milky floral sweet flavour. The tiny deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies are crispy crunchy in texture with mild salty savoury fishy flavour, while the cucumber slices are juicy and burst with vegetal sweet flavour. The sunny side up chicken egg is wobbly soft and carries eggy savoury sweet flavour, the lovely runny yolk just beautiful.
.
The sotong / squid balls are bouncy with savoury sweet flavour, while the signature achar / Peranakan pickled salad (comprising cucumber, pineapple, shallots, garlic, ginger, lemongrass, turmeric, white vinegar, white sugar, salt, red chili, and crushed peanuts) is crunchy juicy crispy in texture with vegetal sour sweet spice nutty flavour. The highlight is the large chunky battered chicken drumstick, crisp outside tender inside, with robust meaty savoury salty flavour. The chunky sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste carries deep savoury salty spice flavour.

The staff upsold us this fish head they claimed to be sea fish and told us it was $40. The one in menu was $32 . When the bill came, it was $45!
The staff just told us he said wrongly and also the head he gave us was bigger. He did not apologise or offer to give us back the difference. Just excuses.

Does not mean you are family run shop, it is an excuse to just price carelessly outside of menu and charge otherwise.
If they can be dishonest about their prices. I am not sure what kind of food they serve. Likely it is the same $32 fish head they have served me.

i saw they scoop beef rendang from a big container. So, likely no difference from a glorified cai fan stall.

review_text:

The minced spinach was smooth and comforting, with just the right seasoning to bring out its natural sweetness. The grilled eggplant had a lovely smoky char that paired beautifully with steamed rice, while the sambal kangkong added a punch of spice and fragrance without being overwhelming.

What I really appreciate is how these simple vegetable dishes were cooked with care—flavorful, balanced, and not oily, making it a perfect lighter option compared to heavier zi char meals. The staff were warm and attentive, and the homely atmosphere made the experience even better.

A great spot in the neighborhood whether you’re here for their famous fish head curry or just a wholesome, fuss-free lunch. Highly recommended!

author: •you key•

restaurant_name: Suki-Ya - All you can eat shabu shabu (Heartland Mall Kovan)
review_text:
Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a Japanese all-you-can-eat shabu shabu restaurant that delivers generous portions, solid quality, and great value. Perfect for groups, families, or casual dinners, Suki-Ya lets you cook fresh ingredients at your table in simmering broth, choosing from two soup bases per pot to suit different tastes.

The buffet focuses on unlimited thinly sliced meats like pork and beef that cook quickly and stay tender. Orders are served fresh straight from the kitchen, keeping each serving hot and just right for tasting. Alongside the meats, there’s a self-service station with fresh vegetables, mushrooms, tofu, noodles, rice, and a variety of fish and meat balls — everything you need for a complete hotpot experience.

Sauces and condiments are easy to customise, letting you mix soy sauce, sesame, garlic, chilli, and more to match your preferred flavour profile. Most buffet packages also include unlimited soft drinks and simple desserts, offering a satisfying finish to a hearty meal.

Located inside Heartland Mall Kovan, the restaurant is easy to reach by public transport and fits well into a casual neighbourhood dining scene. The interior is straightforward and comfortable, designed to accommodate groups without fuss. Prices are affordable compared to premium hotpot spots, making this a go-to choice when you want a filling meal without overspending.

Overall, Suki-Ya at Heartland Mall Kovan is a reliable, well-priced shabu shabu buffet with fresh ingredients, friendly service, and a relaxed atmosphere.

URGENT SAFETY WARNING: Potential Food Contamination & Zero Support

I am extremely alarmed by a food safety incident with my recent order. We ordered "Crispy Fries" specifically for my 2-year-old toddler, as it is supposed to be a non-spicy, kid-friendly item.

Upon eating it, my son immediately started crying and was in visible distress. When I checked the food, I found the residual oil on the liner was not just spicy, but had a strong, lingering, and numbing sensation that felt unnatural and unlike standard food seasoning. We strongly suspect severe fryer cross-contamination or, worse, chemical contamination.

The response from this store has been unacceptable:

I submitted an urgent formal complaint via the official feedback form detailing this safety risk and have received NO acknowledgment.

The store phone number is a complete joke—it is just a useless automated loop with absolutely no way to speak to a real human being.

We have retained the food sample. If this matter is not addressed immediately with the seriousness it requires, I will be escalating this directly to the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) for investigation.

Parents, please be careful before feeding your children from here.

review_text:
We had an early dinner here on a Sunday, and there was no crowd yet. We ordered three dishes and wanted to order only one plate of rice to share for two people, as we are cutting down on rice portions. The staff taking the order informed me that they have small serving of rice (which is half of the normal portion). We agreed to have it. The portion is just nice for those who are on diet or cutting down on rice.

We ordered Siakap masak 3 rasa, Kailan, and Sotong Goreng Tepung. The Siakap Masak 3 Rasa was nice. The taste of the food here tastes better now compared to my previous visit. The Sotong Goreng Tepung was a bit hard, but for those with dentures or not having strong teeth, it might be difficult to chew. The Kailan was acceptable.

I also ordered chicken black pepper as a takeaway for myself. For drinks, we only ordered green apple juice without sugar. Overall, the cost was RM 80+, which is quite reasonable.

The location is a bit secluded, nearer to Sultan Abu Bakar Immigration Customs, which link to Tuas Checkpoint. For bikers, it is convenient to hang out and have dinner here then access the shortcut by passing the R&R Southbound Gelang Patah.

Recommended to dine here.

review_text:
Located inside the Bale Clubhouse, which itself is next to Senibong Golf Club.

Members of the public can patronise this restaurant. Just tell the security guardhouse that you're going to "Bale Social".

The building architecture is fabulous, especially the conical attap roof and the hanging lantern lamps.

The view is good and tranquil, overseeing a football/rugby field. JB International team teens were having lunch and trudging to the field thereafter. The club's feature swimming pools are also adjacent.

There's a long table that can seat 10 pax, and also a long bar counter facing the fields. Most of the other tables are 4-seaters.

Food is a mix of Western brunch/lunch mains/ bar bites and Asian/Malay dishes. They have kids-portion meals too. See attached photo for menu prices.

They allow pets in the designated outdoor seating area, but when dining with pets, all food and beverages will be served in takeaway packaging.

The restaurant doesn't have its own toilets. There is only 1 set of toilets/ changing rooms, located close to the pools.

Sufficient parking lots when we were there (15-20 lots).

Kid meals available. Pools and playground adjacent.

A little tight btw tables.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text:

review_text:

By the bar and pitch they have a good sized infinity pool (with sun loungers) and a smaller pool close by.

It has plenty of tables and seating for customers who want to watch live sports events on the televisions or that are going on in front of you.

The staff are polite and attentive, I will definitely return….given the chance I’d be there every Sunday.
author: Ian Gibson

review_text:
Lunch or dinner at the Bale Club in Leisure Farm is always a pleasure. The menu is broad and varied, with an equally impressive selection of drinks. The house red and white wines are keenly priced and surprisingly good, making them an easy choice.

The club’s setting creates a calm, relaxed dining atmosphere, with pleasant views over a small wooded area and nearby riding stables. For solo diners, an unobtrusive TV screen provides a touch of background interest without disturbing the tranquil ambience.

Service is consistently first class, and special mention must go to Livia, whose warmth and professionalism elevate the entire experience. Congratulations to the whole team — I would highly recommend visitors make a point of trying the Bale Club.

review_text:
Don't need to show up too early in the morning and that would also be helpful to avoid the throngs of people. I think 10am is just nice. The MO is to shop for seafood at the morning market and bring it to the Warung and ask them to cook anything from the menu. We chose Asam Pedas with Pari (from the market), small ones for fried, with omelette and rice. Since we didn't buy any veggies at the market, we opted for their own cabbage goreng.

The Asam Pedas kuah is thick and with black pepper, I noticed. Not spicy tho (at least not for me). It's the Malay version, food that my folks used to cook. Plenty of daun kesum, with rich & tangy flavor. I can't say it's the best asam pedas I've ever tasted but this place really deserves a thumbs up for the food coupled with the background scenery of fishermen's village. Really sets the mood.

This place is as local as it gets! I brought outta town friends here for a Tanjung Kupang/Gelang Patah breakfast experience and they were impressed and they loved it! 😁
author: N.a.d S

review_text:
A Malay-style cuisine restaurant that feels like it's in the rural end of Johor, located right next to a morning fish market where local fishermen bring in their daily catch of fish, prawns and crabs (and if youre lucky, lobster) of various sizes.

Relatively affordable, it doesn't get more sea-to-table than this, where all you have to do is get your seafood from the Pasar Pendekar Laut market and ask the friendly Malay aunties manning the kitchen to whip you something.

Cooking styles will differ based on the seafood you buy, with some chit-chat with the kitchen about what you want.

To get here, just park along Jalan Gelam near a roadside market stall and the Pendas Floating Restaurant, look for the stone bridge walkway that leads you past the small mangrove forest to this restaurant.

The place is clean is enough seating for about five or six tables for a little more than 25 seating capacity, and you'll be greeted by fishermen relaxing after a morning jaunt at sea.

Note: There is little to no data connection in this area.

You can really taste the quality in every dish. Highly recommended for anyone looking for authentic, no-frills, fresh seafood!

review_text:
Nestled by the tranquil lake, LS X Park restaurant offers a dining experience that is as visually stunning as it is flavorful. The restaurant boasts a beautiful ambience, with serene water views and a relaxed atmosphere that makes it an ideal spot for both casual gatherings and special occasions.

The menu features expertly prepared Chinese-style seafood, with fresh ingredients and bold flavors that truly stand out. Signature dishes like the salted eggs fried prawns and the teochew-style fish are particularly noteworthy, showcasing a perfect balance of seasoning and freshness. Each dish is thoughtfully presented, enhancing both the taste and dining experience.

Service is another highlight, with friendly and attentive staff who are always smiling, making guests feel genuinely welcome. Their promptness and warm demeanor add to the overall pleasant experience.

While prices are on the higher side compared to local standards, the combination of quality food, excellent service, and a picturesque location justifies the cost. For those looking for a memorable seafood dining experience by the lake, Lakeside Seafood Delight is well worth a visit.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text:
LS X Park Restaurant is a gem. The service, food, and atmosphere were stellar. The thoughtful touch of providing candlelights to keep flies away greatly enhanced our dining experience. No more swatting at flies, just enjoying great food.

The sesame chicken was a delight, the Ma Po style tofu with minced chicken and spicy bean sauce was flavourful, and the stir-fried kailan with garlic hit all the right notes. The dessert premium snow ice strawberry is really wonderful and pleasing to our tastebuds. Highly recommend this place for a memorable meal.

author: Janice Lee

review_text:
The Korean restaurant at Sunway Big Box Retail Park is a great choice for a cozy and flavorful dinner, especially if you're in the mood for authentic Korean cuisine. One of the restaurant's highlights is its signature spicy stir-fried chicken grill, which is prepared right in front of you on a large pan at your table, adding an interactive and exciting element to your dining experience.

While the menu leans towards spicy dishes, there are also milder, non-spicy options available, making it a suitable spot for families with kids or those with different spice preferences. The one that’s stands out is the "cheese fall" – a rich, gooey layer of melted cheese that’s served in the same pan as the grilled chicken. The combination of the savory chicken and the indulgent, creamy cheese creates a satisfying flavor that’s hard to resist.

Overall, the restaurant strikes a good balance between bold, spicy flavors and more approachable options, offering something for everyone. Whether you're a fan of Korean street food or just looking for a fun dining experience, this spot is well worth a visit.
author: Wesley Wong

review_text: The vibes here are pretty fun! It looks like you went to a real Korean restaurant. I mean, it is a Korean restaurant, but we are in Malaysia, right? So for me, it's like I'm not in Malaysia 🤣 whatever. While I wouldn’t necessarily come here for a romantic date (heh), I definitely recommend grabbing a group of friends. Never have I had a more pleasant meal. The staff was so polite and helpful, going above and beyond to make us feel welcome. We had a great talk, and thank you for that. I will definitely come again to taste other dishes. Oh yeah, the kimchi! Damn it, I almost forgot about it. Anyway, the kimchi totally met my expectations. I almost want to ask them for the recipes, haha, or maybe we can minta sikit untuk bawa balik. Kidding 😂

Had a lovely lunch here at this cosy and comfortable Korean restaurant. The ambience was warm and relaxing.

I enjoyed the signature gimbap - it was delicious and well-balanced, with fresh ingredients and satisfying flavours. I also tried the ox soup ramen, which was comforting and hearty—rich broth, tender meat, and perfect for a wholesome meal. The meal was complemented by a variety of tantalising side dishes, all well-prepared and enjoyable.

Service was pleasant, and the  dining experience felt homely, tasteful and satisfying overall
author: Evan

review_text: A very authentic Korean restaurant — the owners are a Korean family, and the food options are plenty. I especially loved their cheese cake roast chicken! The chicken is freshly roasted with golden crispy skin and tender meat. The cheesy “cake” on top is super rich and flavorful. The gimbap is also really good, and they offer both regular and mini sizes. Prices are reasonable, and the environment is cozy. A great place to bring family and friends!
author: yu wen

review_text: I've been here twice, and the food never disappoints.  I brought more over to try, and they both agreed this is one of the better Korean food around. Pretty authentic taste and place is clean with simple decor. Service is always friendly and good too. Prices are reasonable.
author: Jerry Tang

review_text:
Located in Citrine Hub level 2 beside Mr DIY.
Access via Tuas from Singapore would be nearer than from woodlands checkpoint.

Driving or grab here would both work fine. Public transport not much so.

It was packed on a Sat night at 6+pm. Staff were really friendly. Free flow side dishes were served promptly after ordering. All the side dishes were up to par!

The Mul-naengmyeon came first. It was one of the best I've tasted. Ice kept the dish cold. The sourish taste is balance not overwhelming but makes it very appetising. Buckwheat noodles chewy but not overly like some other places I had. Feels really authentic.

Beef Gimbap came next. Nicely cut and the fillings were generous!

Next up the original fried chicken, it was tender and hot. Pretty much like by the group. Personally loved the flavoured ones more but next time I'll try it.

BBQ pork belly came with some chives and bean sprout. It was really good for me, fatty good but not overly but on the oilier side. But pork belly so ya it's oilier than usual BBQ.

Army Stew came last. It was pretty authentic. Came with 3 ramyeon, spam, cheese, sausages and rice cakes etc. It was on the spicier side (for someone who can't really take spicy).

Overall experience was 👍🏼. Friendly staff who take orders at table. For refill of side dishes, please ask staff.
Price is also decent overall especially with the food quality. Be prepared for queue during peak timing and days although mall isn't exactly the most crowded ones.

Highly recommend if you're around the area

The Jj noodles sauce is not flavorful, bbq pork served on a gas stove (not on charcoal 😥).  The egg gimap got no taste and in strips.  Moreover, the table and metal cups have a sweaty cloth smell. I will bring my friends else where.
