author: Terry Chua

review_text: A very cool place to chill with friends and family. The food is always nice. The servers are helpful, polite and possess good product knowledge. The restaurant has a very relaxed ambience, very suitable for solo diners. I really recommend the Smoked Duck Aglio Olio, Eggs Benedict with Avocado, and Ruby Pink.
author: Azzad Hakimi

review_text:
Awesome Brew at Sunway Citrine is the go-to place for tourists, students, and locals alike whenever you arrived at this side of Medini Iskandar.
We had the Carbonara and Smoked Duck Aglio Olio and their honey lemon and finished the meal with their brownies.  The pasta and brownies were delectable (The Aglio Olio has that umami taste, the Carbonara was not 'jelak', and the brownies fudgy) and the drink refreshing.
We recommend coming here while getting your grocery shopping done or probably a quick coffee session after a stroll/run at the Emerald Lake nearby.
author: Farhan Hazman

review_text:
My family and I had a warm and wonderful dinner here. The food was delicious, the atmosphere was cozy, and the service was outstanding. Emily and the team were incredibly attentive and thoughtful. They even surprised me with a birthday song and cake, which made the evening extra special.
Truly one of the best dining experiences we’ve had. Highly recommended!
author: JADE TEO

review_text: Absolutely wonderful, lovely staff. Everyone was so friendly, welcoming and smiley. They have a lot of good looking things on the menu, and also some set lunches. I ordered a corned beef and arugula pizza. Food came very quickly, and the pizza had a generous amount of toppings on as well. The crust is thin and crispy. Absolutely delicious. Would love to come and try their other pizzas next time, and the other menu items!
author: Kimberley Howarth

review_text:
Pizz@ in Sunway Citrine is a great place for casual Western food, and it consistently delivers on quality. The dishes are well prepared, with flavors that feel a step above typical mall restaurants. Their pizzas are the highlight, but the pasta and other mains are also reliable and nicely portioned. You can tell the kitchen puts care into what they serve.

The service is another strong point. Staff are friendly, welcoming, and attentive without being pushy, which makes the dining experience relaxed and comfortable. Even during busy periods, they manage to keep things running smoothly.

The overall atmosphere is cozy and pleasant, suitable for both quick meals and casual gatherings. Prices are reasonable for the quality you get.

Overall, Pizz@ is a solid choice in Sunway Citrine if you’re in the mood for good Western food and warm service. It’s a place you can return to knowing the experience will be consistently satisfying.
author: Yuki Takei

review_text:
I had such an amazing experience here! We ordered pizza, quesadilla, chicken wings, chicken salad, and fries everything was absolutely delicious and fresh. Each dish was well-seasoned and satisfying, honestly better than expected.

What made the experience truly special was the service. The staff were incredibly kind and attentive, and when they found out it was my birthday, they surprised me by making a cake for me. I was genuinely touched by writing name on the cake🥹🎂

Great food, outstanding service, and a warm, welcoming atmosphere. I’ll definitely be coming back and highly recommend this place to anyone looking for good food and great vibes! ⭐️😄
author: 고효정

review_text: This restaurant is an amazing find. Great food, excellent beers, and a gorgeous  view from the outdoor seating. We grabbed a table outdoors just in time to watch the sky change colours, it was the highlight of our visit. The staff were incredibly warm and friendly, making us feel right at home. Perfect for a relaxing evening. Will definitely be back!
author: Jiah Ming Chong

review_text: Amazing fine dining experience! Food prepared by the chefs was superb, and love the open-concept yet cozy dining area. There were also small interesting stories behind the dishes, shared by the lovely female staff. They were very sweet to prepare a surprise birthday tart. We really enjoyed ourselves and definitely value for money!!
author: Bi Jun

review_text: Nice dining experience over here. We have went there to celebrate for our 13th anniversary together with our kid. Food is decent and is as good as some of the Michelin starred restaurants that we have been to around the world. Thanks for the chef for the small gesture to serves us the noodle and is nice too!
author: Justin Yak

review_text: A unique experience! Celebrating my brother's birthday at Kioku was the best decision. My typically conservative Teochew brother loved the 2.5-hour dining experience. The fusion of modern French and Italian cuisines, with Hungarian-sourced foie gras, was extraordinary. Every dish was a delightful surprise in presentation and flavor. The white and red wine pairings complemented the dishes perfectly. The ambiance was elegant yet cozy, and the staff were exceptionally attentive and friendly. Thank you, Kioku, for a memorable evening. We will definitely be back!
author: Kkenn Kkenn

review_text:
The meals are fantastic! I can definitely say the quality of the food comes from a very highly skilled chef!

I was very welcomed in by everyone when I stepped into their tinted up front door. Ambiance wise, I loved sitting right in front of the kitchen to see them cook my food!

The dessert is so good, that I had to get another one for my girlfriend because I finished all of it!

I highly recommend everyone to come in and try!
author: Deangelo

review_text:
A visit to Kioku is not just a culinary but also a sensory experience. The presentation of each well thought out dish is performed with precision and intricacy, and they can easily be described as unique works of art.
We choose the Meteorite menu which is comprised of dishes solely selected by the chef. This could be viewed as risky, however, Shawn Shum, is skilled in creating an eclectic mix of dishes that compliment each other and deliver a memorable experience.
There were many great dishes included within the menu served, particular highlights being the scallop and truffle, sea urchin fettuccine, potato and the caviar. The guava themed dessert was also outstanding.
A very memorable meal presented by a professional and friendly front of house team, whose descriptions of the dishes and attention to detail very much added to the overall experience. Definitely a restaurant we look forward to returning to.
author: Trevor Cherry

review_text:
Chili chicken is by far the best in jojoba. Korean flavor. Crispy and soft inside, with a spicy and sweet sauce. I'll definitely be back.

It tastes like the delicious chicken I used to eat in Korea. Dakgangjeong is the best. Crispy on the outside, moist on the inside, and the sauce is delicious. Whenever I crave chicken, this is my go-to place. Highly recommended!
author: 예신

review_text:
The staff at this cat cafe are incredibly kind and skilled at handling the cats.
Every cat here is adorable and very friendly toward people.
Please note that the cat zone is kept at a cool temperature. You will have a much more comfortable and enjoyable time if you wear long sleeves and long pants.

The soufflé on the menu is absolutely outstanding. It is so delicious and carefully prepared that this place could easily pass for a specialty soufflé shop.

• Operating Hours: 11:30 – 21:30
• Communication: The owner is very responsive and easy to reach via WhatsApp.

I highly recommend this place to all cat lovers!
😸😻😽😺
author: BD.P

review_text:
An awesome place that you must visit at Iskandar area.
The combination of a cafe + cats area + children playground really make this place so outstanding.
The drinks and desserts are nice, not very sweet and serve in an average size.

Love the cats here, all are so cute, lovely and gentle. They will come to you directly, aren't scare of strangers.
So much fun over here by hugging, playing and picture taking with them.
They are very well taken care by staffs.

The staffs are very friendly and you can see their smiles on their faces.

The environment is good, very cozy, comfortable and clean.
Really enjoy a lot and have a very good experience.

Highly recommended!!!
author: Littlebrownie 1015

review_text:
We had such a wonderful birthday party at Kids X Cats! All we had to do was bring the birthday boy—everything else was perfectly handled by the amazing crew. 🎉

The team made the entire experience smooth, fun, and stress-free. The kids had an incredible time, and all the invited parents absolutely loved the concept. Such a fantastic idea and beautifully executed!

Highly recommended for anyone looking for a unique and memorable party experience. 😻🎂✨
author: Sarah Ng

review_text:
Been here twice before, and each time is a refreshing experience.

The cats are very well taken care of, and they are quite gentle too. They will come to you for pets and head rubs, even without food. They have a wide variety of exotic breeds, and every cat has a different personality too.

If you pass by this area, the cat cafe is a must-go. 🐱
author: Hui

review_text: Awesome place in the Iskandar area for kids to enjoy time with cats. Cat zone is spacious and kept clean. Cats are gentle (e.g., “waited their turn for snacks”) and look healthy. There is also a play area for kids to have fun if not playing with cats. Ample parking.
author: CL Lee

restaurant_name: Sushi House Citrine Hub Sunway Iskandar
review_text: A great place for quality Japanese food with good portions and warm service. Tried the chuka appetizers, which were nicely seasoned and paired well with the meal. The sashimi was fresh and well-prepared, especially the salmon, which was clean, buttery, and generous in portion. The Oyako Don was a pleasant surprise—very generous serving, and very filling. Had a very satisfying Japanese dinner here.
author: Evan

restaurant_name: Sushi House Citrine Hub Sunway Iskandar
review_text:
Had dinner at Sushi House in Citrine Hub and walked away with mixed feelings. The place itself was casual and comfy, and what really stood out was the service—super friendly, attentive, and fast. Staff were polite from the moment we walked in, and they checked in often without being pushy. It made the whole experience feel warm and welcoming.

Food-wise, it was alright. I tried a few sushi rolls and sides—nothing terrible, but nothing that wowed either. The fish was fresh enough, portions were fair, but flavours felt pretty standard. It’s the kind of spot where you get what you expect—satisfying if you’re hungry, but not something you’d go out of your way for.

Still, I left with a smile mostly thanks to how well we were treated. If you’re in the area and want something simple with great service, this place does the job.
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: Sushi House Citrine Hub Sunway Iskandar
review_text:
It was a very great experience at Sushi House ❤️❤️ really feels like Japan whenever me and my family went here when we crave for Japanese food..

The food here serves elite... Really did full I'll our cravings 🙏🙏👍👍 really recommend those who loves Japanese food.. 💗💗
author: Josiah Aeden I Juenaidi Goius

restaurant_name: Sushi House Citrine Hub Sunway Iskandar
review_text: The sushi is delicious and all the other meals are nice too. Love the atmosphere. If only they have sushi belt, it would be perfect!
author: Amirah

restaurant_name: Sushi House Citrine Hub Sunway Iskandar
review_text: Ordered the double salmon roll, sashimi salad and tonkatsu curry rice. The roll and rice were OK, but the salad was disappointing compared to other restaurants as the sashimi were small and little.
author: Ho Yuan Seng

review_text:
Love the ambience.. Clean Warung..
Prefect breakfast buffet to dine.
Food potion just nice.. Food taste just right..
The best thing it is a buffet but been served by friendly and polite staffs like Tina and Komal.
They went extra miles to communicate and build rapport with customers.. Thumbs up guys❤️❤️
author: Juwairiah Hussein

review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ High quality food and great service!

I finally tried their famous Nasi Goreng and it did not disappoint! The flavors were bold and authentic, and everything was served steaming hot and fresh. The portion size is spot on—very filling for an adult.

I was also impressed by the tea; it wasn’t diluted or watery like some places, but had a nice, strong tea taste that was just right.
The service was excellent from start to finish. Friendly staff and a great atmosphere overall. I’ll definitely be coming back for more!

Highly recommended!
author: Jussree Acestrider

review_text:
This place resonates the feeling of home. The open view for outdoor dining yet being sheltered from the sun, adds on to the positive dining experience.
Malay cuisines are definitely authentic and brings back childhood memories.
Western menu selection are also within children's palate.
Thumbs up for the great food and atmosphere!!
author: Jamal Al-Rashid Hussain

review_text: The food is delicious and I think the nasi lemak is the best here in johor. The roti canai is crispy and the curry is nice. The lontong basah is tasty too. Their coffee is also lovely. But too bad they uses syrup for their apple and orange juice which is a letdown or else  would have given them 5 stars. Their strong point is their local fare. And too bad their coffee tea cannot choose kosong as my spouse is allergic to sugar.
author: Belle Lee

review_text:
absolute worst food in jb i’ve tried. don’t trust the hype on tiktok or facebook, it was really bad. and for 30rm+ per pax, it’s poor value considering what you get here.

nasi lemak 2/10 - rendang, rice, sambal were all horrible

coffee 1/10 - can’t believe they used instant coffee instead of kopitiam style kopi.

pancake 3/10 - dry and lack flavour. stingy with the syrup.

bread 1/10 - stale and toaster not even working properly.

lontong kering 1/10 - sambal was not nip

the only thing i give them is their service which was good. but with such poor food, there is really no reason to visit this shop.
author: Haziq

review_text: Love the generous portions and sets (2-3pax) you can choose. I enjoyed the side dishes and every dish were cooked perfectly and tasted authentic.
author: Lisa T

review_text: Super delicious, love the tamagoyaki super delicious. Highly recommend the sweet sour chicken, it was super flavourful and tender. The spam sushi roll was also super delicious, the rice was soft and fluffy. Love the pancake too, it was soft and a generous amount of fillings. The tobokki was also spicy enough and chewy . The zhajiang noodles was also superb, it was seasoned well with the black sauce.
author: xaxxolonch

review_text: Best jajjangmyeon in JB! Have been to the restaurant when they were at Molek and I’m glad that the taste didn’t change despite the extra 40min drive! Ordered their jajjangmyeon with tangsuyuk and mandu and they were very delicious! Missed having it when I was in Korea and it definitely hit the spot satisfying my craving for a good jajangmyeon! The tangsuyuk is a must order and the kimchi sides was very good too. Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a great jajangmyeon and tangsuyuk, along with a variety of other dishes from their menu!
author: Melvin Liew

review_text: Food is super delicious, top notch and portions are huge.My kids especially loved Tangsooyuk(sweet and sour pork) Staffs are friendly and attentive. Must try if you have korean Chinese food cravings. Highly recommended if you are nearby and wondering what to eat !
author: HJ

review_text: Cozy and relaxing environment with good food. The food portion is huge, definitely can share it with a few more people. My favourite is their jjajangmyeon, the gravy is thick and savory with smooth textured noodles. Sweet and sour pork is decent too. Seafood noodle soup however, the soup itself is decent but the ingredients are not so fresh. Overall, it does taste authentic.
author: Jayon See

review_text:
Cafe Green was such a pleasant surprise — clean, cozy space and genuinely friendly staff. My friend and I ended up eating until we were completely stuffed (in the best way), and we’re already planning to come back!

Black Sesame Cream
The black sesame cream was incredibly smooth and just the right level of sweetness. It paired perfectly with the bitterness of the coffee, making the whole drink really balanced and addictive. I’ve seen this combo trending in Korea, so I wanted to try it — and it definitely lived up to the hype.

Creamy Mushroom Chicken Croissant
Since it’s a new menu item, I decided to give it a shot, and I’m so glad I did. It honestly felt like eating a creamy mushroom risotto, but in croissant form. The flavor was deep and rich, and the creaminess was super satisfying.

Tteokbokki
This tasted like proper, delicious Korean tteokbokki — comforting, flavorful, and not overly sweet. The rice cakes were cooked to the perfect texture: soft but still pleasantly chewy.

Mango Bingsu
The milk-based flakes were unbelievably soft and light, and the sweetness was just right. It reminded me of the really good mango bingsu spots in Korea, so it felt extra comforting. I haven’t had one like this in a while, and I absolutely loved it.

Overall, great food, great vibe, and great service. Highly recommend — and I’ll definitely be back!
author: 전지혜

review_text:
Saw a review somewhere below that complained about the Matcha flavour…. Unfortunately I’d have to agree! I usually try to be more forgiving to seemingly newer cafes because I know business is hard these days, but I think in terms of some of the food/drink quality, things need to be improved if not you might not have repeat customers.

Food aside, front counter staff was very friendly!

1. Cheese Matcha Latte but no cheese top?
I remember seeing in the menu that there was supposed to be a cheese top but as you can see from when the drink just arrived, there wasn’t a cheese top. I tried to find the cheese in my drink but I couldn’t either. It was only after a while that I managed to drink some cheese bits.

2. Extremely tough beef in the beef stew
Because my meal had no proteins, I wanted some meat to go with it. Unfortunately the beef in the stew was very very very very tough. It was really hard to chew… The stew had decent flavour though.

3. Ingredient quality for Big Breakfast nothing impressive
It was ordinary bread, mushrooms, chicken sausages, cherry tomatoes. Normally for big breakfast it would as least not be button mushrooms or just white bread etc to make the meal more than just what you can make at home on your own.

As a whole I would say there wasn’t anything too impressive about the food flavour. My main was a Chapagetti to curb my noodle cravings hahaha. It was done quite ok but then again it’s just instant noodles with egg.

Anyways in summary, this is not a place I would return to again. If you happen to be in the area and are looking for something to satisfy your Korean food cravings, maybe you could drop by. If not, it’s not a place I would specially visit.
author: Serene Teo

review_text:
I visited Cafe Green today and I can confidently say it’s a place I’ll definitely be coming back to.

I usually only drink Americano or a regular latte, but the Black Sesame Latte here was honestly the best I’ve ever had. It had a deep, nutty flavor without being heavy or greasy, and it blended beautifully with the coffee aroma. It wasn’t overly sweet like a dessert drink — it tasted clean, balanced, and almost wholesome. From now on, this might be the only drink I order here.

The Creamy Mushroom Chicken Croissant felt like their signature menu item. It reminded me of dipping fresh bread into a rich cream pasta sauce. The sauce was smooth and flavorful, coating the flaky croissant perfectly. The balance of mushrooms and cream was just right — rich but not overwhelming. After one bite, I immediately thought, “I need to come back for this.”

The homemade Greek yogurt was thick yet smooth and pleasantly nutty. It wasn’t too sour, and it paired beautifully with banana and granola. Light, satisfying, and perfect as either a brunch side or a healthy dessert.

The shrimp avocado sandwich tasted fresh and wholesome. It wasn’t overly seasoned, allowing the natural flavors of the ingredients to shine. A great option if you’re looking for something clean and nourishing.

The staff were incredibly kind and welcoming, which made the whole experience even better. I heard the ownership recently changed, and it truly feels upgraded in terms of quality and detail.

If you’re looking for a cozy, clean space with thoughtfully made food and drinks, I highly recommend visiting Cafe Green.
I’ll definitely be back soon.
author: hyunjoo Jung

review_text: Had breakfast here on a weekday and it wasn’t crowded, which made for a relaxing experience. We were greeted warmly by a polite male staff member, and the service throughout was attentive and pleasant. The coffee and matcha latte were excellent, much better than what you’d get at Coffee Bean or Starbucks, and at a reasonable price too. The brunch portions were generous and delicious overall. Only feedback is that the mushrooms had a very strong earthy taste, perhaps consider balancing the flavor a little.
author: Michael Angelo

review_text:
Nice and cosy little cafe. Came in the morning and tied their ham and egg sandwich and banana chocolate waffle. It was really good. And potion were generous. We will come back to try their Bingu which everyone is raving about.
There is also a golf range in the premise
author: GiGATT Admin

review_text:
This Nyonya restaurant truly captures the essence of Baba Nyonya heritage from its nostalgic décor to the charming atmosphere that transports you back in time. The dishes are delicious and authentic, saving me a trip to Melaka just to enjoy genuine Nyonya flavors. Every bite reflects the rich heritage of Peranakan cuisine.

While the portions are a bit on the smaller side, the taste more than makes up for it. The meal ended perfectly with their chendol dessert refreshingly sweet and rich, an ideal conclusion to a satisfying dining experience.
author: Jack Ho

review_text:
20 Dec 2025
Second visit. We over-ordered for 2. This would be ideal for 3-4 pax for first photo.

Love their ayam buah keluak, very flavourful though abit watery compared to what I have eaten in other restaurants. Their sambal chilli is nice but it burned my stomach abit - I still love the lady finger’s with sambal chilli. Sotong with pineapple and tomato was refreshing and abit spicy. Ngoh Hiang was abit normal to me.

The lady boss was around this time and she was warm and nice to take our order and reminded us to try the buah keluak (1 piece / person and additional would need to pay). It was thoughtful that they gave us little spatula to dig out the flesh. This service, we have not seen elsewhere.

9 Oct 2025
The kueh paiti has very good chilli. Poteng chicken was good! Love the sauce! First time having the sambal chilli over the boiled lady’s finger. These were for 2 ladies hence we went as light as possible.
author: Jessie

review_text: Late lunch blind Reece, gate crashed staff’s meal break…decent food served pipping hot, chapchay could be stewed longer, best is chendol topped with scope of durian
author: Patrick Goh

review_text:
The Sambal Ladyfingers was a standout for me—the sambal was flavorful, with a nice balance of spice and tanginess that complemented the tender ladyfingers perfectly. It was a dish I’d happily order again. I bought their ready made sambal

The Egg Omelette was simple yet satisfying. It was well-cooked, fluffy, and had a comforting homely feel to it.

The Rendang Beef meat was tender and the rich, aromatic rendang sauce was packed with depth and spice. It’s clear that the dish had been slow-cooked to perfection, making it a must-try for anyone visiting the restaurant.

To end the meal, I tried the Chendol which was a delightful dessert. The combination of coconut milk, palm sugar, and pandan jelly was refreshing and not overly sweet. It was a perfect way to round off the meal.

Overall, my experience at the Nonya restaurant was enjoyable.
Will come again
author: Boon Leong

review_text: Nice environment with authentic Nyonya dishes. I tried the Ayam Cencalok, Chap Chai, and Duck Soup – all tasty and well-cooked. The highlight for me was the Cendol, which was really nice.
author: James Low

review_text: Authentic Korean Food! Love the fried chicken and soy chicken.. Cold noodles were delicious and refreshing.. Portions were big too..
author: Mel Mel

review_text: This restaurant is a truly authentic Korean establishment, run by Koreans. A must-visit for anyone who appreciates original Korean flavors. I absolutely love their oil-free fried chicken, comforting chicken soup, and delicious pancakes. The food prices are reasonable and within an affordable range.
author: Mei Fei

review_text:
Koco Dak has quickly become a popular spot in Johor Bahru for Korean fried chicken lovers, and for good reason. Here's a breakdown of what you can expect:

What Stands Out:

•	Crispy, Flavorful Chicken: The star of the show is undoubtedly the fried chicken. The batter is consistently crispy, and the chicken itself is juicy and tender. They offer a variety of flavors, from the classic original to the sweet and spicy yangnyeom, and even more adventurous options like garlic soy.

•	Generous Portions: Koco Dak is known for its generous portions. A half-chicken order is usually enough to satisfy two people, making it a great value for money.

•	Authentic Korean Sides: Beyond the chicken, they offer a selection of Korean side dishes like kimchi, pickled radish, and coleslaw, which complement the meal perfectly.

•	Casual and Lively Atmosphere: The restaurant has a casual and lively atmosphere, making it a great place to hang out with friends and family.

review_text: The food was very good and authentic. The batter of the fried chicken is a bit different from what I am used to, but it is still nice and crispy for a wet batter. Noodles were delicious and chewy and full of flavour. Highly recommended to come here to get your Korean fix :)
author: Russell Yap

review_text: Visited many times and the Mee Bandung is still the top favourite. Thick, flavourful gravy with big prawns. Great food and a cozy place to dine.
author: fasyihah

review_text:
They offer many types of local dishes with both set and à la carte options and not much Western food.

I ordered the Nasi Tomato Ayam Masak Merah, the rice was slightly salty on its own, but once paired with the chicken, it tasted just right. The roti bakar wasn’t very crunchy and felt a bit chewy, but overall it was still okay.

A nice bonus is the small playground for kids, making it easier for parents to enjoy their meal.
author: Hasymah

review_text:
Came here to eat a year plus ago maybe and loved their assam pedas ikan, so I came back today for more! Absolutely loved the spice and their coffee was soo thick and good!

The service was so homely and friendly. Lots of families around too so its kid friendly!!!

Definitely drop by if you're looking for some good Malay cuisine with a great environment!
author: Sunantha S

review_text: Chanced upon this lovely bistro at Medini near to Big Box and enjoyed the ambience and food very much. Had laksa johor which was mild in flavour but generous in greens! The fish asam pedas was palatable and the menu for 2 pax portions was very worth the price. The dishes were carefully plated which made the food look appetising. Love that they have healthy green smoothies too, such as spinach apple cucumber (or was it celery?) slushie. And the chendol, mmm unforgettable! Only thing is, we entered the eatery thinking it was muslim owned due to its name but realise it may not be halal certified. 🫢Hope to have some clarity on this pls so we can come back again.☺️ thank you!
author: Wee Gapar

review_text:
It’s cozy, it’s nice, it’s homey, and the portion itself is generous. Owner’s are friendly!

Had a set for two, with fish assam pedas, chicken satay, and bende sambal, it’s fulfilling and honest!

Best vibes, if you are from outside of JB and need a best place to chill with homies and families, i recommend this place!
author: Izzat Ahmad

review_text: This vegetarian cafe is seriously impressive! The atmosphere and interior design are beautiful and very cozy. The food is not only delicious but also beautifully presented, and it’s great to find vegetarian dishes that are both healthy and satisfying. Prices are reasonable, and I’ll definitely keep coming back. Can’t believe I only just discovered this hidden gem, such a comfortable place, and the food is truly amazing. 🌱
author: slbxss

review_text:
First time visiting Vine Café and I absolutely love the vibe!
The café is filled with plants and natural light, making it very comfortable and relaxing.

The vegetarian food exceeded my expectations — tasty, well-presented, and lots of options to choose from.
Highly recommended for anyone looking for good vegetarian food in a nice environment.
author: Venis Ng

review_text:
A total win for vegetarians. Thoughtfully crafted dishes, rich flavors, and zero compromises. Everything felt fresh, balanced, and made with real care. The service was smooth, warm, and on point. An excellent experience overall—I’ll definitely be back.

The service truly stood out—kind, attentive, and effortlessly awesome. Every interaction felt warm and genuine, with the staff striking that perfect balance between being helpful and giving space. It was the kind of care that makes you feel welcomed rather than managed, turning a simple meal into a feel-good experience. Professional, graceful, and full of good energy, the service alone makes this place worth returning to.

🥂
author: DrDurgasreelaxmi Sreemurugan

review_text:
A super worth vegetarian cafe & what I love the most is the Ourh Lurk & Shrooms rendang nasi lemak here. Super recommend it

The coffee & desserts here also nice especially the limited lemon tiramisu, sour sweet is just on point.

Almost every vegetarian choices here are tasty, and lunch hour are full house always
author: 易斯路Lewis Jayson

review_text:
My husband and I held our wedding lunch for our close family at Vine Cafe at the end of November 2025. It was Vine Cafe’s first time hosting an event, and also our first time engaging a cafe for catering, so we weren’t quite sure what to expect.

We were truly surprised and grateful for the extra effort the Vine Cafe team put into every detail, from the food proposal and presentation to the decorations (indoor and outdoor) and even the door gifts for our guests. For our lunch buffet, we had a well-thought-out spread that included appetizers, blue pea nasi lemak, fried mihun, sandwiches, mini burgers, finger food, desserts, and drinks. The menu was proposed by Vine Cafe based on our budget and preferences, and we were able to discuss and adjust everything to find the most suitable options.

All of our guests were very impressed with the food, especially since they didn’t expect such a delicious and well-presented vegetarian buffet at a cozy cafe in Johor Bahru.

We’re really happy that we chose Vine Cafe as the venue for our wedding lunch. It turned out to be a memorable and meaningful experience for us and our family.
author: Wen Chee Wong

restaurant_name: HY YUEXIANG RESTAURANT 红盈私房菜
review_text:
Friday 7pm, we are the only customer. This restaurant is newly opened, maybe not many people aware of this restaurant yet.

review_text:
At the back of my mind I always expect Italian food to be “pizza””pasta” “bruschetta” and wine. I was totally blown away by what my taste buds felt for the night with authentic Italian food.

We were serve on the house tomato bruschetta as an appetiser, followed by soute di vongole. The clamps were fresh with generous portion, the lemon adds zesty texture but be mindful not to squeeze it as it will get too sour.

The mains are sirloin, squid ink pasta and risotto (both out of the menu, you have to ask), and let me tell you it didn’t disappoint. The squid ink pasta was something I’ve never tried or tasted before, and I was fortunate to had ordered it. IT WAS 🤯. It’s hard to put into words, but it has a hint of spiciness, with generous portion of seafood like squid and prawn. If given the chance do order it. IT’S A MUST!
The risotto was savoury with the cheese melting on the broth, creating a creamy texture well balanced with the rice.
The sirloin was tender with medium rare. On the side with mash potatoes and caramelised onions, with pink salt and herbs as condiments. Gently dip the beef in the condiment to add umami. The mash potatoes are a blessing, smooth and buttery, top with the onion to make the perfect combo bite!
We end the night with our favourite must have tiramisu and caramel panna cotta, satisfied!

It was truly a pleasant experience dining in here! Perfetto
author: Lee Eric

review_text: THE BEST and Most Authentic Italian cuisine cooked by the lovely Nonna Patricia. Miss it very much when we are back in KL. Last night we were treated to her signature Almond Biscuits that were sublime. Will keep coming back when in Johor

review_text:
Sep 2025: Reopened. The menu is similar to the previous one. Now open at 7:30 AM. They offer pre-made steamed buns and millet porridge. The braised pork for dinner was also excellent. The noodles with soybean paste were too salty.

They are a bit more expensive than other places we have been to... the bill for 2 people at lunch was around RM50... but we did pick quite a few items. restaurant_name: HUP HONG IPOH WHITE COFFEE 合丰怡保白咖啡
review_text:
We stopped by HUP HONG Ipoh White Coffee (合丰怡保白咖啡) for a simple afternoon tea break, keeping things light with just toast and drinks. The place carries a familiar Malaysian kopitiam feel, clean and comfortable, and it’s clearly positioned as a more branded, café-style version of traditional Ipoh white coffee shops.

The toast was decent — nicely crisp on the outside and soft inside — and paired well with the drinks. The white coffee itself was smooth and aromatic, staying true to the Ipoh-style profile, though it didn’t particularly stand out compared to other well-known Ipoh coffee brands. Everything tasted fine, just nothing that really wowed us.

One thing that stood out more was the pricing. For what we ordered — simple toast and drinks — the prices felt quite expensive for an afternoon tea, especially when compared to traditional kopitiams offering similar items at lower prices. You’re likely paying more for the brand name and the more polished environment.

Overall, it’s a comfortable place for a casual tea break if you’re already nearby, but not somewhere I’d go out of my way for purely on value or taste.
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: HUP HONG IPOH WHITE COFFEE 合丰怡保白咖啡
review_text:
I have always enjoyed this place and have been a loyal customer since I moved to the area. Unfortunately, today’s experience really changed my view.

My simple order, a White Coffee and Mee Hoon Soup, took 30 minutes to arrive even though the restaurant was not busy. When the waiter finally brought my food, I made a friendly remark in Malay, “Wah, long time today.” Her response shocked me. She replied, “Busy lah, not only your order, we have others too,” and walked away with a sulky face.

After waiting so long and being spoken to like that, I honestly lost my appetite.

Will I return? Sadly, no. A relationship of more than a year with this restaurant is now shattered. Still, thank you for the past service.

My friend had to top up his balance and to make matters worse, the signal inside the shop was very weak, so he had to step outside just to get a connection…

Authentic Chinese beef Ramen, the team from 甘肃省 China.

We ordered their famous beef noodles at promotion price of RM9.90. The Ramen(noodles) is superb and tasty. The broth and beef is fresh and delicious too.

We also ordered beef dumplings which is also delicious and at promotional price of RM9.90 for 13 beef dumplings!

Their mutton skewers were very chewy and nicely flavoured with dried chilli herbs. We preferred their grilled chicken gizzards than the mutton.

Thumbs up to the team.
author: Lennox Cheok

review_text:
11 Jul 2025

First attempt to have lunch at this restaurant. Actually attracted by their lunch promotion of beef noodle and dumpling, sold at RM9.90 each

The taste was good. The noodle elasticity is just nice. We also ordered the stir fried beef with veggies that came with rice, tasty.

The only thing is the language barrier with the serving crew so you need to be patient.

Place to be revisited.
author: Cheewee Kok

review_text:
One of my go-to spots for mee tarik in JB!

Mee tarik is smooth and light-never jelak.
Nasi goreng is tasty and well-seasoned.

The highlight? Their beef and lamb skewers. super tender with just the right spices.

Even the fried potato is great-crispy, flavorful, and the portion was huge. 2 people couldn’t finish it. Easily enough 3-4ppl to share.
author: mohamad ariffin

review_text:
Dining at Alchemist felt less like eating at a restaurant and more like coming home to a lovingly prepared dinner.

The food was authentic and delicious. You can truly taste the difference. The Chef prepares everything from scratch, something that is so rare to find in most restaurants today.

Every dish is not just delicious but carried a sense of warmth, care & sincerity. It wasn’t just a meal, it was a comforting experience.

Thank you, Chef Mhon, for creating food that feeds not just the stomach, but the soul. 💛

PS: The carrot cake may not look pretty, but it was one of the best I’ve ever tasted.
author: Joyce Chua

review_text: We had such a wonderful time here ❤️🌟 We tried the momos and the beef burger, and both were absolutely delicious yummy! juicy, full of flavor, and unlike any we’ve had before. The owner was incredibly friendly, personally recommending dishes and making us feel so welcome. The ambience was cozy and warm, and our conversation with the them made the experience even more memorable. We truly enjoyed every moment here! Highly recommended for anyone looking for great food and heartfelt hospitality.
author: kirusnaa ramasamy

review_text: Absolutely loved this place! The food was delicious — especially the momos, which were fresh, juicy, and perfectly spiced. The atmosphere is cozy and relaxing, great for hanging out with friends. The staff were friendly and attentive, making the whole experience even better. Definitely one of the best spots in Iskandar Puteri for great food and vibes. Highly recommended!
author: eric chen

review_text:
The Himalayan pie resembles a curry puff in appearance, but offers a completely different flavor — something new to us, and we really enjoyed it, especially paired with the handmade chili sauce. The beef burger is excellent; every component — the bun, patty, and sauce — is well-prepared and harmoniously combined. It's generously sized, perfect for two to share. The lady boss puts great care into crafting tasty food, and it shows.
The handmade chili sauce is a standout — it pairs perfectly with the Himalayan pie and fries, adds a delightful kick. You can really taste the effort and quality in it.

With its cozy ambiance, friendly and welcoming owners, and delicious dishes, this is definitely a place worth revisiting.
author: Ong NN

review_text:
If I had to describe any meal at The Alchemist in one word, it would be “homecoming.”

I stumbled upon this place purely by chance, and it turned out to be one of the most memorable dining experiences I’ve had in Johor Bahru. The restaurant itself feels like stepping into a hidden world — the décor carries a mystical, alchemy-inspired theme that gives the space a unique personality without feeling overdone.

The real magic, however, is in the food.

The steamed pork momos are outstanding — freshly made, soft and juicy, with delicate handmade folds that show real care in preparation. What truly elevates them is the house-made chilli. It has a flavour unlike anything I’ve tasted elsewhere: vibrant, balanced, and clearly crafted with intention. You can tell immediately that it’s homemade.

The burgers are equally impressive. The patty is juicy, and the cheese melts beautifully with that satisfying stretch that tells you it’s done right. Simple ingredients, executed with skill.

What stands out most is the philosophy behind the food. Everything tastes fresh, honest, and thoughtfully prepared, like a meal made with pride rather than mass production.

The Alchemist truly feels like a hidden gem — the kind of place you discover by chance and then want to return to again.

Thanks to Mhonchumy and Anil for the great hospitality.
author: Evan

review_text: Food was great, every dish that came was very flavourful. The food also was not very oily. The quality of the food and great, portions were good as well. The hospitality was great as the waiters and waitresses always came in to check with us whether if we are ready to move on to the next course. 10/10 would recommend.
author: joshua wong

review_text: Food was excellent! We ordered nachos and salmon sushi (which my 4 year old loved) for the kids. Tenderloin (perfect mid rare) + pappardelle + octopus for 2 adults. Everything was very very tasty and delicious. Can’t find fault. Kids wanted ice cream which wasn’t on the menu so the restaurant staff very kindly gave us ice cream on the house!
author: Gladys Seah

review_text:
1st time experience with said restaurant. I am glad to have known and visited said place. Their manager Hafiz and the team have served me and my family with their smiles. Their waiter is knowledgeable and will try their best to accommodate to your needs even its not in the menu. They are really professional in their job.

They even took the initiative to make something special for my mother without me requesting anything knowingly its an occasion of just an appreciation meal for my mother.

I will definitely come again for their great service and food which are all delicious with good portions.
author: Zulkarnaein Omar

review_text:
We came here under reservation on 29.09 for my birthday celebration & I must say the service was excellent! The staff were very attentive and one of them even explained everything in Malay without hesitation, which was really helpful since it was our first time here and we didn’t know what to order. Truly appreciated the effort and friendliness.

As for the food, I’d rate it 4/5. It was good and enjoyable, though not exactly a wow factor. Prices are definitely on the higher side (“kayangan” level), but still affordable considering the portion sizes and the quality of service provided.

Overall, I’d give the whole experience a solid 4.6/5. Definitely a place worth visiting for a special occasion! 🤌
author: Haura Liew

review_text: Superb value for money. The food was good and portions very generous! Service staff was friendly and attentive to details, would definitely recommend a visit. May they continue dishing out good food and great service.
author: Herwandy Hamid

review_text:
I’m a Turkish citizen living in Singapore, and I was really impressed by how authentic and delicious the food is here! Everything tasted just like home — fresh, perfectly cooked, and full of flavor. The portions are big and definitely value for money.

You can even see the kitchen through a window, and it’s very clean. The owner, Ms. Pınar, and her team are super friendly and polite. They pay attention to small details — from how the plates are arranged to the sides they serve — and it really shows in the quality.

The place is air-conditioned and comfortable, great for both families and friends. Highly recommended if you’re looking for real Turkish food in Malaysia! 🇹🇷

review_text:

author: Bei

review_text:

author: Ong NN

review_text:

author: jenny ng

review_text:
I stumbled upon this simple restaurant while searching for a dinner spot, and I’m so glad I did! This restaurant offers a fantastic Mala soup experience, and here’s why I highly recommend it:

**Variety of Ingredients:**
The restaurant boasts a wide selection of fresh ingredients for customers to choose from. Whether you’re a meat lover, seafood enthusiast, or veggie fan, there’s something for everyone. The freshness of the ingredients really stood out and added to the overall quality of the meal.

**Soup Bases:**
There are several soup bases to choose from, and I opted for the classic Mala broth. The broth was incredibly flavorful—spicy, aromatic, and deeply satisfying. It had the perfect balance of heat and richness, making every bite enjoyable.

**Condiments Counter:**
The free condiments counter was well-stocked with a variety of sauces, fresh coriander, and chili. This allowed me to customize my dipping sauce to my liking, which added an extra layer of fun and personalization to the meal.

**Ambience:**
The restaurant has a clean, comfortable, and inviting environment. The seating was spacious, and the overall atmosphere made for a relaxing dining experience. It’s a great place to enjoy a meal with friends or family.

**Price:**
Considering the quality of the ingredients, the delicious broth, and the overall experience, the price was very reasonable. It felt like great value for money, especially for a satisfying Mala soup meal.

**Overall Impression:**
The restaurant exceeded my expectations. From the fresh ingredients and flavorful broth to the well-stocked condiments counter and comfortable setting, everything was on point. It’s a must-visit for Mala soup lovers or anyone looking for a tasty and enjoyable dining experience.

**Rating:** 5/5
- Pros: Fresh ingredients, delicious Mala broth, well-stocked condiments counter, clean and comfortable environment, reasonable prices.
- Cons: None worth mentioning—it was a fantastic experience overall!

I’ll definitely be returning to this gem of a restaurant! Highly recommended!
author: Crumpled Nomad

author: Kosong Belly

restaurant_name: MyoungDong Korean Restaurant(명동)明洞韩國料理
review_text:
If you’re craving authentic Korean flavors without the plane ticket, Myeong Dong restaurant is your answer. Drawn here by a friend’s glowing recommendation, I left utterly convinced—this spot nails the balance of homely comfort and vibrant Seoul-style dining.

The seafood pancake (haemul pajeon) was a crispy, golden masterpiece, loaded with tender squid, shrimp, and scallions, paired with a tangy dipping sauce that cut through the richness perfectly. But the star was the Korean ginseng chicken soup (samgyetang): a steaming, fragrant clay pot of tender whole chicken stuffed with glutinous rice, swimming in a broth that whispered of earthy ginseng and subtle garlic. One sip transported me back to a cozy eatery in Seoul—that level of authenticity. The pork skewers were juicy and charred just right, while the fresh oysters were plump and briny.

Service here is a highlight—warm, attentive, and quick to offer suggestions or refill banchan (those addictive kimchi sides!). The staff’s genuine smiles and eagerness to share their favorites added a welcoming touch to the meal.

As for pricing? Expect reasonable rates that won’t shock your wallet.
author: Crumpled Nomad

We are glad the boss's wife helped to BBQ the beef and pork belly, they are really delicious.  Definitely will bring my friends/relatives to patronise this restaurant again.
author: Alex Sua

review_text:
We came to RunningMan Korea BBQ and ordered the 2-person buffet and one Korean beer. The total bill was RM120. While the price seems reasonable for two people and a drink, I have to flag a major issue: I was not given a physical receipt and have no idea how the RM120 total was calculated (e.g., breakdown of buffet vs. beer price). I strongly suggest the management ensure receipts are provided for transparency.

The BBQ itself was enjoyable, especially the garlic pork (which I would have happily ordered a second serving of, but never got the chance to order more than the initial set).

My main feedback is about food waste. For the buffet, the waitress brought a platter of all available meats without asking our preference. I specifically asked if there was chicken (which I do not eat) and was told no, I can recognize smoked duck and told her to take this meat away before  touching the food. but as we were cooking, we found lots of chicken included. Since we hate wasting food, we felt compelled to finish it all, which meant we missed out on ordering more of the meats we actually liked.

Suggestion for Improvement: To reduce food waste and enhance the customer experience, please ask guests what meats they prefer for the first serving instead of bringing everything out.

Overall, it would have been a perfect BBQ experience if we had better control over our meat choices and received a clear bill.
author: OB1

review_text:

The kitchen cook meat doesnt taste bbq at all. More on watery and tasteless. Felt so cheated. Will not recommend and never come again. Price is not cheap either for ala carte. 👎👎👎

11 Oct 2025

author: Jessie

review_text:
I recently tried this Korean BBQ restaurant, and overall, it was a pretty enjoyable experience! The service was okay, and I appreciated the BBQ service they provide at the table.We ordered some delicious noodles ( grilled chapagetti), and the sesame fragrance was simply amazing! However, one downside was that the restaurant didn’t have proper exhaust fans (抽煙機), which left our shirts and hair smelling quite smoky afterward.As for the pricing, I'm not sure if it's cheap or reasonable for those living in JB, but for us, it felt affordable and fair.One suggestion I have for the restaurant is to offer a 2-pax set that includes both pork and beef. Currently, the sets are either pork or beef, which made us order an extra pork jaw (which was quite tasty, by the way), but we ended up not being able to finish it all, haha!

One highlight was the banchan offered; they provided a nice variety of small side dishes. Most of them had a delightful sour flavor, which added a unique twist to the meal.However, I think it would be even better if they could include more savory options in the banchan selection. A bit of balance with some savory flavors would enhance the overall dining experience!

Overall, a decent spot for Korean BBQ, but a few improvements could make it even better!
author: OB1

review_text: An amazing Korean dining experience! The side dishes are full of flavor, the grilled pork jowl is juicy and perfectly tender, and the kimchi tofu soup tastes incredibly authentic. Everything was spot on. I’ll definitely be back.

review_text:
\\ A Singaporean Girl Review

RM220 for 2 pax. I think the price is worth it as the meat is quite fresh. I do think this place is better and suited for bigger crowds. There is a comment on wasabi which I agree. Nonetheless, I do recommend to have a light meal here with some alcohol.
author: Michelle Tan

review_text:
A hidden gem! They use incredibly fresh ingredients e.g. fish, tofu, including homegrown vegetables, to create comforting, homestyle dishes.

Salt baked chicken is so tender and 入味! Lotus leaf rice is so fragrant! The hot, ready-to-go 梅菜扣肉 (braised pork with preserved vegetables) and 鸡脚 (braised chicken feet) are must-brings! And don’t miss the Bua Long Long drink—it’s a refreshing must-have! The packed homegrown veggies are especially fresh —truly a must-buy.

Thank you for maintaining such a wonderful place where city folks can enjoy a peaceful, delicious meal. It's a quiet spot perfect for a cozy experience.

The service is excellent—from the staff to the workers. Special thanks to Melvin and the lady serving our table (Lay Choo I believe)!
author: V C

review_text:
Tucked away in Sungei Tengah, Orchidville is a hidden gem for those seeking a rustic dining experience. The "lunch on a farm" vibe here is truly unique, making it a refreshing escape from the urban buzz.

The service was excellent—friendly and attentive staff made us feel very welcomed. We sampled a variety of dishes, and every single one impressed us. The standout? Their signature Salt Baked Chicken. It’s incredibly flavorful, with tender, well-seasoned meat that leaves you wanting more. The stir-fry vegetables deserve a special mention too—so fresh that you can tell they come straight from the source. Mango prawns 😋

If you’re looking for a place with hearty, delicious food and a touch of rustic charm, Orchidville is definitely worth the visit.
author: Jimmy Yu

review_text:
We tried the Salt Baked Chicken ($32), Roasted Pork ($13), Braised Chicken Feet ($5), Lotus Leaf Rice ($15), Preserved Veg with Pork ($6), Brazilian Spinach with Egg & Prawn ($15), Orh Nee ($5) and Buah Long Long drink ($3.50).

The Salt Baked Chicken is a whole bird, super juicy, tender and full of flavour. The Lotus Leaf Rice is fragrant and tasty, with that nice aroma from the lotus leaf. The Roasted Pork is homemade, sold by weight, crispy skin, juicy meat, and just the right amount of fat.

We went on a weekend for lunch, it’s abit like a canteen-style. You order outside and then eat inside the dining hall. Was told there's no service charge  because of this setup.

The Buah Long Long drink was a refreshing surprise, a bit sour from the added plum, tangy and slightly sweet. Rare treat that’s hard to find in Singapore (usually only see it in Malaysia!).

Overall, food’s good, portions are very decent. Place is a bit run-down, but if you don’t mind the travel and simple setting, it’s a hidden gem.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
The food are good. Like their lotus rice and fish maw soup. The place has free car park. They already pre cooked the food and served/packed in disposable ware. I think it is better if they serve it with reusable ware, as disposable ware served in a restaurant setting don't look great, even though the food has restaurant standard.
Their ba long long drink is very unique and quench thirsty.
author: Su YH

review_text: I can’t comment much on their signature dish- volcano roasted chicken. You will have to preorder, and it is better to go with a bigger group to try this dish out. Servings for other dishes are very generous. It is true that their veggies in any fish are a lot- Super fresh and lightly seasoned! Overall prices are on the high end side, considering the place is so far away from the happenings, it wouldn’t justify the value of going without discounts. There’s no cutlery for children though.
author: Low

restaurant_name: Yan Palace Restaurant (Warren Golf & Country Club)
review_text:
Dinner at 6:30pm with my mom on Chu 6 of CNY.

There was about 10–12 tables occupied. Upon arrival, there was no attendant to usher guests to their tables. People began gathering at the entrance, and when the attendant finally appeared, there was no effort to check who had arrived first. Instead, they attended to groups who came later.

Food ordered:

Half Roast Chicken – $30 (1/5)
disappointing. The meat was extremely dry, even the drumstick, and completely lacked flavor. Honestly, a $9 whole roast chicken from Cold Storage would have tasted better.

Seafood Hor Fun – $20 (2/5)
Large portion, but unfortunately bland.

Sweet & Sour Pork – $20 (4/5)
The best dish of the night. Crispy on the outside, tender inside, and the sauce was well-balanced—not overly sour. However, the portion felt slightly small for the price.

We also ordered hot chrysanthemum tea. The total bill came to $89 after service charge GST.

Overall, I was already disappointed with the food, especially from such an established brand. Still, I was prepared to let it go and accept it as an unlucky experience.

However, the service at the cashier was the final straw. The counter area was chaotic, with waitresses shouting orders and the cashier rushing through bills. I patiently waited my turn, not wanting to add to the stress. Then, an aunty waitress approached me abruptly and said in a frustrated tone, “Ni yao shen me?!” (“What do you want?!”)

That moment completely changed my impression. I was ready to walk away disappointed with the food, but the poor attitude made the experience worse.

With only 10–12 tables occupied, staffing and operations should have been manageable. If manpower is an issue, seriously consider solutions like QR code ordering or automation to ease the workload. Please do not project stress onto customers.

Very disappointing experience overall.
author: S. Ang

review_text:

Food is mediocre and service was abysmal, especially by Captain Alice Tan. Food was served with fingers dip into the bowl, zero care for hygiene. When request for change, attitude was rude. Pouring all the desserts into other dishes (still have abalone and vegetable for eating) right at the table.

review_text:

We raised to the server and was just told the shark's fin was simmered in. Not a huge fan of shark's fin but it is a total mis-representation of the dish. What a joke.

The rest of the dishes and service were sub-par as well with the charred glutinous rice and a very wet yam paste.

Not a good experience and totally not worth the value.

Note: The club recently introduced parking charges and you will be expected to pay for the charges for dining there.

The pitcher iced tea is also a good deal and so good on a sweltering hot day!

review_text: See my photo. Leave it to you to decide.. - Went during lunch hour. Couldnt find anymore places to eat around that area so give it a try. Ordered their most affordable main dish, Chicken chop. Greatly disappointed 🫠. chicken chop meat is ¼ size of the whole plate, drizzle with simple bbq sauce. fries is extermely thin and portion is utterly small, portion is lesser than the small size fries pack i can order from Macdonald 😫. Comes with few pieces of lettuce and 1 cherry tomato cut into half. Drizzle with a normal thousand island sauce i suppose? Total cost $20+ after gst. No drinks included. Ehem. Boss, something is wrong. Give it to you that you got a 'Wild wild west' location and unique vibe for late night drinking spot. Food wise i wont recommend ppl to come. Sorry.
author: Lee Gary

review_text:
Came here to explore after going to a similar establishment nearby for a few times and I am deeply disappointed that I deviate from my usual place.

Food review:
Cod fish is not fresh. It was not served with Tartar sauce as well. Had to ask the waiter for it. The place was barely half filled but condiments like this can still be missed.

As for the BBQ chicken chop as you can tell from the picture, it's as thick as a cardboard. Even a coffeeshop western chain serves up thicker, cheaper and better chicken chop. The chicken was not fresh as well. Gave feedback to whom I assume is the manager and he gave me the reason 'it was from the bottom of the pile'. I barely contained my laughter.

But to his credit, he offered another piece of chicken. He took out a raw chicken piece and showed it to me, saying that the chicken are from the same supplier. I nearly laughed out loud again, not sure out of pity for them or the audacity to charge $16.90 for such quality.

Overall nice chill place to just have a drink but definitely not for the food. Would have given one star but add one more star for the attempt of service recovery and the reason for the thinness of the chicken. Funny guy 😂

PS: they need 15mins to cook this portion of chicken chop as well, imagine that.
author: Victor Lee

review_text:

Do check out the beautiful and artsy murals scattered throughout their premises.

We had a nice steak and lamb chops lunch at the George’s restaurant on its premise. Very rustic location.

They also hold farm tours for children where they can see insect rearing, fish feeding, star fish handing.

review_text:
Had a great experience at Tenplus. We ordered the Chicken Satay (10 sticks, $15.90), Torched Aburi Prawn & Clam Pasta ($22.90), and Gyudon Beef Bowl ($16.90). All were very good.

The satay came with generously thick cuts of meat, really worth the price. The peanut sauce was a little mild for my taste but still enjoyable. The pasta was excellent; creamy, rich, and full of seafood flavour. The Gyudon was also delicious, the rice mixed with furikake was not too salty, the beef was well-marinated, and the pickled cucumber added a nice sour kick.

They had a 1-for-1 Bavaria full pint happy hour, which was a nice surprise. The ambience is quiet and relaxing, and there’s plenty of free parking (though limited lots). Service was warm, friendly and polite.

A big plus is the children’s activity room and a shallow fish pond where kids can catch fish. You can also walk around the grounds to see the plants since they’re also a florist and gardener shop.

Overall, lovely food, great vibes, and a family-friendly place. Highly recommended.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
A surprise find inside a nursery. I like the atmosphere, open airy space, surround by greenery. Lots of fans so quite pleasant even when it’s sunny.
The iced latte is good and the nasi lemak is delicious also. The fried chicken is crispy outside and tender inside.
author: Heidi So

review_text:
Really enjoyed the lamb! It's meat falls off the bone, and is almost crispy while juicy. The creamy mashed potato with fried seaweed was delicious, and overall has a striking tomato flavour and acidity.

The classic satay is cooked to perfection, and gives me vibes of being in batam.

The clam and prawn pasta was cooked well, but the sauce slips off the pasta hahhaa. The gyudon meat was thin and fatty, the rice was a bit overseasoned and dry.

Service is good, the server brought out a propeller to fan a persistent fly away from our table xD! And helped us navigate the online ordering system.

Open environment, but hard to get here without private transport. Has parking, and the washrooms are maintained well. Good place to bring someone to, has a live band after 7pm.

3 mains, 1 side and 3 drinks set us back $122, but thr was no regrets on our end.

review_text:
Celebrated my birthday here and had a  memorable experience at Italian Patio. The food was very enjoyable — highlights for us were the grilled squid, crispy chicken wings, and the fresh salad. Everything was flavourful with generous portions,  and we enjoyed the meal thoroughly. We especially loved the chilli sauce served with the wings — it had a strong kick and paired perfectly with them.

The tiramisu deserves a special mention — my friend commented that it was one of the best he has had. Definitely save room for dessert.

The space is cosy and comfortable, making it ideal for both a relaxed meal and special occasions. There are indoor and outdoor seating options. The staff were friendly, attentive, and always smiling, which made the dining experience even more pleasant.

A great dining spot within the club and truly worth visiting. Would be happy to return again. 😊
author: Ester Ong

review_text:
Came to give this a try & was pleasantly surprised by how good it is.
We had the truffle fries starters and fries were really crispy and tasted really nice.

The mains and pizza were all handmade and it tasted really fresh. The service was on point as well, food didn’t take long and staffs were attentive.
The most surprising factor is the price of food. It is so well priced & you’ll never find such good Italian food at these prices. The owner told us this was only possible because of the location. - it is situated within a golf club which might not be the most convenient but it’s well worth the travel!  Parking is free as well.

Was also surprised to know that the head chef is had over 27 years of experience in an Italian restaurant which explained how good the food was.

Thank you for the great dinner & a memorable place for us to celebrate our anniversary. Will definitely be back again!
author: ETH.

review_text:
I recently had the pleasure of dining at Italian Patio, and I can honestly say it was one of the best dining experiences I've ever had! From the moment I walked in, I was enveloped by a warm and cozy ambiance that made me feel right at home. The setting beside the poolside, with the golf range in the background, created a serene atmosphere that was perfect for a relaxing evening.

The menu is a true delight, featuring a range of sumptuous Western cuisine that left me spoilt for choice.

What truly stood out was the impeccable service. The staff was not only attentive but genuinely friendly, making sure I had everything I needed throughout my meal. Their recommendations were spot-on, enhancing my dining experience even further.

Other than that, this is a highly recommended place for those who enjoy authentic Italian cuisine.

Amazing place with delicious food. There is a nice ambience and a beautiful view of the golf course from above. The staff is efficient and very amiable. There is a separate vegetarian menu but it is limited. They have various cuisine such as western and local. They have good dishes and the quantity is huge . There prices are also reasonable and they have a discount if you are a member.
However, they could broaden the vegetarian menu a little bit by adding few more dishes.
I recommend the vegetarian charcoal burger, the pomelo and mango ice cream, the potato wedges and the banana split.
Overall, a good place to hang out with friends and family.

Meegoreng was on the sweeter side and comes with a few peeled prawn. Overall the food was seasoned well and nothing to complain about. Service was attentive and $25++ per bucket of beer was reasonable. Plus the nice view, totally would recommend.

We ordered curry chicken, beef hor fun, fried rice and fish&chips, and we were not disappointed at all. Of course, the sunset view is always so mesmerizing.

review_text:

She then asked if want a coffee or tea. I told her i would like tea. She then asked if i want latte. I told her tea is good as i dont take coffee or milk. Then the older staff that is making my sub told me that latte will have to pay extra. When i was paying, i just realised that they charged for hash brown and tea. Its been awhile since i tried their breakfast and i thought it was $6+. But with the added hash brown and tea i have to pay $8.9. The staff should have told me that hash brown and tea is not included in the $6+ deal. And the way they asked as if its included is very misleading. The advertisement on the board is not clear too.

The bread is heated and the portion of vegies are good. Breakfast bacon only came with one streak of bacon….overall food is fresh and good. But Subway have to train their staff better and modify the advertisements to be not misleading.

review_text:
Canadian Pizza at Limbang never fails to impress — whether I’m dining in, picking up, or getting it delivered.

Dine-in: The place is cozy, clean, and the staff are always welcoming. Service is fast, and the pizzas come out hot and fresh. The crust is crispy, toppings are generous, and the flavors are consistently good — my personal favorite is the Singapura Special.

Takeaway: Easy and convenient. My orders are always ready on time, neatly packed, and still warm by the time I get home. No missing items, and quality is just as good as dining in.

Delivery: Super reliable. They’re usually early or right on time, and the pizzas arrive hot, not soggy like some other places. The drivers are polite, and the food is packed well to avoid any mess. Even during peak hours, they handle orders smoothly.

I also love their 2-for-1 deals — great value for money. Whether it’s a quick lunch, family dinner, or a weekend treat, Canadian Pizza CCK is one of the best.

Highly recommended!

review_text:
Had to write this cuz I think you guys have lost it. The whole deal and jazz of a Canadian pizza outlet is the 2 for 1 deal.
Whereas upon looking at the pricing. It’s clearly not the case? 2 for 1 mean 2 pizzas for the price of 1 pizza? 1 pizza = $18.
But When I want the 2 for 1 deal. Suddenly the price of 1 pizza shoots up to $22?
So in reality it’s 1 pizza for $18. And the 2nd pizza for $4.
I got this quote from your website, “Always 2 For 1 - Pizza is meant to be shared and why not get more value for your money!!” But it seems like the “deal” is to make us pay for the 2nd pizza.

Yes and I know. By all means we can read it as 2 pizzas for $22 whilst ignoring the single pizza option. But this is why I say you have lost it. You’ve lost the whole essence of 2 for ONE but pricing as such.

P.S. I’m well aware that if they priced a single pizza as $22 as well we wouldn’t have this confusion. But still. I think you have to have some ethics and ultimately justifiable reasoning for using your worldwide famous slogan in the first place no?

Visited on a weekend morning, stall had a few customers. The stall itself is pretty small, 2 seats within and 3 tables outside.

Order the standard wanton mee ($3.80). Came with a decent amount of noodles, around 7 pieces of lean char Siew and 3 boiled wantons.

Noodles:
Noodles were drenched in a watery chilli sauce blend and probably some soy based sauce.

The noodles were the thicker kind which gives you a better bite. My issue with the noodles is that it had a very strong alkaline taste, which wasn't covered by the sauce and green chilli taste.

Wanton/Char Siew:
Wanton skins were thick and felt pretty dense. Skin was not the silky soft kind that floats on the soup. Rather felt like those 中国水饺 kind, definitely a miss for me. Meat amount was alright but I didn't really like the taste of the meat.

Char Siew is the standard lean meat 'cardboard' kind. But they did give a generous amount for a $3.80 portion. Not too thin.

Overall, slightly below average for me. Noodles and wantons could be better. But guess it is a somewhat decent food option around this area since there is almost nothing to eat at sunshine place.

Visited Kopi Corner recently — a cozy and classic local coffee spot perfect for breakfast or a quick afternoon bite.

⭐ Coffee (4.5/5):
The coffee was rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced with that traditional kopitiam punch. Smooth and not overly sweet, it pairs wonderfully with the toast.

🍞 Butter Kaya Toast (4.5/5):
The butter kaya toast was crispy on the outside and soft inside. The kaya spread was fragrant and creamy, and the butter melted just right — simple but delicious.

🥞 Prata Set (3.5/5):

The cozy kopitiam feel at Kopi Korner, Sunshine Place, makes it a gem. Quick service, affordable prices, and delish local flavors—definitely coming back! Where’s your fave kopitiam spot? Drop it below! 👇

review_text:
Food is not bad but I would only like to comment on their sales practice. I would consider it dishonest because their staff would always try to "upsell" you on the dishes.

Today, we told the staff we would like 2 plates of chicken rice, add char siew. The guy behind the counter said ok they will make chicken rice for 2 and add a plate of char siew. Technically he is not wrong but the change in combinations turned 2 plates of $5.50 (total $11) into $17. An additional $6. On top of that, the staff kept trying to push additional side dishes to us like gizzards and eggs when they are well aware that it’s already too much food for us.

In the end, we got 2 rice, 1 huge plate of chicken breast meat and a plate of char siew. The chicken breast meat is enough for 3 pax. We couldn't finish the food.

I remembered pre-COVID I had to specifically explain in detail my orders so that the staff could not "misinterprete" it. I guess after 3 years, they are still using the same practice since the staff have already changed.

I wouldn't recommend coming here especially if you're in a big group. You'll end up overordering. But know that its not your fault.
If you have the time, check out the Google Reviews on the other brances. Several have highlighted the same dishonest practice.

Tip: if you really wanna patronize them, study the menu and listen very carefully to the staff when they repeat your order.

review_text:
I visited Kimly Dim Sum recently to try some quick dim sum. The place is located in a typical coffee shop setting and it was moderately busy when I arrived. The atmosphere was simple and casual, which is what most people would expect from a neighborhood dim sum stall.

For this visit I ordered the Siew Mai and the fried stuffed yam pastry. The food was acceptable but overall the experience was quite average and did not stand out.

The Siew Mai tasted decent but nothing particularly memorable. The texture and flavor were just okay and it felt like a standard mass produced dim sum rather than something freshly prepared. It was still edible but it did not give the satisfying bite that good Siew Mai usually has.

The fried stuffed yam pastry was the more disappointing dish. The outer layer of the yam pastry was quite hard and lacked the light crispy texture that this dish normally has. It felt like it had been sitting for some time before being served. Because of that the pastry lost its freshness and the overall texture was not very enjoyable.

Service was also rather average. The staff were not unfriendly but there was not much interaction either. It felt like a straightforward order and eat experience without much attention to detail.

The coffee shop atmosphere was simple and practical for a quick meal but nothing particularly comfortable or memorable.

Overall the dim sum here is just average and convenient if you are nearby and want a quick bite. However based on this visit the food quality and freshness could definitely be improved. Hopefully future visits will offer fresher dim sum and a better dining experience.

review_text:
Food taste is always subjective — everyone has their own preferences and taste buds — so this is purely based on my own experience.

I’ve been coming here since they first opened, and it has become one of my regular spots for paper thosai. Once in a while, I switch things up and order prata or the normal thosai, but thosai is really where they shine.

Personnally, I felt that they are genuinely good at making thosai. The paper thosai is impressively long (about 60cm), thin, and very crispy without being overly oily. It’s the kind of texture that both kids and adults can enjoy. The 3 different sauces are well done too — flavourful and nicely balanced, which complements the thosai very well.

One thing I should point out is the timing. I usually come around 8+ in the morning, before the breakfast rush. With no crowd pressure, you can really feel that the food is prepared with care rather than rushed. That probably contributes a lot to the consistency and quality I’ve experienced.

I’ve tried their prata once. It’s not the best prata out there, but I appreciate that they cook it only when ordered. They don’t pre-cook in batches and leave it sitting around, so at least it’s served warm and fresh.

I’ve also brought a few friends here specifically to try the thosai, and so far, everyone has enjoyed it — which says quite a bit.

Overall, if you’re coming for thosai, especially during the quieter morning hours, this place is a solid and reliable choice. Timing matters, but when done right, it’s clear they know their craft.

review_text:
We ordered four versions of the chee cheong fun — prawn, egg, char siew, and minced meat, each priced at $5. The portion size was generous, definitely good value for money.

The chee cheong fun itself was the highlight of the meal — smooth, silky, and delightfully chewy, almost like soft mochi. The chef clearly has great skill; the texture was so good you could practically slurp it down effortlessly. For the chee cheong fun skin alone, it’s an easy 5 stars.

As for the fillings, they were decent but didn’t quite shine. The char siew was flavorful and the prawn fresh with a nice crunch, but the egg and minced meat felt rather plain and didn’t add much to the overall taste or texture. My suggestion — stick to one or two types of fillings as it will end up tasting about the same.

Now, about the sauce — unfortunately, this was where things fell short. It leaned too salty and lacked the subtle sweetness and umami depth that define a great chee cheong fun sauce. Since the sauce plays such a key role in tying everything together, it was a noticeable letdown.

Overall, while the chee cheong fun skin itself was superb, the sauce and fillings didn’t quite live up to it. A 3-star experience for me this round.

And I'm so glad I did. Here's why:
There was no queue. Arriving on Good Friday during the breakfast peak, I was the only customer. They offer mixed meats, which means you get the best of both worlds. I went with the friendly owner's recommendation – prawn and char siew for $5 – and my order was ready in under five minutes.

The skin was perfect – smooth with a hint of chewiness. I have never come across skin like this in Singapore. The fillings were generous, and I particularly liked the minced char siew. The dark sauce had perfect sweet and savory notes. Additionally, the chilli was spicy and truly elevated the dish. In fact, this is better than the CCF I've had at restaurants.

Overall, this is definitely a must-visit. Make sure you dine in, as CCF won't travel well and that wouldn't do justice to the food.

I always thought of Maki/Gimbap as an ingenious method of getting you to pay more for your food.  If the separate ingredients were to be laid out before you (before being rolled up), I doubt many might be willing to pay between $8 to $12 for those.  But once rolled up, people pay such amounts for what they presume they are getting.  The whole is certainly worth more than the sum of parts.

So I decided to give Maki-San a try only after I stumbled on a Grab Food voucher promotion.  You pay $21 for a $30 voucher.

review_text:
I visited around 2 pm, during off-peak hours, and was immediately impressed by the warm and prompt greeting from the kitchen staff as we sat down. Soon after, we were handed the menu and a QR code for ordering, which made the process smooth and organized from the start.

Our drinks arrived quickly, followed by the side dishes. The chicken karaage was tasty, although slightly on the salty side. The takoyaki was a standout, perfectly crispy on the outside, soft and flavorful on the inside. The gyoza was decent, though again a little salty, but still enjoyable.

For the main, we ordered the Kazan ramen (big) and requested it to be less salty. Even with the adjustment, it was still a bit salty for my personal taste, but I have to emphasize that it was extremely flavorful and satisfying. The broth was rich and aromatic, and the generous portions of meat and noodles made it a hearty and comforting dish. The ramen really felt like the highlight of the meal.

Service throughout was attentive and professional. The waitress was systematic in serving each course, polite, and noticed when I was about to pay, promptly moving to the cashier to assist. These small touches added to the overall positive experience.

Overall, this was a pleasant dining experience, with quick service, a well-executed menu, and a particularly tasty ramen that I would gladly return for. My only note would be that the sides and ramen were a bit salty for my taste, but the flavors and portion sizes make it worthwhile.

This is not a one off incident. I have ordered twice and faced the same rubbish service both times, clearly indicating a recurring and systemic problem at this outlet.
