To make matters worse, I experienced the same issue reported by another complainant in the past. On a previous occasion, I personally went down to the outlet only to be told that the rider was “on the way”.

I also attempted to call the outlet countless times on both occasions, only to encounter a constantly engaged phone line. This does not appear accidental and strongly suggests that calls were being deliberately ignored while the outlet failed to manage its orders. Completely cutting off communication during a service failure is unacceptable.

And please do not insult customers with generic auto replies about “appreciating feedback” and “apologising for inconvenience.” It is obvious that no one genuinely follows up or takes responsibility. Copy and paste responses do nothing to address repeated service failures.

This entire experience highlights severe incompetence, poor operational control, and a blatant disregard for customers time. Domino's need to urgently review the management and service standards of this outlet, as this level of service is simply unacceptable for a delivery based business.

I visited this Encik Tan branch at Junction 10 with some trepidation, having seen a number of negative reviews online, especially regarding food quality. However, I'm happy to report that my experience today was very pleasant and positive.

I ordered their Signature Noodles, opting for the Mee Pok version. The service at the counter was quick and efficient.

The bowl itself was definitely above average. It came with a generous variety of toppings—braised mushrooms, minced chicken, fried wantona, fishball, meatball, fried scallop and half an egg. All the components were tasty and worked well together.

My main point of concern, based on other reviews, was the noodles. Many have mentioned them being overcooked and mushy. For my bowl, this was not the case at all. The mee pok was cooked well; while I personally prefer my noodles even firmer and more al dente, these were "firm enough" and had a decent bite. They were definitely not the overcooked mess I was fearing.

Perhaps this branch has some inconsistency issues, maybe depending on the specific cook on duty, but I can only speak to my own experience. Today, I got a solid, satisfying, and enjoyable bowl of noodles, making it a well-deserved 4-star meal.

Ordered Fish set number 6.. expect "batang" fish like what they shown.. instead I get a lump of fried thing... look like a fried potato.. inside only a little bit of fish meat,  ( maybe a quater of the batang fish with bone ) the rest are all flour... its not fish set.."flour set " maybe.   Maximise the profits maybe.. feel totally cheated.

author: Hafizuddin

review_text:
Noodles are overcooked it tasted very mushy.
Staff cooking the noodles could have blend the chilli together with the other sauces rather than 1 fat scoop of chilli at the side of the bowl. Looks abit disgusting .

Fishball and coffee are nice though.
author: Patricia Lim

review_text: terrible service, ordered the curry rice ($5.00) add on lime juice was additional ($1.00) for small cup, the aunty collected $2.00 instead total $7.00 and i was given the small cup. when confronted the counter, was told that she count wrong but she didn’t even ask in the first place if wanted big or small, and didn’t even bother telling the staff making the drinks which size we ordered, another staff said their drinks add on is fixed large, but the drinks they give is small yet i paid extra for it. not just me but my friend as well, only when confronted they wanted to refund from their tips jar. terrible customer service. disappointing.
author: Alex Le

review_text:
A Hot Hideout @ Junction 10 has truly become my little “secret hideout” whenever I need some quiet me-time, especially during off-peak hours. Their Mala Stir Fry is my go-to—flavourful, balanced, and consistently satisfying. I appreciate how they tailor the spice levels to suit local palates—not overly spicy or numb, but still packed with that familiar mala kick. For those who like it hotter, there’s always Level 3 and the option to add extra numbness.

My wife prefers the Tomato soup base, which is rich, comforting, and just as enjoyable in its own way. While many go for the popular fried potatoes and lotus roots, I personally enjoy sticking with the regular ingredients—it’s all about how well they prepare and season everything.

Great food, comfortable setting, and customisable flavours—this place is a gem, and definitely deserving of 5 stars!
author: Wiz Yeo

review_text:
2nd time at this outlet - Came around 530pm, there was no queue and we got our food within 10-15mins through their self-service ordering system.

I ordered the Tomato Collagen and a Green Thai Milk Tea while my husband ordered the 中辣 with a normal Thai Milk Tea, both of us added scrambled egg which was quite creamy. The tomato soup base is quite thick and flavourful, ingredients were fresh and there was a nice variety available. For about 450g it's about $18-$20 per pax so control your kiapping of ingredients if you're on a budget. They offer unlimited spring onion, coriander and peanuts too. Thai milk tea ($3.50) was a tad bit sweet as usual like all thai milk teas.

Shout out to the service which was very friendly and accommodating - One of the managers - Allan, took the time to help with my takeaway order as I couldn't finish and also spoke to us about their points system with cashback which was helpful.

Overall a lovely experience would definitely return when I have the craving.
author: Cherilynn Ang

review_text: We came at around 8pm and there were plenty of seats available. We were then made to wait for a "good time" to join the already-very-short queue of people in picking out ingredients. The people before us were taking such a long time to decide what ingredients they wanted. This is so inefficient.  I prefer gong yuan mala tang as it works like mala stalls in foodcourt, just choose the ingredients and if u are done just head over to the counter to pay, dont need to wait for others in front of u who are dilly-dallying or indecisive. Waste of time. Also, why cannot enter to get seats first? What if ordered already then no suitable seats for groups or those with kids? I think it's not an efficient system at all. Price wise quite it's on the high side compared to other mala joints, considering we didn't order a lot, and it cost $22+ The rice at $1.50 is overpriced. Also, the peanuts were SALTED! That made the whole mala stir fry too salty. Who adds salted peanuts anyway? Aren't those supposed to be unsalted? Oh well...
author: Emily Ho

review_text:
Disappointing and unwelcoming service

We have visited this mala hotpot place several times before and generally enjoyed the food, but today’s experience was extremely uncomfortable due to the attitude of the staff, the person who seemed to be the manager (with red cap).

When queuing, we were carrying a larger backpack after work. The manager kindly offered to help the two groups in front of us place their bags, but when it was our turn, he completely ignored us. The difference in treatment was very noticeable and made us feel uncomfortable.

Later, while we were waiting for our food, the same person asked us to change tables because a group of six needed space. We were completely fine with moving. However, all tables in this restaurant are two-seat tables that can be freely combined, so there were clearly multiple ways to arrange seating without making things difficult for anyone.

We politely asked to be moved to a place where our backpack could fit, but he insisted that we move to another two-seat table with no room for bags at all. Only after another group left a four-seat combination table did he finally allow us to move there.

This was not about refusing to cooperate — we were willing to move from the beginning. What was upsetting was the repeated lack of basic consideration and respect, despite the fact that the tables are flexible and our request was entirely reasonable.

Unfortunately, this experience made us feel unwelcome, and we will not be returning.
author: Sunnykid Sun

review_text: Craving for their deep fried lotus root so came back after a long while, its expensiveness deters me from patronizing more often. Spiciness seemingly on the milder side today as the mid-spicy level almost the same as low-spicy eslewhere. Rice was disappointingly soft, if ur consumers base prefer softer texture then pls invest on a pearl grain and not just by adding so much water to a normal Thai grain, u are afterall charging $1.50 for just a bowl of rice.
author: Mr Yang

review_text: I ordered delivery and honestly the pizzas were OK. However,  the wedges were horrendous. Uncooked, cheese sauce and mayonnaise had a very weird taste. I couldn't even finish 1 box and I ordered 2. The chicken drumlet is the only thing I'll eat if I ever come back here. Please improve.
author: Best Dragflicker

review_text: Ordered take-away. Before I could even step out of the mall, the pizza boxes were already wet. Pizza looks good and taste good. Overall, good experience.
author: Karin Tan

review_text:
Otterly nice. Not your fancy, not your junk either but homey pizza. Margherita is good, but missing the basil? I guess you couldn’t call that Margherita but! generous on the cheese. Tomato tasted good too. 🍅🧀
May be a little too salty for some.
author: Stef S

review_text: Good pizza. I ordered beef and pineapple pizza and potato wedges. So yummy and 10 min waiting time
author: cri hidh

review_text: Great pizzas. Tasty and nice toppings
author: echidna tc

restaurant_name: 江湖冒菜 Authentic Sichuan Restaurant
review_text: Tried a variety of dishes at this Chinese restaurant, including their BBQ skewers, Hot Pepper Bullfrog, Stir-Fried Shredded Potatoes, and Stir-Fried Bitter Gourd with Salted Egg. For the skewers, we went for beef, pork, chicken, and buns—each one flavorful and well-prepared. All the dishes were enjoyable, except for the bullfrog, which wasn’t as fresh as expected and was overly spicy for my liking. The menu offers a great variety, making it a good spot for those seeking diverse Chinese cuisine.
author: Gibson NG

restaurant_name: 江湖冒菜 Authentic Sichuan Restaurant
review_text:
A comfortable setting for families. QR code ordering system and help yourself to the soft drinks and beers at the fridge. Many mainland Chinese selection and prices of beers are attractive.

Twice cooked pork was dry and tough. It was half eaten. Don't waste calories on this.

Mouth water chicken was probably pre-cut and left in fridge. It was cold and hard. The seasoning was average at best.

Grilled fish with peppers was of average quality and taste. For half a fish of this price, it is noticeably expensive compared to the big brands / chains. The fish was way overcooked and tough in texture. Not something I will come back for.

BBQ squid was pathetically tiny for its price. It was on the overcooked side, save by its seasoning.

Pork and chive dumplings were better amongst the dishes.

Eggplant with garlic was the standout amongst all. Then again, difficult to mess out this dish.

A comfortable setting but let down by its quality of dishes. Service is prompt.

Unfortunately we were super thirsty after the meal throughout the night.
author: MNG

restaurant_name: 江湖冒菜 Authentic Sichuan Restaurant
review_text:
I had a wonderful experience at this establishment. The ambiance is not only clean but also spacious, providing a comfortable environment. The staff is exceptionally friendly, making the overall atmosphere warm and inviting.

What makes this place even more unique is its affiliation with the restaurant next door. As a sister company, it offers a diverse culinary experience. I particularly enjoyed exploring the distinct flavors—Sichuan cuisine in one restaurant and Dong Bei cuisine in the other. It's a fantastic concept that caters to different taste preferences, and I appreciate the effort in bringing variety to the dining options.

Overall, I highly recommend this establishment for its cleanliness, spacious setting, and the delightful staff. The dual focus on Sichuan and Dong Bei cuisines adds an exciting dimension to the dining experience. Looking forward to returning soon!

Total damage for 6 pax S$200
author: Elaina Poh

restaurant_name: 江湖冒菜 Authentic Sichuan Restaurant
review_text:
What's the point of queueing outside when the restaurant is full when...
Your staff just lets the next person that walks in (without even queuing) to get the next seat without even checking outside for the queue???

The staff still dare to say she didn't know.. when we were standing outside the whole time for a good 30 mins (we didn't even sit on the waiting chairs outside) waiting for the next available table.
author: HanYS2601

review_text:
No complaints! Staff were really friendly and accommodating. Nice local coffee and easy food for my kids who are adjusting to local foods.
Nice to have pictures, so that we know what's on the menu.
Totally recommend, especially if you are new to Singapore.
author: Charlene Smith

review_text: Good and decent place. It’s a popular place for parents especially on the weekends when they send their kids to tuition classes. Aside from the typical toasts, they have a good range of savory food and normal dim sum box as well. Humongous sizes for iced drinks. Quite a comfortable environment and many seats around.
author: Abraham Lee

review_text: We ordered Chee Cheong Fun with Siew Mai and the other with Yong Tau Foo plus small coffee and ice milk tea.  The total cost was $17+ considered quite expensive for local breakfast.  But we like the high ceiling and decor of the place.  It was not crowded during weekday morning.  Cashier was friendly and food was ready quite fast.  The collection buzzer was rather loud though and food were not ready for collection at one go thus have to make multiple trips just to collect the order.  The coffee was okay but rather small cup like expresso size.  The ice milk tea was bland and very diluted.  The chee cheong fun has a frozen taste but the yong tau foo was fresh (the veggie was half stalk of bai cai could have cut into smaller bites).  Overall no wow factor.  Not sure if it would be better if we stick to the traditional toast would be a better choice.
author: 樂Fun Homestay

author: K M

review_text: Food was good! Skewers took awhile, but they were nicely seasoned. Pig ears with cucumber was garlicky and tasty. Dumplings had good balance of meat and chives. Overall good value, don't have to travel to chinatown for authentic chuan chuan
author: Stephanie Tan

review_text: Had an amazing experience dining at 友间厨坊 - A Kitchen. The food was fantastic, and the star of the show was definitely the Squirrel Fish (松鼠鱼) as it is crispy on the outside, tender on the inside, and beautifully presented with a sweet and tangy sauce that hits all the right notes. You can tell the chef puts a lot of heart into the cooking. Will definitely come back to try more dishes. Highly recommended!

wish the shredded potato can be spicier

review_text: A Kitchen offers a wide variety of authentic Hunan dishes at reasonable prices. Must-tries include their barbecue chicken and pork skewers, which are spot on. The salt egg bitter gourd was a simple yet refreshing side dish. But the star of the show was the kung bao chicken - one of the best I've ever tasted! A great spot for Hunan food lovers.
author: derek neo

review_text: Food is good. Place quite small but there’s a lot of people. Drinks are self service. Place quite cramp but not too stuffy. Order China Chinese food, the rest just so so.
author: Albert Wong

review_text: The broccoli was not fresh and looked black, the rice was hard and dry, and some items we ordered were not served. The service was also poor, yet we were still charged a 10% service fee. Very disappointing overall — I will not be going back again.

review_text: Meat big cut... Hard to grill, always short of dish. Say miss. After food come must count. Cannot trust.
author: Lian Yit Lee

review_text: Prices are very reasonable. There is a buffet option but items $4 and above are excluded. I think al carte option is good enough and perhaps more worth it. Fish paste noodle was best dish, did not seems to be found easily else where. Meat selection was great. I feel everything was generally sweet, not sure if it’s just sugar or some seasoning. Drinks are reasonably price. Expect to wait during peak hours.
author: 7eleven

review_text: Ate here with friends twice, and the mookata is amazing. There is free ice cream (a la carte free 1st cup, buffet is free flow i believe), something you dont find very often with mookata. Meat is also plentiful for the price. Will come again.
author: thelevitator

review_text: Good place to eat bbq in air-conditioning place. It has an exhaust fan above each table. The food was good and the prawns were fresh. And I like the chilli sauce too. Service was prompt but maybe due to busy timing, at multiple times the service staff literally threw the empty gas can into the waste bin which lead to loud noise. This was quite unpleasant. I hope the Operator can look into this. Other than that, it's a great place to dine.

restaurant_name: Shi Li Fang Hot Pot @ Junction 10

author: Kris Heng

restaurant_name: Shi Li Fang Hot Pot @ Junction 10

Highly recommend if you’re looking for good hotpot and a cozy atmosphere!

restaurant_name: Shi Li Fang Hot Pot @ Junction 10

restaurant_name: Shi Li Fang Hot Pot @ Junction 10

Staff were attentive to our table when we needed the plates to be cleared. Dinner for 4 including a 20% discount was $110+. Will come again!!

麻辣烤鱼 was also good. Surprisingly the fish was not cooked throughly even after they deep fried. It's fine as it was cooked after we left it awhile inside the boiling soup. Will try their other dishes next round.

review_text:
On the eve of Lunar New Year, I found surprisingly many empty tables at this restaurant.

The prata is a must-try; it’s the star of the menu and incredibly crispy and delicious. I also tried the masala chicken biryani, which was one of the better ones I’ve had.

The only downside is the lack of fans for the outdoor seating, which might be too hot for Singapore’s weather. I recommend sitting in the air-conditioned area, but it fills up quickly, so you’ll need to be quick.

Overall, it’s a great place for Indian cuisine, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for good Indian food.
author: Toast

review_text: I come here for my prata fix even though there are other prata places nearer to me. The pratas here are crispier and the choices are wider. The chicken chunks are big and meaty. Also, the free flow of curry gravy is a big plus. Usually has a good crowd of people. However, the indoor seating is small and the door to the outdoor seating area is usually open, so it can get warm inside on hot days.
author: MingCherng Chiang

review_text: Very nice food , the masala chicken briyanni set very worth the price of $9.90 also have teh Tarik in the set , service very good the worker very kind and when I asked for a straw for the teh tarik as it was hard to drink because it’s hot, the worker go take the straw immediately and less than 5 second he give me my straw . The atmosphere is also good , very peaceful place to eat and there is outdoor and indoor sides so you can choose where to eat. Overall , 5 STARS😋
author: Banananana

review_text:
I had the briyani shank and a double egg prata — they were really delicious. You should definitely give them a try.

I also ordered a kopi chino, and the taste was just perfect
author: amirul hisham

review_text: Food is delicious. My favorite prata shop. A place that not only fill my tummy but also giving me the happiness of enjoying the food. Their Prata is always serve crispy . Nobody does that better than spring leaf prata. Always order their coin prata and tissue prata ,mee goreng and teh Tarik.
author: HX Ling

review_text: Tasty Halal food!! Thank you
author: Rahim Aris

review_text: Ordered their black pepper chicken chop with 2 sides, mashed potato and coleslaw. Their portion was big compared to other similar establishments, and this is a good thing. Only downside was their pepper sauce was too salty and they had a lot of mayonnaise on their coleslaw. Downright satisfying but bad for the waistline!
author: Miriam Fong

review_text:
Not recommended.
Salty extreme saltiness, no other taste.
Beef poor quality.

Smoker smoking  around in no smoking area.

author: Eva Jap

review_text: I ordered $12 spring chicken for take away on 8 Oct. They gave me 2 pieces of half spring chicken. Chicken was overcooked/refried. Size was extremely small. Meat was dry. Horrible. The worst chicken I had in my entire life. I rather buy NTUC roasted chicken. Fushion Western, please don't cheat your customers. Karma will hit back at you.
author: Ash Ash

review_text: Always buy my food here . I like their aglo seafood , chicken Bolognese and the whole fried chicken. Love also their western food .
author: Pari goodarzi

review_text:
Perpetual long queue at all times.
Friendly & Reasonable price (large generous servings!)

Piping hot dishes from kitchen almost all ready by 1030am.
author: T Tan

review_text: I can never get enough of the Mee Rebus from this stall. The peanut sauce is so perfect and very delicious. Always fuel my breakfast. Must try for Mee Rebus lover.
author: Sherman Seow

review_text: Good place for Nasi Lemak, Nasi campur or mee siam and Mee Rebus. Always have to queue regardless of weekday or weekend.
author: Kimberly Ong

review_text: Very nice Malay, the Nasi Sambal Goreng is very delicious and other food also nice
author: Nick Lim

review_text:
Great variety of Malay dishes! Super delicious! 😋 Authentic old-school dishes like "sayur lemak turi keledek", "paru lembu sambal belado", which are hard to find & come by unless you visit those "ulu kampong warongs" in Malaysia. The "sambal belachan" is super fiery! Proceed with caution! 😝😜🤪

They have beef bakso noodles, the usual culprits like lontong, mee siam, mee soto, soto ayam, mee rebus etc.

Of course, you should try the mee soto with extra bergedil. 😋😋😋

Y'all must try it, yo!
author: Shaerilynn Scarlet Rose Baker

review_text:
Hidden gem in Bangkit. Tried the crispy prawn pancake.  crispy, flavourful and have wok hey. Their homemade chilli dip is super good, mild spicy and sour. Would definitely visit again to try their char kueh tiaw, carrot cake, hokkien mee and oyster pancake.

Kudos to the old couples!

Gentle remind that they do not open on Sundays. Please also give a little patience while waiting for the good food.
author: Mandy Ting

review_text: I'm a big fan of the fried carrot cake here! The dark version is perfectly balanced - savory and not too sweet. My wife, on the other hand, raves about the white carrot cake, describing it as crispy and packed with flavor. We're both impressed with the quality and taste of these dishes!"
author: Jason Lee

review_text:
Was around the area. Saw the "hidden gem"
5 star star review below and decided to give it a try. Ordered fried prawn mee and carrot cake. First bite, I think the above review was much overrated. The carrot cake blend AF. Definitely can't taste any wok hey. There was a funny taste in the yellow prawn mee. The prawns are fresh though. After finishing the food, I still think it's very much overrated.
Initially thought of just leaving without finishing the food but don't wanna waste. The food is edible.
Didn't want to leave any bad reviews but don't want people to get misled by the hidden gem review below.
author: Al Tan

review_text:
Hokkien mee not good. Also found a hair in it.

Char kway teow OK good.

White Carrot cake okay. My partner liked it.
author: Wang Yu Phua

review_text: Best
author: Ah Huat

review_text: Masala Thosai has been one of my favorites. I passed by Blk 257 Bangkit, Food Hub coffee shop frequently but never tried theirs, so I decided to order one. It was a little pricey compared to the one I had at the Bukit Panjang hawker center. My conclusion is that it's value for money because their potatoes are bigger and more in quantity, and their dipping sauce is thicker - not the watery type.
author: S L

review_text:
Your prata used to be the best I ever ate. I remembered having to queue 20min or more or my prata in a weekend morning. It was crispy with everything spread evenly spread out.

Today, your prata is the worst I ever ate. Dough was thick (it should spread out), it’s not crispy too. This has been the experience for the past couple weeks such that I will give your shop a miss now.

The new king of prata is now at Senja hawker centre. Please go try them to find yourselves back. It’s a pity that you’ve lost the flavour that brings you success.

I hope you will reflect deeply for FnB is cut throat industry. Whoever can’t survive will have to close, I do not see the next one to close is you for I’ve been supporting you for the last decade.

Not sure if it’s a different owner but please go try the prata at Senja Hawker Centre. The queue has since shifted there.

A prata is not a prata without the heart and effort from the chef. Anyone can sell prata but who can do it better?

“If you are not meeting competition, then, you are creating one.”

From: sincerely someone who wish you can do it better
author: William Lim

review_text:
In efficient, Waited long as seems forget my order. Seen Others were served, and does not see my order in progress of cook.
I asked to cancel but shown me bad impressions , saying "you just order ma".
Being a long time customer here, sadly to experience this.
author: Danny Loh

review_text:
I ordered an egg cheese thosai because this is one of the few stalls in Bangkit that sells thosai.

The man taking the order nodded confidently and handed me an oily buzzer.

But when i went to collect my food, it turned into a $2.80 egg sausage prata?? How does "egg cheese thosai" even sound remotely like "egg sausage prata"??

I confronted the man who took my order but he only said " No thosai no thosai" and I have no idea if he actually understood what I said at all.

Don't come here if you really want to get something specific and don't speak Tamil. Prata wise, Samsudeen actually tastes much better as well, and is more value for money.
author: Joanne Ong

review_text: Pls close and go away. Your food is not fit for humans to eat. Just because you want to build houses back in India, you sell tasteless food to us. Your rojak showcase edges is dirty as well.
author: Chan P

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Roasted Chicken and Duck rice
review_text:
have ate this chicken rice for over 15yrs and think its 1 of the best and most value for money chicken rice.
rice is so fragrant and nicely flavoured and not overly oily, does not leave any oily aftertaste.
roasted chicken is tender and not dry. chilli sauce is tangy sour spicy, very appetising.

will continue to visit this delicious stall.

review_text:
I come by the neighborhood and was walking around the area, and came across this stall. It has a rather large frontage and its offerings are displayed across its frontage.

They have a wide variety of bakes and cooked stuff. They include: soon kueh (5 types), bak chang, huat kueh, glutinous rice, dessert kueh, ang ku kueh, carrot cake, old school bread (plain or you can ask them to spread kaya within), Nasi lemak, desserts (pulut hitam, cheng tng and others), biscuits and note.

They have a variety of soon kueh.

I had the bang kuang which has had cut turnip and dried shrimp. It was tasty without the sweet black sauce. The skin is on the thick side.

I also had the yellow colored one, which had leek, beancurd and fried shrimp. This was unique. Will order it again.

A good find and I will patronize when I am in the neighborhood again.
author: Winston Ho

review_text: Moved to this area recently and visited this place on a Sunday morning. There were a lot of people as it is nearby a wet market. They have a wide range of food selection. In the morning, they have noodles, nasi lemak, varieties of kueh and dessert. Even iced one. Didn’t expect that when I ordered a sea coconut. Anyway, it was really hot that day. So I just went with the flow. Happy to find big pieces of sea coconut but it is weird that they have other fruits in the dessert. I wouldn’t recommend to have the lime in it cos it just covers the sea coconut flavour. Plus point, it is cheap. $2 for dessert and $0.80 for white sugar steamed cake.

review_text:
A really one of a kind snack bar in Singapore with all kinds of traditional kueh and Chinese snacks available. I recall there’s one in Hougang Ave 2 and never thought there’s another one right here in Bangkit!

The shop sells literally every kind of snack you can think of: there’s the usual bread buns and pastries outside, Nyonya kueh and carrot cake, Peng kueh, dumplings in the cabinet and a bread station at one end putting jams and spreads to freshly baked bread.

Prices are pretty affordable, bought 4 pieces of kueh (the yellow ones) and it’s $3.20 only. Much cheaper than the other kueh chain B.S. If you like old school snacks, this is the place to go!

restaurant_name: King of Fried Rice - Bukit Panjang
review_text:
The last time I ate here was Jun 2023. It's Jun 2024 now, and they still only accept cash payments. In an era where cashless options like PayNow, PayLah!, GrabPay, and others are widely available, it's quite inconvenient to not have any of these options. There have been several occasions where I came here without any cash and, unfortunately, couldn't patronize them. I wonder how many customers they miss out on due to this opportunity cost. The lack of modern payment methods might deter many customers who prefer cashless transactions.

As for the food, I ordered their fried rice couple of times, which unfortunately didn't meet my expectations. The rice was wet and clumpy, lacking the usual fluffiness and separation you'd expect from good fried rice. Additionally, there were only a few pieces of spring onion scattered throughout the dish. Are they rationing spring onions? This made the dish feel sparse and less flavorful than it could be.

Overall, while this branch has potential, there are significant improvements needed both in their payment options and the quality of their dishes.

review_text:
There are several rojak stalls at Bt Panjang, and this is one of the better ones. The $5 serving (photo) has jicima (bungkwung), cucumber, pineapple, tau pok and yutiao with enough rojak sauce and crushed peanuts to coat every piece generously. They have green mango and apple too, presumably for the more expensive options. The tau pok and yutiao are toasted and crunchy, and the sauce has a good balance of savoury, sweet, tart and floral from bunga kantan (ginger flower).

Service is friendly, and if there's a line, you can place your order and buy other stuff first.

I've seen some poor reviews that doesn't speak or mention enough of the quality and taste of the food, or took issue with their operating hours and supposedly bad service without details.

I'd recommend this next time you need a snack at Bt Panjang.

review_text:
This is one of the best Halal traditional Yong Tau Foo I've ever eaten! Easily on my top 3 list.

You pick your own ingredients, and the selection is fantastic. The items I chose were all incredibly fresh, especially the fish cake, which was so tender. The golden mushrooms were also cooked perfectly and pairs extremely well with this soup

My favorite part was the fried items that came in a separate bowl. The seaweed chicken and chicken cheese balls were particularly amazing, super tasty and fried to perfection.

The service was also really fast; my meal was ready in less than five minutes. What I also loved was the self-service counter where you can fill your bowl with as many yellow beans as you want, and they have the best chili and sweet YTF sauces I’ve ever tasted, plus a light soy sauce with diced chili.

The broth was savory and delicious, and even if it's thanks to some MSG or chicken stock, it doesn't matter because the taste is worth it.

While the prices seemed slightly higher than other coffee shop YTF stalls, it's definitely worth the extra cost for the quality and convenience. The best part? They're open 24/7, so you can get a delicious bowl of YTF anytime. I'll definitely be back the next time I'm in the area!

review_text:
This halal yong tau food stall is a sister chain to Meixi Kitchen. Replicating the taste of traditional yong tau foo with chicken filling is no small feat, and Dou Vegetarian pulls it off admirably.

Prices are reasonable, starting at $4.80 for a 5-piece combo with a choice of carbs. What truly impressed me was the interesting spread of handmade pieces, including a unique longbean dumpling.  Plus, they refry the fried items and king oyster mushroom upon order, ensuring the yong tau foo pieces are served hot and crispy.

For an extra $1, you can even upgrade your soup to Tom Yum or Mala.  I ordered a whopping 8 pieces with rice noodles and opted for the Tom Yum upgrade.  In hindsight, the Tom Yum was a bit of a miss for me – a touch too salty and lacking the depth of flavour I craved.  However, the star of the show was definitely the yong tau foo pieces themselves!

restaurant_name: 龙飞麻辣香锅 Dragon-Fly Mala Hotpot - Bukit Panjang
review_text:
Used to be my good ol' reliable for mala in the west, be it by takeaway, dine-in or delivery. The standard has dropped so drastically these months I double checked if I ordered from the right shop... The other reviews clearly agree.

I've ordered thrice now, hoping that the previous bad experience was a fluke but it's just the standard now. Noodles are hopelessly soggy but I can close an eye for it since it's delivery. I always indicate more sauce, but it's always dry and u can't even pick up noodles without picking up everything else like a bush. They never have coriander either. The spice is inconsistent, and superbly bland— I have to add my own home chilli sauces to eat this. Pork belly is so overcooked I can't even taste the fatty parts from the lean meat. Really disappointing. The best tasting thing is the cheese tofu. Not to mention the prices are ridiculous for its quality. No more fourth chance.
author: Arica Lim

restaurant_name: 龙飞麻辣香锅 Dragon-Fly Mala Hotpot - Bukit Panjang
review_text:
First two visits were decent, so I came back a third time—big mistake. Quality dropped hard. Tried enoki mushrooms for the first time and got charged $5.60, with no option for a smaller portion.

For context, that’s close to 8× the price of a supermarket pack… except you don’t even get the whole thing. Felt like 2/3 of the mushrooms magically disappeared after weighing. Some pieces weren’t even properly cooked.

So yes, you’re forced to pay at least $5.60 even if you just want a small portion—but don’t worry, the vendor’s “generosity” kicks in by only giving you a taste. Overpriced, inconsistent, and honestly feels dishonest. Won’t be back.

review_text:
This stall, helmed by a friendly elderly couple, seems to operate at its own pace. My Monday late morning visit, supposedly an off-peak hour, resulted in a 20-minute wait for my order.

Here, everything is made fresh upon order. I opted for the Mee Hoon Kueh with Dumplings ($5.20, with egg). Each bowl comes with a trio of dumplings, sliced shiitake and straw mushrooms,  shanghai green vegetable and a decent portion hand-torn mee hoon kueh.

The star of the show is the hand-torn mee hoon kueh itself. It boasts a chewy texture that complements the light and flavourful broth. The accompanying pork dumplings are equally unassuming, with a simple seasoning that lets the natural flavours shine.

The portion size might leave you wanting more, especially if you're famished.  This is a perfect option for a light lunch. Overall, I recommend this stall only if you have some time to spare and a hankering for a bowl ofmee hoon kueh.

Greens vegetables choy sum or xiao bai cai has been replaced with cheaper chinese cabbage, where the servings serves less than 1/2 leaf. Plus 2 slices of button mushroom.

Noodle serving serves 4 mouthful, depending on the size of your spoon. Have to dig up just for photo shoot so it looks "more"!

Soup seems like the most expensive ingredient, as i notice others getting even lesser than what you see in photo.

And in the meantime, the 2 chaps were talking about the cost price of replacing the plastic takeaway containers.

restaurant_name: Traditional Handmade Mee Hoon Kueh Ban Mian U-Mian
review_text:
I’ve been a loyal patron of this humble stall for over a decade. Back in the day, it was helmed by Uncle and his wife, whose Mee Hoon Kueh was nothing short of legendary in the neighbourhood — the kind of bowl that warms both the stomach and the soul. Even when their competitor, Fong Hup, opened right next door, they held their ground, retaining loyal customer and serving the superior Mee Hoon Kueh.

Today, the ownership has been passed to a spirited team of young men. While their enthusiasm is admirable and their marketing efforts earnest, the Mee Hoon Kueh I once adored has taken on a very different character — and not for the better. Sadly, the queues have thinned, and more of the regulars I used to see are now heading to Fong Hub next door for their cravings.

review_text:
We enjoyed our two sets of Thunder Tea Rice. One with basil chicken and another one with katsu chicken. We also added side dish basil omelette and hakka beancurd.

Thunder tea rice, known locally as Lei Cha Fan (擂茶饭), is a traditional Hakka dish in Singapore prized for its health benefits. It consists of a bowl of rice topped with various finely chopped vegetables and a distinctive green herbal soup.

The highlight is an emerald-green soup made by grinding a paste of tea leaves, basil, mint, coriander, mugwort, peanuts, and sesame seeds. It has a bold, earthy, and herbal flavor that can be slightly bitter—an acquired taste for some.

review_text:
Murtabak (SGD $8) @ Casuarina Curry.
.
Established in the 1950s and later incorporated in January 1993, this chain of stalls is known for making their dishes from scratch daily. The brand is family owned, run by brothers Ramanan Subramaniam and Ravindran Subramaniam, sister Thenmozhi Subramaniam.
.
Famed for their rendition, which has a crispy light crunchy pan-fried dough which shatters beautifully when bit. Folded and layered with wispy chicken egg, crisp red onion, bouncy button mushrooms, and gooey cheddar cheese, along with a choice of spiced meat or fish.
.
The most popular are tender turmeric spiced minced mutton, chewy shredded chicken, or soft sardine fish. Carries smoky bready meaty eggy vegetal salty savoury spice earthy tangy zesy sour cheesy flavour.
.
They also offer unique renditions, including a vegetarian option with cabbage.
.
.
Mutton Mysore (SGD $7) @ Casuarina Curry.
.
Established in the 1950s and later incorporated in January 1993, this chain of stalls is known for making their dishes from scratch daily. The brand is family owned, run by brothers Ramanan Subramaniam and Ravindran Subramaniam, sister Thenmozhi Subramaniam.
.
Their rendition is a dry richly spiced version, with the chunks of boneless mutton marinated with plain yoghurt and spices including black pepper, turmeric, curry leaves, and powdered red chili, then simmered for up to 2 hours or so.
.
The result is a tender oily dry chewy texture, with sharp meaty salty spicy savoury peppery flavour. Rather fiery, the heat grips and lingers on the palate.

review_text:
Made sure I was full before I typed this so it wouldn’t be out of hangryness, but sadly the service standards and food quality here have dropped drastically over the past year or two. Previously posted a 5 star review 3years back but after my experience the last 2 visits I have to rescind it.

Made a phone order at 5.30pm for pick up at 7.30pm. Arrived on the dot, but was told the food wasnt ready yet, as the chicken was still being prepped - that’s fine.

Paid first and was told to pay with paynow amidst the many paper signs screaming that they prefer paynow. The last visit I asked if I could pay with paywave (to accrue points of course) but was told that I had to pay with paynow, so this visit I didnt bother asking again. But the next gentleman (a regular I presume from the way he was so warmly greeted by the waiter) who came had his credit card readily accepted without question or being asked to paynow! Double standards apparent.

After waiting a good 15-20mins while left standing at their payment counter, finally received my food. Normally I would be fine with that (timing is never perfect), but despite waiting for the chicken to be cooked, in that time it came out skinny, burnt and dry (refer to pictures)

Not only that, the pizza was cold (I live only 5mins away so couldnt have been travel time). $106.40 for everything pictured - kinda pricey imo for the portion sizes and quality but it is what it is (inflation).

Mom suggested pizza hut initially - in retrospect might have been a better idea.

Tldr: dont get the chicken, insist if you want to paywave, if it’s for takeaway consider other options.

fettuccine ala carbonara (remind me of Italy). And the pizza: rucola parma - we pre-ordered one but couldn't resist and order another. The Parma ham are not  too salty and the dough just perfecto.
Don't miss the dessert too,  we ordered creme brûlée, melting chocolate cake and tiramisu.
We are lucky we had 6 of ours so we could sample so many dishes. Many times we were so eager to taste the food that I didn't remember to take picture.😂
Most importantly, it's not expensive and taste really authentic.
author: Maureen Hhk

review_text:
Pretty good, i got the 1 for 1 student deal, 11.30 to 2.30 on weekdays. I tried the lasagna and it was covered in sauce, mozzarella cheese. Very nice. The fettuccine fungi was pretty good too, with bacon and mushrooms. The tiramisu was ok, looked nice and had a little coffee taste.

Pretty good, service was nice and quite fast too. They give water. Total was like $42
author: just_wandering_around

review_text: The pizza and pasta here were fantastic. We got a carnivore pizza and a seafood risotto. Perfectly cooked, simply delicious. We also got a mushroom soup which was yummy. All these made the dessert so much more disappointing. The tiramisu was run of the mill average mass produced tiramisu. After such fantastic food it was a letdown to have such an average dessert. Just come here for the mains, leave the tiramisu alone.
author: Justin Zhou

review_text: Had dinner at Ban Leong Wah Hoe and wasn't disappointed with the items we ordered. Their Moonlight Hor Fun was full of wok hei and was one of our favourites. I would recommend ordering their Prawn Paste fried chicken as well, it was crispy and you can really taste the prawn paste. Chicken was cooked just right.
author: Jason Tsai

review_text: Decent local Chinese restaurant. Hot plate tofu taste like chilli crab sauce. I was served a injured crab at $120 too. Hope that it's only me that got bullied.
author: Kit Mun

review_text: Genuine authentic Singapore at its best, this is the place to come to for black pepper or Chilli crab. All of the dishes they offer are cooked fresh and to perfection, service is prompt and friendly. It is not Air conditioned but has plenty of fans and blower. Great place to bring the family or the overseas guests wanting to experience real Singapore dining. Must Try!
author: Richard Parry

review_text: Delicious food and convenient parking! Service was prompt and staff were proactive to offer new plates. Highly recommended.
author: Damien Chng

review_text: We keep coming back for the past 9 years without fail. Food and service is consistent and very quick despite the crowd. I always order the wet horfun, prawn roll, and kangkung belacan.
author: Isabel C.

restaurant_name: 明星鱼粥 ~ MING XING FISH PORRIDGE since 1974
review_text: Decent comforting bowl of sliced fish soup. The clear broth was sweet and rich in flavour. Fish slices were fresh enough. Downside was their portion was really small, and more pricier then other fish soup stalls.
author: Stanley

restaurant_name: 明星鱼粥 ~ MING XING FISH PORRIDGE since 1974
review_text: this is a gem not to be missed. this stall was passed down to current owner from his father retaining the flavorsome soup like before. the soup while sweet and flavorful does not cloy up your taste buds but has a refreshing aftertaste. their fish slices servings much more generous than other fish soup stall oozes freshness and sweetness from the superb quality of fish used. enoughh said, u have to try it for yourself!!!
author: Lee Jerom

restaurant_name: 明星鱼粥 ~ MING XING FISH PORRIDGE since 1974
review_text: One of the best fish I've eaten! Soup as clear as water but tasty still.
author: Terry Goh

restaurant_name: 明星鱼粥 ~ MING XING FISH PORRIDGE since 1974
review_text: Taste is good but portion is very small. I guess fish and vegie are expensive.
author: J Seng

restaurant_name: 明星鱼粥 ~ MING XING FISH PORRIDGE since 1974
review_text: Super small potion and 2 son yaya.
author: domingo lim

review_text:
Good service, wide variety of choices. Beef Hor Fun and Ham Fried Rice are my favourites. I commend Hans for having seasonal Christmas dishes such as chicken, ham, potato salad and etc. my friends and I enjoyed the Christmas chicken and potato salad. I enjoy eating their cakes too. Their coffee C was thick and fragrant.

I observe that they are going the direction of including local and nostalgic culture with customised coffee bags, kaya and etc. Even though it is quite late for Hans to embark on this trend, it is better late than never. The packaging of these products need further movement. Easily accessible by MRT. Quite a challenge to find parking.

I started dining at Hans at their Far East Branch and also Changi Budget Terminal. My favourite branch remains the one at Springleaf as it is big and spacious with consistent food quality.
author: Toh Bee Leng

review_text:
I had the breakfast platter/big breakfast. The presentation is nice especially the little potato shaped like a smiley face. The potatoes all tasted nice and crunchy (including tater tots which is probably the best I’ve had after trying different ones from different famous cafes in Singapore). The bread was fragrant and crunchy as well - tasted fresh. Even the salad was done quite well with the sauce, which is not easy to find in many places and reflects the care put into something seemingly simple. The sausages, egg, and ham all make for a hearty meal.

although it is a bit on the greasy side (perhaps as expected as most things are fried), it’s overall a great treat to have once in a while when feeling indulgent.

note: 1 sausage is missing from the picture as it has been eaten!
author: T D

review_text: A hidden gem for fuss-free comfort food. The menu is simple, affordable, and surprisingly tasty—great value without the frills. The space is cozy and clean, with a quiet charm that reminds me of an old-school American diner. Staff were efficient, and the overall vibe makes it easy to relax and enjoy your meal. Perfect for casual lunches or no-stress dinners. Will definitely return.
author: John

review_text:
Han’s is my default place to go for a meal. The food is always freshly prepared and the service is usually not bad. Prices at this outlet are slightly higher and the presentation is better.

Yes, some of their food are pre-cooked and packed so that the standard is the same across all outlets if I am not wrong.

I would like to add that during my visit on 3 Nov, I saw Janet who used to be at the Bedok CC outlet. It was really nice to see a friendly and familiar face.
author: Isabella Tan

review_text:
Dropped by Han Union for a quick lunch with my mum, who’s a big fan of their coffee.

This round, the hor fun was slightly burnt, and overall the food didn’t feel as tasty as before, which was a little disappointing. That said, they do offer a wide variety of food, snacks, and pastries, and the waiting time was pleasantly short.

Still a convenient spot for a quick meal and coffee break, but hopefully the food quality gets back to its usual standard soon. ☕🥐
author: Denise Han

review_text: I had the udon at Tamako and was really impressed by the atmosphere. It’s a very clean, quiet space that feels peaceful despite having a TV on in the background. The staff was friendly and the service was excellent. I loved the flexibility of being able to order through a QR code or with a server. Plus, the free Wi-Fi is a great touch. I’ll definitely be back.
author: Vikneswaran Baskaran

review_text: I’ve been going to Tamako Meal quite often, and I’ve finally decided not to gatekeep it anymore—good food is meant to be shared! Their homely Japanese dishes are always so comforting, but the real standout is the bento ❤️ It comes packed with a variety of ingredients, each offering its own taste and texture, making every bite a little treat for the senses.. If you’re craving authentic, heartwarming Japanese comfort food, this is the place to go!
author: Bei Er Ong

review_text:
Tried Tamakomeal for lunch and ordered the Yakitori Set, Tonkotsu Shoyu Ramen, Kitsune Udon, and Tamako Teishoku Set.
The yakitori skewers 10pcs were flavorful though a little uneven in seasoning, while the ramen had a decent broth but could have been richer.
The udon was light and comforting, and the teishoku set felt homely and well-balanced.

Overall, the food was satisfying with fair portions at reasonable prices.
Service was simple and efficient.
A good spot for casual Japanese comfort food,
author: Boon Leong

review_text: Ordered 2 sets of their set bento meal of Pork & Beef.  There is a lot of different food.  Besides the main meat dish, there is potato salad, edamame, fried prawn tempura, one piece of Karaage, dumpling with miso soup.  The taste is not authentic Japanese and both the meat are tough. Disappointed as I heard this restaurant used to supply bento sets to Japanese school as expectations seems not met.
author: Susan Tay

review_text: Nice cosy and clean place. Hoke fish taste good and no fishy smell. Fish Size quite big maybe lucky. Will be trying again next time.
author: Julian Ng

review_text:
My favorite chicken rice.
Chicken is tender and juicy. Roasted chicken is soft too. I love his chilli sauce.
His special sauce and oil match tender meats. Soup contains a lot of chicken feet, corb, etc. But it depends on the day.
It's worth to visit and try!
author: RYKAYOYU

review_text:
A fusion between Mexican & Indian food. They do provide separate Indian food menu.

Overall, the beef tacos are super nice and delicious. The burrito wrap may be a little too thick but it was very content and well stuffed with ingredients.

The Chicken 65 I order was quite close to the one I had at India, so very nice

The one last one, salt lassi, was nice as they made it without added sugar.

Overall, very good.
author: Yung Jer Wong

review_text:
Ordered salmon grill , item was not as per described on the menu.

Menu stated aglio olio but they served tomato pasta instead. Waiter did not inform me of the changed and hence was not made known until the food is here. Which i did ask the staff why is it not aglio olio and his reply "we don't do aglio olio anymore" . And its $26 for a plate of subpar salmon fillet with pasta. can get better standards with $26. Will not be visiting here again.
author: hi

review_text:
Nice and cozy eatery.
Waiter was friendly and recommended what we should get.
That said, their fish tacos were really good. I’m not usually a fan of fish, but the sauce they used and the texture and juiciness of each bite was very enjoyable.
We also ordered truffle fries - it was good
Also ordered fajitas, beef version, and they were not chewy. The onions and peppers are caramelised and we finished the entire hot plate.
Ordered a pint of Guinness to accompany the meal, pour was great. You can buy their 3 for 30 special and save the pint for your next visit.

Will be back!
author: unhackerful

review_text: Celebrated my son’s birthday dinner here on a Thursday evening. We ordered different types of nachos, tacos, quesadillas, burritos and chimichangas to share and all were delicious, authentic and were large portions at reasonable prices. There was also a beer promo for 3 pints for only $30. Service was quick and attentive probably because there was only one other group of customers. It was pretty quiet for dinner. Will definitely come back to try their other Mexican dishes.
author: Jeremy Khoo

review_text: Ordered the kerala beef roast and the striploin fajita. Both were awesome! Not to mention the Porotta. So soft and perfect!
author: Eileen Ng

review_text:
Pistachio & mortadella sandwich is flavourful and portion is good to share. Tomato & clams pasta was yummy and the addition of kaffir lime really made the sauce so drinkable.
Sour cream fried chicken tastes sinful (in a good way), but would prefer the tomato sauce to be served separately as the bottom of the chicken wings were soggy.
Must order the mulberry bayleaf gelato - just refreshing and a great way to end the meal.

They have a good selection of drinks too. Matcha banana milk is good for those who like banana milk taste. Matcha strawberry was smooth but wish the strawberry taste was stronger - maybe because I opted for less sweet...

Service is friendly. Plenty of seating but the place is crowded on Sunday lunch. Waited abt 30min.
Do note there is a waiting list and you can leave your number then walk around.
author: Sabrina

review_text: Just had a great dinner in a very cozy and relaxing place. Had a good chat with Amanda, the owner. She is very inspiring and she wanted to really prepare her food with her heart and serve well. We were all enjoying the food very much and her staff also serves us well. Her Beth Hotcake is really solid. It is really a go to place for friends gathering and chat.
author: Gee Hai Tan

review_text:
Great atmosphere. Great interesting menu. As a pancake, I kinda disappointed on this pancake.
It’s too big for one person unless you call a group of friends to share.
Suggest to create smaller portion for individual. There is no strawberry rhubarb jam on the hotcake. As a rhubarb lover, there is no rhubarb texture.
I like the butter cube. Very nice.
Tea selection is a lot of matcha.
Would like to try their other dishes next time.
Service is great but the cashier is too timid voiced.
author: Av C

review_text: We tried booking a table for 6 pax on Sat morning thru whatapp. Amanda was very helpful. The Mortadella Sandwich n Smoke Salmon sandwiches were very freshly prepared. Foccasia bread was great (sourced). Hot cake unique n excellent with house jam n butter. Matcha with brown sugar good. Except hot chocolate, just average, room for improvement. Overall it is still a great outing for our family. Highly recommended for bf, brunch, lunch or tea. Yet to try the dinner menu. Eyeing the Wayu Bolar Steak :))) and yes, we stayed longer than agreed time, the staff were still very friendly n keep the healthy free flow water going. Keep it up Amanda n Alex.
author: Danny Lim

review_text:
Beth truly delivers an exceptional experience from start to finish. Every dish reflects high standards and thoughtful preparation. The pancakes were incredibly soft and fluffy, with a perfect balance of sweetness and a gentle fermented tang that made them light yet deeply satisfying. The tomato pasta was rich and comforting, with smooth, well-developed flavours and a portion size that felt just right. It tasted refined and carefully made.

The strawberry matcha stood out with its homemade strawberry jam, which was unique, fresh, and paired beautifully with the creamy, lightly sweet matcha. The beef truffle focaccia was equally impressive crispy on the outside, soft inside, and infused with a fragrant truffle flavour that elevated the entire dish.

What truly completed the experience was the service. The staff were genuinely kind, warm, and attentive, greeting us sincerely and fulfilling every request with care. Their friendliness felt natural and made the visit even more enjoyable.

Overall, Beth cafe offers rich flavours, quality food, and heartfelt service. I would absolutely return and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable experience.
author: hyumi w

review_text:
Had the opportunity to have lunch at this restaurant
Ordered, Appam, naadan chicken roast, beef roast Angamali pork roast.
Great food and good service.
The combination  with Toddy makes it unique.
What makes it even great is the fusion of mexican food.. it satisfied the cravings for kids too.
author: J C John

review_text: Fantastic customer service .Good food .Kallu was awesome ,it’s cold .we tried 3 types all good .pork roast and appam are very good combination.over all impressed
author: ADARSH ARAVIND

review_text: Food and drinks are done very well. And great service always given. The choice of Kerala or Mexican cuisine is a great and not usually heard of combo.
author: Sujish Alexander

review_text: It was a good experience. Food was good and fresh. Service was good too.
author: Minerva The Goddess

review_text: Good service and ambience but average food. Especially Porotta & Appam.. very dry and seems not to be fresh. Not sure.
author: Yathu Krishnan K

review_text:
Came in not expecting much left—especially after reading the previous review—but oh boy, I was wrong. There was a whole array of dishes lined up at the counter, so many that I didn’t even know where to start.

They had naan, chapati, and of course, prata. Since I wanted something light for brunch and wasn’t in the mood for rice, I went for a simple, no-frills prata.

Served on a silver plate with banana leaf, the prata was surprisingly flavourful—crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and packed with taste. A simple yet satisfying choice!

Staffs that serve and took my orders are friendly and full of smiles
author: Z BH

review_text: Small portion chicken curry only $4.50 lol 😂 super expensive?
author: rama reddy

review_text: Came here at 1025am and everything finish😂
author: Helen

review_text: Bro today I bought first time chicken Briyani 8 dollars.  taste is OK.. But quantity rmba kammi... Neenga spoon la allipodurenga. That maathere pannama... a chinna bowl thula atinga yellarukum crt ta erukum thank you
author: Mani Kandan

review_text: We celebrate Mothers day event and it was succesful although it rain that day but all goes well..
author: Lorie Mariano

review_text:
Drop your check at the ATM, buy your meat at the Butcher, then sip your coffee at Yahava Koffee Works while waiting for the end of class for your kids, all in one row of shops. Guess where.
(Updated 18/052021: please note that both the ATM and butcher shop are no longer here, but great coffee is still there. )
author: Hang Boon Sin

review_text:
Very cool space. Sort of a cross between a school campus and mall. It's a gorgeous mix of japanese and Scandinavian design.
Very calming space.
author: Paul Pistore

review_text: Why is there a need to block the passageway into the building by the side of the road? Not everyone drives there. It definitely will affect the businesses there for walk-ins
author: Kelvin Lim

review_text: Though out of the way, storage facility here offers at a reasonable rate and easy parking.
author: Michael Lim

review_text:
We visited after seeing their TikTok promos and were not disappointed. We tried the mutton satti soru, chicken chuka masala with bread, cheese pizza, and the signature Commando, paired with cocktails and draft beer. The portions were generous and packed with flavor; the cocktails were well-balanced and the beers fresh and creamy. Service was warm and attentive, the music and vibe were relaxed, and the ambience felt just right. With reasonable prices, it’s a perfect spot for a laid-back weekend chill-out.

#FollowMyTasteBud
author: Shashie Rajantheran

review_text:
i’ve ordered from thirsty horse via grab several times, and visited the outlet twice.

however, the food is inconsistent! used to love the commando satti sorru but today it was a huge let down. the portions of the ingredients was significantly lesser than normal and the taste was way off. however, it must be said that the overall portion of the satti sorru is very generous, and can comfortably feed two people.

as for the lamb meatballs, i urge everyone to avoid ordering this dish at all. the texture of the meatballs was so hard and had a weird after taste to it. and $19 for 5 pieces of meatballs is ridiculously overpriced!

during my visits, it was mostly for drinks so no complains about the service and ambience.
author: Marc Singh

review_text: This Indian bar is an absolute gem! The atmosphere is vibrant and welcoming, with a perfect blend of traditional Indian vibes and a modern bar setting. The drinks are expertly crafted, especially the cocktails with Indian-inspired flavors—they’re unique and refreshing. The food is outstanding, full of authentic spices and rich flavors, and pairs perfectly with the drinks. The staff is friendly, attentive, and makes you feel right at home. Whether you’re stopping by for a casual evening or a night out with friends, this place delivers an unforgettable experience. Highly recommended!
author: Prabhu

review_text:
Absolutely top notch friendly service and wonderful atmosphere to gather after a long day at work. Major food favs are the prawn satti sorru and lamb meatballs
Tina was a brilliant staff who understood our requirements and was such a darling to have a conversation. Absolutely personalised service. Kudos to thirsty horse for excellent staff and food. 😀
author: Geetha Viswambaran

review_text:
Absolutely loved this place! From the moment we arrived, everything was just right. The food was really good — fresh, tasty, and clearly made with care. Every dish we tried was enjoyable and satisfying.
The atmosphere is pleasant and comfortable, making it a great place to relax and enjoy.
author: Rusty Roosti Productions

review_text: Vegetarian World Food has always been one of my top to go for vegetarian supplies!!! The amazing range of products, the awesome and personalised service and the super swift delivery is the key point that keeps customer. They serve with warmth and sincerity! Highly recommended!! Thank you so much for the great experiences! Kudos to the team! Support support!
author: Eileen Ng

review_text: Very friendly security Indian lady, professional and courteous! Tricky entrance to the building for first-timers.  Should turn in on the first entrance you see near the security hut and not the one after if you're driving from the main road.
author: Alvin Lee

review_text: Have bought with them for many years. They have always bring me contentment and happiness through their impeccable services and extensive range of products. There was once that I received a product with defect, a Bakzhang (rice dumpling） with newspaper sticked on it, informed them just to create awareness so that other customers wouldn't be affected. But they go extra miles by compensating the dumpling on my next purchase which really amaze me that day still remember and value each customer. Dealing with them is also fast and fuss free. Always a pleasant experience! Very highly recommended! Will continue to support them! Keep up the job! 👍🏻
author: Helen Koh

review_text: I went to their location on Tagore Drive. It is wholesale only with no retail.  Despite that everyone was very nice and helped me to make order and arrange delivery. Customer service is really excellent.  Thank you very much! I also promise that in future I will order using their website and I will not show up in person!:)
author: Piotr Chlebicki

review_text:
I have been ordering from Vegetarian World Food for almost two years.

On top of the AMAZING range (you can't find a more complete vegetarian ideas anywhere else) that the customer experience that you always can also count on!!

The awesome service by the entire team is always personalized, super swift and serve with such warmth. Highly recommended!!
author: Sc Bong (Coach Bongster)

review_text: Saw this place on Insta and decided to try it out. Only 3 stalls open but quite a wide variety of Thai dishes available including pork trotter rice, beef noodles and cooked dishes. Portions are big, prices are reasonable and taste is authentic. Atmosphere is chill with high airy ceiling, Thai pop music and some Insta props to take pix. Would have given them 5 stars if more stalls were open. Will come back and try the rest.
author: Jeremy Khoo

review_text:
Big bowl of boat noodle for $5.50, has kailan vegetable pork slices and meat ball pretty value for money. Moo Ping was $5 for 3 sticks. Food flavours are more sweet than savoury. Thai Milk Tea was $2.50 each. Overall pretty decent price and food. There’s a variety of Thai dishes here, from Pad Thai to Green Curry with rice. They even have grilled seafood and Mookata here too.

Place is clean, it’s cooling and it’s well renovated. Came during lunch time and there’s ample seats. Staff here seem to be all Thai, feels like I’m back at Thailand 😄
author: Val Tan

review_text: Love this place ! Friendly staff and bosses. Food is authentic and really good atmosphere. Very cooling place with beautiful decorations. They also sell snacks and kueh from Thailand too. Prices are very reasonable. Will definitely visit again!
author: Jiunchyi Chong

review_text: I would say it's not awful but totally not AUTHENTIC. Lack of taste and aroma for all the dishes I ordered. Tom yam and the condiments are so sweet! (you can't taste spicy and sour at all) Pork jerky and Moo ping, oh my god, just a normal bbq pork. (flat, no aroma and taste) Pad Thai(prawn) like Chinese char kway teow and the prawn is not fresh cos it's mushy. Thai noodle, tasteless and have to add more condiments to make it more savory. Baked fish also not authentic.  Basically nothing are authentic although cooked by Thailand. Lok lok can give a pass as well. Where is the chilli, lime and fish sauce taste?? Disappointment
author: Alvin Tan

review_text: Very nice ambience and Thai songs played. Mini boat noddle price at $1 and the portion is very good compared to other places. The taste is superbly authentic Thai. Talked to the staff there, business has not been good. Please support if you are Thai food lover. Also, have mookata with reasonable portion and price and other authentic Thai food.
author: J “Nobita” O

review_text:
24h Food in the Wilderness

Cool thing is they are a 24h place, at least for now.
Prata was freshly made and great. Tea was also good. The guys selling were very friendly and responsive. The place was decent. However, there were a lot of birds in the area. And when I walked in I saw a monkey running out of the place with vacuum packed cake with the guy trying to give chase. Kinda hilarious I gotta say.
author: Beary Beary

review_text:
I am a big eater, as you can see i ordered 3x Double Egg Onion and a serving of Mutton curry.

Their prata is authentic soft and fluffy, its very comfortable to eat. And its not greasy.

Their mutton curry is one of the best. The meat is tender and the curry is very fragrant. It goes very well with rice.

I will recommend their rice meals as well, they cook a wide variety of Indian veggies daily, i treasure my digestive health so its important for me to get lots of veggies in. Theres chick peas, snake gourd, cabbage, all cooked to perfection.

For breakfast, do try their Masala Thosai, the coconut chutney and dhal curry served together is sedap!

Place is clean and airy with high ceiling. The staff there are friendly to everyone.

I always go there for a nice meal before stressful meeting, i feel that the food is blessed.
author: Sally McSales

review_text:
Was hungry on a rainy day, so i came across Al-Rsak while browsing google maps.

Saw the other reviews all make me very hungry, my boss ask me why i salvating while he scolding us. But nvm, it will be worth it later.

So after scolding i fast jog to Al Rsak, i ordered:

1x Masala Thosai
1x Onion Thosai
1x Egg Onion Prata

Thosai is crispy on edges, fluffy on inside, very nice. Some thosai is too thick which i dont like, this one is good.

Egg onion prata is the soft and fluffy type, eat with fish curry is amazing.

After lunch, i go back office take a nap while still being paid coz boss not around hehehe
author: Alven Tang

review_text:
I saw the recommendations and decided to try it during lunch time, very popular place among the office people there.

I ordered rice and a variety of veggies, as well as the mutton. It was really good, very tender. And with rice it was heavenly.

While i was eating i heard a customer asking about the mutton, he say it looked very nice and wanted to try also.
author: Terry McTech

review_text: The lamb hot pot was only 38 dollars ,the food was good value for money and tasted great. I recommend grilled pork intestines and lamb skewers.
author: Cheng Wei Chew

review_text: The taste of the grilled meat is superb and comes with a very nice buttery/corn like flavour✨never tasted something like this but I really love it and the quality is really there. I choose to do my own bbq over charcoal but you can also opt for the staff to grill for you!! Good setting and the staff was very helpful and friendly. Place is clean too and I like the vibe of the place 💖 will really come again, highly recommended!!
author: Teo Xinyan

review_text: Location is out of the way in an industrial canteen. Saw a rat looking for food while we were eating and the staff said it's common occurrence. Food is average. Recommend the grilled prawns
author: Lorraine Lim

review_text:
The 串串 is really very good and well priced. 5 for $5!!
Meat is well marinated and tender.
Solid bird bird. Definitely will be back!
author: Matthew Leong

review_text: Will come here again for good food at good price 👍 the lamb hotpot was huge.
author: Denise Ong

review_text:
Look for the mala shop inside.
The fish is super good and the Lazi Chicken tasted superb

The shop owner is also very friend and great service.
author: Jen Hong

review_text: The prata is made fresh and hot. The fish curry is super nice thick with the right amount of spices not watery type. Super friendly boss. Nearby can try. 👍🏻
author: Adrian Wee

review_text: One of the best prata I had for breakfast! The curry was just perfectly delicious and the prata was right on point! The prata guy was very friendly and polite! Give it a try and you know! Recommended!  👍
author: james petez

review_text: Crispy prata very shiok 🤤 Super crispy, not oily at all. Ordered tissue prata for the kids and they whacked it like nobody’s business 😂 Really solid hawker prata — confirm will come back again.
author: Wilson Tan

review_text: The prata is super crispy and light. Curry is made daily
author: Han Khoon Tay

review_text:
Very decent prata and curry !

Awesome friendly chap mending the stall .

Pleasant eating here

Recommended
author: Spyder

review_text:
Ordered 1 curry puff and 1 chicken curry puff while waiting for my breakfast set.

Cuff puff inside has 1 small part of egg, curry fragrance and nice crisp curry puff. The same for the chicken curry puff, come with a small cut of egg. Curry puff and moist and yet crisp.

Frankly, I don't really tasted chicken, probably it's well minced?

Anyway, it's nice lah. Definitely nicer than the sudden sprouting of curry puff outlets in all over SG.

Later then I noticed got MakanSutra2025 recommendation.
author: Terence Tan

review_text:
The chicken curry puff was hot, crispy and a bit flaky off the shelf. It didn't felt oily at all.

Spiciness was on point - enough to know it's there, not so much that you'll need a drink. While there was definitely bits of chicken in there, the puff was overall on the smaller side. Its size is closer to that of those street side sardine puffs that used to be sold at $1 for 3 pieces.

Not sure how the owner can better balance price and portion, but the curry puff wasn't as satisfying because of the size.
author: Levin

review_text: Good and tasty curry puffs. The pastry shell is crispy and not oily. I had the potato curry puffs. The size is quite small but is packed inside. The filling is spicy but the curry taste is quite subtle.
author: Gooose

review_text:
Puny curry puffs for $1.60 ( chicken) $1.30 (potato)

I guess inflation is real.

I finished mine in 2 bites literally.

Wouldn't come back again but I would recommend the ministers of Singapore to give it a try to understand inflation.
author: J. W

review_text:
Finally got to try this elusive curry puff that’s always sold out.

I got the potato version ($1.20) and it even has some egg inside. The filling is quite spicy but honestly not outstanding. Outside is flaky and crispy.

Good value for what it is and perfect for a tea time snack!
author: Max S.

review_text:
My 1st ever food poisoning experience from this stall.. went down on 18/9 for lunch about 3pm++ as I was just nearby for a quick dine. Ordered 1 roast chicken rice and black bean chicken feet soup. On the same day about 11pm, I felt like vomiting and tummy uncomfortable! Couldn’t sleep all the way due to stomach cramps and vomiting & diarrhoea till the next day morning… (P.S. this was my only last meal that day, I have no appetite for dinner)

eat at your own risk…
author: Kelvin Lim

review_text: $6 chicken rice with additional roast meat. Honestly this is pretty much run of the mill chicken rice. I got breast meat and it was dry and tough. Nothing special and quite pricey. Chilli has a good kick and will recommend to take some to go along with your chicken rice.
author: Max S.

review_text: Taste cam be subjective I'll admit...but I kinda like the chicken rice here  I especially like the eggs （卤蛋）。it's got a nice sweet and herbal taste. This stall has some pretty decent soups too. They go well with the chicken rice for a simple happy lunch in breezy sembawang hills.
author: kevin Luke

review_text: We came here a few months ago.The old man shortchanged us, hence 2 plates of chicken rice cost 8 dollars instead of 7 dollars. Rice was carelessly thrown on plate. Soup swimming in oil. Basically you will be drinking oil instead of soup.
author: Rustic Leaves

review_text: Great chilli, great rice, very tender roasted chicken. And it’s only $3.50. Stall owner is elderly, be nice and patient.
author: CC

review_text: This is a store run by a elderly uncle, which seems passionate about his food. The taste is of the more traditional prawn mee, it's sweet and has not much taste of the prawns. Noodles is of the old style which consist of tomato sauce and not much other flavours. Prawn is of medium size with a few pieces of fish cake and thin pork. The dish is more for the elderly which prefers a light tasting bowl of soup.
author: EQ Xavier

review_text: This place sells unique prawn noodles with clam for $4.00. If you prefer your prawn noodles to be just that, they also have regular prawn noodles at $3.00 only. The prawn broth is different from others. It was very clear and refreshing, with distinct pure prawny taste. Unlike others which they served with pork ribs. Ming Ji prawn noodles served with lean pork, fish cakes, de-shelled prawns and of course, clams. Topped with pork lard, fried onions and chilli, mixed them well, and you will get a bowl of flavourful prawn noodles.
author: Stanley

review_text:
Decently priced prawn noodle in this hawker centre.

The noodles were slightly under seasoned. The prawns were fresh, lean pork was tender and thick fish cake blanched before serving.

Soup was insipid for me which is the soul of this dish.

Not compelling.
author: MNG

review_text:
Not sure why other people rate only 3 for this old school prawn mee. Frankly I am not a fan of prawn mee. But since I am here almost every other week, I decided to try. I ordered dry prawn mee. Even for my husband who do not like seafood, find the prawn soup comforting and I finish it all. The dry mee is really old school with a tinge of tomato sauce. It is sticky and favourful. I like it! The prawns are peeled too! The prawns are also fresh (not frozen kind) though cut in half. $4 is small in serving but sufficient for ladies. Come on la.. prawn is ex leh and the soup definitely took a lot of hard work. I will definitely eat it again.

Sorry no photos because I ate with low expectation and realise it was good.. then i finish in 5mins.
author: Li Yuan

review_text:
Very friendly uncle, very affordable too but honestly the portion is really too small.
Overall a decent bowl of prawn mee but I will not go out of my way for it.
author: Cedric Seet

review_text:
Never know there is this gem food in the part of Singapore. If you think having chwee kuay from those chain store is good.....wait until you try this. The major difference is in the texture of the kuay which gives you more flavour and texture.
4 price $2.20
author: c k

review_text: Can here to try the chwee kueh after seeing some good reviews. But was disappointed at the taste.
author: Andrew Chong

review_text: This is one of the worst chwee kueh I ever eaten.
author: Tyler Lai

review_text: Very nice Chwee Kueh. Tasty, yet not too oily.
author: Nicholas Foo

review_text: Great coffee and service by a very friendly lady boss. Cool and casual settings. Feel very relaxed
author: Francis Chan

review_text: There are some many stalls selling drinks. This Keng Lee has even till now the best aromatic tradition coffee and tea.
author: Li Na

review_text: Best Tea and Tea-C in the area.
author: ming_dude

review_text:
To call this Katong Laksa is so offensive.
The quality of laksa is so bad it’s actually laughable.

I’m hardly one to post negative reviews, but I think the public needs to be warned.

Their fish soup seems wildly popular though, will definitely be back to try
author: Raynard Lim

review_text:
The shop faces the public park, not the car park.

The light, flavourful soup gives this Katong Laksa a refreshing feeling. Still as filling as other Laksa but it is not as heavy on the stomach as others.

This is much better than 328 Katong Laksa and with long opening hours if you ever pass by this food centre. Do give this Laksa a try

Fried Fish soup comes with generous thick portions of fish.

20cent extra for takeaway.

Update July 2024: They have managed to improve their Laksa recipe. Still served with fresh prawns, a must try.
author: Nope Thanks

review_text:
Long waiting time during lunch, it seems their fish soup is more popular than laksa, will have to try it next time.

Laksa not oily, more healthier version compared to other laksas, thick beehoon is cut nicely so easy to slurp with spoon.

Edit : came for their fish soup and gave 5 stars instead,  fish soup is much better than their laksa. Must try. Heavy seafood taste with lots of fish slices and homemade chilli 👍
author: Kyp Teh

review_text: Khoon's Katong Laksa, not too bad. Laksa gravy was of the lighter version, not too spicy, sweet and moderately creamy. The thick beehoon was cut into smaller pieces, easy to scoop with a spoon. It's a good choice for those who can't really take spicy. Must try.
author: Stanley

review_text:
Came here on a Saturday morning around 10:30am and the hawker centre was already crowded. But enough to find seats.

Tried this stall's food before and here I am again because it feels very homey 🏡 the lady boss is super friendly and sweet as well, coming to full circle with the mom home cook meal experience hehe 🤱
