I ate the Fried Fosh Bee Hoon Soup with Milk ($5) and I love that the fried fish is separated from the soup to remain it's crisp. Fish is lightly marinated and has a savory flavour.

The amount of soup given is a lot which I love as I would always finish to the last drop. Savory and sweet broth extracted from fish bones, and the milky aroma really makes the entire dish feels warm and wholesome.

I love that they added their own twist of adding seaweed inside, which really boosts the seafood aroma. And the fermented salted beans in their tangy chilli sauce. 🌶 it whets your appetite and leaves you craving for more.
author: Yi Ling

review_text: Sorry to say. The rice is little for my liking and not very nice to eat. The meat got some small sharp bones hidden inside, please be careful when chewing it. The $4 meal got many bones, the $5 set got more meat but still got hidden small bones inside, need to improve on the chopping skill. Soup tasted a bit sour and bland, no greens in it. Owners were friendly though, still got room for improvements:)
author: R G

review_text:
Finally tried Seng Huat Duck Rice at Sembawang Hills and I get why people queue. Portions are really generous for the price, and the duck was tender and super flavourful. Very comforting, very satisfying kind of meal.

We waited around 20 minutes but it was still worth it, would definitely come back again when the craving hits.
author: life of daph

review_text:
After finishing my noodles I still have some spare rooms inside my stomach so I queued up for this. Long queue and I waited for about 20 minutes. (Usually I don’t queue for food). First time trying this.
Many people said this is one of the best duck rice. Well, I ordered a set for myself at $5 that came with a plate of duck meat which consist of a whole thigh, a small bowl of soup and rice. Price wise, value for money.
Taste, the soup was very light with a hint of herbal ingredients. The duck meat was tender and no fowl (foul) smell. No pun intended.
But there was no ‘Umami’ kick to it. The ‘lor’ or gravy was light.
One time for me is enough. I just do not understand why the long queue.
author: EatSleepChyll L

review_text:
Wanted wings, Owner say open at 10am. Was there 10am to ask again. Owner say sold out. Apparently they will serve n pack to regulars 1st before common ppl. Abit distasteful to experience.
I guess if u r regular it be a great place otherwise u might find experience abit pill to swallow esp early in morning.
Owner n wife attitude can be better n more polite as it still a customer service industry.
author: Jerry Lee

review_text: Really good duck rice with generous portion! Meat is very tender and the skin is really nice. The duck is really affordable and the stall owners are reallly friendly too. Do note that their ducks do get sold out fast so come before 12pm.
author: TSY

restaurant_name: San Ba wang Guo zhi Shu Shi
review_text: One thing you'll notice about this stall's braised sauce is fragrant but not too salty. The kway is bland, which is good in a sense as it balance out the saltiness of the braised meats. This stall's business is so good that on weekends, they typically sold out by noon.
author: Yeou Wei Chua

restaurant_name: San Ba wang Guo zhi Shu Shi
review_text:
Really love the Kuah Chap here! Had this over the weekend and it still tastes as good as ever. I always get my standard order from the uncle. Lean meat, with salty veg, egg and large intestines.

What I like here the most is not just the great good but the excellent customer service by the Uncle and Aunty at the shop. Bought them drinks the other time - they really work so hard to get this lovely dish on the table. Kudos to hawkers! :)
author: Julian Foo

restaurant_name: San Ba wang Guo zhi Shu Shi
review_text: I find it average. The braised sauce and the kway does not stand out. The good thing is that they have variety and the braised pork is tender.
author: Wang Teck Heng

restaurant_name: San Ba wang Guo zhi Shu Shi
review_text:
Love this hwaker centre for breakfast. Especially this Kway Chap which is always very crowded, do come early at about 7am so do not have to wait for long.

Still one of the cheapest and nice food around.
author: Desmond Wong

restaurant_name: San Ba wang Guo zhi Shu Shi
review_text: 30 minutes wait on a weekend morning. Not bad yet not outstanding. Innards were well cleaned. Braised sauce was not fragrant.
author: Jia Lin G

review_text:
15/September/2025
Had Mutton Briyani ($7.50) for lunch, was good. Slightly sweet for my palate, taste was good, portion served was adequate. I'll be back to try their chicken briyani on my next visit.
author: T greensake

review_text: Tried as saw someone bought and looks very tempting. The sauce and the rice is really nice. However the meat is very tough. Asked for tender meat and was told they are the same, hope they would tenderise the meat more so i would still try again. $7.50 a plate.
author: Doreen Koh

review_text:
We bought chicken and mutton briyani. No expectations but surprisingly it was good. Fuss free with just acar at the side, this briyani needs no dalcha. It was finger licking good. The mutton especially is sook tender.
Only issue is the area. Quite secluded in the Upper Thomson with Limited parking.
author: Sham “Shamie”

review_text: Simply loved the mutton briyani. I liked the thick savoury gravy and the fact the meat is still on the bone with bonus tulang on inside it. Comes with a small side of achar that's freshly prepared. Nice balance to the heavy dish.
author: Seng Leong Koh

review_text: Really exceptional briyani. rice was buttery and chicken was cooked well with a good portion, what stood out was the sauce and curry - thick, flavourful and just perfect. Probably one of my best briyani experience.
author: Donavan Lum

review_text:
EmceeRichardStyle Mic Rating:
"The One and Only Late Night Fresh Juice Bar & Fruits Platter in Singapore!
author: EmceeRichardStyle

review_text: Pure fruits juice available late in the evening.
author: Danny Choo

review_text: Fresh fruits :)
author: N N

restaurant_name: #01-11 Economic Bee Hoon 經濟米粉.椰漿飯.囉惹
review_text: Bee hoon is fantastic and has quite a variety of options to choose from. Always get the cabbage, fried egg, and the meat balls/ another veg!
author: Dean Tan

restaurant_name: #01-11 Economic Bee Hoon 經濟米粉.椰漿飯.囉惹
review_text:
Updated . Just purely Beehoon not bad . Food ingredients very normal . Service ok .
__
Go so many times . NEVER ONCE OPEN
author: chocolatto COCO

restaurant_name: #01-11 Economic Bee Hoon 經濟米粉.椰漿飯.囉惹
review_text: Have been buying from the shop for years and even after covid it is still there. Cheap and good fruit juice and fruits.
author: Bosen Teh

restaurant_name: #01-11 Economic Bee Hoon 經濟米粉.椰漿飯.囉惹
review_text: average bee hoon with a short queue. they cook the bee hoon in bulk, then keep it in a steamer - and take out small portions. so it's nice, hot and soft when they serve it to you. ingredients are super oily...
author: Dom Wee

restaurant_name: #01-11 Economic Bee Hoon 經濟米粉.椰漿飯.囉惹
review_text: Place serves very nice economic beehoon - business is brisk and the stall constantly fries its beehoon/mee so its always freshly fried. Eggs are often served hot too as they constantly fry to keep up with demand. Otah is nice, freshly grilled (as opposed to just off the shelf) with discernable fish chunks - a nice touch by the stall owner is they will remove the otah leaf so its convinent to eat when serving you. 2 thumbs up!
author: Alvin T

restaurant_name: Jia Jia Xing Pigs Organ Soup
review_text:
One of the best Pig organ soups in SG. Substantial portion of meats was given just like 20 years back. Price slightly increased despite recent years inflation ..So comforting to have this on a rainy day. ....

Aunty is the sole person managing n cooking. She's getting old and might retired soon. Please treasure it while we can before it becomes part of our memories
author: Nicholas Tan

restaurant_name: Jia Jia Xing Pigs Organ Soup
review_text:
A delicious bowl of black vinegar pork trotter 😋.

There are $7 and $9 portions.  I had the $9.

I remember it was more flavourful previously but that was like a few years ago.

Acquired taste.  Come and support if you are into black vinegar pork trotter 👍
author: Teck Chong Law

restaurant_name: Jia Jia Xing Pigs Organ Soup
review_text: The richness of the organ soup and the generous ingredients justify the cost of this bowl of delicious meal. The quantity was decent. However the taste of the yam rice was not as rich in the flavour. Could be better to make it a perfect meal. Total cost $7.
author: FRan

restaurant_name: Jia Jia Xing Pigs Organ Soup
review_text:
Driving past this Food center, after walking one round decided on trying this store selling Pig’s organ soup.    I ordered pig stomach soup with liver and yam rice.

Service from this old lady is really friendly and giving me extra rice and joking with me.   That’s how business is done ya? The queue is pretty consistent, probably old customers.

Environment is very stiffy and hot, it’s a super hot weather so no choice, eating soupy stuffs and you will start sweating non stop.

Food is not bad I would say.    Soup is savory, salty, tasteful from the salted vegetables.   The stomach and liver is over cooked.   This is the only not good which is the main thing.  It’s nice to try, but won’t go for this store again though.   If they do the stomach and liver cooked nicely, it will be perfect.
author: Tham Willie

restaurant_name: Jia Jia Xing Pigs Organ Soup
review_text:
Chanced upon the pig organ soup at Sembawang Hills Food Centre and it honestly exceeded my expectations. The soup was rich, flavourful, and comforting — not overly salty or oily, just a really well-balanced broth. The ingredients were fresh and well-prepared, especially the pig stomach — clean, tender, and tasty.

What made the experience even better was the lovely aunty running the stall. She was incredibly warm and friendly. Highly recommend if you’re in the area!
author: Zhi Xin A

restaurant_name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
review_text: I used to like this stall a lot. Have not had the food for quite a while and unfortunately I feel that the standards had declined by quite a bit. The prawn crackers were over fried and hard. The sausage was just gelatin and very little meat. Ngoh hiang had little taste. Only the chili was still good. Really do hope they can recover their original taste.
author: Gooose

restaurant_name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
review_text:
Loved the ngo hiang here! Initially got one portion, but we ordered a second portion cause it was so good.
Beehoon is nicely flavoured and warm (not too overpowering)
I love the prawn crackers!! It’s not too hard (or thick) like some of the others I’ve tried, very addictive. Chilli is really good too. Wiped the chilli clean. 😋
I feel that it’s worth the price and don’t think it’s too expensive. Ngo Hiang anywhere is all around the same price. Plus!! They write the prices for all the ingredients clearly on top. You can already count on your own how much it is and not be shocked when it’s time to pay. :-)
author: saltedbun

restaurant_name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
review_text: Friendly stall owners. Traditional Wu Xiang taste. All nice. I got 4 items with bee hoon at $6.90. Will try other items next time. E-pay available.
author: CC

restaurant_name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
review_text: Had this for dinner with an old friend.  Long time have not been here.  Place is very quiet in the night.  Ordered at least 10 items.  The noodles supposed to be 3 plates but requested them to make into 2 plates of 3 plates portion.  Total bill comes to $29.50 for these.  Managed to finished it.  Unfortunately, they do not provide ginger for century egg, but use a kind of “salad mix” to eat with it.  Not to my liking for this combination.
author: Jay Jay

restaurant_name: Sin Sin Ngo Hiang Prawn Cracker
review_text:
5 Spice Roll / Wu Xiang Xia Bing (SGD $13) @ Sin Sin Ngor Hiang Prawn Cracker.
.
Am a fan of this stall at Sembawang Hills, which has been serving the dish for over 40 years.
.
Yes, they can be slightly more pricey than elsewhere, but the range of ingredients available is nearly unrivalled, with many unique handmade items, including yam rolls, prawn cakes, and more. Better still, it's served non-greasy.
.
The visually intriguing squiggle-shaped battered dough fritters are crunchy with sweet grainy savoury flavour, while the fried tofu puffs stuffed with fish cake retain a moist texture and sweet salty savoury flavour.
.
Like that they serve with juicy cucumber, whose vegetal sweet flavour refreshes the palate. Love the spicy sweet savoury kick of the chili, and the simple but well executed fried bee hoon / vermicelli noodles.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text:
Ordered:
Refer to the attached video for my order. Paid a total of $16.

I'm not usually a fan of mixed vegetable rice, but this vintage Chinese mixed vegetable rice stall, managed by seniors, caught my attention. They offer two kinds of chili, both of which complemented the food, price is reasonable as well.
author: Lionel

review_text: Old school Chinese mix vegetable rice, the main cook is an old lady, which brings out the flavor of your grandparents. The dishes are very simple and homely. There is a bowl of braised beancurb, egg and meat sitting at the front of the store, which I think it's a decent additional to the meal. Price is steep compare to other places despite the quality of the food. There is not much queue, thus it's good if u want something quick to fill your tummy.
author: EQ Xavier

review_text: Their mix rice is decent and affordable price(1 meat +2vege for $3.50). Overall 7.5/10
author: Sam Wong

review_text: Old Lady Overcharged Everyone! Food tasteless and does not look clean! Never eat from this DISHONEST stall again!!
author: User

review_text: this pathetic portion for 5bucks? i even had to ask twice as i thought my hearing was failing me this morning
author: avastia

restaurant_name: Five Star • Teo Chew Kway Chap
review_text:
Probably the best kway chap we have eaten! What stood out for me was the kway broth- cooked with fried diced garlic- so so fragrant and delicious. Hubby loves the chili sauce- thick and flavorful. Uncle is generous with his servings too.

Uncle operates daily until 2pm and rests on Wednesdays.

P.s: the sugar cane stall 2units away doesn't have surcharge for sour plum when you order their sugar cane drink too.
author: Momo

restaurant_name: Five Star • Teo Chew Kway Chap
review_text: One of the best Kway Chap around, hidden gem. Pork belly, intestines were well cleaned and braised, herbal flavoured with a sweet aftertaste and no 'porky' smell. Very tasty. Recommended to give it a try.
author: Stanley

restaurant_name: Five Star • Teo Chew Kway Chap
review_text:
One of the best Kway Chap I had in Spore.  The 淉 was a surprise, the soup was herbal based.  So tasty, shld ordered extra bowl.  Plate of mixed meats was generous in portion for a $5 set.
The food centre was very airy and clean.
author: Jaws Lee

restaurant_name: Five Star • Teo Chew Kway Chap
review_text: Friendly kway chap uncle.  Authentic taste and generous portions.  Very reasonable price too.  1st time eating here.  Will be back!
author: Boon Leng Koh

restaurant_name: Five Star • Teo Chew Kway Chap
review_text: This place is actually old school delicious.  It taste homemade by someone whose been doing this his whole life and thats because it is.  No fuss, no glamour, just honest and delicious which is really rare to find these days in a sea of generic tasting food in "modern day" settings.  More people should come here if youre looking for good kway chap.
author: DXH (Ghibli)

review_text:
Had the fuzhou fishball noodles. It was great!

Noodles: firm with a nice bite
Sauce: leaning more towards the vinegar side. If you dont like vinegar, would be good to ask for less
Chilli: As a chilli lover, it was tasty with a little bit of kick
Fuzhou fishballs: Soft yet springy and bursting with juices
Overall: Everything blended well with the different flavours from each bite.

For $3.50, this is a such a bargain for the quality you get. Glad i stumbled upon this hidden gem.

Do note that they open only from 6am to 2pm
Enjoy!
author: Matt Leo

review_text:
Surprise surprise…the noodle is quite tasty actually. Compared to the other Fishball stall at the back, there is no queue here on a Saturday brunch time. And I thought to myself maybe it is not as good as the other stall.
I was wrong. It is good. Though the portion is not big but it is sufficient for me. The soup taste good too. If you hunger for more, add ingredients. Otherwise this decent size portion noodle will keep you full but not too full.
author: EatSleepChyll L

review_text: Very good decent bowl of fish ball dry mee pok. The vinegar and Chilli blends well with 2 fishballs, 1 meat ball and some fish cakes. A bowl cost only $4 which hardly can find anywhere in a hawker centre. Well done stall owner for bringing the price affordable.
author: FRan

review_text:
This stall serves nice decent bowl of noodles.
Nice noodles texture. Ingredients are fresh. Chilli sauce and vinegar proportion well balanced.
Reasonable pricing.
Worth eating.
author: Terence Lee

review_text:
The sauce mixture is very nice. Come support

Boss also very friendly
author: Xavier Ang

review_text: it's a one-woman show here and yet the service was decently efficient :) ordered no.3 - their signature soup + noodles for $5. soup was bussin! super umami and rich in flavour, and it came with so much ingredients - from fishballs to pork slices & minced meat. noodles were AMAZING - it was coated in their special sauce that really elevated the flavour profile of this entire dish. the chilli had a bit of kick, really enjoyable. portion size is just right. really well-priced and yummy, would be back for this! ❤️
author: Joy Ong

review_text: Ingredients are fresh. Probably the chilli mix not to my liking that's all. The portion and price is reasonable. $4 a bowl.
author: C Lim

review_text: Finished the noodles forgot to take a pic first.  What a waste.  Will come back to add pic next round.  Wonder stall holder.  Who cook from fresh ingredients. Fresh meats, fresh fish balls.  Can taste the shrimps in the chilli and tasty 'pig oil'.  Why only 4 stars?  I give it 5 starts especially it's only $4/-.
author: Chye Tan

review_text: Was at the hawker center around 7am on a Sunday morning. Place was half filled so fairly easy to find seats. There was no queue at this stall, which is located near washroom with water cooler. The stall was managed by a friendly and food was served promptly upon orderly. I ordered #2 which was quite tasty.
author: Brandon Wong

review_text: The soup is tasty with generous ingredients. The noodles are cooked well with balance of sauces.  Will definately come back again.
author: Choon Hui Lim

review_text: One of the better pork satay that you can find. Crispy at the right places yet meat is tender at the same time.
author: Low Roy

review_text:
Visited several times as we love the laksa from Khoon’s and will buy the satay if it’s opened.
The satay is succulent and fatty, so delicious. I actually dun like satay sauce but this stall’s peanut gravy/sauce is very different. So yummy and savoury!
author: Priscilla

review_text:
My husband and I had our lunch somewhere around this area and had to dabao for my mother in law's lunch so we stumbled upon this satay stall. I dont know why this somehow attracted me on a HOT SUNNY day! I just couldnt resist and insisted my husband to dabao it since we just finished our lunch [to be honest: i rarely request to dabao satay]

We ordered their chicken and pork satay, and I have to say that their satay sauce is the real stuff man!! Not a single drip left!

We'll definitely be back again!!! Yums!
author: Joanne Chan

review_text: Satay was quite delicious, we had the lamb chicken and pork satay. The pork satay really stood out, very crispy on the outside but flavourful on the inside.
author: derek neo

review_text: Very nice juicy satay. The sauce is very fragrant n well done.
author: SK Ho

review_text: Solid roast duck! Highly recommanded to try. Way better then those chain store even all claim they roast with charcoal but this store really can taste the tenderness of the duck and crispy smoked skin.
author: Kian Hong Lim

review_text: Best, if not one of the best Cantonese roast in Singapore. Easily beat many of those popular chain restaurants in terms of food quality.
author: Jane F

review_text: Reasonable priced roast meats- $5 for roast duck and pork. Good portion but I would say above average in terms of taste.
author: Max S.

review_text: Would say the char siew is good but the hawker himself is arrogant and rude. Asked nicely if got paynow or paylah and he just shoo me away. Very rude. I would be eating char siew elsewhere.
author: james petez

review_text: No pic. Roasted duck is juicy and tender. Lack a little 5spice. One man show. So don’t expect service & he can be snob sometimes .  $4 portion is good.
author: Leen Lee

review_text:
Tried the wanton noodles here and was pleasantly surprised by how good they were. The noodles were springy with a nice bite, tossed in a well-balanced sauce that wasn’t too oily or salty. The char siew was decent, slightly on the leaner side but still flavourful.

The highlight for me was the fried wantons and meatballs – crispy, piping hot, and paired well with the tangy chili sauce. The soup wantons were also plump and satisfying. Portions are generous for the price, and you can also add on items like prawns or extra dumplings if you’re feeling hungry.

Overall, a solid stall if you’re craving a comforting plate of wanton mee. Worth a try if you’re in the area.
author: Jeffrey

review_text:
Jan 2025. Discovered a nice wanton noodle here. The chilli was good and the char siew was tender. What struck me was the wanton soup, not many would be concerned with that, but it brought back memories of traditional, old school flavour. The wantons were decent albeit a bit small in size.
The breakfast made my day after i believed i fell into a speed trap on the 3rd day of CNY.
author: L.G. Wee

review_text:
This review is only for their Laksa. Refreshing Laksa taste that’s on the sweeter side. Robust flavor and yet a creamy flavor.

Crunchy prawns that has been soaked in baking soda, I like!

Cockles size just nice for me, not too small nor big. A spoonful of thick bee hoon, Laksa soup, few of them and taste the complexity coming together in my mouth bursting out.
author: Ojisan “Hiroshi”

review_text: Tried the shabu shabu laksa, generous serving of premium shabu shabu, goes well with the sweet and tangy laksa gravy, $5/$7 options
author: Derrick L

review_text:
Great smile & delicious wanton noodle.
Only imperfection is lack of pork lard
author: Longjon Lee

review_text: Good traditional Kaya toast with soft boiled eggs.
author: Stanley

review_text: Excellent value especially for the quality. $3.80 for a set with an iced drink. Soft boiled eggs were surprisingly very good. Owners were friendly as well. Well worth a visit for tea or breakfast.
author: Dominic Neo

review_text: A friendly person makes coffee and tea early in the morning. Tried the ice teh with milk and sugar, only cost $1.40, it's of good flavor and washed away the oily aftertaste of the food. There is a queue shortly due to the crowd. They also sell some bread and small items for those who want a grab and go. A good experience with many returns. Parking is quite a challenge so remember to come early for the food
author: EQ Xavier

review_text: Nice Kopi O kosong, it was gao. One of the eggs a little overcooked. Bread was crispy with nice kaya & butter. Generally a nice breakfast set at $3.50.
author: Lim Kopi

review_text: Kaya and butter bun was really nice. Soft and lightly toasted bun, with melted flowing butter and kaya, paired nicely with a cup of teh C kosong. Nice.
author: J Seng

review_text: Friendly and buff uncle serving delicious moist carrot cake with loads of garlic! Super affordable and does not get jelak as you eat through the dish! One of my favourite of this type of carrot cake as I’m not too big a fan of the dry kind.
author: Gabriel Lim

review_text: Friendly uncle who fries one plate at a time, so the waiting time is long despite a short queue. I ordered both the black and white versions, each fried in the traditional old-school style. The white version was quite bland, while the black was saved by its savory dark sauce. Overall, not quite the quality I had hoped for.
author: LP Pua

review_text:
Each plate is made to order with a lot of garlic. Can taste the garlic and wok hey very and healthier than other lard styles. What makes my day is the friendly hawker that greats you with heart warmth friendliness. A feel good order that is worth your support.
$4
author: c k

review_text: Manned by a friendly uncle, this no name stall - Fried Carrot Cake has been here for over 30 years. His carrot cake is really the traditional, old school type which is very different from those sold elsewhere. His carrot cake were all handmade. The black fried carrot cake had an eggy texture, soft with a sweet aftertaste. Do remember to ask the uncle to add some chilli as the chilli here, packed a punch too.
author: Stanley

review_text:
My mum like his fried carrot cake.
We have been eating for years.
His fired carrot cake is done in simple no frill fashion.  The cakes are soft , with ample eggs fried , taste is just good not too salty.
We prefer the plain white over black sauce sweet type.
author: BEN LEE

review_text:
Been awhile since I've eaten this and was pleasantly surprised that there's now a young chap helping out at the stall. Good job for helping inject youth into our hawker heritage

This is a no frills fishball noodles, the classic taste that is no longer common these days, tangy and slightly spicy with a hint of lard. The thickly sliced pork liver is expertly cooked, perfect texture and doneness. Auntie taking order is nice and attentive.

Queue can take awhile to clear, but good food is worth waiting for I guess
author: Rei Axl Ye

review_text:
old style traditional minced meat noodles with a super long queue, done to good taste - meat and balls nicely cooked and liver done just right !!
Quickly understood that the long queue is not due to high demand but the slow works that creates the good taste by the cooks !! So sad that many walked away due to the queue and missed the good tradition taste !!
And lastly , the order taking auntie has no smile at all 😔. Would have been a more comfortable queue time if she can put on a smile 😊
author: Abraham-Hannah-Rachel Tang

review_text: Had the FBN MK soup $4. Clear soup, not oily. FBs taste fresh and not fishy, mee is nicely done. Saw on the reviews that the liver is nice. Missed that. Will have to come back for that one. Will come again.
author: jajaish

review_text: Good fishball noodle. Live the noodle texture. Do order the pork liver. Tender and soft. Friendly bosses.
author: Andy Lee

review_text:
Ordered two bowls of dry noodles with pork liver, one with extra liver, for a total of $10.

Saw the queue and decided to try. The pork liver was perfectly cooked—five stars for that fish balls were nice too! But the noodles were pretty average.
author: Lionel

review_text: The food is delicious and Indonesian flavourful. I have tried all their items on menu and they certainly didn't disappoint. Very recommended if you are looking for Indonesian vegetarian food.
author: Desmond Tan

review_text:
Nice Indonesian vegetarian at affordable price! We like the mee rebus and vege fritters. Mee Soto for something light and fresh 😋

Toilet considered clean for hawker center standard.
author: Karen Teo

review_text: The nasi tumpeng tastes as good as it looks 💛 All the components are well prepared and come together nicely. It’s rare to find Indonesian vegetarian (allium-free) food, so this was a really nice discovery! On a side note, I’m not sure if it’s because it was a weekday, but this was the cleanest hawker centre I’ve visited. Highly recommended, and I look forward to coming back! 👍🏼
author: Xuan Xin

review_text: A newly found gem! The food has a truly authentic taste that is hard to find. The lady owner came from Indonesia. Very friendly folks. Definitely will be back. Come and enjoy it yourself.
author: Hendrix Tanoto

review_text:
Tasty foods @ reasonable price 😋😋😋
Difficult to find parking lots though..
Best to take public transport here.
author: Alice

review_text:
$5 Per plate for me one person was good enough.
This plate comes with two prawns.
I think it is worth the money, but it would be better if this plate of noodles was served in a more hotter state (although it was right out from the wok when I ordered)
author: Lui Taye

review_text: Dry version of Fried Hokkien Prawn Mee. Noodles were had mild wok hei taste. Prawns were fresh, pork belly was soft and tender enough. Sambal chilli had a slight sweet taste and was able to blend well with the noodles. And lots of fresh crispy pork lard was given. Not too bad overall, but I just felt that they could do it even better.
author: Stanley

review_text: Personally prefer the wetter version, and this satisfies that craving completely. The chilli isn’t the best, and for a Medium ($6) the portion size seemed more like a small. There’s a lack of wok hey and the prawns are on the smaller side but I don’t hate it, seeing how I’ve tasted worse from other “popular” stores. At 4pm on a Saturday afternoon, the hawker was empty so there was almost no wait time.
author: Crystal

review_text: Decided to finally try this Hokkien mee ($5) after seeing quite a few people buy from this stall. However, it was quite disappointing to be honest. Overall, the flavours didn’t quite come through. I felt like I was eating a plate of plain noodles with some chilli sauce. There were 3 small prawns and some pork belly but other than that a generous amount of noodles. Chilli sauce was towards the sweeter side but without it, this Hokkien mee could have been 1 star..
author: Max S.

review_text:
The original at Changi Village is somehow still better. The wok hei seemed to have dialled down a notch here. Nonetheless, still a delicious option for HKM lovers here in Sembawang Hill Food Centre.

For more details visit 2bearbear today!
author: 2bearbear Tom Lim

review_text: Not my type of chwee kway. Chai po not oily and fragrant enough and the chili is not fragrant. They are stingy on the chili.
author: EatSleepChyll L

review_text:
Nice chwee kway. Texture is good, their chai poh is just nice not too salty and not too oily.
Friendly stall owner.
Worth eating.
author: Terence Lee

review_text: Love the chwee Kueh. The chai Poh is not as oily. Love the rice flavor in every bite. (Not all chwee Kueh has the nice rice flavor in it.) Happen to try the Yam cake too, if you like the yam bits in the yam cake, this have the real yam bits and almost every bite you bite into the filling of mushroom too. The taste is just nice for me to have it bare without any sauce.
author: Epricorn

review_text: Chwee Kueh 水粿 , a traditional Teochew steamed rice cake dish served mainly for breakfast. This stall sells piping hot chwee kueh, topped with fragrant chai poh. Their chwee kueh is very soft in nature. Chai poh is less salty and less oily compared to some others. Their homemade chilli is really very good and you can taste dried shrimp flavour in it. Really satisfying good.
author: Stanley

review_text: Good chai poh that makes this soft creamy chwee kway yummy 50c each
author: Dom Wee

restaurant_name: 你的最愛米粉 THE BEE HOON LIKE
review_text: Had Ban Mian and Red Wine Chicken Mee Sua for lunch. Nicely served with soft boiled egg. Perfect comfort food. Owner Mr Li was very friendly too.
author: Bock Eng Chua

restaurant_name: 你的最愛米粉 THE BEE HOON LIKE
review_text: 5 chicken and 5 pork satay. Not bad, abit sweet.
author: CC

review_text:
Overall, to me, it’s slightly above average and overrated by social media.
Not worth making a return visit.
So far, Chef Lu at Golden Mile Food Centre is still the best.
I’ll try 88 Roasted, roast paradise & etc, for comparison soon.
author: Ben MA

review_text:
Decided to join the queue since it was long and thought it must be good. Waited about 35minutes for my turn. The lady boss was a bit hostile and told me to hurry up with payment when I asked her to repeat the amount. When I mentioned using CDC vouchers, she sighed like I was causing trouble. Like hello if she’s unhappy about using cdc then she should remove the sign from the store front.

Honestly, all she was doing was scooping rice and collecting money—so I don’t see why there was such a rush when the queue was already moving slowly. Food-wise, nothing much to rave about. For the wait and the attitude, I wouldn’t queue again.
author: Angela Hoi

review_text:
Queue was pretty long. Not really moving. But I assure you the food is pretty good. The sambal is good quality. Had the taste of childhood. Spicy, with a hint of dried shrimp taste.

The stall owners may not be the friendliest. But I think that's not how I gauge my food.

I had the Char Siew Siu Yok rice ($4.50). Add Braised taukwa ($0.80).

Siu Yok is crispy too.
author: ʍɾɴ

review_text: The food is delicious, the roast duck is juicy and moist, and has a rich meaty taste. The char siew is roasted as to a nice charred, not very sweet but good enough to be savoury. The archar is a highlight, very crunchy and sour to add to the taste. The owner can remember all the order which is very amazing. However the queue cutting is a problem as they let the regular jump in the order. Soup is also a nice touch to the meal
author: EQ Xavier

review_text:
The roast pork n duck drum are good n will give a rating of 7.5 out of 10.  Ah char was free n generous portion.

Char siew is bad and like those used at WTM stalls n I rate this as 4 out of 10.  Review from others were misleading although individual taste

Q is chaotic but lady operators were friendly n remind to take cutlery.   Overall, 6 for this visit.  May come back for roast pork n duck drum.
author: David Wong

restaurant_name: Kow Loon Hong Kong Dim Sum
review_text: siew mai use fresh pork ingredient & very Q. fried crispy beancurd has fresh prawn. i always order these 2 dish. number 1 & 21. pork porridge also taste good. all dim sum are hand-made. they open every day from as early as 7am to 4pm. come support these old couple who now run the stall with their burmese assistant.
author: Hans

restaurant_name: Kow Loon Hong Kong Dim Sum
review_text: really good place for people to bond over chinese food and dim sum like food. this place is really wheelchair accessible and not only that, there are even noodles and traditional toast shops nearby. this place is really good
author: john doo

restaurant_name: Kow Loon Hong Kong Dim Sum
review_text:
If you find the photos uploaded looked good, that's because of good photography skills, not because the food was really good here.

I was very disappointed with how each Har Kow fell apart when picked up. The meat in the paper-wrapped chicken was tough and not fresh. The Chicken Rice with Sausages came with Taiwanese Sausages, not the Lup Cheong that was stated clearly in the menu. And the porridge was really bland.
author: Nobita C

restaurant_name: Kow Loon Hong Kong Dim Sum
review_text: The queue is always long and that gave me the impression of 5 star food but I would give this place 3.5 stars! There are hits and misses as is the case with almost, if not every restaurant. I find the seasonings of most of their dishes spot on even if some of the dim sum did not make the cut for me. I liked their siu mai, har gow, prawn fritter (明角虾) the best. The rice noodle roll was not bad although I would prefer a thinner sheet. The taro balls would have gotten my thumbs up had the taro's texture been more "powdery" and less dense. I should not compare but I always use Crystal Jade's egg tart as benchmark for flaky Chinese egg tarts. Lo Mai Gai is a must order whenever I have dim sum and although the sticky rice was soft enough, the overall dish did not excite. The kopitiam had decent Kopi peng and Teh-C peng.
author: Samantha Han

restaurant_name: Kow Loon Hong Kong Dim Sum
review_text:
Tim Sum variety remains but the quality had definitely dropped, but taste is still consider ok for a neighbourhood Tim Sum.

The only thing that need improvement is the cleanliness as tables are always sticky as I could tell that the table cloth is hardly rinsed.
author: Amy

review_text:
Be prepared to queue for 30 minutes to an hour, but this bowl of fishball noodles makes every minute worthwhile. This store delivers an unmistakably delicious taste of Malaysian hometown flavor.

The tossed noodles, coated in a fragrant blend of scallion oil and crispy lard crumbles, are irresistibly rich and savory, while the handmade fishballs and fish cakes burst with fresh, pure seafood sweetness. Yes, the wait tests your patience, but the first bite offers instant, heartfelt compensation.

This isn't just a meal, it's a culinary pilgrimage.
author: chan jasmoon

review_text: The best noodle so far that I can find. Expect  long queue. Fresh fish ball & ingredients made by hand, noodle cooked just right, combine with nice spicy chilli. Eat your noodles with wooden chopsticks and porcelain spoon. $5 for a regular bowl.
author: LS

review_text:
Ordered small fishball noodle dry with thin noodle for $5. They have the thin noodle despite it not being indicated.

40min wait. Queue was deceptively long. Everyone infront of me are ordering more than one. I think modal is 4.

Anyhow the fishball and fish cake are great. Probably the best fish cake i had. Fishball is debatable but it is definitely q with the bounce yet firm. I would suggest to eat without any of the sauce. The sour lime chili was great but too over powering end up it is the only taste. But if that is ur cup of tea then by all mean.

Tau pok is unique but is neither better or worse than ytf filled tau pok. Noodle wise it was delicious, with right about of al dente. How it was just too dry despite me mixing it very well. Not enough sauce. Taste wise the pork lard definitely elevates it.

Would definitely be a 5 if it is not so dry.
author: Super Fragrance

review_text:
Malaysian style Fishball Noodles $5.50

I was hoping for more umami from the sauce in the noodles however it only looks good but not much taste, had to add in the soy sauce and chilli padi 🫣 Even with the good amount of pork lards but somehow it was lacking in taste...

However the fishball is good! Nice texture and the taste of it is yummy.
author: S.Y

review_text:
Started queueing for the 1st time (bcos I loved handmade fishball), waited close to 35mins, even though today is working day. Been observing the front few people, the average order per person is 2.
My marks as follows
Handmade fishball - 5/5
Handmade fishcake - 5/5
Noodle (mee pau) - 4/5
Chilli’s - 4/5
Soup - 4/5

My fav breakfast of all time
author: BC

review_text: Both the sous vide and charcoal broil method used by the Mad Charcoal yield tender and smoky flavored meats. It's side dishes are also both generous and tasty. Ambience is tidy and catered to evening diners too. Cleaning staffs are proactive in clearing used dishes too. Recommend an automated queue dispenser in order to avoid tiring queue before the order deadline in person.
author: Alex Ding

review_text: Yong Tau Fu set ($8). Generous serving of ytf and veggies, and noodles were nicely done. Uncle was also giving outa piece of abalone to everyone, so generous of him! Definitely crowded as it's one of the few food places in the area.
author: Darren

review_text: There the some excellent food options here. The yong tau fu is quite decent during lunch. Mad Charcoal is an all time favourite. A decent beer garden at night. Could have a better atmosphere with some music.
author: Nicholas Ng

review_text: Super not recommend for drinking their ice kopi o cause they mix with hot water which is out of the coffee taste.
author: Steven Hung Ting Chia

review_text:
~ Updated on 20240816 ~
Mixed Rice - 1 curry chicken 1 vege 1 steam egg $5.50

~ Updated on 20230630 ~
Had Thai food today, $6.20

~ Updated on 20230621 ~
Mixed Rice - 1 meat 2 vege 1 egg $5.50

~ Updated on 20230620 ~
Mixed Rice - 1 meat 2 vege $4.70
Slightly bigger portion compare to yesterday.

~ Posted on 20230619 ~
Mixed Rice - 1 meat 2 vege $4.70
author: Miss Lee

review_text:
Been coming here for decades, and it’s one of the first few Jack’s Place restaurants from back in the day. There’s a comforting sense of familiarity every time I visit.

Their mushroom soup never fails and is a must-order for me. I also never miss their escargots and it’s becoming a habit every visit. The fish & chips and their signature fire / sambal steak are true classics, having stayed on the menu for decades.

Definitely go for the hot plate dishes for the baked potato, generously topped with their sauce and crispy bacons! Simple but so satisfying.

Service has always been great too. The staff are attentive and helpful, making the overall dining experience pleasant and fuss-free.
author: Eileen T

review_text:
Free dish from aia. Ordered 3 meats. Didn't know there is spaghetti.

I think i will just go with what's great and what can be improved.

Great
Chicken was probably the best part. Very crispily grilled and flavourful plus juicy.

Improvement
Milk served could be warm or hot to ensure coffe remains hot. Otherwise the taste of coffee and milk is above average.

Beef was okay juicy and with beefy taste in some area but no crust.

Cheese sausage cheese was not well distributed. But otherwise it is process food so yeah.

Spaghetti is well cooked. Almost al dente but not there. Plus it could use some taste.

Otherwise taste wise is quite friendly for all ages.
author: Super Fragrance

review_text: Went on a Friday night and the restaurant iis full house. The service and food is still good. My all time favourite,  Jacks special steak, their lobster bisque has not change after all these years,  still yummy. Wish their oyster is bigger
author: Maryann Partymama

review_text: Came here for children’s day dinner after our library trip. Really old school ambience. Food was good. Especially the lamb and chicken. Had the mixed grill. Beef may be better quality if we had gone for the pure steak option. My girl gave thumbs up for the kids pasta meal. Enjoyed our dinner.
author: WDG Dingguo

review_text:
Jack's place is more for people who wish to reminisce old times as these days with competition from many other western food joints, some might feel that the standards at JP have dropped, but eating at Jack's Place, is for the experiential dining and memories,  which many of us went there during teenage days for dates or special occasions.

Prices are not exactly cheap,  but for the occasional nostalgia, is ok.

Service and food quality at this AMK branch is acceptable, unlike some others. There is no crowd,  so a good place for quiet celebrations.

AMK branch also managed to get our steak doneness right,  so we were quite satisfied with it.
author: Botak

review_text: The main courses were generally not bad and value for money. However, the Lobster & Crab Stuffed Mushrooms dish under starters category was utterly disappointing, $11.80++ for 6 pieces of miserable sized mushroom covered in cheese.  No sight or taste of the so called lobster and crab fillings. The photo and descriptions shown in the restaurant's menu were totally deceiving. BEWARE when you order.
author: C W NG

review_text: Ordered set lunch N.Z striploin steak with Diane sauce. The portion I had was pathetic, others were having bigger portions than mine. Steak was cold when served. The restaurant is filled with oily smell. Partition glass panels were filthy.
author: Lianmeng Lim

review_text: The food is great, although the prices are a little too high.
author: Max Lim

review_text: Cosy environment, friendly staff and delicious food.
author: SeeYong Yee

review_text:
Kudos to the students running the place for the food and service. The place is done up well enough though some things can be refined a little.

My overall take is that they have done well but most things could use a little improvement.

1) The pasta I had was too firm. To note I love pasta al dente but this needed a bit more time.
2) The sauce tasted good but it was too dry. Just a tad more liquidy texture would elevate it.
3) The mango sticky rice didn’t really work as a reimagined version of the dish as I would have much preferred the original. Textures, taste and mashed up taken in altogether could be improved on.
4) They only had white or raw sugar and no equal or other type of non-sugar sweetener and it would be good to have that alternative for the hot tea/coffee.

Service wise it was excellent. So great job there 👏🏻

Saying all this they will be closed for reno for a year and after that not sure what the new form will be. All the best to the students there in their f&b journey 👍🏻🙂
author: Raphael Too

review_text:
Food is nice.
Was served by Yue Leng and Ardriana.
Adriana articulated well when introducing the dishes while Yue Leng is attentive and gentle.
Thanks Mr Clemence for the guidance provided to the students.
author: celine tan

review_text:
Fantastic fine dining restaurant run by NYP students. As a member of the public, I paid $18 for a 3 course meal and topped up $2 to get a latte.

The servers do their best to provide the best service. Very attentive, and detailed in their explanation of the courses. The food is light and delicious, but very filling. Great experience!
author: S Tan

review_text:
I visited L’Rez recently and had a mixed experience. I ordered a latte and a cappuccino, but both drinks were disappointing. They lacked any latte art, and the foam was overly thick. The taste was just average.

The appetizer was alright, but the mains were underwhelming. The hamburger patty was slightly undercooked, and while the salmon was decent, it didn’t pair well with the glutinous rice. On the positive side, the cocktails were enjoyable and probably the highlight of the meal.

Dessert was fine but unremarkable—nothing stood out. The service, unfortunately, was a little slow, which added to the overall mediocrity of the experience.

In conclusion, while there were some positive elements, the overall experience was not impressive. I would rate it 3 out of 5 stars.
author: J

review_text:
Note it is at Block F.

Google Map is wrong - not at Block S.

I attended a SG60 Charity Dinner - the menu was curated by a ex-Michelin chef.

Great Ambience for a private event.

The student chefs and servers from Nanyang Polytechnic did a fantastic job in a wonderful fine dining experience.
author: K T Lim

review_text:
My mother saw on their TikTok promotion and wanted to try their food. Restaurant is based in AMK ITE, we arrived around 6pm it was empty but slowly more crowds came.

We ordered half Peking duck, 3x of shark fin soup, braised pork with steam bun, wasabi prawn, French bean and qing long veggie.

Peking duck, not bad and they will help to wrap BUT I prefer to wrap myself because some they put the sauce too much, abit salty for my liking. The remaining meat we have them cooked with Ee fu noodles, it was good! Yums!

Shark fin - not bad, quite a generous amount of shark fin:

Braise pork - kind of salty imo, so-so not my kind of thing.

Wasabi prawn - MUST ORDER! So delicious, the wasabi not overpowering.

Qing long veg & French bean - both good but the French bean stood out!

Overall recommended, the service also good and attentive. Good place for parents and elderly.
author: Vieon Wu

review_text: We did not expect to the food to be fantastic for a place that's relatively unknown compared to the established brands in AMK. We were pleasantly surprised by the standard of food. IlThe restaurant was full as there was a function going on. We were having second thoughts coz usually the wait would be long and food standard not good in such a case. Food came relatively fast and more importantly, tasted good. We will visit the place again to see if the standard is consistently good. There is some promotion now for certain dishes which will lower the cost.
author: Christine Ho

review_text: A hidden restaurant in ITE building with tasty chinese cuisine. The dishes are tasty and worth to try especially the cod fish is cooked and mixed well with the sauce.
author: Xingzhi Cai

review_text: Enjoyed a good casual dinner! We loved the crisped brinjal with meat floss. The Peking Duck was decent, though nothing particularly special. The steamed grouper was definitely fresh and the food was generally ok. Plus, the staff were attentive, and the spacious environment made for a comfortable meal.
author: Ghostguan Raoh

review_text:
2025.6.15 (Sun)
My first and last visit. The restaurant is not filled up, yet the service is slow. We have to wait so long between dishes. The servings are all very small and it works out to $42 per pax. Really not worthwhile despite being well-executed. Especially for the location. For this pricing, I have much better options especially my clubs.
author: L Y

review_text:
Quite crowded on Deepavali holiday but managed to secure two tables for our two families of toddlers. The play area was much smaller than I expected; thankfully there is a large playground outside with plenty of sand, slides and swings.

They forgot to provide cutlery with my hotcakes order and only gave one set when my friend asked, when we needed 3. Quite annoying. Otherwise, well-maintained and clean environment. Nice toilet area with a small waterfall.
author: Jean Seah

review_text: Service is extremely slow. There was only 1 person at the counter she was sauntering around the place delivering singular packets of fries to tables instead of assembling and serving the food at the counter. Someone ordered 3 ice cream cones and they were all melting on the counter. That 1 employee assigned to the counter felt a bit lazy; like she didn’t want to work.
author: SQ

review_text:
Food is fresh from the kitchen and crispy.
Very spacious and kids friendly environment.

I would like to commend staff Augustine and Kayden for their prompt service and helpfulness in cleaning up a little spill of sprite.
author: Joey Chang

review_text: Nice place to enjoy Macs. There is ample carpark lots. Not that crowded. Diners made up of students, residents living nearby & professionals working around here.
author: Del H (Sapphireblue)

review_text: Came here for weekend breakfast, standard McDonald, managed to get a table easily, there’s a mini play area for kids inside. There’s a drive through and a small carpark as well. Unfortunately the area has ongoing construction which will be ongoing for sometime
author: Jerald Kng

review_text:
I had came here a few times. I enjoyed each time. Although the food isn't to my liking, the service was great. Food wise, the portion is okay but I rated down for its taste. I didn't like mushrooms and onions to be on carbonara spaghettis and on mac & cheese. It just makes it so sour. This is only according to my preference.

Staff wise, the food came pretty quickly.You can expect a short line during peak periods. Waiting Staff Irene was very friendly and attentive. She reminded me of my sweet grandmother. Always checking if my food had arrived. Informed me that the icecream might take awhile. She quickly clears away empty plate too. I had seen that she also looks after customers well. Helping them with their orders. For manager Ms. Aznee, she was always on the go. One time, her staff got scalded and she kept checking on her to make sure she was ok. Heard from other staffs that she is indeed a nice manager. ♥️
Atmosphere is nice. I would usually return for the deserts for the least.
author: Faith Lim

review_text: As I was rushing to fetch my kid, so i was like 5 mins earlier to their opening time. Yen Joo was very kind to attend to our needs to take away a yusheng for our afternoon celebration.  She took the initiative to help us with our order and very helpful.  Glad to meet such a wonderful staff and the staff (man with white shirt) also wish us a prosperous year.  Thank you Yen Joo and staff of amk hub. They made my family a wonderful day.
author: Esther Heng

review_text:
The soup of the day was a bit diluted, the baked rice was nice, the chicken tenders were decent, and the kunefe ice cream was pretty good. But for about $35 I don't really think it's worth it.

The manager was friendly but the waiter wasn't...
author: Luke Lau

review_text:
Ordered the Ribeye steak (Medium Rare). Order was overlooked and came after an hour. When the food came, the middle was still purple and raw and tried to ask to cook it. However, I’ve been trying to call the servers for nearly 10 minutes and they didnt come, or told us to wait but never came back.  When they finally took the steak back to recook, it still came out raw in the middle. restaurant_name: Teng Sheng Korean BBQ Buffet - Ang Mo Kio
review_text:
Disclaimer: It is an $18 nett weekday lunch buffet, you pay for what you get. That said, what you get is pretty good.
Meats had a large variety, skip the pork and go for the beef or chicken. Seafood had fish, prawns and squid, of which I only tried the squid, which was tender and fresh-tasting. Cooked foods were an even larger variety, gyoza, ngoh hiang, nuggets, curly fries, cheese balls, fried fish, fried chicken drumsticks. But the only ones worth any stomach space were the gyoza and fried chicken drumsticks. Drinks are included, ranging from your standard sodas to local asian drinks like sour plum and barley. Nothing worth shouting about. My favourite were actually the vegetables, specifically the kimchi and the Chinese style salads, like the bean curd skin salad and the black fungus salad. Uncommon for KBBQs but they were well done; balanced and providing a much needed acidic kick to the greasy meats. Ice cream is also fully included, complete with 10 different flavors. For the price, you're getting unbeatable value. The ambience is nice too, mostly ITE students who fill in come noon time, but not too many either. Staff are helpful and will readily change your hot plate cover or guide you if you've got questions.

review_text:
Stepping into Gim Tim, one is immediately enveloped by the nostalgic gravitas of a classic Singaporean Chinese institution. There is an unmistakable air of heritage here—the kind of place where multi-generational families gather under the glow of ornate chandeliers to celebrate life's milestones. However, as any seasoned gourmand knows, heritage can be a double-edged sword, oscillating between timeless mastery and a comfortable, yet perilous, plateau.

Our journey began with the Abalone Lo Hei. While the ritual of the toss was performed with the requisite vigour, the dish itself felt somewhat perfunctory. The abalone was of a standard grade, lacking that deep, oceanic brine one hopes for, and the vegetable medley—though crisp—offered little in the way of innovative zest. It was a "safe" rendition: mathematically balanced but missing the soul and complexity that elevate a starter from a tradition to a revelation. It was, in a word, average.

Expectations were high as the Roast Suckling Pig made its grand entrance. Visually, it was a masterpiece—the skin possessed a deep, mahogany sheen that promised a symphonic crunch. Unfortunately, the reality was a lesson in technical inconsistency. The skin, while beautiful, lacked that definitive shattering crackle that defines a superior roast; it felt more resilient than crisp. Beneath the surface, the meat lacked seasoning, failing to deliver the savoury depth that only a thorough spice rub and proper curing can achieve. It was a visual triumph, but a textural and flavorful disappointment.

The kitchen found its redemption, however, with the Soya Sauce Fish. Here, the chef’s handle on heat and timing was evident. The fish was the epitome of freshness—its flesh flaking into translucent, succulent petals at the mere suggestion of a chopstick. The soya dressing was a masterful emulsion of umami and subtle sweetness, enhancing rather than masking the delicate provenance of the seafood.
Equally impressive was the Asparagus with Assorted Mushrooms. A dish often relegated to a "side," this was remarkably appetising. The asparagus maintained a snappy, verdant crunch, providing a brilliant counterpoint to the earthy, velvety notes of the fungi. It was a clean, sophisticated palate cleanser that spoke of a kitchen that still respects its vegetables.

Their Xiao Long Bao was similarly packed with juices though perhaps with a slightly thicker skin than at other places. The Mei Cai Kong Rou was also pretty solid, the meats were nicely glazed without being overly salty.

Overall it was a good dining experience and the pricing is very reasonable for the quality of food delivered.

review_text:
Dining Experience @ Rong Ji Seafood.
.
Ambience is shared with the food court its located in. The space is brightly lit and breezy, with modern functional furnishings for groups of all sizes. Decently comfortable and clean too. Parking is a bit of an issue though, due to the limited lots.
.
Service is brusque but efficient. Staff bark orders and exhibit little patience, but the speed at which they fulfil and serve orders helps keep the waiting time down, and the queue somewhat manageable. Staff also clean up quickly when diners leave.
.
Food is Chinese cuisine, focused on zi char wok stir-fried dishes using fresh ingredients. Seafood is the highlight here, and dishes are consistently well executed. Portions are sized for communal group dining. Prices have a slight premium, budget about SGD $48 per person.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text:
Very popular Zichar place. Reservation highly recommended.

Large size Crab Bee Hoon was about $140. Crab was very big and sweet. Broth was flavourful too.

On the other hand, most of the Salted Fish Chicken were not fully cooked. When we feedback to staff after most of us tried and thought it was just one piece which was not fully cooked, the comment was why we didn’t inform them earlier and only after everyone tried then we informed them. The staff then offered to recook the dish who can were only left with those chicken feet and neck portions. The staff then only charge half price but we did not get to eat most of the chicken. The staff didn’t seem to understand the issue.

Claypot fish maw and sea cucumber - Decent dish but nothing stood out. Good flavours though. The quantity increased with loads of in use of onions and sliced ginger

Kai Lan stir fried with 4 big prawns - The highlight of the dish is the 4 big prawns that are fresh.

review_text:

Their pan pizzas are still one of the best when you want something with a soft crust, and the sides like the wings and garlic bread never disappoint.

What I appreciate most is how straightforward the ordering process is. Whether I order online or through the app, the menu is clear and the checkout is quick. Delivery times are usually reliable, and even during busier periods, the food still arrives in good condition.

Thier service has been consistently pleasant and dependable. Staff are usually quick to acknowledge you, whether you are dining in, picking up, or asking a question at the counter. They are patient when you need a moment to decide and helpful when you ask for recommendations or adjustments to your order.

review_text:
We decided to come here for a quick dinner near our home. I ordered a Chicken burger and was taken aback when I was served. The fries were overly toasted. I may have said burnt but in my mind, what is meant was it really overly done and wasn't up to standard. The bun was also burnt. You can see the black mark on top. When I feedback to the lady, she insisted there was nothing wrong. She said the color was because of the coating and so was the bun. She spoke bluntly, non emphatically, simply insisted there was nothing wrong and just wasn't willing to hear from customer's perspective. I was flabbergasted, made more annoyed by her rude attitude of refusing to see from my perspective as a paying patron. Only after she heard me saying it's ok I will post online she confronted me about it. I simply replied, it's ok you do you, I do me. Later on, the chef came out and explained to me politely that this is how restaurant serves burger and fries. His attitude was better. And he offered to redo if i insisted. We were rushing to go to the playground for my child evening play before the other kids goes home. Hence I told him it is fine.
But just for the record, as someone who had been in b2b sales and business development, locally and globally, having dined and been dined at so many restaurants locally and globally, don't try to fool me saying this is restaurant standard.

Anyway, i left the top of the bun alone, ate some fries but really cannot, didn't want to have sore throat. And the chicken portion in the chicken burger is really miserable. Btw, I am writing this post now at 6plus am cos I just woke up with a sore throat.

To be fair, my child beef pasta was good and she finished it. My husband chicken pork chop is also decent. The tomato soup was not bad.
But the chicken burger is really cmi. Don't order this. You can judge from the picture. But of course, if you like this type of overly grilled or toasted burger and fries for $15.90 before gst,  then go for it.

Also, don't expect much service and positive experience from the lady here.

review_text:
From the moment I made the reservation, the entire experience was seamless. The staff confirmed our booking quickly and even sent a gentle reminder before our dining time, which made the whole process feel very organised and customer-friendly.

When we arrived, the service team welcomed us warmly at the entrance. Even though the restaurant was busy, the flow was efficient, and we were seated without much waiting. The staff were attentive, polite, and always ready to assist from helping with menu recommendations to ensuring we had everything we needed. Their professionalism truly set the tone for a pleasant meal.

Once the dishes started arriving, it was just wow. Din Tai Fung never disappoints with their quality. The xiao long bao were delicate, piping hot, and perfectly wrapped with that signature burst of broth inside. Every dish was consistently flavourful  it was the fried rice, noodles, vegetables, or dumplings, everything tasted freshly prepared and well-balanced. You can really feel the effort and standards they maintain in every plate.

Overall, from reservation to stepping into the restaurant and finally enjoying the food, the entire experience was smooth, comforting, and satisfying. This is why Din Tai Fung remains one of the most reliable and enjoyable places to dine. Always worth coming back.

restaurant_name: Song Fa Bak Kut Teh (The Seletar Mall)
review_text:
The pork ribs soup is the highlight: super fragrant, peppery, and comforting without feeling jelak. The ribs were tender and easy to eat, and the best part is the soup top-up! You can keep enjoying that warm peppery broth throughout the meal. The you tiao was perfect for soaking up the soup (crispy outside, soft inside), and it really completes the bak kut teh experience.

We also tried the braised pig’s trotter and it was a great add-on. Rich, flavourful, and nicely braised, especially good when eaten with rice. The kai lan was a good balance to the heavier dishes, fresh, nicely cooked, and a solid veggie to share. Even the honey tea was refreshing and helped cut through the richness.

Service was efficient and the whole experience felt well-run and consistent. If you want a classic, comforting bak kut teh meal with great soup and satisfying sides, this place is absolutely worth it. Will definitely be back!

The sweet and sour salmon sushi was a surprise, it really captured that zhi char sweet and sour vibe, though it wasn't quite my favorite. The cereal prawn was decent too, nothing too special but still tasty.

The ikura sushi was great. no fishy aftertaste, which is always a win in my book. I absolutely loved the mango crepe dessert; it's not too sweet and has a nice hint of sourness that balances it out with a super fragrant mango scent. The fried chicken drumstick was also a hit!

The atmosphere was alright, chairs felt a little small and it did get a bit cramped with people sitting across from each other. But considering the price, I’d say it’s pretty understandable.

Definitely worth trying if you’re into sushi with a local zhi char twist!

review_text:
Murtabak (SGD $8) @ Thasevi Food.
.
Founded in December 1981, the original Jalan Kayu prata stall has seen peaks and troughs in their business, though in recent years, they've made a quiet comeback.
.
Their rendition is well-executed, with fluffy crisp layers of folded dough, filled with wispy chicken egg, crisp red onions, and a choice of either tender turmeric minced mutton or chewy shredded chicken.
.
With smoky bready vegetal meaty eggy sweet salty savoury spice flavour. Paired with juicy cucumber dressed with thick tomato ketchup with vegetal sweet flavour, and a side of curry for a salty spicy kick.
.
.
.
Mutton Mysore (SGD $7) @ Thasevi Food.
.
Founded in the 1960s but officially registered in December 1981, this family-run casual eatery is renowned for popularising the "Jalan Kayu Roti Prata" brand in Singapore, and is currently managed by Thasveerali Ali.
.
Their rendition differs because of the curry gravy, with less use of red chili and more curry leaves. The deboned mutton cubes are simmered within, infusing it with flavour.
.
Has tender chewy textures, with mellow meaty savoury salty spice flavour. Inspired by South Indian cuisine in style, yet different enough to be uniquely Singaporean.

review_text:
Easy-to-find restaurant that is located directly outside of Hougang Mall's exit to the MRT.

Getting the staff to attend to me was a struggle. Even when one cook was not busy and just staring at me, they continued to do their own thing instead of addressing me. I feel like the service needs some work.

I order fried rice everytime I visit. One version in particular I favor is the Dry Laksa Fried Rice with Grilled Chicken. While the normal fried rice has the wok hei aroma and great-tasting rice, the Dry Laksa Fried Rice was a level-up. If you enjoy laksa, then the fusion between fried rice and laksa BY Wok Hey will make you crave for more.

Price range is sort of pricey for Chinese street food cuisine here, so expect to pay almost $10 for one simple meal. Definitely worth it though.

Despite my comments about the fried rice, there were times when the rice will taste watery (NOT because of oil), or even underseasoned. I once bit into a box that had like plain reheated rice. Consistency is a bit of an issue here, but this happens rarely.

There's no quick guarantee of food being served because the staff can be either fast or slow. However from most of my experiences, my order would take 25 minutes on average to prepare (even during peak hours).

It's a good food chain with delicious food, but put some effort to get attention of the staff when you order.

review_text:

Driven by the spirit of giving, WOK HEY has collaborated with The Art Faculty and Stitch — a non-profit organisation dedicated to empowering artists on the autism spectrum, thereby engendering a more inclusive society — to design the boxes and merchandise for Christmas 2023. And the boxes look absolutely gorgeous!

The fluffy grains of rice infused with a wonderful wok hei made the 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗳𝗳𝗹𝗲 𝗙𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗱 𝗥𝗶𝗰𝗲 𝗠𝗔𝗫 ($12.80) marvellously mouth-watering. With the thick and chewy udon soaking in all goodness of the condiments, the 𝗧𝗿𝘂𝗳𝗳𝗹𝗲 𝗨𝗱𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗔𝗫 ($12.80) was similarly stellar.

WOK HEY’s extraordinary Xmas Edition specials are the ideal way to spread some festive cheer!

restaurant_name: Divine Realm Vegetarian Restaurant Blk501 Hougang
review_text:
Nick and May invited me for lunch followed by a cycling adventure. Before meeting up with Kitty, we decided to grab lunch at Divine Realm Vegetarian Restaurant in Hougang, as this is one of May's favorite vegetarian spots.

After a long bike ride, we were looking for a place to refuel, and it was exactly what we needed.

We decided to share a few dishes to get a taste of everything. We ordered the Sichuan Sauce Ramen, the Fysh Slice Soup, Roti John, and Gyoza, along with some XueHua Herbal Tea to quench our thirst. The Sichuan Sauce Ramen was a hit with all of us.  The spice level was just right! The Fysh Slice Soup was surprisingly good; it actually tasted quite a bit like fish, which was impressive for a vegetarian version. The Roti John was alright, nothing too special, but still tasty. The Gyoza were crispy and flavorful, and we all enjoyed them. The White Rice was well cooked.

The XueHua Herbal Tea was the perfect refreshing drink after our ride. This is also a cozy little restaurant with decent air conditioning, and the service was okay.

Overall, Divine Realm Vegetarian Restaurant is a great option for a casual and satisfying vegetarian meal, especially if you're with friends and looking for a reliable and tasty choice.

Pros:

- Delicious Sichuan Sauce Ramen with perfect spice level
- Surprisingly flavorful Fysh Slice Soup
- Crispy and flavorful Gyoza
- Cozy atmosphere
- Reasonable prices

review_text:
After a long day working in F&B, there’s something comforting about sinking into the familiar warmth of a McDonald’s meal. It’s not just food—it’s a moment to pause, breathe, and indulge in something that feels like a treat.
That night, I decided to try their Cheesy Truffle Beef Deluxe, paired with Potato Pops, and finished it off with the Maltesers® McFlurry.

The Cheesy Truffle Beef Deluxe was indulgent—juicy beef patties layered with a creamy truffle cheese sauce that had just the right balance of richness and umami. The melted cheese oozed with every bite, perfectly complementing the soft bun and crisp lettuce. It felt like McDonald’s had taken their classic burger and given it a luxurious twist.

Next were the Potato Pops, crispy little golden bites of joy. Lightly seasoned, they were crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside—perfect for dipping into the leftover cheese sauce from the burger. I couldn’t stop eating them; they were like the snack you didn’t know you needed.

To finish, the Maltesers® McFlurry was a dessert that didn’t disappoint. The smooth vanilla soft serve, swirled with bits of crunchy Maltesers®, created a perfect mix of creamy and chocolatey. Every bite was a reminder of why McDonald’s desserts are such a comfort food staple.

As I savored each bite, I opened the McDonald’s app to check the latest promotions. That’s when I saw it: collect badges on the app and stand a chance to win amazing prizes like the brand-new iPhone 16 Pro, a staycation to remember, or even a pair of flight tickets to anywhere. Suddenly, my meal felt even more exciting—indulgent food and the thrill of a possible big win? McDonald’s truly knows how to make a simple meal feel special.

For a moment, as I sat there enjoying this meal and dreaming of what I might win, the worries of the day melted away. The cheesy truffle richness, the crispy pops, the sweet McFlurry, and the possibility of exciting rewards—it all came together to remind me that sometimes, the little things can brighten your day.

Today, I ventured off the beaten path to Buangkok Crescent, looking for a nice Western meal.

(Good thing there's bus 114 from the new BK bus interchange to this place 😊)

Can't say I found a gem, though 😔

While I was served 2 pieces of boned-in pork chops (the preferred cut for #MHTamChiak), accompanied by sides of coleslaw, baked beans and crinkle cut fries, the poorly done meat left me struggling to finish my late lunch.

The pork was dry and didn't have much flavour. Brown sauce was watery, not starchy like from most Western food stalls. Making it hardly enjoyable trying to chow down those slices of pork!

Come to think of it, this may be the toughest pork chop I've ever tasted 🤔

I'm not sure if I should return to give their striploin steak a go, since this definitely requires attention to delicate cooking.

The food was cooked fast and meal was filled with many items. 💬

The fish was soft and soaked in sour cream. It tasted really delicious and with a great mix of flavors. The fries 🍟 were crispy and the portions were just right, not too much or too little. The baked beans 🫘 were nice and hot. The coleslaw 🥗 was cold but added some nice vegetables to the meal. There are also some lettuce 🥬 hidden under the fish too.

With its fantastic price compared to other western food stalls in Singapore, I would highly recommend people to come and try the dishes especially the grilled fish. 👍

review_text:
17 Nov – Qiu Lian Ban Mee, Hougang 1, Singapore 530956

I was craving Tom Yum, and since I was heading to Hougang 1 for some shopping, I decided to stop by the Kopitiam for a quick lunch. The coffeeshop recently underwent major renovations, and I noticed a stall I had never tried before—even prior to the renovation: Qiu Lian Ban Mee.

I ordered the Tom Yum Mee Hoon Kueh Ban Mee, priced at around $6.30. With the NTUC app, you can get a 10% discount. While the Tom Yum flavour wasn’t exactly traditional, it was spicy and sour enough to satisfy my craving. The dish felt like a fusion of Chinese and Thai flavours, but overall it was comforting and reasonably priced.

The best part was the mee hoon kueh—it was well-cooked, and the addition of crispy fried ikan bilis made the dish even more enjoyable. It’s tasty enough that I’d come back to try their other offerings.

Food Quality: 3.5/5

In lunch  i use to prefer  chapati and vegetable fry.
The chicken biryani was rich in aroma and taste, cooked to perfection with tender chicken and fragrant spices. The vegetable fry was fresh and well-seasoned, and the mutton was incredibly tender and flavorful, just like a home-cooked meal made with love.

The attention to detail, fresh ingredients, and homely flavors made the experience truly special. The staff was warm and welcoming, adding to the overall charm of the place. If you're looking for authentic, homemade-style food, Praiselin Kitchen is the perfect spot. I am visiting daily!

Kudos to the guy who's making the drinks, always saying 'Welcome' the moment you open the door. However, our experience today was quite disappointing due to the service provided by one of your staff members — the lady with glasses. (the one without hijab)

When we arrived, we requested to sit on the second floor, but she seemed visibly unhappy with our request. I understand the outlet was full and only one table near the entrance was available, but I preferred not to sit there as it would have been uncomfortable with people constantly walking in and out, especially since I have young children who are quite active. If you are lazy to walk up to serve us, then don't need to have the top level open, just close it!

Later, when our food arrived, we requested some extra chili from the same LADY. She did not acknowledge our request and simply walked away. A few minutes later, she returned, placed the chili on the table without a word, and walked off again. Even after we thanked her, she did not respond.

This experience left us disappointed, as it is far from the warm and courteous service we are used to at your establishment. We hope that you can address this matter with the staff involved to ensure that future visits for us and other customers are more pleasant.

Thank you for taking the time to read our feedback. We truly enjoy your food and hope to continue supporting your outlet in the future.

Sincerely,
K

We drove all the way from Singapore to dine here — totally impromptu because my husband was craving teppanyaki and we wanted to see what this place was like after finding it on Google.

author: Claire Yeo

review_text:
The restaurant exudes a modern Japanese aesthetic with warm lighting, wooden accents, and a beautiful wall art featuring a pagoda and Mount Fuji, creating an inviting and authentic atmosphere. The seating arrangement around the teppan grill offers an interactive dining experience, allowing guests to watch the chef skillfully prepare dishes right in front of them.
The meal looks beautifully plated and well-balanced. The main dish features perfectly seared slices of beef steak, cooked to a juicy medium doneness with a slight char on the edges. The beef is garnished with fresh chopped scallions, adding a pop of color and a mild oniony aroma. Accompanying the steak are sautéed greens and caramelized cabbage, both vibrant and glistening, suggesting they were cooked with care and seasoned lightly to complement the meat.

The set includes a bowl of fluffy white rice and a steaming miso soup, which adds a comforting, traditional touch to the meal. The soup appears rich with seaweed and tofu pieces, offering a savory umami flavor typical of authentic Japanese cuisine. Small side dishes, kimchi and dipping sauces, provide extra layers of taste and texture.

The beef delivers a tender bite with a smoky, savory flavor, balanced by the sweetness of the cabbage and the earthy greens. The rice and miso soup complete the meal, making it hearty yet refined. The interactive teppanyaki style enhances the dining experience, turning it into both a culinary and visual treat.
Takara Teppanyaki offers a well-curated Japanese dining experience with quality ingredients, appealing presentation, and an engaging atmosphere. It’s an excellent choice for those who appreciate fresh, flavorful dishes prepared right before their eyes.

It was delicious, savoury, and well made. Onsen egg was perfect. Smoked duck was also cooked enough. Portion size is OK. Not big, not small, but just right. After tax, this regular plate of pasta came up to RM41.80. No drinks ordered. Phew. That is, imo, a lot, for a plate of pasta with simple ingredients. If it was handmade, from-scratch fresh pasta, I understand lah. But this was not. Will I visit again? Probably not. I think it's a pleasant place, with pleasant staff. After explaining that we had left our iPad on the sofa in front of FIN, he immediately said he would check and update us as soon as possible.
Within 30 minutes, Mr. Amin called to inform us that our iPad had been found by a hotel bellman named Arjun. We were so relieved and grateful. The honesty shown by Arjun and the helpfulness of Mr. Amin truly reflect the excellent values and professionalism of Sunway Hotel Big Box.
