Really a must try :) not to mention the staff here have an excellent attitude and excellent service. Super attentive from ordering, to preparing the items and serving the items. We really like their boss too, he's super service oriented, friendly and entrepreneurial. I didn't manage to take a photo of the Sinjeon Topokki but I had it a few days ago and it's really good too, spicy was good for me, if you can take chili padi you can go for the Hot selection 🤭, as the spicy brought me to tears already (in a good way). Will definitely visit again, great good, good ambience and I like the baby cutlery that's provided too, very thoughtful gesture 😊
author: Adeline Liew

review_text:
Service is friendly!
Great that free child water is provided. Cute kids utensils.
Food cake fast!
Kimbap was good prob and my kids loved it.

Very very good Korean fried chicken! Nice they have half half option so kids can take the honey soy sauce non spicy version and we can take the sweet spicy one.
The chicken us very very crispy and yet juicy and tender inside, even the breast portion. The meat just falls off.
We wanted to ask for gloves but realised most of the pieces didn't have bones! So easy to eat.

Highly recommend this place!
author: Kelvin Goh

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Outstanding Hospitality, Tasty Food & Great Prices!
I had an amazing experience at this restaurant. The food was really tasty and the prices were very reasonable. The boss was incredibly humble and kind — he even offered us a complimentary dish because the staff took a few minutes to serve the chili sauce.

When I requested chili sauce, they had run out, and the staff took a few minutes to serve it. What truly impressed me was that the boss asked his staff to go across to the opposite shop lot in the pouring rain just to buy chili sauce and fulfil our request.

That level of dedication, hospitality, and care for customers is very rare these days. Tip-top service from start to finish. Highly recommended! 👍🏼
author: Tharushiny R Sinnasamy

review_text:
Amazing food — especially the fried chicken and other fried items!
Everything tastes light and crispy, not oily at all. You can really tell the frying is done well.

The fried chicken is easily 3× cheaper than what you get in Seoul, yet somehow tastes even better. Super juicy inside, perfectly crisp outside.

On top of that, the boss is genuinely warm and friendly, and treated us extremely well. You can feel the sincerity.

Highly recommended — will definitely be back! 👍🍗
author: Hou Dekai

review_text: Recommend cheese toppoki, sweet spice chicken and the hotteok (taste like Chinese brown sugar glutinous , but a Korean style ) open by Korean people. A kind and generous boss. Support 🫰
author: YC

review_text: Nice and cosy cafe, with a large outdoor seating area. They advertise as a cafe + bakery, but they are honestly more towards cafe. They don't really have breads and pastries, they have a few small things for sale like cookies and scones, and some cakes in the fridge. Staff here was absolutely charming and lovely. I felt the bakes were really rather expensive for what they were... Rm20 for 1pc of quite a small chewy cookie. But it is a really cute and cosy place to have a drink, and they also do appear to be rather popular.
author: Kimberley Howarth

review_text:
I went to Thera Cafe last week while staying nearby, and I honestly loved it so much that I came back twice for breakfast.
The cafe has such a cozy, peaceful atmosphere ✨ perfect for a slow morning. It’s quiet, calming, and a really nice place to relax and enjoy your food without rushing.
Breakfast was enjoyable, and the overall vibe made the experience even better. Definitely a spot I’d return to again if I’m in the area. Highly recommended if you’re looking for a calm and comforting cafe to start your day ☕✨
author: Dansy Dalle

review_text:
I’ve been here a few times and I like the vibe here, very aesthetic and makes me feel like I’m at a cafe in Korea (the owner is Korean). The drinks are usually good but it’s a hit or miss, depending on your taste. I prefer their coffee over their matcha.

Unfortunately I just bought a black sesame scone and as I bit into it, I felt a string coming out of my mouth! I can’t tell if it’s a strand of hair or maybe it’s a very long lint, but it’s definitely something not edible. So now I’ll be hesitant with the food here.
author: Jen P

review_text:
Ordered chicken caeser salad. All good till I ate the first piece of chicken. Omg its SUPER SALTY! Asked the chef if there was extra dose of salt added by forgetful  chef de partie. He offered to re pan fry a new piece. I said dun waste food. If he could blanch in hot water let it soak for the salt to ooze out, I dun mind.

And chef did just that, thank you! Chicken is still tender. Pics showed I wallop it all. 6 stars for service with a heart and smile.

Thank you!
author: Victor NG

review_text: Everything about this place was amazing! The pasta carbonara was absolutely delicious, the sweet potato fries were perfectly done and the pancakes were so good. The drinks were great too. Loved the overall vibe and experience definitely one of those cafés you would keep coming back to. Highly recommend!
author: Ashvinie

review_text:
Had mango bingsu and pistachio dessert at BingYou. The texture of the bingsu was light and refreshing!  The mango was fresh and sweet, and the pistachio flavor was rich but not too overwhelming.

The environment is also very cozy and comfortable, had a great time chatting with friends. Definitely a nice spot to hang out and enjoy desserts together! 😍

Highly recommend on a hot day!
author: Yu Rui

review_text: The food and ice cream/bingsu is really good! We ordered nuggets, pistachio dreamland and the mango daydream. It's safe to say i recommend all of them! The ice  are really soft and it doesn't make your brain freeze. The mango one are a mix of sweet and sour that blends nicely, while the pistachio are pure blessing. Thank you for the wonderfull food fufu  [^ ^]
author: Tia Bandung

review_text:
The indoor seating area had a private event but we managed to sit outside.

We ordered the mango daydream. The ice is so light and fluffy! The mango is nice and chunky. Tho some of the cubes were slightly sour. The kids were delighted to find popping Boba at the bottom of the bowl. The cream on top is also so creamy and fluffy.

The grape one was also so light and refreshing!  The grapes were sweet. The bottom also had a surprise, had Boba at the bottom too.

The pistachio one is a big hit! Quite creative. I like the bits of real pistachio, adds crunch to the texture. Then after we dug into it, there's biscotti crumbs layered inside. More crunch and flavour. The red beans at the side goes well with it. I suppose it's the red beans that normally go with matcha. Azuki beans I think.

Will highly recommend this place!
Service is warm and friendly!
author: Kelvin Goh

review_text:
We‘ve been here twice because we really wanted to try their popular bingsu and we couldn’t decide which one to get 😅 so we had the pistachio bingsu and the mango bingsu - both were delicious and refreshing. it was also our first time trying bingsu so we had no idea what it would taste like 🤭

personally I liked the mango bingsu better because it’s sweet, fruity and a bit sour with the mango sauce and the bubbles underneath. my boyfriend liked the pistachio bingsu better since he loves pistachio and doesn’t have a sweet tooth like I do 😄

additionally we tried the 2 vegetarian meals with veg chicken and peach lemon tea + plum juice which were amazing!

tomorrow we’re going to try the matcha bingsu and we’re already very excited 🥰🍧
author: OnlyAnnika

review_text: The pearl, the milk and the read bean goes well and taste excellent on the soy Bingsu. Couple with the cozy environment, we had a wonderful experience here! The red dates soy is very flavorful and tasted wonderful!
author: Stanley Chai

review_text: Do not order toasties. Actual product is so far off the promotional images, cheese is miserable and no sauce. Bread is dry, and its $2.80 for 1 slice - totally not worth.
author: Jing Jing

review_text: I always order chicken ham and like parmesan bread. But hor the sauce sometimes like not enough. I tried before loosing some weight eating subway sandwich and it works. Try eating few days for 1 or 2 months you will see your stomach go flatter and weight go down. Staffs are friendly.
author: Max Lim

review_text: Small outlet with very limited seating at the corner of yew tee point. Cant seat more than 4 pax tgth at any of the seating areas.
author: A1A1A1A1B2

review_text: im a customer at Subway Yewtee Point. i came to visit the store on 27/06/2025 at 0730am and noticed there is a insect in the tomatoes. i have informed about the staff about this (Philippines staff - matured lady in her 40s) and she ignore it. I hope the NEA and managment inspect the place for hygiene maintenance in the restaurant.
author: Haz Ra

review_text: This is my daughter’s favourite food. She has been eating since she was in primary school and now she is a young adult. The manager has been there since she started to eat. Whenever we have no idea what to eat, Subway is always the first options
author: Sewfuntastic 2015

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Yew Tee Square
review_text:
Ming Kifchen now has this promo of 3 dishes for $28, 5 dishes for $48 and Fish Head + 4 dishes for $68, so my family went to try.
They served extremely fast as only got my family orders so the 2 chefs cooked.

However my family was disappointed with the presentation and quality of the zichar dishes as they were thrown haphazardly into the plates. The hotplate tofu dish became tofu in a bowl 🙃, the reason why this dish is on a hotplate is because to keep the tofu warm. The curry sauce on the pork was too watery to be nice. At least the clams seem clean and generous in portion.
author: Liau Yuan Wei

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Yew Tee Square
review_text:
Extremely unhelpful service staff from the stall - full of attitude like they are owed lots of money!

Price is much higher than other sze char nearby which serve larger portion.

This is not worth having a try - I suggest you all go for alternatives. I personally tried myself with my family and we are all utterly disappointed.
author: Brat

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Yew Tee Square
review_text: Disappointing place to dine at. Firstly, it is very disorganised. Secondly, it’s quite dirty. Thirdly, as rightfully pointed out by others, their service staff has quite a bit of attitude. Further, their price is pretty steep compared to others. Overall, it was a very unpleasant meal and I will not frequent it again.
author: Richa G

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Yew Tee Square
review_text:
Probably the worst dinner I had so far~~~

Soup is so salty to the extent till several tables complained along with us.
Got the second batch but still equally bad.

Paying few hundred to get egg white soup.

Fish first time when arrived, was raw.
After which they steam it again and the flesh is over cooked.

Very disappointed as their standard should be better than this but perhaps they are very over-whelmed

Charred rice is as good as soy sauce rice.
Someone probably sponsored them with too much soy sauce that they have to pour plenty into the food they serve.

Horrible Terrible

Wasted money 💰
author: Alger Chua

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Yew Tee Square
review_text:
Ming Kitchen had a huge price increment which I think is unjustified.

Sambal Fried Rice: was $6.00 in October,  now is $8.60 (40% hike)
Hor Fun in gravy: was $5.40 now is $7.30 (35% hike)
HK noodles: was $6.00, now $8.00 (33% hike)

Other ZiChar stores have kept their prices same around Yew Tee/CCK area. I will be giving Ming Kitchen a miss from now.
author: Derrick Cheng

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Yew Tee Point)
review_text: Another branch of Ka Kun available in the indoor mall. Tables are quickly taken at peak hours. Enjoy their coffee quality here just at any other branch. Also just like any other branch, their return trays clears very slowly at the dedicated shelf.
author: Mervyn Phea

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Yew Tee Point)
review_text: When there's a line queued, you know it's decent.  Stopped here for breakfast and enjoyed the kaya toast.  The eggs are soft boiled and with the toast, offers a filling meal to start your day.  With the combo, it also comes with coffee or tea (with or without milk)
author: Simon Lau

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Yew Tee Point)
review_text: This store the tea O is always SO bitter. Really disappointing with such price. My wife likes their bread or else I won’t patronise them
author: Albert Soh

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Yew Tee Point)
review_text: Understand that Yakun had always been packed with customers but i hope that the staff can maintain their services. Our number was called to collect the food but the cutlery wasn’t ready and when my bf is about to take the food, he was asked by the staff if he is going to eat with his hands. So is it our fault to take our food when the number is called? Food here has always been great but service can be improved.
author: Denise goh

restaurant_name: Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Yew Tee Point)
review_text: Overall food is good here and environment nice in the morning. Notice that now they will give the eggs only when  toast bread is ready. Maybe give people the option to take it with coffee as the wait for bread took almost 15min.
author: Sparkley

review_text:
had chicken kolo mee. new on menu. portion of noodles was modest for its price. soup was saltier than normal.
food court got better options.
author: CYE

review_text:
Absolutely unacceptable experience. I ordered a bowl of noodles for $7 and was shocked at how pathetically small the portion was. It looked more like a child’s serving than a proper meal. I even asked the chef if there had been a mistake, and he flatly denied it—no apology, no explanation.

The fact that they think this portion is acceptable, especially for the price, is a complete rip-off. It’s clear they have no regard for customer satisfaction or value.

Do yourself a favour and avoid this place at all costs. There are far better food stalls around that respect your money and appetite.
author: Arthur Ang

review_text:
Order was missing salted egg yolk and even when it came, tasted like egg instead. Double confirmed with the staff so maybe its just the quality of food.

Also, not worth for the amount ur paying
author: Joseph Chu

review_text:
Claypot chicken rice is highly recommended!! It's my favorite outlet @YewPoint .. the staffs here are friendly especially the Malay lady, Most of my visits here during lunch, she is the one who served me. I love the taste of the claypot chicken rice, it's served piping hot (you have to wait 10-15mins for it to be ready) which I don't mind...it's always worth the wait...the rice cooked till crispy on the side (crust) which this is the way to enjoy it.....I always add chicken meat (extra$2). U have to enjoy it with the sambal chilli and the cilipadi with soy sauce....it's to die for!! 😋😋😋

I've tried their claypot seafood noodles too... recommended as well...but noodles portion is small (just nice for me)
author: TINA AYB (TINA)

review_text: Ordered wan tan mee and fish ball noodle with no soup??! How do i eat this without the soup? Feel so cheated. And i came during off peak no crowd and still can afford this kind of mistake??? Not the first time!
author: Nuzul Hakimi

review_text: morning always full. afternoon not much people. online business is good. most bad reviews are afternoon. many seats. many staff so fast service. the food is ok
author: rayblade ng

review_text:
It was my first time eating at this location. The young man on Sunday mid-afternoon (28 Oct 25) who took the order was friendly and polite. However, the two eggs prepared by the young woman in glasses, which came as part of the set, were served cold. 😨 I placed them on the table and ate them within two minutes, yet they were already cold. Curious, I touched the shells – they too were cold.

When I informed the young woman, she reluctantly replaced them. The replacement eggs were not in hot water, she only poured hot water for less than half a minute before handing them to me.

Unfortunately, I later suffered food poisoning. Staff should maintain proper hygiene and follow safe food preparation according to SFA and NEA guidelines so that no customer falls sick. Customers trust that food establishments meet Singapore’s hygiene standards, and it is management’s responsibility to ensure staff take this seriously.

This was an unnecessary and painful experience that left me with a very bad impression 🙅🏻‍♀️🙅🏻‍♀️🙅🏻‍♀️!
author: Monda S.

review_text: A satisfying breakfast at Toast Box Yew Tee to start the day! Tried their Black Sesame Traditional Toast, and it was absolutely fragrant and crunchy — the nutty black sesame spread paired perfectly with the crisp toast. Enjoyed it with two hard-boiled eggs and a hot cup of Milo, the perfect local comfort combo. The staff were friendly, and the service was quick even during the morning rush. A cozy spot for anyone craving a nostalgic Singapore-style breakfast. ☕🍞🥚
author: Jason Sim Hong Teck

review_text:
Cafe is smaller after renovation.
Air circulation is much better than before, no more "greasey" smell on the clothes after having my breaks there.
Service staff are very cheerful and nice as usual.
Still one of my favourite ToastBox outlet.
author: Jasmine Ho (Luxiferette)

review_text: I used to enjoy having breakfast or afternoon tea with family and friend in toast box. This is first time I felt such a disappointment when I saw the breakfast served in toast box @yew tee point.  The portion was so small and totally different from the picture. The red bean soup served to my husband was just half of a small bowl. The peanut butter thick toast, was so thin and small! Same as the flossed toast! What happened to Toast box?
author: Jade Wang

review_text:
Ordered through app at 6am.
Missing chicken mcmuffin, missing drink, didn’t give jam for big breakfast set, didn’t give salt and pepper. Called them but didn’t pick up. I do my job everyday, please just do yours properly.
author: Phyllis Yen

review_text:
sweet deal of 9.9 for 20pc combo chicken nuggets but the joy did not last.
spicy nuggets were cold but thankfully the original nuggets were hot.
ordered 4 curry sauce but got 4 honey mustard instead.
also requested for no salt for the shaker fries but it still salted so after adding only half the seaweed shaker seasoning its still too salty.

prefer the Lot one or Hillion mall outlet as they never get my order so disastrously wrong before.
author: Bimbles

review_text: I ordered 3 Hershey hot fudge sundae to be taken away . When I returned home and discovered I was given 3 vanilla hot fudge sundae . Really disappointed with the staff and the kiosk taking order!
author: Carol Soh

review_text:
Staff ignores cash orders. Despite the restaurant having no orders, they were seen just talking about each other even though I was at the cashier.

Take note, YOU have to approach them, they don’t approach you if you need help. I’ve worked McDonalds before and this is not their customer service SOP 😂

Clearly seen slacking. Management, please do forward this to your staff, thank you!
author: Qin iOS

review_text:
One of the worst McDonald’s outlet I’ve visited.
Been patronizing them for years and majority of the experiences were negative.

1. SLOW FOOD
During breakfast service, food takes a long time to prepare and serve. I’ve waited up to 15 mins for my food to arrive and there’s barely any new customers coming in.

2. BAD SERVICE
During lunch, it’s a little busier. Maybe it’s my luck but self ordering kiosk I used ran out of paper and I approached a staff. The staff just told me to wait. I asked a different staff every few minutes and I’ve waited for a total of approximately 15 mins just for a staff to replace the paper. Then wait another 15 mins to collect my food. With that time, I could have gotten something cheaper and quicker. I thought FAST FOOD would be quicker because it’s in the name.

3. STINGY
They’re also very stingy with the serviettes. 2 pax and they only give 2 serviettes. Pathetic. When I order to go, they only give like 3 packets of chili sauce when I have 2 burger meals.

4. CARELESSNESS
Over the years, I’ve encountered a few wrong orders. Regardless of ordering out or dining in. We should get what we ordered. It’s very basic.

5. BAD ATMOSPHERE
Lastly, the restaurant’s atmosphere is horrible. It’s due for a renovation. It’s dirty and the age showing. Sometimes they block McCafé’s southern entrance, which is good. But mostly it’s left unblocked. The tables and chairs outside the southern glass sliding door are mostly occupied by non patrons as a smoking and gather area. And when people open that door, all the smoke will enter the McCafé.
author: J

review_text: Have been dining in here almost every Friday or weekend. The manager is very welcoming and attends to our requests promptly and effectively. It is an excellent place to enjoy a meal."
author: Endeavaurus Gaming

review_text: ordered an alacart mushroom swiss burger , no sides no drinks, waited more than 25 minutes and the burger wasnt even hot , wasnt cold either but room temperature. Imagine calling yourself a fast food restaurant and take almost 30 mins to serve a single burger and for that long you waited , not even a hot burger. Nice job well done
author: Jnxllx

review_text: Had a great experience at Burger King. The food was freshly prepared, especially the Whopper—very flavorful! The staff were polite and service was fast even during busy hours. Clean environment and good value for money.
author: Olivia Nguyen

review_text: Visited this outlet today and was served by an amazing staff named Elyana! She attended to my needs with great service and was attentive to my orders! I hope managements can reward this amazing staff for her great service!
author: Danial Hakimi

review_text: Sandwiches were served hot and fast…friendly crew whom patiently took my order over counter despite peak hours…kudos to BK would definitely patronise again in near future 🎉
author: David Thena

review_text: I think the food is average. Price is however reasonable. I ordered chicken chop and the portion is quite big. It comes with two sides. There are plenty of sides to choose from. I suggest not getting onion rings as they only give a few - not really worth the money. Other than that, ambience was alright.
author: Bariah Anwar

review_text: One of the best chicken chops I have ever had, portion was huge and the salted egg on top was an absolute game changer. Definitely recommend to those who want to enjoy a hearty meal! 🫡🫶
author: dylan

review_text:
I eat here on a consistent weekly basis for the past 3 years, and I can guarantee 3 things:

1) Big/Oversized portions for their protein (Value for money!)
2) Taste is consistent across all my visits
3) Waiting time when ordering in person is between 10 to 20 minutes

My go-to is the Black Pepper Chicken Chop with French Fries and Coleslaw. Black Pepper sauce lacks strong pepper taste, but it is still flavourful. More akin to Brown Sauce than Black Pepper. French Fries are shoestring and seasoned with salt. Coleslaw is too creamy and thick for my liking, sometimes I eat it all up, other times I do not.

I recommend this place only because its one of the few halal options in the area, portions are big and price is affordable.

However, I do not recommend the Fried Chicken Cutlet. Ordered it 5-10 times and have always been disappointed with the chicken. Cutlet is fried in a awkward shape and is difficult to slice. Too much breading as well.

Overall, if you like it, lucky you. If you don't like it, too bad :(
author: Aemil Harithz

review_text: Ordered a few times overall. Food is nice.  Quantities  just about right. The flavour taste 6/10 consistent.  And sometimes you had mishap here and there. So.... just be extra careful of your hygiene.  Im certain this isn't my hair, but a hair in my breaded fish heh! . 🥴well overall can be better.
author: Starscream

review_text: Paid $16.50 for ribeye steak but got only 4 onion rings as sides. Is this a joke?
author: Jovan

review_text: Bad attitude and argumentative coffee counter staffs. Was ordering two coffee and tow eggs and after it cash registered and served, I asked for total price and it was S$4.50. I told her why it is more expensive than a toast set come with 2 eggs, butter toasts and 1 coffee + additional cup of coffee and she answered me that’s is how you order how they key in. Once ordered and no changed…. What an attitude from the coffee counter ladies…
author: henry choo

review_text: Super popular coffeeshop with many food choices. Overall it’s clean and vibrant since it’s recently renovated. Though the space is rather cramped during evening when beer-drinking uncles are hogging all the tables.
author: KH Chong

review_text: The mixed rice stall offers very insanely tasty dishes for a very affordable price range. I honestly believe this stall deserves a Michelin Star for how good their food is. In my opinion, the best dishes here are their Sweet & Sour pork and their ladies fingers, eggplant is pretty good too! 🤤
author: owen

review_text:
🤕🤒😷🤢 Have you tried soup chinese Rojak!? Really horrible. When I ask the seller he said without peanut is watery.  OMG. The Zhi Char mee goreng and hor fun also so so so...only.

😄😁😍On the plus side , the rest of the stall look OK. The place ventilation was great and windy. 😍🤩🙂
author: W8ll8AM S8M

review_text: Delicious local hawker food.    Yen San Seafood Zhi Char, Economy Bee Hoon morning session, Chicken Rice, Mixed Vegetables Economy Rice, Prata and Mee Goreng, Western Food deserve special mention
author: Kon Yew Tan

restaurant_name: Ah Boy Chicken Rice (Mentor Eric Teo)
review_text:
Relatively (compared to many other hawkers/coffeeshops) GENEROUS portion of chicken (~130g of chicken on avg for $6 set, yes i weighed it out 🙂‍↕️👍). Value to quality ratio is amazing 💯.
Meat is tender and not dry (even for breast, thigh is the best) 4 out of 5 days that i eat from this stall. Soup changes everyday! Chicken is accompanied with pickled veggies which i LOVE.
I always ask for more sauce to be drizzled over my chicken because i like my chicken doused in that yummy sauce. Very minimal to no gaminess 💯.
Non biased review!
I come here so often because I genuinely love their chicken rice, to the point that the uncle recognises our order+xtra sauce even without saying anything to him LOL. The auntie is really nice and efficient in her job as well!! queue can be long but moves super fast❤️❤️ I don’t know why some reviews shit on their service :P  Pls support them!
author: Joycelyn Aw

restaurant_name: Ah Boy Chicken Rice (Mentor Eric Teo)
review_text:
Ordered the non spicy version of the chicken noodles. The soup was sweet and the chicken flavour burst in the soup.

Yellow noodles could be replaced with something that absorbs the soup better.

Cost 5.70
Taste 9/10 😋
Service 10/10
author: jack

restaurant_name: Ah Boy Chicken Rice (Mentor Eric Teo)
review_text:
Rice: 9.5/10. Easily the highlight. Ginger/garlic lovers will love the aromatic punch in the rice - one of the most ‘pang’ i’ve ever tried.

Soup: 8/10. Comforting with real veggies, not the generic chicken soup

White Chicken: 6/10. Nothing to write home about. Not dry, but not very moist either. May try the roast next time

Achar: 5/10. Exceedingly normal. Well at least it isn’t cucumbers only.

Chilli: 7/10. Does the job, not too watery.

Value: 8/10. They don’t flatten the meat which is good. Only 5 small piece chicken, but for $3.8, can’t complain.

Will I come back again? Only if in the area. I don’t see myself making a pilgrimage here just for this.
author: Keanen Ang

restaurant_name: Ah Boy Chicken Rice (Mentor Eric Teo)
review_text: Got the half steamed chicken - meat was very tender and really enjoyed it. Difficult to find chicken rice done well in the heartlands.
author: M L

restaurant_name: Ah Boy Chicken Rice (Mentor Eric Teo)
review_text:
One of the best curry chicken noodle. Noodles are those high quality ones, cooked perfectly and springy. Curry is milky which I like. Chicken thigh add on is $1, cooked perfectly as well.

Chicken rice is also decently cooked. You can feel every grain of rice. Veg portion is good and also on point. Chicken breast however so so, a little powdery. Not sure why.

Chili however is not so spicy, wished it is better. Soup is good, well seasoned.

Will definitely come back and have other dish here as well.

17 Aug 2024 went back to have their half chicken $18. Chicken is really big sized. Wished that it’s more springy. Would only give a 3 star out of 5 for the chicken.
author: Orange

restaurant_name: Sin Xiang Kee Teochew Noodle 新祥记潮州面家
review_text:
My favourite organ soup stall in Yew Tee. For a 4.50 portion, I think there are plenty of ingredients! I love the soup, brewed well and has strong 酸菜 taste. Using loin meat is great for texture, normally they would use small intestines.

Although at night if you purchase, it taste a little too concentrated. Might need to add water periodically!

The auntie’s son can be a little cranky, but he knows how to cook!
author: Benedict Chua

restaurant_name: Sin Xiang Kee Teochew Noodle 新祥记潮州面家
review_text: Paid $4.50 for a bowl of bak chor mee. The noodle was springy. The pork slices were tasty and tender. The pig liver and meat balls were also tender. The free pig organ soup was tasty too. Altough I asked not to add chilli sauce to the noodle, there was no ketchup or black vinegar added - very different from other bak chor mee stalls. Nevertheless, this was the best bak chor mee I have eaten in Yew Tee. Service was prompt as there was no queue.
author: Edward Wong

restaurant_name: Sin Xiang Kee Teochew Noodle 新祥记潮州面家
review_text: in this sin xiang kee teochew noodle stall,the foods and plain rice prices must be adjust downwards please.the plain rice must sell at 50 cent.the foods must be delivered to the customer table.
author: Jim Huang

review_text: Worst mala I've ever eaten. No sichuan peppercorn fragrance at all, in place was a "curry instant noodles flavour packet" taste. Plain salty with no other flavours, I threw the whole serving away. Waiting time was long as well. Hope they improve.
author: Gabrielle Teng

review_text:
$12.10 for this. Portion is ok, ordered big spicy but not super spicy. Not fragrant. But ok to eat.

Meat and veg all weigh tgt same price.
author: Orange

review_text: Been ordering from this stall for delivery. Get from medium spicy onwards. This was $20 worth but lately, the portion seemed to be dwindling. My orders are always intestine, bamboo shoot, 3 types of vege and two meats. All 100 gms each.
author: purple taste

review_text: Convey in mandarin and chinese in a few time.  中辣 *少油*  im the only customer and yet. When i reach home ..open up and all i saw is a load of vegetables in a pot of oil  .....taste more like indian curry rather than Mala. Will never recommend anyone. Waiting time is always long too...so i heard. Wont go back
author: jason tan

review_text: Recently got a takeaway from IMM. firstly the staffs were very friendly and helpful when i was choosing my dishes, the food was also cooked just right especially the potato which i find is very different from the others i have tried so far. Would definitely recommend for others to try out.
author: Joshua Kang

review_text: Food was reasonable, spend slight over hundreds for these. 2 crabs different flavours, all other dishes in small sizes.
author: Don Wang

review_text: The curry fish head was outstanding—rich, aromatic, and deeply flavorful. The curry struck a perfect balance between spice and creaminess, with a fragrant blend of spices that wasn’t overpowering. The fish was fresh and tender, absorbing the curry beautifully, while the vegetables soaked up all the goodness of the sauce. Every bite was comforting and satisfying. A truly classic dish done right, especially enjoyed with steamed rice.
author: Reylan Acuesta

review_text: Insane value for money tze char. Real hidden gem! We never fail to visit every week. Tofu is sooo good! Highly recommend! My 5 pax meal always range from $58-$80+ max. And that’s like 5-7 dishes btw 😭🙏🏻 very crowded store so we always go at 10pm hehe.
author: W X

review_text:
$54.30 for takeaway of beef hor fun large, small three cup chicken, ginger frog leg, claypot tofu.

I came all the way frm cck bc reddit recommended but my fam thinks its average.
author: Ember Shen

review_text:
A little long wait during peak hours but generally ok.

Famous for curry fish head and you must try. So good you might forget your mother’s name.

I also ordered ginger and onion sliced pork 姜葱猪肉 on a hotplate, and it’s pretty good. Kids favourite - cereal chicken; they finished the cereal and showed thumbs up!!

Double boiled soup - diff soups available everyday so go for it!!
author: Felix Ker

restaurant_name: Man Chee Kee 文志记 Pig's organ Soup, Porridge, Braising
review_text: Paid $4.50 and $0.80 for a bowl of mixed pig stomach and lean meat soup and a bowl of steamed rice respectively. The pig stomach and lean meat was tender and no foul smell. The salted vegetables was soft and not overly salty. The soup was tasty. Service was friendly and efficient as there was no queue during lunchtime.
author: Edward Wong

restaurant_name: Man Chee Kee 文志记 Pig's organ Soup, Porridge, Braising
review_text: Newly opened store, food was good and everything was quite value for money. Only gripe was the waiting time.. only one staff handling the orders and cooking, along with handling a the non stop food delivery orders. Bright side is that the one man was pretty fast. Worth trying.
author: Abraham Lee

restaurant_name: Man Chee Kee 文志记 Pig's organ Soup, Porridge, Braising
review_text:
Newly opened stall. Tried their pig organ soup.
Ingredients are fresh and well cleaned. Meat texture are great.
Generous potion.
Soup taste is quite balanced, not too saltish.
Add on a piece of tau-pok, well braised and flavourful.
Chilli sauce is nice.
Reasonable pricing.
Worth eating.
author: Terence Lee

restaurant_name: Man Chee Kee 文志记 Pig's organ Soup, Porridge, Braising
review_text: Ordered via grab. Make your own judgement.
author: Yaji N

restaurant_name: Man Chee Kee 文志记 Pig's organ Soup, Porridge, Braising
review_text: the man chee kee stall food prices must be adjust downwards for the people with financial family background to eat this stall.the plain rice must be 50 cent and not 80 cent.food must be delivered to the customer table.
author: Jim Huang

review_text:
I have recently ordered the food from PK_SL Food Corner Sg and their food was super delicious,
Packing was good with high quantity.  we all loved the cutlet and chicken curry.
Wishing them a good luck.. Keep on going.
author: kulagan sreetharen

review_text: The most authentic and tasty Sri Lankan food you can get in Singapore. The food is very delicious, and I can recommend to all.
author: Harish Jesurajan

review_text:
I’m the regular customer of PK. Every time I feel it was a lovely meal. All the foods are delicious And fresh. It always remember the Sri Lankan food. Specially the kottu, fried rice , sothi , coconut sambal etc 😄
PK cakes are awesome.no words to describe the taste.  the prices are fair for the portion size. Shorteats it’s real high tea quality. !!! Always a great spot to get great food.
Good luck thushy akka 👏
author: pavithirakini saravanapirabu

review_text:
I am a regular customer of PK_SL Food Corner as my family enjoys their delicious food. Every time we serve their food our guests have enjoyed it so much, that they too become customers. I will not hesitate to recommend their food, as it is truly delicious & value for money👍🏿
Keep up your great work PK_SL Food Corner, I wish you great success🙏
author: Anoshie Antony

review_text:
Food is super delicious, portion is large always with nice packing.
I'm a great fan of that cutlet and cake
Wishing you a good luck akka . Keep on going.
author: Anuja Varman

review_text: folk here go for strong, over good   which it is, and isn't particularly.
author: alwyn

review_text: herbal soup
author: Loh Hui Hong

review_text: My first sushi takeaway was at gogo Causeway Point. It was so fresh, good, and reasonably priced, and it has since been my go-to place whenever I crave sushi. It was a great grab-and-go meal as the sushi was well packed. Today, I was at Yew Tee and chanced upon the shop; without hesitation, I went in to purchase Sushi Don. It's so good.
author: S L

review_text: Sushiro gogo offers takeaway only, making it quick and convenient. The sushi was well packed and reasonably priced. A good choice for a simple grab-and-go meal.
author: Peter Tay

review_text: I'm a repeated purchase customer. However, todays fridge was not very cold for the sashimi, chinese lady accepted my payment and rejected providing me my points because she claimed that she has closed of my order. I clearly remembered multiple of times theres multiple of staff who have attended to me allows point accumulation right after i have made the purchase. She could have asked me if i have member and yet she didnt. Seriously... i think the management needs to guide the staff more effectively.
author: Teo Chloe

review_text:
Been patronizing this store since they open in late 2022. They used to sell the truffle sushi and it was simply awesome. But sadly, they don’t sell it anymore.

They also used to be very generous with the soy sauce and wasabi but today the guy only gave a few packets.

There was also a line outside the store today and same guy was slamming on the bell continuously. Probably to get the attention of potential customers but I saw people only looking puzzled and annoyed. Not a good technique to “attract attention”.
author: J

review_text:
I come here regularly almost every week for the past year to get the sashimi and mentaiko sushi. I usually call before coming down after 9pm to check if they are still available. For the past week, I’ve tried calling almost everyday after 9pm, but no one ever answers the phone😠 What’s the point of having the phone number then…

Edit: The situation has improved slightly since I posted my review though sometimes still no one picks up depending on the staff present. Staff Wei Ye is friendly and always answers the call.
author: Zhi Heng

review_text:
Came by for breakfast, this stall has one of the longest queue. Pay with FairPrice app for 10% discount!

Ordered the wanton noodle with shrimp dumpling soup. Shrimp dumplings and Wanton have a good bite & water chestnut added texture. Noodle texture is chewy,
sauce is flavourful enough to cover the ghee taste of noodles. Charsiew was average though, so this is truly a place to get your wanton/ dumpling fix!
author: Chunwen Huang

review_text:
Decent portion for the price ($4.30), but aside from the volume, not much stands out here. Char siew was dry and hard, noodles were standard fare. The wantons were decent though, relatively generous pork filling that was juicy. Soup was nothing special.

I cannot recommend this place, unless you like plain-tasting food at a low price. So possibly if you’re under the weather, this might be a decent option.
author: Adam

review_text:
Probably the best wanton noodle in Yew Tee. I ordered extra wantons and shrimp dumplings with spinach green noodle which is quite uncommon in most wanton noodle stalls.
Wanton and dumplings were fresh and skin were smooth but not dry. Was bit disappointed with the noodle as I can taste hint of "kee" instead of spinach. This is probably their source of noodle supply is not good.
Overall, I am very satisfied with the meal!
author: WT Wong

review_text:
Juicy big Wonton 👍🏻Fresh
Noodles taste good with the sauce
Good portion for the price
If CharSiew can be slice thinner will taste better because they use lean meat thus too thick make it tough to eat
author: Ju J

review_text: Bought the budget meal set which only cost $3! Specifically this meal is not subjected to Kopitiam Discount since it is already so cheap. This meal is also the healthier choice meal, so you get a QR code which you can scan in Healthy 365 and earn points. Service was good as the staff cooked quickly and I received my food about 3-5min after I ordered despite the long queue. The food portion is just right and the ingredients are fresh. The staff are friendly and enthusiastic too. Really a hidden gem if you crave Char Siew Hor Fun/ Wanton Noodles.
author: Joshua Chew

review_text:
Got the Grilled Fish Spaghetti Aglio Olio
While the pasta was delicious, the fish was like half grilled so I threw away the uncooked part. Pls make sure the fish is totally grilled before serving!
author: Liau Yuan Wei

review_text: Food was kinda bad. The fish was one of the worst I've ever had. The breading had zero taste, and the texture was really weird (in a bad way). The chicken chop was edible but nothing more than that. The tomato-based pasta was pretty bad too. The sauce was tasteless
author: WeeKT

review_text: The fish is half in such a weird way. Highly do not recommend
author: Tan Hui Juan

review_text: Not nice. Chicken cutlet small small, carbonara no taste
author: Shuren Lin

review_text: Vast choice of cuisines and satisfying environment .
author: pugalll.__

review_text:
The Yong Tao Foo is nice, also quite big portion. But a little bit pricey..7 pieces + curry is easily $8.50.
Aircon kopitiam is good, but can be crowded during lunch hour 11-1pm+.
author: travel fun

review_text:
I grew up in Yew Tee.. so for 20+ years living here.  Countless times I had been here.
Usual complaints are that the pricing is a little expensive, but it's worth it for its portion and taste.
Soup is yellow bean with fish broth, I think. Better than other Yong Tau Foo stores, that I had tried which only use plain water soup or something bland. This store also has laksa. I frequent this outlet more than other outlets. Their service is good. If you are patient and friendly, they are too. My orders are always correct. Always happy to chat with them during non peak periods.
author: Faith Lim

review_text: This is in Yew Tee Square Kopitam. This Kopitam is air conditioned and is next to a mutli-storey car park. A good place to eat if it is raining, like today. The soup here is thick and fragrance because they use lots of ikan bilis and yellow beans. You can add ikan bilis yellow bean to your yong tau foo because they provide them for free. I believe these are from the soup. The ikan bilis has no more taste as it has all gone to the soup. You can image how good is the soup. They don't serve  cuttlefish here.
author: Avis Peng

review_text: Ate lot of Yong Tau foo before for me this Branch can be on top 3 list. Veggies lots and very fresh not a veggie eater but make me pick lots today. Enjoy mine meal with them keep the standards and will come back for more. 😊☕
author: Fabian Tan Wen Chee

review_text: Their laksa gravy was quite diluted at 12pm, the whole bowl of 6 items + noodle + laksa cost $7.50 (10% discount if u are using fairprice member app).
author: Chaos Foo

review_text:
Have my dinner here on 14 Aug at 1915Hrs at the outlet at Pasir Ris West Plaza & was rather disappointed with the so called 老火汤 where there are more bones than meat.

If the staff knows that there aren’t much meat,then he shouldn’t be selling.

Should honestly tell customers like myself that no more meat left & either top up with some free char-siew/chicken or suggest to me to eat others.

Rather disappointed. :(
author: Rayburn Zhang

review_text: On Friday 7 February 2025, I had roasted chicken rice with egg and crispy beancurd for my lunch at the Kopitiam Corner food court in Yew Tee Square next to Yew Tee MRT station, and I liked this meal as the roasted chicken rice with egg and crispy beancurd tasted very delicious. Overall, the service provided to me was very good and I would love to try these other chicken rice dishes from this outlet in the future.
author: GoAheadGroupFan

review_text: Soup ok.
author: Peter Rock Steady Crew

review_text: This is the BEST value for money Filipino cuisine available in Singapore. It is closest in terms of taste to food in Cebu. Outstanding taste and service. The owner is very friendly and sweet. I cannot recommend this place enough.
author: nadja ybanez

review_text: Overpriced. Ordered 1 dinuguan and 1 sinigang salmon without rice for take out, one of filipino lady cashiers ask me what's the mode of payment and i replied by Cash. She charged me at $8 each. i paid $16 for this, never coming back here.
author: jazer frondoza

review_text: This stall’s portion has been getting smaller and smaller. Today, I bought Lechon meat for $8.00, and this is all they gave me.
author: 周芊邑

review_text: Thick-cut crispy pork belly and pork flower. The meat is juicy and the skin is crispy. It is located inside the air-conditioned Kopitiam.
author: Kooo SS

review_text: the absolute best place for Filipino home cook food ever!!! you’re missing out if you haven’t tried!!
author: Shakthi Shree

review_text: we were here for the first time around 7.30am on a saturday and the food we ordered was fireeee!! the potatoes in the masala thosai was well seasoned (pls stay this wayy) but hope they can work on the sauces that comes w it. it needs more umph. egg prata was good. while we were eating there, the orders at the stall was non stop. Be it for delivery or walk in. Decided to order maggi goreng chicken through the app on another day and for the price paid was so worth it. Chicken chunks was big and the curry flavour from the maggi was delicious. not overly salty. please maintain and i will be your regular customer. thank you
author: Baymax

review_text: I waited 5 mins for them to served me a reheat prata egg n kosong x 2. When i approached the cashier why was i serve a reheat prata and need to wait for 5 mins. And ask for feedback contact. He said no channel to feedback. Wasted my calories on this kind of sub standard food. BOO!
author: Lionel Lim

review_text: My favourite is the egg prata. Always order at least 3 pieces. Nice and fluffy. Prefer the mutton curry over the fish curry.
author: Max

review_text: Bought ghee thosai...  but they said no chutney. A bit disappointed. Thosai without chutney is incomplete.
author: Doreen Lee

review_text: Don't order the chicken biryani, more bones than chicken.
author: Guang Beng Lee

review_text: I love the Nyonya Dumpling from this store!! Even though due to inflation the prices increased but it comes with generous ingredients and it’s very fresh! Haven’t had a good dumpling in a while but this one really blows my mind! It’s a good balance of sweet and savoury 😍
author: Jessica

review_text: Went to buy popiah from this stall tonight 730pm. I was shocked that the popiah was cold and stiff. The ingredients were not hot. I dared not eat it in case it has already turned bad. The 2 popiahs cost $6! I am very unhappy about the purchase.
author: yew thean cham

review_text:
Terrible experience on multiple occasions, but today (16 March 2024 at 6pm) was the final straw that prompted me to write this review.

When I ordered 3 tutu kueh, wanting to have 2 plain ones and 1 peanut, the staff said they don't do such mixed order, and I have to order 5 plain ones instead. I then asked if I could order 2 plain ones and 3 peanut, and she said no again. I told her I just gave the same order (to a diff person) last week and it was accepted, but this staff just said policy has changed. My question: is it very very hard for your company/staff to entertain mixed orders? Moreover, I am actually mixing in plain tutu kuehs, which ought to be cheaper for your company.

Another instance that happened a few months back: when I arrived at the stall at just a minutes BEFORE the "LAST ORDER" timing for tutu kueh, I was informed by the staff that she has already washed and kept the equipment for making tutu kueh. Question: maybe if your staff prefers to be lazy instead of helping your company make money, you should consider sacking her.
author: Stephanie Teo

review_text: Taste terrible! Rice dumpling rice too hard inside not cook and filling too sweet! Eat more definately you will get diabetes!
author: Ksh MLim

review_text: Many years of good tasty dumplings to fulfil my cravings
author: Kelvin Chin

review_text:
Staffs are blur , as they either (1) forgot your order (2) order not in sequence (3) not a good listener by taking wrong order LARGE SIZE becomes REGULAR SIZE (4) for take away   They don’t even inform u when order is ready and let the customer keep awaiting at the stall.

Cannot imagine that 3 stuffs working style r the same , they seems like playing toys instead of getting job done .

This is the worst staffs when I encounter so for the past 40yrs . Guess they r not a good fit for this job .

Yesterday I encountered another challenge again !!! What is this !!!!
author: TAN KATHERINE

review_text:
Pretty decent overall but not really Teochew. Servings were generous. Ordered the mee sua soup and braised pork with preserved veges.

The mee sua soup came with lots of sliced liver which were slightly undercooked and had a very distinct porkish smell.

The braised pork was quite good taste wise, and pork was tender. It was however overly watery and could do with more braised vegetables. The accompanying soup was also overly porky as well.
author: eddy khoo

review_text:
the penang hae mee prawn noodles here is so good,  the broth is thick and flavourful, can control the amount of chilli to adjust spicy level.

normally go for the normal version, 1st time trying the pork ribs version and all the ribs pieces are soft and goes well with the soup.

there is other zichar dishes here which is all not bad. will continue to visit.
author: Bimbles

review_text:
Kway Tiao has wok hey, hor fun not bad but could be a bit saltier (I’m Malaysian) and ngioh huang is nice too (it’s fried after cutting open).

Great service and nice ambience! ☺️
author: Si Jia Lai

review_text: Penang Savour brings the taste of Penang to Yew Tee Point! 🇲🇾✨ From aromatic street-style noodles to hearty local favourites, every bite is packed with Malaysian flavours.
author: Clair

review_text: Of all the dishes ordered, the hokkien mee was decent. Too much sweetness had affected the taste.
author: The Rundown

review_text:
The nasi lemak is the real draw here, with fragrant fluffy rice that is freshly prepared and chicken nicely fried to perfection. Attention is paid to every detail on the nasi lemak dish and my personal favourite are the peanuts and ikan bilis.

The hor fun is richly flavoured with the freshly prepared gravy and stuff, but perhaps the biggest (and only) regret with this dish is that the kway teow felt cold after missing the sauce in. Perhaps it’s been pre-fried too long ago. But nonetheless it’s still flavorful and delightful.
author: XY Sim

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ YewTee Point
review_text: This is what I got for my takeaway. They dont even bother to clean up the soup before delivering to customer. And the soup is more bland than usual, idk what went wrong in the kitchen and I definitely not gonna spend another 20 dollar just for this
author: Choo Hou Yee

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ YewTee Point
review_text: I’ve tried several West branches. Previously, the squid was overcooked and the fish fell apart, with poor service and noisy staff. Now, with new staff, the experience is much better—service has improved significantly, making it more enjoyable.
author: Ling

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ YewTee Point
review_text:
This place has serious hygiene and comfort issues. There were huge flies everywhere, landing on the ingredients—especially the raw meat. I even pointed it out loudly right next to a staff member, but she completely ignored me and walked away. Later, another employee came out to swat them away, but they just kept coming back.

The air conditioning was also weak, making the place uncomfortably warm. This likely contributes to the fly problem and raises concerns about whether the raw food is being stored at a safe temperature. With poor hygiene, improper food handling, and an uncomfortable dining environment, this will definitely be my last visit.

And the price is also on pricer side.
author: J

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ YewTee Point
review_text: My experience at Gong Yuan Malatang was truly delightful. The selection of ingredients was abundant and beautifully presented, offering a wide range of fresh and high-quality choices. The broth was rich, aromatic, and perfectly balanced, allowing the flavours to shine without being overly heavy. The service was efficient and courteous, and the restaurant maintained a clean and inviting atmosphere. Overall, it was a refined and satisfying dining experience, and I would gladly return.
author: Xin yu

restaurant_name: Gong Yuan Ma La Tang 宫源麻辣烫 @ YewTee Point
review_text: First time here after their opening since  2 weeks ago. Did not enjoy the experience. Throughout the meal, there were flies circling around the shop especially the raw food area. The shop is hot, not comfortable. I purchase a soft drink but it does not come with a cup of ice. Food wise not much different from similar establishments but the price is 30% more.
author: Ivan Lim

review_text: unassuming quiet little place in yew tee point, but food was sublime. for $11.80, they gave 3 thick slabs of salmon on top of tamago, and were extremely generous with mentaiko sauce and ikura. even came with a bowl of miso soup, when other places wouldve charged this as extra / wouldve had to upgrade to a set. items were very well plated and it tastes fantastic too. staff were courteous as well. would def come back
author: - adilah

review_text:
Edit on 9 Jan 2025 : Returned to order 3 dishes and 1 drink.
• Teriyaki Chicken don : Unfortunately the Onsen egg was clearly overcooked and was still served. (Lack consistency or just disregard for it hence -1⭐) Chicken , rice and sauce was still good.
• Salon Mentaiko don : salmon was dry after cooking. Might need wet brining or a mix of cooking method to maintain moisture within the meat.
• Chicken Karaage curry don : 4/5 was ok. As expected.
• Mango yoghurt smoothie : 5/5 appreciate the use of fresh mangoes. Will definitely purchase again.

-----
Didn't know the photo was blurry but wanted to leave a positive review.

Teriyaki chicken don : Onsen egg was perfectly cooked and adds great texture to the rice. Rice was great and had adequate sauce. Chicken was well grilled. 5/5

Salmon mentaiko don : Salmon was nicely cooked. Slight crisp that adds great mouthfeel. Mentaiko wasn't too overpowering. Would like to have a tad bit more sauce/gravy on the rice. 4/5

Miso Soup : Light and well balanced. Wish it wasn't half filled.

Chilli : Quite a weird pairing with the dish but as a standalone it's good.
author: Eugene Chan

review_text:
This unassuming dessert shop actually (surprisingly) sells one of the best Japanese and Korean foods in Yew Tee. The cook really knows what they're doing and how to make good food. My favourites from this shop are the Salmon Don with Tamago where you get big slices of salmon, Korean cheese noodles, and Yakisoba with Smoked Duck.

It's very very affordable for the quality and quantity! The service staff are also very friendly, sometimes they will be around for a nice chat. Highly recommended to give it a try, you might be surprised.
author: CJ Chen

review_text: The waffle and gelato were so good! Esp the earl grey!!! The banana choc gelato tasted exactly like eating a banana. Pistachio gelato was sweet, which matches very well with the earl grey gelato. The rice bowls had a lot of ingredients and it's definitely filling. The meat didn't have the frozen taste too, and were well marinated. Passionfruit yakult drink was refreshing and not too sweet. This is my to-go place for rice bowls and gelato/waffles now!
author: Emily Ho

review_text: The food is super nice! I tried curry karage, korean spicy noodle and shishamo. Super good! The korean spicy noodle surprise me! I like chocolate and durian ice cream also!
author: Clarice

review_text: Bought couple times from them! Tried their chicken cutlet spaghetti 🍝  and cream of mushroom spaghetti which was decent & yummy! Food always cooked on the spot so need to wait 5-10 mins. Chicken wing was yummy and salty!!!! Omg love the skin, fried nicely and it’s was hot~
author: J

review_text: Prices have increased since the renovation. The food remains tasty, especially the fried and roasted chicken wings but it no longer feels as value-for-money as before.
author: Peter Tay

review_text: Some days the fries is hot and good.. Some day it's cold (not even warm) like today, when fries are cold it taste really bad.. Need to find some way to keep fries in it's hot/warm edible state.. I bought at non peak hour 11:20am. Eat at 11:30am. Bun is not fried properly and cold as well. Luckily the chicken cutlet is warm. Service staffs are helpful most of the time.
author: Merlin SG

review_text: Highly disappointed. Bought a 3 piece meal. The size of their drumstick is the same size as the chicken wing drumstick. I know there is inflation, but I don’t think you should cheat yr customers this way.
author: Dolly Sim

review_text: Ordered the sss crispy fried rice, but was told that I can't add another chicken with the sauce. There's no option to add. I'm a customer who wants to pay more for more but yet I was denied. Hope the management addresses this and allows such an option.
author: Rohmat

review_text:
First time encountering subpar service at this branch. Was served by staff Teng, who seemed quite impatient when I got confused during the ordering process. Usually the servers will guide you by prompting you with questions (eg "what sauce?"), but she just stared blankly at me 😭 I thought it was her first day here. When we moved on to selecting toppings and I got confused, she responded in an annoyed tone.

Not very pleasant and is part of the reason why new customers feel disinclined to order from places like this. I'm not expecting to be handheld, but at least don't be impatient when I'm figuring things out.

Also the couscous was really bad this time 😥 Not sure why! It usually is fine! It was very hard, dry and tasteless. Quite disappointed in the inconsistent quality.
author: Yuhuan

review_text:
Had a great experience at Stuff’d. The staff were super friendly and fast, special shoutout to Nisha for being so quick and cheerful while preparing my food. Even though it was busy, everything was done really efficiently.
The food was fresh, tasty, and the portions were generous too. Always love how consistent the quality is here. The whole team deserves credit, everyone’s hardworking and pleasant. Definitely one of my go-to places for a good meal on the go!
author: venkatesh prakash

review_text: I’ve ordered the Daily Bowl here many times and it’s usually my go-to. The food tastes good and is generally satisfying. However, one downside is that the staff often don’t replenish the toppings when they’re running low or already finished. Also, the portion size can be inconsistent and seems to depend on which staff is serving. Overall, good food, but consistency and topping availability could be improved.
author: Peng Kong

review_text: The worker Nisha is an excellent worker. She remembers customer faces and even their orders. She works fast and still puts a smile on her face even when she is tired. She helps the new employees and doesn’t scold them if they made a mistake but instead shows them the correct way to do it. The other staffs are also nice and friendly. Excellent service!
author: Damia Danisha

review_text: Im a frequent buyer at yew tee stuff’d. And miss nisha would always serve me with a smile and will never be stingy with the portion. She would treat her customers with care and patience eventhough the FNB industry is a very demanding industry especially in a country like singapore. Me an the rest of the guys at Kranji Camp who usually go to stuff’d , is very great full to have miss nisha serving us !!!
author: Ammar Farouq

review_text: Absolutely love getting the BBQ pork belly set from here every single time. If you come to this kopitiam, make this your first stop

review_text:
The absolute worst service known to Man.

Firstly, the order was delayed. Secondly, the order was totally incorrect. Thirdly, when we tried to call the staff for assistance, we were ignored multiple times and when the staff came, she basically said we were wrong and took off with the incorrect order (despite the order chit saying otherwise).

The food is about the worst quality imaginable, the only redeeming factor was that it is affordable. But I’ve been to many other Saizeriyas with much better customer service than this.

author: Adam

review_text:
I visited the Saizeriya at Yew Tee Point today, and the service was very disappointing. The staff’s attitude from the start was poor, and the food service was slow and disorganized.

We ordered two pastas, two desserts, and one chicken steak. My friend’s chicken steak and the two desserts were served, but our pastas never came — even after waiting over 40 minutes and asking the staff twice to check.

In the end, we only paid for the chicken steak and the two desserts, and the other two items were refunded. It was a frustrating experience. Hope the management can look into improving both the service attitude and kitchen coordination.
author: Ash

review_text: Got our seats fast despite a long queue. Food is better than expected for us, long time customers of Saizeriya. Today's white wine is excellent! Staff are quick and responsive. A young muscular gentleman serving us overheard that we were going to share the dessert order; He brought us 3 dessert spoons when the dish was served! Really appreciate the attention to detail. Please let this young man know that we appreciate his kind gesture. Thank you very much!

Takagi is a soup ramen; the soup is thick and nice except a little oily. Goma Dorai is the dry ramen. The taste is good except it's a little salty and oily. Overall, it's value for money if you want to try Japanese food as it's generally pricey.

review_text:
We enjoy a nice Ramen at Takagi in Yew Tee from time to time.
Today we went for 2 dishes one a là carte one as set. For the set I chose a edamame set, the photo showing a tea and ramen, a set, and a green tea, both items mandatory to chose from the digital menu.
When we pick up the food it only came with 1 tea, despite the indicated tea in the edameme set and the separate tea. So i complained to William, the service staff on duty. After a short discussion, reviewing the digital, misleading menu card, he agreed to give a second tea. Great service from him 👌👌👌
You may wish to update your menu card to replace the misleading photo from your mandatory "sets".
We will come back, the food is nice. On the atmosphere, may be a bit noisy, but that's me.

The noodle bowl, at $8.80, felt a little underwhelming portion-wise, so just go for the set, which includes 4 生煎包 for $12.80.

The 红油抄手 were a pleasant surprise, not overly spicy and each dumpling was generously stuffed.

Overall a good dining experience, and will be looking forward trying their other dishes. Condiments are help-yourself. author: ShuMin. Tan

review_text:
one of the best catering experience that i’ve had!
fongfu catering really came through for us, they were highly recommended by a friend so we decided to give it a try and we’re really glad we did!

we ordered the fried rice, curry chicken, broccoli, mapo tofu, sweet and sour fried fish, salted egg pork, samosa, chin chow, ice lemon tea and some orange brownies!! everything tasted really delicious, and freshly prepared. the samosas weren’t as crispy, but that’s totally understandable given that it was a catering setup.

the portions were super generous. we ordered the 65 pax set ($977) for about 80 guests, and we still had so much food left! Honestly, 40-50 pax set would’ve been more than enough.

many of our guests were pleasantly surprised by the quality of the food and even asked how we found the caterer. it was really heartwarming to hear that everyone enjoyed the food.

the set up was swift, everything was ready before we even reached the venue. tear down was really quick too, staff on site was super patient (he waited for us to pack some of the leftovers). tip: do prepare some tupperwares for leftovers, food was still good till the next day.

overall, fongfu will definitely be our go-to food caterer from now on. highly recommended!

review_text:
So this will come across as unconventional but we actually engaged Loco Loco to provide our post-wedding dinner food! It was a secret kept by everyone except our wedding planner and us and it wasn't anything on their current menu (if you see it online after this review it was cause of our wedding!!).

We engaged Loco Loco to provide INDOMIE W/ NUGGETS AND SAUSAGES and honestly after a meal of fine dining what a way to open the after party. Our emcees announced that there was Indomie available at the back as a secret 7th course and flocks of people rushed to get their indomie fix!

Everyone thought it was so amazing and such a fun idea. We had it on a small food cart with the words emblazoned "INDOMIE" and what a fun way to end the night with alcohol, music and indomie!

Thank you for making our dream come true in the after party and I hope everyone reading this will get an idea to host an indomie (or any other instant noodle party for that matter) party for your wedding soon!

Love, C&J

author: Denise

review_text:
They weren’t kidding when they said “Eat until pain”!

We were treated to a hearty, home-cooked Peranakan meal hosted by Patricia, the wife of the late founding chef Jeffrey Chia. Patricia has lovingly upheld the high standards and spirit of his cooking, and throughout the meal, she shared touching stories about her husband’s passion for food.

By the end, we were not only full, but still had enough leftovers to bring home and savour all over again.

Sadly, Patricia mentioned that she won’t be able to continue doing this for long. So I would strongly recommend trying this slice of traditional Peranakan fare while you still can. A true gem.
author: Mervyn Sim

review_text:
Very bad experience with outlet at Pasir Ris Whitesands Cookhouse.

Recently, they hired a new staff who takes orders from customers. I have been a regular of JJ Food Express at this outlet because they serve decent tasting Japanese food. My family likes it as well, so I often take-away for them to enjoy at home. I usually request for take-away of their Miso Soup, which previous staffs have all been gladly doing so. However, this new staff always gives very little soup, amounting to only one ladle-full regardless of the number of bento sets I take-away. I always have to make a request for her to give me more (I heard other customers requesting the same too, showing that there are indeed other customers who were equally displeased with the lacklustre service). What is worse is that recently, that same new staff told me that there is no Miso Soup for take-away. That sounded odd because I have been a regular and the Miso Soup has always been given. I clarified with her on that, and she condescendingly told me that Miso Soup was indeed given in the past, but not now. The tone that she said it was definitely affecting customer experience.

A few moments later, she gave me some Miso Soup to take away after that conversation. She then told me that she does not give Miso Soup for take-away if she is busy attending to a lot of customers (ironically, there weren't any customers behind me, though there were some customers in front of me). She then told me off that I should just keep quiet and she would serve me Miso Soup when she judges by herself that she is free to do so.

That is terrible service as it implies that customers who take-away should be served lesser than that for customers who dine in. We are all customers, and I am not sure why she is able to attend to dine-in customers with their soup, but not to take-away customers.

I would strongly urge the management to look into this new staff's behavior as she has made quite a few customers upset with her bad attitude. I will not be patronizing again if I see this staff taking my orders at this outlet.

review_text:
Food is actually a celebration of culture, nature and life, which is why I’m so into it. And Tea Appreciation is definitely part of food culture, with the additional subtlety. So when I found out about an exclusive session on Tea Appreciation at Nature's Drop, I immediately looked up on this quaint little teahouse. Impressed with the setting and philosophy of the place, I did not hesitate to sign up for the session.

This teahouse serves excellent Chinese tea blends in a modern setting. And premium Chinese teas is well-loved for a good reason: unique, subtle aromas, smooth texture, right balance of astringent bitterness. In order to bring out these delicate properties in the tea leaves in measured amount,  preparation of the tea is done in certain way, such as whole leaves, optimal temperature of the water, heating up the pot first, seep the leaves for specific amount of time. It is a joy to prepare our own cups of tea, especially when it tastes so good. Yes, the three tea blends we have for the night each have distinctive, unique flavour profile, soothing and refreshing, in a subtle way.

Jasmine Red Tea is mild with light sweet flora aroma. Pu Er with glutinous rice is full of earthy goodness. The Floral blend is fruity with touches of floral scent. There is definitely a tea here that can pleases one's palates.

The teahouse has this tranquil zen atmosphere with willow plants, cherry wooden wall panels, spruce wooden furniture and white-washed walls. It is perfect for a relaxing, calming, soothing tea appreciation time or for a lovely gathering with friends or family.

The owners of Nature's Drop are very friendly and passionate about their teas, going into detail on the origins of the teas and the preparation of the teas. I really enjoy my time here. Appreciation of subtle things in life is so uplifting! Definitely one of my top choices to go for a relaxing good time.

Thoughts: Lovely Appreciation of Nature, Subtlety and Life through Cups of Tea

review_text:
Oh man, I've lived around here for many years but only found out about this place. I work from home all the time and have been going to this specific zi char store for the past 3 months.

They have single person meals for approximately $6 flat (You can pay with cash / card / paynow etc but the fairprice app for discount doesn't work with them). They cook food really fast. Not to give you the same expectation when you're there, but average they take 10mins to cook my meal (1 person).

I have tried their cream chicken cube, salted egg chicken, black pepper pork, black pepper fish, nyonya chicken — it's really good.

Can be salty a little at times but that's balanced with the generous amount of rice they give you, along with a piece of fried egg included. Most of the time they serve with green chilli but if you like spicy, feel free to ask for sambal or red chilli to kick up a notch!! But definitely, try the cream chicken. It's way too good 😭😭

I've read some of the low reviews down here and probably address the ones about insects. This is mainly due to rainy weather, and insects tend to fly around the lights. Sometimes if you're unlucky, they drop into your food. That happened to me a few times but I don't think it's justifiable to give them a low review for something they can't control.

Also, the staffs might look stern, but I had the opportunity to talk to them many times and they're really nice! Don't let looks deceive you!

review_text:
I ordered the Fuzhou Minced Meat Noodle (Item 3a on the menu), opting for Mee Pok. At $5.50 with extra noodles, it is a reasonably priced bowl given the portion size.
​
​Flavour Profile: The stall claims to offer "古早味" (traditional taste) dating back to 1985, and it definitely lives up to that promise. The flavour foundation is solid, largely thanks to the generous use of lard, which gave the noodles a wonderful, aromatic coating.

​The Noodles: The Mee Pok came topped with a generous heap of minced meat. Texture-wise, they were a little softer than I usually prefer. The bowl was also served a bit dry initially, but a quick drizzle of the accompanying soup solved that problem immediately, hydrating the noodles nicely and helping to mix the sauce evenly.

​The Ingredients: The highlight for me was the Fuzhou fishballs. They were excellent—bouncy on the outside and juicy on the inside with that savoury meat filling. It’s rare to find them done this well.

​The Verdict:
Despite the noodles being slightly on the soft side, the flavours here are on point. It’s a satisfying bowl of traditional noodles with great lard flavour and standout fishballs. I will definitely be coming back to try the other items on their extensive menu.

author: KW Chua

restaurant_name: 蛋佬 Dan Lao Scrambled Egg Rice
review_text:
I've now visited Danlao twice, and it's clear that the choice of topping makes all the difference. This is a solid spot for a comforting scrambled egg rice bowl, especially if you know what to order.

On both my visits, the two constants were the egg and the rice. As the name suggests, their scrambled egg good—cooked just right, soft and creamy, blanketing the rice underneath. While it's good and competently made, I wouldn't call it spectacular. The rice was also consistently well-cooked, with distinct grains (粒粒分明) and not mushy at all.

My first visit was a bit of a letdown. I had the Cheesy Char Siew bowl. The char siew was unfortunately on the dry side, and the "cheesy" element was simply a slice of processed cheese laid on top that hadn't fully melted. It felt like an afterthought and didn't add much to the dish.

However, my second visit was a significant improvement and the reason for the 4-star rating. I ordered the Classic Luncheon Meat and added on a Chicken Cutlet. The chicken cutlet was the undeniable highlight of the meal—perfectly crispy, juicy, and flavourful. It provided a fantastic textural contrast to the soft eggs and rice. The luncheon meat was standard fare, good but not memorable.

In conclusion, Danlao offers a satisfying meal, but the experience can be hit-or-miss depending on your protein choice. Based on my visits, I'd highly recommend skipping the char siew and going straight for the fried items, especially the excellent chicken cutlet.
author: Wiz Yeo

restaurant_name: 蛋佬 Dan Lao Scrambled Egg Rice
review_text: New branch at Senja Hawker Centre that is still finding its ground. Had the signature chicken chop scrambled egg rice. Liked the flavour of the fluffy soft scrambled egg. author: Brian Lim

review_text:
It's been over a year since I last visited this stall, and honestly, they used to have the best fish soup in the hood. I decided to revisit on a weekday afternoon, ordering the medium sliced fish soup with extra veggies and rice for $9.20. I don't mind paying a bit more if the food's good, but this visit was a huge letdown.

I really don't like to bash small businesses, especially knowing how tough things are for them these days, but hey, it's my hard-earned money too. As another reviewer pointed out, the batang fish barely tastes like itself anymore. My guess is they've started adding so much starch marinade that it completely alters the texture and that unique fishy umami batang is known for. Now, the fish just has that soft, almost mushy texture, pretty much like the dory or those fish slices you find in Chinese suan cai fish soup. Honestly, if they're going to treat batang like this, they might as well just use dory.

Only saving grace is the free flowing fresh condiments.

If you're still curious, I'd say skip the sliced fish and maybe try the fried fish instead. For me, though? No thank you.
author: Touristmouse

review_text:
The fish is super thin. Seems to have been treated with some process to the extent the meat has become completely tasteless, and breaks easily. Only has vegetables n some thin slices of fish even for the $8 paid.

I think this stall should close asap.

review_text: First time I am trying their fish porridge and must say the fish slices feel fresh. They also added the crispy batter on top of the soup so it is quite nice. Soup is clear and does not taste of msg. I finished almost the whole bowl. Especially yummy on a cold day where it is raining.

review_text: Medium sliced fish soup goes for $8 - portion is generous and fish is tender. Soup on the bland side, good for those who wants a light meal. Quite a long queue for it too.

author: Nathaniel Chew

restaurant_name: Ubi Le Sheng Yong Tau Foo (Senja Hawker)
review_text:
I tried the dry Yong Tau Foo from Ubi Le Sheng at Senja Hawker Centre and was very impressed with the quality of their items. For $9.60, I got 10 pieces ($8.00) plus Chee Cheong Fun ($1.60), which is quite reasonable.

The star of the show is undoubtedly the yong tau foo itself. All the pieces I chose were expertly cooked—the fried items remained crispy, and everything tasted fresh. The absolute must-try is their huge homemade fried meatball. It was flavourful, meaty, and had a fantastic texture that set it apart from the usual offerings.

Unfortunately, the experience was let down by my choice of carbohydrate, the Chee Cheong Fun. I found the rice noodle rolls to be disappointingly soft, lacking the springy, chewy bite that makes good CCF so satisfying. Thankfully, the generous serving of sweet sauce and chilli did a decent job of distracting from the textural issue.

Overall, this was still a very good and satisfying meal, thanks to the high quality of the yong tau foo. This is a stall I would definitely return to. Next time, I'll be pairing their excellent YTF with noodles or beef hoon instead, and I'm optimistic that could well be a 5-star experience.

review_text:
KFC at Mandai Lake Road is a convenient pit stop before or after the zoo, serving the familiar fried chicken, Zinger burgers and sides that most visitors expect.

The chicken usually lands in the “standard KFC” range – crispy enough and well‑seasoned, though nothing particularly special; fries and sides can feel a bit forgettable or salty depending on the batch.

Ambience is functional rather than cosy: a large, air‑conditioned food‑court style space that gets very crowded at peak zoo hours, so tables can be hard to find and the area can get noisy and messy.

Prices are higher than neighbourhood outlets and more expensive than many local hawker options, but still acceptable given the tourist‑zone location, with typical 2‑ or 3‑piece meals around standard Singapore KFC pricing.

Service is hit‑or‑miss – some staff are friendly and efficient, while others seem overwhelmed when queues build, which can mean slower clearing of tables and longer waits.

Overall a decent option in zoo.
