Challenges are finding carpark lots during peak meal hours, however, it's just next to Mrt Thomson East Coast Line TEL Springleaf Station Exit 1.
author: Ng Tiow Seng

restaurant_name: 928 Ngee Fou (Hakka) Ampang Yong Tou Fou
review_text:
The food here is decent and reasonably good. While it is the best I have eaten, it is good enough for me to return for more whenever I am in the vicinity.

The sauce and gravy is nice and the dish comes with lots of kang Kong vegetables. It’s welcoming to my family as we like to eat vegetables.

The Yong tau foo tasted alright. It would be nicer if there is more meat and fish paste in them. Also missing is the one done with red chili.

We also ordered the dumpling soup. This is quite forgettable.

Ambience is expected that if a coffee shop. Nothing to crow about.

Service is acceptable and certainly not expecting any at a coffee shop.

Parking can be a chore. However, the MRT station is right in front of the shop, which is a plus.

Overall, worth a visit if one is in the area.
author: Choon Kit Leong

restaurant_name: 928 Ngee Fou (Hakka) Ampang Yong Tou Fou
review_text: Ordered standard 2 pax set which cost $17+ with rice.  The food is served to your table.  I have been eating here for some time already.  Standard still maintained.  Enjoy the umami sauce mixed with the different items of fried and steam tau fou, spinach, fried been curd, fish balls, quail eggs, brinjal, bitter gourd.  Satisfying!
author: Susan Tay

restaurant_name: 928 Ngee Fou (Hakka) Ampang Yong Tou Fou
review_text: 928 Ngee Fou is a solid go for Ampang-style Yong Tau Foo in Singapore — especially if you appreciate tradition, generous portions, and comfort-food vibes. The flavours and value generally deliver.
author: IamDrew1979

restaurant_name: 928 Ngee Fou (Hakka) Ampang Yong Tou Fou
review_text: This Ampang style yong tau foo located along Upper Thomson is the more popular ytf option. The staff would prep the nos of assorted ytf items according to the nos of pax. The dish is drenched with starchy sweet sauce. Comforting dish, felt like a homecooked meal. Could enjoy it with or without rice. Perhaps there could be an option to choose between rice & noodles.
author: The Rundown

review_text: Services by staffs and boss are great. We dine on Sun 5pm. So managed to get the 10% off. We ordered a 2 paxs set, add on a pork collar and 3 cold barley tea. Very filling for us even through we didn’t order rice. The side dishes are good. Best part the restaurant accept cdc. Just take note the aircon area isn’t big as the place use fans. The soy sauce pork collar kind of very dry and tough due we are not fast enough so the serving grill plate kind of continued cooking even on our table. We spent around s$90. No GST charged, there is service fee. Payment mode I think only cash / paynow or nets.
author: MOUSE AK

review_text: absolutely pleased with my first experience here! food was first of all delicious, portion was generous, price reasonable, service top notched. rarely do i find places that offers refillable fresh lettuce but they do! restaurant is tucked in a cozy corner of the road too! recommend patroning ohh
author: elderwanda

review_text:
Visited Friends Tasty Korea for about 4/5x in total, and they never cease to guarantee a satisfactory KBBQ experience. Their banchan (side dishes) are fresh , refillable, and tasty enough to even satisfy your hunger. Their BBQ platers come with steam eggs, a kimchi stew, and the meats (pork/beef) which they will grill for you. All the elements of the KBBQ platter will guarantee you leave the place happily filled.

Additionally, the owner and the workers have amazing customer service and attitudes that will ensure your needs are met. Do give this restaurant a try and you will not be disappointed, it is definitely one of my go-to places for KBBQ in SG
author: ZX Thian

review_text:
The food is delicious and the service is excellent.Great food with friendly and attentive service.
Amazing food and top-notch service! Highly recommended.
Delicious dishes and very good service. A wonderful dining experience.
The food was tasty, and the staff were very polite and helpful
author: Như Ý Nguyễn

review_text: My family go to supper spot! Owner offered to heat up the soup after noticing one of our family member joined the meal late. Staff always remember to refill despite busy operation. Thankful for the early and hearty meal always!
author: Baofei Teo

review_text:
Ordered merlion breakfast set tht consist of two soft boil eggs, two piece if toast.

Toast is nice. But egg came raw. When i complained, they microwaved the eggs. Still looks raw.

Where is the integrity as a chef/food handler?
author: Amber Seah

review_text: We recently had the pleasure of enjoying lunch here, a hidden gem tucked away amidst lush greenery. They surprised me with their 𝗖𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗯𝗿𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗶𝗱 𝗪𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀, so finger-licking, must try! The highlight of our meal was undoubtedly the 𝗚-𝘀𝗽𝗼𝘁 𝗕𝗲𝗲𝗳 𝗕𝘂𝗿𝗴𝗲𝗿 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗲𝘀𝗲 𝗙𝗼𝘂𝗻𝘁𝗮𝗶𝗻. Each bite was a burst of flavor, with the perfectly cooked beef patty and the indulgent cheese. Will visit again!
author: Connie Lim

review_text:
Tried out this bistro (open to public) at Mandai Executive Golf Course since we were at the nearby Seletar Reservoir Park. It is a pretty serene place to chill out and have light bites while enjoying the view of the golf greens. A nice change from the usual hustle and bustle of the city.

Menu is fusion, with a decent variety of food options. We really liked the G-Spot Cheese Burger, grilled squid and the salmon avocado tartare. For the kids, we got them the crabmeat fried rice and celebrity mid wings which they enjoyed too!
author: Charlene & YZ

review_text:
Dining at Golf Spot Cafe & Bistro in Singapore offers beautiful greenery and serene surroundings. Even if you don’t play golf, it is a great way to combine your meal with the golf course’s landscape. It does provide a tranquil backdrop for dining, creating such a peaceful and enjoyable atmosphere.

If you’re a cheese lover, I’m sure you will love at first sight of that flowing cheese over your yummy Wagyu beef burger!
author: whatoeatagain sg

review_text: Dine at Golf Spot Cafe & Bistro for a few times already. Love the atmosphere, with nice greenery surrounding. Great place to hang out with my friends. Food choices and quality are great too. Highly recommended! 👍🏼
author: Jasmine Yao

review_text: Fried rice was fantastic. Drinks are decent, a bit on the sweeter side. But not diluted at all. Value for money. Nice ambience, good place to chill.
author: Jeremy Moi

review_text: Sambal fried rice was tasty and stall owners were friendly!
author: Brandon Ng

review_text: Food got good value, large portions. Spent about 8$ for tomyam fried rice add egg add chicken cutlet and a bottle of ice coffee. If you get posted to nee soon camp and happen to have free time, definitely make the pilgrimage to this cafe for lunch. One complaint I will make is that the tomyam flavour not well dispersed. Got some bites of rice no taste and got some too much.
author: Mikhail Sufyan

review_text:
Food is really good value for money compared to other SAF messes and canteens, with curry chicken rice being $5. The mess is also covered with plenty of fan coverage, with clean tables and chairs.

The curry was decent but lacked spice, however that's just personal preference.
author: aren

review_text: Had breakfast here, food is generally good, does require a little effort to get here. The stall auntie is very friendly, and they accept cashless payments. Have yet to try their lunch menus.
author: Zi He Goh

restaurant_name: Wong Chiew Restaurant 皇潮餐室
review_text: Came with friends on the fourth day of Chinese New Year, and we had dinner there together. The Lo Hei Yu Sheng serving was big. Do take note that it consists of imitation abalone slices, but we can't complain as the serving was really big. It can serve about 10 pax. The yusheng vegetables were abundant, with two packs of crackers. It was value for money at $33.80nett. The other dishes were good as well, especially the curry fish head, cereal prawns, and salted egg sotong. The fish maw soup was tasty as well. Herbal chicken and trio eggs spinach can be better. There is no service charge and GST applicable, hence it was a really affordable meal. We were seated at the air-conditioned dining area a few doors away, and it was very conducive and quiet enough for our gathering. We will consider to go again. Service was great as well. The staff were friendly and attentive. Parking is available across the road at Hong Heng Mansion.
author: Pearlyn

restaurant_name: Wong Chiew Restaurant 皇潮餐室
review_text: Food isn’t amazing, ordered duck noodles, char siew roasted pork rice and some dim sum. Prefer the rice over noodles. Duck is a bit too tough, depending on the parts but I like the roasted pork. Take note that there’s an aircon area so don’t just sit at the stall there. I took the outdoor seat and it’s not good at all, there are a lot of birds and chickens so when ppl left, the birds came and eat the leftovers. Dim sum also took a while to arrive.
author: JX

restaurant_name: Wong Chiew Restaurant 皇潮餐室
review_text: One afternoon around 2:30 PM, I was driving by when I spotted a coffee shop by the roadside. Noticing it was quite empty after lunchtime, I decided to park and grab a quick bite. I ordered a dark soy sauce chicken drumstick served with fragrant rice. As soon as I took my first bite of the aromatic rice paired with tender chicken, I knew I had to share my experience of this stall. The dish was exactly the flavor I had been searching for for years. The rice was wonderfully fragrant and moist, while the chicken was smooth and juicy—truly perfect for my taste buds. I have no doubt my family would love it too!
author: JonXu

restaurant_name: Wong Chiew Restaurant 皇潮餐室
review_text: Liu Sa  buns we ordered  were spoilt ones n staff changed  to char siew buns for us. Chicken porridge turn to watery very fast n their fried red bean strips taste of horrifying due to the oil repeated frying did not changed. As customers we won’t want to stepped in to this coffee shop anymore. Their standard dropped significantly
author: Jacqueline Lim

restaurant_name: Wong Chiew Restaurant 皇潮餐室
review_text:
+ One of the cheaper eateries near Nee Soon Camp, compared to  The Brooks I and II opposite across Thomson Road.

+ Opens from 6am till 11pm/1am daily. 33 Sembawang Eating House just down the street is also opened till late, but most of their stalls are closed by dinner time.

+ Authentic Cantonese dim-sum and roasted delights/ wanton mee. The charsiew is wonderful.

- No menu or prices displayed on signboard. Prices are slightly higher than other similar hawker stalls, e.g.
@ Wanton Mee ($4.30) Add noodles for $1.50
@ Roast Duck Rice ($5)
@ Roast Duck + Roast Pork Rice ($6)
@ Vegetables 油菜 ($5)
@ Lime Juice ($2)

+ Portions are thankfully slightly larger than usual.

- Hargow was freshly made/steamed, but the skin fell apart too easily when picked up by chopsticks.

+ Seating - They took over another shophouse unit and has 10 more tables over there, so seating should not be a problem.

- However, parking is a challenge. Limited unmarked parking along Thong Bee Rd.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text: Small cafe providing indonesian style food. Service staff was friendly, smiling and fantastic. Food pricing is affordable. Car park is available too. Beef rendang was very tasty with multitude of spices and heat. Gado gado is good and they do allow separation of sauce. Goreng pisang ball need to refine its texture. Drink was also good. Overall a great food experience. The food outlet is beside a small park for those light work out before a good meal.
author: Randy Tan

review_text:
An unusual little Indon find tucked away in a park … easy to miss, but worth the detour. We tried afew dishes, and the clear winner was the beef rendang: incredibly tender, deeply flavourful, and slow-cooked to perfection.

The chicken sambal belado was enjoyable, though the sambal leaned a bit too salty for my taste😓. A savoury-SWEET balance would have lifted it to the next level. (Owner pls note 🤭)

Bonus points for convenient gantry parking nearby, which makes this hidden spot even easier to love. A great place to explore Indonesian flavours, with the rendang stealing the show.

Do check for opening hrs before u go.
author: Josephine Tan

review_text: Caught the lunch deal today! The Grilled Chicken smells amazing and is cooked so well that it falls right off the bone, but the meat itself was a little tough and lacked tenderness on the inside. Tried the Blueberry Lemon too - it’s a good choice if you don’t like sugary drinks, but the flavor is very subtle (almost too faint). Parking is easy!
author: K

review_text:
The food quality is very good and delicious.

However, we were quite disappointed with the presentation. Based on what we saw on social media, the food is usually served on banana leaves directly on the table, but ours was served on a tray instead, which made the overall experience feel less special.

Not sure what happened, but for the price paid, I believe presentation does matter.

On a positive note, there is ample car park space within the park area, and the staff are attentive.
author: Chai Fong Lee

review_text: Got in before 12noon. Had the grilled ox-tail rice set before at the TPY branch so decided to try the fried chicken sambar set instead for lunch at the Springleaf outlet. Ordered and paid at the counter and sat down in the air-conditioned indoor area. There was no crowd on a weekday afternoon and soon I was served the food within 10 mins. Did not expect the fried chicken to have such a light crispy batter. Thought the chicken meat would be dry inside but was delightfully surprised it was still tender on the inside. The balado looked spicy but was totally manageable and on the light savoury side. Came with refreshing slices of cucumber to cut the grease and crackers for the crunch and change in texture. Overall a good meal. Will want to try other things on the menu.
author: Desmond Ling

review_text: Housed within the famous yong tau foo eatery. Sambal was quite balanced, giving a slight spicy kick. Soup was like the typical fishball noodle kind.
author: The Rundown

review_text: Went at 2pm, Fuzhou fishball sold out. Tried minced meat instead. Soup and chilli tasted different from the usual.
author: Elite

review_text:
FOOD
Fu Zhou fishball was a little too salty with msg, but texture was soft and bouncy. Noodles was mid, missing the pork lard!
Carrot cake was sweet, nice and delicious!
author: Javier Tan

review_text:
Always there for YTF but... ... Today let's do something different...

💗 my Laksa soup thick... My husband gave a 👍🏻 Thumb Up to the 🦐 noodles. Yy carrot cakes still good...
author: Angie Goh

review_text:
This stall sells fishball noodle & also fried carrot cakes.

When we were there, only a young girl who seems to be in her teenage year was there attending to customers…

Honestly I was doubtful of her skills as she is young & dun seem experienced… but her sunshine smile & friendly approach made the wait bearable 😀😀

We ordered the “yuan yang carrot cake” and it was very nice!!!  Thumbs up to the young teenage girl for the hard work!
author: 阿宝

review_text:
This unassuming American-themed casual dining spot serves up the heartiest nostalgic favourites & alcohol, AND is CDC-friendly with no service charge !!

I had their Sausage Platter ($19.50), which had well-seasoned chicken, pork sausage & beef hot dogs with onions and fries. Pretty addictive — sausages weren’t overly salty, & fries had just the right crisp.

Fried Brussel Sprouts ($12.50) had bacon bits dressed in sriracha honey mayo. Portion size looked a bit small, but taste-wise, nothing to fault.

Cheesesteak Sandwich ($23) had thinly sliced beef rump, melted cheddar, sautéed onions & green pepper in savoury homemade brown sauce, packed into warm, crispy toasted ciabatta with mildly spicy Cajun fries. Tender, umami, & so yummy.

Thick Lamb Chops ($29) was 450g, grilled medium doneness, with mushroom cream sauce, tangy mint sauce (my friend liked this as it helped cut through the gaminess) & baked beans. Better eaten fast — it hardened a bit in the cold aircon :”)

Insane New Orleans Bread Pudding ($11.50) had bread loaf, milk, vanilla extract, spices & tequila sauce — this is sweet, warm & dense without feeling jelak. Couldn’t taste the tequila, but insanely addictive for sure.

Warm Banana Cake w Rocky Road Ice Cream is homemade with salted caramel, vanilla ice cream, marshmallow & toasted almond. Loved the warm-cold contrast and prominent banana flavour !!

Free water provided; coffee, tea, beers & cocktails available too!

Honestly, dishes are pretty reasonably priced for the quality, & this is a spot I’d consider if I’m in the area :)
author: Sera // IG: diningwithsera

review_text:
This place is truly a hidden gem in the north. We really liked how they offered a DIY breakfast platter in their menu so we can just choose what we like. Coffee was great. Food was good.

The walkway is also big enough so it doesn’t feel so claustrophobic for the outside seating area when the public walks by. (A plus point for dog owners.)

Only downside is the shortage of parking space nearby but thankfully there’s a carpark a short walk away (at Springleaf park).

Overall lovely place! We will definitely be back. 😊
author: LY

review_text: Comfort food at very good price! Beer and red wine promotion available too. Chilli con carne, grilled salmon, honey chicken, ribeye steak, blackened fish, waffles are a must order!!! Can choose you sides which is good to share too, fries, grilled vegetables and more.
author: Cherrlyn Lim

review_text:
This is such a rare find. I pass by this place several times and decided to eat in this place. A local owned diner with good food charging reasonable prices with no service charge. Accepts CDC vouchers and has Wifi.

I had the Honey baked chicken which has a savoury, lightly sweet and citrusy juice; Chicken Gumbo was peppery and flavourful; and the Fish & Chip was lightly breaded which is the standard way of doing a good Fish & Chip. Overall very filling and satisfying.
author: Sean Lee

review_text:
Awesome place, i paid $12 (excluding 9% GST) for the (dinner) brunch-set cajun chicken, LP mushrooms and Lyonnaise potato. Everything was very well done, the chicken was a little bit dry, but the grilled taste and cajun seasoning makes up for it. Their homemade salsa was super good, and the tortillas r quite normal.

Had abit of lamb, steak and ribs as well from sharing with my party, and they were all very well done too.

Steak was medium rare, super nice and juicy.

The ribs were a little dry, but the seasoning made up for it in flavour.

Overall, some absolute bangers, and some stuff done better than average. Abit pricey, but for the quality of everything, absolutely worth it.
author: Cath Palug

restaurant_name: 922 Beng Cheng Hakka Ampang Yong Tau Fu
review_text:
Not been here for a long time.
Food is just as good.
Ordered a plate for 2 with extra fried bean curd skin.
Came with lots of Kang kong veg, tofu, soft brinjal, fried wanton, stuffed green chilli with fish cake?fried tauhu...
Also got a bowl of wanton soup.
Yammee...
Enjoyed coming back here.
Brought back memories when I used to come here often during reservist training late 1990s.
author: Colin Liew

restaurant_name: 922 Beng Cheng Hakka Ampang Yong Tau Fu
review_text: Had lunch with the family there after a few years of not visiting. Fried options were freshly fried, but the gravy was really salty, and not as flavorful as before. Price was very expensive. Just 4 rice, a bowl of wanton soup and their signature Hakka Yong Tau Foo. $51. No drinks. Suggest to ask them the price first before ordering.

restaurant_name: 922 Beng Cheng Hakka Ampang Yong Tau Fu

Haven’t been here for a long time. Parking is a problem here. That’s one of the reason we haven’t been coming. Yong tofu not as good. Standard dropped tremendously. Very salty.

Hubby order a plate of kway chap. That was really salty as well.
author: J

restaurant_name: 922 Beng Cheng Hakka Ampang Yong Tau Fu
review_text: Ordered Yong Tau Foo and Kway Chap. The YTF was okay—nothing particularly special. But the Kway Chap was a letdown: too salty and had an overpowering pig intestine taste.
author: LP Pua

restaurant_name: 922 Beng Cheng Hakka Ampang Yong Tau Fu
review_text:
I think the duck meat is very nice.
And the 酿豆腐 Kang kong especially nice!
Parking is a problem as hard to get parking lot. Went for massage nearby that why walk over.
Resend review here as I realise I post in wrong stall.. 🫣
author: EL

review_text:
This is by far one of the best mookata places I’ve ever eaten at. The restaurant is quite far inside, and it can get very hot, but thankfully it was quiet despite having over 1,000 reviews. The location itself is a bit inconvenient, especially if you’re staying in the north or east — and parking is definitely not easy to find.

But the service makes up for it. The waiters were awesome and friendly, always smiling. The meat was tender, tasty, well-marinated, and juicy. Really enjoyed the mookata here. Would come back again despite the distance.
author: Britney Khu

review_text:
Overall nice and somewhat fun dinner experience here.  Seated at a big round table outdoor.  Plus points:

1) Reasonably priced Hotpot - well stock set:

Basic set aka Yum Mak Mak Set ($39.90 Nett) comes with meat and seafood, such as marinated pork, marinated chicken, pork belly, pork liver, prawns, squid, crabstick, meatballs, fish balls, and hotdogs. Plus basket of Chinese cabbage, xiao bai cai, spinach, vermicelli, beancurd skin, enoki mushroom and two eggs.

For 5 of us, we added on prawns, pork, tofu cheese, thai abalone, thai mama noodles and quail eggs. For drinks, we had cold lemongrass.

2) Ingredients are fresh - Meat not heavily marinated and sliced thinly, prawns are fresh.

3) Staff are friendly and attentive

“Minus” points:
Non airconditioned. Blind does not block away totally the strong late afternoon sun.
author: Harriot NN

review_text: A quiet and cosy place for mookata — nice if you prefer a more relaxed atmosphere. The food was okay and generally enjoyable. There was a small miscommunication and we only got the chilli towards the end, which was a bit of a pity since the chilli really makes a difference for mookata. Still, the overall experience was pleasant and the staff were polite.
author: Y. X. Wong

review_text: really good supper spot located right outside upper thomson mrt station! service was attentive and the meat in the $39.90 (no svc & gst) set for 2 pax was delicious. charcoal grill was superb! highly recommend
author: Carolyn Ng

review_text: Popped by on a Sunday at 11am and was thankful they were open 🤩 got their chicken rice with drink combo and was blown away by the tastiness of the food 🍚 the rice alone was so flavourful that I couldn’t wait to put another spoonful in to my mouth ❤️ I’m sure it is very popular for its mookata which I’ll be sure to return and try one day
author: Marklin Ho

review_text:
underrated place outside springleaf mrt. everything i ordered was delicious. i ordered fish, chicken, kambing soup, 2 ginger tea and 1 lassi for $21.40 (check the pics)

the owner might stare you down but he's just attentive to his customers. never seen a guy so eager to serve customers that i felt compelled to leave a review. great experience i highly recommend.
author: milk

review_text:
We got the cheese onion egg prata and the cheese egg prata. It was really good and cheap - a really quaint little spot right outside springleaf MRT.

We also got the chili chicken, which was more like chicken 65 than chili chicken (typically chili chicken would include some sort of gravy).

The tea was also quite refreshing and nice! Overall a good spot for late night prata indulgences.
author: Aravind K. Saravana

review_text:
Food is cooked. Very salty.

But there are nice and uncommonly seen dishes like pongal, upma and Puri! I love the pongal
author: Matthew Leong

review_text: Dosai was tasty and not bland. Prata was thick kind, could be fluffier and more soft but its just personal preference. Just a little bit pricier but their portion makes up for it. Will be back if in the area
author: JY Lee

review_text: Freshly made prata that is crispy and flaky for the kosong and the egg is chewy. Served with 2 different curries and a sweet chili makes it a wonderful meal for breakfast or tea break. Definitely one of the better prata places in Singapore.
author: Jeremy Matthew

review_text:
⭐️ Springleaf Roti Prata: Crispy Perfection in a Cool Setting!

If you’re cruising down Upper Thomson and looking for a reliable spot to satisfy your prata cravings, Springleaf Roti Prata at Springleaf Estate is a fantastic choice. It’s an iconic location for a reason, offering a comfortable dining experience that’s a step up from your usual open-air coffeeshop.

If you are a fan of serious crunch, this is your place. The prata here is exceptionally crispy—each bite offers that satisfying shattered-pastry sound that many prata lovers dream of. Personally, I tend to lean towards a more doughy, chewy style of prata, so while these were technically very well-made, they didn't quite hit my "best ever" list. However, for anyone who prioritizes that golden, flaky exterior, these are undeniably top-tier.

The set came with unlimited self serving of fish curry, which was pleasant and well-balanced, though it leans towards a mildly spicy profile. For those who, like me, prefer their curry to be a fiery, mouth-numbing experience, this version might feel a bit tame. That said, it’s a very accessible flavor that won't overwhelm those with a lower spice tolerance, and it complements the crispy prata without masking its taste.

One of the biggest draws of this particular outlet is that the restaurant is air-conditioned. It makes the dining experience clean and comfortable, especially during a hot Singapore afternoon. It’s a great place to hang out and have a long chat without breaking a sweat.

It seems they take their time to ensure that every prata comes out perfectly crisp, so don't come here if you're in a massive rush. However, the wait is justified once that hot, crackling plate hits the table.

ISpringleaf is a breath of fresh air from the usual fiercely competitive prata market because they’ve carved out such a specific identity for themselves.

Even if it isn't the absolute "best" I've ever had, I still really love the prata here and would highly recommend it for a solid, reliable meal in a great environment!
author: Frederick Tan

review_text: Very nice place to have prata. They are quite creative with their tissue prata, quite a few of varieties, i ordered the red bean tissue with a smile on my face, crispy and sweetness is just right.  Highly recommended.
author: Lim Jason

review_text:
Murtabak (SGD $12) @ Springleaf Prata Place.
.
Opened by S.V. Gunalan in February 2003, this popular chain of eateries is best known for their 'Ultimate' series - modern and creative prata inventions, with 1 new creation every year since the inaugural Singapore Food Festival Ultimate Hawker Fest in October 2012.
.
The Mini Ultimate Murtabak (SGD $10.90), created in October 2012, features crispy soft dough folded and loaded with tender chunky marinated spiced tandoori chicken, bouncy portobello mushrooms, wispy chicken egg, and gooey mozzarella cheese. Has smoky bready eggy vegetal earthy meaty savoury sweet salty cheesy flavour.
.
The Double Murtaburger (SGD $12), created in October 2013, features crispy soft dough folded and stacked with 2 juicy minced lamb patties, wispy chicken egg, thick black pepper sauce, rich chili sauce, and gooey mozzarella cheese. Resembling a classic Ramly Burger, this carries smoky bready eggy meaty savoury salty cheesy peppery spice flavour.
.
Pair with thick chicken curry with sweet savoury salty spice flavour, or thin fish curry with fishy savoury salty spice flavour.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text: Springleaf prata never fails. What I love about this outlet is their accessibility as it is just beside the MRT station. And this place is serene and quiet because the surrounding area is a landed enclave. Compared to the outlet at Tampines Safra, somehow their fish curry here is nicer.  I will definitely come back here again though I stay at Bedok. Just take a bus to Siglap MRT and take TEL line and it is super convenient.
author: Justin Thong

review_text: Springleaf Prata Place @ Springleaf is where I first met my Queen. We have different prata eating styles and preferences but it doesn’t conflict or affect each of us eat. Very cutely, I’m a rock throw away from my house’s very own Springleaf Prata Place too. Still finds this more memorable and filled with meanings. Anyway overpriced for a prata but the quality is high standard. Seats wise a little bit scarce, especially on the weekend.
author: Kong Wen Sheng

restaurant_name: 四海珍餐馆 si hai zhen restaurant
review_text: Steam Chicken here is super nice. The curry fish head also very rich and tasty. Honestly, every dish we ordered was good, no misses at all. Definitely worth coming back again!!!
author: VHong Tan

restaurant_name: 四海珍餐馆 si hai zhen restaurant
review_text:
Really good tzechar place that’s affordable! We got the curry fish head for only $30 and it was spicy shiok that goes so well with rice. Stir fry veges were very freshly cooked. Pork knuckle was a miss though, can skip I feel. We also got the half white chicken and it’s really tender even the breast meat.

Will def be back for more. Remember to reserve in advance as it’s really crowded during dinner time. I think one issue is the parking but nothing much can be done about it.
author: Kah Wang Tan

restaurant_name: 四海珍餐馆 si hai zhen restaurant
review_text: Good service with affordable pricing. The tze-char dishes were enjoyable—in fact, I found them better than the chicken rice. The place feels comfortable and welcoming, making it easy to settle in for a meal. I look forward to coming back to try more from the menu.
author: KC Wong

restaurant_name: 四海珍餐馆 si hai zhen restaurant
review_text: Good quality food and comfortable environment, will be back to try the zichar dishes. Prices are economical with no gst and service charge, crabs were going at 2 for $90.
author: Kosong Belly

restaurant_name: 四海珍餐馆 si hai zhen restaurant
review_text:
We had the Garlic Sweet Potato Leaves, Enoki Mushroom Tofu, San Bei Claypot Chicken, and HK Sotong. They all tasted great, my favourites were the tofu and the chicken. The tofu gravy was thick and rich, and the tofu was so fresh and soft! The claypot chicken tasted so homely and the basil was a lovely touch!

The portions are really generous, we ordered 4 dishes for 3 pax and though the food was great, it was a little too much for us.

Service was good and fast too! Would recommend to my friends and family next time :-)
author: Seetha S.

restaurant_name: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记
review_text:
Hong Ji serves exceptional Bak Kut Teh with aromatic herbal flavours. As well as the food being delicious, the value you get here is unmatched. The pork Bak Kut Teh I ordered was only $7, and had so much meat that I asked for another bowl of rice. Amazing service from the restaurant as well, they were friendly and took care of any problems I had.
Overall, amazing restaurant experience and food at hawker food prices. Cannot recommend this restaurant enough!
author: Andy Ma

restaurant_name: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记
review_text: Very wholesome herbal bak kut teh. When you dont feel thirsty after that. You know they are thr real deal. They sell prawn noodles too. Many diners order too. Will try next time. Update: The prawn stock is v clean. Prawns are sweet. Its very good.
author: Chobo Chocobo

restaurant_name: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记
review_text: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记 offers exceptional claypot bak kut teh with a rich, aromatic herbal broth that perfectly complements the tender pork ribs. Their signature dish comes with generous portions of fried tofu, lettuce, and delicious side dishes including kidney beans and pickled vegetables. The casual setting opposite Springleaf MRT provides an authentic Singaporean dining experience with reasonable prices. A hidden gem for traditional herbal bak kut teh enthusiasts. 😊👍🏻✨
author: Local Guide .: : :::

restaurant_name: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记
review_text: Came for the herbal bak kut teh, but it was very meh. You'd probably like it if you like milder taste, but can definitely get richer tasting ones elsewhere. Should have seen the red flags when they are also selling other types of non bak kut teh type food (prawn mee, braised pork rice, etc)
author: Darren Ho

restaurant_name: Hong Ji Herbs Bak Kut Teh 宏记
review_text: BKT herbal soup was light and fragrant. Lots of ingredients. Mee sua and prawn soup were tasty and flavourful.
author: Anna Lee

review_text:
A small place with cosy setting. Staffs were welcoming & service was prompt.

Ordered their beef hor fun which was highly praised by many. I like how the dish was loaded with wok hei. Beef slices were tender, could taste the usage of baking soda though. Hor fun was tender & blanketed with a layer of thick savoury beefy gravy. The fermented beans were infused intensely into the dish making it more aromatic. Every mouthful was such a delight.
author: The Rundown

review_text:
Having tried beef noodles across the island, we saw this place from the bus window and simply had to try it. What a great decision! The service was excellent, with smiling and friendly and efficient staff, while the chef was working his/her magic in the kitchen.  The seating is cozy, the ‘outdoor’ feel is cooled by ceiling fans. There is even a washroom/toilet. The food was super tasty with help-yourself chili to compliment the already fantastic tastes even further! 3 thumbs up to this establishment. We will be back…, you must visit! You WILL become a regular here! Note: this place is closed on Mondays! Always delicious, always friendly on every visit!

It’s not often that a restaurant manages to maintain its magic after relocating—but this beloved spot has not only carried its charm to its new home near Springleaf MRT, it’s elevated the experience altogether.

From the moment you step into the new closed premises, the cool embrace of air conditioning is an instant win—especially welcome after a long day or a warm walk. But it’s the familiar warmth of the staff, ever-smiling and attentive, that truly makes the difference. Service here hasn’t skipped a beat; it remains friendly, efficient, and full of heart.

And then, of course, there’s the food. Oh, the food. Still absolutely top-notch—authentic, generous, and packed with flavour in every bite. Whether you’re a returning regular or a curious first-timer, each dish delivers that same consistent excellence that earned it such loyal fans in the first place. Portions are hearty, the ingredients fresh, and every meal leaves you full and deeply satisfied.

The move has brought nothing but positives: more comfort, better accessibility, and the same unbeatable taste. If you haven’t visited the new location yet, do yourself a favour—go. It’s every bit as worth it as it ever was, if not more.
author: Pete Klimek

review_text: Fried carrot cake was nice and slightly crispy. Beef hor fun with wokhey. Beef is tender.
author: Yvonne A

review_text:
Chance upon this restaurant. Can be quite crowded during peak period.

All the dishes were really delicious. Highly recommend trying the Beef hor fun & frog leg with porridge. They are really good!

Price is afforable! Worth trying!
author: munchwithvienna

review_text: An absolute gem discovered by accident! For the record, didn't even order their signature beef hor fun. The frog legs served in a claypot was definitely above average. The porridge of generous proportion was served in a claypot too. Both can't go without the you tiao which was slightly crispy and not too oily. And the dish that impressed us the most? The Yee fu noodles! This was 100% restaurant standard that you can hardly find in coffee shops or even zi char stalls. Love this place and will be back! Definitely trying their signature dishes the next time!
author: Al Lim

review_text:
Famous for their beef hor fun. However, the flavour is clearly missing as compared to the one originally from Geylang. Beef slices are rather tough and chewy.

Dim sum choices and taste are good though
author: Dewy

review_text: Superb beef hor fun! Really tasty and valued for money
author: TC

review_text: Great beef kway teow. Dim Sum is decent too and my parents enjoyed their Bee Hoon
author: Patrick Kay

review_text: Shiok food
author: Angel Tan

review_text: Almost as good as the original location!
author: Karsten Heil

review_text:
Ordered prawn dumpling, pork dumpling, 小笼包，fried carrot cake, steam rice rolls w shrimp, frog congee, 干炒牛河，韭菜水晶包, fried chicken skin. The wok hei for the stir fried beef horfun was excellent.  The fillings of the dumplings are generous and QQ texture. Frog congee is smooth and flavourful. Only the fried chicken skin is a tad hard. Overall food is tasty. Most of all, we are most impressed by the integrity of this restaurant. Originally ordered 3 servings of congee thinking that each is only enough for one person. Aunty at the restaurant made the effort to advise that each order of congee comes in an earthen pot enough for a few people. ( not the typical small bowl) She suggested that we reduce to just one congee.
This, and the excellent food has won us over.  We shall certainly eat here again.
author: Cherylggwifi Tay

review_text:
We tried 3 dishes and all were great!

1. Fried dumplings with pork & seafood 👍
2. Beef hor fun 👍
3. Prawn paste chicken chop noodles 👍

1. Fried dumplings with pork and seafood looked lackluster but don't be fooled by the appearance! The pork and shrimp were a good mix (great texture) and the frying batter tasted fresh and not stale!

2. Beef hor fun tasted like beef char kway teow with tender slices of beef! Came with great wok hey and good mixture of black sauce and eggs 👍 Portion was huge too!

3. Prawn paste chicken chop is juicy and tender and noodles were like fresh la mian texture! No weird alkaline taste and not too soggy! A little chewy and the portion was huge too!

We prefer to sit outside cause it's quite echo-ish in the shop! They have 2 shops just right across the road and there's no difference in the food served  between the two 👍 They accept CDC vouchers too!
author: kopiandmilktea

review_text: Originally wanted to come here for the beef kway teow but it seems like the shop has been taken over. Nonetheless we settled for some Zichar and dimsum. Food was pretty good with decent prices. The HCG wasn’t the best also there was no chili provided.
author: Kenny Yap

review_text: Yangzhou fried rice, pork ribs king, broccoli, honey citron tea, and milk tea were good. Roasted pork fried rice and chicken porridge were bland. Food is served fast. Can walk in at 6pm, gets crowded after. Parking is limited, location is fantastic as it is right above mrt exit.
author: Joyce Lim

review_text: Had breakfast: century egg porridge, siew mai, char siew cheong fun, prawn mango puff, pan fried carrot cake. Siew Mai has not fatty meat. Porridge came in a claypot with large portion at $6.50. Carrot cake was crispy on the outside and soft inside. We also had a kopi o and a horlicks. Total $31.
author: Rachel Ang

review_text:
First thought after dining at this place, "I NEED TO BRING MY MOM HERE COS SHE'S GONNA LOVE THIS"

Must try: pan fried dumpling, har kao.

The portions were generous, the seafood was fresh, and the pan fried dumplings were well fried, not oily! The steam pork ribs and San Lou Hor Fan were full of flavor. Pity it's a small place so it gets packed quite easily, but it's worth coming down to have a meal with your family if you're up for a good dim sum, Hong Kong food!!
author: Lee Miao Wen

review_text: Confused staff poor management. Was told can use CDC voucher prior to ordering but was rejected when making payment. Was informed not allowed after 10pm cos collection of money by different boss.  Food first round was acceptable. When 2nd round of order, fish cake fried twice, dumpling very steamed till skin came off and char siew noodle was super sweet.  Not able to maintain food standard. Unpleasant experience.
author: Grace “Chin” Chin

review_text: chanced upon this place after taking a random bus from mandai bird paradise because no taxi wanted to pick us up - dropped down at this springleaf MRT area and walked past an entire street with empty stores, but this place was PACKED! curiosity got the better of us so we popped in and wah. no regrets. the fried rice there is bombastic, like primo wokhei, very fresh prawns used in the yang zhou fried rice, and my partner loved the beef fried rice!!! i would have ordered the dimsum if it wasnt so busy. highly recommended if you are in the area! Cash only or nets or paylah - no credit card, so be prepared!
author: jermine tan

review_text:
Fantastic zhi char with wok hei
Dim sum is excellent. Char siew is KL style. Fish maw soup full of maw
author: Rodney Lim

review_text: Excellent service from wait staff. Enjoyed their signature beef hor fun. ☺️Good variety, will come back again to try their dimsum~
author: Tim

review_text:
Food was really good had the steak and ribs. ( no i did not do this review for free ice cream )

Unfortunately the service was non existent
Thankfully for the female staff there made is still ok.

Sorry to say but The male staff is not cut out to be in the service industry.

author: Terence Tan

review_text: i really enjoyed my first time dining in this restaurant. didnt expect for the meat to be so tender and the chicken to be so well seasoned. the oysters were fresh as well. i would love to come back again!
author: Ooo Kkk

review_text: Celebrated a friend's birthday here. I got a sirloin steak and changed my fries to mashed potatoes. The steak was super yummy. I had written in our booking that we were celebrating a birthday, and the staff very kindly brought out a slice of coffee crepe cake for my friend, which was delicious!!! I'd visit again because the food was very yummy and it's right next to Springleaf MRT 👍🏻
author: Joey

review_text: I came here on Christmas Day with my friends and absolutely enjoyed the food—it was delicious and satisfying. Because of that great experience, I decided to visit again with my brother. Once again the food did not disappoint. Consistent quality and great taste. Highly recommended!
author: Angeline Tay

review_text: Had rack of pork, halibut and fish and chips! Quality of food is good! Nice ambience with tv (movie from Netflix). Provided free ice cream with review.
author: Jolene K

review_text:
We had the double milk pudding with ginger and cheng tng. best chinese dessert we’ve had so far and we’ve eaten at almost all the famous chinese dessert places around singapore.

milk pudding was flavourful with the right consistency; cheng tng was refreshing with a variety of ingredients inside including ginkgo nuts. both desserts were not too sweet so one feels satisfied after eating.

the atmosphere is also great and comfortable with excellent mandopop songs. great air-con temperature.
author: T D

review_text:
It is a new humble dessert cafe (next to springleaf MRT) with freshly own made ingrediant. We tried the black sesame paste (pure taste) and pulut hitam. Its not too sweet.

This shop is an extension from mingkok dimsum cafe nearby.

Will come back for more.
author: P K

review_text:
got the mango shaved ice and yam paste

More mango bits would be good to go along with the shaved ice

Yam paste was rather sweet and sticky, I was curious how they made it so smooth, check with staff if oil to make it smooth but staff mentioned that no oil were used so it was rather to know that no oil was used.

not the best but good enough!
author: Clara Tey

review_text:
Nice, airconditioned, cosy and clean premise.

For desserts we had: Chengtng, barley beancurb with ginko nuts, bo bo char char, double milk pudding with ginger and Tangyuan in ginger soup.

Recommend: Tangyuan and barley beancurb.
author: Harriot NN

review_text:
Ordered a bobochacha and mango pomelo sago dessert which were honestly too sweet and underwhelming. The bobochacha soup was thin and didn’t have a strong coconut flavor. The mango pomelo sago dessert had very little sago and pomelo and did not have any coconut flavor.

Why? 😅

Step up your game, Mongkok!!!
author: Rachel

restaurant_name: Famous Hangout Alfresco Restaurant and Bar (Pet Friendly)
review_text: Good service from Jane we feel very welcome and her hospitality was great thanks for the recommendation on the whiskey
author: Jason Ldx

restaurant_name: Famous Hangout Alfresco Restaurant and Bar (Pet Friendly)
review_text: Love the family like bistro and restaurany here. The Famous kitchen is just beside Hangout bistro under the same management. The owner boss here are very welcoming, friendly and helpful. Most diners and drinker here are the regular customers like a big family. They have many choices of bottle craft beer or you may just have their draft Stella or Black Cab stout (these two are the one for happy hour until 8pm). They serve wines and hard liquor too. Love the vibe and people here. Food from Famous kitchen are very good too, love the roast duck go with beer😘. Will be back to try their other dishes. Usually the restaurant and bistro will be full on weekend. Book a table to avoid disappointment. Let them know you prefer to have a seat at the bistro or restaurant.
author: lim may sally

restaurant_name: Famous Hangout Alfresco Restaurant and Bar (Pet Friendly)
review_text: Alfresco bistro linked to Famous Kitchen. They has extensive food menu and very high quality cooking, won Michelin star ⭐️ previously. Must try the cold cockles, dip in generous portions of chili paste. Fried pork in beancurd paste is also very savoury, pair with lots of fried garlics. They also have a lot of live seafood for selection, tried their crab 🦀 for few times, always fresh and juicy meat. Special thanks to Lorraine for the great service 👍
author: Brenda Yip

restaurant_name: Famous Hangout Alfresco Restaurant and Bar (Pet Friendly)
review_text: Very nice environment with lots of landscaping & the sound of their water features are a calming & soothing factor.. lastly, service is definitely a thumbs up too.. Highly recommended for a chill time..
author: Michael Sim

restaurant_name: Famous Hangout Alfresco Restaurant and Bar (Pet Friendly)
review_text: Amazing place with phenomenal vibes! Special shout out to our server Jane for her exceptional service. Going above and beyond!
author: Gabriel Loy

review_text:
This braised sharks fin c/w crab meat and burner and keep the whole bowl boiling, taste so delicious 10/10 out-beat Thai village

The xi hum - chili cold cockles is a must to order (i eat 1 plate by myself)

Lobster is sooo yummy 😋 nicely done not overcooked

Taiwan Cauliflower is a must to order, crunchy crunchy super nice

Appetizer: tomato with sour plum is sooo good & crunchy

I ❤️ all their service crew all very smiley and attentive.

Today i am served by Ms Summer.
I am here to pay a deposit for 27 pax dining for CNY and meantime have a sumptuous meal by my own
author: Cher Cher

review_text: This is their CNY set dinner. Every dish was well executed 👍 I’m impressed with the service as well. Definitely will be back again to try out other dishes
author: LYSL28

review_text: Food was fantastic. In essence, simple traditional dishes made very well. Waitress who waited on our table was enthusiastic to recommend dishes suitable for both young and old and she was spot on. The family enjoyed the dinner 😊 $320++ for 8 pax which was worth it for the quality. Downside is that we were seated next a table of avid drinkers who could share their conversation from across the table occasionally.
author: Shi Leng Teo

review_text:
Famous Kitchen @ Sembawang
We used to celebrate family occasions here, but hadn’t visited in a while as Google Maps previously showed this location as permanently closed. The staff clarified that this was a mistake—it was the Seletar branch that had closed, not this one.

We were glad to be back to celebrate my father's birthday. The service was excellent. The staff were attentive and helpful throughout, especially Ms. Yan Zi, who assisted with our ordering and made thoughtful suggestions—including helping with our birthday cake arrangements. She also made sure we didn’t over-order, which we appreciated.

As we had pre-ordered the Peking Duck, and informed of the birthday celebration, the restaurant kindly served us with complimentary birthday buns—such a nice touch for my father's 81st birthday!

The promotional dishes were great value for money, with no compromise on quality or portion size. I'd highly recommend that. The popular three layers roasted pork on the normal menu was good too. They served several vegetarian dishes which was good for us, with a vegetarian family member.

What made the evening even better for us was the availability of a handicapped-accessible toilet, which made it much easier to manage with a parent in a wheelchair. We’re truly thankful for this facility.
author: Ling Sg

review_text: Cozy restaurant with a nice family-friendly vibe. Staff were warm and helpful, and my kids enjoyed dining here. The roasted duck, crispy pork belly, and barbeque pork were really tasty, and the steam marble goby was fresh and well-cooked. Convenient location near SpringLeaf MRT with parking available. Great spot for a family meal.
author: Chiew Puikit

review_text: Great place to hang and watch the English Premier League and enjoy yummy Indian cuisine and many other food choices 😋. Bring your bicycle along and you can cycle to The Rocket after watching soccer 😀!
author: Chillaxxer (TheGoodLife)

review_text: Overall, would rate this place 3.5/5. We ordered fish and chips. While the food was nice, we waited 45 minutes for the food to arrive. The staff only informed us of the delay after we had waited for 30 minutes. It would have been good if he could inform us earlier as we were rushing for time. That said, the place had good and chill vibes. It was not crowded for a sunday evening.
author: Q

review_text: Good place for those who appreciate good food, good drinks and good ambience. A shoutout to the owners and the chef for elevating this place to another level. Will keep coming back!
author: Kiran Kaur

review_text: Chanced upon this place as it was near to our dinner place. Pretty decent ambience and some cool promotions. Service was good. Really nice place to chill with friends.
author: XY

review_text: I eat daily from Brew house,suppebbb food and service, that's why i go again and again..... Many Verity in beers 🍺.
author: Mandeep Kumar

review_text: Awesome Food served. For full variety please be there before 11am for best experience. Friendly owner & staffs. Well prepared food products with a touch of authenticity in every bite. Those driving, kindly park at ample paid parking lots available opposite the shop.
author: Syahir Osman

review_text: Shop location is easy access. I tried her lauk before she open pondok. Followed her ig & check up on her lauk for daily updates. Really love Kak June’s cooking. She’s truly one of a kind. Spice level of the food is acceptable to be honest. Price is affordable. Pondok truly makes you feel like home & the staff is great too. Come early to avoid disappointment & please be patient with them as the queue is quite long. I wish your business flourished in 2026 kak June!
author: Felisciana Nyangun

review_text:
Salam 👋
This place is one of the best nasi padang I've had , portion is huge can pack afterwards if you feel the price is higher- you're getting huge portions + delicious food and consistency . Owner is a soft in the core but tough outside org baik la overall. Bring your friends , family , everyone & they will thank you 100% come early get the dish fresh and hot enjoy your food coma 😌
author: Mohd Zamir

review_text:
Came to try after seen it's instagram and read reviews. It was pass 2pm, and was happy that there were still seats available, tho, tables are arranged in twos, meant for 4pax. Table size is not that big, smaller that those at coffee shops. I came with my mum, daughter, her husband and 2 young kids. Sadly, they do not have highchair. So, we had to eat while holding the kids in our arms. I must say, that the food was good. Not fantastically good, but acceptable, probably a 3.5 cos I tasted better (sorry). I would say that all the dishes are spicy, even to soup daging (meat) which was clear soup and I thought could be ideal for my 3yo grand-daughter. But, I was wrong. You can taste the spicyness at the tip of your tongue. On a positive note, the staff were friendly, even tho I had a tough time trying to organize the seating with 2 young kids.

So, overall, we didn't have a pleasant experience. It was like, eat quickly and then get out of there! I am unsure of the 5-star ratings ... but I definitely disagree (sorry again). Probably can give a one-time try to see it for yourself. Just leave your kids behind, as it is not a kid-friendly place.
author: My Dear

review_text:
Always the best. Worth every cent!
Parking can be easily found opposite the shop (just walk abit to burn extra calories before indulging) haha! Pucuk ubi crispy, lemak sipot sedot, daging kicap and ayam goreng (power) was what we had.. even tapao home more food! Keep it up June 💕
author: Suzy

review_text:
Came here for dinner on a Sunday. We were seated very quickly since the restaurant wasn’t full, but the menu was quite limited with many items unavailable. We ordered tamagoyaki, a 3-kind sashimi, soft shell crab roll, grilled hamachi fin (wanted the big size but only the small was available), and the 6-kind oden.

The only highlight was the grilled hamachi fin — that was good. The rest of the dishes were just okay. The tamago was a bit too sweet, the soft shell crab roll had more rice than filling, and the sashimi was quite underwhelming for the price point. The oden wasn’t to my taste, though my partner liked it.

Service was also on the slower side. The staff saw our empty plates but didn’t bother clearing them. I even accidentally spilled some oden soup on myself, and the staff standing at the next table noticed but walked away and pretended he didn’t see anything. Really not the kind of service you expect when there’s a service charge. Overall, a pretty average experience.
author: Angela Hoi

review_text:
Happened to drop by Springside to pass something and was craving Japanese food, so I chanced upon Miyuki Izakaya. The restaurant is very nicely decorated and has a really nice vibe. The food was really good .

Ordered the salmon sashimi  it was fresh and The hamachi was so good, and the hokke shioyaki was super tender and yummy. The ikura chawanmushi was my favourite.

Served by two young girls who were very friendly and welcoming. Will definitely come by again. Thanks for the delicious meal and great service!
author: huixin

review_text:
Went there because it's pet friendly. Ordered some stewer, bara chirashi and rolls. Food is quite good but price is on the higher end.
Can accept cdc voucher.
author: Wen Kang Tang

review_text:
Warm, cosy restaurant with reasonably fast service (I went on a Fri night when it’s about 80% full) and very good food.

Most of the food we ordered were delicious, except maybe the Cha Soba. The texture of the soba and the dipping sauce did not hit the right spot. Pls see photo captions for more details regarding the food.
author: L. A_#

review_text:
Our family have had multiple wonderful dining experiences at Milan Shokudo. I went with my wife and our two kids, and from the moment we stepped in, we were greeted with warm smiles and a cosy, welcoming atmosphere. The décor had a charming Japanese‑Italian fusion feel, setting the tone for the meal ahead.

We decided to order a variety of dishes to share, and every single one was a hit. The kids loved the cheesy baked doria; bubbling hot with perfectly seasoned rice and a generous layer of gooey cheese. My wife couldn’t stop raving about the smoked duck carbonara, which was creamy, rich, and cooked to perfection. I went for the quattro cheese pizza, served with a drizzle of honey, the balance of sweet and savoury was simply divine.

What made the evening even better was how family‑friendly the place is. The staff were attentive and patient, happily accommodating our requests and making sure the kids felt included. Service was quick, but never rushed, allowing us to enjoy our food and conversation at a relaxed pace.

The free‑flow drinks bar was a fun touch for the kids, and the portion sizes were generous without being overwhelming. By the end of the meal, we were all happily full and already talking about what we’d try next time.

Milan Shokudo is now firmly on our list of go‑to family restaurants: delicious food, great value, and a warm, inviting vibe that makes you want to come back again and again.
author: Axeltsn

review_text:
i live nearby, and this was my childhood go-to place for lunch. however', in the past few years, the prices has risen exorbitantly to the point that its ludicrous. two vege and 1 meat used to cost 2.50, now its roughly triple. others have commented that the standard has dropped and while that is true that is not my main gripe with the place, its mostly the crazy pricing. i gave them two chances in case the first time they miscalculated or something, but seems like they have done some crazy inflation.

its just sad really. there are better options than this overpriced nonsense nearby.

this place has also become available on deliveroo recently, perhaps they need it to offset their low revenue. i still remember the times where the average queue length was around 10 people, those were the golden days of this place.
author: John Ang

review_text: Food was cold. 2 veg 1 meat costed me $5.50
author: N L

review_text: come at your own risk.... getting more and more expensive lately , food quality standard had dropped as well, very mediocre....
author: BulbasauR BucK

review_text:
It was stated 24Hrs in google but its Bot.I travelled all the eat and its closed
Too disappointed !
author: Lynn Tan

review_text: It's decent teochew fare. Portions were not big so I would consider it to be fairly pricey for the amount paid. Quality was so-so.. good thing is extra bowl of porridge cost only 40c. Free but limited parking on site, but visitors clear quite fast. Btw they changed name to Soon Soon?
author: Charlene and Serwin

review_text:
There's a variety of selection for teochew porridge. Standard had dropped but still taste alright if you are craving for it when you are near the area.

They usually close around 1-2pm
author: Boon Chong Tan

review_text:
Inconsistent pricing.

Paid $3.60 for 1 meat + 2 veg

Came a month after and paid $6.40 for 1 meat + 1 egg + 1 veg

How is the increase of $3 for an additional meat justifiable?

Food quality is sub-par. Better teochew porridge options around the area.
author: Noel Ong

review_text:
Teochew style porridge with options of steam fishes and other dishes 😋 reasonably priced as well. Satisfying the crave.
PS.
PS. It's located in a coffee shop, this should be the expectations of the 'service and atmosphere'.
author: Daron TNG

review_text: Soon Kee porridge is located along thomson road and they are famous for their steam fish in teochew style. The fish they served is fresh and tasty. They are also famous for their braised pork belly. Unfortunately, the vegetables they cook are too oily including their fried eggs. Car park is small and limited hence it's a challenge to eat there if u drive. Not convenient for handicapped as it is a very old coffee shop, it doesn't come equipped with handicapped parking lot nor path.
author: Ann Tan

review_text:
Had a hearty breakfast at Daruma Tavern at the Springside brunch as it was around the neighborhood. I truly enjoyed the breakfast set coupled with a cup of ice cold sour plum finished with the nice warm welcome from the service crew.

The breakfast set that I got was more than enough especially for me as a heavy eater I tend to eat a lot. I assure you that the portion wise is more than enough for breakfast or even the rest of the meals. The sautéed mushrooms were done to perfect and the scrambled eggs was just as creamy with a very fragrant butter savory taste that lingers in your mouth palette. The cherry tomatoes were also roasted to the right spot not too charred and not too raw which comes in perfectly with the salad.

The service crew was also extremely friendly and patiently explains dishes to your likings as well as dietary needs! Kudos to the team at Daruma Tavern wonderful to start my day there!
author: Javier Chai

review_text:
Had a really enjoyable dinner at Daruma Tavern and honestly, it exceeded expectations. The atmosphere is lively and inviting, with that bright neon frontage giving it a fun, casual vibe — perfect for group dinners or chill nights out.
We ordered their prawn noodle and a seafood platter, and both were solid. The broth for the noodles was rich, savoury, and packed with flavour — you can tell it’s been properly cooked down. Ingredients were fresh, especially the prawns and seafood, which were juicy and sweet. The chilli added a nice kick without overpowering the dish.
The seafood platter was a highlight — generous portions, well-balanced, and great for sharing. Everything came together nicely with crispy bits, eggs, and that comforting gravy tying it all up.
Also tried their pork knuckle (didn’t manage to take a photo), and it was seriously good. The skin was perfectly crispy while the meat inside stayed tender and juicy — exactly what you want from a good pork knuckle.
Service was friendly and efficient despite the crowd, and the overall experience felt smooth. Definitely a spot I’d come back to again. Highly recommended if you’re looking for hearty, satisfying food in a casual setting.
author: Shawn Ng

review_text:
Came across this place after a friend recommended it. It’s a very cosy, trendy place which has lots of specialty craft beers, sake and alcohols from around the world. I particularly love the ambience and decor, you can even buy your own durama doll!

Staff were attentive, polite and very friendly. Food was served hot and fresh. Would highly recommend this place if you’re looking for a mix of local dishes and fusion. I particularly love the soft shell crab and prawn mee!
author: Daisy Tan

review_text:
I frequent this place many times.
Suitable for small and big groups.

Highly recommend their black sauce wanton mee.
A wide array of Japanese foods and an even wider array of Southeast Asian foods.
author: Mr Ree

review_text: Visited this Daruma outlet today. The restaurant setup is pleasant and the food presentation and quality were both decent. However, I was quite surprised that the service staff was munching while taking our order. While I wasn’t expecting fine dining service, this did catch me off guard.

review_text:

I’m still giving 3 stars to be fair, as it seems they may specialise more in seafood rather than zi char, which could explain the gap in quality.
author: Jayden Woo

restaurant_name: 33 Xian Seafood Village 33 鲜味园海鲜村
review_text:
A typical neighbourhood coffee shop.
Spacious.
Seafood has a wide spread.
the fried sotong and chicken wing is quite good, honestly.
author: Shark Sharkey

restaurant_name: 33 Xian Seafood Village 33 鲜味园海鲜村
review_text: Amazing seafood zi char in north area Singapore. Hardly to find a restaurant open til 5am. Every dish are flavourful with reasonable price, they taste flash back to our neighbourhood Malaysia like seafood restaurant. Fresh seafood with many choices and would love to come back try every menu they had offer. Will recommend friends and family. Definitely will come back again! Thumbs up.
author: Britney Khu

restaurant_name: 33 Xian Seafood Village 33 鲜味园海鲜村
review_text: We have steamed Australian crab for $80 and chili Sri Lankan crab for $66, totaling about $335 for 10 people. The seafood is fresh and delicious.
author: S L

restaurant_name: 33 Xian Seafood Village 33 鲜味园海鲜村
review_text: The place is in a industrial area which is quite far off from public transport. Located at a building name TAG A. The service was good and pricing reasonable. Our food cost $88.50. Bring cash as they accept nets and cash payment only. The fish was fresh and tasty. The vegetable was a bit salty due to the oyster sauce. The salted egg squid was ordinary. The herbal prawn soup was nice though and prawn was tasty.
author: Randy Tan

review_text:
OMG! 😳😳😳
Their Mutton Satti Soru was amazing!!! My plate was completely spotless, That’s how delicious it was. You have to go down to Semma to try it yourself to believe it. Very friendly ambiance and knowledgeable staffs.
Highly recommended 👍🏾👍🏾👍🏾
author: Ranjinikanth Alivalahgan

review_text: Came here on a Saturday night, they had live music and all tables were occupied. The food was good, their special drink tasted diluted. The service was quick and the staff were responsive. Had a pleasant experience, would return! Do join their membership programme if you would like a free shot on the house.
author: S Raveen

review_text:
A very cosy yet intimate dining atmosphere. Even though I made a reservation at 9pm I had to wait for about 30mins to get a table with my family. It’s usually full house in the late evenings till around 9.30pm, So if your heading for dinner, do go earlier.

As for the food, I was totally shocked by the speed it came upon placing the order.say within 10mins for 5 dishes and 3 drinks…now that’s fast!

1. Satti Sorru (mutton) - this is a MUST TRY! The spiciness, food portion and the generous amount of soft tender mutton chunks!! Worth every penny!
5/5

2. Cheese Sticks - You would be surprised by the portion and SIZE…these aren’t your normal small sized cheese sticks which you see in most eateries.These are gigantic and the cheese just oozes out upon your 1st bite!
5/5

3. Goreng Biasa - a very unique presentation when it gets to your table. but only 1 setback…The noodle seemed slightly over cooked and soft.But other then that, portion and taste is great!!
3.5/5

4. Garlic Butter Masala Prawns - served on a hot plate sizzling with spiciness. Portion was nice for 3pax.
4/5

5. Thalapathy Drink - a unique name for a cocktail with rum infused but sadly I couldn’t taste the rum but more of the pineapple…pretty disappointing..
2/5

6. Semmaya Oru Punch Drink - a drink which deserves its name! U gotto try this.
You will never be disappointed.
5/5

Overall, satisfied with the food,drinks,atmosphere,service but totally not their mobile ordering platform. And to top it up, there seems to be a blind spot for mobile networks.
author: Charles Ruben

review_text:
Food wise it is good but drink wise I find the teh halia not enough ormph. The chicken curry is good but the fish curry is a bit let down as I find it missing the depth of flavor that I always look for in a nice curry.

We ordered the Tasha Special Murtabak ($15). It is FULL of ingredients. It has cheese, mutton, ham, egg, mushroom, capsicum and tons of other stuff. Surprisingly it goes nicely together. 5 stars here.

The mee goreng is the wet style. It spicyness level is there and it has nice chunky potatoes and tau kwa. It has a thick sauce coating every strand of the noodles. Nice!
author: Kwong Fei Yee

review_text: My first time dining. A cozy environment. Everything was good, but it would have been better if the chairs and tables for 2 were of better design. It gave us back ache with cramped legs after dining. Takeaway was kinda disappointing as it was given in plastic bags. Overall experience was good as the staff were very polite.
author: Discover me

review_text: Authentic Thai food at affordable price. Taste amazing! Highly recommend!
author: Suprawee Horikawa

food very good I will come back again 👍 pad Thai

author: Ableson Chan

review_text: Food is delicious. Tom yum soup is very nice and authentic.
author: 安安

review_text: The food here is really good! Everything tasted very authentic and flavorful. The crispy fried snacks were perfectly crunchy, the braised pork was tender and rich, and the spicy noodle salad was super fresh and delicious. The seafood soup was also very comforting. Definitely a great place for Thai food in Singapore!
author: Sudarat Butrasri

review_text: Amazing food at affordable price. My favourite is their tom yum seafood soup. Would highly recommend it!
author: Suphannee Srito

review_text: We are satisfied with all the food that we ordered, especially the signature Wasabi beef tenderloin. The gravy coated all over asparagus and beef cube, without too overwhelming. Also the stir fried chives with garlic, authentic HK taste. Not forgetting the curry fish ball, which is a must try. Plain polo bun with crunchy crust on top and sliced butter also not bad. Service provided was attentive too. Will visit again for more food adventures without going to HK.
author: Jojo

review_text:
I was trying to get away from the dead heat of the afternoon and initially wanted to just go for a cold milk tea

But since I was there and seeing their extensive menu, I decided to go for a comfort bowl of beef noodles which I intentionally asked for instant noodles.

I saw quite bad reviews saying it’s expensive and just instant noodles etc but come on, what outside food is cheap now? Business need to survive and I don’t think you can just based on price on reviews, the food is the key component too!

Back to what I ordered.
I find this bowl of beef noodles fantastic .
I got huge chunks of beef, thick ones ok. Tendons and also beef meat balls 3 to be exact.
I seriously don’t find it’s not aligned to its price. Generous portion.

I would revisit again. Their service staffs are also very friendly and accommodating when I asked for ice and Chilli.

Nice place to chill.
author: Keith Er

review_text:
I was really looking forward to my second visit here after a fantastic first experience. During my last trip here, I had the beef brisket noodles and a polo bao that was easily the closest I've tasted to the authentic ones in Hong Kong.

Unfortunately, today's visit was a huge disappointment. I had raved about the polo bao to my family, but the one served today was the complete opposite of what I remembered. It was not up to standard at all.

It's a shame because the taste just isn't there anymore.
author: L L

review_text:
Friends Cafe朋友冰室
The place
It's a small cafe in Spring Brook Building along Sembawang Road, opposite the Nee Soon Camp.
Dace with bean sauce stirred fried with Indian Lettuce ($13): The vegetable was well handled, with skillful stirfrying, such that it still retained its crunch. A good accomplement to a bowl of rice.
Beef tenderloin with wasabi
sauce($16): The beef was tender (though slightly over-tenderized), and covered with a tasty sauce. It was a bit too salty though, I supposed it was meant to be eaten with rice.
Prawn fried with garlic and chilli in Typhoon Shelter style($18): The prawns were well fried with mixture of chilli, garlic and shallots in the unique HK Typhoon Shelter style (common in seafood restaurants in Hong Kong). It's a little too salty for me though.
Baked Rice with Chicken Chop($12): A typical Cha Chan Tang favourite, the taste matched expectation, though not outstandingly so.
Pandan flavoured milk tea($3.8): The silky smooth milk tea was above average, though the pandan was an unique but unnecessary addition to the taste of the tea.
The verdict
The cafe was worth a visit if you are around the area (and also there are not many other choices of F&B around the area), at a reasonabale price point. Especially if the chef can tone down the salt a little.
author: Trancemaster

review_text:
A hidden gem (legit) tucked near Springleaf Mrt. About a 7minutes walk from Springleaf mrt. For drivers, there’s a carpark nearby as well. Upon entering, the place felt like I was teleported to Hong Kong. Seating was like an iconic Hong Kong Cha Chaan Teng with the booth style seats. What’s better was the foood, ordered the Cheese Baked Tomato Chicken Chop Rice and kid you not, this was better than the one I had in Hong Kong 2 months ago.  Cheese was melted thoroughly with some crispy bits, tomato sauce was zesty enough, chicken chop was very well seasoned and tender although it was oven baked. An additional touch of surprise was the rice - underneath the sauce is egg fried rice and not plain rice which made the dish even more flavourful.

Ordered the Hong Kong style crispy bun with condensed milk and milk pudding too and both were good, nothing to pick on.

Overall, this is an under rated cafe that deserves more attention. Good vibes, good service, good food👌will be back

review_text:
For new years eve, we decided to try something new and patronage this pizza joint and ordered the following:
Sausage & cream, Beef Lasagna, Midnight Express, Nutella Dream & Gelato.

Thoroughly enjoyed each and every single dish especially their dessert pizza Nutella Dream. The Midnight Express pizza that we tried was light and flavourful, and left us feeling satisfied. Beef lasagna was also very tasty and much recommended. Ended off amazing night with gelato. All dishes were wiped off clean leaving the plates spotless!

author: Haidar Junidi

review_text:

author: Emily

review_text:
Chanced upon this eatery as we were nearby, saw the high reviews, and decided to give this place a try. Absolutely no regrets, and we’re soso glad to have found this gem!

Pizzas, sides, and especially the beef lasagne were all on point. You can just tell that each dish was made with love and genuine passion, and not rushed out for the sake of it. It’s why you might have to wait awhile for your food to come, but i’d say it’s worth it.

We recommended this place for our gathering with friends just a few days later, and everyone had only good praises for the food. We ordered online and picked up the food - Fadil (owner) made sure to communicate any delays in our food being ready, which is always appreciated.

We’ll definitely be back many more times :)

review_text: I really, really wanted to like this place since I drove past its banner last year. Unfortunately I found the Mutton Rendang Goreng to be very bland. author: Peter Yeo

review_text:
