What truly elevated the experience was the customer service. Warm, attentive, and genuinely friendly, the staff made us feel welcome from the moment we arrived. You can tell they take pride not just in their food and drinks, but also in how they treat their customers.

A random night session turned into a memorable experience. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates great teh tarik and heartfelt service.
author: Suren Piero

review_text: I saw this shop at TikTok so I decided to drop by. The staffs are super friendly & helpful when it comes to asking about the menu. The customer service is top tier. We ordered the egg prata, make your own goreng & masala fries. It was superb. 10/10. Would recommend. Would come again. Love it here.
author: nur syafiqa

restaurant_name: Red Lantern Live Seafood @ Sembawang Country Club
review_text:
Dining at Red Lantern Live Seafood is a true gourmet celebration of Singapore’s seafood heritage. From the moment you arrive, the lively atmosphere, fresh seafood displays, and warm hospitality set the tone for an exceptional dining experience.
The live seafood selection is outstanding,
impeccably fresh and expertly prepared. Each dish showcases masterful wok skills and perfectly balanced flavours, whether it’s the signature chilli crab rich with depth and aroma, succulent black pepper crab bursting with spice, or delicate steamed fish that highlights the natural sweetness of the seafood.

Every plate arrives beautifully cooked, generous in portion, and deeply satisfying. The sauces are luxurious and layered, perfect for soaking up with mantou, while the seafood itself remains tender, sweet, and never overpowered. It’s clear that quality ingredients and traditional techniques are treated with great respect here.
Service is attentive and efficient without being intrusive, and the staff are knowledgeable, happy to recommend dishes, and ensure everything runs seamlessly. Despite its popularity, the restaurant maintains excellent consistency which is a mark of a truly reliable establishment.
For those seeking an authentic, high-quality seafood experience in the north of Singapore, Red Lantern Live Seafood at Sembawang is a standout. Ideal for family gatherings, celebrations, or hosting guests, this is a restaurant that delivers both heart and craftsmanship. A five-star experience that keeps you coming back.
author: Daxter Yeo

restaurant_name: Red Lantern Live Seafood @ Sembawang Country Club
review_text:
First time to this Red Lantern @ Sembawang Country Club, reached early after 6pm where there isn’t much crowds yet & there are lots of available tables (not reserved). We seated nearer the golf field, shining under sunset, had a good view of Sunset scenery.
We ordered their promotion dishes - Sharkfin soup @$9.90 which the soup is thick & flavorful , plus their Drunken Prawns in Claypot at $15 which their 15 prawns are quite big & they are very fresh.
Signature Golden Chicken is slightly towards sweetness, but overall taste is good. Dual taste Kaikan is good as well, hot plate beancurd added fresh prawns, cauliflowers, black fungus, peppers on eggs are generous in small portion, last dish small portion Sweet & Sour pork don’t look small too.
All foods are served gradually.
Their service & attentiveness of their staffs are excellent!
author: Liau J

restaurant_name: Red Lantern Live Seafood @ Sembawang Country Club
review_text: Everyone enjoyed the food and I felt it was quite reasonably priced. there was Chilli crab promo so that was super worth it. Only the roasted duck was a bit too tough.. but all other dishes were good! One super plus point they managed to accommodate our big family of 14 (including the kids) at one single table. The large portions were also big enough for our family such that everyone had a bite of every item. :)
author: Cheryl Tan

restaurant_name: Red Lantern Live Seafood @ Sembawang Country Club
review_text:
I recently dined at Red Lantern Live Seafood located within the Sembawang Country Club, and I must say, it was quite an experience! The restaurant offers a spacious and inviting atmosphere, making it a nice spot for both family gatherings and casual meals with friends.

First, let's dive into the food. The portions here are generous, and considering the pricing, I found it to be quite reasonable. One standout dish for me was the BBQ pork ribs. Although the portion size was on the smaller side, the quality of the meat made up for it. It was cooked to perfection—so tender that it practically slid off the bone. I can see why this dish would be a hit for diners of all ages, including older folks who might find it easier to enjoy.

On the other hand, I did find the Yam Ring to be a bit disappointing. It lacked the flavor and fragrance I was hoping for, leaving me a bit underwhelmed. I would recommend skipping this one, as it didn’t seem to match the quality of the other dishes.

Next up was the Chilli Crab. While the crab itself felt a bit average and didn't come across as the freshest, the amount of sauce provided was a pleasant surprise. It paired wonderfully with the fried buns and was definitely enjoyable. Just a note: if you're a fan of crab that’s bursting with freshness, you might want to manage your expectations with this dish.

Another highlight for me was the Braised Pork Trotters. This was well-prepared, rich in flavor, and quite satisfying. However, I did encounter one minor drawback; the Chinese mushroom nestled within the dish wasn't cooked through properly. It was a bit tough on the teeth which detracted slightly from the overall experience.
author: Andrew Chwee

restaurant_name: Red Lantern Live Seafood @ Sembawang Country Club
review_text: We had a wonderful dining experience at Red Lantern! The food was delicious and served promptly. Service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive. We also appreciated the frequent promotions, which offer great value for the quality. Currently Red Lantern Seafood is offering promotions on Salad Prawn Balls and Steamed Tiger Grouper, both available until the end of August 2025. The Salad Prawn Balls (8 pieces) are priced at $6 (originally $21), and the Steamed Tiger Grouper (Hong Kong Style) is $48 (originally $88). Highly recommended!!!

restaurant_name: Royal Palm @ Orchid Country Club Restaurant
review_text:
Poor handling of billing issue and disappointing service at Orchid Country Club & Royal Palm

My elderly father and his partner stayed at Orchid Country Club early October 2025 and had dinner for two at Royal Palm restaurant. Unfortunately, the restaurant staff did not capture the card payment that night and later called to say the bill was unpaid.

The next morning, they were told the issue would be resolved. However, they were charged $113.79 instead of the correct senior citizen rate of $70. Despite assurances that the $43.70 refund would be processed via PayNow, it has still not been received.

When they followed up, the restaurant manager, Mr Raju, was rude and blamed them for the error, which was very upsetting. The OCC finance team then told them to “get the refund from Royal Palm” even though the overcharge was made by OCC.

This has been an unnecessarily stressful experience for two elderly guests who acted in good faith. Absolutely shocking.
author: JC C

restaurant_name: Royal Palm @ Orchid Country Club Restaurant
review_text:
Went for Ramadan buffet dinner 1 for 1. The restaurant was not capable of holding the large crowd yesterday. Firstly, there was only 1 live station BBQ, where they only grilled about 40 chicken and 40 mutton satay sticks at a time. So in a queue of 5 people, the satay sticks would instantly disappear and we would have to wait another 10 minutes for the next batch. Same goes with the other sotong, kambing golek etc, which were not refilled. The containers for the normal dishes were small too, so for the popular dishes like chilli crab etc. it was almost instantly gone when it just refilled. The same pattern happened with the ice, coffee, drinks, plates, foods and dessert. If there were 50% fewer customers, the food would barely be enough for everyone.

Taste wise it was pretty normal except for the teh tarik was just hot milk, the syrup drinks were bad. Satay was undercooked, Sotong was rubbery, Kambing Golek was cold even though these were the highlights of the buffet.

At this price point you are better off going for other buffets.

restaurant_name: Royal Palm @ Orchid Country Club Restaurant
review_text: Went today for the ramadan buffet. Very very crowded. Seems very 'squeezy' in between tables. However ingredients wise , doesn't seem to meet the other franchises ratings. (I have not tired others. It appears to have decent ratings at other outlets). Ingredients does not seem as fresh, deep fried items are too dry and laksa curry was not as flavourful and slightly watery. review_text:
Chapati (SGD $3) @ Mr Teh Tarik Eating House.
.

.
With a soft stretchy chewy texture, their chapati is good for pairing with morsels of meat, vegetables, or curry. Typically sold with 2 pieces, or as a set meal.
.
.

.
Tracing its history back to May 2004 when it was founded by Hassan Bin Abdul Kadir, this casual chain eatery is a reliable place for South Indian dishes.
.
Their rendition is generous with minced mutton and diced potatoes (replacing peas), with a robust and deep blend of spices, including a pronounced use of black pepper.
.
Has a thick chunky chewy tender texture with bold meaty savoury salty starchy earthy peppery spice flavour.
.
.
.
Mutton Soup And Sup Kambing (SGD $9) @ Mr Teh Tarik Eating House.
.
Their rendition is strong and rich, the thick cloudy hot soup / broth being stewed over hours. Has deep spice earthy savoury salty meaty flavour.
.
Light on garnishes, the mutton shank meat is chunky yet tender chewy, with meaty savoury spice flavour. Seems to carry a hint of 5-spice powder as seasoning. Served alongside crisp fluffy baguette bread slices with bready sweet flavour.

review_text:
I met my brother and his family of four for our Chinese New Year of the Horse 2026’ lunch gathering. My brother ordered a vegetarian set for me while he and his family had their usual beef’s, chicken, seafood claypot, fried rice, sweet and sour pork etc

author: Botak

restaurant_name: Ban Heng Restaurant @ Orchid Country Club
review_text:
Based on the past reviews, I actually didn’t have high expectations when I dined at Ban Heng today. So it was my family and my first time trying their a la carte buffet and I was impressed by their variety of food, taste and service. Felt I had to do them some justice by providing more balanced review.

We tried their every 3 adults 1 free promotion. My folks were happy and satisfied with the spread and quality of the food and we had a good lunch experience with satisfactory service and didn’t encounter any rude staff at all. Plates were cleared regularly and we had no complaints at all. All in all, we liked the food there and it was value for money. Will return again to try to seafood and meat dishes instead of the dim sum!

1. So they actually have self-service buffet counter including drinks (Nescafé coffee machine), desserts (tau suan, ice jelly, orh Nee), soup, and carbs (XO sauce fried carrot cake, laksa, e-fu noodles, fried rice). Soup of the day was lotus root pork rib soup which tasted homely and I also liked the carrot cake and laksa!

2. The a la carte menu was super extensive and we should have started ordering the main dishes first! After ordering most of the dim sum items, we were already so stuffed and didn’t get to try other meat, seafood and veg items like cereal prawn on their menu. We only ordered fried soon hock, fried fish skin and oyster omelette only.

3. Dim sum was actually pretty decent, freshly fried and hot. There was super extensive variety and we should be more discerning and order selective dishes only! Again we had to force ourselves to finish the food.

4. Apart from the self-service desserts, the a la carte Dessert was restricted to 4 types - ice cream, cheese cake, herbal jelly, osmanthus jelly and bubble tea. We could order one serving of each dessert but we were too full already. So I tried herbal jelly which was bite sized, osmanthus jelly which was decent. Bubble tea was a small cup but the pearls were not well cooked and not chewy at all. My son had ice cream and there’s quite a lot of flavors to choose from. There’s also pop corn machine there which got my son excited!
author: Zhang Er Lee

restaurant_name: Ban Heng Restaurant @ Orchid Country Club
review_text:
Ban Heng – CNY Eve Dinner Review

Came here for Chinese New Year Eve dinner expecting a proper reunion-style experience. The atmosphere for CNY was there but the execution fell short.

Food quality was so-so. Nothing terrible, nothing memorable. For a CNY set dinner at this price point, the dishes felt rushed and lacked refinement.

Dinner started at 8:15pm, but it felt like we were being pushed to finish by 10pm. Dishes came out extremely fast, one after another, which killed the pacing of the meal. It felt more like a turnover operation than a festive dinner meant to be enjoyed slowly with family.

CNY atmosphere was present. There was Chinese opera, face-changing performance, and live singing between courses. However, the volume was excessively loud. Conversation at the table was almost impossible unless you were shouting. The only voice clearly audible was the MC on the microphone.

Overall experience was not good. For Chinese New Year Eve, people come for warmth, flow, and time together. This felt rushed, noisy, and transactional. Not an experience I would repeat for CNY.

review_text:
Dock one star due to lack of consistency on choco bear filling amount. Sometimes reasonable and sometimes sad.

————————————-

I have visited Bread and Butter Bakehouse a number of times since discovering it and it's a good find in the area.

They have a variety of bakes, cakes, sandwiches offered and for the items I have tried (which isn't a lot), the standouts so far for me are (1) choco bear (2) ondeh ondeh muffin and (3) grilled beef and cheese sandwich.

Choco Bear 🐻 is a very happy bear until Raph goes bear hunting ( -_•)▄︻テ══━一💥A soft bun with a dense, rich chocolatey filling that’s not too cloying. It’s best enjoyed at room temperature; heating it up makes the bread lose its texture and become a bit of a mess.

The grilled beef and cheese sandwich in sourdough was good too, packed with thin beef slices and melty cheese in toasted bread.

I also enjoy the ondeh ondeh muffins, which have a good pandan and gula melaka taste to it. The banana choc one I have tried was decent too.

Beyond this, Bread Butter also showcases some cute crafted cakes but I have not tasted any as yet. They look cool though so maybe someday soon. It's a cosy enough spot for dine in and worth returning to for me for it's comforting bakes, cute creations and... choco bear 🐻
author: Raphael Too

review_text:
We stumbled upon this charming little café while exploring the area on a hunt for durian, and were instantly drawn in by the buttery aroma wafting through the air. Still relatively under the radar, this café-cum-bakery specialises in small bakes that are delicate, thoughtful, and full of charm, in my humble opinion.

The menu is intentionally curated, reflecting what feels like the baker’s best picks — from muffins and artisanal cakes to Swiss rolls and French brioche breads, all of which are well worth trying.

On our first visit, we tried the Ondeh Ondeh, Mixed Fruit, and Oreo muffins. The muffins were moist without being oily, something we really appreciated. We also ordered a double espresso and a flat white, both of which were aromatic and well-executed, making them great companions to the bakes.

⸻

Revisit · 21 Jan 2026

I dropped by again intending to have a short latte. While it was on the pricier side for the size, I genuinely enjoyed the depth and aroma of the coffee.

What truly caught my attention this time were the adorable buns — a little bear and crab that seemed to wave at me from the display. I ended up getting the crab-shaped bun with luncheon meat and a chocolate bear bun, both as cute as they were satisfying.

Of course, I couldn’t resist picking up my favourite sultana muffin again — consistently good, just as I remembered.

Definitely a place I’d return to if I’m around the area again.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text:
Bread-Butter is a lovely coffee spot for anyone craving authentic Italian flavors. Their handmade sweets are absolutely delicious, and the freshly baked bread and focaccia taste just like in Italy fragrant, soft, and full of flavor.

What makes the experience even better is the kindness of the staff: warm, welcoming, and genuinely attentive. A small place with a big heart and truly exceptional baking.
author: Francesco Fanicchi

review_text:
Bread Butter Bakehouse: Waffles, Ice Cream, and Pure Dessert Comfort! (A Hidden Gem for Locals)

My recent trip to Bread Butter Bakehouse was dedicated entirely to dessert, and I was certainly not disappointed! This is a lovely neighbourhood gem that truly understands the art of a perfect sweet treat.

I ordered the Pistachio Ice Cream with Waffles, and the dish was fantastic. The presentation was charming, adorned with crunchy sliced almonds and a chocolate drizzle. The waffles themselves were beautifully made—crisp on the outside and wonderfully fluffy within—a perfect base for the main event.

The Pistachio Ice Cream was the star; a large scoop that was incredibly creamy, nutty, and clearly made with authentic flavour. The cool, rich texture of the ice cream melted beautifully into the warmth of the waffle, creating that essential contrast that defines a great dessert. The combination of textures and flavours was simply delicious. I can wholeheartedly say, I like it! (and truly, the quality speaks for itself).

A Note on Logistics:
While the food is excellent, visitors should be aware of the location. Parking is quite limited around the area. Because of this, I wouldn't highly recommend making a specific, dedicated trip if you have to drive a long distance. This spot is best suited for residents, people working nearby, or those passing through the Ang Mo Kio Street 66 vicinity. If you are already in the neighbourhood, however, it's an absolute must-visit for a satisfying break!

Highly Recommended for: Local Residents & Passersby!

review_text:
I chance upon this Korean restaurant NAYANA Kpop Cafe & Restaurant located in Flora Vista, and it was an absolutely delightful experience. The food here is authentically Korean, with a focus on rich flavors and quality ingredients.

From the moment I stepped in, the ambiance felt welcoming, and the pet-friendly outdoor seating is a thoughtful touch, perfect for those who want to enjoy a meal with their furry friends. There are also plenty of vegetarian options, making it inclusive for everyone.

I tried several dishes, and each was fantastic in its own way. The spicy beef soup was bursting with flavor, offering a satisfying heat balanced by tender vegetables. The cheese-covered Tteokbokki was indulgent and comforting—perfectly chewy rice cakes in a rich, savory sauce topped with melted cheese. And the Korean fried chicken was exceptional: crispy, juicy, and coated in a sweet-spicy glaze, topped with sesame seeds that added a lovely crunch. The portions were generous. The overall dining experience was excellent. The staff were friendly and attentive, adding to the warm, homely atmosphere of the restaurant.

For anyone craving authentic Korean food in the heart of Ang Mo Kio, NAYANA Kpop Cafe & Restaurant is a must-visit. I left feeling thoroughly satisfied and will definitely return!

author: Audrey Lim

restaurant_name: Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story
review_text:
Day 6 of CNY, a group of friends visited Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story and had a truly delightful experience. The café is cosy and welcoming, with charming touches like colourful bread toasters that add warmth and character to the space.

What stood out most was the attentive service and deep product knowledge. Freddie personally introduced the different blends of coffee and tea, thoughtfully explaining how each could be paired with specific breads, house-brand jams, and butters. His passion and understanding of flavour profiles were evident in every recommendation, making the tasting experience both educational and enjoyable.

The selection of breads was impressive — Balmuda-toasted Hokkaido milk bread, black sesame bread, chocolate swirl loaf, nai su toast and mentaiko toast — each prepared beautifully and paired wonderfully with drip coffee blends such as Blue Note, Nutty Collections, Taiwan Symphony, American Rhapsody and African Waltz. The coffees were aromatic, light and well-balanced, never overpowering.

The jams and spreads were exceptional. Unique flavours like lychee & orange flower and pineapple vanilla rosemary were refreshing and refined. Braun Kranfill’s chocolate spread, with its sweet, rich flavour and bits of crispy feuilletine, was indulgent yet not too heavy. The passion mango spread was vibrant and well-balanced. Paired with Yotsuba Hokkaido butter and creamy French butter, every bite felt thoughtfully curated.

We also enjoyed their roasted tomato, mushroom and pumpkin soups — creamy, comforting and flavourful, pairing perfectly with garlic toast.

Overall, Fred Bread SG offers not just quality bread and specialty coffee, but a carefully crafted tasting experience guided by genuine passion and attentive service. Highly recommended for those who appreciate artisanal bread and thoughtful pairings.
author: Peck Wee Ng

restaurant_name: Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story
review_text:
we came excited as bread lovers, and it really exceeded our expectations!

freddie was a passionate, sincere and fun host. the entire experience was enjoyable and very interactive. atmosphere and interior set up was such a vibe. surprised that those expensive toasters, gooseneck etc. weren’t just for show, but actually used to toast our bread. honourable mention was definitely the mentaiko toast that stole the morning for us, it ain’t your typical aburi mentaiko. freddie was honest with his business, offering high-quality-everything, completely blown away! i would definitely be bringing more friends back here.

thank you freddie, appreciate what you’re doing.
author: elderwanda

restaurant_name: Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story
review_text:
Don't expect the usual sit and eat experience, this was a really unique and amazing experience. Fred was super welcoming and friendly, he explained his menu and all the different flavour profiles of coffees and teas which is interesting change from Singapores fast paced rhythm, this offset truly is relaxing taking your time to enjoy the smells and aromas of the coffee, the touch of all the carefully curated leather mats and coasters.
As for the food it was nothing less than amazing, the Hokkaido Milk toast did not fail to amaze me with the flavour and chewy QQ texture with a spread of well spread Passion fruit, a crunchy chocolate spread and a creamy milk caramel, the coffee was also another star, beautifully brewed to perfection while Fred guides you through all the aromas of each coffee. Their soups are also well done, a leek soup with potatoes paired with garlic bread with a profound rosemary flavour. Words cannot describe my experience here so I can definitely recommend coming here to experience this for yourself. 10/10 would come back again.
author: Jon kai HAMPTER

restaurant_name: Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story
review_text:
I visited Fred's some months back and it was an interesting ‘bread for lunch’ experience. Fred is a friendly, affable chap and a good host.

I think everyone who's keen on good bread/buns should give what’s on offer here a try.

Sharing my views on what I had:

1. Black Sesame Hokkaido Milk Bread and the Hokkaido Milk Bread - They both tasted fine but I also had a Mini Black Sesame Sea Salt Butter Bun whilst there and I enjoyed that more than the bread.

2. B de L Lychee and Orange Flower Jam - This was nice. I’m not a jam connoisseur though, so I couldn’t fully appreciate the premium placed on it.

3. Braun Kranfill's Chocolate - Described as "Sweet, chocolaty with pieces of paillete feuilletine (French crispy, caramelized crepes)" and it tasted as described and was nice.

4. Yotsuba Hokkaido Butter - Creamy and yummy.

5. For the coffee, I tried the Blue Notes coffee. The coffee served there is drip coffee and I did not enjoy it so much as I found it mild and not so robust, but I would put this down to personal preference.

I may try different items in future if I do decide to dine there again.

One thing I will most likely be purchasing again though is the yummy buns.

Definitely worth checking out if you’re into good bread/buns or are in the area.

restaurant_name: Fred Bread SG & The Toast Story

The experience felt almost like an omakase of bread — unhurried, intimate, and full of little surprises. The atmosphere was calm and relaxing, perfect for lingering over a good cup of coffee and conversation. The lady at the counter was incredibly warm, and together with Fred, they made the experience feel genuinely hospitable and personal.

The highlight for me was the black sesame bread — toasted to perfection, fragrant, and wonderfully nutty — paired with rich French butter that elevated every bite. It’s clear that every element here is crafted with care and love.

I’d definitely revisit in a heartbeat — though I hope I can snag a seat next time, as this place deserves to be full!

review_text:
Mad Charcoal @ Orange Point
Visited this place on two occasions.
The place
A canteen stall nestled in building in an industrial park, the deco were functional but nonetheless tastefully organized. The canteen was an open-concept one (meaning no air-con), but the open frontage on one side, kept a nice breeze going, making the ambience comfortably pleasant.
Grilled beef cheek with side of Ratatouille ($25): the meat was flavoursome and tender, with a touch of smokiness from the charcoal grilling. While the flavour of the beef cheek could have been better with a little more fat, the meat noththeless has a nice texture from the deft handling by the chef. The sauce was delicious without overpowering the subtle taste of the beef cheek. The Ratatouille, a mixed vegetable stew of French origin, is not commonly seen in hawker stalls, is a must-have side item to go with the meat.
Pork Belly with Ratatouille lunch set ($11.50): The pork belly was roasted to a melt-in-your mouth texture, with the buttery fat providing an indulgent mouth feel. The Ratatouille was expertly cooked and a veritable explosion of flavours. A side of pickled vegetable was provided for a refreshing balance from all the richness.
The verdict
This eatery is worth multiple visits, despite of it's rather 'ulu' location.

author: Frankie Lim

review_text:
My recent excursion to Mad Charcoal during the sun-drenched lunch hour proved to be more than a mere meal; it was a masterclass in the delicate choreography between fire and freshness.

The plate arrived with an architectural grace that belied its rustic origins. Resting atop a dark, leaf-shaped vessel, the Pork Belly sat in a triumphant row of golden-brown tiles. Beside it, a verdant sprawl of romaine, punctuated by the ruby-red arc of tomato wedges and the golden shards of what appeared to be crisp beancurd skin, offered a vibrant visual counterpoint.

One does not simply eat this pork; one experiences the Maillard reaction in its most evolved state. The skin boasted a glass-like shatter, yielding to a layer of rendered fat that possessed a velvety mouthfeel, nearly liquifying upon contact. The meat itself remained impeccably succulent, whispering of a long, disciplined roast that preserved its structural integrity while infusing it with a deep, umami-rich soul. The subtle, char-kissed aroma lingering on the palate provided a haunting reminder of the charcoal’s transformative power.

To find such technical proficiency at a lunchtime special price point feels almost like a heist. While the evening service may offer a more lingering ambiance, the midday experience at Mad Charcoal is a streamlined, high-octane celebration of smoke and seasoning. It is proof that high-caliber culinary execution need not always come with a staggering premium.

author: Muhammad Yi En Bin Muhammad Iqbal

review_text:
Dining at He Jia Huan 合家欢 in Lentor Modern was a mixed but overall enjoyable experience. The restaurant offers hearty Chinese comfort food, and while some dishes truly impressed, others left me wishing for a more traditional touch.
Highlights
- Sliced Potato (5/5)
This dish was a standout. The potatoes were perfectly cooked—thinly sliced, crisp yet tender, and seasoned with just the right balance of salt and spice. It had that addictive quality where you keep reaching for another bite. Easily one of the best versions I’ve had.
- Tomato Paste Ribs (5/5)
Another winner. The ribs were succulent, with the tomato paste sauce adding a rich, tangy-sweet depth that complemented the meat beautifully. The flavors were bold but not overpowering, and the texture of the ribs was spot-on—fall-off-the-bone tender.
Letdowns
- Big Plate Chicken
Traditionally, this dish is served with wide, flat noodles that soak up the sauce and spices. Unfortunately, He Jia Huan opted for thin noodles instead, which didn’t carry the flavors as well and changed the overall experience. The chicken itself was flavorful, but the choice of noodle felt like a compromise that took away from the authenticity of the dish.
Overall Impression
He Jia Huan delivers some excellent dishes that are worth returning for, especially the sliced potato and tomato paste ribs. However, the deviation from tradition in their Big Plate Chicken was disappointing, especially for diners who expect the classic flat noodles.
Final Verdict:
- Hits: Sliced potato and tomato paste ribs are must-orders.
- Miss: Big Plate Chicken needs a rethink to honor its traditional roots.
- Atmosphere and service were pleasant, making it a comfortable spot for family-style dining.

review_text:
My friends and I had an unexpected but amazing experience today at Shiok Burger during their pre-opening food preparation and tasting session for staff. We were just passing by and curious to try, when the boss noticed our interest and very generously invited us in. That alone already set the tone for what turned out to be a great experience.

I got to try three items: the spicy mala chicken burger, the original chicken burger, and the non-spicy mala chicken burger. Every single one impressed me, but the mala versions really stood out. The mala sauce was bold, fragrant, and properly numbing without overpowering the chicken. You can tell it’s been thoughtfully crafted, not just thrown together for trend value.

What really elevates Shiok Burger is the pita bread. Soft, fluffy, and slightly chewy, it complements the fillings perfectly and makes the burger feel both indulgent and refined. The chicken was juicy, well-seasoned, and cooked just right.

Honestly, this easily trumps the big fast-food chains in Singapore. There’s heart, quality, and originality in what they’re doing. If this is the standard before official opening, I can’t wait to see how Shiok Burger does once they launch. Definitely one to watch and to eat again.

Caveat: this is not a paid review, I rarely write reviews for fast food chains and this one definitely deserves it.

review_text:
Came across this place on Instagram and decided to try it since it’s just across the road. The space is quite small, but we were lucky to get a table before the queue started forming.

Food-wise, service was slow but manageable. We ordered the signature pasta, vongole, and black truffle flatbread. We also wanted to try the uni tartufo, but it was already sold out by 7pm, which was a little surprising. The signature pasta was good — seasoning was on point and had just the right amount of garlic, exactly to our liking. The vongole was okay, not bad but not particularly memorable.

The black truffle flatbread took about 45 minutes to arrive, which we didn’t quite understand. I also added $3 for hot honey, thinking it would be served on the side, but it was poured directly over the flatbread. That was disappointing, especially since my boyfriend doesn’t like honey with his food. But the flatbread was good. We also felt unusually thirsty after the meal, not sure if it was due to MSG.

One downside was leaving the restaurant with our clothes smelling strongly of food AND food flies hovering around because of the open kitchen and lack of ventilation, which was quite unpleasant. Overall, it was an okay experience

author: Max Wee

review_text:
Really surprised to see a Canteen show up in a Police Station on Google Maps. Even more surprised to learn that this Canteen is actually Open to the Public!

Here are the procedures to enter:

1) Exchange your Singapore NRIC for a Visitor Pass at the Guardhouse, provide your Mobile Number and declare your intention to visit the Canteen.

2) Wear your Visitor Pass and display it prominently

3) Enter the Main Glass Door Entrance of the Police Station and the Canteen is just left of the Main Reception Desk. You can't miss it.

Its not a Huge Canteen, and consists of only 1 Thai Food Stall, 1 Muslim Food Stall and 1 Drink Stall.

For the Thai Stall however,  what impressed me most is that the Stall Lady is an Actual Thai. This gives me confidence that the Food sold here should be more authentic. There are many Dishes on sale and most cost around S$6.00

--------------------

泰国猪脚饭 (Thai Pig Foot Rice) = S$6.00

This was the Dish that made me want to come here after seeing photos of it in other Reviews of this place.

When this was served to me, I admit I was slightly disappointed that the Veggie given is Kailan and not Salted Veggies as shown in other People's Dishes. This means that the Ingredients are not standardized, or maybe I was unlucky and they were out of Salted Veggies? There are also no Pork Intestines in this version. Also no Soup given as compared to other people's photos.

While I cannot say the Pork leg is the Soft until Melt in Mouth type. Portion given is acceptable for the price. Rice portion is also reasonable and filling. I like the Sauce they lum in this Dish as it is both Salty and Savoury.

The Chilli is Bitingly Spicy with a Slight Sweetness. Adding this to the Dish elevates it to another level making it more enjoyable to eat. Overall I would say this is not bad, but could be better.

--------------------

Pad Gaprao (Stir-Fry Basil with Minced Pork and Fried Egg) = S$6.00

This is of course the Classic Thai Dish and the version here taste not bad at all. Amount of Minced Pork is Very Generous and is even More than the Rice Given! Smells Really Amazing and its not overly Wet type. The Basil Taste is not that strong, but perhaps this is modified to suit the Singapore Palette more. Dish is not very spicy.

Overall Dish has a Nice Salty and Savoury taste. $6.00 is worth it. Special Note to the Fried Egg as I thought it had a Nice Bouncy Fluffy Bite Feel even though the Yolk is not the Runny Type.

--------------------

1 Cup of Hot Kopi-O = S$0.90

This Kopi-O is of course from the Drink Stall. Its not the Gao Gao type and I feel its somewhat sweeter than usual Kopi-Os. The Main Reason i'm even listing it here is because I can finally tell someone I have "Lim Kopi in a Police Station!" hahaha!

--------------------

This is my first time eating in a Police Station and I'll admit it is quite interesting to be eating Lunch with so many Police Officers.

The Thai Food here is not bad. The Thai Stall Lady is Very Friendly and it is worth the money, and I highly recommend coming here to give it a try if only to have the unique experience of dining in a Police Station!

At the very least, now you finally have a Legal Way to tell others you "Lim Kopi in a Police Station!" hahaha!

Important Notes:
1) As this is a Police Station, it goes without saying that you should behave yourself and not anyhow suka suka treat this place like some Tourist Attraction and wander all over the place and take photos willy nilly ok?

Even my photos I posted here are also abit Grey Area tbh. Dear SPF, i've only taken photos of the Canteen and Food and nothing else. Please let me know if you want me to delete them and I will do so immediately.

2) As Members of the Public, it would be Gracious if in the event of a queue, to allow our Police Officers to order their meals first as they may have very limited time for their Meals due to their Duties. Lets be nice to our Police Officers ok?

review_text:
Happy to be labeled a unsophisticated Singaporean, I just like my pizzas Hawaiian.

For a start, we entered the restaurant on a Friday evening (before 6pm), no customers, and 4 staff at the front/ entrance.

I don't expect warm welcomes, but a simple acknowledgment won't be out of order, but we didn't get one, so I had to ask for attention from staff standing just 1 meter away.

We got a table. Ordering was via QR code, and the experience was the usual. But the check out ain't great, took half a dozen attempts to get the order to kitchen.

Not to mention the unnecessary request for name and phone number to compete the order (does this pass PDPA?) Also, the not too subtle request for tips, which is clearly not our culture.

Most critically, we didn't like the pizza. I paid for extra tomatoes sauce but it did not make it any better/ sweeter (I'll have to be imaginative to figure how it'll be like with the standard tomatoes sauce). Also, the pineapple cubes were also not sweet, but the pizza base/ crust was ok.

review_text:
Had dinner at Wheeler’s Estate with the family and here’s my honest take. We ordered four dishes for three adults and one kid. The bill came up to slightly over $100.

The Korean Fried Chicken and Pork Jowl were the standouts. They were flavorful, tender, and worth the try. The BBQ Pork Ribs, however, were a bit of a letdown as they were too dry for our liking. The pizza was tasty but best enjoyed while it’s hot, as the crust gets a little tough when it cools.

We went on a Tuesday night and were pleasantly surprised by a live band playing mostly Chinese songs. I loved the open-concept dining area and the relaxed vibe. It’s definitely a nice spot for a chill evening with friends.

review_text:

The outdoor ambience was fantastic — spacious, green, and relaxing. The addition of live music made the evening even more enjoyable, creating a laid-back yet lively atmosphere.

Overall, Wheeler’s Estate is a great spot for quality Western food in a scenic setting. Perfect for a casual night out with friends or a date night.

author: Suresh vinod

review_text:
We came as a group of 16 pax, so we were given 3 tables when we arrived. (We made reservations ahead of time)

Food came very promptly and was all piping hot, something we really really appreciate with both elderly and children in our group!! The food was great too, everyone loved the food - the tomahawk was done to the right doneness, the beef cheek was wonderful, the roasted chicken, burgers, fish and chips all wonderful.

The service we got that night however, was downright appalling.

The service staff kept trying to clear our table even when we were still eating. They did not seek our permission before trying to clear the table - they simply leaned over us and reached for our plates and tried to clear them.

I had to stop the service staff twice (not including my other family members) from clearing our plates because we still had food on them??? They did not apologize either.

The whole meal we either had the service staff hovering around our tables staring at us eat, or interrupting us and trying to clear our plates all the time. It was very uncomfortable and unpleasant.

When we tried to ask about water, your staff told us rudely “order from the app”. We couldn’t hear him because of the music so he repeated in an even ruder way “SIR, ORDER FROM THE APP”

Shortly after, one of the service staff took a customer’s water bottle and filled it for her, for free.

When the children at our table went to the playground for a short break, the staff immediately cleared the whole table of all plates and cutlery without asking if we were done. At one point there were 2 staff gesticulating at the empty tables that they cleared, unhappy that it was unoccupied (the children were at the playground)

One of your service staff glared at me with hostility, so I simply held his gaze until he turned away. I went to ask the hostess if there was a dining time limit, just to be sure we were not overstaying our welcome. She confirmed there was no dining time limit and I was free to stay for as long as I liked.

Strange how we were made to feel like we had to clear out of the restaurant ASAP. She later came back to whisper to me to say “there is no time limit for eating but please let me know if you are done with the tables so we can release the tables”, which I completely understand. I told her we were going to cut a birthday cake and then going to leave.

So we called for the cake, sang the song and cut the cake. When your very diligent service staff once again cut in front of us to clear our near-empty and unused plates, I told him we were done with one of the tables (at the end) and we were happy to release it.

(At this point there were still more than 15 empty tables in the restaurant)

He scoffed at me and said there’s no need to because we are still using the other 2 tables and there’s “no point” while rolling his eyes and gesticulating at me. I did not respond to him but chose to sit back down instead.

The music by Shirlyn and the Unexpected was wonderful though and made things a little better in the end!!!!

Full marks for the food and the music, but the service here desperately needs work.

author: Jas Blur

review_text:
The restaurant at Seletar Country Club offers an open-air dining experience, with both covered and uncovered seating areas. While the setting is pleasant, our visit was marred by extremely poor service, which overshadowed what could have been an enjoyable meal.

We were seated at the far end of the restaurant near the stage, but despite waving multiple times, no staff came to take our order even after 15 minutes. It was frustrating to be completely ignored, especially when other tables seemed to be getting prompt service. Eventually, we had to walk up to the front to request assistance, only to be met with an unprofessional and rude response from a staff member who simply said she was busy and then proceeded to serve another table in front of us without offering any help.

After another frustrating wait, a different staff member finally came over with a tablet to take our order. While the food itself was good, the poor service and dismissive attitude of the staff left a lasting negative impression. No matter how good a restaurant’s food is, customer service plays a crucial role in the dining experience, and unfortunately, this place fell far short of expectations. Unless the service improves, I wouldn’t recommend this restaurant, as no one wants to spend their meal feeling ignored and frustrated.
author: Wesley Wong

review_text:
Hosted guests to dinner at the Seletar Tavern over National Day Weekend.
Opted for the open section which have a very nice alfresco vibe. However rain clouds gathered n all the diners started moving into the sheltered area. We asked one of the waitress for option and help and all she did was just simply shrugged off and ignored our pleas for help.
We had to, on our own accord, request another table to shift n we sorted out table nto the sheltered area amongst the diners without a single assistance from the staff
Later as we waited for the waitress to take our ordered, we tried to get the attention of another waiter to help get water for our guests. Despite almost shouting at the top of our voice for his attention and he obviously heard and saw it, he  ignored and walked off!!!
Later when the waitress came up take orders, she was rude and curt to the extent one of the guest had to remark that the service here was terrible!!!
Throughout the entire evening, all the waitresses and waiters were all very unpleasant and just not bothered about their serving attitude.
We understand that it was a busy evening and no service charge for this tavern, however this terrible attitudes cannot go on!!! For that matter, we have been here several times before( because of the good food ) but we have never failed to be disappointed repeatedly for this lack of service and unpleasant attitude.
Thankfully the quality of the food really saved the day.
Hopefully the club management would look into this matter which is not a one off and also experienced by other reviewers!!
To add a note, usually a staff by the name of Karen would save the day with her pleasant attitude but unfortunately she was not around during this weekend.
author: Janczz W

review_text:
A perfect evening out with friends to celebrate SG60 turned out to be one huge disappointment. While the food was tasty and ambience relaxing, the experience was tarnished by the lack of service by the waiters/waitresses. It was difficult to get their attention for anything else other than taking your orders (which they did all in a haste and gives one the feeling that they cannot wait to brush you off - zero eye contact with a face that mops the floor)
I hope the management can do something about this team of servers...Ive been here several times before and each time I was greeted with a sub standard service...I'm not sure I will return to patronize again
author: soh-ping Elliot Eng

review_text:
We recently visited here for a small birthday dinner with 19 people, including 5 young children and our helpers. We were seated in the outdoor area where casual attire, such as shorts and singlets, seemed acceptable as many were dressed down, However, once we were seated, we were informed that our helpers, wearing slippers, were not allowed to be at the table with us. This was surprising given the outdoor setting.

Despite our request for understanding due to the small children, the staff (lady in black shirt) ignored our request for menus twice and insisted we sort out the slipper issue. Their response was uncompromising: either send the helpers away or receive no service. We eventually found spare slides (open toe slipper) for the helpers from our car , and only then did we receive service.

This situation severely affected our celebration. The service was poor, and two waitresses were heard badmouthing and commenting on other guests right behind us.

The only positives were the view (5/5) and the food (4/5). Unfortunately, the staff's attitude and behaviour ruined the ambiance. They were clearly lacking on knowledge on how to behave anywhere near or in clear sight of guest.
author: Rohit Roshan

review_text: Excellent live band every Saturday evening!
author: Chris Ng

review_text:
Overall experience is 3.5/5 food wise squid is the tougher side and sauce combination does not match with the grill. Types of Sushi is limited. Grill
Salted salmon belly is skin is well grill to perfection. Didn’t try the sashimi so this is base on cook food selection.
author: Yi Qi Yee

review_text: Great place for a cozy Sunday Japanese luncheon. Very attentive service by the wait staff 👍🏻. Dishes were well executed , well presented and with fresh ingredients. Kudos to the Chef and the entire team. Appreciate the service and great food.
author: Damien Tan

review_text: A little pricey for items served for the lunch Omakase at SGD 80 but if I put price and value aside, I enjoyed the meal and ingredients were fresh eg. Sashimi and Deep fried breaded fish.
author: Dylan S

review_text:
We’ve dined at Jo Japanese Restaurant at Seletar Country Club a few times now, and the experience has been consistently good. The restaurant has a quiet, calm atmosphere that’s perfect for a relaxed and unhurried meal.

During our recent visit, we had the chance to meet the boss, who was incredibly warm and hospitable. He even treated us to sample several different types of sake, which made the evening feel extra special and personal.

Food-wise, the tempura is a must-try - light, crispy, and not oily. Another highlight is the meatballs, which are handmade in-house rather than processed. You can really taste the difference, juicy, and flavorful.

Overall, this place truly feels like a hidden gem for Japanese food, good sake, and genuine hospitality. We’ll definitely keep coming back.
author: Xin Lua

review_text: A nice jap restaurant situated in the country club. Food was decent and priced reasonably. Dont expect Japan standard quality but it was still good.
author: Chang Yi Tong

review_text: Checked the ratings here before we decided to make a reservation. Seletar CC welcomes public to dine here as well. You will be glad it’s free parking with ample lots. Restaurant is located at level 2. The superb green fields view greeted us and we even gotten a window seat which is awesome. We ordered the buffet and it was a great choice. The beef cuts, pork loin were surprisingly very tasty and easy to cook. Even have honey of garlic beef options. Staff were on the ball to change bbq plate and even offered to cook for your table. You will find it easy to pop in the clean toilets that were inside the restaurant. A good choice to visit this branch!
author: Mervyn Phea

review_text:
BBQ with a view! ⛳️🔥

Really enjoyed the vibe here! The restaurant has a stunning view of the golf course, which makes for a very comfortable and relaxing dining experience.

The food was generally good across the board. The BBQ Pork was tender and well-seasoned, but the highlight for me was the steam egg with cheese- so fluffy and delicious! Definitely a great spot if you want quality K-BBQ with a peaceful atmosphere.
author: Elias Pong

review_text: A very authentic Korean restaurant. A must get is definitely their Beef Soybean Stew (Doenjjang Jjigae) - very umami, flavourful, and generous beef slices. The Grilled Beef Ribs were also amazing. The flavour is so good!! Salty with a hint of sweetness. Kimchi stew is on the sour side. The quality of the food here is amazing and very consistent, I have been a regular here for a few years and the food quality has remained excellent.
author: iateyuwei

review_text:
Had dinner at Ju Shin Jung and left thoroughly impressed. The staff were friendly, attentive, and genuinely happy to help — whether it was refills or special requests, nothing felt like a chore to them. You can really taste the care in every dish. Even the white rice had a delicious scorched finish that added depth.

The barley drink was a standout — rich and flavourful, unlike the watered-down versions you get elsewhere. Every side dish was excellent, and their sauces, especially the gochujang, were packed with flavour. The lettuce for wrapping the pork was fresh and perfectly shaped, making each bite satisfying.

We tried the Korean pancake, steamed egg, and pork — all spot on. You truly get what you pay for here. The environment is clean, with nearby washrooms and a lovely view of the golf course. Definitely planning a return visit!
author: John

review_text:
This place is amazing!🤩 At first, I didn't want to go here, but when I tried  it, I felt like...I was in a place where it is very very expensive and only very rich people can go. The beef was a little bit fatty but at the same time, juicy!

There was one thing i really liked about the place - the shrimp pancake was crispy and aromatic, so scrumptious!

I had fun cooking the beef, even though the pan was very hot.

I would definitely come back every weekend if my parents allow us to because it is ssoooooo expensive.🤑🤑
author: SH G

restaurant_name: Seletar Terrace at Seletar Country Club
review_text:
Local fare at Seletar Country Club.
Hokkien mee and Har Cheong gai were good.
Decent hawker fare but service lacking.
author: A T

restaurant_name: Seletar Terrace at Seletar Country Club
review_text:
Took away Kaya toast set for brother. Take note that if the menu says kaya toast, they literally mean kaya with no butter. So basically I can either buy “kaya butter toast” or “kaya toast with egg”. The bread is just some supermarket bread and kaya taste like the fairprice brand. That’s all fine but it’s not supposed to be worth $5+.

Also, adding two eggs cost $2.50, and they do not even crack it for you. Imagine if someone want takeaway to eat it on the go but is left with a couple of uncracked eggs. Other places like Heavenly Wang will always crack the eggs free of charge if the order is to go.

Standards of this place is rock bottom because they run a monopoly within the club, they are essentially holding guests on a food hostage by letting them run like this.
author: Siah Rui Heng

restaurant_name: Seletar Terrace at Seletar Country Club
review_text:
It was a breezy and cold afternoon, so the Nasi Lemak and Latte is the perfect combo to chill.

Food wise, nothing much to shout about, the chicken wing is at least crispy and tasty, the rice is OK, the fish, not so much.

All in all, go there enjoy the quietness and chill because of the weather is cool. Hot afternoon may have to choose a seat further away from the sun.
author: Kelvin Soh

restaurant_name: Seletar Terrace at Seletar Country Club
review_text: Good food but they prioritise members. That means you got to stand in queue till they clear all members.
author: JC C

restaurant_name: Seletar Terrace at Seletar Country Club
review_text:
What has happened to the food??? We have not been back to the terrace for a few months, but the flavour profile of the Hokkien mee, fish and chips, carrot cake and chicken satay have ALL changed.

The carrot cake is drier and less tasty overall. The chicken satay still has the outer glaze but after the initial bite, the blandness completely overwhelms your entire mouth. The Hokkien mee likewise is also now an inferior version of what it used to be. The fish and chips…. DRY. Devoid of moisture. These all used to be our favourite dishes because they were all full of unique flavours.

Dinner today was a shock to the palette. We are sadly filled with sadness and disappointment. Please go back to what it used to be!
author: DT

review_text:
Environment/Atmosphere: I think this is an area where the old British house are being built previously and revamped for restaurants/bars. Very serene and chill vibes, if you want to escape from the city frills.
Food: Overall is good but not to the extent of mind-blowing. Manage your expectations well.
Service: Friendly Staffs. Food are served within the expected time.
author: Alvin Teo

review_text: Food is AMAZING. Not sure why I saw some mixed review about the taste is not authentic or strong enough but the dishes we had today were all a big hit for us. MUST TRY their dry laksa and lemongrass chicken. Will definitely come back to try other food on their menu.
author: éLife

review_text:
Came with my in laws to celebrate a birthday, and I must say overall this place is decent and I would most probably come back and bring my grandma who’s a peranakan to try the next time around.

There were hits and misses with the food, would still recommend to try what you want to try but here’s my take on it.

Kueh Pie Tee was great, but they already pre fixed how much chilli/ condiments in it, personally I prefer it spicier but this was already very decent.

The nonya chap chye here is a tad lighter in flavor compared to other places who serve it however, I kinda loved it and it gives you a home cooked feeling which I absolutely adore. Somehow the flavor it just flows.

Curry duck was a tad dry as expected but still ok.

Lemongrass chicken was great it may look plain but it’s prolly one of the better dishes here.

For the sambal petai, it was harder/crunchier than most places and I’m sure some people might love it some people might prefer it to be a tad softer.

The HBH okra were the bomb, definitely a great combination together simply loved it.

Udang lemak nenas, pineapple gravy prawn was my favorite of the night. It’s also a rarer dish imo in peranakan places and I absolutely loved it. Will come back again cause of this.

The omelette was basic but yeah always a joy to have egg dishes.

Service wise they were great at times but somehow they seem to be understaffed and it can take awhile before the busy servers get to you.

For the ambience they had singers singing which was a great idea but it was a little too loud and definitely during their gigs you couldn’t talk to each other.

All in all 4 would be an accurate rating in my opinion and I would definitely be back for the Udang!
author: Cedric Seet

review_text: The food was average. The fried century egg was the only interesting dish, the rest tasted quite ordinary, and the omelette and signature laksa were below expectation. None of the dishes were spicy, not even at a typical Nonya level, so it’s suitable for people who prefer very mild flavors. The service, however, was excellent.
author: Isabelle Lim

review_text:
We had a pleasant experience at Martin Kitchen and definitely plan to be back.

The standout factors here are the service and the environment. The service was genuinely good—our server was attentive, friendly, and made us feel well looked after. The environment is also fantastic; the space is comfortable, well-designed, and has a lovely ambiance that makes it a great spot for a relaxed meal.

As for the food, it was okay. Everything was perfectly satisfying, well-prepared, and tasty.

Overall, the combination of the excellent service and good environment makes this a great place to dine.
author: OB1

review_text:
This place gives a nice warm feeling. Nice lighting Great customer service. Great food and recommendations from the waiters. Self brewed beer. Air con and out door area.
Waitress Chloe is a great help. Very kind and thoughtful with great recommendations who took care of our table.
author: Desmond Tan

review_text: The food was delicious and the atmosphere was great! We ordered the mushroom pizza and the kids’ meal (fish and chips). The kids’ meal came with a drink and ice cream, which was a lovely touch. The mushroom pizza had a great variety of mushrooms and was very tasty. We also tried the craft beer — the Circuit Breaker New England IPA — which was very fruity and smooth. A special shoutout to Raine for being so helpful and even helping us take photos. Overall, a wonderful dining experience!” 🍕🍺
author: chiahuei lim

review_text:
Impeccable service equivalent to that of a top tier fine dining restaurant. Every single waiter/waitress on duty this date, served with warmth and friendliness which is rare on our little bustling island.

The Angus Beef Ribeye and Pork Cheese Katsu were immaculate. The desserts, Oatmeal Stout Beeramisu and Caramelised Date Pudding are worthy of high praise. Shoutout to the chefs we didn't get to meet, you guys did one hell of a splendid job mesmerizing our tastebuds with this pandora box of flavours.

A bonus point for this wonderful place is the song selection, great taste in music just as the food tasted great!

We didn't get the name of everyone we met but, thank you all from the bottom of our hearts. Truly amazing experience and we will be back for round 2, 3, 4 and perhaps the next decade.

Once again thank you Brewerkz team at Seletar Aerospace Park!
author: Erwin “Commander of Survey Corps” Smith

review_text: Kudos to service staff who begin the meal with friendly and attentive service. It’s really comforting after a week work. Atmosphere vibes is easy-going & relaxing, it’s a wonderful place to hang out with good food/ beer, great music and excellent service.
author: Eve Leow

review_text: It is a dog friendly cafe. Good to bring your pet to enjoy a weekend afternoon or evening. For outdoor space, it is better to have some stable big umbrella or automatic outdoor blind installed so that it can refrain from heat during lunch or afternoon tea time, although It was windy and cool for the day we visited and we enjoyed the light breeze and our food ordered. Yet to try it for dinner. Hope there will be more food items that we can order from the menu in future. Overall, it is a hidden gem in Seletar Aerospace for dog owners.
author: Anita

review_text:
My partner surprised me with a birthday dinner at Youngs and it was insanely good. The food was amazing. Wine was good too!

Special mention to Alex, great service and hospitality. Exemplary service, very hands on and very attentive. Keep up the good work! Looking forward to back at Youngs soon☺️
author: Jayke Grundy

review_text:
Was cycling around seletar with my wife when we stumbled upon Youngs. While finding a spot for our bicycles, the service staff came by and directed me to the available spaces. This gave us a great impression as it was unexpected that the staff would reach before we even ordered or step in.

Upon entry, the staff supported me with ordering, sharing about their buffet options for the day "buffet with mains" and "buffet without mains".
We took up the buffet without mains and was informed that it actually came with pasta and an omelette as well!
The pasta was in a singular serving which was sufficient considering the other buffet options. The omelette was amazing though, it filled the plate and remained fluffy in the middle.

The buffet spread definitely can't be comapred with international buffets, but it did come with pizzas, fries, sandwiches, sausages, popcorn chicken and an assortment of desert options!

The environment was great as well, not too crowded and was nicely decorated in an american diner style. This is a great place for a chill afternoon in the northern side of SG.
author: Alfred Pang

review_text:
The food was above average — every dish we tried was delicious.

We made our reservation the day before, but at 3 p.m. on the same day, the restaurant called to inform us that we needed to pay a $20 deposit per person and pre-order our meals. The payment could only be made via PayNow, not by credit card, which was a bit inconvenient.

When we arrived, we were seated right away. We had chosen an indoor table, but unfortunately, there was no air conditioning, and it was extremely hot. The staff tried to help but couldn’t resolve the issue.

Another thing that left me disappointed was the service during dinner. Our reservation was at 7 p.m., and we requested for the food to be served at 7:10 p.m. Around 8 p.m., an Indian waitress began clearing the tables even though there were still 11 of us at the table and one person hadn’t finished eating yet. The rest of us were just chatting. She politely asked before clearing, but the constant interruptions made us feel like we were being rushed to leave — even though there were no customers waiting for tables.

If there is a dining time limit, I think the restaurant should inform customers when collecting the deposit or upon arrival. Personally, I don’t think 1.5 hours is too long, and in our case, we had been there for less than an hour.

Overall, while the food was great, the prepayment process and the rushed service affected the dining experience.
author: Serene Tham

review_text:
Made a reservation to dine there for my dad's birthday. Wait for the food was ok as we did not wait too long, but it was also not too crowded at that time.

I would give high marks for their food, their steaks are excellent, even the sides are delicious. My mum had the seabass which was also very good. My dad had the chicken, the breast meat part was a bit dry.

Overall environment is also cosy, though the music was blasted too loudly.

Service staff was not attentive though, they are friendly but we need to really get their attention.

Empty plates are not cleared before they serve the dessert, and we even have to ask for cutlery and plates for sharing.

As I was walking out after finishing my dinner, one of the staff made a tsk sound at me for blocking his way instead of allowing me to pass through.
author: Marilyn Teo

review_text: Went with my friend on Saturday, cozy environment & surprisingly not crowded at all. Very friendly service staffs…. Suitable for families & friends gathering & chill … Food was nice & has variety of drinks too. You can walk around The Oval after food … sunset is beautiful…
author: Laylan Goh

review_text: Usually eating kbbq = super smelly. This place their exhaust is right at the charcoal stove there which makes it really enjoyable. The service is good and food was great special mention the soybean paste seafood soup! I felt that the fried rice lacks the oomph thou but the rest are great! There's even free Hagen das Ice-cream
author: Jaecee Lim

review_text:
This Korean BBQ restaurant is located in a beautifully refurbished building within the conservation development of Seletar Aerospace Park. The surroundings are serene and peaceful, offering fresh air and a relaxing atmosphere. Inside, the décor is modern and inviting, especially the expansive glass windows that provide a great view while you enjoy your BBQ experience.

The meat is grilled nicely by the attentive staff, tender, and with excellent flavor. The side dishes are equally impressive; their refreshing tanginess not only enhances your appetite but also cleanses the palate between different cuts of meat. The doenjang (fermented soybean paste) stands out for its premium quality, adding a rich depth of flavor that elevates the entire meal.

Don’t miss the kimchi soup and seafood pancake - they’re delicious and complement the BBQ perfectly.
author: J Seng

review_text:
Was excited as it is situated near the aerospace park. Food was a letdown despite its 4.5 star rating by with 1000+ reviews.

We ordered marinated short ribs, ox tongue, rice and garlic fries as we were quite full. Thankfully we didn’t order more…

When the box of leaves came, there was like only 2-3 greens? They did replenish with a box but it felt like we had someone’s leftovers.

Meat wasn’t well cooked asked for medium rare but it was mostly well done, hard and chewy. The tongue was utterly hard that we didn’t even eat more than two pieces. First one to try and second to confirm.

Even the rice was starchy.

The garlic fries was just fries with bits of mostly raw garlic thrown over it.

And the bill came up to be $60 per person?!? Most unsatisfying kbbq in a while.
author: Marcus-Averil Lin

review_text: We enjoyed our time here a lot! Delicious food and drinks with good service, had Haiman helping us with cooking the meat to perfection and Jason coming up with individualized cocktails (because they ran out of the on menu ones) 👍🏼
author: Ann SKP

review_text: Came here for a family birthday dinner - the whole Seletar Aerospace Park is very chill. We love the vibe. Great parking. Most of all, Chingu is a great discovery. The set BBQ is very worth it and great quality meats. We ordered ala carte mains and they were all very delicious. Food served within 10 mins of ordering despite it being a very busy PH eve and they were short staffed. Good job to the team, we will come back again for lunch!
author: Melvin Ryan Tan

restaurant_name: The Embun SG | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (HALAL)
review_text:
Nice food, great atmosphere, and excellent service.

Honestly surprised by how good the food was! Loved everything we ordered. Came during weekend lunch and it wasn’t crowded at all, which made the experience even better.

The staff were attentive and checked in with us to make sure everything was okay.

Will definitely be back!
author: Eileen T

restaurant_name: The Embun SG | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (HALAL)
review_text:
Coz of our large party size of 18pax, the restaurant requested a holding cost of $90.
We reserved earlier timing so that we dun miss out on the seafood/fish which we wanted them to grill. The grilled stingray takes quite some time to arrive. Slightly undercooked and some parts quite tough to bite though. The sambal is ok for our tastebud.
2 stingray (4pcs) = $166+ & cockles = $24+

We ordered the other cooked food and these seems to arrive quite fast. Most of the food are non spicy although it may looks spicy. 😅

Parking wise best to come about 6pm to get more parking slots during weekends. Otherwise u will need to look for carpark slightly further to walk from the restaurant.

Cost wise..it seems quite a stretch though. About $8++ for 18 of us. They only have service charge and no GST.

Nice ambience to enjoy the food. But it wont be 'anytime too soon' for us to come back again given the cost 🤭
author: Fizah Rahman

restaurant_name: The Embun SG | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (HALAL)
review_text: Ample parking spots within the area. The food was excellent — well-presented, flavourful, and clearly prepared with care. Each dish tasted fresh and satisfying, making the overall experience enjoyable. Serving portions huge and good for big crowd. There are live stations available for your seafood cravings with customised seasoning to meet your liking and the chef present with a smile and sincerity to recommend you their best selling recipe. Good ambience of music for romantic lunch and dinner or special occasion. Area within spots of unique bird species like the hornbill and also lake nearby to walk off those calories before heading home.
author: Alfa Runsi

restaurant_name: The Embun SG | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (HALAL)
review_text:
Alright, Google Level 8 hat on. Let us give Embun the respect it quietly demands.

Embun is one of those rare finds that does not shout for attention. It sits calmly in the Seletar area, tucked among roads with very London-sounding names, as if it knows confidence does not need advertising.

The halal food here is, quite frankly, a pleasant surprise. Not the “it is good for halal” kind of good. Just good, full stop.

The cereal prawns arrive unapologetically coated, crunchy, aromatic, and indulgent. The cereal is fragrant without being greasy, and the prawns still taste like prawns, which already puts this dish ahead of many pretenders.

The banana leaf fried rice is comfort done right. Simple, balanced, and not drowned in oil. Each grain stays distinct, the vegetables are fresh, and the egg is folded in properly instead of being an afterthought.

The grilled squid deserves a quiet nod of respect. Nicely charred, tender, and paired with just enough acidity to keep things lively. No rubbery drama, no over-seasoned regret.

And then there is the sambal stingray. Generously coated, smoky, spicy without being reckless, and clearly grilled with intention. This is the kind of dish that makes you slow down and eat properly instead of talking.

The atmosphere matches the food. Relaxed, unpretentious, and quietly confident. It feels like a place locals return to, not a place chasing trends or Instagram validation.

Embun is proof that you do not need hype, fancy interiors, or loud branding to serve excellent halal food. You just need consistency, care, and a kitchen that knows what it is doing.

If you are in Seletar and you miss this place, that one is entirely on you.
author: Zul M

restaurant_name: The Embun SG | Live Seafood • Ikan Bakar • Fresh Seafood (HALAL)
review_text: Came here with my family for dinner. Alhamdulillah everything was delicious and i love the environment. But a few things i wish could be better, the butter taste for butter garlic. And pls don’t dilute the soap for hand washing. For a restaurant i think thats the least yall could do. But other than that everything is good!
author: Filzah Rahmad

review_text: food was amazing - we ordered fish head steamboat, veg, caipo tofu, noodle, grilled sambal prawn and everything was great! 10/10 recommend especially when Seletar Aerospace gets very crowded. This place also serves alcohol and has darts as activity.
author: Leong

review_text:
Fish head steamboat with thick and delish broth. A hidden find in this quaint estate. All dishes we had are good!

76$ for a steamboat and 4 dishes. Great value!
author: Wenny Ow

review_text: Food average… More disappointing.. other then cheap nothing stands out
author: Pintaro Cookie

review_text: good food
author: chi'n steven

review_text: Great dining experience, very suitable for big friend groups and family gatherings! Warm atmosphere and the staff are very friendly as well. We thoroughly enjoyed their signature wings, butter fried sotong and black pepper crab
author: Xin Yi Low

review_text:
Used to patronise their main outlet at Sembawang and when they opened a branch at Sembawang Yacht Club (which has ceased operation).

Was happy to know they have recently opened a new outlet at The Oval (not so north up, so easier for my friends coming from other parts of Singapore).

Went for my birthday dinner yesterday but was disappointed. I was a fan of their creamy butter crab but when we ordered one yesterday, somehow it didn’t taste as delicious.

The salted egg pork ribs we ordered were also not fresh. One bite and we could tell they were frozen pork, not fresh pork.

We ordered their crab bee hoon soup too. While the crab was fresh, somehow the soup just lacked the wow factor, compared with Mexxbxxn Seafood or Uncle Lxxng.

The sambal lala was a letdown too. It was merely sambal sauce and egg, stir fried with the lala.

It has been a tradition to eat my favourite crab dishes on my birthday. However, this year’s meal was so unmemorable. My friends paid for the treat, so I don’t know how much they spent. But from our dining experience, we did not enjoy it and therefore it was not money well-spent.

Lesson learnt: for creamy butter crab, only go to their main outlet.
author: laybit

review_text:
Generous portion, though the curry fish head sauce was a little salty but tasted just fine with plain rice.

Polite and friendly staff - they’re very attentive to patrons’ needs even though we were seated outdoors.
author: Bernice L

review_text: Revisited 1036. Food was actually edible but it's really a hard to swallow scene to see only 2 staffs running the service for not even a full house crowd split over 3 area of sittings. Luckily went earlier & got the food after slightly more than 1 hour. Not sure the history of this brand but something needs to be done about the service & the menu as it's just feel out of place in Oval.
author: Heng Luan Ting

review_text: First time at this place. Simple and good food. Reasonably priced too. Had darts that was a plus for darters. Owner very friendly and approachable. Staff was attentive too. Only slight downside is the waiting time for the food, however, the freshness and taste compensates it all. Thank you.
author: Christina Tan

review_text:
I had such a wonderful experience dining here. From the moment I walked in, I felt genuinely welcomed and cared for. The staff especially Angela, Prisca, and Serena was incredibly warm, attentive, and friendly. Their hospitality truly made the visit special.

They took the time to introduce and recommend several delicious dishes, explaining everything with enthusiasm and patience. You can really feel their passion and sincerity in the way they serve guests.

Every dish came, and i cleared the plate as it was that good and paired with such lovely service, it made the entire experience even more memorable. Thank you for the great hospitality~ I’ll definitely be back again!
author: Pintaro Cookie

review_text:
Was here for dinner on a Friday night. Parking was right below the restaurant so it was convenient.

Food was great. Had the pork collar & duck leg for mains.

Ambience was good. Restaurant manager Narresh was very hospitable and friendly as well. Definitely looking forward to future visits.
author: Eric David

review_text:
We held our wedding luncheon at SummerHouse on 29/11/2025, and we are so glad we chose this venue over the traditional hotel ballroom setting.

The venue itself is stunning—a perfect blend of modern vintage design with a beautiful garden atmosphere, and it comfortably accommodated our 130 guests. We also had a special request for a Teh Tarik station (Raja Tarik, PartyMojo), and the team was incredibly accommodating in making that happen.

A huge shout-out to the manager, Narresh, who went above and beyond for our wedding. From our first food tasting to the actual day, Narresh was patient, professional, and proactive in addressing our many concerns.

We also want to recognize Celest, our venue-appointed wedding coordinator. She collaborated seamlessly with our wedding planner (Amperian) to manage all the logistics, which allowed us to actually focus on enjoying our big day.

I highly recommend considering SummerHouse if you are looking for a venue that breaks away from the conventional.
author: edison lau

review_text:
I was here for a wedding, so the wait stuff were very busy I must give kudos to them for trying to keep up with all the tasks, such as serving, clearing plates, topping up drinks. The good thing about this place is that it is pet-friendly. However if you have elderly family members, it’s not so easy to get up the stairs because there is no elevator.

The food was part of a set menu, the warmly baked bread with butter was delicious. Then we had tomato basil soup which had a piece of ravioli inside. After which the mains was a choice of fish or beef. The taste was average but the portion is huge. I think when they mass prepare the dishes somehow part of the flavours was being lost. The fish skin was grilled but not crispy, and same for the kale. Lastly the dessert was mind-blowing I really liked it, a citrusy dessert with some light sponge. It was refreshing on a hot day.
author: Donovan Leong

review_text:
not badd the fish i quite like

but my chicken was quite mehhh

a bit expensive also i guess but its cause its a nice venue so they upcharge for that
author: Justin Chong

review_text:
We had a fantastic dining experience at Botanico. From the moment we arrived, the service was warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming. The staff were really friendly, offered helpful recommendations, and ensured we were well taken care of throughout the meal.

The food was excellent — beautifully presented, thoughtfully prepared, and full of flavour. Each dish was well-balanced and showcased the quality of the ingredients. The pacing of the meal was just right, allowing us to fully enjoy every course.

The ambience also deserves a mention, with its serene, greenery-filled setting creating a relaxed yet elegant atmosphere. Overall, Botanico offers a complete dining experience with great food, outstanding service, and a lovely environment. Highly recommended, and we would definitely return.
author: valerie

review_text:
Had such a great experience at Botanico! The ambience is honestly one of the highlights — surrounded by lush greenery, it feels like a peaceful garden escape away from the city. Perfect for a date night or just catching up with friends.

The food was beautifully presented and tasted just as good as it looked. Everything was well-balanced and flavourful, and you can tell they put real thought into the ingredients and plating. Service was attentive without being overbearing, and the staff were friendly and welcoming.

Overall, Botanico is a great spot if you’re looking for good food, relaxing vibes, and a slightly upscale but comfortable dining experience. Would definitely come back again!
author: wylie pang

review_text:
