Experience at the Botanico at the Summerhouse was great! The ambience was chill, service as also great with the team being attentive to all guests. We tried the festive menu which was definitely value for money.
Appetizers were fresh and great (oysters were awesome and the skewered salmon was lightly smoked and delicious). The turkey and the beef tenderloin for the mains were also delicious and to finish off was a really light yet sweet matcha dessert.
author: Stephanie Chin

review_text: Some of the best food i have ever had in my whole life. I ordered the private dining course meal. Just amazing. Service was very attentive too. 100/10 recommend
author: Ashley Kee

review_text: A BIG thank you to Narresh at The Summerhouse – Garden Dome for making our birthday dinner so memorable. His deep knowledge of the dishes, photographic skills for capturing the perfect photos, and thoughtful attention to our needs—even without being asked—truly made the evening special. We really appreciate his care and professionalism! Highly recommended!
author: Vijayandren Suppiah

review_text:
First off, good things first.  Service was impeccable, the team running Nomads deserves credit where it is due.

Ambience was good too, they really made hanging out there feel like camping.

Really pleased with how they put in effort to make sure furry friends were comfortable and well taken care of too.

What I didn’t like?  The food.

Ribs were dry.  The beef in their Beef & Asparagus rice in a Mess Tin was dry and tough.

Sliders were a mess to eat.

Everything else fried, like onion rings, calamari and fries, were so so.

Come for the amazing ambience and awesome service.  Makes a nice place to hang out.

Just don’t expect to be blown away by the food.
author: Ed T

review_text:
I feel the best month to come here is in January. It is sunny, but there is plenty of breeze and I was here this month (Jan), sat at the outdoor camping tables under a tent! Nonetheless, if you prefer shade and indoors, there are tables available too. But the ones under the tentage do give a better vibe and correlate to their brand name better.

We had brunch here. Their menu is both normal from other cafes and also quite a variety to choose from. The rosti, according to my partner, was average. I had the avocado toast with poached eggs which I felt was good and they are very generous with the mashed avocado and nuts. Also, the truffle fries portion is huge too, perhaps too much for a couple and should be good for sharing if you come in 4s or more. Coffee is average and nothing to comment about.

Service is pretty fast. Despite watching them to be very busy at the front area, actually there is calmness to what they do. Food is served at the right pace even though the place is crowded. They also had some dog snacks so that the dogs can also have some food while their hooman is enjoying theirs. The outdoor lawn is very clean and neat and I feel that I can just roll around.
author: Alan Tan

review_text:
Cozy area catered for doggies

Finger food were great, ordered the platter and had a bit of everything. Main dishes served in mess tin were rather disappointing. Pork ribs and sliders weren’t fantastic as well.

Service on the other hand was fantastic!

Overall nice camping experience but more for finger food and doggies to mingle. Reservations highly recommended
author: TTT

review_text:
January 2026
- Variety of seating available; indoors, bar, tables, but the most fun was the outdoor tents with camping tables and chairs.
- Pets allowed, and saw many diners with their dogs.
- During the day, it can get hot and sunny in the tents.
- Service staff were friendly, and quick.
- I enjoyed the food, it was about as expected for the price and location.
- The coffee was good.
author: Wei Yuet Wong

review_text:
What an incredible find!! Loved the creative menu - appreciate the chef's take of adding a twist to your usual cafe food.
Service was great as well - there when you need them and food + drinks were served quickly.
Will definitely be back to try their extensive selection
author: Ju Amir

review_text:
Absolutely zero regrets traveling all the way to Seletar for Cinder! Such a wonderful delight.

Arguably the best lobster bisque in SG. Both in terms of taste and quality and quantity. Unlike many other places where the bisque is more cream than essence or very few lobster pieces. Cinder lobster bisque is a solid and substantial dish that one must order. Thumbs up! 👍🏻

Service crew were extremely polite courteous and friendly. Making us feel very at ease and at home. Really enjoyable.

Tried the lobster linguine, beef carpaccio and iberico pork chop which were great as well. Beef was very fresh.

Will definitely return again for more!
author: Desmond Tan

review_text:
Truffle fries set us up for a great meal right from the start. Crispy, fragrant, and hard to stop snacking on. The lobster pasta was very flavourful and satisfying, with generous seafood taste in every bite.

The steak was done right, perfectly cooked to medium rare and full of flavour. It paired beautifully with the recommended wine, which really elevated the whole experience.

Lovely interior with a warm, stylish atmosphere, plus a wonderful walkable outdoor area that makes it even more enjoyable. A great spot for a relaxed and quality meal.
author: Ruth Go

review_text:
We visited Cinder Steakhouse at Wheeler’s Estate and were seated on the 2nd floor, which was beautiful and private.

The staff were very welcoming, especially Ling, who brought smiles and laughter not just to us, but to our baby as well. Even when our baby was a little fussy, she made us feel comfortable and at ease.

Food wise, we enjoyed the foie gras and lobster bisque, both were well executed and flavourful.

Overall, good food and thoughtful service. Would return.
author: Jenny Cheng

review_text:
Service:
Had a lovely dinner celebration for my wedding anniversary at this place. Told them ahead of time about the occasion and they prepared a nice table along the verandah which was more secluded and could hear the music from Wheeler's Estate (which we enjoyed). The music was not too loud and the restaurant atmosphere was cost and comfortable. Subsequently, the staff also prepared a brownie and a small card which is an excellent gesture. They made arrangements for a table at Wheeler's Estate subsequently where we could enjoy the live music. Staff were attentive to our needs, professional, and hospitable.

Food: We ordered the Wagyu Ribeye, Lobster Linguine, Truffle fries, and Sapporo White Draught (Which was part of happy hour). The steak was cooked perfectly, and accompanying portion of the truffle fries was very generous. Bernaise sauce was a perfect accompaniment. Lobster Linguine was perfectly cooked. Most of the meat was already removed from the shell, hence eating it was not an inconvenience at all. The broth that it was cooked it was rich and umami.

Price: I found the price to be reasonable for the quality of the food, the ambience and professional service of the staff. It is what you would expect for what was served and it's impeccable quality.

I will recommend this place for special occasions and will definitely try to visit again.
author: Leon Seow

review_text:
Enjoyed a wonderful birthday dinner at Cinders.

Steaks were nicely cooked and paired with various types of sauces.

We want to give a big shoutout to Ramd and Kamal for their attentive service. Their care from adjusting the aircon temperature to automatically refilling our water was truly appreciated. We couldn’t have asked for better service. They even surprised us with a cake, Polaroid and signed card, making the birthday celebration even more memorable.
author: Huiloon Ang

restaurant_name: Laddas House (Private Home Dining - Bookings only)
review_text: Cannot imagine a flat could house a literal restaurant serving amazing quality Thai dishes that you may not find on your trip to Bangkok. Loved the flavours and heartfelt dishes. Portion was huge, you will definitely leave stomach and heart full😋
author: Kimberly Foo

restaurant_name: Laddas House (Private Home Dining - Bookings only)
review_text: My 2nd time at this private home Thai dining experience last night. Every dish was full of flavour, care and authenticity. The host and his wife made the evening extra special - welcoming, knowledgeable and clearly passionate about what they do. Highly recommended.
author: Jasmine Wah

restaurant_name: Laddas House (Private Home Dining - Bookings only)
review_text:
It was an amazing experience dining at Laddas House last night. We thoroughly enjoyed the authentic Thai cuisine (catered specially to the spice level of some of our family), the friendly yet professional service, and the chance to have our own chit chat time in between courses.
Absolutely recommend it!
author: Sharon Chen

restaurant_name: Laddas House (Private Home Dining - Bookings only)
review_text: There were 8 of us for dinner and we totally enjoyed ourselves! The cozy ambience, friendly hosts & superb delicious meal! I had “幸福感” when biting into every bit of the dishes! Must thank our friend, Will for the good recommendation!
author: Angela Hong

restaurant_name: Laddas House (Private Home Dining - Bookings only)
review_text:
WOW! What an amazing food experience. We were blown away by Terrence & Laddas hospitality, amazing food and amazing home. We wanted to spend our wedding dinner at a place that we knew we would like the food (a family of mega foodies with heavy salty taste bud!). Laddas house was so amazing that we want to make sure that they are a staple private dining place for our relatives EVERY TIME they come down from Malaysia.

Terrence was amazing that he made sure that communication is timely, our food preferences were surveyed previously, our dietary requirements were understood and even down to the last detail of the type of playlist we like during dinner.

The esthetic of their home was beautifully decorated that it came off an interior design magazine. The crockery and cookware was so pretty that we wanted to steal one home.

When we couldn't finish the 8-course meal, they were kind enough to offer us take away bags.

OH MY GOD I so want to gatekeep this secret but i just have to spread the joy of food through Laddas cooking.

There isn't enough stars we can provide ♥️♥️♥️♥️♥️

Price = $720 for 6 pax and worth every penny. You know when you're at a good place when you're already full at course #2, and licked every drop up until dessert.
author: Abby Ho

review_text: I had a fantastic experience at Lao Hero Kitchen. The food was absolutely delicious—everything tasted fresh and flavorful. What really stood out, though, was the service. The staff were incredibly friendly and made us feel right at home. I highly recommend checking this place out!
author: Toh Anderlin

review_text:
Recently, I had the chance to visit  this restaurant. It was crowded with people, and we had to wait a short while to be seated. The restaurant service was not up to the mark as the server was inexperienced and didn't seem to know what to do. The service was slow, and it took us more than half an hour to get our food served, even though we arrived early.

The black pepper crab, which was supposed to be the restaurant's signature dish, was overcooked and not very fresh. The taste was average, and it didn't live up to its hype. The best dish we ordered was the vegetable dish, which was delicious.

The fish maw soup disappointed us, and the prawns were not very fresh. It was the least worth ordering.

The restaurant had an upmarket and elegant setup, but the food quality and service standards didn't match up. It could be a concern for those who are short on time due to the slow service.

On the bright side, the restaurant had a clean toilet, which was a good experience. Overall, the restaurant wasn't a great dining experience, but it was worth it if you're in the mood for good veggies or a clean restroom
author: Moses -

review_text: Based on the few dishes we had. An average place that anyone can/will go for meal.
author: Terence Chew

review_text: Good value Malaysian and Chinese fusion. Flavourful without being salty.
author: Kelvin Lim

review_text:
Was there the first time to try out as it's pet-friendly. The service was remarkable and the lady boss( I assume) promptly seated us and informed us about the promotions that they are having. Very kind to move us to a table of 6 as we have 4A and 1 dog.

It's basically a zi char eatery albeit pricey as they have 10% service charge and the charges of drinks r slightly pricier. Besides, the portion of the food doesn't justify the price. I can finish the vegetables like within 4 to 5 mouths and it's like $13 per plate, there were less than 8 to 9 pcs of meat in the meat dish that I've ordered ( about $17.50) each. Fish and Chips had a fishy smell. The best dish I would say is the sambal lala.

All in all, I'll probably be back to try other dishes when I wanted a pet-friendly and no frills Zi char meal.
author: Tricia Lau

restaurant_name: Food & Beverage International Holdings Pte Ltd
author: Tay Lay Hong

restaurant_name: 友间厨坊 A Kitchen (Jalan Kayu)
review_text:
The chicken skewers are excellent - done just right! The fried squid is also tasty and cooked well.

Overall quality of the food is good, though the fried rice was quite disappointing.

Pricing is reasonable. There is a large car park nearby.

Recommended.
author: Ron Yang

restaurant_name: 友间厨坊 A Kitchen (Jalan Kayu)
review_text:
The prawns were very fresh and only steamed after ordering, so they came out hot and tasty. The meat was firm and sweet, and the soy dipping sauce made it even better.

The braised sliced beef was soft and full of flavor. It paired really well with a cold beer.

The skewers are fried and not grilled so I will skip that in the future.

The restaurant is next to a busy road, so it can be a bit noisy.
author: J Seng

restaurant_name: 友间厨坊 A Kitchen (Jalan Kayu)
review_text:
[Downgrade] Messy and no Q System.

Hidden gem in Jalan Kayu, comparable standards to those known Chinese restaurants in Chinatown. Must try their Cumin Beef and skewers, just that it can be quiet noisy, if you dont mind and just focus on the good food, it is a definitely must try!
author: Alexander Reinaldo

restaurant_name: 友间厨坊 A Kitchen (Jalan Kayu)
review_text: Serving portion could really be reduced. Cumin pork was well cooked and not too oily. As for the pickle fish, the fish could be sliced thinner and maybe a little more spice to the soup.
author: TTT

restaurant_name: 友间厨坊 A Kitchen (Jalan Kayu)
review_text:
casual Chinese restaurants specialize in Northern Chinese and Sichuan cuisine, featuring flavorful dishes and skewers. Cheap Beer & Reasonably Priced.

Must Try 羊蝎子，串串，香辣掌中宝 and 炖大鹅.
author: Lizard C

restaurant_name: Xi Guo 喜锅 火锅&烤肉 BBQ & Hotpot
review_text:
Most exp price is $29.90++ per pax, which is reasonable. You get free flow condiments and sauces (even have bbq powder and chilli powder), free flow items in the menu (less ala carte and drinks). Get free flow drinks at $1++, and soup base at $8++ (regardless whether is it 1, 2 or 4 soups).

Chicken soup, tomato soup and mala soup all very nice. Tried mushroom soup, which was a bit bland, but maybe because it's more for vegetarian? I'm not sure.

Meat wise, we only ate chicken and pork, pork tasted better for bbq than chicken.

Free flow drink top up of $1++ only allows you to take from machine - coffee (2/5), milk tea, orange juice (3.5/5).

The waitresses actively clears your empty plates, service is not too bad. I asked many questions because this was my first time there, and they were very patient to answer me.

There was indoor area with aircon, most importantly is that the bbq plate and soup pot is side by side. The bbq plate worked a bit slower, just bbq longer lor. Outdoor area the bbq and soup is like mookata, not very good I feel. Oh yes, there's no time limit, and the staff doesn't really chase you. We were there for 2ish hours haha. Can use credit card to make payment after meal.

Will go back again 👍
author: Swee Teng Low

restaurant_name: Xi Guo 喜锅 火锅&烤肉 BBQ & Hotpot
review_text: This restaurant is unique in the sense that they have a basement for dining. The meat and vegetables are fresh, but there are limitations in seafood. Do not forget to collect your ice cream in the main entrance before you leave.
author: Jason Tan

restaurant_name: Xi Guo 喜锅 火锅&烤肉 BBQ & Hotpot
review_text: Great steamboat and BBQ 2in1 buffet. All the meats are marinated very well and they are so tasty after BBQ. If you’re looking for a fantastic steamboat and BBQ experience, this restaurant is a must try. The variety of fresh ingredients, including premium meats, fresh seafood, and crisp vegetables, ensures that every bite is flavorful. The broths are rich and aromatic, with multiple options to suit different taste preferences.Downstairs there is a VIP room with KTV accessories. This is very amazing and very fit for family or friends gathering. Great eating experience here. We will visit again.
author: Selina Lee

restaurant_name: Xi Guo 喜锅 火锅&烤肉 BBQ & Hotpot
review_text: BBQ and hotpot at the same time feeling very content! The owner is super nice ! Fast service and fresh ingredients, the brown super rice cake is highly recommended! Must try !
author: HOICHING CHAN

restaurant_name: Xi Guo 喜锅 火锅&烤肉 BBQ & Hotpot
review_text: Newly Open China BBQ Steamboat Buffet in the Sengkang/ Fernvale Neighbourhood. 性价比高! Ingredients were fresh and good variety for price! BBQ Meat was good as well! Visit with empty stomach!! Must Try Mala Soup Base!!
author: Lizard C

review_text:
Anyways, I did not expect the medium size horfun to be this huge 🤣  Mala was fantastic as well ❗️

Portion is guaranteed fantastic 🤩Taste is superb, my non vege friends loved the Mala too 😍

Best Vege Supper Place 🎯
author: Sebastian Lim

review_text: Before heading over to Bike Station to check out their stock clearance, Kitty and another couple enjoyed a meal with me at SHU Vegetarian on Jalan Kayu. The location was super convenient, setting us up perfectly for our next stop. We were all really pleased with the food,  everything was quite tasty and satisfying. The highlight, for sure, was their "Samba Juice," which was incredibly refreshing and a great way to kick off our meal. I'd definitely recommend SHU Vegetarian to anyone looking for a delicious vegetarian meal in the Jalan Kayu area. It was a fantastic choice and made for a perfect start to our outing.
author: Doraemon

review_text:
SHU Vegetarian: A Great Start Before Bike Station!

Before heading over to Bike Station to check out their stock clearance, Donkey, myself and another couple (whose wife is vegetarian) enjoyed a meal at SHU Vegetarian on Jalan Kayu. The location was convenient, setting us up perfectly for our next stop. We were all pleased with the food – everything was quite tasty and satisfying. The highlight, without a doubt, was their "Samba Juice," which was incredibly refreshing and a great way to kick off our evening. SHU Vegetarian is a fantastic choice for anyone looking for a delicious vegetarian meal in the Jalan Kayu area, and it made for a perfect start to our outing.
author: oXRYSTALo Ong

review_text: I WISHHH there were more vegetarian supper spots in singapore 😭😭😭 like this is lowk the only one that a veg girlie can satisfy her midnight cravings with the wide array of pratas (they even have pizza prata? it’s $10 though but can try is can try!) they do have other foods like mala, zichar & caifan too! they’re also located in the famous supper stretch so it’s a vibeeee (sorry i can’t find any more pics)
author: forehead girl

review_text:
Good value fantastic taste freshly cooked food in aircon (warm!) or alfresco. Served promptly but don’t expect much customer oriented care. Can be a squeeze inside especially on Buddhist calendar days.

At 9pm to 1am there is a range of dishes that customers could pick from, like scoop scoop or teochew muay style.
Nasi lemak only starts at 9pm (not at lunch time:(
author: Jo K.

restaurant_name: NEW TASTE 新食代 @ Jalan Kayu
review_text:
As far as fragrant spicy grilled fish is concerned, Boon Keng New Taste is one of the best that I had in Singapore. The spiciness level is just right and the soup is delicious. The fish is fresh and the meat comes right off the bones. The French beans were also my favourite, soft inside while crispy on the outside. The salted minced pork adds some saltiness to balance out the vegetables. Pork belly skewers were really tasty as well.

Service was efficient and quick. Outdoor seating is available as well if you prefer an open area.
author: Henry Cheng

restaurant_name: NEW TASTE 新食代 @ Jalan Kayu
review_text:
Weekdays before 7pm the grilled fish less than$14!
Non spicy flavor is gd, the mala as always is great. Weekends $28 can order the tofu mala.
author: Agnes “ManKiller” Sem

restaurant_name: NEW TASTE 新食代 @ Jalan Kayu
review_text: The grilled fish could have been spicier, but it was fresh and flavourful. The skewers were also tasty and well-seasoned. Overall, a cozy spot with decent food.
author: TTT

restaurant_name: NEW TASTE 新食代 @ Jalan Kayu
review_text:
Not bad grilled fish and skewers.

Not as spicy as I like it to be, else it would have been an easy 5 star.

Prices are very reasonable, and what you get, taste is comparable to many other places which are much more expensive.

Close to home, food that fills the heart.
author: Ed T

restaurant_name: NEW TASTE 新食代 @ Jalan Kayu
review_text: Ordered takeaway for dinner on 31 Dec 2025 and was extremely disappointing. We were told to wait 30–40 minutes, but after more than an hour there was still no food, while dine-in customers who arrived much later were served first. At the counter, we even heard staff scolding the kitchen for picking and skipping orders instead of following the queue, clearly prioritizing dine-in orders over takeaway and delivery. Food was overpriced, taste was average, and definitely not worth the excessive wait or the price paid.
author: HuiLeng T

review_text:
I only managed to snap a few photos from the 7 items that we ordered. My favourite is the fried rice and tempura.
I decided to meet my friend here who visited from Indonesia. The food ingredients were fresh, taste was not bad at all and affordable. Service was great with friendly staffs. The ambience is not as per what expected compared to what I saw on Google reviews. But then, I love the fact that it was quiet so we can have a  peaceful dinner.
Will come back to bring my husband next time.
author: Chim Mei

review_text:
We ordered sushi and was informed by the waitress that it will ready in 20 mins to be served. Nothing fancy about the decor of the restaurant.
Should have a QR ordering system so that we do not need to wait for the waitress to serve us. She was the only one serving us indoors.
author: Sue Is.

review_text:
We visited with a reservation for a family dinner. While we were seated immediately, the experience quickly soured due to the service.
The food itself was acceptable: the oysters were fresh, the sashimi was okay, and the broth was good. However, the sushi portions were disappointingly small, feeling overpriced for what they offered compared to other local options.
The waiting time for the initial food was decent, but a major issue arose when they forgot one of our main courses. It was clear it had been overlooked, especially after we watched the exact same dish delivered to a table that ordered well after us. When we inquired, we were told there would be another 10-15 minute wait due to the "kitchen being full." This was a baffling excuse, as the dining room was quiet and the kitchen appeared far from busy. There was no apology offered for the mistake.
The lack of attentiveness continued:
• We asked a server for soy sauce for our sashimi. They were utterly confused and presented us with chili flakes instead. After we pointed out the soy sauce bottle on a nearby table, they bafflingly tried to claim there was one on ours, which there clearly was not.
• A simple request for a straw was completely ignored.
Simply put, the entire experience was not worth the 10% service charge. The service was non-existent, rude, and incompetent. We left feeling dissatisfied and had to go to the restaurant next door to finish our meal. Management should seriously consider switching to QR code ordering to minimize server error.
author: putri nazar

review_text:
Poor service, lack of care, and disappointing food. Definitely not a place I would recommend.

We had a really disappointing experience here. When we arrived, no one greeted us or told us whether to wait for a seat. We had to approach a lady clearing tables to ask if the table was taken, and she said no. Just as we were about to sit, another staff member suddenly came over and told us that table was already being held for another couple. The whole process felt disorganised and confusing.

There was totally no customer service. The staff gave off the impression that they didn’t want to be there to work. They were unwelcoming.

When the food finally arrived, it was underwhelming. The sushi pieces were tiny, the salmon sashimi was just average, and the soba was bland to the point I couldn’t finish it. Portions overall were small. Honestly, I don’t understand why TikTok reviews made this place seem so good. The reality did not match the hype.
author: Sunflower

review_text:
5 stars
Daya Izakaya has truly outdone themselves with the revamp! The newly refreshed space feels warm, welcoming, and perfect for gatherings — almost like stepping into a cozy Japanese family restaurant.

What really stands out is the massive variety of food options available. From classic sushi and sashimi to hearty rice bowls, grilled skewers, and even kids-friendly meals — there’s something for everyone, young or old. You can clearly tell they’ve put thought into making it a place for families and groups to enjoy.

Service was prompt and friendly, and the overall vibe was relaxed yet authentic. Whether you’re looking for a casual dinner or celebrating with loved ones, Daya Izakaya now ticks all the right boxes.

Highly recommend checking out the new concept! Will definitely be back.
author: yazami halim

review_text: Very packed with people so it’s understandable service suffered a little. But the food taste-wise is not really good. The mee goreng still has the strong alkaline noodle taste and the plain prata is not really plain but very oily and with a sweet glaze. At least the chicken briyani is not bad.
author: Jo Jo

review_text:
Can't believe their prata has gone sub-standard!

Plain one was tough. Egg one didn't fare better -- you'd expect the egg to moisten the texture; but no, it was like an overnight piece!

At much higher price points of $1.70 and $2.70 respectively, there's better value to be found elsewhere (fortunately :)

The only saving grace is perhaps the teh tarik... and the consistently spicy curry lol.

Somehow, Jln Kayu has lost its shine as the preferred prata place; sadly :(

(Still, I remain hopeful that things will turn around... While I seek out other places to makan...)

#MHTamChiak
#WhichPrataGotStandard
#Relegated
author: Mark Heng (Infosphere)

review_text:
I came at 12am for supper . A lot of people .
Long Q to order food   ,Service almost zero . Nobody clear the tables.  The lights are the most irritating bright white LED lights which blind the eyes type . A turn off . Will never come again
author: tommy Chan

review_text: I wouldn't say this is the best because there are now so many Roti Prata restaurants in Singapore now. However, Jalan Kayu is the place that started it all and is worth visiting one of these here whenever passing by.
author: Velochrome

review_text: Curry fish head is excellent, roti prata is good too. Fast service. Thumbs up!
author: Siewyen Ng

review_text:
I was probably the last customer on a weekday just before they close (~4pm). Service was quick, no bad experience of any sort.

Ordered the dry prawns beehoon mee with extra chilli. The noodles was ok, not spectacular, and perhaps considered pricey for $7 a pop (small). The soup was pretty robust but it's got an 'odd' flavor which was quite distinct and I can't say I liked it.
author: Leon Kwang

review_text: Soup has rich flavour. Prawn was sweet. Pork ribs (1/3) was soft. Ordered number 1 at $7
author: L ZF

review_text: Broth is on the heavier side. Opt for the thick beehoon instead because the yellow noodles will make the soup a lot more salty. The ngo hiang is amazing and a must-have!! But please only visit before 11.30am! The lunch crowd is INSANE and extremely stressful—too many tourists yelling and staring at you eating while they queue.
author: Fion Lee

review_text:
I visited here in weekday am after morning brisk walk. I ordered a bowl of pork rib prawn noodle dried version.

The pork ribs were well cooked very tender and it shattered to small pieces when you bite on it. The prawn were cut into half as shown in the photo and fresh. Overall it was a very good bowl of dried prawn noodle which you can find in Singapore. The chili paste elevated the entire bowl to the next level.

The flavours packed broth was balanced  ( you can taste the herbs, pepper, and sweetness of pork rib in it). Invariably this will be a comforting dish in cool rainy day.
author: Gim Chong Teh

review_text: Seems like a family owned establishment, the soup is hearty and ingredients are generous. It’s $7 for the smallest bowl but it’s enough. Some people may not know but most prawn mee shop allow you to top up the soup which is the best part of the meal! Service is usually quick as well. Thank you to all the kind staff there.
author: ftn a

review_text:
Ordered via GrabFood. The first time I ordered with them the drink spilled thru the cup and contaminated the solid food items. Ordered again and figured that was a one-off incident.

Turns out I horribly misjudged the quality issues of their packaging. This time the drink spilled AGAIN and a common thing between the two incidents is the fact that they pack the drinks with the meal in the same bag.

Not ordering with them again.
author: rcs.singapore

review_text: Location is good with bus stop nearby. Usually their maki rolls are quite good but disappointingly, this order they seem extra stingy with the sauce. Not enough sauce so the maki rolls turn out to be kinda dry and wasn't as enjoyable.
author: Juliett Tango

review_text: usually they're good at it but this particular order is bad. BCB wasnt coated with sauce at all.... feels like being rip-off. i hope they do something to keep up with the standards~
author: Zahidah Mohamed

review_text: Have a total of 5 pick up orders. Given the number to the lady staff and only 4 items were given to me and nothing was conveyed to me. I thought the lady staff went to pick up the other item or probably the item is not ready yet. Waited for another 1 minute and a guy ask me what I'm waiting for. I told him I got a missing item, he get the item and just throw at the counter top and unhappily told me to pick up the item from his side and not from the lady side. Both the staff I met seems to have bad attitude.
author: H P Lim

review_text:
I'm happy with the service recovery. Aida was the one who attended to my complaint about my previous order. And Im very satisfied with her service. To 4fingerz: pls appreciate and retain staff like her.

On top of that, the malay girl cashier was friendly and wished me luck for the blind box. And perhaps coz of her gd wishes,  I got the quby charm I wanted at this outlet, good day overall.
author: Cia Licia

review_text:
I’ve been ordering from this company for quite some time because I genuinely used to love the food and flavours. Unfortunately, been very disappointed recently. The standard of the food has gone down massively ,The meals now lack the flavour, freshness, and finesse that originally made me choose this service.

The only consistently positive aspect has been the delivery, which has always been reliable and on time , that’s honestly the main reason I’ve continued ordering despite the new change of deliveries. However, with the current quality of the food, I would rather eat out or look for other meal prep services that offer better taste and overall quality
author: Sarah J

review_text: Into my second week of trying Tsquared Eats. Every meal is 350 calories, which makes it easy for me to track my diet. I like that there is a good variety of meals with lamb, beef, chicken and fish.  The food delivery is for two days except for Friday meals and they come packed with more than sufficient ice packs, so once I get home, I take them in and plonk them in the fridge. Food taste and quality is excellent, so I highly recommend!
author: TheCityJammer

review_text:
Trying out the meals delivery for a week. This is my first time ordering and honestly the food is great! Thank you chef! I can't wait to try the Aug menu.

I would like to say thank you to the delivery team, every morning rain or shine the food is at your door when you wake up. The feeling of warmth, like someone is taking care of you.

Overall, 5 stars service and food! 😍
author: Amelia Ding

review_text:
In an effort to lose unwanted fat and weight, I tried a few healthy meal prep companies. Unfortunately, they always fell short of my expectations. Inconsistent portion size, dry meat, bland taste or way too much sauce used - they were not worth the money spent. I stopped ordering deliveries,... until I found TSquared Eats.

TSquared Eats uses premium ingredients, the meals taste absolutely delicious, the portions are generous, and the meats..... oh they are tender and juicy!! I have ordered a few rounds of their Balanced meals and it really helps fast-track my fat and weight loss progress!

Kudos to Utso and the team! Keep up the great work!

PS: Their deliveries are always on-time, too :)
author: Sarah Siregar

review_text:
TSquared Eats exceeded my expectations.
I have went through multiple meal prep companies and so far this is the best one on many levels.

1) Timely delivery 3 times a week
2) Chilled not frozen
3) retains quality after heating up
4) Doneness of ingredients cooked with precision (nothing is overcooked)
5) Every delivery of meals(3) comes in a mylar bag with cooling pouch to ensure freshness
6) Taste good and clean at the same time
7) Regular feedback on meals delivered
author: PokePokePoke

review_text: We had one fried spring chicken and one onion blossom. Food portion is reasonable. Feels like the mayo is homemade. Salad with the chicken tastes fresh. The restaurant was crowded on sunday lunch time. The restaurant is cosy and comfortable. Self service corner where u take yr own cultery etc. And if u need to pack yr food, there are containers and plastic bags for u to self serve too. Dont expect much service from staff.
author: Jasmine Goh

review_text: From Nasi Lemak to KFC style fried chicken to BBQ grill chicken to western pasta.. this place has it all covered and with great taste too! Onion loaf is great with generous sauce. Can hardly find this. the other place I tried once was Outback and this tasted as great.
author: William Toh

review_text:
Had the crispy chicken chop with brown sauce. I requested not to have coleslaw and was given a choice to substitute it with either bread of French fries.
Chicken was juicy and skin was crispy. Ok, I’m not sure what is the brown sauce but it helps add flavour. There is ample parking nearby making it a convenient spot for a meal.
author: Kimmy Sim

review_text: Tried the new Gino’s East menu and the deep dish pizza was actually not bad (but I think it’s frozen).
author: Eric Lee

review_text:
Had lunch at Tenderbest Makcik Tuckshop at Punggol East from 11.30am to 2.00pm over the weekend. The atmosphere was beyond my expectations, as I had anticipated a noisy, crowded restaurant with long waiting times. Instead, it was pleasantly relaxed and comfortable for a casual gathering.

There were four of us, and we ordered five different main courses along with several side dishes. All the food was served within five minutes, which allowed us to enjoy our casual conversation and birthday celebration without any delay. The dishes were well prepared and nicely presented.

The servers at the counter were fast, efficient, and polite, and they remained calm and attentive while checking that all our orders were correct and intact. Their excellent service really enhanced our dining experience. Bravo, Tenderbest Makcik Tuckshop, for the wonderful food and outstanding service.
author: Darien Tock

review_text:
Had a satisfying meal at Yisilan Mala! Love that they specialise in Halal build-your-own mala hotpot, so everyone can enjoy without worries. The bowl was packed with flavour — rich, fragrant, and with a solid spicy kick that was super addictive.

I went for their build-your-own mala hotpot with udon, and it was absolutely delicious. The ingredients were fresh, well-coated in mala seasoning, and the balance of heat and flavour was just nice — shiok without being overpowering.

Also tried their Mala Spicy Chicken, which was crispy, aromatic, and very flavourful with the perfect mala punch.

If you’re looking for a solid Halal mala spot with bold flavours and customisable options, Yisilan Mala is definitely worth a visit. Highly recommended 👍
author: Rudy Marwan Yunos

review_text:
When I entering the shop I sees many choices of food and feel like it was decent. After trying out their food was delicious and fresh
Their medium mala spiciness was good enough for me. Highly recommended stall I ever had. Will come back for sure !
author: ShiroRay

review_text:
I love everything about this Mala place. HALAL AND YUMMY. Very worth it. Reasonable price point! Awesome staffs! Delicious recipe! This is definitely my Mala benchmark! Everyone in Singapore should try this Mala once in their lifetime and get a taste of heaven in their mouth. Once again, I love everything about this MALA place. I would recommend this to everyone, friends and family. If I could choose one food to eat for the rest of my life, it would be this Mala!!!!!!! Please don't ever close down, I need my Mala fix at least once a week!!!!! I love this Mala so much.

PS: I suggest yall to try their BEEF STRIPE OH LORD HAVE MERCY SO DELICIOUS
author: Nurul Izzah

review_text: The food is awsome, it's really fabulous food. Very recommend to have a try. 👍👍
author: Alex Chin

review_text: The best HALAL mala I ever had! The price is good, the taste is amazing and the cook is so nice! I always have my mala fix here and nowhere else 😮‍💨
author: Noor Hidayat Abdul Wahid

review_text:
Resident of Sengkang West Avenue. Stayed here near 6 years which is as long as the stall was around.

Overall, food had never been even on an average one in par with similar competitor hawkers. To further aggrevate, they had a change of team some 2 to 3 months back. The taste of the food went from average to terrible.

Those familiar faces are no longer around which makes the entire ordering rigid unlike those instance when customers preference were remembered along with a lively vibe. Question to Habib Express here is, why is there a necessity to change the team when all was good unlike how it now is.
author: Ibrahim Hairunnisha

review_text: Ordered two pratas and opted for mutton curry. Love that the pratas weren't oily and curry was flavourful, and came with a juicy portion of mutton. Friendly and fast service! Will patronise again.
author: Chase Jawn

review_text: Bought briyani twice from them it was good! So i thought would try the prata but the coin prata (takeaway), dough was not cooked thoroughly and was mushy due to too much oil absorbed. So disappointed
author: Muneerah M

review_text: $7 for briyani. Rice alot, chicken not big. Taste ok
author: Xiaodoudou

review_text: Situated in a very spacious coffee shop. Sad that we could only dine in 2s though. The mee goreng was not bad. Usually Habib express franchise shops all are not bad in their noodle dishes. I did see many non Indians queueing at the shop too. Would want to try other dishes too.
author: Rummaging4Food

review_text: Paid $8.80 for rice with very miserably little amount of vegetables. Never buy from such disappointing service . Worst seafood stall I have encountered in Singapore. Please don’t con when we trust you to deliver.
author: JS JS

review_text: Ordered tiger prawn wrapped in beancurd skin as shown in picture for a whopping $13. However, they turned out to be fried batter. The inside of the batter wasnt even prawn meat. Confronted the stall but they said it was correct. Felt cheated.
author: Ying Han

review_text:
Food was lousy for quite some time. However recently, went to try again. The hor fun is nice and hot.

Dishes were much better than before. Not joking. Glad the improvement was tremendous. Keep improving and It could be my daily staple.
author: Daryl Bay (Ah Bay)

review_text: The food quite so so and the fried lemon chicken more flour than the meat.
author: Alexander Reinaldo

review_text:
I think this store very much depend on the mood of the cook, quality is inconsistent from the few times I eat there. The food wasn't bad, wasn't good, it's mediocre, sits squarely at 5/10.

Seafood fried rice (pic) comes with 2 mid-small prawns, 1 bigger piece of squid or 2 smaller pieces, 2-3 slice of fish cake, standard frozen veggies (carrots, corn, peas).

Crispy egg seafood noodle had 2 small squid, 2 slices of fish. They did seperate the gravy and noodles for tabao which I appreciate.

Beef fried rice comes with acceptable amount of beef slices (not much just not offensively little) and standard frozen veggies.

Curry chicken is quite spicy, the offensive, sharp kind of spicy not the mellow coconut milk kind. But quantity of chicken is ok, good with rice.
author: Juliett Tango

review_text:
Review of Fatty Bom Bom @ Sengkang Block 455

One of the worst Western food experiences I’ve had so far. I ordered the grilled chicken chop, which came with a small, uninspiring chicken thigh drowned in mushroom sauce, along with a bun and fries. The fries could be swapped for mashed potatoes or spaghetti, but that didn’t make much difference.

The chicken tasted frozen and unpleasant — it seemed like the kind you’d find in a supermarket pack of 6–8 pieces. For a dish priced at $8.20, this felt like a complete rip-off. They really shouldn’t be serving this kind of low-quality chicken at such a price.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text: Tried the tender beef steak today. First time eating here. It was done just right (not overcooked or too bloody). Loved the fried bun and mashed potato was good as well. Fries I didn’t like that much cos a little soggy.
author: PK Ong

review_text:

author: Yang

review_text:
This was the 5th time patronised and the last time (branch 455 Sengkang West Ave #01-01)!!!

During the 1st & 2nd patronised, encountered the most excellent service from another slim male staff (even short-handed too at that point of time, he still remained good attitude) and seems to be transferred to other outlet somewhere 1 year plus ago.

Were given much grace period, trust & patience to try patronise yet again encountered the same attitude, impatient and rude speaking tone staff (seems on afternoon shift today 25/6/24). His bad attitude was since from my 3rd to 5th patronised (till date).

It was not the first time having rude tone when enquired on the food related matters or upon ordering. The last too he requested to pay exact $9.20 amount when provided a $10.00 note, (when it is not a $1.00 or $2.00 purchased, one expected customer to have exact amount when open business should find ways to hv smaller change) or at least with a more polite tone yet with an harsh tone and attitude face too.

Moreover, the crunchy fried chicken / food standard dropped big time, chicken was harden and sour (unsure stale chicken), the fries & mashed potato were tasteless too and was fried by the same staff. Previously the food still delicious by same staff apart oversee the bad service.

Respect is given by both, customer and the work place is not your punching bag. One should be thankful that customer did not vent anger along with your attitude. Everyone required work somewhere outside there enduring hardship in different situation, what makes you that different / special to vent anger or show attitude not only once!

The management should have do something about it; the food quality, staff attitude and short-handed issue if any. Staff only focus more on delivery orders rather than walk in customer too. Even customer willingly to wait doesn't mean your staff can take customer for granted keeping them waiting longer time at the cashier, moreover providing the impolite attitude to customer!
author: RTs

review_text:
Rubbish pricing which changes each day and terrible value. Almost tasteless most dishes and high priced. For example, a piece of chicken and 1 vege, rice is $7.50! And today .. just to try again, 1 vege of beans, 1 sambal egg and no rice.. $4.50!!

Just to compare prices, at the Chinese mixed rice stall at same place, i got 1 vege, 1 sweet sour fish, rice for $4.

Really, save your money and patronsir elsewhere..even the seafood stall thereis better value!!

review_text: No idea if the food is good or bad as was standing at the stall for almost 10mins before a lady seated just at the table in front of the stall tell me that only have nasi left. I asked her the reason for her to leave me standing in front of the stall for so long before telling me that.
author: Zoe Boey

review_text:
Dropped by to get b'fast for my mom and myself yesterday morning. When I reach the store, I saw the team were packing nasi lemak for bulk orders.(Must be more than 30 orders).There were 5 people before me and I was surprised that I did not have to wait for more than 5mins for my turn.
The lady was handling the bulk orders and the gentleman was handling normal orders.
I got my 3 orders less than 15mins. For the price,the portion is reasonable.
Service was good. Food was good.
I saw the negatives reviews but my experience was a good one.
No complaints.

Store is also always severely understaffed during peak hours. If I had other choices for Malay food in the vicinity, I wouldn’t patronise this stall.

review_text: Was honestly worried about the less than stellar reviews before coming here. Had the char kway teow, assam laksa, and a kaya butter set. Sure the service isn’t polished but the food was good! Not mind-blowing good but genuinely surprised by the quality. CKT had lots of lard and cockle, wasn’t too salty. Ok maybe the wok hei could be more. Assam laksa was one of the better ones you can find in SG. The iced kopi was unexpectedly tasty. Will be back to try the rest of the menu.
author: Gerald Tan (gt_yb)

review_text:
Ordered sweet potato leaves 清炒 ($10), penang char kway teow ($8.80) and nonya kapitan chicken ($20)

Portion of the sweet potato leaves was bigger than normal (despite ordering small size) -- could feed at least 3-4 people, so it was quite worth the price :) Would have preferred if it was fried with more garlic though (as seen in the picture -- quite little garlic). Penang char kway teow had some wok hei. I liked that the amount of lap cheong they added and the portion was slightly bigger than normal CKT size.

Nonya kapitan chicken was a big let down...served with 7 sad, dry and small pieces of frozen chicken breasts, and coupled with a very sweet gravvy, this dish could not justify its steep price...
author: Evan

review_text: Traditional, simple & hearty breakfast to start the day. Milo gao very gao very shiok. Amazing!

review_text:
NEW (3⭐): Came back after a first good experience only to feel a bit let down (maybe it's just a consistency issue). The 炒粿条 was a bit wet, and the 麻油鸡 was lacking flavor.

OLD (4⭐): It's pretty obvious that the chef has got a good control of the wok & fire. review_text: Dropped by because I spotted Penang Hokkien Char! Not something you see often in SG. Love the slight wok hei and generous pork lard – quite satisfying for a version you can find here. Of course, nothing beats the real deal in Penang lah! Enjoy, guys!
author: Andrew Ong

review_text:
Review of Ding Ji Teochew Noodles

“Not too bad” would probably be the most accurate way to describe this stall — and I think that’s something many people can relate to. It’s a tough job for the hawkers, standing for hours in front of what feels like a furnace, so some understanding is due.

Finding a bowl of noodles at $5 these days is almost impossible, even at hawker centres, let alone in a coffee shop. While the lady taking orders didn’t sound particularly pleasant, it thankfully didn’t affect how the noodles tasted.

This isn’t the best Teochew noodles out there, but it’s certainly acceptable. The minced pork noodles had a nice tanginess, with a generous amount of minced pork, mushrooms, and meatballs on top.

One tip: do yourself a favour and tell the staff clearly what you want — whether it’s chilli level, vinegar, or noodle texture. It makes a noticeable difference to the final bowl.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text: Tried the mini bowl noodles, I liked the texture of the noodles and appreciated the extra chilli provided. The vinegar was self-service, which was convenient. The soup was decent, though the ingredients were a little limited.
author: TTT

review_text: Attitude of staff rude and sulky. Food is ok except for lack of veggies (all i got was 3 fishballs, noodles, and 2 slices of fish cake). Fishballs were decent but rest was average. Photo shows $4 meal. Will not revisit.
author: Audrey S

review_text: Ordered takeaway fishball noodles. Fishball has super strong fishy smell like spoilt I tried to eat but it's too overwhelming. People who are sensitive to this kind of taste advise not to get this, you will end up eating noodles and soup. Quite stingy with the fish cake only found one small slice. No veggie also. Very disappointing. Maybe can try other items on menu
author: timoo tee

review_text:
Kitty and I were craving some good fishball noodles, so we decided to cycle over to the Food Hub at Sengkang West Avenue. Kitty had been to Ding Ji before and raved about their noodles, so we were excited to try them ourselves.

The stall is run by a Chinese national lady who seems to work solo, and we were immediately struck by the stark contrast between Kitty's previous experience and the low 1.8-star rating on Google reviews.   Reading through the reviews, we realized most of the low ratings were related to service - people mentioned a lack of warmth, smiles, and a general "uncaring" attitude from the lady.

Unfortunately, we experienced some of the same things during our visit. The lady wasn't very smiley or outgoing, which Kitty attributed to her probably being tired. We understand that service styles differ across cultures, but it was definitely noticeable compared to the warm service we're used to in Singapore.  Kitty even mentioned that the lady seemed like she just wanted to get the food out and get the job done, which is a stark contrast to the typical Singaporean service culture.

Now, onto the food!  We ordered the minced meat with mushroom fishball noodles (Kitty) and the Xiao Wan Mian (me).  The noodles were delicious - the seasoning was good, the ingredients were fresh and nice, and the overall taste was slightly above average. However, we did notice that the noodles used were a bit lower grade, so they tended to soak up the soup quickly, leaving them drier.  I always had to add a spoonful of soup to make them moister.

Despite the service, we felt the food was worth a try, especially if you're craving fishball noodles.  The flavors were acceptable, and the ingredients were fresh. Just be prepared for a less-than-enthusiastic service experience.  If you can overlook that, Ding Ji is still worth a visit for its food.
author: Doraemon

review_text:
I understand that some items may be unavailable early in the morning, so I immediately changed my order. However, the staff didn’t inform me that the second option I chose was also unavailable, in fact, three items weren’t available. I ended up ordering one beef and one chicken energy bowl, but she was wearing a mask and I couldn’t fully understand what she said. After some argument, then I understood that both beef and chicken were not available.

Since I had never ordered this item before, it was already hard for me to follow. I usually order the chicken rotisserie energy bowl, and when I found out it was unavailable, I asked if I could get any other chicken option. She didn’t say no. So I kept trying to clarify what I wanted, but it seems there was a communication error. I’m quite sure of that, and I saw no point in arguing because I really didn’t understand why she didn’t just tell me directly that the chicken couldn’t be replaced. I’m sure I would have been okay with the price difference. Why make it so complicated? I respected it anyway, but I ended up being forced to take the avocado, which I’m allergic to. This made me feel very disappointed, as I clearly said I didn’t want avocado! By then, I really felt tired. I spent $21 on something I couldn’t eat and ended up being treated like I was a picky customer.

To add to the point of why I got scolded, I repeated my question several times, but it became frustrating. Then the other “staff”, another lady, suddenly jumped in and raised her voice after hearing me say that I was asking if I could replace the meat! She told me I couldn’t change the meat (excuse me, I had been asking that repeatedly from the moment she said “not available bla... bla... bla...”). That made it feel like I was in the wrong. But shouldn’t she try to understand the full situation first, especially since the item wasn’t available, and maybe apologise instead of blaming the customer with that tone of voice and expression? Where did I go wrong if the two staff in front of me weren’t listening to the customer? And then the last one jumped in and scolded me! What’s the logic?

review_text:
Paradise Hotpot delivered a roomy, family-friendly Hong Kong-style all-you-can-eat hotpot with a clear DIY focus and good value if you time it right. The self-serve ingredient stations are extensive — lots of fishballs, processed items, sliced meats and fresh veg — and the sauce bar lets you build classic combos (sesame paste, soy, chilli, spring onion). I also liked the herbal-drink dispensers (sour plum, water chestnut) and the visible menu board that states an 80-minute individual hotpot format and Early Bird pricing (starting as low as S$19.90 shown). Staff were efficient with replenishment while kids happily helped themselves at the counters.

Practical tip: aim for the Early Bird or lunch session for best value and go for the "Beef and Premium Set" as i think it gives the best both worlds; note the board shows a weekend/public-holiday surcharge (S$3) and a food-wastage charge (S$10 per 100g). Minor note: the sauce station gets busy and a little drippy during peak times — a quick tidy would help presentation.

Photos show the condiment station, ingredient wells and the pricing/menu board. Good choice for families and value-seekers; I’d recommend it for a casual, hands-on hotpot outing.

Finally, hot food is available while you wait for the main steamboat food to be cooked.

Special tip for kids: Go for the famous pancake machine for fresh pancakes. This is the same machine available in hotels today.

The soup:
This is what stood out the most - light yet flavorful! It's gentle and savoury without being heavy or overly salty. The kind of broth that comforts without overwhelming your palate 💚

The chicken karaage and fried salmon added nice protein variety to the meal - crispy, golden, and delicious additions!

When you want reliable, comforting Japanese food without the fuss, Yoshinoya always delivers 🙌

review_text:
Ya Kun Kaya Toast (Compass One) - Comforting Local Fare That Feels Like a Warm Hug

After my medical appointment at Sengkang Hospital, Donkey and I were looking for a comforting bite – since we’re both big fans of Ya Kun, we checked Google Maps to check which level the outlet is at Compass One!

We’ve actually visited twice now, and each time has been great. Our 2nd visit was on 21 Jan, where we ordered a kaya pandan muffin, a large less-sweet tea, and a large less-sweet coffee – the total came to just $9.60 including 9% GST. The muffin was warm, fluffy, and had a lovely pandan-kaya aroma, while the drinks were perfectly balanced without being too cloying.

This recent trip after my hospital check-up was just as satisfying. The outlet at #01-37 is clean and well-lit, with plenty of seating for both quick takeaways and relaxed meals. The staff are friendly and efficient, and we appreciate that they’re open daily from 7 am to 9 pm – perfect for early mornings or late afternoon snacks.

As a homegrown Singaporean brand, Ya Kun never disappoints with its consistent quality. Their kaya spread is made without preservatives, and you can really taste the difference. Whether you’re going for their signature toast sets or just a simple drink and pastry, it’s always great value for money.

Highly recommend this spot for anyone in the Sengkang area looking for authentic local fare that feels like a warm hug!

Char Kway Teow
The wok hei was real — noodles, prawns, sambal, all fried to perfection 😮‍💨

Assam Laksa
Tangy, spicy, and full of OG Penang flavour.

White Kopi Chicken
crispy bites glazed in sweet-bitter white coffee sauce. Mind = blown

And you have to try the Penang Fish Skin Rojak — sweet, nutty, crunchy.
Plus the Salted Egg Mantis Prawn… crispy, creamy, and dangerously addictive 💛

The Penang-style Oyster Egg? Fluffy, smoky, and packed with juicy oysters 🤤

Nonya Chap Chye for that comforting, home-cooked vibe 🍲

And don’t even get me started on dessert — unlimited chocolate fondue, ice cream,

and don't skip their King of Cendol topped with fresh durian 💚

The staff Shirley was very helpful and friendly.
author: Zozo

restaurant_name: Penang Culture | All-day Buffet | Halal Certified | CompassOne
review_text:
Penang Culture is full of bold Penang flavours is so value for money! I enjoyed the cuttlefish kangkong, rojak, fried kway teow, oyster omelette, claypot four heavenly king, kueh pie tee, otah, ampla juiced calamansi juice and King of chendol!

All You Can Eat Halal-Certified Penang Buffet
with Unlimited Free Flow Chocolate Fondue & Ice Cream Available. Will be back for the food again! Very good value.
author: Cherrlyn Lim

review_text: Tasted the food at this outlet a few times and the general impression is quite good, for this visit , curry rice with curry chicken is not bad or in fact is quite good. Seems like the fried chicken was quite good. Especially with the curry sauce . Craypot rice was quite tasty previously but now the cooked rice is totally tasted flat with no fragrance. Not sure if the rice was changed. The chicken cooked with the craypot is only 2 or 3 small miserable pcs of chicken meat and it is not seasoned and tasted plain. Overall, this claypot rice is nothing to enjoy the food,not unless one can’t find any decent food. Not recommended.
author: E Ang

review_text:
Ordered claypot lala ee mian
Hmm basically, not much taste, quite plain. Lala little bit only.
Soup is plain color.. I thought should be black rich with gravy which I saw on the banner.
Disappointed.. 🫤
author: Chuin Fang Eu

review_text:
Kitty and I were looking for a good meal and decided to check out Encik Tan at Compass 1.  We were intrigued by their claypot dishes, which are not commonly found at every restaurant.  Encik Tan offers a variety of stalls under one roof, including a claypot stall, a fishball noodle stall, a curry rice stall, and a drinks stall.  We decided to try the claypot rice and the yi mian claypot.

Even though Encik Tan is a halal establishment, their claypots looked exactly like the traditional Chinese claypots we're familiar with. We were impressed that they managed to recreate the classic claypot flavor without using pork lard or any ingredients not permitted in halal cuisine. The claypot rice, with its fragrant soy sauce, was particularly delicious. Even Kitty commented, "Wow, the claypot tastes alright, even though it's halal"

My yi mian was also enjoyable.  While both the claypot rice and yi mian were flavorful, we felt there was a subtle something missing, a taste that we couldn't quite pinpoint.

The service was friendly and efficient.  After we finished our meal, a friendly uncle went around to help clear our dishes.  There was also a designated tray return station for convenience.  The ambiance was bright and spacious, which we appreciated.
author: Doraemon

review_text:

Rating:

• Food: 4/5 (Delicious claypot dishes with a unique halal twist, but a subtle missing element)

Even though Encik Tan is a halal establishment, their claypots looked exactly like the traditional Chinese claypots we're familiar with.
