review_text: Ordered their famous bowl meal that comes w small fries and a drink. Their famous bowl is actually whipped potato topped w popcorn chicken and cheese sauce. The food is pretty ok, value for money. Just that throughout the meal i kept seeing birds around , picking at food crumbs.. And when i wanted to wash my hands at the sink, i was appalled to see their service staff spit into the sink, and didnt even press the tap to flush down his phlegm .. Think this is v crude mannerism of the service staff
author: R Tan

review_text:
Visited KFC Causeway Point on 30 August 2025 and ordered a Popcorn Chicken Snacker. Unfortunately, the experience was quite disappointing.

I waited around 10–15 minutes for my order (which I didn’t mind as the fries were still cooking), but when I got home, I discovered that the sauce was wrong. I had requested BBQ sauce but was given Flaming Hot Sauce instead.

While waiting, I also noticed at least two other customers having issues with missing or incorrect sauces. This suggests that more care is needed at the counter when preparing orders.

The bigger shock was the serving size of the Popcorn Chicken. For $3.95, the portion was extremely little compared to expectations. Unless this is the standard serving, it felt as if I was just given whatever was left near closing time as the chef didn't bother to fry more popcorn chicken for me.
author: W Lee

review_text:
Extremely disappointed with the service today at around 6:39 PM.

I’m a regular customer and don’t complain easily, but this experience was unacceptable. I ordered a 1-for-1 meal, a custom wrap meal, and paid extra for an onion cheese sauce.

I was told the sauce for the 1-for-1 meal wasn’t ready. I was okay with waiting, but the staff asked me to take a plain wrap instead, which I declined as it wasn’t what I paid for. After waiting about 5 minutes, I politely asked how much longer it would take and was met with a rude response: “I told you you have to wait, what.”

I ended up waiting around 30 minutes just for my wrap. When I finally received my order, the onion cheese sauce I paid for was missing, and the staff insisted she had already given it to me when she hadn’t.

Poor communication, unprofessional attitude, and an incorrect order. Very disappointing service.
author: Wong sok yen

review_text: 2 stars for their cheese fries and 0 stars for inconsistency of service standards. Ordered dine in at 9:59pm (closes at 1030pm). Food was given takeaway and explained after 10 it's only takeaway. As a F&B manager I understand this. But right beside me they served a guy for dine in .. And a few more dine in trays on the runner table.. what does this represent to me am I not a customer also ? I tasted the chicken there & it was a standby in warmer taste not freshly cooked at 10pm(?!) , that's just terrible!

author: Benjamin Mogensen

author: Kino Ong

review_text: These outlets which are found all round Singapore provide a trip down memory lane bringing almost all the fried snacks of my childhood into 1 hole in the wall take out outlet. The quality and service does vary between outlets and even at different times of the day, but the fritters and fried dough sticks and buns are still pretty yummy. At under S$2, generally, per piece, one just needs to not be too greedy! If you’ve not tried these before, I suggest starting with goreng pisang - a whole sweet banana battered and fried - or a slice of sweet potato.
author: Possy Psoh

review_text: went to Dough Culture for the first time today and honestly had no idea what to get, Alice was super friendly and patient and she took the time to explain everything which made me feel really comfortable. Ended up trying something new (butterfly bun) and I loved it! Really appreciate the great service :) Thanks again Alice!
author: Husband !

review_text:
Sells Halal Vegan-friendly dough snacks.

Had the Tau Suan ( split mung beans dessert with fried dough fritters). Only $2.20, it’s really good for the price.
The dessert was warm and the fried dough fritters were crispy. Would give a 5 ⭐️ if the service was as warm as my dessert.
author: Yellow Bear

their tau suan was really gd, gd taste and the amount of you tiao slices was alot (unlike the pathetic qty i got from foodcourt which i could literally count with 6 fingers).
author: grizz

review_text:
See how dirty their oil they used for frying is!! Look at those black coloured bits. And I already removed some bigger black pieces before taking this photo. Dough Culture charged a premium for their product but delivered sub standard products to her consumers.

Not patronising this brand anymore. Buyers beware.
author: Hans Chua

restaurant_name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken @ Causeway Point
review_text:
Recognized the name. We ordered 3 bowls of noodles - one signature, and two fisherman. Both types of dishes failed us...

I had the abalone noodle. The amount of abalone was so little, the extra money didn't seem worth it. The bowl looked like it had a lot of chilli but was really bland. The soup was somewhat better, and the fried fishball and chilli dip was best.

My parents had the fisherman dish. She felt the fried fish bean items would be better deep fried.
author: Cuifen Pui

I hv been to a few of their outlets and this store is really the worse tasting.

Sometimes noodle is tasteless , sometimes is ok.

Pls improve , spoiling the brand's name
author: Pekka (DeStinAr0)

restaurant_name: Lam's Noodle & Salt Baked Chicken @ Causeway Point
review_text:
A favourite of mine for chewy mee pok (spicy fried version)…
Not sure IIRC but they have this San Wan noodles (3 balls in translation) & we also tried the Crunchy Prawn ball noodles.
The San Wan tasted the same as the regular bowls, just giving us 3 kinds of different meat balls.
The prawns balls were as it says crunchy! Soaked up the gravy really nicely 👍
I do hope that they try cutting the chili padi into smaller bits cos it goes so well with every bite of the noodles 😅

review_text:
Tasty Food and Cozy Vibes at Saizeriya, The Woodgrove 🍝🍕

I recently visited Saizeriya at The Woodgrove, and overall, I had a very enjoyable experience. The menu offers a wide range of Italian-inspired dishes at very reasonable prices, which makes it perfect for casual dining. I tried a few items during my visit, and the pasta dishes were my favorite — perfectly cooked al dente with flavorful sauces. The pizzas were also very good, with a thin, crisp crust and generous toppings that made each slice satisfying. 🍕😋

I also really appreciated the affordable drink and dessert options. The soft drinks and Italian sodas complemented the meal nicely, and the desserts were sweet, light, and a great way to end the meal. 🍨🥤

The ambience of the restaurant is cozy and welcoming, ideal for both family outings and casual meals with friends. The seating is comfortable, and the lighting and decor create a relaxed, casual atmosphere. The staff were polite and attentive, although during peak hours, service was a bit slower than I expected.

The only reason I’m giving 4 stars instead of 5 is that some dishes could use a touch more seasoning, and the restaurant does get quite crowded at times, which can affect the overall dining pace. Still, considering the quality, portion size, and price, it’s a great place for a satisfying Italian meal without spending too much.

Overall, I would definitely return to Saizeriya at The Woodgrove. It’s a reliable choice for tasty, affordable pasta and pizza, and the cozy atmosphere makes it a pleasant spot to enjoy a casual meal. 🍝💛 Highly recommended for anyone looking for good food, good value, and a comfortable dining experience!

restaurant_name: Tongue Tip Lanzhou Beef Noodles 舌尖尖 (The Woodgrove)
review_text:
I went with the Signature Beef Noodles and was a bit stuck on which noodle type to pick, but the staff recommended the Erxi (thicker round noodles) as their most popular choice, so I went with that.

The soup was very clean-tasting and not gamey at all, which was great. I asked for less chili, which really let the natural beefy sweetness shine through. They are also quite generous when topping off the noodles with green onions, leeks, and coriander, which made the broth even more aromatic and refreshing. The daikon was also crunchy and had soaked up all that beefy goodness.

Since the Hui people are famous for their skewers, I had to try some on the side. The mutton skewers were juicy with a nice kick of cumin and chilli, while the beef tendon had good flavour and a melt-in-your-mouth texture.

Prices here are a bit on the steep side (about $3 for a single skewer), but the quality is definitely there.

review_text:
Delish hand stretched noodles, appetising sides, so so skewers

Newly opened. It's about one month old. Did a takeaway on a wet cold day, and the noodle soup hits the spot right on. Ordered an original broth and one with suan cai. Both were good but I prefer the original. Broth was delightfully appetising, full of umami yet light enough not to be overwhelming. Saltiness was to my liking. The hand stretched noodles was really good. It retained it's qq-ness despite a takeaway. Meat portion  were generous too, and was tasty. Selected chicken and picked bamboo and mushroom. The former was ok, the latter is well pickled, crunchy and very appetising.

Skewers were so so. Had the chicken, beef, tendon and tripe. Meats were tender, and large compared to other skewers I have had, but taste could do with more spices. And it's expensive too... A better value if ordered as a set with the noodles. Individual skewer is $3++ for ONE skewer.

Place is bright and well air conditioned. Service is also welcoming and well oiled.

Will definitely return to dine in and watch the noodle chef at work.

restaurant_name: Tongue Tip Lanzhou Beef Noodles 舌尖尖 (The Woodgrove)
review_text:
Tldr: zero expectations, still disappointed. Pricy, and operational flaws

Food: $19.40 for 1x large signature beef noodle and 2 beef skewers

Please note restaurant is not charging gst as of date of review (still registering gst), so price may be higher in future

Portion: generous noodles, but poor ingredient to carb ratio. Consider reducing noodle quantity and lowering prices. Portion size seems to be like in China, too much for SG.

Taste: had authentic lanzhou lamian in China. Average taste. Soup was quite salty. Noodles, though freshly pulled, clumped together due to delays in serving. Beef appear to be factory packed and sliced in-store.

Skewers are small, and $2.5 each. Do note minimum order of 2 skewers. Taste is average. These are fried, not grilled.

Only positive aspect are the friendly staff.

Significant wait time during off-peak hours. Noodles were prepared quickly, but sat there as skewers were delayed.

Poor dine-in design with cramped seating, opposing traffic flow as there are 2 entrances on opposing sides. Awkward waiting experience as no electronic buzzer system. Did not seem to have designated collection point, adding to the congestion as customers wait inside the small restaurant.

Cramped layout combines ordering, serving, prep and cleaning. Open-air kitchen makes hygiene hard to maintain.

Should have just closed off back entrance for the kitchen. I guess they wanted to showcase the freshly pulled noodles? But they could still achieve this with glass partitions.

If I had to pick, we personally preferred the rice noodles over the glass noodles, but either way, everything hit.

The price is honestly crazy — only $0.80 per bowl! We ordered quite a lot and our total came up to just $12.50. Couldn’t even believe our eyes when the bill came. Considering how tasty everything was, this easily became one of my favourite supper spots in SG.

Another bonus: the place closes at 2am, so it’s perfect if you’re out late and craving something comforting and affordable. The vibe is casual, quick, and perfect for a late-night bite with friends.

Honestly, if you’re missing ORTO’s boat noodles or just want cheap, shiok noodles late at night, this spot is a must-try. Full marks for flavour, price, and convenience.

review_text:
I reviewed several customer comments before deciding to post this, and unfortunately my experience aligns with many of the concerns raised.

This was my second visit to this outlet. During dinner hours, the restaurant was not crowded, yet staff were largely inattentive. Several employees were seen standing around or walking about without actively attending to customers. Despite the low volume of orders, service was slow and disorganized.

There appeared to be a supervisor on duty who was frequently raising his voice to direct staff, but this did not translate into effective coordination or leadership. Issues on the floor were not resolved promptly, and active involvement to manage service flow was lacking.

Order management was particularly problematic. The order screen showed no active orders at one point, yet the McDonald’s app notified me twice that my order was ready when it clearly was not. I placed two orders during this visit, and in both cases the items received were incorrect—mirroring issues I experienced on my previous visit. For example, I ordered a Prosperity Burger but was instead given two pieces of fried chicken. This level of inaccuracy is unacceptable, even with various complaints raised over the MCD feedback app.

As the franchise operator, Hanbaobao Group should take greater accountability in upholding McDonald’s service standards. This outlet ranks among the poorest McDonald’s experiences I have had probably in SG : comparable to another lousy outlet in Yishun Northpoint with persistent operational issues.

I hope this feedback is taken seriously and addressed through proper staff training, stronger on-site leadership ( not discrimination but it happened to ethnicity who were minority), and improved order management controls.
Terrible experience ever.

We ordered the Coriander Fried Chicken with Lime Rice ($7.90), Coriander Fried Chicken with Indomie ($9.40), and the Indomie Balado Egg ($6.50).

The lime rice stood out — beautifully infused with strong lemongrass fragrance, refreshing and very enjoyable. That said, if you’re not a fan of lemongrass, this might not be for you. The Indomie was cooked just right and carried a wonderfully fragrant aroma, though it leaned far too salty for my liking.

On the sides, the fried veggie fritters were deliciously crispy with a satisfying crunch, while the fried tempeh was a little plain — essentially tempeh coated in batter — but paired with sambal, it transformed into a tasty bite.

The coriander fried chicken itself, while flavorful, felt rather small in portion for the price point. Similarly, the Indomie Balado Egg at $6.50 came across as too steep for what was essentially a very simple, modest dish.

Overall, there are some flavorful highlights, but the pricing versus portion size may leave some diners feeling shortchanged.

Today marks the opening of a new traditional handmade pau dian at our neighborhood coffeeshop, and I had the pleasure of trying it out. I sampled a variety of items — yam cake, chicken feet, fan choy, bamboo shoot soon kueh, and chee cheong fun — and every single dish was impressive.

The flavors were authentic and comforting, clearly made with care and experience. The yam cake was crispy and fragrant, the chicken feet were well-braised and flavorful, and the fan choy had just the right balance of savory and sweet and had generous toppings as well. I was especially impressed with the bamboo shoot soon kueh — the skin was delicate and smooth, with a deliciously fresh filling. The chee cheong fun was silky and satisfying as well.

Best of all, quality is top-notch and prices are very reasonable. A true gem in the area.

Highly recommended for anyone who loves traditional handmade delights! 🫰🏻🫰🏻

I like them as they are serving the nasi lemak in ceramic big plate. Nowadays not all dine in have proper plating for serving as most wanted convenient using plastic. This is my plus point to this place. Chicken is fried to crispy crunch from the outside and well marinated from the inside and juicy. The sambal chili is good with both fragrance coconut milk rice and the fried chicken. It will be 5 stars if they have their egg sunny side up. 😍 Definitely worth a trip there to eat.
author: HC Lum

restaurant_name: Makan Empire by Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang
review_text: Anamira gave us good service and always manage to cook for us just in time before the store close! Will always eat here after gym 🤭
author: Emma A

restaurant_name: Makan Empire by Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang
review_text:
Nice fragrant fried chicken.
Fish fillet is also nice.
Mee Soto soup is flavourful.
Teh with pandan leave is ok, but lacks tea intensity.
author: KKT

restaurant_name: Makan Empire by Nasi Lemak Ayam Taliwang
review_text:
Was hungry, so dropped by this place on my way to MRT station. There are self ordering kiosks outside. After making an order, made my way in. Greeted the staff but got no reply. Sad.
After abt 10mins, collected my meal. Honestly, my meal looked identical to that of Encik Tan food but abit more money value to it.😜. Food was okok. Teh drink was decent. The return tray shelfs was crowded. Had to move a cup to return my tray. A decent size floor plan. Can cater abt 40pax. Don't think i would return back sadly.
author: Mohamed Haniffa

review_text: The restaurant offers Halal-certified Thai cuisine with quite a decent selection of dishes. It is reasonably priced, and the customer service is excellent. I even dropped some drinks, and the staff was kind enough to clean up the mess and replaced the new drinks for us free of charge. Highly recommended!
author: Lindt MM

review_text:
Tom Yum Soup
- A bit odd to have hard boiled egg inside
- Liked that they put enough kafir leaves to enhance the taste
- Chicken meat was tender
- Not too spicy

Basil chicken + Beef rice
- Comes with brown rice which is a plus point
- Chicken was tender but beef was chewy
- Sauce itself was slightly on the sweeter side

Beef Boat Noodle
- Noodle sauce is kinda sweet not to my liking
- Unfortunately Beef slices were chewy and hard to eat
- Do not recommend at all
- Comes with a side of soup which doesn't taste that nice either

Overall would not recommend their Beef dishes at all. Better to go for chicken and their rice
author: Yuin Kuan

review_text: Situated at basement walkway between TEL line mrt and the woodlands heath campus. The portion  of beef for the double beef rice is big. Cooked hot and delicious.
author: Peter Rock Steady Crew

review_text:
Had dinner there.
Modest crowd but service was fast.
The food are nice and tasty.
The serving size is value for money.

Overall? I think the experience was good.
author: Michael Long

review_text:
The rice was dry, you really need soup to eat with.
Buzzer called but was given wrong order. I told staff this is not mine, staff checked its #30 and staff expect me to pass to #30..? 0How would i know who is #30?

Fried chicken was more batter.

But if you really want eat there. I suggest getting the beef thai soup. Not sure what its actually called but get with noodles instead.
author: Hello Chester

review_text:
Dining at Elemen Woodlands was such a wonderful and memorable experience! From the moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the restaurant’s calm and elegant atmosphere, modern, cozy, and filled with a sense of natural tranquility. It’s the kind of place that makes you instantly feel relaxed and at peace.

The service was exceptional warm, attentive, and thoughtful without being intrusive. The staff explained each dish beautifully and made sure our dining experience was smooth from start to finish.

Now, the food absolutely impressive! Every dish was plated like a piece of art and tasted even better than it looked. I loved how Elemen combines creativity and balance, the flavors were clean, refreshing, and perfectly seasoned, highlighting the freshness of the ingredients. Their signature sets are especially worth trying each course felt carefully curated to deliver harmony in taste, texture, and presentation.

The truffle wild mushroom soup was rich and aromatic while the drinks and desserts added a perfect finishing touch, light, fragrant, and beautifully done.

Overall, Elemen Woodlands offers not just a meal, but a mindful dining experience that nourishes both body and soul. Whether you’re vegetarian or simply looking for something wholesome and different, this is definitely a place worth visiting.

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates good food, calm ambiance, and genuine hospitality. I’ll definitely be back!
author: Lexter Daniel

review_text:
The food was amazing and the service was professional and prompt. Great eye for detail and they tended to our needs promptly.

I gave a lower rating for atmosphere since there were kids running around and screaming. It'll be appreciated if staff would advise parents on keeping their kids from running around.
author: K

review_text:
Good food and service! Place is a little hard to navigate. Took bus 900 alighted at block 589 and walked 10 mins, prepare an umbrella. Their 5 course set is $28.80, about $35 per pax. Their tiramisu and cappuccino cake is good. Look out for their seasonal specials, this time it was Thai.
Tried their seasonal specials - Christmas edition! Good! I think their seasonal specials are better than their usual menu. Also, their membership is really worth it.
author: Gladys Teo Le Ya

review_text:
Very nice place with pleasant ambience for family or friend meet up. Or even a business meal.

Food is tasty and presented beautifully. Portion is reasonable too. Do note 3-course set is only available during lunch hours.

Staff service is friendly and helpful.

If u are looking for vegetarian/vegab option this is indeed a good choice to consider.

Located at Koufu HQ at Wlands Height. Carpark is available on site at a fee.
author: Siah Hx

review_text:
The business is really good👍 the design of the restaurant is not easy for them to serve and they have done their best. The waiters did good job 👍 The manager shall find out a better way to make sure the efficient food serving system !
We love the food and definitely will come back😄
author: Eva Su

review_text: Chicken rice here is fragrant and well-cooked, with tender, juicy chicken and flavourful rice that isn’t too oily. The chilli and ginger sauces complement the dish nicely, giving it an extra kick. Portion size is reasonable for the price, and service is generally quick and efficient. Overall, a satisfying spot for a simple and comforting meal.
author: derrick

review_text:
I’d like to share some feedback about my recent visit. I ordered chicken rice and was quite surprised by the pricing — it wasn’t clearly displayed, and I only found out the amount when paying. While I can afford it, the lack of transparency made it feel like a rip-off.

On top of that, the Malay lady staff who attended to me had a rather unpleasant attitude, which made the experience worse. I hope the stall can be more transparent with pricing and remind staff to treat customers respectfully. It’s not about the money, but about fairness and service.

See the photos for yourself.
author: Don Ng

review_text: The food quality was exceptional. Every dish tasted fresh and thoughtfully prepared, with balanced flavors and great attention to detail. You can tell the kitchen prioritizes quality ingredients and consistent execution.
author: Naim Hassan

review_text: Awesome chicken rice. Very friendly staff al amin and jaslina. And fast service. Ask jaslina to sing u a sing. She have nice voice
author: Shahrin Sanudin

review_text: Amazing chicken rice! The chicken is super tender, rice is fragrant, and the chilli is on point. Portion is generous and service is fast. Definitely one of the best around in woodlands koufu will be back again!
author: Henrik Shah

review_text: Ordered the signature mee hoon kueh - there were mushrooms in the photo but when served, only had a few small strips of black fungus. When asked, the staff said it’s all together with the minced meat. I did not see a single mushroom slice :(
author: A

review_text: Ban main so so, hot plate taste good but oily
author: Peter Rock Steady Crew

review_text: Good tom yum ban mian. spicy! 5/5.
author: Ida Einjaw

restaurant_name: Mari Mari Seafood - Woodlands Koufu Headquarters
review_text:
I don't usually provide negative feedback unless warranted. Check my reviews. I was a customer of Mari Mari, back even when they were at Blk 182, Woodlands St 13/St 11. They were still pretty good. Things have taken a turn for the worse recently.

Now, I feel that potential customers should know where (NOT) to spend your money.

In short, don't eat at Mari Mari, unless you like to waste your hard-earned money and have horrible time with family and friends.

This food eatablishment simply just don't have the chef and/or people skills to make your meal experience a good one.

Our CNY eve dinner was totally ruined today (16 Feb). The soon hock fish was so over-fried (too much fire and for too long a duration) and dry, that fish lovers among us at the table tried to consume but had to give up trying to eat the fish.

This dish is something that even the most novice zhi char chef should never mess up this bad.

A feedback to the male boss resulted in a ”会注意” response with no service recovery whatsoever. None.

It was totally unacceptable for a F&B service on a festive day, or any day for that matter.

Seriously, it was horrible. Please, do yourself a favour. Avoid at all cost. That poor fish - died in vain.

The elderly folks at the table were displeased with the fish. Again, to provide a chance for recovery of service, I asked for a token discount off the bill. I don't expect a full refund of the fish, since we sort of ate some of it to discover how horrible it was.

The owner guy laughed like it was a joke. Novestine, it was never about the money, it was about recovering the experience and make it a better outcome for both parties.

It was the attitude that was repulsive. Sorry bro, that's not how you do business.
author: Henry

restaurant_name: Mari Mari Seafood - Woodlands Koufu Headquarters
review_text:
We visited on Chinese New Year night and ordered a few dishes. Most of the food was fine, although the Salted Egg Sotong was quite chewy.

At payment, we were asked if we had been informed about a $10 surcharge. We were not told beforehand, and if we had known, we might not have ordered from them. The cashier said she would waive the surcharge, but it was still keyed into the bill. When we asked, she said it was not charged.

I’m fine with festive surcharges, but customers should be informed clearly in advance. There was no need to say it was waived if it was still added to the bill.
author: Darina Latiff

restaurant_name: Mari Mari Seafood - Woodlands Koufu Headquarters
review_text: Boss of Mari Mari Novestine is a friendly and creative guy in food. We enjoyed every dishes he recommended at a reasonable price. One special dish - Kampong chicken in 2 way cook was juicy and flavourful. Will definitely come again.
author: Joyce Han

restaurant_name: Mari Mari Seafood - Woodlands Koufu Headquarters
review_text:
First time testing out Mari Mari Seafood here. Overall i would say mostly excellent. Good service and food was great overall. But I'm guessing the kitchen staff was overwhelmed by orders. Food comes out slow. Also sensed some sorta favouritism with the boss there. I let it slide as they were probably friends or relatives.

Food ordered.
Sweet n Sour Seabass 10/10
Baby Squid 8/10 ( kinda little amount for price charged. But tastes good)
Tofu Claypot 6/10 ( Initially looks plain tasted bland, almost like no oyster sauce. Asked them to take back and fix it. 8/10 after)
Fresh Oysters 9/10 ( Really taste the freshness)
Chilli Crab 8/10 ( Crabs size were awesome. Fresh crabs. U can taste it. Only problem is its more to the sweet side. Would be nicer if spicier a bit.)

Would i come back again? Yeah definitely. Hopefully they stabilised kitchen and fixed the chilli crab. Needs 🌶 🌶
author: Md Hafizal Md Tahir

restaurant_name: Mari Mari Seafood - Woodlands Koufu Headquarters
review_text:
Contacted Novestine via Whatsapp and he prepared the menu for us based on our budget. He was very thoughtful and i did not regret leaving the choice to him. He was honest and said that as there were only 4 of us, there would have been too much food if he gave me a big fish and so he reduced the size. We had fish maw soup with baby abalone to start and this was one of my faves. It was not starchy. Even the abalone was  yummy and tender. Their signature flying noodles was packed with flavour. Pomfret was super fresh and the scallops, smothered in garlic was awesome! Another favourite dish for me. By the time the crab came, we were so full! Still we stuffed our faces. The crab was plump with meat and sweet! Sauce was a little on the sweet side and not spicy. I would have preferred it spicier. Overall, a really finger licking good meal and Ethan was very friendly too. He made sure we saw our crab before it, erhm, made its sacrifice for our meal . Will definitely be back for more.

Note to non- smokers: sit further away from the shop and nearer to the caifan shop next time as smokers kept going to where we were seated. It was quite unpleasant to have folks smoking when we were eating. But this has nothing to do with mari mari! In fact, their guys smoked far far away from the kopitiam!
author: Pearly Ang

review_text:
Newly opened Indian Muslim food store. Halal certification is still in progress.
Tried the mutton briyani for $8. Generous amount of rice and mutton came in one pice with bone is tender and easy to tear off using fork and spoon.
Thai fried rice needs to wait as the will cook after receiving the order. The Thai fish sauce flavour is strong and it came topped with a runny egg.
author: Lim Rick

review_text: Mee Kuah very nice  and tasty . Lots of meat ,potatoes , fish cakes and other ingredients inside the gravy .

author: Shereen Ng

review_text:
I come here with my family at least once a month. Even though it gets crowded & cramped, usually theres seats & once you sit, its cozy. The aircon is good!

Service is good, the guys are friendly & always helpful! They will recommend you stuff if you’re unsure haha the menu is extensive! Thats how i found out about poori :)
author: Kara

review_text:
I recently visited KNS Restaurant at *Ace the Place* with my friend, and it was a great experience! We tried their mutabak and teh tarik, both of which were delicious; flavorful and satisfying.

What I loved most was that this place is open 24/7, making it a perfect spot to hang out at any time of the day or night. Whether you're craving a late-night snack or just want a cozy place to chill with friends, KNS is a great choice.

The atmosphere was relaxed, and the service was friendly. Definitely a go-to spot for good food and good vibes!

author: Kimyuu Hanriiya

restaurant_name: Xiao Bao 晓宝 / Pig’s Trotter Rice
review_text:
One of the better pork trotter rice I’ve had. Not as good as Shinian, but definitely above average. I really like their braised sauce; it’s bold and full of flavour.

The pig trotter itself is more on the chewy side. Personally, I prefer Shinian’s more tender version, but that really comes down to personal preference. The soup is also quite flavourful. It’s nice to drink at first, though it does get a bit too salty towards the end. Their chilli is decent, but I wish it was spicier and had more chilli bits. Right now it feels a little too watery.

Overall, it’s probably not worth travelling just to eat it, but I’d definitely come back if I’m in the area again.
author: Tan Wei Liang

restaurant_name: Xiao Bao 晓宝 / Pig’s Trotter Rice
review_text: As a fan of pig trotter, I drove a long way here to try theirs because of the relatively high rating. But I was really disappointed. The braise is nearly tasteless, almost like they only added soya sauce to the boiled trotter.  Even the coriander used is devoid of flavour.  It looks good on the picture, but it's far from good.  Not worth the calories!
author: John Kaiser

review_text:

$5.90 + $2 (add intestine).
Generally ok, less oily, different from bai nian version which is more drenched with pork oil but nice. To me, Cai Xin doesn't seem to match well here.
author: KKT

restaurant_name: Xiao Bao 晓宝 / Pig’s Trotter Rice
review_text: Very good braise pork. The braising liquor is gelatinous and sticky, great for women who wants pretty akin. 😂 Interesting a la carte menu so you can pick and choose what you want.
author: Ida Einjaw

restaurant_name: Xiao Bao 晓宝 / Pig’s Trotter Rice
review_text: A relatively new stall in this food court. Tried the "flagship" Pig's Trotters Rice ($5) today and was definitely surprised and delighted by the excellent quality and generous portion. The meat was well braised and tender, rice was fluffy, the sauce was just right. Definitely will return in future. Hope this genuine review is helpful for you, please give me a ❤️ or 🙏 if it does. Cya around.
author: D Yong

restaurant_name: Hua Zai HK Style Roasted Delight
review_text: Paid $4 and $5.50 for a plate of soya sauce chicken rice and a plate of char siew and roasted pork rice. The taste of the soya sauce chicken, char siew and roasted pork was ok. However, the roasted pork skin was not crispy and the char siew was slightly hard. The chicken rice was fragrant but the white rice was a bit dry and hard. Service was friendly but a bit slow. There was free flow of ordinary soup.
author: Edward Wong

restaurant_name: Hua Zai HK Style Roasted Delight
review_text: Ordered three treasure noodles not spicy for my kid take away. Before i leave the place ask the staff again to confirm no chilli. Bring back home found it with chilli when my kid eat.
author: Christine G

restaurant_name: Hua Zai HK Style Roasted Delight
review_text:
One of the branches of this HK roasted delight chain
Maintained the same standard as other branches.
Surprisingly having a plate of high quality roasted pork with plain rice for $3.80
Soup is free flow.
Very friendly and polite staff to go with it
author: TANG CHEONG SING

restaurant_name: Hua Zai HK Style Roasted Delight
review_text:
This is a very popular chain that is popping up everywhere. I find the food consistently good. The portion is big and come with complementary tasty and nice soup! The soup has chucks of meat in it too.

If you go in the morning, they have special offer too.
author: Kwong Fei Yee

restaurant_name: Hua Zai HK Style Roasted Delight
review_text:
I give it 5 stars for two reasons: The staffs are always friendly and there is a free soup you can take yourself.

Mom and I like to go for morning walk and usually this is one of the few options for decent breakfast around here. The young chinese guy who wears cap is always friendly and patient, which is very different compared to opposite stall's hostility (not a typo, definitely not hospitality. I was not at the receiving end of the hostility, but had witnessed many).

Kudos for him because his friendliness and service is the main reason we always eat there.

Sell variety of pork, chicken, duck.
Free soup can be very good.

During CNY, there was a holiday surcharge, didn't know it was a thing but it's okay lah, everyone else was not open.

Update to add more pictures as we visit more often and compliment to the same staff.
author: Buren

review_text:
***React to this if it helps. I realise many people give this place one star stating that it is closed. However, based off the pictures, this store is actually located ~1.5km away in an industrial building coffeeshop --757048. Take note!

I ordered their special budget meal, Fried chicken rice ($5). At first glance, while it doesn't look like much; it does look well prepared enough to whet one's appetite. Well, the taste's even better.

Curry on rice was on point. A slight spicy kick but never really taking too much out of the dish. Nice sour chilli which accentuates the spice to a more refreshing level. Soured Achar does its job as well.

Now for the main star, the chicken. Portion wise its a big drumstick, sprinkled with some fried bits.

The chicken is so well prepared it singlehandedly makes the dish worth the $5. Batter is fried to perfection, leaving a very crispy and nice salty taste in every bite. While separating the skin, the meat is firmly tender. Able to pull off with the fork with juice overflowing, yet firm enough to the bite. I don't know how they prepare their chicken, but they just have to stick to it.

Overall, the chicken provides a satisfying bite each time. There's a huge portion of meat, so it makes the chicken and rice really enjoyable. Overall, the fried chicken deserves high praise, a bit like penyet chicken. If you're near the area (757048) and craving some spice or fried chicken, honestly this is the spot.
author: owen

review_text:
Always come here for the best crispy ayam penyat chicken at the most affordable price ever! 5 bucks each set!

Heard the chicken comes fresh and prepared on the day itself! No wonder the meat is so tender & Well marinated! It will blow your mind away! 🤯 I always order the thigh side~

Definitely one of the hidden gem in a coffee house! Been recommanding friends here ever since! 😊
author: Jolene Yang

review_text:
What's great?
Signature budget $5 set chicken white rice. Aircon coffee shop.

What's to improve?

Visit again?
Yes.
author: K M

review_text:
Highly recommended for their quick service and fragrant dishes!

Chicken was thicc and moist. The crispy skin on the outside was flavourful. Even the curry, chilli and mutton sauce were incredibly fragrant.
author: Jed Lim

review_text: Got recommended to give it a try and it didn’t disappoint. Their fried chicken is the bomb - really succulent on the inside, and crispy on the outside. Their curry is pretty decent too, though I wish it could be a tad stronger. Enjoyed their acar side and the sambal too. Definitely worth a try!
author: Tan Wei Liang

review_text:
This is the western food stall. Overall still okay, hawker taste but price slightly higher. Probably rental here is higher.

The dine in area occupied with air con. You can eat comfortable during day time. Not too hot.

Food taste is acceptable. Price also acceptable, starting from SGD 5+

Mostly serve the resident at woodland glen or worker nearby.
author: William Tan

review_text:
I had a really bad experience at Amigo, Woodlands Drive 16. I paid using PayNow, but their system wasn’t working. Instead of handling it properly, the staff at the counter had a bad attitude and even asked me to pay in cash.

I was quite upset because I had already paid. Their payment issue shouldn’t become the customer’s problem.

The food was also disappointing. The meat wasn’t hot, and the garlic bread was soft and not crispy at all.

Honestly, I wouldn’t recommend this place. The service is bad, and the food is not worth the price. I won’t be coming back.
author: Kira 99

review_text: $10.50 just chicken and pasta , I have it for breakfast very full and yummy. Maybe add some veggies or a corn better balance the diet, they cooked fresh and hot .
author: Ming Qing Lye

review_text: I asked myself, would the chef and his staff want to eat food that is too oily like this. No wonder. Just seen all the reviews. Their pasta its very very oily (mushroom spaghetti and cream penne). My oh my, refer to pics. Tried to take out the foods from box but the oil still dripping. So terrible, waste of $. Even my toddlers doesnt want to see the food. Other foods (burgers, yellow rice, finger foods, soup) taste just ok, not a wow thing.
author: Sonya Dubey

review_text: Ordered happiness plate at ,$7.90. Its so little portions. Supposed to hv 1 wing, drum and thigh. But they packed 2 wings n 1 drum. The frirs is so little too. Very disappointed.
author: Michelle Kang

review_text:
I ordered with my mee soto with noodle & bee hoon mixed which is my usual order.  I was shocked to be charged with an "extra vegetable dish", when i questioned the stall lady, she said it is their practise to charge as such for mixing bee hoon to my mee soto.

I told her i have been buying mee soto for years from her stall and never had this experience before, and told her she should had informed me about this change upon my order. She later muttered and ask if i want the "normal" order, i paid and left as i did not want to make things difficult for her.

I have been patronsing this halal food stall for over 10 years and this is the first time i am writing this review to warn fellow neighbours.
author: Spawn Spawn

restaurant_name: Pin Wei Hong Kong Style Chee Cheong Fun
review_text:
delicious Michelin chee cheong fun. the rice sheets are smooth thin and tender. sauce is light, sweet and savoury. I ordered prawns and char siu. prawns are good size, char siu are chopped very small. chilli sauce is good too For the amount of meat it's I feel it's pricey but it's hand made to order.

Aircon Kopitiam.

review_text: Comes with a variety of Chee Cheong Fun, plain ones, with Char Siew, with prawns all taste super nice. The Chee Cheong Fun is so smooth that it really bring back memories of old Hong Kong. And it's also affordable too. Go try it out and you will get addicted to it.

review_text: The chee cheong fun is soft but the char siew can be more defined instead of being mashed up. The chee cheong fun was drowned in the sauce that is too sweet and oily. Could have put lesser sauce.
author: Teresa Leong

restaurant_name: Pin Wei Hong Kong Style Chee Cheong Fun
review_text: Nice

review_text:
I had a very unpleasant experience at this food store and feel it’s important to share due to serious hygiene concerns.

My friend and I ordered a Nasi Goreng and Mee Goreng combo. While our food was being prepared, we noticed the cooking oil overflowing and dripping onto the floor while they were frying fries. More concerning, the staff repeatedly used their bare hands to handle the fries and even the mutton, directly placing ingredients into our food without gloves or proper utensils.

When they noticed that my friend and I were clearly uncomfortable and judging the situation, they attempted to hide the cooking area by covering the see-through glass. However, we could still see that they continued using their bare hands for everything.

At one point, one of the staff members was using his mobile phone and then immediately went back to touching our food and serving it, without washing his hands. This was extremely unhygienic and unacceptable.

After eating the food, my stomach felt uncomfortable, which made the experience even worse.

I strongly believe that proper SOP and hygiene standards need to be checked and enforced here. This is a serious issue and could pose health risks to customers. Please look into this matter carefully, as food safety should never be taken lightly.

review_text:
Ordered 5+pm , Late delivery for close to 2 hours. Called 3 times to expedite and finally got it by 730pm! Restaurant apologies in the call that the lateness is because of new system , Do u think it’s reasonable?
And food was slanted to the side. Had adjusted to center when taking pic Pic. Drumlets overburnt , Taste wise was soso ,maybe ruin by the late delivery 🚚. Restaurant should compensate but didn’t!
author: Asphalt 9 gamers

review_text:
Got their Deepavali special festive menu. Delivery on time. Highlights include the Tandoori Chicken Tikka Pizza (Festive), featuring marinated tandoori chicken on a minty tomato base with onions, mozzarella, coriander, and a touch of lemon for a vibrant, mildly spicy taste. The Butter Chicken Pizza (All time), is a creamy, flavourful option with butter chicken gravy, chicken chunks, mushrooms, red chilli, and coriander, offering a bold, spicy kick.

Other treats include Tandoori Chicken with Mint Sauce (Festive), a mildly spicy, smoky dish, and refreshing Quenchers like Mango Lassi and Canadian Maple Berry Twist.
author: Yang

review_text:
I've ordered 5 times from this place always on time or early for delivery approximately 15-30 mins after the pizza is done

The pizza is delicious and cheese is stringy while hot so I recommend eating while still hot

Their 2 pizzas for 20 is a great deal and the pizza is a good size much better value than dominos or pizza hut

review_text: Waited 2 hours with the calls being declined and no news only for my already cold food to be left on the floor. Please do better. This is unsanitary. I even have a hook on the door to hang my food deliveries, or just ring the doorbell, there’s really no need to leave my food onto the ground where there are ants from my neighbours plants crawling on the ground. author: Yi En Peh

review_text:
Complaint to Domino’s Management

I placed my order at 9:16pm, and the app reflected that it was already on the way. However, after waiting more than two hours, no delivery arrived. I tried calling the outlet multiple times (7x), but no one answered. At 11:30pm, I went down personally to check on my order.

The staff informed me that my unit number was not stated and that my mobile number was “invalid.” I showed proof that my unit number was entered correctly, my mobile number was valid, and that I had called repeatedly with no response. The staff then handed me a cold pizza that had been sitting there all along.

I requested for my order to be remade, as I could not accept cold food after such a long wait.

Domino’s has always been a favorite for my family and me, but this experience was very disappointing. If the outlet is unable to cope with high order volumes or manpower shortages, the app should not continue accepting orders. Customers should not be left waiting endlessly and treated this way.

I sincerely hope management looks into this issue, as many other reviews reflect similar complaints. Please take immediate action to improve service standards. Thank You.
author: Nis Nis

review_text: Ordered at 9:30pm. Marked 'completed' at 9:50pm. Called repeatedly. No pick up. LOL. Don't bother. Ridiculous service - why bother serving? Fyi this store was auto assigned by Dominos themselves through their website. Ridiculous.
author: little humming bird

review_text: Good plate of nasi lemak served on plastic plate & spoon off sembawang roadside shophouse.  $5.70 for the lot. Aromatic coconut rice. Chilli is very sweet but savoury. The nostalgic banana leaf wrapped egg nasi chilli feel. Taste pretty good overall thou and wide selection. Great for supper as this place can be hard to park during dinner timing.
author: Asia Apparel

review_text:
The chilli is my type. Not too spicy and have a hint of sweetness.

Fried chicken is so so.

Rice is fragrant but not extremely good.

Otak is good. Must try.

Price is very reasonable I must say.
author: SG Food Legends

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $9.50) @ Chong Pang Nasi Lemak.
.
Established in 1973, this stall is well-regarded for its consistent heritage taste and value-for-money prices coupled with generous portions.
.
The fragrant coconut rice is loose and fluffy in texture, carrying aromatic grainy earthy floral sweet coconutty flavour. The crunchy juicy achar / Peranakan pickled salad carries bright vegetal sour sweet spice flavour, while the crisp crunchy deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies carry fishy savoury salty flavour. A beautiful wobbly soft sunny side up chicken egg with runny yolk bursts with eggy sweet savoury flavour.
.
The large and soft otak-otak / otah / spiced mackerel fish paste has fishy savoury spice flavour, while the springy bouncy sotong / squid balls have savoury sweet flavour. The battered chicken drumstick is a highlight, tender and juicy with robust meaty salty savoury flavour. Their smooth sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste has a sharp fiery kick at the onset, followed by mild sweet savoury sour spice flavour.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text: Been awhile since I've had this. Went for a cycle and decide to come here, so ordered a bigger portion. The Nasi is so-so, but the Fried Chicken Wing and Fried Fish is still just as good as I remembered them. The other veggies are good too. Best of all, value for money! My plate was just $6.50!
author: Wei Lun

review_text:
It's been a while since we've dined in here for Nasi Lemak together. Prices have definitely gone up - $2.50 for 3 pieces of shrimp? Ouch!

The Nasi Lemak rice and chicken wing still taste good, but the service has been a letdown. They don't allow water bottles on the table, which was a bit of a hassle. And to top it off, a can of Coke at the in-house drink stall costs $2.20!

Unless we're craving it, maybe it's time to limit our visits to occasional treats only.
author: Low Bao Heng

restaurant_name: Sincerity Vegetarian Food 佛心素食
review_text:
Delicious foods 😍

author: Siah Hx

review_text:
Mai gong bo jio!
Warning! Bring more tissues! It was sooo yummy with lots of sauce.
I don't mind the mess as it was worth it..

This ChillI Crab mantou Zinger was what you should try when you heading to KFC.

The taste of the sauce was so authentic that if you close your eyes, you would thought that you're having chilli crab at that moment!

author: Helen Chen

review_text: They give a larger piece of chicken. The cheesy fries is always the bomb. The connection here is abit bad. The service is quite fast too. The food is quite hot. author: you-foodie-nice

review_text:
Had a wonderful meal at Bei Sheng Seafood. The food is really good, fresh, and well-cooked, especially their seafood and zi char dishes. Portions are generous and prices are reasonable.

The environment is clean and comfortable, making it very suitable for families to dine together. Service is friendly and efficient, and food is served quite fast.

A great place for family gatherings, casual dinners, or bringing elderly parents for a nice meal. Highly recommended for anyone staying in Yishun area. Will definitely come back again! 👍😊

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

review_text: Their Kangkung Balacan is great, Chilli Crab is good as well. I love their pineapple fried rice too ❤️❤️❤️
author: COEN

review_text:
Usually very crowded on weekend mealtimes, do come at slightly off peak timing to avoid the queue (no reservation).

The restaurant is pretty no frills, food portion is generous and overall very value for money! Love the tomyum soup and prawn tang Hoon.
author: Elanor W

review_text:
Paid $138 for 8 persons dinner after I jokingly feedback that the 咕噜肉 was hard when the boss came to collect payment and asked for feedback at the end of our meal. Then, the boss immediately gave $2 discount (original bill was $140) 😄 Well, the 咕噜肉 was in fact hard to me.

- The pineapple fried rice has sufficient wok hei.
- The sauce of the claypot toufu was flavourful and the prawns were fresh.
- The sambal kangkong was ok.
- The fried sotong was chewy but it was a bit bland.
- The steamed cod fish with soya sauce was nice.
- The fried fish was crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The sauce that came with it was mildly spicy and tasty.
- The tom yum soup was mildly spicy and tasty too.

Service was friendly and efficient. The serving of food started after 5 minutes we had finished ordering. There was not much of waiting time.
author: Edward Wong

review_text: Visited the place for lunch and it was not crowded when we arrived, crowd started to arrive after awhile! Had a hearty and filling lunch that was reasonable priced even thought we ordered small portion for all. The honey chicken and pineapple fried rice seemed like hot favourites as it was ordered by most of the patrons there at that time! The honey chicken seemed like it was prepared differently as the meat was slightly larger pieces and more juicy. Slightly disappointed with the fish maw soup as it was a little too salty to taste. However portion is enough for 4, if you just want a small bowl each. Else is enough for about 2 small bowls per person. Washed it all down with the standard lime juice that is also a popular choice when visiting this place. Overall a good meal for two, and would recommend! Will come back and order the fried fish next time when we have more people to share 😋

author: Exe Cell

review_text:

Nasi padang is always more pricy due to the amount of effort to make them and the amount of spices used. Ordered a sotong with stuff eggs, bragadil and veg. Cost me about 14 + with a kopi which I think is fair as sotong is expansive. The sotong is cold (- point) but taste nice with the curry gravy which goes well with the rice. Sambal chilli is hot but adds " life" to the food....

Overall, a good place for nais padang in Yishun with a nice relax deco of old school stuff.

Their main competitor will probably be Hjh Maimunah outlet at Yishun central. Overall, I prefer Hij but coba coba is a strong contender for a change of taste once in a while.

review_text:
I ordered Delifrance pastries on two mornings recently and was quite disappointed with the quality.
On the first day, I had the sultana croissant, which tasted very different from what I remember years ago. The texture and flavour were lacking, and there are noticeably better options elsewhere, such as Tiong Bahru Bakery.
Today, I tried the madeleine, and unfortunately it was the worst I’ve had — dry, with no taste of butter. Much better versions can be found at Henri Charpentier, while decent everyday options can get from Paris Baguette or even Swee Heng. In fact, even the more affordable pastries from Swee Heng tasted significantly better; Delifrance should be ashamed.
It’s disappointing to see Delifrance’s standards drop to this level. This experience makes me hesitant to purchase from Delifrance again.
author: Aedes Lee

review_text:
Had a really pleasant experience at Delifrance Northpoint. The food was always consistently nice.

I especially want to commend Aizeel Bin Zubir for his excellent service. He was friendly, attentive, and very patient, making the whole visit even more enjoyable. It’s always nice to be served by someone who is polite and genuinely cares about customers.

Great service and a lovely experience overall — will definitely be back!

Love this place. Has been coming since I was really young. Their Mutton Bryani is always the best. Theres really nothing more to say except that everyone has to try it. The portion and the quality of the food is always so worth the price.

We always come for the Mutton Bryani, Mango Lassi and the Garlic Naan. Phenomenal family-run restaurant.
author: Joo

review_text:
It’s popular for good reason. The food is consistently mouth-watering and the staff are warm and welcoming. Can’t go wrong with this choice if you’re in the mood for biryani.

My only gripe would be the pricing. While the food is very good, the overall package just doesn’t justify the high price. I would still recommend it anyway if you’re in the area.
author: Sriram Rengachari

review_text: We thoroughly enjoyed our meals here. The dum mutton was super tender and delicious. The staff recommended chicken on a hot plate and if you like the wok smell, it will be a palatable dish for you. Fried cauliflower was also a good recommendation but if you don’t like fried food, do give it a miss. The papadam served was fragrant too. For the chicken, I would recommend you skip the dum chicken and go for the chicken Bryani instead as it also comes with few side vegetables. I find the dum chicken not overwhelming and prefer the bryani version. The place is well ventilated, spacious and cool. Service was friendly especially an elderly service lady who was smily and approachable. Definitely one of my favourite Indian fare restaurants.
author: BeholdHim

review_text: Absolutely yummy. Devoured it in 20 mins. Better than Chinese curry (yes I am Chinese). Taste is a WOW 😳. I feel like i am in flavour heaven.
author: Alyssa

review_text:
A true hidden gem!

The food was delicious — especially the dum briyani, mutton ribs masala, and sambal quail eggs. Everything tasted hearty and authentic, with a warm, homely touch. What truly stood out was the exceptional service — the owner and staff (mostly elderly) were incredibly attentive and kind, making it feel like a comforting meal at a relative’s home.

One small note: I’d personally recommend going for the dum briyani or white rice with dishes, as the regular “briyani rice” was more like plain colored rice and lacked the richness you’d expect.

Highly recommended overall for both the food and the heartfelt hospitality.

Strong 8.5/10
author: Ryan

review_text:
Came here for lunch during CNY 15 days period.
It’s been many years since I ate in tbeor previous location at the nearby kampung plantation.
This new location is much better in terms of seating area/ space between tables, and car parks lots.

Ordered their signature lobsters porridge, and the standard/ freshness of lobsters are still very good.
So are the rest of the dishes eg Steven’s chicken, the mayo prawns, HK style steam soon hock, seafood sea cucumber claypot tofu etc..

Overall a nice seafood restaurant place value for money…
author: YL Wong

review_text:
We visited when the restaurant was only 1/3 full, yet the service was strangely rushed, all the dishes were dumped on the table quickly one after another while we were still on our first.

The Food:
Lobster Porridge: Disappointing. While the broth had body, the fishy taste was apparently and it wasn't served hot enough. We didn't even touch the lobster in it.
After we gave feedback, the staff replaced it with Garlic Steamed Lobster. This was much better, the lobsters tasted fresh, clean and without fishiness. It proves the lobster is of good quality; they just need to refine the porridge stock to obliterate that fishy note.

HK Style Soon Hock: The fish was fresh, but like the porridge, it was not served hot enough, which is a shame for such a delicate fish.

The Kailan was bland and watery, and the Sea Whelk Tofu was mediocre, lacking flavor even with the Thai sauce. The Steven Chicken remained a solid highlight.

Service:
Basic attention was missing; we had to ask for tea refills despite the quiet floor. I’m glad they recovered the meal with the steamed lobster, but for a signature porridge specialist, the technical execution and dining rhythm need work.
author: Julius Tan

review_text: Fab place to get fresh Lobsters! Their signature is the lobster porridge so you are at the right place. Select from their delightful menu with promo sets or Ala Carte. Choose from their fresh seafood or other meats like chicken drumlets which is pretty good or fish selections. Massive restaurant so seats are aplenty. Staff were very attentive and helpful. A service you should enjoy.
author: Mervyn Phea

review_text:
Orchid Live Seafood never fails to impress with its exceptional freshness and quality!
The lobster is a clear highlight. Naturally sweet, juicy and beautifully prepared in every style. From the perfectly braised Australian Greenlip Abalone with signature sauce to the comforting Steven Chix, Homemade Ngoh Hiang, and fragrant Lobster Fried Rice, every dish tastes refined yet always so satisfying.

Our family’s go to resto - Year after year for its super fresh live seafood. Highly recommended.
author: Lecinlurve

review_text:
Since 1999, Orchid Live Seafood has stood out for its unwavering commitment to fresh, premium live seafood, made possible by its long-standing role as a leading direct importer of lobsters and crustaceans.

For a limited time, enjoy 50% off Live Alaskan King Crab (2kg) at only $199 (U.P. $188/kg)! Savour it in one of the ways:
🦀Steamed - the purest expression of its sweet, delicate flesh
🦀Chilli - a well-loved local interpretation with heat and tang
🦀Pepper - bold and aromatic with a savoury kick
🦀Salted Egg - rich, umami-laden and indulgent
🦀Drunken - perfumed with Chinese wine for a fragrant, warming finish

Alaskan King Crab, prized for its meaty legs and naturally sweet, briny richness, is one of the world’s most luxurious seafood delicacies. Orchid Live Seafood sources live crabs over 2kg and keeps them in pristine tank conditions until cooking, delivering a dish that showcases both exceptional freshness and the culinary finesse the restaurant is known for.

Beyond its signature king crab offering, Orchid Live Seafood continues to impress with a diverse selection of live seafood, each sourced from its on-site tanks and cooked upon order:
🐟Steamed Turbot Fish
Steamed in Hong Kong style with a light soy-based sauce, the turbot’s smooth, clean-tasting flesh speaks clearly of its exceptional freshness.
🦑Poached Cuttlefish with Housemade Cai Poh
A contemporary creation unique to the restaurant. The cai poh adds depth, savouriness and a touch of crunch, complementing the tender poached cuttlefish beautifully.
🦞Signature Live Lobster Porridge
A beloved bestseller - the broth, simmered for no less than four hours, carries a comforting sweetness that only fresh lobster can impart.
🍗Signature Steven Chicken
A non-seafood standout. The chicken pieces are pushed to the ends of the bone, deep-fried, and glazed in a marmite-honey sauce before a final toss in sesame seeds. Crisp, caramelised and highly addictive.

📞 Reservations are strongly encouraged. Please call to check availability of live catch to avoid disappointment.
author: fatspoting

review_text:
Dish was served fast.
Had it back at the industrial park
The fried fish is a must order
The fried rice is also delicious
The tomyam soup is really a miss, in fact quite pungent.

For now, I think the dishes are delicious. Steam fish is nice. I would say its a typical good place for gathering. Dishes are predictable but taste reasonably good. author: Stevez Chua

review_text:
Still as good as 5 years ago.
