Winnie recommended me the Ebi Salad Tapas. Refreshing and light on the palate.Spicy Salmon Fish is best to go with rice. I just want some rice and order Aburi Iberico Pork Cheek Don but could not finish the rice. I am able to taste 3 ingredients from the complimentary dessert: the red beans, chewy cake and matcha ice cream in a shell made from cracker. Eat with happy tears 😂 Great recommendations and thank you for the great service both front and back end. 👏👏👏
author: Nicole Lee

review_text:
I am very disapointed by the way the store manager attitude 😡
Bought a party pack and ask for pickle ginger his answer was no and that I have to pay for it, I have been going to sushi restaurants but never once ask me to pay for pickle ginger. I have decided not to buy or eat at Sushi Tei again. Even Sakae , Sushi Express and others never once ask to pay for ginger.
Advice to sushi lovers not to eat at Sushi Tei North point.
author: Pauline Uchida

review_text: My family always comes here when we feel like having Japanese food. The place is cozy and the staff are friendly. My favorite dishes are their salmon and unagi, both are fresh, tasty, and well prepared. We enjoy the quality and consistency every time. It’s one of our go-to spots for a nice meal together.
author: ABXY

review_text:
Ordered via Domino’s app and delivery was so slow. Came almost 2 hours later. Pizza arrived cold. Not warm at all. Very disappointing. Not our first time and this is the worst Domino’s outlet we’ve experienced.

Look how dry and cold the pizza looks… taken 2 mins after it arrived.
author: Nira Donah

review_text:
Ordered food delivery via foodpanda today at 6.10pm. until now still not yet receive my food. number at the store not reachable and cannot cancel order. There write will be delivered by the restaurant but at 9.10pm send me a notification will deliver by grab express. At the end the grab driver cancelled the order also. Terrible service. Will blacklist this restaurant.
UNTIL NOW 10.33PM NOT YET RECEIVED THE FOOD
author: Jasmine Ho

review_text:
Staff were friendly, nice and welcoming.
Pizza was delicious. It was still warm and crispy 20mins after collection.
author: WL Y

review_text:
This is the collection point nearest to my place. Service from the staff is always welcoming. Dominos is your quick fix for a basic warm bread pizza craving. Value for money when using promo codes.

The shocker was the Brownie bites - 6pcs. Didn’t expect 1 pcs to be about the size of my tablespoon. 😂😂😂

Taste wise - needs to reheat before consuming.

Will still be a staple when you just crave that basic pizza.
author: D. Lim

review_text: Horrible service. Pre-ordered our pizzas one week in advance. However, our pizzas were not delivered on the day. When we drove down to request for our pizzas after waiting for 30mins past the delivery time, they told us that it would need at least another hour to make our pizzas as they had large order volume that day. Dominos, if customers made a pre-order in advance, shouldn’t those orders be prioritised instead?
author: Benjamin Spencer

review_text: They don't weight what they sell by grams so they overcharge as they please. Plus they had discount shown that the lady didn't apply.
author: Georgiana Iuliana

review_text: I always come to Mcdonald’s when new ice cream flavors are available. I really enjoy trying their creative and delicious flavors. The ice cream is smooth, tasty, and never disappoints. It’s always a treat to stop by. The staff are friendly and helpful too, which makes the experience even better. A great place for ice cream lovers like me.
author: ABXY

review_text:
We usually order from there as it's close to the house but we took a walk there.
The food was missing my ice cream but the auntie assisted into getting it for us after she checked the order details. Also, she took my wife's phone to show the counter folks which was funny and kinda unprofessional however she was an old auntie so we just let it slide.
They definitely need to make the glass frosted as it feels like we are sitting in the middle of the mall like eating with strangers and some people look into your table like they are about to dip in!
author: Sol

review_text:
This review serves as a formal complaint regarding repeated order fulfillment failures by McDonald's delivery service.
In my most recent order, I ordered two meals item, however only one meals was delivered. The delivery rider has officially noted this discrepancy. I request that management review CCTV footage to confirm the missing item.
This incident is not isolated. I have experienced multiple occurrences of missing items in past orders. The repetition of this issue demonstrates a systemic lack of quality control and failure to meet basic service standards.
I am requesting immediate refund and/or compensation for the undelivered item. Customers should not be required to repeatedly report errors for items that were paid for but not received.
If this issue continues without proper resolution, it raises serious concerns regarding service reliability and accountability. I expect this matter to be addressed promptly and professionally.
author: Benjamin Edward

review_text: Nice average sized McDonald's restaurant located at Northpoint City. The self order kiosks worked well and the service by the staff was good. I received my meal fast and they were polite. 👍✨ 🍔🍟
author: Besharps

review_text: 6th feb at 1825hrs, I wanted to get a orange twist chococone. Was told by the staff that they cant do it because mandarin orange soft serve is too soft, cant hold the chocolate coating. So I requested to change to normal chococone. Then she asked me if Im paying by paywave, which I replied yes. However, before tapping, I realise the wrong item was ordered, so I nicely told the staff again that I wanted chococone, she then annoyedly asked me again "paywave?" (Shes definitely not happy and throwing attitude). Which I said yes again, then she turned her body wanting to make the ice cream, that was when she realise she clicked the wrong item, and proceed to make amendment. This whole incident made me so angry, why are you showing me attitude when you are the one who clicked the wrong item for payment, and I corrected you nicely. Manager of the outlet, please speak to your staff, this is definitely unacceptable.
author: Hwee xin

review_text: Ordering from the kiosk was pretty easy, the food came promptly. The chicken was nice and crispy, the la zi ji is really good. The laziji bites were pretty small tho and the fries were room temp and not crispy. The sinks were nasty. Overall it was still okay, the area wasn’t dirty except some spills on the table from the previous customers and the food was satisfactory.
author: jareau

review_text:
I would like to compliment one of the staff members ( Laily) at KFC Northpoint for the excellent service provided. The staff was very friendly, patient, and polite while taking my order. Even during a busy period, they remained calm and professional, which made my experience very pleasant.
It’s not often you come across such genuine and attentive service. I truly appreciate the positive attitude and would like to thank them for making my visit enjoyable.
author: Siti Syazana

review_text: We gotten GOLDEN HUAT BUCKET at Yishun North point KFC outlet! Please come and try your luck! Good service from the store manager!!!
author: lim chien boon

review_text:
❌ DO NOT BUY THE BREAKFAST LIL CHICKEN MACARONI SOUP MEAL ❌

I want to preface this review by stating that this is a review of the meal and not the restaurant and staff itself. The restaurant was quite nice, it was clean and quiet when I visited in the morning.

I decided to order the limited lil chicken macaroni soup meal ($4.95) that came with a bucket to give it a try. I am absolutely serious when I say this, this is one of the worst thing I ever ate in my life. I would give it a negative 100 stars if possible. The meal looked nothing like the picture in promo pics, instead of having fried chicken it was more like steamed chicken in a soup mixed with some macaroni and small corn/carrot pieces.  The entire thing tasted disgusting but I ate it up since I sadly paid money already. The meal also came with a small apple juice, it tasted ok but it wasn't much. You could choose a coke instead but I chose the apple juice to try.

But seriously, this "meal" if you can call it that was not filling nor tasty. The only good thing is the bucket but other than that, it was absolutely atrocious 🤢🤮 I should have got paid to eat it instead of paying for it.
author: Besharps

review_text: Are these front desk staff not being paid? Their attitude was extremely poor. An elderly person waited for almost 15 minutes, and the staff completely ignored them. Do they think elderly people are easy to bully? Your chain store has such terrible service, treating elderly people like dirt—you must be pretty arrogant.
author: cass choo

review_text: A lot of round tables for big group gathering! The place feels very homely! My first time and I enjoyed their fried noodles and fried mee sua! Tried their yam too! Interesting! The dumpling soup is supposed to be their signature, but I feel quite “meh”. Would wanna order the egg omelette next time. And yes, be prepared to wait during peak hours. 😂
author: Eileen Neo (Sgsohotleh)

review_text:
One of those Yishun gems we keep going back to. Their  dishes are super comforting, simple, flavourful and very “home-feel”. The portions are good and the dishes all have that nice, clean taste but still shiok!

Service is straightforward & fast, and the food always comes out consistent. Nothing fancy~ just solid Heng Hua food that hits the spot every time.

If you are around Yishun &  want something comforting, this place wont disappoint✨️
author: Joanne Chan

review_text:
Visited on a weekday evening, might need to wait a while, not many seating available.

Food was generally nice, highly recommend the yam and the noodles. Crispy pork trotter were mostly fat and collagen, go for it if that’s your liking. Tofu was fine, nothing spectacular.

Overall worth a try if you’re in the area.
author: Zhi Le Tan

review_text: One of my fave restaurant that served chilled deshelled blood clams, deep fried pig trotters and yummy lor mee. Staffs were extremely friendly and helpful. Food were authentic and doesn't have the MSG aftertaste. Good for value and for family or couple.
author: Ann Chua

review_text:
A hidden gem of a restaurant at a quiet corner of Yishun not too far from the MRT station.
Came here for a celebration for the very first time and was surprised by the savoury and delicious dishes served.
Was crowded even on a weekday so be prepared to queue especially for dinners.
author: Andrew Ho (何德财)

review_text: Plain water costs $0.50. Oh well at least it was warmed. The set lunch was at best presentable only. Had also the grilled chicken rice bowl, no photo as it's really sparsely done. Seriously as much as I'd like to support local F&B, the food served here is what you'd expect from a beginner's kitchen (perhaps leave out the word Gourmet?) Atmosphere is quiet though with some old time music. Overall give this a miss as there's better choices nearby.
author: Joseph

review_text: Took more than an hour to deliver our two main dishes and they were barely warm. Food didn’t taste good either. Was not worth the wait time. Service staff was nice and polite but kitchen was probably understaffed.
author: David Khoo

review_text: I went there ok the last day that my AIA voucher expire- my mistake because a lot of other people had the same idea. I tried to make a reservation through Google for 7:30pm and they said that the reservation is not valid because they do not partner with chope anymore. If they didnt call me to confirm the reservation, it is not confirmed! Note to everyone else who plans to eat there. I waited outside for about 20 minutes and then we sat in and ordered. My friend and I only received our food at around 10pm because even though they took our orders at around 8:20pm, they only put it into the system at 9:47pm as indicated on the receipt. I added this to the review to show the timestamp. Server realised he made a mistake and gave us free soup and bread because we were so hungry by then. Our side of fries came soon after and we received all of our food after 10pm. Food was decent, nothing worth waiting 2 hours for and he gave us a 10% discount of our receipt, but that just waives the service charge. If you are hungry, dont come here because u will be going insane by the time you receive your food.
author: nafla yousuf

review_text:
I decided to choose Eatzi Gourmet @ SAFRA Yishun to celebrate my b'day with a nice dinner, and I'm sooo glad that I made the right choice!

After ordered a table of dishes, I gave my son a piece of bread and he ate while falling asleep on the baby seat. We were so scare that his head will bang onto the table as he dozed off completely. Lucky, the staff were quick to help us shift the tables and chairs so we could allow our son to lie down in the stroller while we can have a whole table of the warm food. While shifting the chairs, we overheard the restaurant manager, Ms Doris Wong advising her staff to shift it gently so it does not make loud noises which might awake our child. She is the type of good leader who are hands-on and give good advice to her staff so they can provide excellent customer service. Then, the table next to us with other children playing we were worried they might wake up our child whom just fallen asleep. And again, we were lucky to have such good staff there whom then quickly helped us to move all the dishes and stuff to the table outside. Outside there is no aircon, but there are big ceiling fans and a very nice view of the swimming pools. I had truly a wonderful b'day dinner with the nice and romantic atmosphere overlooking the swimming pools in the evening.

All these wonderful and memorable experience would not be possible without the restaurant manager, Ms Doris Wong and her team for their excellent and friendly service, I would like to highly compliment them for their spontaneous and enthusiastism in assisting all the customers.

This is my first time written such a long review for any restaurant, so when I do, this is truly a highly recommended restaurant we are truly impressed with. Not only the food is yummy and special, most importantly the staff there made my day a truly Happy B'day! Kudos to Ms Doris Wong who shown care and concerns for my son, and also her spontaneous team! We will definitely be back to visit again!
author: VV Ang

review_text: Mus and his staff were polite and very sporting in service. We had lovely gathering of 20 people thanks to them. Our gathering was a sudden one, so nothing was planned. But the staff made sure that everyone was taken care of and went smooth.
author: N M

review_text:
Located in the community hub of the area with plenty of parking available.

Thosai is very well done, crispy around the edges, light and fluffy when you get into the middle. Accompanying sauces are pretty good pairs well with the bread. Fried fish looks unappealing but the marinate and flavour is spot on. Fresh, crispy outside and moist meat when you tear it open.
author: David Lim

review_text: I'm not sure is the workers' attitude or lack of ingredients .. We were there to get our supper last night. Ordered mee goreng.. Maggi goreng.. Fried rice.. Sup kambing and nasi briyani. Mee goreng had nothing in it.. Just plain noodles with dark soya sauce.. Not even a stripe of beansprouts or vege..not even with sambal.. N yet tasteless at all.. We all were very very surprised n dissatisfaction with the food. Eat halfway n end up in dustbin chute. Haven't mentioned that each of the food was priced at 5-6 each. Sorry to say even hawkers economic noodles looks n taste better. Sup kambing was just spiced with water, only 4pieces of small cut of meat in the Sup..n not to mention was full of grease. Chicken Briyani rice just don't feel like it..to cut the bad time short.. Too harsh to say.. We hope you may cheat us that night... But hope that others will take note. That's our first and last. Next time we definitely go for McD. Thanks
author: nicholas chong

review_text:
Breakfast in the morning is always a slow affair.
There’s one Indian man who takes the orders, handles the payments, and serves the food. Funny thing is, the food and drinks are prepared at a different location — across the block. He walks over to deliver them from there. Strangely, the stall owner didn’t seem to consider the hygiene concerns of carrying food and drinks through open air, especially with all the vehicle pollution from the road. This is bad.
author: Diana Mohamed Amin

review_text: Been here since our teenage years. Great spot for Indian food, be it dining in or takeaway. It does get crowded on weekend mornings and the service can be pretty slow then, so try to avoid peak hours.
author: Nurul Jalil (exploretomakan)

review_text: butter mill taste like roasted chicken , try making a malay butter chicken milk instead im at your shop right now come and find me
author: mohamed ashrel

restaurant_name: Xing Fong Seafood 興豐海鲜
author: XIN YI TAN

restaurant_name: Bukit Ho Swee Charcoal Curry Fish Head (664 Yishun)
review_text: Was expecting the food to be very nice since seeing so many positive reviews in social media but it’s definitely OVER-RATED. Their Hor fun (didn’t manage to take the pic of it) and the dried shrimp french beans were very salty. The cereal prawn was overly sweet. The fried “Dao Gi” on the curry fish head were crashed rather than the big pieces seen on social media. We reached at around 4.40pm and was asked to wait as it’s their dinner time. Chef will resume back in the kitchen at 5pm. They should highlight when publishing to inform customers on the delay.
author: Shirley Koh

restaurant_name: Bukit Ho Swee Charcoal Curry Fish Head (664 Yishun)
review_text: My friend and I were here today (7 JANUARY 2026) for lunch. We heard a lot about this place that is supposedly famous and popular for its "Claypot Curry Fish Head" and its other signature zi char dishes. So, we duly ordered (since there was only the two of us) the following: a "Claypot Curry Fish Head" that was from a red snapper, and an Oyster Fried Omelette, and, of course, white rice to go with the aforementioned. Overall, the food here was excellent. The "Claypot Curry Fish Head" was moreish yet clean-tasting with lotsa "fu chok" and vegetables. The Oyster Fried Omelette was very good and the belachan paste condiment for it, paired perfectly. Service here was very good - very friendly and courteous. The dining ambience here at a kopitiam was very good considering it was not air-conditioned.
author: edtayjb

restaurant_name: Bukit Ho Swee Charcoal Curry Fish Head (664 Yishun)
review_text: The claypot fish tail was served piping hot and delicious! 梅菜扣肉 was delicious too. The wine taste in the prawn paste chicken was too strong. French beans were nice. They took about 25 minutes to serve our food. Not suitable if  you a quick meal. It was not crowded during lunch on a rainy Monday. I will dine here again.
author: Toh Bee Leng

restaurant_name: Bukit Ho Swee Charcoal Curry Fish Head (664 Yishun)
review_text:
Visited for Saturday lunch for 2 pax.
Ordered the signature one size red snapper curry fish tail and stirfried long beans.

Curry gravy was quite "gao" and flavorful without being too much of a coconut taste. Fish tail meat portion was substantial though its only on single side of the fish tail. Rarely any fish bones compares to those in fish head, which tend to scattered in the gravy after removed the meat) so its safer for patrons with elderly members in my opinion.

Curry fish tail is fresh and came with binjal, lady fingers, long beans, abundance tau ki, cabbages, tomatoes so to request to the shop if not taking binjal (quite a lot was given in the serving).

Long beans was above average as there isn't any noticeable "green" taste in it, crunchy and tasty with deep fried hei bi (dried shrimps).

Curry fish tail - 4/5. Worth the slightly high pricing $35 than curry fish head, will be better to share among at least 3-4 pax as may feel a bit overwhelmed with the taste as we experienced.

Long bean - 4/5. Tasty without being too oily.

Recommended.
author: Patricia Fan

restaurant_name: Bukit Ho Swee Charcoal Curry Fish Head (664 Yishun)
review_text: Went in for early dinner but have to wait for about 40mins for the claypot curry fish tail to arrive, followed by other dishes that came later. The fish tail curry was not too bad, but I still prefer JB’s Kam Leong curry fish head. The meicai Korou was so so, as I was disappointed that the meicai was diced up so finely. The other dishes long beans and king pork ribs were good. Would rate this overall as 3.9 star
author: Bosch Xie

review_text: I visited this stall for fishball mee, despite many other stores being open, and was glad I tried it in the morning. The stall is managed by an uncle and two ladies, one of whom appears to be in training. The noodle portion was generous, consisting of 5 large fish balls, and easily filled my stomach with at least 15 mouthfuls of noodles. As a big eater, I can confidently say that this serving size would satisfy anyone. While the taste was average, the atmosphere was wonderful and the staff were exceptionally polite. Overall, a pleasant experience.
author: EQ Xavier

review_text:
Gave it a try for breakfast due to a small queue. But quite disappointing. For $4.50, ingredients are minimal, noodles too salty.

Not sure what’s the positive review abt unless u like salty or heavy-tasting flavours then this might be for you.

Meatball & fishball also those standard factory produced kind so really cannot find anything unique. Any foodcourt noodles at this price would have done better.
author: Sim YM

review_text: We tried this with minimal expectations and were surprised by how good this is. Portion is ok, the price is reasonable for coffeeshop stalls. Chilli has a good kick, no vinegar but tastes savoury and enjoyable to the palate. Only down side is they close relative early, sold out by 1130am when I was there
author: Rei Axl Ye

review_text:
UPDATE: From 5 stars to 3 due to the store always being closed whenever I visit. It's a waste of time for me and it already happened 3x. This is not proper management of the store.

PREVIOUS REVIEW: A pleasant surprise. Tucked in a quiet neighborhood hawker/kopitiam spot so it is not a packed place but you won't miss this place with it's long queue of customers. Though you might get lucky during off-peak hours.

The Mushroom Fishball Noodle is superbly tasty and enjoyable. Perfect texture and mix of flavor. If there's anything I'll complain about then it's definitely the lack of meat and ingredients for a $4 meal. To some big appetite food goers, you might want an upgrade to $5 or $6 but not just on the noodle but also on the ingredient like fishball, mushroom, vegetables, or meat.
author: JP Bautista

review_text: Finally reopen!!!!!! Heard that the stall owner took a break recently due to an injury. Hopefully all is well now. Had been eating it since secondary school with my family and the uncle there always know I want mee pok extra spicy and extra noodles. Standard remains the same and price is still relatively cheap compared to other places that sell the same dish with lesser aroma.
author: Chin lim chu

review_text:
Excellent food and portion size. I can say this is the best pasta I’ve ever had for this price. Al dente and very tasty. The fried fish is reminiscent of swensens in the early days. Best part is most of their meals are $5.

Please keep this place alive, their service is good and they work with pride!

It’s a coffee shop so expect coffee shop atmosphere!
author: Nissan Skyline GTR32

review_text:
wallet friendly western food. there is a wide variety of dishes at $5! 🫨🫨 fish and chips, chicken chop with pasta, etc.  Hearty portions that’ll leave you satisfied! Their prices are either $5 or $10! We got the whole spring chicken meal for $10! So worth it 😌

Steak, lamb chop, salmon steak are also $10.
author: Melissa

review_text:
An excellent Western food stall hidden somewhere in Yishun Khatib area below a row of HDB flats inside a coffeeshop.
Was recommended by a friend who said that their cutlets are bigger than your palm.
They did not disappoint and the food was really good and portions are big as well.
Worth a try if you are at the area which is accessible by MRT and you can opt to walk for 12 minutes or take a shuttle bus.
author: Andrew Ho (何德财)

review_text: I have ordered from here a few times through GrabFood. The service is so quick! I'm always surprised by how quickly the food arrives. The portions for pasta are good, and the food is piping hot and really delicious. 😋 One of my favourite Western places around here, and certainly where I go if I need food to arrive quickly.
author: Sivaroobini Kalaimani

review_text:
🔥 Sizzling Western Delights at Five Ten Western Grill! 🍗🐟🍝

Craving a hearty meal? Swing by Five Ten Western Grill at Block 632, 632 Yishun Street 61, Singapore 760632 for these mouthwatering dishes:

🍗 2pcs Wings Set - Crispy, juicy, and packed with flavor! Perfect for a quick bite.
🐟 Fish n Chips - Golden, flaky fish paired with crispy fries—classic comfort food done right.
🍝 Chicken Chop Pasta - Tender chicken chop atop a bed of savory pasta, a fusion of Western and cozy.
🐠 Grilled Salmon - Fresh, perfectly grilled salmon that melts in your mouth with every bite.

📍 Location: Block 632, Yishun Street 61, Singapore 760632
author: raymysterio

review_text: Went down to eat 2 days ago. Was quite appalled at the hygiene standards here. As I was eating with my  friend, we were basically sharing/battling with multiple cockroaches running around our food. There is definitely no excuse and I do hope they can improve on their hygiene standards/pest control. Walk in and served pretty quick. Food came around 15mins after ordering. Overall food was still passable
author: Darius

review_text: Siam Square Mookata at Wisteria Mall (Level 1) is conveniently located in the heartlands. The shop is located outside of the mall and reservations are allowed. The shop is not big but the food is quite good. The thai green and normal milk tea is good (maybe be quite sweet). There is no hot drink option. The buffet is about $40 per pax (with GST). Family place so don't expect it to be a quiet place.
author: LiV3 LiFe

review_text: Singapore’s favourite mookata. Glad it opened near our place at this Wisteria Mall branch. Can opt for buffet or ala carte. Ala carte has ice cream for free for one serving. Got the mushroom and vegetable set which was for $10 each and super good value. Made our soup into vegetable/ mushroom soup. Tasty and amazing seeing the evolution of taste as the pot brews.
author: Yong Han

review_text:
Rather take buffet than ala carte. Remember to circle on the form correctly if you are taking buffet. During payment mine was charged as ala carte, and i Said i came for buffet, appointment made, order forms circled as buffet as well got a shock to see suddenly ala carte during payment. Luckily I circled both order forms buffet and staff billed me buffet.

Drinks are ala carte items. Do take note.

Food was good. A little salty. The cheese drip was quite good and interesting. I liked it.

Otherwise id give 5 stars.
author: Daryl Bay (Ah Bay)

review_text: Food was good, price decent. Excellent service and the staff was attentive and helpful. It’s abit too oily but expected. Thai milk tea was not too sweet, just the way we like it. Overall good experience!
author: Yingying

review_text: At their peak, the mala is super good, spicy and most importantly, tasty. Had been a frequent customer at their admiralty outlet and was ecstatic they opened an outlet near my house! They are not stingy and their ingredients are mostly fresh. Honourable mentions: The mutton is nice and tender, and their cheese tofu is different from the ones you get in the supermarket. A little fishier but smoother. Their $1 mystery dish from grab is really worth it, great portion and so delicious!
author: jareau

review_text: They have a self service free pickled veg bar which is great. The laziji was alrighr but overcooked, i felt it lacked compared to others that I've had. The fried rice was disappointing as no wokhei. I wouldn't really order again. The brown sugar rice cakes($6) were fresh and delicious though. Total paid about 31 dollars for 3. Wouldn't really eat again unless it was that i chose the wrong dishes. Maybe would try the mala.
author: Tania Koh

review_text:
I ordered the Sichuan Fish with Pickled Mustard Greens and was really disappointed. The taste was strange, almost like the oil used to fry the fish had been reused too many times. The flavor was so unpleasant that my friends and I could barely eat half the dish. For something that should be fragrant and appetizing, it turned out oily, stale, and honestly awful.
When we gave feedback, the staff brushed it off by saying “the taste is like this.” On top of that, the service was rude. One of the staff even asked my friend’s son, “So what do you want us to do if the food is bad?” That’s not the right attitude at all.

Instead of offering a solution like replacing the dish, giving a discount, or showing any form of sincerity, they told us to “keep the receipt” and we could get a discount on our next visit. Honestly, after such a bad experience, do they really think we’d want to come back?

Very unprofessional and disappointing. Definitely not recommended.
author: Joey Low

review_text: Nice restaurant with tasty mala dishes, open till 5am in the morning. Wide selection of classic mala dishes from grilled fish to fried rice. Very fast service. Friendly prices and good portion sizes.
author: Harriet L. Dineen

review_text: Ordered a Mala Spicy Grilled sea bass (small order). The serving size was generous enough to feed two adult diners. Wait time was about 10min for the food to be brought to the table after placing the order. The service staffs were attentive and provide good service. The restaurant smell like the kitchen and I walked out smelling like the fish I had. It will be great if the restaurant can improve the ventilation system.
author: Andrew Lek

review_text: Butter milk chicken had eggshells in it, tasted super bland too and almost like salted egg butter water. Surely they cant mess up cereal chicken right??? they mess it up. Cereal chicken so full of sugar i was eating crispy rice fully covered with sugar.
author: Key hon Tham

review_text: Ordered black carrot cake. Really taste disgusting despite having read the 1 star reviews here and on foodpanda. It just tastes really saltish.
author: Hel L

review_text:
Ordered at 7.30pm. Waited until 8.10pm and still no news. Was given a buzzer but never rang. I only ordered 1 packet of fried rice.
Obviously not enough staff to work yet the lady at the counter kept taking orders and collecting money.

Many food delivery personnel also stuck here while waiting. People are getting hungry and impatience, yet when one customer approached the lady at the reception to enquire why his buzzer have not rung, all she did was brush him off by asking him to keep waiting.

Very disappointing. Will not order from here again in future.
author: Wee Yeong Lai

review_text:
Group ordered Buttermilk Chicken, Chicken Chop and Oyster Omelette. Everything tasted bland, portion is small for the price and not worth the money at all.
The $8 oyster omelette contains no oyster but prawn instead.
DO NOT RECOMMEND!
author: FIR BK

review_text: Ordered the set bundle which tasted very good for the price. Good for 3-4 pax
author: Ollie

review_text:
New outlet. Visually appealing. Not too hot or cold. Ordered 3 new dishes and a old time favourite. Here is mine honest review,

1) spicy cream garlic asparagus & bacon - weird flavoring, taste sweet, after eating awhile you feel sick of it.

2) black truffle mushroom pizza - strong flavor from the mushroom and sauce but the truffle smell is light and tomato based underneath is a no-go. Should op for a cream based instead.

3) seafood chowder - very flavorful,  with lots of ingredients. Very recommended,  u will not regret ordering this.

4) carbonate - taste very blend, after adding lots of pepper , chili flakes and cheese, it will b much edible.

Overall experience is a 4/5 stars for me. What about you?
author: Nate Javier

review_text:
Standard student place to go and dine at. You get what you pay for.

Good thing is that hot pasta comes out hot and fairly tasty with tobasco added. At $7.90, it’s hard to complain
author: Joseph Mathews

review_text:
had a really nice family meal at this outlet with my husband and 2 kids. and had the most wonderful service from this one server who was super patient and kind, especially with our noisy and rowdy kids haha! her name is claire and she took great care of our family and made sure we were comfortable throughout the meal.

really appreciate her warm service, it made the whole experience much more enjoyable especially as a mother who appreciates service more than anything when it comes to my family. will definitely come back if we are around the area again!
author: abqurah qisma

review_text:
Living in Singapore, I have never tried Saizeriya but decided to try today so I went to this outlet that is one of the closest restaurant as a first time patron.

I asked the staff if I could order and she said to use my phone and scan QR code to order. Although I find that a little convenient, it's also quite troublesome and there might be issues like what if a person didnt bring a phone or their phones are out of battery, those thoughts flooded my mind.

Regardless, I ordered my meal which is a Carbonara with Poached Egg ($6.9). The meal was prepared swiftly, and I received it pretty fast. (time to receive: 8 minutes) ⌚

The food tasted pretty good, the egg was runny and the carbonara pasta was coated with egg sauce as well. 🍝🥚

The meal also consisted of some bacon bits which were tasty 🥓 but honestly after the meal I didn't felt very full from it.

The restaurant had a nice design and ambience. The staff were alright, I didn't receive any bad services and they had a quite friendly attitude. I think the restaurant listened to the feedback as well as there was some nice chill air con so it's not as hot as other reviews says now 👍

Overall it was not bad, had a good meal as a first time patron of Saizeriya 👍
author: Besharps

review_text:
Great Ambience ,instagram worthy interior , a brand name and a fancy menu ... but the coldest service ever !
We hit the place cause it was a new outlet in the neighbourhood and thought we 'll try something different , it was our Anniversary day and we shouldve known better !
After waiting for sometime we were directed to a table and that was it really ! We couldn't find anybody to take our orders even after requesting for a while ...
The seatings were really comfy and the interior designs were surely pleasant to eyes...
There was a staff later on who got our orders with the coldest face ever but prolly He had a long day ! We ordered wine with the food and the wine glasses were literally stumped on the table , wondering if it is a Sin to order wine ... Whatever ,when the food arrived it was another waiter who literally slapped the plates on the table and left !
The food was average but the presentation seemed pretty ... The portion size was decent as well ...
Definitely not going back to this place ONLY cause of the wonderfully pathetic service !
author: emerald manoj

review_text:
If you fancy Hot and piping ,super yummy banana fritters, this is a place you should strictly visit ! These crispy snacks are extremely addictive , though you are aware that they are deep fried and not so healthy , it becomes tedious to stop with just one or two ! The portion size for the price is pretty good too.
They have variants of the fritters that include yam and pineapple but the banana fritters are the best in my opinion... They also serve sweet potato balls which are mediocre though
The staff are super quick and  pack your order neat and well
author: emerald manoj

review_text:
Seriously, their crunchy, sesame-infused golden batter is so addictively crispy, I almost finished all 3 boxes by myself

Their signature Thai fried pineapple? Sweet, juicy, and perfectly balanced with a subtle crispiness. Despite all the frying, I barely felt any grease—thanks to their oil-draining machine, making this a slightly healthier indulgence. Plus, the ingredients are sourced directly from Thailand, so you know it’s top-notch!

Shoutout to the amazing staff who tirelessly keep frying up fresh batches 🙌
author: Zozo

review_text:
Saw this place on social media and decided to visit and give it a try.
Visited on a weekday afternoon and it was rather quiet and no queue. It's located at the basement but definitely not hard to find because their signboard with the word banana is really very easy to spot.
This is a takeaway place so there are no seats and you have to find somewhere to sit and enjoy them.
Not a lot of items on the menu, but it's special because it has fried pineapple! Had someone to share with me and we wanted to try everything so we ordered a mix, and had to order the fried pineapple separately as it is not included in the mix and match.
Preparation was very fast because there were already some in front of the display. The packet we got was somehow still a little warm for some items, but the pineapple ones were like just out from deep frying so it was still quite hot.
Decided to eat while fresh so had to find a place to sit and try. Tried the mix and match, everything was okay, the banana tasted pretty good. The sweet potato balls were light and hollow and was a little lukewarm so didn't taste that crispy. The fried sweet potato was not bad but the yam one was dry and cold.
The highlight for me was definitely the pineapple because it was hot and fried to perfection. It's kinda unique cause it's not common to find deep fried pineapple and you know that pineapple actually sweetens itself after applying heat on it. I felt that the sesame actually enhanced the taste of the fried items a lot and it's more pronounced here and more fragrant as well.
Could feel that the oil was well drained from the fried items couldn't feel that it was greasy from holding it or feel sick eating something oily.
I would love to visit again, though it's a little out of the way for people not visiting Yishun. Not near the MRT and requires shuttle bus there.
author: Matthew Lee

review_text:
🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟
I absolutely loved my snack stop at Mrs Banana (IMM #01-41)! The traditional Thai fried bananas were crispy on the outside, warm and soft inside — just the right amount of sweetness without being greasy. They really brought back the nostalgic joy of Thai street snacks, but with a polished twist.

I paired it with their milk tea, which was the perfect combo. Not overly sweet, super refreshing, and exactly what you need to balance out the fried treat. The packaging was neat and convenient for takeaway — great for munching while strolling through the mall.

Plus, the service was fast and friendly. The front tagline says “Every Bite Brings a Smile", and the team delivered honestly. Highly recommended if you’re craving a unique snack at IMM!

📍 Mrs Banana @ IMM
🥇 Try the Fried Thai Bananas + Milk Tea combo!
#MrsBanana #ThaiSnacks #IMMFoodie #FriedGoodness #BananaLovers #SnackTime #MilkTeaMagic
author: Aman Kozha

review_text:
The new fritter snack shop, BANANA, has opened in Yishun’s Wisteria Mall, bringing crispy Thai fried bananas and other fritters to the area. Known for their oil-free, low-calorie treats, BANANA uses a special oil spinner machine to create a non-greasy, crunchy snack. I tried the Mix & Match ($7) option, allowing you to choose up to nine items from an assortment of Thai Fried Banana, Yam Fritters, Sweet Potato Fritters, Sweet Potato Balls, and Purple Sweet Potato Balls.

Each fritter had an impressive crunch, enhanced by the coconut-flavoured batter and a sprinkle of sesame seeds for a light nutty taste. The Thai fried banana was soft, fruity, and naturally sweet, while the yam and sweet potato fritters offered a nice bite with mild sweetness. The sweet potato balls, both regular and purple, were pleasantly puffy and chewy, though fairly standard in taste.

BANANA’s clean and oil-free finish makes these fritters a guilt-free snack worth trying. I’ll definitely be back for their fritters!
author: Yang

review_text: Really solid Japanese comfort food at very affordable prices. If you’re staying around Yishun and craving Japanese food that doesn’t break the bank, this is definitely worth checking out. Come early because their ramen was already sold out around 2pm, so very popular spot. Would come back again.
author: Rita L

review_text:
Recently I found this tiny Japanese outlet at the mall. There’s limited dine in area, but quite cozy with very interesting decorations on the walls.

Seafood Tonkotsu Ramen (S$10.90)
Opt for non-spicy version. The broth tasted quite creamy and milky. The ramen was served topped with clams, prawns, Ajitsuke Tamagotchi, chopped leek, and sesame seed.

Unagi Donburi (S$12.50)
Flavourful thick slice of eel over rice, served with pickles and tamago slices. Love the flavourful sauce over the rice.

Accompanied the meal with
Homemade Iced Lemon Tea (S$3.50/ cup)
which was quite refreshing.

Finished off the meal with
Caramel Pudding Cake and Mochi (S$6.90)
The creamy cake was served with caramelized top. Not too sweet. The chewy chocolate mochi was stuffed with chocolate flavour cream.
author: Doreen Tan

review_text:
A cosy restaurant that serves up tasty ramen that is better than ramen joints around the area. We were impressed by the cha shu, there's a really nice smoky taste to the meat and the soup was really comforting.
Would return again to try other things on the menu! 😊
author: Prisca Kong

review_text:
We came to this small ramen shop for a late lunch. It wasn’t busy, and the service was prompt and friendly. We ordered different types of ramen, and all of them were good.

For an additional $3.50, we upgraded to a set that came with side dishes and a drink — definitely value for money. One thing worth mentioning is that, unlike many places where set drinks are quite diluted, the drinks here were properly concentrated, which was a pleasant surprise.

The food quality is solid, and the staff were happy to provide takeaway packaging and extra sauces when we couldn’t finish our side dishes, without any additional charges. Excellent customer service and a very satisfying meal overall.
author: Eyogurt

review_text: Ramen house should try 👍👍! The tonkotsu broth is so creamy, the kurobuta melts in your mouth, and the portions are generous. The staff here are kind and efficient, and the restaurant is clean. Great value for the quality highly recommend to any ramen lover. And the desserts? A must-try!
author: Hennylou Paras

review_text: We came to Wisteria Mall for a quick lunch. Saw BK and went in. Our girl was excited with the scooby doo toy and we were greeted by Kevin who offered to assist us with our order. He showed us the deals that BK was offering and even let my daughter choose the toy she wants. We were please with his customer service. Keep it up young man!
author: Asad Uzayr

review_text:
We usually visit Burger king when I fancy a Plant-based burger , most burger joints don't serve anything plant-based except for fries or onion rings ...
Anyway the staffs in this joint are usually lethargic , I think they are understaffed prolly ... So the service is sluggish most of the times ...
The food however is almost all the times standard , the Plant based whooper is yum and has a good portion size ...
I wish something about the service can be done !
author: emerald manoj

review_text: Visited Burger King Wisteria Mall recently and had such a good experience. The place was clean, food came out quickly, and everything tasted fresh. Manager Hazli was really approachable and made sure customers were well taken care of  you can tell he runs the place with heart. It’s nice to see this kind of service, will definitely come back again.
author: Nur Khatijah Abdul Rasheed

review_text: I left my handphone on the table on 28 Feb at 6plus and the staff kept my handphone for me. When I realised my handphone was missing , I called my handphone number and the staff asked me to go back and collect. Thank you Burger King staff @ Wisteria for your kind deed. 👍👏🏻👏🏻
author: Esther Teh

review_text:
This time was greeted by friendly staff at the entrance and the counter.
Ordered snow combo meal of whopper with ham....absolutely delicious 😋. The size is big like the original whopper unlike those standard size buns. And the burger and buns weren't dry.
Ample lettuce and onions, 2 slices of tomato, generous sauce.
This burger meal along with the quality should stick permanently to the menu.
author: blaq catz

review_text: I love this Subway outlet here. The bread it's freshly hot, it's fluffy and quite big that's the way I like it 😀👍🏻that's subway should be in America. It's not like other shop I at in Paragon mall outlet the bread I ate there quite hard or dry. I will coming here often when craving for Subway it's near by my home. Service it's good and veggies are so fresh.
author: Valerie Sagun

review_text: Service staff are very impolite. The way they serve the food is like wrap in the paper without thinking that it’s for human food.
author: Jireh Goh

review_text: It is not working to place all the interns in the frontline during peak hours! There are 4 or 5 staff and yet i have to wait for 10-15mins for a simple order. There's just 3 customers in front of me. We are all being very patient but the speed and skills is way too slow.
author: SJ Chen

review_text:
Ordered flat bread, that is not flat bread in the picture.

You guys just care about taking the money but don't give a **** about what you serve.

Not the first time you mess up orders.

Get the order RIGHT for once.

But this is my last time ordering from this place.

I hope other people do the same to your food.
author: E-way Chieng

review_text:
I visited this Subway hoping to get a simple order: just chicken with egg mayo, no bread. When I asked for it, the staff, who was a tall guy responded rudely, questioning “how to add egg mayo on only chicken” like it was a big problem. I also asked for salad and was told “it’s going to be expensive” in a dismissive tone.

I wasn’t asking for anything unreasonable — just customizing a meal I was willing to pay for. The attitude made the whole experience uncomfortable. I hope staff can be more respectful and customer-friendly in the future.
author: Nguyen Brandon

review_text: Nice enviornment and staff very helpful, polite. Most imptly, food is good and serves very good pizza!!
author: Kopi LIM

review_text:
Food is great as usual. Nothing to complain about.
But service...first off when i asked if my order is ready cause the order says completed. The man checked and then said: "you having here or take away?"
When i told him dine in, he say chey i thought you takeaway, need to wait la.
So fine. Anyway I was just checking.
After another 5mins they served the pizza without the drinks. When I approached them again for the drinks, they said they don't have sprite or green tea, only coke.
Im like then why do you sell it on the menu?
They just handed me the coke and went away.
Gosh. This is really bad.
The staff is only bothered and focus on preparing the mass amount of takeaway orders and cant even be bothered to take a second look or speak a word more to anyone else standing at the counter.
Pizza hut desperately needs to send their staff for some customer service experience training.
Also, every table is just left there after dine ins. A table has soiled dishes left over when I arrived but until im done like an hour later, it was still left there. Staff cant be bothered to step out of the prep area to do any clearing.
author: Eugene Tjon

review_text: All staffs are always smiling!! Elvin Chan was very helpful with everything that we need. Will definitely eat here again!! Thanks 🫶
author: Patricia Ann Barles

review_text: Service staffs are polite and knowledgeable of products/items. Food is prepared in acceptable duration and served to table hot. Restaurant is generally clean.
author: Sharmaine Zhang

review_text:
Came here to break fast and had such a pleasant experience. All the staff were thoughtful and friendly, especially Jeslyn and Rina. 😊 Staff at the counter was clear in communicating the waiting time to us.

Everything we ordered was yummy, from the pizza to the honey wings. We will definitely be back!
author: Mirshasha

review_text:
I ordered through Grab and accidentally selected the wrong flavor. I called the restaurant, and they were very kind and helpful in changing it for me. I really appreciate the great service!

The food was really yummy and satisfying. Kudos to the person who answered my call and assisted me so patiently.

Garlic Parmesan and Louisiana Rub flavors are best!
author: Sittie Sarah Marasigan

review_text: Visited this foodstore 4 weeks ago during Valentine's day as I can recall. Service was chaotic, witnessed an indian lady manager scolding a young part-timer in front of customers amid the busy dinner hours. I believe this can be settled privately in another area? 😐 Food was tasty, but definitely won't be back due to the unpleasant atmosphere. Not worth the stress. Had to give it a 3 star instead of 1 because there was a friendly employee that was flipping the chickens gave me my missing ranch hastily.
author: Raymond

review_text:
First time dining in with our kids and it was a great experience. Our eldest son chose the meal, and the chicken was fresh, tender, and flavourful. The ambience was a little noisy as it’s located next to a mini arcade, but still manageable for a family meal.

Special mention to Yesh, our server for the day. He was very helpful in assisting us to choose the best deal, well-mannered, and patient. Despite the restaurant being busy with orders, he served with joy and a genuine smile.

Well done, Yesh! Keep up the great service! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
author: MumOfChamps S.

review_text:

review_text: it was amazing! the staff was kind and recommend me some of the best flavours since it was my first time here . The tables and floors was clean , will come again with more friends as it is a nice place to eat and dine.
author: putri nur balqis

review_text:
Nasi Lemak (SGD $5) @ Pak Mandor Nasi Lemak.
.
Established in 2001 by Misniati Binte Sagio, this long-serving stall is now co-run together with her daughters. Popular for their high-quality, authentic, and affordable rendition.
.
Their unique green-hued rice is naturally infused with coconut milk and pandan / screwpine leaf essence, fluffy moist in texture and carrying a distinct grainy earthy floral sweet flavour. The egg omelette patty is springy soft with eggy savoury flavour, while the deep-fried ikan bilis / anchovies are crispy crunchy with fishy salty savoury flavour.
.
The breaded fish surimi fillet is springy tender with sweet savoury flavour, while the battered chicken sausage is snappy springy with meaty salty savoury flavour. The battered chicken wing is crispy tender with smoky meaty savoury spice flavour. The sambal tumis / stir-fried chili paste is chunky with sweet savoury salty spice flavour, the heat lingering slightly on the palate.
author: Ivan Teh

review_text:
Q for 20min on a late Sunday morning. Ordered chicken wing, egg, ikan bilis peanut, fish cake and chicken cutlet. Cost $4.50.

Summary
Rice : great (when cold)
Chicken : great
Ikan bilis peanut : average
Egg : great
Fish cake : great
Chicken cutlet : average
Sambal : poor

Some stall of long queue because their food are master but others might just because they are cheap. This I feel is more of the later.

Rice was fragrant but I was definitely not impressed at the start as they are far too wet. They only gotten better when it is cold aka when I was about to finish it. Basically the rice need airing and taste of coconut became apparent but it is a bit late.

Chicken was great. Very crispy but not very meaty so lacking in juice and also not much batter.

Ikan bilis and peanut was standard. Doesn't hurt jaw and add crunch to the meal.

Egg and fish cake was surprisingly good. Egg being thick and fish cake crispy exterior is always a win.

Chicken cutlet is bad. Not juicy and is soggy plus since it is not popular it is cold.

Sambal is sweet minimum spice. No shiok factor.

At this price point it is okay lah. Not much to complain that it is overcharging
author: Super Fragrance

review_text:
Rice is too wet and doesn't taste lemak at all. Sambal taste got no kick, more like some type of sauce.
Overall whole dish quite dull taste. Just not for me.
But then it's super affordable. 5 bucks for this is hard to beat.
author: Lim Ray

review_text:
Packed at 648 Yishun
Nasi Lemak (chicken wing and fish set, added 1 extra wing) — $5.00
The coconut rice is nicely cooked — soft, fluffy, and rich with a pleasant coconut aroma that blends well with the sambal chilli. The chilli has a good balance of sweetness and spice, complementing the fragrant rice perfectly. The chicken wings, though not big, are crispy outside and juicy inside — no wonder they’re popular here.

review_text: A football bar type of concept, and located in a more ulu corner of Singapore. A very nice place to chill, have a drink, and watch football. Food is not too bad, but not overly fantastic either. Parking is available just at the side road beside, but park at your own risk.

review_text: What I find ideal of this place is just the ambiance... Relaxing and enjoyable to be at. In the menu, our table ordered chicken wings, club sandwich & fish & chips... The chicken wings texture: crunchy skin, aromatic and tender meat. Club sandwich bread was toasted well with butter, followed by homemade beef patty. It wasn't the typical club sandwich that was done anyhow in clubs or hotels. The beer battered fish & chips: fish batter was fried till super crispy, yet the fish meat still moist😊. Although it may get crowded during the weekends, but due to the spaciousness, neighbouring chattering didn't bother us much. Lastly, the staff were kind and friendly... In particular, Mae. She's quick to take orders attentive, and friendly! Definitely a thumbs up!

restaurant_name: Tiong Bahru Hainanese Boneless Chicken Rice
review_text: This chicken rice stall is a standout for its perfectly executed balance of flavors and textures. The rice is exceptionally fragrant and fluffy, with each grain separate and infused with a rich, savory chicken stock aroma that allows it to be enjoyed even on its own. The chicken is consistently tender and succulent, often featuring a smooth, gelatinous skin that indicates expert poaching techniques. Completing the meal is a robust, chili sauce and aromatic ginger dip that provide a powerful "kick" to every bite. Combined with friendly service and generous portions, this stall offers a truly comforting and high-quality hawker experience. A true gem in Yishun area!

review_text:
A new place that's opened in my 'hood. I had it twice, once for dinner and once for breakfast.

The quality of the food is consistently good! Noodles have an excellent crunch; the flavours are mouthwatering and balanced. They are generous with their ingredients, a lavish serving of char siew and the wantons(fried and soup)/dumplings are chock-full of fillings that provide a nice bite!

Overall, it is a fantastic addition to the neighbourhood!

Each mouthful of the noodle reminds of the good old style of wanton. The chilli is not too spicy but hit the right spot. So, if u are a fan of wanton mee, pls at least try once.

restaurant_name: Yao Ji Ban Mian. Fish Soup. Congee
review_text:
(Update: This stall will permanently close by the end of June 2026 as there are not enough customers to keep the business going due to low footfall at the coffeeshop.
(The much-raved ‘Oh My Don’ Japanese stall has already shut due to this)
So best enjoy the food before this stall shuts permanently!)

This stall is run by a very friendly middle-age couple previously from China.
Their ban mian/u mian noodle which the husband painstakingly kneads by hand every morning (no machine is used) is consistently very good.
What sets this stall apart from other ban mian stalls is that they have fried u mian and fried bee hoon which is very Heng Hwa style on their menu.
What’s more, they are flexible to tweet the ingredients depending on customer’s dietary restrictions.
For instance, as I am a pescatarian, the ingredients for my order of fried u mian or fried bee hoon can be changed to fish slices instead of the usual la la, etc  .
The owner is even very readily willing to fry ban mian when requested…
It is something customers never get to taste anywhere else in Singapore.
The stall’s dumplings are big and delicious too - value for money.
Plus, they give fresh green vegetables instead of the usual cabbage and the fish they use is fresh batang instead of the cheap tilapia…
Highly recommended…

review_text:

author: Syful Baqtiar xbluexmoonxrisingx

review_text:
When we popped over to Hai Ge Ji’s Hainanese Chicken Rice restaurant along North Bridge Road we were then excited to see if it lived up to the promise to serve real authentic Hainanese style chicken rice. It did. And the fact that it is halal is such a blessing for us Muslims who wanted the real deal but find it hard to come by. So when they informed and encouraged us to pop over and support their Beef Noodles brother little restaurant we agreed wholeheartedly should we swing over to that part of Singapore. Well we finally did, when my wife had some work nearby, and eagerly looked forward to trying it.

Well when they say it is a small shop they weren’t kidding. Only a few tables with a hole and counter to the kitchen next to it with ordering kiosks preparing the classic traditional Chinese beef noodles with thick gravy. It is not something that most Malays or Muslims will be familiar with, especially with its lightly herby laced spice beef broth served with springy noodles covered by a thick dark sauce, since halal versions are hard to come by easily; with one offered and fondly remembered and missed by the OG halal foodcourt Banquet a long time ago. As we are not Yishun natives we tapao’ed or ordered for takeaway for the family. I did warn my wife that it is better to dine over freshly made noodles piping served hot in an inviting bowl but we were packing for the kids to have dinner together back home. My wife and I went for the dry noodles with thick rice noodles while my daughter opted for the same but with kway teow. To try the different types of beef served I went for the all-in mixed beef. My son opted for the soupy one. I must say they were not only wonderfully and carefully packed for not only ease of travel but with the soup separated it really made reheating for mixing at home a delight to eat when delivered or packed.

Now for the food. It’s good, comfortingly satiable and rather authentic in taste. We noted with delight that the beef portion for each serving is generous, and is tender and lovely. The kway teow was not a good choice as it does not pick up the beef taste well so my daughter was unsatisfied with hers. The soup or broth is, as I had hoped, wonderfully hearty and delicious. We are glad we ordered extra beef balls – they are really good and nice – and the tasty fried fish beancurd is really good. Is it a wow, it is not. Is it good, it certainly is. With its heavier beefy with thick sauce it needed that all important signature zesty chili dipping sauce to cut through. Theirs are fine but could be better to truly balance it out. The delicate balancing is key. The calamansi lime given to me doesn’t come with an instruction to either squeeze it into the noodles or over the chilli sauce for your own preferred balance. I do believe without help on how best to eat for the best tasting sensation for those unfamiliar some may come out of the experience possibly not altogether satisfied or appreciating it fully. What a shame, for it is good. No wonder some actually asked if its sister Hainanese Chicken Rice could be sold there too. The latter is more comforting and familiar for those unfamiliar.

As for us it’s good enough for a repeat order or perhaps we should sit down and truly dine there. Personally, I am just grateful a halal version is available.

review_text:
The kitchen is actually helmed by Thai chefs, which usually bodes well for the authenticity of the stir-fry. However, be prepared for the service, which can be best described as curt. The staff are very transactional and there to take your order and move on to the next person as quickly as possible.

I went for the Minced Pork Pad Krapow with the quadruple yolk, mostly for the novelty, and shared it between three people (unless you’re on a massive bulk, one person probably shouldn't tackle four eggs alone).

Because the quadruple yolk isn't a "standard" order, they cooked it fresh on the spot. This was a win, as the single and double yolk eggs are often pre-fried. There is nothing like a hot, crispy-edged egg to break into and it’s much better than the lukewarm ones sitting on the counter.

The pork was the star. You can really taste the layers of oyster sauce, soy, and fish sauce coming through. It’s a complex, savoury profile rather than just being salty. We opted for Level 3 spiciness, which hit that sweet spot which had enough kick to keep it interesting without ruining your day.

If I’m being picky, I wish the basil aroma was more pronounced. It felt a little quiet compared to the heavy savoury notes of the sauces. Also, we tried the beef version, but it didn't quite hit the same heights as the pork as it lacked that same depth of flavour and complexity.

I recently tried the garlic naan with mutton keema at Drubinah Yishun and it was nothing short of amazing. The naan arrived warm, fluffy and perfectly baked, with just the right balance of crisp edges and soft centre. The garlic flavour was fragrant but not overpowering, making every bite incredibly satisfying even on its own.

The real star, however, was the mutton keema. It was rich, well-spiced and packed with deep, authentic flavours. The minced mutton was tender and juicy, not dry at all, and the masala was beautifully balanced without being too oily. When paired with the naan, the combination was pure comfort food at its best.

Portion size was generous and definitely value for money, especially considering the quality. Service was also fast and friendly, making the overall dining experience even better.

If you are in Yishun and craving hearty North Indian flavours, do not miss out on the garlic naan and mutton keema at Drubinah. It is easily a 5-star dish and I will definitely be back for more.

review_text:
There was a time when Bah Kut Teh in Singapore wasn’t all pepper and MSG or slave to fall-off-the-bone standards that modern locals seem to crave.  For a version of that bygone flavour, De Yun comes excitingly close!

The first thing that hit me was the clean aroma of fresh pork and garlic.  The stock was well-seasoned, made full by whole cloves of garlic boiled to a mashable consistency.  But the real surprise was the hint of mushroom that made the soup taste even more meaty.  Soft, even hints of cloves, ginger and white pepper complete the palate, resting warm on the lips and throat only towards the end of the meal.  Yes, there is MSG, but balanced only to maximise what the stock has to offer.

Then the pork ribs, blessed with just enough fibre that helps the flesh to cling loosely to the bone and develop bite.  Every chew releases more flavour and slows down and desire to gulp and swallow… what a clever, satisfying treat!  For more, try the variety of sides and pig innards, all prepared with much consideration and not too much salt.  My favourite so far are the staples of stomach (tripe), soy peanuts and chopped preserved vegetables.  The braised pig trotters are also good if you have a party of 2-3 at least.

Despite costing a shade more than most coffee shop establishments, the meal was still value for money for its old-school standards of quality.  Most sides are priced at $1 each while the soup is refillable at no extra cost.  Carb lovers may find rice at 80 cents per small bowl pricey.

I can’t wait to return for another taste of my childhood.

review_text:
First posted in February 2024, updated Nov 2024

Sundays regularly find me in Yishun, where I often take a late lunch.  I must admit my initial hesitation to eat at Just Greens because of their poor rating and reviews.  Then again, if we don’t try, we never know, so guess what…?

It was good!  The vegetarian operators certainly know how to make vegetables tasty.

There were enough flavour profiles and textures to choose from, ranging from the soy sauce infused crunchy black fungus and braised mushroom, through gently salted bean curd skin ‘egg’ roll and the judiciously tomato-sauce inflections in the brinjal and long bean stir-fry.  The brown rice was unsalted and unflavoured, its mildly nutty flavours coming through in grains moist and tender, almost tending to clump.

Yet, this was the perfect complement to the variety of dishes, some of which were seasoned more gently  so that the plainer vegetables could hold their own in sauces that aren’t starchy or cloying.  Except the brinjal, which had a tendency to suck up fat, the dishes didn’t show any trace of oiliness in the mouth.  Those seeking some animal protein can take solace in an egg omelette, displayed separately from the other options.  You will also find gentle amounts of dried anchovy flavouring their spinach, belacan for their vegetable curry, etc.

My $6 bought me a satisfying meal of 4 dishes on brown or white rice.  Servings were generous so that I finished the rice before the dishes.  So, while it wasn’t exactly cheap, it certainly was value for money.  Most importantly, the meal was honest and well considered, paying due respect to the various ingredients.

I specifically asked for a fully cooked egg. Not runny, not soft-boiled, just a properly cooked egg. Shouldn’t be hard, right? Well, apparently it was too much to ask. The first plate came with a half-cooked, borderline raw egg. I politely sent it back. Second try? Still soft and barely touched by heat. By the third attempt, I was already irritated and hungry but guess what? Still not fully cooked. At that point, I gave up and just left it on the plate.

The ginger chicken itself was fine, but honestly, it’s hard to enjoy your meal when your patience is already fried. I spent over 30 minutes waiting for what should’ve been a fast, no-nonsense dinner. Instead, I left frustrated, unsatisfied, and wondering if I should’ve just gone home and made instant noodles.

If a place can’t get a basic request right after three tries, I’m not coming back. Dinner time should not feel like a test of endurance.

review_text:
Dear Michelin Guide / Relevant Team,

I am writing to express my disappointment with both the food quality and customer service I experienced at:

Hai Nan Zai Fried Hokkien Mee
417 Yishun Avenue 11, #01-351, Singapore 760417

Date of Visit: 3 June 2025
Time: 9:31 PM
Dish Ordered: Fried Hokkien Mee ($4.50)

⸻

🍜 Food Review:

I requested Hokkien Mee with all pork and no seafood – a standard request I often make at other hawker stalls. The chef told me, “no more pork,” and I clearly responded that it was fine to proceed with the normal version (i.e., with seafood).

However, when I received the plate, it was just noodles and egg – no pork (understandably), but also no prawns or squid. I went back to clarify, and the chef said, “You said no seafood.” I explained that I agreed to the regular version after they said no pork, and I had already paid.

This came across as dishonest and careless, especially since this was only made known after payment was taken.

When I returned to the stall, neither the chef nor the two ladies showed any concern or apology. Instead, they threw some prawns and squid on top of the plate without re-cooking or mixing it into the dish. When I asked, “That’s it?”, they just nodded — no explanation, no effort, no remorse.

⸻

😠 Service Review:
•	Staff were rude, impatient, and dismissive.
•	No proper communication or accountability.
•	Absolutely no sign of service that reflects a Michelin-recognised establishment.

⸻

🔻 Overall Impression:

This experience was frustrating and disappointing. The food served was incomplete, the situation was mishandled, and the staff lacked basic courtesy. If this stall still carries a Michelin mention or recognition, I strongly urge a re-evaluation. The current standards do not reflect the excellence Michelin represents.

Thank you for your attention.

review_text:
Food Review – 20 May 2025
What We Ordered: Shellout Sambal, Salted Fish Fried Rice with Fried Egg, Chicken Soup, Iced Milo & Apple Juice

We tried a variety of dishes at a humble local eatery, and honestly—it was so good!

The Shellout Sambal was the star of the meal. It was absolutely delicious, packed with flavor and spice. I even ate it without rice and it still tasted amazing—really impressive.

The Salted Fish Fried Rice came with a perfectly cooked fried egg on top. The flavors were well-balanced, and every bite was satisfying.

The Chicken Soup hit the spot too—rich, homey, and seasoned just right.

As for drinks, the Iced Milo and Apple Juice were refreshing and a nice finish to the meal.

The place itself is pretty basic—no air-conditioning, but the tables and chairs were neat and pleasant. There’s even a TV to keep you entertained. Service was quick and friendly.

Overall:
If you’re looking for great food at a reasonable price and don’t mind a simple setup, this place is worth it. We’d definitely recommend it!

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Authentic Teochew Kway Teow Soup – A Hidden Gem!

If you’re a fan of simple yet soul-warming comfort food, this Teochew kway teow soup is a must-try. The broth is clear but incredibly flavorful — light, fragrant, and full of depth from hours of slow simmering. Every spoonful feels wholesome and satisfying.

The kway teow noodles are silky smooth and perfectly cooked, while the slices of fish cake, lean pork, and minced meat add a lovely balance of textures. What really stands out is the freshness of the ingredients — especially the tender fish balls and crisp vegetables.

Add a dash of their homemade chili and a few drops of dark soy sauce, and the whole bowl just comes alive. It’s the kind of dish that reminds you why Teochew cuisine is so beloved — clean, honest, and comforting.

The lemak daging salai is good! The asam pedas ikan siakap taste really fresh. Part of the shop has aircon. Will definitely return.
author: Sofina M Y

review_text:
Had a satisfying dim sum experience at 大四喜 (Da Si Xi) in Eco Botani. The selection is solid with all the classic favorites you’d expect. Har gow and siu mai were well-executed, with fresh fillings and good texture. The cheong fun was smooth and silky, and the buns were soft with flavorful fillings.

Service was efficient despite the crowd, and dishes came out fairly quickly. The place itself is clean and comfortable, making it a good spot for family meals or casual gatherings. While a few items could be a little more refined in flavor, overall quality is consistent and enjoyable.

A dependable choice for dim sum in Eco Botani, and I’d happily return when the craving hits.
author: Shawn Chua

review_text: had a really good experience dining here, in the eco botani area. the price is quite affordable, my 5 friends spent about 200RM here! the best dishes for me are the siew mai, har gow, chicken feet and cheong fun. and radish cake
author: Joseph Koh

review_text:
Food is good.
The xiao long bao breaks easily, so they put a small alum cup on each, so we can still enjoy the soup although they don't have the skill of DTF.
The hong you chao shou tastes of 麻辣  instead of the usual 酸辣. I think it's ok too.
The Or Nee is also good.
Fried carrot cake has wok hei!
There's this chim toi looking with prawn ball, which is also good.
author: Collin Ng

review_text:
Nice ambience - felt like in Hong Kong

Staff - generally friendly, some are quiet direct.. our empty plates were cleared promptly

Food - food came fast & hot, staff came regularly with trays of steam food to select

Though it was crowded, service was fast & prompt.

Will come back again...
author: Sam

review_text: This is my favorite dim sum spot in Iskandar Puteri. I usually go on weekdays to beat the crowd, no queuing required, and the food always comes out fresh and piping hot.
author: Chen LP

restaurant_name: Four Seasons Dumplings 四季鲜饺
review_text:
The indoor space is comfortable and cool, and everything in the restaurant is neatly organized and very clean.
It was impressive to see the chef wearing a mask while making the dumplings.
The ingredients inside the dumplings were fresh and full of flavor—you can really tell they don’t hold back on the fillings.
Even though I don’t speak Chinese, when I said “thank you” in Chinese, they smiled warmly and greeted me back. It left me with a very warm impression.
author: 진윤정

restaurant_name: Four Seasons Dumplings 四季鲜饺
review_text: I actually made a Grab order, that Grab messed up. But these guys deserve 5 stars and more, for the way they tried to handle it for me. Grab took more than an hour to assign a driver, for some strange reason (no rain, no weather issue etc, and distance not unreasonable). The restaurant had closed, but they called me and stayed open for up to 50mins beyond their closing time to ensure a driver picked up my order. For this I am so very grateful. I dont think many restaurants will bother doing the same. The dumplings I ordered too were excellent. They were cold by the time I got them, but easily reheated by scalding them a bit. Very delicious with premium ingredients and real big chunks of king prawn inside. I will absolutely order again, or pay them a visit myself in person one day. Thank you so much... you all are really awesome and amazing.
author: Kimberley Howarth

restaurant_name: Four Seasons Dumplings 四季鲜饺
review_text: This place serve authentic chinese dumpling with next level of taste. The premium like King Prawn with Fish roe and pork is very nice. We tried a few flavours like pork with sweetcorn and cheese, pork with black truffle and bamboo shoot dumping are also good too. The only disadvantage is the shop is at 2nd floor which requires you to climb a flight of stairs. Serving the dumpling takes time as they are fresh handmade and cook before eating. Shop wise is a small shop with 3 person manning so expected to take time to do. Overall it is very good in terms of the food but only issue is to walk a flight of stairs.
author: Kenneth Khoo

restaurant_name: Four Seasons Dumplings 四季鲜饺
review_text: Had the most delicious Beijing-style dumplings here! Everything is handmade fresh, and you can really taste the quality. The owners are warm and friendly, and the environment is pleasant and welcoming. A wonderful family-owned restaurant that I’ll definitely be coming back to!
author: Yvvone Yee

restaurant_name: Four Seasons Dumplings 四季鲜饺
review_text: Relaxing and friendly environment. Enjoy authentic Beijing handmade dumplings. I visited 3 times in 7 days!
author: Bill Chan WY

review_text:
Chanced upon this after finally found parking and went for this instead. Good assortments of local food. Portions are huge. We had the regular Thunder rice and Wanton noodle. Wanton is chicken meat and tasty, noodles had a unique bite to it. Thunder tea rice is decent with lots of ingredients. The nonya kuih is the highlight, people enjoying them throughout the meals, each pc is RM1.80. We packed ours home.
Will be back to try the ice kacang & chendol.
will be
author: Twoelf 787

review_text:
Dropped by this café in the afternoon for some coffee and Nyonya kuih. The place has a cozy vibe and is nicely decorated — a comfortable spot to chill for a short break. We tried a selection of their Nyonya kuihs, but honestly, they weren’t as fragrant or flavorful as I expected. The texture was decent, just missing that authentic pandan-coconut aroma that makes traditional kuih stand out.

We also ordered the rojak, which turned out to be better — fresh fruits, crunchy fritters, and a good balance of sweet and tangy sauce. It’s definitely the more enjoyable dish of the visit.

One thing to note: they close quite early, around 5 PM, so it’s best to come before that if you’re planning an afternoon snack or coffee break. Overall, a decent place for a casual stop, though the kuih could use a little more punch in flavor.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: Food was excellent!! The rojak, mee siam curry, wantan soup, red bean & kaya mantao was soooooo good. Pity they close at 4:30pm. Will come back for sure.
author: Snowie Snow

review_text:
After we came last week, my wife crave for the kuek. It is really nice hence we dine in again this week.

Love the ambient n the environment. Bright n n well lid. Service is nice.

We came early this time cuz kuek i noticed last week some kuek seem to sold out pretty fast. Enjoyed the rest of the food i personally love the dry fried thin noodle.

Will definitely come back since it open at 0730hrs earlier than most makan place.
author: Bernard Ong

review_text:
The food served very fast. Within 15 minutes all served. Thanks for the nyonya kuih treat. maybe due to the closing hour which Im arrived at 420pm. Will come again next time. Many food choices than other Kopitiam. Im ordering Kampung Fried Rice. Surprisingly deep red color which is spicier than other Kampung Fried Rice. But I still can tahan the spicy.
Air-conditioning with no smelly on clothes.
author: Ng su ting

review_text:
It was the first time we had dim sum for lunch at this restaurant. Our highly recommended favourites were Har Gow, Salted Egg Buns, Century Egg Porridge and Fried Mango Prawn Rolls.

However, some of the items were pricey such as a small portion of Chinese Lettuce in Soya Sauce at RM12.00++ and 2 pieces of assorted Yong Tau Foo at RM6.30++. Furthermore, the Prawn Chee Cheong Fun Rolls were quite bland too.

We were surprised to see the dim sum being served in trays instead of being pushed around in a trolley.
author: Jonathan Lum

review_text:
Great food, good price and excellent service (special shout out to Jenny! She was super attentive and very friendly. ) We happened to walk by and saw the bustling customers inside and decided to give it a try. And now we found a new fav dim sum place at Eco Botantic! Dim sum is served like trolley style, but on trays.
Definitely will go back!
author: Iva Lim

review_text: Dimsum not my liking. So so taste.
author: Leslie Liew

review_text: Very friendly staff. Special thank you Jenny
author: Felix Chan Chee Seng

review_text: If you like quality Arab fare, this is really a superb place to fulfill your cravings for Arab fusion food! I come here often for their fantastic selection and quality. The service here is friendly, helpful and welcoming. Rakib made good suggestions on what to select for the group.
