He proudly told that his boss insisted on quality ingredients making their food authentic, delicious. Good job, Rakib and all!
author: Gabrielle Lew

review_text:
We visited Matam AlBarakah Bistro for Arabic food, and it turned out to be an incredibly satisfying experience. The servers were awesome — warm, friendly, and genuinely welcoming. They patiently recommended dishes, and we really felt taken care of from the moment we stepped in.

We ordered the claypot chicken briyani and butter chicken with garlic naan, and both dishes were rich, flavourful, and infused with Middle Eastern herbs that gave them a distinct and aromatic taste. The briyani was hearty and fragrant, while the butter chicken paired perfectly with the warm, soft naan.

The interior is also worth mentioning — beautifully decorated, with even small cubicle-style dining spaces that resemble a Middle Eastern home setting, giving the whole meal an extra touch of authenticity and comfort.

Overall, a fantastic find. Great food, lovely ambiance, and top-notch service. Glad we tried this place!
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: I’ve been wanting to come here to try the food for a long time, and finally got the chance! Brought my son along, and I didn’t expect both the food and service to be this good. The staff were friendly and helpful—especially Rakib, who served us from start to finish. Really appreciate the great experience and will definitely come back again!
author: Jookok Loh

review_text: Superb and delicious food. We ordered 1) Lamb shank biryani 2) Chapli Kabab 3) Gaajar Halwa 4) Tandoori Tea.. All r extremely delicious. The staff RAKIB recommended these items and they are really nice and thanks to RAKIB for his lovely hospitality 🙏
author: Durga Prasad

review_text:
We have been frequently visiting this place. Their food both Indian and Arab cuisine is delicious, and despite our manh visits, the quality and standard of service had always been great. They uphold their quality of taste, and service. Surprisingly, the Indian cuisine taste better than any Indian fine dining in Johor.

I would like to give a big shout out to Mr Rakib who remembered us from our last visit, including where we sat and what we ordered! This is really heart warming. His generous smile would forever be in our hearts.
author: Tanusha Ramani

restaurant_name: ROLLS RICE 喜粤 石磨肠粉
review_text: Food is good. The porridge is the watery type but taste is okie.  They play 80s and 90s Cantonese HK songs, very nice.  The fried yam rolls are so crispy.  The Chee Cheong fun got chewy texture, nice. Kopi C kosong just nice.  The chicken feet taste is ok but a bit tough, should have steamed longer. The chilis are good especially the garlic type.  Will come back next time.
author: fb fb

restaurant_name: ROLLS RICE 喜粤 石磨肠粉
review_text:
Came here for lunch and was quite impressed with the overall experience. The restaurant has a very Cantonese vibe — simple, clean, and focused on flavor. Their signature rice rolls are freshly made daily and truly stood out: soft, silky, and smooth with that authentic stone-milled texture. I ordered the prawn version, and it was delicious — the prawns were fresh and tender, perfectly paired with the light soy-based sauce.

We also tried their claypot rice and a few other dishes, all of which were well-cooked and comforting. One thing I really liked about this place is that they let you add your own soy sauce to every dish, so you can control how salty you want it to be — a thoughtful touch that makes a difference.

Service was friendly and efficient, and the overall atmosphere was relaxed and pleasant, making it a great spot for a casual lunch or dinner. The food quality and value definitely make this restaurant worth revisiting, especially for their rice rolls! 😋
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: ROLLS RICE 喜粤 石磨肠粉
review_text: Saw this relatively new restaurant and decided to try it. Service was prompt and friendly but they made an error while serving our our dish which they nicely explained to us and we accepted it without any issue. Food wise, it was a huge disappointment. Started with the chee cheong fun. It was good and I liked the aftertaste. There was a strong peanut smell. As we progress to the other dishes, they all failed together my standards. The porridge was the watery kind and was a little too bland. The fried yam fritter was a little too hard and over fried. Dumplings were just average. So overall, IMO, only the chee cheong fun can make it. Hope they improve on their food.
author: Rex Tan

restaurant_name: ROLLS RICE 喜粤 石磨肠粉
review_text: We had two kinds of rice rolls, the bbq pork and the prawn, both were delicious. It feels different from the usual rice rolls we eat, maybe due to the preparation process (they do the grinding of the rice). We also had the yam ball with salted egg filling which I think was not bad, the outer crust had some crispy flakes. Quite interesting. I also ordered the porridge and the clay pot. Porridge is likely subjectively like what you read in the reviews but personally I think it's nice too. It has got that light feel to it which I enjoy. The clay pot was also good. Can tell the ingredients are fresh. All in all, I think this is definitely a place worth dropping by. I know I will be back.
author: Wei Tiong Ang

restaurant_name: ROLLS RICE 喜粤 石磨肠粉
review_text:
I simply love Cheong fun and this new place specialises in just that. I was informed that this is Guandong cheong fun and owners from Guandong import their rice and other ingredients from Guandong. They grind the rice into flour every morning to make the rice rolls. I appreciate such dedication to getting it just like ‘home’.
I ordered the prawn and vegetarian rice rolls and a steamed pork ribs. It was way too much for 1 person. The cheong fun is rolled in amazing thin layers and add up to a substantial roll! The texture is not ‘wat’/ silky smooth or what we are used to in most dim sum restaurants. The ingredients are fresh and ample and I love the sauce on the side to help myself. The ribs were good, none of that ‘porkyness’ to it.
Overall, I enjoyed it very much. The texture would be something to overcome, but it’s ok, it’s not bad, it’s just different. I would come back again. Oh, the tea was good too!
author: Judy Millar

restaurant_name: Hong Dae Ip Gu Eco Botanic
review_text:
New Korean restaurant at Eco botanic!
We just traveled back from South Korea and we missed Korean food and wanted to give it a try.
First expression, love the Korean style vibe, and music selection (instead of those girls&boys groups 👍🏻👍🏻)
Clean, no oily bbq smell.
Very nice and friendly staff which I like and feel good about it.
Next, food tastes good. I can’t get the chance to try the bbq meat because I’ve no appetite during that time so I ordered noodle for myself.
Definitely come back next time.
(Restaurant owner has a super cute dog😍😍)
author: Bulldogmama

restaurant_name: Hong Dae Ip Gu Eco Botanic
review_text:
Overall dinner dining experience is good.
Dinner gets served in good ample time and waiters are efficient and move quickly.

#Served cold water should be replaced with Cold buckwheat tea to enhance the taste of a good Korean BBQ dinner.

Do observe there is a tall young Korean lady staff in apron whom will focus on the tables but won’t interact with the customers …

Ordered 2-species of beef and another 2-species of pork. Added the steam egg RM5 and Cold Buckwheat noodle RM31 + a few rounds of Banchan (8-species).

A raw occasion we get to order Hanwoo (Korean Beef Sirloin RM135) in JB although ##portion served is small for 4-pax IMHO. Both the beef genre goes well with the green.

The marinated Pork Thin Slices are good whereas the marinated Pork is a tad too salty for our palate liking ; will encourage all to focus your firing power on the beef !!

Cold Buckwheat Noodle soup base is towards the sweet but manageable as a starch for dinner and recommended.

Steam Egg is always a welcome, didn’t come in a volcanic eruption but do get a nod from us all.

All the ordered meats are cooked at the kitchen and served on rectangular HOT grill plates which keeps the meats hot except the marinated pork (very salty) which has been served to the table in the porcelain plate.

A good place for family of 4 and a few friends to dine with the option for Hanwoo !!
author: Alan Goh

restaurant_name: Hong Dae Ip Gu Eco Botanic
review_text: One of the best Korean restaurants I’ve tried. The flavors were rich and authentic, especially the kimchi and grilled meats. Portion sizes were good and the food was served hot and fresh. Highly recommended for anyone who loves Korean cuisine.
author: Wen Ai Liew

restaurant_name: Hong Dae Ip Gu Eco Botanic
review_text:
4 adults and 2 children.
Ordered jjm, mackerel, crab gimbap, seafood pancake, and set 4. Slightly more than enough.
They will cook the meat for you and put it on the hot plate.
Side dishes are great, especially enjoyed the potato salad, kimchi and quail eggs.
Will definitely come again!
author: Jolene Lee

restaurant_name: Hong Dae Ip Gu Eco Botanic
review_text:
Ordered their 2pax set and added beef.

Super yummy, good service. They grilled the beef in front of us, then grilled our other meats in the kitchen before bringing it out. Love how I don't need to do it myself and my clothes don't smell.

The meats were really yummy, beef was so soft and melt-in-your-mouth.

The rabokki was good too, we loved the sauce and it wasn't too spicy.

Steamed egg was alright, nothing too special.

Love the spread of banchans they gave. Usually there's always one or two that i don't eat but i ate every single one this time!

Definitely will come back next time i want some kbbq!
author: Jaelyn Loh

review_text: I miss the Jiro ramen in Japan so much!! It’s so hard to find Jiro ramen in JB. Delicious but the broth tastes not as rich as the one in Japan, maybe to cater the taste of the locals.
author: Lee Xin Wei

review_text:
The family was there for dinner. Wanted to try out this restaurant for a long time and finally we were there.

Ordered the tonkatsu ramen and the tempura prawns. The broth was flavourful and the noodles cooked al dente. It seemed that the noodles were made in-house. The entire bowl of ramen also came with a Japanese boiled egg cooked to perfection. With a great salty flavour and the yolk was watery. The char siew was thick and flavourful as well.

The prices were reasonable. Simply decorated and appropriate service standard.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: Very authentic Japanese Ramen, Jiro-kei style. I was surprised to have nice Ramen with reasonable price and satisfactory portion.
author: T. S

review_text:
Noodles are made inhouse.
Tsukemen 4.5/5 thick springy noodles, flavourful broth with strong katsuobushi taste. Recommended.
Tonkotsu Ramen 4/5 flavourful porky but not smelly.
Chashu tender and tasty.
Onsen egg failed unfortunately.
Female service staff wasn't happy. No "thank you" or "welcome" even after we made payment. =(
author: Jonathan Tye

review_text: Nice ramen restaurant in Eco Botanic. Ordered God ramen and sukiyaki ramen. The soup is flavorable, and the meat is tender. Noodle is springy as well. The gyoza is very delicious as well. Worth to come and eat if around Eco Botanic area.
author: Xplorer SEA

restaurant_name: 壹号擂茶One Kopitiam Eco Botanic
review_text:
Heard about the nice toast and fragrant coffee, so without hesitation, I ordered it. The wall mural seemed to promote Lei Cha; the yellow wine chicken is unique, and the prawn dumpling looks delicious too. As I'm a fan of fish soup, the only option I thought most appropriate would be the bitter gourd fish slices and minced meat soup. The Lei Cha can feed 2 pax; the soup is good with a mild green taste. The yellow wine chicken is delicious, and the chicken was tender. As for the bitter gourd fish slices & minced meat, it's not to my liking. The coffee and toast live up to expectation - coffee's awesome, toast's crispy, kaya just nice, not too sweet. The service and atmosphere are great - very clean and spacious. I'll try other dishes if I'm around that area.

Today, I'm around this area and decided to try other dishes. I ordered Black Pepper Chicken Chop, Assam Pedas Stingray Rice, and Curry Chicken Rice. The chicken chop has more breadcrumbs than chicken, but it's crispy on the outside and tender inside. The French fries are also nice. The stingray is fresh, but the gravy is too sour for my liking. The curry chicken is tender, but the gravy is too diluted. The coffee is still thick and fragrance.
author: S L

restaurant_name: 壹号擂茶One Kopitiam Eco Botanic
review_text: Very spacious and comfortable space for dining. They're selling typical kopitiam food with leicha as signature dish. Only managed to try their leicha and it's good! Very balanced flavour overall. Will visit again to try other dishes.
author: Long Shien Kiew

restaurant_name: 壹号擂茶One Kopitiam Eco Botanic
review_text:
New kopitiam place at Eco Botanic. Decent food, decent prices. Place is clean but seems to be very empty. The concrete flooring makes it feel like eating in a factory canteen.

Staff are friendly but the operations clear need some tightening. They missed out on one main even though the restaurant was not busy. Staff had to do double takes on orders.

Portions are generous. Will return to try other dishes.
author: Melvin Liew

restaurant_name: 壹号擂茶One Kopitiam Eco Botanic
review_text: I love the abacus seeds and assam stingray! The yellow win chicken is interesting too, though I find the taste pretty strong. Also tried the curry chicken. Still many more food worth to give them a try! My 2nd time here in 2 days
author: Vivian Ng

restaurant_name: 壹号擂茶One Kopitiam Eco Botanic
review_text: We came here for breakfast,  the place is relatively new. We order pan mian and teochew kueh teow soup. Both taste delicious. The menu are comprehensive and we are spoiled for choices.
author: Jason Tan

review_text:
If you're craving Malaysian-style baozi and dim sum but prefer the convenience of enjoying it at home, this shop is a must-try! Their frozen offerings are surprisingly delicious—just steam or heat them up, and it’s like having a **fresh dim sum feast** in your own kitchen.

Highlights:
✔ Fluffy Malaysian Baozi (包子) – The dough is soft and slightly sweet, just like the ones from kopitiams. Fillings are well-seasoned and generous.
✔ Siew Mai (烧卖) – My absolute favorite! Juicy, porky, and with that perfect bouncy texture. Always stock up on these.
✔ Haw Kow (虾饺) – Packed with whole shrimp and a thin, chewy wrapper. Tastes just like yum cha quality.
✔ Black Bean Pork Ribs (豉汁排骨) – Tender ribs with rich, savory black bean sauce. Great with rice!
✔ Braised Chicken Feet (凤爪) – Super flavorful, with that melt-in-your-mouth texture.

The prices are reasonable, especially for the quality, and the shop is strictly pick-and-go - no frills, just good frozen dim sum ready for your steamer. Perfect for busy folks who still want a taste of authentic Malaysian-style breakfast or supper.

Verdict: Highly recommended if you love dim sum but want the convenience of enjoying it at home. Will definitely be back for more!
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: BOD at Eco Botanic is a stylish and modern spot that offers both great food and a relaxed environment. The menu has a mix of local and Modern options, with portions that are generous and well-presented. The drinks selection is refreshing, and desserts are a nice treat after a meal. Staff are welcoming and attentive, creating a pleasant dining experience. The interior is clean and contemporary, making it suitable for families, groups, or casual meetups. Parking is available nearby, and the café is wheelchair accessible with wide entrances and spacious standing arrangements.
author: Brian Wong

review_text: Yummy, super yummy bao. All staffs are friendly and approachable. Always go to this shop to restock my bao.
author: vivian lee

review_text: A lot of variety here, large range of frozen items. Their bao bun is really the best I have ever tried because it's so soft and fluffy! However some buns could use more filling. But I guess the fluffy buns make up for it. The XLB is apparently herbal but no overpowering herbal taste, my kid loves it.
author: E G

review_text: Always goto dimsum shop. Food and quality are as good as restaurant standard. Cheaper in price.
author: Chong Hwee Ng

review_text: Really enjoyed my meal at Yes Yakiniku! The quality of the meat was excellent—tender, juicy, and full of flavor. Portions were generous and everything tasted fresh. The staff were polite and helpful, making the whole experience even better. Cozy atmosphere and great value for money. Highly recommended for yakiniku lovers!
author: Frh Ain

review_text: Since the restaurant just opened only about 1 month, please expect some delay in food preparation due to high demand. I don’t mind waiting as long as the quality served excellent. Thanks! Sedap gilerzzz. Will share with my friends and repeatttt!
author: Yun

review_text: Very impressed with the food and service here. Everything was flavorful and fresh, and the price felt reasonable for the quality. Staff were helpful and friendly too. Would definitely recommend trying it.
author: Syafiqah Suhaimi

review_text: Great place to dine in eating something grilled. the price is reasonable with good portion size. the staffs are trained to explain well to the customers on the how-to.
author: syasya johan

review_text:
Saw this place on my way home from work and decided to give it a go. Place is nice and clean as it’s newly open but you can tell that they really prioritize cleanliness as staff are constantly wiping and tidying up.

Menu is very clear and food came quick. Grilling the meat yourself is fun and I can see this place being a great dating place due to the interactive nature of the food.

Food was delicious and portion size is good. All in all, I had a good experience and will gladly return again. Good to support new places who try something different.
author: Bryan Bong

restaurant_name: XIAO DOU FU MAN川菜小豆福满
review_text: Well, the food quite appetizing and the service crews are quite niceeee. Lovee it, tried the mapo tofu and nong jia xiao chao rou. Taste superb, well definitely coming again
author: ZHEN SHEN YEOH

restaurant_name: XIAO DOU FU MAN川菜小豆福满
review_text: Having been to Chengdu and Chongqing, I was just walking by and glanced at the menu and cudnt resist to try.. And wooww... Yes it is authentic and delicious. Definitely a must try if u are in eco botanic
author: Sa To

restaurant_name: XIAO DOU FU MAN川菜小豆福满
review_text: Food excellent, service very nice! Will come back again 👍
author: TA CUI

restaurant_name: XIAO DOU FU MAN川菜小豆福满
review_text: It was surprisingly delicious! The cream and crispy pork floss in the egg pancakes were incomparable to ordinary quality. The twice-cooked pork was also very fragrant and authentic. The Mapo tofu was delicious, and the seaweed in the pig's trotter soup was also tasty. The dipping sauce was excellent. The snacks tasted just as good as the ones in China, like red bean and crabapple snacks. Just look at the kimchi jar to know how authentic it was!
author: Danni

restaurant_name: XIAO DOU FU MAN川菜小豆福满
review_text: I had the most authentic Sichuan cuisine in Malaysia. The environment was great, bright and clean. I highly recommend the stir-fried pork with Mapo tofu.
author: rosa zhao

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Ba Kut Teh Restaurant
review_text:
I had a great meal at Shun Fa Bak Kut Teh.

The bak kut teh was rich, deeply aromatic, and very well balanced—comforting without being overwhelming. You can really tell they know what they’re doing, and it’s the kind of place that makes you want to come back for the same dish again.

My only small gripe is that they don’t accept credit cards, which can be a bit inconvenient.
That aside, the food alone is more than enough reason to visit. Highly recommended.
author: Changsu Siris Woo

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Ba Kut Teh Restaurant
review_text: actually I don’t put high expectation but it came out quite good for me. Is not like Klang BkT those very dark soup, but it still has its herbs taste. I personally likes their salted vege. Seldom BKT place with aircond. Good that we can eat even is a hot sunny day .
author: Sze Yih Cheo

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Ba Kut Teh Restaurant
review_text: Service was good. Environment is great but the soup is very salty. Few hours after eating we felt very thirsty. Not recommended.
author: David Chan

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Ba Kut Teh Restaurant
review_text:
Tried the bak kut teh here which is as the name says what they are good at.  It came out sizzling hot, the soup broth was herby but not too strong flavour and just the right level of saltiness.  This was the first time I tried authentic bak kut teh as i have tried other versions too and now I know the difference and this was way better.

The place is also got comfortable seating and quite spacious.
author: Wilson Shum

restaurant_name: Shun Fa Ba Kut Teh Restaurant
review_text: There are many Ba Kut Teh around the area, decided to try Shun Fa. The BKT was good with mixing of all the pig organ and others. The soup was just peppery and nice. You have to order first before getting a table. It was crowded during lunch times.
author: Yap Hoe BENG

restaurant_name: 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street @ Eco Botanic
review_text:
Dropped by 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street at Eco Botanic for a late dinner around 9pm+, and I was honestly glad to find that they were still open till 10pm — a lifesaver for late-night cravings. The place focuses on Teochew-style comfort food, offering classics like braised duck, braised pork, and a choice of kway teow or noodles, all done in a very traditional way.

What really stood out was the warmth of the experience. The boss was around that evening and personally checked in on our table a few times, making sure everything was alright. That personal touch made the meal feel even more comforting. The herbal soup base was thick, rich, and aromatic — exactly how a proper herbal broth should taste, deep and satisfying without being overpowering. It paired beautifully with the braised meats.

The chilli sauce was complimentary and added a nice kick to the meal. Overall, it was a genuinely good and authentic Teochew-style dinner, and I was pleasantly surprised to find such a comforting, traditional spot in Eco Botanic. Definitely a place I’d return to when craving old-school flavours.
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street @ Eco Botanic
review_text: Yummy Kway Tiao kia, ordered duck meat too besides the pig skin, intestines etc. Place is spacious and air conditioned. Service is good and fast.
author: Mel Mel

restaurant_name: 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street @ Eco Botanic
review_text: A relatively new shop selling kway chap. I like the herbal soup. Not overly powering yet still having the herbal taste and fragrance. Goes well with the kway chap. Service was prompt and friendly. Nice and clean environment too.
author: Rex Tan

restaurant_name: 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street @ Eco Botanic
review_text:
Comfy place for traditional thin-flat-noodle soup with stewed pork. Creative menu. Price points are on the high side.

Uniqueness: 8
Value: 7
Experience: 8
author: Peng Tang

restaurant_name: 南洋老街粿条仔 Nanyang Old Street @ Eco Botanic
review_text: Wonderful and attentive service. The duck is awesome and the other dishes are all up to par. Good place for Kway Chap otherwise known in Malaysia as Kway teow kia!
author: Winston Benjamin Chua

review_text:
The cold dishes tasted incredibly fresh! They weren't the wilted kind that come from being left out for too long; the vegetables were very crisp, and the seasoning brought out the natural sweetness of the ingredients.

Thumbs up for the owner's skill! It had a home-style flavor, but it was made exceptionally well and tasted delicious.
author: jin Oh (沉默的小鱼)

review_text: It's rare to find authentic Korean cuisine in Johor Bahru. The food was so delicious and satisfying! The side dishes, beef soup rice, and warm noodles were all truly authentic. The service was excellent, the environment was pleasant, and the food was clean and safe to eat. 👍 Highly recommended!
author: xian piao

review_text: The pig stomach soup was absolutely top-notch - I couldn't resist having a second serving! And the steamed fish was fresh and tender. The presentation was on par with hotel. We ordered other dishes too, but we were so busy enjoying them that we forgot to take photos!
author: Jessie Chua

review_text:
We came across this restaurant at Eco Botanic and decided to have our dinner here. It turned out to be a pleasant experience.

The lobster was fresh, tender, and naturally sweet, cooked just right to bring out its flavour. The other dishes were flavourful too, and we were delighted that our kids enjoyed the food as well.

The restaurant has a nice ambience, simple yet cosy, with a welcoming space that suits both family and group gatherings. The staff were friendly and attentive, which added to the overall experience.

Our family truly enjoyed the meal and the setting. It’s a great spot if you’re looking for good food in a relaxed, comfortable environment. We’ll be back again!
author: zhang jiaqi

review_text:
4.5 stars.
Dry Fried Beef Ho Fen tasted good and really hard to find in JB.
Nice fry skill and less oil been used.
Old school wider Kuey Tiao with rice fragrance and been nicely stir fried. Dry but no oily
Beef is really good taste, large slice, tender and juicy.
But whole dish is a bit burnt otherwise 5 star for it
author: Walker. T

review_text: This place is a Gem! A must try especially the  Jellyfish flower, spinach tofu, pork tripe chicken soup, and dongpo pork. Food is really delicious! Except for the rice that was a bit undercooked but did not ruin the whole experience. I recommend this place!
author: Rhea Siangko

review_text: First time tried this restaurant at Eko Botanic area. Serving Chinese dish mainly. Taste is mediocre and no wow effect to me. Price is definitely on the high side. The shrimp paste chicken wing is so small. Yam ring portion is rather small too. Not worth for the price we pay.
author: Xplorer SEA

restaurant_name: 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE
review_text:
One of the best value hot pot spots in Johor!

​I absolutely love the concept here, everyone gets their own individual pot, which is perfect because you can try multiple soup bases without having to share.

​The ingredients are fresh, and the broths we ordered were all savory and flavorful without being overly salty. The restaurant itself is very clean with bright, welcoming lighting, making for a great dining atmosphere.

​To top it off, the staff is friendly and the prices are extremely affordable. This is easily one of the best value-for-money hot pot restaurants in Johor, if not all of Malaysia. Highly recommended and I will definitely be back!
author: britr

restaurant_name: 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE
review_text: 2nd time here, attracted by the unique condiments which lady boss said imported from China. Couldn’t find anywhere else condiments better than here. Service is super good, staff constantly alert of customer needs. Feels home eating there 😍
author: Diana Chin

restaurant_name: 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE
review_text:
We decided to check out 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE, a newly opened spot for dinner, and it turned out to be a pleasant surprise. Unlike the usual big shared pot, here each person gets their own small pot, which I found quite refreshing – no more fighting over soup bases or dipping at the same time.

I went for the mala broth, which packed a nice punch without being too oily, while my missus opted for the Chinese herbal pot, which was fragrant and soothing. Both bases were flavorful and well-prepared. The ingredients were fresh – from the meat slices to the vegetables – and portioned well.

Service deserves a shout-out too. The staff were attentive and quick, making sure we had everything we needed without us having to ask twice. For a new restaurant, they’re already running things smoothly.

Overall, it’s a modern twist on the Chinese hotpot experience, with quality broths, fresh ingredients, and good service. Definitely worth a visit if you’re looking for a comfortable hotpot meal without the hassle of sharing one giant pot.
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE
review_text:
Price range is quite affordable for the portion served. The golden (chicken) soup was nice but a little too salty, while the Mala was a little underwhelming (we didn’t like that it was bland and it had quite a lot of spice bits). However, ingredients were fresh (except the udon & spinach noodle as it had an “old taste”).

Service was great, though they could do a bit more manpower at level two to cut down the wait for customers to be served. Place was clean, spacious, not too noisy to chat, and staff were friendly.

Would come back again to try other soups 👍🏼
author: Faye Tong

restaurant_name: 大吉利涮涮锅 SHABU SHABU & HOT POT HOUSE
review_text: The Chinese girl’s service was awesome. However, another girl mistakenly changed my hotpot soup base, which ruined my meal. I almost ate the spicy milk soup base instead of the caviar spicy soup base. Staff need to be more careful, especially for customers with lactose intolerance. I’m not happy with the experience.
author: Yuki

restaurant_name: HanYuan Daily 韓源 - Eco Botanic
review_text:
Food is ok, staff is very friendly and helpful!

The steamed bread was soft and fluffy, though the amount of Kaya was kinda little, could be more generous with it.

The toasted bread was crunchy on the outside. Had it with peanut butter.

My kids enjoyed the pratas but my daughter said the curry was not spicy enough.

The nonya kuehs were very good! I like the ang ku Kueh skin, it was very QQ bouncy. Though the picture showed The yellow ang ku Kueh was peanut, the filling inside was red bean instead. The Kueh seri muka was ok, rice was soft and nice, not hard like some can be.

It's great that this place opens early! We crossed the border early to avoid the jam so we arrived around 730am.

The place was full house by 830am!
author: Kelvin Goh

restaurant_name: HanYuan Daily 韓源 - Eco Botanic
review_text:
Not sure why the low reviews but I had a great experience at HanYuan Eco Botanic. Food & drinks were served fast - and tasted yummy too! The toast was thick, toasted to perfection and kaya was fragrant. The steamed and panfried buns with homemade kaya was also great (I love the pandan kaya more). The roti jala with curry was also savoury, with the fragrant curry as the star!

Service staff were also attentive and friendly. Ordering via QR code was fuss free. Place was clean, turnover of tables were fast and I would definitely come back again!
author: Faye Tong

restaurant_name: HanYuan Daily 韓源 - Eco Botanic
review_text:
A nice clean atmosphere but there were some ants on the table. The food was only okay and a bit small for the price. Everything was kind of plain with not much taste.

The coconut bun was probably the best thing we ordered. It came nice and toasted with a good flavour. Maybe this place is better for just bread.
author: Kaylee Kat

restaurant_name: HanYuan Daily 韓源 - Eco Botanic
review_text:
The service is consistently excellent, I have been here countless times and it never disappoint.  If you need to work or browse, their Wi-Fi is fast. For me it's their drink menu, there are a lot of variety: from traditional coffee and espresso to creative fruit teas.

They also have an enormous selection of food, including vegetarian choices, finger foods, and desserts. You can try their breads like Kaya toast and fried rice if unsure what to order. If you spend a certain amount, you get a voucher for your next visit. For anyone looking for a quiet, chill spot, this is the place to be. (not sponsored)
author: Lonesome Boss

restaurant_name: HanYuan Daily 韓源 - Eco Botanic
review_text: Hanyuan Daily at Eco Botanic is a lovely café-style eatery serving fresh, wholesome meals and drinks in a cozy setting. The menu offers a good variety, from rice and noodle dishes to light bites and desserts, all presented neatly and reasonably priced. The drinks are refreshing and not overly sweet, which I really appreciated. Staff are attentive and polite, ensuring orders come out promptly even during busy hours. The interior is clean and modern with comfortable seating, suitable for both solo diners and groups. Parking is convenient, and the café is wheelchair accessible with a wide entrance and clear pathways.
author: Brian Wong

review_text:
Good place to have meals, suitable for any group sizes

Portion of vegetables is very generous

Ordered the Japanese Kunbu soup, thought it was a little underseasoned to my taste

Friendly staff
author: Mr Ree

review_text: RM29.9 per individual pot, and they have a fair variety for you to choose from with flexibility in ordering (e.g. if you don’t want vegetables you can replace that dish with another protein).
author: J H

review_text: Giving it a 5 stars because it duplicates those same type of steamboat restaurants we saw in Taipei street. Nothing atas. Nothing fanciful. Just a nice pot of soup of your choice, with a big bowls of mixed veggies (which usually don’t see here) and the generous portion of main course meat. Soup may be bland at first. That’s why u put in the corn, pumpkin, cabbage to make it more savoury. Of course, please don’t compare it to those high end steamboat restaurant. It was never meant to be. Our kind of place! Will definitely come back again!
author: Liwei Chiang

review_text:
Personal pot steamboats are always a little less vibey than sharing pots. Not a very ideal place if you wanna have a more reunion-style dining experience. It’s rm30 per pax per pot, you can choose to share a pot but you have to top up rm5. The menu is pretty large. I’d say go for one pot and add on more sides so you can try more things together! Also because the food in the normal set is not that great haha mainly consists of fishballs meatballs balls ….

Love the sauces though! Not splendid but tasty :)
author: Fangqin Chuah

review_text: Serves only set meals at rm29.90 per person. The set gives a choice of broth, meat selection, vegetable with variety of fishball, noodles or rice, drink & dessert. Sharing option available. Just need to top up rm5.00 per person on top of the set meal price. Staff is courteous and service is quick.
author: Aronica Lee Xavier

review_text: Writing this review as I’m craving for their spicy braised monkfish & fish intestines at 1221am. This dish is not something you see often and I thoroughly enjoyed it. You can tell it’s good with so many locals in their restaurant. We also ordered the flounder sashimi and while it was fresh, probably won’t order it again as it’s on the pricier side.
author: C W

review_text:
Had an amazing dining experience at Madfish Eco Botanic! The food is absolutely delicious and truly value for money. Beef + Octopus Set (RM90) and Chicken + Octopus Set (RM78) — both portions were huge, easily enough for 3 people even though they’re meant for 2.

What makes it even better is that they serve free appetizer and free dessert, which really adds to the overall experience. The restaurant environment is very relaxed, super clean, and perfect for a comfortable meal.

The staff are friendly, attentive, and always ready to help, which made us feel very welcome.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for a satisfying meal at a great price. 👍 Come support them — you won’t regret it!
author: JW RollsRoyce

review_text: Was craving Korean food and saw this place by chance. No regrets. Came in, had the best spicy octopus + slice beef set with my loved ones. The staff were so friendly, helpful and made our dining experience such a wonderful one, we truly appreciate it! :) we definitely will be back and recommend this to others! Thank you for your amazing work! Mashisoyo!
author: Celina Ong

review_text: Ordered octopus chicken set for 2 pax but the portion extremely generous and can easily feed 4. The price was very affordable too. Side dishes have a variety of options and taste really good. Super value for money and super yummy.
author: Terence Low Kien Teck

review_text:
The Sashimi quality is just average, but rest of dishes are not fresh enough and softened texture already.
Staffs were watching TV and talking each other. No pay attention to customer.
It is very simple and nothing special interior but price point is not cheap at all. 2pax with Wooruk sashimi (우럭) costs us RM600 with 2 soju and 1 beer.
author: Joony Lee

review_text:
Qiao Di Kopitiam – Nostalgia Without the Value

IMO, Qiao Di Kopitiam is rather poorly managed and disorganized. They seem overstaffed, yet service is slow and inefficient—something I find quite common in many restaurants in JB.

This is a traditional kopitiam serving classic breakfasts and local kuih, offering a nostalgic vibe. However, it lacks both the polish and service quality to justify its positioning.

What we tried:
1.	Butter Kaya Toast – Crispy and well-toasted; it didn’t turn soggy, which was a plus.
2.	Taro Bolo Bun – Disappointing. The taro paste was too watery, more like jam, and didn’t enhance the bun at all. A thicker paste would work much better.
3.	Bolo Bun with Condensed Milk – Nicely crisp and tasty, but lacked buttery richness. Worse still, it was served with honey instead of condensed milk, yet we were still charged extra.
4.	Roti Prata with Curry – Prata wasn’t crispy, and the curry lacked coconut richness and depth.
5.	Wanton Noodles – One of the better dishes. Flavorful char siew and crispy pork lard added good texture and taste.
6.	Ham & Egg Croissant – Croissant was crispy, but the waiting time was unreasonably long.
7.	Iced Tea, Hot Tea & Iced Hor Kah Sai – These were enjoyable, with reasonably rich flavors.

Overall:
I don’t see the value in returning. The prices are simply too high for what’s offered, especially considering its location in Eco Botanic. Nostalgia alone isn’t enough to make up for inconsistent food quality and poor service.
author: WanderWithWit

review_text: Tried their yam paste polo bun. Not so nice actually. Ordered kampong pork braised noodle. Yikes...full of fats in the pork meat. End up threw away. If you like to eat fats, you can try this dish. You can see from 2nd picture. The kopitiam is over-rated.
author: Jeleona Jel

review_text:
Very disappointed with my dining experience at here.

I clearly requested extra noodles (yellow noodles), but was served rice vermicelli instead, which did not meet my order. Communication with the staff was difficult, as they seemed unable to understand the order properly.

In addition, the food took over 20 minutes to be served, even though the café was not busy at the time. For a simple bowl of laksa, this waiting time was unacceptable.

The food itself was average at best. The only positive point was the drink, which was decent.

Overall, slow service, order mistakes, and poor communication made this a disappointing experience. I would not recommend this place.
author: Chan Yee Sheng

review_text:
Curry noodles don’t taste like curry or laksa. The fried wanton is one of the worse. Has a bad oil taste.

Wanton mee so so as well.
author: Orange

review_text:
Tried several dishes here — the Wanton Noodles were tasty, and the Char Siew was delicious though a little fatty. The Hakka Fried Pork was on the salty side, but the Yam Paste Pineapple Bun was really good.

For drinks, both the Iced Lemon Tea and the “Hor Ka Sai” were excellent — highly recommend the beverages here!
author: Jiaxin Wan

review_text: This Kirean restaurant is on 2nd floor and has very simple entrance with no fancy decoration like others. But don't be fooled by the set up, it served one of the most authentic Korean food in Eco Botanic. The shop is full of Korean when we entered on Christmas Day and this is a good sign that it serve good food. We ordered Ramyeon, japchai glass noodle, soy taste bean tofu soup, fluffy steam egg and grill pork. All the dishes are like home cook and really delicious. And the price is reasonable too. Highly recommend this restaurant if crave for Korean food in this area.
author: Xplorer SEA

review_text:
Entering , I am welcomed by a most courteous young lady (don’t get me wrong), and it hit the spot 🫰

Been to Eco Botanic for past 2+ years and many times to Go K and Hongdae. Both are different concept.

Nice atmosphere, being reminded I’m missing Seoul.
Young ones please come here for dates !

I pop in for lunch at 2pm.

Ordered only pork belly and a soju.
Nicely cooked 👊
(I was worried coz I like to grill my meats)

Amazing value for the food 👍
author: Rick

review_text:
Passed by there few days ago, i was surprised when i was entering the cafe. The outlook looked standard, no deco at the stairs area. But inside of the cafe, it was so beautiful!!!, I just simply fell in love with the deco and ambience of the cafe, very comfortable and relaxing, and the colour combination just made me feel calmed. Now it is close to Xmas, they have some decoration too and great to take some photos. Looked at the menu, they provided main courses and drinks, and some light bites. All looked delicious, but what that attracted me the most was the Kongguksu. I tried twice in korea, and it is hardly to be found in Johor, finally i got one, and the taste was so authentic, love it so much. And the grilled pork gimbap was so flavorful!! very tasty!! Another dish we tried, was the beef stew. It was abit salty, so i didnt like it that much.
The service is good too. The staff and the ladyboss were so friendly. Would definitely revisit to explore more.
author: grassy

review_text:
Dooboo Korean Restaurant looks very unassuming from the outside, but the food is genuinely delicious.

The dishes are not overly salty, and you can really taste the care and thought put into the cooking. It feels like the food is prepared by someone who truly takes their ingredients and customers seriously.

Honestly, everything i tried was really good.

Don’t miss this spot — it’s located upstairs and definitely worth going up to the second floor.
author: HUEY IK LAI

review_text: One of the best “home cook” style Korean food I’ve ever eaten in malaysia. Literally typing this review in the restaurant after a meal voluntarily cos they deserves it. Every single dishes is so flavourful - The cold buckwheat noodle is so chewy, grilled pork(not pork belly) is perfectly marinated , tender and with a bit of sweetness - unlike many other Korean places which meat is tough/ tasteless, the seafood pancake is crispy at the outside and soft in the inside, the sundubu soup has very generous amount of homemade mince tofu with some meat bites! Their tofu is homemade so the texture could be a bit rough but it’s so healthy !  The place also has some compartmented spaces for privacy perfect for 2-4 pax. Ms Park the owner and her staff is so friendly ! We really enjoyed our meal here - simple , reasonably priced, cozy and tasty. Will be back for sure ! Photos might not look as appealing cos we took it after a good meal so some dishes are already finished, we packed away the remaining and left nothing behind 👍🏻
author: Happy Jo

review_text:
Simple street side stall selling home made muah chee. First time seeing this stall located right at the cross street in front of bierhaus.

It’s been sold by a foreign lady as she don’t really understand when I was speaking with her. Probably someone hire her to sell there. Anywhere the muah chee was soft and the peanuts generous. One packet for 5 ringgit seems reasonable.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: Tiz review Is meant for their stall in Permas Jaya on Sunday. Used to be managed by chinese owner. But now leave to foreign lady worker to manage. Hygience is an issue. On 1 Sept 2024, I saw her touching her bare foot while waiting customer. and later served Customer without washing hand, not wearing glove. So disgusting.
author: Rachel

review_text: Their muah Chee is warmy and soft with peanut coating is so satisfying.
author: Lim Yee Weon

review_text: Visited this restaurant recently and had a great experience. The food was tasty, fresh, and well-prepared. Shisha was smooth, flavorful, and lasted long. The staff were friendly and the place had a nice, relaxing atmosphere. Prices are reasonable. Highly recommended for food and shisha lovers.
author: Aran Kumar

review_text: Very nice food & The Shisha Superb
author: Kaviraj Velmurugan

review_text: Very nice shisha& service
author: ALI

restaurant_name: Gather Pizza Eco Botanic - 100% Sourdough Pizza in Johor Bahru & Handmade Pasta
review_text:
its a bakery and cafe downstairs, and a slightly more restaurant style upstairs! but u can buy drinks/food from either side and they’ll bring it to you. the haiwaiian sunshine pizza was reallyy good, soft and fluffy, and i love the variety of toppings on it! its baked in a furnace as shown in my vid :)
truffle chicken was slightly nice smelling at first but tasted pretty normal. we actually ordered a burrata salad as a side at first but they served wrongly and i guess it was a blessing in disguise? bec the broccoli dish tasted REALLY good with the grated cheese on top and mashed potato at the bottom (u can taste it isnt the powdered type but actual mash bec of the small bits). tiramisu was also really rich in flavour and it soaked up the coffee liquor enough to kinda burst in ur mouth. didn’t know the steamed brioche was famous! might come back to try that.

overall, food was really good but if only there was a QR code ordering system! bec we faced some language barriers and my drink order was also mixed up.

also, i’m surprised they didn’t discount us anything and still charged us the original price of broccoli with additional burrata even though we reluctantly accepted it rather than our burrata salad (didn’t want them to waste food and didn’t mind trying a new dish — thought they would give us the burrata free)
author: Rachel Sau

restaurant_name: Gather Pizza Eco Botanic - 100% Sourdough Pizza in Johor Bahru & Handmade Pasta
review_text:
I ordered the Margherita Classic Pizza with cheese, and it was really good—the cheese had a slightly milky taste that made it unique. The drinks were delicious too, and the lamb racks were excellent.

I also asked about whether the meat was halal, and the staff showed me the halal logo on the packaging for the pizza beef, while confirming that the lamb racks are halal as well. That gave me peace of mind. The restaurants is not halal certified because they sell alcoholic drinks.

A special shoutout to Josephine, our waitress—she was very friendly, helpful, and guided us through the halal options clearly. She even gave us a cute Instapix photo to remember the visit.

Overall, a really nice dining experience with tasty food and great service. Keep it up, Josephine!
author: Muhammad Muawiz

restaurant_name: Gather Pizza Eco Botanic - 100% Sourdough Pizza in Johor Bahru & Handmade Pasta
review_text:
A flight of stairs to reach the restaurant, small and cozy.

The four cheese pizza was the best I had in my life, very unique, unlike normal four cheese pizzas, they have caviar, and honey on it! Not your crispy crust type, more chewy, but it really goes well. Brings a new light to what pizzas with cheese alone can be.

The rest that’s not pizza dont buy, pasta was bad, bland, and watery. Fried broccoli was bad, can vomit. Try at your own risk.

Pizza was life changing, but the rest just was disappointing
author: Benjamin Chay

restaurant_name: Gather Pizza Eco Botanic - 100% Sourdough Pizza in Johor Bahru & Handmade Pasta
review_text: Hidden gem alert! The pizza was insanely good – perfection on a plate. Drinks were stunning too! 🔥
author: Lam Ka Wong

restaurant_name: Gather Pizza Eco Botanic - 100% Sourdough Pizza in Johor Bahru & Handmade Pasta
review_text:
I was genuinely looking forward to dining here after all the positive buzz, but unfortunately, the experience fell far below expectations.

The mushroom soup was watery and lacked flavor. The pizza arrived soggy and overly wet. The lamb ribs were undercooked, with very tough tendons that made them difficult to chew, and the sausage was not fully cooked either.

Overall, it was a disappointing experience — definitely hit a landmine (a letdown after the hype). I truly hope the restaurant can improve the food quality and consistency moving forward.
author: Eugene Lau

review_text:
So I decided to drop by Mamu Junction one quiet afternoon, and when I say quiet, I mean library-level quiet. Not many customers around — which I thought would mean lightning-fast service. Plot twist: it didn’t.

Let’s start with the food.
The poori came out looking like it had just won a swimming competition… in oil. Not a total disaster, but definitely a bit more shiny than I prefer my food to be. Taste-wise, still alright — nothing to write home about, but also nothing to dramatically flip a table over.

Then came the drinks. Or more accurately, the waiting for the drinks. For a moment I wondered if they had to harvest the ingredients from a distant mountain or if the blender went on strike. Still not sure why it took longer than expected, especially since there were more fans spinning in the shop than actual customers.

But the real highlight — the unexpected entertainment — was when my eyes casually drifted to one of the workers. And I kid you not… this guy strolls in carrying a bottle of Tiger Beer like he’s auditioning for a beer commercial. In a place that didn’t exactly look like it sells alcohol. To make it funnier, the man wasn’t even working at that moment, so maybe he was just clocking in with “refreshments”? Who knows. I just watched quietly like it was an episode of some local sitcom.

Overall, the place wasn’t terrible, but the vibe was… interesting. Food was okay, service could’ve been faster, and I got a bonus side quest involving a bottle of Tiger Beer. If you’re bored and want some mild afternoon drama with your meal, Mamu Junction might just be the place.
author: Amar Naqiu

review_text:
Possibly the worst mamak in JB. Avoid at all cost.

When my partner and I were seated, none of the staff approached us or provided a menu. We waited for a while before I had to personally call a staff member to ask for one, which already set a poor first impression.

A tall male Indian waiter, wearing an AirPod in one ear, took our order. I clearly stated “roti prata telur” twice to avoid any confusion. However, when the food arrived, I was served nasi goreng ayam telur instead. This was not even close to what I ordered.

This shows a lack of attentiveness and professionalism, especially considering the restaurant was not overly crowded at that time. Wearing an AirPod while taking customers’ orders is also inappropriate and may explain the mistake.

Overall, the service was inattentive and careless. I hope the management can improve staff training, attentiveness, and basic service standards to prevent similar experiences for future customers.
author: Sharul Lyzan

review_text: Cozy area to chill. They have variety of food. Indian, western, thaiand malaysian delights. If miseed shisha in Singapore, you can try the shisha here. Foodwise pretty decent and nice.
author: Rosliza Ramli

review_text:
Passing nearby here.
My 1st visit, up dates bistro mamak restaurant.

Nice and cosy place.
Price average and cheap.
author: Jefry Liew

review_text:
The service was really extremely bad. Highly not recommended to go this restaurant. They dint even on the fan even after we ask the staff to on the fan, and they on the fan after 5minutes of multiple time of asking to on the fan.
Coming to food we order 2 set of half boiled egg but we received 75-85% almost cooked egg for our breakfast.
Coming to how long we waited for the food, I think I might go n get the egg from chicken farm rather ordering food over this restaurant.
Really very terrible service.
HIGHLY NOT RECOMMENDED TO THIS RESTAURANT, I WOULD RATE 0 OUT OF 10.
author: Neshvik

review_text:
We decided to chill at The Bierhaus @ Eco Botanic, a cozy spot known for its beers, cocktails, and Western dishes. The vibe was warm and inviting.. dim lights, and that relaxed pub atmosphere that makes you want to stay longer and order another drink.

We started with some drinks — their beer and cocktails were refreshing and nicely balanced. Perfect for a casual night out with friends or even a relaxed dinner date.

For food, we ordered oysters, pork chop, and chicken. The oysters were fresh, and the dishes overall were well-prepared. But the real highlight? The pork chop. It was juicy, flavorful, and cooked just right definitely the star of the night.

The only downside was the waiting time. The chicken took more than 30 minutes to arrive, which felt quite long, especially when you’re already hungry. It would have been a perfect experience if the food came out all together.

On the bright side, the staff were very friendly and attentive. They checked in on us and served with a smile, which made the wait more bearable. The cozy ambiance and good service definitely add points to the overall experience.

✨ Overall rating: 4/5
Great food (especially the pork chop), good drinks, cozy atmosphere — just be prepared for a bit of a wait during peak hours.

If you’re around Eco Botanic and craving beer with good Western food, this place is worth trying 🍻
author: Caren Hao

review_text: Attentive and super friendly staffs. Their food is delicious! Our go to order; spinach and the curry chicken wings *chefs kiss*. Indoor and outdoor dining available. Good place to gather to watch soccer games.Clean washroom and adorable pool table.There’s a lot of food and drinks options.We came here several times,they never fail us till today.Thank you Bierhaus#ecobotanic for always giving us the best experience,special thanks to Dhandhan and her team♥️♥️♥️
author: Espyi Jeesev

review_text:
Weekday lunch promotion 15.90, with free drinks (free flow mushroom soup, coffee, tea, ice lemon tea). With this price the food/ environment considered appropriate cp value. Burger taste good.
Is.not crowded. The staffs are friendly.
author: Ong NN

review_text:
Ribs was good, marinated very well and super flavourful. The schnitzel and fries was deep fried really well too which was nice.

Hated the mash potatoes though, could be the driest mash potatoes I’ve ever had, it tasted like mashed cardboard 😂

Looking through the reviews, it seems like the lunch menu would be more attractive. Food was so-so for the price charged, 200RM for 3 dish + 3 drinks. Smoking was also an issue for us, nobody wants to inhale second-hand smoke 👍
author: dolce bibobi

review_text: I have dined in a few outlets; this is my first time here. The atmosphere is chill and cosy. Nice music. Kids are enjoying their pizza, spaghetti, and fries. Overall, the food is nice. Service is good, too! 😋🍕🍝🍟 #Restaurant #Family #Dinner #GoodFood #ChillVibes
author: jerry cheah

review_text:
Stopped by the Coffee Bean at Eco Botani after lunch on a Saturday and was surprised by how quiet it was. The space was clean, cool, and had a relaxed vibe—perfect for a mid-day break.

Ordered a coffee and just sat there for a while enjoying the peace. There were only a few other customers, so no crowd, no rush—just a calm space with background music and the occasional sound of the espresso machine. Sometimes that’s all you need to reset for the rest of the day.

It’s not a huge outlet, but there were enough seats both indoors and outside. Definitely one of those places I’d return to when I need some time to myself or to get a bit of work done with a warm cup in hand.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text:
Come here few times a month.
So far service received is good. No rude services so far.
Ice chocolate is still the best.
Atmosphere is cozy when there’s no much crowd.
author: Vivian Eng

review_text:
The food was good😋
So in love with their carrot cakes!😍
The staff so attentive! Highly recommended! 👍🏻
author: norwanis mohd nor

review_text: Excellent service! All the staff are kind, friendly, and approachable. The environment is very pleasant, and the place is clean and well-maintained. Definitely a lovely spot to enjoy a cup of coffee! ☕😊
author: Choun 1406

review_text: Congratulations to CBTL Eco Botanic for having staff who are good, friendly, and customer-oriented. All questions are answered clearly and patiently. CBTL Eco Botanic Iskandar Puteri is excellent because many of the staff are locals who understand customers’ needs. The baristas are also experienced and make delicious drinks. ☕😊
author: leo jaszy

review_text:
One of my go-to spots for food in this area. All the fried rice options are great and full of spices. The spring rolls are also tasty, especially when paired with sambal kicap.

They use takeaway-style packaging for all orders, whether you dine in or not. The value sets are quite affordable, especially considering the location.

Food is usually served within 10–15 minutes. The vibes are nice and comfortable. They’re currently doing some renovations, but there’s still a seating area available.
author: Selvinia Nofy

review_text: Chow chow just had a facelift and I love the vibe! I tried their Curry Fried Rice with Chicken 65. It’s super tasty, and the mint raita really hits the spot. I couldn’t even finish the combo, and the friendly cashier kindly gave me a takeaway bag at no charge. I had their chicken 65 for two days in a row!
author: Jade

review_text:
===02/20 update===
Since the owner is very entitled, I think I should also leave my feedback here.

First, I’m still not sure whether the owner genuinely doesn’t understand or is just pretending not to understand.

We are not upset because you didn’t give us small change. We are upset because you accused us of using counterfeit money, that actually came from your own register 😅 That part seems to be conveniently forgotten.

And yes, I came with my wife, so it’s completely reasonable that she leaves her own review too. Apparently, that also needs clarification.

Anyway, I’ll just let the public judge the owner of this place. Anyone can scroll through the other negative reviews and see the pattern. Instead of reflecting or taking responsibility, the owner prefers to blame disappointed customers. Interesting management strategy 🤔
================

On 17 February 2026 at 19:34, I ate at this place. The total bill was RM47.50, and I paid RM100.50. They gave me RM53.00 in change: one RM50 note and three RM1 notes.

Later, I realized I needed smaller banknotes to pay for a taxi. My wife asked an older Chinese lady there if she could exchange the RM50 note for smaller notes. However, the lady accused us of having a counterfeit RM50 note and refused my wife’s request.

After we arrived at our hotel, I realized that the RM50 note actually came from them as part of our change.

It was very rude and strange behavior. Their staff gave us the RM50 note as change, and then she accused us of using counterfeit money.

Foreign tourists, please be careful when eating here.
author: Agus Lesmana

review_text: I love how good the service is. During my 1st visit, I ask some recommendation from the cashier and she really well knowledge with her product. And the recomendation that I received was good ! The mala fried rice was incredible and the fried chicken was also amazing. Surely will comeback. Reasonable price. The only thing is when it comes to lunch time it was pack since there is quite a few seats available. However, overall satisfied my craving of hot food. 😊 Please open more branch in Johor area.
author: Cik Lynnto

review_text: Good value fried rice and fried mee. Freshly made, hot and with wok hei! 👍
author: YK (Dimsumguy9)

review_text:
Probably one of the best Nasi Lemak and Asam laksa I’ve tried.
The Nasi Lemak has a very traditional sambal taste to it while the coconut rice has just the right balance of fragrance.
Asam laksa, comparable to the ones I’ve tried in Penang those days. Very generous on the fish as well. The Fried kuay Teow is also fragrant with wok hey like the Penang style unlike the sweet ones here.
Comfortable simple setup and no fuss service. Will surely recommend my friends and family to try
author: Alvin Chuang

review_text:
Came by on a weekend and it was not crowded. The place was spacious. Looks wheelchair friendly (handicap parking with ramp) but be mindful there is a step to the restaurant.

Food seems below average. The coffee was great and strong, which stood out. The bolo bun was disappointing. It was not crispy or buttery and felt more like a normal bun with butter. The crust was soggy.

The traditional breakfast was abit below average. Soft boiled eggs were fine, and the peanut butter toast was very standard. Thick bread with a thin spread of peanut butter though I expected a bit more peanutbutter. There wasnt any butter as well, just the peanut spread so kind of disappointing.

The char kuey teow was tasty and flavourful though.

Overall, the food was hit or miss. I am open to returning to try other items, but it did not leave a lasting impression.
author: Ellynn O

review_text: Dropped by for lunch and ordered the Nasi Lemak with Curry Chicken set that came with a drink of choice. The nasi was fluffy and fragrant with coconut and the papadam and ikan billis were crispy. I liked that the chicken curry had a good balance of richness and spice, and the meat was tender. Wished that the sambal was a tad spicer than sweet. The kopi siu dai waa thick and rich, and had just a nice sweetness to it.
author: Jessica Chew

review_text: The laksa was really yummy, and the portion is big. Presentation of the food looks really nice, and the service is friendly and fast. However, the chinese tea is a bit on the watery side, and the food doesnt come around the same time if youre eating with others. Other than that, the ambience of the restaurant is chill, and overall a nice place to eat and hang.
author: Hyan Tang

review_text:
The food portion is super small and is not to expectation .

Nasi lemak but the portion size is like a phone size only

The shredded chicken keuy teow is very oily, some more it’s form the kids menu… why so oily?

And the toast! Was a total disappointment!! Ordered the hainanese kaya butter toast, but no butter at all!!

Never visiting this shop again!
author: Lois Lim

review_text:
Not as hot as compared to other lala hotpot shop.
Ingredients are quite special. Thumbs up for the soup base too. Worth a visit if u are around the area.
author: Lim Kenz

review_text: The lala hotpot was really good! Freshly cooked at our table. The meats and fish etc, all other food ingredients weren't that "WOW though. But we really love the soup!! Soup was refillable too! I guess I will be back for the lala soup but not really the add ons to the pot! Oh!! But the chicken wings were very yummy!! We love that!!
author: Rebecca Tan

review_text:
Drove past this restaurant many times and finally got to try them out yesterday for dinner. We had the lala hotpot and added some other dishes like pork belly and some vegetables.

The broth was good as the lala served was fresh. We added some Chinese wine which patrons could readily used placed on the condiments table.

Service was very friendly and forthcoming which we appreciated. The price was reasonable.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text:
This is my first time trying out lala hotpot … and OMG this is now one of my fav food! 🤩

The lala hotpot is really good - cooked over charcoal giving it that X-factor yummines 😋 the soup is 👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ nice balance of flavour, not overpowering not too bland … very yummy

The pork belly is nice & fresh - not too thinly sliced & not too much belly fat 😁
The vegetables are fresh & decent size portion too.
The only thing I didn’t quite fancy is the fish paste - the flavour is ok but don’t really enjoy the texture. Will try the shrimp paste next time.

The service is pretty good too - attentive but do note that quite a number of the workers are foreigners, so their English & Chinese are not great.

And I love the ‘hanging tissues’! And they also provide free snacks.
Highly recommended, will definitely be back again & again & again ….
author: WPin P

review_text:
Good fresh lala.
Soup is sweet , yet not thirsty after drinking it.
Service is good.
Price a little high I feel and portion a bit small
author: Tony Too

review_text:
Hidden gem in Eco Botanic! 🍝🥩
Fatboi is a nice Western restaurant located on the 2nd floor, next to Bierhaus. Cozy vibes and surprisingly good food.

We tried the Italian Spaghetti Marinara with fish, signature pork chop, grilled chicken, and chicken cheese chop — all were delicious. The mushroom soup is a must-try too (we had two, that says a lot 😄).

No GST or service charge, and prices are very reasonable and affordable for the quality.

Definitely worth a visit if you’re around Eco Botanic. 👍✨
author: Steven YCS

review_text:
Surprise with the effort from boss and crew for simple birthday celebration, taste of the food and drinks also surprising us with reasonable price.
100% recommended.
author: Chloe Low

review_text:
Took dinner at Fat boi restaurant with friends, the spaghetti grilled chicken taste good but the portion was very less couldn’t satisfy my appetite which was disappointing.
Atmosphere was great, felt more like bar type restaurant.
Service would be 4 star had to wait a long time for the meal to arrive.
Moreover the price is definitely not worth for the portion we paid.
In my opinion, the restaurant was too overrated and maybe just a one time experience for me.
author: Darrchana

review_text:
Had a great experience here! The Chef/Waiter was so kind and servant hearted!

The Restaurant was noisy as there was drilling but he was still very patient and met our each and everyone of our needs!

And the Food matches the Service too! Amazing! The waiting time is reasonable as it was made to order. The wings took longer than usual but when I tasted it I was short of words and it was AMAZING...!

All in love this place and definitely deserves more recognition.
author: Tran Minh Quang

review_text:
Ordered the striploin steak, black Angus ribeye, pork ribs, crayfish pasta, salad and mushroom soup. Soup was great, very flavourful and filled w mushroom bits. Striploin was the best choice for its juicy and soft texture. The black Angus was a let down, priced at RM149 as compared to striploin at RM47, the latter tasted much better. Pasta wasn't that great, lacked flavour to it, was just cream.
Ambience was alright, we went at 130pm so it wasn't crowded. But I could see why diners will feel noisy if it's crowded, place is quite echoy. Only the chef was able to explain the dishes to us, other server there couldn't say anything when we asked simple questions.
author: Jasmine Chye

restaurant_name: Sushi Issin • Eco Botanic • 一心寿司
review_text:
Clean, relaxing and beautiful restaurant, serving very fresh sashimi (any fresher it will be swimming) and reasonably priced sake. Went to another restaurant at Iskandar Puteri and the sake was more than double in price!
Service was personable and warm, the staff gladly gave us an extra bowl of salmon miso soup (this is the free ubiquitous soup that accompanies every Japanese dish. This restaurant actually puts tender loving care into making it ultra delicious, using salmon bones and a pressure cooker to get out all of the sweetness and goodness. Oh and this place is really value for money. We had an extra plate of sashimi, one bottle of sake, 2 dons, 1 salmon special roll, for only RM468.
author: Dr Wee Lyn Teh

restaurant_name: Sushi Issin • Eco Botanic • 一心寿司
review_text: Monday, 6pm the air-conditioned restaurant was clean and peaceful. Overall, the food was good and we enjoyed every dish we ordered. The katsudon portion was generous, with a pork cutlet that was crispy on the outside and juicy inside. The young waiter was polite and friendly. Our only comment is that the wall-side seating is a bit too high and not very ergonomic for adults. The total bill includes a 10% service charge.
author: Ong NN

restaurant_name: Sushi Issin • Eco Botanic • 一心寿司
review_text:
* delicious food. One of the better jap food around iskandar area.
* we came around 2:30pm food, the only table. Food were served relatively fast as we were the only table. Shortly another 2 table of guests joined.
* one of the better thick pork ramen in this area of town. Thick and tasty. Big portion enough to fill a big adult.
* the grill fish head was nice, tender on in the inside and crunchy on the outside. Salt level just nice.
* the maki were nice.
* definitely would return again to try out others. My children love the dishes here. Keep up the good work
author: Lawrence Siow

restaurant_name: Sushi Issin • Eco Botanic • 一心寿司
review_text:
Was disappointed as had high expectations after seeing the good reviews.

Service was meh. Food was soso, not quite value for money either.
- aburi set was disappointing.
- garlic fried rice was qt nice cos of the fragrant garlic but a tad too salty
- the taco looked promising and was reccomended. Totally not worth the money.
author: J T

restaurant_name: Sushi Issin • Eco Botanic • 一心寿司
review_text: Came at 2pm on a Sunday, solid solid choice of Japanese food. There wasn't a lumch crowd as it was quite late, so the whole restaurant was quiet. Service was prompt. Food VERY decent! I think in comparison with Warakuya Japanese Garden, this is definitely a more affordable option and the taste is VERY comparable to that, if not better! 10/10 will revisit for Japanese food craving!
author: Gbmy Pqie

review_text:
Very nice food… and good service!
Seafood noodle is the best, got wokhey in the soup, and jjajang myeong taste is just nice and not like other restaurants if eat too much will feeling greasy.
author: Eliane Tan

review_text: I ate Jjajangmyeon here the portion was so big, really appreciated that! The side dishes were nice too, but the Danmuji was a bit lacking in crunchiness, and the kimchi didn’t seem very fresh. The toilet was a bit dirty, and the dustbin didn’t have a plastic liner. overall, it’s worth the price !! Thanks to the owner of this shop with such generous portion , will come back again !
author: Melissa ong

review_text: Good food and very affordable! Good value for money set meals available. Recommend
author: irene

review_text:
the vinegar pork was so tasty 😭😭😭
meat hotplate was great too
noodle portions were huge
author: celine yee

review_text: The kimchi is very nice and crispy! Loved the noodles, so yummy and the soup is very mouth watering! The flavours are not too strong. Furthermore the portion is very big. Super satisfying. Will come again and recommend to others.
author: Siew Chiao Wong

review_text:
This Japanese restaurant exceeded my expectations. The sushi was fresh and beautifully presented, especially the spicy tuna roll. The ramen broth was rich and flavorful. The staff were welcoming and attentive, and the atmosphere was cozy and relaxing. Great value for the quality. I’ll definitely return!”

Naing Naing provided excellent service. Very friendly, attentive, and professional. She made our dining experience enjoyable. Highly recommend!

We had a wonderful experience thanks to Naing Naing. She was very welcoming, polite, and attentive throughout our meal. She checked on us regularly and made sure everything was perfect. Her great service really enhanced our visit. Thank you!
Naing Naing gave us outstanding service! She was kind, patient, and always smiling. She made us feel comfortable and well taken care of. We truly appreciate her hospitality.

The sushi was fresh and delicious. The sashimi was high quality, the tempura was crispy, and the kushiyaki and yakimono were perfectly grilled. Everything tasted amazing!

We had a wonderful meal. The sushi and sashimi were very fresh and beautifully prepared. The tempura was light and crispy, not oily at all. The kushiyaki and yakimono were flavorful and grilled just right. Highly recommended for authentic Japanese food!

Excellent Japanese cuisine! The sushi was fresh and full of flavor, and the sashimi melted in the mouth. The tempura was perfectly crispy and light. The kushiyaki and yakimono were grilled beautifully with great seasoning. Every dish was well prepared and delicious. We will definitely come back!
author: Angela Chia

review_text:
We just dined at Niki Japanese Dining and had a very enjoyable experience overall.

The sashimi was fresh and well-prepared, and we also enjoyed the maki, tempura, and grilled squid — all done nicely with good flavour and texture. The only dish that could be improved was the shishamo, which tasted a bit plain and lacked the distinct grilled flavour I was expecting.

Service was forthcoming and attentive, and the ambience was comfortable, making it a pleasant place to relax and enjoy a meal.

Overall, a satisfying Japanese dining spot in JB.
author: Tony Tan

review_text: Reasonable price Japanese restaurant in JB. Cozy renovation in restaurant. First come saw XHS recommend. All their food is good. Fresh seafood available in grill raw or cooked. Nice grilled unagi. Their wasabi doesn’t choke your nose. Another must try grilled scallop. The scallop comes with or without cheese can choose. Add in shiitake mushrooms when grilled is add point for this dishes. Good to re visit again.
author: Anique Lim

review_text:
Loved this Japanese restaurant! The place feels really classy and comfortable the moment you walk in.

The food was amazing — super fresh, nicely presented, and everything tasted really clean and flavourful. Honestly one of the better Japanese meals I’ve had in a while. Their assorted ice cream is a must! 😍

Service was great too. The staff were friendly and attentive without being intrusive, which made the whole dining experience really pleasant 👍🏻

Overall, such a good place to enjoy quality Japanese food. Totally worth a visit! 🍣✨
author: EMILY LEONG YUNG XING

review_text:
This Japanese restaurant that just opened few months ago in Eco Botanic is really perfect! The interior and exterior design is very classy, spacious, modern, and comfortable. 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

The dishes are really delicious too, the salmon and eel are both very fresh, tender, and juicy. The kushiyaki is reasonably priced and tastes great as well. The matcha mochi and ice cream are beautifully presented.

It’s suitable for family gatherings, meals together, reunion dinners, and birthday celebrations. Will definitely visit again.
author: slbxss

review_text:
Food is good. We ordered the cockles kway teow (chicken), mee rebus, toast and coffee. The mee rebus was a little too sweet for our liking but the kway teow was on point. Coffee was good too. The food came pretty fast so we didn’t have to wait long, but we had to ask the waiter to be seated because even after standing in line for 5 mins, no one acknowledged us. There was a vacant seat all these while so we just asked to sit.

Will still give 5 stars since the food was good and it was served quickly.
author: TW

review_text:
Nicely and strategically located among lots of dining cafes in the same area/street. Eventually, this is one of few Halal certified cafes around there. Place serves mostly Hainanese dishes with mixture of Western dishes but with the Asian way of preparation.

Atmosphere was busy but ample seatings available. Place can fit around 40pax at a time. Seatings was organized but can be too close to next table when there’s a crowd. Ambience is sort of cozy for an average local cafe. Decorated with posters of the historical original first Hua Mui JB restaurant building sketch. Nice simple decoration with running video TV screen of historic events and signature dishes.

Service is excellent. Attentive, professional and courteous. Workers is truly Malaysian, had a Malay Guy taking our order, an Indian lady served us. Drink maker and cashier are Chinese. They all Malaysian, just like the good local Malaysian food.

Food quality and taste is pretty good, served hot and portion do commensurate with the price. Overall the place is worth a visit or as a regular place for good local Hainanese dishes.
author: Azaharin

review_text:
Hua Mui is my favorite kopitiam in town. The food is always tasty, no matter what you choose, and they have plenty of options. I’ve tried several dishes, including Mongolian chicken, spicy sambal chicken, fried carrot cake, tom yum, and others, and I’ve never been disappointed. They also offer lunch packages that include food, a drink, and pudding, which is a nice deal.

The staff are helpful and friendly. Parking can be a bit challenging during lunch since spaces are limited and the area has many restaurants, but if you visit in the morning or evening, it’s usually manageable to find a spot nearby.
author: Selvinia Nofy

review_text:
Dining at HuaMin Eco is always a great experience. The moment you step in, you’ll notice how lively and vibrant the atmosphere is. The restaurant is often packed with people coming and going, which speaks volumes about its popularity.

Despite the crowd, the service is impressively fast and efficient. The team handles everything with a smile, making the place feel friendly and welcoming. It’s the kind of environment where you can relax, eat, and just enjoy the moment.

When it comes to food, HuaMin Eco delivers on taste. Every dish I tried was flavorful and satisfying. The portions could be a little bigger, but the quality makes up for it. A special mention goes to the mashed potato,  while a bit thick in texture, the flavor was spot on.

The space itself is cozy but slightly small, so expect it to feel bustling during peak hours. But that energy is also what makes it such a fun spot to dine.

✨ Overall, HuaMin Eco stands out as one of those places where good food, fast service, and friendly vibes come together perfectly. Whether you’re here for a quick meal or to chill with friends, this is a spot in Eco you don’t want to miss!
author: Dhania Ellsha bt Abdullah

review_text:
Reach there when they just opened
Food portion is big and taste good
Food comes after a short wait.
Drink seems to be on the sweet side even if less sugar.

The hainanese noodle was well cooked and satisfying.
The mee Siam was relatively good and the bread is ok.

Downside is both toilets are down during the visits.
author: ethan chew

review_text:
This place was recommended by a friend, and I didn’t expect my family elders to enjoy it so much. There’s a wide variety of food choices, and every dish we tried was delicious with generous portions. If you have a smaller appetite, two people can easily share one dish. The prices are very reasonable as well.

The chicken breast is marinated in-house, so it’s tender and not dry at all. I highly recommend the fish head bee hoon, the soup is very flavorful, and they’re generous with the fish head portions. It does get busier during lunch hours, but the food is served quickly.
author: yu wen

review_text: This restaurant is a good place in the Eco Botanic area. They serve breakfast as well as dinner dishes, and the food is really delicious with a strong hometown taste! The ingredients are specially brought in from Segamat. Other dishes are also very good and worth trying. Prices are affordable, portions are generous, and the boss lady is very friendly and patiently explains the dishes.
author: slbxss
