review_text: This is my second visit to this place, and it's all because the owner made a great impression on me during my first visit. She was extremely polite and patient, taking the time to recommend their specialties. When we mentioned our preference for less oil and salt, she went out of her way to accommodate our request. What really stood out was her personalized service - while we were enjoying our meal, she checked in on us to ensure everything was to our liking. It's rare to find service like this, and I'd definitely visit again if I'm in the Eko Botanic area.
author: S L

review_text: Their food is unique compared to the other restaurants as their food taste is Jementah-based. Do not be fooled by the restaurant name as their speciality is noodles and Chinese stir-fried food. The portion is generous and the food is delicious. They serve breakfast, lunch and dinner but their last call is 8.30pm. They have some dishes like fried pork belly, lala soup, fish head soup, etc. I like their fried noodles also.
author: L MK

review_text:
Chanced upon this place while I'm looking for bf, staff was recommending us the hor fun, etc.
We ordered the hor fun, mee siam, curry Chicken etc. Very special taste for hor fun. Crispy and soft.. Mee goreng is good too, spicy.

restaurant_name: Da Cheng Lok Lok Eco Botanic
review_text:
bit of a miss. the sticks r v affordable at 1.10myr/stick. also got premium stuff lah. but flavour to me not there. we chose not to have chilli when the staff asked. but then like macam no spices no sauces at all on our sticks sia only fried plain.

the mantou inside also got filling which im not a fan of, thought they got offer plain mantou. also dont have condensed milk.

i like their sweet thai chilli sauce and sour spicy chilli sauce!

drinks r also pricier than the 7/11 next door which doesnt really makes sense 😅

maybe next time ill choose to add spice then might be tastier. will also want to try their lu rou fan and their sambal stingray/sotong here.
author: chu xuan

restaurant_name: Da Cheng Lok Lok Eco Botanic
review_text: Pretty good lok lok at a aircon environment. Their seafood sauce is nice and chilli is spicy!  Will be good if they can increase their beer selections.
author: tay dickson

restaurant_name: Da Cheng Lok Lok Eco Botanic
review_text:
The lok lok items tasted quite good.  a good variety of items to choose from at very affordable prices.
I love the satays fm one of the carts outside the shop. Ordered the chicken and beef satays, the marination of the meat and the quality of the meat  is good. Maybe the peanut sauce can improve further.
We also ordered the stingray and it was v v good. The stingray was v flavourful and not grilled till too dry as the flesh was still juicy. They also added ladies finger over the fish making the dish more balanced. Ordered the sugarcane drink fm the shop and it was very well with the food we ordered.
We sat outside the shop at the carpark and surprisingly it was quite breezy. Quite a nice outside dining experience.
author: Eric Toh

restaurant_name: Da Cheng Lok Lok Eco Botanic

restaurant_name: wán Masak Family Cafe @ Eco Botanic
review_text: Came around 5pm and we were the only ones. Perfect for my little one to explore the area freely. Would be great if there were more balls at the ball pit though. Carousel needs staff to activate upon request. Food is okay. I asked the staff if the kids meal braised pork rice and kids meal version, if there's any difference but she couldn't really understand or advise me. author: C W

restaurant_name: 王奶奶面粉粿 Grandma Ong Eco Botanic
review_text:
Dined in recently and had a very disappointing and concerning experience.

During the meal, I discovered a foreign object in my food, which was only noticed after consumption had begun. I immediately informed the staff, and after clarification, the object was confirmed to be plastic. This was particularly concerning as the restaurant operates an open kitchen.

At the time, there were many families and children dining in the restaurant, which further deepen my concern regarding food safety and handling practices.

While the staff attended to the matter, the presence of a foreign object in a dine-in meal raises serious questions about hygiene, quality control, and food preparation standards.

I am sharing this experience to encourage greater attention to food safety and to allow other diners to make informed decisions.
author: See Huey Leong

restaurant_name: 王奶奶面粉粿 Grandma Ong Eco Botanic
review_text:
I made my first visit to this stall to try their “Ban Mian”- the flat, short hand-pulled noodles that the hawker scene does so well. I went for the dry version noodles make from spinach and added a helping of vegetables.
The Ban Mian had a satisfying chew, true to its hand-pulled texture. Dry style with spinach added a welcome greens note and a bit of earthiness. The taste is mild, but you can kick it up a notch with chili if you like spicy.
A touch on the salty side, which isn’t unusual for stalls that focus on punchy flavors. If you’re pairing the dry version with a spoonful of soup, expect that saline lift. There’s a noticeable MSG presence after the em, giving the overall taste a distinct, savory finish.
MYR 16.79 for the noodle dish is on the higher side for local standards. Given the portion and the texture of the noodles, it leans towards premium territory in this market.
If you’re not chasing a bargain, this is a decent try for first-timers curious about the Ban Mian texture and the dry with greens.
If you’re sensitive to saltiness or MSG, you might want to pace your intake or opt for the lighter broth if available.

review_text: The laksa was awesome, and the portion is big enough for me. Order with set, comes with fish cake and drink. Will come back for another dish, looking forward to the volcano noodles

There's side dishes which are nice

Service,  they were prompt. However I see the servers are very busy as there's no Trays or trolley for them and so they have to take the dishes or drinks one by one.
author: 是无名

review_text: This mala tang place is really good. The prices are reasonable and the food, ingredients, and overall setup are clean, neat, and hygienic. The environment is comfortable as well. The mala tang, tonkotsu soup, and mala dry hotpot are all quite tasty. Definitely worth trying! 🌶️
author: slbxss

review_text:
Dropped by 爱情麻辣烫 Aiqing Malatang (Eco Botanic) for lunch and it was a comforting, fuss-free meal. The setup is clean and casual, and the ordering process is straightforward — pick your ingredients, choose your soup base, and let them do the rest.

The broth was fragrant and nicely spiced without being overwhelming, making it easy to enjoy even if you’re not a hardcore spicy-food lover. Ingredients were fresh, portions were reasonable, and everything came together as a satisfying bowl of malatang. It’s the kind of place you’d come back to when you want something warm, customizable, and filling without overthinking it.

A solid lunch option in Eco Botanic, especially if you’re craving something hearty and a little bit numbing-spicy.
author: Crumpled Nomad

review_text: The bone broth is good. Myself cant take mala. Quite a lot varieties to pick ur liking eg. different types meatball, mushrooms, veges, noodles, etc. Resto is clean.

review_text: such a good place for rich mala! my friends love it and i love it too
author: aly !

review_text: Very nice Malatang. A lot of selection and choices.
author: メルトBlue

review_text: The skewers are delicious and the beauty service is very good😋❤️
author: yunqian yek

review_text: This restaurant offers a wonderful dining experience with its warm and inviting ambience. The food is absolutely delicious, with flavors that feel both authentic and satisfying. Prices are reasonable, making it a great choice for casual outings or family meals. The service is impressively fast, ensuring you don’t have to wait long to enjoy your meal. so everyone can find something they love. Highly recommended!
author: EE LONG Yeo

review_text: Delicious. We are regular customers here. They’re always very generous with their banchan serving more than 10 types of them and you can ask for refill for those that you like. The staff and lady boss here always make you feel welcomed and are very helpful and friendly. We love their kimchi stew and kalguksu. Tried the cold noodles today and it’s also good. If you’re nearby come and support this family friendly establishment!
author: E L

review_text: We had a fantastic time at Ssam! Not only was the food delicious, the service was great! They were very generous with the side dishes and their boiled pork, and pancakes were nice. They had a good variety of pancakes so if you’re looking for pancakes other than kimchi and seafood pancakes, this is a good place to visit. Not to mention that the lady boss and staff were really friendly. It was a very pleasant dinner experience for us. Will definitely be back again! :)
author: Joey Teo

review_text:
SSAM Korean Food! Family, today we checked out SSAM Korean Food in Johor Bahru, Malaysia! 😋 The owner warmly welcomed us as soon as we entered.

After ordering, the side dishes arrived immediately. The selection was amazing, and each one was incredibly flavorful. My favorites were the mashed potatoes and pumpkin. The kimchi soup was also excellent—tangy, spicy, and refreshing, a truly comforting sip. And let's not forget the potato pancakes; they were fried to a golden brown and crispy perfection, with an amazing texture.

Their grilled meat is absolutely superb! The meat was tender and juicy, sizzling on the grill, releasing an irresistible aroma. Paired with their special sauce, every bite was incredibly satisfying.

I highly recommend everyone try it and experience authentic Korean cuisine! 👏
author: zhonghe sun

review_text: Banchan was great variety and taste. Chives pancake was served hot. Beef soup was good. The BBQ meat was cooked in the kitchen. We ordered BBQ beef and jowl, both too fatty and don’t look fresh. So I was hugely disappointed with the meat. Probably should have ordered their boiled pork, that may be their specialty.
author: D R Taylor

review_text: The black truffle chasiu bun was very fresh, the bun itself was soft, and the filling was generous. The truffle flavor wasn't overpowering, and it paired perfectly with the char siu. Their seasalt coffee was also unique, with just the right amount of sweetness. If you want to try coffee made from fresh beans, you can choose their Arabica coffee. They sell more than just buns; they also have dim sum, rice noodle rolls, noodles, rice dishes, and soups. Most importantly, the prices are very reasonable, making it suitable for families, seniors, and children. The environment is comfortable, the prices are affordable, and the service is excellent.
author: Chai Jia Xin

review_text:
The design of the place feels like olden Hong Kong. The noodles are great and dishes are great
The lychee balls are decent.

As we sat near the counter, the staff keep looking at us. Abit uncomfortable tbh.
author: Leo Quah

review_text: Deco is nostalgic HK cafe style. We came here as didn’t want to queue for another cafe. Was pleasantly surprise. The lava custard bun was so good that we bought the frozen pack home. The steam rice roll with prawns was yummy. The chef special pork chop noodle was on point with nice fragrance of the pork lard. Service was attentive. The coffee is ok.

Saw the reviews of the wanton mee and it did NOT dissapoint!

The flavour of the pork lard mmmmm and the egg noodles were really authentic, personally preferred the white style over the sauces black dark one but both were good!

Top wanton mee tier
Cheong fan & coffee Yuanyang tasted good too!

Highly recommend if you are craving some wanton mee
author: N Y

review_text: They seriously have some of the best wonton noodles in JB. I like the dark sauce version—it’s a bit sweeter, and the noodles are super springy. It be even better if the wontons weren’t deep-fried, but they still taste great. Dim sum was pretty good too. I’ll recommend the glutinous rice - it has a nice savoury peppery flavour to it.
author: Helen Ng

review_text:
A new satay stall that’s opened right in front of jia Yi tea house, close to the carpark. In fact, the tables are set on top of the parking lots itself.

The stall was quite busy when I visited on a Saturday night. If you are eating the lok lok next door, you can actually order the satay and have them served to your table.

The satay was quite generous in terms of its meat. The chicken is selling at 1.30 ringgit per stick and the beef at 1.60 ringgit. Not bad and they tasted good. The gravy was good as well. Sitting by the roadside eating satay had a rather nostalgic feel to it. Try if you are around the area.

review_text: Such a sweet lady and juiciest satay in town 😼🔝

author: Derick Ng

restaurant_name: 吴孃孃骨汤米粉 Auntwu Bone Soup Rice Noodles Eko Botani
review_text:
Aunt Wu specialises in bone-broth rice/noodle soups — the signature being a slowly simmered bone broth (often pork bone) that’s rich, savoury and comforting.
The noodles are typically rice-noodles or rice-vermicelli (米线 / 米粉 / 米线-type), soaked in that bone broth.

Noodles + broth combo gives a comfort-food vibe — often as “soul-warming” or “comforting” meal, especially in cooler weather or after a long day.
Portion can be shared and free refill for noodles.
author: Peter

restaurant_name: 吴孃孃骨汤米粉 Auntwu Bone Soup Rice Noodles Eko Botani
review_text: Food wise are good, generous portion. We ordered 2 for 3 sharing without refilling the rice noodle. The fried pork tastes good but the portion is small. Tomato soup with fried egg is fantastic. The soups are even tastier with vinegar added which makes it more intense.
author: MOLLY CHONG

restaurant_name: 吴孃孃骨汤米粉 Auntwu Bone Soup Rice Noodles Eko Botani
review_text: We decided to have dinner here and trying out some restaurants that we did not try before. They served some kind of noodles and the lady was telling us that it’s Sichuan styled noodles. My wife ordered one with salted vegetables and I ordered the mapo tofu. I should have ordered the noodles as well as the broth was really tasty. The noodles was also kinda special. The mapo tofu was quite a disappointment. Don’t taste authentic. But the noodles were really worth a try. Prices were reasonable.
author: Crumpled Nomad

restaurant_name: 吴孃孃骨汤米粉 Auntwu Bone Soup Rice Noodles Eko Botani
review_text: The non-spicy pork broth was initially abit too porkish but after adding the vinegar, it totally transformed it to a very nice comfort food while the Mala soup base one was abit too spicy for me despite I always order medium spicyness. The fried egg is mediocre though. The portion here are huge and the ingredients are generous. They even offer complimentary both free flow preserved vegetables (not recommended) and sour plum drinks which is very helpful when the food gets too spicy. I like their style of business and I am typing this while using their WiFi.  The non spicy pork broth type is a must try. If you are not big eaters, 1 noodles with soup portion is good enough for 2 to share.
author: David Wong

review_text:
One thing I like the most is the foods served were dam hot 🔥.

Food portion are great.

The "Mui fan" quite special as the rice is not a white rice. They take the rice to fried with egg first then put the sauce on top. But then the whole thing become a bit too salty.

I quite like the half boiled egg on top of the kaya toast: just a bit disappointed the egg yolk is not a piece when served. The taste is a bit sweet and a bit salty if u put the soya sauce on top of the half boiled egg.

The ordered the laksa and they have the option to choose mee Huey Kyue but then they said no stock Liao.. so I choose thick mee Hoon. Overall is quite nice also but a bit costly as not much meat and with a piece of hard prawn.

Service is fast.

Can try it if u passby there.
author: Jasminelcf

review_text:
April 2025
Ordered the mee rebus again and this time I reminded chef not to over cook the noodles. It was delicious this time.  The chicken rendang was disappointing - gravy was good but meat was tough. Otah was good.  Their Thursday special Fried Bee Hoon was tasty, the bottom was crispy with a little burnt taste served with starchy seafood gravy, less salty would be better.  And the next best item on the list was the Root beer float on an extremely hot and humid afternoon!!

Sept 2024
First time trying out food from this cafe. The place is clean and spacious. Both laksa and mee rebus gravy were very good EXCEPT both noodles were over cooked. My laksa thick bee hoon was the chewy type, so not really what i was looking for.  However it should be ok if not overcooked.  Coffee is too diluted for my liking.  Will come back to try other food items.
author: L Wong

review_text:
My parents have dined here several times and the food is pretty decent, although perhaps a hit and miss for some dishes. I recommend the seafood fried keuy teow—really good flavours, albeit light on the seafood. The laksa is good, but my parents have their favourite somewhere else. My husband enjoyed the nasi biryani with rendang chicken.

The polo bun was underwhelming. It had a pleasant flavour, but the crust was stodgy instead of being light and crisp.

I would avoid the crispy mihun (Thursday’s special). We thought that the noodles would be deep fried, but it appeared that they just served the dried raw noodles with the sauce and toppings poured over. Either someone new or inexperienced was working that day (5th December) or the restaurant just doesn’t cook it properly. The noodles weren’t very edible.

review_text:
Our Al Safa Senadi Hills has very good service. The staff are fast and efficient, so even when it’s busy, you don’t have to wait too long for your food. For me, the most important thing is that they have air kelapa. Sometimes it’s really hard to find, especially when you’re not feeling well or having fever, and I really appreciate how fresh their air kelapa is.

The food taste is not that great, but still okay and acceptable, especially because the service is quick and the drinks are good. Overall, everything was fine,  just hope they can improve the taste of the food a bit more in the future, then it would be even better.
author: Dhania Ellsha bt Abdullah

review_text: Al Safa in Senadi Hills is a top restaurant with amazing food and an upscale ambiance, including live Premier League football screenings. The prices are unbeatable — we spent just 10 RM per person including drinks and left completely full. The staff is friendly and helpful, making the whole experience even better. An absolute gem and highly recommended! Open 24/7!
author: Dominique Rey

review_text:
ordered the garlic naan set with tandoori chicken (RM11.50) and it was very tasty! The naan was fragrant and the tandoori was flavourful but abit dry. Service was excellent too, the staff noticed I was struggling to cut my naan and immediately offered to help. Really thoughtful and friendly. Not forgetting the humongous teh o iced limau🤣
Great value for money! Will definitely come back again.
author: Jo Anna

review_text: Al Safa at Senadi Hill JB is a welcoming restaurant serving hearty Middle Eastern and local dishes at reasonable prices. The food is flavourful and portions are generous — the grilled meats are tender, and the biryani is aromatic with rich spices. Staff are friendly and attentive, ensuring that service is prompt even when the restaurant is busy. The dining area is spacious, clean, and suitable for families or groups. There is ample parking outside, and the restaurant is wheelchair accessible with a wide entrance and comfortable seating layout.
author: Brian Wong

review_text: NOT WORTH THE PRICE! 3 pieces chicken for RM12.90.. plus need to wait for half and hour just for 3 PIECES CHICKEN and get a smelly chicken! not recommend to eat this menu.tq
author: nurul dafinah

restaurant_name: Jin Cheng Stimbot Cina Muslim Lanzhou Ramen
review_text:
Jin Cheng Lanzhou Ramen

Mi tarik goreng daging here is seriously power 🔥 The noodles are springy, full of “tarik-tarik” chew, and the beef is tender with just enough wok hei and spice. I ordered one plate and immediately felt like I should’ve packed another to bring home.

We also tried their steamboat set – only RM40 and really worth it. The portion is besar gila: plenty of sliced beef, fishballs, vegetables, tofu, mushrooms and noodles, so it’s perfect for sharing. Soup base is comforting, not too salty, and they give enough sauces so you can adjust your own flavour. For the price, it’s one of the most value-for-money Chinese Muslim steamboats I’ve had.

Jin Cheng is a Chinese Muslim restaurant (Lanzhou style ramen), so it’s family-friendly and suitable for Muslim diners.  ￼ The shop is clean, simple and comfortable to sit and lepak with friends while you slurp your noodles. Staff were helpful when we asked about the menu and they served our food quite fast even though there were other customers.

If you’re craving hand-pulled noodles and a budget-friendly steamboat in one place, this is a good spot to try. I’ll definitely come back for the mi tarik goreng beef and steamboat combo again.
author: Dhania Ellsha bt Abdullah

restaurant_name: Jin Cheng Stimbot Cina Muslim Lanzhou Ramen
review_text: If we usually eat Thai-style steamboat. This time we tried Chinese-style Szechuan steamboat. I recommend eating buffet style because it is very worth it. There are many unique types of soups other than those usually eaten in Thai or Japanese steamboats. We can choose 2 soups. Lots of lamb that we can eat repeatedly and other premium ingredients are the uniqueness of this place. The price is very reasonable. If we don't want to eat steamboat, there is also a cart style. The shop is clean and the service is fast.
author: Syameerah Hisyam

restaurant_name: Jin Cheng Stimbot Cina Muslim Lanzhou Ramen
review_text:
Decided to try this place after passing by several times. We dined for ala carte instead of the buffet as it was too late to eat a lot.

First impression? The decor is playful, a bit on the whimsical side, alot of modern Chinese features. Tastefully done!

What we ordered:
1. Beef noodle soup - I am not a big fan of soupy dishes but I can say this isn't too bad compared to the ones I had in China & Taiwan. I find the beef broth flavourful without the msg taste. Can really taste the beef in the soup. I am a Malay at heart tho, I wished that it'd be spicy. Even after pouring tons of chili oil, it still wasn't spicy 😂 I'll bring my own chilli next time. Oh, the noodle itself is delicious! It's not too thin, somewhere between the size of meehun and Mee kuning.
2. Dumplings - I would pass for next time, I find the beef does not have the good ratio vs the dumpling skin. The beef ball was too small. I tasted more flour than beef.
3. Mutton satay - Yeah, a winner! But I love mutton so I'm biased. The herbs seeps into the meat well, it is a bit salty but still acceptable.
4. Scallion pancake - This pancake is made from the same flour as the noodle, sprinkled with some scallion. It has a crispy outer layer, a bit like our roti canai but not quite. Order this as a starter or side dish or to be dipped into the beef soup. It's versatile but just as good to eat it on its own.

Would I go again? Yes, most definitely. Next time I'll probably try the buffet or the fried noodles. Do drop by!
author: N.a.d S

restaurant_name: Jin Cheng Stimbot Cina Muslim Lanzhou Ramen
review_text:
Both the ala carte and steamboat buffet are very affordable. For the serving size and quality of food and the price, this one of the best (if not the best) in town.

Great customer services, high level of hygiene on food, utensils and the restaurant, super delicious dishes, unique and best ramen.  It is difficult to find another in town.

Good job by the restaurant manager and team there.

It is a must try restaurant in JB.
author: Teong Teck Lee

restaurant_name: Jin Cheng Stimbot Cina Muslim Lanzhou Ramen
review_text: For the quality and variety offered, the price was reasonable. RM39 per head (if im not mistaken), add on rm19.90 for 2 soups with unlimited meat. Staffs were attentive and frequently checked on our table, ensuring we had enough soup n refill. Overall we had a fantastic experience having lunch here 🙌🏻
author: Nur Syazana Md Shariff

review_text: Proper fried rice here. Hopefully can maintain and sustain the quality. I will be definitely come to have more food here.

review_text: the best

review_text: Delicious. Generous portions. Perfect tomyum. Please be consistent for the sake of our customers.
author: MUHAMMAD IZZUDDIN BIN YAACOB

review_text: All the food tasted delicious. Only the fried rice was pale in color and seemed to be the same even though it was a different type of fried rice 😆 (kg fried rice, belacan fried rice & turmeric chicken fried rice)
author: najwa nasir

restaurant_name: 中国.穆斯林.兰州拉面 Lanzhou Ramen China Muslim
review_text:
This place is top notch. Such great value.

Authentic China Chinese cuisine - and halal cos the owners and workers are Muslim, it seems.

Large, comfortable space for dining. Well air-conditioned. Has 2 separate areas; one for hotpot kinda eating, one for non-hotpot. We've tried both and they're both high value, for the utility you get and the price you pay.

We came with our 4 young kids - no problem at all, they were very accommodating.

Kids loved the signature sliced beef noodles. I had the big plate chicken noodle - "dapanji". Wife ordered the lamb skewers. All great.

5/5 would come again. I hope this shop becomes a chain that lasts a good long time.

Pro tip: If you're a chopsticks noob like us, ask for scissors to snip-snip the long homemade noodles.
author: Saiful Shahril Saini

restaurant_name: 中国.穆斯林.兰州拉面 Lanzhou Ramen China Muslim
review_text: The food is really great, environment is also quiet nice, but the waiters doesn't speak Malay or Chinese which is funny to us and obviously just a young amateur and untrained foreign workers
author: Simon Kam

restaurant_name: 中国.穆斯林.兰州拉面 Lanzhou Ramen China Muslim
review_text: Food was extremely good! This is the first pulled noodles in Malaysia that tasted like in China. The soup is thicker than normal mee tarik in malaysia which is usually plain. In this restaurant, the umami aftertaste is quite mild which for me I favor that. idk why people talking about bad waiter service but so far, the two waitresses understand Malay and are friendly. Price for braised noodle also not bad. The only minus point is that idk why they served other table who arrived 10mins after us ermm. Ohh can be full house during peak hours as well
author: raudha nadiah

restaurant_name: 中国.穆斯林.兰州拉面 Lanzhou Ramen China Muslim
review_text:
Nice food and unique taste and worthwhile to try. Second time we go and this time took the kids along and they even loved it more than us. Price is reasonable and so are the portions. For sure recommend.
We ordered the beef fresh noodles and beef dumplings and beef skewers. Also their coffee and homemade tea has a unique taste.
Went again with kids for lunch. Tried potato slices and beef soup with bamboo shoots. See photos. We all enjoyed the food, especially the kids.
author: patrick przybylski

restaurant_name: 中国.穆斯林.兰州拉面 Lanzhou Ramen China Muslim
review_text: Was recommended by a colleague to try this newly open restaurant. The place is nice and clean. The service is fast and friendly. The cutleries and bowls are kept in sanitized cabinet with temperature controlled. The food are fresh and the portions are generous. I love the cooked lamb, so soft and succulent. The beef is amazingly soft and tender. I noticed lots of malay muslims patronised the restaurant. The home-made yogurt is incredibly delicious that you’ll want more than one cup! Definitely worth it and value for money! Wish the restaurant more success! Will definitely becoming again to be our favourite place for halal chinese muslim steamboat.
author: LEGO Knight12

review_text: A local cafe offering a decent breakfast- pre-cooked noodles/rice that you select, lontong (dry and gravy) as well as made-to-order rotis. The serunding on the lontong was delicious and elevated all the ingredients, of which there was enough- a triangle of tofu and various vegetables. The rice cake was soft to the bite, yet did not disintegrate prematurely. All this swimming in an attractive yellow gravy that is rather umami. You can request sambal on the side. My husband enjoyed his dry lontong and seemed happy with the portion. The star of the show for me was the Kopi Ais in a large glass - just look at the layer of foam bubbling over the sides! It is made from local coffee and the taste is well-balanced. A great motivation to visit this cafe.

review_text:
\\A Singaporean Girl Review

The curry when ate together with the egg and roti canai is absolutely perfect. Perfect in spice, spicy and temperature!!!

The show stealer are our drinks. Creamy, tasty, and well made. The drinks are worthy of cafe standards. Kopi and teh are done just right.

Generous servings, lovely wait staff, quite environment despite the bustling business and many many customers. I am so excited to visit this place again and set this as my weekly mental reset for the week ahead. I really appreciate the restaurant aiming to serve good food and drinks to the community as a way to help us to reset, recover and rediscover ourselves. ❤️❤️❤️

review_text:
Neapolitan-style pizza with a Malaysian twist, what’s not to like?

Tucked away in a quiet neighbourhood, this pizzeria is truly a great find. Freshly made to order and baked in a gas-fired oven, the pizzas come out beautifully blistered, chewy, and flavourful.

The combo deals are surprisingly affordable considering the quality of the pizzas. After three visits, we can confidently say the consistency in both service and pizzas are its greatest draws.

On our third visit, we got a little adventurous and tried the Spicy Kambing. While it was tasty and unique, I think we’ll stick with the more classic flavours next time. No fault of the pizza.

All in all, great value pizzas, friendly down-to-earth service, and consistent quality will definitely keep us coming back.

restaurant_name: 阿彬养生肉骨茶 Restoran Ah Peng Bak Kut Teh (Eco Botanic 分店)
review_text:
If you’re craving a comforting bowl of bak kut teh while exploring Eco Botanic, 阿彬养生肉骨茶 (Restoran Ah Peng Bak Kut Teh) is a solid choice — especially for those who enjoy rich herbal flavors and tasty ribs cooked just right. This branch offers a cozy, casual dining environment that feels familiar and inviting, perfect for a relaxed lunch or dinner.

The meat in the bak kut teh was tender and flavorful, with the traditional herbal broth lending warmth and depth without overpowering the dish. The herbs were well balanced — fragrant and soothing, a nice contrast to the heat or humidity outside. Pair it with rice and some youtiao (fried dough) for dipping, and you’ve got a classic, satisfying meal.

Service here was friendly and prompt, and the portion sizes are generous enough to share. It’s not a fine-dining experience, but it hits all the right notes for hearty, unpretentious comfort food — exactly what you want from a good bak kut teh spot.

Overall, Ah Peng Bak Kut Teh at Eco Botanic delivers good flavors and a reliable taste of local heritage cuisine.

review_text:
We tried a mix of their dishes, both signature and non-signature, and surprisingly, the non-signature luncheon meat fried rice actually outshined their noodles. Their signature tea had a slightly stronger, heavier flavour (probably black tea?) but we personally prefer the usual lighter taste.

The signature noodles were quite thick and firm, which wasn’t really our preference. It makes us wonder if that’s just the style people like, since the ratings are so high. The soup was also pretty mild for handmade noodles, which could be a plus for those looking for something healthier or kid-friendly.

The shop itself is modern and visually appealing, almost to the point of being overstimulating, but it probably helps draw in a crowd. One downside: there were quite a few houseflies buzzing around the food, which raises some concerns about hygiene in the long run.

review_text: I first came on a weekend... and the queue was super long. Forget getting a table haha! So I came back on Tuesday for an early dinner. The restaurant was fairly empty then. They have lots of great looking items on the menu. The "Lor" pan mee sounded interesting and unique so I decided to try. It wasnt what I was expecting... I expected a more aniseed flavour associated with braised meats, but this was not the case. They also served it with black vinegar... which is actually not bad if you like black vinegar. But the bottle they served it in had a loose lid , which fell into my bowl when I tried to pour haha. Anyway, portion size is large, and really not too bad at all. Staff were all really nice and friendly. They dont have tissues on the table and you need to ask for them... I also ordered a kaya butter toast... which was only mediocre. review_text: This is outrageous! The menu said adding chicken was 4 yuan, so I ordered two servings of chicken tails, expecting it to be around 8 yuan. But the waiter came over and said they were out of chicken tails. I asked for chicken legs instead, and he didn't mention anything about extra charges. Then, when I paid, a chicken leg cost 10 yuan! That's outrageous! If you need to charge extra, please let customers know immediately. Otherwise, it's consumer fraud. When I paid, I even asked the waiter why he didn't tell me a chicken leg cost 10 yuan, which was different from the 4 yuan for adding chicken on the menu. At first, I didn't want to argue about 20 yuan, but after thinking about it for a long time, I think they probably use this tactic (often saying they're out of chicken tails, so people naturally order chicken legs, since chicken lovers know that if there are no chicken tails, it's chicken legs, but nobody would expect chicken tails to cost 4 yuan and chicken legs 10 yuan) to deceive consumers. So I wanted to warn everyone here to prevent others from being fooled by this trick again! Here's a piece of advice: if you're going to charge 10 yuan for a chicken leg, put it on the menu. Trust me, nobody will order it. Don't try to cheat us consumers with these deceptive tactics. We don't need your 10 yuan, but nobody likes being ripped off!

restaurant_name: YouKee XO 有记烧臘之家 (Eko Botani)
review_text:
Dropped by YouKee XO 有记烧臘之家 to check out this newly opened outlet, and the first impression was honestly quite striking. The interior decoration is surprisingly grand for a roast-meat restaurant, with a spacious layout, multiple VIP rooms, and even an alfresco dining area. It feels more upscale than your usual char siu shop, making it suitable for both casual meals and family gatherings.

I kept my order simple — char siu and roasted pork belly noodles, along with one of their signature double-boiled soups. The char siu was well done, with a good balance of fat and lean meat, nicely marinated and flavorful without being overly sweet. The roasted pork belly impressed too, with crispy skin and tender meat beneath. The highlight for me was the soup — comforting, rich, and clearly something they take pride in.

Overall, it was a satisfying meal with solid food quality. The only downside was the service, which felt a little mechanical and impersonal. Still, a good start for a new opening and definitely worth trying if you’re in Eco Botanic.

We ordered the fish and chips $22, Hokkien pasta $22, and a couple of drinks. The dishes were generally mild in flavour and may suit those who prefer lighter seasoning. The environment was pleasant and a nice place to sit back and relax, and the service staff were friendly and attentive.

Overall, it is a comfortable spot to visit if you are in the area, and others may enjoy it more depending on personal taste.
author: Melvin J.

review_text:
A hidden gem tucked away in the rural part of Singapore, away from the busy city life. Great ambience, amazing service - the staff was friendly and attentive without being intrusive, and service was prompt. Nice outdoor seating, with plenty of room to run around!
The ribeye hor fun is splendid - the steak compliments the wok hei hor fun. Salad is fresh, with dressing on the side instead - so you can decide how much dressing you want! The lamb rack is nicely done - we didn’t want fries with it, and the staff recommended to change our sides.
A huge parking lot for those who drive. For cyclists on the popular Kranji/LCK route (like us!), it’s a perfect stop as you have lots of room to park your bikes!
We’ll definitely come back again!

review_text: A 10 min walk from Sungei Buloh's northern visitor centre, a perfect place to stop by for lunch after walking all morning. This is a hidden gem with an amazing fish and chips. The fish was fresh and a good size portion. The lunch special was a great deal, as it included a soup, drink and some ice cream as well (goat milk from the nearby farm, I believe). Though it's an outdoor venue, there are some fans which help to ventilate, so the heat isn't too oppressive. If only the bus service was not discontinued in this area! It's pretty hard to get around Sungei Buloh without a car, and getting Grab/Taxi isn't very easy either. At least we were able to rest comfortably at this restaurant until we finally managed to book a ride home. Thank you!

author: Gela

review_text:
This started as a recommended find to be honest, by Gemini the AI presumably by algorithm answer to my prompt for a best for halal food. We are not native nor familiar with Woodlands intimately but wanted something authentic. And satisfyingly good of course. Something natives there would recommend themselves as their goto. We drove over and realised it is located tucked away in not your typical address for an eatery but possessing almost a gem-like quality that one finds or chances upon.

Utterly charming and in a time of slickness and packaging it oozes rustic soulful familiarity which to me is its appeal. Doesn't matter that it is a tiny spot in a community club. Above all it feels homely and welcoming. And I'm a sucker for that. Trust me although the group of ladies - admirably cooking, preparing and servicing from a tight lil back of the serving front - are not effusive - part of the charm is the warmth that comes after one breaks the ice - but it's in the little things they do that is telling. Like ensuring you get a full tall glass iced unasked when you helped yourself to a canned drink. Personally serving your plate of inviting food like your grandma or auntie hands it to you knowingly without saying much but to simply eat the delightful plate and enjoy. That pretty much sums up the food they offer. They're OG authentic as I had hoped and I can understand why we saw many patiently waited for their table turn or order. And at the reasonable prices they charge it is a steal.

Let's talk about the wonderful food. The Mee Rebus my wife had was thank goodness not sweetened in flavour like a lot on offer today but has a nice familiar comforting gravy. My longtong kering is delish with each component to the whole the real deal. Real paru or lungs cooked slightly crunchy but tender inside. Begedil nicely holding the lovely flavoured potato filling inside. And the sambal is perfectly balanced, again thankfully not just heat and sweet. The kacang pool I had to sample is absolutely spot on. I was unsure over the more pureed-llike gravy but it's really really good. The toasted bread that came with it just comfort and soak up the beautiful whole. At the prices they charge they are not only a steal but to be savoured. Love on a plate and in a bowl for sure.

As for Kueh Kueh which I could not resist to sample although we were already so full, are the real deal. They are homemade quality and again not soaked in sweetness only. No wonder the table next to us grabbed literally a whole platter of variety to share as an appetite opener.

It's like dining at a family home where you get love on a table. This is definitely one sublime gem we will return to whenever we are at Woodlands.
author: Hamzah Alsagoff

review_text:
Tucked inside Marsiling Community Club, My Kitchen My Lab is a small but charming café with only four tables—so expect a short wait during peak lunch hours. I’ve visited multiple times with colleagues, and it’s become a regular lunch spot for us.

The menu offers familiar local staples like Nasi Lemak and Mee Rebus, but the real draw is their daily specials, which change every day. We usually go for the special menu, paired with traditional appetizers like ondeh-ondeh, freshly prepared by the friendly aunties.

I’ve tried the Nasi Goreng Ayam and Asam Pedas on separate visits:

Nasi Goreng Ayam: The rice was firm and flavorful, with each grain distinct. The fried chicken was tender and tasty, and their chili sauce added a spicy kick that elevated the whole dish.

Asam Pedas: Served in a claypot to keep it warm—nice touch. It came with generous portions of stingray and lady’s fingers in a rich, tangy sauce that paired beautifully with rice. The meal also included assorted vegetables, a fried egg, and a solid sambal belacan.

Bonus points: they accept CDC vouchers. The aunties are always warm and welcoming, making each visit feel personal.

Not sure if she didn't see the number written on the packet or what. Even so, such anyhow charging is a bad experience for me as first time customer. I will not go back to the stall again.

author: Monkey Skye

restaurant_name: Mr Grumpy Nasi Ayam (Lucky Plaza Nasi Ayam Goreng) - Marsiling (Woodlands)
review_text:
Ordered the original at Fiie's cafe and 6 months on, trying this. Review compares both stalls to one another, and I must say off the bat this stall does have a slightly lower standard, still decent in its regard.

Rice was (semi-) fragrant, felt like a chicken rice, yet wasn't that strong tasting enough that it felt close to white rice. It's a bit neither here nor there, kind of wasted.

Chilli is the nasi lemak kind, sweet. Actually pairs really well with the rice.

Chicken is amazing, meat was tender and skin was crispy. Only downside is that the cook on it wasnt perfect, some fat under the skin wasn't fully rendered (see pic).

Added $1 for sides (4 sambal quail egg) I think its okay, definitely cheaper than the Orchard original. Overall it shares similar nodes of the delicious chicken rested on a plate of nice rice. Solid 4 stars, not perfect though. Not reaching original's standard.

Soup was just a seasoning bomb, a bit disappointed that the soup portion is so small.
author: owen

restaurant_name: Mr Grumpy Nasi Ayam (Lucky Plaza Nasi Ayam Goreng) - Marsiling (Woodlands)
review_text:
The chilli seems to be of those for nasi lemak. I like it though. The rice a little lose out cause I find it a little wet. I find the chicken is really good, crispy and tender. However my friend says the meat could be better. The sides nothing spectacular. Put everything together, you got a plate of flavourful Nasi Ayam Goreng which taste quite well. The crew are very friendly.
My verdict : can eat
author: Ken Lim

restaurant_name: Mr Grumpy Nasi Ayam (Lucky Plaza Nasi Ayam Goreng) - Marsiling (Woodlands)
review_text:
The chicken was left out for some time so when I ate, it was not hot. The taste is quite ok but if it's hot will be better.
Personally think is just ok but the flakes add some texture to the dish. $6.50 for a plate
author: Zj

restaurant_name: Mr Grumpy Nasi Ayam (Lucky Plaza Nasi Ayam Goreng) - Marsiling (Woodlands)
review_text:
Fast, delicious, hearty and hits all the right spots!

Finally had the chance to try out Mr Grumpy and it definitely didn’t disappoint.

Went there in time for lunch and, although there was a queue, the line moved quite fast so it doesn’t even matter.

Even the ordering process is quite fuss-free!

Coming to the food, the chicken thigh is impeccable. Juicy and tender doesn’t even do it justice. It is honestly one of the best chicken you can get in the North.

But the star of the show had to be the sambal and soup combo. Both added so much flavours to the meal and it really elevated the whole dish to the next level.

There are three side dishes for you to choose from and they are really generous with their portions so you really can’t go wrong with them.

Highly recommend a visit if you are nearby!
author: YongCheng Lee

restaurant_name: Mr Grumpy Nasi Ayam (Lucky Plaza Nasi Ayam Goreng) - Marsiling (Woodlands)
review_text:
We had an amazing experience at Mr Grumpy Fried Chicken! The chicken was really crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Even my boy loves it too! The flavor was spot-on. Don’t forget their tasty chili too, if you a chili lover is a must to try it too. The side dish to add-on comes with quail egg, hot dog & bergedil.

The staff were friendly and attentive.  Perfect place for comfort food lovers like me. Highly recommend trying their signature fried chicken if you're in the mood for something delicious and satisfying!
author: Jorynn Tan

review_text: Al-Falah Restaurant actually is the Indian Muslim stall selling biryani, Roti John crispy prata and kambing soup among others. They are very well-known for their crispy prata but of course, being crispy, it has to be oily. Their kambing soup is only available from around 4.00 pm onwards only, which is a bit late. The service is quite fast though, which helps to clear the queue fast.

review_text: Carrot cake, oyster. Tastes very good. I like it here, hard to find these stalls in coffee shop

Been tasting all over SG, but i still like it here, not over powered, many nowadays are "over taste" which doesn't feel like eating more.

review_text: 말레이시아 조호바루에서 기차로 당일치기 싱가폴여행 할때 보통 10시가서 21시15분 기차로 복귀하는데요 저녁을 어디서 먹을지 고민이되고 힘들더라구요 또한 높은물가와 우드랜드역이랑 먼곳에서 식당 찾고 헤매고   기차시반에 불안해서 않먹고 조호바루에서 먹게 되더라구요 근데 마실링역건너편 로컬식당가인데 가격 저렴하고 종류도 많아요 음식에 냄새가 않나서 좋았어요 저희는 비프라면4싱달 곱빼기5싱달과 비프튀김에 밥해서 싱달2.9 먹었는데  향없고 잘먹었네요
author: 김YG

review_text: delicious
author: Danny

review_text:
The place was easy to find. The parking spots near the place were limited but free.

Ordered a Smoked Burger, Madhen Chicken, Stuffed Cheese Burger and Gourmet Burger. The ingredients used in these burgers were all fresh and flavorful. The patties didn't taste frozen at all and reasonably thick for its price. My only complained was that they put alot of sauce under the bun which caused the bun to soak up those sauce and become soggy. The breading / coating for the chicken patty was really good. There was a hint of spiciness in it.

The premise was not really cool for me since I sweated abit while eating there.

Would love to come here again in the future even though the prices were a bit to steep for an a-la-carte burger.
author: Kwinera

review_text:
Have been hearing about it for a long time. Decided to try it since we were staying at Double Tree Hilton.

Burgers were so good. I had that mixed Patty burger (chicken and beef). That chicken was nicely fried and succulent. Beef patty was on point. Even the Angus steaks are great!

Just the location is abit off city center but it's still not that far out. Could be a good place to visit if you are near the Johor Zoo I think!

Value for money as well!
author: Max H.

review_text:
We tried the Smoked Burger and the Mushroom Burger and both was thick and generously loaded. The Smoked Burger had tender and flavourful bacon that paired well with the patty. The Mushroom Burger had a hash brown inside added a great crunch and texture.
The only drawback was the buns which soaked up the sauce a little too quickly and became soggy. The circle fries used the same sauce as the burgers and while some might enjoy it, the sweetness wasn’t quite to my taste.
author: Madeleine Tan

review_text:
we got the signature burger and beef brisket; both flavour-wise an 8/10. quality ingredients too! burger had great textures, bun was soft and didnt stick to your teeth. brisket was tender and fatty, but not as tender as ive tried before.
portion sizes could be bigger, though! especially the brisket.
the whole place looks very cinematic, so very cool.
author: Jin Yang Thai Low

review_text: Tried the Brisket Burger and Smoked Beef Burger — both packed with flavour and generous in portion. The beef was juicy and tender, though a bit rich after a few bites. The curly fries and cheese-loaded beef fries were crispy and satisfying. Restaurant was quite full during lunch, but service was quick and friendly. Overall, a hearty gourmet burger spot worth trying if you’re craving something indulgent in JB.
author: Li Feng

review_text: Food is super delicious. Tired their nasi goreng daging kicap. Portion was perfect. Taste is chef kiss. Amazing and great price. Highly recommend. Drinks, tried their Neslo ice and hot tea o.
author: Afifah

review_text:
Sangat lazat/very tasty! I quite liked the food, though my friend who's more a foodie, only liked the special Mee goreng, which really was amazing! I liked the chili sauce with both dishes. Stay from nearby was good, though but too fatty...

I think it cost RM38 for three dishes + teh tarik.
author: J. Springall

review_text:
Visited Al Hambra recently, and it was a delightful experience! The food is absolutely delicious, and the service staff are exceptionally friendly. They always greet and serve customers with a warm smile, which adds to the great atmosphere.

The location is easy to find, and parking is convenient—just across the street. You can enter via the gantry and tap your Touch 'n Go card.

My dad absolutely loved the food here! His favorite is the nasi ayam penyet with its flavorful chili. He enjoyed it so much that he requested extra chili, and the staff were happy to oblige. He also asked for an extra serving of rice, and they kindly accommodated him. Thank you, team, for such thoughtful service!

The satay, paired with its rich, delicious gravy, was another highlight for us. Every bite was bursting with flavor. My dad has officially approved this spot and is already planning to come back and try more dishes.

A special thank you to my niece for recommending this gem. Keep up the fantastic work, Al Hambra team—your smiles and excellent service make all the difference! 🫡
author: S J

review_text: Just Had our dinner here at this cafe, the food was good and the portion is really worth the price. Definitely recommend for family and friends who likes to have a leisurely evening. Good job to the crews . They were very efficient.
author: Devaraj Raj

review_text:
Great food and friendly service!
Me and my husband always come here and we really enjoy it every time. The food is really good. Our favorite is the Nasi Goreng Special Alhambra, it’s super delicious! Big thanks to the chef for making such amazing food. The cashier, Ms. Quraisya, was very friendly, polite, and always has a warm smile that makes us feel welcome. The waiters are also really nice and helpful. Love the vibes here. Definitely will keep coming back!
author: nadzirah hani

review_text:
I was looking for somewhere local with live music (especially rock music, which I usually enjoy) and we came across RockStone near our hotel. We were already quite full, so we just ordered the fish & chips and a few snacks, but everything we tried was really tasty. The prices were very reasonable too, which made it even more worth it.

The owner and staff were super friendly and welcoming. The owner even shared some great local recommendations for first-time visitors to Johor Bahru, which we really appreciated.

I’m writing this review because I truly believe this place deserves more attention! I saw someone had left a 1-star review and honestly, it felt unfair. Even if the food wasn’t their favorite, the service, atmosphere, and overall experience here don’t deserve such a low rating.

If you’re looking for somewhere with good vibes, great music, and a more local night-out experience (outside the malls and night markets), give RockStone a try!
author: Katharina

review_text: Super nice for an old rocker like me. Food is superb and very tasty with the right portion. Music could be super niche for some but metalheads will love this place for sure.
author: Arthur Lee

review_text:
Gf and I wanted to have dinner and found this on google map with good rating so decided to give it a try. When we arrived, we realised it’s not restaurant setting but more of a pub setting, was surprised to see all the high tables and chairs, still we gave it a shot. Not their fault, we didn’t really read thoroughly.

Anyway we ordered signature beef burger, fish and chip and calamari, along with green tea, and Oreo milkshake. The burger was really delicious, fish & chips was golden brown which meant it was cooked just nice. Milkshakes are flavourful, only the calamari tasted rather plain but the French fries that came with the 2 main food made up for it! The size is just nice, the way we like it.

Moreover with the low price, it is super worthy. All these for just rm$102 and to sweeten the deal, the staff informed that they are having promotion with Grab now and can get 30% off directly from the total bill if we use Grab food to pay. So we only paid slightly over rm$70! 😁

I’m helping to write this review becos I really think they are really worth it! I can’t apprehend why did the previous review gave a 1 star rating. If she didn’t think the food is that fantastic, at least rate correctly. 1 star ratings are for really terrible service, food and hygiene of shops etc and I really think it’s a very unfair rating.

Anyway highly recommended to visit while the awesome discount is going on. Honestly, even after the promo is over, I’m pretty sure I’ll still be back for the burger. I’m a big sucker for beef burger. Haha.
author: Notle Chew

review_text: The food was good and nice portion . The environment was very nice . Small and good . It’s a very good place to chill and food .

I tasted the BBQ sliver pomfret (BEST) and 3 BBQ chicken wings, my daughter love most 166 BBQ chicken wings. You have to sometime understand the couple hardwork to serve the best quality, tasty, healthy, delicious foods. Give them your full support so they can survive and provide good foods here at blk 166.

Serving varieties of BBQ including Chicken Wings, Satay (Mutton, Chicken & Pork), whole Chicken and Fish (Stingray & Pomfret). They did the BBQ slow and good. Prices are reasonable/cheap compared to Marsiling Mall (poor quality foods). God always bless them and their family, their business 💕

review_text: Serving varieties of BBQ including Chicken Wings, Satay (Mutton, Chicken & Pork), whole Chicken and Fish (Stingray & Pomfret). They did the BBQ slow and good. Prices are reasonable.

author: Qingyu Smith

review_text:
Still one of the best satays around this area.
Best to call and order in advance, in order to reduce waiting time.

restaurant_name: Rong Kee Roasted Delights - Woodlands Street 13
review_text: One of the best Roasted Delights stall in the area serving all sort Roasted delicacies including Wanton Noodles. The Roasted Duck & Roast Pork cost $49./pc & $49./kg respectively. The Wanton Noodles cost at a budget price of $3.50.
author: Jimmy Chai

restaurant_name: Rong Kee Roasted Delights - Woodlands Street 13
review_text: They have wanton mee promotion at $3.30. The noodles were quite good - fragrant and springy. No complaints with the char siew nor wanton. Overall a plate of decent wanton mee that is budget-friendly.
author: laybit

restaurant_name: Rong Kee Roasted Delights - Woodlands Street 13
review_text:
Their Char Siu have been one of my favourite since young.

I like its lean and less fat yet it is still having this soft chewy bite.

Their style is more similar to HK style which has more savoury taste than sweetness and its colour is darker in soy shade.

And you can self help yourself with the fried pork fats!

Hope they can open more branches.
author: J Li

restaurant_name: Rong Kee Roasted Delights - Woodlands Street 13
review_text: It has been years but they have not gotten a shoutout. So here is one of those rare finds in an obscure neighbourhood that serves one of the best Hong Kong style roasted meats. A tad sweet for some meat items but overall very satisfying because of the enormous portion given!

review_text:
Today I tried the mandi at this restaurant.
The rice and chicken were incredibly delicious — honestly, I haven’t tasted anything like it anywhere else!
The shawarma was also juicy and full of flavor.
Thank you guys! I will definitely be coming back again very soon.

review_text: The food is amazing and delicious, and the place is very clean. It's the best.
author: Asem Alnadesh

review_text:
I recently visited the restaurant Abi shawarma Al Damascus Johor Bahru
I ordered the chicken shawarma and nasi arab, and both were delicious. The shawarma was juicy and well-seasoned, and the rice had a nice aroma with just the right amount of spices. The portion size was generous, and the food felt freshly prepared.
author: Khan Ijaz

review_text: Nice food and friendly people
author: Khann19 Ijaz

restaurant_name: Triple K Cafe 牛肉面家
review_text:
Stepping into this row of pre-war houses while experiencing time stand.

Teh C was frothy and flavorsome, which was surprisingly good.

Homemade Siew Mai was excellent and it did not contain too much fillers.

Its signature Beef brisket with radish soup was rich and deeply flavored. The beef cubes were tender.

The elderly lady was friendly and eager to please.

Definitely worth a visit.
author: MNG

restaurant_name: Triple K Cafe 牛肉面家
review_text:
This place is situated at far end the streets. I decided to try this as I felt that it doesn't look overly commercialised like the others.
I ordered the Beef (Mixed) dry noodle to try. It's not too bad but I don't think it came with all the mixed beef pieces. Perhaps that's cos we ordered the smallest sized.
粿条面 Guo Tiao (the noodles) seems to be a little too sticky (overcooked) for my liking. Maybe I should order other types of noodles. But their soup is tasty though it's quite a small bowl.
Decor seems run down but that's ok for me.
author: Michelle Tok

restaurant_name: Triple K Cafe 牛肉面家
review_text:
This is an old school cafe with retro vibes. Walls are bare concrete n paint peeling. But the whole shop is clean n toilet does not have any funky smell.

Beef noodles were not suitable for me, beef was tough n tendon were too chewy.

The coffee was e star here! rich and creamy..e 2 inch foam at the top would put Starbucks to shame. It was thick n well down smoothly.

Would come back here just for e coffee 👍🏾
author: Donny Lim

restaurant_name: Triple K Cafe 牛肉面家
review_text:
This is a very authentic post-war old shop, and it brings back many memories of me playing on this street when I was a child.

The beef noodle and dim sum is tasty, I like it. You shouldn't miss it.
author: Roy Chan - Property Consultant

restaurant_name: Triple K Cafe 牛肉面家
review_text: Love the tiny little Chinese couple who runs this coffee shop, serving up the best mutton noodle soup, enormous homemade siew mai and easily the best kopi o kosong peng along that street. Please support them! You won't regret it!
author: Sharon Mah

review_text:
Ate at Gerai Norizah. Auntie was super friendly and kind. The food was good and their goreng goreng was popular.

I ate their nasi campur. love the asam pedas gravy. was charged RM10 for nasi campur dan RM12 for the sizzling at different shop
author: Syaza

review_text:
We have been going to this Gerai Norizah some 30 years ago. At that time, this gerai was located at the medan selera at Wisma Persekutuan parking area (opp Tabung haji) When the two-row of gerai were demolished, we went looking for it but in vain. Post-covid, this is our first visit to this place.

My favorite is definitely the laksa goreng. Laksa goreng has its tanginess from bunga kantan. Balanced of spiciness and sweetness. Not oily at all. Such an indulge!

So when we went recently and to have the laksa goreng just like it used to be. Now, kak leeza doesnt do the cooking anymore but we were glad it's just the same. Not many eateries can maintain the consistency in taste. But this is a winner!
author: mini teddy

review_text: Eating at Norizah's stall.. really delicious.. friendly owner... Like going back to my hometown to eat what my mom cooked.. good service... Other stalls are not as tasty...
author: muh zaki khairul insan budin

review_text:
I’ve been to King of Fried Rice a few times(different outlet) and it’s consistently satisfying. The fried rice is nicely done, fragrant, with good “wok hei” elements, and the portions of meat (especially the pork cutlet) are generous. Several outlets get positive feedback for both taste and value.

One standout element: the chilli they serve. It’s described by multiple diners as “amazing” and a flavour-elevater that you really shouldn’t skip.  Having tried it myself, I’d say yes, definitely add a good dollop right into your rice.

Overall, King of Fried Rice is a strong choice when you’re craving a comforting, well-executed plate of fried rice, go with the chilli, enjoy the generous meat topping, and maybe pick a slightly quieter time to visit for a smoother experience.
author: Koko

review_text: Ordered 2 pack of eggs fried rice and was given scratch card. Lucky! I gotten a free topping of luncheon meat and wanted to redeem immediately. The staff rejected the redemption and said that is for next purchase. I read thru the conditions and did not say we cannot redeem or next visit. The staffs said it was their Manager instruction. Why stop customer to redeem if you want to run a promotion. I may not live around the area and will not come back here again. Very disappointed and return the card to the stall. I believe the staffs saw my disappointment and unhappiness, they add the free item to me and told me they added although their manager instruction was next visit. Thumb up to the chief for his quick recovery but supposing a happy feeling turned to a dissatisfied purchase. Still give 3 Stars as the food quality is good.
author: Chia Jeslyn

review_text: good value always get their pork chop fried rice. equivalent to ding tai fung but at better price. can use cdc vouchers
author: TL Chan

review_text: Delicious pork cutlet fried rice at affordable price. Pork cutlet is thick and it taste as good as that from Ding Tai Feng.. Hopefully there won't be a price increase after 1 Jan 2024.
author: Geraldine Yong

review_text:
The drink stall at this hawker 🤢 Pls BEWARE of the drink stall 🤮 Only after 30 min did me and my partner got stomach ache after drinking their tea and coffee,, had gastric reflux after their drinks, dude what is up with their drinks....

And the fried rice here is classic to any other branch in Singapore
author: Yukiki

review_text:
I came to eat subway as I was very hungry and many told me they have the best cookies.
I ordered their spicy taco beef sandwich. And the spicy taco beef was actually very very delicious!!! With so many different vegetables, it is a healthier fast food choice.
When I tried their cookie, firstly, it was very very sweet (I already knew it) and I tried the macadamia nut white chocolate cookie. It is soft and hard and personally I dont really like it
author: Lew Yi Chen (Rvhs)

review_text:
I am a regular at this outlet whenever I attend my evening classes and my previous experience here was very positive. However, this time, I had a disappointing experience with a staff. She began conversing with her colleagues in front of me before completing my transaction. Additionally, her customer service was lacking and her tone when asking me questions came across as arrogant and unpleasant. It left me wondering how someone with such behavior could hold a supervisory position at this outlet.

author: ToujiangX

Not helpful on clarifying prices for set meal

review_text: The sandwich is always keep FRESH for eating. Furthermore, so pleased to see the team of servicing crew do a great job to customers. Keep it up!
author: Roy Siek

review_text:

Wanted to use CDC voucher, her iPad was clearly functional but she didn’t know how to scan….. I had no cash so paynow instead.. and even so, had to show her the transaction twice -.- arghhh
author: Michelle Tan

review_text:
I went down at night to order and didn’t see that the aunty had placed tray on the counter, i then made an order for the signature noodle, in which she pointed to the tray with a rude and silent expression, followed by saying “shop already closed what signature you still want?”, stared at me for awhile then walked off.

review_text:
Incredible Experience at Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza! 🍕SG

I honestly cannot recommend Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza enough! From start to finish, my experience with them was nothing short of fantastic, and I feel like every detail deserves praise. First off, the delivery was unbelievably fast! 🚗💨 I placed my order and, in no time at all, the pizzas arrived at my doorstep hot, fresh, and ready to enjoy. In this day and age, it’s rare to find a place that prioritises speed without compromising quality, and Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza nailed it perfectly.

The pizzas themselves were absolutely delicious and packed with generous toppings. 🍕😋 I ordered a couple, and every slice was loaded with cheese, meats, and veggies. You can really taste the care and quality in every bite — none of that stingy topping nonsense you sometimes get elsewhere. The crust was cooked just right: crispy on the edges, soft in the middle, and perfect for holding all the toppings together.

Another thing I loved was how affordable the pizzas were. 💰 Compared to other pizza chains, the prices are super reasonable, yet the quality is top-notch. It’s rare to find a place that combines tasty, generous pizzas with great value, and Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza delivered on both fronts.

To top it all off, they even included a free fridge magnet with my order! 🧲 I know it’s a small gesture, but honestly, it made the experience even more memorable and enjoyable. It’s clear that they put thought into making customers feel appreciated, and it really shows that they care about providing not just food, but a full, positive experience.

The staff behind the scenes must be doing something right, because everything was smooth, friendly, and efficient. From ordering to delivery, it felt like a seamless process, and I could tell they take pride in their service. 🙌

Overall, I am beyond impressed with Canadian 2 For 1 Pizza. Fast delivery, affordable prices, generous and delicious toppings, and even a thoughtful little freebie — what more could you ask for? 🍕💯 I’ll definitely be ordering from them again, and I highly recommend them to anyone who loves great pizza, excellent service, and awesome value. This is easily one of the best pizza experiences I’ve had in a long time, and it deserves every bit of a 5-star rating!

review_text:
Incredible Experience at Pizza Hut Singapore! 🍕🇸🇬

I just had to share my experience because Pizza Hut Singapore absolutely deserves a full 5-star review! From start to finish, everything about my order and the service was flawless, and it truly exceeded my expectations in every way.

First off, the ordering process was smooth and easy. The website/app was intuitive, and I was able to customize my pizza exactly how I wanted it. I love having the option to choose toppings, crust type, and even add extra cheese or sides — it makes the experience feel personalized and special. 📝✨

Then came the delivery — and wow, I was genuinely impressed! 🚀 My order arrived super fast, well before I expected it, and the pizzas were hot, fresh, and perfectly cooked. There’s nothing worse than a cold pizza after waiting, but Pizza Hut Singapore got it absolutely right. The packaging kept everything intact, and it was clear that care had been taken to ensure my order arrived in pristine condition.

Now, let’s talk about the pizza itself — absolutely outstanding. 🍕😋 The crust was golden, crispy on the outside yet soft and chewy on the inside. The sauce was rich and flavorful, perfectly balanced with the gooey, generous cheese. And the toppings — wow — they were plentiful, fresh, and full of flavor. Every bite was a delightful mix of textures and tastes, and it was obvious that high-quality ingredients were used. Each slice was satisfying, hearty, and incredibly delicious. I could taste the care and passion that went into making every pizza.

One thing I truly appreciated was the attention to detail in the overall experience. The staff were professional, polite, and attentive. Even with a busy day, they managed to handle everything efficiently and ensure that my order was perfect. It really shows that Pizza Hut Singapore values its customers and takes pride in its service. 🙌

The value for money is also worth mentioning. Pizza Hut Singapore consistently delivers delicious, filling pizzas that are reasonably priced. It’s rare to find such high-quality food that’s also affordable, making it perfect for both casual meals and family gatherings. 💰 Every pizza was hearty and generous, and I left feeling completely satisfied.

Beyond the food, what really made this experience memorable was how professional, efficient, and customer-focused the entire process was — from ordering, to delivery, to the enjoyment of the meal itself. It’s rare to experience this level of consistency and care, and I truly appreciate it.

Overall, I can confidently say that Pizza Hut Singapore is one of the best pizza experiences I’ve ever had. Everything, from the smooth ordering system, fast delivery, and friendly service, to the generous, flavorful, perfectly cooked pizzas, was exceptional. 🍕💯 Whether you’re ordering for yourself, for friends, or for family, Pizza Hut Singapore delivers a complete and delightful pizza experience that’s worth every penny.

I will absolutely be ordering from them again and highly recommend them to anyone who loves delicious, high-quality pizzas paired with excellent service. Thank you, Pizza Hut Singapore, for making this such a wonderful meal — you’ve earned a loyal customer for life! ❤️🍕🇸🇬

review_text:
Ya Kun Family Cafe (Causeway Point): A Classic Singaporean Experience (4.5/5 Stars)

Rating Breakdown:

• Food: 4.5/5 (Delicious kaya toast and coffee, classic Singaporean flavors)

• Service: 4/5 (Friendly and efficient service)

• Ambiance: 4/5 (Warm and inviting atmosphere)

• Value for Money: 4/5 (Reasonable prices for the quality of the food)

Overall: 4.5/5

Donkey and I were on our way to Malaysia when we got caught in a sudden downpour. We stopped by Causeway Point to wait out the rain and decided to have lunch at the food court.  After lunch, we headed over to Ya Kun Family Cafe for a cup of coffee before continuing our journey to Malaysia.

We were surprised by the long queue when we arrived, but we were happy to wait for a taste of Ya Kun's famous kaya toast and coffee. The wait was about 25 minutes, but it was definitely worth it.

The coffee and tea at Ya Kun are always delicious. They use pure coffee and tea brews, with no water added, which makes for a truly flavorful experience.  The kaya toast is also a classic, and it was just as good as we remembered.

Ya Kun is always a favorite of ours. Whenever we see one, we can't resist stopping in for a cup of coffee or tea. It's a classic Singaporean experience.

Overall, we had a great experience at Ya Kun Family Cafe. The food was delicious, the service was friendly, and the atmosphere was warm and inviting. We'll definitely be back for another cup of coffee and a slice of kaya toast.

review_text:
I would really call this place a hidden gem (for real) because it’s been operating here within this industrial area for 5 years and no entry was ever made onto Google Map!

I stumbled upon it by chance because I was cycling past this area (yes one of the bike sharing parking is located beside this kopitiam, very hard to find). The price may be a bit steeper than those you’d find in typical hawker stalls. But I think the quality of the food can spar with BKT big names like Songfa and Founder.

The soup is the clear, garlicky and peppery type. The salted vegetable comes with a slightly sour kick. The braised dishes, which I think is a must order, is layered with the usual sweetness but with shallots, star anise and cinnamon, which is hard to come by nowadays (given the rising costs hawkers would often substitute with just soy sauce and the 5 spice powder).

Nonetheless I gave it one less star cos the food was not piping hot (I prefer it so), perhaps cos I was there near closing. I’d be curious to try it another time during lunch when the ingredients would be freshly prepared.

review_text:
Dear Nur Muslim Delight Management,

I am writing to express my disappointment and concern regarding the food I recently purchased from your outlet at 131 Marsling Rise.

On 2 August 2025, I bought several items totaling over $30, including:
1.	4 packets of Nasi Lemak – The egg in all packets was spoiled, had a sticky texture, and gave off a sour smell and taste, indicating it was no longer safe for consumption.
2.	Lontong – Similarly, the gravy had a sour and off taste, which suggests it was also spoiled.
3.	Mee Siam Kuah – The noodles were overly soggy and the overall taste was unpleasant, raising concerns about its freshness and quality.

I am very disappointed that such food was served and sold to customers. Selling spoiled food is not only unhygienic but also poses serious health risks. As a paying customer, I expected the food to be fresh, safe, and enjoyable to eat — unfortunately, this was far from the case.

I truly regret spending over $30 on this purchase and urge your team to investigate the matter seriously. Please ensure that proper food handling and storage practices are enforced to avoid endangering the health of other customers.

I would appreciate a response regarding this matter and what actions will be taken to prevent such incidents from happening again.

Thank you for your attention.

Every ingredient including ccf is priced at 90 cents each. We both had a plate of 5 ingredients + ccf @$5.40 each and added red sauce and the recommended curry sauce.

Ccf pcs are firm and smooth. Generously drizzled with sauce and curry and sprinkled with lots of sesame seeds. Red sauce is really good, tinge of sour which I love the traditional kind of sauce for CCF 👍 😋. Curry sauce is very good too, thick and super spicy 🥵🥵🥵. Overall, a filling meal and we are happy to eat something different.

They also serve ctk, ckt & fried oysters. Saw other customers having and that’s our next goal! Will be back!!

review_text:
I ordered the Lamb Shank Briyani tray via the website, which came with 2 pieces lamb shank and 4 boiled eggs and was stated to be suitable for 4–5 pax. I selected the delivery option and requested for it to arrive before iftar, as it was meant for my family’s iftar meal.

The food arrived at 6pm, nicely packed and very presentable. My family and I had it for iftar yesterday, and we truly enjoyed every part of the meal.

The lamb shank was incredibly tender, with generous portions—there were two large pieces of lamb shank. As a family who loves meat, this was perfect for us. The lamb shank gravy was rich, thick, and full of spices. We especially loved the strong, flavourful taste, as we always prefer thick, high-quality gravy, especially for curry or masala dishes.

The briyani rice was very fragrant and packed with spices—exactly how briyani should be. The portion of rice was very generous and more than enough for the five of us to enjoy during iftar.

We will definitely be ordering again soon, as long as the quality and quantity continue to be well maintained. Highly recommended!
author: Jannah Nana

review_text:
I recently tried Ajmir Briyani at the Woodlands Bazaar and I must say, it was absolutely delicious. I ordered their mutton masala briyani along with a cup of teh tarik, and both were amazing. The briyani rice was fragrant, fluffy, and full of rich spices. The mutton was tender, juicy, and cooked perfectly every bite was packed with flavour. The masala was thick, aromatic, and blended so well with the rice, making the whole dish very satisfying.

The teh tarik was the perfect drink to go with the meal. It was smooth, creamy, and had just the right balance of sweetness and tea flavour. You can really tell that care was put into preparing both the food and the drinks.
Overall, it was a very enjoyable experience. If you’re visiting the Woodlands Bazaar and craving authentic, flavourful briyani

Ajmir Briyani is definitely worth trying. I’ll surely come back again for another plate. I hope they can bring in their famous teh tarik at admiralty in future! Kudos to the entire team 👏
author: Kumaran

review_text: Honestly it was really average. I ordered the mutton briyani and the meat was an average size and it was not really tender. The rice was really average as you would get from neighbourhood coffeeshop. The price was above average and ithe briyani did not live up to the hype.
author: Huzaini Sarip

review_text:
Tried their fried chicken briyani, massage chicken mee siam briyani and their mutton briyani.
Their mutton briyani isn't too bad. Gamey enough with a nice blend of spice, I like this the most out of the 3.

Fried chicken lacks taste which is a disappointment.
The chicken masala has the same issue. Is not flavorful enough.

The curry and chilli wasn't too bad.

The briyani rice and mee siam, very disappointing, lack taste and flavor and without the curry, it just doesn't taste much.
author: G Casey

review_text: Good

restaurant_name: 九品轩炖汤 东北铁锅炖
review_text: The food was delicious and the service was attentive, but the wait could be a bit long during peak hours; 5 stars.
