restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Woodlands Link
review_text:
The soup was very well flavoured with fried ginger and XO sauce. Was also pleasantly surprised by the portion of fish slices - 5-6 thickly cut fish slices! The thick bee hoon was tender and easy to slurp unlike some places whereby it can be rather tough.

Went there at about 530pm and the food was ready in less than 5 minutes. There is plenty of seats in the food court at that time and it is air conditioned and clean.
author: Jolene Poon

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Woodlands Link
review_text:
Very powerful and thick milky and very flavourful fish soup bee hoon can be found in this zichar stall. Soup added wine & fried ginger to enhance a very smooth taste. Sliced fish is generously huge and thick. The thickest I had eaten. And it was 5 pcs huge meat with fish skin. $6.50.

😋😋😋😋😋😋😋
author: Jodeci Fine

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Woodlands Link
review_text: Location isn't very accessible (but we knew it from the beginning so it was alright).  When we reached, there was no one who bothered to attend to us and we had to ask around before obtaining the menu.  That was also when we knew that they do not honor the promo on weekends (they can really just state down isn't it?).  Fish steamboat was a delight to have, chilli crab sauce was to the salty side.  Crispy noodle was good!
author: Dylan Tan

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Woodlands Link
review_text:
Go there if you want to have a 4 hr dinner waiting for them to serve you 1 dish every 30min.

Staff can only repeat “来了” without providing explanations.

They are busy working on delivery/takeaway orders instead of serving dine in customers.
Don’t waste your time on mediocre Tze char, when you can have better meals elsewhere.
author: Xander Chua

restaurant_name: Ming Kitchen Live Seafood 名厨活海鲜 - Woodlands Link
review_text: Location is more accessible by car. Their tze char is good especially the xo fish soup noodle. Xo seafood fried rice is so not bad.
author: Alicia Lee

review_text:
There is quite a variety of foods at economical price here.
The foods ordered so far are tasty and value for money. Except goreng Pisang the banana is quite raw and dry.
The place is spacious and comfortable to dine in.
author: KKT

review_text:
Newly opened air conditioned food court run by Great Wall, the food holdings company. The tze char there serves tasty and fresh food at a reasonable price. Pop corn chicken in salted egg sauce is recommended. There are also other food stalls to patronize just like a usual food court.
Sliced fish been hoon is actually quite good with plenty of bite and a decent soup.
You may want to give the dim sum a try. I think it's almost on par with a decent dim sum restaurant.
author: FoodieDirectory

review_text:
Had dinner here for 6 pax to try their fish head pot!
Fish provided was fresh, soup was not as rich as desired, however packed a stronger milk taste.

Overall it was pleasant but have tasted better. Could have added more yam.
What's unique is the amount of vegetables given and they were pre stir fried lightly to be tossed into the soup.
The fried shallots used were generous in the soup and could be tasted from the first drink.

Service was great as they topped up the soup automatically.
Would have been better if it was used with the traditional pot and charcoal.

Place is air-conditioned and was comfortable to dine in.

As this is a foodcourt, there are other options available as well.
author: Kai Xian Wong

review_text: Nice place to have lunch or dinner! There's different varieties and the Zi Char stall is really good too! Always come here for their fish head steamboat or curry fish head as well as others.  Never fails to disappoint.
author: Roland Seh

review_text: The Zhi Char is fast, taste good and delicious for most of the dishes . Price not too expensive . Generous with the portions. The Pepper Beef & Curry Fosh Head 👍👍👍. 27 Feb 2022 , Brought Fried Rice. Again, I have to ask for extra sambal chilli 🌶.  Don't understand why they need to be so stingy on these chillies.  😟😶😒 . The reason why we order what we order was because their sambal is good. So please be more generous.😶😶😶
author: W8ll8AM S8M

review_text: This review is for Lionel at McDonald’s Woodlands Mart — really appreciate the small kindness he showed. He took the initiative to give a balloon to my boy without us even asking, and it honestly made his whole day. It’s such a simple gesture, but it shows the kind of heart and attentiveness he brings to his job. The outlet is always busy, but he still took a moment to make someone smile. These are the little things that make a huge difference, and staff like Lionel deserve to be recognised for it.
author: Chris

review_text:
Service absolutely suck here nowadays, it used to be so great with floor manager going around chatting with customers, making sure their food is served on time and correctly.

Now is just a nunch of people wayang wayang the shift away, so many wrong orders and when approached the manager at the counter is not attentive and rude and no situation awareness at all.

I am still going to visit every now and then simply I live near by but I highly not recommended this branch if i have the choice.

PS: Even though I gave the food 4 stars but the Chicken mccrispy is the absolute worst I thought I'm eating tree bark.
author: Tom Koh

review_text: Ordered on the Foodpanda app on 28 Jan 2026, this was how my Hershey McFlurry was served. The fries were very salty as well, if only Mcd has the option of selecting no salt for the fries. It’s too salty to be acceptable.
author: Sheryl Lee

review_text:
I order for a table service on 04/12/25 at 0706AM

Order Food at 0706 am
Food is ready on the counter at 0708 am
Food need to take 10 min to serve to my table serve at 0718am ?

Food has turn cold if you guys cant offer a table service kindly turn it off in the system , do not expect us to keep wait and wait for the Food . STAFF are busying chatting and laughing at the counter. Hope the management can look into it .Cant provide table service kindly OFF it .
author: Ndee Lem

review_text: Worst McD service I had. Waited for >20 mins and not served until I checked with counter and they missed out. Not even a word of apologize to the customer for the miss out. Terrible service!!! Always out of black peppers.
author: 恩惠日常小確幸JE & EU

review_text: the best kfc chicken ever. the food was so fresh and the chicken was soo juicy. I was starving the whole day and this kfc chicken was the best thing that has ever touched my tongue this year. Also when I asked to change my hot & crispy chicken breast to thigh , the manager there ( Ms Jane I believe ) was very patient even though it was very busy. thank you so much
author: Yang Tian En

review_text:
worst KFC ever, will be first and last KFC tried in Sg...
ordered Zinger box, the spicy fried chicken is super dry, feels like sitting for display whole day... no taste also....

burger bun is dry, the chicken fillet is also tasteless....
hopeless kfc
author: Jeffery Ngu

review_text: The outlet is spacious and good with nice hand wash area and washroom. Service is fast. Food quality is not that good though and cleanliness can be improved. For vegetarians you can order fries, whipped potato, coleslaw or OR bowl telling them to customize it and not add chicken. Similarly in breakfast you can get porridge without chicken as special order.
author: A

review_text:
This is not the first time 888 kfc always messed up with my grab order ...either wrong or missing item or they passed to the wrg grab driver ... - communication fails btwn staff and rider. But mostly my complaint is missing or wrong order....all they can do is to refund back. Is not about the money..is about children waiting and hungry..and time wasted ...and got to reorder and especially having plans that day or morning....

Pls improve on the services...

Thank you. I have no pblm at other area accept 888!
author: Nurul Shas

review_text:
Mar'24 - came for breakfast in the morning. Only 1 aunty prepare and serve at the counter, rather messy lar.
2023- I think it is pretty standard KFC. But my friend say it is the best KFC in Singapore.
author: Yi Lin Tan

review_text:
I recently purchased the Waffle Chicken Set Meal (almost $10) from this outlet and was disappointed with the quality.
* The chicken piece was unusually small and overly salty.
* The waffle was the only redeeming factor.
* The egg portion was satisfactory.
* Hash browns were smaller than expected.
Considering the price, the meal was not value-for-money.
Cleanliness also needs improvement - almost all chairs had noticeable stains.
Hope the management will take note and make necessary improvements.
author: Alicia Lim

review_text: Clean restaurant and fast service. But the chicken seemed to be considerably small for some reason. Ordered at 11.30am, Thursday 15 Jan 2025. Perhaps KFC Singapore standard has dropped significantly, or their chicken supplier has short-changed them on quality. Refer to photo for reference, chicken is tiny compared to my hand. And this 2-piece chicken meal is $10+.
author: Suf

review_text:
Missing order of whipped potato, la zi ji bites and cheese fries for order number 8266(just)! Total of nearly $10 worth of food missing! Kfc how can do this......

Updated:
To add on, just realised 2pieces of chicken missing too!
author: Joe Ho

review_text: Bought takeaway KFC breakfast this morning for my family, came back to find the wrap looks rather small, almost the size the of the hash brown. I felt disappointed as I always buy my KFC from there. Please ensure better quality in the future.
author: Toh Xin Yu

review_text: I really enjoyed my meal at KFC! The chicken was crispy, juicy, and full of flavor. The service was fast and friendly, and the restaurant was clean and comfortable. I always love coming here because the food quality is consistent and satisfying. Keep up the great work! 🍗😊
author: tham nguyen

review_text: So-so wanton noodle. It’s a bit dry and the chicken feet is not tender enough - the meat doesn’t fall off the bone.
author: Adrian Lee

review_text: Nice wanton mee, with sufficient level of spiciness and dry lean meat of char siew. Soup was flavorful and meat in the wanton is generous. They accept Paylah, Paynow and Grabpay. Could be better if the noodle is more springy. Price is very reasonable at $3.5 per set.
author: Alexander Reinaldo

review_text: Just an average bowl of wanton mee, nothing special. Noodle is quite bland, and meat is dry. Only good thing is price is affordable.
author: WB IsMe

review_text: Noodle not soggy but not chewy either. Acceptable. Char Siew taste 👍. Soup is nice. Sauce is 👍. Wonton is alright but just not the traditional type. Taste different but acceptable. For $3.50, it is reasonable. Can try if you are heading there. Hard to find place to seat. So go off peak hours.
author: Sophia Tan

review_text:
Massive place.
Like giant MRT station without trees,
which makes noodles & plates smaller.
And oblique characters of stall
Tasty Q noodles & hae bee chilli
petite but umami wantons & fresh dumplings
Large cavernous stall, full kitchen to roll wantons properly

author: CHIN ANG

review_text:
Update
Ordered fried ytf. Very satisfying very filling. Frying really enhance the taste yet they are don't feel oily. Cost $6 might wanna try their fried tofu or mix if possible next time.

~~~~~~~

Ordered happiness bowl for $5.

Plenty of different yong tau foo which you don't get to pick but is okay probably cost alot more if it is ordering from pick what you want yong tau.

Taste wise quit average. Fish balls and meat balls i would said are great better than average. Bouncy and tasty. Broth is definitely better than average great sweetness to it. Plenty of watercress doesn't harm either.

Sweet sauce is probably the go to. I really don't like the chili here. More sour than spicy.
author: Super Fragrance

review_text: Curry Yong Tau Foo, $4.5.  Abt 5 to 7 items, delicious, esp the curry soup base, so fragrant.
author: Jaws Lee

review_text: Staff prepared the takeaway happiness bowl in speedy mode after ordering, even I’m the only customer in the queue. All pieces of Yong Tau Foo are nice, chunky and the stuffed meat is decent for a $5 bowl. Although they don’t have the options to pick your own YTF, but all the pieces are popular items. The non-fried items are only fish and meat mixed balls, the rest are mostly fried. Their curry gravy is good as well.
author: HC Lum

review_text: Very nice and comforting soy bean based broth, with excellent portions since years ago. Their yongtaufoo pieces are very generous in size with lots of fish paste, and always taste fresh and good. Enjoy their sweet sauce and chili sauce too!
author: Jasmine Khoo

review_text: It’s value for money. There’s so many pieces of YTF in this bowl that costs just $5 + $0.50 for noodles. Good variety of ingredients. Taste however, is pretty light for liao and soup too.
author: Rennie Lee

review_text: Delicious 🤤 affordable hot and cold desserts. Stall owners always polite  and friendly. Located at Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre which is next to Admiralty MRT Station 🚉.
author: Eileen LKY (Hungry Mama)

review_text:
The chocolate taste is solid! I like it!

Aunty confirmed it's vegetarian.

Good dessert to have (instead of eating ice cream).
author: Faisal Zubaid Akbar

review_text: What on earth…their bobochacha does not even have the traditional colorful jelly. I mean, if you want to be a dessert stall, at least do it right… The sweet potato and the yam were not well brewed. Sorry but worst than koufu even..
author: Benedict Chua

review_text: Selling chin chow without straw, how to drink? Rude attitude from male cashier.
author: Shin

review_text: Visited numerous times and the toppings were just nice. Don't have a very sweet tooth but the sweetness are all just nice for me. :) Love the green bean soup!
author: Alyssa C

review_text: Used to support this stall eventhough one protein with vegetables will cost about $6.50. Unfortunately had a shock when they decided to charge $8.50 for same food I have been ordering for awhile! 1 protein 1 vegetable with rice! Shocking! I even saw an Aunty that was infront me also asking abt her order price thought that was perhaps a first timer. Hawker food that’s abit too much no wonder I don’t even see the main cook around anymore moved. Apparently she’s says not sustainable so decided to move too.
author: E

review_text: I’ve purchased the same items from this shop multiple times within the few months, and the price increased each visit by up to $1 for the exact same product. I checked my past transaction records and the changes were inconsistent. When I asked the staff, they denied any changes. Just sharing my experience so others are aware. Please don’t buy from this shop!!! Spoiled my entire day!
author: Ravathi M

review_text:
It is disappointing, dissatisfying and upsetting experience. One of the cooks said “starts 7:30am” when I clarified if nasi lemak is available (I acknowledged the sign says operate from 7am to 4pm as I clarify) at few minutes to 7am. Obviously, working adults do not have that much time to wait as we need to travel to work which takes time. So I have to compromise and change my crave from getting nasi lemak to prata. At 7:08am, two pak ciks went and they sell them the nasi lemak I wanted.

Thoughts?
author: Jacko Le

review_text:
I ordered nasi sambal goreng Paru Takeaway.  Pricelist on menu stated $5. Cashier said its $6.50; a 30% price hike. She mentioned what I ordered is not listed in the menu. She insisted it isn't the second time i asked her. I told her yes it was & price is $5. Why are you charging $6.50?

She told me Price list wasn't updated. So I had to pay $6.50. My advice was please update your price list as its misleading & I wish they had honored the menu price to me.
She assured me the price list will be updated. I'm writing this with hopes they look into the price revision updated seriously. Food is good & oh yes, as of date, this stall is also not applicable to use CDC vouchers. It would have made a nice option since this is located at Admiralty hawker centre. I hope the business owner will take this request into consideration.
author: Mas M.M

review_text:
Rude service! I clearly ordered Set A nasi lemak, yet the auntie looked at me weirdly as if I didn’t say anything. Instead of interrupting and being disrespectful, at least listen to your customers’ orders first.

How do you expect to attract customers with that kind of attitude? If you don’t want to get scolded for no reason, don’t come here!
author: Xaf Shaf

review_text:
Bought the black chicken soup for $6.00, standard size bowl, but not super boiling hot.

It came with a quarter black chicken , some herbs and roots, red dates etc. Chicken was fall off the bones, quite tender - but expected coming from the steamer. All soup are from the drawer steamer so do expect some quality being traded off there. Soup aren’t refillable so savour while it last.

A good option for a light dinner if you are around the area.
author: DataDriven Foodie

review_text: Came on a rainy evening, craving for warm soup.. They have adjusted their prices upwards again🙁🙁🙁.. Their black chicken soup is now at $7. It comes w black chicken and some chinese herbs.. This time round the soup seems more diluted.. Hope they wont increase the price anymore
author: R Tan

review_text: Ordered 梅菜扣肉饭. Meat was well-marinated. The fats looked thick but actually melts in your mouth. Went well with the 梅菜. They could have given more of the gravy though.
author: laybit

review_text: Serving varieties of herbal soup and other side dishes at a reasonable price.
author: Jimmy Chai

review_text: Bought the sichuan veg pork rib soup. Very salty. I didn't finish more than half of the veg.
author: Berta Tan

review_text:
Visit date: 22 Jan 2026
Actual rating: 3.5

Travelled a fair bit to have a go at pork chops... but, the Western stall here wasn't open (at 3pm+)!

So I thought mutton curry with boned-in meat would sate my craving 🤔😆

Thus I ordered prata, after I'd ascertained I could get curried mutton.

However, it wasn't the best of culinary experience, both bread and meat 😞

Plain prata was the "rigid" kind, quite crispy like Springleaf's. My preference is for kosong that is fluffed and not doughy; crispiness is not a key criteria.

Egg prata was also typical, but a much better eat imho.

Unfortunately, mutton meat was not tender even though the curry was fantastically flavoursome and thick! 😲

You'd have to be deft with fork and spoon (acting as the knife!) in cutting through the mutton! For a moment I was thinking about going to the Western stall to get a steak knife to saw the meat 🤣

I really did struggle to have my mutton!

Nevertheless, I do sincerely hope to see an improvement in the texture of their mutton, as the curry is really remarkable fitting of a 5 star rating 👌
author: Mark Heng (Infosphere)

review_text:
Hawker centre is airy and cool, lots of seats on weekdays. Weekend expect all the usual crowded situations expected from Hawker centres all over Singapore.
Prata from this stall is so crispy and fluffy and best eaten fresh than packet home.
To the young chefs making these delicious pratas, keep up the good work 👍🏼👍🏼. Love your pratas.
author: ngyannee

review_text: At least is daily enough (except Thursdays iirc) for me to eat Prata at Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre. Following the success of 3 Plain Pratas on 17 November 2025, i'll go for 4 Plain Pratas in the future! Worth the try for me
author: Trusten Ng Rui Han

review_text:
as far as taste goes, the prathas are pretty good i reckon. the curry that comes with it too is not so bad - just wished they could maybe include some fish curry. staff working there have been pretty friendly too, so far.

(update) fish curry seems to be available now, to go with your prathas - but the availability seems too depend on the the day.
author: Rizal Farok

review_text:
Very good service. They only take orders after completing order. Queue was orderly. Place was clean. They were courteous. No attitude shown.

Prata were all Cooked freshly. With good fish curry. Don't understand the negative reviews but those were long ago. I went today and was very good.

Keep this up would return. Long queue by the way so cannot be so bad ah 😅👍🏼
author: Kamal Raj

review_text: I’ve never gave a one star review to a food stall or restaurant, but this is really giving me a headache. The food was okay, but the counter Chinese lady’s service and attitude were so bad, like I owned her money. NEVER COME AGAIN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
author: PingYew Tan

review_text:
Food is spoilt. I ordered mala with broccoli, luncheon meat, noodle, beansprout and Taiwan sausage… and these costed me $16. Food not fresh too - felt like it’s spoilt as they have some smell…

Not coming back again
author: Michelle Tan

review_text:
大辣was disappointing, oily , not spicy at all for someone that ate 中辣 all the time this is not at all spicy . and this mala have no 麻椒。

finished eating for respect of food and money
author: Kerine

review_text: Located in a hot and smelly corner of the hawker centre (right outside the toilet). The ingredients are not fresh and have a stale smell but its expensive. They also mixed other materials that are not ordered in the mix. Very dishonest. Instead of rectifying the situation, the stall assistant also became defensive and said it was us that order the items. Be warned when ordering from this stall. I would stay far, far away.
author: Brad Ang

review_text: The mala is quite affordable,  picked quite lot of stuff - pork, chicken, pork belly, luncheon meat etc ... costs around $15. Taste wise is a salty, not spicy for  小 辣.
author: c tzehow

review_text: Went there at 5.15am on Wednesday and there isit anyone. Ordered the bacon eggs sandwich, the sandwich itself was great but the hash brow tasted dry.  The ice coffee was full of milk which makes it bland. Nice & friendly dude took my order and pass me a straw when I was seated.
author: Elgin Ng (Ginny)

review_text: The dirtiest LJS outlet that I ever encounter. Restaurant is not even busy but yet all dustbins are overflowing. Saw cockroaches crawling. Staffs busy chit- chatting and scrolling handphones behind the counter rather than taking care of restaurant cleanliness. Staff wearing slippers while working? Is this even allow, restaurant no proper dress code?
author: Fendi Saini

review_text:
A Truly Disappointing Dining Experience

My recent visit was profoundly disappointing.  From the moment we arrived, the experience was marred by a lack of attention to detail and basic cleanliness. The floors and tables were sticky and oily, immediately creating an unappetizing atmosphere.

Unfortunately, the food failed to redeem the experience. The presentation was haphazard and uninspired.  More critically, the dishes themselves were poorly executed.  The food was excessively salty, burnt in places, and swimming in oil(look at the plate and you will know how oily the food are. Only managed to eat the scrambled egg and the rest were thrown.  The overwhelming greasiness left an unpleasant aftertaste and a lingering feeling of discomfort.

Overall, I cannot recommend.  The combination of poor hygiene and substandard food quality renders it a place to avoid.  I hope management addresses these serious issues to improve the dining experience for future patrons.
author: Garry Ng

review_text: I was waiting for my number for take away.  I have been checking the monitor if my food is ready. I never see the number at all. Maybe i missed out. Not sure. Staff are putting take aways on to the counter. I noticed that there are no accompanying number to check whether thats your food or not. I finally catch to ask the staff  how come i didnot notice my number on the ready to pick up. He said the number will only be there for 1 minute. It will disappear after that. What a hussel. And the staff is lacking customer service. As if he is telling me ” not his problem” , “its like that” He kept on mentioning about the 1 min on the screen. Pls value your customers. I just went off because i dont want to waste my energy and we wont get to a final amicable conclusion . He just want to insist that 1 minute on the screen! The end.
author: ma agnes israel

review_text: Several times make a take away order, The more I asked for more crumbs, the staff will not put any crumbs at all! I don't understand their attitudes what is their understanding of put more crumbs. In fact I don't mind paying extra for it but end up all 5 sets orders has no crumbs.
author: Ross MD

review_text:
The rojak is nice. All the ingredients are fresh and the prawn paste mixture is fragrant and not overly sweet.
The popiah is okay only. The sweet sauce used here has a peculiar taste.
author: Jacob TAN

review_text: this Rojak stall is located inside Kampung admiralty. Best Rojak Ever!!!, Surprising no much ppl review it. Try it and you will never eat other Rujak stall like what I do.
author: Johar Kwan

review_text:
Poh Piah wrapping abit loose, but taste quite good.
Rojak to me some what average lower abit..
author: KKT

review_text: Very rude popiah seller.pointed his (maybe her -not sure the person’s gender) finger at customer and scolded her because he/her can’t cope with the order.
author: Miss Rain

review_text: Nice and decent rojak with option to add youtiao for $1
author: Alexander Reinaldo

review_text:
As far as I am bothered to find out, there are 2 baked rice reviews from this stall. 1 of them is a bit harsh (square cheese and what not), while the other seems a bit too good to be true (sounded like they savoured paradise while eating the baked rice)

I would say it meets my expectations of being very DIY vibes, and having a small portion of meat. I think you’ll be better off buying a chicken chop or something from this stall.
author: Steve Deng

review_text: Absolutely love the western food here at kampung admiralty hawker level 2. Pictured is the chicken chop spaghetti. The chicken chop here is my favourite, very lean and tender meat. I usually order the breaded fish and chips as well. The mains with spaghetti and chips(fries) are great, though the rice is ordinary. The young owners are very friendly as well, great service overall.
author: Sebastian Ng

review_text: Ordered the Fish and Chip. Average.
author: Peter Rock Steady Crew

review_text: Highly recommended 👍. Affordable, delicious, great chicken chop experience.  Very friendly owners.
author: Freddy Chong

review_text: Generous portion at really affordable prices. The chicken chop we ordered cost us less than $6. Would definitely come back again
author: Luna Tan

review_text: Good old school pepper soup Bakuteh in singapore. Peppery soup but notspicy with sweet finishing. Meat is full of soup aroma, chewy, more fats and pretty delicious but chopped randomly so fragmented bones. The chilli padi is the spice if you experience the soup spicy, actually not the soup. Pretty decent as a lot of soup a bowl and meats for $6.00. Next time will try the braised meat. Saw a lot of young people takeaway while old folks like me likes to order Bakuteh.
author: Asia Apparel

review_text:
A pretty decent Bak kuh teh stall in the food centre located at admiralty MRT.

There are 2 queues (1 to order food and the other to wait for the food to be cooked).

It was raining and we wanted something to warm our stomach. This stall had a queue so we tried it.

Taste was good. Not too much pepper and soup is also not over salty. Just the right amount to warm our stomach.
author: Kevin Y

review_text: Best Bak kut teh in the North. Pork rib super tender, peppery bkt soup definitely not thirsty and no rock sugar taste . Salted veg & tau kee was excellent . Reasonable price .... Need not travel to balestier rd  for that expensive BKT anymore.
author: 东风

review_text: Good food. But sadly the inflation is getting in. All item increase from 20% to 40%. Pig’s Trotter increases from $4 to $5.6. Serving also a bit smaller. :(

author: Calvin Yang

review_text:
This hawker centre offers a good variety of traditional local food at reasonable prices, making it a pleasant spot for everyday meals.
For vegans and vegetarians, there are several welcoming options. Gong Fu Yuan Vegetarian serves a range of Chinese vegetarian dishes with many vegan-friendly choices, while Xi De Li offers classic fried vegan snacks that are both nostalgic and satisfying.

Even non-vegetarian stalls provide meatless options. Kopi Kiosk includes vegetarian selections within its Signature Breakfast Sets, Hao Cheng Kee Carrot Cake offers a meat-free carrot cake that’s flavourful and comforting, and Saamsudeen Indian Muslim Stall has various Prata options suitable for those avoiding meat.

Overall, it’s a convenient and enjoyable place to find tasty local food, with plenty of choices for plant-based diners.
author: Yellow Bear

review_text: Had He Le Rong porridge. Presentation of food pleasing, good choice of food for a cooling weather in an indoor hawker centre. Some pigeons eyeing on your food here and there, but overall place is quite clean
author: timoo tee

review_text:
Modern and open space hawker centre with high ceilings and big as fan (sorry might get banned for spelling the real name). The food here is affordable but taste wise, very plain and basic, catered to the old people. The Bak Kut teh that food king reviewed is over hyped (see my review for this). Pleasantly surprised by the ah Ma meesua when I gave it a second chance. It tastes better when dining in than take away. Avoid egg tarts at all costs as it tastes like rock. Friend say it’s usually good but when he bought at 8pm, the taste is bad.

One downside is the seats. Very hard to find proper seats especially during peak hours as the seats are all weirdly shaped and built for 8-10 people. The designer of this place doesn’t know that loners with no family or friends exist in the society. Even for family of 2, also need to share table. I guess, if you like to make friends with strangers sitting at the same table, do give here a visit.
author: Truth Fairy

review_text:
It was hard to choose been a few times for hot to take pics .
. Malay m Chinese food is good

author: Carrie Bradshaw

review_text:
It’s only my third visit here after so many years, and I’m surprised by how popular the Muslim food stalls are at Kampung Admiralty Hawker Centre—even on a weekday dinner hour. The queues were so long I almost fainted just looking at them!

I ended up choosing Soon Kee Roasted Delights. The roast pork skin was crispy and flavourful—loved the crunch. The lower layer had quite a bit of thick, soft fat, which fans of that texture would definitely enjoy. I even added some chicken rice chilli to my plain white rice (I know, unorthodox), and it turned out surprisingly tasty. 🤤

Although the space is large and not too crowded, I still had a hard time finding a seat. 😅

But hey, taste and service are always subjective. ☺️

review_text: The food is overall nice and affordable at the same time . I had a great meal there, i ordered the hotplate chicken and it was good .

I’ve decided to write this review after visiting this establishment several times.

The food consistently meets expectations for a high quality chain. It is flavorful, well prepared, and noticeably healthier than many of its competitors, without sacrificing taste in the process.

What truly stands out, however, is the professionalism, courtesy, and genuine friendliness of the staff, which are beyond reproach.

Thank you all for the excellent service.
author: Nuevo Occidente

review_text:
I would like to complement this young chinese guy who works in this Kampung Admiralty MOS Burger outlet.

Very helpful and friendly. Provided good customer services to the customers.

I saw him patiently assisting a old uncle with lots of queries and payment issue.

And also maintaining the area neatly and cleanly when no one is watching.

Well done young men!
author: Chee Hao Lim

review_text:
Yesterday I was experiencing sudden stomach cramps, nausea, suspected gastric attack and I stopped by Mos Burger Kampung Admiralty outlet to grab a quick meal.
Despite being in a rush and not feeling well, I received not just timely service, but also thoughtful care: San kindly offered me a cup of warm water without me having to ask. That small but considerate gesture made a real difference to me in the moment.
In my view, going the extra mile in this way exemplifies the highest standards of customer service. It is rare and refreshing to experience staff who are not only efficient but also empathetic and attentive to customers’ needs beyond just the transaction.
I sincerely hope San’s thoughtful act is recognised and appreciated by the company. Her kindness reflects very positively on MOS Burger’s brand and the kind of culture and service you promote.
Thank you for hiring and empowering people like San. Please pass along my thanks and commendation to her.
author: Evangeline Koh

author: Kai Siong Leck

review_text:
First time eating here and had a bad experience. Ordered pork ribs noodles but noodles came semi cooked. Approached the cashier and told her about it, she said “it’s like that one” and tried to dismiss me. After telling her I can’t eat this bowl of uncooked noodles, she passed the bowl to the cook.
Guess what, instead of throwing in a fresh batch of noodles to cook, she threw in the noodles from before. I already took a bite of noodles before realising it’s uncooked…
No issues with the taste of food but the hygiene levels here remains to be seen.

review_text: food poisoning waiting to happen store! was there around 7pm and was served by an aunty (not friendly at all), i asked for takeaway, while she was picking up dirty trash and scraps in the floor and placing it next to the chopping board (i kid u NOT..), she proceeds to grab a container and ask me what i want, 0 hygiene 0 awareness, i asked her why she never wash her hands and walk off, saving my family from inadvertently getting food poisoning 💀
author: Cherie Lim

review_text:
Food is mediocre. Can eat. But the staff I have been here twice, and twice I felt mocked at when I make my orders. I don’t know if it’s because of my looks or what but they make it VERY OBVIOUS especially the second time I was there. The two aunties were packing my food and one whispered to another, then both giggled.

I find this EXCEPTIONALLY RUDE and unnecessary. In service line, we respect all our customers regardless race, gender and looks! Will never patronise again and for all of you out there, don’t risk yourself being placed in an uncomfortable situation when ordering food. Don’t let this experience spoil your day.
author: jagga bee

review_text:
Place was ok, standard clean.

Buffet was not that appetising.. $30 for a wkend dinner excluding gst and service charge.

1) upon payment, was asked either mee goreng or nasi goreng. Mee came with a plate of fried dishes - onion rings, nuggets, mantou.

Upon leaving, I asked "there's no hot food? Staff said they gave us the mee goreng or nasi goreng and the fried dish. I told her I thought there's self service food? She said we could have told her and they will prepare. I mean how would we know if you never tell us?

2) food wise the selection was ok, not much. Variety of different meats BUT no label. Marination was not optimal, other buffets are way better.

3) Quail eggs were abit off. Even after cooking for some time, the yolks was still soft.

4) dessert was only 2 flavours of ice cream - chocolate and vanilla

5) drinks no hot drinks, just lime and rose syrup.

6) staffs was fast and attentive to clear plates and helpful to want to help in the temperature setting in case customers doesn't know.

7) location is good as it near mrt and place still sells ala carte food.

I've been there before Yassin have the hot pot/bbq. I find the ala carte food was better.

Imo, if u do come here, better to get the ala carte dishes.
author: Hello Chester

review_text:
First time trying this buffet.

Buffet price is cheap. SGD$ 22.90 per person. Every time I walk🚶🏻‍♀️ pass this restaurant, it’s pretty empty. Not sure how they can still survive cos the restaurant is huge. They have some big long tables so it’s suitable for big dine in groups .

Their chiller not sure if it’s very cold temperature or what, but whenever open the sliding doors , so much smoke 💨 come out , so we can’t see the ingredients clearly. My daughter feels they should have label the ingredients so we know what meat we are taking.

The meat 🥩 like not marinated and not sure if it’s frozen many days old so after grilled, they taste dry and hard. I ate 1 piece. My daughter said she had to chew chew but didn’t eat the meat in the end but 🤮 onto the plate.

The fried items : fried pandan mantou ( should have provided condensed milk for the fried mantou though ) , chicken nuggets and onion rings taste good 👍🏻, we finished them all.

Can choose 2 soup bases and either fried rice or fried noodles.

The fried noodles was 🆗 but cos of the grilled meat made me lose my appetite, so I didn’t finish the fried noodles.

I chose both soup bases chicken soup as the other 2 soup bases are tom yam and mala and my daughter doesn’t eat spicy food. The chicken soup base a little bland.

The vanilla and chocolate ice cream 🍨 taste creamy and nice .

The rose syrup drink and lime drink are 🆗 too. Rose syrup drink not too sweet and lime drink not too sour.

Take note they have Chinese New Year surcharge.

I won’t go back again.
author: Eileen LKY (Hungry Mama)

review_text: The menu has a good variety of local favourites, and most dishes are flavourful and reasonably priced. Service is generally friendly, though it can be a bit slow during peak hours when the place gets crowded. Seating is simple but cozy, making it suitable for families and casual meals. Overall, a decent spot around Admiralty for affordable comfort food
author: Muhammad Syahrul

review_text:
I had dinner at around 6:45pm for two pax. The service staff and food were good, and we had a pleasant dining experience overall.

However, upon making payment, we were attended to by the manager at the cashier who informed us that their system was down and only cash payments were accepted. NETS, credit card, and CDC vouchers were unavailable. I noticed that the receipt was printed at 7:15pm, which suggests there was ample time to inform customers earlier that the payment system had issues.My total bill for 2 pax is $104.10

Unfortunately, there was no apology offered—only a statement that it was cash only. This could have been handled more professionally. What if customers did not carry enough cash? It would have been a very inconvenient situation.
In addition, the Chinese New Year surcharge should be clearly displayed at the entrance before customers enter the restaurant, rather than surprising them when they see the final bill.

I believe the situation could have been managed better by the manager. Clear communication and a simple apology would have made a big difference.
author: Fafa Abdullah

review_text: We dined in for lunch and had a wonderful experience. There was no wait for a table, and the staff were incredibly attentive throughout our meal. They constantly checked on us, topped up our soup, monitored the burner, and even helped us exchange items when needed. Everyone was very welcoming, and their warm service made our visit especially enjoyable. Highly recommended!
author: Fiqahh Johar

review_text: The standards for this chang fen have really dropped. The texture is disappointing—soft and mushy, almost like it’s been sitting overnight. It lacks the freshness and smooth, springy bite that good chang fen should have. Definitely not the quality I used to expect.
author: Alicia Lim

review_text: Thanks to the Shift Manager today. She was very helpful, great & nice. When I arrived she told me to check the order first before leaving the outlet & on the spot she took my drinks out from the fridge after I’ve done checking my food order. When i reached home my drinks still cold. Thank you once again to the shift manager.. 😊
author: Wawan Wan

review_text:
Ordered chicken curry pizza & it came curry potato pizza, ridiculous I paid for potato curry pizza?? So disappointed in the service
Kitchen crew need to improve & set things right. I’m not asking for a free FOOD. I’m paying for my meal. Disappointing outlet
author: Kannan Kanna

review_text: Would like to compliment on the fast and prompt service by the boys working at JMM outlet earlier today. Ensuring my pizza are hot. Ordered a couple of boxes and it was still not enough because my guests were too hungry. Really love the drumplets compared others. Looking forward to order more during CNY. Thanks for the great service!
author: Havana Buttercup

review_text: Had a really nice meal here! The staff were super friendly and the service was quite fast. Pizza came out hot and fresh, and the toppings were generous. The place was clean and comfortable too. Overall a good experience and I’ll definitely come back again 👍
author: Yan Aryan

review_text: Food was good! Pizza hut is my favourite. Served by Anisah who so friendly!! Was always smiling despite being very busy. She was also upfront about the wait time.Will definitely order from here again!
author: Fian Iswandy

review_text: My meal at Hei Sushi in Sembawang Shopping Centre was excellent. The salmon sashimi, hotate (scallop), oysters, and Hana Maki were all incredibly fresh and delicious, with standout flavors and quality. The service was prompt and attentive—we were seated immediately, and the staff ensured our food arrived smoothly despite the quiet, uncrowded setting of a weekday afternoon. Overall, it was a relaxed, enjoyable dining experience with fresh sushi and great service. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be returning!
author: Mrs Sim

review_text:
Visited on 17 July 2025 at 7:30 PM and was shocked by the lack of basic customer service. No one was at the entrance to greet us—we stood there for 10 minutes. An older lady with short hair finally came out from the kitchen, glued to her phone. We had to call her four times before she even looked up, and she didn’t look happy to serve us at all.

Only after we were seated did the rest of the staff appear. Where is the host? Where is the manager? The elderly staff were cold and rude, with no sense of customer care. The only decent service came from a younger staff member who was at least polite.

This outlet is a mess—no leadership, poor attitude, and totally unprofessional. It’s no wonder the place was nearly empty compared to other restaurants nearby. I won’t be coming back, and I don’t recommend this place to anyone who values proper service.
author: yazami halim

review_text: First time dine in at Hei Sushi. It is pleasant experience. Order can be done  using QR code. There are varieties of Sushi plates on moving conveyor by the side of tables. The air conditioner is really great for such hot weather. Food quality wise, I think it is matching the price, not bad. My kids enjoyed the food here 😋
author: YK Lai

review_text:
I’m truly disappointed with my recent visit. The quality of the sushi has dropped tremendously, and there were very limited choices on the conveyor belt. The Japanese rice was hard as well, which made the experience even more upsetting. I chose Hei Sushi to celebrate my wife and daughter, but sadly it turned out to be the wrong decision. It was a very disappointing experience.

Hei Sushi, I sincerely hope you can step up the quality of your food and service. There are not many halal sushi restaurants in Singapore, and many of us genuinely hope to continue supporting you.
author: Firmansyah Kamsani

review_text: Food was served very slowly perhaps due to the timing and kitchen staffs shortage. Food taste was okay but waited for too long and became full quite quickly. Overall, could not finished but the service staff was accommodating to help pack the unfinished food.
author: Erin Yap

review_text:
Came here to have a sushi fix. This was the first time we came to this branch. It was almost a full house but there were still a few seats available.

There are some menus that need to be ordered through staff, like miso soup, chawanmushi, tempura etc. The rest we can pick from the sushi conveyor. There are three color plates in correspondence to their prices, ranging from $1.50++ to $3++.

The tea uses tap system on the table, with utensils like chopstick and soy sauce. However, the wasabi and ginger are on conveyor belt, which is inconvinient. I like ginger but had to wait for one or sometimes two rounds to get it. And the ridiculous thing is the spoon. There are on the conveyor belt as well! We waited for a long time to eat a puding and settled to reuse a spoon after my chawanmushi arrived. Seriously though, why the spoons have to be on the conveyor ride?

The conveyor also has many desserts that belong to the fridge. I don’t want limp mille crepes and unappetizing looking cake.

The taste, some were good, but some were disappointing. The chawanmushi was pretty good, I had two servings (it uses shallow bowl and mostly because there were not many other varieties that I like). I am a fan of classic ebi sushi but all it has is the semi transparent crunchy ebi that tastes like those abomination frozen prawn that dominate Singapore food now. This is very dissapointing because that is my main to go when eating sushi. The salmon is good, ebiko, tofu, tamagoyaki are okay. The spicy mushroom in the bowl, not sure what is the name, is good. The jellyfish taste is standard, however, the eating experience is borderline repulsive. It was frigging long! Because of that it was hard to chew and slimy to swallow.

The lack of variety of other basic sushi like kappa maki to clean the palate, endamame, yasai tempura, is dissapointing.

Another thing to note, the size of the sushi is almost half of the normal sushi I eat elsewhere. The price became not cheap plus the high ++.

Based on those reasons, I won’t be back anytime soon.

review_text: If you’re looking for a place that delivers authentic Cantonese flavours while also surprising you with thoughtful modern touches, East Bistro is a must-visit. Tucked away yet consistently buzzing with repeat customers, the restaurant strikes a balance between traditional comfort dishes and contemporary interpretations that still stay true to Cantonese roots. One of the standout highlights is their Vinegar Pork Trotter—a dish I would strongly recommend to anyone who loves this classic. East Bistro executes it with remarkable finesse. The trotter is braised to perfection: tender, deeply flavourful, and so soft it practically melts the moment it touches your tongue. The vinegar is well-balanced—fragrant, not overpowering, and harmonising beautifully with the natural richness of the pork. It’s easily one of the best renditions I’ve had in recent memory. Another dish that deserves special mention is the Pao Fan. This is not your average serving; it’s hearty, generous, and clearly meant for sharing. The broth carries a depth of flavour that speaks of long simmering, and when poured over the rice, it creates that soothing, comforting texture Pao Fan lovers crave. I would recommend having at least four people at the table if you plan to order it—any fewer, and you might find the portion a little overwhelming, though deliciously so. For something with a modern twist that still pays tribute to classic Cantonese flavours, don’t miss the Sweet and Sour Pork on Ice. This dish continues to be a crowd favourite, and for good reason. The pork is crisp and glossy, with the sauce striking that ideal balance of tangy and sweet—but what truly sets it apart is the presentation on ice. The cold plate keeps the pork crisp for longer and adds a refreshing contrast that elevates the entire experience. Overall, East Bistro delivers a satisfying blend of familiarity and innovation.

We placed our order at 3:05 PM and were told to wait for the 6 pcs Hot & Crispy Bites. Around 3:20 PM, my colleague checked at the counter, but staff looked unsure and asked what we had ordered. By 3:35 PM, still no update, so I approached the manager, who seemed unaware and suggested replacing the item. I insisted on waiting, and she said it needed to be cooked again. The buzzer only rang at 3:42 PM — over 30 minutes later.

What’s disappointing is that no one apologized, not even the manager. The team clearly forgot our order and made no effort to recover the situation. Even after such a long wait, the food was not served to us directly. I understand there was an NSF audit, but customer service should still come first. Very poor coordination and service today.

Suggestion: Please retrain staff on communication, order tracking, and proper service recovery when handling delays.

I hope you will look into this matter seriously and take steps to improve service standards at the KFC Sun Plaza outlet.

Order #3901

Absolutely terrible experience.

By 3:30am the food still hadn’t arrived, and the new rider dispatched said he couldn’t find my address. Why isn’t GPS being used properly for deliveries in this day and age?

review_text:
This review is purely based on my own opinion and personal taste.

Patronise Sabrina’s Kitchen and ordered a fairly wide range of dishes so I could get a good sense of their cooking. Ordered Assam stingray, sambal brinjal, sambal lady fingers, tahu goreng, mutton rendang, black sauce squid, and a few others.

To be honest, most of the sauces and gravies leaned heavily towards a salty profile, but without the full depth and complexity you would have expect from a rempah and spices based dishes. The best way I can describe it is, it felt like almost as if after cooking, the kitchen realised the sauce was insufficient, added a fair bit of water, then compensated by adding salt to bring out the saltiness and resulting in dishes just having its saltiness, but lacking of the spices' and rempah's aroma. E.g The sambal brinjal and lady fingers were cook well, but again, the sambal didn’t carry the fragrance and tasted flat overall.

Nothing was outright bad, but nothing stood out either. The dishes felt flat, and missing that extra something that makes you want to go back for more.

In my own opinion, it’s not terrible, but also not particularly fantastic. If you’re looking for bold rempah flavours, aromatic gravies, and dishes with strong character, this might fall a bit short of expectations.

That said, taste is subjective, and others may enjoy it more than I did. For me personally, I was hoping for more depth, more fragrance in the cooking.

restaurant_name: Xing Hua Delights 回味轩兴化菜馆
review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️
Had a great dinner at Xing Hua Delights 回味轩兴化菜馆 @ Sembawang—a clean, casual restaurant serving authentic Henghua (Xing Hua) cuisine at friendly prices. The place is simple yet well-maintained, and the comfortable environment makes it suitable for families and everyday meals. No long waits, and the food came out promptly.

We ordered several dishes, and all of them exceeded expectations:
•	Xing Hua Lor Mee: The broth was rich, thick, and full of depth. Smooth and comforting with a nice balance of savory flavors. Noodles had a good bite and absorbed the broth well mix, this dish alone is worth returning for.
•	Re-fried Sliced Pork: A standout dish! tender pork with a lovely wok hei (wok-fried aroma). Slightly crisp on the edges and packed with flavor. A must-try for meat lovers.
•	Homemade Prawn Rolls (Hei Zho): These were juicy, well-seasoned, and not overly greasy. You could taste the freshness of the ingredients crispy on the outside, moist inside.
•	Cabbage Stewed Tofu Soup: A gentle, homestyle soup perfect to balance out the richer dishes. The broth was light but flavorful, with soft cabbage and tofu that had absorbed the soup beautifully.
•	Deep-fried Pork: Crispy on the outside, tender inside. Not oily, and well-seasoned as great as a side to share.

We were also pleasantly surprised by the reasonable prices. Portions were generous and satisfying, making it a great alternative to Putien. While Putien offers a more upscale experience, Xing Hua Delights gives you equally delicious traditional dishes at a more wallet-friendly price are definitely a worthy replacement for regular dining.

Service was polite and efficient. Staff were friendly, and the overall experience was smooth and pleasant.

In summary:
✔️ Clean and comfortable setting
✔️ Authentic Xing Hua (Henghua) dishes
✔️ Generous portions & wallet-friendly pricing
✔️ Flavourful, satisfying, and homely cooking

If you’re craving traditional Henghua dishes like Lor Mee or prawn rolls, this is a hidden gem in Sembawang you shouldn’t miss. We’ll definitely be back to try more!

restaurant_name: Leaf Corner Sembawang Vegetarian 慈素餐馆
review_text:
Very disappointed with our reunion dinner experience here. Despite making a reservation in advance and paying a deposit, the food took a very long time to arrive.

Unfortunately, the quality of the dishes did not justify the $368 package price. The yusheng (green veg portion) tasted sour and did not seem fresh. The shark fin soup was very watery, and the mango sago dessert was also diluted and tasteless — it felt like there was barely a spoonful of sago in it. Even the fried rice lacked flavour.

It is surprising that such dishes were allowed to be served during a reunion dinner, which is supposed to be a special and festive occasion. Overall, it was not worth the price. I would have rather had instant noodles.

While making payment, we also overheard other diners sharing similar feedback about their experience, which shows that this was not an isolated case.

We shared our feedback with the staff, but instead of acknowledging the issue, they shared with us and insisted the food was fresh. They also mentioned that due to Chinese New Year, ingredients were kept to a bare minimum — which is even more disappointing given the premium pricing.

For comparison, we have had their regular (non-Chinese New Year) dishes before and they were much better. Unfortunately, the festive package did not meet the usual standard.

Sadly, this experience fell far below expectations.

review_text:
I’ve had this place on my wishlist for a long time after seeing a private dining chef Henry post about it! Since I was finally in the Sembawang area, I decided to give it a try. To be honest, I was quite surprised to see it only has a 3-star rating on Google, because our experience was much better than that.

We ordered a few dishes to share:
• Roasted Duck
• Mui Choy Kai Lan (梅菜芥蓝)
• Cantonese Soup (霸王花例汤)
• Salted Fish Pork Patty (咸鱼肉饼)

The Kai Lan and the Soup were our absolute favorites. The Kai Lan was very fresh and crunchy (not old/tough at all) and had a great amount of wok hei. The soup was naturally sweet, very flavorful (入味), and clearly boiled for a long time.

The best part? The food wasn't overly salty, and we didn't feel thirsty at all after the meal, which usually means they don't go heavy on the MSG.

The service was good, and we noticed a steady stream of people walking in just to collect their takeaway orders—always a good sign for a neighborhood spot!

We will definitely be back again to try other dishes. Don't let the 3-star rating fool you; it’s worth a visit!

Enjoy

review_text:
There's a reason why people keep coming back here even though their noodles are kinda pricey for a hawker dish - Oil Town serves one of the best and most authentic Sarawak Kolo Mees in Singapore.

I usually go for the premium version of the original kolomee ($8) because, apart from the delicious noodles and minced pork, it comes with a generous portion of fried pork rinds and fried shallots & garlic. Some diners might like to add a portion of wantons ($1) to complement the meal, but the wanton seasoning oddly made them taste more like siew mai / siumai to me.

For those who can tolerate a bit of heat, do ask for their dried chilli flakes to go along with the noodles.

Oil Town, which is probably named after the Sarawak town of Miri, where the first Malaysian oil well was discovered, offers a few versions of kolomee here, including the red version which is tossed in char siew sauce. The stall owner is also a humble and friendly chap who's a lot more chatty when he's not busy churning out back to back bowls of noodles.

Do note that this is located in a very small coffeeshop so it might be challenging to get a seat during the breakfast and lunch peak hours.

review_text:
Oil Town Sarawak Kolo Mee, located at 285 Yishun Ave 6, #01-02, Singapore, is a hidden gem serving up delicious and authentic Sarawakian noodles. This humble stall has garnered a loyal following among locals and tourists alike, thanks to its commitment to delivering a taste of Sarawak in every bite.

Taste

The star of the show at Oil Town Sarawak Kolo Mee is undoubtedly the noodles. The curly, pale yellow noodles are springy and perfectly cooked, with a slight bite that is characteristic of authentic kolo mee. The noodles are tossed in a blend of shallot oil, soy sauce, and chili, creating a fragrant and savory base.

The minced pork and char siew (barbecued pork) add a satisfying meaty element to the dish. The pork is tender and flavorful, complementing the noodles beautifully. The addition of pork lard also contributes to the overall richness and depth of flavor.

Price

Oil Town Sarawak Kolo Mee offers excellent value for money. A standard bowl of kolo mee is priced at just $5, which is quite big for the price. Considering the quality of the ingredients and the authenticity of the dish, this price point is more than reasonable.

Ambience

The stall itself is small and unassuming, with limited seating available. However, this adds to the charm of the place, as it feels like a genuine Sarawakian hawker stall. The space is clean and well-maintained, with a friendly and efficient staff to ensure a smooth dining experience.

Authenticity

One of the standout features of Oil Town Sarawak Kolo Mee is its commitment to authenticity. The owner, who hails from Sarawak, has carefully crafted the recipe to ensure that the noodles taste just like they would in Kuching. The use of traditional ingredients and cooking methods sets this stall apart from other kolo mee offerings in Singapore.

Conclusion

If you're craving a taste of Sarawak without the need to travel, Oil Town Sarawak Kolo Mee is the perfect solution. With its delicious noodles, flavorful toppings, and unbeatable price, this stall is a must-visit for anyone who appreciates authentic and satisfying Sarawakian cuisine. Don't miss out on this hidden gem in Yishun!

I had also clearly told the staff to hold the cooking first as we were waiting for our family members to arrive and might change the order. She then went to the kitchen and came back telling us that the prawns had already been cooked — but it was not the cereal prawn we wanted.
