Sorry but no.

Wanted a crispy waffle, was told their recipe can't make crispy. Fair enough. Well, I definitely got a little crispy lump of flour 🙃 (there was more, threw both waffle away)

Based on my observation of how the uncle spoke, I don't think the owners/staff are happy running the biz.

I try not to give negative reviews on Google but I think it's a good platform for owners to understand where to improve on and such.
author: Eugene Chan

review_text:
A little shop run by a humble couple that used to sell these snacks at Pasar malam! The takoyaki was freshly made and the sauces were generously given. It is so yummy! :)

Perfect for a snack! 😋
author: Hazel Faith

review_text: Great homemade taste ! Really brings back the memories... A convenient takeaway outlet. Good for a small snack after a nearby meal. Will definitely come back to support !
author: Nomis Haes

review_text: Below average unauthentic snacks made by common folks. Not tasty and less value for money.
author: Gary Ng

review_text: Surprised to find a shop at Jalan Tampang selling traditional "TuTu Kueh". Nowadays it is not easy to find nice handmade TuTu Kueh. Enjoyed all the favours, from peanut, coconut, chocolate. Sometimes you don't need to have a lot of favours, to me this is good enough. I tried Thai Green Tea, I really love drinking it as I have never tried it before. My daughter loves the Sausage Egg Roll (normal flavour), she said yummy yummy.  A humble nice couple running the business. Kindly be patient and understanding if they are busy as they have online platform orders from Grab, Food Panda and Deliveroo🤗  The price is reasonable, I will be back for their snack. Trying out their takoyaki too 👍🏻 😊.  It is not easy to do business nowadays ever since the pandemic. Come down and support them.
author: waytochrist Faith

review_text: Dinner was a reasonable $19.90/pax for seafood and meat spread. Lots of varieties of marinated chicken and pork, seafood are all fresh, including prawns, crayfishes, baby lobsters, green mussels, squid, flower crabs, and many more! We especially enjoyed the garlic pork and cajun chicken! Their Thai red and green chilli sauces are delightful, in fact, the best mookata chilli sauces I’ve had so far! Will definitely recommend to others and revisit again soon!
author: Sara “Hunter” K

review_text:
Came down for a dinner meetup to enjoy some long awaited mookata.

Took the 19.90 seafood mookata which included all meats, vegetables and a fridge full of seafood choices. They also have a loklok option where you grab skewers and the stuff for loklok which will be seasoned with their spices after frying.

Do refer to pictures uploaded for the variety of ingredients available.

It is definitely value for money. Staff were rather friendly. Will return for more
author: Bryan Fang

review_text:
Family Mookata in Yishun Northview Bizhub is a cosy spot for steamboat and grill lovers. This restaurant offers fantastic value at $14.90 nett for a protein (non seafood) buffet and $19.90 nett for a seafood option.

Parking is pretty easy if you are driving, the location is however only accessible by buses or hired vehicles.

The ingredients are fresh, with a good mix of meats, seafood, and vegetables. These are neatly stored in refrigerated counters, keeping them fresh and hygienic. The soup base is flavourful, and the marinated meats cook well on the grill without sticking.

It offers a “lok lok” option for all buffet that adds to the variety of ways you can have your meat fix. The cheese dips are also free flow here too, a real good value.

Service here is friendly and prompt, and the atmosphere is casual and welcoming, ideal for small groups or family gatherings.

Prices are reasonable for the quality and variety offered, the value is hard to beat for such a good combination of price, service and quality!
author: bh

review_text:
The meat and seafood were very fresh, and the Thai dipping sauces really elevated the whole experience — very authentic flavors.
The soup base gets more fragrant as you cook, and it’s honestly hard to stop eating!
Prices are reasonable, portions are generous, and the service was excellent.
A great spot for gathering with friends or family.
Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys Family Mookata BBQ and hotpot! 🔥
author: Kelvin Fon

review_text:
We had a really good lunch, just for $14.90 .. it’s an all-you-can-eat mookata! A buffet that doesn’t kill your wallet 💸

* 🥩 Free-flow meats & vegs buffet starts - $14.90
* 🦐 Seafood upgrade - $19.90

Worth to give it a try!

IG - @adblehs / @at.foodcrawls ✨
author: Amanda Tay

review_text: Overall slightly above average experience. Portion of the food is good. Fish & Chip is a bit oily and salty, chicken chop mushroom sauce is good but the chicken is bland. The Tom Yum Fried rice taste good, carbonara is a bit too dry. There is a free pool table usage for dining in. The staff mending the counter is friendly.
author: Alwin Tan

review_text:
If everyone order a main dishes and share the side dishes, buffet will be definitely very good choices!
Can eat many side dishes!
Got darts and pool table to play while waiting, pool is free.

Fried Hor Fun is very 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻!
Stingray is slightly salty but 👍🏻.
Fried pork belly is better than grilled pork.
Skip the beef burger, a bit dry, other than, all 👍🏻!

Drinks charge separately.
author: Jolin Min Min

review_text:
Absolutely unacceptable experience. The chicken served was raw inside — not slightly under, but visibly pink and clearly unsafe to eat. This is basic food safety, not a matter of taste. Serving raw chicken is a serious lapse that no restaurant should ever make.

To make things worse, we ordered two pasta dishes that arrived cold. Not “warm-ish”, not “cooling down” — straight up cold. We had to ask the staff to reheat them, which completely ruined the dining experience and raised even more concerns about how the food was prepared and handled in the first place.

What’s most baffling is the price point. At $15 per dish, this is absolutely ridiculous for food of such poor quality and execution. These prices suggest a standard this restobar clearly cannot meet.

Between the raw chicken, cold pasta, and unjustifiable pricing, this was a deeply disappointing and frankly alarming experience. I would strongly advise others to think twice before dining here — food safety and basic quality should never be compromised.
author: VS

review_text:
2nd time here July
Stingray was a disappointment. Too too thin n not much meat.
Sotong remains as best.
Prawns wasn't so fresh

June 25
Was looking for a place to chill in Yishun and was glad we found this.
Huge spacious plac with darts and pool.
Would be great if they added Ktv system as well or to listen to songs.
Food was mostly great except for the steak. That was a huge disappointment. So dry n rubbery = Not nice.
But wings + thai sotong was excellent.
So fresh n nice until we ordered twice.

Beer prices was reasonable as well.
Had a great time indeed.

Guess this place is mostly for those who stays in the hood as its a little secluded and not so accessible.
Will be back again thou as we kinda like it.
author: Ars 3276

review_text: Food was normal but took very lying to come out since there was only one chef. Very little choices for food but nice atmosphere with darts and pool tables
author: Sum Wung

review_text:
Had the grilled chicken chop. 1 piece of protein + 3 sides, all come in huge portion, at only $6.
The chicken tastes amazing. Tender, well-seasoned, with some char-grilled parts that add a nice flavour and texture.
The sides are alright, decent but not amazing. There's free mushroom soup but I'm not a fan of it. I'm not complaining at this price point and portion size though.
The shop owners also seemed like very friendly welcoming, and generous people.
author: yh8445

review_text: Ordered the chicken cutlet and pork chop fried rice. Superb man! The fried rice really got standard and the sunny side up is just nice with the egg yolk oozing out. The chicken cutlet portion is very generous and there is not one, not two, but total THREE sides for you to choose from! Mushrooms soup and sauces are also self served, come to show how kind and generous the boss is. Crazy, in such an economic climate, you can still get a very delicious western meal here at only $6 per set. I really respect the boss for maintaining such a friendly price. What are you waiting for if you are in this area, don't wait, come down and support this stall!
author: Ken Peh

review_text: Main plus 3 side dish $5.50. Taste average, portion is good and the price is consider cheap compare to surrounding western stall
author: H P Lim

review_text: Most amazing gravy on the chicken chop. Delicious meal. So good I had to rate it.
author: james greenough

review_text: Easy-to-understand menu and reasonable pricing. Foods are decent and served very quickly after ordering.
author: Benito Linus

review_text:
Prices vary anyhow.
Check price of each item and then order.
author: Jo Marko

review_text: Nasi Biryani is very nice
author: Ragumathull Ragumathulla

review_text: Ordered take away. No queue when I was there. Got the Unagi, Salmon Mentaiko, Double up chicken and Beef steak bowl. Overall not bad. Beef steak was a bit hard but probably because we left it for a while. Will be back next time to try others
author: Steven Chow

review_text:
Pretty good food. It's quite filling especially with the Japanese rice. The onsen egg is perfectly cooked. The wait time is always quite long since this is a 1-man operation, but everything is freshly cooked to order.
* Had to downgrade the rating due to the steak.

Teriyaki chicken: The chicken is tender, but this meal can feel a bit too much after a while because of the sweet sauce. It would be nice to balance out the flavours with some kind of pickled vege or kimchi.

Butter beef patty: Very flavourful and tender beef patty with slightly crispy edge, but the pepper taste can be a bit too strong.

Truffle steak: The most expensive but worst meal I've had here. The steak flavour is ok but the pink part in the middle is insanely chewy that the only way to eat is to swallow it. I ended up just eating the outer part and had to spit out the chewy inner part. Not sure if I'm just unlucky here since other reviews said it's tender. The chef didn't ask how I'd like it cooked and I also didn't mention it, but I'd imagine him cooking it the optimal way by default. Quite disappointed since this meal was expensive for me and I was getting it as a treat.
author: yh8445

review_text: YUMMMMMMY!!!!!!!! Portion is really filling and so generous with the mentaiko sauce!!! $11.90 for salmon mentaiko don, can use cdc to pay. About 15 min wait for the food during weekday dinner time, but understandable because it is a one man show. Man is very dedicated, food very well presented and really tasty!
author: MC SM

review_text: 3rd time back here and brought my child along. Owner is v nice, he wanted to give me free drink even tho I only ordered 1 item :) The cutlet don is amazing. I tried before their salmon don also v nice. Flavour is there, crispiness of the cutlet and freshness of ingredients are all there. I would say this is North area’s most authentic Japanese Don. Food pic taken was half eaten within 1 min; my kid couldn’t wait😂
author: Teeny Huts

review_text: My favourite Japanese don spot downstairs never misses. The Beef Truffle Don is perfectly tender and fragrant, and the Salmon Belly Don is always fresh and buttery. Consistent, generous, and insanely satisfying every single time. This has became my favourite place ever since i moved in to this neighborhood and i truly appreciate the boss who is friendly and remembers me everytime :-) Thought i’d drop a review as this shop deserves even more attention than it already has for its amazing food and service!
author: Jillian Ng

review_text:
Uncle's rojak is one of the best I have had. The you tiao was toasty, crispy without being hard. The hicama slices were thick and juicy. Pineapple chunks were sweet. Cucumber pieces were big. Tau pok was also warm and crispy.

You can choose a less sweet version, which is cool. We ordered both the black and white versions. The black is more savory, while white is more sour and sweet. Both were delightful.

Hidden gem right here in Yishun.
author: Gabriel Png

review_text:
Well, this is my first time eating Rojak at this stall.

Verdict?

Another 5 stars! What is right with this coffeeshop? Seriously? It is so good. The cuts are thick and I can really taste the fruit, vegetables, Tau pok, fried you tiao. Really a mouthful in every bite and flavourful too!!!!

Seemed like the stall's has a lot of hidden and talented people preparing tasty meals.

I am just thinking. should I even write this review, later many people come to eat then how? Have to wait long long.😅

Oh yes. Thank you Uncle for serving the food to us! Appreciate it!🙏

Anyway, recommended!

Sorry huh.  I took a half eaten dish to show because I forgot to take before eating. 😂
author: KingKong 99

review_text:
Got the large regular rojak, less spicy, less sweet. While the rojak paste is typical, the ingredients like the mango and pineapple were good and fresh and sweet, and the you tiao and taupok decently toasted. There is also extra crunch from the fried bread crumbs? that were scattered on top together with the peantus. Generous portion! Uncle is also liberal with the small slices of limau, which provide a fragrant sour contrast (just watch out for the seeds). It’s a good option for rojak if one is in this part of yishun.

White rojak is available but didnt get to try. The stall’s opening hours are now 10am - 2pm and 6 - 8pm if i recall correctly, and closed on Sundays. Suggest to dine in as the rojak sauce will be absorbed by the bread crumbs after a while.
author: Windy Days

review_text: The rojak is dry. That is most important and the you tiao is toasted heated to have the crispy texture. Boss use red apple instead of green and also lime juice and rojak flower to add aroma.
author: Nate Yong

review_text: Quite decent rojak done by an Ah Pek. Crispy you tiao. Lots of peanuts. Sweet thick sauce.
author: FoodieDirectory

review_text:
Their satay is not your regular typical satay. It has its own amazing flavour unlike any other places. Tender meat with crispy charred edges are a treat for your taste buds plus their peanut gravy tops it off for the perfect score. The bbq prawns are also marvelous done to perfection. Fazs satay really got me hooked.
Great service and friendly owner. My new favourite heartland stall definitely.

April2025 Hari Raya Aidilfitri
Ordered Raya catering with Fazs and was very impressed with his service. We ask for a normal buffet setup but Fazs went the extra mile and made it super nice complete with fairy lights. We received many complements from our guests saying that all the food tastes amazing. Thank you Fazs for the awesome service, setup and marvellous food. 10/10 ⭐
Overall ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
author: DanniiAnn Joe

review_text:
We ordered 120 sticks of satay: 100 sticks (mutton) & 20 sticks (chicken).

Both chicken and mutton meat is moist and well marinated. The cook is perfect.👌

The peanut sauce is delicious.

Even the cut vegetables are fresh.

Overall, a very value for money purchase with excellent freshness.

Even the delivery guy was polite and professional.

Thank you Fazs Satay for a 5 star home dining experience. Keep up the good work!

Will definitely support you more 👍😁
author: Enigmatic

review_text: Excellent satay. Bought $83 worth of satays and otah. No regrets food was delicious and owner provided ample amount of satay peanut gravy! Highly recommended
author: Adil Morgan

review_text: Went to their stall on 10 Dec 2024, 745pm and it was already closed - they were washing the equipments. Not a problem if I'm a customer nearby but we came all the way from Jurong & Woodlands. Please update the store opening time or learn how to honour them properly.
author: Nabs

review_text: A must try is their Duck Satay! The  meat is soft and i enjoy it very much. Their satay overall is pretty good, sauce can be better but overall experience is definitely pleasant!
author: Ashley Lee

review_text:
Discovered this stall when I was here to buy something last week. So today I purposely made a trip down to try their chicken rice! The chicken leg is huge, meat is soft and juicy, and the rice is fragrant too. Chilli sauce is spicy and a little tangy. I’ve also added $1 for fried chicken skin! So tasty and definitely value for money!

The stall owner was friendly, greet you with a happy face and thanks you when making payment. It’s very rare to see such good attitude stall owner nowadays.
author: Benito Linus

review_text:
Where can you get good flavoured chicken rice now It is for $3.50 but still good top notch taste …
Per plate . Serving is sufficient to fill your stomach . All the sides can get at $1 each . In plate there are two sides only $2 guys . Where to get . Family business open 11-7pm daily .
author: Haslinda Ekoan

review_text:
Northpoint Bizhub
2 Yishun Industrial St 1
S768159
Daily 11am to 7pm

This coffeeshop renovated since we last came across it but glad that this nasi ayam stall kept to its still reasonable prices.

First time eating nasi itik. Don’t think many places have this. $4 given generous plate of lightly braised boneless duck breast meat which were very tender. Rice used is the chicken rice type. Very fragrant. 😋

Nasi ayam $3.50. Another generous portion of meat and rice. Chicken is also cooked well and quite tender. 😋

$1 fried chicken skin is a must order. Nicely seasoned with turmeric spice and very crispy. Super addictive and yummy! 🤤

😋😋😋😋😋😋
author: Jodeci Fine

review_text: My go to chicken place. The highlight for me is their fried chicken skin. It is so crunchy & crispy and goes well with their Chili sauce. They give big chicken rice portions too so you will not be disappointed. Budget friendly and delicious food, I highly recommend!
author: Gerianne Escandor

review_text: I love this place, owner were humble and friendly, price was affordable, portion was generous, taste was great! How can you complaint? Haha love the chicken skin... Be sure to check it out
author: Kopyory

review_text:
This is 2nd time here. First time food nicer but this time slightly different, maybe more pack and busy so standard drop.
But still the food is good and price I think ok as it’s coffee shop so not too expensive for the taste.
Have parking place and can be quite crowded there.
author: EL

review_text:
Great find. Passed by this zichar stall many times, finally tried it.
San Lou Beehoon very well done. Not as oily as the JB version. Lala Huadiao Wine Beehoon soup is another highlight. Son loves the $18 claypot wine chicken.
Service was quick and efficient.
Located in an industrial building.
author: Poh Soh Lee

review_text:
Slightly cheaper than Bukit Ho Swee claypot curry fish head but just as good.

Very generous with the vegetables in their claypot curry fish head.

Ingredients are all very fresh and tasty.
author: Mikail Yah

review_text:
My first and last time here definitely. Extremely long wait time for ONE dabao dish. ONE. As at writing I have already waited 30 mins.

When I asked the staff, she said that I’ll have to wait for another 20mins and that they are busy on weekend. If the wait time is ridiculously long, it is only right that you inform customers about it and let them decide if they want to order or not.

Do not recommend.
author: Yihui Low

review_text: Food was not bad but waited for 20mins even though there weren’t many patrons at the coffeeshop. Also, the auntie at the counter doesn’t seem to want to take our order. Even though we were standing right in front of her, she just kinda ignore us and took the order of the guy behind us first. I assume the guy must be their usual patron but that’s not how u do business what.
author: felfelfel

restaurant_name: Golden Prosper 金旺 Wanton Mee (Yishun)
review_text:
Regular customer that works nearby here. My personal favourite is the dumpling. Thin skin filled generously with tasty homemade pork filling and half a small shrimp inside. At this price, it's amazing. The wanton is equally as good. The texture of the noodles here has a good bite feel. The fried chicken chop comes in large portion and is fried to perfection. The curry is flavourful. The free-flow crispy onion is very nice.

Some personal complaints/suggestions:
- The soup and the dry noodle sauce are the salty, strong flavour type instead of being actually fragrant. It's the kind that feels addictive when you eat but will leave a strong lingering aftertaste.
- Crispy pork lard would be nice.
- More noodle option for the horfun such as meehun and yellow mee.
- I don't like the charsiew here, it's the type that often has chewy part.

The boss and the female workers are very friendly. The prices are reasonable, especially the chicken chop horfun so I can understand if my requests are unrealistic.
author: yh8445

restaurant_name: Golden Prosper 金旺 Wanton Mee (Yishun)
review_text:
One of my favourite wanton mee in Singapore.
The noodles are springy, and the sauce is Malaysian-style.👍🏼 👍🏼👍🏼
The No.1 signature is really good. Sometimes I ask the boss to add a bit of curry gravy, and it tastes great too 😋

Must try!
author: Chuah Eileen

restaurant_name: Golden Prosper 金旺 Wanton Mee (Yishun)
review_text:
Friend thinks curry horfun is good.
Average wanton mee.
author: Lim Ray

restaurant_name: Golden Prosper 金旺 Wanton Mee (Yishun)
review_text: Great wanton mee . Interesting is the curry hor fun
author: Han Sin Alvin Low

review_text:
Visited this Korean fusion eatery and had a pleasant experience overall. The customer service really stood out, the staff (possibly the owner) was friendly and made an effort to engage in small talk, which was a nice touch.

The menu offers a mix of fried chicken, pasta, burgers, and some Korean inspired dishes. While it may not feel fully authentic Korean, the food was tasty and enjoyable. I ordered the cheese chicken, and my kids were especially happy with it, they even commented on how generous the cheese portion was.

Portions are good, prices are reasonable, and the overall experience was satisfying. Worth a visit if you’re looking for a casual Korean fusion spot with good service.
author: jianhao lee

review_text:
Very happy with their chicken wings! We ordered Soy Garlic and Sweet and Sour and my husband and I absolutely love it. Huge serving for a very good price. The staff were all welcoming and polite.

Definitely will go back very soon
author: Miss G.

review_text:
The fried chicken is very well done, crispy and tender. There are a good amount of flavour you can choose from, and the portion is quite good. I personally recommend the garlic one since its the best one among the other options.

The burgers and pastas are good too, but I believe the flavour is lacking a bit. You can get a set with a side fries and a drink if you top up a few more dollars. The fries are not bad. Overall good restaurant,  great price. Only downside is theres no air condition and transport is not the most convenient one.
author: Atlas Por

review_text:
Had the soy garlic and spicy gang jung Korean fried chicken.
The chicken was really good. Juicy and crispy. I like that they served it on a nice ceramic plate. Great presentation that makes you hungrier just looking at it.

I wouldn’t order the spicy gang jung again though, it really can’t compare to the soy garlic. Worth getting the large portion next time so you can mix two flavours and get more value.

The ginseng chicken soup was surprisingly good. Not cheap, but the flavour was strong and authentic. Came with a bit of glutinous rice and two chestnuts, which made it feel properly done. I’ll order this again.

Overall, I’ll visit again for both the soy garlic chicken and the soup.
author: Cqlee

review_text: First time trying. Staff were friendly and chatty. The food were very reasonably priced. Portion is great too. Fried chicken were juicy and tender. Surprisingly the chicken Alfredo is yummy too and the kids love it. Recommended to have some Korean fried chicken quick fix at a fraction of restaurant price. 👍🏻
author: Adrian Zhang

review_text: Great food and environment. Most importantly is the service is good and staff is super friendly 👍🏻
author: B.K.

review_text:
Their staff are extremely kind and helpful in helping us and making choice and suggestion.

Service are top notch.

Ginseng chicken taste good especially if you add rice into it like how the korean made it.

Chicken Alfredo are good as well
author: The Doodle

review_text: Hidden gem in Yishun. Good korean fusion food. I must say the quality is good and value for money. Pleasantly surprise how juicy and bursting with favour the burger is. Should have order a double instead. Overall good experience. Will try their hotpot in my next visit.
author: JN

review_text: I ordered takeaway yesterday, and I have to say, this is one of the best ginseng chicken dishes I’ve ever had! I’m pleasantly surprised to find such a hidden gem in Yishun. Every piece of the fried chicken was incredibly juicy, and the sauce was unique and delicious. The staff were also very friendly and welcoming. I’ll definitely be visiting the shop again soon!
author: heather lee

review_text: Hidden gem for the nearby residents to come and specially over the weekend. Highly recommend for its very affordable food and selection of locals, Koreans and western food. The place is very spacious and the varieties are good. Very good portion for the 2-1 BBQ and steamboat package for 2. It also offer soju for people want to have the bbq food together. It’s worth a family or 2 to come and have a great weekend of dining.
author: Ben Ng

review_text:
Had a great lunch here today. I ordered the egg with dark soy sauce, bitter gourd, and tofu with 卤味—all were super tasty and well-cooked. The flavours were rich and comforting, especially the tofu.

Simple, affordable, and very satisfying. Highly recommended for anyone who enjoys good vegetarian food! 🌱👏
author: kenny ong

review_text:
This Tong Xin Vegetarian stall has the same name as the veg stall in Canberra hawker, but different boss, n not related to one another.

Initially really quite confusing😅

Today's specialty is mee siam... Not sure is it every Friday mee siam though. I usually order economic veg rice, which is not oily, fresh n healthier. Quite a few dishes to choose from.

Boss is friendly. Usually she has 1 helper, but today she's alone...
author: Alice

review_text: Vegetarian stall within Coffeeshop. Quite a number of selections. Taste good too!
author: Guy

review_text: Im a frequent diner. All the dishes are nice! Comes with hearty bowl of soup with vegetables inside too (except for lunar dates first and fifteenth bcos they are swamped then)
author: Lauren GCY

review_text: Very friendly aunty, with good portions. quite cheap also, compared to other vegetarian stalls. But the coffee shop gets a little crowded during lunch time.
author: saai Raghupathy

review_text: Nice plain prata.  Choice of different curries.  I had the fish curry and it's delicious.
author: Teck Chong Law

review_text: Had one of the stingrays i have ever had. Better than the ones i had in Singapore. It’s good it’s cheap. The people there are kind and have good service as well. Would recommend to come here for seafood dinner
author: Lwin Thant Maung

review_text: The dim sum here is definitely good and worth the trip. May be on slightly higher price but many good stuff.  I like their char siew pau which is delicious and tasty with juicy source inside. Other steam dim sum is also good.  Fried stuff may not be that crispy as I expected it to be.  Lots of tour bus with tourists and it is very crowded.  Finding a seat for bigger family may be challenging during morning breakfast peak hours
author: Eddie Goh

review_text: Nice place with a lot of variety that is affordable and local priced. Dim sum is decent for a Coffeeshop and food. Variety is really a lot! Worth coming
author: Nick GC Tan

review_text: Good food and prices. Enjoyed the Dim Sum.
author: Ng Tze Kean

review_text:
Not much choice, the food quality not good
CKT                            6/10
Lou Si Fun                  5/10
Bittergourd soup    7.5/10
author: Royston Toh

review_text:
This is an interesting place to have a meal of shell out. The dining area is actually an extension from a corner house painted orange in a residential area, which gave rise to its name I think.

Although they have ala carte order, most customers are here for the shell out which in my opinion is value for money.
author: BY Ang

review_text: Rustic charm kampung food. For breakfast - can try lontong,nasi lemak, soto ayam & roti canai. They also serve economy rice with Asam pedas Johor style. At night, another vendor take over for shellout (grilled seafood)
author: Amin Ali

review_text: Nice!......already try Mee Racun...quite astonishing but taste almost same as Mee Bandung Muar, the barista quite religious person and kind, like him very much
author: Muhaimin Azmi

review_text: For dinner a bit slow service.  Some variety for breakfast and the roti prata is quite good,  but this shop is quite famous for shell out set meals every Ramadhan. One of the very first poineer in doing shell out, and is still the one that stood the test of time. For it to be undying so this shop must got the 'it' factor.
author: hafizuddin iqbal

review_text: Took a while but surprise with the portion.
author: Hilmi

review_text:
I would like to file a complaint regarding my recent GrabFood order (Lontong).

When the order arrived, all the gravy had completely spilled out inside the plastic bag. As shown in the attached photo, the container had a hole at the bottom, which caused the sauce to leak everywhere. The food was soaked and in a very messy condition, making it unpleasant and difficult to consume.

The driver mentioned that the restaurant did not pack the food properly. From what I observed, the packaging was indeed not secure, and the container was damaged before or during delivery. Proper sealing and quality packaging should be ensured to prevent such incidents.

I am disappointed with this experience, as the food was not delivered in acceptable condition. I kindly request that this matter be investigated and that appropriate action be taken.
author: jiahui lim

review_text:

restaurant_name: 阿华牛肉面 Ah Hua Beef noodles
review_text:
We visited Ah Hua Beef Noodles on a Sunday evening and found it pleasantly quiet. The shop is located outside the main tourist zones, but it's easily accessible by Grab or car. There was plenty of parking available, which made the visit hassle-free.

The place is a no-frills coffee shop, but service was surprisingly good. A male staff member stood out for being attentive and quick to assist, which made the experience more enjoyable.

We ordered the claypot beef with tendon and tripe — a generous portion, perfect for sharing between 2 to 3 people. It arrived piping hot, and the beef was tender and full of flavor. My companion had the signature beef noodles. The broth was tasty, though the portion of noodles was quite large and started to absorb the soup quickly.

We ended up taking away some of the claypot dish, and even after reheating the next day, it remained flavorful and tender — a pleasant surprise.

While the food and service impressed us, the shop could improve its interior ambiance. Brighter lighting and a bit of decor would make it more inviting. Also worth noting: there was a pungent smell and quite a few flies, which might be off-putting to some diners. The majority of customers during our visit appeared to be Chinese nationals.

Overall, we enjoyed the food and service and would definitely return. With a few improvements to the environment, this place could become a real "hidden gem".

However, there was an unpleasant smell in the restaurant that made the dining experience a bit uncomfortable. The floor area also felt messy, with a lot of things placed around, especially near the seating on the floor, which affected the overall cleanliness and comfort.

Another downside was the service towards the end of our meal. The staff asked us to leave early because they were closing, even though we were still eating. review_text:

I tried their beef noodle, beef stew, and steamed dumplings. The beef noodle featured smooth, hand-pulled noodles in a clear yet deeply beefy broth that hit all the right notes, while the beef stew was rich and comforting, with tender beef pieces absorbing every bit of the savory seasoning.

The steamed dumplings were a delight—the filling was perfectly balanced, enhanced by a touch of chili oil that added just the right kick without overpowering the natural flavors.

Overall, it was a meal that delivered authentic taste with a modern twist, making it a must-visit spot for anyone craving hearty Chinese-Muslim cuisine.

review_text:
It seems that this restaurant is quite popular among residents in the area.

We went there for a Ramadan pre-dawn meal (sahur) on a Saturday at around 4.30 a.m., and it was already well patronised, with some customers even bringing their young children along.

There was a wide variety of nasi kandar dishes available, and the service was quick, with many waiters on duty.
author: iinsa01

review_text:
A friend recommended this place for its good and affordable Indian fare in a clean and comfortable setting — and it truly didn’t disappoint. The kuah campur was rich and flavourful, and the portions were very generous. My friend’s crispy sotong covered almost half the plate! I had the fried chicken and sotong masala; the chicken was crispy and juicy, and the sotong was tender, not chewy at all. The place was clean, and there wasn’t a queue, which was a bonus.

Definitely coming back again!

review_text:
Food-wise, no complaints at all — whether it’s nasi kandar or goreng-goreng, everything was superb!!

restaurant_name: Restoran Xing Hoo 星和粿条汤 ah SONG
review_text:
Amazing food in an unassuming place.

I resist to call this a hidden gem 💎 but this is indeed one hidden 💎.

To be a hidden 💎 it has to be unvisited by tourist and foreigners. Most patrons are local Malaysians to that is a ✅.

The food is simple, ingredients are fresh, simple goodness.

The boss is friendly and accommodating.

I customised my order just tells him what I want to add, more pork liver, more 🦐 prawns, more kidney. Which he gladly obliged.

Big shout out to the kidney slices, it is nicely cleaned, no gamy taste. If you love to eat pork kidney, you know what I mean.

The rest of the ingredients are cooked just nice perfection.

The broth contained the sweetness from the ingredients.

No MSG which is a huge ➕.
author: OrLeo

The level of spiciness was just right, not too strong, and the waiter was thoughtful enough to recommend what suits those who prefer milder sambal.

One small suggestion: the flavors reminded me of Indonesian food, where we’d often enjoy meals while sitting on the floor (duduk bersila). If the restaurant could offer a few seating spots like that, it would truly elevate the whole experience.

restaurant_name: 四季好 Lucky Four Season Restaurant
review_text:
Place: air conditioned restaurant with ample seats that specialises in Chinese cuisine dish based foods. They have free WiFi here. (lucky1919). Wonderful.

Service: prompt and swift with taking and recommendations for food even for my 1st time. The problem was the speed in which the dishes were coming out. I felt the gap was too far apart between each dish.

Food:
1. Steamed asam fish: I liked the flavour of this asam right here. Its just the right amount spicy + sour + sweet for me. Just the right sweet spot. Verdict: 4.6/5.

2. Sweet and sour pork ribs: boneless, flavourful and pork cooked to perfection! Wow. I loved this dish! Verdict: 4.5/5.

3. Salted vegetables taufu soup: fairly standard dish here. Verdict: 2.5/5.

4. Prawn pase fried chicken: the prawn paste was very strong and overpowering. Some may like it. Verdict: 2.3/5.

review_text: An absolute gem! From the moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the inviting aroma of delicious cuisine. The Nasi Lemak was fragrant and paired wonderfully with the flavorful sambal. And let's talk about their Crunchy Fried Chicken - crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside, simply irresistible! The restaurant's cleanliness and hygiene standards were impeccable, adding to the overall enjoyable dining experience. Plus, the value for money here is unbeatable. A definite must-visit for anyone craving authentic Malaysian cuisine in a welcoming and hygienic environment. Plenty of parking spaces and FREE!!

review_text:
Plenty of parking and no parking fees – such a relief! The restaurant itself has a beautiful, cozy interior that makes you want to stay longer.
They serve a wide variety of Hunan dishes, and everything we tried was delicious — especially the Sliced Pork Belly with Pickled Mustard Greens, Tomato Scrambled Eggs, Spicy Fried Chicken, and Stir-fried Cabbage with Pork Lard Crisps.

Besides a good range of alcoholic drinks, they also offer cocktails and creative beverages.

In the evening, there’s live music, which makes it a great place to chill, enjoy a drink, and chat with friends.
In the afternoon, when it’s quieter without the live band, it’s also a nice spot for business meetings or catching up with clients.

Highly recommended whether you’re here for the food, drinks, music, or all of the above!

author: hao lim

review_text:
I’ve been here a few times, and the food is generally decent with reasonable prices, especially for this area.

My favourites are the fried rice and fried chicken cutlet. The fried rice is well balanced—not too oily compared to many places—with good flavour and some wok hei. It’s rare to find a good fried rice around town. The fried chicken cutlet comes in a generous portion, is crispy, but a bit less tender. Given the price and portion size, that’s acceptable.

The coffee is slightly above average for me, as I’m a heavy coffee drinker, but I would still recommend it.

The environment can feel stuffy during peak hours, especially in the afternoon. It would help to keep the door closed when not in use. There were also some flies, which was quite annoying. Better table cleaning would help, as the tables felt sticky and attracted flies.

Overall, I would recommend this makan place. It offers a wide variety of local food at reasonable prices.

I will come again next time. ☕😋🍽️ #coffee #bistro #breakfast #brunch #meals #desserts #drinks #food #taste #service
author: jerry cheah

review_text:
Uncle Five Coffee – Not Quite a High Five 👋☕

Right next to my yoga studio, this spot scores points for convenience — perfect for a quick power meal before a stretch and a sweat.

Uncle Five Coffee is a homegrown kopitiam brand serving the familiar “Taste that Belongs to Malaysians” — toasts, nasi lemak, noodles, rice dishes, and even Singapore-style items like Hainanese Chicken Rice and fried prawn noodles.

But as one of the many halal cafés now sprouting across JB, it doesn’t quite stand out from the crowd. The food is decent but lacks that spark or signature twist to earn a true high five.

So while I might pop by for a quick fuel up  before yoga, it’s more of a Namaste and go, not a “see you again soon.” 🧘‍♀️

author: Jerry Wai

review_text:
La Providence has always been one of my favourite spots in JB — and this visit marks my fourth time here. The food is consistently excellent, but what truly makes the experience special is Mae, who has been with the restaurant for the past three years. Her warmth and passion for what she does make every visit an absolute delight.

Mae is also the creative soul behind all the desserts in the restaurant — and she makes them with such tender loving care that you can taste it in every bite. I’ve never been a fan of panna cotta and would normally never order it, but Mae insisted I try the one she made, even offering it complimentary just for me to taste. And wow — I was completely blown away! It was smooth, perfectly balanced, and simply divine. I now have a whole new appreciation for panna cotta thanks to her.

She also let us sample her homemade pistachio ice cream, which was equally amazing — creamy, fragrant, and not overly sweet.

Every time I visit, Mae’s food and drink recommendations are spot-on, and I always leave completely satisfied. The restaurant itself is cosy and intimate, with lovely background music that adds to the charm.

If you’re ever heading into Johor Bahru and want to treat yourself to an authentic French dining experience, La Providence is a must-visit. Don’t forget to ask for Mae — she’ll make sure your meal is as memorable as mine every single time! 🇫🇷
author: Julian Ng

review_text:
La Provence, tucked away in a quiet part of Horizon Hills, was such a gem of a find.

While on the pricier side, the menu was extensive and supported by a specials board, which added to the appeal. My mistake for assuming it was Italian—looking back, the name should have given it away.

Ordered a Margherita pizza and initially thought it odd that there wasn’t a basil leaf to complete the traditional Neapolitan look (symbolising the Italian flag). That said, it did come with the classic chewy dough and charred corners—not for everyone, but oh so satisfying for me.

We had two sides—oysters and fried calamari. Both were excellent, so much so we finished them before my wife even arrived. A small faux pas though: the shucked French oysters weren’t fully separated from the shell before serving. For the price point, I’d have expected that to be done. Intentional or a mishap, I’m not sure.

For the mains, we went with the wait staff’s recommendations (who, by the way, were extremely friendly and attentive without being intrusive). The grilled lamb shoulder was generous in portion—slightly gamey, with the herb marinade not fully masking it, but still tasty. The accompanying green peppercorn sauce was excellent, as you’d expect from a French restaurant. The grilled chicken with pesto pasta surprised me. The pesto sauce was less herby than I’m used to, but the pasta was clearly freshly made. Some may find the texture unusual compared to dried pasta—it reminded me more of wantan noodles—but personally, I loved it.

All in all, a solid experience. We’d definitely return to explore more of the menu.

author: William

restaurant_name: Jiah Xiang Dim Sum - Horizon Hills
review_text:
Jiah Xiang Dim Sum is a popular spot in Johor Bahru for casual dim sum, especially if you are looking for something affordable and satisfying without a fine-dining setting. It is clearly well known among locals, which explains why the restaurant is almost always busy during lunch hours.

One of the highlights here is the xiao long bao. The dumplings are well made, with a good balance between the wrapper, filling, and soup inside. They are enjoyable to eat and stand out compared to many other casual dim sum places in JB. For the price point, the quality is solid and consistent.

The menu overall is suitable for everyday dim sum dining rather than special occasions. Portions are reasonable, prices are affordable, and it works well for quick meals with friends, family, or colleagues. This is the kind of place people return to regularly rather than visit only once.

Because of its popularity, the restaurant does get loud, particularly during peak lunch hours. The atmosphere is lively and crowded, which may not be ideal if you are looking for a quiet meal. However, the turnover is efficient. Even during busy periods, the waiting time is usually around 10 to 15 minutes at most, which is quite manageable compared to other crowded dim sum spots.

Overall, Jiah Xiang Dim Sum is a good option in Johor Bahru for casual dim sum at an affordable price. If you do not mind the noise and crowds, the food quality and short waiting time make it a practical and reliable choice, especially for lunch.
author: Yuki Takei

restaurant_name: Jiah Xiang Dim Sum - Horizon Hills
review_text:
The staff here are really friendly. Most of them are Myanmarese but they try their best to speak Mandarin. The food is consistently good. We have eaten here a number of times. This round we tried the shao xing tofu, stuffed eggplant, broccoli in garlic, xiao long bao and crispy leek pie.
I like the leek pie the best as the crispy wafer enclosed lots of juicy prawns. The Xiao long bao was a big surprise as it was full of wine-laced soup. Very shiok.
In fact the tofu and eggplant were yummy too, like those you get at Ampang yong tau fu stall.
Bought the frozen pork bao back to eat another day. It's big enough for lunch with a side of vegetables. Someone at the next table was eating and I couldn't resist trying.

Overall, there are many choice of dim sum. Can suit every age range. But the taste to me is like a box of chocolates, taste good or bad depends on your own preference. author: Kimberley Howarth

review_text:
And why would i visit such a faraway restaurant in Horizon Hills JB? My crazy friend suggested i eat "healthy" food after i told him i had bad digestion problems.
This restaurant features "box-lunches" - bento type Taiwanese featured meals. There were quite a few people there as it was lunchtime.
We ordered fried chicken bento sets. They come fried and in very mild, non-spicy and light marinades - all in the name of health and wellness. Each bento set comes with salad, miso soup, a small saycer of kimchi and noodles or rice. There is even specific cuts of chicken offered(like breast meat) for those health conscious.
Overall, the taste is mild, down to extremely light. Not for people needing high salt and high umami meals. Their drinks are mostly winter-melon based(they call it white-gourd). For their price, i'll deem it affordable and filling. You need to keep to these type of offerings for at least three months to lose weight and get healthily weaned from heavy-tasting processed food.

restaurant_name: Bamboo Seafood Restaurant • 知竹海鲜
review_text:
I absolutely enjoy dining at this spot – it’s a great place with a wide variety of choices, especially if you’re into seafood and flavorful fried rice combinations. Their menu is quite impressive, offering different skewer options like chicken, pork, lamb, and even deer meat for the adventurous eaters.

Here’s what we had today:

1. Shrimp Ball – My top pick! Each bite was packed with real prawn chunks – crispy on the outside and juicy inside. A definite must-try.

2. Mala Spicy Fried Rice with Chicken Skewer – Served beautifully on a bamboo plate. The portion was generous, easily enough for 2 to 3 people. The mala kick was just right, and the chicken skewer paired well with it.

3. Black Pepper Prawns (300g) – We got about 7 to 8 prawns in our serving. Perfectly cooked and coated with a bold black pepper sauce – finger-licking good!

4. Grilled Stingray – This came with sambal that was rich and full of flavor. It also included ladies' fingers (okra), and we added petai (stinky beans) as an extra – cooked just right and added a great depth to the dish.

The restaurant itself is clean and spacious, offering both indoor and outdoor seating. Plus, there’s plenty of parking available, which is always a bonus.

Highly recommended for anyone craving seafood with bold flavors and a good variety of sides!

review_text:
We were recommended to this place by a friend during our short visit to a JB confinement centre that nearby this place.

While we thought it was just another café , to our surprise, it turned out to be a real hidden gem that we think more people should know about ✨

With the “safe” food orders like Portobello Mushroom Fries, Spaghetti Prawn Aglio Olio, and a Beef Burger with a homemade burger bun that we had,  the taste and freshness of the food were beyond our expectations. We would say every dish impressed us.

We also had the chance to meet the owner, Ryan, who was super friendly. Through our conversation with him, we could really feel his passion toward food, the attention to detail, and high standards of quality when he shared how he personally selects the ingredients fresh from the market every day.

We will definitely come back again to try out other food items that he recommended eg. Gulai Ikan Patin Tempoyak with the special rice variety specially imported from Borneo

review_text:
Came here on a late Sunday afternoon, the atmosphere was really nice and was not too crowded. Lots of parking available.

Tried the "best fish and chips in JB" and it did not disappoint. Also tried the calamari and cajun chicken and they were quite appetizing as well. For desserts, the Guinness cake was not too sweet and had tasty notes of rum in the cream.

The food was really great and delicious, price point was quite value for the quality of food that you are paying for. The staff was also very friendly and noticed my camera so we got to chat for a while and found out that he was also a photography enthusiast.
author: Chen Jun Ming

review_text:
Had dinner at Habitat Bistrot with my wife for her birthday on 08/09/2025, and it was such a wonderful experience! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

We spotted fried calamari on the menu and were initially hesitant to order it because of too many bad experiences elsewhere in JB. I asked Ryan if it was fresh, and he assured us it was—saying they get it daily from the “pasar,” even joking that the only thing frozen in their kitchen is the fries. That immediately gave us confidence, and he was right—the calamari was fresh and delicious.

We also had the fish & chips and aglio olio, both of which stood out compared to what we’ve had before. The tartar sauce was really unique and paired perfectly with the fish. The food here feels thoughtfully prepared and of great quality. While their western food shines, they also have a few Asian dishes on the menu, which makes it versatile for everyone.

A special mention to Ryan for his exceptional service—polite, friendly, and always ready to explain the dishes with a smile. He truly made the dinner even more enjoyable.

Overall, I’d give it 5/5. This place has become our go-to spot for good western food in JB, and we’ll definitely keep coming back.

author: ‘Aliah Mohamaddillah

review_text:
Waiting an Hour at McDonald's Due to Being Treated Unequally**

Today, my family and I went to McDonald's with high hopes for a pleasant meal, but we ended up having a terrible experience (attached is the receipt).

We waited about half an hour at a table upstairs and were confused to see other customers who arrived later already enjoying their food. So, we went downstairs to inquire about our order. The staff member(picture that guy) informed me that they couldn't provide my fried chicken due to insufficient stock. However, he did give me some other main dishes, unfortunately excluding the extra fried chicken, fries, drinks, and the happy meal.

My sister later asked again and managed to get the drinks, which shouldn’t have required any waiting.

During the long wait, we finished our drinks, and I went to the counter to pay and refill my drink. At that moment, I saw customer number 137 picking up their order and receiving fries. This made me feel unfairly treated, so I asked why I, as number 120, couldn’t get fries, and why the happy meal was just chicken nuggets still cannot provide first? I received nothing but silence in response, and the staff member's attitude was terrible; he clearly didn’t want to help.

He told me to keep waiting, so I stood at the counter with several other customers. I tried to communicate with two or three different staff members about my missing items, but none provided a reasonable response. The guy even rudely put fries into a takeout bag for me, despite my order being for dine-in. In the end, he told his colleague that I only lacked fried chicken, which baffled me since I had clearly stated what I was missing. Perhaps this reflects McDonald's overall attitude?

Some staff even accused me of having already received my order, which drove me crazy. After waiting for over an hour, I advise everyone to be cautious when taking kids to this fast-food restaurant. My niece wanted McDonald's for her birthday, but she ended up hungry for an hour and was even accused of having received her children’s meal. I hope McDonald's can review the CCTV to clear my name.

The last female staff member packed my items for me, but I didn't even check what she gave me because I was too frustrated to eat. In the end, I just gave everything away to others.
author: Thera Chen

review_text:

I don’t understand those bad comments and complaints below, but I have been to this McDonald’s over 20 times since their new opening until now. Nothing bad has ever been experienced, and I have always been well-served.

Sometimes people need to understand that the service line is not there to serve you at each step, but as a customer, you should take the initiative to check, confirm, and ask about any unforeseen circumstances if you are a reasonable person.

Step out and see their business and how the staff are trying hard to serve at their best level, be nice, be kind, and be considerate to everyone. They are human, not machines. They are someone’s loved ones.

review_text:
🐾 D Fern Café – Where Even a Dog Feels Photosynthesized

I trotted into D Fern Café as the only customer —
lady boss munching happily at her meal while I padded in quietly.
No problem… I’m used to walking in on hoomans eating.
(We dogs call that “research.”)

🌿 A Name That Actually Makes Sense

D Fern really is all about the ferns.
Lined up at the entrance like a leafy welcoming committee,
sprinkled across the café like Mother Nature’s décor team.
Honestly, it felt like dining in a forest minus the mosquitoes —
a full-on negative-ion spa session for my doggie soul.

Add the soothing music and you’ve got a space that can calm even a nervous chihuahua.

🍜 Food That Made My Tail Twitch

The menu was varied — lots to sniff at.

And then…
Laksa!
My ultimate weakness.
I was thrilled it wasn’t made with ikan kembong
(a fish my hooman and I both refuse to sniff, let alone eat).

The lobak?
Tasty, with good seasoning…
though a tad oily.
Would’ve been even more paw-fect if they’d patted it dry instead of letting it swim in its own oil bath.
A little shake-shake and blot-blot goes a long way!

🚗 Will This Dog Return?

It is a bit far from my den,
but who knows?
Maybe one day this dog will trot back in, nestle among the ferns,
and pretend I’m a Zen puppy again.

The menu leans towards local Penang and Nyonya favourites, which was a treat. We tried:

Kapitan Chicken Curry
Nasi Lemak Ayam
Nasi Goreng Kampung
Asam Pedas

Everything tasted pretty decent – the fried chicken in the nasi lemak was especially crispy and full of flavour. Portion sizes are generous, and the plates are quite large, so if you're seated at a small table, it might be a bit of a puzzle arranging everything.

We also ordered the Chicken Lobak as a side, nicely done and worth trying!

Parking was easy, and service was friendly and efficient. Overall, a good spot for casual group dining with authentic local flavours. Highly recommended!

review_text: Never know they got breakfast set. Went to try their breakfast menu. It’s very affordable, mostly less than RM10 and the taste is extremely delicious. Even the toast tastes better than outside, cos they used premium butter. You can even see the butter dripping. As for coffee, it’s French press and the portion is about two or three cups. It has a fragrant aroma and i just can’t stop drinking it, even though I am not a coffee lover. For RM6, you can enjoy a plate of freshly fried mee hoon full of ingredients plus a sunny side up egg. Their nasi lemak is also same price and comes with chicken wing but didn’t try this time. My son ate the scrambled egg with rye bread and sausages. The sausages are not the cheap type of sausage and the egg, you can still see smoke coming up. Their homemade otak with egg fried bread is also special, just that it is a bit oily. They also sell other type of breads like focaccia, croissant, scones and baguettes. Breakfast time is only from 8am - 10.30am, so do come early. Or else can also try their lunch menu. Lastly, their service is good and even comes with complementary food and drink
author: L MK

review_text:
I came here for lunch and had a pleasant experience overall. There are two restaurants likely under the same management, and the place is spacious, comfortable, and suitable for group dining. Some tables were already reserved when I arrived, which shows it’s quite popular.

The food portions are generous, and considering the portion size, the taste and price are definitely worth it. The aglio olio was decent, with an interesting twist of fried mushrooms as a topping, while the fish and chips was simple but satisfying. The only downside was the waiting time, as the food took more than 20 minutes to arrive despite the place not being too crowded.

Service was generally good. A few staff were friendly and welcoming, while some seemed a bit new, but they were polite and trying their best. Parking can be a bit challenging during peak hours, but it’s still manageable to find a spot nearby.
author: Selvinia Nofy

review_text:
It was my first time dining at this café, and it turned out to be a wonderful surprise. Every dish we ordered was beautifully plated, flavourful, and executed with impressive finesse, truly top-notch. The interior resembles an elegant fine-dining restaurant, yet the prices remain refreshingly affordable. I also noticed a striking replica of a Van Gogh painting on the wall, adding a familiar artistic charm to the space.

The ambiance was cool, cosy, and refined, an ideal setting for hosting special guests or celebrating meaningful moments without straining the budget. The service was equally commendable; the waiters were attentive, friendly, and genuinely accommodating. They even served complimentary croissants with butter as a warm and buttery starter, which set a pleasant tone for the meal.

For our mains, we ordered the BBQ Beef Steak, cooked medium-rare. The steak was tender, juicy, and infused with a smoky barbecue depth, paired with steak-house cut fries that were crisp on the outside and fluffy inside. The Italian vegetables on the side added a nice balance of freshness and herbaceous aroma.
We also tried the half-bird barbecue smoked chicken, which was succulent and perfectly seasoned, with a delicate smokiness that complemented the roast potatoes, crisp-edged and buttery soft within.

The garlic cream spaghetti with grilled chicken was rich and aromatic, the sauce silky and well-emulsified, coating each strand without being overly heavy. The kids’ creamy mac and cheese was comforting and indulgent, with a smooth, velvety cheese sauce that children (and adults!) would enjoy.

Our drinks were also delightful. The hot chocolate was smooth and intense, the soursop drink refreshing with a natural tang, and the kombucha had a clean, crisp acidity that balanced the richness of our mains. The French press coffee was another highlight. It had a full-bodied, robust flavour with a natural richness that you only get from an immersion brew.

Dessert ended the meal on a high note. The tropical lime pie was zesty, bright, and beautifully balanced. The Chonky cookies lived up to their name, thick, soft-baked, and wonderfully decadent.

This café has definitely earned a place among my favourites in Iskandar Puteri. I’m already looking forward to returning and trying more of their dishes.

review_text:

The chicken was very tender and juicy, well seasoned, and the baked potatoes and vegetables also stood out, though slightly salty. The waiting time was reasonable. This time, I ordered their special Jamaican chicken, and it was good as well.

What I really appreciated was the complimentary starter bread served upon seating. It is a warm and thoughtful touch while waiting for the main course.

The environment is cozy and bright during the daytime, with plenty of windows. There are also many books placed near the windows, which is a nice bonus if you enjoy reading while dining.

Overall, I would recommend trying their menu. Do note that dinner time can be very crowded, so making a reservation in advance is advisable to avoid waiting.

review_text:
Asia Authentic Cuisine is a hidden gem for anyone seeking a delicious and healthy dining experience. The food here is simply outstanding—flavorful yet balanced, with dishes that are not overly salty, making it a great choice for health-conscious diners.

Their steamed fish is a must-try! It’s incredibly fresh and cooked to perfection, with flavors that truly highlight the quality of the ingredients. The variety of dishes on the menu ensures that there’s something for everyone, from classic favorites to unique options that keep you coming back for more.

What sets this restaurant apart is its affordability, especially for seafood. It’s rare to find such high-quality seafood dishes at such reasonable prices, particularly in this area.

If you’re looking for a restaurant that combines great taste, healthy options, and excellent value, Asia Authentic Cuisine is the place to go. Highly recommended!

review_text:
My family and I had a wonderful dining experience at the restaurant today. Every dish, from the food to the drinks and dessert, was absolutely satisfying!

🍗 Fried Chicken: The fried chicken was served hot with a perfectly crispy coating, while the inside remained tender and juicy. The seasoning was well-balanced and suited everyone’s taste.

🍕 Two Pizzas: Both pizzas were delicious. The crust was lightly crisp, fresh dough, with fragrant melted cheese and generous toppings. Each flavor had its own charm, and both were very tasty and enjoyable.

🥤🍰 Drinks + Cake: The drinks were refreshing and not overly sweet. The cake was soft, fragrant, and not too heavy—perfect as a dessert after the meal.

✨ Overall, everything matched my family’s taste perfectly. Every dish was flavorful, enjoyable, and simply made us happy.

Besides the delicious food, I was also impressed with the staff at the restaurant. Everyone was attentive, friendly, and always ready to help with quick and polite service.

The restaurant is very clean, from the dining tables to the surrounding area. The soft background music added a relaxing and pleasant atmosphere, making our family meal even more enjoyable.

The roti canai sarang burung was delicious and flavourful. The roti canai was not rubbery and the way it was swimming in curry gravy complemented it. The eggs was cooked perfectly and it was easy to eat and not too messy.

Overall a great place for breakfast. Not that many food options but still okay to eat.

Moving forward, the restaurant could have decorated interior with a bicycle stye shop witth accessories hanging on the wall and displays of spare parts for sale. A missed branding opportunity but can still be implemented if they are serious of their brand. Please turn this place onto a cool cafe/shop that will be a unique experience for customers!

author: Danny IT

review_text: The location is strategic and you can spot lots of shops around this residential area.The facilities are good and convenient. The security is good and the staff are helpful as well. The space for vehicles to go around this place however is a bit tricky - one needs to rely on the convex mirror to pay extra attention on the coming cars.
author: Hajar Zainal

review_text: Place: once a top rated condo with supposedly leading service staff, but over time, degraded to the worst low class condo within the area. Outwardly looking nice, but inwardly, poorly serviced lifts, dirty pool, poorly maintained facilities, and ill managed crazy individuals in the lobby (and I don't JUST mean a psychiatric patient sleeping in the lobby) but also the lackadaisical attitude of management staff working here. My experience staying here was bad and was 1 of the places that I just couldn't wait to get out of. Parking is a hassle all the time  and I'm appalled that some units here don't even have allocated parking lots. Visitor parking are mostly reserved by shops setting up front with hardly any room to sometimes drive (especially on the end of C&G) and constant blocking by management due to renovation works. Really poor management. Good thing I got out fast.
author: C RM

review_text:
How on earth the fire alarm system goes wrong causing all resident can't even go back to their home?
Elevator isn't working i can understand, but staircase's exit door is locked? What if there are really fire outbreak and i was trapped there? GET BURNED TO DEATH DUE TO MANAGEMENT'S NEGLIGENCE?

author: J神_ Jason.ROK

review_text: Security is high because all doors need access card , laundry 24 hours below this residence , parking also is easy to access.
author: QiqiLala Maishaitui

review_text: Condominium apartment in the budding Nusa Sentral area. Newly built with clean apartments. Very good security system; downside being you have to come out to let your guest in at the main entrance. Location is directly accessible and about 5km from Bukit Indah, Medini, Kota Iskandar, Mutiara Rini and Gelang Patah.
author: Bosede Edwards

review_text:
My first time visiting, though I've heard of this Japanese-owned bakery a couple of years back. Quaint space offering a variety of freshly baked bread and buns. I tasted a few types which were tasty. Their Curry Pan stood out with its bold, flavourful chicken curry filling.

Hot Cross Buns are currently available for the upcoming Easter season. I tried the Original which had a pronounced cinnamon and lemon zest profile, with a generous amount of raisins.
author: Alanna

review_text:
We went after the lunch hour, and the bakery was empty. There wasn’t much bread left, and the space felt quite dimly lit.

The bread has a generous filling, but the texture wasn’t as soft as we expected given the price. The pricing is on the higher side compared to local brands, whose bread tastes better and remains enjoyable even the next day.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text: One of the must come shops if we were around here. Came here today after a few months. While the varieties and taste of the bread are still the same, the quality of service by the service counter staff is no longer as before.  Instead of feeling as a valued customer, I am feeling that the customer is at mercy of the service counter staff with no smile and customer didn't know how to count for the current store promotion of buy 3 get 1 free. May not want to patronise more although the bread is nice.
author: Hammie Devil

review_text:
Some bakeries make bread.
But Pan Kobo—helmed by Tomo, a kind Korean baker married to a Malaysian—makes magic. ✨

Pan Kobo – oh woof, my Saturday ritual is set in stone: trot straight here for their sourdough fruit loaf. 🍇🍞 Forget Verona’s soft airy loaves that leave my tummy still grumbling—Pan Kobo’s sourdough is hearty, chewy, and fills me up just right.

Their rusks are a crunchy delight (way better than factory biscuits), and come festive seasons they shine with hot cross buns at Easter and Christmas cakes & chocolates that make tails wag across JB. 🎄🐾

But here’s one thing this loyal pup has to bark out—please, dear Pan Kobo, cut down the sugar in your cakes, especially the carrot cake. 🙏 A little less sweetness would mean I could enjoy my slice without dragging my hooman on a guilt trip.

If I could I bark it from the rooftop  Pan Kobo is the best bakery in JB, paws down. Better than SDS, Lavender, Secret Recipe, Donna Bakehouse, Verona, Verbena , Manzanita—you name it.

So Pan Kobo, keep up the quality, mind the sugar, and you’ll stay the knockout champ of JB bakeries—a true Pan “KO”bo win! 👊🥖
author: Patience SS

review_text:
Pan Kobo in Horizon Hills is one of the few truly authentic Japanese-owned bakeries in Johor, and the quality is consistently impressive. Their signature Curry Pan bread stands out for its soft, fluffy texture and rich, buttery flavor that feels genuinely Japanese in style. The bakery keeps a clean, welcoming atmosphere, and service is quick and polite.

Popular items tend to sell out early, especially on weekends, so visiting earlier in the day is recommended. Overall, Pan Kobo is a reliable choice for anyone looking for high-quality Japanese baking made with care.
author: Yuki Takei

restaurant_name: Uncle Pou Wok Restaurant (補鑊佬福建面)
review_text:
Every 11 of the month has buy 1 free 1 hokkien mee. We happened to be there and got this deal.. hokkien mee is not bad. Ordered sweet and sour pork too..its nice n fresh meat. Crispy and crunchy. Ordered steam grouped fish fillet and we xiang as well. Price is reasonable for 2 pax at rm105.

The sambal chilli comes with fresh lime and was good. Can tell its home made.
author: Alice Yeo

restaurant_name: Uncle Pou Wok Restaurant (補鑊佬福建面)
review_text: We had the Hokkien Mee, Yong Tao Fu, Chicken, Garlic Deep Fried Pork, Salted Egg Bitter gourd, and Nai Bai... maybe the taste is not quite our cup of tea, dishes were all on the sweeter side , not enough wok hei on the hokkien mee. Kids all agreed the vegetables were the best..

Lovely spot to enjoy dinner. No prior booking and we were able to find take for 8 of us, on the eve of CNY Eve. Plenty of parking space.
Food wise, special fried rice must order! Some kind of Basmati rice I suspect, very unique texture. Salted egg sauce crab very tasty, not overly sweetened.
Other dishes were above average. We enjoyed our dinner and everyone left happy and full.
author: Poh Soh Lee

review_text: Decided on this restaurant due to high Google reviews. Ordered crab (RM208 per kg for Size L), with a milder salted egg taste suited for lighter palates. The sambal prawn and shrimp paste chicken are worth trying. It’s a bit pricey, but good for dining experience.
author: Kai Kai The Panda

review_text:
Crowded restaurant and pretty easy parking. Lots of local enjoying the seafood here. Ordered a pair of baked oyster and also two medium Size crab 🦀 requested black pepper style.
The oyster 🦪 is 4/5, tasty and fresh. However, the crab is only average, not up to par. The shell is soggy and doesn’t taste fresh at all, Seasons is also so-so, I rate it 2/5 at best.
Restaurant atmosphere is great and plenty of family enjoying dinner l. Maybe need to come back and try other dishes. Overall, the main reason for 2 stars is price vs value for money.
author: John Koh

review_text:
I had dinner at Yi Jia Seafood, Bukit Indah, Johor Bahru, with my family and another friend’s family, a total of seven people. The overall experience was decent but fell short of expectations, especially considering the final bill of RM239, which felt slightly on the high side for a standard dinner selection.

We ordered several familiar dishes, including vegetables, tofu, egg, and some meat dishes. The food was fine but nothing particularly memorable. While the flavors were acceptable, they did not stand out compared to other Chinese seafood restaurants in Johor Bahru that I have tried. It was a good meal, but not one that left a lasting impression.

On the positive side, service was attentive and efficient. The staff were quick to take our orders and dishes were served promptly, which made the dining process smooth. The restaurant atmosphere was comfortable and family friendly, although fairly typical and not especially distinctive.

Overall, I would rate Yi Jia Seafood at three out of five stars. For me, food is a three, service deserves a four, and atmosphere earns a three. It is a reasonable option for casual dining, but I would explore other places for better value or a more memorable culinary experience.
author: Atwood Chai

review_text:
Saw great review before coming over.

Parking and queue. Arrive at around 5pm so there is totally no queue with lots of parking

Food. Ordered frozen sweet/sour pork, sambal kangkong, tofu, butter crab, golden big head prawn. Food was generally good, but not exceptional.

Service. Service was pretty prompt since there is not much people. The uncle that took our order kept pushing for bigger portion for the dishes when we clearly only had 3A+1K which was not really helpful. In the end, the golden big head prawn was too much.

Price. Much more expensive than what we tot it would be. End up with a bill of 450+rm. The other dishes were pretty affordable, but the crab was alright at 130 but the big head prawn was so expensive at 267rm.

Conclusion: Seafood was overpriced and food was not nice enough to justify the price. Probably wun recommend to others.
author: Sir Seng

review_text: A hidden gem mamak inside Horizon Hills. Looks so ordinary but the food are so great. Maggie goreng is so delicious, roti canai is one of the best I have had, very 'garing'. Definitely better than another mamak restaurant around the corner. My first choice for mamak shop now.

best italian food and pizza ever！！！
had been here since 2023 and the standard still remain it! Fresh ingredients and best cocktail ever!!! Definitely would come again, come for it if you look for authentic Italian restaurant!

review_text: Cosy little restaurant / bar. The host and staff are all very nice and friendly, and really try their best. They have the same menu as Coppola it seems, and the same menu from the grill outside. When they are busy sometimes the service is slow as the waiters need to run both sides for Coppola and Sofia. But the food is excellent, as always. The best pizzas in Johor, and award winning tiramisu.
