author: Gejendrran Siva Kumaran

review_text: Good service with friendly Staff  ♥️ Cocktails looks elegant 🍸Nice experience ❤️✨
author: Aliena Emelo

review_text: I believe this is the network/chain of restaurants comprising of Coppola Pizzaria, Sofia di Stefano, Istanbul, Cafe Anatolia and Mexico.... all in one row together. We are frequent patrons of ALL of these restaurants, and we are extremely happy with their food and service. Coppola is a family favourite with their pizzas. I personally love Istanbul best, and occasionally drop in to Mexico or Cafe Anatolia for a lunchtime takeaway. We rarely have to venture out of Horizon Hills when we choose to eat out because of this great selection of international restaurants. Really kudos to the management - running one restaurant is tough enough... but to run a string of them, and successfully too? Very well done indeed 👏
author: Kimberley Howarth

review_text:
Had a really lovely experience here. We tried the lamb pizza and the tiramisu, and both were excellent. The pizza was flavourful and well balanced, and the tiramisu was a perfect way to finish the meal.

The service was attentive and friendly throughout, and the overall atmosphere of the restaurant was warm and comfortable. It’s a great spot for a relaxed meal, and we genuinely enjoyed our time here.
author: Khoo Yu Kee

review_text:
Had such a lovely experience at Capolo Pizza Restaurant. The atmosphere was warm and cozy, perfect for a relaxed meal. The food was amazing, honestly might be the best pizza I’ve had in a long time.
As a sweet surprise, the house treated us to a tiramisu cake for Valentine’s Day, which made the evening even more special. Great food, great vibes, and thoughtful service. Will definitely be back!
author: CWY

review_text:
We went for group dinner. We ordered the spaghetti with truffle. When the food arrived, we were not informed that adding truffle into the food requires an additional surcharge of RM88/g, and we could not see the weighing scale to know exactly how much truffle was added. The waiter then told us that he has put 3g of truffles on our pasta. Then I asked him why he never ask me first beforehand & he could not answer my question. We all felt that we were fooled by the waiter on this pasta. It costed us RM306 for a plate of pasta.

The restaurant resolved this by charging us for only 2g of the additional truffle. However, all of this could had been avoided if the waiter was better at communicating with the customers.
author: Foodie25

review_text:
place was nicely decorated, servers were quick and attentive!

we had the mushroom/bruschetta toast, creamy garlic prawns, prosciutto pizza & mushroom ravioli!
everything was pretty good except the ravioli (the skin was good but the sauce was a little bland) and the pizza was a little bit burnt on some parts. items are also on the pricier side but worth a try!
author: nangg -

review_text: Amazing spot open till late night. New carbonara on the menu is fantastic, creamy but not too heavy. Best tiramisu I have had for a long time too. Outdoor seating at night is a huge plus! Thumbs up for the service crew too, highly recommended!
author: Oh Jun Sheng Jeremy

review_text:
Has a strong reputation for high-quality Ottoman Turkish cuisine. The owner will proudly tell you they serve Dato's, politicians and royalty :-D

+ Ambience - We felt like we have stepped into Turkey. The place was beautifully and traditionally decorated, has "pavilion booths", and used exquisite tableware.

+ Must take off shoes, which creates a cozy, homely vibe.

+ Excellent polite service from staff like Taha, Saddam.

+ All the dishes are rich, flavourful and authentic.
- Some of the grilled meat can be dry though.

- Mineral water bottle (RM5,10)
- RM40 charge if bring own (birthday) cake.
- Avg RM80-100 per pax, excluding alcohol.

+ Toilets are clean and beautifully adorned with medieval-design taps.

Tip: Reservations highly recommended via WhatsApp, as the venue frequently reaches capacity.

Much better than its namesake restauarant in Singapore, which is known for overcharging for basic sides.
author: Yong Hui, Ronny Tan

review_text:
Great experience and nice food and service. Shout out to Saddam who is really doing great job. Keep it up.
Its a hidden gem at Horizon Hills.. Very nice place, plenty of parking. We will definitely be back.
(ps: slightly on the pricey side but worth it)
author: Kathy 's

review_text: Great place for a delightful dining experience with authentic Turkish cuisine. The food is rich in flavor especially the kebabs and lambs. Service is warm, attentive, and efficient, making guests feel genuinely welcomed. The staff are knowledgeable and helpful when recommending dishes, and the portions are generous. The ambiance is cozy and suitable for both families and casual meetups. Definitely a go-to spot in the area for quality food and great service.
author: Peng Wan Choo

review_text: Thursday evening, 6pm: The restaurant was about half full, nicely decorated with a unique Turkish lamp, and dimly lit. Guests are required to remove their shoes before entering. The food was quite good, though on the pricier side, and the service was excellent. We especially enjoyed the bread.total bill rm480, included a 16% tax.
author: Ong NN

review_text:
Stepping into this place truly feels like being transported straight to Turkey. From the warm ambience to the decor, everything sets the perfect mood before the food even arrives.

The dishes are simply marvelous – rich, flavorful, and absolutely authentic. Every bite bursts with spices and textures that remind you why Turkish cuisine is world-renowned. The kebabs are juicy and perfectly grilled, the bread soft and fragrant, and the dips creamy with just the right balance. The flavors carry that unmistakable touch of tradition, as though they were prepared in the heart of Istanbul itself.

It’s rare to find food this genuine outside of Turkey, but here in JB, this restaurant delivers it beautifully. A must-visit for anyone who loves authentic flavors and wants to savor a little piece of Turkey without hopping on a plane.
author: Alhidir Syah Akim

restaurant_name: Mykonos Greek Restaurant, Horizon Hills JB
review_text: Very nice atmosphere and deco. Definitely great for dates. Was here for an anniversary. All the food were savory in taste and of great quality. So I think it really justified the cost. The boss and staff were also all very cheerful and polite. Feel like I'm no longer in JB but in a Greece when dining. The boss also owns the Istanbul restaurant next door which is also great.
author: Jason Aw

restaurant_name: Mykonos Greek Restaurant, Horizon Hills JB
review_text:
Saturday, 12.30pm the restaurant was peaceful and comfortable.
It occupies two shop lots and is beautifully decorated. They offer lunch sets where you can choose your main dish, bread, and salad, with prices clearly listed. Draft beer from their sister shop is also available, and they can bring it over upon request.

The service team is warm and helpful. We enjoyed the food with lightly seasoned so you can really taste the freshness, we like especially the grilled salmon. The prices are on the higher end, but with the ambience and food quality, it’s definitely a great spot to enjoy a good meal.
author: Ong NN

restaurant_name: Mykonos Greek Restaurant, Horizon Hills JB
review_text:
Always satisfied dining in Mykonos Greek Restaurant. It was good to see Stefan (owner) and I was excited with my fresh hand picked, air-flown white truffle from Piedmont Italy on my pasta! It was delish down to the last bit. Our dinner started with shots of ouzo, gotta be a Greek style! Enjoyed my fave Meze Dip platter as always while Mom savored her Grana Padano Cheese Carbonara. Grouchy had a big serving of chicken Souvlaki. Greek wines, as it should be to accompany our mains and ended with lovely orange burnt cheesecake, bougastas, and of course,  coffees for the road.

The Wine Dinner event was great too!

#iamkbonita #horizonhills #malaysia #famtime
author: Khristine Bonita

restaurant_name: Mykonos Greek Restaurant, Horizon Hills JB
review_text:
This place has a distinctly Greek blue vibe. Every snapshot looks great.

The food selection is quite extensive, mainly Greek dishes with generous portions, perfect for sharing with a group. However, the taste wasn't really to my liking, so I won't go into much detail about the food!
author: Kenji Aiba

restaurant_name: Mykonos Greek Restaurant, Horizon Hills JB
review_text: What a lovely dinner at Mykonos! A pretty restaurant coupled with delicious food and excellent service. We really can't ask for more! It was our first time eating Greek food, thank you Raj for making some very good recommendations for us and being very attentive to our needs throughout the meal. We enjoyed the fresh and yummy seafood and your warm service. Will definitely recommend to our family and friends, see you again soon!
author: Julia

restaurant_name: 新天地烧腊小厨 Restoran Shintianti
review_text: best fish head curry. Must try glass char siew and crispy roast pork
author: Wilson Ho

restaurant_name: 新天地烧腊小厨 Restoran Shintianti
review_text: We had dinner here after golf at Horizon Hills. The server was very helpful and recommended good dishes for our dinner. Also helped us download Touch and Go app for payment. The food is authentic and portion served is huge for 3 pax. Will definitely return to try other dishes
author: Bian Lee

restaurant_name: 新天地烧腊小厨 Restoran Shintianti
review_text:
Uniqueness: 8/10
Experience: 8/10
Value: 9/10

Rare found in this part of the city. Horizon Hill & Iskandar areas. Family owned and managed. Clean and neat place for fresh and delicious cooking of local dishes for dinner. At lunch, BBQ-pork is superbly crafted by charcoal - absolutely tasteful. Nanyang coffee before 16:00 is a bonus by Grandpa Sifu Cheng. Private home kitchen.
author: Peng Tang

restaurant_name: 新天地烧腊小厨 Restoran Shintianti
review_text: Tried their curry noodles with chicken and char siew. Flavours were decent, but the price was relatively expensive. The restaurant was quite hot inside — could use better ventilation.
author: James Low

restaurant_name: 新天地烧腊小厨 Restoran Shintianti
review_text: Dropped in for lunch with wife and we had their curry fish head, bittergourd with salted egg yolk and roast pork. The food was quite tasty and the restaurant was clean. The price is a little higher than I would have expected, but it wasn't a big issue as I felt it was still value for money.
author: Oliver Khaw

review_text: Good place vibe with friends and family. We had cheese fries amd quesidilla. Food presentation and service was very good. Especially night time to have shisha and chill with friends.
author: Chaithralakshmi VR

review_text: this is our second visit to Anatolia since our last visit last year, the best nasi mandhi we ever tried, traveling all the way from Singapore to again try their mutton mandhi, however turned out they only open at 4-5pm, we reached there at 3pm, the restaurant manager was so kind and nice by trying his best to serve us the mutton mandhi, thank you so much for the 5 star service! And thank you so much for the cheese cake compliment to us, will definitely come back again!
author: Panda Panda

review_text: Visited Kafe Anatolia today. Without any doubt the place was beautiful and the staff were really nice but the food didn't impress us. May be because our expectations were too high by reading all the comments and by looking at the place. The lamb and chicken were too dry, fillings were too less and the bread was hard. Serving sizes were also small. I hope they can improve their quality and quantity
author: Ayesha Ali

review_text: Definitely the best Turkish food I've ever had, I really have no other feedback. I strongly recommend everyone to dine at this restaurant when you're in Johor Bahru and craving for Turkish food (the Chef is from Syria). All their dishes (Mandi Lamb, Meze Plater of 4 {vegan}, and Lavash Döner) that we tried tasted really great. I'd like to come back again next time; all the staff were very friendly and professional as well
author: SeungJun Kim

review_text: We had hummus and shasuka to start off. The hummus was smooth and creamy while the shashuka featured nicely roasted red peppers. We had a recommended lamb kebab wrapped in cheese and dough which was perfect with the crisp raw onions and yogurt dip. Ambience was a 10/10 outdoors! This restaurant, as well as the Greek and Mexican restaurants flanking it are owned by the same owner.
author: Roaming Ramblers

review_text: First trying the Korean foods here, never expected the taste is quite nice, and I ordered the set meal during weekday is only at rm18.90, free flow for side dishes, including the main dish, pancake and drink as well. The staff are all very friendly and helpful. Will definitely come back again.
author: Yong Kek Ting

review_text:
A cosy Korean spot that you probably wouldn’t guess serves Korean food at first. They’re really generous with their banchan (반찬), though the kimchi was a bit too sour for our taste.

Portions are big too, and we like that they have a wide variety of popular Korean dishes on the menu. This is our second time here and definitely won’t be our last.
author: Mabbel Elroy

review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Great Christmas Atmosphere at Good Box Korea Restaurant Bukit Indah

I visited Good Box Korea and the experience was wonderful. The restaurant was beautifully decorated with festive lights and ornaments, creating a cozy and cheerful holiday vibe.

The food was delicious — everything was fresh, flavourful, and served hot. The crispy Korean seafood platter & the abalone porridge was so delicious & enjoyable.

Overall, the Christmas ambiance and great food made our visit very memorable. A lovely place to celebrate the festive season! 🎄🍽️✨
author: Ben Chua

review_text: One of the best and most authentic korean restaurant we tried in JB so far. The flavor, presentation and quality of ingredients are top notch. Comes with complimentary side dishes and a deviled egg. Prices abit on higher side but it is served in a big portion so it's totally worthit. Ambience is pretty and clean.
author: Bea G.

review_text:
Our Singaporean-Citizen-but-JB-resident friend says this is the best Korean-Western restaurant in JB and hence brough us here :-)

+ Has a very nice bakery section

+ Free and refillable Korean side dishes (banchan) served upon arrival.

+ Pork Cutlet Set (RM 38.9) - thick, juicy, not oily
+ Big Size Pork Cutlet set (RM 39.9) - face-size meat
Cold Soba Noodles (RM 32)
- Bulgogi glass noodle - beef has a strong taste

+ Kimchi Fried Rice w Cheese (RM 32)

review_text:
Really love this restaurant!
The moment I walked in, it felt like I was in Mexico.
The interior is colorful and beautifully decorated, with plenty of Instagram-worthy corners to take photos.

The atmosphere is calm, relaxing, and very comfortable.

Although it wasn’t crowded, the food was absolutely delicious.
There are plenty of choices, both meat and vegetarian dishes, and everything looks so unique.
Every dish I ordered today was amazing — the ingredients were generous, the portions were big, and it’s perfect for sharing.
The flavors were spot on and matched our taste perfectly.

The staff were also very friendly and attentive, recommending their signature dishes and desserts. Unfortunately, I was already too full to try the desserts this time, but I’ll definitely save that for my next visit.

This place is truly worth a try!!!

review_text:
recently had the pleasure of dining at JB Mexican Restaurant, and it was an absolutely fantastic experience from start to finish.

The atmosphere is vibrant and welcoming, with colorful décor that immediately sets the tone for an authentic Mexican dining experience. The staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and made us feel right at home the moment we walked in.

The food was outstanding. Every dish was packed with bold, fresh flavors and beautifully presented. The tacos were perfectly seasoned, the enchiladas were rich and satisfying, and the homemade salsa had just the right balance of heat and freshness. You can really taste the quality of the ingredients and the care that goes into each meal.

review_text: We really enjoyed the food here! Everything was delicious and high quality. What we appreciated most however was the service and the friendly staff. review_text: Came here for lunch. Parking is a little bit tricky at this time in the area in general because of the many restaurants in the area. The staff here are all very friendly and kind. The restaurant is also airy and clean, but unfortunately felt a bit hot. Not many stalls were open during lunch, seems like only the nasi kandar. I wanted to try to order some roti, but didn't seem like there was anyone to take my order. The nasi kandar had many different dishes and it also looked like you can order mee. I had some kari kambing, tempeh and 1 fried egg. The person serving me was very friendly. You can't take/choose your own dishes, which was a bit of a bummer. The staff gave me 1pc of mutton with my kari kambing that looked very big, but it was unfortunately just a big chunk of bone with not much meat. So sad. The kari sauce however was very delicious. My tempeh and fried egg were so-so. They give you a card that you can bring to the counter and scan. The price here is quite expensive imo... rice + kari kambing (with 1 piece of mutton that was mostly bone) + small portion of tempeh + 1 fried egg, plus a glass of plain water came up to RM17.

review_text:
Extremely disappointing Ramadan buffet experience.

Before making our reservation, we specifically called to check what would be served. We were told clearly that there would be satay and crab. However, when we arrived, neither of those items were available. When we asked the staff about it, we were told it was a “miscommunication.” That explanation is unacceptable — especially when customers are making decisions based on what was communicated over the phone.

On top of that, by 7:30pm most of the food was already finished. When we asked if the dishes would be topped up, we were told that it was “finished already.” For a paid buffet, food should be replenished throughout the dining period.

To make matters worse, we were served using disposable cups and plates, which felt very unprofessional and not reflective of a proper buffet experience.

Overall, this did not feel like a Ramadan buffet at all. Very disappointing and not worth the price.

This place serves the herbal dark broth version of bak kut teh, which I personally prefer over the peppery white version. The soup was rich and flavorful, with generous portions of pork.

We also ordered an extra side of liver, which turned out to be a great choice. Thick, perfectly cooked slices that were absolutely delicious. Everything we had was tasty. The restaurant itself was clean, including the toilets, and there’s even a handwashing sink with soap in the outdoor seating area, which was a nice touch.

Overall, a satisfying meal with quick service and a convenient location.

restaurant_name: 腾茗记云吞面 (TMJ Wan Tan Mee)
review_text:
TMJ Wantan Mee is a well-loved eatery, famous for its signature dish: Wantan Mee. This classic Cantonese noodle dish features springy egg noodles, savory dumplings (wantan), and fresh leafy greens.

Authentic and Delicious Flavor, A hallmark of TMJ Wantan Mee is its genuine Cantonese taste. The broth, noodles, and dumplings combine to create a deeply satisfying culinary experience.
The wantan are a standout feature, known for their generous filling and delectable savory flavor
A significant highlight is the texture of the noodles themselves. They are consistently described as being incredibly tasty and remarkably smooth, a quality that keeps patrons returning.
Wantan Mee generally offers very reasonable prices, making it a popular choice

review_text: Love the wanton here. Tried the black sauce one with chilli. One of the better ones I've tried. Noodles are not overcooked.the best part is the wanton and soup. super flavourful and fresh. the meat in the wanton remains moist. even the fried version, the meat retains the moisture well.

Beside the noodle, we ordered the fried wanton and dumplings, and I must confessed that they provide very generous stuffing, unlike most which just merely gives u enough meat and passed off as wanton or dumpling.

The stall offers "black or white" version depending on your liking. Will visit again.

review_text:
201 砂拉越叻沙 Sarawak Laksa Normal (Mee Hun) = RM15.90
Service Charge 6% = RM0.95

This is another one of those Modern Kopitiams in the Area. The place doesn't look new and feels like it has been around for quite a few years already. There weren't much Customers within on a Friday Late-Afternoon at around 3.00pm. The Interior is Air-Conditioned and it is Cooling.

The Lady Boss is from Sarawak herself. While she is Friendly, my First Impression of her is that she has a Very Tired and Very Stressed Out Overall Appearance 感觉整个人很憔悴. I will elaborate more on this later in the Review.

201 砂拉越叻沙 Sarawak Laksa Normal (Mee Hun) = RM15.90

This Sarawak Laksa was the Main Reason why I'm here because I thought it looked very Unique being served in an Egg Omelette Bowl.

The Chilli they served with this is No Joke. It's Very Intensely Salty with an Initial Fiery Heat although it doesn't linger long. Adding Lime intensifies and gives it a Very Strong Sourish Kick. This is a Very Robust and Intense Chilli they have here. Excellent.

Presentation-Wise, its served in an Egg Omelette Bowl which I reckon is made up of at least 2 Eggs. To be fair, it is just an Egg Omelette, nothing particularly special about it, but I just love how Adorable it looked!

As for the Main Dish itself, the Distinct Smell of Sarawak Laksa is there. It is Fragrant, but also slightly Less Intense compared to others that I've tried. Broth is Creamy, Smooth and Savoury. Its also Salty, but not Overly So. There is a Inner Spicy Heat to it and I feel this may even be a Tad Spicier than Poh Lam Laksa in Kuching Sarawak.

Amount of Chicken Slices felt Generous and they taste Meaty, Tender and Not Dry at all. I liked that they also don't have too strong Chickeny Taste.

The Type of Mee Hoon they use is Accurate for a Sarawak Laksa. Not Too Thick, Not Too Thin. Its not QQ but also Not Too Soft. Amount is Acceptable for the Price. Slurping this with the Broth, Chicken, and Taugeh is Enjoyable. There are 2 Fat Mid-Sized Prawns and while they don't have a Super Bouncy Juicy Bite Texture, they are also Not Nua Nua.

As Adorable and Generous as the Amount of Egg Omelette was, I felt that it actually worked against it. As the Meal went on, it did start to feel Jelak, too much "Eggy Overload". If I have a Suggestion, perhaps only make a 1 Egg Omelette instead of 2 Eggs?

Genuine Concern for the Lady Boss's Mental Well-Being

The Lady Boss really gave me the Impression that she is Very Stressed Out even though she was Friendly in her Mannerisms and Tone. I Especially sensed her Stress when I Complimented her Sarawak Laksa and her reply to me was:

"Thank you, but sadly many people don't feel the same way as you do".

It was Heartbreaking to hear her say that. 💔 And to reveal this to a 1st Time Customer tells me that she must have cooped up this feeling and wasn't able to confide in anyone else.

Conclusion and Closing Thoughts

At at Total Combined Price of RM15.90 (S$4.60) this felt slightly more expensive compared to the Sarawak Laksa I had at 猫城茶餐厅 Kuching Style also in Bukit Indah which was RM12.90 (S$3.70). But I felt the Overall Amount of Ingredients here felt alot more.

Personally, I feel this is a Very Well Made Bowl of Sarawak Laksa that tastes Legit. It has a Higher than Usual Level of Spiciness that can even challenge the Famous Kuching Poh Lam Laksa. And in a way, it even wins Poh Lam because Poh Lam don't even put Egg Slices.

The Egg Omelette Bowl is a Solid Idea but I felt it did worked against it as I ended up feeling Jelak towards the End. Despite that, I still respect the Creativity in this.

The Lady Boss will probably not see this Post, but I do hope that she takes a Well Deserved Rest and Come Back Fighting Fresh. Through her Sarawak Laksa, I can tell that she is a Creative Person and has a Good Culinary Sense. It would be very sad to see her Burnout and her Passion for Cooking completely crushed. 加油 Ganbatte!

Not really full house then and I was thinking there might be take away orders. Anyway, it was quite a long wait. I thought we waited around an hour for our first dish to be served. As I started to recce around, I realised that the kitchen was small and there was only one person tending it. He did the preparation and cooking all by himself. This explained why the wait.

We ordered the fried fish in soy sauce, sweet and sour pork, Nai bai in garlic, sambal sotong and a lala with spring onions. All the dishes were good and I especially liked the fish. It was well fried without being too oily and the sauce was awesome. The sotong was cooked to perfection as well without it being too rubbery.

Prices were reasonable and the only drawback was the waiting time.

review_text:
I ordered from Diya Cuisine Restaurant on Foodpanda today and tried their Vegetarian Briyani and Vegetarian Thali Set. Overall, I’m very satisfied with the taste. As a bonus, they even included Kesari as a complimentary dessert !

One thing I really want to highlight is their excellent packaging. Each item was packed individually, curries, appalam, and rice all had their own secure containers. The boiled rice and briyani came in sturdy plastic boxes, and everything was tied properly with an extra layer of plastic to avoid spillage. Although there was a slight spill, it was very manageable thanks to their extra care in packing.

Honestly, I was a bit nervous at first because when you order food via delivery, you never know how the rider might handle it. But Diya Cuisine really impressed me. Compared to many other restaurants, which simply wrap everything in paper without much care, this place shows they respect the customer’s experience. We’re paying for food, and they make sure we receive it in good condition and with quality.

I definitely recommend checking reviews before ordering, and this restaurant truly deserves good feedback. Well done, Diya Cuisine! Keep it up! Food taste need improvise, and thats all👌

review_text:
No wonder we're not able to search online map to find this restaurant because this restaurant has changed owner/boss.
We saw their food advertisement on FB and tried search using the name but to no avail. We decided to drive there and physically finding the shop only to find out it is called Crab Kee restaurant.

We tried the RM89.90 (L-size x 3pcs) mud crabs. The crabs are picked fresh, kept in a box outside the shop straight to fire wok.
We ordered the chili crab dish. The meat is undoubtedly fresh, tender and juicy but the thick gravy can be improved because it lacks the punch of rich tangy sweetness and the aroma spiciness of chili blend with egg.
Overall, still quite satisfactory crab dish due to the price and the L size still acceptable, not too small.

Other dishes we ordered are salted egg sotong, signature tofu, qing long cai, cereal oat prawn.
Salted egg sotong is very aromatic, batter fried crispy on the outside and soft chewy texture on the inside. Signature tofu is very flavourful with soft tofu coated with rich gravy and lots of minced meat. Qing Long Cai is lightly stir fried and maintain its vegetable crispiness and lastly, cereal oat prawn is fragrant coated with sweet and crunchy cereal oat.

Overall, a very good dining experience. The ladyboss is approachable and friendly.

The food might look simple but actually it’s quite tasty. Fish is fresh and does not have “soil” smell associated with Seabass, dove in Teochew steamed style. The hot plate tofu is good and goes well with the rice. The sambal kangkong is not oily and not too spicy, done right and we enjoyed the veg.

For price of $98 without service charge, 4 dishes, 4 plate of rice and pot of tea, I think it’s reasonable and food is good too.

Family owned zhichar with cute sons to take orders. As they cook orders table by table, the food will take some time to be served during peak hours.

Fish head steamboat is tastes nice and generously filled with ingredients; fish, fish maw, yam, tofu, tang oh vegetables and white cabbage.

Minced meat omelette was also really well done, crispy and flavourful, cooked to perfection. Of course expect it to be oily since it’s the egg is fried.

Not pictured is the tumeric lemongrass chicken which is also tasty, turned out in a claypot and more soupy than we expected but still surprisingly yummy!

However do note that the food is on the salty side, may want to inform the chef to reduce salt when ordering.

Cleanliness of table is not the best as well, but will visit again for the food.

review_text: This coffee shop is where I go for breakfast almost every day, except on weekends. The morning mee xiam and rice noodles at the vegetable stall are both good, and the afternoon vegetable vendors are also quite seasoned. The chicken rice stalls don't open until after 10:00 AM. While it's unlikely to be ranked among the top ten chicken rice stalls in Johor Bahru, you'll find it pretty good! And the food is very affordable. Teo O (my go-to drink) is still only 1.40! And the reason I come here isn't the cheap and delicious food, but the authentic coffee shop atmosphere. The customers are almost all regulars, many of whom come daily like me. The owner, the uncle, won't wait for you to finish your rice noodles before asking, "Where's your tea?" I was seriously ill for a while, and the uncle even sat down to check on me and offered a bunch of easy ways to recover. Breakfast: a cup of hot tea, a plate of affordable rice noodles, and a bunch of uncles chatting away. It's as classic as it gets.

Parking is also hassle-free with plenty of spaces available, both free and paid, making it convenient for diners.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to enjoy great food at an affordable price.

author: Ezzeline Iswan

review_text:
This ice cream shop will definitely make you smile from the moment you enter until you leave!!!
Colourful design, cutie decoration, nice desserts, awesome services!!

The staff is so friendly, always putting smile on her face. This really enlightened my day!!

There are a lot of choices for ice cream in a day when you compare to other ice cream shops.
They have common flavours like chocolate mint, chocolate, matcha, french vanilla and etc and unique flavours like strawberry peanut butter, black sesame and lychee osmanthus.
The tastes are just perfect, not overly sweet and of course homemade.

You even could choose to have a combination of waffle and ice cream.
Surprisingly their waffle is heavenly delicious!!!

If you don't like desserts, they do serve main course!!

Highly recommended!!

**Thank you for giving me a mini french vanilla cone

#Ichigo nutto ice cream
#Pistachio ice cream
#Kunafa waffle
#Nian gao with churros waffle
author: Littlebrownie 1015

review_text: We had such a wonderful time here with the whole family. The ice cream was delicious with plenty of choices, and the atmosphere was very relaxed and welcoming. We spent a good amount of time enjoying our ice cream while playing board games and cards together, which made the experience even more special. It’s a great place to unwind, bond as a family, and create happy memories. Highly recommended for families looking for a fun and comfortable spot to spend quality time together.

review_text: We ordered the nian gao waffle and it was so good!! Chips and tea was great too after our ice cream.  Staff is super friendly and let us try out the flavors before we order. Very spacious place, nice deco and plenty of board games available if you wanna hang out with your friends or families. Will definitely come back again for a chill afternoon.
author: Melody Yap

review_text:
Located along coastal line at Danga Bay.
Its built Kelong-style .. with a wooden plank bridge from beach to restaurant.

Serving usual Seafood Restaurant menu items.
We tried their Black Pepper Crab @ RM168.00 / kg - nice saucy peppery taste, not overwhelming...
Had 2 varieties of their "Big Head" mussels - in ginger and onion sauce, the other in sambal
The former style is better, both in taste and meat texturing.
Beers, Stouts and a variety of soft drinks and juices are available.
As there are a few of similar styled restaurants along the coastal, we decided to try each restaurant on other visits and update here.
author: Perry Pacific

review_text:

review_text: First time visiting with a group of eight, and we were thoroughly impressed! The seafood was delicious,fresh, prices were reasonable, and the staff were incredibly friendly. Highly recommended to seafood lover for a great seafood meal here .

review_text: Not so sure about the hygiene as this restaurant is on a kelong but the food sure was tasty. Fish was steamed to perfection. Salted egg squid was one of the best. Staff were friendly and they are honest about the pricing. Side note, the toilets are horrifying.
author: lion_doge

review_text:
Good place to eat with family! I came around 12pm, and we were the first customers at that time. We waited about 10–15 minutes before the waitress came to take our order, probably because they had just opened and were still preparing. The food arrived about 15–20 minutes later, served hot and nicely presented. The portions are generous and great for sharing.

The place itself is pleasant, located right at the edge of the land with a partial view of Country Garden and even Singapore in the distance. Despite coming at noon, it wasn’t too hot. The restaurant is quite spacious, with round tables similar to those in Chinese or sushi restaurants. You can also see their fresh seafood displayed in tubs near the entrance. Parking isn’t too difficult, but you’ll need to walk a few minutes from the parking area to the seating area.
author: Selvinia Nofy

review_text:
Appreciate that this seafood restaurant provides my friend and I a very delicious vegetarian meal, even though vegetarian food is not in their menu.

We had a satisfying meal of  curry mock meat, fried vegetables, Thai Tofu, omelette with dried preserved radish and Thai coconuts. We truly enjoyed the food and hospitality here, with its beautiful Kelong view and nice romantic English ballads.

A truly beautiful Malaysian experience.

review_text: 1st time trying out this Seafood Place , TBH The food here was really too good till me and my friends ordered one more plate of the Kam Heong Lala. The steam Nyonya and Thai Chicken was yummy. The prawns was really fresh and the size was huge . All the dishes was recommended by the lady Boss. The service was top notch and the food delivered superb fast to our tables. Definitely if you’re looking for a Muslim friendly restaurant do give a try at This Restaurant, highly recommended. Overall, it’s terrible—a complete disappointment.

Spent 700rm for 3 crabs plus 6 other dishes. About 180rm per crab, slightly more than 1kg each.

The walk there from carpark is quite an experience, lots of dogs (but they are not aggressive) and had to walked past some houses.
author: Yuanxiong Tan

The only down sides to this place are that it's a little hard to find and a little smelly (from the ocean). You might get bitten by mosquitoes too, so bring insect repellent.

author: Akmal Hamdy

review_text:
I’ve been ordering the nasi goreng petai from this place for almost 3 years now — yes, THREE years. At this point, I think this nasi goreng and I are in a serious relationship.

The taste? Always consistent. The spice? Never misses. Every single time I order, it tastes exactly like the first time — which is rare, because we all know sometimes food quality can go on “holiday.” But not here. These people are serious about their petai business.

Sometimes I try to convince myself to order something new… then I see “nasi goreng daging petai” on the menu, and my loyalty gets tested again. Spoiler: it’s also amazing.

Basically, if consistency was an Olympic sport, this restaurant would take home gold. I don’t even check other nasi goreng petai places anymore — why risk heartbreak?

So yes, this review is long overdue, but consider it a love letter to the one dish that never lets me down. Keep up the good work, chef — you’ve kept my stomach and soul happy for years ❤️🔥
author: Amar Naqiu

review_text:
Hi, we come from KL and we saw this on TikTok. We ordered Nasi Goreng Kampung Ayam & Nasi Goreng Kampung Sotong plus Daging Masak Padprik & Tomyum Seafood.

Trust me, the food here is so delicious!!! The best nasi goreng, tomyum and Padprik I ever tasted. Next time we come to JB I’m definitely coming again and inviting my whole family.

The Nasi Goreng was super spicy tho! They even add more sambal belacan for extra kick. But if you order with the daging padprik, the soy sauce helps to neutralise the spiciness. Oh, and the portion is huge - can share 1 plate between 2 people.

Total paid with drinks was RM51 - shared among 3 people. So affordable. The owners are super friendly and kind.

Semoga dimurahkan rezeki and bisnes semakin maju! 🤲🤲🤲

The portion was generous and they put 3 big medium size, fresh prawns in our seafood orders (tomyam seafood and nasi goreng seafood). Drinks were nice also. Please visit this restaurant if u happen to pass by this area.

review_text: This warung is located near Taman Perling, in Kampung Danga. You order at the counter, and they’ll bring your food to your seat. The food is great—I’ve tried the lontong with sambal kacang, lontong kering, nasi ayam penyet, roti bakar, nasi lemak, and soto. The lontong has a rich, thick santan gravy, so if you’re health-conscious, it might not be for you. But for me, all the food here hits the mark, making it a must-try breakfast spot. Parking is limited, but you can park in the open space or along the side road. With generous portions and decent prices, it’s definitely worth the money. Happy tummy, happy me!

Highly recommended. We will definitely come again.

review_text:

•	Situated at 8, Jalan Abad, Taman Abad, Johor Bahru, 80250  ￼ ￼

Cuisine & Concept
•	A fusion of Arab and Indian cuisine, blending spices, cooking techniques, and culinary traditions from both cultures  ￼ ￼ ￼
•	Signature dishes include Alfaham Chicken with Saffron Rice (RM27), Lambshank Biryani (RM45), Red Snapper Curry (RM130 for a whole fish), platters (RM80–RM120), and claypot dishes (RM25–RM30)  ￼ ￼
•	Also praised are matka biryani, lamb maqluba, kebabs, cheese naan, hummus, Butter Chicken, Mandhi Chicken Rice, Fish Kebab, Prawn 65, and welcoming drinks like Indian milk tea  ￼ ￼ ￼

Ambiance & Service
•	The restaurant boasts a colorful, geometrical décor blending Arab and Indian aesthetics, enhanced by soft lighting and comfortable seating, ideal for gatherings or casual dining  ￼ ￼
•	Described as cozy, welcoming, and clean, with attentive, friendly staff delivering pleasant service

Try signature dishes like Butter Chicken, Biryani, or Matka Biryani for standout taste  ￼
•	Reserve ahead on weekends—the restaurant can get busy  ￼
•	Visit during off-peak hours for a quieter dining experience  ￼

review_text:

Mango lassi was delicious to start, I ended up drinking 3.

We started with hummus and a naan to dip which were great. Very delicious hummus.

I had butter chicken masala for my main whilst my fiancé had the grilled fish. Again super flavourful.

I knocked off points for atmosphere due to it not feeling neither Indian or Arab despite the cuisine being served.

Would come back happily 🙏

The restaurant is located in Straits View Hotel. Dishes are yummy - had the roasted chicken, oatmeal prawn, romaine lettuce with fermented beancurd, lotus root with celery,  ginger spring onion sliced fish.

review_text: Went for a small group celebration, the staff claimed is served no pork. We ordered small portion to try out some of the their food such as steam fish, fried squid, Indonesian style prawn and broccoli. Taste was decent, portion was good enough for 4 adults and 5 kids. We were there quite late so not many patrol and parking space was ample. Location is beside the highway. The washroom was inside the attached hotel. The building is considered bit outdated but still stand tall. Overall experience was quite alright. But the premise served beer. So do clarify with the retail 1st if not comfortable.
author: wong christopher

review_text:
I recently visited Ashhryshoshedap Restaurant and had such a wonderful experience. From the moment I walked in, the atmosphere felt warm and welcoming. The ambience strikes a perfect balance between cozy and stylish, making it a great spot for both casual dining and special occasions.
The food was absolutely delicious. Every dish was beautifully presented and packed with flavour. You can really tell that fresh ingredients and careful preparation are a priority here. The menu offers a good variety, so there’s something for everyone to enjoy.
The service was also outstanding. The staff were friendly, attentive, and knowledgeable about the menu, making helpful recommendations without being pushy. The overall dining experience felt smooth and enjoyable.
If you’re looking for a place with great food, lovely ambience, and excellent service, Ashhryshoshedap Restaurant is definitely worth a visit. I’ll definitely be coming back!
author: anis syahira

review_text:
Loved the vibe here! ✨ Food was beautifully plated and tasted just as good. The staff were warm and welcoming, and the whole place feels very cozy. Perfect spot for a date or a chill hangout with friends.

And this restaurant also delivers a well-balanced dining experience. The menu offers a good variety, with fresh ingredients and well-executed flavours. Service is attentive without being intrusive, and the environment is clean and comfortable. A solid choice for anyone seeking quality dining.

Staff siap datang nyanyi for my parents anniversary. Very joyful! Staff siap ambilkan buaian baby to cater for our baby.

They were very welcoming and made us feel comfortable throughout our visit. Definitely one of the best dining experiences I’ve had. Highly recommended and I will surely come back again!

author: Divya Balan

Overall, both the food quality and service were very disappointing. Definitely will not return.
author: S Wei

review_text:

It's a beach bar, not really a restaurant so don't expect the food to be Michelin standard. Light bar bites and alcohol available. The alcohol is not cheap, you can consider coconut juice instead.

Pro tip: Order a drink, enjoy the view, take more photos and decide if you want to stay for dinner.

review_text: The atmosphere was great and the place looked really nice, but the service was very poor. The staff were slow and not attentive, and the food took a very long time to be served. review_text:
One of the best Shisha experience in town! (And we can say that from our “double” visits).
The staff is super friendly and will choose and perfect the flavor you like. They are also always around to help and you will never end without hot coal warming your Shisha.
Their fresh juices (watermelon, orange) pair really well with the Shisha. Food is very limited - they have a few nuggets and fries but they are very accommodative and let you get pizza from the amazing “Brew N Chill” store next door.
Everything is priced decently and you can enjoy the Shisha either indoors or outdoors watching the sun go down and enjoying the sea breeze.
They don't accept credit cards so remember to carry cash or Touch & Go.

review_text: Just wanted to recommend this great spot by the beach where you can relax and enjoy some shisha. It's a perfect hangout for couples and friends. Perfect way to unwind.

review_text:
Beautiful Place, Extraordinary Food, Great Service - Highly Recommended and Great Place to Celebrate Special Occasion! We celebrated my Hubby's birthday here and we truly had a great experience.
Beautiful Place: the stunning garden entrance itself is so gorgeous. Inside offers a stylish, spacious and nice ambience. Outside you will get a beautiful beach and pool view. Recommended to go during sunset to enjoy the golden hour view!
Extraordinary Food: they offer exquisite menu, more on pricey side but with that flavor and quality is totally worth it. Food was flavorful and really delicious (salute to the chefs!). We ordered in advanced their burnt cheesecake (only available cake they have) and they plated it beautifully for hubby's birthday.
author: Bea G.

review_text:
It’s a very interesting dining outlet located at Danga Bay Johor Bahru.

936 Kitchen is located at level 1, which you have to enter a lobby and take the elevator. If you are driving you will have to park your car at the opposite at the Mall and walk across.

Reason for the five star rating is because of the unique atmosphere, friendly faces and unique fusion food. They also have a terrace overseeing the sea (for smoker) to have a drink before their dinner.

In terms of food, it was pretty interesting and new to me. From presentation to texture and taste… was surprisingly very good. I didn’t pay for it, but I guess it ain’t cheap.

If you are thinking of a nice candle light dinner or impressing your friend or family for a unique dinner experience this will be a nice place.
author: King Kaizer

review_text:
This restaurant is absolutely beautiful.
The moment you step inside, it feels like entering a forest, very Instagrammable and perfect for photos.
The interior is quite spacious and thoughtfully designed, and with the Christmas decorations added, the whole place feels even more festive and cosy.
The food selection isn’t very extensive, and most of the dishes focus on seafood.
If you’re not a seafood lover, the options may feel a bit limited.
It would be great if they could add more non-seafood choices in the future, such as chicken or pork dishes, or classics like fish and chips or chicken chop, to cater to a wider range of preferences.
The food taste good and is well-prepared.
The prices are quite expensive but it’s still worth trying, especially for the ambience and experience.

Food were regular dishes like spaghetti and Rosti, but they were tasty. It's definitely worth a visit.

review_text: Went last night having read the positive reviews. Service was good and staff were attentive. Chef was friendly. Ordered a selection of starters, butter masala paneer and their special chicken biryani. The naan, onion bhajia and  seekh kebab was nice.  The rest of the food lacked the authentic North Indian depth of flavour and was under seasoned. Would not recommend the special biryani, squid or the butter masala paneer as it was simply lacking in flavour however the paneer itself was fresh. Would liked to have tasted a mutton dish but unfortunately there was no mutton available. Squid rings was probably the worst I have had, did not taste fresh and batter arrived soft rather than crisp.  For the dessert tried the chefs recommendation, a molecular fried egg, concept is great, execution needs improvement as texture would be better if the 'egg white' was smoother rather than tasting curdled. On the whole, environment and staff very nice, has potential but unfortunately there was more style than substance and we left disappointed for a place that I had high hopes for.

their level of spiciness when i requested for pedas was just right, not too unbearably spicy either. the teh tarek was flavourful n can taste the tea not just sweet.
my total bill for 3 main dishes, 2 drinks, was RM32 which was very reasonable for what i got.

The staff are super friendly and knowledgeable, making great recommendations and ensuring a fantastic shopping experience. The packaging is neat and keeps the squid fresh for a long time, perfect for gifting or snacking on the go.

review_text:

The zhajiang mian is tasteless, worst noodle I ever tasted.

My dad asked if there is hot tea, the lady said only cold bottled drinks. So my dad ordered it, and RIGHT AFTER the lady gave us free hot tea. This gesture is so distasteful, they must have done it on purpose to earn more.

restaurant_name: 大姐粿条汤(Sister Kuey Teow Soup)
review_text:

Their pork & pepper rice is a must-try — super flavourful and the meat is marinated just right. The special soy-marinated tofu, drumstick, and duck leg are all delicious too. Even the simple dishes like stir-fried cabbage and their soup or fried noodles are surprisingly good.

Portions are big, and the best part? The food isn’t overly salty or spicy — just nicely balanced. Honestly, once you take the first bite, it’s hard to stop. Even their white rice is perfectly cooked.

Looking at the empty plates and bowls, you can tell how much we enjoyed every bite.

The whole place feels very homely, with a warm, family-run atmosphere. Highly recommended if you love comforting, honest cooking. 🍚🍜✨

restaurant_name: Melor House by Nurul Restaurant JB
review_text:
I usually trust high ratings when choosing a place. That is why I decided to try Melor by Lina. I had also seen several TikTok reviews praising it, so my expectations were reasonable. Unfortunately, this visit proved that online praise can sometimes be more generous than reality.

I have worked in several resorts and hotels where Buffet Ramadan was one of the seasonal main revenue driver. With that experience, I understand the importance of planning, refill management, service flow, and guest comfort. Sadly, this was one of the worst Buffet Ramadan experiences I have had.

Parking was very limited. Before organizing a Ramadan buffet, proper parking planning should be considered. I had to deal with security who could not communicate in Malay or English, which delayed me about 15 minutes just to resolve parking.

When I went to take food (only about 15 minutes after berbuka), 2–3 main dishes were already empty and not refilled. Ikan bakar was very limited, and it appeared they only prepared a fixed amount, and once finished, that was it. For a RM68 buffet, this is disappointing. I don't asking for Kambing Golek. Buffet should mean continuous refill, not limited supply.

There were repeated blackouts throughout dinner. The singer mentioned it happened only 2–3 times, but it was clearly more than 7. That difference speaks for itself.

The table setup was careless,  tablecloths too long and curtains brushing diners while eating. There were also mosquitoes and ants in the dining area. Food quality was average at best. The asam pedas lacked authentic taste, and even the ondeh-ondeh was hard to eat.

Honestly, for the same price, nasi kandar offers better value and consistency. I cannot recommend this place unless serious operational improvements are made.

My go to makan place when ever i stopped by tepian tebrau.
Our fav menu will be ikan merah masak lemak cili api nenas, udang telur masin, baby sotong madu n kangkung belacan. This can never be wrong, same delicious savoury taste for many years. During PKP, we even came here for a takeaway.
Wishing their business will be more success n thriving in the future.
author: shima mahyon

review_text: Seafood is pretty fresh. delicious.
author: Winston Chan

review_text: Servis slow..
author: Ice lemon tea

review_text:
First of all, the stingray is extremely fishy and foul. It's so fishy that you can't even swallow it and feel like vomiting. Seriously, it's a complete waste of time.

When it came time to pay, my friend asked the staff if the stingray had been there for a long time. The staff could only answer, "I don't know, sir," with a blank face, no apology, nothing. The service was terrible.

I paid full price for this and I'm beyond disappointed. Not worth my RM43 at all. If you're not good at lunch, don't even think about selling it.

This is a bad review because the service was unacceptable — no apology, no accountability — and the stingray was disgustingly smelly.
author: naryssa -

review_text:
Zikgu Burger is known for their burgers, but I tried the Nasi Zikgu instead. It comes with crispy chicken skin, popcorn-style chicken, boiled egg, special sambal, fried onions and nasi lemak rice.

I loved the crispy chicken skin and fried onions, but the popcorn chicken pieces were quite small and the portion felt a bit little. The fries were a bit too dry for my taste. The place itself is nice and cozy, a good spot to lepak. Overall, it’s worth trying something different, maybe next time I’ll try their burger.
author: Hasymah

review_text:
On 17 Jan 2026 at around 7:24pm, I ordered a takeaway of Zikgu Meat Up Sambal Nasi (RM13.90). When I reached home and opened the package, I noticed that the chicken pieces were not included, unlike what was shown in the advertisement.

On 19 Jan 2026 at around 5:15pm, I returned to the restaurant to clarify the matter and provided proof. The Manager, Ahsan, kindly assisted in investigating and confirmed it was an unintentional mistake by the staff.

He took responsibility on behalf of the restaurant and personally compensated me with a King Deluxe Nasi Lemak and a Zikgu keychain. I appreciate Ahsan’s professionalism in resolving the issue properly.

This was an isolated case and does not affect my intention to visit again.
author: 相約琴聲

review_text: The beef burger was smashing good, the chicken kaarage also sedapppp!! Only problem wished the patty was thicker and the portion abit more, for the price the portion is quite small. Nice environment too.
author: Rachael Gunaseelan

review_text: It is very appetizing and it fills up our stomach just at the right moment! I very much enjoy this restaurant because of how it is not cramped or loud. I love the food, it's so delicious and quite spicy for a non-spice lover, such as myself! Thank you for the food:)
author: zara khayla

review_text:
Dropped by Zikgu Burger recently and was surprised to find the place completely empty not a single customer in sight. The vibe gave off serious McDonald’s-in-the-90s kinda feel, but without the buzz or energy. Definitely missing that lively atmosphere you’d expect from a burger joint.

The service, though, was fast and efficient. Only spotted 3 staff working, but they handled everything smoothly. Plenty of seating and tables, so space is not an issue at all.

Price wise, not exactly cheap, especially given the limited options the menu only had three types of burgers. That said, I’ve got to admit: the burger I tried was surprisingly good. Tasty, juicy, and clearly made with care.

Overall, zikgu has potential, but it’s missing that “something” to draw people in. Maybe a more exciting vibe or expanded menu could help. Still, worth a try if you’re nearby and craving a solid burger.
author: Athirah Azizan

review_text:
Love the ikan Pari bakar, sedap!

Tofu & cakoi bakar was nice, loaded with peanuts bits.

Abc Koko was special, 1st time trying this combo, but would not order it again as it's too sweet for our liking 😅

They helped us order salted fish kailan from next stall, it's delicious too
author: Wai Ling Yeow

review_text: Highly recommended by locals, and it is really packed during meal times. However, service is quick and the taste doesn't disappoint. Dishes to order include ikan bakar, tahu bakar, sotong bakar and cikong. Exactly what I had when I came for a late dinner.
author: Emily Lowe

review_text: Hidden gem! Their BBQ stingray was so good! Recommended 👍
author: Muhammad Fauzie Abdul Rahim

review_text:
Hidden Gem. Great BBQ fish. Best of all is the rojak and toasted Tahu. Tahu is crispy and the prawn paste w generous peanut sprinkle on top is magical. Must try.
They are open from 3pm.
author: at home

review_text: Got diarrhea after visiting this outlet. Went to toilet non stop for 15 hours. Ate ais koko & tahu bakar. RM5.50 for ice koko - just ice & coco only no other condiments is nonsense. Sorry first & last
author: Shamsul Bahrin

review_text: Incredible seafood platter with crab, shrimp, muscles, veggies. Friendly owner and great price too!! Must try!
author: Fox Myers

review_text: The seafood is all fresh but the cooking is a little lacking. The food is bland, the sauce is runny and I don't know what kind of food it is. The price is expensive. Usually, any shellout shop will have a set for 2-3 people to eat for under Rm40. This shop is Rm55 but the portion is small. This is not to put you down, but an honest review.
author: Nur BAE

review_text: The food is not tasty + expensive. There are no grilled clams, only boiled ones, and the clam sauce is not tasty enough.
author: Aiman Faiz

review_text: expensive, slow, and the dishes are not cooked
author: LazyBug Ebliss

review_text: Shop closed
author: hani muhyid

review_text:
Fast Food with Middle Eastern items, Nice Environment, Friendly Service.
I visited everytime if I am around this area Kolam Air.
I love their Shawarma, full ingredients, juicy and delicious. Price is on above average level but acceptable because of the ingredients and texture.
For Fried Chicken, it's a bit pricy but compatible with mamak. First try is OK and will not repeat order.
Tried Lamb Burger, size is small and texture is dry and pricy too.
Generally, they are specialised in Shawarma, I have no doubts and it's must try. Other items are just to accommodate the fast food restaurant requirements from public.
author: Brian Lee

review_text: The service is quite nice. Almost the same as other popular fast food chain. Very clean. There are also prayer room for Muslim customer. Their shawarma is one of the best. I tried 3 different burger set and they all tasted good. I ordered the spicy fried chicken which is quite okay with a taste of black pepper.
author: A. Zaphara

review_text:
1. Food was abominable. Fried chicken was too dry and flaky indicating multiple time reheating/refrying and the flour coating was not in proper ratio. It’s an insult to call the shawarma here a shawarma. Too much sauce within, meat was too less, the wrap was not cooked properly, was dry and waxy in texture. The mashed potatoes were not seasoned well and the sauce was not properly cooked.

2. No paywave machines here, huge minus. Almost no purpose to put the auto ordering computers since you still have to line up at cashier to pay. Food here came quickly which explains its bad taste.

3. The only good thing here is they clean the tables quite quickly.

Conclusion, there are 10 plus more better shawarmas jn JB area. Please improve your food. An insult to Middle Eastern cuisine!
author: Sockalingam Sharven

review_text: My first time had my meal here and ordered the beef shawarma. They have a la carte and set menu, from burger, shawarma to fried chicken. The place is clean and spacious and you can choose to order at the machine or at the counter.
author: ani mahadi

review_text:
The fried chicken that is spicy is ok, the one that is not spicy, what is the difference? Its like they just removed the spicy part of the flour just flour and chicken the taste is so plain. The shawarma is densely filled but the parata flour that wraps it is like using old flour.. soft then turns yellow.. His burger is big like a full Whopper, not the junior Whopper, the meat is juicy with just enough spice, but it's a bit skimpy on vegetables.

Even though its a very good effort and kudos for the bravery to open a fast food restaurant.

Try to hire some gastronomy experts and QC maybe it will help the business in the long run. Anyway love it. 😍
author: Mohd Faiz Bin Isham

restaurant_name: Sri Dataran Maju Asam Pedas A1 no. 32
author: Mohamad Farid Bin Mohammed

review_text:
For this pricing and the amount of food, it was a steal. The fish tasted fresh. Penang kway teow tasted great, and the nasi lemak was very fragrant. The squid could’ve been better but maybe because we came an hour before closing. Thus, this standard with only one hour before closing, I would say its great. Air conditioning, plenty of parking, food delivered by a robot (lol, quite entertaining), a clean prayer space, family friendly and nice staff.

Would definitely recommend and I will definitely be coming back.
author: Haverick Braun

review_text:
| 29.09.2025 |

Food : for me it basic. kueh also just ordinary. lontong kuah are too plain, not much vege inside. mi rebus okay👍

services : feels like high end restaurants, got robot. food comes early

environment : airconditioner, spacious.

review_text: Everything tastes great! Fast service & nice ambience and also kids friendly.

review_text: Unfortunately, the service here was terrible. The staff were rude, noisy, and unprofessional. They were rushing around, creating unnecessary noise, and when I asked for my food, I was met with an unfriendly facial expression. The whole place felt messy and stressful instead of welcoming. Definitely not an enjoyable dining experience.
author: alyssa damia

review_text: They got all the local staples like lontong, mee bandung, and plenty of kuih. Food was alright, but prices are a little on the high side. I also ordered cendol, and I’m pretty sure they used frozen coconut milk which kind of took away the freshness. Overall, just okay for me.
author: Low Key

review_text:
A dining venue for who is looking for authentic johor dishes. Located within the vicinity of the Kompleks Warisan Johor. It is a very relax and open air concept restaurant for all ages.

As you dine, you will be entertained with Johor traditional folklore dance and music.
