review_text: Good food and a suitable place for corporate event and funtion . Good location at dataran Johor Bahru .
author: sc张来星

review_text: Quite high-end restaurant with good and recommended dishes and panoramic views. Quiet surronding and peace are really suitable for discussion over the meals. Breakfast, lunch, tea time, dinner and supper are available either buffet or order separately.    Price a little bit higher than normal restaurant but satisfaction guaranteed.
author: Ungku Ahmad Ungku Rizlan

review_text:
We celebrated my daughter’s birthday yesterday at McDonald’s Nong Chik, and I just want to say a big thank you to the whole team for making it such a wonderful experience!

From my initial inquiry to the planning and the actual day, everyone was so accommodating and professional. Special thanks to the staff member who patiently assisted me over the phone with all my questions.

Our host, Kamarul, truly stood out. He is kind-hearted, calm, friendly with all guests, and full of energy during the games — actually even before the games. He assisted with the meals, talked and sat down with the guests, and made sure all is smooth. You can really feel his sincerity and joy in helping everyone throughout the whole 3 hours. All my friends, including us love interacting with him ❤️

There was also another male staff member who helped with the event setup — he even suggested the best spot for our piñata and assisted during the games. Super friendly and quick-witted!

And of course, thank you to Juliahti, who made sure everything behind the scenes went smoothly — from preparing the venue to handling the orders and payment. I really appreciate how she recommended downloading the McDonald’s app before paying — I didn’t realize I was missing out on so many perks!

Thank you again, McDonald’s Nong Chik Team, for making my daughter’s birthday so memorable! 🎉
author: Astrid Regina Lai

review_text: ordered thru grab , sambal leaked everywhere not only that but when wanted to eat my COOKIE MCFLURRY den whn i opened it there’s NO COOKIE IN SIGHT , its HALF EMPTY and there’s a plastic cover IN THE MIDDLE OF THE ICECREAM. Mind you , I did NOT even eat it yet . Disappointed considering i waited for more than 30 minutes .
author: Becca Yendersan

review_text:
It's a typical McDonald's. So the food and the surroundings are the same as in any other branch.

But what upsets me is that I get ripped off at every McDonald's. You always get the same toys. It's as if they only open one pack with the same toys and then hand them out one by one. Is this a system to keep attracting people who wouldn't otherwise come to the restaurant? I'd like an answer, McDonald's. And another question: which organization does the food get donated to? You can donate at the kiosk.
author: Viktor Metzger

review_text:
Loved the ambience here, less noisy and crowded compared to JBCC outlet on weekends.

Parking is free for 1st hour, but subsequently, you will be charged RM5/hour.
author: Jason

review_text:
It's our first time in JB and this is the worse experience ever. This McDonald's is probably the worst branch out there. I've been to several countries and it's my go-to food but that will now change because of the bad experience here.

Firstly, I ordered and paid my food. I got a number so they will serve my food but it didn't come! They did not prepared my food even after a loooong wait. My friend almost finished her food and I thought I need to follow up so I did. I was shocked to see that they aren't preparing my food that was readily available there. My order is only Nasi Lemak and fries, nothing fancy they need a long time to prepare. 😬 Also, there's not much customers so you'd think you can get your order quickly (I guess the service is the reason why).

No one talked to me and said something when I followed up, they just got my receipt and they just talked among themselves, laughing and joking around. No sorry or whatever, most of them side eyed me too. 😩

Before I followed up, some staff just passed by me on the table and most likely saw the number on the table but didn't bother to ask about my order. Meanwhile, I saw them ask other people about their orders when they saw they have a number. Ridiculous.

I've never felt racism stronger than ever and it's here, in a McDonald's branch which is a multi-country company.

I don't recommend this branch. Bad service and attitude of staff are not pleasant. I am not even sure if there's a manager around because why do things like this happen when in fact, everything was automated when I ordered and paid. 😤
author: De

review_text:
Pros If you're looking for a place where nobody talks to you and you can work in peace—congrats, you've found it. Solitude level: monk mode. Other than that? Nope, nothing else worth mentioning.

Cons The “free Wi-Fi” is just a myth. It’s so overloaded it might as well be a decorative feature. The self-order machine is like a stubborn grandpa—can’t customize drinks, can’t claim rewards unless you’re in a car. McDonald’s machines would laugh in its face. Air-conditioning? More like air-confusion. My car’s AC does a better job, and that’s saying something. If McDonald’s next door hadn’t started charging for parking, I wouldn’t be caught here. Ordered spicy chicken, got original instead. Dry, tough, and emotionally disappointing. Salad tasted like regret. Rice was hot, but so is lava—doesn’t mean it’s good. They have a screen and a system, yet staff still shout out names like it’s a school canteen. Comedy gold. Honestly, this place feels like it’s auditioning for retirement. And it’s nailing the role.
author: Tony

review_text: The nasi lemak for breakfast was nice. I was there for 6 hours so I also got the burger for lunch. The aircond was not cold and I was sweating. Is ok since it was my first time there at KFC Seri Gelam. Good location as people who go the hospital come to eat or wait there. And schoolchildren from EC also come there after school. It gets crowded at lunch time. Good to see this KFC is doing well.
author: Anne Sucila

review_text: 19/9. I was here at 11.48 pm. U stated there it is closed at 2 am. How come already closed at this time? I saw people eating inside but this one male staff didnt want to let us in. What is this kind of service?
author: Nyssa Faisal

review_text:
I’m very disappointed with my recent order at KFC. I ordered a Zinger Riser, but when I opened it, there was no chicken inside — only egg. This is unacceptable as the main item was completely missing.

Although the staff replaced it for me afterward, the mistake itself shows a lack of professionalism and attention to detail. It made the whole experience feel careless and not handled seriously.

On top of that, the staff inside were playing around and making loud noise instead of focusing on their work. It did not feel professional at all.

I hope the management will take this seriously and improve both food quality control and staff attitude..
author: Yaohui Chin

review_text: Today I ordered Turkish Spice Burger Box Meal with cheesy veggies in food panda but what I get is whole set or normal burger and chickens nothing in it and also the cheesy veggies don’t have cheese in it. People who work there, is tjis how you guys serve customers don’t you recheck before send it to rider? I’m really disappointed and angry with this. It’s like I got scammed
author: Privacy Content

restaurant_name: Buffet Ramadan The Cave @ Malay Village Restaurant
review_text:
The ambiance is top notch, with decor and music are both calming and relaxing. Anyone coming here would not have to worry about parking spaces as there is aplenty with the mosque nearby.

On the food, I can honestly say it is of medium par. The durian goreng is quite unique, so is the black pepper beef which is quite tasty. However none could be say about their cendol, which devoid of gula Melaka, a signature taste. Hope they could rectify this
author: Fadhil Basery

restaurant_name: Buffet Ramadan The Cave @ Malay Village Restaurant
review_text:
This restaurant, Halia and The Cave are all the same owner. Guess they don't have enough staff. Very slow service. Food is so so only. Norhing to shout about. Luckily we arrived early, else we may not get our food.
Quite pricey in my opinion. And it also include service charge.
author: MT

restaurant_name: Buffet Ramadan The Cave @ Malay Village Restaurant
review_text: To be honest, this place is overrated, look cozy and luxury, but service is a bit slow. Price quite expensive and the taste is just meet standard. So don’t judge book by it’s cover. We really expected high this restaurant, but it’s not. 😓😓
author: Muhammad Syahrin

restaurant_name: Buffet Ramadan The Cave @ Malay Village Restaurant
review_text: NOT EVEN WORTH THE 1 STAR.Bad experience ever. Waited the food for about an hour++. The food is tasted so so.. the tomyum and veggies is super BAD. The stir fried egg is too salty. BUT The price is PREMIUM. YOU DIDN'T GET WHAT YOU PAID FOR. FIRST AND LAST
author: Asyraf Hanafi

restaurant_name: Buffet Ramadan The Cave @ Malay Village Restaurant
review_text:
For RM85, this buffet is seriously overpriced. Why? The food is just NOT good. Very limited choices, nothing special at all. The desserts? Meh. Western food? Super plain, no flavor. If u wanna do a buffet, at least do it properly. Right now, it feels like a RM30 experience max.

Honestly, I’ve had way better buffets for cheaper. Not sure who u are targeting, but it def doesn’t feel like it’s for locals. Feels more like it’s meant for Singaporean tourists or ppl who don’t mind overpaying. Definitely not worth it for what u get.
author: Hadif Aiman

review_text:
I had the best server service today. Very attentive to our request and when we gave feedback on the meal, it was replaced with a smile. Good service and impressed me.

The minus point was parent letting their kids screaming. They can play and enjoy but please educate your kids on how to behave. 3 screams and i had it. Thank you Bigfood. Sedap
author: yadi 4u

review_text:
The potion is quite big for single person eater. You need to share with your partner on the food you intend to eat.  Recommended to have two set plates for four person. You can order the food/drink via the QR code. Wifi is provided on each table. The price posted does not include the Service Charge  (5%) and SSTax (6%).
The place is aircon and ceiling fan fitted.
Kid play area provided with slides,  small house, etc.,
Two WC provided in reasonably hygiene condition however lacking of soap and toilet paper.
author: Zulkifli BMO

review_text: Garlic bread is yummy but not toast long enough so aroma not there. Menu should indicate the portion is for how many pax.
author: R Ng

review_text: Who would have thought I ate at 2 western restaurants this weekend and let me tell you this one was absolutely quite full. The parmesan chicken has a kick to it with its tomato sauce and some chillis in it and the other dishes were scrumptious too. The staff were friendly and nice to us as well. Overall the experience was mediocre and would like to dine in alone some day
author: Erfan Emran

review_text: We were here for breaking fast on Wednesday. Overall I would rate a 4 star experience dining in this restaurant. Food is decent but big portion. Can share up to 2-3 person if you are not a big eater. Reasonable price but we’ve expected more in terms of its tastes. We loved the ambience of this restaurant. It is so cozy and clean. Ice creams were super good tho. Staffs are friendly. Recommended restaurant for you and family.
author: M. Asyraf Shariffuddin

review_text: This has to be the straw that broke the camel's back. The first time when I tried their premium waygu, it was really good. Hence that was why I kept patronizing this place. However, the subsequent visits really proof to be unnecessary. My friends and I ordered the 235 odd RM beef, we really regretted it. Our 60rm ribeye tasted way better than the premium beef. How is that even possible? We paid 200 odd for a beef, I don't think it is ridiculous of us to expect a little standard out of it. I have given many chances, but I am moving on for sure. But thank you for the first try though. It was good till it lasted.
author: Nei Hou Mou

review_text: I read so many good reviews about this place, but it's a disappointment. The taste of the meat is so plain as if there's no taste to it. (I ordered Wagyu by the way) the mash potato is as though it's blended potato. Nothing great, for the price I'm paying, it's not worth going at all.
author: Derrick Ng

review_text: Nice place, the meats look small but it really fills your stomach. The prices are reasonable. Just hoping for more drinks choices to choose when you order your steaks. Or maybe refillable drinks perhaps.
author: Jane Isa

review_text:
Went there for berbuka puasa. One of the best (if not the best) Angus I had in my life. It is served with the speciality souce, mashed potatoes and some vegetables. Similar/comparable to Menate.

Didn't had the chance to taste the Wagyu meat yet.

Spouse ordered lamb. Nothing special about it.
Still gave a 5 star since the speciality is beef.
author: Muhammad Iskandar

review_text: One of the nearest place to get A5Miyazaki and Wagyu beef. For those who are prime for some premium beef. They sell normal standard price beef between RM50-100 depending on weight.
author: Muawiz Mazlan

restaurant_name: ZZ Sup Tulang Restaurant, Kampung Bahru, Johor
review_text:
11/12/25 Limited parking and we were fortunate to get a spot. This is an open area restaurant with covered seatings.
Had mee rebus and sup leher. The noodles was good but the meat was on the tough side.
There's a man selling kueh cara berlauk among others and it tastes very good.
Their watermelon juice could be great if it had little more fruit.
All in all, atmosphere included, it's a restaurant that's worth a visit
author: Razgrid Kasim

restaurant_name: ZZ Sup Tulang Restaurant, Kampung Bahru, Johor
review_text: I really enjoyed the soup daging with a squish of lime. The mee rebus and mee bandung was good too. Price is abit on the high side but worth it  and location is inside a residential area. Parking can be a problem here.
author: Pk C

restaurant_name: ZZ Sup Tulang Restaurant, Kampung Bahru, Johor
review_text:
If you love tasty protein and collagen, you are in for a big treat!

👍🏻
1) The Laksa Johor is packed with amazing taste of mackerel, so much fish that I though the Laksa is like a blended fish gravy, superb!

2) Love how much Omega 3 one could get by just enjoy a hearty bowl of Laksa Johor here

3) The Mee Rebus broth is boiled till it releases so much collagen which many ladies and perhaps men would love, especially if you wanna have a great skin care!

4) The Ayam Penyet sambal is strong in taste with not so much spiciness.

5) The chicken of Ayam Penyet is fried till crisped.   So tasty!

6) It is a great away from busy city center for great meals.  So calm and relaxing.

7) Reasonable prices.

👎🏻
8) Lots of flies!   But heck, they too attracted to the great Johor cuisines!
author: Samuel Tan

restaurant_name: ZZ Sup Tulang Restaurant, Kampung Bahru, Johor
review_text:
Another off the beaten track find !!!
This old Kampong styled restaurant has single floor zinc roof, timber flooring and modern seating for customers to decide.

Their Sop Kambing Tulang, which is lamb bone with Marrow and meat, is One of the Authentic Best that I have tasted!!!
Cooked with a slight tinge of lamb flavouring, the chef had made it possible for every diner to enjoy.

We also had their Special Lamb Marrow Mee Rebus, served with thick sauce and cut green chilli - a must try !!!

Other dishes includes rendang, sauces and goreng.

A not to miss place .. good for couples,  families and groups.

Staff's are helpful and friendly.... they will explain the dishes so you know what to order.
author: Perry Pacific

restaurant_name: ZZ Sup Tulang Restaurant, Kampung Bahru, Johor
review_text: Gone for weekday lunch which is quiet, fast service and the food tastes great. More parking along j.petri 5/1 . Will visit again to try more items. Very Kampong feel .
author: Jj Kok

review_text:
This is a landed house restaurant.
The food is homely and the kitchen is open to all the visitors.
Glad we found this hidden gem that serves best Indian food in JB.
The place and the people make you feel home.

This is run by a family in memory of their grandmother who loved feeding people. Thanks to them for keeping the tradition alive and serving the best authentic food !

Will definitely go back again!
author: Tejasri Gopi

review_text:
2nd trip here in 2 years. Emphasis of the 2 years because we were so impressed with the food that for that we searched for this place again although none of us could remember it's name.
The chicken 65 was very good, butter chicken was delicious for us to wipe up with the Naan. Again this visit did not disappoint just like the first visit 2 years ago
author: Jean Loy

review_text: Food was good. North Indian taste buds satisfied. I have had better but that doesn’t mean things bad. Finding such good North Indian food in JB is in itself a big deal. Very few good ones there.
author: Rohit Singhal

review_text:
“Dear Chakra Restaurant Team,
We recently dined at your restaurant and really enjoyed 👍🏻👍🏻👍🏻 the cosy bungalow setting amidst busy JB city. Prices are slightly on the higher side, but the ambience and atmosphere made it worthwhile.

What stood out the most was your staff  they were truly first-class 🌟 very attentive and professional, right from the parking queue communication to the table service. It left a very positive impression on us as guests.

One small point for new visitors: the entrance road is narrow and may cause concern for parking. However, we found an empty land just 100m away, next to the nearby Petronas station, where guests can park and walk. Perhaps a small sign or note on your social media could reassure first-time visitors.

Thank you for a lovely dining experience, we will be back again.” ❤️❤️❤️❤️❤️
author: MATHEW K

review_text:
Chakra Restaurant truly exceeded my expectations! The attention to detail, especially in separating vegetarian and non-vegetarian options, is commendable and greatly appreciated.

The food was absolutely delicious—each dish was flavorful and beautifully presented. Whether it was the rich curries or the perfectly spiced tandoori items, every bite was a delight. The ambiance was inviting and perfect for a relaxed dining experience.

The staff was attentive and knowledgeable, making the overall visit even more enjoyable. I highly recommend Chakra for anyone looking for a fantastic meal in a welcoming environment. I can’t wait to return!
author: Prajwal Prasad

restaurant_name: Top One BBQ Seafood Ikan Bakar
review_text: Frustrated ..the taste of sambal  inconsistent.. sometime ok.. sometimes no taste. We  are regular customer since 2002... lately the ikan bakar sambal very poor...not consistent
author: Muslim Harun

restaurant_name: Top One BBQ Seafood Ikan Bakar
review_text: Place have a crowd seafood is so good have to try ...  You can select and then they cook the meal ... Nice place
author: Dr.Siyan Mohamed

restaurant_name: Top One BBQ Seafood Ikan Bakar

**Nasi Beryani Pak Abib - A Timeless Culinary Gem in JB**

Nasi Beryani Pak Abib stands out as one of the best in Johor Bahru, offering a taste that brings back cherished memories. I’ve been enjoying their beryani since the days of Pak Abib’s father, who has since passed away, and the tradition has been carried on with the same excellence.

The rice is perfectly fragrant, with a special blend of spices that is distinct from any other beryani I’ve tried. Each bite has a unique depth of flavor, making it truly unforgettable.

What also sets them apart is their acai, which is crunchy, sweet, and incredibly appetizing. The texture adds a wonderful contrast to the dish, enhancing the overall dining experience.

For anyone looking for a meal that’s rich in tradition and flavor, Nasi Beryani Pak Abib is a must-try. It’s more than just food – it’s a nostalgic journey!

review_text:
The Sting of Deception: Tip Top Ikan Bakar Has Lost a Loyal Customer

Tip Top Ikan Bakar was my absolute favorite. Since 2023, I have consistently recommended this place to friends and family, praising their incredible grilled seafood, particularly the signature grilled stingray with sambal and the excellent cereal prawn dish. I even posted a review praising this place more than a year ago. I believed in this seafood gerai, but my trust was shattered during my final visit on October 26, 2025.

On this last visit, with our party of five, we ordered the grilled stingray. The owner informed us that the piece on display was the last one she had. We trusted her, but the dish that arrived was appalling. The stingray was distinctly acidic and rotten-tasting, and the sambal was raw and harsh.

We managed to get a few mouthfuls down and within an hour, we all suffered upset stomachs, and I personally ended up vomiting at the roadside.

When we provided feedback to the owner that her fish was spoiled and inedible, her response was shocking: she nonchalantly attributed the quality issue to "bad luck." This dismissal was not just unprofessional, it was a staggering failure of responsibility and accountability. It is the owner’s duty to ensure the ingredients are fresh and safe.

The situation turned from negligence to appalling deception when we went to pay the bill after our upsetting meal. We were told the rotten piece was the last one, we observed several new, fresh pieces of stingray being brought out from the freezer and placed on display when we went to pay the bill.

The owner deliberately lied to us. She consciously chose to sell a rotten, bad-tasting piece of fish to loyal, paying customers instead of being honest and taking accountability for her stock. This is a profound betrayal of trust and clearly shows that she prioritized a quick, dishonest sale over customer health and loyalty.

This is how restaurants close down: by lowering their standards for a quick buck. I have zero confidence in Tip Top Ikan Bakar’s integrity and I am actively informing everyone I previously recommended this restaurant to that they should avoid it.

Secondly had the Kway Teow Goreng Seafood (Fried Kway Teow Seafood). Dish looks deceptively simple but is packed with flavor and is full of wok hei. Seafood were small deshelled prawns. Amazing dish.

The Kakak serving who happens to be the cook also is friendly and approachable. Will definitely return for both the food and service.

We ordered a delightful spread that included sotong, egg omelette, kailan vegetables, steamed fish, chili crab, and butter prawns, accompanied by teh tarik and coffee. Every dish was freshly prepared and bursting with flavor. The chili crab was delicious, but the highlight of the meal was definitely the butter prawns — perfectly cooked, rich, and fragrant.
We enjoyed every bite and finished everything we ordered. We enjoyed every bite and finished all the food we ordered. The prices were reasonable and worth every ringgit. Overall, it was a satisfying meal, and we’ll surely return for another round of fresh and tasty seafood in the future.

review_text:
Food Review: 17 Asam Pedas Power

Our first visit to 17 Asam Pedas Power, and it definitely won’t be our last! The food? Super sedap and worth every penny.

Here’s what we ordered:
✅ Sotong Tepung – Crispy, light, and not overly oily.
✅ Butter Prawn & Cereal Prawn – Both were rich, flavorful, and cooked perfectly.
✅ Ikan Masak Lemak Cili Padi (Non-Spicy) – Creamy and fragrant, still full of flavor even without the usual spice.
✅ Kailan Ikan Asin – Nicely stir-fried with a perfect balance of saltiness.
✅ Ikan Pari Bakar – The highlight! Smoky, juicy, and grilled to perfection—my all-time favorite.

Location & Parking
Easily accessible and not too far from CIQ. There’s an open-space car park, and a friendly uncle helps with the parking. We paid RM20—a small price for convenience. Sharing rizqi, right?

The restaurant has good vibes, friendly staff (not pushy), and a cozy atmosphere. Truly recommended for anyone craving delicious, comforting food.

Payment made was cashless, super convenient too😇

Till then, we’ll definitely be back!

The golden-brown wraps are perfectly charred and filled with mouthwatering, flavorful fillings that will leave you wanting more.

The staff at Mahgoub wear vibrant uniforms and work efficiently, creating an organized and welcoming atmosphere despite the busy environment. The aroma wafting from the stall itself is enough to draw you in, and watching the preparation process adds to the overall experience.

The shawarma is well-balanced—not overly greasy—with just the right amount of spice and seasoning to cater to a variety of palates. Perfect for a quick bite or a satisfying meal, the portion sizes ensure you get great value for your money.

If you’re in the area and craving Middle Eastern flavors, this spot is worth the visit. Highly recommended for a fulfilling and delicious shawarma experience!

review_text:
A Must-Visit Burger Spot in Johor Bahru

Visited Made on Monday (Johor Bahru) for dinner with my family of five, and it was an excellent all-round experience.

The first thing that stands out is the ambience — thoughtfully designed with both indoor and outdoor seating, giving diners the flexibility to choose between a cosy or more relaxed, open-air setting. Great for families and groups.

Food-wise, this place delivers. The burgers are a clear highlight: fresh, well-seasoned meat patties paired with soft, quality buns. We tried the Northender and MOM Beef Bites burgers — both were unique, flavourful, and clearly made with care rather than being generic café burgers.

Service was consistently warm, friendly, and prompt, which made dining with kids smooth and stress-free. Staff were attentive without being intrusive.

We also ordered the pesto and carbonara pastas, which were creamy, well-balanced, and satisfying. The fries deserve a mention too — crispy on the outside, fluffy inside, and served in a sensible portion (not overly greasy or excessive).

Overall, Made on Monday nails the key pillars: ambience, food quality, and service. A solid spot in JB for both casual meals and family dinners. Would happily return and recommend.

🦀 Harlan Restaurant – Seafood Lovers’ Paradise! 🌊

If you’re a fan of fresh seafood and bold flavors, Harlan Restaurant is a must-visit spot. Their signature chilli crab truly lives up to the hype — rich, spicy, and full of flavor that clings perfectly to every piece of juicy crab meat. No wonder it’s one of the most famous dishes here! 🔥

The seafood is incredibly fresh, cooked to perfection, and served with that irresistible aroma that makes your mouth water even before the first bite. Every dish bursts with taste, from prawns to clams — everything screams quality and freshness.

💬 The restaurant gets quite busy, especially during dinner time, but that’s just proof of how loved it is by locals and travelers alike.

If you’re in the mood for authentic seafood and a finger-licking good chilli crab, Harlan Restaurant should be at the top of your list. Highly recommended! 😋

review_text:

We had the chili crab (RM105 for 700g). It wasn’t spicy, leaning more towards a tomato-based flavour. We also ordered fried mantou (minimum order of 3 at RM1.10 each). It was served first, so by the time the crab arrived, the buns were already at room temperature.

The hotplate tofu was good — a mix of egg, tofu, prawns, meat, and ginger slices. The stir-fried garlic French beans were also well done, crunchy and flavourful.

The steamed prawns, however, were a letdown as they weren’t fresh; the flesh stuck to the shells when peeled.

The restaurant accepts credit card payments (with a sign indicating a minimum spend of RM12, written in Malay). Only a credit card slip was provided — no itemised receipt — but the main cost was definitely the crab at RM105.

A lovely surprise was that the desserts were complimentary from the boss, which made the experience even more special. The crème brûlée was silky smooth with a nicely caramelised top, and the chocolate lava cake was indulgent and decadent, with warm molten chocolate flowing out on the first cut.

For mains, my undisputed number one is still their lamb shank, tender, flavourful, and consistently perfect. We also tried their Mala Risotto and creamy mushroom soup this round, and both were fantastic.

What truly sets Whisk & Wink apart is their service. Mr Alf and the ground staff are always warm, attentive, and genuinely hospitable. Their smiles, their patience, and the quick response to every request make the whole experience feel personal and memorable. I even came twice within a week because it’s just that good.

On top of the amazing food and service, the place itself is a huge bonus. It’s very convenient, clean, cosy, spacious and super child-friendly too, which makes dining with family so much easier. Parking is also easy to find, which is a big plus.

This is officially my go-to restaurant whenever I’m in JB. If you’re looking for authentic French cuisine at a very reasonable price, this is the place to be.

review_text:
Food Review – Tulsi Curry House
During our recent visit to Tulsi Curry House, we ordered Masala Thosai, Rawa Thosai, Veetu Thosai, Roti Canai, and Teh Tarik.
Unfortunately, the overall food experience was a major disappointment. Previously, when the restaurant was located in Bukit Indah, my family and I used to visit frequently for breakfast due to the good taste and excellent service. After the relocation, both the food quality and service standards appear to have declined significantly.
The taste of the food was below expectation. However, the Teh Tarik was good and enjoyable. I sincerely apologise for not attaching any photos, as the disappointment during the meal did not encourage me to take any.
In terms of service, it was evident that the restaurant was operating with limited manpower. Although the dining area was only about 30% occupied during breakfast hours, the staff struggled to manage the customers efficiently. That said, the workers were polite, well-mannered, and showed positive attitudes. They clearly have the potential and confidence to handle operations better, but I believe having a dedicated supervisor could greatly improve coordination and overall service flow.
This feedback is shared with genuine care for the restaurant, as I have experienced and appreciated the excellent food quality and variety that Tulsi Curry House once offered.
Overall, the experience was below expectation. I truly hope the management will address these issues and restore the taste, quality, and service standards that customers valued previously.

Please also note that individual rooms do not come with washing machines. Laundry services are available at Level 33A where there are two washers and two dryers, operated by coins (RM5 each). Unfortunately, it was a horrible experience for me and my family.
The room that we were in (3008) had issues:

- The wifi is unreliable thus, we used our data.
What is most traumatic is that on during our stay, our water supply (showers and sink) were completely cut off. When I called the reception around 10am, the reception told me that they will look into it.
30 minutes later, the water did trickle in a little, so I thought, okay, let's give them time to fix the issue.
A few minutes later, much to our horror, urine spurted out (I know what I saw and it was unmistakeable because it smells). I called the reception again to ask why does it came out in the sink and they said that it was due to water pump maintenance. The reception is nice to let us know it will they said that it take 30 min to 1 hour to fix the issue. But by that time, we would already be check out.
Could be better to give us a heads up like a notice on the lift or paper to our room.
In conclusion, we won't want to patronise here again because the thought of having the pipe sharing the same drainage as sewage leaves us questioning about the hygiene in our water.

restaurant_name: New Hong Kong Restaurant (JB) 新香港
review_text:
In the early 70's, 80's and 90's, this was the GO-TO place to host your wedding dinner, full moon dinner and all forms of family get-together makan-makan event. They had the best Hong Kong Chef and together with his crew, they dished out the best of Hk dishes.
At the turn of the century, the Chef and his staff left. Now we are only left with the memories of good food and our loved ones who are since long gone.
The Dimsum is just ordinary - nothing to shout about but comparatively their prices are WAY above their competitors (Loon Sing, De Shanghai, Jiah Xiang, Changman) who each, despite not having an acclaimed name like them, managed a signature dish in their own right.
Order the Har Gao, siew mai, carrot cake, vinegar pig trotters, fried beancurd roll with shrimp and chee cheong fun. All are passable. Stay away from their big pao, steamed ribs and paper-wrapped chicken. They are below standard (thawed product) and are dry and tasteless. Even their Chinese Tea tastes like the normal kopitiam ones though their prices are not.,
Their attendants speak fluent Cantonese and the ambience very much remains the traditional Cantonese restaurant of the bygone era.
My family patronized this place for three generations (1970-2009). But i am afraid it would be our last visit to this beautiful, memorable place with our seniors. All the best!

review_text: The female staff is patience to explain those foods n sauces suitable for Vegetarian to eat. Foods are tasty too, especially like their crispy bread. :)
author: Alice

review_text: Sandwich here specially the Tuna sandwich is the best no doubt about that but my only concern is the staff who lack of communication skill, they must train on how to speak and listen in English words because no one wants to repeat their orders again.
author: Miko

review_text:
AK Noodles House - City Square, Lot J2-12, Level 2, Bandar Johor Bahru, 80000 Johor Bahru, Johor, Malaysia

Stopped for lunch at the city square and decided to give AK Noodle House a try. I ordered:

Bean Paste Yong Tau Foo – RM16.90

Grouper Soup – RM24.90, with an extra bowl of rice

It was a simple lunch with my parents, and overall the food tasted good. I felt it was a value-for-money meal, perfect for when you’re craving something light and refreshing. The restaurant serves Halal food, and the portion of grouper was impressively large. The Bean Paste Yong Tau Foo was first fried and then topped with the bean sauce. It wasn’t overly salty, yet had the distinct flavour you’d expect from a wholesome Yong Tau Foo dish—tasty without feeling heavy or sinful.

Food Quality: 4/5
author: Meditate Zen

review_text:
I had gone to their restaurant at Taman Sentosa - Ah Koong Restaurant- the first time, and tried their yong tau fu. It was delicious, especially the deep fried prawn cake.

I didn't realise that they had an outlet at JB City Square. I popped by here, and ordered their dry version with mee pok. At this place, you don't pick out the pieces yourself, but you can order what you want. Or go with a standard order like I did.

The prawn cake is still the best, and I also like their mini ngoh hiang fish roll. The prawn cake cost RM14.50, the same price as my dried mee pok with yong tau fu. Not exactly cheap, but still affordable.

Their restaurant is more comfortable and fun to eat in; air conditioning really blasting 😆. But a bit out of the way unless you're driving.

Their TV screens indicate they supply Fairprice and Sheng Siong. When I enquired, as of the time of this review (30 July 2025), it's only the dried packet laksa noodles of theirs. Not their yong tau fu.
author: LT Wong

review_text:
Been my favourite go to place to eat whenever I come JB. Even brought friends to try this place with me!

Food the Yong tau foo is the best for me. Portions are huge and taste of soup is just right. Not tasteless nor oily..
author: Hello Chester

review_text: The shop is clean and bright show very well maintained. The staff is good manners and supportive. Above all, the foods are well prepared and tasty.
author: Sean Chong

review_text: Love the noodles at this place. The chewy-ness, the springy taste of the noodles give it an additional texture that enhances it's flavour.
author: Yong Chieh Gooi

review_text:
Shihlin Taiwan Street Snacks has always been my go-to spot for a quick snack or light meal, especially when I'm craving something familiar and comforting. One thing I appreciate is that the prices here are cheaper compared to Singapore, making it feel like a better deal overall.

The oyster mee sua is pretty much identical to what you'd get in Singapore — warm, savoury, and satisfying. The fried chicken cutlet here comes with bones, which makes it juicier, but might not be everyone's preference. If you prefer boneless but slightly drier chicken, then the Singapore version might suit you more.

I also tried their crepe chicken floss snack, which was not too bad — nothing extraordinary, but enjoyable enough as a side. The only real letdown was the winter melon drink, which I found overly sweet and a bit cloying after a few sips.

Overall, it’s a decent place to satisfy your Taiwanese street food cravings, especially if you’re looking for quick bites at more affordable prices than what you’d find back in Singapore.
author: Ming Shen Tham

review_text:
Quick and easy. It’s almost the same taste at each Shihlin stalls. Our favourite is the oyster mee sua and XXL crispy chicken chop.

The chicken chop is so handy, we can hold in our hand and eat while shopping. We ordered both mild and strong spicy. The skin is always crispy and depends on the chef’s skill, some were juicy inside. The 2 chicken chop we had tonight both juicy inside. Thumbs up!

Another observation is this stall is quite clean :)
author: Lennox Cheok

review_text: I love their oyster meesua, but had stopped eating them in Singapore as the price keeps going up. Was pleasantly delighted to find the prices here much more friendly..Taste-wise, they are quite consistent, flavourful with fresh oysters. The staffs on duty were friendly and serviced with 😊😊😊.. I will be back soon ! Oh and i bought their bento home for my husband, he likes it a lot 👍👍👍
author: R Tan

review_text: This is a small place with limited seats. The tempura combo set I ordered comes with a red date drink & sweet potato fries. The 甜不辣 taste kind of weird. The sweet potato is nice though. The red date drink is pre packed & is too sweet.
author: Aileen Organic

review_text: Tried the tuna and egg crepe. It's better for sharing as it got too jelak halfway through. The business at this outlet is slower and has slightly more tables than the one at City square.
author: Ning Xuan

review_text:
​I decided to visit at an off-peak time to avoid the dinner crowd, but I’m honestly surprised this place can survive with these standards. Despite the low traffic, the service was incredibly slow. And they were not understaffed at all.

I dined for over an hour, but spent 80% of that time just waiting for food to arrive. It took 20 mins for my Iced Tea to arrive...The staff seemed quite indifferent to the delays.

​While the total bill was reasonable for an average Jap sushi place (around RM51), the quality wasn't even average. If you're looking for authentic Japanese cuisine, this isn't it. I don't know why people still.choose to eat here.

It’s "Japanese-sounding" food that might satisfy a quick craving, but the quality and pacing definitely don't match the price point.
author: Yi Ling

review_text: Sunday 11:30am. A clean restaurant located in the mall. Overall, the food tasted okay. We were the second table to arrive and ordered a salmon bento, which took about 20 minutes to be served. The food was decent and very reasonably priced. However, if you are in a rush, you may want to choose items directly from the sushi conveyor belt instead.
author: Ong NN

review_text:
No wonder there's no queue and not many customers in the restaurant. When I stood at the door, all the staff just looks at me. It didn't even look like anyone was going to attend to me. Then I saw a staff just raised her arm and point to the inside of the restaurant, which I take it as I can just sit anywhere.

Upon sitting down, I had to figure out everything myself. No one mentioned anything about ordering through the tablet for more choices.

When my miso soup came, I realised my table did not have spoon, and I had to grab one from the table next to mine.

I ordered the sashimi from the tablet, when it came, the colour looks very off. Like all the other reviews, I'd say unappetising.

The restaurant can work on improving their customer service and food quality if they wish to do better than current performance.
author: L L

review_text: Thank you Marlisaaaa for your good service! Helps me to get an free ice cream bcs this month is my birthday month! And thank you for your incredable service towards your customer
author: Siti Nor Azliza Ali

review_text:
One of the worst sushi restaurant.

The salmon looks pale, doesnt look nice nor taste nice. The inari looks pathetic. The unagi don is served with overcooked egg that is burnt. The miso soup by itself seems nice, but it has tofu toppings that almost made me throw up. The takoyaki is the most acceptable one taste wise, even so it has almost no octopus fillings because the octopus is diced in tiny pieces that i can barely notice, with no bonito flakes on the top.

Overall it is not recommended. For the restaurant itself, please check the quality of the food you serve.
author: Della Nadya

review_text: A peaceful and nourishing lunch. The tonic soup, made with fresh meat and herbs, was rich in flavor and packed with health benefits. The herbal chicken was cooked to perfect tenderness, with the meat falling off the bone effortlessly. Its gravy was deeply infused with the essence of chicken and herbs, enhancing both taste and nutrition. The monkey head mushrooms remain my all-time favorite, offering great texture and health benefits. To top it off, the sour plum drink aided digestion, making the meal both satisfying and good for overall well-being.
author: Ankori

review_text:
Souper Tang is a haven for soup lovers and anyone craving wholesome, flavorful Chinese cuisine.  While the prices are on the higher side, the quality and comfort make it worth it.  Great when you need a little TLC for your tummy!

Pepper Pork Tribe Soup Ramen (RM33.90): The soup is rich, peppery, and deeply warming—perfect for a chilly evening.  The  ramen soaked up all that delicious broth.

Mee Suah with Dried Scallop and Abalone Slice (RM29.90): The mee suah was silky smooth, and the dried scallop and abalone added a luxurious umami touch.  Light but satisfying.

American Ginseng Black Chicken Soup with Aged Black Garlic (RM33.90): The ginseng and black garlic combo was aromatic and soothing, while the black chicken was fall-off-the-bone tender.  Perfect for replenishing your energy.

Paper Wrapped Chicken with Rice (RM29.90): Juicy, flavorful chicken wrapped and steamed to perfection.

Mulberry Enzyme Tea (RM13.90): A refreshing, slightly tangy drink that cleansed the palate and added a bright finish to the meal.

Visited in Mar 2025
author: Larktiss

review_text:
Disclaimer: sorry I did eat some food and then took the photo, my bad.

Total price : 240 ringgit ( including the lemonade with enzyme)

I didnt fabricated anything, it is exactly as how it went.

Went on Saturday 19th April 2025, around 12.30pm. Clearly almost everywhere is crowded because it's lunch hour.

Went in as there was no queue, but the restaurant was fairly crowded, and stepped outside to wait for someone to perhaps notice us and let us in since I didn't wanted to just barge in.

But I saw a worker but definitely an auntie from my perspective using phone and wasn't sure watching something or what, but heads down and engrossed on it while manning the entrance. 🤔 so I just approached and asked if there was table for two, which a lady guided us.

So we sat down and choose the menu and went onto order. Clearly understaffed. There are around 20 tables with 2-3 staff serving and taking orders.

So we had to caught the attention of the young female staff to take our order and she wrote it down and went to take another person's order and we waited afterwards.

Past 20 minutes no one came down to check on us or serve our food. So given that I've been in FnB, I gave the benefit of doubt, and just checked in with the same lady to perhaps pass us the order invoice and she told her she will get it but another 10 minute she breeze past us and didn't give us anything.

I don't mean to say anything bad, but it got me wandered, what could be the problem.

So we got the guy staff instead to check, and he got back to us stating that we didn't order anything and asked who took our order and when we shared, he just shook his head, so I guess he knew it as well.

Then we got our food.

As you can see in the photo, I got to say, the soup good. Everything else, pretty much suck. I gotta be honest. This place has some great soup and really I feel it's worth it. But everything else it's very questionable.

Also, it's seems specialised in soup, yet only when we are ready to order, the staff tell us 80% of the soup wasn't available? And it was only 12.30pm so if most of it is not available, what are they selling exactly???

Usually in msia, I don't get such unpleasant experience in terms of food, but this place wasn't beyond acceptable.

You can be the judge, and if you want soup, I'd recommend, but everything else, haha...it's entirely up to you.

I think they do excel at photo editing skill 😀
author: Do Hyun Im

review_text: I stopped by the Soup Restaurant midweek, eager to relax and sample their cuisine. While the service staff appeared to be in training, I was delighted by the outstanding quality of the Double Braised Abalone Rice, featuring tender abalone and a deep, savory flavor. The dessert was enjoyable, and I'm excited to return and try more dishes.
author: Stephen Lim

review_text:
Heard alot of Singaporeans raving about this place so decided to try it. Overall food was really good and they had some unique dishes. Loved the hotstone rice and tofu dessert. The fish maw soup was average but generous amount of fish maw. The price is not very cheap though.

May come back again if we are just popping by city square.
author: Isabelle Tay

review_text: Authentic and delicious food! Good ambience to have a nice and quiet spot for brunch, during low season, I've been served by one aunty, there is one old man working as waiter and very unfriendly, pity him though, not suitable to work there , you better quit before ruining people's business. Anyhow , I'm not talking about him, my favourite review is the mee siam which has a balance of sweet and sour, super tasty and crunchy served with fried chicken, very unique, no soup. Will definitely be back!
author: Bakhtiar Syed Badran

review_text:
Tried this cafe for brunch as there was a long queue for the neighbouring (popular) restaurant at B1. There were renovations at upper level and I mistakenly thought that the restaurants there were closed.

Ordered nasi lemak and add on curry chicken, thinking that I'll be given a chicken thigh as advertised (can see the photos posted) but was given a drum stick instead. I felt cheated. The curry chicken was so-so and quite hard, not tender at all. I hope it was not reheated from the previous night leftover. The rice also didn't have much of the coconut milk taste. Some grains of the rice were hard and seemed undercooked.

Initially wanted to order teh tarik and the wait staff told me that it's actually 3-in-1 tea, so I order hot tea (as I always like to drink tea with milk). Came a cup of Lipton tea-o (without milk). Therefore, the menu for drinks is a western style drink, not the typical local/Malaysian/nanyang style. I asked for milk and was told that they don't have fresh milk and was given powder creamer.

Overall a disappointing meal experience. I regretted not joining the queue to the popular restaurant next door.
author: jeff T

review_text:
Very bad service. Staff got attitude problem (Indian man). Ordered Ice lemon tea, I got choked when I took the first sip. They totally forget to add sugar. I ask the waiter which also the cashier and complain. He say then how? You drink already, then I explained to him that the drink is without sugar. I thought he understood and take the drinks back and change. He returns with the drink and I took a sip, again it's without sugar.
I approached another staff and ask why  wrong again, he say that I rejected the drink due to have sugar in the drink, I explained I order a standard ice lemon tea, why is it without sugar? The Indian staff come and ask is it I want to add sugar? I told him off saying that I don't want to add extra sugar, I just want the standard ice lemon tea which supposedly sweet .
author: Ng Boon lei

review_text:
Seats - can be a challenge during peak hours.
Service - Self service, qr code scanning to order. Not much communication for service staff except they will pass you the utensils once your order is received in the system.
Food - Expect 15-20mins wait upon order. Food was hot and served immediately.
Drinks - Lots of the drink menu was not available. Lots of caffeinated choices with limited options if you prefer otherwise
Payment - QR code available for scanning.
Pastries - Tried the Oreo cheesecake, it was good. Have to inform the cashier to bill to your table otherwise they will expect you to pay over the counter.
author: Mohd Amin

review_text: A tall guy at cashier working attitude was bad, impatient, despite service charges incurred. Snatched over my receipt when I was passing it, and asked me furiously and repeatedly “what payment?”. In overall very bad services. Food serving was really slow, waiters response only after few calls. However, kudos to the auntie who is also working came over and save the situation.
author: Lay Lay Ding

restaurant_name: Great Room, restaurant under Holiday Inn Express & Suites Johor Bahru
review_text: Comfortable basic hotel. Generally hip and nice. We encountered heavy rain when we were there and our hotel room window leaked. Other than that, no real issues. If you do not bring your own toothbrush, you do have to request. Cleanliness could be improved as the bed sheets is fairly dirty. Stayed for 1 night in the cosy 2 bedroom. Staffs were helpful and polite.
author: Poh Leong Kian

restaurant_name: Great Room, restaurant under Holiday Inn Express & Suites Johor Bahru
review_text:
I would rate this hotel 5 star for its price.
Really clean and new we had really good experience here! It’s about 10mins walk from city square.

But i would recommend girls to take grab because there were many Bangladesh foreign workers gathered/sleep in front of the hotel.

Side note the hotel doesn’t provide toothpaste and toothbrush so bring your own.
author: Low Jing Yi

restaurant_name: Great Room, restaurant under Holiday Inn Express & Suites Johor Bahru
review_text: Hotel was clean and staffs are very helpful. It provided everything except for toiletries. The hotel is near to the checkpoint. However, you'd rather take a cab for ease of mind when going out of or returning to the hotel. Do not expect any kind of scenic views for a budget hotel, the interiors are quite impressive enough. Amenities are limited, but why stay inside when there's lots to do around JB?
author: M Farhan O

restaurant_name: Great Room, restaurant under Holiday Inn Express & Suites Johor Bahru
review_text:
Friendly receptionist. Smooth check-in and check out. Parking available easily nearby the entrance. Newly refurbished & rebranded hotel. Good price for a family suite (two bedrooms). Adequate size bathroom & WC. Adequate toiletries. The suite comes with microwave & fridge plus sofa bed in the living room so you fit 5 occupants easily. We chose this hotel over any homestay apartment (cheaper option) to avoid all the hassle to check in, get the keys and parking of an apartment.
My kids loved it as they get to have their own TV in the bedroom. Although the overall size of the suite is kinda compact but hey, we just want to have a comfortable rest without any hanky panky.
The total price includes breakfast as well so, clearly this one is our favorite in JB.
author: rifqee m

restaurant_name: Great Room, restaurant under Holiday Inn Express & Suites Johor Bahru
review_text: This is one of the best hotels I've ever stayed so far. The room was very clean, the breakfast was nice, all the staffs were very kind and helpful. The shuttle bus was really helpful also (one of the reasons why I chose this hotel in the first place). Will come back for sure. 10 out of ten!
author: Nathania Khorasani (Nath)

review_text: Tasty, cheap
author: Dave Rafiel

review_text: A place where gomen people hang out.
author: Akmal Muslim

review_text: Ordered Kolono Rice from KFC and it came already burnt and hard. Really disappointed how can you serve this kind of food to customers? I even attached a photo to show the condition.  check your quality before sending out orders next time.
author: Priya Ranjini

review_text:
Today visited this branch. Staff informed can only order at kiosk and not at counter.

Ordered and paid for chicken and mantou combo set. When collection, just only informed mantou and gravy is out of stock and replaced with wedges. Requested to change to other item but other options available only French fries and nuggets. After asking, staff only allow change to small portion of chicken popcorn. If want to cancel order and change, refund of payment takes 21days to the card.

At the first place if the stock is unavailable, should not be displayed for payment. This is a non-matching menu vs actual food selection for a consumer. KFC management shall look into this case and hope other customer will not get into this misleading information and expectation. If knew the combo set is out of stock, will not pay for this.
author: Shawn

review_text: The worst KFC in Johor Bahru, the chicken and drinks are terrible. I didn't notice it the first time I ate there, and I went back a year later, and the taste was still the same. The Ice brown butter oat latte is delicious in other places, why is it so bad here? The latte has no fragrance and no sweetness.
author: Sky Lee

review_text: Don't understand why the male staff in grey uniform like to leave the dustbin open as below picture while customer eating near the area. As a management guy does he know this will affect customer eating experience.
author: Kelly

review_text: One thing I should do from now on, is to check whether the food is spoilt or got contaminated with the 'flies egg'. !! The fried chicken I ordered from Grab THANK GOODNESS I did some checks before I consume, otherwise I'd lay on bed in the hospital. The cleanliness is concerning, please monitor more carefully as it could bring harm to customers, mind you this is a F&B!
author: Matt Lim

review_text: The portion looks really underwhelming. For a sandwich that should be filled and satisfying, this one seems poorly assembled and not worth the price. The fillings are uneven, some parts look empty, and overall it doesn’t feel like you’re getting a proper, full portion. For what you’re paying, this portion is definitely disappointing.
author: Farreyh_ Ika

review_text:
First time trying their salad bowl, didn't know you could order subway in such a way! Literally all the ingredients in a bowl plus a roasted chicken breast without the usual subway bread.
Its pretty awesome! The vegetables are definitely more compared to the normal bread variations.
Will definitely order and try different variations of sauces next time!
author: jayden

review_text:
A very bad experience about the staff!! No manners at all, i love to eat Subway with my Children. But tru all branches, this is the most no manners at all, Please train all the staff with manners, however we are customers.
First I am politely tell my bread with smile (honeyoat please,thanks) but, suddenly the staff who serving me is busy coz of the bread oven sounds, (order from other front to me) its okay to wait, then one girl came and ask me want i want but i manage to see the bread is very dark, as my son is the one who eat i requested to change, but the staff was so rude to ask me what bread?
