Came to enjoy very traditional lei cha dining located in this large (air-conditioned) food court. Brown rice with generous ingredients for an affordable price of $4.50 and rice with 5 pcs of homemade ytf for $4.50. Their ytf pieces are all generously filled with tasty minced meat.

Amazed by the freshly fried delicious/crispy homemade side dishes at $0.80 each. They have Saturday specials '南乳炸鸡翅' or '南乳炸肉'.

Stall owner is a very friendly lady. I’d say most reasonable and delicious lei cha by far. Surely we'll be back for more!

😋😋😋😋😋😋😋l
author: Jodeci Fine

restaurant_name: Hakka Fat Moi Lei Cha Rice
review_text: Considered one of the best traditional Lei Char in Singapore. Reasonable price with generous portion. The soup or tea is not hot enough. They also serve mixed Yong Tao Foo.
author: Jimmy Chai

restaurant_name: Hakka Fat Moi Lei Cha Rice
review_text: The Lei Cha here is very yummy, Can eat almost everyday! The lady boss is also very nice and friendly :)
author: Lim Pei Luan

restaurant_name: 远东面食-传统炒福建虾面
review_text:
The food here taste amazing especially the Hokkien mee,the prawn they put in the noodles are not halved like they usually are in hawker centres but a whole with the head still on the prawn
The Lor Mee taste amazing too
The sauce for the noodles are very thick and the owner always give a large amount of filling inside.
I would say this place has one of the best noodles I have ever eaten in Singapore
Would 100% recommend tourists to eat here.
author: Simon Tai

restaurant_name: 远东面食-传统炒福建虾面
review_text: Very good Hokkien mee. Reasonable price and good portion too!
author: Sherine Tang

restaurant_name: 远东面食-传统炒福建虾面
review_text:
Yuan Dong Noodle: Tried the Hokkien prawn mee. S$4.50 (they have increased the price to $5) the plate was full and had generous amount of ingridients, meat, fish cake slices, and the prawns were on the bigger size than other hawkers. The stock/sause kept the noodles steaming hot. They had a container of chilli where you can scoop up as much chilli as you want. Money for value and quality. Very much recommended. Since it is located inside a commertial building opearting time 9:30am to 1pm only.

Came again to this place the fried hokkien prawn noodle is the best with sambal + calamansi

7th Oct 2022 : Yuan Dong Noodle, tried the Laksa  $4 and was glad I did. Steaming hot with lots of ingridients. Noodles was firm. Scoop up the soup until the bowl was dry. Value for money. Recommended.

19th Dec 2022. Second time ordering Lor mee.  Very good. Large serving.
author: Edward Joseph Paulino

restaurant_name: 远东面食-传统炒福建虾面
review_text:
This is my favorite Hokkein mee place. Way better than Toa Payoh Lor 1.  It's in Northtech building food court. Because it's so far out, nobody has heard of it.
The thick stock with strong umami prawn/ pork flavor saturates the entire plate of noodles. No stock comes close. Most other hokkein mee stocks are just watered down nonsense. The sambal is great.
They are also generous with the pork and prawns. It's not your typical hokkein mee flavor for purists but once you try this, you won't bother with the rest.
I often take this away for my friends to try and everyone have been impressed so far.
author: FoodieDirectory

restaurant_name: 远东面食-传统炒福建虾面
review_text: Very Good Hokian Prawn Mee in this store!
author: Woon Fong Cheong

review_text: Ready to acces place with good Malay, Korean and Chinese Food. Big generous portion of Saba Fish and super tasty Traditional Thunder rice with option to add various topping.
author: Alexander Reinaldo

review_text: randomly damn nice nasi padang in middle of industrial area.
author: Annabelle Khoo

review_text: One of the best rendang, Malay nasi Padang dishes here. Affordable price and great service 👍🏽👍🏽👍🏽👍🏽
author: Zul B

review_text: Home style cooking. Wide range of Tamil style cuisine from breakfast to dinner. Reasonable price
author: Abdul Nasheer

review_text:
Some industrial places offers good food and this is one place I need to create on the Google map for this stall and a nice review!

For a price of $5.50, I ordered the Black Pepper Chicken Biryani, and I am visually shocked on the portion of food given. Chicken, Veg, Egg, heap of Biryani rice, curry and paapdum!

Tasted every food on the plate and they are authentic and flavourful. I can attest also by the flow of customers eating here even at 2pm here.

This is a hidden gem. Taste is different from those food courts that caters to the public taste. For this one, I can come back again to try their other food items.

Thank you for the food experience!
author: Benjamin Tong

review_text:
Their roasted chicken is meaty, juicy and tender(8.5/10); roasted pork is very crispy outside and tender inside(8.5/10). Both meats are medium portion with a bit salty.

Tom yam mee hoon kueh is about average(simple, sour and spicy),7/10.

Coffee (less sweet) is thick and bitter with nice coffee aroma, 8.5/10. Coffee with tea(standard) is well balanced(smooth and thick with some coffee aroma), 9/10.
author: Sam Wong

review_text:
Nice and clean place.

Great Muslim food...

Sambal goreng is delicious.

Sayur lodeh is also very nice n fresh tau kwa.

Kari Ayam is also very tender and savoury.

Thumbs upz
author: Rayson Seah

review_text: The noodles are really good here! It's handmade and the meatballs are made by themselves! The factory that makes the food is just beside it. The soup is good and I love that it is msg free. The place should be a workers cafe but they are opened go public. Order the bak kwa spring roll and homemade barley! It's so good no complains :)
author: Alicia Lee

review_text:
I stumbled upon the Malay stall and decided to try their Nasi Lemak and let me tell you, I was pleasantly surprised!

Imagine fluffy rice infused with the warmth of coconut, and perfectly complemented by a sambal that dances between sweet and savoury on your tongue.  The chicken wing, which is an important part of any nasi lemak meal, was delightfully crispy with a flavourful batter and moist and tender meat.

The real shocker? It only costs $4! Parking is also free but spaces can get really limited during the peak morning hours and lunch time.
author: Ursa Major

review_text: Was here for a job, and did I find a very good food place, with sea salt coffee with ok pricing.
author: yang wenting

review_text:
Only found out this bar when travelling on bus 169. Pretty interesting place to have a bar. Slightly difficult to come if you do not have car.

The food overall was good. Pleasantly surprised by the Asian food. In my opinion, it was better than the western dish. But that doesn't means the western dishes are bad. They are pretty decent. The pizza was interesting. It's base is a biscuit type instead of those bread type.

The bar can do better by having better ventilation. There is a kind of cooking smell in the place upon entering.

Overall, a pleasant place to come by for decent food at a good price.
author: Maxwell CCH

review_text:
A hidden gem in the quiet Woodlands industrial area!
The Carpenter Bar serves tasty and reasonably priced dishes — the charcoal prawn burger is unique and delicious, and the curry prawn rice is full of flavour. Drinks are refreshing and the place has a relaxing atmosphere — perfect for a peaceful meal or weekend chill-out.
author: Calvin Hooi

review_text: A surprising cozy Bristol Bar located totally out of nowhere in an industry area at Woodlands, Admiralty Road West. Love the ambience coz it is not overly packed. Great for gatherings or group dinning. There's also pool table to help kill time. Parking is free, consider at plus for that. The food is reasonable & portion servings acceptable. However the steak & salmon seems a little small. The fusion burger (nasi lemak burger) is just awesome. A must try...
author: viking T

review_text:
first visit. the food is good.
the chicken wing is spicy good.
the place is quiet and comfortable but that's exactly what i wanted so that i can have a chill time with my teens.
author: Wee Hock ONG

review_text: Nice place to chill. Food is good. Beer is the normal kind. Hard to reach if no car
author: Yusna Murphiyana

review_text:
This was a very unpleasant experience, and unfortunately my first and last time ordering from Saladroom.

I fully understand that the merchant might be busy and may not be able to fulfil the order. I even offered to have the order cancelled if they were unable to proceed. However, after placing my order in the morning around 9+am, the merchant instead asked if the delivery could be pushed to the next day. I clearly informed them that I needed the food today. I was then promised delivery before 2.30pm, but the delivery was delayed again with no proper updates and the merchant eventually went completely unresponsive.

Near 3pm, when I approached Grab to cancel the order due to non delivery and unresponsive, the merchant suddenly contacted me via WhatsApp claiming that the food had just been delivered. I was then asked to either make payment immediately or reorder again in the system as the merchant said they were unable to contact Grab.

This was extremely frustrating, as the responsibility was unfairly pushed onto me even though the delays and miscommunication were clearly not my fault. I also do not understand why a merchant would be unable to contact Grab directly and instead expect the customer to resolve it.

Overall, this was a very poor first time experience. I hope Grab looks into this matter, as this is not how customers should be treated.
author: Nichole

review_text:
Poor quality of vegetables, poor customer service, ordered vegetables for the next day but only informed me that they cannot deliver after my dinner service has ended.

Gave me mushrooms that were at least 4 days old already all mushy and dark, quality is thrash even after letting them know they still continue to give us rubbish quality mushrooms.

Delivery timing also all over the place, tell me 3-4pm delivers at 6pm instead. Then goes ahead to change delivery timing to 6pm-7pm, then proceeds to deliver at 8pm. It’s just ridiculous how can the customer service be so poor.

FYI my business is located in the same building as them, but they can’t even be bothered to deliver on time or give us acceptable levels of vegetables and mushrooms.
author: benjamin sng

review_text:
Checked the delivery schedule before placing order on Wednesday, was informed the delivery will be on the next day.
They informed me via shopee chat that they do not have stock for asparagus and delivery will be pushed to the following day (Friday).
Had to asked them on the delivery status as I did not receive until late evening.
They told me that the delivery will be before 9pm when i was gonna use to the ingredients to cook dinner for that day. Delivery was not made at 9pm, and they told me delivery will be delayed till 10pm. Actual delivery was made after 10.30pm, driver didnt bother to give me a call and just left the box outside my house.

Items delivered was incorrect (normal lettuce instead of romaine lettuce), asparagus was not fresh, the stalk had already wilted, and strawberries was 230g inclusive of box when it was supposed to be 250g.

The quality other items are also not very fantastic.
author: Khaing Yee Oo

review_text: This is my first time buying from Saladroom.sg and I’m very satisfied with how fresh their produce is, particularly their mushrooms. The $30 mystery box (on discount at $22.50 when I purchased it) is a bargain. Made my family an IG-worthy brunch that cost a fraction of what we’d pay at any cafe. I will be back regularly to stock up.
author: stella thng

review_text: Merchant is so recommendable not only they are prompt in replies but also so accommodating. Error made on the delivery location was on my end but it was quickly acknowledged and notified to the delivery lady.  Eventually my orders was delivered to the correct address intended and even received a notification it was safely delivered...great job!!! I am a super happy customer today! Thank you Sir🥰
author: Angie Ozara

review_text: Poor hygiene food , food contain bugs , Don’t buy any food
author: Kavin Fun

review_text:
Nice ambiance, attractive decoration.
Attentive service crews and generous portions of food. 🍱 Great place for gathering.
I’m actually having team building here. 8 of us ordered 2 sets of shell 🐚 out. Menu stated the portion is for 2 pax. But it is enough for 8 of us. I cannot say cheap, but value for money.
Verity of food choices. Drinks 🍹 also not bad.
Recommended 👍🏻!
Had spent $500 + in total, upon paying, received 2 pcs of $5 cash vouchers 🙂
Then I got a valid reason to revisit the restaurant again 😂
author: Kiko

review_text: Ordered the sweet and sour fish rice, the amount of fish slices rice is a bit pathetic. Less than 5 pieces.. but taste nice.. only thing is the fish portions too little.
author: O O

review_text: 22SGD++ for a buffet with aircon and good spread: beef, mutton, crab and prawn. I cannot complain any about it. Super super affordable. The meat quality also not bad.
author: Terry Ding

review_text: Love the ayam penyet, ikan penyet and kacang pool! Bakso mie was decent and tauhu telor was yummy! Lontong also super sedap, western food was well marinated. Love the super friendly staff, special shout out to Nana who always tries to fulfil her promise on making kacang pool for me 🥰.
author: Adaline Teo

review_text: Had my dinner with husband on 27 Nov'25. BBQ stingray, sambal kangkong and seafood tom yum cost me $84 which i think is abit too expensive and the taste was horrible. Stingray is so dry and overcooked. Sambal kangkong was sweet. Tom yum soup was serve not hot, sweet and taste of coconut milk instead of spicy tom yum red soup. First and last to have my seafood spread there.

review_text: The drink cannot make it
author: Christopherson Ho

review_text: Beef briyani. Something that doesn’t happen often. Same style of mutton curry but it’s beef. I don’t know if many shops that do this. It’s not bad and a nice refreshing change. Only problem is that this is a rather ulu place.

author: Smart Sathish

review_text: Circuit breaker food was a big headache. We ordered delivery for classic chicken murtabak, nasi goreng seafood, beehoon goreng and fried chicken! Fried chicken was crispy and yummy. Chicken murtabak was Sedap as well. Great portions for beehoon goreng and nasi goreng seafood. Highly recommended if you have cravings for old classic singaporean Indian food.

review_text: ordered mutton dam briyani from grab, no mutton :’)

review_text: Excellent food, especially roti with mutton.
author: Md Kazi Masum

review_text:
Solid spot for Indian food. Good variety, plenty of options, fair prices, and most importantly, it tastes good. I’ve been here many times and honestly have no complaints so far.

It’s close to a dormitory, so most of the customers are the residents there. Definitely a place I’d recommend, and one I’ll keep coming back to.
author: S Raveen

review_text:
I ordered 2 parottas. First, I was told to stand in the cashier line, so I waited patiently. After that, I informed the order taker three times about my order, but there was no proper response. It felt like my request was being ignored, which wasted a lot of my time.
Later, the cashier finally gave the order. If the food was going to be given directly, I don’t understand why I was asked to stand in the line in the first place.
The taste of the food was good, but the service was very poor and unorganized. I paid for the food — it’s not free — so I expect basic respect and proper service.
Hope they improve their customer service.
author: SAKTHI KUMAR

review_text: Used to be great food and reasonable price, now it's only slightly good with increase pricing. Hopefully doesn't get worse. Portion reducing slightly. Good for take away.
author: Mukash Vengadasan

review_text:
the food is really good and my friends and I had thoroughly enjoyed it!!

the beautifully spiced and fragrant briyani rice, paired with juicy and tender mutton, was absolutely mouthwatering. the vendakkai fry was equally amazing, adding a delightful crunch and flavour to the meal.

the lady boss is also an exceptionally nice and capable young lady!! she treated us with much kindness and patience.
author: Melissa Leow

review_text: They accepted my order, I had a driver arrive but they cancelled my order when they will still be open for another 45minutes. I already had a driver waiting and they decided that they would not fulfil the order. Not sure if they know they are losing a lot of revenue. If they do then why not set the closing timing earlier on grab?
author: Mukesh Kalungan

review_text:
Newly opened in 2025 year end.
Die die must take sanba
belacan chilli is nice.
Hor Fun With Beansprouts & Sliced Fish 三捞河粉 very simple dish, but taste good 😋👍🏻.
Chili crab and Curry fish head having promotion now, best to order one day before to confirm.
Staff was very friendly, will come to try other dishes again.
author: Johnny lkh

review_text: Chilli crab is fresh with a rich, flavourful sauce. Fish head steamboat is comforting with a tasty broth and generous ingredients. Fish head curry is thick, fragrant, and not watery at all. Everything was freshly cooked. Highly recommended 👍
author: Tan Ck

review_text: Happened to visit this Ah Ma Kitchen at Woodland Industrial Park E9 last week after meeting my client. Understand from the master chef, this is another sub outlet from the Nee Soon branch. $19 for curry fish head and it was a huge 1. Still as good compared to their main branch. Promo also include 3 crabs for only $60 in 1 favour, the size of each crab was ard 600g. I think decent size ba. Will be back to try.
author: Edmund Lee

review_text: Stone throw away from where I stay , food is good ...The fish head curry is good 👍
author: Dan Feng

review_text: The food is super good and service is fantastic .

review_text: Bad, super bad. I got burnt fish for my boiled fish, missing egg fried wifh tomato. The food got no quality

author: Random

review_text: Tasty malaysian style Mee Goreng, but bit pricy for the prawn paste chicken wing, $10 for 7 pcs.
author: Alexander Reinaldo

restaurant_name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
review_text: This is a humble stall that you may find rare in an industrial building. There are a wide varieties of dishes i you come early. Brown rice is available too and they often have special of the day & 擂茶 (初一十五暂停). As it’s an industrial area hence they are only open from Monday to Friday and from morning till 1:30pm.
author: HC Lum

restaurant_name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
review_text:
Vegetarian stall with vegan options, food contains no alliums. Good food at a reasonable price. The healthy vegan Lei Cha is good, highly recommended.

**Vegan Lei Cha ( not available on lunar New Moon Day and Full Moon Day )

** do help yourself with a nice bowl of free vegetables soup.
author: Yellow Bear

restaurant_name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
review_text: Brown rice is not of good quality as looks dry and separated: no plump grains seen. Taukwa looks really processed and fried until have they hard edges. Happy that the peanuts are not burnt :) Chaipoh is oily and has a strong smell. Would skip it, if I would buy Leicha rice from this stall once more. Mani leaves are missing, substituted by Chye sim which brings a watery, bitter taste element into the dish. Shredded cabbage and finely cut longbeans are sweet.
author: Jane Ang

restaurant_name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
review_text: Good food. Do avoid lunch time as there may be a queue. Check out their daily specials and lei cha too!
author: Z X

restaurant_name: Wan Yuan Vegetarian Stall Woodlands Spectrum 1
review_text: Bad service from the aunty with short hair at this stall, bought thunder tea rice and is super oily. Bad service with bad food...
author: Stan Yap

review_text: Great service & food 💯 When I had to take away midway while eating, owner removed the chili & peanuts and gave a packet one packed separately. The care they have is unbeatable, you can feel it in the service & the food. The most well cooked chicken I've had with noodles, tender with generous portions. Not to mention the generous portion of high quality veg.
author: Rachel Chong

review_text: Had a really enjoyable meal here. The Thai food tasted authentic, with bold flavours and fresh ingredients. The menu has a good variety, prices are affordable, and the portions are generous. Staff were polite and service was fast. Highly recommended for anyone who loves Thai cuisine!
author: Yanzhi toh

review_text: Authentic Thai Cuisine by Thai chef! Affordable and delicious. Just had Khao Ka Moo and wow… tender pork, rich sauce, and that tangy mustard green on the side makes it pop. Comfort food level 💯. Highly recommend if you want something hearty but not too heavy!”
author: CH Tan

review_text: Authentic Thai food at a reasonable price. I even have to order extra bowl of rice. Chef is friendly and clean. 👍🙏
author: Lee QX

review_text:
Just happened to have my lunch in this area, the Khao Ka Moo was the best that I have ever tried!
Every bite is a flavor explosion. Definitely worth it if you’re craving something hearty, affordable and stomach filling!
author: Shishiboo Pets

review_text: Tried the Prawn Noodles for bf'.. Soup is tasty asked the owner for Flat Rice Noodles... kuay-tiau she will do it soon... SG'eans like Flat Rice Noodles. PS: With a dash of hot red Chilli is a must...
author: CH4543 Heng

review_text:
Made reservations over the phone, table was ready but 1 high chair requested was not prepared. Good but not great.

Between 2-3 stars but removed 1 for error drama, removed another 1 for pricey dishes.
Won’t return.

Severely understaffed, small portions.
We ordered medium or large for 12pax but everything is tiny.
Food was actually quite delicious but not say “AMAZINGMUSTRETURN”.

Not aircon area but was not warm.

Buyer beware, place was charming and you pay for it.

The collagen soup was 96$ (are you mad)

Egg fried rice was 22$ literally rice egg and corn.

Pulut hitam with ice cream was passable.
We ordered coconut cream but they gave ice cream. (Score!)

Anyway surely their kitchen just have bad system or workers are tripping like mad.

Drama:
Ordered 2 yuzu; but 2 barley came. No event here.

Ordered 2 yam paste; 3 came. We started eating but didn’t touch the 3rd one. Multiple scanned the qr to order; we didn’t know how many we ordered.
One lady came to us saying they served 3 instead of 2; asked to pay for 3rd one. We said but we didn’t order it nor did we touch it. Then she said let me check the bill. (???) it said 2x.
Multiple elders at our table wanted to flip the table. We laughed that why don’t she just serve us whatever she can’t sell, and ask us to pay.

What a weird place. Severely understaffed. Made each staff wants to just serve the guests as efficiently as possible without thinking of customer service.

No offence to the owners but too bad.
author: Alex Chew

review_text: Had a great birthday celebration here! The seafood was fresh and really delicious, and the overall atmosphere was nice and relaxed. What stood out most was the staff were super friendly, helpful, and made us feel very welcome. They were attentive without being overbearing and helped make the celebration extra enjoyable. Would definitely come back for another special occasion!
author: Ranjini Shree

review_text:
Truly a hidden gem that is literally located on the edge of Singapore! Ambience was lovely dining in an old colonial era building very near the beachfront, you can even see Johor right across

Food was all very fresh and portions were generous, we really enjoyed dinner here. Service staff were all friendly and proactive too

Location is pretty far out north but that is a positive as you can escape the hustle and bustle of the city. If only there were more places like this in Singapore..
author: Arnold Teo

review_text:
Overall, the food was delicious, flavourful, and truly enjoyable, complemented by a nice ambience with a sea-view.
Especially, the curry fish head, fresh fish with a smooth texture, paired with a deeply aromatic and well-balanced curry 😋😋
author: Warren Tan

review_text:
The food is good overall but what I really appreciate is the ambiance.
The prawn paste chicken and the laksa is good it comes with a free coffee.
Prices are a little bit on the higher side especially the broccoli scallop.
Will go there again sometimes it is literally like a walk in the park.
author: Sarah Loh

review_text: Beautiful restaurant serving awesome Peranakan food… love the ambience and how serene the surroundings are… never been to this part of Singapore before… today is our first visit, just 2 person and this set meal is just perfect for us to try the must try dishes…. Will bring my whole family here next time and order more dishes…highly recommended
author: Joanne Peng

review_text: This is a cosy, home-run Peranakan café with limited manpower, so it’s best to come with the right expectations. Don’t expect professionally dressed service staff but do expect heartfelt hospitality. The food is excellent, service is polite, and both the servers and bosses are genuinely friendly. The waiting time can be a little long, but it’s worth every minute. We truly enjoyed the comfortable, relaxed, homey atmosphere.
author: elizabeth lim

review_text: Service speed was average. Uncle was very friendly. The food was absolutely delicious. Everything was made with love, from scratch and with a twist. The chilli was wonderfully spicy packs a real kick! Atmosphere was a cool chill retro. From a time long ago and nowhere to be found. Loved the effort and love that the chef put into each of her dishes which made the wait for the food and the travel time absolutely worth it
author: Jacob Lee

review_text: The place is hidden within bungalows. A very nice place to chill out with family & friends. The  food is delicious, especially the chicken soup. Most of their food are spicy but they have kids meal for children who can't take spicy food. We ordered their CNY menu which comes with a small Yusheng. The Yusheng has ingredients like apple, mango and mandarin orange slices for a refreshing taste.
author: Jenny Lee

review_text:
November 2025
- Came to try after learning about them through the media.
- Food was decent. I enjoyed the nasi ulam. My parents, who love nasi ulam, said it was good.
- We made a reservation, and went as soon as they opened on a Saturday. Apparently, our reservation was not recorded, but we did not have to wait to get seated, and the first round of our food was served reasonably quickly.
- But, the diners who came after us, even though it was not too crowded, they had to wait quite a long time for their food.
- We ordered a second round because we wanted to try some more finger food, like satay, and that took a while.
- The decor and vibe of the place is rustic, and rather unusual nowadays.
author: Wei Yuet Wong

review_text:
This Bistro is one of our favorites recently. It has good music, food and service. The boss is a humble and friendly individual who ensures all customers are comfortable and strives to ensure everyone is happy and enjoys themselves. Take feedback positively and makes efforts to improve on the overall standards. Located within a Recreation Centre, this bistro is located on level two away from other establishment within the centre.
Kudos to the team lead by the owner's daughter and staff. Do drop by one of the weekends for good food, live band and ambience.
author: Kannan Kumar

review_text:
I've eaten only one thing on their menu. So, I can't give an accurate review. However, the one menu item that I've had multiple times was the Chicken Maggie with egg. It was really good.

My only complaint is that the often don't see Grab orders. It says that their orders are complete but no food is cooked. At least they honor the payments.

It's a good hangout joint/bar, especially for Indians. It's one of my favorite places to order lunch now.
author: Maurice A. Tillman

review_text:
I decided to try this place because it’s tucked away in a unique location. Unfortunately, the experience was not great. The food took a long time to arrive—at least a 30-minute wait. The staff seemed unfamiliar with the menu, which made ordering quite difficult.

After having the vegetarian mee goreng, which I ordered, I ended up with severe food poisoning and am still dealing with stomach cramps after almost 5 days, although other symptoms are gone. Based on my experience, I do not recommend eating here. If you do visit, perhaps just stick to drinks and be very cautious with the food.
author: Maha Ammal

review_text:
Nice place to hang out with friend and family ..
Friendly staff and price are reasonable!!🤩🤩
author: Mary An De Castro

review_text:
Hidden gem alert! 💥
Tucked deep inside a migrant workers’ recreational centre (yes, you’ll need to ask for directions—total maze), this little bistro is small but electric.

We stumbled in to find Vasantham singers belting out tunes, and even the crowd joined in. Loud thou 😆 🎤 Drinks? Cheap. Crowd? All local, with a few expats sprinkled in.

⚠️ Food takes forever, but trust me—the satti soru mutton is worth every second. Absolute bomb. 💣

Pro tip: Make a reservation. You’ll thank me later.
Fun night, 10/10 vibes.

review_text:
The Patio is pleasantly tucked away in a quiet corner of northern Sembawang, offering a peaceful escape from the city. Located on Level 2, the restaurant enjoys a lovely sea view and a relaxed, breezy atmosphere. The menu is well-rounded, catering to diners of all ages.

The Thai basil chicken was juicy with a satisfying kick of spice. The classic burger was cooked just right, with a hint of pink at the centre and a generous serving of fries. The highlight of the meal, however, was the satay, grilled prawns, and sambal stingray platter priced at $65 — excellent value in our view. The satays were well-grilled and flavorful, the prawns were sizeable, deshelled, and perfectly cooked, while the sambal stingray was thick, meaty, and generously coated with chilli. The sambal sotong was more average, slightly on the chewy side. Paired with a cold beer, the meal came together beautifully. Our total bill was around $145.

The restaurant itself is small and cozy, with limited seating and both indoor and outdoor options. Only two outdoor tables offer unobstructed sea views, so reservations are highly recommended. On a breezy evening, the pet-friendly setting, good food, and relaxed ambience made for a very enjoyable family dining experience. Do note that the location is quite secluded, with limited access to public transport — but that’s part of its charm.

We’re happy to recommend The Patio and look forward to returning.

review_text:
Media Invite~

Started in the 50s, Nelson Bar used to be frequented by sailors and captains who docked at the Sembawang naval shipyard, making it one of the oldest bars in Singapore.

The bar’s history is still retained through pieces left by sailors – old pictures, life buoys and scribbles on walls – and a pool table that’s made out of decommissioned ships.

You must visit Nelson Bar to experience this nostalgic spot and perhaps learn a thing or two about this bar’s past over some drinks and a game of pool with friends. Pool table is not available due to COVID-19 restrictions these days.

For vegetarians and non alcoholic people like me,they do serve a range of mocktails and plant based dishes etc.

It is a place to rest,relax,listen to music and mingle with nice people.

Zila served me well.

Thank you Mashel for inviting me to such a historical place.

review_text:
Visited this place on a weekend morning and honestly, I’m appalled by the experience. You’d think an empty restaurant would mean quick service, but despite there being only two other tables filled, the experience was a disaster.

It took almost 20 minutes just for my drink (an overly sweet Teh Tarik which was honestly mediocre at best) to be served. After waiting 45 minutes for food that never came, I finally gave up and decided to leave.

I spoke to the staff and found out they were severely shorthanded as there were only two people running the entire floor, and they were completely overwhelmed by a non-stop flood of delivery orders.

I don't blame the two poor staff as they were clearly doing their best while being overwhelmed. This falls squarely on the management. If you know you're popular on delivery platforms, you need to either add more manpower on weekends or find a way to regulate the order flow. It’s not fair to let walk-in customers sit at a table for nearly an hour while delivery bags fly out the door. At the very least, inform customers of the wait time before they sit down.

I paid for my drinks and walked over to the coffeeshop nearby (1036 Live Seafood near the open carpark). I ordered one egg and one plain prata from the Indian Muslim stall, and it was served piping hot within 2 minutes for a grand total of $3. Fast, efficient, and actually valued my time.

I will never visit Mr Uncle ever again.

The only issue I have was I felt the seasoning on the meat and soup itself is quite sweet, and is either a lot of sugar and/or MSG added. Nonetheless, will be back again and maybe also try the other non-mookata dishes.

review_text:
Our visit to what is purported to be a "hidden gem" in Johor Bahru left us with mixed feelings, with more of the latter than the former. While the restaurant has clearly put effort into its aesthetic, the overall dining experience fell short of expectations, particularly in key areas that matter most: food and cleanliness.
The food quality was a significant letdown. My Maryland Chicken arrived with an unappetizingly thick layer of grease, making it difficult to enjoy what should have been a simple, classic dish. The chicken burger also failed to impress, lacking in flavor and overall quality. The food and drink prices feel unjustified given the poor execution and ingredients. It's disappointing when the cost doesn't align with the value received, especially for what is meant to be a special dining spot.
The ambiance, unfortunately, was a major concern. While the outdoor seating area had potential, it was marred by a serious cleanliness issue. Finding what appeared to be animal droppings near our table was unsettling and instantly ruined the atmosphere. This kind of oversight is a deal-breaker and speaks volumes about the restaurant's hygiene standards. The location itself is also a drawback. It's a bit far from the main city areas, and the ongoing road construction makes the journey difficult and inconvenient.
On a positive note, the restaurant's main redeeming quality is its visual appeal. The property is filled with numerous "Instagrammable" spots, with interesting decor and thoughtful design that make it a great place for photos. Additionally, the service provided by the staff was genuinely humble and kind. They were attentive and polite, a welcome contrast to the other issues we encountered. While the beautiful decor and friendly service were appreciated, they were not enough to outweigh the significant problems with the food, price, and most importantly, the cleanliness of the dining area.

review_text:
This is a Klang bak kut teh stall which also sells tze char dishes. As I wasn't particularly in the mood for bak kut teh on a hot afternoon, I went for a Marmite Chicken Rice topped off with a sunny side up egg instead.

While the portion was decent, I thought it was kinda pricey as it came up to $7.90. The chicken was tasty, but I think it was because it had enough MSG to make Uncle Roger go "Fuiyoh!" as I was hit with a terrible bout of thirst after the meal.

The turnover in this kopitiam is remarkably high, and I think the pricey items are definitely a contributing factor to this.
author: Ursa Major

restaurant_name: Chi Liu Xiang Klang Claypot Herbal Bak Kut Teh
review_text: Ordered dry bak kut teh which one bowl of herbal soup is also given in addition. For the dry bak kut teh at $10.80, it comes with premium pork rib and portion is enough for 2. The dry BKT is very nice to me as it has good spices and it's a little spicy. Herbal soup is also good with strong herbal taste. Me and wife also ordered the pig trotter vinegar which is flavourful enough to our likeing. I can only say if u wan a good meal, then order like us, x 2 items and eat till shiok. Price point wise, for such nice food, I don't find it expensive.
author: Jun Ming Alvin Soo

review_text:
I ordered a seafood set priced at RM67 with an additional squid add-on costing RM66. The food was decent and the seafood tasted okay, but personally I felt that the pricing was quite high for the portion and overall experience.

The presentation was simple and the flavours were acceptable, however for the total price paid, I was expecting either a larger portion or something more special. While the meal was enjoyable, I don’t think it fully matched the price point.

Overall, it was an okay experience, but I hope the pricing or portion can be improved in the future.

review_text:
Restoran Jom Singgah Pak Din is the kind of “no-frills, makan puas hati” place, not fancy, but super practical when you’re hungry and you want food fast.

At 6AM, the best part is the nasi campur / lauk pilih sendiri setup. They have a good spread of berkuah dishes (red curry/masak style gravy), sayur-sayur, and simple goreng options (even saw telur mata, plus snacky sides like sausages/nuggets on skewers). You also get the usual ulam/side table vibes,  cucumber slices and basic condiments ready to grab, with cutlery and tissues set up for self-service.

For drinks, it’s convenient: there’s a big chiller with canned/boxed drinks, and they clearly stock a lot of bottled water, perfect if you’re coming after a long day and just need to hydrate and eat quickly.

Atmosphere-wise: very kedai makan style, spacious seating with simple tables and plastic chairs. But honest note, the place looks a bit old-school and worn (the flooring and lighting are quite harsh), so if you’re coming for “aesthetic cafe photos,” this is not it. This is more for people who care about portion, speed, and variety.

The staff seem not entertain even at the counter, but I came in the morning 6AM.

Overall: a solid stop if you want a straightforward meal, many choices of lauk, and easy drinks. If they improve a bit on the lighting/cleanliness details, this place can feel even more inviting, but as it is, it’s already a good “singgah & kenyang” spot.

review_text:
I recently had dinner at Sarifah Kitchen Steamboat, located at Gelang Patah, and I was thoroughly impressed. The restaurant boasts a pleasant and well-thought-out environment with plenty of tables available. Finding parking was a breeze, and the venue maintained a calm atmosphere—likely because it is new and situated away from the main road.

The menu is diverse and thoughtfully organized into several sections: grill, steamboat, veggies, ready-to-eat options such as fried dishes, ice cream, drinks, and more. I was particularly pleased with the seafood selection, which was undoubtedly fresh and well-stocked, contrary to some opinions I had heard.

One standout dish was the lamb with black pepper sauce. It struck the perfect balance—not too sweet, with exceptional seasoning that truly made it the star of the meal. Additionally, the restaurant offers a sauce section that allows you to customize your flavors, which is a unique and enjoyable touch.

For the soup options, you can choose between a steamboat white soup and tom yum. The tom yum, in particular, delivered an authentic Thai experience with its vibrant, spicy notes that were simply amazing.

The service was superb throughout the evening. The staff was friendly and attentive, and when I inquired about walk-in availability beforehand, they responded courteously and helpfully.

One thing to note for dine-in customers is that you pay upfront before enjoying your meal. Overall, Sarifah Kitchen Steamboat is a great place to gather with friends or family for a delicious and satisfying dining experience. It is definitely worth a visit!

review_text:
This restaurant is located in Lima Kedai, Gelang Patah, just beside the main road and about 1 km from JDT Stadium.                It is a 12-minute drive from Bukit Indah and roughly 30 minutes (27 km) from JB CIQ. Parking is limited, customers must park along the roadside, which can be challenging during peak hours.
Open after 5.00pm till 3.00am.

We visited on 12.7.2025 and tried several dishes:

Fish & Chips, acceptable taste but the portion was smaller than expected for the price.

Thirivizha Saappadu (Mutton & Chicken Mix) both meats were cooked together, which was unexpected. Another plate of the mutton gravy was served separately but had an overly sweet taste, lacking the traditional Kara Sara masala flavour we anticipated. At RM50, the dish was underwhelming.

Chicken 65 – Well seasoned and enjoyable.

Squid Satti Soru – The highlight of the meal!
Perfectly cooked with balanced spiciness.

Service & Ambience:
The service was decent, though the restaurant could improve in consistency with traditional flavours, especially for premium priced dishes. The ambience is casual, suitable for a quick meal.

An average dining experience with a few standout dishes (Squid Satti Soru, Chicken 65) but some disappointments (Thirivizha Saappadu). Worth trying if you are nearby but not a must visit destination. Might revisit for the squid but would skip the mutton dishes.

Recommendation:
✔ Try the Squid Satti Soru and Chicken 65
✖ Thirivizha Saappadu needs flavour improvement for its price
⚠ Parking can be inconvenient

Rating: 3/5 – Decent for casual dining, but with room for improvement.

restaurant_name: Tong Dim Sum Restaurant 同心圆港式点心楼
review_text:
102 咖啡O Kopi O Kosong = RM2.40
26 烧卖 Siew Mai = RM6.90
06 虾饺 Har Gao = RM6.90
37 叉烧包 Char Siew Bao = RM5.00

No Service Charges

This is a Kopitiam Styled Dim Sum Eatery located in Bukit Indah. It looks just like any other such Dim Sum Eateries in JB. The Most Distinctive Difference is that this is the Dim Sum Eatery that Famous Taiwanese Superstar Jay Chou 周杰伦 himself visited.

The Place is relatively Cleanly Maintained, not Air-Conditioned and staffed mostly by Myanmar (Thai?) Folks who are Friendly, Polite and Mostly Keep to Themselves. There weren't much Customers when I was there at 7.30am on a Friday Morning.

Once you're seated down, a Staff Member will bring a Big Tray of Fried Items over to your Table for you to choose.  If you are not in the Mood for them, just politely reject.  The Garlic Chilli they have at this place is most certainly from some Bottle.  Standard Garlic Chilli type of Taste with a Slightly Elevated Spiciness that doesn't bite.

I do like that the Dim Sums are all served in a Traditional Bamboo Basket instead of those Plastic Mr DIY type of Faux Containers.  They use Standard Parchment Paper as a Base though. It took 1 Min for both the Kopi and CSB, 5 Mins for the Har Gao, and 10 Mins for the Siew Mai. Everything was served up within 10 Mins.

102 咖啡O Kopi O Kosong = RM2.40
26 烧卖 Siew Mai = RM6.90
06 虾饺 Har Gao = RM6.90
37 叉烧包 Char Siew Bao = RM5.00

Conclusion and Closing Thoughts

At the Price of RM2.40 (S$0.80) for this Cup of Kopi-O-Kosong was Affordable, but also Unremarkable. Its a Very Standard SG Kopitiam Level.  Not Super Gao Gao but still can wake you up type.

At the Price of RM6.90 (S$2.10) for the Siew Mai at first didn't look impressive because of how Small they looked, but its the Bouncy and Juicy Bite Texture that impressed me.  This Siew Mai tastes better than it looks.

At the Same Price of RM6.90 (S$2.10) for the Har Gao was surprising because Har Gao usually costs Slightly More than Siew Mai.  Again, like their Siew Mai, they looked Unimpressively Small but the Highlight is also a Delightful Bouncy Juicy Bite Texture.

At the Price of RM5.00 (S$1.60) for 2 CSBs was an Affordable Price. Again, they're Small (Can you see a Trend for the Dim Sums at this place?)  The Filling is an Interesting Cross-Mix between Sweet and Braised Type.

I'll be honest I did not have any High Expectations when I came here because I expected the Taste to be Very Standard Acceptable Dim Sum Taste.  What really impressed me was the Juicy Bouncy Bite Texture of both their Siew Mai and Har Gao.  Now I'm not saying the Dim Sums here are Super Mind-Blowingly Amazing but they are Certainly still Above Average.

No Idea why Jay Chou visited this Eatery of all Places in JB when he visited. Hahaha, maybe he also enjoy a Meaty and Juicy Dim Sum Bite Feel?

Overall a Decent, Above Average and Affordable Dim Sum Eatery that even Jay Chou himself approves.  I went up to the Friendly Lady Owner to compliment her which she appreciated. Hahaha, she also verified that this is the Real Jay Chou and not some Random Celebrity Impersonator.  Decent Place. I can certainly recommend this place to give a Try if you are ever near the Area.

review_text:
While many visit for the confectionery for cakes, pastries and coffee, let's not overlook L.Cafe's by Lavender truly exceptional handmade gelato – a hidden gem. Recently, I indulged in dark chocolate and pistachio gelato at Venchi in Raffles City, Singapore, a venue often cited as a benchmark for gelato excellence. Their gelato was undoubtedly superb, rivaling even the renowned La Strega Nocciola Gelateria Artigianale in Florence, Italy. However, the two-flavour cup, at a cost of S$11, was rather petite in portion but high in price.

Now, consider Lavender's L.Cafe gelato. I would argue it is comparable to, if not superior to, Venchi's, especially the roasted pistachio. L.Cafe's roasted pistachio flavour possessed an intense, lingering toasty nuttiness. The dark chocolate, while excellent, lacked the same depth and richness as Venchi's. Nevertheless, it was still a highly enjoyable experience. Importantly, L.Cafe's gelato is priced significantly lower, ranging from RM8.90 to RM10.90 – approximately half the price of Venchi's – and the serving portions are generously larger, at least 20% more.

One might aptly describe L.Cafe's gelato as "Venchi gelato on a budget." It offers a similar, if not superior, gelato experience at a fraction of the cost. If you find yourself in Malaysia, treating yourself to L.Cafe's handmade gelato is an absolute must.

The staff were friendly, attentive, and made us feel very welcome. The environment was clean, comfortable, and perfect for both family gatherings and casual meals with friends.

If you love authentic Hunan cuisine with real flavor and quality, this is definitely a must-visit. Highly recommended, and I will definitely come back again

After a while, the waitress Aishah came politely and informed us that the Mediterranean rice was finished, and offered to replace it with spice rice. I mentioned that one of my friends doesn’t like spicy food, and she kindly explained that it’s spice rice, not spicy rice.

I jokingly said, “I should get a complimentary meal for the mistake,” and she just smiled. A few minutes later, she came back with a chocolate muffin as an apology. I was so touched! Even though it was a small thing, her kindness and smile made my day.

Aishah truly went above and beyond — she served everyone with a smile and such positive energy. Please keep her — she’s a gem! 💛

review_text:
Just had a meal that totally ruffled my feathers at Nando’s, that juicy grilled chicken was cooked to perfection, tender and packed with smoky, charred flavor. The real star was that extra hot sauce delivering a fierce, fiery kick right from the first bite, warming me up in the best way without going overboard. To balance the heat, the creamy garlic sauce was rich and velvety, with a bold garlic punch that mellowed the spice beautifully. Crispy golden chips added the perfect crunch, and the fresh, tangy coleslaw brought a cool, creamy contrast to every bite. Flavor-wise, the combo nailed it, spicy, savory, creamy, and crunchy all at once.

The food was on point, but the staff weren’t. No greetings, no thank you, just a cold and unfriendly vibe that really brought down the experience. Still, if you want bold, comforting flavors with a spicy twist, this meal hits the spot.

restaurant_name: Face To Face Noodle House 面对面 (Bukit Indah, Johor)
review_text:
The shop is quite spacious and clean, providing a comfortable environment for dining. I tried a few dishes and overall, the experience was pleasant with a few highlights and some minor drawbacks.

The traditional Sarawak noodles (dry with chili) stood out for their robust flavor — well-balanced and authentically seasoned. It’s a must-try if you enjoy a bit of heat with your noodles. The curry noodles were also delicious, with a rich and fragrant broth. However, the potatoes in the curry were slightly undercooked, which affected the texture.

The house specialty pan mee was unfortunately too salty for my liking. The ikan bilis (anchovies) topping, which is usually a savoury complement, was overly salty as well, overpowering the dish rather than enhancing it.

Apart from these points, the rest of the meal was satisfying. With some adjustments, especially on the seasoning, this place has great potential to be a regular go-to for comforting local noodles.

review_text:

It's now more appropriately to rename it as small Mac, as everything has shrunk. Burger when first started had good size whopper n quarter pounder, now also become pathetically unsatisfying in serving size.

Woodfire brisket burger.... It's equivalent to the size of 2 x "big" Mac.  Unlike the "big" Mac, which has more bun then meat, here the brisket burger is filled with juicy meat n bacons. It sinful, messy(gloves provided) but simply delightful.   Haven't had a burger this good for very very long.  3 weeks ago I had Dr double prosperity burger from macdonald in jb n it was thrash (2bun,2patty,black pepper sauce,that's it, no other ingredients), and it is literally nothing compared to this delicious brisket burger from woodfire I just had. Well the brisket burger is not cheap as the price is around rm40. But with the generous amount of meat, it's really worth the deal !!!!!

review_text:
Ordered 2 boxes of chicken and specifically requested 2 thighs and 1 drum for each box as they were meant for different households. The staff agreed but mentioned there were no more thighs at that moment, so we waited 20 minutes for the next batch.

After waiting, he packed the chicken into 2 boxes and also upsold me to get the cheese sauce, which I bought (2 cups). But only after I paid, he told me each box would only have 1 thigh instead of 2 as promised, saying it’s because each order can only have 2 thighs in total.

I felt cheated. If that was the case, he should have told us clearly from the start instead of agreeing and letting us wait so long, only to change the story after payment. I also would not know if the chicken given was from the new batch or the older one.

By doing this, it feels like they are discouraging customers from buying more boxes. If there’s a party of 6 to 8 people, only 2 can get the thigh part. If the demand for thighs is high, they should adjust the cost for it and order more thigh parts instead of limiting customers. Really disappointed with the experience.

review_text:
The food here is generally flavorful, with portions that are more suitable for small eaters. Both the seafood fried rice and the Chinese-style fried rice are well-prepared, boasting a distinct wok hei that enhances the overall taste. However, I was a bit disappointed with the kueh teow. The seafood used, particularly the squid and shrimp, had a slight fishy odor, and the texture of the shrimp was a bit mushy.
The chicken served with the noodles and rice was fresh, but the texture was a little tough. Perhaps tenderizing the meat more evenly before cooking could improve its consistency and make it more enjoyable.
On a positive note, the food is prepared quickly, making it a convenient option for a fast meal without the hassle of cooking. Overall, it's a good spot to fill up your stomach quickly, though there’s some room for improvement in the finer details of ingredient preparation.

Sambal Chicken lacked even a hint of spice, it was just some red-coloured gravy. The portion of Chicken and Kailan given was really underwhelming, definitely not enough for more than one person.  The only standout was the steamed fish as it was cooked properly, the meat was soft and blended well with the lemon stew, but the quantity of fish would definitely not satisfy 3-4 people. review_text:
Recommended by a friend when I asked for the best Tomyam in the area. To be honest, the place looked unassuming and my first impression wasn't wow, but that's the case with a lot of Tomyam places, magic happens in the kitchen!

Surprisingly, the menu also came with an English description. Kudos! We ordered Tomyam Sotong which I asked to be extra thick, Padkrawpaw Beef and Kerabu Mangga Betik.
- Tomyam, while it was okay, I expected an extra kick just like in Thailand but sadly it did not surpass my expectation. It wouldn't be something I would order again in the future.
- Padkrawpaw Beef was unexpectedly really delicious. It came with sliced beef, not the usual minced beef and the gravy was thick with a strong aroma of Thai Basil, giving a rich flavor to the dish. It's one of the best Padkrawpaw I've ever tasted.
- Kerabu Mangga Betik transported me to Golok 😂 A mix concoction of sweet, sour, and spicy (on the spicier end tho!). I'm sure the fish sauce is from Thailand bc Msian fish sauce isn't as strong. I liked how they used unripened mango to which it lends the sour taste paired with lime juice. And they used real lime! Not from the bottle. Our mistake was that we requested for spicy.

Would I go here again? Of course, next time I wanna try other dishes e.g. 3 rasa, masak merah and the nasi goreng². For now, this is my #2 Tomyam place in the vicinity of Iskandar Puteri. Highly recommended.

Duck confit major let down. Though comes in two duck legs and nicely flavours, but too too too too dry and stringy.
Iced water not served till asked. And it felt weird when service staffs stand around watching you eat.
author: Thomas Cheah

review_text:
A good place to have peaceful time over a nice lunch near Aeon mall in Bukit Indah. The staff is courteous and friendly with good efficiency. They have set lunch menu on weekdays but also have a good collection of regular dishes which can be explored using the QR code provided.
They do have 50% off regular priced items for members which can be bought for few restaurants at a simple price valid for three years.
We will explore this membership next visit to maximize the time.
Try yourself when you are in the vicinity to appreciate.
author: Ravish M

review_text:
Had a wonderful meal at Marco Polo Restaurant! 🍝✨
The food was absolutely delicious and the service was excellent from start to finish. The environment was warm and comfortable, making it a great place to relax and enjoy a good meal.

I especially loved their risotto and lasagne—both were rich, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. Definitely a place I’d come back to again!

Highly recommended if you’re looking for a nice Italian dining experience. 🇮🇹
author: Grace Wong

review_text:
Greeted by the wonderful Ina & Ruby, we came to celebrate my birthday for the first time there and everything was amazing. From the service, to the menu to the hospitality - we were impressed till the end.

Albeit the slightly warm atmosphere, the toilet was amazingly clean, the place smelled nice and the songs were just nice to complete that italian dining.

Thank you Ina, Ruby & the whole team for not making it a dull experience! Will definitely come and again, and try the other sister companies ❤️
author: Hanie Sofea

review_text: Came for the lunch buffet, many choices at reasonable price, drinks not included. Mushroom soup, mango chicken salad and gelato were our favourites. Staff were professionally dressed but seem cold. Also noted a difference in service between alacarte and buffet orders- with the former receiving better service like hot towels to freshen up, complimentary salsa and chips which were available for order via buffet nacho chips too.
author: vellyne Chua

review_text: had buffet dinner here ...the food is good, reasonable price. The staff are friendly. Recommended for people to held a party here.
author: Ashraf Azman

review_text: Presentation of dishes are awesome! Make the meals feel appetizing. First class services from waiters.  Prices very reasonable.
author: Dominic Koh

review_text: The best nasi goreng ever... Affordable price and the potion is big.. I will repeat to order again
author: Ruhila Razlan

review_text: The place is very comfortable and the food is very good, I will come again later😍😍😍😍
author: Mohd Ardy Hakim

review_text: Went here for buffet Ramadhan 2024. I was very disappointed with the food. Kambing golek can hardly be chewed, mee kari mee sup they only prepare condiments I was expecting at least chicken, no varieties for main meals, if I’m not mistaken there were only 4-5 lauk?? And they topup the food late. Near azan almost everything is empty for mains. For price RM110+ for buffet Ramadhan, it was really not worth it. Definitely will not recommend to anyone.
author: WAWA

review_text:
My friend brought me out to The Spice Kitchen in Bukit Indah in Johor Bahru to try out their Dabba Wala set and wow the place looks fantastic, spacious and modern with a few private rooms but let me tell you the food were simply fabulous.

This place has recently launched their Dabba Wala promo and here you can choose from a host of items, mix and match them and the food will be served in a typical tiffin set. Some of my favorites includes the Chicken 65, Dry Cauliflower Manchurian, Afghani Sheekh Kebab, Punjabi Chicken Tikka, Chicken Butter Masala, Classic Lamb Curry, Keema Matar, Lamb Dum Briyani, Garlic Naan and their Special Kesari.

Parking is also very easy here.
author: Andrew Chan (www.roadtrippers.asia)

review_text: Ate here last November. The RM35++ buffet per pax is honestly worth it. I’m not sure if this option is still available since I saw a review saying it might be removed, but it was there when we went. Portions were generous and every dish we ordered was excellent. The food was flavorful, well balanced, and really enjoyable. We loved everything we had.
author: Yuva

review_text: Tuesday evening, this restaurant offered both Chinese and Indian cuisines, and the overall food was good. The menu prices were on the higher side, but my friend mentioned that members enjoy certain discounts. The service crew did their job.
author: Ong NN

review_text:
It was a very beautiful and enjoyable experience at the restaurant. My family and I truly enjoyed it after the exhaustion of travel ❤️

The staff were very friendly and cooperative, and their service was excellent.

The food was absolutely delicious, the flavors were clear and distinctive, and we enjoyed trying many different dishes.

The prices were very reasonable compared to the quality of the food and service.

We will definitely visit again ✨
author: Yasmin Abdullah

review_text: The foods were delicious and superb. Service on top. Mak lurveeee. Come eat and you will never regret it. The price affordable. The portion is big enough to 2 -3 person. All foods superbbbbbbbbbbbb!!!!!
author: nor ashikin zulkifli

review_text: Malsiya
author: Jabar Sathick

review_text:
Of all the dim sum tried so far in JB, this is one of the best ones.
Its connected to tf mall. Was abit lost initially as came from a different side, though it was inside the mall, but its just at a corner near the mall parking.
Place was packed in the morning around 9am. But got a table easily. Order through a little paper chit, its not like those canto places with a trolley going around.
Food orders came in about 10-15 mins, all fresh and hot.
Siu mai prawn was super good, fresh prawns. Yam was also very good, alot of yam inside.
Only the fried carrotcake was too soft and soggy. Taste was ok.
Will definately come here for dim sum. One of the nicer ones.
author: Kim Guan

review_text:
Sudden craving for dim sum, googled around for a restaurant nearby and this one popped up. Arrived 10+ am and was ushered into the seating area within the "mall" opposite the claw machines.
Here goes:
1. Lor Mai gai - dry, mostly glutinous rice without much meat, flavour so so
2. Prawn chee cheong fun - thick skin not so many prawns
3. Porridge - not wow-able
4. Siew mai - big and thick with meat
5. Char siew bao - big and fluffy skin however fillings can be more
6. 虾圈 - have to be eaten when served else soggy
7. Fried yam cake - nothing special. Tastes like the prepared ingredients you can buy from supermarket.
WIR - there are much better ones to try
author: Edward

review_text: Relatively empty, quiet and peaceful for a late lunch during weekday. Our dim sum were served hot and they came quickly after ordering. Ingredients used were fresh. Would recommend!
author: Qian Ting Young

review_text: Was looking for dim sum near our homestay and chance upon Changman. The prawn fritter, steam pork rib, custard bun and siew mai is really good. the char siew bun skin is abit rough.
author: simin wu

review_text:
Food is nice to eat and effort placed in plating as well. Quite rare for a kopitiam style setting. Porridge is cooked in piping hot stone bowl. Excellent! Most places will just scoop out from a pot n serve you.

Price is value for money , reasonable and most importantly it is opened till late.

Recommended!
author: benson ang

restaurant_name: Restoran Kah Kah Loke @Tmn Nusa Bestari
review_text:
\\A Singaporean Girl Review

Truly local. Hard to find a place that specialises on bitter gourd soup these days. I love how the taste of bitter gourd in the soup.

PRO TIP!
Order their Lala! Every shell comes with MEAT. This is such a generous dish with money well spent!

Love the local spirit.

Will come back with more friends for their fish.
author: Michelle Tan

restaurant_name: Restoran Kah Kah Loke @Tmn Nusa Bestari
review_text: Kah Kah Loke at Nusa Bestari is a great spot for Johor local delicacies. The bittergourd soup is flavourful and comforting, while the deep fried pork is crispy and juicy. Sambal kangkung was also quite nice. Portions are generous.
author: James Low

restaurant_name: Restoran Kah Kah Loke @Tmn Nusa Bestari
review_text: Always very welcoming and warmth to be able to dine in here. 几十年不变好味的家常菜. Love it. When you enter the staff greeted you readily and lotsa smile, take order and 上菜很快. The dishes are al warm and lovely. Not too salty, big portion, eat liao will be full and happy. Not very expensive. Free refill of soup. Great for all ages and gender and group sizes.
author: CK Melody

restaurant_name: Restoran Kah Kah Loke @Tmn Nusa Bestari
review_text: Nice local food. We like the vegetables and pork.
author: J

restaurant_name: Restoran Kah Kah Loke @Tmn Nusa Bestari
review_text: Bittergourd soup broth was great. Didn't taste like msg. Amount was just right. Price was reasonable too. Would love to try other dishes when there's more people together. Love the small detail of giving fresh chopped chilli instead of those soaked ones.👍
author: HOTBLOOD ED

restaurant_name: Starry Sky Marina Hotpot 星空码头豚骨火锅
review_text:
We had a wonderful family dinner at Starry Sky Marina buffet! The soup (especially the broth) was really good — rich and flavourful, and surprisingly, I didn't feel thirsty at all after eating, which is rare for hotpot-style meals.
The handmade balls and the paste (I think they mean fish paste or similar items?) were absolutely delicious — fresh, bouncy, and full of flavour. We kept going back for more!
The best part though? My 4-year-old kept saying "Delicious!" while eating, and right after finishing, he looked up and asked, "Can we come back again?" That says it all — when a picky little one loves it this much, you know it's a winner.
Great value, tasty food, and kid-approved. Highly recommend for families! Will definitely be returning soon. 🌟
author: Tony Too

restaurant_name: Starry Sky Marina Hotpot 星空码头豚骨火锅
review_text: The hotpot broth is very delicious, especially the pork bone soup. The ingredients are fresh, the prices are very reasonable, and the service is excellent. A highly recommended hotpot restaurant to dine at.
author: KS Choy

restaurant_name: Starry Sky Marina Hotpot 星空码头豚骨火锅
review_text: cosy hotpot place with prompt service and a comfortable vibe. The handmade dishes are the highlight — fishball and fish noodle are excellent, and the soup base is rich and satisfying. I like that they offer one-person set meals, which makes it convenient for solo diners. Pricing is reasonable given the quality. Only downside: several handmade dishes were unavailable when I visited, which was a pity as they seem to be the specialty. Still, a solid spot worth returning to.
author: Wei

restaurant_name: Starry Sky Marina Hotpot 星空码头豚骨火锅
review_text: Service crew were friendly and always fast response to serve. The atmosphere was good and the KTV system was good. It s a good place for a group of friends to gather together. Strongly recommend.
author: Chun Yung Bryan Choo

restaurant_name: Starry Sky Marina Hotpot 星空码头豚骨火锅
review_text: This place offers a cozy atmosphere and a great selection of fresh ingredients, including meats, seafood, and vegetables. With diverse broth options and attentive service, it’s a perfect spot for both casual dinners and special occasions. Reasonably priced, it's a must-visit for hotpot lovers!
author: JunNam Ho

restaurant_name: 鼎记牛腩粉 Din Kee Beef Noodle (Bukit Indah Branch)
review_text:
Very delicious beef noodles! The soup is very umami and beef is soft too, i added peanuts and salted vegetables for that additional taste!
Must try, taste so good at 17rm.
Had the dry one with tendons! Go for it!!
author: Cheryl Lee

restaurant_name: 鼎记牛腩粉 Din Kee Beef Noodle (Bukit Indah Branch)
review_text: Very affordable and comforting bowl of beef noodle. Had dry version, very slurpy and balanced with the peanut and picked veg. Soup is extremely beefy. Would love it if the tripe was braised instead of boiled in water, soft nonetheless.
author: Eddie Loh

restaurant_name: 鼎记牛腩粉 Din Kee Beef Noodle (Bukit Indah Branch)
review_text:

author: Kris Tan

restaurant_name: 鼎记牛腩粉 Din Kee Beef Noodle (Bukit Indah Branch)
review_text: Tried the fresh beef this morning and still have stock. Meat tender and portion is good size.
author: Koon Lim Sim

restaurant_name: 鼎记牛腩粉 Din Kee Beef Noodle (Bukit Indah Branch)
review_text: Their beef soup is so flavourful and rich. Coupled with what is probably the best braised beef in the region (ok on par with Taiwanese beef), you get one mouth watering bowl of braised beef noodle that will keep you coming back for more. After about a dozen visits, my favourite has switched from soup to dry. The dry version gets you the black sauce with some peanuts, and a big bowl of soup. The soup version is also very nice but when you compare that with the soup without the noodles, it’s a tad nicer without the noodles. The beef is so tender it melts on your mouth, yet it is amazing that it retains all that flavour when you bite into it. Try to get there well before 2pm cause they do sell out before 3pm sometimes. The version with fresh beef is more expensive but it is worth a try.

review_text:
Not my first visit but never fail to be impressed with the food experience.

Always went for live fish whenever I visit and ensure that it’s either the marble goby or the hybrid grouper.

This visit we went for the goby.

Size was perfect and well steam with Hong Kong style, the liver will always be included in the dish, always the hot target amongst those who love fish.

The iced sweet and sour pork opens the appetite. Cold and crunchy on the outside while warm and tender inside.

The deep fried squid was slightly on the down side, the batter seems insufficiently season making it only good with the mayonnaise.

The lala fried with spring onion is good, size of the clam is big with sizable flesh within. Another hot dish amongst the kids.

For the 辣子鸡, was well cooked however it tasted that they were fried and coated with seasoning powder.

The charcoal tofu was acceptable along with the fried rice.

Overall experience was great like every past visits.

The price is well defended by the quality of food.
author: ethan chew

review_text:
An outstanding dining experience! The restaurant offers a large, beautifully designed space with an elegant atmosphere — perfect for family gatherings or business lunches.

The dim sum is truly superior ! Fresh, flavorful, and skillfully crafted. We love their purple Ubi rice roll, steamed cabbage wrap with fresh prawns in superior broth, and seafood horfun ( full of wok Hei).Their seafood selection is equally impressive!

What made the visit exceptional was the top-notch service. The staff were attentive, polite, and genuinely cared about the dining experience. A special mention to Assistant Manager Jeffrey, who went above and beyond to ensure every detail was perfect.

Highly recommended for anyone looking for an elevated Chinese dining experience with great food and impeccable service. Up to 50% discount offered for dim sum on weekdays and 25% off on weekends! Great deal 😀.

review_text: My first visit here after a friend recommended that the Tim sum taste super good. Truly the Tim sum are freshly made and all ingredients are fresh and plentiful. Even the hor fun was fried with lots of wok heng. On top of this, the service is very good. Jeffery Toh was quick to clear used plate and bowls from the table and very attentive to serve us tea. Very impressed and will surely come back again :)

Special shout-out to Jeffery for his excellent food recommendations and attentive service. He also ensures that all the service crew are well coordinated and that my kids’ needs are well taken care of, which we truly appreciate.

restaurant_name: 好一家海鲜火锅餐厅 Good Family Bukit Indah
review_text:
Had a really enjoyable meal at 好一家海鲜火锅餐厅 Good Family Bukit Indah. Tried both the fish broth and tomato soup base and both were very good, comforting and full of flavour without being overpowering. The ingredients tasted fresh and went perfectly with the soups.

The menu is quite extensive with plenty of choices. I especially liked the noodle made from fish ball, very unique with a nice bite and it paired really well with the broth. The condiments station was well stocked and thoughtfully prepared. Special mention to the fried shallots, very fragrant and added a great boost of flavour to the dipping sauces. Overall a satisfying hotpot experience and I would happily come back again.
author: Ryan

restaurant_name: 好一家海鲜火锅餐厅 Good Family Bukit Indah
review_text: Visited on a Saturday evening and had a lovely time. The meats were fresh and the soups were very flavorful. We loved the meat paste so much that we did a second order.
author: Xinyi Ong

restaurant_name: 好一家海鲜火锅餐厅 Good Family Bukit Indah
review_text:
Came here with my family. The staff were friendly and helpful to guide us on how much food to order based on our appetite.

Chili was their own house blend, has a great kick to it. Pairs wonderfully with the meats offered.

The soup bases were very flavorful and my kids absolutely loved it. The staff were also prompt to top up the soup once the section was low. Best part is they don't top up a standard soup base like other hot pot places, they top up the same soup that's in the pot.

Will definitely return if I'm in the vicinity.
author: Quek Kar Seng

restaurant_name: 好一家海鲜火锅餐厅 Good Family Bukit Indah
review_text:
A Delightful Steamboat Experience
My recent dining experience at Good family proved to be a truly delightful affair. The steamboat offered a fantastic array of fresh and high-quality ingredients. The broth, a rich and flavorful  served as an excellent base for the diverse selection of meats, seafood, vegetables, and noodles.
The service was impeccable. The staff were attentive, friendly, and efficient in ensuring a smooth and enjoyable dining experience. The restaurant itself was clean and inviting, creating a relaxed and pleasant atmosphere.
Overall, this restaurant offers a highly recommended steamboat experience. The combination of fresh ingredients, flavorful broth, and excellent service makes it a standout choice for a satisfying and enjoyable meal.

review_text: Food was really flavourful and tasty. Claypot chicken rice is a must try. The claypot white rice was surprisingly delicious too with the steam chicken. Vegetables were really fresh and delicious too. Definitely will be back to try other food!
author: TSY

review_text: Claypot chicken rice and claypot lao shu fen are acceptable for the price. Food serving was quite fast, and the pricing is considered affordable, especially at Bukit Indah area. However, parking can be difficult to find during weekends, and the restaurant is usually very crowded.
author: James Low

review_text:
710 Barley (Cold, No Sugar) = RM2.30
101 Claypot Chicken Rice (Small) = RM14.50
No Service Charges

This was an Eatery that I passed by Several Times while Exploring Bukit Indah. Although Not Crowded until Full House on a Saturday at 12.00pm Noon, it still seems Quite Popular.  The Place is a Big Kopitiam, Not Air-Conditioned but still feels relatively Airy.  Interestingly has Free WIFI available.

Staffs are Friendly and Welcoming, no issues with Customer Service here.  Ordering is using a Dry-Erase Marker on a Laminated Menu Sheet.  I do like that they will Re-Verify my Order upon receiving it.

If you are watching your Sugar Intake, do take note that their Chinese Tea does have Sugar.  The Only Zero Sugar Drink in this place is their Barley. I appreciate the Staff who let me know about this. Not bad, at least they understand what they are selling here.

I also notice there is a Sign that pre-empted that Peak Hour may take up to 30mins for the Claypot to be Served.  This is Quite Good actually because it means their Claypots are all Made Fresh.  Anyway, it took 3 Mins for the Barley and 17 Mins for my Claypot Rice. Not Bad Timing considering the Elevated Level of Customers when I was there.

101 Claypot Chicken Rice (Small) = RM14.50

Already I'm impressed with how this was served up.  This is the 1st Claypot Rice that I've eaten in JB that provides a Rubber Handle with the Claypot for Customers to be able to Grip Easier.  Such a Simple but Brilliant Solution, this makes it much easier when you Mix the Rice.  Why don't more Claypot Rice Places offer to have such a Rubber Handle Solution?

When this was served up, there was a Nice Delicious Braised Aroma of Claypot Rice wafting from it.  This Claypot is the type where the Zhup is Pre-Lum already for you.  The Dish comes with 6 Bite Sized Pieces of Chicken  that are Mostly Breast Cuts although they're Quite Tender, Not Dry. Nicely Braised and Not Overly Salty.

Amount of Lup Cheong was Acceptable. There were Decent Amount of Pieces of them.  Rice is of course Classic Jasmine Rice.  Amount of Rice given felt Acceptable for the Price. Topping all off is a Piece of Salted Fish on a Small Saucer.

When Everything is Mixed Together, I thought the Overall Taste is Neither Too Sweet or Too Salty.  What I particularly noticed is that compared to other Claypot Rice i've eaten, I thought this one has a More Noticeable Presence of what I would describe as "Earthy Robustness" to it.  Really Not Overly Sweet at all, in fact the Only Sweetness I've tasted comes from the Lup Cheong.

I really like how Earthy Robust this Claypot Rice tasted.  Never Overly Sweet or Overly Salty. Its Very Decent Tasting. If there is a Critique I have, its that I felt they could add More Veggie  because I feel this is quite a Meat-Focused Claypot.  But perhaps this is the Characteristic of Ipoh-Styled Claypots? I wouldn't know as I haven't been to Ipoh yet.

Conclusion and Closing Thoughts

At the Price of RM2.30 (S$0.80) was an Affordable Price for this Cup of Cold Barley.  I liked that it is Homemade, and although Not Super Gao Gao Type, I thought it still tasted Very Decent in Quality, not Overly Dilluted. Worth to Order.

At the Price of RM14.50 (S$4.40) for this Claypot Rice wasn't particularly Cheap or Super Amazing but I thought this was still Decent Enough in Taste.  As I've not been to Ipoh, I have No Idea if this really tastes Authentic though.

Among Claypot Rice I've tasted so far, this was the one that had a Much More Noticeable Robust Earthier Taste  and is Much Less Sweet and Salty compared to others I've eaten.  So if you feel Normal Claypot Rice is too Sweet for you, you might enjoy this one.

If you are craving for some Claypot Rice while you're in Bukit Indah, I can recommend this place to give it a try if you are ok with a Less Sweet, More Robust Earthier Tasting Claypot Rice.

review_text:
Went there for dinner around 7+ near 8pm. Poor experience because they had limited food items left, not enough vegetables, no noodle dishes. Understandable since they said there were a lot of singaporean customers in the day.

However, I find that it’s not ok for them to let us order Luo Han Zhai (Buddha’s delight dish) when they know they cannot make the proper dish. I’ve never seen one like that. It’s just a stir fry mixed veg dish. What is a luo Han Zhai dish without items like black fungus, baby corn, glass noodles, tau kee? I hope they could be more honest about the vegetable choices that they have and not cook randomly to what we ordered.

Herbal monkey head mushroom tasted average. A little plain on the herbal taste. Could do better with some dang gui.

Claypot tofu tasted good, typical to what you’d find everywhere.

Shark fin soup was good. I’d order it again if I ever come back.

They have small and big rice. Small rice is a really small portion so beware to check with them if you order a small rice.

Lastly, we did check with one of the staff regarding the Luo Han Zhai dish that lacks of quality and authenticity. She said she’ll feedback but the people in the kitchen (or perhaps she meant the owner/boss) are hard to speak to, meaning to say her feedback’s won’t really be heard.

I believe their stir fry noodles or rice might be better tasting than the ala carte dishes. But I think overall to do well as a business, one should be honest to customers.

Even with our feedback and obvious disappointment, they didn’t offer to discount the stir fry vege (Luo Han Zhai). I mean it’s for sure not hard to notice our disappointment considering there were only around two or three tables of customers of 2-4pax.

They can do better for sure.
