review_text:
Curry Mee (Small) = RM8.50
1 Otak Otak = RM1.30 per Piece
No Service Charge

Apparently this place is so Famous, some people even proclaim this to be the Best Curry Mee in Taman Perling or even the Whole of JB!

This is a Large Eatery. The Owners are a Friendly but Shy Middle Aged Chinese Couple. There was a Staff grilling some Otak Otak outside the Entrance and it smelt very nice. It took 2 Mins for their Curry Mee to be served up, and 4 Mins for the Otak. Everything was up within 4 Mins.

1 Otak Otak = RM1.30 per Piece

The Otak is not a Big Piece. Appearance looks Dry on the Outside, but the Inner Filling Meat is Juicy Hot. The Fish Paste is not Overpowering and there is a Lingering Taste of Turmeric that permeates the Whole Thing. Has a Slightly Elevated Level of Spiciness but nothing that will bite your Tongue. Acceptable Tasting Otak but nothing really Mind-Blowing tbh.

Curry Mee (Small) = RM8.50

You can either order Noodles or Rice to go with the Curry. I chose Noodles for my Carb. The Type of Gravy they serve for this is Chinese-Styled Chicken Curry. Super Thick Gao Gao Gritty Type and Not Overly Spicy.

This is the First Curry Mee in JB that I've encountered that uses this type of Curry Gravy because most others are just Variations of Laksa. Really taste like Grandma's Chicken Curry. So Thick, Rich and Creamy with a Nice Power Saltiness to it that never overstays its Welcome.

Even for the Small that I ordered, there are 4 Big Solid Pieces of Chicken Meats of Various Bone-In Thick Cuts. Big and Meaty, Breast Meat was Not Dry and Nice to Chew. Thigh and Drummy were Soft and Tender. Amount of Meat is Very Acceptable for the Price. 口口有肉. 😋 And they soaked up that Beautiful Curry so well.

There is also Half a Potato and its Creamy Melt in Mouth Smooth. 1 Big Taupok cut into 2 Pieces they work well like a Sponge to Soak up all that Curry. Yellow Noodles are used and while they're most likely from a Package, not Homemade, the Amount of Noodles felt Generous and Filling for the Price.

The Soul of the Dish is definitely their Beautiful Curry. That said, because this Curry is the Super Thick Gao Gao type, ordering Rice would probably pair better with it. Both Rice and Noodles pair Well with this Curry. Its just what type of Carbs you prefer only.

Conclusion and Closing Thoughts

At RM1.30 (S$0.40) for 1 Otak Otak, this was a Reasonable Price to pay for what it is. Its Decent and Acceptable as an Otak but I thought it was Nothing Really Special. Eating this with Curry was alright, it didn't improve or worsen the taste. If you feel like adding it as a Side Dish, sure why not.

At RM8.50 (S$2.60) for the Curry Mee, this was Absolutely Worth the Money for sure! The Quality of Curry is exactly the type that I loved most. So Thick, Gao Gao and Creamy. THIS is how I imagined Malaysia Curry Mee to actually taste like when I first heard of it, instead of the Mostly Laksa Variation around.

Most Surprised with how Generous they are with Chicken Pieces even for the Small that I ordered. They were Big, Fat, Meaty and Juicy and paired perfectly with the Curry.

Everything else also worked Very Well and Nothing Clashed. This was a Very Satisfying and Filling Meal. I was so happy with the Meal, I even went up to the Owners and gave them a Thumbs Up. They appreciated the Gesture.

Ultimately is this the Best Curry Mee in all of Taman Perling or even the Whole of JB?

I haven't eaten enough Curry Mee in JB so I can't really say, but this one sure comes VERY CLOSE! If you enjoy Chinese-Styled of Thick Thick Gao Gao Chicken Curry cooked like Grandma's Style you will definitely enjoy this one. Both Noodles and Rice work, but I'll have to lean closer to Rice for this one because of how Thick this Curry was.

review_text:
聯姐粿條仔 Kway Teow Kia (1 Person Mixed, No Pig Skin) = RM11.00 (S$3.50)

This Kway Teow Kia Stall is located within 金嶺美食阁 Kim Ling Food Court Kopitiam. It is the Largest Stall.

The Owner 聯姐 is a Very Friendly and Jolly Elder Lady who was quietly cleaning some Vegetables and Processing some Ingredients at a Side-Table when I arrived. Really Welcoming and Friendly, she totally gives off a Very Motherly Vibe.

This is the 1st JB Kway Teow Kia that actually understands me when I say: "Hello, 我一个人吃的, 全部料都参参, 不要猪皮, 给我一碗 Kway. 我在这里吃. 谢谢"

I don't know why but EVERY other KTK stall in JB will look at me blankly, don't understand, completely blur, don't know what to do and 1 even want to argue and fight with me say I cannot finish it lah.

In this Stall however, there is No Blur Blur, No Confusion, No Resistant like other KTK Stalls in JB. 聯姐 immediately understood what I want perfectly.

That said, I don't think they gave me 100% of all the Available Innards or Meats that they have, but I have no issues with it. Hahaha I'm already grateful that she is so nice. Thank God.

How does the Actual Kway Teow Kia Taste?

The Chilli Condiment they serve with this has an Elevated Saltiness and Some Vinegary Sourness with a Mild Spiciness that won't bite your Tongue and also Doesn't Linger Long. Definitely tastes like they mixed it themselves. Not Bad Chilli for Kway Teow Kia.

The KTK Soup Broth has a Delightful Herbly and 清甜 Sweetish Taste. But one thing is they don't give alot of this Broth. In fact as the Meal went on, I thought the Kway Teow sucked up alot of the Broth and it dried up quickly in the end. This was Very Unusual and is the 1st Time I'm seeing Soup Broth being sucked up like this.

The Thin Kway Teow itself felt Slightly Thicker than Usual. It had a Noticeably Chewy and Niam Niam Bite Texture especially when it got soaked up with all that Soup Broth. Amount given is not alot. This was a Very Small Bowl of Kway Teow.

The Braised Sauce that they lum all over the Meats and Organ Pieces surprisingly reminds me of the type of Dark Sauce that you would normally find in Wanton Mee. It is Slightly Thick in Consistency and has almost the Same Sweetish Taste Profile.

Pork Meats are cut into Small Pieces and they have a Robust Meaty Chew with No Pigginess. Intestines were Tender and Chewy. There is a Slightly Elevated Level of Pigginess but not too much.

2 pieces of Tofu they served with this has unique little holes within that served to help soak up all that Braised Sauce. I liked that they immediately deflate in your mouth and expelled the Sauce all over. There is also 1 Whole Egg is given. 🥚 Its a Small One and is cut into Quarters. Standard Tasting for a Braised Egg.

At RM11.00 (S$3.50) for this Solo Diner Platter I ordered was affordable for what it was. Having said that, I feel the Portion of Kway Teow given wasn't alot. So if you are a Bigger Eater and want to eat more Carbs, you might want to order more.

I also thought the Amount of Soup Broth felt Lesser compared to other KTK that I've visited. I couldn't drink the Soup at the End of the Meal because of how little there was. I suppose you can ask for more Broth, so if you want you can just ask them. I'm sure they'll top up more for you.

If I were to give my Honest Opinion of this KTK, I'd say its Decent and Above Average, but not Super Mind-Blowing. If I were to score this normally, I would give 4 Stars to this. I can recommend to give this a try because it is Decent Tasting and Affordable for what it is.

I am however giving this my My Highest Top Score 5 Stars simply because this is the 1st JB Kway Teow Kia that actually understood me without Confusion or any sort of Resistance. You have no idea how happy that made me feel when I ate here. 聯姐 Herself is such a Nice Friendly Lady!

review_text:
There are 2 Stalls that I visited in this Kopitiam.
----------------------
聯姐粿條仔 Kway Teow Kia (1 Person Mixed, No Pig Skin) = RM11.00 (S$3.50)

I love this Stall as it is the 1st Kway Teow Kia in JB that actually understood how I order KTK without any Blur Blur Confusion. You can read my review for it in its own Google Maps Entry called "聯姐果條子". 聯姐 herself is a Very Friendly Lady!

----------------------
Nameless Penang CKT Stall (Small, Spicy, Add Hum) = RM8.00 (S$2.50)

This Penang CKT Stall is quite discussed in Google Reviews about this place. Alot of Google Reviewers enjoyed this alot, although there are also some Detractors too.

This Stall does have a Name but for some reason, their Signboard was blocked behind a Pillar and I couldn't make out what it wrote. I think its called "亚春"?

Run by what looks like a Mother and Son Team, the Young Chap is a Friendly Fellow. When you order this, they will give you a Metal Tag. It took about 2 Mins for my CKT to be served up.

When it was first served up, I was immediately impressed with the Amount of Kway Teow that was given even for their Small. There is a Slight Amount of Wok Hei though not alot. The Kway Teow does clump together and I didn't mind as I thought it gave it a Fuller Bite. Even when I ordered Spicy, It was Not Spicy at all, not even a little bit.

I like that some pieces of Eggs are in Bigger Pieces for a Nicer Bite Texture. For this Price you also get 5 Small Hums and 1 Big Juicy Bouncy Fat Prawn. The Hums here aren't Big Sized but thats ok because the Hums given in even the Michelin-Rated Siam Road CKT in Penang itself were Smaller Sized than the ones here. I liked that the Amount of Taugeh is Generous and gives alot of Satisfying Veggie Crunch in the Dish.

Overall Taste is on the Lighter Side. This reminds me of Jin Kor CKT which I had in Penang, except that the Portion here is More Generous. Having eaten 3 Different CKT in Penang itself:

Jin Kor Char Kuey Teow 仁哥炒粿条
Siam Road Charcoal Char Koay Teow
Tiger Char Koay Teow 老虎炒果條

Actually I feel all of them 来来去去 are pretty similar. Till today, other than Penang CKT is fried lighter and Less 重口味 than Singapore's Black Black Version of CKT, I don't know what other differences there are.

Is this a Good Penang CKT? I suppose so? Honestly I don't feel its any different from the 3 CKTs I've eaten in Penang itself. Maybe I'm just not a CKT Connoiseur. If you aren't fussy and is looking for a Affordable Decent Tasting CKT, I can recommend this one to give it a try.

review_text: An elderly man in a white shirt with Thai tattoos on his back was selling durians. We thought we'd support him and decided to buy one. We wanted to try the bitter variety, but he boasted that he knew how to choose durians. So we chose that one. After he opened it and we took a bite, we told him, "Uncle, please try one. It's not bitter, it's very sweet." He immediately retorted, "Bitter is bitter! I don't eat durian." (How can someone who doesn't eat durian know whether it's sweet or bitter?) Then he said, "The one I just picked up was bitter. You're being sarcastic!" (We realized we'd been tricked.) We said we didn't want it anymore, but the man blocked our car and started acting like a thug, forcing us to return the durian he claimed was bitter! (I advise everyone to check the bottom of the durian when buying it from this uncle, and to lift up the stem that he's deliberately covering with leaves. There's something fishy going on. Don't believe him when he says the durian just cracked at the bottom and he's using a rubber band to tie it back together. Also, make sure the stem is brown and the whole durian has been exposed to direct sunlight.)

review_text:
Hua Zai Roast Duck: A Generous & Delicious Lunch Spot!
My lunch at Hua Zai Roast Duck eatery was a thoroughly decent and satisfying experience! We ordered a half roast duck for RM45, and the portion was incredibly generous – easily enough for four people to share. The duck itself was perfectly cooked, boasting crispy skin with wonderfully tender and juicy meat. The accompanying sauce was fantastic, complementing the duck beautifully with a subtle yet distinct herbal aroma.
What's great about Hua Zai is their huge variety beyond just duck. You can also find roast chicken, roast pork, and BBQ pork. Their menu offers flexibility with your carbs, allowing you to choose between white rice, oil rice, or plain noodles. Plus, there's a good selection of side dishes, including steamed fish, fried fish, and stir-fried vegetables, making it easy to build a complete meal.
Whether you're looking for a quick lunch for one or a full family lunch or dinner, Hua Zai Roast Duck is a great choice with something for everyone.

I visited Angsana Mall KFC at 8:30 PM, a good two hours before their stated closing time of 10 PM, but the experience was highly unsatisfactory from start to finish.

Upon arriving, we attempted to use the self-ordering kiosk, only to be stopped by a staff member who directed us to order at the counter instead. Odd, but we complied. At the counter, before I could even begin my order, the lady rudely informed me, "Only fried chicken and Zinger burgers are available." While it’s understandable that certain menu items might run out close to closing time, this was two full hours before closing.

We ordered a snack box, a Zinger box, and two sides—loaded cheesy fries and cheesy wedges. Things took a turn for the worse when our order was delayed because the staff had misplaced it. They called me back to the counter to retrieve my receipt because they weren’t sure what to prepare. This was unprofessional and frustrating but still not the worst part of the experience.

When we finally received our food and sat down, we noticed that the loaded cheesy fries were incomplete, missing the chicken bits that were shown in the display. Politely, I approached the counter to clarify if the kitchen had made an error. A staff member simply stared at the fries before saying, "We don’t have those here." I began explaining that the bits were part of the menu item as displayed, but before I could finish, the lady who had taken my order interrupted loudly, saying, "That’s in Singapore. We don’t have that here."

Her tone and volume were unnecessarily rude and humiliating, especially in front of other customers. All I had done was politely ask a question, and her response felt like a personal attack, even bringing up my nationality. Embarrassed but calm, I returned to my seat, only to hear her mocking me to her colleague, referring to me as a "demanding Singaporean." When I confronted her, she denied it but offered no explanation or apology.

I tried explaining how her behavior was unprofessional and hurtful, but she turned her back on me mid-conversation and walked off without a word. Another staff member apologized on her behalf, but the damage had already been done.

This experience was disappointing, unprofessional, and outright disrespectful. Misplacing an order, failing to deliver complete meals, and humiliating customers in public is unacceptable. KFC, you need to improve your staff’s training and professionalism.

To the management: if your staff are unhappy working, they shouldn’t take it out on customers.

KFC, do better.

restaurant_name: Kedai Bak Kut Teh Hin Hock
review_text:
The BKT here is definitely for those who love a heavy medicinal profile. For me, the herb flavor was a bit too intense and overpowered the natural sweetness of the pork. If you prefer a lighter or more peppery broth, this might not be your personal cup of tea, but herbal purists might appreciate the depth.

The Standouts (The Real Reason to Visit)
The Steamed Fish: This was excellent. You can tell the fish was incredibly fresh, steamed to a perfect, delicate texture. It’s easily above average compared to most BKT joints and worth the visit alone.

Yam Rice: This was exceptional. Every grain was fluffy and packed with the savory aroma of yam and dried shrimp. It’s rare to find yam rice this well-executed.

Vegetables: We ordered the greens with garlic and bean sauce. They were well-prepared, retaining a nice crunch without being oily, and the sauce had the perfect balance of savory and pungent notes.

While the herbal intensity of the soup wasn't to my personal liking, the quality of the other dishes was undeniable. I’d return in a heartbeat just for the steamed fish and that incredible yam rice.

The you tiao was great for dipping and the minced meat tofu was soft with a tasty sauce that made us wish for rice. Great food, though the place gets very hot.

review_text:
Din Seafood & Yong Tau Fu, located in Kampung Pasir, Johor Bahru, offers a delightful culinary experience for those seeking authentic Malaysian flavors. The restaurant boasts a wide variety of Yong Tau Fu selections, each freshly prepared to cater to diverse palates. Guests can choose from an array of stuffed vegetables, tofu, and other delicacies, all filled with flavorful fish paste. The freshness and quality of the ingredients are evident in every bite, making it a haven for Yong Tau Fu enthusiasts.

Beyond the Yong Tau Fu, Din Seafood presents an impressive seafood menu. Diners can indulge in dishes like succulent prawns, tender squid, and a variety of fish, all cooked to perfection with traditional Malaysian spices and herbs. The harmonious blend of flavors ensures a memorable dining experience.

The ambiance of the restaurant is warm and inviting, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Johor Bahru. The staff is attentive and friendly, ensuring that guests feel welcomed and well-cared for throughout their visit. Whether you’re a local or a tourist, the genuine hospitality adds to the overall charm of the place.

For those seeking a culinary adventure that combines traditional flavors with fresh ingredients, Din Seafood & Yong Tau Fu is a must-visit destination in Johor Bahru. The combination of delectable dishes, a cozy atmosphere, and excellent service makes it a standout choice for anyone looking to savor authentic Malaysian cuisine.

review_text:
Jot Kiutchen Danga Bay serves one of the absolute best shellouts I’ve ever tried in JB! From the moment your platter arrives, the aromas of freshly cooked seafood and savory, slightly spicy sauce hit you, instantly making your mouth water. The presentation is impressive — a colorful, overflowing mix of prawns, squid, mussels, clams, and corn, all glistening in their signature sauce.

The first bite is unforgettable: succulent, juicy prawns explode with flavor, tender squid melts in your mouth, and mussels and clams soak up the sauce perfectly, giving each bite a burst of savory, slightly sweet, and mildly spicy goodness. The textures are incredible — chewy yet tender seafood, crunchy corn, and perfectly balanced sauce that clings to every piece.

Portions are generous and filling, making it a perfect choice for gatherings with friends or family. The interactive nature of shellout dining — picking, dipping, and sharing — makes the meal fun, lively, and satisfying. Every bite is indulgent, and the bold flavors linger long after you finish.

If you’re craving fresh, flavorful, and perfectly cooked seafood in JB, Jot Kiutchen Danga Bay is a must-visit. One serving, and you’ll understand why it’s so highly recommended — you’ll be planning your next visit before you even finish the first bite!

We chose the Original Signature sauce and added a side dish of Siakap 3 Rasa (sea bass cooked in three flavours: sweet, sour and spicy). It turned out to be fantastic choice, as the meal was incredibly delicious.

Jot Kitchen also offered a variety of other dishes on their menu, making it a great dining spot with plenty of options.

review_text:
Last week, my colleagues and I had dinner at Kapten Steamboat to bid farewell to one of our staff members. The location was convenient, with plenty of parking available, making it easy for us to find a spot. The environment inside was pleasant, with music playing and air conditioning to keep it comfortable.

The menu offered unlimited refills, which was great, but the steamboat selection was quite limited and lacked variety. On the other hand, the grill options were much better, with a wide range of choices like fish, lamb, chicken, clams, prawns, and more. I also tried their signature dish, the honey lamb. Unfortunately, I found it too sweet, and the stickiness lingered in my throat, which made it less enjoyable. The tom yum soup was okay, but nothing extraordinary.

The biggest downside was the ventilation system—it wasn’t functioning properly. The place was overly smoky, which made it uncomfortable to stay for long, especially while grilling food.

Overall, Kapten Steamboat has its good points, like the parking, ambiance, and grilling options, but they really need to improve their ventilation and steamboat variety. Without these improvements, it’s hard to fully enjoy the dining experience.

No mention whatsoever. Ended up ordering a cake above rm8.80.

Fine, so I agreed, and asked for an RM 8.80 cake and iced lemon tea. Guess what the store manager says? "Oh, we've already given you a gift voucher, so that's the promo. So the promo is either a voucher OR the complimentary cake/drink."

WHAT?! Where in this reputable establishment was it stated that a promo of SR's choosing can easily replace any promo that they so vividly display on the customer's dining table?

Absolutely poor customer service. Here it is, in point form:

1. Slow, nonchalant and indifferent attitude.
2. When we complained about the misinformation, the store manager just turned his/her eyes elsewhere.

Don't try anything kuey teow here. The noodles were tangy (kenyal), they'd be mistaken as rubber noodles.
author: David Leong

restaurant_name: Yummy Nasi Lemak House Johor Bahru
review_text: The food is reasonably priced and tasty. I tried the nasi lemak with ayam goreng berempah — the chicken was juicy and smooth, really enjoyable.
author: Foo chang kiat

restaurant_name: Yummy Nasi Lemak House Johor Bahru
review_text: Saturday lunch in JB's Yummy Nasi Lemak House was delicious. We ordered nasi lemak mutton rendang (M$16) and mee goreng ayam (M$13).  Mutton was cooked just right without the gamey flavour that is usually associated with mutton.  The fried chicken was tasty, crispy outside and tender inside.  The nasi rice had the right balance of herbs. The restaurant makes its own kueh on a daily basis.  We ordered a pack of 3 kueh dadar and a pack of 4 keuh lapis, each pack was M$5, a steal considering Bengawan Solo sells a single piece at S$1.50.  The kueh dadar's crepe was thin with fresh coconut, just the way we used to eat in the old days.  I had a lot of fun peeling the kueh lapis layer by layer too!  Overall, a truly yummy and sumptuous lunch!
author: Veronica Hui Neo Tan

restaurant_name: Yummy Nasi Lemak House Johor Bahru
review_text: Solid breakfast or brunch spot that serve nasi lemak and noodles.  Kueh are marvelous too over here. Rice is not overly frangant but kept it's act together. Herb fried chicken is tender and juicy. Rendang is full of favours but just a little hard for my liking. Kueh are not overly sweet just the right amount. Coffee is ok. Chilli is a little sweet type but good enough.
author: Mark Ong

restaurant_name: Yummy Nasi Lemak House Johor Bahru
review_text:
Very nice and delicious nasi lemak with relatives for breakfast during outing.
Friendly and courteous  staff.
Efficient service.
Thank you!

restaurant_name: Yummy Nasi Lemak House Johor Bahru
review_text: Good Food, cozy place. Nasi Lemak is nice, Curry Chicken is average. Price is standard
author: Jong

review_text:
MB Cafe is located inside KPJ Hospital. The food taste is normal but good enough to fill your hunger. They have bread, muffins, coffee, chocolate drinks and hot milk etc…

Nothing fancy, but it does the job when you just need a quick bite or a warm drink.

review_text: friendly staffs! i ask a security at hospital, where is the nearest canteen and he showed us the direction. nice lontong for my Indonesian taste. they also sell nasi and lauk (ayam rendang, ikan goreng, tempe sambal, and more). would come here again.
author: WINDY

review_text: Cafe in the hospital. Reasonable price. The yellow curry chicken and the asam curry stingray were tasty. Open for breakfast, lunch and dinner. Close at 8pm. Staff are unfriendly.
author: Chee Chin Cheng

review_text:
This place isn't closed, it's OPEN and doing business VERY WELL.
Though it may be in a private hospital , its offerings are more inclined to the elderly and the unwell - hence you will find more healthy and low-carbs foods here. Of course they also serve those sinfully tasty and cholesterol-binding stuff like nasi lemak, chicken porridge and oily pastries.
Staff attitude are good, your orders are delivered to your table and turnover is extremely fast. While there are two more eateries within this hospital, Mb Cafe is the most affordable(the rest are pocket-draining expensive!!), with a good ambience and pleasant food smells greet you when you go through its doors. I am NOT telling you to go there to est, but if you chanced on visiting someone in this hospital and need a little food, pick MB Cafe. It is better than the rest.
author: Jackie
loi kok Sang loi kok sang

review_text: There are 2 Marrybrown's cafes in Johor Specialist ! This is the latest cafe and it is located beside the main entrance. A cozy corner to have a leisure coffee/tea time. More jb's makan vlog on youtube>>dailyvlog@willywilly
author: Willy Willy

review_text:
Not many people choose to dine in here; most customers prefer to take their food to go. The place gives off a simple, no-frills vibe — more of a spot to grab a quick meal than to sit down for a long time. The quality of the food is actually not bad; it’s consistent and decent enough. They don’t seem to be focused on creating trending or best-selling menu items, but rather on just providing meals that are filling and reliable.

One good thing about this place is its location — it’s right next to the specialist private hospital and conveniently situated along the main road, making it easy to find and stop by. While it may not be the kind of restaurant you visit to be impressed by unique dishes or fancy presentation, it’s a practical option if you just want a straightforward meal, especially if you’re in the area for hospital visits or passing through the main road.
author: Amar Naqiu

review_text: Overall, the food was nice !  especially the kampung selection and the goreng-goreng dishes. The drinks were good too. I ordered fresh orange and iced tea, both were really nice. RECOMMENDED!!

review_text: Nice atmosphere and delicious food, the staffs are friendly too 👍🏻👍🏻

No more fishballs given as before. Bt if U're searching for tis type of dishes.. U cn try it.. As d taste is still acceptable .

author: Mohd Firas

review_text: My hubby and I really enjoyed our dining experience here. The ambience is simple yet so calming in the middle of the streets. We really enjoyed their food and drinks especially the roti jala and curry puff. Came in the afternoon so kuih was limited, will go earlier next time to try more. Price is very reasonable too.
author: Bea G.

review_text: Quite a good place with lots of seating. Prata is ok. Nasi lemak is rm4, egg with ikan bills. Cheap and rice is fragrant. Overall 6 pratas and 2 nasi only rm29. Very affordable. Curry and chilli sauce also not bad. Can visit if around the area but not a must in my opinion. Opens as warly as 7.30am without queue.
author: Loo Zheng Rong

review_text:
We came here for breakfast today after dropping off our son at playschool this morning. It’s been awhile since I came here but it was my wifes first time.

We ordered 2 teh tarik, 2 roti kosong for my wife and 1 lontong basah for myself. You have to order/pay your food at the cashier and wait for your food with the exception of roti/drinks which you’ll have to go to another counter with your receipt to self collect.

Thoughout the years, the ambience has become much nicer and it was getting more crowded by 9am. So do come here earlier.

The roti is one the of the best if you are ever in JB. But the lontong was so so as the “soup” could have been thicker and more flavourful.

Well, parking is an issue cos you’d have to park by the roadside beside someones house.

Other than that, I’d recommend this establishment for your morning breakfast if you like malay local food.
author: Adrian Tan

review_text:
We came to Onn Kitchen JB for breakfast and was really impressed with the food and kampung-style ambience. The roti canai/prata is crispy outside, soft and chewy inside, and easily one of the better ones I’ve had in JB, especially with their dhal and sambal. Their (pre-packed) nasi lemak is very flavorful, with rich sambal and generous portions that make it very value-for-money.

The menu is quite extensive, so there’s something for everyone. Service is fast and efficient and the self-service system (order and pay at the counter, then collect your food) keeps things moving smoothly.

We also love that the atmosphere here is casual and breezy, so we were happy to linger and chat for some time even after finishing our breakfast. Roadside parking around the shop was convenient too, which made the whole visit feel easy and relaxed.

The place has a relaxed, village-like atmosphere with outdoor seating under a big tree. Overall, highly recommended for a hearty, authentic Malaysian meal in JB.
author: Hock Lye, Khaleel, CHAN

review_text:
Nice restaurant serving great variety of local delights. Nasi Lemak, Nasi dagang, Nasi goreng, roti canai with unlimited curry supply 😋

The crew were friendly and efficient. Clean and clear tables in seconds for new arrival customers.
author: Lennox Cheok

restaurant_name: Murtabak Singapura Sungai Chat Kolam Air
review_text: One of the best place to get murtabak singapura in JB. Friendly service but just need to wait a bit if there are many orders. Just request for their ais sirap limau and you'll be fine.

restaurant_name: Murtabak Singapura Sungai Chat Kolam Air
review_text: Love the murtabak! It’s better to eat it there compared to take away. The texture is better that way I think. Not so many parking spaces so you might need to park at roadside. Drink was kinda sweet so ask for less sweet if you don’t like sweet much. Price is good. Recommended 👍🏽

Went there in the afternoon and there was barely any people. overall would come again if the parking was better.

restaurant_name: Murtabak Singapura Sungai Chat Kolam Air

I'm not so fans of murtabak. But this place makes me want to eat murtabak. It's so delicious and i really like their 'kuah dal'. Simple and delicious.

I wanna try cheese murtabak, but at that time they already sold out 😔. But it's okay, next time will visit again.

review_text: A simple, small indian restaurant located along a busy main road. Parking is almost non-existent as it is in a neighborhood area with a narrow road. Food was good, as were the drinks. Service was also, adequate - quick and pleasant. The restaurant is not air-conditioned, so it may be a bit hot for those who aren't used to regular fans to keep cool. This is my second time here. Overall quite pleased with the quality of the food and the service here. Will visit again.

review_text:
If you want to know the actual authentic taste of Korean food,  then this restaurant is one of the choices you should consider. The ambience mood is nice there. I visit with my friend past the lunch hour, the place is not crowded.
The price might be a bit difficult to accept.

But, the food tastes delicious and it comes with a lot of side dishes. Love the side dishes a lot (see the picture). Plus you can refill it! To me, it is worth the money I spend.

Probably will give another visit in coming few months.😊

review_text:
I took lunch with my wife here. When seeing various side dishes, we surprised and speechless. After tasting I surprised more at their taste each. They were very delicious and made me happy.
After eating I ask a elderly staff where the side dishe foods were supplied. Then I surprised at her answers that she has made all the foods by herself for last 35 years here. She is a Korean originated. I vowed her with my respect. I am happy finding this kind of restaurant here in Malaysia.
Definitely, I will come back with my valuable friends.
author: johney “OHO”

review_text:
Want to eat an authentic Korean meal? Look no further than Korea House Restaurant - the owner is a Korean & she cooks the dishes too! The dishes are as authentic as it can be, and the ingredients are quite fresh.

The banchan dishes are on rotation, and everytime we come here, they would serve a different side dish - though some such as the fried anchovies and seaweed are a staple.

Prices are a bit on the high side, but the dishes and flavour is authentic - it has not been “Malaysianised” in any way. The decor is also beautiful, and you would feel like being in Korea. 안녕하세요!

I have been coming to Korea House since they were in operation at Jalan Noja. I highly recommend you to come and try this restaurant.
author: Iskandar Rahmat

restaurant_name: WW Laksa House 水塘。辣沙
review_text: Lovely food, this is the way Laksa should taste! Well staffed, the team knew what they were doing  and service was fast. But would implore them to upgrade the venue, spruce it up and ensure the floor is regularly swept up of used napkins and other rubbish.
author: Jeffrey H

restaurant_name: WW Laksa House 水塘。辣沙
review_text: Worth trying. Laksa more on the salty side like Japanese ramen. Price is more expensive than usual Laksa, big bowl portion with cockles is not very big actually in terms of noodle and soup base, nonetheless cockles are very fresh! Apparently traditional recipe since 1978!
author: Jer Jian Siow

restaurant_name: WW Laksa House 水塘。辣沙
review_text:
✨ Foodie Diary: The Legendary Laksa & Curry Noodle! 🍜

If you’re a fan of rich, spicy flavors — this bowl of laksa curry noodle with cockles is pure heaven! The broth is thick, fragrant, and packed with that perfect coconut-creamy curry aroma that instantly makes you crave more. The cockles are fresh and juicy, giving every bite a nice briny kick that balances beautifully with the noodles and spice.

It’s one of those dishes that carries a long history and traditional flavor, yet still feels comforting every time you eat it. Honestly, I love it so much — it’s one of those bowls that remind you why you fell in love with Malaysian food in the first place. 💛 Highly recommended for anyone who loves authentic taste and a bit of spicy warmth! 🔥
author: SURASAK “Bill” ABE

restaurant_name: WW Laksa House 水塘。辣沙
review_text:
There are many different versions of Laksa, and this is one of the versions that a lot of other type of laksa should look up to.
The business and operation model for this place is very good, they only sell a limited number of foods, noodle soups, laksa, otak, and home cook drinks, and with each of them, they do it very well.
You would notice that every when the place is very busy, there is only one to two service staff that give out instructions.  The girl at the front counter manages it very well.  The place does get very busy at times.
Everything is good here, the standout food is the fresh clams (serve with laksa), the sambal sauce, and of cause, the otak.
I sincerely hope that there are more of this type of eating houses around.  But unfortunately, they are like hens' teeth, rarely that you can find one.

restaurant_name: WW Laksa House 水塘。辣沙
review_text:

Otak2 is moist and the flavours are balanced with no fishy taste nor overpowering santan taste.

Portion wise is small but just nice. Very very unique laksa johor, quite delicious. they have homemade Kuih as well. It was delicious as well. Highly recommended.
author: Lily G

review_text:
I have been craving for laksa Johor for a long time. After researching, I learnt from various reviews that Bumbu Asli serves one of the best laksa Johor in Johor Bahru. When I visited, I ordered the laksa Johor and the laksam. Both dishes were great but my preference was the laksam - the herbs and spices of the dishes came together very well.

Next time I come, I would like to try the Penang laksa and also the nasi lemak. The rice that was displayed at the self-service area looked so good. Actually, I wanted to have some when I visited but I was too full already and could not have eaten anymore.
author: Luke out

review_text: I just loved all the foods here. Home cook feels. They have laksa and laksam. In the morning u can choose to buy a kueh too for breakfast. They selling a tid bits and traditional snacks too. Just the parking is so limited same as the table to dine in. If the table full, just do the take away.
author: Nora Nfs

review_text: Laksa Johor is the best. This is the place I would visit if I am craving for Laksa Johor. Besides that, this restaurant also offered other food such as Soto, Mee Rebus, Nasi Lemak, etc. On top of that, traditional delicacies such as kuih were also sold during breakfast. Price were on the lower side, as it is very cheap and affordable. This place sometimes get packed with locals and tourists during peak hour.
author: Kenny Ganie

review_text: Nasi Lemak lasted until the evening. From JB to Klang, just stay in our car.
author: Shahrir Aie

review_text: Want nasi lemak..find it here..it's delicious..
author: Nuaim Adenar

review_text:
To the Owner: Feedback from a Loyal Regular Customer

I’ve been coming to Petals & Bakes for about a year now — almost every Saturday. It’s one of my favourite spots for breakfast, desserts, and a peaceful ambience. The food is consistently good, and most of the staff have always been kind, friendly, and respectful. I really enjoy being here regularly; it has become part of my weekend routine.

However, I recently had an unpleasant experience during an evening visit. I was outside the café on a business call around 4:30 p.m., planning to wrap up before closing at 6 p.m. One of the female staff members came out and told me they would close at 5:30 p.m., which I completely understood. But less than 10 minutes later, she came out again and raised her voice to remind me about closing. It felt unnecessary and quite disrespectful, especially since I was clearly in a work call and had already acknowledged her the first time. I truly believe in giving feedback because I really like this place. I hope the management can train the staff better in handling communication with regular customers, especially when tone and approach matter.

That said, I want to thank the other staff member who came and apologized afterward — that gesture meant a lot and reflected the warmth I’ve always associated with Petals & Bakes. I’ll still be coming here because I genuinely love the place, but I hope this feedback reaches the owner and helps make things even better.
author: Jaysrini Moorthy (Jay)

review_text: The restaurant has a pleasant atmosphere with soft lighting and a relaxing beige color theme, making it a great place to dine in. It's definitely worth a visit! I absolutely loved the brownie—the rich chocolate aroma and the creamy chocolate topping were delightful.
author: Kiew Hui Yee

review_text:
The food was really delicious! 😋

Pleasant experience with friendly staff. Didn't get to try the bakes cause we were too full but it looks really good! Would definitely come again to try them☺️
author: Yan

review_text: Food was good. Service was a bit slow, probably because we came when it just opened. The overall environment was nice, with cozy interior.
author: Hajar Alwi

review_text: Always my to go place for brunch. Love the ambience, easy parking, cosy place, clean and the food was good too. Price quite reasonable with the service. Food portion is okay. (some menu quite big portion for me haha)
author: Kristal Ais

review_text: Great seafood overall. The Sambal Udang was the standout — fresh, juicy prawns with a rich, spicy sambal. Tom Yum Gong was fragrant and nicely sour with generous prawns. The siput were well-cooked and tasty with sambal. Solid spot for bold, spicy seafood.
author: Hiezam Hasan

review_text: Nice restaurant. The food are exceptionally delicious, their staff are friendly and helpful. The ambiance is also nice. However, the price is quite pricey but it's totally worth it for the food they served. Suitable for family gathering.
author: arif isa

review_text: Went here for dinner with wife and sister in-law family. So far the food is good, their salted egg prawn was amazing. Their ikan bakar and 3 rasa were okay. Crab i think not very fresh (for my order), Tomyam was generous, got lots of seafood inside (but i think i didnt found any squid). The place are crowded after 8pm, so you better come early. Parking also quite difficult, so pls carpool to save time and space. Some table you have to sit on the floor (bersila), so if you cant do that, better make a reservation before coming here. Good place to explore, as I also didnt know about this place even though already stay in JB for 15 years 😀
author: Aizat Aziz

review_text:
The price is reasonable for the generous portion. Parking is easy, and the restaurant offers a comfortable, relaxing atmosphere with soothing background music. Service is fast too. The only thing that could be improved is the staff’s friendliness so that would make the dining experience perfect.

Additional tip: Make sure to check the seafood prices when making your selection so you can stay within your budget.
author: Shaaa

review_text: The food phenomenal especially the ikan bakar which is the star of the meal and their specialty. No need for extra drippings as the sambal topped with chili's and onions does the job of elevating the crispy edges, tender and juicy fish. The tomyam is tangy, flavourful and fragrant and keeps you wanting more. Highly recommended.
author: M F

review_text: Staff were fast and friendly, immediately coming to our table to refill beef and lamb without us having to ask. The soup was flavourful, and the ingredients were fresh and well-prepared. I really liked the variety of sauces and the self-service counter for vegetables and seafood. The atmosphere was cosy and clean, making it comfortable to enjoy our meal. Price is also affordable for the quality and portion served .definitely worth coming again!

review_text:
Good day.

Service from the staff is excellent, from top to toe, but the place is not really conducive. Cooker hood must be placed at the top of every stove so that heat are not trapped inside the restaurant. It is very uncomfortable, guys. I am sweating, lack of oxygen. I am really looking forward to the room of improvement cause they have potential. In order to sustain, please do improve.

I'm not comparing this shop with others but perhaps with RM45, we're allowed to have a variety of choices,
1. Not too many varieties of foods and drinks. Glad we can refill the chicken, beef, lamb slices as many as we want. The concept is similar with Sukiya.
2. No free desserts such as ice cream.
3. The soup is quite salty. I have mushroom beef bone and miso for steambot soup. Not quite sure which one is salty.

But, to have a steambot and grill at one place, I am glad.

RM45/pax. Have toilet, clean. Open at 3pm-12am.
Booking if you want to come in a group. Can whatsapp.

From,
Food lover.

review_text:
The whole place for this location has mixed reviews and we needed to fully grasp what is what..

Lets dive in!

Food:
The ordered food was rather nice and simple. We did enjoy that part. The snacks and spread options at the front was rather appealing and basically it was the source of hype. With many different choices, one could be lost in wonders. Similarly, the drinks had rusty cups and we were torn to to even touch.

Service:
Staff wasnt really smiling. In fact, at times, we were not able to find any staff to seek for assistance.  The seating area was too differentiated. One was right behind the spread, while the other area is along another corridor towards another side.

Atmosphere:
We would say that it does give out a unique charm and definitely they have strong selling points. But they are not maximizing on this leverage. One strong thing we noted was the tables.. it wasnt even cleaned/wiped.. having a great established restaurant without cleanliness as priority, leads to insects and inconvenience to many customers.

All in all, we would recommend to come over at least once.. the place has a unique charm.. but just needs some improvements on their business take; for a cleaner perspective and foundation, to push it up a level.

Cheers!
author: Sten (Piqued Wanderer)

review_text:
Came here with high expectations due to the hype, but unfortunately our experience fell short in many aspects. The nasi lemak was tasteless and slightly undercooked, which was disappointing for such a basic staple. What made it worse was noticing a trail of ants near the nasi lemak basket, which was quite off-putting.

We sampled several kuih, and honestly, none were enjoyable except the kaswi, which was soft and genuinely nice. The kuih sagu merah was extremely hard — my husband had to press down three times just to cut through it. The same goes for the cara manis, which was thick and not soft at all, definitely not freshly made. The mee soto tasted oddly sweet, and although my husband tried his best to finish it, the taste was unpleasant. Drinks didn’t fare any better. The teh ais was extremely “ceroi” (diluted); I could only manage a few sips. The hot coffee was just so-so, nothing memorable.

Service and queue management were another letdown. Based on the guidelines pasted on the door, someone was supposed to handle the queue numbers, but no one was manning it when we arrived. When we went inside to ask, we were told off rudely by the same staff member that other reviewers have already mentioned. This was confusing, especially since there were many empty tables inside, yet the queue was poorly managed. Overall, I genuinely don’t understand the hype. The food and drinks were below expectations and not worth the prices paid. This visit felt like a waste of money, and sadly, it’s not a place we would return to.

review_text:

review_text:

We informed the employess to hopefully give every table a wipe down but only gave ours a wipe down. Thats crazy. Your night crew AND morning crew didnt do a once over? The mess on the table was literally rotting over night. Then when he came to wipe down he literally wiped it off the table. So then it was on OUR CHAIRS??? Ridiculous. I ended up wiping it myself. Other customers were also looking around to see who was going to help them out but i guess hunger won out.

The food? Pretty decent. There are better versions out there but this isnt a bad place to land. The kuehs are also not bad. Lots of variety and decently tasting but clearly most of it is a prepacked factory made situation.

The ulam served were cabbage and cucumber only.
Ulek is the traditional& manual way Indonesians prepare the sambal terasi. In Malaysia we use the lesung batu. Some ulek/cobek is made from stones /volcano stones, some made from wood.

review_text:
I was really looking forward to eating here because of the good reviews and the aesthetic of the place. But i ended up being disappointed by the whole experience.

Food:
Select the ayam bakar because the only thing available was that or ayam goreng. Ayam taste average,it comes with ulam,telur asin,tempeh and tahu.My father ulam had a tiny snail still attach on the ulam. They also give sambal and sambal kicap. Its more on the sweeter side with barely any spice kick.

Service:

Shop stated they open at 9am, we came at 9.20am and the staff said they werent ready?! The staff were still cutting  tempeh and tahu at the dining area when we came in. It’s like makcik2 doing dishes kenduri style.I was going to order since no one acknowledge our existence for the first 10mins. Only then the staff said they werent ready and the only dish available was the ayam bakar. Was upset about it because i really want to choose the kambing bakar. Since we already here,we said okay and she said to wait first. The staff was courteous and told us to enjoy the free flow drink and kuih in the mean time.

At about 9.45am then only a staff came up to take our order. And then he told us they only have ayam goreng or ayam bakar.

My food only arrive at 9.54am. Honestly if you guys not going to be ready by 9am, might as well open at  10am.

Atmosphere:
I really like the aesthetic. Reminded me of the old kampung house of my relative. There’s surau at the outdoor and the toilet is also a standalone toilet at the outdoor area. Lota of ants crawling but i dont really mind because it’s a kampung experience.

review_text:
Came here for lunch with my parents. We were excited about the P.Ramlee-themed eatery.

The restaurant was not that decorative, except for a few memorables, murals and paintings in an attempt to give off that Classical malay movie theme vibe. Most importantly the place was clean and spacious.

Ordering was relatively easy, via pencil and menu method. However, waiting for your order to arrive was slightly longer than i expected, since there was barely a lunchtime crowd. Honestly, without my mobile, i wouldn't know how to keep myself entertained.

Prices were reasonable.
Small menu selection.

Just one thing i need to point out is that because i am a fan of Malay breakfast especially the gravy ones, i was quite baffled about the gravy.

It says Laksa but its flavour was not distinctive. Sometimes i feel like I was having Laksa with a Lontong gravy. 3⭐

Mee Kicap was sweet. Maybe a tad too much Sweet Soy Sauce for me. And this was a feedback from my dad who is diabetic. 3⭐

Dry Mee Na Mi was ok. The setup is like the Laksa Nyonya but the gravy is separated, since its called Dry Mee Na Mi. 3⭐

Buttery Bites, which i came for because many influencers made it viral. It was ok too. Its like Kaya Toast but the fillings are coated outside the bread. But credit to them for not making them overly sweet. 3.5⭐

Eskrem & Loaf was the saviour of the Day. Nice blend of warm pastry and ice cream. 4⭐

Thank you Mee Na Mi for the wonderful experience. Hopefully, you can add more items on the menu, other than noodles. Maybe some rice or western menu or live fried food station. Would i come again ?

Yes, i would, in Shaa Allah.

review_text:
Had lunch at this little shop. The Mee goreng and Nasi lemak were excellent. As a spicy food lover, the Mee goreng pedas gila was really good. Not soggy in any way. The Nasi lemak was fragrant and the sambal had a wonderfully full flavour that made the Nasi with the accompanying freshly fried peanuts and ikan bilis a really good treat. Wish they had some ayam goreng berempah that would have rounded it off nicely.

The shop also has a selection of cakes, of which I can attest that the cheese cakes are excellent as well. They are just right, being not too sweet nor overly rich that leaves you feeling jelak.

Overall I would give 5 stars for the experience and food.

If you have kids, they also have a traditional games corner- with 5 stones and bottle caps to keep the little ones entertained.
